title: KS-2055's two fragments disagree: the cheat says the product code changes by one line, the flow says two lines (G276-1)
description:
**BLUF:** The two documentation fragments that PR 2113 added for KS-2055 give different sizes for the same product change. The cheat fragment says "Product code changes, by one line"; the flow fragment says "The product change is two lines". The diff of `Blockchain/Dev/services/transfer/src/index.ts` is +2 -1 (one line added, one changed). A wording defect between two fragments; no code or behaviour is affected. Low: accepted at the merge and ticketed by the board seat after it. Read at develop `e8d23ce366e2` (PR 2113's squash).

Source: finding G276-1 (low, wording), line 51 of `/Volumes/DevMASTER/WEDNESDAY/0_Brain/reference/2026-11-09_gate276-tier2-pr2113-ks2055h1/verdict.md`, on PR 2113 head `521ffe0f777f`, gate 276 (tier 2), verdict GO WITH NOTES. The gate's words: the diff is +2 -1 ("one added line, one changed line, plus the comment on the added line"), "Harmless but the two fragments disagree."

## Where

At `e8d23ce366e2`, read through the contents API:

* `Projects Documents/fragments/cheat/KS-2055-transfer-cancel-history-records-the-status-it-moved-from.html`, line 3: "Product code changes, by one line. ... gains one const previousStatus and fromStatus reads it (+2 -1)".
* `Projects Documents/fragments/flow/KS-2055-transfer-cancel-history-records-the-status-it-moved-from.html`, line 7: "The product change is two lines. A const previousStatus placed before the assignment, and fromStatus: previousStatus in place of fromStatus: transfer.status."

The PR (read at the API): merged 2026-11-09T06:31:57Z, 4 files, +165 -1: the product file above (+2 -1), the new test file `Blockchain/Dev/services/transfer/src/__tests__/ks2055-transfer-cancel-history-records-the-status-it-moved-from.test.ts` (+134), and the two fragments (+18 and +11).

One more thing I saw in the same fragment, not part of the gate's finding: the cheat's Figures row (line 15) reads "2 files against develop" and names the product file (+2 -1) and the test file (+134), while the PR is 4 files, +165 -1 because the two fragments are the other two. That is the same Figures-row shape as KS-2150 (PR 2111), and a fix to this ticket can take both.

## Fix shape (the owner's call)

Docs only, size S, a new change on develop. Make the two fragments say the same thing about the product change, for example "two lines of `Blockchain/Dev/services/transfer/src/index.ts` (one added, one changed; +2 -1)" in both. The Figures row can name the whole PR or say what it counts.

## Not done, not read

I did not render the page or run the test file, and I did not read the PR body or the ticket comment 872bc167 (the gate lists both as not tested). The gate's two Info findings on this PR (G276-2, no cell cancels a draft transfer; G276-3, one cell does not assert the 200) are recorded and not ticketed, by Wednesday's ruling.

title: The platform-admin login stamps a claim of its own, so the gateway can refuse tenantless tokens except platform admins (KS-619 follow-up)
description:
**BLUF:** KS-619 needs a marker that does not exist yet. The gateway should refuse a token that carries no tenant, except for a platform admin; but nothing in a platform admin's token says it came from the platform-admin login, and the roles that login mints are not in the shared platform-role list, so a refusal keyed on role locks them out of the whole gateway. The fix Kam chose: the platform-admin login stamps one claim that only that branch sets; the gateway's tenant refusal excepts it; refresh tokens carry it; platform admins re-login once after it deploys. Two services (auth and api-gateway), tier 1, security. Kam ruled the split on 2026-11-09 17:20:38 (card `secuura-ks619-platform-admin-login-no-marker-1109`, option a, "Split"); the tenant-refusal half of KS-619 comes out of PR 2128, which keeps only the user-id and role guard (no lockout), and this ticket carries the rest.

## The ruling, quoted

Kam, verbatim (live board, 17:20:38): "Decision secuura-ks619-platform-admin-login-no-marker-1109: a — Split". Option a: "PR 2128 keeps only the user-id and role guard (no lockout). KS-619 becomes its own ticket: the platform-admin login stamps one claim and the gateway excepts it. Two services, tier 1; platform admins re-login once after it deploys."

## Facts, each with its source

1. **The refusal locked a population out (gate 285, finding G285-1, MEDIUM).** Source: `/Volumes/DevMASTER/WEDNESDAY/0_Brain/reference/2026-11-09_gate285-tier1-pr2128-ks1208-ks619/verdict.md`, from line 21, on PR 2128 head `aff0f43e4079`. The login issues the roles `platform_admin`, `platform_viewer` and (the Azure default) `admin`, with no tenant. The shared `isPlatformRole` (`Blockchain/Dev/packages/shared/src/security/keyRevokePolicy.ts`) is false for all three (the gate measured it with node on the built dist; controls `super_admin`, `system_admin` and `Super_Admin` are true). With the refusal in place and a token shaped as that login mints it, the gate's cells read: platform_admin on a required mount, develop 200 and head 401; platform_viewer on a required and on an optional mount, develop 200 and head 401; controls (a super_admin with no tenant, and an owner token) unchanged. It fails closed, so the gate did not call it a hole.
2. **Reach was not measured.** The gate did no live count. The note in KS-1536 says a Kintsugi count found no `platform_admin` rows on that path; `platform_viewer` and `admin` were not counted, and Azure was never counted.
3. **The code today, re-read by me.** At develop `6beac8734a2f` (Wednesday's addendum cites Seat G 31st's read of the same lines), the platform-admin login in `Blockchain/Dev/services/auth/src/routes/auth.ts` builds its `syntheticUser` with `tenantId: undefined` and `tenantSlug: undefined` (lines 394 to 410) and mints with `role: platformAdmin.role` (lines 470 to 473). `generateAccessToken` in `Blockchain/Dev/services/auth/src/services/jwt.ts` (lines 187 to 209) builds one claim set for every login mint (`userId`, `email`, `role`, `organizationId`, `verificationLevel`, `sessionId`, `type`, `tenantId`, `tenantSlug`, then scopes or the OAuth labels), and `signToken` (lines 175 to 182) signs with the single provisioned key with no issuer or audience option. So no claim distinguishes a platform-admin login from any other mint, which is why the refusal had to go by role.
4. **The build shape is Kam's** (card above, option a): the login stamps one claim only that branch sets; the gateway's tenant refusal excepts it; refresh tokens carry it; platform admins re-login once after the deploy. Which claim name and value, and how the gateway verifies it, are for the build to propose.

## Not done, not measured

No live count of platform-admin rows (point 2). I did not re-read the gateway's present handling of a token with no tenant claim, or the refresh-token path. Nothing was run.

## Related

KS-619 (the gateway falls through to the caller's tenant header when a token has no tenant claim; this ticket is its remaining half) and KS-1208 (a verified token without a role or userId claim; PR 2128 delivers its guard). Both are linked as related.

## Searched before filing

Board, includeArchived, title and description and every comment of each open candidate; controls pass (the positive control hit its known ticket KS-1379, a random token hit 0). `KS-619`: 13 candidates, 10 open literal hits (KS-621, KS-1032, KS-1084, KS-1091, KS-1536, KS-1553, KS-1673, KS-1704, KS-2109, KS-2145), none a ticket for a login claim; KS-619 itself was read (its description to 2,600 characters and its two newest comments). `platform-admin login`: 94 candidates, 5 open (KS-783 and KS-919 on TOTP recovery and the demo account's MFA, KS-1132 on an infrastructure failure read as no admin, KS-1384, KS-2120): KS-2120 was read, it rewords one comment about this login (PR 2112) and carries no claim work. `tenantless token`: 93 candidates, 4 open (KS-1406, KS-1652, KS-1655, KS-1740): KS-1406 was read, it is the users lookup and stub guard that fails open for a tenantless token, a different route and fix. `platform_admin`: 108 candidates, 18 open, judged by title and search context; the near neighbours are KS-1536 (the role vocabulary) and KS-1132. No open ticket carries the claim-and-exception work.

---

nodes.body:
**Cause:** UAT's `entra-vid-client-secret` is stale. The app log shows `AADSTS7000215: Invalid client secret provided` for the shared app registration `platform-s-verified-id` (`f445c68d-…`). That app's secret was rotated on 26 Oct 2026 and dev-ps was updated the same day. UAT's copy dates from 11 Sep, so UAT has been broken since 26 Oct, not since today's deploy. The details and the fix are on PS-1613.

**Moved from Issues Dev-ps to Issues Uat-ps.** It was filed under dev-ps because UAT shares dev-ps's PostHog project, and that project's only destination (`Linear: Issues Dev-ps`) doesn't filter on the event's `environment` property. The fix is in PostHog: filter that destination to `environment = dev-ps`, and add a `Linear: Issues Uat-ps` destination filtered to `uat-ps` (`docs/runbooks/posthog-bug-report-destination.md`).

title: Anchoring docs must say, after KS-1384 stage 1: one anchor row per document, a paid transaction per share and lifecycle event
description:
**BLUF:** The platform-k pages that describe anchoring do not yet record how anchoring behaves now that KS-1384 stage 1 is on both boxes (Stuart's words, 2026-11-09). They must state two facts, and nothing else new: (1) there is one anchor row per document and network; (2) until KS-1384 stage 2, every admitted share and lifecycle event pays its own Cardano transaction on that same row, and the row then names only the latest transaction. Stuart asked for this ticket before KS-1807 closes: it is the part of the S<->K contract that systemTest most needs written down. This is a DOCS build item: a build seat writes the pages. No code changes, and nothing is built for the paid-transaction behaviour (Kam's ruling below).

## What the pages must state

1. **One anchor row per document and network.** The unique key on `(document_id, network)` is migration 031. A repeat post upserts that row instead of adding one.
2. **Until KS-1384 stage 2, each admitted share and lifecycle event pays its own transaction on the same row.** An admitted event carries a new payload, so no earlier attempt counts as the same one; it builds a new transaction, and the row then names only the latest transaction hash. Stage 1 did not add this and was not built to stop it: its shared-coin rule covers repeat attempts of one payload. Stage 2 gives each event its own row, on its own schedule.
3. **Do not write** that stage 1 stops an event paying again, or that a share is "idempotent" at the transaction level. The route's code comment says "idempotent: reuses the document's existing anchor", which holds for the anchor id and not for the transaction.

## The authority, quoted

Kam's card `secuura-ks1384-share-pays-second-tx-before-stage2-1106`, ruled option a at 2026-11-06 21:04:52 (AEDT): "Leave it until stage 2". The option's own words: "Admitted events keep paying one fee each. Nothing is built for this. Stage 2 gives each event its own row, on its own schedule."

## The measurement behind it (KS-1384, two comments of 2026-11-06, read whole)

* Comment e0731289 (08:36:03Z): the share route calls `emitLifecycleAnchor`, which posts to `POST /api/anchors`; the upsert sets the row back to pending with a null hash and `processAnchor` runs again. Every post stamps its own `timestamp`, so the payload differs. Measured on the real submitter and wallet view with a stand-in chain and the upsert simulated from its SET list: a share whose payload replaces the stored one built a second transaction on a second coin and the row ended naming the second hash. Transfer-custody, revoke and lifecycle events use the same emitter, so by code they behave the same; not observed. Not measured: the fee of either transaction, which route posted the share, any other document.
* Comment 2126a1f7 (08:40:40Z): a read-only box read on kintsugi at 2026-11-06 08:34:59Z found 1 row in the anchor table for the document, status confirmed, naming the share's transaction; the upload's transaction was in 0 rows. The comment's own limit: one table at one moment, no history, no chain read.

## Where today's docs stand

`Blockchain/Dev/docs/S-K-OWNERSHIP-CONTRACT.md` still marks the anchoring part ON HOLD until the KS-1384 build lands: line 17 ("ON HOLD until the KS-1384 build lands and not assessed: flat-anchor `onBehalfOf`, `metadata.rowHash` ...") and line 302 ("The flat-anchor part is ON HOLD (KS-1384)"), read at develop `204e62acdc35`. Stuart's comment of 2026-11-09 05:09Z on KS-1807 says the same: that section "is still marked on hold until the KS-1384 build lands. Stage 1 is on both boxes." The builder finds any other page that describes anchoring; I read only the contract's lines above, not the other pages.

## Not decided here

When stage 2 lands, what it changes in the pages, and whether the flat-anchor `onBehalfOf` and `rowHash` parts can come off hold: those stay with KS-1384. This ticket records today's behaviour only.

## Related

KS-1807 (the docs-up-to-date ticket; it stays open until these pages land, by Stuart's request) and KS-1384 (the build; stage 2 is its next part). Both are linked as related.

## Searched before filing

Board, includeArchived, title and description and every comment of each open candidate; controls pass (the positive control hit its known ticket KS-1379, a random token hit 0). `one anchor row`: 89 candidates, 4 open literal hits (KS-607, KS-1384, KS-1385, KS-1664): KS-1384 is the build this ticket documents; KS-607 (anchor and verify statuses disagree), KS-1385 (emitted anchors carry no documentType) and KS-1664 (recertify anchors before it writes its row) are different subjects, judged by title and search context. `anchoring pages`: 100 candidates, 1 open (KS-1807, the docs umbrella, which holds Stuart's request as a comment and is not a ticket for these pages). `one fee each`: 1 open, KS-2107, read whole: it rewords five code comments in originate (PR 2103), text only, no documentation page. `its own Cardano transaction`, `anchoring documentation` and `anchor row per document`: 0 open hits. `ON HOLD until the KS-1384`: 1 open (KS-1807). `stage 2`: 4 open (KS-1384, KS-1385, KS-1807, KS-2107). Read whole besides KS-2107: KS-1384's two comments of 2026-11-06 and KS-1807's newest comment. No open ticket tracks the anchoring documentation pages.

title: UAT deployment runbook: promote develop to uat-ps (3690b63 → develop), with the secrets, KMS terraform and backup steps it needs
description:
## Goal

Deploy `develop` to uat-ps, following a written runbook: `docs/runbooks/deploy-uat.md`. It is linked from `ssd/dep-aws-uat/README.md`, which keeps the mechanics.

The runbook sets the order: what UAT runs now (read over SSM) → the gap (deploy-file diff, new migrations, secret names against `setenv.sh` fetches) → terraform for the missing secrets → pre-deploy checks (dev-ps first, platform-k order, `mysqldump`) → `build-and-deploy-manual.sh` → post-checks → rollback.

## Gap measured 9 Nov 2026 (names and metadata only, no values)

* UAT runs `3690b63` (develop, #1145, 24 Oct), `restarts=0`. It is 709 commits and **24 migrations** behind develop (`a77652e`), so a rollback means restoring the database dump.
* **Required and missing:** `log-pseudonym-key` ([PS-1385](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1385/retire-appspecificdocstoragekey-its-only-remaining-job-is-the-log)). `setenv.sh` aborts without it.
* **Optional and missing:** `document-keys-instance-role-arn` **and** `document-keys-admin-role-arn`**.** The [PS-951](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-951/key-store-abstraction-key-vault-kms-wrap-unwrap-with-a-local-dev) KMS terraform is not applied, so the AwsKms key store would refuse every key operation.
* Optional and missing, a choice each: `posthog-project-token`, `github-client-id` / `github-client-secret`, and the four `*-retired` slots.
* `doc-storage-key` is no longer fetched. Delete it after a healthy deploy.
* `identity-data-encryption-key` is now required and present (set 11 Sep, the rebuild day). `3690b63` has no identity sweep, so record the Health identity figures after the deploy.

## Steps

- [X] Docs-only PR for the runbook (#1435)
- [ ] Stuart: add `log-pseudonym-key` to UAT `terraform.tfvars`, plan (the instance must not be replaced), apply, and push the tfvars back to the store
- [ ] Recheck secret names; mysqldump on the box
- [ ] Deploy and post-checks; record the results here
- [ ] Delete `doc-storage-key` from `kv_secrets` afterwards

nodes.body:
**Entra Verified ID fails on UAT with "Failed to obtain access token". This is a stale secret, not caused by the deploy.**

The app log has the cause: `AADSTS7000215: Invalid client secret provided` (`invalid_client`, 401) for app `f445c68d-c73f-4519-a4d0-53e98058f982`.

Metadata only, no values:
- UAT uses the shared app registration `platform-s-verified-id`, the same as dev-ps.
- The app has one client secret, `dev-ps-entra-verified-id-Rot-Oct26`, created 26 Oct 2026. The previous secret was removed at that rotation.
- dev-ps Key Vault `secuura-ps-dev-kv` / `entra-vid-client-secret` was updated on 26 Oct 2026 at 09:46 UTC.
- UAT `/secuura/uat/entra-vid-client-secret` was last set on 11 Sep 2026, so it holds the removed secret. UAT's Verified ID has been broken since 26 Oct, before this deploy.

**Fix (Stuart, a secret):**
1. Set `entra-vid-client-secret` in the UAT tfvars to dev-ps's current value. Use the secret's value, not its ID.
2. Run a targeted plan and apply on `aws_secretsmanager_secret_version.app["entra-vid-client-secret"]`. Expect 1 to add, 1 to destroy.
3. Push the tfvars back to the store.
4. Restart services on UAT so `setenv.sh` re-renders the config.

**Runbook point:** the step 2 secret check compares names only, so a rotated value elsewhere does not show up. When a shared app registration (Verified ID) is rotated for dev-ps, UAT needs the same value.

**UAT deployed: `a77652e` is running** (9 Nov 2026, container started 06:02:50 UTC).

**`build-and-deploy-manual.sh` ran end to end with exit 0:**
- demo-pk spec check passed (14 verbs).
- Trivy gate passed.
- Pushed `ssd:a77652e`, digest `sha256:02b289698d746aa58ff9587f928c512feed7e1ab2fe0f78cd657738bb404e1d9`.
- SSM deploy printed its completion marker.
- Sign-in page returned 200 on the third attempt (two 502s while the app started).
- platform-k reachable from the container.
- The container runs the pushed digest and reports `a77652e`.

**Post-checks:**
- `/Health/Data`, read as an Administrator:
  - Commit `a77652e`, ref develop, PR 1432.
  - Migrations: 101 applied, latest `20261106063728_PS1583AttachCopiesSetting`, none pending. All 24 new ones applied on this start.
  - Errors in buffer: 0.
- Box: `restarts=0`, no `exited with code 137`, 827 MB available.
- Document keys:
  - Store is `AwsKms`, and 13 `alias/secuura-uat-org-*` keys exist.
  - The migration sweep is draining legacy blobs: 6 → 4 within the first minute, 0 failures.
- Signing: PDF signatures inside the file, the three timestamp authorities all issuing, nothing awaiting a timestamp. Same as dev-ps.
- Platform-k: 11 organisations registered, 0 failed, connector keys 0 under a retired key, 0 unopenable.

**Expected warnings, none caused by this deploy:**
- Admin MFA not enforced (PS-438 ruling for UAT).
- Anchor failed: 2 (K-side, KS-535).
- Stripe webhook: none yet since the restart.
- Mail provider "(not set)" means the Mailgun default.

**Open:**
- **Identity rotation figures are "not measured yet"**, because `Identity:RootRotationEnabled` is false on develop's template. Whether any identity value was under the old fallback root can only be read once the sweep runs, which needs #1435 merged and a config sync. The dump above is the way back.
- After #1435 is merged: sync `ssd/dep-aws-uat/` to the box and restart, then read both rotation sections.
- tfvars: put `doc-storage-key` back until the new build has run long enough to trust, then remove it from `kv_secrets` and apply. `ciam-client-secret` is already scheduled for deletion (recovery until 16 Nov).
- A real flow (sign in, upload, share, sign one document) has not been driven yet.
- The `Deployed to UAT` state for the tickets this build carries has not been set.

**UAT deploy starting: `3690b63` → `a77652e`** (develop, #1432). The build runs under amd64 emulation and the Trivy scan comes before the push, so expect the whole run to take 20–40 minutes.

**Preconditions met (9 Nov):**
- dev-ps runs `a77652e`, with 0 restarts since 6 Nov.
- Terraform, a targeted apply at 13:50 created:
  - `log-pseudonym-key` and `posthog-project-token`;
  - the KMS role `uat-document-key-admin` and its policy;
  - the `document-keys-instance-role-arn` and `document-keys-admin-role-arn` secrets;
  - the server policy's KMS statements;
  - the IMDS hop limit change, 1 → 2, in place.

  It also scheduled `ciam-client-secret` for deletion, with a 7-day recovery window.
- A second targeted apply at 13:56 replaced six secret values with the tfvars values, as Stuart asked: `azure-openai-key`, `exchange-rate-api-key`, `mailgun-key` and the three `stripe-test-*` keys. `posthog-project-token` was in that plan too but unchanged (still its 13:50 version).
- `doc-storage-key` is kept for now. The current build still requires it, and the tfvars must have it back before the next full apply.
- Secret names: every required fetch in develop's `setenv.sh` is present. The only optional ones missing are the GitHub pair and the four `*-retired` slots.

title: No cell pins verify() resolving verified:false where it used to reject: all 8 KS-1973 cells call private methods via a cast (G273-2108-3)
description:
**BLUF:** PR 2108 (KS-1973) changed what the credential verifier's public `verify()` does when a DID resolver throws an unreadable value: it used to reject, it now resolves with `verified: false` and `checks.issuerDID: false`. None of the 8 cells the PR added calls `verify()`. All 8 reach the private `verifyIssuerDID` and `verifySignature` through an `as unknown as Priv` cast, so the headline change is pinned by no cell: a later edit that lets the issuer lookup's failure escape `verify()` again would leave all 8 green. Low, by Wednesday's ruling on gate 273: accepted at merge, ticketed Low by the board seat after the merge. A test-coverage gap; no behaviour defect was found. Read at develop `e028786a0921` (PR 2108's squash).

Source: finding G273-2108-3 (Low; test quality), line 98 of `/Volumes/DevMASTER/WEDNESDAY/0_Brain/reference/2026-11-09_gate273-tier1-g30-batch/verdict.md`, on PR 2108 head `678512909761`, verdict GO WITH NOTES. The gate's words: "All 8 cells drive the private verifyIssuerDID/verifySignature through a cast. The PR's headline behaviour change (verify() used to reject and now resolves verified:false) is pinned by no cell. I measured it (above). A cell on the public verify() would pin it."

## Where

`Blockchain/Dev/packages/shared/src/__tests__/ks1973-vc-verifier-issuer-lookup-and-ed25519-catches-unreadable-throw.test.ts`, added by PR 2108. At `e028786a0921`: lines 14 to 17 declare `type Priv` with the two private methods; line 38 calls `(verifier as unknown as Priv).verifyIssuerDID(...)` and line 47 calls `(verifier as unknown as Priv).verifySignature(...)`. The file holds 8 `it` cells (controls C1 to C3, RED cells R1 to R5) and 0 calls of the public `.verify(`.

The code the cells do not reach, in `Blockchain/Dev/packages/shared/src/vc/verifier.ts` at `e028786a0921`: `verify()` starts at line 102 and calls `await this.verifyIssuerDID(credential)` at line 136; `allChecksPass = Object.values(checks).every(Boolean)` is at line 187 and `verified: allChecksPass` at line 202. The PR's hunks sit at lines 400 to 408 (the Ed25519 inner catch) and 463 to 471 (the issuer-lookup catch).

## What the gate measured (its Q3; I did not re-run it)

With a scratch cell driving the public `verify()`, develop against the PR head: a DID resolver rejecting a revoked Proxy, an object whose `toString` throws, or a Symbol makes develop's `verify()` REJECT; the head resolves with `verified: false`, `checks.issuerDID: false` and the entry "Failed to resolve DID ...: unreadable thrown value" (or the Symbol's text). An ordinary Error gives `verified: false` on both trees. Hunk B (the Ed25519 inner catch) is text-only on develop already. That scratch cell was not added to the PR.

## Why it stays Low

The gate found both hunks unreachable from the only two production callers (the two vc-issuer routes pass no `didResolver`, so the lookup is skipped), and nothing becomes more permissive. The class is exported from the shared package barrel, so an outside consumer that wires a resolver is the one a `verify()` cell would protect.

One cell on the public `verify()` per RED value (R1 to R3: revoked Proxy, throwing `toString`, Symbol) expecting a resolved result with `verified === false` and `checks.issuerDID === false`, plus one control for an ordinary Error expecting the same shape. Size S, one test file. Not decided here.

title: An ORG_ADMIN can read another tenant's counts: GET /api/admin/dashboard reads the raw x-tenant-override header (split from KS-1847 item 4)
description:
**BLUF:** By a reading of the code at develop `273de443c30c`, an `ORG_ADMIN` can read another tenant's document, user, verification and anchor counts, or the platform-wide totals, through `GET /api/admin/dashboard`. The route reads the raw `x-tenant-override` header itself and runs its count queries under platform scope, and none of the four files I read between the client and the route removes the header for a caller who is not a platform role. Counts only. Read from code, not exercised live; NOT read: the generic proxy's default header pass-through. Split from KS-1847 item 4 by Wednesday's ruling of 2026-11-09 10:28 AEDT. Medium.

## The chain (each line read at develop `273de443c30c` through the contents API)

1. Edge. `Blockchain/Dev/services/api-gateway/src/utils/trustHeaders.ts` line 41: `TRUST_HEADER_ALLOW_LIST = new Set(['x-tenant-override'])`; line 49 exempts that header from the edge strip, so a client-supplied value passes.
2. Gateway auth. `Blockchain/Dev/services/api-gateway/src/middleware/auth.ts` lines 696 to 704: the header is read at 696 and decides `x-tenant-id` only when `isPlatformRole(decoded.role)` (697 to 700); otherwise `x-tenant-id` comes from the JWT (701 to 704). The file's only references to the header are lines 696 to 698: it is never deleted for a caller who is not a platform role.
3. Gateway proxy. `Blockchain/Dev/services/api-gateway/src/routes/proxy.ts` lines 1256 to 1269: `/api/admin/` passes `authenticateToken(true)` and `enforceAdminProxy`, then proxies to originate. `enforceAdminProxy` admits `isPlatformOrOrgAdminRole(user.role)`.
4. The predicate. `Blockchain/Dev/packages/shared/src/security/keyRevokePolicy.ts` lines 163 to 166: `isPlatformOrOrgAdminRole` is true for SYSTEM_ADMIN and SUPER_ADMIN (`PLATFORM_ROLES`, line 60) and for ORG_ADMIN.
5. The route. `Blockchain/Dev/services/originate/src/routes/adminConfig.ts`: line 45, the router gate `requireRole('SYSTEM_ADMIN', 'ORG_ADMIN')`; line 603, `GET /dashboard`; lines 621 to 623 read `req.headers['x-tenant-override']` and accept it when it has a UUID shape; lines 632 to 679 count documents (joined to users), users, verification audit rows and anchors under `runWithPlatformScope`, filtered to that tenant when the header is set and platform-wide when it is not.
6. originate keeps the header on a vouched request. `Blockchain/Dev/services/originate/src/utils/gatewayProvenance.ts` lines 140 to 147: the header is dropped only from an unvouched request, because it is "deliberately ALLOWED through the gateway's edge strip" for the auth middleware to decide.

## Not read, not done

NOT read: the generic proxy's default header pass-through (http-proxy-middleware's own behaviour; `Blockchain/Dev/services/api-gateway/src/routes/proxy.ts` carries no header list, and `Blockchain/Dev/services/api-gateway/src/utils/originateForward.ts` mints the vouch header only). No runtime probe: no box, no live call, no token. Everything above is the text of the files at the sha named.

## Independent reads

1. KS-1847 item 4, read from code at develop `530f09112` on 2026-10-30.
2. Our QA gate 275, finding G275-2111-2 (Info in the gate, "Severity if confirmed: Moderate, as its own ticket"; pre-existing, outside PR 2111's diff), line 61 of `/Volumes/DevMASTER/WEDNESDAY/0_Brain/reference/2026-11-09_gate275-tier1-t19-d5d6/verdict.md`, read from code only.

## Why a ticket of its own

KS-1847 (Backlog, board account, priority 3) holds this as one of five docs-versus-code items. An ORG_ADMIN reading another tenant's counts is a cross-tenant authorisation defect on an auth surface, and its fix (a gateway strip or an originate scope) is a different change from the docs items. KS-1847 keeps its other items, with a pointer comment; its state and priority are not changed.

Either the gateway removes `x-tenant-override` for a caller who is not a platform role (the else branch at line 701 of `Blockchain/Dev/services/api-gateway/src/middleware/auth.ts`), or originate's dashboard honours the override only when the verified role is a platform role, read from the verified request context rather than the raw header (the direction KS-1847 names). MEASURED by the gate (positive control `ln -sf "$JQ_BIN" "$root/bin/jq"` judged yes): the predicate needs the line to START with `ln`, to carry a flag word with an `s`, and to END with `bin/jq`, an optional quote, then the end of the line or one of `;&|#`. title: Launcher census refuses an exec-only script: start, stop, kill, rm, pause and unpause match as any word after docker compose (F-2070-1)
description:

A committed script that only runs `docker compose exec api npm start` is therefore flagged as a platform launcher and refused with "A script runs the platform compose stack but is in neither list (KS-1355)". Medium is Wednesday's ruling (ANSWER to B 106th, point 1, finding G243-F1).

Source: `/Volumes/DevMASTER/WEDNESDAY/0_Brain/reference/2026-11-07_gate243-tier2-batch/verdict.md`, finding F-2070-1 (Minor to Moderate) on PR 2070, head `0ae8aa98046c`, verdict GO WITH NOTES, accepted at merge.

## Evidence

MEASURED by the gate (it extracted the PR's own `_launcher_calls_compose` and ran one-line probes; positive control `docker compose up -d` FLAGGED):

* Flagged on the PR head, clean on develop before it: `docker compose exec api npm start`, `docker compose exec -T api pm2 stop all`, `docker compose exec api rm -rf /tmp/x`, `docker compose logs api rm`, `docker-compose exec api kill 1`.
* Develop already flagged `docker compose exec api npm run build` (the existing class for `run`).
* The suite `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/__tests__/ks1355_slot_blind_launchers.test.sh` pins a bare `exec` and a word that merely STARTS with a verb ("startup"); it does not pin a verb as an argument of `exec`, so nothing fails on this.

READ ONLY (the board seat, at develop `5d6a95c552fd`, `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/check-stack-safety.sh`): the scope comment at line 133 lists the six new verbs; the `lit` regex at line 189 is `(^|[^-[:alnum:]_])docker([[:space:]]+|-)compose([^|;&#]*)[[:space:]](up|run|restart|down|start|stop|kill|rm|pause|unpause)([[:space:]]|$)`, whose `([^|;&#]*)` lets any text sit between `compose` and the verb; the variable-name branch at line 205 repeats the same alternation; the function `_launcher_calls_compose` is at line 212.

Effect: a launcher that only `exec`s into the stack must be sourced through the slot derivation or declared in `LAUNCHER_EXCEPTIONS` with a ticket, a wrong-reason refusal. The guard runs on the push path and in the retired CI workflows.

## Item 1 (N-2068-1): other skip warnings do not increment the skip count

READ ONLY (the gate, and the board seat at develop `6c9a593df4ab`). In `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/smoke-test.sh`, line 275 warns `GDPR endpoints — skipped (no auth token)` and line 402 warns `Platform API — skipped (no admin token)`; neither touches `SKIP` (the counter is declared at line 34 and incremented at lines 45 and 54). READ ONLY. Line 24 is `[ "$GATEWAY" = "http://localhost:6882" ] || DIRECT_PORTS=no`. The gate found nothing that parses `All checks passed.`: `git grep` finds only the suite itself, and the Makefile and the package manifest call the script without parsing it (READ ONLY, the gate's read).

title: systemTest format gate: the line-730 selection pipe may close early on GNU grep and select no package on a large push (gate 247 F74-1)
description:
**BLUF:** `systemTest/scripts/check-package-format.sh` line 730 selects packages with `printf '%s\n' "$changed_paths" | grep "^systemTest/${p}/" > /dev/null`. On the macOS host that works. Gate 247 recalls that GNU grep treats output to `/dev/null` like `-q` and stops at the first match. If so, on Linux the pipe closes early, the pipeline returns 141 under `pipefail`, the package reads as not selected, and the gate exits 0 at line 739 without a word. The GNU premise is the gate's memory and is UNMEASURED. First step: measure the line-730 form on Linux with GNU grep. Medium is Wednesday's ruling (ANSWER to B 104th, PR 2074 notes).

Source: `/Volumes/DevMASTER/WEDNESDAY/0_Brain/reference/2026-11-07_gate247-tier1-tests-tooling/verdict.md`, finding F74-1 (Major, conditional) on PR 2074 (KS-1728 batch 2, merged as `15dca468b86f`). The gate says it is not a reason to hold that PR. The verdict's label is F74-1; the fleet's shorthand "G247-F1" names this finding and also PR 2069's F69-1, so this ticket uses the verdict's label.

## Evidence

* MEASURED AT RUNTIME by the gate (macOS, `/bin/bash` 3.2.57, BSD grep 2.6.0-FreeBSD, the only grep on that host): a wrapper `grep` on PATH that adds `-q` only when stdout is `/dev/null`. With a 1.1 MB changed list, real grep gives exit 1, REFUSED, 3 of 3; the wrapper gives exit 0 with no refusal, 3 of 3; a one-path control gives exit 1, REFUSED. So if a grep behaves like the wrapper, the gate goes silently green.
* UNMEASURED: that GNU grep behaves like the wrapper. No GNU grep was available to the gate.
* READ ONLY (the board seat, at develop `6c9a593df4ab`): line 730 is as quoted; lines 737 to 740 take `selected` empty to `exit 0` with the comment "nothing under a gated package — say nothing, cost nothing". `.githooks/pre-push` lines 375 to 380 speak of Linux and dash, so the hook contemplates Linux pushers.
* The failure needs a grep that stops early and a changed list larger than the pipe buffer. The gate rates the likelihood low on today's macOS pushers, where it does not occur (measured).
* The census behind KS-1728 cannot find this form, because its regex looks for `-q`.

## History

KS-1716 (Done) proposed this exact form as the "read to EOF" fix for the original `grep -q` loss and measured it (3 of 3 runs selected all five packages); the ticket names a 64 KiB macOS pipe buffer and never mentions GNU grep. PR 2074 converted twelve other product lines to the same form. The same measurement also settles F74-2 (the statement "grep reads to EOF" stated without its condition), which Wednesday recorded on the PR without a ticket.

## Fix shape (READ ONLY, not applied)

After the measurement: if GNU grep stops early, select without a writer process (a pure-bash `case` match on the list, as KS-1716 notes PS-1254 did) and add a cell over a path list larger than the pipe buffer on a platform that stops early. If GNU grep reads to EOF, record the measurement here and close.

title: pre-push hook: a failing git diff reads as no change and the hook exits 0 before leg 1, so a RED commit pushes (gate 263 G1)
description:
**BLUF:** The real pre-push hook treats a failing `git diff` as an empty change set. With `git config diff.orderFile` naming a missing file, `git diff` exits 128 with no output, the changed set stays empty, and the hook exits 0 before leg 1: a RED commit pushes with rc 0 and no preflight line. Gate 263 measured this on the hook fixture at `35bcfa000`; the same lines are on develop `6c9a593df4ab`. High is Wednesday's call.

Source: `/Volumes/DevMASTER/WEDNESDAY/0_Brain/reference/2026-11-09_gate263-tier1-x8-prerun-driver-r3/verdict.md`, finding G1 (a note outside the tool under test, which the gate calls the most important thing it found). Not a PR-merge item: it waits on no PR. A build seat fixes the hook; this ticket only records it.

## What was measured, and what was only read

* MEASURED AT RUNTIME by gate 263 (scratch worlds, local bare origins): `git config diff.orderFile <missing file>` makes `git diff` exit 128 with empty output, while `status`, `rev-parse` and `merge-base` still exit 0. The gate probed 17 `diff.*` and `core.*` faults and found this one shape. The real hook fixture, called directly with a new-branch stdin line on a RED commit: with the fault, rc 0 and "Blockchain/Dev changes detected" is never printed; without the fault, rc 1, the preflight ran and failed. Evidence in the gate folder: `evidence/order.out`, produced by `evidence/g263_order.py`.
* On the same fault the pre-run tool (X 8th's) still runs the preflight, so the pre-run path is stronger than the hook here.
* READ ONLY (the board seat, at develop `6c9a593df4ab`; I did not run the hook): in `.githooks/pre-push`, lines 129, 143 and 252 end `|| true` after `git -c core.quotePath=false diff --no-renames --name-only ...`. Line 251 sets `_informative=1` before the diff at line 252, so the KS-882 branch at line 271 (every base contains HEAD, run unconditionally) does not fire. With `changed` empty, line 372 `[ -z "$changed" ] && exit 0` returns success before the preflight message at line 374. These are the lines the gate cited at `35bcfa000`; the gate's fixture hook is not necessarily develop's current hook, and the lines match.

## Why it is the same class as two fixed holes

The hook's own comments record KS-854 (lines 156 to 160: an unresolvable base left `changed` empty and the hook returned success before leg 1) and KS-882 (lines 181 to 187, banner at line 272: a base equal to HEAD gave an empty diff and the same exit). Both fixes treat "cannot compute" as "run the preflight" (lines 276 to 277 and 284 to 285 set `changed` to an unconditional marker and `st_all=1`). A diff that fails is the same case: an uncomputable change set is not a clean one.

## Fix shape (READ ONLY, not applied)

Capture the diff's exit status at lines 129, 143 and 252 instead of discarding it with `|| true`; on a non-zero status take the KS-854 and KS-882 path (banner, unconditional marker, `st_all=1`). Regression test: in a scratch repo set `diff.orderFile` to a missing path, push a RED commit, expect rc 1 and the "changes detected" line; the same push without the fault expects the same result.

## Related, not this defect

* KS-1483 (Backlog): the hook diffs HEAD, not the pushed ref. A different cause, same symptom class.
* KS-2091 (Backlog): no hook suite proves that a red preflight makes the hook refuse a push.
* KS-989, KS-1063, KS-1482 (Done): earlier holes in the same hook.
* Gate 263's G2 (the pre-run's own copy of the changed set, Minor) and G3 (clean means clean to `git status`) concern the pre-run tool and are not filed here.

## Searched before filing

Board, includeArchived, title and description and every comment of each open candidate; controls pass (a made-up token hits 0; `msgpackr` hits KS-1379). `orderFile` 0 hits; `gate 263` 0; `gate263` 0; `skips the preflight` 1 open hit (KS-1483, different cause); `pre-push` together with `git diff` 6 open and 3 closed hits, none holds a failing-diff case.

title: auth: a PATCH on an OAuth app with no scopes skips the privileged-scope check, so an app that stores admin:read or admin:write keeps it
description:
**BLUF:** On `PATCH /api/oauth/apps/{id}`, the privileged-scope check runs only on the `scopes` in the request body. A PATCH without `scopes` skips it and leaves the app's stored scopes as they are, so an app that already stores `admin:read` or `admin:write` keeps it, whoever the caller is and whatever other fields the PATCH changes. PR 2061 (KS-1536 3b, merged as `092d30706b95`) described the loss for a bare `admin` token as "cannot register or keep" those scopes. The register half holds; "keep" is not enforced. The wording is already corrected in place (KS-1536 comment `dec43279`); this ticket records the behaviour behind it.

Source: gate 244 (KS-1536, PR 2061 section), finding F7 (recorded as G244-F7): `/Volumes/DevMASTER/WEDNESDAY/0_Brain/reference/2026-11-07_gate244-tier1-ks1536/verdict.md`. Every line below I read myself at develop `092d30706b9561bb7d28aeffedf1e37ba62b4cd5`, the merge of PR 2061.

1. The check. `Blockchain/Dev/services/auth/src/routes/oauth.ts` lines 1245 to 1250: `OAUTH_PRIVILEGED_SCOPES` is `admin:read` and `admin:write`, and `privilegedScopesIn(scopes)` returns the privileged ones among the scopes it is given, or none for no scopes. In the PATCH handler (line 1397), line 1412 splits `scopes` from the rest of the body, line 1413 builds `updates` with `allowedScopes` only when `scopes !== undefined`, and lines 1421 to 1424 refuse with 403 only when `privilegedScopesIn(scopes)` is not empty and the caller is not a platform admin.
2. What follows. A PATCH with no `scopes` gives `privilegedScopesIn(undefined)` an empty result, so the 403 never fires, and `updates` carries no `allowedScopes`, so the stored scopes are untouched. Evidence class: READ ONLY (the gate's and mine); no request was sent.
3. Who holds such an app. UNMEASURED. The gate looked for no app that stores a privileged scope, and neither did I.

The gate gives no fix shape. Whether keeping a stored privileged scope is intended is the owner's question; this ticket only records that "keep" is not enforced, which the corrected comment on KS-1536 now says.

Not claimed: no run by me, no request, no database read.

Related: KS-1536 (the parent; comment `dec43279` was edited in place on 2026-11-08 to say this) and KS-1846 (scope vocabulary and enforcement drift, a different gap; read whole, no mention of PATCH).

Priority: Low, as ruled by Wednesday.

title: transfer: a transferAccess comment says no person can carry a connector role; the platform-admin login mints platform_admins.role as stored
description:

That is wrong for one login: the platform-admin login mints `platform_admins.role` exactly as stored, and platform admins are not in the closed `users` tables. Nothing changes at runtime today. The comment overstates what rules out a person carrying a connector role, and on the Azure path the column is not constrained.

Source: gate 240 (PR 2077, KS-2081), note N2, `/Volumes/DevMASTER/WEDNESDAY/0_Brain/reference/2026-11-07_gate240-tier1-pr2077-ks2081/verdict.md`. Every line number below I read myself at develop `7eda23b34d3b7a413ca8f9c0945c7843708ce9f4`, which holds the merge; they match the gate's.

2. The case it misses. `Blockchain/Dev/services/auth/src/routes/auth.ts` lines 470 and 471 build the platform-admin token with `role: platformAdmin.role as any`. `Blockchain/Dev/services/auth/src/repositories/userRepo.ts` line 1941 returns `role: row.role` straight from the `platform_admins` row (the query is at lines 1928 to 1930). So that token's role is whatever the row holds.

The docker platform schema limits `platform_admins.role` to three values by a CHECK (`Blockchain/Dev/docker/init-platform/01-platform-schema.sql` lines 79 and 80). The gate's reading: the role only matters if someone writes `connector` into that table directly. It also checked that no admin is refused by the id test, since the id is a UUID in both sources and the seed id is a GUID.

Fix shape: the gate gives none and says no behaviour change is needed for PR 2077; the comment is wrong in one case. My reading: correct the comment to name the platform-admin login as outside the closed tables. Whether to constrain the Azure column is KS-1536's question, not this ticket's.

title: transfer: a transfer row opened by a key that names no real users has no exit, and nothing expires it
description:
**BLUF:** A transfer row that a key opened, and whose two named parties are not real users, has no exit. Approve, reject and execute read 404 for everyone, cancel belongs to the initiator (the key), and PR 2077 refuses a key before that is checked. The row stays `pending_approval` and nothing expires it. PR 2077 (KS-2081, merged as `765701307eb3`) stops keys opening new rows, so this concerns rows that already exist. Whether any exist is not measured.

Source: gate 240 (PR 2077, KS-2081), finding F2, `/Volumes/DevMASTER/WEDNESDAY/0_Brain/reference/2026-11-07_gate240-tier1-pr2077-ks2081/verdict.md`. Every line number below I read myself at develop `7eda23b34d3b7a413ca8f9c0945c7843708ce9f4`, which holds the merge; they match the gate's.

1. Why there is no exit. `Blockchain/Dev/services/transfer/src/index.ts` lines 377 and 378 check only that `currentOwnerId` and `newOwnerId` are GUID-shaped (`z.string().guid()`), not that a user holds them. `decideTransferAccess` in `Blockchain/Dev/services/transfer/src/services/transferAccess.ts` (lines 82 to 88) answers 404 to anyone the row does not name, and reads no role (its comment, line 79, says so). Its cancel table (lines 54 to 59) lets only `initiatedBy` cancel, and on a key-opened row that is the key's principal. So "its parties can still reject" holds only if the parties exist. A person-opened row keeps the initiator's cancel as an exit; a key-opened row loses it.
2. No expiry. A search of `Blockchain/Dev/services/transfer/src/index.ts` at develop for `setInterval`, `cron` or `expire` finds 0 matches (the control, `createNotification`, finds 8).
3. The measurement. Evidence class: MEASURED by gate 240, cell O6. A row was warmed through `loadFromDb` with two random GUID parties. A SYSTEM_ADMIN read approve, reject, execute and cancel as 404, 404, 404, 404; a key read cancel as 403; the status stayed `pending_approval`.
4. Whether any such row exists. UNMEASURED. The gate's question Q4 gives a read-only query for someone commissioned to run it on each box: count `svc_transfers` rows whose `initiated_by` is not a canonical UUID, grouped by status, then check the pending ones' owner ids against `users.id`. `initiated_by` is TEXT in all three schemas, so key-opened rows do persist. I ran nothing against any box.

The gate names no fix shape for F2. If the count is 0, nothing is needed beyond this record. If it is not 0, an exit for such rows (an expiry, or an administrator's cancel) is the owner's decision, and an administrator's cancel would reverse the "no role is read" rule that `Blockchain/Dev/services/transfer/src/services/transferAccess.ts` states at line 79.

Not claimed: no query run, no box read, no stranded row seen. The notification read that also needs key-opened rows to exist is a sibling ticket, filed next.

title: KS-1152 follow-up: the spec and the cheat fragment say a count of 0 carries a warning; a new organisation gets none
description:
**BLUF:** Three sentences in PR 2073's published text are untrue for a NEW organisation. On a rotate of a new organisation with a count of 0 or more, the reply is 201, `rotated` false and no warning; the spec's `rotated` and `rotationWarning` descriptions and the cheat fragment say a 0 always carries `PRIOR_KEY_STILL_ACTIVE`, or that a rotate that did not retire a prior key carries it. The code is right and the PR body's table is right; only the three sentences are unqualified. Low is Wednesday's call in the ADDENDUM; the gate graded it minor.

It is unqualified; the 0 warning is for an existing organisation only.
   * The spec's `rotationWarning` description, the same file, line 765: "Present when a rotate did not retire a prior key". For a new organisation with a count of 0 nothing was retired and there is no warning.

title: Connector-key rotate answers rotated true with no warning while an older organisation key with no connector id still validates
description:
**BLUF:** The connector-key rotate (register-connector with rotate on) answers `rotated: true`, a count of 1 and no warning while an older key of the same organisation, one that carries no connector id, still validates. It happens on the retry after a count of 0, and also on the first call when the organisation holds both kinds of key, so no 0 is needed. The cause is in security's retire, which matches only the connector id; the gateway cannot see the older key. Gate 257 measured it on real PostgreSQL. It is old behaviour that PR 2073 narrows (the 0 itself is now honest) and does not remove. Priority High is Wednesday's call; the gate graded the finding Medium. Wednesday's ruling on the fix direction, under Kam's card `secuura-ks-1152-rotate-says-rotated-when-old-key-lives-1106` = b ("Keep rotating, but answer 'rotated: false' and say why", ruled 2026-11-06 15:00:34 AEDT, read with `tools/decision_queue.sh show`): the fix extends that honest answer to these keys; it does NOT retire them.

Source: gate 257, tier 1, round 2 of 2, PR 2073 (KS-1152 R-880-1), finding F1 and the section "For Kam, at the top", `/Volumes/DevMASTER/WEDNESDAY/0_Brain/reference/2026-11-08_gate257-tier1-pr2073-r2/verdict.md`, lines 17 to 34 and 40 to 49. Wednesday's ADDENDUM to the board seat, 2026-11-08 11:39:30Z, orders this filing. Seat Y 8th had recorded the retry case first (its probe P2, in its entry in `5_Project_History/history.md`) and proposed a distinct code for Kam's and Stuart's monthly agenda.

1. What was measured. Evidence class: MEASURED by gate 257 on real PostgreSQL 15 (the gate's own cluster), through a real gateway route over real security, at PR 2073's head `2684a29d8f576ff74634f07ad6576af5bd00370b` and again on the develop merge.
   * G2a, the first call with a count of 0: 200, `rotated` false, `priorKeysRevoked` 0, `PRIOR_KEY_STILL_ACTIVE`. The older key and the new key both validate.
   * G2b, the retry: 200, `rotated` true, count 1, no warning. The older key is still valid; the key the 0 call returned is no longer valid.
   * G3, an organisation that holds both an older key with no connector id and a key with the connector id, first call: 200, `rotated` true, count 1, no warning. The older key is still valid; the connector key is retired.
2. Where. Evidence class: READ. `Blockchain/Dev/services/api-gateway/src/routes/platform.ts` at PR 2073's head, line 979: `rotated: rotate && existing.rows.length > 0 && priorKeysRetired && priorKeysRevoked >= 1`. `Blockchain/Dev/services/security/src/index.ts` at develop `abd044f63a9dd5673f1b9ff7a2b1e42e1c26de82` (the file is not changed by PR 2073), lines 239 and 246: both retire statements end `WHERE connector_id = $1 AND tenant_id = $2::uuid AND id <> $3 AND is_active = true`, so a key with no connector id is never matched.
3. Why it is old behaviour. By the gate's reading, develop answers `rotated: true` on the 0 itself, on the retry and on G3. PR 2073 makes the 0 honest and leaves the retry and G3 as they were.
4. The fix direction. Ruled by Wednesday (ADDENDUM 11:39:30Z): extend the honest answer, `rotated: false` with a reason, to these keys; do not retire them. The gate's two fix shapes were that security reports how many active keys of the organisation remain after the retire, or that the retire also takes the organisation's keys that have no connector id. The first fits the ruling; the second is what the ruling excludes. A regression test the owner should add (the gate): G3's shape, asserting that `rotated` is not true while the older key validates. If this behaviour stays for now, the gate asks for one sentence each in `Blockchain/Dev/docs/S-K-OWNERSHIP-CONTRACT.md` and in the spec: "`rotated: true` says nothing about an older key with no connector id; a retry after a 0 answers `rotated: true` with that key still active."
5. The cost the gate names in Wednesday's ruling A2. One code now carries two instructions, so a client that reads only the code retries after a 0 and lands in G2. The PR body calls that retry "futile, not harmful"; the gate disagrees, because the retry ends in a false all-clear. The gate leaves that trade-off to Kam.
6. Who reads `rotated`. By the gate: rotation is platform-admin only (its GUARDRAIL 1), so a K admin reads the reply; whether Platform S reads `rotated` is unknown; the only code reader is systemTest, which stops at `rotated: true`. The contract Stuart's team reads says a retry does not help but not that the retry answers `rotated: true`, and it does not mention G3.

Not claimed: how many keys with no connector id exist on any box (the gate did not measure it); whether Platform S reads `rotated`; any run by me. PR 2073 is not merged: the line numbers for `Blockchain/Dev/services/api-gateway/src/routes/platform.ts` are at its head and may shift when it merges.

title: Issuer and verifier portals have no catch-all route, and admin and issuer logins drop a deep link by always landing on /

title: Admin Settings page pollutes Object.prototype on save when a stored settings category is named `__proto__`
description:
**BLUF:** If the stored platform-settings document holds a category named `__proto__`, the admin Settings page's save grouping writes that category's fields onto `Object.prototype` in the admin's browser. This is pre-existing: the same at develop `cfb6c1573ba9` and at the head of PR 2058 (`527d67b1852e`), which did not introduce it. Gate 256 measured it on both, and by its model any admin caller of the settings PUT can store such a key. It found no gadget and looked for none. Medium is Wednesday's default; the gate graded it minor to medium.

Source: gate 256 (Secuura / Blockchain, PR 2058, KS-1231 portal half, tier 1, round 2 of 2), finding N5, `/Volumes/DevMASTER/WEDNESDAY/0_Brain/reference/2026-11-08_gate256-tier1-pr2058-r2/verdict.md`, lines 52 to 56. The code lines below I read myself, at the shas named.

1. What was measured. Evidence class: MEASURED by the gate (tsx; the head module against develop's grouping logic copied out). It planted the wire document `{"settings":{"general":{...},"__proto__":{"g256polluted":"yes"}}}` (the contents of `general` are elided as in the verdict); `JSON.parse` makes `__proto__` an own key. A control read before each run gave `({}).g256polluted` as undefined. After one save build it was `"yes"` at both the head and develop. The save request body itself did not carry the key.
2. The line on develop. Evidence class: READ at `cfb6c1573ba9`. `Blockchain/Dev/frontend/admin/src/pages/Settings.tsx` lines 63 to 71 group the form values by category: `if (!updates[category]) { updates[category] = {}; }` (lines 67 to 69), then `updates[category][field] = formValues[key];` (line 70). For the name `__proto__`, `updates[category]` is not empty (it is the object prototype), so the branch is skipped and line 70 assigns onto `Object.prototype`. That last step is my reading of the two lines; the gate's run is what measured it.
3. The line at PR 2058's head. Evidence class: READ at `527d67b1852e`. `Blockchain/Dev/frontend/admin/src/lib/settingsSavePayload.ts` line 84 is `const target = (updates[category] ??= {}) as Settings;` and line 85 assigns `target[field] = value`. That file exists only on the PR's head (it is absent from develop at `cfb6c1573ba9`); the same reading applies, because `??=` keeps a value that is not null or undefined.
4. Whether such a key can be stored. Evidence class: MEASURED by the gate on a model of the gateway's spread (it keeps an own `__proto__` key), plus READ at `cfb6c1573ba9`. title: Tokenisation's key-generation and key-rotation routes have no cell that can see their gate; requirePlatformRole has no undefined-role row
description:
**BLUF:** The two tokenisation routes that generate and rotate a tenant's key are gated by `requirePlatformRole()`, and no unit cell in the repository would go red if that gate were removed or let a user with no role through. Gate 244 planted two defects and both stayed green: an ungated `/api/rotate-key` with a stray `void requirePlatformRole();` left above it (97 of 97 cells green), and a `requirePlatformRole` that passes a user with no role. The wiring is correct at the gate's head and at develop `cfb6c1573ba9`, so this is a coverage gap, not an open door. It is rated Medium because these routes generate and rotate tenant keys.

Every line number below I read myself at develop `cfb6c1573ba9c948ebbe898fb2aec283bb9954ab`, the merge commit of PR 2060; the gate's two route lines (225 and 294) are unchanged there.

In `Blockchain/Dev/services/tokenisation/src/index.ts`, line 49 mounts `app.use('/api', jwtAuthenticate());` above both routes; line 225 is `app.post('/api/generate-key', requirePlatformRole(), ...` and line 294 is `app.post('/api/rotate-key', requirePlatformRole(), ...`. A comment at line 216 says why (these are control-plane key operations that take an arbitrary tenant id in the body, KS-175), and line 223 records Kam's KS-1536 ruling (card option a) that they use `requirePlatformRole` instead of a local list. `requirePlatformRole` is defined at line 162 of `Blockchain/Dev/packages/shared/src/middleware/index.ts`: no user answers an unauthorised error, and line 168 refuses a role that `isPlatformRole` refuses.
2. The only cell that names the routes. Evidence class: READ at `cfb6c1573ba9`. Cell G5 in `Blockchain/Dev/packages/shared/src/__tests__/ks1536-one-role-vocabulary.test.ts`, lines 169 to 173, reads the entry module's text, expects the string `requirePlatformRole()` to occur exactly twice, and expects `PLATFORM_ADMIN_ROLES` to be absent. It does not read which route each occurrence sits on. The middleware's own cells (M1 to M3, lines 80 to 84) drive the function, not the routes: M1 admits five spellings, M2 refuses `platform_admin`, `ORG_ADMIN`, `ADMIN` and `OWNER`, and M3 passes no user. title: KS-1536 follow-up: the one-role-vocabulary guard counts one shape only, and three pointers name removed lists
description:
**BLUF:** PR 2060 (KS-1536 3a, merged as `cfb6c1573ba9`) added a source guard that its body and its ticket comment describe as refusing a new inline platform-role list. Separately, three comments or doc lines still point at role lists that the PR removed. Nothing here is a runtime defect: gate 244 found that every gate it drove behaved as the PR says. **What the guard is**, read at `cfb6c1573ba9` in `Blockchain/Dev/packages/shared/src/__tests__/ks1536-one-role-vocabulary.test.ts`, lines 89 to 133. It walks the `.ts` and `.tsx` files under `services/*/src`, `packages/*/src` and `frontend/*/src` (lines 97 to 116) and skips test, spec and declaration files. It counts a list only when a quoted `super_admin`, `system_admin` or `platform_admin` sits inside one flat bracket or parenthesis group of at most 1200 characters (lines 90, 91 and 129). A second rule refuses the quoted string `platform_admin` on any line (line 89) unless that line names `tenant_scope_bypass` (line 94). The lists that remain are frozen in `ks1536-inline-role-lists.baseline.json` beside it.

1. The six shapes the guard does not see. Evidence class: MEASURED by gate 244 (planted files; the guard's rules G1 and G2 run per plant in the gate's clone; its four control plants, a plain list, a `platform_admin` list, a `.tsx` `new Set` and a lower-cased `"platform_admin"`, were refused as expected). Each plant stayed green:

   * a `.js` file under `src` holding `['super_admin','platform_admin']`;
   * a `.ts` file outside `src` (`services/auth/integration/`);
   * a `.ts` file in a frontend with no `src` (`frontend/status/`);
   * a nested bracket, `['super_admin', x[0]]`;

     Why each is invisible is my reading of the guard's code, not a run: a chain has no bracket group, `.js` fails the `.tsx?` test (line 104), a path outside `<package>/src` is never walked (line 111), a group cannot hold a nested bracket (line 91), and the exemption (line 94) is per line.
2. Real product sites with the first shape. Evidence class: READ at `cfb6c1573ba9`. The gate's F1 names four: `Blockchain/Dev/services/originate/src/routes/documents.ts` lines 313 and 1129 (the gate wrote 1125), `Blockchain/Dev/services/originate/src/routes/certifications.ts` line 1026, and `Blockchain/Dev/services/auth/src/middleware/authenticate.ts` line 249. The gate's F2 adds `Blockchain/Dev/services/originate/src/routes/documents.ts` line 1488 (the gate wrote 1484) and `Blockchain/Dev/services/originate/src/routes/certifications.ts` line 123. The first five are the chain `x === 'system_admin' || x === 'SYSTEM_ADMIN' || x === 'super_admin'` with the variable named `userRole` or `role`. Line 249 of `Blockchain/Dev/services/auth/src/middleware/authenticate.ts` is a chain over `SYSTEM_ADMIN`, `super_admin` and `SUPER_ADMIN`. Whether those chains omit a spelling they should admit is KS-1701's subject, not this ticket's.
3. Three stale pointers. Evidence class: READ ONLY (the gate gives file and line; the readings below are mine at `cfb6c1573ba9`).
   * `Blockchain/Dev/services/api-gateway/src/index.ts` lines 327 to 329: a comment says the auth middleware enforces `SUPER_ADMIN_ROLES`, cites `middleware/auth.ts:380-382` and the expression `SUPER_ADMIN_ROLES.includes(decoded.role)`, and says to grep for it if the line moves. `SUPER_ADMIN_ROLES` has 0 matches in `middleware/auth.ts` at `cfb6c1573ba9`. At develop `b27f5fb30f4a`, the gate's reading, it had 2 (lines 695 and 697), so the cited 380 to 382 was out of date before the name went.
   * `Blockchain/Dev/services/api-gateway/src/utils/trustHeaders.ts` line 37: the comment says the tenant override is gated on `SUPER_ADMIN_ROLES`, the same removed name.
   * `Blockchain/Dev/docs/security/AGENT-DOCUMENT-OPERATION-RULES.md` line 55: it says `enforceAdminProxy` uses `PROXY_ADMIN_ROLES` in `services/api-gateway/src/routes/proxy.ts`, "which lists human roles only". At `cfb6c1573ba9`, `enforceAdminProxy` (`Blockchain/Dev/services/api-gateway/src/routes/proxy.ts` lines 1256 to 1263) asks `isPlatformOrOrgAdminRole(user.role)`, and `PROXY_ADMIN_ROLES` appears once, in a comment at line 1255 that says it was the local list.

Fix shapes. From the gate for item 1: state the shape limit where the claim is made, or count comparison chains too. For item 3 the gate gives none; each is an edit to one comment or one doc line. Comment `9d6455f1` on KS-1536 was edited on 2026-11-08 to say the guard sees one shape, so the claim made to humans there is already narrowed; this ticket is for the guard and the pointers themselves.

title: originate: five code comments call the lifecycle anchor emit idempotent, but a repeat admitted event builds and sends its own transaction
description:
**BLUF:** Five code comments in originate's documents routes say the lifecycle-event anchor emit is idempotent and "reuses the document's existing anchor". That holds for the anchor id. Seat AA 5th's probe shows it does not hold for the transaction: a repeat admitted event builds and sends a new one, and the row then names the second. Kam ruled that this behaviour stays until stage 2, so the comments are the only thing out of line with it. Evidence class: the behaviour is PROBED by AA 5th against a stand-in chain; the comments I READ at develop; nothing was run on a box. Text only, no behaviour change.

The comments, in `Blockchain/Dev/services/originate/src/routes/documents.ts` at develop `14ac61bd1a4c854c17539f1cd0f518631f998fbb`:

* Line 1390, the doc block of `emitLifecycleAnchor`: "Anchoring is idempotent per (document_id, network): re-anchoring an already-anchored document returns its existing anchor id." This one is written about the id.
* Lines 2501 (custody transfer), 2921 (share) and 3023 (revoke): "return a resolvable anchor id (idempotent — reuses the document's existing anchor)".
* Line 3149: "shared emitter: idempotent per (document, network) — the event anchors against the document's existing anchor".
* Line 700 also says "idempotent", about an external-id match; that is a different subject and is not part of this.

The probe. Source: `/Volumes/DevMASTER/!CODING/Secuura/Blockchain/5_Project_History/2026-11-06_seatAA-5th/evidence/ks1384/probe_share3.lines`, measured by AA 5th at develop `c5c26b2835df`. Instrument, not a committed cell: the real submitter, the real `spendFromView` and `WalletView`, a stand-in chain, the upsert simulated from its SET list. Reading `PROBE admitted-share`: after a first confirmed share, a second admitted share built 2, sent 2, spent coin a then coin b, and the row names the second transaction.

The ruling. Card `secuura-ks1384-share-pays-second-tx-before-stage2-1106` = a, ruled 2026-11-06T21:04:52+11:00, option text read with `show`: "Leave it until stage 2". title: governance castVote: a lock-free read, change and whole-row save loses a concurrent vote's tally and can write back an erased wallet address
description:
**BLUF:** In governance, `castVote` reads a proposal, changes it in memory and writes the whole row back with no row lock and no transaction. So two votes on one proposal at the same moment lose one tally, and a vote in flight during an erasure can write back the wallet address the erasure has just blanked. Evidence class: READ, not measured. Nobody has driven two concurrent requests, and the window has not been timed.

What I read, at develop `14ac61bd1a4c854c17539f1cd0f518631f998fbb`, in `Blockchain/Dev/services/governance/src/services/governanceService.ts` (1357 lines):

* Line 952: `castVote` starts with `dbGetProposal(proposalId)`. `dbGetProposal` (line 329) is a plain `SELECT * FROM svc_proposals WHERE id = $1`: no `FOR UPDATE`, no transaction.
* Lines 998 to 1011: the vote is pushed onto `proposal.votes`, `proposal.voterCount` is incremented, and `votesFor`, `votesAgainst` or `votesAbstain` grows by the voter's power. All of it in memory.
* Line 1013: `dbSaveProposal(proposal)` (defined at line 144) upserts the whole row. Its `ON CONFLICT (id) DO UPDATE` sets `votes_for`, `votes_against`, `votes_abstain`, `voter_count` and `votes` from the in-memory object (lines 153 to 157).
* Line 989: each stored vote carries `voterAddress: voter.walletAddress`, so the `votes` array holds wallet addresses.

What follows from that reading:

1. Two requests that read the same row each add their own vote to their own copy. The second upsert replaces the first, so one vote and its tally are gone, although the first request has already answered success.
2. An erasure that blanks a wallet address inside `svc_proposals.votes` while a vote on that proposal sits between its read (line 952) and its write (line 1013) is overwritten by the vote's pre-erasure copy. The address is back in the row.

The same read-then-whole-row-save shape stands at the `submitProposal` call sites (lines 883 and 910) and the `finalizeProposal` call sites (lines 1052 and 1096) in the same file. I read the call sites only, not those function bodies.

Not claimed: no concurrent run, no measurement of the window, no read of the erasure handler (it is Seat U 18th's local commit for KS-2060, not pushed when this was filed).

Related:

* KS-2060 (the erasure work). Seat U 18th's finding file says KS-2060 states the in-flight vote as a limit.
* KS-2058 (the co-owner limit).
* KS-2092 (`castVote` counts a delegator's stake twice): a different defect in the same function.
* KS-1950 (Done): the same class on the participant row. The code comment at line 1014 says the voter row now gets a counter-only update.

Source of the finding: Seat U 18th, finding 1 of "Two findings for you to route" in `/Volumes/DevMASTER/!CODING/Secuura/Blockchain/5_Project_History/2026-11-08_seatU-18th/drafts/02_q_ks2059_order.txt`, marked there "Read, not measured". I re-read the lines above myself at the develop sha named.

Duplicate search before filing (board account, includeArchived, open tickets read with all comments): `castVote`, `dbSaveProposal`, the full path of the service file, "votes array", "lose one tally", "row lock" with "vote", "concurrent" with "vote", "lost update". No open ticket describes this race; the closest hits are KS-2092 (open) and KS-1950 (Done), both under Related. Output: `/Volumes/DevMASTER/!CODING/Secuura/Blockchain/5_Project_History/2026-11-08_seatS-36th/evidence/search_n1_castvote.out`.

Priority: Medium, a default set by the board seat because the finding gives none. A raise is Wednesday's call.

title: mcp-server: customer packages already issued keep the server-file hash hole, and a package from a current tree may not start
description:
**BLUF:** a customer package that was issued before PR 2059 (KS-1410) keeps the server-file hash hole until the package is regenerated, and our deploy does not reach it. QA gate 239 measured the hole on the code before PR 2059: a caller could make the mcp-server web interface return the sha256 of a server file such as `/etc/hosts` and send that hash upstream to the API (a hash, not the file's contents). PR 2059 removes path reads from the HTTP interface and is not merged (round 2, under gate). The package generator copies the web interface's source files into every customer package, so a package issued before the fix carries the old server. Gate 250 adds, read only and not run: a package generated from a current tree may not start at all, because nothing supplies `@secuura/shared`. Kam's card `secuura-ks1410-issued-packages-keep-hole-1107` = a, "File a ticket, count issued packages, then decide (recommended)", ruled 2026-11-08 at 20:32:43 +11:00; its detail: "A board seat files a ticket with this finding, assigned to the board account, and a seat measures what can be measured about issued packages. If any exist, it comes back to Kam with a short text for Stuart or Peter. Nothing goes to a customer without Kam." This is that ticket. **Count of issued packages: UNMEASURED, owed.** This seat has no box and read none, and no seat is named to measure it.

**Measured (gate 239, MEASURED AT RUNTIME on a real running server):** control: on the code before PR 2059, in the same harness, the server returned a sha256 for `/etc/hosts` and sent that hash upstream to `/api/documents` and `/api/verification/verify`. At the PR 2059 head: none, in 67 probes.

**Read only (gate 239, N2 and F2; gate 250, C2):**

* `Blockchain/Dev/services/mcp-server/src/package-generator.ts`, line 38 (re-read by this seat at develop `a65ae7ed1d60`), lists the web interface's HTTP server and hashing source files among the files it ships in a customer package. Packages already issued keep the old server until regenerated, and "Deploy owed: mcp-server on both boxes" does not reach them. How many exist is unknown.
* Gate 239's F2, now fixed in PR 2059 round 2: a parser error answers the error text and a stack naming server file paths whenever `NODE_ENV` is not `production`, and the generator writes no `NODE_ENV` into a package's `.env` (`Blockchain/Dev/services/mcp-server/src/package-generator.ts`, lines 72 to 74). * Gate 239 on exposure: on our own boxes the port is unpublished and the gateway re-serialises the body, so by source it is not a route to the outside today. Customer packages on a tunnel are the exposed case. The generator's own text tells users the server "must be publicly accessible" (line 196 at gate 239's tree).
* Gate 250 C2: the mcp-server's HTTP server source (`Blockchain/Dev/services/mcp-server/src/http-server.ts`) imports `@secuura/shared`; neither the generator nor the mcp-server package manifest supplies it (zero hits for "shared"; control: 48 hits for "secuura"). A package generated from a current tree may therefore not start, which changes what "regenerate" means. Not run.

title: anchoring: an empty or null 2xx reply from a configured chain client reads ABSENT, which can lead to a second fee-paying transaction
description:
**BLUF:** with a configured chain client, a 2xx reply with an empty body or a JSON `null` counts as the chain answering and reads ABSENT in the anchoring confirmation poller, and a body of `{}` reads confirmed with no block hash. A false ABSENT lets guard 3 schedule the ordinary retry, which is a second fee-paying Cardano transaction; its fee and its on-chain record cannot be undone. QA gate 248 found it while gating PR 2081 (KS-1171 8k). It is older than that PR, which cannot add the outcome (1,364 attempt sequences, 0 widened). Kam's card `secuura-anchoring-second-fee-on-empty-reply-1107` = a, "Merge PR 2081, and fix the empty reply before anchoring next deploys (recommended)", ruled 2026-11-08 at 20:31:42 +11:00; its detail: "Two tickets by a board seat, High for the empty reply and Medium to measure the mint on an image. A build seat fixes the empty reply next, tier 1 gate. Anchoring's deploy stays held for your word." This is the High ticket. The Medium half is carried on KS-562, whose gate 70 comment already records the open question, "whether the anchoring image's install layout reproduces the split in a built container". Evidence class: MEASURED AT RUNTIME for the client and the poller result, with the real client and poller; guard 3's retry from this input follows from an existing cell's path (cell C1) and was not driven end to end.

**Measured (gate 248):** the real blockfrost-js 6.1.1 on a loopback listener returns an empty string for an empty 200 and for a 204, `null` for a body of `null`, and `{}` for a body of `{}`. HTML on a 200 throws; a 404 and a 502 throw with their status. The real provider and the real poller on the production schedule, at develop and at the PR 2081 head, with the transaction lookup resolving each body: an empty string and `null` give `polled` 30 and `definitelyAbsent` true; `{}` gives `confirmed` true with no block hash.

**Why it matters (gate 248):** the code's own comment defines an answer as "the transaction or not found". An empty 200 is neither. It is the same second-fee harm that PR 2081 closes for the no-client case, on the configuration that really pays fees, where 8k itself has no route. PR 2081's sentence "An empty 200 is '', so it still counts as an answer, as it does today" is true, but nothing there says it reaches guard 3.

**Likelihood (gate 248):** low. It needs an upstream or a proxy answering 2xx with no body. Not seen in service; no box was read.

**Where:** `Blockchain/Dev/services/anchoring/src/cardano/confirmation.ts`, lines 94 to 103 at the PR 2081 head (gate 248's tree). On develop `a65ae7ed1d60` the same polling logic starts near line 81, where the `polled` counter is incremented. Gate 248's probes are in the evidence folder next to its verdict.

**Fix shape (gate 248, for the owner):** decide whether the poller counts only `null` and a real transaction as answers, and pin it. That touches the 2026-09-25 definition of "answered" (card `secuura-ks1171-when-is-an-anchor-absent` = c); Kam's ruling above sends it to a build seat under a tier 1 gate. Anchoring's deploy stays held for Kam's word.

**Not measured:** a real Blockfrost, a real node or a real unreachable chain; any box, image or gateway path; guard 3's retry end to end from this input; how often a provider sends an empty 2xx.

**Source:** gate 248 verdict, finding F1 and the chain-cost section, `/Volumes/DevMASTER/WEDNESDAY/0_Brain/reference/2026-11-07_gate248-tier1-pr2081-ks1171/verdict.md`. This seat re-read the verdict and the line locations and ran nothing else. Related: KS-1171 (the ticket PR 2081 belongs to), KS-562 (the thread-token mint question).

The anchoring confirmation path: open KS-485 and KS-1171, closed KS-489 and KS-1810 (the reconciler's 24 h give-up cannot tell an outage from an absent transaction; a different matter). "empty 200": KS-485, KS-772 and KS-1673 (unrelated). No duplicate.

title: api-gateway: ten rateLimit instances (login included) set no shared store, and the bicep allows up to 20 replicas: each may count alone
description:
**BLUF:** the api-gateway sets up ten `rateLimit` instances, including the login limiter on `/api/auth/login` (15 attempts per 15 minutes in production), and none passes a `store` option, so each keeps the library's default in-process store, while the production template lets the `apiGateway` app run from 1 to 20 replicas. The gateway's own comment on its Redis fallback describes the effect of a per-pod counter: "each replica has its own counter (effectively no rate limit when N replicas are behind a load balancer)". QA gate 241 found it while gating PR 2079 (KS-657), which deletes an unused Redis-backed security store. Kam's card `secuura-ks657-redis-security-store-delete-1107` = a, "Delete it, and ticket the gateway rate limits (recommended)", ruled 2026-11-08 at 20:32:21 +11:00; its detail: "Nothing uses it and git keeps it. A fresh ticket measures the rate limits and picks a store, assigned to the board account." This is that ticket. Evidence class: READ ONLY. It was not driven against two replicas, and the default-store behaviour is the library's documented default, not observed.

**What was read (gate 241 at its tree; this seat re-read each point at develop a65ae7ed1d60):**

* `Blockchain/Dev/services/api-gateway/src/index.ts` has 10 `rateLimit({` calls (lines 489, 576, 982, 994, 1001, 1008, 1015, 1022, 1029 and 1054) and 0 `store:` options. The login limiter is at line 982: a 15-minute window, `max` taken from `LOGIN_RATE_LIMIT`, default 15 in production and 100 outside it.
* `Blockchain/Dev/services/api-gateway/package.json` lists `express-rate-limit` ^7.1.5 and no `rate-limit-redis`.
* `Blockchain/Dev/deployment/azure/services.bicep`, resource `apiGateway` (line 597): `minReplicas: 1` (line 732) and `maxReplicas: 20` (line 733).
* `Blockchain/Dev/services/api-gateway/src/services/redis.ts`, lines 124 to 127: production refuses to start without Redis because "Rate limit + sessions are both Redis-backed; falling back to per-pod in-memory means each replica has its own counter". The per-client limiter (`Blockchain/Dev/services/api-gateway/src/middleware/rateLimitEnforce.ts`) and the brute-force lockout are Redis-backed (gate 241); these ten appear not to be.
* `.planning/codebase/CONCERNS.md` (lines 26, 165 and 166, per gate 241) names the per-replica risk and the unused Redis store as the fix. Gate 241 found 0 hits for MemoryStore, per-replica or express-rate-limit in the repository's backlog file.

**What the card asks:** measure the rate limits, then pick a store. Neither is decided here. Related work with a different scope: KS-170 (done) wired the per-client counter to Redis; KS-616 (deployed to UAT) is the limiter failing open on error; KS-946 (done) is four path spellings that dodge every path-scoped limiter.

**Not measured:** two replicas behind one load balancer; a real Redis; whether any box runs more than one gateway replica today (no box was read).

**Source:** gate 241 verdict, finding F3 (MEDIUM, pre-existing, not caused by PR 2079), `/Volumes/DevMASTER/WEDNESDAY/0_Brain/reference/2026-11-07_gate241-tier1-pr2079-ks657/verdict.md`.
