title: PR 2076 (KS-2058 follow-up), gate 242: five wording and test-cell notes in a code comment, two fragments, a docstring and cell R3
description:
**BLUF:** PR 2076 (KS-2058 follow-up, head `8ce56b0f9a86`, open and not merged when this was filed) changes comments and two documentation fragments, and adds one test cell. Compiled with comments removed, the two product files are byte-identical to the base. QA gate 242 returned GO WITH NOTES with five notes, H1 to H5: four Low and one Info, all about words or one test cell, none a code defect. This ticket carries them as items, one test pass. Wednesday decided on 2026-11-08 that PR 2076 gets no new round: its text stays as it is and is corrected under this ticket. Evidence class for all five: READ ONLY (gate 242 read the code against the words; it ran no PostgreSQL and did not re-run the seat's mutants).

**H1 (Low, words).** Where: `Blockchain/Dev/services/governance/src/db.ts`, the two new lines 236 and 237 at the PR head. Found: the comment says "with one disabled holder and one live one, the admin's request binds the live one." That holds on the owner-read path, which `registerParticipant` reaches only when `dbGetParticipantByAddress` finds no row for the wallet (`Blockchain/Dev/services/governance/src/services/governanceService.ts`, around lines 630 to 637). If the disabled holder already has a participant row for the wallet, the request lands on that row and the owner read never runs. The enclosing docstring scopes itself to "a new row", so the sentence is not false in context, but it stands alone as a "Stated limit". The cheat fragment's "What to know" row is scoped to "wallet with no row" and is fine. Fix shape: scope the sentence to a wallet with no row.

**H2 (Low, words).** Where: the flow fragment, row "The retry's own save", `Projects Documents/fragments/flow/KS-2058-an-erased-user-is-not-a-wallets-owner-and-an-omitted-did-keeps-what-the-row-holds.html`. Found: it says "In nature it is vanishingly rare" and "my driver reproduces that". The first is a frequency claim; the only measurement behind it is forced timing (10 of 10 under forced interleaving) and no rate in nature was measured, so a reader may take it as a measured bound. The second is first person in a document a Secuura reader sees, and names a tool that is not in the PR. Fix shape (gate 242): drop the phrase, or say "not measured outside forced timing"; drop the first person. Both phrases stand in the tree for now, by Wednesday's decision above.

**H3 (Low, words).** Where: the cheat fragment, row "Not measured here", `Projects Documents/fragments/cheat/KS-2058-an-erased-user-is-not-a-wallets-owner-and-an-omitted-did-keeps-what-the-row-holds.html`. Found: it gains the G1 limit but not the two limits the flow fragment and the `registerParticipant` docstring now state: "the 201 can differ from the row on the did", and "an omitted flag is written from the default, which can lose a flag or grant one". Its "What to know" row says "An omitted did keeps what the row holds when the write lands", which a reader can take as covering the response body too. Evidence: gate 242 read both fragments against the code (`asStored`, lines 640 to 649; the upsert, lines 182 to 197, writes `is_drep` and `is_constitutional_committee` from EXCLUDED).

**H4 (Low, test).** Where: `Blockchain/Dev/services/governance/src/__tests__/ks2058-an-erased-owner-is-not-an-owner-and-a-read-miss-keeps-the-did.test.ts`, the new cell at the end (about lines 551 to 565), named `control ks2058 R3 the did changes between the holder read and the retry's save: the newer did stays`. Found: the cell checks status 201 and the row's did. The comment in the code says the 201 can name the older did; R3 pins the fix (the row keeps the newer did) and says nothing about the stated limit (the response names the older). Not wrong, but the "state the limit" half of the PR has no cell. Gate 242's own planted defect shows other cells cover the re-read of the holder.

**H5 (Info, words).** Where: `Blockchain/Dev/services/governance/src/services/governanceService.ts`, lines 606 and 607. Found: "A row an erased user already holds still takes the admin's stake here and keeps its vote power". The code recomputes `votePower` from the new stake and writes it; the row's power does not stay as it was, it stays counted. Cosmetic. Gate 232's G7 asked that the docstring not say "not touched", and that is fixed.

title: systemTest: skip review — 2 fixmes wait on closed tickets, and the timestamp skips give an instruction that cannot work
description:
## Summary

A review of all 46 authored skips, on `develop` at `a77652e` (7 Nov 2026), found these need action. **Each listed test was run and passes once its condition is met.**

## 1. Two `test.fixme`s wait on tickets that are Done

| Test | Ticket | Result with the fixme lifted |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `tier_change_session:52` | [PS-1143](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1143/a-demoted-user-keeps-the-old-role-in-their-live-session-demoted-power). Stuart ruled on 21 Oct 2026 that refusal within the stamp interval is intended, and asked for this fixme to be lifted | Passed |
| `lineage_share_requests:394` | [PS-1451](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1451/share-a-share-past-the-onward-depth-limit-is-refused-but-the-page), fixed in round 11. Peter's comment says he lifts it once the fix is on `develop` | Passed |

**Proposed:** delete both `test.fixme` lines, and move both tickets to the closed list in `tests-unit/helpers/fixme_ticket_status.ts`.

**Why the guard didn't catch it:** `fixme_open_ticket.test.ts` reads that checked-in list, whose `CHECKED_ON` is 2026-10-20. It is offline and can't see Linear, and the list is meant to be re-checked before a full-suite gate. Re-check it as part of this ticket.

## 2. The timestamp skips give an instruction that cannot work

`timestamp_authorities:89` and `:120` say to set `TSA_URL_*` in the slot's `.env`, "then [up-slot.sh](<http://up-slot.sh>) N". Since [PS-1542](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1542/local-only-test-switch-to-close-the-timestamp-authorities-for-one), `slot_env_tsa` in `slot-env.sh` rewrites those keys every time a slot comes up, so that instruction undoes itself. `systemTest/CLAUDE.md` still describes the old way, and its bullet says [PS-1542](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1542/local-only-test-switch-to-close-the-timestamp-authorities-for-one) "asks for" a switch that has since shipped.

These two tests therefore stand down in every normal full run, even though the seam exists to prevent that. No file under `systemTest/` calls `/testseam/timestamps/close`.

**Both tests pass when the setting really reaches the app:** `:89` with the first authority closed, and `:120` with all three closed. To apply it, `docker-compose up -d --no-deps obeden-ssd` was run with the values in the shell. `dock_run` won't do this, because `clear_inherited_slot_env` clears them on purpose.

**Proposed:** switch these tests to the [PS-1542](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1542/local-only-test-switch-to-close-the-timestamp-authorities-for-one) seam, so they run in every full run, and correct the skip reason and `systemTest/CLAUDE.md`. [PS-1439](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1439/systemtest-timestamps-falling-through-to-the-next-of-the-three)'s C2–C6 cases are blocked on the same step.

## 3. Reviewed and correct, no action

| Skip | Evidence |
| -- | -- |
| `companion_signature:163` | Passed with `COMPANION_SIGNATURE=false` |
| `detached_pdf_signing:60` | Passed with `EMBED_PDF=false` |
| `preflight:104`, `:116` | K's spec answers 404, as the reason says. **Not run:** enabling K's `ENABLE_PUBLIC_API_DOCS` was out of scope |
| `document_key_byok:53` | Read only: the local key store can't import a customer key |
| `assurance_share_gate:116` | Read only: a deliberate deployment setting ([PS-659](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-659/systemtest-the-share-assurance-gate-ps-369-has-never-been-exercised)) |
| `tier_document_limit:49` | Read only: the allowance is not enforced ([PS-283](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-283/enforce-annual-verified-document-allowance-tier-top-ups)). That ticket is in Backlog but **archived**, so check it still tracks this |
| `tls_certificate_expiry:37` ×6 | Read only: a local stack's certificate regenerates itself ([PS-720](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-720/warn-before-a-certificate-expires-not-after-the-expiry-window-check-ps)) |
| 6 `[pair]` skips | Read only: each stands down for its sibling on the opposite condition |

The 23 attach skips are on [PS-1608](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1608/systemtest-attach-specs-do-not-turn-on-ps-1583s-organisation-setting-3).

## 4. A sweep that times out under load

`testid_coverage_sweep` hit its 60-second test timeout once in each full run, on different tests: `:190` on 6 Nov, then `:183` and `:334` on tablet landscape on 7 Nov. All three passed when repeated alone (`:190` 5 of 5, the others once each). Load averages above 100 are not proven to be the cause, but a test that walks every sidebar route has little margin under a 60-second limit. Consider a longer per-test timeout for it.

nodes.body:
**Part done in https://github.com/Secuura/platform-s/pull/1436.** This ticket stays In Progress for the parts left.

**Done in the PR:**

- **Fixmes:** lifted for PS-1143 and PS-1451. Both tests ran and passed in the full run.
- **Ticket list:** `fixme_ticket_status.ts` re-read from Linear on 9 Nov. 14 of its 16 "open" tickets had closed, and only PS-283 stays open. The contract shows no other fixme relied on the 12 others.
- **Timestamp guidance:** the skip reason and `systemTest/CLAUDE.md` now give the step that works (`docker-compose up -d --no-deps obeden-ssd` with `TSA_URL_*` in the shell). A unit test keeps the reason from pointing at `up-slot.sh`.

**Still open here:**

1. **Timestamp seam:** move `timestamp_authorities:89` and `:120` onto the PS-1542 seam (`POST /testseam/timestamps/close`), so they run in every full run instead of standing down.
2. **Sweep timeout:** `testid_coverage_sweep` timed out under load on 6 and 7 Nov, though not in the 9 Nov run.

title: systemTest: 32 tests fail on behaviour round 11 changed on purpose (#1356 group A), and 4 send_docs tests behind them never run
description:
## Failure and cause

[Secuura/platform-s#1356](https://linear.app/secuura/review/ps-1434-platform-s-uxui-round-11-cc49314f889f) (round 11) listed these as specs needing updates, and asked Peter whether they should land before or just after that merge. It merged on 4 Nov 2026, and they still fail.

**Proven on 7 Nov 2026:** with the changes in the attached diff, all of these pass (slot 2, `a77652e`), so these causes are no longer taken on trust from #1356. Three things needed more than #1356's list said; see "Corrections" below.

| Cause on #1356 | Specs (cases) |
| -- | -- |
| [PS-1563](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1563/share-permissions-read-view-only-and-view-and-download-everywhere): labels now read "View only" / "View and download" | `verb_matrix:87`, `email_templates_sharing:136`, `lineage_event_labels:218`, `lineage_share_manage:151`, `lineage_share_roundtrip:92`, `lineage_share_visibility:277` ×2, `multi_share_journey:118`, `once_per_press_share:110`, `send_docs:176`, `share_revoke_notify:316`, `status_badge_affordance:39` |
| [PS-1464](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1464/lineage-manage-share-revoke-skips-the-revoke-dialog-and-emails-no-one), [PS-1510](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1510/manage-shares-edit-delete-revokes-the-share-with-no-reason-no-email): Revoke and Edit Link's Delete open the shared dialog, and Notify starts ticked | `share_edit_matrix:193`, `lineage_share_manage:263`, `:314`, `:362`, `once_per_press_share:147`, `share_revoke_notify:174` ×2, `:189` ×2 |
| [PS-1456](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1456/create-an-account-an-invisible-character-in-a-name-shows-a-browser): a refused name shows under its field, not in the browser's bubble | `person_name_characters:47` ×3, `:63` ×3 |
| [PS-1479](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1479/a-user-who-has-not-accepted-the-terms-can-open-verify-a-document-every): the Terms gate no longer exempts Verify | `access_matrix:124` ×2 (NoTcPrivacy, and its second login) |
| [PS-1544](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1544/sign-up-answers-uniformly-for-a-registered-or-pending-address-and): a taken address gets the uniform answer | `signup_journey:142` |
| [PS-1475](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1475/an-erased-member-shows-as-erased-user-former-member-erased-user-never): "Former member (erased)" | `person_erasure:140` |
| [PS-1486](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1486/manage-shares-every-rows-control-is-share-details-for-recipient-so): row name "Share details for {file} to {email}" | `share_form_feedback:93` |

`send_docs:176` also stops the 4 tests after it in its serial group from running.

## Proposed change

Update each spec to what the listed ticket ruled, one cause at a time, starting with the [PS-1563](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1563/share-permissions-read-view-only-and-view-and-download-everywhere) labels because that row is the largest. Each ticket's wording and `docs/USER-MANUAL.md` are the source of truth, and any test that still fails after its label or default is updated should be treated as new.

## Corrections from the live proof

* `lineage_share_manage:151`**:** the labels alone don't fix it. `RETIRED_MESSAGE` must read "Choose View only or View and download." (`SharePermissionRule`). The report says "element not found" only because the toast dismisses itself during the retry; the toast itself is fine.
* `lineage_share_manage:263`**,** `:314`**,** `:362`**,** `once_per_press_share:147`**:** Lineage has its own revoke dialog (`lineage-revoke-*`), not the shared `revoke-modal-*` one. `pages/lineage_link_modal_page.ts` must pick a reason and confirm there, and the POST follows the 5-second Undo.
* `send_docs:176` also stops 4 tests (`send_docs:192`, `:202`, `:215`, `:222`). All 4 pass with the fix.

The attached diff uses `#id` selectors in the Lineage dialog for speed. The real change should use the `lineage-revoke-*` testids.

title: systemTest: signed_package_journeys:98 shares a PNG as View only, which PS-902 no longer offers
description:
## Failure

`signed_package_journeys:98` times out clicking `senddocs-share-permission-view-btn`, because the button is disabled. Its `aria-describedby` points at the non-PDF note.

## Cause

`6a17ea1` ([PS-902](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-902/a-view-in-browser-recipient-of-a-docx-is-handed-the-complete-file), 5 Nov 2026): View only isn't offered with a non-PDF file selected, because the recipient's page can't draw it. The note reads "View only works only for PDFs, because other file types can't open in the browser."

The test's document comes from `signedPng`. Its first half, the View and download share, reaches the failing line without trouble.

## Proposed change

The second half asserts that a view-only share offers no package, and that can no longer be set up with a PNG. Two options:

1. Run that half on a detached-signed PDF. It needs a slot with `EMBED_PDF=false`, so it would normally stand down `[env]`.
2. Replace it with an assertion of the new rule: on a PNG, View only is disabled and the note is shown. Check first whether a [PS-902](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-902/a-view-in-browser-recipient-of-a-docx-is-handed-the-complete-file) test already covers this.

Which to pick is Peter's call. A view-only share with no package may also be better pinned in xUnit.

## Proven on 7 Nov 2026 (slot 2, `a77652e`)

For a PNG, View only is disabled, View and download is enabled, and the note is shown. For a PDF, View only is enabled. With option 2 applied, the test passes.

title: systemTest: credential specs post the form PS-909 removed, so 2 tests fail and 13 more never run
description:
## Failure

`credential_verify:153` and `identity_credential_revocation:108` get 404 from `POST /identity/credentials/issue`, where they expect 200. Both are the first step of a serial group, so the rest never run: 7 in `credential_verify` and 6 in `identity_credential_revocation`.

**Those 13 include the forgery controls from** [PS-1440](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1440/systemtest-credentials-a-self-signed-credential-must-not-verify-as) (`credential_verify:245`, `:265`) and the revoked-credential checks, so this security coverage is not running at all today.

## Cause

`392f5a9` ([PS-909](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-909/any-signed-in-user-can-mint-an-issuer-signed-authentic), 4 Nov 2026): the endpoint now takes only `documentStoreId`, for a document the caller owns or holds rights over, and anyone else gets 404. `IdentityApiPage.issueCredential` still posts a type, a free-text hash and a title. **The 404 is the security fix working.**

Stuart's [PS-909](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-909/any-signed-in-user-can-mint-an-issuer-signed-authentic) comment of 4 Nov says these specs "need to upload a document and pass its id", and that the ticket's browser test is also Peter's.

## Proposed change

* Change `IdentityApiPage.issueCredential` and `IssueCredentialInput` to take a document id.
* Have each serial group upload its own document first and clean it up, per [PS-806](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-806/systemtest-specs-leave-uploaded-documents-behind-non-pdf-document).
* The specs compute `documentHash` themselves, so take it from the uploaded document instead.
* `identity_vc_routes.spec.ts` is named on [PS-909](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-909/any-signed-in-user-can-mint-an-issuer-signed-authentic) too. It did not fail in this run, so check whether it still reaches the endpoint.

## Proven on 7 Nov 2026 (slot 2, `a77652e`)

| Request to `POST /identity/credentials/issue` | Answer |
| -- | -- |
| Old form (type, hash, title) | 404 |
| A document the caller owns | 200 |
| A document the caller doesn't hold | 404 |

With the page object uploading a document and passing its id, both failing tests and all 13 blocked tests pass, including the forgery controls `credential_verify:245` and `:265`. `identity_credential_revocation` also needs its by-hash calls to use the uploaded document's hash.

title: systemTest: attach specs do not turn on PS-1583's organisation setting — 3 tests fail and 23 skip with a misleading reason
description:
## Failure

| Spec | Line | What happens |

| `share_edit_matrix` | 293 | "attach block missing — ShareAttachments:Enabled did not reach the mounted config" |
| `signed_package_outlook` | 48, 95 | Consent answers 403, where the spec expects 200 |

## Cause

[PS-1583](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1583/decision-should-attaching-a-copy-to-a-share-be-off-by-default-allowed) (Stuart, 6 Nov 2026, "Org setting, per user too"): attaching is off for each organisation until an Account Admin allows it. `AppSpecific:ShareAttachments:Enabled` stays as the outer limit. No file under `systemTest/` names `/settingsorgattachcopies` or `org-attach-copies-*` yet.

Stuart's [PS-1583](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1583/decision-should-attaching-a-copy-to-a-share-be-off-by-default-allowed) comment of 6 Nov says these specs "need their organisation turned on first".

## Coverage being lost without a failure

**23 more tests skip, and this matters more than the 3 failures, because a skip doesn't show up as red.** Their reasons say the feature is disabled on this deployment:

| Spec | Lines | Skips |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `send_docs_attach` | 23, 38, 54, 72, 88, 123 | 16 |

| `signed_package_compromised` | 63 | 2 |
| `lineage_event_detail` | 154 | 1 |
| `signed_package_journeys` | 147 | 1 |

The likely real reason is the organisation setting: the Outlook spec's own message says a 404 would mean the deployment switch is off, and it received 403. This is an inference from that status and from `MayAttachAsync`. **Not checked:** the skip's own condition on a slot, or which of the 23 were already skipping before [PS-1583](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1583/decision-should-attaching-a-copy-to-a-share-be-off-by-default-allowed).

## Proposed change

Organisation 3 has one writer ([PS-1004](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1004/organisation-3s-name-is-written-by-two-specs-running-at-once-and-each)), so a shared seeded organisation needs care; a per-run organisation may be simpler.
* Correct the skip reasons and the `share_edit_matrix:293` message so they name both switches.
* Add a browser check that an organisation left off offers no attach block. xUnit already pins who may attach under each setting.

## Proven on 7 Nov 2026 (slot 2, `a77652e`)

This settles the inference above: **the real reason for the skips is the organisation setting, not the deployment.**

| Setting | Attach block | Consent | Settings page's "deployment off" notice |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| Off | Absent | 403 | Not shown |
| Everyone | Shown | 200 | Not applicable |

With it on, all 23 ran instead of skipping: 17 passed, and `send_docs_attach:38` failed on all 6 projects, because [PS-1580](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1580/attach-a-copy-warning-say-the-link-is-under-your-control-and-that-you) reworded the warning to "not be able to revoke or expire". With that string updated, all 6 pass. So **a skip was hiding a stale assertion.**

The 3 failing tests also pass with the setting on.

**Still not checked:** which of the 23 were already skipping before [PS-1583](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1583/decision-should-attaching-a-copy-to-a-share-be-off-by-default-allowed), on stacks where the deployment switch was off.

title: systemTest: 8 Health tests fail because isRefused does not accept the app's 302 /PageNotFound
description:
## Failure

`signed_out_shell:91` (1 test) and `system_health_by_role:120` (7 roles) report `GET /Health → 302 /PageNotFound?url=%2FHealth` as not refused.

## Cause

[PS-1432](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1432/health-is-administrator-only-health-healthdata-healthprobek-and) (`117b77f`, 4 Nov 2026) made Health Administrator-only, and `HealthPageGateAttribute` answers everyone else NotFound. The browser sees that 404 as a redirect to `/PageNotFound`, through the app's status-code pages.

`isRefused` in `utils/health_routes.ts` accepts 401, 403, 404, or a redirect to sign-in or access denied, but not this redirect. The specs' own comment says "Page not found" counts as a refusal. **So the product is doing what** [PS-1432](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1432/health-is-administrator-only-health-healthdata-healthprobek-and) **asked, and the helper is what needs changing.**

A [PS-1432](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1432/health-is-administrator-only-health-healthdata-healthprobek-and) comment of 5 Nov already records these as "waiting on Peter's `isRefused` change".

## Proposed change

Have `isRefused` accept a 3xx to `/PageNotFound`, with a unit test on the helper. Match the path rather than a loose substring, so that a page merely mentioning it can't count as a refusal.

## Proven on 7 Nov 2026 (slot 2, `a77652e`)

The Administrator gets 200 from `/Health`. The Account Admin gets `302 /PageNotFound` on every Health route, the helper returns false for each, and the browser lands on a 404 page. With `isRefused` accepting that redirect, all 8 pass.

title: systemTest: 55 tests fail on develop because specs have not followed deliberate product changes (PS-902, PS-909, PS-910, PS-1432, PS-1583, round 11)
description:
## Summary

**55 systemTest tests fail on** `develop`**, and the triage found no product defect behind them.** Each traces to a deliberate product change that the specs have not followed. Until they are updated, every full run on `develop` starts with these 55 failures, which makes a new failure hard to see.

Stuart asked for this triage on 7 Nov 2026. These are proposals for Peter, as `systemTest/` is his area. No spec has been changed.

## Evidence

Measured for [PS-1600](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1600/systemtest-page-objects-still-name-testids-ps-1436-and-ps-1540-removed) on 6 Nov 2026 on slot 2, reset first and paired with platform-k slot 2:

| Run | Passed | Failed | Skipped | Did not run |
| -- | -- | -- | -- | -- |
| Full suite on `d3686a7` | 3,144 | 56 | 46 | 20 |
| Same 31 spec files from `develop` at `87b0c0b`, no `ssd/` difference | 414 | 55 | 1 | 20 |

The 55 are the same tests by name in both runs. The spec-by-spec table is on [Secuura/platform-s#1433](https://linear.app/secuura/review/ps-1600-page-objects-stop-naming-testids-ps-1436-and-ps-1540-removed-978fdb96944d).

## Causes

Each row has its own sub-ticket.

| Tests | Cause | What the spec needs |
| -- | -- | -- |
| 32 | Round 11 changes, as listed in #1356 group A | Update labels, the Notify default and field messages |
| 9 | [PS-910](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-910/admin-add-user-org-silently-creates-a-second-assuranceorgwhitelabelcom) removed the support account | Stop creating and removing the support persona |
| 8 | [PS-1432](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1432/health-is-administrator-only-health-healthdata-healthprobek-and) made Health Administrator-only | `isRefused` must accept `302 /PageNotFound` |
| 3 | [PS-1583](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1583/decision-should-attaching-a-copy-to-a-share-be-off-by-default-allowed) turned attaching off per organisation | Turn it on first (also 23 skipped tests) |
| 2 | [PS-909](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-909/any-signed-in-user-can-mint-an-issuer-signed-authentic) changed the credential issue endpoint | Upload a document and pass its id (also stops 13 tests) |
| 1 | [PS-902](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-902/a-view-in-browser-recipient-of-a-docx-is-handed-the-complete-file) removed View only for non-PDF files | Rework the view-only half of the journey |

## How far this was checked

* **Traced to code, a commit and a ticket:** the 23 tests in the last five rows.
* **Not re-derived test by test:** the 32 in the first row. Their causes come from the #1356 failure list, and the error messages seen in this run are consistent with it.
* **Not run again since the triage:** no fix was tried, so "fixed" still needs a live run.

## Not included

`testid_coverage_sweep:190` is the 56th failure. It failed only on the [PS-1600](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1600/systemtest-page-objects-still-name-testids-ps-1436-and-ps-1540-removed) branch, with a 30-second `page.goto` timeout on `/SendDocsLinksAdmin`, and passed 5 of 5 when repeated. It has no ticket; reopen it if it recurs.

## Done

All 55 pass in a full run on a reset slot, or carry a `test.fixme` naming an open ticket.

## Proven on 7 Nov 2026

title: Share tokens still reach the application log and a mangled 404 URL
description:
Left over from [PS-1601](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1601>), which stopped a share token in a failed URL reaching PostHog or the Google tag. A token alone opens a share, and a View and Download share's file, with no sign-in. Both items below are from reading the code.

## To fix

1. **Application log.** `SDViewDownloadController` writes the token in clear: `LogInvalidToken`, and the stream and download failure lines (`"SDViewDownload stream failed for token {Token}"`, `"SDViewDownload download failed for token {Token}"`). `LogInvalidToken` logs tokens that matched no link, which can include a mistyped live one, while the failure lines log live tokens. These should carry a link id or a masked or keyed form instead.
2. **Mangled links.** `RequestedUrlForNotFound` recognises a share route by `sdviewdownload` in the path. A token on a path without it, such as `/v/{token}`, can't be recognised, so it is still repeated in `/PageNotFound?url=`, on the page and in the 404 log line, and the Google tag sends that URL as `dl` for someone who opted in. `/PageNotFound` is not recorded by PostHog. Decide whether a 404 should stop repeating the requested path altogether.

## Also owed from [PS-1601](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1601/a-share-token-in-a-404-or-error-url-reaches-posthog-or-the-google-tag)

[Secuura/platform-s#1434](https://linear.app/secuura/review/ps-1601-a-share-token-in-a-failed-url-no-longer-reaches-posthog-or-the-8e09b5596eed) merged on Stuart's instruction with the full systemTest suite left for later (6 Nov 2026). Still to do once a run is possible:

* The full systemTest run on `develop`, with the numbers on [PS-1601](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1601/a-share-token-in-a-404-or-error-url-reaches-posthog-or-the-google-tag) and here.
* A real check on dev-ps: a failed share URL with a real token, confirming neither PostHog nor the Google tag receives it, and that the Dashboard's incoming Download link is blanked in a replay.

## Done means

* No share token in the application log, proven by a test.
* A decision on the 404's `url=`, with a test.
* A draft PR to `develop` with `dotnet test` green. CLAUDE.md sets the PR gates.

title: PR 2057 forged-tenant cells stay green if the tenant resolver falls back to the token's tenant claim: a blind spot, not a defect

QA gate 235 found what the cells cannot see: if the tenant resolver also fell back to the token's own tenant claim, all 5 stay green, so the cells would not notice the stored tenant moving from the default tenant to the caller's own tenant. Gate 235's own tamper, the tenant resolver additionally falling back to the token's tenant claim (`req.user.tenantId`), left all 5 green. Cell M1 pins the default-tenant behaviour, but only for requests where that field is not on `req` at resolution time.

**What the cells do show (gate 235):** the test imports the real `Blockchain/Dev/services/originate/src/index.ts` (real mount order, provenance middleware, tenant resolution, `authenticate()`, `requireRole`, the admin router) with only `express.application.listen` and `prisma.$queryRaw` replaced, and a control cell asserts the listen spy fired. The INSERT's tenant slot is pinned by M1.

**Not measured:** which tenant the stored key should take from a signed-in caller through this route; that is the question the blind spot leaves open. Gate 235 did not read the PR bodies.

**Source:** gate 235 verdict, finding F8 on PR 2057, `/Volumes/DevMASTER/WEDNESDAY/0_Brain/reference/2026-11-06_gate235-tier2-pr2054-2057/verdict.md`. This seat did not re-run the cells.

title: PR 2056 residues: a failed SMTP send still logs the recipient address, a contact email at INFO, cells blind to a partial leak
description:
**BLUF:** PR 2056 (KS-1937, merged 2026-11-06 11:51:28Z as `90b500e19883`) took the recipient address out of ten originate log lines, but a failed SMTP send can still log it, because the line prints the error text and an SMTP server echoes the address in its refusal. Two smaller residues from the same gate: a third-party verifier's contact email is logged at INFO, and the PR's 12 cells stay green when the log line carries the recipient's domain. Item 1 is MEDIUM (MEASURED AT RUNTIME); items 2 and 3 are MINOR. Found by QA gate 235 (round 1); no fix here.

**Item 1, MEDIUM, MEASURED AT RUNTIME (gate 235, a loopback stub SMTP server with real nodemailer 10.2.1):** `Blockchain/Dev/services/originate/src/services/email.ts` line 210 (read again at develop `90b500e19883`) is `` console.error(`[Email/SMTP] Failed to send: ${error.message}`) ``. The stub made it print: `[Email/SMTP] Failed to send: Can't send mail - all recipients were rejected: 550 5.1.1 <ks1937.probe.recipient@example.test>: Recipient address rejected: User unknown`, address present. Gate 235 also read nodemailer's `smtp-connection/index.js` line 1221, which builds `'Invalid recipient ' + JSON.stringify(address)`. The PR's tests forward the text `ks1937 smtp boom` and so prove nothing about what a server echoes. Same class, not measured: the ACS error object (line 164 of the same file at the PR head), `err?.message` (line 167), `String(err)` in the WARN lines of `Blockchain/Dev/services/originate/src/utils/notificationClient.ts`, and its `body.substring(0,200)` of the notification service's reply. The ruling behind it is Kam's card `secuura-ks1346-logging-thrown-objects-leaks-secrets` (a: never their values) and Wednesday's KS-1937 answer (log the template, never the address). Fix shape (gate 235's): log the error's class and code (`error.code`, `error.responseCode`) instead of its message, or strip the recipient first; test with a stub server that echoes the address.

**Item 2, MINOR, READ ONLY:** the PR's fragment says a scan of every log call flags the two sites in KS-2036 and nothing else. `Blockchain/Dev/services/originate/src/routes/thirdPartyVerifiers.ts` line 87 (read again at `90b500e19883`) is `logger.info('Third-party verifier registered', { id, organizationName, contactEmail })`: a contact address, not a recipient, but an address in an INFO line, and not in KS-2036's list.

**Item 3, MINOR, MEASURED AT RUNTIME (gate 235 tamper X):** with the allow-list refusal line changed to print the recipient's domain, `...refusing to send: ${options.to.split("@")[1]}`, all 12 cells stay green: they look only for the full address. The ACS path's "the address still reaches the mailer" is also unpinned (cells E1 to E3 never check the arguments of `beginSend`); only the SMTP path pins `mockSendMail.mock.calls[0][0].to` (cell E6). Tampers Y (full address on the SMTP Sent line), Z (address back on the client fallback INFO line) and W (blank SMTP `to`) were each caught by exactly one cell. Tests: `Blockchain/Dev/services/originate/src/__tests__/ks1937-email-service-logs-never-carry-the-recipient-address.test.ts` and `Blockchain/Dev/services/originate/src/__tests__/ks1937-notification-client-logs-the-template-never-the-recipient-address.test.ts`.

**Source:** gate 235 verdict, findings F2, F4 and F5 on PR 2056, `/Volumes/DevMASTER/WEDNESDAY/0_Brain/reference/2026-11-06_gate235-tier2-pr2054-2057/verdict.md`. Items 1 and 2 were re-read by this seat at develop `90b500e19883` through the GitHub API; nothing was run by this seat.

**Board search (2026-11-06, includeArchived, paginated):** `services/originate/src/services/email.ts` and `contactEmail`: 0 hits. `Failed to send` and `[Email/SMTP]`: 1 open hit each, KS-1964 (the auth service's own email sender, a different service). `thirdPartyVerifiers`: 3 open hits (KS-1868, KS-1945, KS-1946), none about the log line. `KS-1937`: 6 open hits (KS-1937, KS-1964, KS-1965, KS-1966, KS-2036, KS-2076). KS-2036 was read whole: it covers `routes/certifications.ts` line 1385 and `routes/adminConfig.ts` line 2123 and none of these three items.

title: Pre-push hook leg 14 refused a push on 4 failed controls of the slot-literals suite, which passes 11 of 11 alone (one occurrence)
description:
**BLUF:** The pre-push hook refused a push because the shell suite `systemTest/__tests__/no_hardcoded_slot_literals.test.sh` failed 4 of its 11 cells, on a diff that cannot touch that suite. Run alone on the same worktree it passes 11 of 11, and it passed in an earlier hook run. So this is a hook suite refusing a push intermittently, by one occurrence. Cause UNMEASURED. The refusal cost Seat Z 4th about 23 minutes of the push queue. No fix here.

**The occurrence (MEASURED, one run):** Seat Z 4th pushing KS-1670, head `83ee8509c985`, worktree `worktrees/s-z4-m365err`. Evidence file `/Volumes/DevMASTER/!CODING/Secuura/Blockchain/5_Project_History/2026-11-06_seatZ-4th/evidence/item2/push/push.out`, hook leg 14 of 16 ("Every shell test suite must actually RUN"), lines quoted:

* line 2713: `=== systemTest/__tests__/no_hardcoded_slot_literals.test.sh ===`
* line 2720: `FAIL CONTROL: planted 54 literals, the guard reported 0`
* line 2724: `FAIL CONTROL: a bare 'slot-literal-ok:' exempted a literal`
* line 2728: `FAIL CONTROL: an untracked source file was skipped`
* line 2733: `FAIL CONTROL: the membership check cannot catch a non-from_runs element`, and line 2734: `exempted=0 violations=0 (both must be >= 1)`
* line 2736: `no_hardcoded_slot_literals: 7 passed, 4 failed`
* line 3629: `shell suites: 116 passed, 1 failed, 0 skipped (of 117)`; line 3630: `FAILED: systemTest/__tests__/no_hardcoded_slot_literals.test.sh`

The same suite alone, `/Volumes/DevMASTER/!CODING/Secuura/Blockchain/5_Project_History/2026-11-06_seatZ-4th/evidence/item2/slot_literals_standalone.out`, ends `no_hardcoded_slot_literals: 11 passed, 0 failed`.

**What the four failures share (READ):** each is a control that needs the planted control tree to be a git work tree, and each reads as if the scan found nothing (planted 54, reported 0; exempted 0, violations 0). The two checks before them passed in the same run (lines 2715 to 2718: the 45 computed patterns, and 1383 files scanned with no unmarked slot literal). The suite builds the control tree at line 157 of `systemTest/__tests__/no_hardcoded_slot_literals.test.sh` with `git -C "$TMP/st" init -q 2>/dev/null` (read at develop `90b500e19883`), and its comment at line 156 says the scan lists files through git.

**Seat Z 4th's one reading (UNMEASURED):** that `git init` failed under load (load average about 8 at that moment), the `2>/dev/null` hid it, and the four controls then ran on a tree git did not know. Not measured: that the init failed, the load figure, and any second occurrence.

**Board search (2026-11-06, includeArchived, paginated):** `no_hardcoded_slot_literals` has 1 open hit, KS-1451 (In Progress: a bare `slot-literal-ok:` marker exempts a quoted value; a deterministic defect of the same guard), and 1 closed hit, KS-1450 (Done: leg 14 failing every time since 89dff83aa on 8 unmarked slot-2 literals). `planted 54 literals`, `no unmarked slot` and `pre-push hook intermittent` have 0 hits. title: Public API examples show blockHeight as a string ("4615780"); a client typed as a number would fail to read it
description:
**BLUF:** Two public examples show a transaction's `blockHeight` as a string, `"blockHeight": "4615780"`. A client typed as a number would fail to read it. Gate 238 read Platform S's `long?` height with its JSON options in a June snapshot and found no number-from-string handling, so its verify page would fall to "temporarily unavailable" on such a body. Pre-existing and docs only; gate 238 grades it MINOR. Evidence class: READ ONLY (the deserialisation was not run).

**Where (READ at develop** `90b500e19883`**):** `Blockchain/Dev/docs/VERIFICATION.md` line 64 and `Blockchain/Dev/services/api-gateway/src/docs/developer-portal.html` line 202, the same example wrapped in HTML. Both sit inside a `blockchain` object with `"network": "preprod"` and a `txHash`.

**Platform S side (gate 238, READ from a June snapshot, not run):** `CardanoAnchorService.cs` lines 19 to 23 hold the JSON options with no number-from-string handling, and the verify page's fallback text is at lines 332 to 340. The deployed Platform S has moved since that snapshot (gate 238, finding F2), so what it does today is not known.

**Related, read in KS-1129 (In Progress):** anchoring's `block_number` leaves `buildResponse` as a string because `pg` returns BIGINT as a string, and a healed document can carry that string into the public verify answer; KS-1628 ruled that the successor verify accepts a positive-integer digit string as well as a number. So the example may show real output and not only a docs slip, which is why the contract (number, or number or digit string) comes before the wording. **Not measured by this seat:** which routes answer a string today. PR 2054 (KS-1509) moves the stored height toward a number or null, which gate 238 reads as the right direction.

**Source:** gate 238 verdict, finding F10, `/Volumes/DevMASTER/WEDNESDAY/0_Brain/reference/2026-11-06_gate238-tier1-pr2054-ks1509/verdict.md`.

**Board search (2026-11-06, includeArchived, paginated):** `docs/VERIFICATION.md` and `4615780`: 0 hits. `developer-portal.html`: 5 open hits (KS-485, KS-772, KS-967, KS-1473, KS-1651) and 3 closed, none about the height example (KS-1473 is the undocumented verify-batch route). `blockHeight`: 8 open and 16 closed hits; the nearest is KS-1129 (In Progress): anchoring's raw `pg` BIGINT block number reaches readers as a string.

**Possible shape (mine, not a decision):** settle the height's contract with KS-1129 first, then make both examples match it; a Platform S owner should say whether the deployed reader accepts a string.

title: GET /api/documents/:id answers anchored true for a pending document: anchored is true for any blob that is not anchor_failed
description:
**BLUF:** `GET /api/documents/:id` answers `blockchain.anchored: true` for a document whose anchoring is only pending and that has no transaction hash. `anchored` is true for any blob that is not `anchor_failed`, so a pending blob reads as anchored. Gate 238 grades this NOTE and pre-existing; it is filed at Medium on Wednesday's call, because PR 2054 (KS-1509) removes the `0` height from the same answer and leaves this larger claim in place. **Where (READ at develop** `90b500e19883`**):** `Blockchain/Dev/services/originate/src/routes/documents.ts` line 1224: `anchored: !!document.blockchain && document.blockchain.status !== 'anchor_failed'` (line 1228 at the PR 2054 head, where gate 238 read it). The comment above it (lines 1221 to 1223, KS-520) says `anchored` is status-derived so that the fail-closed state does not read as anchored; a `pending` status passes the same test. Gate 238 records the shape a pending document gets: `anchored: true, status: 'pending', txHash: null`, with `blockHeight` 0 at develop and null at the PR head.

**Who keys on it (READ at the same sha):** the issuer portal, `Blockchain/Dev/frontend/issuer/src/components/DocumentDetail.tsx` line 185, builds its anchor list from `raw.blockchain?.anchored`; gate 238 notes it is saved only by the hash guard at line 490, which hides the card when there is no hash.

**Source:** gate 238 verdict, finding F6, `/Volumes/DevMASTER/WEDNESDAY/0_Brain/reference/2026-11-06_gate238-tier1-pr2054-ks1509/verdict.md`.

**Board search (2026-11-06, includeArchived, paginated):** `anchored true`: 0 hits. `pending document`: 4 open hits (KS-772, KS-1087, KS-1184, KS-2006), all about the workflow-approve forward or a review stream, none about the `anchored` flag. `blockHeight`: 8 open and 16 closed hits; the nearest are KS-1509 (the height default) and KS-1129 (the BIGINT shape). title: Both portals print Block 0 for a document with no block: the verifier's Block Height row and the issuer's Block card
description:
**BLUF:** Two portal screens show "0" as a block number for a document that has no block, so the claim of a block 0 survives on screen even where the API now answers `null`. The verifier portal prints `Block Height 0` for a pending document. The issuer portal prints `Block 0` for every real anchor, even a confirmed one, because it never carries the height through. Neither is a regression and neither is cured by PR 2054 (KS-1509); gate 238 asked for both to be ticketed. Evidence class: READ ONLY (not run in a browser).

**F4, the verifier portal (READ ONLY at develop** `90b500e19883`**):** `Blockchain/Dev/frontend/verifier/src/components/ResultPage.tsx`. The "Blockchain Proof" card shows when `result.verified && (result.blockchain || result.anchor)` (line 449). Its "Block Height" row (lines 495 to 498) prints `(result.blockchain?.blockHeight || result.anchor?.blockNumber || 0).toLocaleString()` (line 497), so an unknown height prints 0. `verified` is true for a pending row. Gate 238 records the same lines at the PR head and that the card sits beside a failing "Anchored on blockchain" check. Fix shape (gate 238's): hide the row when there is no height.

**F5, the issuer portal (READ ONLY at develop** `90b500e19883`**):** `Blockchain/Dev/frontend/issuer/src/components/DocumentDetail.tsx` lines 185 to 192 build the anchor from `raw.blockchain` with `id`, `status`, `network`, `txHash` and `anchoredAt` and no height; gate 238 records that GET document returns no `anchors` key, so line 120 (`blockNumber: anchor.blockHeight || anchor.block_height || 0`) always falls to 0. title: originate publishEvent swallows every Redis failure in an empty catch: a failed user.erased publish is silent and the log says published
description:
**BLUF:** originate publishes `user.erased` through its own `publishEvent`, and the `catch` at lines 143 to 145 of `Blockchain/Dev/services/originate/src/events.ts` is empty. A Redis failure while publishing is therefore silent: the erasure returns success, `gdprService` logs `user.erased event published`, and no stream entry exists, so no downstream service ever erases the subject's copy. With `REDIS_URL` unset the same happens. The `warn` branch in `gdprService` that says the cascade may be incomplete cannot fire on a Redis failure, because `publishEvent` never throws. Found in Seat U 17th's walk of the erasure; no fix here.

**Measured (MEASURED AT RUNTIME), Seat U 17th, 2026-11-06:** the real compiled originate on PostgreSQL 15.19 and redis-server 8.10.3 at develop `b7d433fda83c` on Node v26.8.1; not a box, not Kintsugi, not demo. Evidence file `/Volumes/DevMASTER/!CODING/Secuura/Blockchain/5_Project_History/2026-11-06_seatU-17th/evidence/walk/run_erasure.out`, lines 12 and 13, quoted:

* `E8 dead Redis {"result":{"label":"E8","success":true,"tables":["users","pii_subject_keys"],"ms":89},"warned":false,"newEntries":0,"status":"deleted","walletKept":true}`
* `E9 REDIS_URL unset {"result":{"label":"E9","success":true,"tables":["users","pii_subject_keys"],"ms":95},"saidPublished":true,"newEntries":0}`

Seat U 17th predicted a `warn` for E8 before running it (`predictions_erasure.txt` line 10 in the same folder) and the run showed none: success true after 89 ms, no warn line, 0 stream entries, and the log line `user.erased event published`. Its STATUS of 2026-11-06 about 11:55Z (item W1) records the same.

**Where (READ at the same sha):**

* `Blockchain/Dev/services/originate/src/events.ts`: `publishEvent` (line 118) returns at once when there is no client (`if (!redis) return;`, line 123); otherwise its `try` runs `xadd` and the `catch` at lines 143 to 145 holds only the comment `// Fire-and-forget — never let event publishing break the service`. `initEventBus` warns once at start-up when `REDIS_URL` is unset (line 62); no later erasure says anything.
* `Blockchain/Dev/services/originate/src/services/gdprService.ts`: lines 962 to 981 wrap `await publishEvent(EventTypes.USER_ERASED, ...)` in a `try`, log `user.erased event published — downstream services will cascade` after it (line 970) and log `Failed to publish user.erased event (cascade may be incomplete)` in the `catch` (line 980). That `catch` is unreachable for a Redis failure.
* What does not happen when the entry is missing, per the same run: auth deactivating the user (E3) and wallet-connector deleting the wallet's session rows (E4); per KS-1955, kyc's deletes. KS-1955 also says originate marks the data-subject request completed at step 12, before the publish at step 13.

**Not measured:** a Redis failure that appears only after the `xadd` is accepted, and the running Kintsugi or demo originate (neither was touched).

**Board search (2026-11-06, includeArchived, paginated):** 0 open and 0 closed literal hits for `originate/src/events.ts` and `event published`. `user.erased` has 7 open hits, none about the publisher: KS-239, KS-485, KS-772, KS-1868, KS-1931, KS-1955, KS-2060. KS-1955 (Backlog, High, 0 comments) is the handler half: a failed kyc or wallet-connector handler after the bus, and its text does not name `Blockchain/Dev/services/originate/src/events.ts` or `publishEvent`. KS-2004 is an empty catch in the demo user seed, a different file. `publishEvent` appears in KS-1651 (the `ownership_transferred` payload) and `initEventBus` in KS-1868 (unguarded thrown-value reads); neither covers this empty catch.

**Possible shapes (mine, not a decision):** have `publishEvent` return whether the entry was added, or log inside the catch with the event type and the error message, and make the `gdprService` info line depend on that result so the existing `warn` can fire.

title: governance POST /api/governance/proposals/:id/execute checks no role: any signed-in user of any tenant executes a queued proposal
description:
**BLUF:** `POST /api/governance/proposals/:id/execute` checks only that the caller is signed in. It checks no role, no proposer or committee membership and no tenant. Measured on a real compiled service: a user of one tenant with the OWNER role executed a queued proposal created by a user of another tenant and got 200 with `status` `executed`. Limit: today execution only logs each action and flags it executed (no contract call), by Seat U 17th's read, so the effect is the proposal's status moving to `executed`. Found in Seat U 17th's walk of the governance service; no fix here.

**Measured (MEASURED AT RUNTIME), Seat U 17th, 2026-11-06:** the real compiled governance service on PostgreSQL 15.19 at develop `b7d433fda83c` on Node v26.8.1; not a box, not Kintsugi, not demo. Evidence file `/Volumes/DevMASTER/!CODING/Secuura/Blockchain/5_Project_History/2026-11-06_seatU-17th/evidence/walk/run_base.out`, line 14, quoted (T1 and T2 are the two tenants of the walk):

* `X8 execute a T2 queued proposal as T1 OWNER {"s":200,"t2Status":"executed"}`

A 200 also means the timelock check passed, because the service answers 409 before the proposal's execution time. Sibling routes in the same walk do check the caller: cancel by a non-committee user answered 403 `Only proposer or constitutional committee can cancel` (line 11), and process-expired by an OWNER answered 403 where a SUPER_ADMIN got 200 (line 13).

**Where (READ at the same sha):** `Blockchain/Dev/services/governance/src/routes/governance.ts` lines 300 to 315: the handler reads `userId`, answers 401 when it is absent, and calls `governanceService.executeProposal(req.params.id, userId)`. `Blockchain/Dev/services/governance/src/services/governanceService.ts` line 1103: `executeProposal(proposalId: string, _executorId: string)`. The executor id is named `_executorId` and appears nowhere else in the file; the body checks that the proposal exists, is `queued` and is past its timelock, then marks its actions executed and saves.

**Not measured:** a rule in front of the service. The walk's STATUS lists originate, auth, wallet-connector and governance as the compiled services, so whether the api-gateway narrows this path is not measured.

**Board search (2026-11-06, includeArchived, paginated):** 0 open and 0 closed literal hits for `proposals/:id/execute`, `executeProposal` and `_executorId`. The nearest tickets are the same class on other services: KS-1814 (the document anchor route) and KS-2038 (the transfer doors).

**Possible shape (mine, not a decision):** a check like the cancel route's (proposer or committee) or a role set on `execute`, with a cell for the 403.

title: governance castVote counts a delegator's stake twice: the delegator still votes with it and the delegate's vote adds it again
description:
**BLUF:** In the governance service a delegator keeps full voting power after delegating it, and the delegate's vote adds the delegated power on top, so the same stake is counted twice in `votes_for`. Measured on a real compiled service: with one stake of 1000 delegated, `votes_for` reads 3000; in both controls (no delegation, and after the delegation is revoked) it reads 2000. Found in Seat U 17th's walk of the governance service; no fix here.

**Measured (MEASURED AT RUNTIME), Seat U 17th, 2026-11-06:** the real compiled governance service on PostgreSQL 15.19 at develop `b7d433fda83c` on Node v26.8.1; not a box, not Kintsugi, not demo. Evidence file `/Volumes/DevMASTER/!CODING/Secuura/Blockchain/5_Project_History/2026-11-06_seatU-17th/evidence/walk/run_base.out`, lines 2 to 5, quoted (a is the delegator, d the delegate, each owns a stake of 1000):

* `4B control no delegation {"a":1000,"d":1000,"status":[200,200],"votesFor":2000}`
* `4B delegate {"s":200,"delegatedPower":1000}`
* `4B delegated {"a":1000,"d":2000,"status":[200,200],"votesFor":3000}`
* `4B after revoke {"a":1000,"d":1000,"votesFor":2000}`

The delegator's own vote was accepted (status 200) and counted 1000; the delegate's vote counted 2000, its own 1000 plus the delegated 1000.

**Where (READ at the same sha):** `Blockchain/Dev/services/governance/src/services/governanceService.ts`. `castVote` (line 946) gives every voter `voter.votePower` plus `getDelegatedPowerFor(voterId, proposal.category)` (lines 982 and 983) and nowhere checks whether the voter has delegated their own power away. `delegateVote` (line 1193) stores `delegatedPower: delegator.votePower` (line 1224) and leaves the delegator's own `votePower` as it was. `getDelegatedPowerFor` (line 1259) sums `delegatedPower` over the delegate's active delegations. The early-finalise check (lines 1038 to 1045 of the same file) reads `votesFor`, so the doubled figure can decide an outcome.

**Not measured:** a category-scoped delegation (`categories`), several delegators to one delegate, and a proposal whose outcome flips because of the extra power.

**Board search (2026-11-06, includeArchived, paginated):** 0 open and 0 closed literal hits for `getDelegatedPowerFor`, `delegated power` and `votes_for`. `castVote` has 0 open hits and 5 closed ones, none about delegation (KS-450, KS-1940, KS-1942, KS-1950, KS-1951).

**Possible shapes (mine, not a decision):** refuse or zero a delegator's own vote while an active delegation covers the proposal's category, or subtract the delegated-away power in `castVote`; either needs a test cell holding the 2000 and 3000 figures above.

title: No hook suite proves a red preflight makes the pre-push hook refuse a push: its final exit 1 can become exit 0 with every suite green
description:
**BLUF:** No hook suite proves that a red preflight makes the pre-push hook refuse a push. The final step of `.githooks/pre-push`, the `|| { ...; exit 1; }` after the preflight call, can be changed to `exit 0` and every hook suite that can run on a sparse tree stays green. If that line regressed, every leg of the preflight would become advisory and no suite would say so. Found by gate 228 (tier 1, round 2 of 2, GO WITH NOTES) on PR 2047 (KS-1728) as its finding F3: pre-existing, outside that PR's diff, for routing. The hook is correct at the gate's head, so this is a missing test and not a defect today. Verdict in full: /Volumes/DevMASTER/WEDNESDAY/0_Brain/reference/2026-11-06_gate228-tier1-pr2047-ks1728/verdict.md, finding F3 from line 51 (gate head 0dbf24bc0ce40135ed98fcff92661d752b95f350).

## What the gate measured (evidence class MEASURED AT RUNTIME)

* Mutant H3 changes that `exit 1` to `exit 0`, placed in the gate's own worktree as the real hook. All 8 hook suites that are green on that sparse tree stayed green, at base and at head where run. Files, under /Volumes/DevMASTER/WEDNESDAY/0_Brain/reference/2026-11-06_gate228-tier1-pr2047-ks1728/evidence/: `q1_h3_all_hook_suites.txt` and `q1_matrix.txt`.
* The ninth suite, `preflight_deps`, is red with and without H3 on the same 5 FAIL lines, because the gate's sparse tree lacks files it reads. It is not evidence either way.
* A grep of every shell test suite finds no fixture preflight that exits non-zero and no assertion on the refusal text (same folder, `q1_h3_coverage_search.txt`).

## Grade and priority

The verdict grades F3 Minor, which is its technical grade. The priority here is Medium, set by Wednesday on this ground: one line carries every leg of the preflight, nothing proves it, and a regression would make the whole push gate advisory with no suite saying so. It costs one cell to close.

## Fix shape (the gate's, not built)

A regression test: give the fixture preflight a non-zero exit and assert that the push did not land, and that the refusal text appears.

## Not this ticket

The gate's other findings on PR 2047 (F1, the here-string temporary file; F2, the empty pattern; N3, the early-closing pipes) stay with PR 2047 and KS-1728. No comment on KS-1728.

## Searched before filing

2026-11-06, includeArchived, titles and descriptions, paginated, in two runs; controls: the term msgpackr hit KS-1379 among open tickets, a random token hit 0. `.githooks/pre-push`: 16 open and 27 closed hits. `pre_push_hook`: 2 open (KS-1728, KS-1759) and 10 closed. `preflight refuses`: 0. `red preflight`: 0. `no hook suite`: 0. `refuses a push`: 3 open (KS-1422, KS-1611, KS-1646). `swallowed`: 20 open and 21 closed. H3: 5 open and 10 closed (the two characters match unrelated text). Read by title around the hits: none states that no hook suite proves a red preflight refuses a push. The three nearest by subject were read whole (description and comments) and probed for the shape (exit 0, swallow, H3, refuses the push, red preflight, advisory): KS-1759 grades the prose of the hook by three counts; KS-1646 is a fresh clone that runs no hook at all; KS-1483 is a push of a branch that is not checked out skipping the preflight. None holds this finding. The key KS-1728 returned no ticket other than its own.

Items:

1. F1, Low. Blockchain/Dev/scripts/check-shared-relink.sh line 522 still says the code "falls to the $ refusal below". No such refusal exists since PR 2053 removed it; line 509 was corrected and lines 330 to 333 annotated, but line 522 was missed, and "below" was already wrong because the function sits above it. Fix shape: reword line 522 as line 509 now reads. A comment only.
2. F2, Low. The sentence "an unreadable base name is refused" is overbroad. A base written as a whole-reference variable with a slash in its default, for example a FROM line of the form ${BASE:-docker.io/library/nginx:1.27} after an ARG naming a node image, with a COPY --from=shared-builder line and no re-link, reads rc 0 exempt at develop and at the gate head alike, because the name kept after the last slash is nginx. Not a regression, and no real Dockerfile uses the shape (9 distinct FROM spellings, none contains a colon-dash default). Where it is said: Projects Documents/fragments/cheat/KS-957-relink-guard-derived-claims.html line 3, and the new comment at Blockchain/Dev/scripts/check-shared-relink.sh lines 496 to 503, whose root cause sits at lines 529 and 530. 3. F3, Low. The invariant cell reads one split(), so a key added another way passes 17 of 17 while a FROM line made of a bare variable is exempt. Measured by the gate: with NON_JS_BASES\["$foo"\] = 1 assigned beside the loop in Blockchain/Dev/scripts/check-shared-relink.sh, the suite in Blockchain/Dev/scripts/**tests**/check_shared_relink_derived_claims.test.sh stayed at 17 passed, 0 failed, and the guard then read rc 0 for FROM $FOO (develop's guard with the same key reads rc 1; the same key inside the split() is caught). This is the one place PR 2053 makes the gate looser; it needs a reviewed edit that puts a dollar sign in an image allow-list. Fix shape: derive the keys from the awk program at run time, or add a cell asserting NON_JS_BASES is assigned only by the loop over the split() list. The gate's own planted case is the regression test.
4. F4, Low. The flow fragment's list of hand-written counts left in the guard omits one that is false and is printed to authors. Blockchain/Dev/scripts/check-shared-relink.sh line 569 says "it skips all 13 preflight legs", and Blockchain/Dev/scripts/preflight/preflight.sh line 185 sets TOTAL_LEGS=16. Fix shape: add line 569 to the fragment's list and correct or remove the figure.

Note carried from the verdict, not a finding: the new suite is a new refuser at every push. Blockchain/Dev/scripts/**tests**/check_shared_relink_derived_claims.test.sh runs at leg 14 of the pre-push preflight, reached by the runner's glob (the gate measured leg 12 rc 0 over 120 suites). title: a11y sweeps miss contrast failures below the fold: axe sees 169 of 776 serious or critical failures at 1280 x 800
description:
## BLUF

**The axe sweeps don't check text below the fold of** `<main>`**, on any page that scrolls.** Across all 119 swept routes in both themes, they report 169 serious or critical failures, and 600 more are there once axe can see the whole page. Those 600 are on 18 routes.

**Proposal for Peter:** add one temporary style around the scan in `run_axe.ts`. It found 769 of the 776 at about the same scan time and moved no layout. The change is yours to decide, and nothing under `systemTest/` has been changed.

## Why axe gives no verdict

`.secuura-shell-rhs` has `overflow: hidden` (`ssd/wwwroot/css/secuura/shell.css:85`), and `<main>` scrolls inside it. So anything below the fold of `<main>` lies outside that wrapper's box, and axe 4.14 treats it as clipped:

* **Text (paragraph, cell, link, button, label):** `colorContrastMatches` drops it, so there's no violation, pass or incomplete. `link-in-text-block` skips below-fold links too.
* **Inputs and selects:** these pass the match, then `colorContrastEvaluate` calls them hidden and records a **pass**, even at low contrast.

It isn't limited to pager links. At 1280 x 800 the visible part of `<main>` is 709 px, and 117 of 237 route and theme combinations scroll past it. All 237 have this wrapper, including the public pages. A 390 x 844 viewport doesn't have the problem, because `<main>` doesn't scroll there, but the sweep doesn't scan at that size (the only projects listed for `a11y_axe_sweep` are the four desktop Chromium ones).

## Measurements

Slot 3, `216ad3f`, Chromium, 1280 x 800, the sweep's own route table, sessions and tags. "Failures" means serious or critical nodes; "as loaded" is what the sweep sees today; "whole page" uses the style proposed below.

**Whole sweep (pass 2, 237 of 238 combinations):**

|  | As loaded | Whole page |
| -- | -- | -- |
| Serious or critical failures | 169 | 769 |
| Text nodes `color-contrast` checked | 12,479 | 21,065 |

No failure seen as loaded was lost. The rules that changed were `color-contrast` and `link-in-text-block`.

**By page (as loaded → whole page):**

| Page | `<main>` height (px) | Light | Dark | Contrast allow-listed? |
| -- | -- | -- | -- | -- |
| Cardano anchors | 5,004 | 6 → 102 | 6 → 100 | yes |
| Document transactions | 16,518 | 2 → 50 | 4 → 98 | yes |
| Document transactions, verify all | 3,402 | no change | 10 → 39 | yes |
| Admin logs | 26,926 / 32,824 | 2 → 80 | 0 → 22 | yes |
| Cardano anchors, organisation integration | 2,424 | 11 → 37 | 8 → 34 | yes |
| **Stripe products** | 1,622 | 0 → 14 | 0 → 13 | **no** |
| System health | 6,460 | 1 → 5 | 3 → 13 | yes |
| **Identity** | 1,321 | 0 → 9 | 0 → 7 | **no** |
| Register | 1,535 | 0 → 5 | 3 → 4 (pass 1) | yes |
| Subscription portal | 1,832 | 13 → 17 | no change | yes |
| Admin users | 1,116 | 0 → 1 | 8 → 11 | yes |
| Manage shares | 1,049 | 4 → 6 | 4 → 6 | yes |
| Login | 898 | 4 → 5 | 1 → 2 | yes |
| Login (cookie banner) | 898 | no change | 4 → 5 | yes |
| **Organisation users** | 1,719 / 1,709 | 0 → 1 | 0 → 1 | **no** |
| **Delete person** | 1,719 / 1,709 | 0 → 1 | 0 → 1 | **no** |
| **Dashboard (fixture documents)** | 1,019 | 0 → 2 | 0 → 2 | **no** |
| DevTools upload table | 1,237 | 0 → 1 | 1 → 2 | yes |

**Document lists with 12 documents kept on the AccountAdmin's organisation (pass 3):**

| Page | Light | Dark | What appears |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| Dashboard | 0 → 1 | 0 → 1 | disabled pager link ([PS-1590](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1590/disabled-datatables-pager-links-fail-colour-contrast-1771-light-2261)) |
| My documents, Organisation documents, Sign, Watermark | 0 → 2 each | 0 → 2 each | disabled pager links ([PS-1590](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1590/disabled-datatables-pager-links-fail-colour-contrast-1771-light-2261)) |
| Lineage | 6 → 14 | no change | card call-to-action, 2.2:1 ([PS-1485](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1485/colour-contrast-below-wcag-aa-on-28-pagetheme-views-sign-in-button-221)) |

This confirms [PS-1590](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1590/disabled-datatables-pager-links-fail-colour-contrast-1771-light-2261)'s account of why the pager failure came and went: the Dashboard's pager is only scanned when the table is short enough to fit.

## Options compared

The same comparison, measured on every route and theme.

| Method | Failures found | Scans per page | Catch |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| As loaded (today) | 163 of 657 (pass 1) | 1 |  |
| Scroll in 90% steps, scan each stop, combine | 627 of 657 | 323 extra across 238 (2.4 times as many); scan time 244 s → 500 s | content scrolled away drops out, so results must be merged; I capped it at 40 stops, which Admin logs hit |
| Viewport sized to each page | 591 of 657 | 1 | changes the layout; Admin logs hit my 20,000 px cap |
| Fixed 1280 x 3000 viewport | 464 of 776 (pass 2) | 1 | 26 combinations still overflow |
| Plain `overflow: clip` on the wrapper | 650 of 657 | 1 | **moved the layout on 116 of 238**, because a clipped grid item grows to fit its content |
| `overflow: clip` **+** `min-height: 0` **on the wrapper** | **769 of 776 (pass 2)** | **1** | **layout moved on 0 of 237** |

The 7 it misses are on the cookie-banner rows, where `body.modal-open` is itself `overflow: hidden`. The Register and Login rows without the banner catch those same elements.

**Run time:** median scan 649 ms as loaded and 680 ms with the style (p90 1,000 and 995 ms). A full suite was running on slot 2 at the time, so compare these with each other, not with other runs.

## Proposal

In `systemTest/utils/run_axe.ts`, wrap the `analyze()` call in `runAxe` and `runAxeAsIs`, so every sweep and seeded-state scan picks it up:

```ts
const unclip = await page.addStyleTag({
    content: '.secuura-shell-rhs { overflow: clip !important; min-height: 0 !important; }',
});
try {
    results = await excludeThirdParty(new AxeBuilder({ page }).withTags([...WCAG_AA_TAGS])).analyze();
} finally {
    await unclip.evaluate((tag) => tag.remove());
}
```

An offline contract test could pin the selector against `shell.css`, so a renamed wrapper doesn't quietly bring the gap back.

**What goes red when it lands:** `Identity`, `Stripe products`, `Organisation users` and `Delete person`, in both themes. That's on this data, and a fuller run could add others. Each has a ticket ([PS-1594](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1594/identity-assurance-badges-and-nist-labels-fail-colour-contrast-down-to), [PS-1485](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1485/colour-contrast-below-wcag-aa-on-28-pagetheme-views-sign-in-button-221) for Stripe products, [PS-1595](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1595/pager-links-on-grids-without-the-shared-footer-are-007bff-on-white)), so they can be fixed first or allow-listed against those tickets. `Dashboard (fixture documents)` should stay green, since [PS-1590](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1590/disabled-datatables-pager-links-fail-colour-contrast-1771-light-2261) (#1427) merged at 11:09 UTC today and marks those links disabled. That's inferred, because this was measured before the merge.

**What won't change on its own:** the other 13 routes already tolerate `color-contrast` completely. `a11y_known_debt.ts` has 74 contrast entries, 73 of them `intermittent` and none with a `match`, covering 147 of 238 combinations. A new contrast failure on those routes passes wherever it is on the page, until [PS-1485](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1485/colour-contrast-below-wcag-aa-on-28-pagetheme-views-sign-in-button-221) removes those entries.

**Alternative:** the same two declarations in `shell.css` would fix it for every scan, manual ones included, with no test change. That's a product change for Stuart, and I haven't measured it as one. The wrapper also stops being scrollable by script, so it would need its own regression check.

## Product failures this found

* [PS-1485](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1485>): the additional views are listed in a comment there, including Stripe products, Register light and Lineage.
* [PS-1594](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1594>): Identity assurance badges and NIST labels, down to 2.82:1.
* [PS-1595](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1595>): working pager links on grids without the shared footer, 3.97:1, white in dark mode (Organisation users, Delete person, Admin users, upload table).
* [PS-1596](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1596>): admin status badges and table links, down to 1.52:1.
* [PS-1597](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1597>): Register's sign-in link relies on colour alone, the one `link-in-text-block` failure.

## Limits

* **Viewport:** 1280 x 800 Chromium only, so the counts differ at other sizes.
* **Data:** a fresh slot plus the sweep's own fixtures, so these counts are a floor. Long pages grow with the run. Admin logs went from 161 to 80 failures in light between passes because the log contents changed, so treat single-page counts as approximate.
* **No platform-k:** slot 3 ran with `--no-k`, so some Cardano anchors badges say platform-k isn't answering. The colours are real, but that badge state wouldn't show with K up.
* **One failed test:** Register dark timed out waiting for the loading overlay in pass 2 and passed in pass 1, so its figures are from pass 1. The slot had `RestartCount` 0 at the end.
* **Re-run on current** `develop`**:** these numbers are from before #1427 merged.

The probe, offline reproduction and raw results are on Stuart's MacBook Pro, in the side-session notes folder `local_3382f4d3-3435-45fd-9f36-eb2ccf2bd99e/fold-probe`.

**Update for Peter: the product side of this has moved, and the proposal itself hasn't changed.** [#1431](https://github.com/Secuura/platform-s/pull/1431) merged to `develop` as `87b0c0b`, with PS-1594 to PS-1597 and part of PS-1485. Nothing under `systemTest/` changed.

**What that does to "what goes red when it lands":** Identity, Stripe products, Organisation users and Delete person should now pass, so the proposed style may turn nothing red. That's inferred from xUnit and a static-page axe check. The numbers on this ticket are still from `216ad3f`, and #1431 had no full systemTest run, so re-measure on current `develop` before relying on it.

title: Kintsugi renders FRONTEND_URL as localhost:6882 for m365-integration, kyc and api-gateway, so the M365 connect redirect goes to localhost
description:
**BLUF:** Read, not run by me: on the Kintsugi box, the compose render of the running stack gives `FRONTEND_URL=http://localhost:6882` to api-gateway, kyc and m365-integration, and `FRONTEND_URL=https://kintsugi.secuura.net` to auth. m365-integration builds its browser redirects from that value, so, by reading the code, a person who finishes or fails the M365 connect on Kintsugi would be sent to localhost, which is their own machine. A different value is not a defect by itself; this ticket records the read, and what the right target is stays the owner's. Low. Evidence class: the box value is Seat D 59th's READ-ONLY box read (a `docker compose config` render filtered to four names); the code lines are READ ONLY by me at origin develop `a6cd828e820d`; I ran nothing and made no box contact.

**The box read**, recorded by Seat D 59th in `/Volumes/DevMASTER/!CODING/Secuura/Blockchain/5_Project_History/2026-11-06_seatD-59th/evidence/kintsugi/i0_composeread.txt` (host `secuura02-kintsugi-vm`, 2026-11-06T10:13:25Z, labelled BEFORE_RSYNC, that is before its deploy round; compose project `dev` from the box's `docker-compose.yml` and `docker-compose.override.yml`):

* Rendered `FRONTEND_URL=http://localhost:6882` for 3 services (api-gateway, kyc, m365-integration) and `FRONTEND_URL=https://kintsugi.secuura.net` for 1 (auth).
* `GATEWAY_PORT` and `WEBSITE_PORT` are held by no service's rendered environment and by no line of the box's `.env` (counts 0). The published ports render as nginx-gateway 6882 and website-frontend 6881.
* By name only, with no value read: the box's `.env` holds one `FRONTEND_URL` line, and so does `.env.local` (`/Volumes/DevMASTER/!CODING/Secuura/Blockchain/5_Project_History/2026-11-06_seatD-59th/evidence/kintsugi/i0_extra2.txt`, 2026-11-06T10:18:53Z). Wednesday reads the localhost value as coming from the env_file `.env.local`; the record itself does not name the source.

**The code**, in `Blockchain/Dev/services/m365-integration/src/index.ts` at origin develop `a6cd828e820d69b7a48f9d28d54023bc1a628437` (read 2026-11-06 by Seat S 32nd through the GitHub contents API at that sha):

* Lines 631, 635, 649, 682 and 689: five `res.redirect` calls to `${process.env.FRONTEND_URL || 'http://localhost:6882'}/admin/integrations?...`, for a provider error, a missing code or state, an invalid state, success and a failed token exchange. So the success path as well as every failure path leaves the browser at that host.
* Line 655: the redirect URI used for the token exchange is `process.env.ENTRA_REDIRECT_URI` or, when that is unset, `FRONTEND_URL` plus `/api/m365/callback`; line 1136 defaults a redirect URI to `http://localhost:6882/api/m365/callback`. Whether `ENTRA_REDIRECT_URI` is set on the box is unread.
* Line 1466: the Adaptive-Card link uses `VERIFIER_URL`, then `FRONTEND_URL`, then the localhost default (KS-349, closed, introduced `VERIFIER_URL`).

**Not established:** the source of the box value; whether `ENTRA_REDIRECT_URI` is set on the box; kyc's and api-gateway's own uses of `FRONTEND_URL` (unread); whether the M365 connect has ever been exercised on Kintsugi; what the redirect target ought to be. On the old Container Apps demo KS-344 set it to the admin host. Separately, `/admin/integrations` is not a route the admin app declares (KS-1641, KS-1744), so a correct host alone would not land the person on a working page.

**Related, not duplicates:** KS-344 (Done; the same symptom on the old Container Apps demo, fixed in bicep; those apps are deleted and the VM's own `.env` is the authority, as KS-1355's comment a65f302b records); KS-1381 (In Progress; the code fallbacks to `:6882`, the compose `ENTRA_REDIRECT_URI` default and bootstrap's `FRONTEND_URL` on local slot-N stacks, and it does not name Kintsugi); KS-1355 (In Review; its comment a65f302b says no record names any box's `FRONTEND_URL` value, and this read is one such record, left for that ticket's owner); KS-1744 and KS-1641 (the redirect path); KS-1670 (reflection sites); KS-1617 (auth: an unset `FRONTEND_URL` outside local should fail loudly).

**For the owner to decide:** what `FRONTEND_URL` should be for m365-integration, kyc and api-gateway on Kintsugi, and whether m365 should refuse to start without it (the fix shape KS-1381 names).

**Source:** Wednesday's ADDENDUM of 2026-11-06T10:25:24Z, from Seat D 59th's read. Nothing about the demo box is claimed; the demo is frozen and was not read.

**Board search before filing** (2026-11-06, Seat S 32nd, board_search tool, both controls held: the term msgpackr hit KS-1379 among open tickets and a random token hit 0; includeArchived; open candidates checked on title, description and all comments): `FRONTEND_URL` 100 candidates, 6 open hits (KS-485, KS-772, KS-1081, KS-1355, KS-1381, KS-1617) and 6 closed (KS-241, KS-344, KS-349, KS-1096, KS-1558, KS-1641); `localhost:6882` 124 candidates, 15 open hits and 81 closed; `/admin/integrations` 93 candidates, 3 open hits (KS-772, KS-1670, KS-1744) and 6 closed; `m365` with `redirect` 137 candidates, 16 open hits; `env_file` 103 candidates, 2 open hits (KS-668, KS-972); `OAuth callback` with `redirect` 84 candidates, 5 open hits. Read whole: KS-1381, KS-1744 and KS-344. Read for their FRONTEND_URL and Kintsugi lines: KS-1641, KS-1670, KS-1355, KS-1617 and KS-1081. None records the Kintsugi box value.

title: OpenAPI examples after PR 782: five checks KS-256 left unchecked, and a LoginRequest example that locks its own account
description:
**BLUF:** Kam has ruled that KS-256 closes and that its five unchecked items and one lockout finding move to one new ticket on the board account: his card `secuura-ks256-sign-off-or-split-1106` reads status ruled, choice a, "Close it; the five items and the lockout go to one new ticket on our account (recommended)", ruled_ts 2026-11-06T21:04:32+11:00. This is that ticket. PR 782 (squash `a9b63bbd71c8`, merged 2026-09-02T07:23:23Z) delivered the inline examples; the five boxes below were unchecked in KS-256's description when I read it on 2026-11-06, none was re-measured by me, and the lockout comes from a sweep comment of 2026-09-14. This ticket holds them and claims none of them done. Priority High, KS-256's own (priority 2, read at source), carried with the work. Evidence class: READ ONLY of KS-256's description and comments, and of the PRs through the GitHub API; nothing was run.

**The six items**, as KS-256 states them (its description and comments, read 2026-11-06):

1. **Every published example is runnable**: no volatile ids, no `null` standing in for a value. KS-256 says this is no longer gated, because KS-481 is Done and archived (2026-08-12, PR 603) and the branch carried the seeded canonical document it added; "remaining gap is the long tail, not the blocker".
2. **Schemathesis and Akto pre-merge suites run and green.** The box is unchecked. I read nothing in KS-256 that records such a run for the merged tree.

KS-256's comment 8c499846 (2026-11-03T22:59:12Z) carries a deploy record from 2026-11-01 that the tree deployed to Kintsugi at `b1fb543640e7`, marked there as carried and not re-measured. Nothing here says either target carries the examples; the demo is frozen.
4. **Triage the 26 x 400**, the API rejecting examples the spec publishes. The line, as corrected by the 2026-08-19 review §4: 5 strictly example-fixable (4 placeholders that violate a documented constraint, and 1 example that pins two mutually exclusive fields, `transfer-custody` sending both `newHolderId` and `newHolderEmail`), or 8 if parameter examples count; the rest are not example-fixable (6 `onBehalfOf` connector-only, 2 `TENANT_REQUIRED` persona config, 3 state-dependent). The five example-fixable 400s already have a home, section 1 of KS-665 (In Progress, board account); they are not re-filed here. The other parts of this item are not in KS-665.
5. **The verify-spec-examples check is non-deterministic** (2/6/6/10 across four cassettes, as KS-256 states it) and ships ADVISORY. KS-256's line: it needs an accumulated evidence model before it can gate anything.
6. **The LoginRequest example locks its own account on every sweep.** The spec's inline example for `POST /api/auth/login` (`demo.issuer@example.com` with a placeholder password) is sent about 34 times per run by the examples and coverage phase; the first five consecutive 401s trip the F-06 lockout (5 failures per email and /24, a 15-minute lock). The comment's evidence: auth log "lockout: threshold reached ... count 5", HAR entries 656 to 660 on the run `pre-merge-2026-09-14T12-56-17Z-slot3`, reproduced on every run since; slot 3, from-scratch stack, develop `64c386e04`. It calls the effect harmless (no such account) but five guaranteed failures charged to one key per sweep, and names two options: an RFC 2606 `.invalid` address in the example, or keep it and note it, since it is the one thing in the sweep that exercises the lockout. Source: KS-256's comment a4940bab (2026-09-14T15:33:46). KS-665's comment 9b21b836 points to it. Not re-measured by me.

**NOT measured by me:** any of the six at runtime or on current develop; whether the five example-fixable 400s are still published (KS-665's counts were taken at an older head, and its comment 83cb4cf6 of 2026-09-21 reports the examples-phase 400 set unchanged by a Schemathesis upgrade); the lockout today.
