PR 568 was closed unmerged; PR 314 (the earlier report change) merged 2026-06-23. KS-256 has no children. Related: KS-256 (closing), KS-665, KS-481, KS-678, KS-188.

title: transfer: the JavaScript SDK and the e2e specs post initiate and approve bodies the transfer validator refuses with 400
description:
**BLUF:** The JavaScript SDK's `transfers.initiate()` and `transfers.approve()`, and the e2e specs that call the transfer doors, send bodies that the transfer service's validators refuse, so those calls answer 400 today. They were already failing before PR 2048 (KS-2038): gate 229's callers table reads 400 at the base and 400 at the head, so this is not a regression of that PR. Low. One coupling matters for whoever fixes it: PR 2048's code comment relies on the SDK's refusal body still reading 400, and fixing the callers alone would turn the SDK's reject into an approval (KS-2082). Evidence class: READ ONLY by me at origin develop `a6cd828e820d` (callers and validators); the 400s are gate 229's table, which I did not re-run, and I ran nothing.

**Where**, at origin develop `a6cd828e820d69b7a48f9d28d54023bc1a628437` (read 2026-11-06 by Seat S 32nd through the GitHub contents API at that sha):

* The validators, `Blockchain/Dev/services/transfer/src/index.ts`. Lines 373 to 402: `initiateTransferSchema` requires `documentId`, `transferType` (simple, sale, inheritance or corporate), `currentOwnerId` and `newOwnerId` (both guids), `documentHash` (64 hex characters), `documentTitle` and `documentType`. Lines 404 to 415: `approveTransferSchema` requires `approverId` (a guid) and `approverRole`. `POST /api/transfers` and `POST /api/transfers/initiate` are the same handler (lines 604 and 605).
* The SDK, `Blockchain/Dev/sdk/javascript/src/modules/transfers.ts`. Lines 53 to 59 and 87 to 89: `initiate` posts `documentId`, `toUserId` and the optional `reason`, `requiresApproval` and `workflowType` to `/api/transfers/initiate`; it sends none of `transferType`, `currentOwnerId`, `newOwnerId`, `documentHash`, `documentTitle` or `documentType`. Lines 113 to 125: `approve` posts `{ action, comment?, signature? }` to `/api/transfers/:id/approve`; it sends no `approverId` and no `approverRole`.
* The e2e specs, all under `Blockchain/Dev/tests/e2e/tests/`: `api/transfer.api.spec.ts` lines 15 to 21 initiate with `fromUserId`, `toUserId`, `reason` and `requiresApproval` and expect ok (line 28); lines 104 to 110 and 121 to 127 post `{ action: 'approve', signature }` and `{ action: 'reject', reason }` to the approve door and expect ok and `rejected`. `integration/full-certification-flow.api.spec.ts` lines 123 to 127 initiate with `toUserId`; lines 145 to 148 and 161 to 164 post `action: 'approve'` and `action: 'accept'`. `Blockchain/Dev/tests/e2e/tests/full-stakeholder-browser.spec.ts` lines 793 to 800 and `Blockchain/Dev/tests/e2e/tests/local-platform-smoke.spec.ts` lines 318 to 325 post `fromUserId` and `toUserId` to `/api/transfers`.

**Gate 229's callers table** (its Question 5; 400 at base and head for each of these): SDK `initiate` and the two initiate specs with `toUserId`; SDK `approve` and the e2e approve and accept calls with no approver id; the e2e reject-through-approve call with no approver id, which also skips because no transfer is created. The two specs that post `fromUserId` assert only "under 500", so they still pass at 400. SDK `cancel` is the only call that newly fails after PR 2048, and by the ruling.

**The coupling, with KS-2082:** `Blockchain/Dev/services/transfer/src/index.ts` line 711 is a PR 2048 comment: `approverId` stays required so that a body that names nobody, "such as the SDK's { action: 'reject' }", keeps its 400 and is never read as an approval. KS-2082 records that a body that does carry `approverId` and `action: 'reject'` is recorded as an approval. So a fix on the caller side that adds `approverId` to the SDK's `approve()` would, with KS-2082 open, make `approve(id, 'reject')` approve. KS-2049 also bears on the initiate side: it records that the handler takes both parties from the body, and what `currentOwnerId` must be is its question.

**For the owner to decide:** change the callers to the shape the validators require, or change the validators and the published contract to accept what the SDK and the specs send; which, and in which order relative to KS-2082 and KS-2049, is the owner's call.

**NOT measured:** by me, any of the 400s at runtime; a gateway path; whether any real integration uses the SDK's transfer module. PR 2048 merged 2026-11-06T09:30:58Z as squash `bdbb11b21585`; a squash on develop is not a deploy and I have read nothing about a deploy of it.

**Source:** Seat W 29th's filing candidate "the SDK and e2e send a body the validator refuses" (its HANDOVER of 2026-11-06, lines 8 and 41), which Wednesday ruled to file Low naming gate 229's callers table: `/Volumes/DevMASTER/WEDNESDAY/0_Brain/reference/2026-11-06_gate229-tier1-pr2048-ks2038/verdict.md` (a coordinator-local file), Question 5. Related: KS-2038 (hands-off), KS-2049, KS-2082.

**Board search before filing** (2026-11-06, Seat S 32nd, board_search tool, both controls held: the term msgpackr hit KS-1379 among open tickets and a random token hit 0; includeArchived; open candidates checked on title, description and all comments): `toUserId` 1 candidate, 0 hits; `fromUserId` 0 candidates; `validator refuses` 87 candidates, 0 hits; `SDK` with `transfer` and `initiate` 53 candidates, 2 open hits (KS-485 and KS-772, review streams, not this); `approverId` 4 candidates, 3 open hits (KS-1697, KS-2038, KS-2052) and 1 closed (KS-498); `full-certification-flow` 100 candidates, 2 open hits (KS-1631, KS-1697) and 1 closed (KS-318); `TransferInitiateSchema` 0 candidates. Read whole: KS-2038 and KS-2049. KS-1631 (e2e callers of a retired verify route) and KS-2052 (the workflows approve door) were judged by title and are different doors.

nodes.body:
**BLUF:** Three points to add to this ticket, from Seat T 18th's read of develop `6c9a593df4ab`, which the board seat re-read at that sha: the SDK has no way to reject that can succeed, the SDK's `accept` action matches nothing in the service, and the service comment this ticket cites at line 711 is now at line 721. The schema and SDK lines this ticket cites are unchanged.

* The schema: `approveTransferSchema` is at lines 404 to 415 of `Blockchain/Dev/services/transfer/src/index.ts` and is parsed at line 711. It requires `approverId` (a guid) and `approverRole` and declares no `action` key. The SDK's `approve()` (`Blockchain/Dev/sdk/javascript/src/modules/transfers.ts`, lines 113 to 122) posts `{ action, comment, signature }` and sends neither required field, so every SDK approve answers 400 (READ ONLY; the 400 is this ticket's gate 229 table).
* No SDK reject: the module has no reject method. `approve(id, 'reject')` is the only way the SDK can reject (the type at line 115 allows `'approve' | 'reject' | 'accept'`). The service's reject door is a separate route, `POST /api/transfers/:id/reject` (line 794 of the service file), which the SDK never calls.
* `accept`: no quoted `accept` string appears anywhere in `Blockchain/Dev/services/transfer/src/index.ts` (a search for its quoted forms returns 0 matches), though the SDK's type allows it.
* The service comment at line 721 reads: "It stays required so a body that names nobody, such as the SDK's { action: 'reject' }, keeps its 400 and is never read as an approval." So the 400 on the SDK's reject body is relied on, as this ticket's paragraph on the coupling with KS-2082 says.

Evidence class: READ ONLY (the board seat, at develop `6c9a593df4ab`; Seat T 18th's read agrees). Nothing was run. Related: KS-2082 (a body that carries `approverId` and `action: 'reject'` is recorded as an approval) and KS-2117 (the SDK README; not commented on here).

Priority: raised from Low to Medium today, on Wednesday's ruling: a client-facing SDK method that cannot succeed (every approve answers 400) and an SDK with no reject path.

title: transfer after PR 2048: no cell pins the executor reject row, the restart proof has no assertion, the cancel summary disagrees
description:
**BLUF:** Three Low items from gate 229 on PR 2048 (KS-2038), none of them a wrong behaviour of the shipped rule: (F6) tampers that remove the executor from the reject row on simple, sale and corporate transfers turn no test cell red, although the spec publishes that clause; (F7) the committed tests stub the authenticator and run with no database, and the one restart proof is an uncommitted tool with no assertion in it, so it cannot go red; (F9) the published cancel summary says "before execution" while the description and the code say draft or pending approval. One ticket for the three, as three items. Low. Evidence class: MEASURED AT RUNTIME by gate 229 for F6 (its own tampers); READ ONLY by me for F7's assertion count and F9's lines, at origin develop `a6cd828e820d`, nothing was run by me.

**Item 1, F6: test gaps found by the gate's own tampers** (the gate's record is `evidence/q6/tampers.out` in its folder beside the verdict):

* Survived, and the gate says they matter: G1, G2 and G3 remove the executor from the reject row on simple, sale and corporate transfers: 0 red cells. The spec publishes the clause ("the executor where one is named") and nothing pins it. Seat W 29th had noted this debt. The gate's probes show the current behaviour is right.
* Survived, lower value: G6 (a hex-only case fold), G7 (the fold trims) and G10 (the caller id is trimmed).
* Caught: G4, but only by one unit cell, so no door cell exercises a non-uuid principal and the HTTP test file contains 0 mentions of a connector (the same gap KS-2081 needs a regression cell for); G5, G8 and G9.
* Not counted: G11 was the gate's own mistake (it only reorders a list, an equivalent mutant). Seat W 29th's own set: the gate re-ran 3 sampled tampers, all red in the cells named; W's record reads 61 of 61 with bytes restored.

**Item 2, F7: what the committed proofs leave unproven**

* Seat W 29th's HTTP cells stub the authenticator and run with no database. The gate ran the real authenticator itself; the committed tests still leave unproven the persistence of the recorded actor, a restart, the `ON CONFLICT` upsert and the real token path.
* The restart proof is a tool, not a committed test: `/Volumes/DevMASTER/!CODING/Secuura/Blockchain/5_Project_History/2026-11-06_seatW-29th/tools/restart_proof_w29.test.ts` (sha256 957e3c6386b9b162378908e9ded26f48a3fe7fb7f80fc8687f75ddd26af0e0ac). I counted its assertions myself: 0 occurrences each of `expect`, `assert`, `toBe`, `toEqual` and `toThrow` in its 130 lines, against 2 `it(` calls and 1 `writeFileSync` as the control that the pattern can match. It records rows, so vitest exits 0 whatever they say; the gate read the rows by eye and found them in agreement with the PR body and the code. The gate also notes it stubs the authenticator by a header. The gate notes its schema source is named (docker/init plus migrations); I did not check that.

**Item 3, F9: published text disagrees with itself on cancel**

* `Blockchain/Dev/services/transfer/src/transfer.openapi.ts` line 1095: summary "Cancel a transfer (initiator only, before execution)". Lines 1097 to 1099: description "Who may cancel: the initiator, while the transfer is a draft or pending approval."
* `Blockchain/Dev/services/transfer/src/index.ts` line 935 refuses unless the status is `draft` or `pending_approval`, so an approved transfer, which is still before execution, cannot be cancelled. The description is the true one (the gate's reading, and mine at that sha).

**For the owner to decide:** the gate lists the items, not the shape: add door cells for the executor reject row and for a non-uuid principal; give the restart proof an assertion or turn it into a committed test against a real database; align the cancel summary with its description. The split into separate tickets, if wanted, is the owner's.

**NOT measured:** by me, anything at runtime; the tool was not re-run; a gateway path; Node LTS (gate 229 F10 records that every run, W's and the gate's, was on a non-LTS Node). PR 2048 merged 2026-11-06T09:30:58Z as squash `bdbb11b21585`; a squash on develop is not a deploy and I have read nothing about a deploy of it.

**Source:** gate 229 verdict, findings F6, F7 and F9: `/Volumes/DevMASTER/WEDNESDAY/0_Brain/reference/2026-11-06_gate229-tier1-pr2048-ks2038/verdict.md` (a coordinator-local file). Related: KS-2038 (hands-off), KS-2081 (F1), KS-2082 (F4), KS-2054 and KS-2055 (other transfer defects, not these).

**Board search before filing** (2026-11-06, Seat S 32nd, board_search tool, both controls held: the term msgpackr hit KS-1379 among open tickets and a random token hit 0; includeArchived; open candidates checked on title, description and all comments): `restart_proof_w29` 100 candidates, 0 hits; `restart proof` 100 candidates, 1 open literal hit (KS-2038), 0 closed; the transfer service's openapi file name (searched as the bare name) 86 candidates, 2 open hits (KS-256, KS-2054) and 1 closed (KS-481); `before execution` 100 candidates, 1 open hit (KS-2054, about payment verification); `executor` with `reject` 13 candidates, 2 open hits (KS-441, KS-2038) and 2 closed (KS-1185, KS-1271); `tampers` with `transfer` 106 candidates, 1 open hit (KS-485) and 2 closed (KS-1215, KS-1267). Read whole: KS-2038 and KS-2054; KS-256, KS-441 and KS-485 were judged by title. No ticket records any of the three items.

title: admin: the platform audit log page has no way to show the partial marker KS-1545 adds to the response, and depends on that PR

title: Security: a role change at PATCH /api/users/admin/:id leaves a person's sessions alive, so the old token keeps the old role until it expires
description:
**BLUF:** When an administrator changes a person's role at `PATCH /api/users/admin/:id`, the person's sessions stay alive, so the token minted under the old role keeps working, with the old role, until it expires. The handler ends a user's sessions only when the new status forbids a credential, never for a role-only change. Seat Y 6th measured the walk-around this opens: a demoted org admin uses the old token to raise a second account to org admin, and that second account then passes the live-row check built for KS-2063. High, the same priority as KS-2063 (priority 2, read at source 2026-11-06 about 21:12 AEDT). Kam has ruled that it be built: his card `secuura-ks2063-add-session-end-on-role-change-1106` reads status ruled, choice a, "Both", ruled_ts 2026-11-06T21:04:39+11:00, and its option detail reads "live-row check as ruled, plus session end as its own small PR (recommended):Y's recommendation and mine. A new ticket, red-first cells, tier-1 gate, Kintsugi only." This is that new ticket. Evidence class: MEASURED by Seat Y 6th (two separate probes, no real stack, as recorded on KS-2063 and on the card); the handler lines READ ONLY by me at origin develop `a6cd828e820d`, nothing run by me.

**Where**, at origin develop `a6cd828e820d69b7a48f9d28d54023bc1a628437` (read 2026-11-06 by Seat S 32nd through the GitHub contents API at that sha), all in `Blockchain/Dev/services/auth/src/routes/users.ts`:

* Line 693: `userRoutes.patch('/admin/:id', authenticate(), ...)`, the route commented at line 691 as "Admin: update a user (role, status, etc.)".
* Line 813: the write, `userRepo.updateUserPlatformScope(id, safeUpdates)`. Nothing between it and the response touches sessions except the block below.
* Lines 838 to 841: `if (accountStatusForbidsCredential(updatedUser))` calls `revokeAllUserSessions(id)` and logs "Admin status change revoked active sessions". The comment above it (lines 819 to 837) records that KS-360 added the revoke for suspend and deactivate, and that KS-796 derived the condition from the credential doors' status allow-list. A role-only change makes the condition false, so no session is revoked.

**Measured by Seat Y 6th** (KS-2063's description and its comment 6642212f; the card's BLUF carries the same):

* A role-only demotion leaves the session alive. Through the gateway the old token still works until it expires (1 hour by the code default, 1 day by the compose default; the real value on a box is unread).
* On the key routes, 4 of the 8 non-live shapes still reach them through the gateway while the session store is up: the role-only demotions. The deleted and suspended shapes changed through the same `PATCH` end the session first, so the gateway answers 401 and forwards nothing. While the gateway cannot reach the store it forwards anyway. Measured as two separate hops with an in-process stand-in for the store: no real Redis, no box, no real login.
* The card reports that ending sessions on a role change stopped the walk-around in the probe, adds no database read, and covers every route.

**What the session end does not close, as the card states it:** a Redis outage (the gateway forwards by design), a row edited by hand, and keys minted before the demotion. **Its cost, as the card states it:** anyone whose role changes, promotions included, is logged out at once.

**Asked for, by the card's option a:** the session end as its own small PR: red-first cells, tier 1 gate, Kintsugi only. Seat Y 6th builds it (Wednesday's ANSWER to Seat Y 6th, 2026-11-06T10:08:50Z); the change is one condition at the line 838 block plus cells, in the auth service only. The live-row check for KS-2063 is a separate build under that ticket.

**NOT measured:** a real demotion through `PATCH /api/users/admin/:id` against a real Redis or a box; the real token lifetime on any box; whether any user on a box holds a live token under a stale role. I read nothing about a deploy: the demo is frozen and nothing here has been built.

**Source:** KS-2063 (description and its comments 6642212f and b7eb928b); the card named above; Seat Y 6th's plan mail to Wednesday of 2026-11-06T10:08:06Z, which gives this ticket's title. Related: KS-2063 (the live-row check; this ticket is its sibling), KS-2032, KS-360 (closed; the original suspend and deactivate revoke), KS-1407 and KS-1692 (session handling in the same service, judged by title).

**Board search before filing** (2026-11-06, Seat S 32nd, board_search tool, both controls held: the term msgpackr hit KS-1379 among open tickets and a random token hit 0; includeArchived; open candidates checked on title, description and all comments): `PATCH /api/users/admin` 90 candidates, 5 open hits (KS-485, KS-591, KS-1017, KS-1364, KS-2063) and 8 closed; `role change` 100 candidates, 1 open hit (KS-2063) and 3 closed; `role-only` 100 candidates, 1 open hit (KS-2063) and 2 closed; `session end` 100 candidates, 1 open hit (KS-2063), 0 closed; `keeps the old role`, `sessions alive` and `ends the session` 100 candidates each, 0 hits; `revokeAllUserSessions` 9 candidates, 5 open hits (KS-1407, KS-1690, KS-1691, KS-1692, KS-1969) and 3 closed (KS-360, KS-570, KS-1967). Read whole: KS-2063. None of the others records a session end on a role change; KS-1407, KS-1692 and KS-360 were judged by title.

title: transfer: an approve body carrying action reject is recorded as an approval, because the schema drops the action key
description:
**BLUF:** `POST /api/transfers/:id/approve` records an approval for a body that says it is a refusal. A named approver who sends their own id with `action: 'reject'` gets 200, `fullyApproved: true` and 0 rejections; `decision: 'rejected'` does the same; a sale owner who sends `action: 'reject'` with `comment: 'I refuse'` gets an approval that carries the comment "I refuse". Medium severity, low likelihood (the gate's grade), and pre-existing: the result is the same at the base and at PR 2048's head. Evidence class: MEASURED AT RUNTIME by gate 229 (same result at base and head); the code lines were READ ONLY by me at origin develop `a6cd828e820d`, nothing was run by me.

**Where**, at origin develop `a6cd828e820d69b7a48f9d28d54023bc1a628437` (read 2026-11-06 by Seat S 32nd through the GitHub contents API at that sha), all in `Blockchain/Dev/services/transfer/src/index.ts`:

* Lines 404 to 415: `approveTransferSchema` is a non-strict `z.object` with `approverId`, `approverRole`, `reason`, `signature`, `walletAddress` and `comment`. It declares no `action` and no `decision`, so zod drops them. The schema's own comment at lines 407 to 410 says that zod's non-strict objects silently drop unknown keys.
* Line 701 parses the body with that schema. Lines 726 to 735 build the approval from the signed-in caller plus `data.signature`, `data.walletAddress` and `data.comment`. Nothing in the handler reads a refusal word.
* The gate read the published request as permitting the extra key (`additionalProperties: {}`); I did not re-read the yaml.
* Line 711 is a code comment from PR 2048: `approverId` stays required so that a body that names nobody, "such as the SDK's { action: 'reject' }", keeps its 400 and is never read as an approval. The hole is the case where `approverId` is present.

**Who could hit it, as the gate read it:** no real caller today, because the SDK and the e2e specs send no approver id and read 400 (gate 229, Question 5). The refusal shape is advertised, though: the gateway's `/api` text says "Approve/reject transfer" (`Blockchain/Dev/services/api-gateway/src/index.ts:851`, the gate's citation, not re-read by me); the SDK comment at `Blockchain/Dev/sdk/javascript/src/modules/transfers.ts:111` reads "Approve or reject a transfer" and its `approve()` takes `'approve' | 'reject' | 'accept'` (lines 113 to 125, read by me); and `Blockchain/Dev/tests/e2e/tests/api/transfer.api.spec.ts` lines 118 to 132 post `action: 'reject'` to the approve door and expect `status` `rejected` (read by me).

**Why it matters, as the gate put it:** a silent inversion, and on a simple transfer the owner's reject is then gone (the owner's right to reject ends once the recipient has approved, which reads 400).

**For the owner to decide:** the gate's fix-shape is to refuse any `action` other than approve. Declaring the key on the schema or making the schema strict are the other shapes visible in the code; which one, and what the reject path at the approve door should do, is the owner's call.

**NOT measured:** by me, anything at runtime; a gateway path; a real database. PR 2048 merged 2026-11-06T09:30:58Z as squash `bdbb11b21585`; a squash on develop is not a deploy and I have read nothing about a deploy of it.

**Source:** gate 229 verdict, finding F4: `/Volumes/DevMASTER/WEDNESDAY/0_Brain/reference/2026-11-06_gate229-tier1-pr2048-ks2038/verdict.md` (a coordinator-local file). Related: KS-2038 (the PR's ticket, hands-off), KS-2043 (the reject door drops a valid signature, a different door).

**Board search before filing** (2026-11-06, Seat S 32nd, board_search tool, both controls held: the term msgpackr hit KS-1379 among open tickets and a random token hit 0; includeArchived; open candidates checked on title, description and all comments): `fullyApproved` 2 candidates, 1 open literal hit (KS-1697, a transferee read, not this), 0 closed; `action: 'reject'` 100 candidates, 0 hits; `recorded as an approval` 100 candidates, 0 hits; `approve` with `reject` and `action` 120 candidates, 9 open hits (KS-188, KS-412, KS-485, KS-525, KS-663, KS-1017, KS-1087, KS-1235, KS-1327) and 7 closed (KS-202, KS-467, KS-518, KS-566, KS-955, KS-1270, KS-1354), none about the action key; `transfer/src/index.ts` 100 candidates, 9 open hits (KS-1697, KS-1703, KS-2038, KS-2043, KS-2044, KS-2049, KS-2050, KS-2054, KS-2055) and 3 closed (KS-274, KS-1435, KS-1881); `Approve/reject transfer` 100 candidates, 0 hits. Read whole: KS-2038, KS-2043, KS-2049, KS-2054, KS-2055; none describes the action key. KS-518 (closed) is the ticket the schema comment at lines 407 to 410 cites for declaring `reason`; I judged it by that comment and its title, not read whole.

title: launcher census, gate 224 notes on PR 2045: non-shell lifecycle calls, missed shapes, a partial port list passes, no down cell, no Linux run
description:
**BLUF:** The five notes of the tier-2 gate (gate 224) on PR 2045 (KS-1558), which merged as cd773edc2bb8 on 2026-11-06. GO WITH NOTES at head 816bafd9007e. None is a defect today: the guard and the checker are correct at that sha. Filed so the notes have a ticket before KS-1558 is closed, on Wednesday's ruling of 2026-11-06 09:11Z. Low. One file family, one test pass.

Verdict: `/Volumes/DevMASTER/WEDNESDAY/0_Brain/reference/2026-11-06_gate224-tier2-pr2045-ks1558/verdict.md`, with its evidence folder beside it. Files: `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/check-stack-safety.sh`, `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/check-compose-stack-safety.mjs`, `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/__tests__/ks1355_slot_blind_launchers.test.sh`.

### F1 (Minor, pre-existing, outside PR 2045): the census reads shell files only

Lifecycle calls in `Blockchain/Dev/package.json` (lines 12, 15, 20, 21 and 23: up, down, and `down -v --rmi local`; lines 26 and 27: prod up and down), `Blockchain/Dev/Makefile` line 8 (`COMPOSE := docker compose`) and `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/openapi-examples/orchestrate.ts` (lines 64 and 415: the project pinned to the literal `distributed_secuura`, then a restart of api-gateway) are invisible to a census that lists tracked shell files. A slot-N session that runs `npm run docker:down` or `docker:clean` acts on slot 1's compose project with the guard green. Read only; no script or stack was run. A pointer, not a home: the guard names KS-1381 (lines 135 and 137 of `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/check-stack-safety.sh`) as the ticket that extends the rule to env templates, and KS-1381 is about slot-1 URLs and env templates.

### F2 (Minor): shapes inside shell files that the census does not flag

Quiet for: a function wrapper; an array; a defaulted variable; two variables; a command-substitution assignment; a verb in quotes after a variable; two spaces or a tab between docker and compose; the verbs stop, kill, rm and start; a backslash then a newline then `compose up`. New in this PR: the continuation join in the awk program joins with no space, so a continuation with no space before the backslash becomes `...a.ymlup -d` and is missed (cosmetic in practice, real continuations nearly always have the space). A heredoc body line `docker compose up` after `cat <<X` is flagged (a pre-existing false positive). No instance in the real tree today. Fix shape: join with one space, and add a cell for a continuation with no space before the backslash.

### F3 (Minor): a partial port list still passes

The real `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/stack_env.sh` yields 12 ports and has 13 PORT_OFFSET lines, so the derivation is complete today. With the five cardano lines and the Ollama line written as `export NAME=$(( N + PORT_OFFSET ))`, the anchored regex drops those 6 ports and the real checker still printed `OK - 27 compose-level shared-stack invariants hold`, rc 0. The suite caught it only through the cardano cell; the Ollama port (11434) dropped with no cell reddening. Fix shape: compare the derived count with the count of PORT_OFFSET use lines and refuse (exit 2) on a mismatch, with a cell for an `export` or reordered line. The regex also rejects `PORT_OFFSET + 6090` and lowercase names without saying so.

### F4 (Note): the literal `down` verb has no fixture cell

Removing `down` from the literal regex only reddened exactly one cell, the real-tree cell, because a tracked script happens to need that verb today. No fixture cell carries a down, restart or run literal; a tree without such a script would not catch the removal.

### F5 (Note): not run on Linux

The awk program (in the guard and in `_LAUNCHER_AWK`) runs on ubuntu-latest under mawk; the gate ran macOS (BWK awk 20200816) only. Read, and nothing mawk-incompatible was found. Not run on Linux; no CI result read.

**Related:** KS-1558 (the ticket PR 2045 raised), KS-1355, KS-1381.

title: auth verification routes: with no DATABASE_URL a request answers a generic 500, and the routes and their 503 are not in the spec

A search found no spec file naming me/verification, so neither the routes nor the 503 are published.

**Ruling.** Wednesday, 2026-11-06 01:49Z: option (a), record it and leave it. Not taken: declaring memory-only mode unsupported for verification (a product change that makes the process-local map dead code in production), and publishing the three routes and their 503 in the auth spec (a spec change that moves the generated spec and the gateway's served paths).

title: Docs: the architecture reference sends /api/rewards to Staking, the gateway sends it to Referral; the dev-debug override has no staking port
description:
**BLUF:** Two statements from Seat C 36th, relayed by the coordinator and checked here in source at develop `35bcfa000b44`, show two places that disagree with the gateway and the compose file. The architecture reference sends `/api/rewards` to the Staking service, but the gateway sends it to the Referral service. And a comment in the compose file says a dev-debug override re-publishes the staking port, but that override has no staking lines. This seat read files through the GitHub API and ran nothing. Priority Low (4): documentation and comments only. Facts only, nothing is built.

## Item 1: the routing table in the architecture reference

* `Projects Documents/Secuura-Architecture-Reference.md` line 279, under the table headed "Path Pattern, Target Service, Auth Required": `/api/staking/*`, `/api/rewards/*`, `/api/pool/*` goes to "Staking (:4015)".
* `Blockchain/Dev/services/api-gateway/src/routes/proxy.ts` lines 1052 to 1055 say `/api/rewards` is intentionally not routed to staking: it is proxied to the referral service, and staking's own `/api/rewards` routes are gateway-shadowed by design. Lines 1090 to 1093 are the mount: `router.use('/api/rewards', authenticateToken(true), proxy('referral', ...))`.
* The same comment (lines 1047 to 1050) says the staking service mounts its routers at `/api/stake`, `/api/rewards` and `/api/tiers`, not `/api/staking`; lines 1057 to 1059 keep `/api/staking` as a shim that strips the prefix to `/api/stake`.

## Item 2: the compose comment and the dev-debug override

* `Blockchain/Dev/docker-compose.yml` lines 1055 to 1057, on the staking service: "Pen-test F-04: backend ports no longer published on host. Use `docker compose -f docker-compose.yml -f docker-compose.dev-debug.override.yml up -d` to re-enable for local debugging. Was: - "6015:4015"".
* `Blockchain/Dev/docker-compose.dev-debug.override.yml` has 44 lines and none names staking, 4015 or 6015. Control: the same read lists the override's nine service keys (`originate`, `prism`, `wallet-connector`, `auth`, `timestamping`, `anchoring`, `security`, `analytics`, `m365-integration`, lines 23 to 39); staking is not one of them. The override's own comment at line 18 says each host port is 6000 plus the service port minus 4000, which would be 6015 for staking. So the way the compose comment gives to re-enable staking's port does not do so.
* The architecture reference, same file as item 1, line 192, still lists 6015 as staking's external port in the table headed "Port (External)".
* The comment in `services/api-gateway/src/routes/proxy.ts` at lines 1054 and 1055, "Direct hits on the staking service port still work", holds on the compose network. From the host, by item 2, it does not, as read and not run.

## Noted while reading (not part of Seat C 36th's statement; one grep, not conclusive)

* The reference's row at line 280 reads `/api/referral/*` to Referral (:4016). `services/api-gateway/src/routes/proxy.ts` mounts `/api/referrals` at line 1080 (plural), and the grep for single-quoted `/api/referral` mounts found no singular one.
* Row 279 also lists `/api/pool/*`. The same grep of `services/api-gateway/src/routes/proxy.ts` found no `/api/pool` mount. Another file may mount it; this seat did not look.
* No other row of the table was checked.

## Timing note

The comment at `services/api-gateway/src/routes/proxy.ts` lines 1054 and 1055 goes stale if the change for KS-2071 lands (Seat C 36th's statement). It is not a defect on develop now.

## Not known

* Whether other rows of the routing table or the port tables drift. Nothing was run.

## Adjacent, not duplicates

* KS-296 (Done) fixed the dev-debug override's miswired ports for the port registry. KS-2071 is the staking routes ticket and belongs to another seat.

## Searched before filing (board, includeArchived)

Read-only, run 2026-11-06 with controls: a known term hit KS-1379 and a random token hit 0. Counts are candidates, open literal hits, closed or archived literal hits.

* `Secuura-Architecture-Reference` 100, 0, 0. `dev-debug.override` 100, 0, 2 (closed: KS-296, KS-713). `api/rewards` 100, 2, 5 (open: KS-485 and KS-1963, neither about this routing).

title: No notification service is defined in the stack: originate posts to one, then falls back to SMTP; the gateway keeps them in a Map
description:
**BLUF:** Two statements from Seat E 39th, relayed by the coordinator and checked here in source at develop `35bcfa000b44`, point at one gap: the stack defines no notification service. The originate notification client posts to `http://notification:3008/api/notifications` by default and falls back to direct SMTP; the gateway's notifications routes keep their data in a process-local `Map` under a comment that says it is backed by the notification service in production. Nobody has measured the runtime effect, and this seat ran nothing. Priority Low (4) for that reason. Facts only, nothing is built.

## Item 1: the originate client posts to a service the stack does not define

* `services/originate/src/utils/notificationClient.ts` line 19 to 20: the URL is `process.env.NOTIFICATION_SERVICE_URL` or the default `http://notification:3008/api/notifications`.
* Lines 28 to 33: the doc comment says it sends through the notification service and "falls back to direct SMTP if the notification service is unreachable". Line 35 is the `fetch` to that URL.
* Lines 44 and 60: on a non-OK reply and on an unreachable service the client logs a warning that it is falling back to SMTP. Lines 71 to 73: the fallback skips the notification with an INFO line, "SMTP not configured", when SMTP is not configured.
* So with the default URL and no service behind it, each send is expected to try the `fetch` first, log a warning, then use SMTP if it is configured or skip. That sequence is read from the source, not observed.

## Item 2: the stack defines no such service (read at the same sha)

* `Blockchain/Dev/docker-compose.yml` defines 44 services and none has "notif" in its key (control: `staking` is defined, line 1045). Its only mention of notifications is a comment at line 634 about SMTP.
* No other compose file in the tree names "notification" at all (the 14 other compose files in the tree were read for the word, case-insensitive: 0 hits), and none of the 16 files under `Blockchain/Dev/deployment/` with a bicep, shell, YAML or JSON extension names it (all 16 were read for the word; control: 13 of the 16 contain "container", "image" or "resource").
* The tree holds 27 service directories under `Blockchain/Dev/services/` and none starts with "notif".

## Item 3: the gateway's notifications routes are held in a process-local Map

* `services/api-gateway/src/routes/notifications.ts` line 69 is the comment "In-memory store (backed by notification service in production)", and line 72 is `const notifications = new Map<string, Notification[]>();`.
* The router declares six routes: list (line 115), unread count (162), mark one read (183), mark all read (212), delete (240) and create (270). This seat did not read the handlers. If they all use the `Map`, the data is per process and lost on restart; that is not measured.

## Not known

* Whether `NOTIFICATION_SERVICE_URL` is set in any deployed environment (Kintsugi, demo, staging). No compose file sets it; no environment was read.
* Whether any portal shows in-app notifications, and whether SMTP is configured in any deployed environment.
* What a send does at runtime with the default URL when the name `notification` does not resolve.
* A related datum, not interpreted here: KS-256 has a comment of 2026-08-18 that says "the notification service times out under load" for the client's 5000 ms `AbortSignal.timeout` and names it as the trigger of a gateway breaker tripping. It does not say whether a service was running or the host was unreachable.

## Open decision (not made here)

Build the service the client and the route comment assume, or remove the first attempt and state SMTP as the transport, or keep the route data in a store. This ticket does not choose.

## Adjacent, not duplicates

* KS-1937, KS-1964 and KS-2036 are about the recipient's email address written to logs by the originate client and the auth email path. A different defect.
* KS-1868 and KS-256 mention the notification service in passing and do not say it is absent.

## Searched before filing (board, includeArchived)

Read-only, run 2026-11-06 with controls: a known term hit KS-1379 and a random token hit 0. Counts are candidates, open literal hits, closed or archived literal hits.

* `NOTIFICATION_SERVICE_URL` 100, 0, 0. `notification:3008` 79, 0, 0. `backed by notification` 100, 0, 0. `notification service` 100, 3, 0 (KS-256, KS-1868, KS-1937; matched lines read). `notificationClient` 6, 4, 0 (KS-256, KS-1937, KS-1964, KS-2036).
* This is "not found by these searches", not proof of absence.

title: observability: npm run down exits 1 with no message when slot 1's redis container is absent, so the stack cannot be stopped
description:
**BLUF:** Peter appended this finding to KS-1388 on 2026-10-07 (comment `9e36fdd5-db2e-4467-94bb-42a548f84531`). It has no fix and no ticket of its own. In `observability/`, `npm run down` exits 1 with no error message while slot 1's Redis container is absent, and the observability stack keeps running. The runtime observation is Peter's, on his Mac; this seat ran nothing. This seat re-read the script at develop `35bcfa000b44`: the Redis password lookup runs at file scope before the action switch, under `set -euo pipefail`, with no guard. Priority Low (4). Facts only, nothing is built.

## What Peter observed (his comment, quoted in substance)

* Peter's Mac, 2026-10-07, observability started from the KS-1445 worktree. Slot 1 had been stopped by another session.
* `npm run down` ran `bash scripts/observability.sh down` and exited 1. All 9 `secuura-obs-*` containers were still up.
* `bash -x` showed the run stopping inside `resolve_redis_password`, called at file scope, after `docker inspect secuura-redis` found no container. The `down)` branch was never reached.
* Workaround he used, from `observability/`: `docker compose -f docker-compose.yml --profile phase2 down`. It removed all 9 containers and kept the 3 data volumes.

## What the source shows at develop `35bcfa000b44` (read through the GitHub API, not run)

File `observability/scripts/observability.sh`, 268 lines.

* Line 25: `set -euo pipefail`.
* Lines 132 to 149: `resolve_redis_password` runs `docker inspect "$container" --format '{{json .Config.Cmd}}' 2>/dev/null` into a Python filter. There is no `|| true` or other guard on that pipeline. With `pipefail`, a failing `docker inspect` makes the pipeline fail.
* Line 151: `_redis_pw="$(resolve_redis_password)"` is at file scope, before the action switch. Under `set -e` a failing assignment from a command substitution ends the script.
* Lines 257 to 260: the `down)` branch is only `docker compose ... --profile phase2 down`. It needs neither credential.
* The Postgres lookup differs from what Peter's comment says. His comment names both `secuura-redis` and `secuura-postgres`. At this sha `resolve_pg_dsn` (line 91, called at line 115) runs `docker exec` at line 100 and guards it with `|| creds=""` at line 101, so an absent Postgres container is guarded at that line. His trace stopped in the Redis function. Whether the Postgres path can also abort elsewhere in its function (lines 91 to 112) was not traced by this seat.

## Not known

* Whether current develop reproduces Peter's exit 1: his run was on the script at develop `b280b74ff`, and no one has re-run it since. The reading above is from the source only.
* Which Docker version or shell the exit status depends on.

## Fix direction (Peter's suggestion, quoted, not done)

"Resolve the platform credentials only for the actions that start containers (start / up / phase2), or make the lookups non-fatal for down / status / logs. Stopping the stack should never depend on the platform being up."

## Related

* KS-1388 holds the original comment and the slot-awareness record for `observability/`. It stays open; its priority is not changed by this ticket.

## Searched before filing (board, includeArchived)

Read-only, run 2026-11-06 with controls: a known term hit KS-1379, a random token hit 0, and the non-zero control `KS-1388` gave 3 candidates, 2 open literal hits, 1 closed. Counts are candidates, open literal hits, closed or archived literal hits.

* `npm run down` 100, 1, 0 (KS-1388). `resolve_redis_password` 89, 1, 0 (KS-1388). `resolve_pg_dsn` 100, 1, 0 (KS-1388). The script's file name, `observability/scripts/observability.sh` taken by its last path segment, 100, 4, 1 (open: KS-1381, KS-1388, KS-1550, KS-1558; closed: KS-200).
* The full text of KS-1550, KS-1558, KS-1381, KS-1415 and KS-1388 was read for `npm run down`, "exits 1", the script's file name, `secuura-redis` and `docker inspect`. Only KS-1388 states this finding: in Peter's appended comment, and in KS-1388's newest comment, which records that no commit after PR 1387 names it. The other four name the script only in lists of slot-1 scripts.
* This is "not found by these searches", not proof of absence.

title: security: a revoke or mint acknowledged while the database flag is down is never written (boot race write side, gate 225 on PR 2046)
description:
**BLUF:** Gate 225 (PR 2046, KS-1377) found that the write side of the security service has the same flaw PR 2046 fixed on the read side. While the database availability flag is down, a key revoke or a key mint is acknowledged to the caller, is never written to the database, and the key behaves wrongly after recovery. Facts only, no fix is built. Priority High on Wednesday's reading. PR 2046 merged on 2026-11-06 at 07:39:23Z as squash `35bcfa000b44`. This seat measured nothing at runtime; every runtime figure below is gate 225's, on a stubbed store.

## Source and what was checked here

* Gate 225 verdict: GO WITH NOTES at head `dadd6e3df78a`, PR 2046, KS-1377, tier 1, round 1 of 2. File: `0_Brain/reference/2026-11-06_gate225-tier1-pr2046-ks1377/verdict.md` in the coordinator's tree. The items below are quoted from it.
* This seat read the cited lines of `services/security/src/index.ts` at the merged sha `35bcfa000b44` through the GitHub API (read only, nothing run). They hold the code the verdict names: line 403 is the `!isDbAvailable()` branch in `saveKeyAndRetirePriors`, line 482 is `if (!isDbAvailable()) return;`, line 560 is `if (isDbAvailable()) {`, line 620 is `memApiKeys.clear();`, lines 2011 to 2014 are the row-gone branch, line 2023 reads `revokedInMemory`, line 2026 is `memApiKeys.set`, line 2055 is the second `memApiKeys.set`.
* One ticket with several items, because one test pass proves them (Kam, 2026-09-07 13:23, the standing ticket-creation line).

## Priority and class

* Wednesday's reading: High (Linear priority 2).
* The verdict's words for F1: "Major by class, low likelihood, NOT a regression (base identical)".
* The oracle the verdict names: Kam's card text "A revoked key is never honoured", and the KS-888 ruling as quoted at `services/security/src/index.ts` line 1680 (the source comment names card `secuura-ks888-revoke-validate-on-failed-save`, option a: a revoke whose save did not persist is not acknowledged; the verdict says it did not read that card itself, and neither did this seat).

## Item F1: a revoke acknowledged during a boot race is not stored, and the key answers valid:true after recovery

* Anchors: `services/security/src/index.ts` lines 482 (dbSaveApiKey returns at the flag), 560 (dbGetApiKey falls to memory), 620 (loadFromDb clears memory on recovery).
* Found: the save side still decides from the flag alone, the same flaw `databaseExpected()` removes from the read side.
* Measured by gate 225 at runtime, twice with equal results, real routes on a stubbed store and flag (`evidence/table_read.txt`, case S4 in the gate folder). Flag down, URL set, database reachable: validate answers valid:true and caches the key; DELETE /api/keys/:id answers 200 "API key revoked" with 0 writes and the stored row still active; validate answers "Key revoked" in this process; then with the flag up and loadFromDb run, validate answers valid:true.
* Control S4 with the flag up: 1 write, and "Key revoked" after the reload.
* Reachability, read only in the verdict: it needs a revoke in the window between the database coming up and the next retry probe (the backoff in the security service's database module, at most 30 s), on a key already cached in that window. An uncached key answers 404, which is visible. Other processes read the active row throughout.

## Item F2: a key minted during a boot race is issued and cannot be used

* Class in the verdict: Minor, pre-existing, its visible effect changes on head and the PR does not name it. Anchors: `services/security/src/index.ts` lines 403, 482 and 2011 to 2014.
* Measured by gate 225 at runtime on a stubbed store (case S5). Base: mint answers 201 with a key and 0 writes; validate in the race answers valid:true whether the read fails or the database is readable; after recovery "Key not found". Head: mint answers 201 with a key and 0 writes; validate in the race answers 503 when the read fails, and "Key not found" with the entry evicted when the database is readable; after recovery "Key not found".
* Oracle in the verdict: the KS-888 rule, as quoted in the header of the KS-888 failed-mint test in the security service (the card was not read), that a mint whose save did not persist is never acknowledged. Base loses the key at recovery, head loses it at first use.

## Item F4: no test pins a row that is gone during a boot race, nor an empty DATABASE_URL

* Class in the verdict: Minor, test gap. Anchors: `services/security/src/index.ts` lines 2011 to 2014 and 1954.
* Measured by gate 225 (`evidence/tampers.json`, `evidence/tampers_live_proof.json`): tamper G3 (row gone with the flag down answers valid:true from memory) survives the whole unit suite, 514 of 514. Tamper G1 (an empty URL counts as configured) also survives 514 of 514. Both tampers are live: the gate's table sees G3 in 2 cells and G1 in 9. Head's real behaviour is correct in both states; only the pin is missing.
* Regression cell owed (the verdict): boot race, cached key, no rows answers "Key not found" and evicts. G3 is the one that matters: a deleted key honoured in a boot race would pass every suite.

## Item N5: an in-flight validate undoes a KS-888 in-memory revoke

* Class in the verdict: Note, pre-existing, not touched by PR 2046. Anchors: `services/security/src/index.ts` line 2023 reads `revokedInMemory` from the object held before the await, and line 2026 overwrites memory.
* Measured by gate 225 at runtime, twice, base and head equal (case S7): a validate holds its read open; a revoke whose save fails answers 503 and memory reads revoked; the validate finishes valid:true and memory reads active; the next validate answers valid:true. The revoke caller was told it was not stored, so the harm is narrow.

## Item: saveKeyAndRetirePriors retires prior connector keys in memory only

* Anchor: `services/security/src/index.ts` line 403. Same family as F1.
* Read only. The gate read this function and did not drive it ("NOT tested ... saveKeyAndRetirePriors in a boot race"). Its behaviour in a boot race is unmeasured at runtime.

## Item F3 documentation half: a false sentence in the flow fragment

* Class in the verdict: Minor, documentation and ruling premise. The sentence "Only keys minted in this process can be cached during a boot race." sits in `Projects Documents/fragments/flow/KS-1377-validate-answers-503-in-a-boot-race-on-both-arms.html`, line 2, and is on develop at `35bcfa000b44` (read by this seat through the GitHub API). The verdict names two other places it appeared: the PR 2046 body ("Keys minted in this process during the race are the only cached ones") and the coordinator's ANSWER of 2026-11-06 01:24:12Z.
* It is false by gate 225's measurement: the cell (flag down, URL set, cache none, read active) reads the stored row, answers valid:true and leaves it cached (`cachedAfter: true`, `services/security/src/index.ts` line 2055). A key minted in the race has no row, so under the stated premise cells B2 and B3 (the verdict's names) could not happen; they can, through this path. The cached-key arm guards stored keys, including ones revoked elsewhere.
* No code change follows from this item. PR 2046 has merged, so the correction is a new change. Whoever builds this ticket corrects the sentence in the same change.

## Fix shape (a proposal quoted from the verdict, read only, not decided)

* F1: "refuse the revoke with the existing 503 when databaseExpected() is true and the flag is down, or attempt the save and classify the failure".
* F2: "refuse the mint in this state, as F1".
* N5: "read the current map entry after the await".
* Regression tests the verdict names: a revoke in this window is either stored or refused, and validate after loadFromDb is not valid:true; plus the F4 cell above.

## Not known and not tested (from gate 225's NOT tested list)

* No running stack, no real PostgreSQL or pgbouncer. F1, F2, N5 and every table result are on a stubbed store. The real-driver arms covered only a closed port and a silent listener.
* Still unproved: a real database coming up mid-race (the flag flip, loadFromDb under FORCE RLS, F1 and F2 on a real row), the read under the real application role during the window, pgbouncer's error shape and delay, the gateway and auth against a live security service.
* The verdict states a live sweep is owed before KS-1377 is Done, including a real start with postgres stopped and then started.
* Everything ran on Node v26.8.1, not an LTS line. Not run: the four platform suites, integration suites, any box, any deploy.

## Adjacent, not duplicates

* KS-1569 (Backlog): the revoke route writes memory before its database save commits and fails 40001 under REPEATABLE READ or SERIALIZABLE. A different failure from F1.
* KS-1556 (Done): read `saveKeyAndRetirePriors` for a failed COMMIT, not for a boot race.
* KS-888 (Done): holds the rule these items break.
* KS-1377: the read side, PR 2046, merged; it stays open for its own owed checks. KS-1370 is its parent.

nodes.body:
**BLUF:** PR 2067 (https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/2067, head `0d08681c616d`, base develop `cd773edc2bb8`) gates staking's whole rewards router behind a new default-off flag, `STAKING_REWARDS_ENABLED`, on only for the exact string `true`. It carries no migration. This corrects the "Owed" line above, which prescribes creating the table. Not merged. QA gate pending.

* **Why no migration.** Wednesday's ruling, 2026-11-06 07:32:58Z (not a ruling by Kam). A migration is forward-only, and creating the table would switch on routes that check for a token and nothing else: `rewards.ts` reads no role and no owner, and takes the address from the path or the body. Read from code, not run: nothing in the repo credits the balance except `POST /add-mock`, and nothing in the repo calls these routes over the network. The gateway sends public `/api/rewards` traffic to the referral service.
* **"Whether a migration once created the table" is answered: none did.** The name entered `rewards.ts` in `ba078c8df` (2026-03-20). `git log --all -S` over `*.sql`, `*.sh` and `*.js` across 994 refs finds 0 commits; the control `svc_reward_claims` finds 4.
* **What changed.** With the flag off, all eight rewards operations answer 404 to a valid token and reach no handler. A missing token is still 401. The boot probe does not run, so the error line staking logged at every boot should clear. `GET /api` stops listing the routes. `rewards.ts` is unchanged, and `/add-mock` and `/simulate-distribution` go off with the rest.
* **Turning it on.** The flag is in `services/staking/.env.example`. staking's compose block has no `env_file` and passes no such variable, so on a compose box only a compose or override change can turn it on.
* **Proof.** A new test file boots the real `index.ts` with the real `authenticate()` and an RS256 token. Red on develop: 24 of 32 failed by assertion, 8 controls passed, 0 skipped. After: 32 of 32. 14 of 14 tampers reddened exactly the predicted cells. Staking suite 99 of 99 before, 131 of 131 after. Node v26.8.1, not the images' Node 24.
* **NOT covered.** No PostgreSQL ran: the database in the cells is a stand-in, so how a real box boots is unmeasured. No image, stack or box. The four platform suites were not run. Whether anything outside the repo calls these routes directly is unmeasured.
* **Owed by others after merge.** The staking image at the next Kintsugi round, and a read of staking's access logs there. Demo is frozen, so demo keeps today's failing routes.
* **Open.** Whether a rewards product is planned goes on the monthly agenda with this finding (card `secuura-ks2071-is-a-staker-rewards-product-planned-1106` = a, ruled by Wednesday on Kam's word to go with the recommendations). The routes stay off behind the flag until then. The older reward cells in `staking.test.ts` set the flag on, so they pin code no deployment runs.
* **Also seen, not changed here.** `Projects Documents/Secuura-Architecture-Reference.md:279` still routes `/api/rewards` to staking. `Blockchain/Dev/docker-compose.yml:1057` says the dev-debug override re-publishes staking, and that override has no staking lines. `services/api-gateway/src/routes/proxy.ts:1054-1055` says direct hits on the staking port still work, which this PR makes stale for `/api/rewards`.

title: Audit export CSV: values starting with = + - or @ go out unneutralised, so a spreadsheet can read them as formulas (gate 202 N4)
description:
**BLUF:** The admin audit export (`GET /api/admin/audit/export`) writes CSV through `escapeCSVField`, which quotes a value only when it contains a comma, a double quote or a newline. A value that starts with `=`, `+`, `-` or `@` therefore goes out raw, or quoted only by accident, and a spreadsheet can read it as a formula. Gate 202 measured this on PR 2012 (KS-1645) at base and at head and graded it a Note; no ticket carries it. Whether any consumer opens the export in a spreadsheet is not known.

## What the gate measured (gate 202 on PR 2012, finding N4; its G-CSV cells, base and head)

* `escapeCSVField` (`services/api-gateway/src/routes/audit-export.ts`, lines 90 to 97, unchanged by the PR) quotes only values containing a comma, a double quote or a newline.
* `+1+1`, `-2` and `@SUM(A1)` go out raw.
* `=HYPERLINK(...)` is quoted only because it contains a comma, and it still starts with `=`.
* A bare carriage return is not quoted, at base or at head.
* `userAgent` and `ipAddress` can be set by the caller and were populated at base too. PR 2012 newly fills `action`, `resource` and `timestamp`, which the service sets.
* The gate's grading: a Note, not a hold, "per the commission".

## What is NOT known

* Whether any consumer opens the export in a spreadsheet.
* Whether a caller-controlled value can reach the export with a leading formula character in practice. The rows above are the writer's outputs for the listed strings; the seat filing this read the verdict and ran nothing.

## Owed

Decide the writer's contract for values that start with a formula character, and add a cell that fails when one goes out unneutralised.

## Searched before filing (2026-11-06, includeArchived, titles, descriptions and comments)

* "escapeCSVField": 0 issues, 0 comments. "CSV injection": 0 and 0. "formula injection": 0 issues and 1 comment, which is KS-1645's own close comment saying it found no ticket for N4.

title: RLS verify-fail-closed.sh reports PASSED and exits 0 on a database with no rows: every count is 0 and the users definer check is skipped
description:
**BLUF:** `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/rls/verify-fail-closed.sh`, the KS-458 check that the fail-closed tenant_isolation policy binds, prints "RLS FAIL-CLOSED VERIFICATION PASSED." and exits 0 on a database whose checked tables hold no rows. Every check compares a row count with 0, and the one check that needs a real row is skipped without a line. Found by reading the script at develop c5c26b2835df08e7e6addc1aec30939cf5531377; nothing was run.

## What the script does on an empty database (read, not run)

* Lines 99 and 100: with no tenant context the count must be "0". An empty table gives 0, so it passes.
* Lines 108 to 111: under a wrong tenant the count must be "0". An empty table passes here too.
* Lines 119 to 126: platform scope must see at least as many rows as the default tenant. 0 against 0 passes. Line 132 prints "OK <table> (closed=0, wrong=0, tenant=N, platform=N)", with "closed=0, wrong=0" as literal text rather than the measured counts.
* Lines 156 to 166: the definer check picks a user with `SELECT id FROM users LIMIT 1` under platform scope (line 156). When users is empty, `uid` is empty, the `if [ -n "$uid" ]` block at line 158 is skipped, and no line says so (no SKIP and no FAIL).
* Lines 168 to 173: with `fail` still 0 it prints the PASSED line (169) and exits 0 (173).

So on an empty database the script cannot tell a policy that hides rows from one that hides nothing, and it still reports the run as verified.

## Why it matters, as far as it is known

KS-458's acceptance records two PASSED runs of this script, local and demo. Those comments report counts with the right tenant, which reads as databases that held data; the runs themselves were not re-checked. The exposure is a fresh database: a rebuild, a restore before data, a new slot. There the script would print PASSED without exercising anything.

## What is NOT known

* Whether any run of the script has been done on an empty database. The seat filing this ran nothing.
* Whether the default tenant's row count is ever 0 on the stacks the script is pointed at.

## Owed

A run of the script against an empty database (a fresh compose stack before seeding) to confirm the PASSED line. Then either seed before verifying, or make an all-zero run fail or print an explicit SKIP line, and print a line whenever the definer check is skipped.

title: Security: a demoted or deleted ORG_ADMIN or ISSUER_ADMIN whose token is still live can mint and revoke API keys (tenant-level and own organisation)
description:
## BLUF

A user whose token says ORG_ADMIN or ISSUER_ADMIN, and whose `users` row no longer holds that role or is no longer active, can still mint and revoke API keys: 201 and 200 on every shape measured, tenant-level and own-organisation alike. The key routes read no `users` row for these two roles. It is the same harm as KS-2032, for the two roles a login actually issues. KS-2032's predicate is ADMIN-only and its card rules ADMIN, so it does not reach them. Facts only; nothing is built. Whether the rule extends is Kam's.

## Measured

Seat Y 6th, 2026-11-06. The real `POST /api/keys` and `DELETE /api/keys/:id` on real PostgreSQL 15.19 as the least-privilege app role, on develop `299b9d6a3827` plus the KS-2032 working tree (which does not touch these two roles). Node v26.8.1, not an LTS line. Tokens hand-signed RS256: token role, tenant T, organisation A1, the user's id. Each row is one run of all four calls.

| token role | stored role / status | mint, no organisation | revoke a tenant-level key | mint for own organisation | revoke own organisation's key |
| -- | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- |
| ORG_ADMIN | org_admin / active (control) | 201, key created | 200, key inactive | 201 | 200 |
| ORG_ADMIN | user / active | 201, key created | 200, key inactive | 201 | 200 |
| ORG_ADMIN | verifier / active | 201, key created | 200, key inactive | 201 | 200 |
| ORG_ADMIN | org_admin / deleted | 201, key created | 200, key inactive | 201 | 200 |
| ORG_ADMIN | org_admin / suspended | 201, key created | 200, key inactive | 201 | 200 |
| ISSUER_ADMIN | issuer_admin / active (control) | 201, key created | 200, key inactive | 201 | 200 |
| ISSUER_ADMIN | user / active | 201, key created | 200, key inactive | 201 | 200 |
| ISSUER_ADMIN | verifier / active | 201, key created | 200, key inactive | 201 | 200 |
| ISSUER_ADMIN | issuer_admin / deleted | 201, key created | 200, key inactive | 201 | 200 |
| ISSUER_ADMIN | issuer_admin / suspended | 201, key created | 200, key inactive | 201 | 200 |

Instrument control: the same mint with a token for another tenant answers 403.

Evidence: `5_Project_History/2026-11-06_seatY-6th/evidence/ks2032/finding2_head.json`; the probe is `tools/ks2032_finding2_probe.integration.test.ts` in that folder. Evidence only, not committed to the repo.

## Read at source, not run

Lines at develop `299b9d6a3827`.

* `packages/shared/src/security/keyRevokePolicy.ts:235`: for an org-bounded role, an unqualified target is allowed same-tenant. Kam's 2026-09-03 ruling for org-less keys.
* `services/auth/src/routes/users.ts:838`: an admin's change to a user revokes that user's sessions only when the new status forbids a credential. So a role-only demotion leaves the session alive.
* `services/api-gateway/src/middleware/auth.ts:672`: the gateway checks the session, not the `users` row, and fails open if the session store is unreachable. So through the gateway, a status shape above should die at 401 while the store is up, and a role-only demotion should not. Not run through the gateway.
* `services/auth/src/repositories/userRepo.ts:257`: `mapDbRole` issues ORG_ADMIN and ISSUER_ADMIN from stored rows, and has no key for ADMIN. So, by reading, these two roles are the ones real logins carry, and ADMIN is not (KS-2032's PR records that).
* `services/security/src/adminScope.ts:45`: `LIVE_ADMIN_USER_PREDICATE` is ADMIN-only and cannot serve these roles.

## Not measured

* A real demotion through `PATCH /api/users/admin/:id`, or any of this through the gateway.
* The real token lifetime on any box (compose default 1 day, code default 1 hour; the box values are not read).
* Whether any user on a box is in one of these states with a live token.
* Whether a tenant-level key reaches more than an organisation key: KS-2032's open item, still open.

## Open question (a decision, not made here)

Should these two roles also need a live `users` row holding that role at mint and revoke? It would be a new authorisation rule, not KS-2032's predicate, and it costs a database read on these roles' mints and revokes. Wednesday cards it for Kam with this figure.

Filed by Seat Y 6th on Wednesday's ANSWER 2026-11-06T05:02:31Z, from Finding 2 of the KS-2032 design QUESTION. Proposed priority: High. Related: KS-2032, KS-1585, KS-1570.

title: Audit run: a scan that is still failing exits 0 from the second run on, because job 09 fails only on new findings and run-internal-audit.sh exits from the aggregator alone
description:
## BLUF

**A scan that is still failing makes the audit run exit 1 once and then exit 0.** The aggregator (job 09) fails only on findings that are new since the previous run, and [run-internal-audit.sh](<http://run-internal-audit.sh>) takes its exit from the aggregator alone. So "a failed scan is not a clean image" holds for one run only: a persistently broken trivy reads green at the exit-code level from the second run on, with only a "failed: 1" warning line in the summary.

* Medium, proposed. Found by gate 221 on PR 2041 (the KS-1136 fix), finding N1. The gate measured the aggregator half at runtime and read the orchestrator half; I read both in the PR's tree and did not re-run the second-run probe myself.
* Pre-existing as a design. Before PR 2041 the same scan failure was rc 0 on every run, so the fix is better than base but quieter than its title reads.
* A design question for the owner. Not built here; PR 2041 is not changed by it.

## Detail

* Repro (the gate's, real aggregator, two consecutive run directories under one runs/ directory, bash 3.2.57): a job-04 artefact holding one image with an error. Run 1: one high finding "image/scan-failed", rc 1, new 1. Run 2 on the same artefact: rc 0, new 0, "NEW findings: none", while the high total still counts it and it is still listed under all findings.
* Where, at PR 2041's head dfa1c633b329: Blockchain/Testing/jobs/09-aggregate-report.sh computes new as current minus the previous run's fingerprints minus baselined, and exits 1 only when the new, non-baselined findings reach the threshold. Blockchain/Testing/run-internal-audit.sh counts a failed job (FAIL_COUNT) and prints a warning, then exits from the aggregator's status alone (0, 1 or 2).
* This is the aggregator's documented design (it fails on new findings only), which is why it is a design question and not a defect report. KS-1136 recorded the same behaviour as context ("R-1") and PR 2041's cases assert the first run only for that reason.

## Recommendation

Prose only; the owner's call. Either of these, plus a test that pins the second-run behaviour so the choice is recorded:

* have the orchestrator count a job-04 failure toward its own exit; or
* key the scan-failed finding as always-new, for example with a fingerprint that includes the run id, so every run that still fails exits 1.

Priority is the humans' call.

## Searched before filing

Linear literal substring matches over issues (title and description) and comments, archived included, 2026-11-06 about 04:50Z. Control: an absent term returned 0, and "unreadable-artefact" returned the known KS-1136 and KS-878.

* "second run", "new-only", "fails only on new", "rc gate": KS-1136 only among the issues (its own R-1 context item). The two comment hits I read are KS-105 (the TypeScript CI orchestrator's blocking model, a different aggregator, Done) and PS-322 (an accessibility sweep); the many "second run" hits are other subjects and I read none of them beyond their titles.
* "run-internal-audit": KS-1787, KS-1382, KS-923, KS-868 (slot guard, TARGET_BASE default, a stage-2 guard, [orchestrate.sh](<http://orchestrate.sh>)), none about the exit status.
* "scan-failed": KS-1274, KS-1273, KS-1136 (the shapes job 04 turns into scan-failed), none about the second run.
* "AGG_EXIT", "prev_run": 0 hits.
* "09-aggregate-report": KS-1136, KS-878, KS-868, KS-676 (the artefact reads).

**BLUF:** Erasing a user leaves their wallet address on the users row, and leaves any governance participant row they hold in place with its vote power. KS 1951's follow-up only stops new binds to an erased user, so rows that already exist stay counted. Nothing is fixed here.

**What is there:**

* **users.wallet_address is not cleared by either erasure writer.** originate's executeErasure (gdprService.ts) sets status to deleted, and auth's user.erased subscriber (userErasedSubscriber.ts) sets it to deactivated. Neither statement names the column. QA gate 219 ran the auth statement on real PostgreSQL and the wallet stayed. The originate statement is read from source, not run.
* **Governance does not subscribe to user.erased:** 0 hits for USER_ERASED under services/governance. The gate found no other service that touches svc_governance_participants, so the row keeps its wallet, its stake and its share of total vote power.
* **The gate measured the vote power:** a row bound to an erased id added 200000 to total DRep vote power, for an account that can never log in or vote.

**Why it is not simply covered:** KS 1955 is about kyc and wallet-connector steps failing, and names no governance data. It does treat the wallet address as the subject's data. KS 239 is the decision on triggering erasure and names neither.

**What needs deciding:**

* What happens to a participant row with votes cast or proposals created, when its owner is erased: delete it, keep it with the wallet and vote power cleared, or keep it for audit.
* Whether clearing users.wallet_address at erasure is wanted, given the position on on-chain immutability in KS 234.

**Not measured:** how many erased users hold a wallet or a participant row on any box. No box was read.

nodes.body:
**BLUF:** PR 2099 is up for KS-2060 at head `8967de8b1755`, built on develop `c0e6e744b7b2`. After an erasure, the user's wallet is gone from the users row, and from governance unless a legacy participant row (one whose id is not the user's id) holds it or a stale write puts it back (see Limits). Their address is blanked from governance history, with tallies kept. Migration 059 drops NOT NULL on three address columns. Its tier 1 gate (our QA gate 266) returned GO WITH NOTES at `0d747d09ab23`. The notes changed words only, in a fourth commit, which has its own check before merge. Nothing is merged or deployed.

**Kam's rulings this builds, as ruled (card id, option text):**
- `secuura-ks2060-clear-wallet-null-migration-1106`, choice a: "[a] NULL, with migration 059 (recommended)". Detail: "U 17th builds it under the tier 1 gate, spec line and refusals included; goes through Kintsugi first."
- `secuura-ks2060-address-in-history-dpia-1106`, choice a: "[a] Remove it from governance history (recommended)". Detail: "Votes, proposer and delegation addresses blanked on erasure; tallies kept. Data-destroying path, tier 1 gate. The DPIA's tables updated after you rule."
- `secuura-ks2059-design-tenant-scope-named-route-1106`, choice a: "[a] Take the package, one global DAO (recommended)". Detail: "U 17th builds it after KS-2060, migration included, under a tier 1 gate." It is not in this PR; it is built on its own ticket after this one.

**What the PR does**
- Originate and auth clear `users.wallet_address` on erasure, and the wallet link route refuses an erased caller.
- Governance handles the erasure event by user id, in one transaction:
  - the row's wallet, stake, tier, vote power, both flags and did clear;
  - delegations to and from the user are revoked;
  - the user's address is blanked from their delegations, from `proposer_address` and from `voterAddress` in their votes.
- A delegation to or from a cleared row answers 404.
- Three response fields are declared nullable in the spec.
- The DPIA's 4.1, 4.2 and Net effect say what is now cleared. Its 4.2 and Net effect name the legacy-row case; its Not yet covered paragraph names the twelve wallet tables the cascade still does not reach, the legacy-row case and the stale-write limit.
- Migration 059 has three statements, so it is wider than the first card's "one statement". The wallet link refusal also stops an admin-disabled user who was never erased from linking until reinstated. Both widenings are the coordinator's rulings.

**Measured** after the rebase onto PR 2076's squash: Node v26.8.1, not LTS; PostgreSQL 15.19; Redis 8.10.3; a shared Mac.
- The new real-PostgreSQL suite passes 15 of 15 cells. It went red first, by assertion.
- Governance 386 of 386. Originate 2601 of 2601.
- Auth 1845 of 1847. The 2 are `ks949`'s cells at vitest's 5 s limit under load, and pass 31 of 31 alone.
- 50 of 51 named mutants killed at their named cells; one declared survivor.
- A whole erasure on the real compiled services held every prediction written before the run.

**P10.** After an erasure, an admin naming the old wallet reads 404 "Wallet owner not found", because no row or owner holds it, unless a legacy participant row (one whose id is not the user's id) holds it: that row is left as it is, and the admin's stake still lands on it. A live co-holder of that wallet now registers with 201 where it read 409 before.

KS-2058's G1 still not met: backfill not done.

**Deploy precondition:** 059 must reach a box before or with the governance image. Without it, the handler's first statement fails NOT NULL and the event is dead-lettered after three attempts. This was measured on the compiled services. An event dead-lettered that way is lost, not delayed: nothing replays it, so that subject stays uncleared until the backfill.

**Not run:** the images, Node 24, pgbouncer, a booted gateway, real CIP-8 signatures, the four platform suites, and any box.

**Limits:**
- Users erased before this ships keep their wallet in governance until a backfill runs.
- A legacy participant row whose id is not the user's id keeps the wallet, stake and votes until the backfill. Whether any box holds one is not measured.
- Twelve other tables hold a wallet column the cascade does not reach.
- A write that read a row before the erasure and saves after it puts the address back. An admin wallet registration in that window restores the wallet, stake and DRep flag, and any proposal save (a vote, cancel, finalize, execute, or the 60-second expiry job) rewrites the votes array. Measured by our QA gate 266 under a forced order on real PostgreSQL, not under real concurrency. A self-registration in that window puts the wallet back, and the did when the request carries one; read in the code, not measured. Not fixed here.
- 059 has no down migration. After one erasure writes a NULL, NOT NULL cannot be restored.

**BLUF:** When wallets are cleared at erasure and the backfill is done, decide whether KS 2058's status filter on the owner read stays. Nothing else in this ticket changes.

- **The filter:** getUserIdsByLinkedWallet in services/governance/src/db.ts (PR 2051) does not count a user whose lower(status) is deactivated, inactive or deleted.
- **What clearing the wallet does to it:** this ticket's ruling clears the wallet on the users row, so an erased user is no longer found by that read at all. The filter's erased half then does nothing.
- **What remains:** its effect on disabled users. A sole disabled holder reads 404. With one disabled holder and one live one, the admin's request binds the live one and the disabled one reads 409 once reinstated. QA gate 232 measured that as G1, and it is a stated limit by the coordinator's ruling of 2026-11-06.

**BLUF:** Kam ruled this: keep the row for audit, clear its wallet and vote power, and clear the wallet on the users row. Nothing is built yet. A separate seat takes it after KS 2058 lands, and rows that already exist get a backfill proposed on their own card.

- **Card:** secuura-ks2060-erased-user-wallet-vote-power-1106, option a, ruled 2026-11-06 at 15:29:02 AEDT (the card's recorded time).
- **Option text:** "Keep the row for audit, clear its wallet and vote power, and clear the wallet on the users row"
- **Detail:** "A seat builds it for new erasures and proposes a backfill for existing rows on its own card. Data-destroying path: Opus, tier 1."

title: governance: an admin in one tenant can set stake and flags on another tenant's existing participant row
description:
**BLUF:** A platform admin in tenant T1 can change the stake, DRep status and committee status of a participant row owned by a user in tenant T2. QA gate 219 measured this at PR 2039 and at the develop before it, so it is not a regression. Nothing is fixed here. It needs a ruling, then a migration.

**Measured by the gate** (real compiled service, real JWT verification and router, real PostgreSQL as secuura_app):

* An admin in T1 on a row owned by a T2 user: 201, and stake, DRep and committee all change.
* One wallet linked in both tenants: the T1 admin binds it to the T1 user, the T2 owner gets 409, and a T2 admin's registration then writes onto the T1 user's row.

**Cause:** svc_governance_participants has no tenant column and no row-level security. Ruling D2 (a) on KS 1951 protects only the first bind, when no row holds the wallet yet. Once a row holds it, the admin path writes without reading a tenant. The comment in db.ts saying an admin in one tenant never binds another tenant's user is true only for a new row.

**What the ruling has to weigh:**

* **Precedent:** Kam's KS 1906 ruling keeps vc-issuer's owner-less credentials with "platform administrators of their tenant". Whether that reaches governance is not ruled.
* **The seeded SYSTEM_ADMIN sits in the default tenant** (userRepo.ts:1420). Today the only way that admin can stake a user in a provisioned tenant is this path: the owner self-registers, then the admin's stake lands on the row. Closing it plainly takes that away, so someone needs a named way to stake those users.
* **Other writers:** this was measured on the register route only. The other governance routes that read this table were not walked for the same shape.

**Fix shape, read only, not tried:** a tenant column on svc_governance_participants, backfilled from users, with row-level security and the same GUC the users read uses. A row whose id is not a user id (a legacy uuid row) has no tenant to backfill from, so it needs its own rule.

**Proposed priority:** High, because it writes vote power across a tenant boundary. The priority is for the humans to set.

nodes.body:
**BLUF:** Kam ruled this: close it, tenant admins only, and give stake a named route. Nothing is built yet. A separate seat takes it after KS 2058 lands, and the design returns to Kam before any migration.

- **Card:** secuura-ks2059-cross-tenant-stake-1106, option a, ruled 2026-11-06 at 15:29:05 AEDT (the card's recorded time).
- **Option text:** "Close it, tenant admins only, and give stake a named route"
- **Detail:** "A seat designs a tenant column with row-level security plus a named way to stake users in provisioned tenants; the design returns to you before the migration. Opus, tier 1."

title: governance: gate 219's notes on PR 2039: an erased owner can be bound, a read miss drops the owner's did, no cell pins the token's tenant
description:

title: Idea from Phil: an email to verifiers with no links or attachment, telling them to verify in their Secuura account
description:
## BLUF

From Phil Cuff, on [Asana](<https://app.asana.com/1/1211403151293995/task/1220196579744826>), 5 Nov 2026. **Phil's own words: no action needed yet.**

> "This is just a thought (so no action needed yet) following my comments in Linear earlier today, but I suspect we may need an alternative version of the email to verifiers that contains no links but simply tells the recipient they have a document to verify and to go to their Secuura account to do the verification"

Recorded so it isn't lost. **Not scheduled.**

## To settle before any build

1. Which of Phil's Linear comments this follows. I didn't find them when filing this.
2. Which email: the Verification flow's step email, a share to a verifier, or both.
3. When the no-link version is used: every verifier, by a setting on the flow, or only for recipients who already have an account. A recipient with no account has nowhere to go, so a no-link email can't be the only version.

## Acceptance, when it's picked up

1. **Automated test:** xUnit pins which template is chosen for which recipient, and that the chosen one has no link or attachment.
2. **Docs updated:** `docs/USER-MANUAL.md` on Verification flows.
3. **systemTests updated:** Peter's call. The email-template spec for this step.

**Classification:** Flow, email.
