title: pgbouncer entrypoint.sh writes the four userlist credentials unescaped: a newline in a value adds a userlist entry
description:
**BLUF:** `Blockchain/Dev/docker/pgbouncer/entrypoint.sh:27-30` writes four user/password pairs into `/etc/pgbouncer/userlist.txt` with one `echo` per pair and no escaping. A value that contains a newline therefore adds a userlist line of its own: an extra auth entry, not an upstream. Seat E 33rd found this during KS-915 round 3, and it was ruled out of that PR. KS-915 comment 820f9aff names it for a ticket. Low: the values come from the operator's own `.env` or compose environment.

**Read at develop** `5c1ca287ed74` **with** `git show` (the same blob is at `ee1e1b832115`):

* `:13-24` map eight environment keys to four pairs:
  * POSTGRES_USER / POSTGRES_PASSWORD
  * PGBOUNCER_ADMIN_USER / PGBOUNCER_ADMIN_PASSWORD
  * PGBOUNCER_STATS_USER / PGBOUNCER_STATS_PASSWORD
  * APP_DB_USER / APP_DB_PASSWORD

  The admin, stats and app passwords default to the Postgres password.
* `:26` writes the header line; `:27-30` write one quoted `"user" "password"` line per pair.
* The source sentence names six keys. The file reads eight: the two PGBOUNCER\_\*\_USER keys are echoed as well.
* The file's own header (`:5-6`) says the list holds md5 hashes. `:27-30` write each password as given.

**Source:** `/Volumes/DevMASTER/!CODING/Secuura/Blockchain/5_Project_History/2026-11-04_seatE-33rd/mail/01_plan_confirmation.txt:32`.

**Fix direction only:** refuse a newline or a double quote in these eight values at start-up, or double each quote and refuse newlines before writing. Also correct the header comment, or write md5 entries as it says.

**Not measured:**

* Nothing was run.
* Whether pgbouncer accepts the extra line as a working entry.
* What a double quote inside a value does to its line (pgbouncer's userlist format escapes a quote by doubling it).
* Whether any deployed environment holds such a value.

**Searched** (board: title, description and comments, archived included):

* `userlist.txt`: 1 hit, KS-915 comment 820f9aff, which names it for a ticket.
* `pgbouncer/entrypoint.sh`: 2 hits. KS-915 (the same comment), and KS-762, whose comments cite `entrypoint.sh:24` only as a fallback to another variable, which is a different matter.

title: e2e fixtures register with breached passwords: since KS-1968 B1 seven register call sites get 422 instead of an account
description:
**BLUF:** Since KS-1968 B1 (PR 1988, squash `1cbf260548e7`, deployed to kintsugi at `ee1e1b832115`), `POST /api/auth/register` and `POST /api/auth/reset-password` answer 422 to a password that the HaveIBeenPwned range check finds. Seven e2e call sites send such a password to register on the success path, so on a stack with the check on they get 422 instead of an account. Fix: give those fixtures generated, non-breached passwords (or run them with `HIBP_ENABLED=false`, if that is the ruled choice). Medium priority, because a merged and deployed change breaks known test sites. This was measured by reading the code, not by a run.

**Source:** `/Volumes/DevMASTER/!CODING/Secuura/Blockchain/5_Project_History/2026-11-04_seatD-50th/evidence/hibp_corpus_ee1e1b832115.txt`, Seat D 50th's corpus at target `ee1e1b832115`.

* 148 distinct literals, 44 of them breached; 210 breached occurrences, 21 of those within 15 lines of a register or reset mention. Its positive and negative controls fired.
* The file tags 16 rows `[reg/reset]` (the header's 21 counts occurrences; the rows are what it tagged).
* No literal is copied into this ticket.

**The 16 rows, each read at** `ee1e1b832115` **with** `git show`**:**

* **Register on the success path (7): affected.**
  * `Blockchain/Dev/tests/e2e-v2/tests/tier1-api/email-notifications.api.spec.ts:48`. Asserts a status below 500, so a 422 passes silently and no account is made.
  * `Blockchain/Dev/tests/e2e/tests/email-notifications.prelaunch.spec.ts:76`. Registers, then waits for the verification mail.
  * `Blockchain/Dev/tests/e2e/tests/email-notifications.prelaunch.spec.ts:125`. Registers before the reset-mail cell.
  * `Blockchain/Dev/tests/e2e/tests/full-stakeholder-browser.spec.ts:749`. Asserts a status below 500, so it passes silently.
  * `Blockchain/Dev/tests/e2e/tests/auth.api.spec.ts:14`. The `testUser` that the file's later cells register and log in with.
  * `Blockchain/Dev/tests/e2e/tests/documents.api.spec.ts:18`. Registered in `beforeAll`.
  * `Blockchain/Dev/tests/e2e/tests/fixtures/test-utils.ts:28`. `createTestUser`, a shared helper.
* **Weak-password cells (2 sites, 3 rows): not changed by KS-1968 if the literal fails the strength rules.** `Blockchain/Dev/tests/e2e/tests/auth-exhaustive.spec.ts:651-652` and `auth.api.spec.ts:56`. Register checks strength before the breach list (`services/auth/src/routes/auth.ts:205`, then `:214`, at `ee1e1b832115`).
* **Duplicate-email cell (1): not changed.** `Blockchain/Dev/tests/e2e/tests/sysadmin-exhaustive.admin.spec.ts:998` registers an existing email. The conflict answer at `auth.ts:198-201` comes before both checks.
* **No register call (2):** `systemTest/schemathesis/tests/unit/hooks/test_principal_shield.py:164` (a unit fake) and `systemTest/fixtures/provision.ts:269` (a JSDoc example line of `redactSecrets`).
* **Docs mentions (3):** `Blockchain/Testing/USER SIMULATED TEST/runs/2026-04-27_summary.md:249`, `Blockchain/Testing/README.md:62`, `USER_TESTING/BUGS-FOR-CLI-AGENT.md:180`.
* **Also read:** `Blockchain/Dev/tests/e2e-v2/fixtures/api-client.ts:65` (corpus group B01, not tagged) is a login default for a seeded account, not a register call. KS-1968 does not check at login.

**Not measured:**

* Whether `HIBP_ENABLED` is `false` on kintsugi or on any local stack. The code's default is on; only the string `false` turns it off, per KS-1968's description.
* Which stack these e2e suites run against.
* Whether each affected literal passes `checkPasswordStrength`. If one does not, that site was already failing before KS-1968.
* No suite was run.

**Searched** (board: title, description and comments, archived included):

* `breached`: 8 hits. Open ones are KS-1968 (the check itself; its open items are change-password, admin create and the OpenAPI 422 text, not fixtures) and KS-1868 (unreadable thrown values, unrelated).
* `provision.ts`: 7 hits. The open ones (KS-485, KS-973, KS-1718) concern the pre-suite step and its redaction, not breached fixtures.

title: restore-local-secrets.sh: a .env line that closes stderr hides the PATH refusal (G180-F1); compose config has no time limit; census pin misses 4 of 8 keys
description:
**BLUF:** Four follow-ups on `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/restore-local-secrets.sh` (KS-915, PR 1989, merged 2026-11-04 as squash `26d8314e4f77`). QA gates 174 and 180 named them, and KS-915 comment 820f9aff lists them "for tickets, not in this round". They are one fix to the script and its suite, proven by one suite run, so they are one ticket (Kam, 2026-09-07: the unit of a ticket is the test pass). Item 1 is the one Kam ruled to ticket (live board 2026-11-04 12:51 AEDT, card `secuura-pr1989-round3-go-hold-demo-accounts-1104` = a: "Merge it, and ticket G180-F1"). All are LOW or INFO; none was ruled blocking.

The code was read at develop `5c1ca287ed74` with `git show`. The script blob is the same at the merge squash: `7eef8a0e47e6` at both.

1. **G180-F1 (LOW): a** `.env` **line that closes stderr hides the readonly-PATH refusal.**
   * The bash reader (`restore-local-secrets.sh:306-307`) sources the file under `readonly PATH; set -r; set -a`. It counts refusals by piping the reader's stderr into `grep -c ': PATH: '`.
   * A line that runs `exec 2<&-` before the PATH assignment closes stderr. The refusal is then never counted, while bash still skips the rest of that line.
   * Gate 180 measured a crafted two-line `.env`. At head: rc 0, ADMIN written, mode 600. At round 2: rc 3.
   * Independent readers: dotenv and both compose entries read the local host; a plain `set -a` read a remote POSTGRES_HOST. No command executed (the gate's r3 cell: the PATH lock holds).
   * Measured on macOS bash 3.2.57 only, NOT on bash 4/5 or Linux.
   * Source: `/Volumes/DevMASTER/WEDNESDAY/0_Brain/reference/2026-11-04_gate180-ks915-pr1989-r3/verdict.md`, section G180-F1.
   * Fix direction (the gate's, direction only): a sentinel the reader must print after the source, whose absence counts as a refusal; or a stderr-liveness check after the source.
2. **G174-F4 (LOW):** `docker compose config` **has no time limit.**
   * The three compose reads (`:326`, `:329`, `:479`) run with no timeout.
   * Gate 174 made `docker compose config` hang. In 3 of 3 runs the script hung until the gate's 45 s alarm (rc 142). The `.env` stayed byte-identical and nothing was written, so it fails closed.
   * In 3 of 3 runs the compose child was still running after the script ended.
   * Source: gate 174 `verdict.md` lines 35-36 (`/Volumes/DevMASTER/WEDNESDAY/0_Brain/reference/2026-11-04_gate174-ks915-pr1989-r2/verdict.md`).
3. **G174-F3 (LOW, test strength): the census pin catches 4 of 8 planted address keys.**
   * `CENSUS_JS` (`Blockchain/Dev/scripts/__tests__/restore_local_secrets.test.sh:623`) is name-based.
   * The gate planted one key per run through a compose override. The pin caught DB_READ_HOST, PGBOUNCER_UPSTREAM_HOST, READ_REPLICA_URL and SQLALCHEMY_HOST. It missed REPLICA_HOST, TYPEORM_HOST, AUDIT_STORE_ADDR and PRISMA_URL.
   * Source: gate 174 `verdict.md` lines 31-33.
4. **G174-F5 (INFO): the repo-root note is asymmetric.**
   * When ADMIN_USER_PASSWORD is kept (`:537`) and the repo-root entry passes a different value, no note prints. For a kept ALLOW_DEFAULT_SEED_PASSWORDS the note does print (`:482-490`).
   * Gate 174 called this truthful under the note's own rule, "an asymmetry, not a defect". To decide: make the two cases symmetric or leave them.
   * Source: gate 174 `verdict.md` lines 38-39.

**Not measured for this ticket:** none of the four was re-run; every result above is the gate's. Whether item 1 reproduces on bash 4/5 or on Linux is also not measured.

**Related, not filed here:**

* The wider class of a hostile `.env` forging the bash reader (G173-F2), and the looping `.env`. Both are named in KS-915 comment 820f9aff.
* The pgbouncer `entrypoint.sh` userlist echo from the same comment, filed as its own ticket (a different file, fix and test).

**Searched** (board: title, description and comments, archived included):

* `G180-F1`: 0 hits. `exec 2<&-`: 0. `CENSUS_JS`: 0.
* `G174-F3`, `G174-F4`, `G174-F5`: 1 hit each, all in KS-915 comment 820f9aff, which names them for tickets.
* `restore-local-secrets`: 2 hits (KS-915; KS-600, closed). No ticket covers these items.

nodes.body:
**BLUF:** Two more items for this ticket. They are in the same script and are proven by the same suite run, so they belong here rather than in tickets of their own (Kam, 2026-09-07: the unit of a ticket is the test pass). KS-915 comment 820f9aff names both "for tickets, not in this round". Reading the code at develop `5c1ca287ed74` shows both are still there. Neither was re-run for this comment.

5. **G173-F2 (MEDIUM): a crafted `.env` can forge the bash reader's verdict.**
   * The reader (`restore-local-secrets.sh:306`) sources the file, then prints its result record with `printf` behind a fixed marker.
   * Gate 173 measured two forms at round 1:
     * A `printf()` function defined by the file: rc 0, ADMIN written, while an independent `set -a` read NODE_ENV=production, or a DATABASE_URL naming the gate's remote marker.
     * A file that prints its own record and then exits: rc 0. The gate did not count this one as a slip, because the exit also ends a consumer shell.
   * At develop, by reading: the record is still printed with `printf` after the source, behind the same fixed marker. The script has 0 hits each for `unset -f`, `set -o posix`, `builtin printf` and a per-run marker (`RANDOM`, `urandom`, `nonce`); the control `readonly PATH` has 2 hits.
   * Item 1 (G180-F1) is one form of this class: it shuts the reader's stderr first.
   * Source: `/Volumes/DevMASTER/WEDNESDAY/0_Brain/reference/2026-11-03_gate173-ks915-pr1989/verdict.md:44-56`.
   * Fix direction (the gate's, direction only): print through something the file cannot redefine (`set -o posix` with `export -p`, or `builtin` after `unset -f printf builtin`). Use a per-run random marker, and refuse when a second marker appears.
6. **The looping `.env` (LOW): the bash reader has no time limit.**
   * Gate 173 (G173-F3, "Hang"): a `.env` holding `while :; do :; done` kept the script running until the gate's 60 s alarm (rc 142). Nothing was written. The looping reader outlived its parent, and one sandbox directory was left in TMPDIR.
   * At develop, by reading: the reader (`:306-307`) runs with no time limit. The script has 0 hits each for `timeout`, `alarm`, `watchdog`, `kill ` and `sleep `.
   * Item 2 (G174-F4) is the same gap in the compose reader. One reader time limit that fails closed and reaps its child would cover both.
   * The other half of G173-F3 is closed: `history -w` writing a file under `set -r`. `:306` now runs `enable -n history kill; HISTFILE=/dev/null`, and gate 174 measured 0 of 7 history routes writing.
   * Source: gate 173 `verdict.md:57-69`.

**Searched** (board: title, description and comments, archived included):
* `G173-F2`: 2 hits, KS-915 comment 820f9aff and this ticket.
* `G173-F3`: 0. `while :; do :; done`: 0. `RLS-KS915`: 0.

This supersedes the "Related, not filed here" line in the description for these two.

title: M365-7: declare (certify) the open document from inside Word, Excel or PowerPoint
description:
## BLUF

A user working in Word, Excel or PowerPoint should be able to **declare (certify) the document they have open** without leaving the application: register it with Secuura, then run the Certify flow on it, and get the certified copy back. Today nothing offers this. No ticket asked for it either (checked 4 Nov 2026): [PS-446](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-446/m365-1-decide-the-feature-set-per-host-share-does-not-exist-in-word) lists verify, upload, a share link and provenance as the candidate features for a document host, and certification is not among them; [KS-130](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-130/outlook-add-in-add-platform-s-upload-corporatedomain-deployment-public) and [KS-242](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-242/euro-office-officeeu-connector-joint-platform-k-platform-s-build) name "certify" only as a suggestion awaiting confirmation. This ticket makes it a decision and a piece of work.

**Blocked by** [PS-446](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-446/m365-1-decide-the-feature-set-per-host-share-does-not-exist-in-word) (the feature-set decision, which should now include this) and [PS-449](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-449/m365-4-first-document-host-verify-and-upload-the-open-file-word) (the first document host, whose upload step this builds on). Both relations are recorded on the ticket (the six M365 tickets were unarchived into this project on 4 Nov 2026).

## What exists on `develop` that this reuses

* **The Certify flow** ([PS-841](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-841/flow-11-the-certify-flow-page-start-add-a-note-declaration-waiting)): declaration, optional watermark, sign, with a `certified` chain event ([PS-837](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-837/flow-05-flow-completion-chain-events-certified-verified-with-non-pii)). User-facing word is **Declare**; the wire verb is `certify` ([PS-585](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-585/terminology-upload-register-certify-declare-across-all-user-facing), [PS-612](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-612/rename-the-certify-verb-to-declare-across-s)).
* **Any supported file type can be certified** since [PS-1042](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1042/epic-sign-every-supported-file-type-embedded-where-the-format-allows): a `.docx`, `.xlsx` or `.pptx` is signed inside the file ([PS-1046](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1046/signing-formats-p4-ooxml-embedded-signing-engine-for-docxxlsx-spike), [PS-1049](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1049/signing-formats-allow-powerpoint-ppt-pptx-upload-and-so-signing)) when `SigningFormats:EmbedOffice` is on, detached otherwise. [PS-1030](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1030/certify-is-offered-on-documents-it-can-never-finish-four-steps-run-and) refuses up front a file the flow could never finish.
* **The Outlook add-in's upload** (`POST /api/outlook/documents/upload`, [PS-424](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-424/outlook-add-in-multi-select-share-upload-and-send-mode-outlook-share)), which registers a stored document and is the step [PS-449](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-449/m365-4-first-document-host-verify-and-upload-the-open-file-word) reuses for Word.
* **Dialog-API sign-in** on `/Outlook/Auth` ([PS-345](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-345/ps-d-planned-authenticated-features-list-and-register-via-platform-s)) and the 30-minute bearer token.

## What the Outlook history settles already

* **Certify needs a stored document.** Register-from-hash was dropped in [PS-345](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-345/ps-d-planned-authenticated-features-list-and-register-via-platform-s) because originate needs a `DocumentStore` row; the add-in's "Register for Declaration" button is compiled out (`FEATURES.register = false`). So the Office path is **upload first, then certify the stored document**. There is no hash-only declare.
* **Who may declare** is the platform's rule, not the pane's: the certification tier in `docs/role-classification.md`, a base User is not offered Certify ([PS-1250](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1250/a-base-user-is-offered-and-can-open-the-certify-flow-flow-lists)), and an organisation with no usable signing certificate cannot start it ([PS-1272](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1272/certify-flow-pauses-with-no-default-signing-certificate-is-set-for), [PS-1388](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1388/certify-settings-an-organisation-with-no-usable-signing-certificate-is)). The pane must show the platform's refusal, never a second rule.

## Design question to settle first

Two ways to drive the flow from the pane:

**A. Hand off to the web Certify flow.** The pane uploads the open file, then opens `/Flow/certify/{id}` in an Office dialog on the Platform S origin, where the cookie session works. Every gate, message and step of the flow is reused as is, including "Add a note?" and the signing-certificate pause. Least new code; the dialog is the same bridge [PS-345](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-345/ps-d-planned-authenticated-features-list-and-register-via-platform-s) built for sign-in.

**B. A pane-native certify.** A new `POST /api/outlook/documents/{id}/certify` that starts the flow for the caller, and the pane renders the steps. More to build and a second rendering of the flow's rules to keep in step.

Recommendation: **A first**, and revisit B only if the dialog proves unusable inside the Office hosts.

## Open questions, for the ticket to answer before code

1. **What happens to the open document afterwards.** Certify produces a new signed copy; the file open in Word is the unsigned original. Does the pane offer the certified copy for download, replace the open document, or just link to it? Office cannot overwrite the open file from an add-in, so "download the certified copy" is the likely answer; say so in the pane.
2. **Unsaved edits** (the [PS-449](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-449/m365-4-first-document-host-verify-and-upload-the-open-file-word) trap): the bytes Office hands over are the saved file. The pane must say that the saved document is what will be registered and declared.
3. **Watermark on a non-PDF.** [PS-1449](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1449/docs-question-does-certify-ask-add-a-watermark-on-a-non-pdf-now-that-a) asks whether Certify offers the watermark step on a non-PDF. The answer decides what the pane can promise for an Office file.
4. **Cross-host.** Does the same control serve Excel and PowerPoint unchanged ([PS-451](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-451/m365-6-remaining-hosts-excel-powerpoint-and-what-microsoft-family)), or does declare belong in Word only?

## Acceptance

* From Word, with the add-in signed in: **Declare this document** uploads the saved file, opens the Certify flow on it, and on completion the pane shows the document as Certified with a link to or download of the certified copy.
* A user the platform does not allow to certify is told so in the platform's own words, and the control is not offered where the role gate says no.
* An organisation with no usable signing certificate sees the flow's existing pause message, not a pane-specific one.
* A document already registered (same bytes, same organisation) is not uploaded again; the flow starts on the existing registration.
* Unsaved edits are named before anything is sent.
* The `certified` event appears on the document's Lineage and on the web Verify page the same as a certify started on the web.
* The Outlook add-in's behaviour is unchanged ([PS-448](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-448/m365-3-split-the-add-in-into-a-host-agnostic-core-and-an-outlook-host)'s rule).

## Tests

* **xUnit**: any new endpoint's gate, ownership scoping and refusals, in the shape of `OutlookShareAndUploadTests`.
* **vitest** in `outlook-addin/`: the pane's states (not signed in, not allowed, unsaved edits, certified).
* **Playwright**: through a document-host task-pane mock against a slot, the way `outlook_taskpane_mock.spec.ts` drives the Outlook pane; the flow's own specs ([PS-1169](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1169/systemtest-flow-certify-verification-the-record-manage-flows-the)) stay the control.
* **Not tested**: the live add-in inside Microsoft Word, as with Outlook ([PS-1444](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1444/systemtest-outlook-add-in-and-signed-documents-signatures-on-record)): Microsoft 365 is recorded as Not tested.

## Docs

`docs/USER-MANUAL.md` gains a section beside §6 *Verifying from Microsoft Outlook*; `docs/role-classification.md` gains the declare-from-Office row; the two testing documents in `docs/` gain the area.

nodes.body:
**Design question settled. Stuart, 5 Nov 2026: Flow A.** The pane uploads the open file, then hands off to the web Certify flow (`/Flow/certify/{id}`) in an Office dialog on the Platform S origin, so every gate, message and step is reused. There's no new pane-native certify endpoint.

Still blocked by PS-446 and PS-449. This ticket's four open questions are unchanged.

title: health-dashboard checkService: no test pins the DOMException name probe (gate 177 mutant H5 survives and is not equivalent)
description:
**BLUF:** In `Blockchain/Dev/services/api-gateway/src/routes/health-dashboard.ts`, `checkService` (line 44) tells a timeout from other failures with `error instanceof DOMException && error.name === 'AbortError'` (line 83 at develop `ea5134d6b98c`, before KS-1868 pull request 1993 guards the reads). Gate 177's mutant H5 (drop the DOMException-name probe in `checkService`) survives that pull request's tests and all 17 value classes, and it is NOT equivalent: no test pins the probe line. Test gap, not a defect in the pull request, and not a hold for it.

## Measured (gate 177, read from its verdict)

Source: `WEDNESDAY/0_Brain/reference/2026-11-03_gate177-ks1868-pr1993/verdict.md`, finding G177-F5 (LOW, test gap).

* For a `DOMException('...','AbortError')` whose `name` getter throws (the gate calls it VX, outside the 17 classes), the pull request's head lists the service `down` with the constant error. The H5-mutated head and base both lose the service from the dashboard (the oracle fails: `expected undefined to be 'down'`). So head handles VX correctly, but nothing would notice if the probe were removed.
* Evidence: `scripts/mut_h5.sh` and `results/mut_h5.txt` in the gate's folder (head rc 0, H5 rc 1, base rc 1).

## Follow-up cell

One test cell in the api-gateway `checkService` test: a rejected probe whose value is a `DOMException` with a throwing `name` getter; assert the service is listed `down`. Depends on pull request 1993 being merged (the guarded reads are only in its tree until then).

## Not measured

A real timeout (`AbortController`) path; the gate drove only a stand-in fetch.

title: vc verifier: with no DID resolver configured, a credential signed with the source's default development key verifies, also under NODE_ENV=production
description:
**BLUF:** In `Blockchain/Dev/packages/shared/src/vc/verifier.ts`, when no DID resolver is configured (as the vc-issuer routes configure it) and `VC_SIGNING_KEY` is unset, a proof starting `zDEV_` is checked against an HMAC made with the literal default key in the source (line 356), so a credential "signed" with that known key verifies, including with `NODE_ENV=production`. Pre-existing: base = head; these are not the lines KS-1868 pull request 1993 changes. LOW (the gate's severity). **Measurement limit: measured on the module; the route was not driven; whether any deployed vc-issuer runs with the key unset is UNMEASURED.**

## Measured (gate 177, read from its verdict)

Source: `WEDNESDAY/0_Brain/reference/2026-11-03_gate177-ks1868-pr1993/verdict.md`, finding G177-F7 (LOW, PRE-EXISTING).

* `verify()` with an empty config and `VC_SIGNING_KEY` unset: a `zDEV_` proof made with the default key gives `verified: true`, `signature: true` under `NODE_ENV=test` AND under `NODE_ENV=production`.
* A forged Ed25519-form proof (`zFORGEDgate177`) verifies under `NODE_ENV=test` and is refused under production ("No DID resolver configured").
* A control proof (`xBAD`) is refused at both. All 6 cells are identical at base and head.

## What the gate did not measure

Whether vc-issuer runs with `VC_SIGNING_KEY` set (the production compose passes it through; when it is set, the `zDEV_` key is that value, not the default) and with `NODE_ENV=production`; and the routes' revocation resolvers, which fail closed on an unknown credential id, so a forgery would also need an id with a stored, unrevoked record. The gate did not check whether this is already ticketed; the board was searched for the default key, `zDEV_` and the `secuura-dev` literal (no ticket found; related reading only: KS-1352, KS-624, KS-625). It does not bear on any merge.

Wednesday's disposition (her 2026-11-04 00:19 note): a ticket candidate for a Secuura seat, to be told to Kam once as an FYI on the morning card with the measurement limit above.

title: An Error instance with a non-string message passes the new guards in the credential verifier, the identus client, the service client and the health dashboard
description:
**BLUF:** The catches that KS-1868 pull request 1993 guards protect a message read that THROWS. They do not protect a read that RETURNS a non-string. For an Error instance whose `message` is a Symbol, or an object whose `toString` throws, the read succeeds, the guard is passed, and the later use breaks. Pre-existing: base = head, and these classes were outside the 17 the pull request was commissioned for (the gate added them as V18 and V19). Low: every cell fails closed.

## Measured (gate 177, read from its verdict)

Source: `WEDNESDAY/0_Brain/reference/2026-11-03_gate177-ks1868-pr1993/verdict.md`, finding G177-F3 (LOW, PRE-EXISTING, extra classes).

* Credential verifier: the template literal `Signature verification error: ${msg}` sits outside the guard, so `verify()` REJECTS at triggers T1, T2 and T3 (6 cells) and T5 (2 cells), at both trees.
* `IdentusClient.resolveDID` returns an `errorMessage` of type symbol or object (6 cells); `ServiceClient.healthCheck` returns an `error` of type symbol or object (4 cells); the dashboard entry's `error` is dropped from the JSON (Symbol) or becomes `{}` (8 cells). In all of them `didDocument` stays null, `healthy` stays false and the status stays `down`.
* It is the gate 175 and 176 F2 shape: the use of the value sits outside the guard. Not that pull request's regression.

## Files

title: vc verifier: when the resolver also throws an unreadable value at the issuer-DID lookup, verify() still rejects; the inner Ed25519 catch is unguarded
description:

With one resolver that throws an unreadable value on every call, `verify()` still REJECTS, so the claim "verify() now answers instead of rejecting" holds only when the issuer-DID lookup does not also throw. Pre-existing: base = head. Low: every affected cell fails CLOSED (a rejection or `verified: false`, `signature: false`); none is more permissive than the ordinary-Error outcome.

## Measured (gate 177, read from its verdict)

Source: `WEDNESDAY/0_Brain/reference/2026-11-03_gate177-ks1868-pr1993/verdict.md`, finding G177-F2 (LOW, PRE-EXISTING).

Both sites are in `verifier.ts`, share the fix shape (coerce the message to a string inside a guard), and one recorder pass over the same value classes proves both. The related non-string-message gap across four files is a separate ticket.

## Not measured

A real resolver or credential stack; the vc-issuer routes were not driven. Related, same class: KS-1904 (six other sites).

title: event-indexer: isRateLimited reads the thrown value before handleError, so for three value classes poll() rejects or the indexer re-reads one block forever
description:
**BLUF:** In `Blockchain/Dev/packages/shared/src/blockchain/event-indexer.ts`, `isRateLimited(err)` (line 334) reads `err?.status_code` and `err.message` with no guard, and it is called before `handleError` at lines 200, 223 and 326 (the `handleError` calls follow at 210, 232 and 329). For an Error whose `message` getter throws, a revoked Proxy, or a throwing get trap, that read throws first, so the guard in `handleError` is never reached. Pre-existing: base = head for these classes (before and after the merged KS-1868 pull request 1992, which guards `handleError` but not this earlier read). Liveness bug for those classes: with a persistent bad value the indexer retries the same block forever.

## Measured (gate 176, read from its verdict)

Source: `WEDNESDAY/0_Brain/reference/2026-11-03_gate176-ks1868-pr1992/verdict.md`, finding G176-F3 (LOW, PRE-EXISTING; Wednesday called it a liveness bug).

* Site 210: `poll()` REJECTS on every poll at both trees: 6 cells. The production caller is `setInterval(() => void this.poll())`, so this would be an unhandled rejection. That is read, not driven.
* Sites 232 and 329: the throw reaches `poll`'s catch as a new, readable Error, so `lastProcessedBlock` is NOT advanced and block 11 is re-fetched on every poll: 3 of 3 polls, 12 cells.
* Default path: `handleError`'s `console.error(error.message)` still throws for the getter class (it is an `instanceof Error`, so it passes through the guard unconverted): 2 more cells (sites 133 and 321, `onError` off).
* Total: 20 cells where head differs from base-ordinary, all base = head. Line numbers above are mine, read at develop `ea5134d6b98c`.

## Fix shape (not chosen here)

Read the value inside the guard that `handleError` already has (or guard `isRateLimited` itself) so a throwing read counts as "not rate limited" and the block advances.

## Not measured

The real `setInterval` path and real Blockfrost; whether any real client emits such a value.

title: ssrf-guard: for three value classes the DNS-path guard rejects instead of returning its refusal, because the refusal string is built outside the guard
description:
**BLUF:** In `Blockchain/Dev/packages/shared/src/security/ssrf-guard.ts`, `resolvePublicAddresses` (line 310) reads a failed lookup's message inside a guarded block (lines 325 to 330) but builds the refusal text with the template literal on line 333 (`could not be resolved (${reason})`), outside any guard. For an Error-like value whose `message` is a Symbol, a revoked Proxy, or an object whose `toString` throws, the read succeeds and the template literal then throws, so the function REJECTS instead of returning `{ ok: false, error }`. The rejection reaches `assertResolvedHostPublic` (351), `assertSafeOutboundUrl` (364) and `safeOutboundRequest` (483): 3 classes x 4 functions = 12 cells. Pre-existing: base = head for these classes (before and after the merged KS-1868 pull request 1992, which guards the read but not the template literal). Low: every one of those cells is LESS permissive than the ordinary refusal (nothing allowed, 0 requests built), so this is a robustness gap, not a bypass.

## Measured (gate 176, read from its verdict)

Source: `WEDNESDAY/0_Brain/reference/2026-11-03_gate176-ks1868-pr1992/verdict.md`, finding G176-F2 (LOW, PRE-EXISTING).

* Downstream in originate's `dispatchEvent`, the same 3 classes at DNS abort the dispatch loop (it returns 0 and the later subscribers are not sent): 3 cells. `{message: BigInt}` and a revoked-Proxy message at request construction do the same: 2 cells (the request catch returns a non-string `error`).
* Line numbers above are mine, read at develop `ea5134d6b98c`.

## Fix shape (not chosen here)

Build the refusal text from a string produced inside the same `try` (coerce the message there), so the template literal cannot throw.

## Not measured

A real DNS lookup; whether any real resolver emits such a value. Related, same class: KS-1904 (six other sites).

title: auth: five places say sessions fall back to memory when Redis is down, but session.ts has no in-memory session store
description:
**BLUF:** The auth service says, in a log line, a health message, a status string and two comments, that sessions fall back to memory when Redis is unavailable. `services/auth/src/services/session.ts` has no in-memory session store: with Redis down, `createSession` throws and every session read answers null, false, 0 or an empty list. The wording is false, so a person reading the log or `/health` is told a fallback exists when users simply cannot sign in or stay signed in. This ticket is about the wording only; whether a fallback should exist is a design question it does not take.

## Measured at develop `79145a312f01` (read only, `git show`)

False wording (sessions and Redis):

* `services/auth/src/services/session.ts:86`: `logger.warn('Redis unavailable — using in-memory session fallback', ...)`, in the catch of `initRedisSession`.
* `services/auth/src/routes/health.ts:30`: `'Redis not connected (using in-memory fallback)'`.
* `services/auth/src/index.ts:9`: comment `Sessions: Redis when available, in-memory fallback.`; `:172`: `sessions: 'Redis (with in-memory fallback)'`; `:255`: comment `Initialise Redis for sessions (non-blocking — falls back to in-memory)`.
* The test `services/auth/src/__tests__/ks1868-auth-session-listener-and-init-catch-unreadable-throw.test.ts` pins the text: line 8 (comment) and line 81 (`const INIT = 'Redis unavailable — using in-memory session fallback'`), so a wording change has to edit that test too.

What `session.ts` really does with Redis down: `createSession` throws `Redis is not available — cannot create session` (line 171); `getSession` returns null (270); `revokeSession` returns false (314); `revokeAllUserSessions` returns 0 (332); `getUserSessions` returns \[\] (346); `extendSession` returns null (384). The only array named `sessions` in the file (line 353) is the local result list of `getUserSessions`.

Not the same claim and NOT part of this ticket (about the database and challenge stores, which I did not examine): `db.ts:254`, `routes/users.ts:6`, `routes/wallet.ts:40`, `routes/auth.ts:6`, `routes/health.ts:50`, `index.ts:8`, `:171` and `:248`.

## Fix shape (not chosen here)

Correct the five strings and the two test lines in one change so they say what happens (session creation is refused and session reads answer empty while Redis is unavailable). Behaviour does not change.

## Related

KS-1965 describes a different defect in the same catch (the availability flag never returns to true after a boot-time Redis outage). Gate 160 (G160-F5, LOW, test gap) also noted, for this catch, that the tests have no null cell and no null-message cell (nice-to-have).

Found while raising KS-1868 passes (Seat R 78th and Seat R 80th read the wording; Seat R 81st re-read every line above at develop `79145a312f01` and read the session functions).

title: auth: the breached-password check (isPasswordBreached, pen-test F-12 item 3) has no caller, so sign-up, reset and change-password accept a breached password
description:
**BLUF:** in the auth service, `isPasswordBreached` (`Blockchain/Dev/services/auth/src/services/password.ts:130`, the HaveIBeenPwned k-anonymity check) has **no caller anywhere in the repository**. The file's own header (lines 5-15) titles its list after pen-test F-12 and makes this check item 3. So sign-up, password reset and change-password accept a password that appears in a public breach list, provided it passes `checkPasswordStrength`, and the `HIBP_ENABLED` switch controls nothing. Pre-existing. Measured by QA gate 161 (finding G161-F2, rated HIGH); the pen-test report itself is UNREAD, so whether F-12 item 3 was accepted as residual is not known.

**Authority.** Kam, live board 2026-11-03 15:53:02, card `secuura-hibp-breach-check-never-runs-1103`, verbatim: "Decision secuura-hibp-breach-check-never-runs-1103: a — Wire it in: refuse a breached password at sign-up, reset and change-password; if the breach service is down, allow it (as written)". Option a's detail, verbatim: "A Secuura seat files the High ticket and builds it behind the existing HIBP_ENABLED switch, tier 1 Opus gate. The user sees 'this password has appeared in a data breach, choose another'. Outage = allowed, so sign-ups never depend on a third party."

**The code** (read at develop `10edf375ac31` with `git show`, by Seat F 27th):

* `password.ts:130-162`: sends `https://api.pwnedpasswords.com/range/<first 5 hex of the SHA-1>` with `Add-Padding` and a 2 s timeout, matches the suffix locally, and answers false on a non-200 or a throw (fails open). `HIBP_ENABLED` is read only at `:131`, and only the string `false` disables it, so the default is ON.
* Call sites: 0 (`git grep isPasswordBreached` hits only its definition, one KS-1868 test and two KS-1868 docs fragments). Positive control: `verifyPassword` has 4 call sites (gate 161).
* `HIBP_ENABLED` is set in 0 of 46 env-example and compose files (names only; positive control `REDIS_URL` hits 12). Once wired in, the check is ON in local, demo and every team build.

title: api-gateway register-connector answers rotated: true and drops priorKeysRevoked when the prior key's retire failed, so a re-keyed leaked credential can stay valid unannounced
description:
**BLUF:** When the security service's rotate mints the new key but the retire of the prior key fails, it answers 201 with `priorKeysRevoked: null` and the prior credential stays valid (the deliberate KS-577 design: mint first, then revoke). The one production caller that rotates, the api-gateway's register-connector route (`Blockchain/Dev/services/api-gateway/src/routes/platform.ts`), drops that field: it only writes a `console.error`, records its audit entry `connector.key-rotate` without the failure, and answers its own caller `rotated: true` with no `priorKeysRevoked`. A Platform S admin re-keying a leaked credential is told it rotated while the old key still works. Pre-existing, and not caused by pull request 1981; found by QA gate 164 (G164-F3, MEDIUM). The same behaviour is already recorded as item R-880-1 on KS-1152 (the omnibus gate-records ticket, classed "design choice, pre-existing"); this ticket is the standalone with the measurement and the two remedies. Related to KS-577.

## What is read (develop `32921f7921c2`, `Blockchain/Dev/services/api-gateway/src/routes/platform.ts`)

* `:877-879` the gateway types the mint body with `priorKeysRevoked?: number | null`.
* `:884-889` when `rotate && mintBody?.data?.priorKeysRevoked === null`, the only action is `console.error('[KS-577] rotate minted a new key but the prior-key revoke FAILED — prior credential STILL VALID', { externalRef, organizationId })`.
* `:895-907` the best-effort audit POST records the action `connector.key-rotate` with details `{ externalRef, keyId, keyPrefix, tenantId }`: there is no field for a failed retire.
* `:909-921` the response (200 for an existing connector, 201 for a new one) carries `rotated: rotate && existing.rows.length > 0` and no `priorKeysRevoked`.
* Callers of the security service's `POST /api/keys` that send `rotate` (gate 164, whole repository, with a positive control): only this route (`platform.ts:847`). `tenant-provisioning/src/meteringKey.ts:52` never sends `rotate`.

## What gate 164 measured (G164-F3)

With a real Postgres lock timeout on the retire (a superuser holding `FOR UPDATE` on the prior row, the app role at `lock_timeout=500ms`, nothing injected), the security service answers 201 with the new key valid, the prior key valid and 2 active rows, and logs "canceling statement due to lock timeout"; the same before and after pull request 1981. Likelihood is low: only a statement-level failure of the retire UPDATE alone fails open (a lock or statement timeout, a cancel, a deadlock), and the security service sets no `statement_timeout` or `lock_timeout` in code, so server defaults wait on a lock. Impact is high: the rotate exists to cut off a lost or leaked credential. The gate read, and did not drive, the gateway route, and read no retry or sweep that retires the key later.

## Two remedies, named neutrally (nothing is built, and neither is chosen here)

* (a) The gateway passes `priorKeysRevoked` through in its response and records the failure in its audit entry, so the caller is told the truth. The old key stays valid until it is retired some other way.
* (b) The rotate fails closed when the retire fails: no new key is issued unless the prior key is retired. The failure then becomes a failed rotate, which KS-577's ruling weighed as the worse failure.

Wednesday will bring (b) to Kam with the other fail-closed rulings.

## Not measured

The gateway route over HTTP; `statement_timeout`, a cancel or a deadlock as the real trigger (only `lock_timeout` was driven); a non-zero `API_KEY_ROTATION_GRACE_SECONDS`; concurrent rotates.

## Board search (duplicate check, `tools/file_ticket_r78.py`)

Terms: `priorKeysRevoked`, `rotated: true`, `connector.key-rotate`, `prior credential`, `STILL VALID`. Positive control: the phrase "recipient's email address" returns KS-1937; negative control: a random token returns 0. Candidates read by title and named as reviewed: KS-1152 (R-880-1 and the gate 90 note record the behaviour from source, with no measurement, no audit finding and no remedies), KS-1370 (validate reads keys from a boot-only memory map), KS-583 (a DR rehearsal that expects the old key dead) and KS-869 (connectorId persistence); none reports the gateway's `rotated: true` after a failed retire. KS-577 was also read (the original rotate ruling and its comments).

Source: gate 164's verdict, `0_Brain/reference/2026-11-03_gate164-ks1868-pr1981/verdict.md`, finding G164-F3.

title: auth: if Redis is down when the service boots, the session availability flag never returns to true, because the ready listener is only attached after the first successful connect
description:
**BLUF:** In `Blockchain/Dev/services/auth/src/services/session.ts`, `initRedisSession` attaches its `error`, `reconnecting` and `ready` listeners only AFTER `await redis.connect()` and `await redis.ping()` have succeeded. If Redis is down when auth boots, the connect rejects, the catch sets the availability flag false and returns, and no listener is ever attached. ioredis keeps reconnecting in the background (the retry strategy from KS-617 never gives up), and when Redis comes back the client reaches `ready`, but nothing sets the flag true again. The flag stays false until the process is restarted, so every authenticated request is refused and no login can mint a session, while the container keeps running. This is the boot-time sibling of KS-617 (which addressed the same symptom after a blip, when the listeners already exist). Found by QA gate 160 (G160-F8, read only); MEASURED here.

**Relation to KS-617:** KS-617's fix (the retry strategy never returns null) covers a client that was established and then lost Redis, not this boot path.

## Measurement (read-only, loopback only; no real Redis, no box)

Real `session.ts` at develop `32921f7921c2`, real ioredis 5.11.1 (wrapped only to capture the client), a minimal RESP stub server on 127.0.0.1; recorder `5_Project_History/2026-11-03_seatR-78th/drafts/ks617/rec_redis_boot.test.ts`, recording `evidence/ks617/rec.json`.

* **Scenario A (the claim): Redis down at boot, then up.** `initRedisSession` returned after 1066 ms with the flag false. The client existed with status `reconnecting` and had 0 listeners for `error`, `ready` and `reconnecting`. After the stub came up the client reached status `ready` (the stub saw a connection and the commands `client`, `client`, `info`), yet the flag was still false after 12 s and `getRedisClient()` still returned null.
* **Control B (the listeners ARE attached): Redis up at boot.** Flag true, 1 listener each. A simulated `error` set the flag false; after an outage (connections reset, server closed) the client was `reconnecting`; after the stub restarted it reached `ready` and the flag returned to true within 12 s. So the instrument can see the flag returning to true.

## What the flag false does (read from the callers, per gate 160)

`getSession` returns null, so `authenticate` answers 401 to every authenticated request; `createSession` throws "Redis is not available", so no login mints a session; password change and reset answer 503; the refresh denylist fails closed; the login lockout fails open (already tracked as a decision for Kam). The service's own log line says "using in-memory session fallback", which is false (there is no in-memory store).

## Not measured

A real Redis server (the stub speaks only enough RESP for ioredis to reach `ready`); a booted auth service or any HTTP request; the same boot-order case in api-gateway, originate and governance, which KS-617 also names; whether a deployment's orchestration (depends_on, health checks, restart policy) makes the boot-time case reachable in practice; any fix. No fix is proposed here; the fix shapes are open (for example attaching the listeners before the first connect).

## Compose ordering and priority (read, not run)

Read at develop `32921f7921c2`, `Blockchain/Dev/docker-compose.yml`, service `auth` (starts at line 729):

* `:836-842` `depends_on` lists `pgbouncer` (`condition: service_healthy`), `redis` (`:839-840`, `condition: service_healthy`) and `migrations` (`condition: service_completed_successfully`). So a `docker compose up` starts auth only after Redis reports healthy; the redis service has a healthcheck (`:227-231`, `redis-cli ... ping`, retries 5).
* `:738` `restart: unless-stopped`. `Blockchain/Dev/docker-compose.production.yml` is an override used with the base file (`-f docker-compose.yml -f docker-compose.production.yml`, its own header and `Makefile:9`) and sets `restart: always` for auth (`:149`); it does not remove the base file's `depends_on`.
* Priority is **Medium**, because `service_healthy` guarantees the order on a cold `up`: the boot-time case then needs Redis to be down when auth (re)starts. What the file does not show, and what is NOT measured here, is whether a restart policy brings auth back before Redis is healthy (for example after a host or Docker daemon restart), since `depends_on` is applied by `docker compose up` and not by a restart policy. The Container Apps deploy template (a different deployment form) was not read.

## Board search

KS-617 (Deployed to UAT) describes the latch after a blip and corrects the retry strategy; its description and six comments have 0 mentions of `initRedisSession`, `lazyConnect`, a listener, or the boot-time connect failure. The terms `initRedisSession`, `lazyConnect`, `ready listener`, `after a failed connect`, `availability flag` and `session availability` each return 0 issues (`tools/file_ticket_r78.py`; positive control: the phrase "recipient's email address" returns KS-1937; negative control: a random token returns 0). No candidate to review.

title: auth email.ts writes the recipient's email address in clear to the console on send, failure and refusal (seven lines)
description:
**BLUF:** `Blockchain/Dev/services/auth/src/services/email.ts` writes the recipient's email address (`options.to`) in clear to the console at seven places: the ACS sent line, the ACS send-failed and send-threw lines, the allow-list refusal, the no-provider line, and the SMTP sent and failed lines. This is pre-existing, unchanged by pull request 1978, and not a thrown-object leak. It was disclosed by the author of pull request 1978 and raised by QA gate 161 (G161-F8). It conflicts with Kam's card `secuura-ks1346-logging-thrown-objects-leaks-secrets` = a ("Log what kind of thing was thrown and the NAMES of its fields, never their values"). Related to KS-1937, the same pattern in originate's notificationClient (the recipient address at INFO). A separate fix in a separate service, so a separate ticket (Kam, 2026-09-07). Nothing here is a fix; no code change is proposed or made.

## What is read (develop `32921f7921c2`, `Blockchain/Dev/services/auth/src/services/email.ts`, 331 lines)

* `:161` `console.log` of `[Email/ACS] Sent to ${options.to}: ${options.subject}` (ACS sent)
* `:164` `console.error` of `[Email/ACS] Send failed for ${options.to}` (ACS failed status)
* `:167` `console.error` of `[Email/ACS] Send threw for ${options.to}: ${err?.message}` (ACS catch)

* `:207` `console.error` of `[Email/SMTP] Failed to send to ${options.to}: ${error.message}` (SMTP catch)

Three of the seven are failure paths (`:164`, `:167`, `:207`); the other four are the sent, refused and no-provider lines. The gate's finding names the catches; this ticket lists every line that carries the address.

## What is not measured

Whether this console output reaches a persisted log file or a log collector in any deployment; the same lines on the head of pull request 1978 (not re-read here); whether the address is ever a user's personal address rather than a system one in a given flow.

title: referral: duplicate milestone reward rows the re-award bug already stored stay stored and still count as pending rewards
description:
**BLUF:** The referral re-award bug (KS 1956) stored duplicate CLAIMABLE milestone reward rows in `svc_referral_milestones_rewards`: the same user and milestone, more than once. The repair in pull request 1979 stops NEW duplicates; it removes none. The rows already stored stay stored, and `GET /api/rewards/user` still counts every one of them as a pending reward that can be claimed. Any cleanup is a DATA change and Kam's decision later; this ticket proposes nothing destructive. Pre-existing, High (QA gate 162).

## What is measured

* **QA gate 162** (2026-11-03, real PostgreSQL 15, the real referral service over HTTP, on pull request 1979): before the repair the same user and milestone reached 2 to 4 rows across its cells. After the repair, new checks add none, and the progress row records each milestone once. Every duplicate row stored earlier is still there and is still a pending reward.
* **QA gate 153** (2026-11-03): `GET /api/rewards/user` shows these rows as pending with `canClaim: true`, which inflates the balance a user sees.

## What is not measured

* Whether production has `svc_referral_milestones_rewards` at all (the repo has no DDL for it, KS 1956), and if so how many duplicate rows it holds. Nothing in the repo shows production's schema or data.
* Claiming: `POST /api/rewards/claim` reads `svc_referral_rewards` only, so milestone rewards cannot be claimed through it (read, not run). No money moves inside the referral service.

## A first step that changes nothing

Size it, read-only: count rows per (`user_id`, `source_id`) where `source_type = 'MILESTONE'` and the count is above 1, on whichever database holds the table. What to do with any duplicates found is for Kam to decide; it is not proposed here.

## Related

KS 1956 (the re-award bug and its repair, pull request 1979), KS 1957 (the owner and role check on the award routes, pull request 1980).

title: originate document signing: a sign, sign-cert or sign-wallet request can answer 500 after the signature or signed document is saved, and a retry duplicates it
description:
**BLUF:** In originate, `POST /api/documents/:id/sign`, `/:id/sign-cert` and `/:id/sign-wallet` can answer 500 after the signature, or the signed derived document, is already saved. A retry then saves a second one. This is pre-existing: it happens the same way for an ordinary Error at base, and pull request 1964 does not cause it. Found by QA gate 149 on PR 1964 (findings G149-F1 and G149-F2).

**What happens** (measured by gate 149: the six real document routes in their own Node process, with an in-memory documents model that rejects AFTER it has applied the write; the identical request is then retried with no fault):

* `POST /:id/sign` (`updateDocument` is the write): the signature is persisted and the status is `signed`, the caller gets 500, and the signing nonce is NOT consumed. A retry with the same body inside the 5-minute nonce window answers 200 and appends a SECOND signature entry (1 signature, then 2).
* `POST /:id/sign-cert` and `POST /:id/sign-wallet` (`saveDocument` is the write): a derived document with status `signed` is persisted, carrying the sigJson or sigWallet envelope. The caller gets 500 and no `document.versioned` event is published. A retry mints a second derived signed document (derived 1, then 2, one event). For sign-cert the orphaned envelope can be fetched from the public `GET /:id/sig-json` route.
* `POST /:id/sign/request`: not affected. Its only write is synchronous and nothing is awaited after it; an orphan nonce expires after 5 minutes.

**Same at base:** with an ordinary `Error('Connection terminated unexpectedly')` at base, and with each of six unreadable thrown values at the head of PR 1964, the persisted state and the retry result were identical in all 288 compared cells. At base an unreadable value was worse: the caller got no answer, and so was just as likely to retry.

**Suggested shapes (from the gate, not chosen here):**

* sign: consume the nonce before the write (delete it, write, restore it on a definite pre-commit failure), or make the append idempotent on (signerId, nonce).
* sign-cert and sign-wallet: an idempotency key, or a deterministic derived id with `conflictMode: 'skip'` keyed on (parent, signature).

**Not tested:** a real PostgreSQL or Prisma client (the documents and lifecycle tables were an in-memory model); a real ambiguous commit (modelled as "write applied, then reject"); the real `authenticate()` and the gateway hop; a real Redis event bus; Node 24 (host Node v26.8.1).

Related: `KS-1831` (the sign route: authorization, revoked status and no signature verified), `KS-1693` (the same sign-cert and sign-wallet routes: no provenance recorded for the derived document).

title: vc-issuer: revoke() swallows a failed DB UPDATE — the route answers 200, the row stays unrevoked, and a restart reloads it as valid
description:
**BLUF:** In vc-issuer, `credentialRepo.revoke()` swallows a failed database UPDATE and keeps the revoke only in memory: the route `POST /api/credentials/:id/revoke` answers 200 "revoked successfully", the database row stays UNrevoked, and after a restart `loadFromDb` loads it unrevoked, so the credential verifies as valid. Measured by gate 152 for an ordinary Error (its scenario C); the restart is read, not run. Pre-existing, not introduced by pull request 1968 ([https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/1968](<https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/1968>)); found by gate 152. Same fail-open family as KS-1958.

## What happens

* `Blockchain/Dev/services/vc-issuer/src/repositories/credentialRepo.ts`: when `revoke()`'s database UPDATE fails, the error is swallowed ("kept in memory"). The credential is revoked in this process's memory only.
* The route answers 200 "revoked successfully" although the database row is unchanged.
* After a restart, `loadFromDb` (the only place memory is filled from the database) loads the row unrevoked, and the credential verifies as valid (read, not run past the restart).

## Measured (gate 152, scenario C)

The real route and repository were run; only `../db` (an in-memory fake table that can fail its UPDATE) and the logger were replaced. With an ordinary Error on the UPDATE: the route answers 200 "revoked successfully", memory is revoked, the database row is not. Base and head (pull request 1968) behave the same.

## A hostile value at the same place (finding G152-F4, read from source and measured for revoke)

For a revoked Proxy or an Error with a throwing `message` getter on that UPDATE, the revoke answers 500 after memory is already revoked, because `revoke()`'s own catch (around line 502) still reads `err?.message` unguarded. Three sibling catches in the same file still do too: `store` (around line 98), `getReadableByHash` (around 324, the by-hash route's path) and `selectList` (around 413, the list route); `db.ts` `probeDb` as well. Those belong to the KS-1868 site list.

## Fix class

Not chosen by the gate. A revoke that cannot reach the database should not answer success; how it should behave (refuse and leave memory unrevoked, or accept and retry) is the same availability-against-fail-closed ruling as KS-1958.

## Limits

Not tested: a real restart, a real Postgres, the revoke route over HTTP beyond the route dispatch used by the sibling suites, Node 24. Related, not the same defect: KS-1295 (`store()` falls back to memory silently), KS-1684 (the creator refused on the memory fallback after a revoke), KS-1899 (`revoke()` has no ownership check of its own).

title: Colour contrast below WCAG AA on 28 page/theme views: Sign in button 2.2:1, Pricing prices 1.63:1 (PS-921's pairs)
description:
**BLUF.** An axe WCAG 2.1 AA scan finds `color-contrast` failures on 28 page/theme views, signed out included: the Login **Sign in** button is white on #06c693 at **2.2:1**, the Pricing prices are #ffc107 at **1.63:1**, and Account settings' Save is 2.2:1. The manual says every refactored surface targets WCAG 2.1 AA. [PS-921](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-921/brand-palette-contrast-secuura-green-06c693-on-white-is-221-and-blue) **(Done, 16 Oct 2026)** listed these same colour pairs, and the systemTest known-debt file still tolerates them under [PS-921](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-921/brand-palette-contrast-secuura-green-06c693-on-white-is-221-and-blue), so this is a possible regression, or [PS-921](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-921/brand-palette-contrast-secuura-green-06c693-on-white-is-221-and-blue) was closed without the colours changing.

**Builds.** Slot 4: platform-s `706e1fea9f405090d1c4a83d2deb59986e3926c3` (tree-identical to `develop` `502fd14acc8711945cc9f322956c90cf9f39e4b3`), platform-k `2d3b3bb3d3865689e3cad843f9ebb90a2f606960`. Personas: signed out, NoTcUser, AccountAdmin ([firstone@lhsg.com](<mailto:firstone@lhsg.com>)), FlowUser (Certification), Admin ([stuart@lhsg.com](<mailto:stuart@lhsg.com>)). Browser: Chromium, 1440 × 900, light then dark.

**Steps to reproduce.**

1. Run axe-core (`AxeBuilder`) with the WCAG 2.1 AA tags and `excludeThirdParty`, the same settings as `systemTest/utils/run_axe.ts`, at 1440 × 900.
2. Scan each page below in the light theme, then the dark theme.
3. Read the `color-contrast` (serious) nodes and their measured ratios.
   (Manual check: on the signed-out Login page, the white "Sign in" label on the green button is visibly faint.)

**Expected (from the docs).**

* `docs/USER-MANUAL.md:363`: "Every refactored surface targets WCAG 2.1 AA: visible focus, full keyboard navigation, ARIA labelling, and status that never relies on colour alone … Light and dark themes ship at equal quality".

WCAG 2.1 AA requires 4.5:1 for normal text (3:1 for large text and UI components).

**Observed.** Identical sets in both re-runs (node counts r1 / r2):

* **Signed out:** Login light (4/4): `login-submit-btn` "Sign in" white on #06c693 **2.2:1**; Forgot password and Resend links #06c693 on white 2.2. Login dark (5/5): Google/Apple labels #0b64f4 on #142034 3.22; cookie-banner links #0366d6 3.01. Register dark (6/6): provider labels 3.22. Forgot password light (2/2) 2.2; dark (3/3) cookie links 3.01. `/contact` dark (1/1): #0063af 2.64. `/pricing` light (3/3): #ffc107 **1.63**; dark (3/3): cookie links.
* **NoTc:** `/TcPrivacy` light (4/4): Terms/Privacy links and the Send button 2.2.
* **AccountAdmin:** `/Flow/Manage` dark (2/2) 3.08; `/Lineage` light (7/7) card call-to-action 2.2; Account settings light (2/2) 1.91 and 2.2; `/support` dark (1/1) 2.64; `/WatermarkTemplate/Index` light and dark (2/2 each) 3.13; Subscription Portal light (13/13) 1.63 and 2.32.
* **FlowUser:** `/Flow/certify` light (1/1) 1.63; dark (1/1) 3.01.
* **Admin:** `/AdminUsers` dark (8/8) 3.01; `/AdminOrganisations` light and dark (1/1) pager 3.97; `/AdminSubscriptions` light (5/5); `/AdminFinance` light (3/3); `/AdminLogs` light (7/6) Information chip 3.68–4.08; `/stripe/products/admin` light (8/8, outline-warning 1.38) and dark (7/7); `/help` dark (1/1); `/Health` dark (2/2) 2.75 and 2.92.
* No other axe rule fired on these pages. 28 page/theme views in all (the explorer's "25" grouped some light/dark pairs).

**How this was concluded.** Found by the area 8 explorer (74 pages × 2 themes); re-run from scratch twice by a separate verifier on the same slot (2/2, identical sets); `USER-MANUAL.md:363` re-read. PS and KS searched for "contrast" (all states, then Backlog, Todo and In Progress separately) and PK "platform-s contrast": no open ticket. [PS-921](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-921/brand-palette-contrast-secuura-green-06c693-on-white-is-221-and-blue) **(Done, 16 Oct 2026)**, "Brand palette contrast: Secuura green #06c693 on white is 2.2:1 and blue #0b64f4 on navy is 3.22:1 …", lists the same pairs (Sign in 2.2, #ffc107 prices 1.63, #aaaaaa 2.32, `badge-success` 3.13, #0366d6 cookie links 3.01/3.08, provider labels 3.22); every one is still measured: **possible regression, or** [PS-921](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-921/brand-palette-contrast-secuura-green-06c693-on-white-is-221-and-blue) **closed unfixed**. `systemTest/config/a11y_known_debt.ts` still tolerates `color-contrast` under [PS-921](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-921/brand-palette-contrast-secuura-green-06c693-on-white-is-221-and-blue), so the debt is pinned to a Done ticket. Related, Done: [PS-1149](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1149/dark-theme-three-labels-are-near-invisible-certificate-expires-in-n), [PS-1223](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1223/axe-findings-on-pages-the-accessibility-sweep-now-covers-about-and), [PS-1298](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1298/identity-standard-domain-verified-badge-colour-3b82f6-fails-wcag-aa), [PS-1017](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1017/dashboard-dark-the-row-view-button-and-the-view-and-download-badge-are).

**Evidence.** Pricing (signed out, light): the yellow prices are the 1.63:1 nodes:

![r1-axe-SignedOut_pricing-light.jpg](https://uploads.linear.app/ee72b345-5a75-4c1a-9bbb-09a6955f4499/58332e62-0afd-4bd8-a61e-e2ec21de9c5e/b2a22a2a-0a27-4976-a4d1-2cf7b9844182)

Also on Peter's machine (`ps-explore-2026-11-02/shots/8-cross-cutting-verify/`): `r?-axe-<persona><route>-<light|dark>.jpg` for every view above, e.g. `r1-axe-SignedOut_Identity_Account_Login-light.jpg`, `r1/r2-axe-AccountAdmin_Identity_Account_Manage-light.jpg`, `r1/r2-axe-AccountAdmin_Stripe_ManageSubscription-light.jpg`.

**Acceptance criteria.**

1. **Product**
   - [ ] Every view listed above has zero `color-contrast` violations at WCAG 2.1 AA in both themes: text at 4.5:1 or better (3:1 for large text), including the primary green button, links, the Pricing prices, cookie-banner links, provider labels, badges, pagers and chips.
   - [ ] Light and dark reach AA alike.
2. **xUnit**
   - [ ] N/A: surface only (colour tokens). If the palette is pinned in a contract test, extend it to the pairs above.
3. **systemTest** (from the mapping, 8-D3; **TOLERATED today**: about 60 `color-contrast` entries in `config/a11y_known_debt.ts` owned by [PS-921](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-921/brand-palette-contrast-secuura-green-06c693-on-white-is-221-and-blue) (Done), all `intermittent: true`, e.g. Login `:225`, Login cookie banner `:223`, Register `:213`, Account settings `:109`, Manage shares `:189`, System health `:218`; swept by `a11y_axe_sweep.spec.ts:61-85` and `a11y_responsive_sweep.spec.ts:68`)
   - [ ] REMOVE the [PS-921](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-921/brand-palette-contrast-secuura-green-06c693-on-white-is-221-and-blue) `color-contrast` entries from `config/a11y_known_debt.ts` (or re-key them to this ticket, never as `intermittent`), and update `tests-unit/a11y_known_debt.test.ts` to match.
   - [ ] ADD `/pricing` to `config/a11y_routes.ts` (the public rows are at `:147-158`, `:271-272`).
   - [ ] The sweep asserts zero serious `color-contrast` violations on every route in both themes; each failing cell lands as `test.fixme('PS-<this ticket>')` until fixed, ticket in the title, Playwright `issue` annotation, Arrange / Act / Assert comments.
   - [ ] Optional: explicit pair checks for the brand colours through `utils/colour_luminance.ts`.

   - [ ] `docs/platform_s_testing_cheat_sheet.html` and `docs/platform_s_testing_architecture_flow_diagrams.html`: the Accessibility coverage says contrast is asserted with no tolerated debt and that Pricing is swept, by area only ([PS-693](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-693/the-testing-docs-exact-test-count-and-mention-list-conflict-on-nearly)).

Stripe products isn't allow-listed for contrast, and its failures are all below the fold at the sweep's 800 px, so the sweep passes it today. This ticket's systemTest criterion, "zero serious `color-contrast` violations on every route", won't cover below-fold text until the sweep can see it.

**Round 11 triage (Stuart, 3 Nov 2026): out of this round, and Steve's decision.**

Every failing pair here is a **brand-palette colour**: Secuura green `#06c693` on white (2.2:1), `#ffc107` prices (1.63:1), the `#0366d6` cookie links, and the `#0b64f4` provider labels on navy. Changing the brand palette (darker greens, or new token values) is Steve's call as owner of the brand-alignment project, so it isn't built in round 11.

2. Whether any surface keeps a brand colour that fails AA on purpose. The manual would then have to name that surface as out of scope.

Once you've decided, this ticket carries the fix. The known-debt entries then move from PS-921 to this ticket, and are removed as each pair passes.
