title: GDPR erasure: a failed kyc or wallet-connector user.erased step leaves the subject's data in place and nothing reports it (dead-letter unread; request already marked completed)
description:
**BLUF:** When the kyc or wallet-connector `user.erased` handler fails, the erasure is left silently incomplete and nobody is told. The shared event bus tries the handler 3 times back to back, then writes one dead-letter entry with the constant text `Failed after 3 attempts` and acknowledges the message. Nothing reads the dead-letter stream and no retry job exists. The data-subject request was already marked completed: originate's erasure marks it completed at step 12, before it publishes `user.erased` at step 13. What stays behind is the subject's data in that service, as measured below.

**What survives, measured by QA gate 147** (the real kyc `index.ts` and wallet-connector `server.ts` handlers through the real shared `EventBus` subscribe loop, with only the database and the bus's Redis client replaced; the subject has one verification, three document images, one consent with IP address and user agent; a second user's rows are never touched). kyc's four deletes run in this order with no transaction: select verifications, delete images by id, delete images by user id, delete consents, delete verifications, then evict the subject key. Each attempt re-runs the whole sequence.

| failure point (fails on every attempt) | attempts | dead-letter entries | left after the dead-letter (images / consents / verifications) |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| kyc: delete images by id | 3 | 1 | 3 / 1 / 1 (everything) |
| kyc: delete consents | 3 | 1 | 0 / 1 / 1 |
| kyc: delete verifications | 3 | 1 | 0 / 0 / 1 |
| wallet-connector: delete sessions | 3 | 1 | every session row for the address |

A failure on the first attempt only (consents once, or the wallet delete once) completes on the second attempt and leaves nothing. By schema (`migrations/002_*.sql` lines 474 to 533 and 813 to 820): the surviving kyc verification holds `provider_application_id`, `provider_check_id`, `liveness_score`, `overall_score`, `risk_level`, `status`, `review_notes` and `documents`; the consent holds the IP address, user agent and timestamps; wallet-connector rows hold the address, wallet type and connected time, all plaintext. Columns written under the subject key (`d1:` envelopes such as `documents` and `review_notes`) are crypto-shredded by originate's step 11. Legacy `v<N>:` kyc rows are under the platform keyring and stay decryptable; that is the same class as `KS-1953`, a different erasure gap (originate lifecycle rows).

**Not new (measured):** an ORDINARY Error at develop's base already leaves exactly this state. PR 1963 (the thrown-value guard on both handlers) does not cause it; it only makes the unreadable-value case behave like the ordinary one (same attempts, same rows erased and left, same dead-letter entry).

**Suggested fix shapes (the gate's, not a decision):**

* a dead-letter consumer or alarm that reopens or flags the data-subject request per service;
* a backoff between attempts, or a re-delivery schedule, instead of three immediate tries;
* wrap kyc's deletes in `transaction()` (the service's `db.ts` already has one) so a failure leaves all or nothing;
* record per-service cascade completion against the request.

**Related (pre-existing, read from source, not run):**

* kyc `dbDeleteUserData` returns 0 when `isDbAvailable()` is false (`index.ts` line 373). The handler then logs `handled` and the bus acknowledges: an erasure silently skipped with no dead-letter. wallet-connector's handler never clears `memConnectedWallets`, so in-memory sessions for the address persist until a restart (gate finding G147-F3).
* The `user.erased` stream entry (user id, request id, `performedBy`, wallet address) is acknowledged but never deleted: `publish` has no XDEL or MAXLEN. A dead-letter copies the raw event into `secuura:events:dead-letter`. So the subject's wallet address stays in Redis after an erasure, whether it succeeded or not (gate finding G147-F4).

**Not tested:** a real Redis (the stream, consumer group, pending list, redelivery after a crash between attempts and the acknowledgement, recovery from a missing group); a real Postgres (the real SQL semantics and the foreign-key cascade are modelled; the timing of the three attempts); a booted service, and the admin HTTP delete path at kyc `index.ts` line 1224, which calls `dbDeleteUserData` directly; originate's publish side end to end; the auth, m365 and other `user.erased` subscribers; backups; Node 24 (host Node v26.8.1).

**Found by:** QA gate 147 on PR 1963, 2026-11-03 (verdict finding G147-F1: HIGH, pre-existing, measured; not caused by `KS-1868`'s PR 1963, not a merge block).

title: transfer approval sweep: when the workflow reads fail, every overdue step is marked timed_out (terminal), including steps set to escalate, so escalations are silently lost
description:
**BLUF:** In the transfer service's escalation sweep (`processEscalations` in `Blockchain/Dev/services/transfer/src/services/approvalWorkflowService.ts`), when the reads that look up a step's workflow fail, every overdue pending step is marked `timed_out`, including steps configured to auto-escalate. `timed_out` is terminal: a later sweep does not select it again and `processApproval` refuses a step that is not pending, so the escalation is silently lost and running the sweep again cannot repair it.

**Cause:** `findWorkflowByStepId` (line 670) reads the workflows through `dbGetActiveWorkflows` (line 238, with a bare `catch { return []; }` at line 243) and then a second `SELECT * FROM svc_approval_workflows` whose failure is swallowed by a bare `catch { /* fall back to active-only */ }`. If both reads fail the workflow is `undefined`, so `stepDef` is `undefined`, the test `stepDef?.autoEscalate && stepDef.escalateTo && !instance.escalatedAt` (line 611) is false, and the `else` branch (lines 622 to 625) sets `status = 'timed_out'`. (The gate cites lines 235 to 243 and 695 to 698 at the PR head; the lines above are at develop `4d1ab2cb6574`, so cite by function name.)

**Measured by QA gate 146** (the REAL transfer service booted as its own Node process for every cell, the real routes and authentication; only the `pg` module replaced, by an in-memory model of the two workflow tables with a unique-id upsert). Setup: 4 overdue pending steps; I1 and I3 on a custom step with `autoEscalate`, `escalateTo: boss-user` and `timeoutHours: 1`; I2 and I4 on the default `step-1`, which times out; `POST /api/workflows/escalate` as a platform administrator. Cell `sweep_wfread`, with the workflow reads failing: the answer is 200 with `{ escalatedCount: 0, timedOutCount: 4 }`. I1 and I3, which should escalate to boss-user, are marked `timed_out`, and a second POST cannot repair them. The result is the same at develop's base and at PR 1962's head, for every kind of failure value including an ordinary Error.

**Effect on approval:** the state refuses rather than grants. The transfer's own execute path gates on the transfer record, not on step instances (`index.ts` lines 802 to 814, read, not run), so nothing this sweep writes can let a transfer proceed. What is lost is the escalation to the named escalation user.

**Suggested fix shape (the gate's, not a decision):** when the step's workflow cannot be found, skip the row and leave it `pending` instead of marking it `timed_out`.

**Related:** a sweep that fails part-way answers `200 success: true` with partial counts and no error indicator (gate finding G146-F4; pre-existing, true at base for an ordinary Error and now for an unreadable value too). The admin caller cannot tell the sweep was incomplete; only a log line says so. Also KS-1881 (the route's platform-admin check, Done) and KS-1868 (PR 1962, unrelated cause).

**Not tested:** a real PostgreSQL (the store is a model; the real WHERE and ON CONFLICT semantics are emulated, not executed); pgbouncer or a mid-statement connection loss; the api-gateway hop to the escalate route (whether and how it is proxied is not traced); a production-mode boot; multi-tenancy pools; Node 24 (host Node v26.8.1).

**Found by:** QA gate 146 on PR 1962, 2026-11-03 (verdict finding G146-F3: recommended follow-up, pre-existing, measured, base = head for every value including an ordinary Error). PR 1962 does not cause it.

title: originate GDPR erasure: a lifecycle event row skipped by the erasure sweep stays decryptable under the platform keyring after the erasure reports completed
description:
**BLUF:** In originate's GDPR erasure, a lifecycle event row that the sweep skips keeps the subject's email recoverable by anyone holding the platform keyring, in live data and in backups, after an erasure that reports `success: true` with the data-subject request marked completed. Step 11 destroys only the subject's own data key (the DEK); lifecycle payloads are encrypted under the platform-wide `v<N>:` keyring (`encodeLifecyclePayload` calls `encryptField`, `Blockchain/Dev/services/originate/src/utils/lifecyclePayloadCodec.ts` lines 34 to 38), not under it. Step 5d skips a row when `decodeLifecyclePayload` reports `payloadUnavailable` (`Blockchain/Dev/services/originate/src/services/gdprService.ts` lines 688 to 690). The deletion log and the DSR record say nothing about the skipped row; the only trace is one error line carrying the event id.

**Not new (measured):** an ORDINARY decrypt error at develop's base already leaves the same row in the same state (a key version that is not loaded). PR 1961 (the thrown-value guard) does not cause this. It routes the unreadable-value case into that same ordinary state; before it, a hostile throw aborted the whole erasure loudly (`success: false`, DSR left open), and that abort was not atomic: the earlier steps and rows had already been written. The old state was also not a real remedy, because a retry hits the same row and aborts again (read, not run).

**Measured by QA gate 145** (the real `executeErasure`, the real lifecycle codec, the real `SubjectDekProvider`, real AES-GCM `encryptField` / `decryptField` / `encryptFieldWithDek` with keys generated in-process, the real winston logger; only the database replaced by an in-memory SQL stand-in). E2 is a lifecycle row holding the subject's email whose decrypt fails; after the erasure the whole platform keyring (v1 + v2) is loaded and E2 is tried.

| version | failure on row E2 | erasure result | DSR completed | subject DEK destroyed | row E2 rewritten | E2 decrypts with the platform keyring | E2 still holds the subject email |
| -- | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- |
| base | none (control) | success | yes | yes | yes | yes | no |
| base | ordinary decrypt error | success | yes | yes | no | yes | YES |
| base | unreadable thrown value | `success: false` ("Erasure failed") | no | no (DEK still live) | no | yes | YES |
| head (PR 1961) | none (control) | success | yes | yes | yes | yes | no |
| head (PR 1961) | ordinary decrypt error | success | yes | yes | no | yes | YES |
| head (PR 1961) | unreadable thrown value | success | yes | yes | no | yes | YES |

Head with an unreadable value equals base with an ordinary error in every column. In the success rows the log says `Erasure completed`; the deletion log does not mention E2.

**Why step 11 cannot shred it:** `executeErasureImpl` step 11 (`gdprService.ts` lines 893 to 894) calls `subjectDeks.destroyDek(userId)`, which sets the wrapped DEK to NULL in `pii_subject_keys` (`Blockchain/Dev/packages/shared/src/crypto/subjectDek.ts`). No lifecycle payload depends on that key. The shared module's own comment in `Blockchain/Dev/packages/shared/src/crypto/encryptedField.ts` says the `v<N>:` format "makes single-subject erasure impossible to guarantee in backups (there is no per-subject key to destroy)". After a completed erasure the skipped row can still be decrypted by `listLifecycleEvents` (`lifecycleEventRepo.ts` line 138, tenant-scoped document listing), which would show the email to whoever can list that document's events (read, not run).

**Retry does not reach it (read, not run):** `payloadUnavailable` is read only at line 690. A second erasure looks up the subject email at step 5c from a users row that step 10 already set to a placeholder of the form `deleted_<id>` at the `anonymized.local` domain, so it cannot match the address inside E2, and nothing else revisits the row.

**Suggested fix shapes (the gate's, not a decision):**

* (a) count skipped rows, and do not mark the DSR plainly `completed` while any remain; record them in the deletion log as `skipped` with the event ids; and/or
* (b) move lifecycle payloads to the subject-DEK (`d1:`) envelope so that step 11 shreds them, as the KS-291 design does for users, consents and DSRs.

**Not tested:** the live PR body; a real Postgres or Prisma client (the SQL stand-in answers by statement prefix, so the real SQL semantics of the other steps are not exercised); a real Key Vault or production keyring (keys were generated in-process); whether a real decrypt ever throws an unreadable value (none is known; Node crypto throws Errors); the HTTP routes (`POST /api/gdpr/erasure/:userId`, `executeErasureByExternalRef`) and a booted service; a second erasure run against the same subject; `listLifecycleEvents`; backups; Node 24 (host Node v26.8.1).

**Related:** KS-537 (lifecycle payload encryption and erasure), KS-291 (the subject-DEK design for users, consents and DSRs), KS-1868 (PR 1961, unrelated cause).

**Found by:** QA gate 145 on PR 1961, 2026-11-03 (verdict finding G145-F1: recommended follow-up, HIGH priority for data protection, pre-existing, measured).

title: api-gateway: with Redis unavailable, enforceDocumentTypeRules passes every document (catalogue reads empty), so MFA-required types are allowed
description:
**BLUF:** When `isRedisAvailable()` is false (every Redis outage: an ordinary error on the client, a socket `close`, or the 4th retry), `enforceDocumentTypeRules` (`Blockchain/Dev/services/api-gateway/src/services/enforcement.ts`, called at `routes/verification.ts` line 856) reads an EMPTY document-type catalogue on every replica (`documentTypesStore` is only written while the flag is false), `resolveDocumentType` returns null, and the "catalogue empty" branch returns `{ ok: true, docType: {} }`. A document type registered with `requireMFA: true` is then allowed.

**Measured by QA gate 144** (real `redis.ts`, `enforcement.ts` and winston; only `ioredis` replaced; two replicas sharing one store): a type registered with `requireMFA: true` is REFUSED with 403 `MFA_REQUIRED` while the flag is true, and ALLOWED on both replicas while the flag is false, with Redis up or down, at develop's base AND at PR 1960's head after an ordinary Error. Evidence: `logs/probe_site3_table.log`, enforce block, rows `base trigger=ordinary` and `head trigger=ordinary`: `ALLOWED ok:true docType={}` on replica A and B, with `down=0` and `down=1`.

**By reading, not run:** the same pass-through skips the `isActive` check, the verification-level check (`creatorVerificationLevel`), the auth-provider check (`allowedAuthProviders`), the metadata-schema check (`metadataSchema`) and the approval-workflow gate (`createWorkflowInstanceIfRequired` sees no `requiresApproval`).

**Where it sits at develop** `4d1ab2cb6574`**, read by the filer:** `resolveDocumentType` calls `redisService.getAllDocumentTypes()` at `enforcement.ts` line 72; `enforceDocumentTypeRules` reads the catalogue again at line 126 and returns `{ ok: true, docType: {} }` at lines 117 and 137, where the code comment says an empty catalogue means "never seeded, or Redis TTL expiry". The gate cites `enforcement.ts` lines 78 and 128; the statements I read are at lines 72 and 126, so cite them by function name.

**Reach:** every Redis blip in production puts the gateway in this state (an ordinary error, `close`, or retry 4). PR 1960 (the `redis.ts` error listener and `initRedis` catch) does not cause it and does not change it; it makes the unreadable-value path land in the same state an ordinary Error already reaches.

**Not tested:** a real Redis or `ioredis` client (a stand-in was used; the `ioredis` emit, close and retry path was read in `node_modules` 5.11.1, not run); a booted gateway over HTTP (the middleware and `enforceDocumentTypeRules` were called directly); `createWorkflowInstanceIfRequired` and the `isActive`, verification-level, provider and schema skips under fallback (read, only the MFA rule was run); admin routes in fallback; Node 24 (host Node v26.8.1).

**Suggested fix shape (the gate's, not a decision):** in fallback mode `enforceDocumentTypeRules` should refuse with 503 instead of treating an unreadable catalogue as an empty one, as the connector-create and connector-info readers already do (`routes/verification.ts` line 795 and `services/health.ts` line 54, which gate 144 read as answering 503 when the flag is false).

**Related:** KS-1256, KS-1540, KS-1532, KS-1627 (readers of the same flag); KS-1466 (untyped creates never meet the catalogue's document rules: a different defect); KS-1868 (PR 1960, unrelated cause).

**Found by:** QA gate 144 on PR 1960, 2026-11-03 (verdict finding G144-F1: recommended follow-up, HIGH, pre-existing, measured).

title: originate retention sweep: give each policy's unit a real per-statement bound in both modes (SET LOCAL statement_timeout and lock_timeout right after BEGIN)
description:
**BLUF:** the originate retention sweep has no real per-statement time bound. In single-tenant mode each policy's unit (PR 1945, KS 1943) runs under Prisma's default interactive-transaction timeout of 5000 ms, and that timeout does not cancel a blocked statement; in multi-tenant mode there is no bound at all (QA gate 127 verdict on PR 1945, G127-F1). Candidate: `SET LOCAL statement_timeout` and `lock_timeout` right after BEGIN, in both branches of `withPlatformScopeTransaction` (originate `src/db.ts`). Filed on Wednesday's instruction (ANSWER 2026-11-02 12:51:19Z). The values and the multi-tenant change are decided when this is worked, not now.

**Evidence** (QA gate 127 verdict on PR 1945: FINDINGS G127-F1 and G127-F2, and section Q3; measured on a throwaway PostgreSQL 15 with all 58 repo migrations, as the non-superuser app role):

* Prisma checks the timeout only when the next query or the COMMIT is issued, so it does not cancel an in-flight statement (G127-F1).
* With a superuser holding `FOR UPDATE` on the expired user_sessions rows, the single-tenant DELETE sat `active / Lock:transactionid` for 7.5 s and more, holding RowExclusive and tuple locks. The sweep settled only after the lock was released, at about 9.06 s. Then the unit rolled back: 3 rows remaining, no log row, no stamp, the other 4 policies stamped, and afterwards 0 idle-in-transaction backends and 0 app locks (G127-F1, Q3).
* Multi-tenant mode has no timeout: the unit waited, then committed after the release (G127-F1).
* Base (develop `0e3a9b65cdd6`) behaves the same in both modes, so PR 1945 makes nothing worse (G127-F1).
* In single-tenant mode a policy whose unit exceeds the timeout does all its work and then rolls back on every run, so it never progresses. Base already had this for the DELETE alone (G127-F2).

**Unmeasured:** live table sizes, so whether any live policy's unit comes near 5 s is unknown; pgbouncer in the path; the right values.

**To decide when worked:** the two values; the multi-tenant behaviour change (multi-tenant has no bound today, so adding one changes its behaviour and needs a ruling, per G127-F1).

**Board search before filing** (read-only, 2026-11-02, Seat E 29th): the control term `withPlatformScopeTransaction` found KS 1943. `statement_timeout`: 3 hits, KS 1582 and KS 1587 (a transaction-local timeout on the auth users read, the nearest precedent) and KS 1585 (another gate's follow-up); none covers the retention units. `SET LOCAL`: KS 1582, KS 1587. `enforceRetention`: KS 1938, KS 1943, KS 1944, none of them a bound. `lock_timeout`, `retention timeout`, `retention sweep timeout`, `interactive-transaction timeout` and `transaction timeout`: 0 hits.

**Related:** PR 1945, [https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/1945](<https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/1945>) (KS 1943), open and not merged when this was filed.

title: systemTest: Outlook add-in and signed documents — "Signatures on record", the signed-package note, stripped Content Credentials and the attach-name check are not tested through the task-pane mock
description:
## Status (3 Nov 2026): partly done; the ✅ parts are on develop in `c1499536` (#1339, merged 14:28 UTC); stays In Progress

| Item | Status |
| -- | -- |
| 1: one row per signature mode, with the "Secuura's record" caveat | ✅ passed on the project branch |
| 2: an unsigned registered document shows no signature rows | ✅ passed on the project branch |
| 4: a stripped Content Credentials image keeps its row and shows the note | ✅ passed on the project branch |
| 3: the `.asics` sentence | ⬜ not done yet |
| 5: another organisation's bytes add no row | ⬜ not done yet |
| 6: the attach name, with no download recorded for the skipped duplicate | ⬜ not done yet |

* **Evidence:**
  * `outlook_signed_documents.spec.ts` 5/5 on slot 4 (commits `8e0e08d0`, `40b692fe`), after earlier reds while the spec was corrected.
  * **Full systemTest run**, slot 4 at `74eb96d4`: 8 failed (all pre-existing, [PS-1432](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1432/health-is-administrator-only-health-healthdata-healthprobek-and), none in this spec) · 3,212 passed · 24 skipped.
* **Waiting on:** nothing outside this work.
* **Still to do:** items 3, 5 and 6, on a new branch from develop once PR [PS-1441, PS-1444, PS-1438, PS-1439, PS-1002, PS-1447, PS-1448, PS-1528, PS-1530: systemTest coverage, Nov 2026 (full run 8 failed, all pre-existing PS-1432)](https://linear.app/secuura/review/ps-1441-ps-1444-ps-1438-ps-1439-ps-1002-ps-1447-ps-1448-ps-1528-ps-a72057cef772) has merged (it has: `c1499536`). The project branch and its worktrees are deleted; the next branch starts from develop.

---

## BLUF

Now that any file type can be signed, the Outlook add-in's Verify pane lists the signatures Secuura recorded on an attachment. It also explains a signed package (`.asics`) and says when an image's Content Credentials were stripped in transit. Separately, it checks a document's real attachment name before attaching, so a document already on the message is not attached again ([PS-1320](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1320/outlook-add-in-show-the-signatures-secuura-recorded-on-a-verified) to [PS-1323](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1323/outlook-attach-know-the-attachments-real-name-before-fetching-so-a)).

xUnit and the add-in's own unit tests cover these. The systemTest suite covers only the attach and its 409 refusal (`signed_package_outlook.spec.ts`). Nothing checks, end to end against a real slot, what the pane tells a recipient.

Priority Medium: the add-in is an optional deployment feature.

## What the feature does, in the docs' words

From `docs/USER-MANUAL.md` §6 (*Verifying from Microsoft Outlook*):

> The pane lists the signatures Secuura recorded on the attachment: how it was signed, by whom, when, and whether it was timestamped. This is Secuura's record, not a check of a signature file. A file sent from Secuura with a separate signature arrives as a **signed package** (`.asics`). The pane checks the document inside it; the signature file it carries is checked on the Verify page. An image whose Content Credentials were removed in transit is still found, and the pane says that copy no longer carries them.

From `docs/outlook-addin/PS-1042-signed-documents.md`:

> **Signatures on record** … each signature is one row, worded as the web Verify page words it: "Separate signature file (.p7s)", "Signature inside the PDF", "Signature inside the Office file" or "Content Credentials inside the image", then the signer, the date and "timestamped".

> \[For a `.asics`\]: "This is a signed package (.asics). Secuura checked the document inside it, `minutes.docx`. The signature file it carries is checked on Secuura's Verify page."

> The real name is known before the fetch ([PS-1323](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1323/outlook-attach-know-the-attachments-real-name-before-fetching-so-a)). … The panel asks for it first, so a document already on the message is skipped **before** the fetch that records a download.

> Identical bytes registered in another organisation never contribute a signature.

## Already tested (no change needed)

* **systemTest:**
  * `signed_package_outlook.spec.ts`: the attach returns the named package, and a swapped `.p7s` is refused with 409;
  * `outlook_backend.spec.ts` and `outlook_taskpane_mock.spec.ts`: the gate, the hand-off page and the pane mock.
* **xUnit:** `SignedPackagingTests`, `OutlookVerifySignatureRecordTests`.
* **vitest:** `asics.test.ts`, `verify.test.ts`.

## Acceptance tests

Through the task-pane mock against a slot (the same way `outlook_taskpane_mock.spec.ts` runs). Written from the docs, not the product code. Each carries `(PS-1444)` in its title and an `issue` annotation.

1. **One signature row per mode:** an attachment of a document signed in each of the four ways (PDF inside, Office inside, image with Content Credentials, separate `.p7s`) shows **Signatures on record**:
   * the caveat that it is Secuura's record, not a check of a signature file;
   * one row per signature, with that mode's wording, the signer, the date and "timestamped".
2. **Unsigned:** an unsigned registered document shows no signature rows.
3. **Signed package:** a `.asics` from the add-in's own attach is checked by the document inside it, and the pane shows the signed-package sentence naming that document.
4. **Stripped Content Credentials:** a signed image with its Content Credentials stripped is found as the earlier version. Its Content Credentials row says this copy no longer carries them.
5. **Another organisation:** identical bytes registered by a second organisation add no signature row.
6. **Attach name:** attaching a detached-signed document uses the `.asics` name. A document already on the message is skipped, and no download is recorded for it (check the access log or Lineage).

## Related: the different-name note (added 2 Nov 2026)

Today a registered document attached under Secuura's own download name, such as "… (signed).pdf" or "… (watermarked).pdf" ([PS-1244](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1244/download-watermarked-copy-and-download-original-save-under-the-same)), shows the [PS-723](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-723/verify-still-confirms-if-filename-has-changed) note "this attachment has a different name" in the pane. That is a false alarm, reported by Phil on UAT. [PS-1435](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1435>) (round 11) fixes it in the pane and on the web Verify page. Once it lands:

* any test here that verifies a signed or watermarked copy by its download name should expect **no** name note;
* a genuinely renamed copy still shows the note.

## Not tested, and why

* **The live add-in inside Microsoft Outlook:** it needs Microsoft 365, and Microsoft-backed features are recorded as Not tested. Only the backend and the task-pane mock are exercised.

## Test classification (systemTest)

* **Areas:** `@area-outlook`, `@area-integrity`, `@area-certify`
* **Feature:** `@verify`, `@certify`
* **Type:** `@regression`
* **Roles:** `@role-power`
* **Smoke:** not `@smoke`

## Sources

* `docs/USER-MANUAL.md` §6, *Verifying from Microsoft Outlook*
* `docs/outlook-addin/PS-1042-signed-documents.md`
* Feature tickets [PS-1320](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1320/outlook-add-in-show-the-signatures-secuura-recorded-on-a-verified), [PS-1321](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1321/outlook-add-in-recognise-a-signed-package-asics-attachment), [PS-1322](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1322/outlook-verify-say-when-a-matched-image-no-longer-carries-its-content), [PS-1323](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1323/outlook-attach-know-the-attachments-real-name-before-fetching-so-a)
* Signing any file type in the web app is [PS-1433](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1433/systemtest-sign-any-file-type-is-a-new-feature-ps-1042-946-t111-and)

title: systemTest: onward sharing stops five deep — PS-1367 T1.9 still asserts only "some hop is refused"; assert the documented limit, the missing Share onward and the refusal sentence
description:
## BLUF

A document shared onward can now be passed on at most five times below the owner's own share. The fifth person down is not offered **Share onward**, and a forced attempt is refused with a named sentence ([PS-1395](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1395/share-onward-the-maximum-re-share-chain-depth-and-its-refusal-are-not), documented 30 Oct 2026).

The existing test was written before the limit was documented. It still only searches for *some* hop that is refused. This ticket asks it to assert the real limit and wording.

Priority Low: the limit works today and the test does catch a missing limit. It just cannot catch the wrong one.

## What the feature does, in the docs' words

From `docs/USER-MANUAL.md` §6 (*Sharing a document*):

> A chain of onward shares is at most five deep below your own share: the fifth person down cannot pass it on again, so **Share onward** is not offered to them, and an attempt to share it anyway is refused with "{document} has already been shared on too many times."

[PS-1395](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1395/share-onward-the-maximum-re-share-chain-depth-and-its-refusal-are-not) measured the refusal at hop 7 on 28 Oct: hop 1 is the owner's share, and hops 2 to 6 are the five onward shares.

## Today's test

`systemTest/tests/functional/lineage_share_requests.spec.ts`, "[PS-1367](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1367/systemtest-share-from-lineage-the-certification-user-and-certify-with) T1.9 · a chain has a maximum depth ([PS-1395](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1395/share-onward-the-maximum-re-share-chain-depth-and-its-refusal-are-not))". It probes up to 10 hops and passes when any hop is refused. Its header comment says the limit is not yet documented. It now is.

## Acceptance tests

Change T1.9 (keep its [PS-1367](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1367/systemtest-share-from-lineage-the-certification-user-and-certify-with) and [PS-1395](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1395/share-onward-the-maximum-re-share-chain-depth-and-its-refusal-are-not) annotations, and update the comment):

1. The owner shares with onward sharing allowed.
2. Five recipients in turn each share it on (View, onward allowed). Every one of those five shares is accepted.
3. The fifth recipient down is **not** offered **Share onward** in Lineage or in their inbox row menu.
4. An attempt to share it anyway (a direct request, as the test does today) is refused with "{document} has already been shared on too many times.", with the document's name in place of {document}.
5. The fourth recipient down **is** still offered **Share onward** (the control, so the test cannot pass by never offering it).

## Test classification (systemTest)

* **Areas:** `@area-sharing`
* **Feature:** `@sharing`, `@lineage`
* **Type:** `@bva`, `@validation`, `@regression`
* **Roles:** `@role-account-admin`, `@role-power`, `@role-user`
* **Smoke:** not `@smoke`

## Sources

* `docs/USER-MANUAL.md` §6, *Allow recipients to share this onward*
* [PS-1395](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1395/share-onward-the-maximum-re-share-chain-depth-and-its-refusal-are-not) (the measurement and the documented answer)
* [PS-1367](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1367/systemtest-share-from-lineage-the-certification-user-and-certify-with) T1.9

title: systemTest: Credentials — a self-signed credential must not verify as AUTHENTIC, and the Your Identity card's "Verified by" line, are not tested
description:
## BLUF

Until 27 Oct 2026, anyone could sign a credential with their own key, name Secuura as the issuer, and the public **Verify credential** check (signed out, no account needed) answered **AUTHENTIC** ([PS-1375](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1375/rotation-tooling-for-the-at-rest-keys-retired-slots-in-deployments-re)). That is fixed in the code, and xUnit holds the rule. But the public check itself, the thing an outside verifier actually calls, has no test that tries a forged credential.

This ticket also covers the **Your Identity** card, which now names each credential and says who verified the person ([PS-1383](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1383/identity-wallet-a-held-credential-shows-its-raw-type-name)).

Priority High: a forged credential reading AUTHENTIC to the public is the most costly mistake this area can make.

## What the feature does, in the docs' words

From `docs/IDENTITY-LAYER.md`:

> **Credentials this platform issued are checked against this platform's issuer keys (**[PS-1375](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1375/rotation-tooling-for-the-at-rest-keys-retired-slots-in-deployments-re)**).** … Until [PS-1375](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1375/rotation-tooling-for-the-at-rest-keys-retired-slots-in-deployments-re) verification trusted that key as given, so a credential anyone signed, naming any issuer, verified as AUTHENTIC on the anonymous `POST /verify/credential`. Now a credential verifies only when its key is the current issuer key or a retired one still listed …, and it names this issuer.

From `docs/USER-MANUAL.md` §7:

> The **Your Identity** card (on Your details, and on the *Verifiable credentials* tab beside Signing certificates) lists the credentials you hold by name, such as *Identity verification*. When a check by an outside provider issued the credential, the card also says who verified you: **Verified by** *Stripe Identity* or *Microsoft Entra Verified ID* ([PS-1383](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1383/identity-wallet-a-held-credential-shows-its-raw-type-name)).

## Already tested (no change needed)

* `credential_verify.spec.ts`:
  * an unknown hash is a clean not-found;
  * a non-credential is INVALID;
  * a genuine credential is AUTHENTIC, and a tampered one is INVALID;
  * the presentation round-trip, and a wrong challenge.
* `identity_wallet.spec.ts`: the card and the tab load.

## Acceptance tests

Written from the docs, not the product code. Each carries `(PS-NNNN)` in its title and an `issue` annotation.

**A. A forged credential is not AUTHENTIC** (signed out, `@public`)

1. A credential built by the test, signed with a key the test generates, naming this platform as issuer, is **not** AUTHENTIC on `POST /verify/credential`. The answer says the issuer is not trusted, never a 500.
2. A genuine credential from this platform, with its proof's key swapped for the test's own key, is **not** AUTHENTIC.
3. The genuine credential still reads AUTHENTIC (the control, so the two tests above cannot pass because everything fails).

**B. The Your Identity card**

1. The KYC persona (`@persona-kyc`), verified through Stripe Identity in test mode, sees its credential listed by name (for example *Identity verification*), with **Verified by** *Stripe Identity*.
2. The same card on the *Verifiable credentials* tab beside Signing certificates shows the same lines.
3. A person holding no credential sees no "Verified by" line.

## Deliberately left to xUnit

* [PS-1380](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1380/presentation-proof-is-verified-against-its-own-didkey-not-bound-to-the) (a presentation signed by someone else's key) and [PS-1384](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1384/credential-verify-by-hash-answers-from-an-arbitrary-credential-a) (which credential answers for a document's hash when there are several) are rules. [PS-1384](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1384/credential-verify-by-hash-answers-from-an-arbitrary-credential-a) says in its own text that the two-credential case belongs in xUnit, not the suite. No browser test is asked for here.

## Not tested, and why

* **Verified by *Microsoft Entra Verified ID*:** Microsoft-backed features are recorded as Not tested on every slot and live.

## Test classification (systemTest)

* **Areas:** `@area-identity`, `@area-integrity`
* **Feature:** `@identity`, `@verify`
* **Type:** `@validation`, `@regression`
* **Roles:** `@public`, `@persona-kyc`, `@role-user`
* **Smoke:** not `@smoke`

## Sources

* `docs/IDENTITY-LAYER.md`: *Credentials this platform issued are checked against this platform's issuer keys*
* `docs/USER-MANUAL.md` §7
* `docs/runbooks/rotate-identity-issuer-signing-key.md`
* Feature tickets [PS-1375](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1375/rotation-tooling-for-the-at-rest-keys-retired-slots-in-deployments-re) (phase 4), [PS-1383](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1383/identity-wallet-a-held-credential-shows-its-raw-type-name)

title: systemTest: Timestamps — falling through to the next of the three authorities, and a timestamp added afterwards when all three fail, are not tested in a browser
description:
## Status (3 Nov 2026): partly done; the ✅ parts are on develop in `c1499536` (#1339, merged 14:28 UTC); stays In Progress

| Part | Status |
| -- | -- |
| A: Health shows all three authorities working | ✅ passed on the project branch (slot 2, normal; and in the full run) |
| B: fall-through to the next authority | ✅ passed on the project branch (slot 2, `TSA_URL_1` closed). Stands down `[env]` in a normal full run, by design. |
| C1: all three down, the signature is saved and the confirmation says a timestamp will be added | ✅ passed on the project branch (slot 2, three different closed addresses). Stands down `[env]` in a normal full run, by design. |
| C2–C6: the timestamp added later, Verify on the earlier copy, the `.p7s` case, Content Credentials not retried | ⬜ not done yet |
| D: the `timestamp` event never sent to platform-k (`@k-live`) | ⬜ not done yet (needs C2's event first) |
| The 168-hour give-up | 🚫 not tested (needs a week, or a seam) |

* **Evidence:**
  * `timestamp_authorities.spec.ts`, with `utils/timestamp_authority_probe.ts` (unit 6/6), commits `f3e0758b` and `c1026959`.
  * **Full systemTest run**, slot 4 at `74eb96d4`: 8 failed (all pre-existing, [PS-1432](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1432/health-is-administrator-only-health-healthdata-healthprobek-and), none in this spec) · 3,212 passed · 24 skipped; A passed, B and C1 stood down `[env]`.
* **Waiting on:** [PS-1542](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1542/local-only-test-switch-to-close-the-timestamp-authorities-for-one) (Stuart), a per-organisation switch so B, C1 and C2–D run in every full run. Not blocking: the slot-restart route still works.
* **Still to do:**
  * explain why the retry gave up on C1's signature (Health showed "Signatures left without a timestamp: 1");
  * then C2–C6 and D, on a new branch from develop once PR [PS-1441, PS-1444, PS-1438, PS-1439, PS-1002, PS-1447, PS-1448, PS-1528, PS-1530: systemTest coverage, Nov 2026 (full run 8 failed, all pre-existing PS-1432)](https://linear.app/secuura/review/ps-1441-ps-1444-ps-1438-ps-1439-ps-1002-ps-1447-ps-1448-ps-1528-ps-a72057cef772) has merged (it has: `c1499536`). The project branch and its worktrees are deleted; the next branch starts from develop.

---

## BLUF

Every signature now asks three independent timestamp services in turn (DigiCert, then GlobalSign, then Sectigo). If all three are down, the signature is still saved and the timestamp is added automatically later. Nothing in the suite checks either behaviour in a running app. A signature without a timestamp is what made every signature on every environment untimestamped until 13 Oct 2026 ([PS-1207](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1207/pdfsigningtsaurl-is-httpstimestampdigicertcom-in-every-template-but)), and nobody noticed for weeks.

This ticket asks for browser tests of the fall-through and the later timestamp. Priority Medium: signing still works without these tests; they protect the evidence a signature carries.

Signing non-PDF files is a separate ticket ([PS-1433](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1433/systemtest-sign-any-file-type-is-a-new-feature-ps-1042-946-t111-and)) and is not repeated here.

## What the feature does, in the docs' words

From `docs/signing-formats-design.md` (*One timestamp service, three authorities*, and *The timestamp added afterwards*):

> DigiCert, GlobalSign and Sectigo … three independent operators, asked in order … a token is accepted only when it answers this exact request and comes from a trusted timestamping certificate; otherwise the next authority is asked. … Each signature records the authority that stamped it.

> When every authority fails at signing time, the signature is saved without a timestamp and … queued; the signer's confirmation says one will be added automatically. … after 5, 15 and 30 minutes, then hourly, until … 168 hours after signing, when it gives up and the Health page counts it.

> **Detached (**`.p7s`**):** the `.p7s` is replaced … while the document is unchanged. **PDF** and **Office:** the timestamped file is a new signed copy … and a download serves it. Either way the ledger gains a `timestamp` event (actor: Secuura, automatic) … **never sent to platform-k**.

> The copy signed before the timestamp arrived may already have been downloaded; Verify still recognises it as **Signed** (not current). Verify says when a timestamp was added after signing: it proves the signature existed by then, not at the signing time. Content Credentials are not retried.

From `CLAUDE.md`: the Health page has one "Timestamp authority N" row per authority. `TSA_URL_1` in a slot's `.env` replaces the first authority to exercise the fall-through, and `TSA_URL_1..3` together close all three.

## Already tested (no change needed)

* **xUnit:** `TimestampAuthorityTests` covers the rules: the order, the trust check, and the never-anchored verb.
* **systemTest:** nothing drives a signature through a failing authority.

## Acceptance tests

Written from the docs, not the product code. Each carries `(PS-1439)` in its title and an `issue` annotation. These tests need the slot started with different timestamp addresses, so they cannot share a run with tests that expect normal timestamps. Say in each test which slot setting it needs, and stand it down `[env]` when that setting is absent.

**A. Health shows all three**

1. On a normal slot, an Administrator sees three "Timestamp authority" rows on the Health page, each reporting a working timestamp.

**B. Fall-through to the next authority**

1. With only the first authority closed (`TSA_URL_1`): signing a PDF succeeds and the signature carries a timestamp.
2. The Health page shows authority 1 failing and authorities 2 and 3 working.

**C. All three down: the timestamp arrives later**

1. With all three closed: signing a PDF still succeeds, and the signer's confirmation says a timestamp will be added automatically.
2. With the authorities working again, within the first retry window (5 minutes) the document gains the timestamp:
   * its ledger and Lineage show a **timestamp** event by Secuura, automatic;
   * **Download** serves the new timestamped copy.
3. Verify on the copy downloaded **before** the timestamp arrived reads **Signed** (not current).
4. Verify says the timestamp was added after signing.
5. The same for a detached `.p7s` (a .txt or a .docx with Office embedding off): the document's hash is unchanged and the `.p7s` download is a new file.
6. An image signed with Content Credentials while all three are down gets no later timestamp.

**D. Never sent to platform-k** (`@k-live`, with K slot N up)

1. The `timestamp` event has no anchor and never appears in platform-k's records for the document.

## Not tested, and why

* **The 168-hour give-up and its Health count:** it needs a week of wall-clock time, unless a seam ages the signature (as [PS-1265](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1265/systemtest-mintexpiredshare-never-produces-an-expired-share-the-edit)'s seam ages a share). Record it as Not tested until such a seam exists.

## Test classification (systemTest)

* **Areas:** `@area-certify`, `@area-integrity`, `@area-admin`, `@area-k-integration`
* **Feature:** `@certify`, `@verify`, `@lineage`
* **Type:** `@regression`, `@k-live` (part D only)
* **Roles:** `@role-power`, `@role-admin`
* **Smoke:** not `@smoke`

## Sources

* `docs/signing-formats-design.md`: Timestamps ([PS-1207](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1207/pdfsigningtsaurl-is-httpstimestampdigicertcom-in-every-template-but)), One timestamp service, three authorities ([PS-1209](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1209/timestamping-as-one-service-three-tsas-in-order-and-an-automatic-retry)), The timestamp added afterwards ([PS-1209](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1209/timestamping-as-one-service-three-tsas-in-order-and-an-automatic-retry) *phase 2)*
* `CLAUDE.md`: *Timestamps come from ONE service, over three authorities, over http*
* Feature tickets [PS-1207](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1207/pdfsigningtsaurl-is-httpstimestampdigicertcom-in-every-template-but), [PS-1209](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1209/timestamping-as-one-service-three-tsas-in-order-and-an-automatic-retry)
* Open neighbour: [PS-1359](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1359/timestamp-retry-orphans-the-superseded-p7s-nothing-names-it-so-it), the superseded `.p7s` left orphaned by the retry

title: systemTest: Document encryption card — its status lines, Re-encrypt through to Completed, the emails it sends, the Account Admin rule and the 30-day key destruction are not tested in a browser
description:
## Status (3 Nov 2026): partly done; the ✅ parts are on develop in `c1499536` (#1339, merged 14:28 UTC); stays In Progress

| Part | Status |
| -- | -- |
| A: the card's status lines | ✅ passed on the project branch |
| B: re-encrypt asks first, reaches Completed, the document opens throughout, the account admin is emailed once | ✅ passed on the project branch |
| C: rotate asks first; Cancel changes nothing | ✅ passed on the project branch (Cancel, not Escape: [PS-1471](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1471/document-encryption-rotate-key-confirmation-ignores-escape-and-opens)) |
| F1: the dissolve impact summary's 30-day key sentence | ✅ passed on the project branch |
| D: only the Account Admin role acts | ⬜ not done yet |
| E: the key-unavailable email | ⬜ not done yet |
| F2: the destruction itself, 30 days later | 🚫 not tested (30 days of wall-clock time) |

* **Evidence:**
  * `settings_document_encryption_lifecycle.spec.ts` 3/3 together on slot 3 (commit `19327249`).
  * **Full systemTest run**, slot 4 at `74eb96d4`: 8 failed (all pre-existing, [PS-1432](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1432/health-is-administrator-only-health-healthdata-healthprobek-and), none in this spec) · 3,212 passed · 24 skipped.
* **Waiting on:** [PS-1471](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1471/document-encryption-rotate-key-confirmation-ignores-escape-and-opens) (Escape in the confirm dialog). The tests use Cancel until it lands; it is not blocking.
* **Still to do:** D and E, on a new branch from develop once PR [PS-1441, PS-1444, PS-1438, PS-1439, PS-1002, PS-1447, PS-1448, PS-1528, PS-1530: systemTest coverage, Nov 2026 (full run 8 failed, all pre-existing PS-1432)](https://linear.app/secuura/review/ps-1441-ps-1444-ps-1438-ps-1439-ps-1002-ps-1447-ps-1448-ps-1528-ps-a72057cef772) has merged (it has: `c1499536`). The project branch and its worktrees are deleted; the next branch starts from develop.

---

## BLUF

Every organisation's documents are now encrypted under the organisation's own key. The **Document encryption** card on *View / Edit Organisation Settings* lets an account admin rotate that key, re-encrypt everything after a suspected breach, or bring their own key. The suite already tests the panel, rotation, the authenticator-code gate on re-encrypt, the "key unavailable" message and the key-use audit.

What it does not test is the part a customer relies on in a breach:

* re-encryption actually finishing (*Completed*);
* the emails telling every account admin and Secuura;
* the card's status lines;
* that only the *Account Admin* role can act;
* the warning that a dissolved organisation's key is destroyed after 30 days.

Priority High: this is the platform's documented breach response (`docs/BREACH-RESPONSE.md`).

## What the feature does, in the docs' words

From `docs/USER-MANUAL.md` §8:

> The panel shows where the key came from, when it was created, its current version and when it was last rotated, whether it is enabled, and how many of your documents are still on the older platform-wide key while the migration moves them. It never shows the key itself.

> An account admin of the organisation (the *Account Admin* role — being the main contact, or an organisation admin, is not enough on its own) can act on the key from that card.

> **Re-encrypt every document** … It **starts at once** — nobody at Secuura has to approve it — so it asks for a current code from your authenticator app, and every account admin of the organisation and Secuura are emailed that it has started and by whom. The card shows how many documents are left and says *Completed* when it has finished.

> When that happens \[the key cannot be used\], every account admin of the organisation and Secuura are emailed (at most once an hour) naming the key that stopped working.

> Rotate and re-encrypt each ask you to confirm first.

> The panel also shows **Migration failures**: documents of yours that the background move onto the organisation's key could not complete — they still open as before.

From §10, *Dissolve*:

> The organisation's document encryption key is destroyed 30 days after it is dissolved (the impact summary says so).

On dev-ps (2 Nov 2026), a new organisation's card reads:

* Key source *System*; Last rotated *never*;
* Rotation *Never rotated — 0 to move.*; Re-encryption *Never re-encrypted.*; Status *Enabled*;
* *Documents still on the platform key: 0. … Migration failures: 0.*

## Already tested (no change needed)

* `settings_document_encryption.spec.ts`: the panel, the timestamp helper, version and last-rotated, no key material shown, the plain-user gate.
* `document_key_rotation.spec.ts`: documents open through a rotation; re-encrypt needs a valid code; an Administrator can act on any organisation; the plain-user gate.
* `document_key_byok.spec.ts`: the Local store refuses an import; the warning comes first; the plain-user gate.
* `document_key_unavailable.spec.ts`: the one sentence on every surface while the key is disabled, and recovery.
* `document_key_use_audit.spec.ts`: an open records a key use.

## Acceptance tests

Written from the docs, not the product code. Each carries `(PS-1438)` in its title and an `issue` annotation.

**A. The card's status lines**

1. For a new organisation, the card shows the lines listed above, with the values a new organisation has.
2. After one rotation: *Last rotated* is a date (through the house timestamp format), *Rotation* counts what is left to move, then 0, and *Versions in use* lists the versions still in use.

**B. Re-encrypt, all the way through**

1. An account admin enters a valid authenticator code and presses **Re-encrypt now**. They are asked to confirm first; cancelling changes nothing.
2. On confirm, the card shows how many documents are left and then *Completed*.
3. A document opens before, during and after the re-encryption.
4. In Mailpit, every account admin of the organisation and the Secuura address each receive one email saying it started and by whom.

**C. Rotate key asks first**

1. **Rotate key** asks for confirmation. Cancelling leaves *Last rotated* unchanged; confirming changes it.

**D. Only the Account Admin role acts**

1. An organisation admin who does not hold the *Account Admin* role sees the card but no **Rotate key**, **Re-encrypt now** or **Use your own key…**.
2. A direct POST from that user is refused.
3. The same holds for a main contact without the role. (Today's tests cover only the plain user.)

**E. Key unavailable: the email**

1. With the key disabled (the seam `document_key_unavailable.spec.ts` already uses), each account admin and Secuura are emailed once, naming the key.
2. A second failure within the hour sends no second email.

**F. Dissolution**

1. An Administrator dissolving a single-member organisation sees, in the impact summary, that the organisation's document encryption key is destroyed 30 days after it is dissolved.
2. The 30-day destruction itself is **Not tested** (it is a scheduled job 30 days later).

## Not tested, and why

* **Bring your own key, propose → adopt by a second person → cancel:** needs a hardware vault (AWS KMS or Azure Key Vault). The Local store on a slot refuses an import, and that refusal is already tested. See `docs/runbooks/byok-onboarding.md`.
* **The "Recent changes" lines from** [PS-1375](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1375/rotation-tooling-for-the-at-rest-keys-retired-slots-in-deployments-re) (*Blockchain connector key re-encrypted under the current platform key*, *Signing certificate re-encrypted under the current platform key*): an operator's platform-key rotation produces them, and a suite run does not perform one.

## Test classification (systemTest)

* **Areas:** `@area-org`, `@area-admin`, `@area-email`, `@area-access-control`
* **Feature:** `@organisation`, `@two-factor`
* **Type:** `@crud`, `@validation`, `@regression`
* **Roles:** `@role-account-admin`, `@role-organisation`, `@role-user`, `@role-admin`
* **Smoke:** not `@smoke`

## Sources

* `docs/USER-MANUAL.md` §8 (*Document encryption* card, *Responding to a data breach*) and §10 (*Dissolve*)
* `docs/BREACH-RESPONSE.md`
* `docs/document-key-hierarchy.md`
* `docs/runbooks/byok-onboarding.md`
* Feature tickets [PS-948](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-948/organisation-document-encryption-keys-system-generated-or-customer), [PS-955](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-955/customer-supplied-organisation-key-byok), [PS-956](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-956/organisation-key-rotation-re-wrap-and-optional-document-re-encryption), [PS-957](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-957/key-lifecycle-disablerevoke-erasure-dissolution-audit-docs-and-runbook)

Each test runs on a throwaway organisation, signed in as that organisation's own account admin. Re-encryption needs an authenticator, and enrolling one rotates the security stamp, so a shared persona can't be used. Expectations come from USER-MANUAL.md §8 and §10.

| Part | Status |

| A1/A2: the card's first state, Last rotated in the house timestamp format | ✅ |
| C1: Rotate asks first; Cancel changes nothing | ✅ (Cancel, not Escape: PS-1471) |

**Results:** 3 passed, 0 failed on slot 3 (5.7 min), all three run together on the final code. Before that, B was red three times while two test-side problems were fixed. Both fixes are in `pages/document_key_rotation_handler.ts` and the spec:

**Docs:** both testing HTML files name the spec (`74eb96d4`). The full systemTest run is still to come.

title: systemTest: Document storage — moving older files, environments that never store with Secuura, Dropbox and Box, and the "storage not responding" messages are not tested in a browser
description:
## Status (3 Nov 2026): not started on `project/systemtest-coverage-nov26`, stays In Progress

* **Not started:** none of A, C, E or F2 was built on the November branch; that branch went to PR [PS-1441, PS-1444, PS-1438, PS-1439, PS-1002, PS-1447, PS-1448, PS-1528, PS-1530: systemTest coverage, Nov 2026 (full run 8 failed, all pre-existing PS-1432)](https://linear.app/secuura/review/ps-1441-ps-1444-ps-1438-ps-1439-ps-1002-ps-1447-ps-1448-ps-1528-ps-a72057cef772) without it.
* **Already decided:** B, D ("not responding", "full") and F1 went to Stuart as [PS-1532](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1532/local-slots-cannot-reach-three-storage-states-ps-1437-must-test-an); F3 is [PS-1409](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1409/storage-providers-provision-the-first-providers-app-credentials-and).
* **Waiting on:** nothing outside this work for A, C, E and F2. They are testable on the fake-cloud seam every slot runs.
* **Still to do:** A, C, E and F2, on a new branch from develop once #1339 has merged (it has: `c1499536`). The project branch and its worktrees are deleted; the next branch starts from develop.

---

## BLUF

Organisations can now keep their documents in their own storage instead of on Secuura's disk (merged to `develop` 29 Oct 2026, #1200). The suite already tests the main journey: connect, use the new location, reconnect, Amazon S3, and who may change it. It does **not** yet test four things a customer will meet:

1. moving files that were stored before the organisation connected its own storage ([PS-1403](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1403/move-an-organisations-existing-files-off-secuuras-disk-into-its));
2. an environment that never keeps documents itself ([PS-1391](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1391/customer-storage-only-a-deployment-can-be-configured-never-to-store));
3. what people see when the storage stops working;
4. Dropbox and Box.

This ticket asks for browser tests of those. Priority High: these are customers' documents, and a mistake here loses access to them.

## What the feature does, in the docs' words

From `docs/USER-MANUAL.md` §8, *Document storage*:

> Everyone who can open the Settings page sees the current location — **Secuura-hosted** by default, or the connected storage with its account, folder, status, who connected it and when it was last checked. Only an **account admin** of the organisation … can change it.

> Nothing changes for your documents until you choose **Use this location** and confirm. From then on new documents are stored there … documents already stored stay where they are and still open.

> **Disconnect** removes Secuura's access … a location that still holds files cannot be disconnected until they are moved, and the card shows how many each location holds.

> If a document's storage is not responding, is full, needs reconnecting, or no longer has the file, every place you open it says which — and someone you shared it with is told only that it is temporarily unavailable.

> Account admins are also emailed once if the person who connected the storage leaves the organisation. If the organisation is closed, Secuura deletes its files from your storage where it still can … then removes its access, before the organisation's key is destroyed.

Files from before you connected storage ([PS-1403](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1403/move-an-organisations-existing-files-off-secuuras-disk-into-its)):

> Once your storage is in use, the card says how many there are and offers **Move them to** your storage … every document keeps opening throughout. While that runs the card says "Being moved". A file Secuura's records name but its disk no longer holds cannot be moved; it is counted and skipped, and the rest still move.

Environments that never store documents with Secuura ([PS-1391](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1391/customer-storage-only-a-deployment-can-be-configured-never-to-store)):

> There the card shows **No storage connected** until an account admin connects storage and chooses **Use this location**, with a warning that nothing can be saved until then; there is no "Switch back to Secuura-hosted" … Until storage is chosen, uploading, signing, watermarking and adding a watermark image are refused with: "Your organisation has no document storage connected, and this service does not keep documents itself, so nothing was saved. An account admin can connect storage in Organisation settings › Document storage." (an automatic flow step waits with that message and carries on once storage is chosen).

## Already tested (no change needed)

`settings_document_storage.spec.ts`, `settings_document_storage_lifecycle.spec.ts`, `settings_document_storage_s3.spec.ts`:

* connecting fake-cloud and storing a new document there;
* a refused consent;
* a provider that is switched off;
* a personal workspace;
* the role gates;
* revoke and reconnect in place;
* emptying a location before it goes;
* S3 through an assumed role.

## Acceptance tests

Each test is written from the docs above, not from the product code. Each carries `(PS-1437)` in its title and an `issue` annotation.

A. Moving files from before ([PS-1403](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1403/move-an-organisations-existing-files-off-secuuras-disk-into-its))

1. An organisation with documents on Secuura's disk connects fake-cloud and chooses **Use this location**. The card shows how many documents are still on Secuura's disk and offers **Move them to** the connected storage.
2. Pressing it shows *Being moved*, then a count of 0. One of those documents opens before, during and after the move.
3. A document registered after the move opens, and is stored in the connected location.
4. If the slot can produce a record whose file is missing on disk: that file is counted and skipped, and the rest still move. If it cannot without editing the disk by hand, record this check as **Not tested** with the reason.

B. An environment that never stores with Secuura ([PS-1391](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1391/customer-storage-only-a-deployment-can-be-configured-never-to-store))

Needs a slot set up that way. The setting is decision 11 in `docs/storage-connector-model.md`.

1. The card shows **No storage connected**, with the warning that nothing can be saved, and no *Switch back to Secuura-hosted*.
2. Registering a document, signing, watermarking and adding a watermark image are each refused with the exact sentence quoted above.
3. A flow whose automatic step needs storage waits with that message, then carries on once an account admin connects storage and chooses **Use this location**.
4. After that, registering a document works.

**C. Disconnect while files remain**

1. **Disconnect** is refused while the location still holds files, and the card shows how many each location holds.
2. After **Move files** (or Switch back plus a move), Disconnect succeeds.

**D. When the storage stops working**

1. For each failure the fake-cloud seam can produce (not responding, full, needs reconnecting, no longer has the file), opening the document from View, Download, Sign and Watermark names that failure.
2. A share-link recipient (signed out) is told only that the document is temporarily unavailable.
3. Where the seam can revoke access: every account admin is emailed **once** (checked in Mailpit), and the card and each account admin's dashboard say so.
4. Nothing is silently moved back to Secuura's disk.

**E. People leaving, and closing the organisation**

1. When the account admin who connected the storage leaves the organisation, the card warns, and each remaining account admin is emailed once.
2. When the organisation is closed, its files in fake-cloud are deleted and its access removed.

**F. Dropbox and Box**

1. With Dropbox or Box switched on for the slot, **Choose a location** lists it with its own line on what the organisation then owns.
2. With it switched off, it is not listed.
3. The full connect journey against a real Dropbox or Box test account runs only once such accounts exist (credentials are [PS-1409](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1409/storage-providers-provision-the-first-providers-app-credentials-and)'s job). Until then it is **Not tested**, with that reason.

## Not tested, and why

* **Microsoft OneDrive and SharePoint:** Microsoft-backed features are recorded as Not tested on every slot and live.
* **Real Dropbox and Box accounts:** none are provisioned yet ([PS-1409](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1409/storage-providers-provision-the-first-providers-app-credentials-and)).

## Test classification (systemTest)

* **Areas:** `@area-org`, `@area-documents`, `@area-sharing`, `@area-email`
* **Feature:** `@organisation`, `@upload`, `@sharing`
* **Type:** `@crud`, `@validation`, `@regression`
* **Roles:** `@role-account-admin`, `@role-organisation`, `@role-user`, `@role-admin`, `@public` (the share-link recipient)
* **Smoke:** not `@smoke`

## Sources

* `docs/USER-MANUAL.md` §8, *Document storage*
* `docs/storage-connector-model.md`
* Feature tickets [PS-1075](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1075/organisation-chosen-document-storage-the-account-admin-sets-where), [PS-1079](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1079/account-admin-document-storage-configuration-menu-choose-secuura), [PS-1081](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1081/dropbox-storage-provider-dropbox-api-v2-app-folder-access-first), [PS-1083](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1083/box-storage-provider-box-content-api-oauth-2), [PS-1084](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1084/customer-hosted-storage-lifecycle-changing-provider-disconnect-revoked), [PS-1391](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1391/customer-storage-only-a-deployment-can-be-configured-never-to-store), [PS-1403](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1403/move-an-organisations-existing-files-off-secuuras-disk-into-its)

title: staking: POST /api/stake takes address and amount from the caller, so any signed-in user can create or grow a stake position for any address
description:
**BLUF:** `POST /api/stake` (`services/staking/src/routes/stake.ts:189-245`) takes `address` and `amount` from the request body and saves a stake position for that address with no ownership or chain check. By the same shape, the unstake routes (`POST /api/stake/unstake` `:263`, `POST /api/stake/complete-unstake` `:317`) also take the address from the body; they were not read line by line. So any signed-in caller can create or grow a stake position for any address. `txHash` is optional and is logged but never verified. KS 1942's design treats `svc_stake_positions` as NOT a trusted stake source for this reason.

## Where (develop `0e3a9b65cdd6`; read from source, NOT run)

* Mount: `services/staking/src/index.ts:80` applies `jwtAuthenticate()` to `/api`, and `:82` mounts the stake routes at `/api/stake`. Any signed-in caller reaches them.
* `routes/stake.ts:189-245`: the handler parses `StakeSchema` from `req.body` (`:191`), takes `{ address, amount, txHash }` (`:196`), loads the position for that address (`:199`), adds `amount` to it or creates it (`:213-228`), and saves it (`:230`). It also adds to the in-process pool stats (`:233-236`).
* `req.user` is not read anywhere in `routes/stake.ts`. `txHash` is optional in the schema (`:33`), and its only other use is the log line (`:243`).

## Why it matters

KS 1942 (the governance register route takes stake from the caller) is being fixed by making stake and roles admin-set only. Its design rejected `svc_stake_positions` as a stake source because this route lets any caller assert any position.

## Not checked

The unstake and complete-unstake handlers line by line. Whether the gateway restricts `/api/stake` to a role. Whether any client other than the tests calls these routes. Whether the Aiken staking validator is meant to be the source of truth (no service reads it).

## Related

KS 1942 (governance register route, same class). KS 1845 (covers only the admin listing `GET /api/stake/all`, not these routes).

## Searched first

Board search over issue content and comment bodies:

* "svc_stake_positions" and "routes/stake.ts" find KS 1845 (an issue covering only `GET /api/stake/all`) and a KS 1544 comment.
* "POST /api/stake" finds comments on KS 188, KS 256 and KS 492, about business-rule refusals and OpenAPI examples on `/unstake` and `/complete-unstake`, not ownership.

title: auth seeder: no test drives ADMIN_USER_PASSWORD='' through requiredSeedPw, so changing || null to ?? null (a blank password on the cross-tenant SYSTEM_ADMIN) keeps ks949 green; the KS-966 F1 guard never scans env.example
description:
**BLUF:** the only thing between an unset `ADMIN_USER_PASSWORD` and a **blank-password seed of the cross-tenant SYSTEM_ADMIN** is one operator, `process.env[envVar] || null` (`Blockchain/Dev/services/auth/src/repositories/userRepo.ts` :1371, used for the admin at :1407), and no test in the repository drives `ADMIN_USER_PASSWORD=''` through it. If that read were changed to `?? null`, docker-compose's empty-string default (`${ADMIN_USER_PASSWORD:-}`) would become a seeded blank password, and the whole ks949 suite would stay green. Separately, the `KS-966 F1` guard in the same suite never scans the canonical template `Blockchain/Dev/env.example` (no leading dot), so a future non-empty `ADMIN_USER_PASSWORD=` there would not be seen by it. Both are pre-existing. Found by QA gate 119 on PR 1937 (KS-1081), which neither introduces nor relies on either. Proposed work, from the gate's two findings: add `ADMIN_USER_PASSWORD: ''` cells to `ks949-platform-admin-seed-identity.test.ts` so that `|| null` to `?? null` goes red, and widen the KS-966 F1 guard's walk to `env.example`.

## What I read (develop `777643aa6e1a`)

* `userRepo.ts` :1371 `const requiredSeedPw = (envVar: string): string | null => process.env[envVar] || null;` and :1407 `password: requiredSeedPw('ADMIN_USER_PASSWORD')`. A null password takes the `account.password === null` branch (:1670).
* `docker-compose.yml` :810-815 records the dependency in a comment: the `:-` default delivers an empty string, which is safe only because the seeder reads it as `|| null`; a change to `?? null` "would become a seeded blank password on the cross-tenant SYSTEM_ADMIN".
* `services/auth/src/__tests__/ks949-platform-admin-seed-identity.test.ts`: `runSeed(env)` is at :115, and every `ADMIN_USER_PASSWORD` in the file is `undefined` (:408-500); there is no `ADMIN_USER_PASSWORD: ''` anywhere in it.
* The guard `KS-966 F1 - no .env.example ships an admin password value` is at :505-575. Its walk matches `e.name === '.env.example' || e.name.endsWith('.env.example')` (:533). `'env.example'.endsWith('.env.example')` is false (checked in node; control: `'.env.example'.endsWith('.env.example')` is true). The guard's other read is the legacy `Blockchain/Dev/.env.example` (:573).

## Reported by QA gate 119 (PR 1937), not re-run here

* A copy of the ks949 suite with `''` at all 9 `ADMIN_USER_PASSWORD` sites: every behavioural cell behaves as with `undefined`. The mutant `?? null` against the original suite: survives (29 pass). The same mutant against the `''` copy: 6 cells go red (admin reported, hints, id/email-row remediation). The seeder ran with a mocked database, not PostgreSQL.
* PR 1937's own shell suite does catch a non-empty `ADMIN_USER_PASSWORD=` in `env.example`, so the template has cover once that pull request merges; the older guard keeps the naming gap.
* The gate also suggests the same `''` family for `DEMO_SECUURA_PASSWORD`.

## Related, not duplicates

KS-967 (2026-09-07, "Neither credential guard can see a value in a .env.example"; written before `env.example` became the canonical template, and it does not mention the no-dot name or an empty-string cell), KS-986 (`requiredSeedPw` returns null when `ALLOW_DEFAULT_SEED_PASSWORDS=true` is set; a different problem), KS-1081 (the template ruling).

## Not known

* Nothing was run against PostgreSQL or a booted auth service.
* Whether any other reader of `ADMIN_USER_PASSWORD` uses `??` (the gate reports none in the tree).

title: third-party verifier approve: a throw after the UPDATE leaves the verifier active with a stored key hash and answers 500 without the one-time key; re-approve answers 404 (thirdPartyVerifiers.ts lines 172-201)
description:
**BLUF:** in the approve handler (`Blockchain/Dev/services/originate/src/routes/thirdPartyVerifiers.ts` :158-203, read at develop `c70f339063ee`) the UPDATE that sets `status = 'active'` and writes `api_key_hash` (:172-181) runs before the one-time key is returned (:192-197). If anything after the UPDATE throws, the catch (:198-201) answers 500 with no key, and the verifier is left active with a stored key hash that nobody holds. Approving again cannot recover it: the UPDATE only matches `status = 'pending'` (:180) and a zero-row result answers 404 (:183-188). Pre-existing, and it holds for an ordinary Error as well.

## What I read (develop `c70f339063ee`)

* `generateApiKey()` and `hashApiKey()` run first (:168-169); the UPDATE follows (:172-181, `WHERE id = ... AND status = 'pending'`); then `logger.info` (:190); then `res.json({ success: true, message: 'Verifier approved', apiKey, note: 'Store this API key securely. It will not be shown again.' })` (:192-197).
* The key exists only in that response body; only its hash is stored.
* The catch (:198-201) logs and answers the constant 500 `Failed to approve verifier`. Nothing undoes the UPDATE.
* Within `services/originate/src`, the only write of `api_key_hash` is that UPDATE (:175) and the only read is the `/verify` lookup by key hash (:328). The router's routes are register, list, approve, suspend, reinstate, verify and records; none issues a new key. I did not check outside `services/originate/src` (admin tooling, other services, manual SQL).

## Reported by QA gate 118 (PR 1936), not re-run here

With the real handler on a loopback listener and a statement recorder: in the cell that throws after the write (`approve | after`) the UPDATE is issued once (status `'active'` and `api_key_hash` written) and the answer is 500 with no key, for an ordinary Error at the base and at the head; the success cell returns the key, and the sha256 of that key equals the hash in the recorded UPDATE. Pull request 1936 does not change which paths return the key. The earlier gate that raised this as candidate G104-F3 read it from the source.

## Not known

* Nothing was run against a real PostgreSQL.
* No trigger for a throw at that point is identified in the code (a logger call, building the response); how likely it is in production is not measured.
* Whether another path can give an active verifier a new key.
* No fix is proposed here.

title: originate nominate and register: the duplicate (409) branch tests error.code === '23505', which the single-tenant Prisma 7 client may never raise, so a duplicate would answer 500 (signatories.ts:126, thirdPartyVerifiers.ts:103)
description:
**BLUF:** the duplicate branch of signatories nominate (`Blockchain/Dev/services/originate/src/routes/signatories.ts` :126-130) and third-party verifiers register (`.../routes/thirdPartyVerifiers.ts` :103-107) answers 409 only when `error.code === '23505'` (read at develop `c70f339063ee`). In single-tenant mode originate's `prisma` is a Prisma 7 client on `@prisma/adapter-pg`, and the adapter turns pg 23505 into a `UniqueConstraintViolation` kind, not into an error whose `code` is `'23505'`. If the client then surfaces it under a Prisma code (QA gate 118 reports `P2010` or `P2002`), a duplicate nomination or registration in single-tenant mode would answer the constant 500 and log the Prisma message instead of 409 CONFLICT. **Read from the installed runtime, NOT run; the first step is a measurement.** Pre-existing; pull request 1936 (KS-1868) keeps the same test.

## What I read (develop `c70f339063ee`, and the installed package in a worktree)

* Nominate inserts with `((req as any).db || prisma).$executeRaw` (`signatories.ts` :87); register the same (`thirdPartyVerifiers.ts` :72). The catches test `error.code === '23505'` and answer 409 (`signatories.ts` :126-129, "This user is already an authorised signatory for this organisation"; `thirdPartyVerifiers.ts` :103-106, "A verifier with this email is already registered").
* A unique key exists for each: `signatories` `UNIQUE(organization_id, user_id)` and `third_party_verifiers` `contact_email ... UNIQUE` (`migrations/001_initial-schema.sql` :827 and :836). Later migrations 009, 011, 012, 038 and 039 touch these tables (row-level security, tenant id); I did not read them for constraint changes.
* Single-tenant `prisma` is built with the adapter: `services/originate/src/db.ts` :138-140 (`new PrismaPg({ connectionString })`), under `MULTI_TENANCY_ENABLED` not `'true'` (:22). With `MULTI_TENANCY_ENABLED=true`, `req.db` is `getRequestPrisma(req)` over the tenant pg pool (`services/originate/src/index.ts` :226-235), where node-postgres puts `code: '23505'` on the error.
* Installed `@prisma/adapter-pg` 7.8.0, `dist/index.js` :472-478: `case "23505"` returns `kind: "UniqueConstraintViolation"` with the constraint fields.

## Reported by QA gate 118 (PR 1936), not verified by me

That the Prisma client surfaces such a raw-query driver error as a `PrismaClientKnownRequestError` with code `P2010` or `P2002`. The client runtime that does that mapping is not installed in the worktree I read, so I could not check this half.

## Not known

* Nothing was run: no real PostgreSQL, no booted originate, no duplicate request.
* Which environments run single-tenant mode.
* No fix is proposed here.

title: POST /api/gdpr/retention/enforce answers 200 "Retention enforcement complete" when the policy read or a policy failed, and its count is not a policy count (routes/gdpr.ts lines 625-636)
description:
**BLUF:** the SYSTEM_ADMIN route `POST /api/gdpr/retention/enforce` (`Blockchain/Dev/services/originate/src/routes/gdpr.ts` :625-636, read at develop `91ccb1553f02`) answers `200 {"success":true,"message":"Retention enforcement complete. N data types processed.",...}` even when the policy SELECT failed or a policy failed in the middle of the sweep, and `N` cannot tell "nothing had expired" from "the sweep could not read its policies". Pre-existing; an ordinary Error reaches it, not only an unreadable thrown value.

## What the source does (read, develop `91ccb1553f02`)

* The route awaits `gdpr.enforceRetention()` and answers `` res.json({ success: true, message: `Retention enforcement complete. ${logs.length} data types processed.`, deletionLog: logs }) `` (:627-632). Only a throw reaches `fail500` (:633-635).
* `enforceRetentionImpl` (`services/gdprService.ts` :438-507) never throws for a database failure: the per-policy catch (:498-500) and the outer catch (:502-504) only log, and the function returns `logs` (:506).
* So when the policy SELECT (:442-444) fails, the outer catch logs and returns an empty list: the route answers 200, "0 data types processed". When one policy fails mid-sweep, that policy is missing from `logs`, the others carry on, and the route still answers 200 "complete".
* `logs.length` counts only policies whose `affected > 0` and whose deletion-log INSERT returned a row (:484-490). It is not a count of policies, nor of policies that failed.
* The other caller, `services/retentionScheduler.ts` :40-58 (`runEnforcement`), reads the same resolved list and logs `Enforcement complete` or `Enforcement complete — no records required processing`; its own catch is reached only if `enforceRetention` throws.

## Reported by QA gate 117 (PR 1935), not re-run here

Measured with the real route handler on a loopback listener and a statement recorder: for an ordinary Error and a string the SELECT failure answers 200 "0 data types processed" at the base and at the head, and an Error on `DELETE user_sessions` answers "2 data types processed". PR 1935 moves the unreadable-value cases onto this existing answer; it does not change it.

## Not known

* Not run against a real PostgreSQL or a booted originate.
* Whether any client or operator procedure reads the message or `success` as proof the sweep ran is not checked.
* No fix is proposed here (the route could report failed policies, or answer a non-200 status; not decided).
