title: nginx sends /analytics/ straight to the analytics service, so a revoked-session token still works there and the gateway's rate limits and audit are skipped
description:
**Read from code at develop** `e43a289c1c7b`**, not run against a stack.** Found while checking `ARCHITECTURE.md` for KS-1807 PR-4 and re-read by me.

**What the code does.** All three nginx configs route `/analytics/` straight to the analytics service, not through the api-gateway: `location /analytics/ { set $svc_analytics "analytics:4010"; rewrite ^/analytics/(.*)$ /$1 break; proxy_pass http://$svc_analytics; }` in `docker/nginx-gateway/nginx.conf`, `nginx-production.conf` and `nginx-demo.conf`. The analytics service guards `/api/*` with the shared `authenticate()` (`services/analytics/src/index.ts`, `app.use('/api', jwtAuthenticate())`), and that middleware (`packages/shared/src/middleware/index.ts`) only verifies the RS256 signature and expiry of the bearer token. It does not consult a session store.

**What the gateway does that this path skips.** The session-revocation check (`SESSION_INVALIDATED`, `services/api-gateway/src/middleware/auth.ts`), the gateway's rate limiters and its audit middleware. So a token whose session was ended (logout, eviction, admin revoke, erased user) keeps working on `/analytics/...` until the token itself expires (1 hour by the code default, 1 day as the local compose file sets it), and calls on that path are not counted by the gateway limiters or recorded by its audit middleware.

**Searched.** No analytics route has a role gate (searched `services/analytics/src/routes` for `requireRole`, `requireAdmin` and `role`: no hit; positive control: the same directory's route files exist and mount handlers), which is KS-1856's finding for exports. This ticket is the separate point that the route to the service avoids the gateway at all.

**Not established.** Whether the deployed demo and kintsugi edges use these configs or put another proxy in front (the VM runs Caddy in front of the compose nginx per the project notes); whether anything in the portals actually calls `/analytics/`: I found no literal `/analytics/` in `frontend/*/src`, so it may be reachable but unused. Whether the gateway's own CSRF check matters for a bearer-token caller (it is skipped for any bearer token anyway).

**Related.** KS-1856 (analytics exports readable by every caller), KS-1855 (gateway stand-ins), KS-1846 (scope drift), KS-1758 (the gateway's own revocation check fails open when the session store is down; this ticket is the case where the check is not on the path at all), KS-1280 (a revoked session's bearer forwarded past the gateway check).

**Docs.** `ARCHITECTURE.md` will state the real entry point and the bypass in KS-1807 PR-4; the behaviour itself is not fixed by the docs series.

title: Reconciler R7 not built: non-final anchor rows with a placeholder hash are never settled on a real-chain box (census needed first)
description:
## BLUF

**Rule R7 of the KS-1384 recovery table (design rev 2 §9) is not built, and the KS-1384 train will not build it.** A non-final `anchor_store` row (`pending`, `submitting` or `submitted`) whose hash is a placeholder (`mock_tx_`, `tx_sim_`, `mock_batch_tx_`) is never settled by anything on a real-chain box today: the reconciler skips any hash that is not 64 hex (`services/anchoring/src/reconciler.ts:123` at F0c's head `dfc0dd61d75e`), and no other code writes it. Rev 2 §9 says such a row, when no process is driving it, should be written `failed` with KS-587's wording, with no chain call.

Facts only. No row, box or code was touched.

## Why it is a ticket and not part of KS-1384 F-b

Wednesday ruled on 2026-10-30 (ANSWER 07:03:15Z to Seat W 13th) that F-b PINS today's behaviour for R7 and does not add the write:

* it would be a new terminal write class on a real-chain box, outside F-b's listed scope (rev 4 §4.3 and §14);
* it would touch kintsugi-shaped rows (KS-1751) with no census of the rows it would change;
* a `failed` row is what Platform S parks and re-reads, so the write has an external effect.

F-b's cell (j) row R7 pins exactly that: the reconciler never chain-checks and never writes a fabricated non-final row.

## What building it needs first

1. **A read-only census on each box**: the count of non-final rows with a placeholder hash, by status, `simulated` flag and age. KS-1751 measured kintsugi's FINAL simulated rows (two `simulated = true` and `confirmed`); the non-final population is not measured anywhere I could find.
2. A ruling on the wording and on whether a `simulated = false` placeholder row (the KS-587 incident shape) is treated the same.
3. The same "not driven" rule F-b introduces (the in-memory driving set), so a row a live mock-mode process is still writing is never touched.

## Searched before filing (board search over title, description and comments, archived included; controls: a literal in archived KS-336 found, a nonsense token 0)

* `KS-587`: 30 issues; `fabricated`: 44. Read the closest:
  * **KS-1751** is the kintsugi rows that are simulated AND confirmed: FINAL rows, a different shape.
  * **KS-683** is the consumer-side standoff over `failed` rows: no K-side settling write.
  * **KS-587**, **KS-520** and **KS-522** are the honest-labelling work on read paths and the demo corpus.
* `never chain-checked`, `fabricated hash on a real-chain`, `non-final fabricated`, `KS-587 owns`: 0 each.

Refs KS-1384, KS-1751, KS-587.

title: oauth GET /authorize: for an app registering '*', an array redirect_uri still answers 500 (generateConsentPage: s.replace is not a function)
description:
**BLUF:** `GET /api/oauth/authorize` still answers 500 `server_error` when `redirect_uri` arrives as an array (`?redirect_uri=a&redirect_uri=b`, or `redirect_uri[]=https://evil.example/cb`) **for an app whose** `redirectUris` **holds** `'*'`. The redirect check (`routes/oauth.ts` line 268) is `!app.redirectUris.includes(redirectUri) && !app.redirectUris.includes('*')`, so the wildcard lets the array through; per gate 37, `new URL(array)` then stringifies it, `generateConsentPage` calls `escapeHtml` on it, and an array has no `replace`: `s.replace is not a function`. Latent: the census on KS-797 (2026-09-05) counted 0 of 21 registered apps holding the wildcard on both environments, and nothing unsafe is emitted (no `Location`, no consent page, nothing minted). Found by QA gate 37 on pull request 1834 (finding F2); the same class as KS-1797, whose guard covers `state` and `code_challenge` only.

**Where.** `Blockchain/Dev/services/auth/src/routes/oauth.ts`, the `GET /authorize` handler. It reads seven query fields (`client_id`, `redirect_uri`, `response_type`, `scope`, `state`, `code_challenge`, `code_challenge_method`), casts them all to `string`, and type-checks only `state` and `code_challenge` (KS-1797); a repeated `scope` is refused separately (KS-1219). The KS-1797 description lists the other parameters as arrays under "Not probed"; this is the first measured one.

**Measured, and by whom.** Gate 37's probes H16 (repeated `redirect_uri`) and H17 (`redirect_uri[]=https://evil.example/cb`) at head `d261b3cfa9c7`, on an app that registers `'*'`, under the test file's mocks and no real database (gate 37's NOT TESTED list). Verdict: `/Volumes/DevMASTER/WEDNESDAY/0_Brain/reference/2026-10-30_gate37-1834/verdict.md`, F2. The filing seat read the handler and line 268 and did not re-run the probes.

**Fix shape, not chosen here.** One `typeof` guard over all seven fields ahead of the resolver, instead of one guard per field, with a cell per field in the bracket and repeated forms. It is deliberately not part of pull request 1834.

**Not known.** Whether any registered app holds `'*'` today (the 0-of-21 figure is from 2026-09-05 and neither gate 37 nor the filing seat re-measured it); real Postgres behaviour. Related: KS-1797 (open); the archived KS-797 holds the census.

title: 253 catch and log sites read a thrown value unguarded (X instanceof Error ? X.message : String(X)) across 15 services: one safeReason(e) helper would cover the class
description:
## BLUF

253 non-test sites under `Blockchain/Dev/services` read a thrown value with `X instanceof Error ? X.message : String(X)`, and none of them is guarded against a thrown value whose property read or string conversion itself throws (a revoked Proxy, an Error whose `message` getter throws or returns a hostile object). What a throw there does depends on where the site sits; the read is unguarded at all 253. One helper, `safeReason(e)`, that reads and coerces inside a single `try` and returns a constant fallback would cover the class. Low: no real path that throws such a value is known (not measured).

## Measured

* Tree: develop `a8c554659cb3`. `git grep -n -E 'instanceof Error \? [A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*(\??\.[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)*\.message : String\(' <develop> -- 'Blockchain/Dev/services/*.ts'`, then test files removed, then only the same-identifier form kept (the identifier before `instanceof` is the one in `.message` and in `String(...)`): **253 sites in 15 services** (originate 93, nft-certificate 29, auth 22, billing 21, mcp-server 21, analytics 19, governance 12, api-gateway 9, kyc 8, tenant-provisioning 7, tokenisation 6, security 2, vc-issuer 2, demo-service 1, m365-integration 1). Identifier used: `err` 150, `error` 88, fifteen other names. Largest files: index.ts 25, documents.ts 19, billing.ts 17, certifications.ts 16, gdprService.ts 16, nft.routes.ts 15.
* QA gate 36 (the coordinator's gate on pull request 1833) counted **88** with the literal identifier `error`, 9 of them in certifications.ts and 15 in documents.ts. I reproduced those three figures under that narrower definition; the wider same-identifier family is 253. The 88 is therefore a subset, not the class.
* Controls in the same run: the same-identifier pattern does not match the guarded form `String(error instanceof Error ? error.message : error)` (0), matches the unguarded form (1), and does not match when the two identifiers differ (0). The count of `instanceof Error` in non-test services code is 294.
* Not counted (so 253 is a lower bound for the family): other shapes of the same read, such as `err.message` on its own, `err instanceof Error ? err.message : 'unknown'`, or a thrown value interpolated into a template literal.

## What it is

* Reading `.message` off a thrown value, or calling `String()` on it, can itself throw. A revoked Proxy throws on every property read and on `instanceof`; an Error whose `message` getter throws, throws on `.message`; a `message` that is an object whose `toJSON` throws, or a Proxy whose `getPrototypeOf` trap throws, throws later, in the logger's formatter.
* Where such a read sits in the catch of an async Express 4 handler with no `try` of its own, the rejected promise is not forwarded and the request gets no answer. Measured on one route, GET /api/certifications/:id (KS-1844, pull request 1833): the coordinator's gate 36 reports 12 of 16 hostile shapes hang at the base, and 3 still hung after the first change because the `message` value reached the real logger as a non-string. Those figures are the gate's, not re-derived by me.
* Per-site siblings already on the board: KS-1346 (a non-Error throw logged as \[object Object\]), KS-1771 (api-gateway log-line describers), KS-1772 (originate log-line describers), KS-1780 (17 originate catches), KS-1798 (mapGdprWriteDbError), KS-1802, KS-1817, KS-1844. Searched with title, description and comments, archived included: none proposes one shared helper, and `safeReason` has 0 hits.

## Proposal (structural; not done by this ticket)

* One helper in a shared package, for example `safeReason(e: unknown): string`: read `e instanceof Error ? e.message : e` and coerce it with `String()` inside one `try`, and return the constant `unreadable thrown value` when anything throws. Each site becomes a one-line replacement and the class has one test with a revoked Proxy, a throwing getter and a throwing `toJSON`.
* No site is changed here. KS-1844 keeps its own change at its one route.

## Not measured

* Whether any real code path throws such a value into any of the 253 sites; the shapes used so far are synthetic.
* How many of the 253 sit where a throw leaves a request without an answer, as opposed to a log line that is merely lost.
* The production logger path (`NODE_ENV=production`).

Facts only. Priority Low.

**BLUF (corrected 2026-10-30):** the api-gateway test files carry 27 type errors in 7 files, and they are the **recorded baseline of the KS-1000 ratchet** (`scripts/typecheck-tests/baseline-api-gateway.txt`; api-gateway was added to the ratchet by KS-1090 and the check is wired into pre-push leg 16 by KS-1487). So a NEW error already fails the push, and the push hook printed `typecheck-tests: api-gateway (tsconfig.test.json): tsc examined 166 files, 130 of them under __tests__; 27 errors: 27 in the baseline, 0 new`. What nothing tracks is burning the 27 down. The service `tsconfig.json` still excludes `src/__tests__`, so `npm run build` never reads them. This ticket is the burn-down of those 27 and nothing else; test-only work, no product file involved.

**Correction:** the first version of this ticket said "nothing fails". That was wrong. I searched the board by the seven file names and by `tsc --noEmit`, and did not read the preflight's leg list or the `scripts/typecheck-tests/` baselines, which name the same seven files with the same counts (10, 4 + 1, 1, 2, 1 + 1, 1, 6).

**The 27 errors, by file (TypeScript 5.9.3):**

| Test file (under `Blockchain/Dev/services/api-gateway/src/__tests__/`) | Errors | Codes |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `csrf.test.ts` | 10 | TS2345 |
| `rateLimitEnforce.test.ts` | 6 | TS2345 |
| `ks1165-api-gateway-csrf-excludedpaths-carries-no.test.ts` | 5 | TS2345, TS2571 |
| `ks1457-audit-finish-reads-use-the-entry-path.test.ts` | 2 | TS2322 |
| `ks1464-limiter-key-hygiene.test.ts` | 2 | TS7006 |
| `ks1374-global-limiter-at-demo-limit.test.ts` | 1 | TS18046 |
| `ks695-ask3-erase-connector-door.test.ts` | 1 | TS7006 |

The `csrf.test.ts` message reads: `Argument of type 'Mock<Procedure | Constructable>' is not assignable to parameter of type 'NextFunction'`.

**How it was measured (2026-10-30, Node v26.8.1, not an LTS line):** a child tsconfig that extends `services/api-gateway/tsconfig.json` with `include: ["src/**/*"]`, `exclude: []`, `noEmit`, `types: ["node"]`, run as `tsc -p <child>` from `services/api-gateway`. The 27 error lines are equal line for line between a clean worktree at develop and a worktree carrying the KS-1534 test-only change. A planted type error in a scratch file was reported once, by file name.

**Not known:** whether the same errors appear with `types` left unset in the child config (I set `["node"]`); whether the fix is mechanical for the `Mock` versus `NextFunction` cases; whether a type-checked test leg should be added once they are clean.

**Searched the board first (Secuura-PK, archived included, 2026-10-30):** the seven file names (`csrf.test.ts`, `ks1165-api-gateway-csrf`, `ks1374-global-limiter`, `ks1457-audit-finish`, `ks1464-limiter-key`, `ks695-ask3-erase-connector-door`, `rateLimitEnforce`) and `tsc --noEmit`, `NextFunction`, `TS2345`, `Mock<Procedure`. No open ticket is about these errors. Hits that name one of the files are about other subjects: KS-525 names `tests-unit/csrf.test.ts` in a Playwright plan, KS-1488 (Duplicate) names the ks1457 test, and the `rateLimitEnforce` hits are limiter-behaviour tickets. Positive control `allow-list guard` returned KS-1534; the random token returned 0. Same root cause, other scopes: KS-1090 (api-gateway and originate tsconfigs exclude `src/__tests__`, scoped to three wiring tests from one change), KS-1000 (services/auth), KS-1329 (packages/shared, its own 10 errors).

**Suggested done-state:** the 27 errors fixed in the seven test files, with `tsc --noEmit` clean over the program that includes them. A candidate for the Spark: test-only files that no live seat holds. Not fixed by the seat that found it (outside its eight pull requests).

title: Workflow configurations are one shared table with no tenant column: an ORG_ADMIN of any tenant can list, change and delete all of them
description:
**BLUF:** The workflow-configuration routes in originate (`GET`, `POST`, `PUT` and `DELETE /api/admin/workflows`) read and write one table, `workflow_configs`, that has no tenant column, with no tenant filter, behind a router gate of `SYSTEM_ADMIN` or `ORG_ADMIN`. `ORG_ADMIN` is a tenant-scoped role, so an `ORG_ADMIN` of any tenant can list, change and delete every workflow configuration, including ones another tenant uses. `docs/MULTI-TENANCY.md` drew "workflows" as a tenant-scoped table (`workflows + tenant_id`). Read from code, not probed on a running stack.

Found while re-verifying `docs/MULTI-TENANCY.md` for KS-1807 (PR-3). Whether these configurations are meant to be platform-wide was not found written down.

## What the code does

Under `Blockchain/Dev/`:

* **The table has no tenant column and nothing adds one:** `workflow_configs` is created in `migrations/002_verification-tiers.sql` and `docker/init/05-admin-tables.sql`. No `ALTER TABLE` in the TypeScript services adds `tenant_id` to it (searched non-test TypeScript; control: `startup-migrations.ts` has 19 `ALTER TABLE` statements), and no SQL line ties the table to `tenant_id` (the two migrations that add a tenant column generically, 026 and 030, name other tables).
* **The router gate:** `services/originate/src/routes/adminConfig.ts`, `adminConfigRouter.use(authenticate(), requireRole('SYSTEM_ADMIN', 'ORG_ADMIN'))`. The gateway's `/api/admin/` proxy admits `ORG_ADMIN` as well (`PROXY_ADMIN_ROLES`).
* **No tenant filter on any workflow route:** the list is `SELECT * FROM workflow_configs ORDER BY name ASC`; create inserts `(name, description, type, is_active, steps, document_types, sla_hours)`; update and delete address a row by `id` alone (`DELETE FROM workflow_configs WHERE id = ${req.params.id}::uuid`).
* **Why it looks this way:** the gateway's `clone-to-tenant` route copies platform workflow templates with `tenantPool.query("INSERT INTO workflow_configs ...")` (`routes/platform.ts`), which assumes each tenant has its own database. On the shared-database path every tenant's pool is the same database, so that route and the admin routes above all write the one table.

## Effect

A tenant administrator can read and alter the configuration of workflows that every tenant shares, or delete one. Because there is no tenant column, row-level security has nothing to key on. Whether the rows are in practice shared platform templates, and whether anything reads `workflow_configs` at request time for another tenant, was not checked.

## How to confirm

As an `ORG_ADMIN` of tenant A, `GET /api/admin/workflows` and note the ids; as an `ORG_ADMIN` of tenant B, `PUT` or `DELETE /api/admin/workflows/{id}` on one of them. Expected by the tenancy rule: refused or invisible. By this reading: allowed. Not run.

## Suggested direction (your call)

Decide whether workflow configurations are platform-wide (then restrict the routes to platform roles and say so in the docs) or per tenant (then add a tenant column, backfill it, and key the routes and a policy on it). Per the ruling recorded on KS-1668 the docs lead and the code aligns; Kam decides which side moves.

Searched the board before filing: `workflow_configs`, `admin/workflows`, `workflow config`; nothing covers this. Control in the same session: `Connector keys are minted` returned KS-1433.

title: PII tokenisation is on no request path: the gateway helpers have no callers, skipTokenisation is read by nothing, and only key generation uses the service
description:
**BLUF:** PII tokenisation is on no request path. The tokenisation service exists and tenant provisioning asks it for a key, but nothing calls its `tokenise` or `detokenise` endpoints, the gateway helpers that would (`tokeniseFields`, `detokeniseValues`, `extractPiiFields`) have no callers, and the default tenant's `skipTokenisation` flag is read nowhere. `docs/MULTI-TENANCY.md` says PII "is tokenised at entry and stored in encrypted form" and that new tenants "get full tokenisation from day one". Read from code, not probed on a running stack.

Found while re-verifying `docs/MULTI-TENANCY.md` for KS-1807 (PR-3). Related: KS-1336, KS-1860 and KS-1861, which sit next to it in the same document.

## What the code does

All paths under `Blockchain/Dev/`.

* **Helpers with no callers:** `services/api-gateway/src/services/tokenisation.ts` defines `tokeniseFields` (`:101`), `detokeniseValues` (`:136`) and `extractPiiFields` (`:178`). Searching `services`, `packages` and `frontend` (non-test, excluding `node_modules`) for each name outside that file finds 0 hits. The gateway's `index.ts` imports only `setTenantKey`, `getTenantKey` and `removeTenantKey` from it. Control: `setTenantKey(` is called once outside the file (the tenant-key load route in `routes/platform.ts`).
* **The service's own API has one real caller:** searching for `api/tokenise`, `api/detokenise` and `TOKENISATION_URL` outside `services/tokenisation/` finds only `services/tenant-provisioning/src/index.ts` (which requests a key) and the unused gateway helper file. No request path tokenises or detokenises a field.
* `skipTokenisation` **is read by nothing:** it appears in `docker/init-platform/02-seed-default-tenant.sql` and in no non-test source under `services` or `packages` (0 hits). The default tenant's data stays plaintext because nothing tokenises any tenant's data, not because of the flag.
* **What PII encryption does exist:** auth encrypts user PII columns itself, per user (`services/auth/src/repositories/userRepo.ts`, `encryptPiiCol(value, column, userId)`); that is a separate mechanism from the tenant tokenisation key and vault.
* **Not audited either:** tokenise and detokenise write no audit row (`services/tokenisation/src/index.ts`); only generate-key and rotate-key call `emitAudit`, and that writes to the main database's `audit_logs`, not the platform audit table the document names.

## Effect

The per-tenant key lifecycle is real (generate, load, rotate), but the thing the key is for does not run. A reader of the architecture document, or a customer told that their PII is tokenised and decryptable only with their key, is told something the code does not do. Whether any contract or marketing text makes that promise was not checked.

## How to confirm

Create a tenant, load its key, create a user and a document containing an email address, then read the stored rows: expected by the document, tokens (`tok_...`) and `vault_entries` rows; by this reading, the original values and no vault rows beyond those from direct `POST /api/tokenise` calls. Not run.

## Suggested direction (your call)

Decide whether request-path tokenisation is still intended. If it is, wire the gateway helpers (or the service) onto the request path and record the default-tenant behaviour in code; if it is not, the documents and the key-lifecycle endpoints should say that the service is key management only. Per the ruling recorded on KS-1668 the docs lead and the code aligns; Kam decides which side moves.

Searched the board before filing: `tokeniseFields`, `KS1336`, `vault_entries`, `suspend`; nothing covers tokenisation being unwired. Control in the same session: `Connector keys are minted` returned KS-1433.

title: register-connector is idempotent only for sequential calls: two concurrent first registrations of one externalRef create two Organisations and two live keys
description:
**BLUF:** `POST /api/platform/organizations/register-connector` is only idempotent for sequential calls. Two concurrent first-time registrations of the same `externalRef` can both create an Organisation row and both mint a live `sk_` key: the lookup is a plain `SELECT ... LIMIT 1` with no lock and no transaction, there is no unique index on the reference, and the one constraint that would have stopped the second insert (unique `slug`) is turned into a successful second insert by a collision retry. The S-K ownership contract says registration is "idempotent on the Org GUID so retries and replays are safe". Read from code, not probed on a running stack.

Found while re-verifying `docs/S-K-OWNERSHIP-CONTRACT.md` for KS-1807 (PR-3). Related: KS-1549 (two concurrent rotates), which is the same class on the rotate path and is a different defect.

## What the code does

All in `Blockchain/Dev/services/api-gateway/src/routes/platform.ts`, the register-connector handler:

* **Lookup (:729):** `SELECT id, tenant_id::text AS tenant_id, slug, name FROM organizations WHERE metadata->>'externalRef' = $1 LIMIT 1`, run under platform scope. No `FOR UPDATE`, no advisory lock, no transaction around the lookup, the insert and the mint (searched `platform.ts` for `advisory`, `FOR UPDATE`, `BEGIN` and `transaction(`: 0 hits; control: `runWithPlatformScope` has 6).
* **Insert (:827-832):** `INSERT INTO organizations (name, slug, ...) ... metadata = {"externalRef": ...}`. The reference lives in a JSON key of `metadata`, not in a column. The only uniqueness on `organizations` is on `slug` and `did` (`docker/init/01-schema.sql`, `migrations/001_initial-schema.sql`); no index covers `metadata->>'externalRef'` (searched every `.sql` under `migrations` and `docker` for `externalRef`: the only hit is a comment in `041_action_provenance.sql`).
* **Collision handling (:835-839):** the slug comes from the name, or from `org-<externalRef>` when there is none. Two concurrent calls for the same reference therefore compute the same slug. The second insert fails with `23505`, and the code answers that with "one deterministic retry with an entropy suffix" (`slugBase` plus 4 random hex characters), which succeeds. Its own comment calls the fallback slug "collision-free"; the retry is what lets the duplicate through.
* **Mint (:848-873):** both calls then reach the key mint with the same `connectorId: 'platform-s:<externalRef>'`, their own `organizationId` and `rotate: false`. The file's own KS-577 comment says that without `rotate` "the mint is purely additive", so neither call retires the other's key.

## Effect

Two Organisation rows for one S Organisation GUID and two live keys for it, each key carrying a different `organizationId`. Later registrations of the same reference read `LIMIT 1` with no `ORDER BY`, so which row they return is not defined.

## How to confirm

Two parallel `register-connector` calls for a fresh `externalRef` with a provisioning key, then `SELECT count(*) FROM organizations WHERE metadata->>'externalRef' = '<ref>'`. Expected by the contract: 1. By this reading: 2, and two keys returned. Not run.

## Suggested direction (your call)

A unique expression index on `(metadata->>'externalRef')` (or a real column) plus handling `23505` on that index by re-reading, or an advisory lock keyed on the reference around lookup, insert and mint. The slug retry should not be the path that absorbs a same-reference collision.

Searched the board before filing: `register-connector`, `idempoten`, `two organisations` and `concurrent`; KS-1549 (concurrent rotates) is the nearest and is a different path; nothing covers concurrent first registrations. Control in the same session: `Connector keys are minted` returned KS-1433.

title: auth: the Google, Facebook, LinkedIn and Microsoft sign-in adapters read access_token from the token answer unchecked, as the GitHub adapter did before KS-1792 (gate 33, F5)
description:
**BLUF:** Four social sign-in adapters still take `access_token` from the token endpoint's answer without checking it: `google.ts:87`, `facebook.ts:82`, `linkedin.ts:85` and `microsoft-personal.ts:87`. The GitHub adapter did the same until pull request 1830 (KS-1792), which refuses a 200 answer with no usable `access_token` before any profile call. Lower risk for these four, per the gate: they answer errors with a non-2xx status as RFC 6749 section 5.2 requires, so GitHub's "200 with an error body" case does not apply to them; the defensive posture is still weaker than the GitHub adapter's. A follow-up candidate, not a defect measured on a running system.

**Source.** QA gate 33 on pull request 1830 (KS-1792; tier 1, GO WITH NOTES, 2026-10-30), finding F5 (Note, out of that pull request's scope, follow-up candidate). Verdict file (the coordinator's reference, local to her): `/Volumes/DevMASTER/WEDNESDAY/0_Brain/reference/2026-10-30_gate33-1830/verdict.md`. Related: KS-1792 (the GitHub fix), KS-1791 (the callback echoing an unreadable provider answer), KS-1240. Apple is in the gate's note too (`apple.ts:86` takes `id_token` unchecked, so a missing one is a TypeError on `.split`), but that part is already recorded in KS-1617, item 8 ("It throws a TypeError if `id_token` is absent") and in its comment on the unverified signature, so this ticket is scoped to the four `access_token` adapters. Filed on Wednesday's word.

**The verdict text, quoted (F5, lines 35 to 39 of the verdict, unedited):**

**F5 - Note (out of scope, follow-up candidate). The sibling adapters keep the unchecked read.**

* google.ts:87, facebook.ts:82, linkedin.ts:85 and microsoft-personal.ts:87 still take `access_token` unchecked.
* apple.ts:86 takes `id_token` unchecked, so a missing one becomes a TypeError on `.split`.
* These providers answer errors with non-2xx, as RFC 6749 §5.2 requires, so the GitHub-specific "200 with error" case does not apply to them. Their defensive posture is still weaker. None of them is touched by this PR.

**Board search before filing** (issues filter over title, description and comment bodies, archived included, 2026-10-30): random-token control 0 hits; positive control `access_token` 5 hits including KS-1792. `microsoft-personal` 5 (KS-1617, KS-795, KS-722, KS-712, KS-485), `linkedin.ts` 3, `facebook.ts` 3, `google.ts` 6, `id_token` 4 (KS-1791, KS-1687, KS-1617, KS-1240), `tokenRes.json` 1 (KS-1792), `RFC 6749` 12 (none about a provider's token answer). KS-1617 and KS-1791 read for `access_token`, `id_token`, unchecked and "200 with": KS-1617 item 8 records Apple's missing `id_token`; nothing records the unchecked `access_token` read of the other four.

**Not measured by this filing:** none of the adapters was run against a provider; what each of Google, Facebook, LinkedIn and Microsoft answers for a bad code is the gate's statement (non-2xx), not tested here.

nodes.body:
**BLUF:** PR 2084 (head `223499281cb9`, one commit on develop `9cdb9321aa8a`) is raised for gate 211 finding F1 on this ticket and waits for its gate. It is test-only: one new test file in `services/auth`, no product code. Nothing is merged or deployed.

- **The change** (`ks1858-a-usable-token-is-sent-exactly-as-the-provider-answered-it.test.ts`, +93, 6 cells): for each of the five social sign-in adapters (google, facebook, linkedin, microsoft-personal, github), an answered token with a leading and a trailing space must reach the profile call unchanged (the `Authorization` header as handed to `fetch`; for Facebook, the tail of the URL), plus a control that an untouched token is sent as is.
- **Proof, measured by Seat T 14th:** the cells pin existing behaviour, so they pass on develop by design (6 of 6). The gate's five named mutants (each adapter trimming the sent token) each turn exactly their own adapter's cell red and no other, by assertion, and the control stays green. `services/auth` suite with a 120 s test timeout on both sides: 146 files, 1736 of 1736 before; 147 files, 1742 of 1742 after. At the default 5 s timeout one existing file (`ks949-platform-admin-seed-identity`) times out on this loaded host, before and after; none of those timeouts is an assertion.
- **Not covered:** a real provider call, what a real `Request` does to the value on the wire (gate 211 N2), the four platform suites, Node 24 (this was Node v26.8.1), any box.
- The pull request says Refs, so it does not close this ticket.

**BLUF:** Pull request 2022 (https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/2022, head `1a0fa7c23b24`) covers gate note G67-F3: the Google, Facebook, LinkedIn, Microsoft and GitHub sign-in adapters now refuse a whitespace-only `access_token` before any profile call. Raised for its QA gate (tier 1 proposed); not merged, not deployed. This ticket stays open.

- **What changed:** in the five guards under `Blockchain/Dev/services/auth/src/providers/social/`, the emptiness test `access_token === ''` became `access_token.trim() === ''` (+3/-1 per adapter, with a two-line comment). A usable token is still sent exactly as the provider answered it; the log line and the error text are unchanged. `github.ts` is included on Wednesday's ruling, because G67-F3 names it; its `error`-field clause is unchanged.
- **Cells:** ten new, two per adapter (W1 a single space, W2 only characters `trim()` removes), appended to the four `ks1858-<provider>-refuses-a-token-answer-without-an-access-token` files and the `ks1792-github-` file.
- **Evidence:** red first on develop `1b1b65c7415f`, 10 of 38 failed by assertion (the blank-bearer profile call happened); 38 of 38 with the change. Mutants: 10 of 10 killed. Whole auth suite: 1,723 of 1,724 on the branch, 1,711 of 1,714 on develop; every failure on both sides is a `ks949` cell at the 5 s timeout, and that file passes alone 31 of 31. Service tsc 0 errors, test-type ratchet 0 new, eslint clean. The pre-push hook's verdict is in the PR's Test Evidence block.
- **Not covered:** the `error`-field parity for the other four adapters (KS-1917); G67-F3's other two observations, unchanged (a `null` body still rejects with a TypeError, a non-JSON 200 with a SyntaxError); no real provider was called (the cells stub `fetch`).

**BLUF:** Delivered: PR 1879 merged as 9bc1cf3b538b on develop, deployed to kintsugi at b1fb543640e7 (recorded deploy, 2026-11-01). Verified by code read at b1fb543640e7, not observed live (it needs a provider that answers 200 without a token). Left open: gate note G67-F3, a whitespace-only token, passes the new guard on all four adapters.

- **The four guards are in the code:** under `Blockchain/Dev/services/auth/src/providers/social/`, `google.ts:88`, `facebook.ts:83`, `linkedin.ts:86` and `microsoft-personal.ts:88` refuse a token answer whose `access_token` is not a string or is `''` before any profile call; each adapter has its own `ks1858-<provider>-refuses-a-token-answer-without-an-access-token.test.ts`.
- **Left open, as comment 66562408 records it:** G67-F3 (`{access_token: ' '}` resolves on all four and the profile call goes out with a blank bearer; `github.ts` also tests only `=== ''`), recorded in the thread only. G67-F1 and G67-F2 are KS-1917.

**BLUF:** pull request 1879 (KS-1858 PR 5, merged as `9bc1cf3b538b`, Refs) passed QA gate 67 with GO WITH NOTES. Two of the gate's notes are recorded here; the other two are filed as KS 1917. This ticket stays open.

**G67-F3 (file-only):** a whitespace-only token passes the new guard. `{access_token: ' '}` resolves on all four adapters and the profile call goes out with a blank bearer (Facebook: blank in the URL). `github.ts` also tests only `=== ''`, and the change claims "missing, non-string or empty", which is what it does. Also unchanged by the change: a `null` answer body still rejects with a TypeError (the message differs only by V8's wording for Facebook, LinkedIn and Microsoft), and a non-JSON 200 still rejects with a SyntaxError; neither is a refusal under the new guard.

**G67-F4 (file-only):** the `ks949` timing flake did not reproduce at the gate. Develop alone: 113 files, 1365 pass, 0 fail, 0 skipped; the merge: 117 files, 1385 pass, 0 fail, 0 skipped, twice, with `--maxWorkers=2`, load1 6.8 to 6.9 under nice 10 (3 runs, 0 occurrences). The gate says this does not disprove a timing flake on one machine; there is no instrument to force one. My own runs on develop did hit the 5 s timeout of two `ks949` cells and a 10 s hook timeout that skipped one whole file, at higher load.

**Where the other two went:** G67-F1 (the `error`-field clause the four guards lack, against `github.ts`) and G67-F2 (the `logger.warn` line is pinned by no cell and logs only the provider) are KS 1917.

**BLUF:** pull request 1879 (https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/1879, head `6b867a532ee7`) makes the Google, Facebook, LinkedIn and Microsoft sign-in adapters refuse a 200 token answer with no usable `access_token` before any profile call, as the GitHub adapter has since KS 1792. Raised for its QA gate (tier 2); not merged, not deployed. This ticket stays open.

**What changed:** four guards (+6/-1 in three adapters, +5/-1 in Google), four new test files (5 cells each), two docs fragments. Four held Spark passes applied strictly; no hand edit.

**Evidence:** red first 12 of 20 cells failed without the guards (3 per adapter, by assertion), 0 with them; the whole auth suite 117 files / 1385 cells, 1385 pass on the merge with develop (untouched develop: 1357 pass, 2 fail, 6 skipped, develop's own timeouts); tsc and the test ratchet 0 new, eslint 0/0. The pre-push hook verdict is in the pull request's Test Evidence block.

**Open for the gate, not done:** unlike the GitHub adapter, these guards do not also refuse a 200 answer carrying an `error` field; Facebook's token stays in the profile URL query (pre-existing); the sign-in error paths were not run against a real provider; Apple's `id_token` is KS 1617.

title: GET /api/analytics/exports lists every caller's exports with their files inline, and any signed-in user can request users and revenue exports: no role, tenant or user is used (KS-1703 covers only the by-id read)
description:
**BLUF:** `GET /api/analytics/exports` returns every analytics export the service holds, whoever asked for it, and a completed export carries its file inline (`downloadUrl` is a `data:` URI), so one list call returns other callers' files; and any signed-in caller can request the `users` and `revenue` report types, because the analytics service checks no role. KS-1703 already covers the by-id read (`GET /api/analytics/exports/{id}`, found by Schemathesis) and records that for exports "it may be deliberate" and needs a ruling; this ticket adds the list route, the missing role check on creation, and a rule the docs state that the code does not meet. Read from code; not probed on a running stack.

Found while re-verifying the platform-k docs for KS-1807 (PR-2, `WORKFLOWS.md` section 3). Related: KS-1703.

## What is not in KS-1703

* **The list route:** `router.get('/exports')` in `services/analytics/src/routes/analytics.ts` calls `exportService.listExports(limit)` (default 20), which returns the values of the service's process-wide map (`memExports` in `services/analytics/src/services/exportService.ts`) with no caller or tenant filter. KS-1703's table names the by-id read only. The list makes ids discoverable, so the by-id read does not even need a guessed id.
* **Creation has no role check and stores no caller:** `router.post('/exports')` parses the body and calls `exportService.createExport(request)`; the request carries no identity and `createExport` stores none. Accepted report types: `certifications`, `verifications`, `users`, `governance`, `revenue`, each built from `analyticsService.get<Type>Metrics(query)` where `query` holds only `period`, `startDate` and `endDate`. The gateway mount `/api/analytics` (`services/api-gateway/src/routes/proxy.ts`) is `authenticateToken(true)` and the service mounts only `jwtAuthenticate` (`services/analytics/src/index.ts`): no role, no scope.
* **Persistence:** the newest 500 export rows are reloaded into the map at boot, so the exposure survives a restart.
* **Tenancy:** the word `tenant` appears in the analytics service's non-test source only in `db.ts`; the routes and `exportService.ts` never read a tenant or user from the request (control: the same search finds `req.params` in the routes file).

## A rule the docs state that this contradicts

`docs/security/ROLES-AND-AUTHORIZATION-INVENTORY.md` section 2.1 (as rewritten in KS-1807 PR-1) says services without a role gate "rely on gateway-level auth plus ownership and tenant checks"; for the analytics exports neither exists. PR-1 lists five routes as exceptions; this is a sixth, and PR-1's text will need one more name once this is ruled.

## How to confirm

As two users in different tenants: user A creates a `revenue` export and waits for `completed`; user B calls `GET /api/analytics/exports`. Expected by the platform's tenancy rule: B sees nothing of A's. By this reading: B receives A's export including the file. Not run. Not assessed: whether the metrics functions return platform-wide totals or are narrowed by a database tenant setting that this reading did not find.

## Suggested direction (your call)

Per the ruling recorded on KS-1668 the docs lead and the code aligns; Kam decides which side moves, and KS-1703 holds the open question whether exports are meant to be shared. If they are not: store the creating principal and tenant with each export, filter the list and the by-id read the same way and answer 404 to anyone else (as KS-1116 did for credentials), and decide which roles may request `users` and `revenue`.

Searched the board before filing: `analytics exports`, `listExports`, `exportService` and `analytics/exports` returned KS-1703 (by-id read, referenced above), KS-1853 and KS-1846 (this pass's tickets, about the export contract and the scope table) and KS-188 (stateful testing); none covers the list route or the missing role check. Control in the same session: `Connector keys are minted` returned KS-1433.

title: The gateway answers four admin and verify routes from stand-ins registered before the proxy: fixed audit-log arrays, an always-empty verification queue, and certification verify that always says verified:false
description:
**BLUF:** The api-gateway answers four routes itself, from stand-ins registered before the proxy to the real service, with no environment guard around them: `GET /api/admin/audit-logs` and `GET /api/security/audit` return fixed arrays of fabricated rows (actor `admin` at `test.local`), `GET /api/admin/verification-queue` returns an array nothing ever writes to (so it is always empty) and its action route answers `success: true` for any id without changing anything, and `POST /api/certifications/{id}/verify` always answers `verified: false` with a hard-coded issuer `test-issuer`. The real database-backed handlers in originate are never reached for the first three. Read from code; not probed on a running stack.

Found while re-verifying the platform-k docs for KS-1807 (PR-2, document lifecycle, status codes, error envelope). The docs and the published spec describe these as real operations; the code comment on the queue says "in-memory, development only" but nothing enforces that.

## Evidence

* **Registration order:** `app.use(createAdminRoutes(...))` and `app.use(createVerificationRoutes(...))` in `services/api-gateway/src/index.ts` come before `app.use(createProxyRoutes(...))`, so a route defined in `routes/admin.ts` or `routes/verification.ts` answers before the `/api/admin/` proxy to originate is reached. The only environment check in `routes/admin.ts` is the demo-seed flag; none wraps these handlers.
* **Audit logs:** `router.get('/api/admin/audit-logs', requireAdmin, ...)` in `services/api-gateway/src/routes/admin.ts` filters a literal 4-row array (`evt-1` to `evt-4`, actor `admin` at `test.local`) by `action` and `resourceType` and returns `{ success, logs, events, total }`. `router.get('/api/security/audit', ...)` does the same with a literal 3-row array. Originate has the real handler (`adminConfigRouter.get('/audit-logs')` in `services/originate/src/routes/adminConfig.ts`); it is shadowed.
* **Verification queue:** `const mockVerificationQueue = []` ("in-memory, development only") backs `GET /api/admin/verification-queue` (always `items: []`, `total: 0`) and `POST /api/admin/verification-queue/{id}/action`, which validates the action word, updates the array entry only if one exists, and answers `{ success: true, id, action, ... }` for any id. Originate's database-backed `GET`/`POST` for the same paths (`adminConfig.ts`) are shadowed.
* **Certification verify:** `router.post('/api/certifications/:id/verify', ...)` in `services/api-gateway/src/routes/verification.ts` ("MOCK ... ENDPOINTS (for E2E tests)", "for test compatibility") checks that the certification exists, then answers `verified: false`, `status: 'issued'`, `issuer: { id: 'test-issuer', verified: true }`, `blockchain.anchored: false`, `confidence: 'pending-onchain'` whatever the certification is. Its comment says it is a stopgap "until the originate→anchoring rewire lands". Originate's own verify handler is never reached.
* **What the docs and spec say:** `QUICK-REFERENCE.md` lists all four as working endpoints (certification verify, the verification queue and its action, audit logs and the `security/audit` alias). The published spec declares only `GET /api/security/audit`; certification verify, `admin/audit-logs` and the two queue routes are live routes with no spec entry (0 hits for each path in `secuura-api.yaml`; control: `/api/billing/customers/by-email` hits).

## How to confirm

As a platform admin, call `GET /api/admin/audit-logs` on a stack with real audit rows and compare with the database; call the verification-queue action with a random id and read `success: true`; call certification verify on a real certification. Not run.

## Suggested direction (your call)

Per the ruling recorded on KS-1668 the docs lead and the code aligns; Kam decides which side moves. Either remove the gateway stand-ins so the proxy reaches originate, or gate them to test environments behind an explicit flag and document that they are test doubles.

Searched the board before filing: `verification-queue` and `audit-logs` are not covered by an existing ticket about the gateway stand-ins; KS-736 is about mount authentication, not these handlers. Control in the same session: `Connector keys are minted` returned KS-1433.

title: Reset-password has no rate limit of its own (the limiter is mounted on /api/auth/password-reset, which has no route) and billing GET /customers/by-email can never match (/customers/:id is registered first)
description:
**BLUF:** Two routing slips in code that the docs describe as working: `POST /api/auth/reset-password`, the route that consumes a reset token, has no rate limit of its own because the reset limiter is mounted on `/api/auth/password-reset`, a path no route serves; and billing `GET /customers/by-email` can never match because `GET /customers/:id` is registered first and takes `by-email` as an id. Read from code; not probed on a running stack.

Found while re-verifying the platform-k docs for KS-1807 (PR-2). `WORKFLOWS.md`'s rate-limit sheet lists `password_reset` as 15 minutes, 5 attempts, on `POST /api/auth/password-reset`; the published spec declares `GET /api/billing/customers/by-email`.

## 1. The reset limiter guards a path with no handler

* **Limiter mounts** in `services/api-gateway/src/index.ts` (`app.use(...)`, in this order): `/api/auth/login`, `/api/auth/register`, `/api/auth/forgot-password` (1 hour, 5 in production, `PASSWORD_RESET_RATE_LIMIT`), `/api/auth/refresh`, `/api/auth/password-reset` (15 minutes, 5 in production, 50 otherwise), `/api/auth/verify-email`.
* **Auth routes** in `services/auth/src/routes/auth.ts` for the same flow: `POST /forgot-password` and `POST /reset-password`. There is no `/password-reset` route (control: the `/login` route is found by the same search).
* So `/api/auth/forgot-password` is limited, and `/api/auth/reset-password`, which takes the token and a new password, is limited only by the global limiter (300 per 60 s per IP in production). The 15-minute limiter on the dead path never sees a request. Not assessed: how guessable a reset token is; not probed.
* The login brute-force guard has a related defect already on the board: KS-1372 (nothing calls `recordFailure`).

## 2. Billing by-email is unreachable

`services/billing/src/routes/billing.ts` registers `router.get('/customers/:id', ...)` before `router.get('/customers/by-email', ...)`, so Express matches `by-email` as an `:id` and the by-email handler is never reached. The published spec declares `GET /api/billing/customers/by-email`.

## Not a finding (recorded in the PR for KS-1807 PR-2 as a doc correction)

`GET /billing/pricing` needs a login although a code comment calls it public: `services/billing/src/index.ts` says the public marketing endpoints are "intentionally behind JWT" (`app.use('/billing', jwtAuthenticate())`), so the doc is what is wrong.

Searched the board before filing: `password-reset`, `reset-password` and `by-email` returned no ticket about these two slips. Control in the same session: `Connector keys are minted` returned KS-1433.

## Suggested direction (your call)

Per the ruling recorded on KS-1668 the docs lead and the code aligns; Kam decides which side moves. Mount the limiter on `/api/auth/reset-password` (and drop or fix the dead mount), and register `/customers/by-email` before `/customers/:id`.

title: Spec and docs describe contracts the code does not follow: analytics export sends no Location or Retry-After and returns a data URI; kyc/submit and kyc/status are listed but absent; KYC approval never raises a verification level
description:
**BLUF:** In three areas the published spec and the docs describe a contract the code does not follow: the analytics export, the KYC steps, and the link between KYC and a user's verification level. The analytics export 202 declares `Location` and `Retry-After` headers and a poll-until-`done` flow; the code sends neither header, returns the file inline as a `data:` URI, and calls the field `downloadUrl`, not `url`. The spec's `info.x-workflows` lists `POST /api/kyc/submit` and `GET /api/kyc/status`, which do not exist. And no code path raises a user's verification level when a KYC verification is approved, although `WORKFLOWS.md` says it does. Read from code; not probed on a running stack.

Found while re-verifying the platform-k docs for KS-1807 (PR-2). The contract is generated from `services/*/src/*.openapi.ts`, so correcting it is a product-source change and is held (findings only this round); this ticket is where it is decided which side moves.

## Analytics export (`services/analytics`)

* **Headers:** the spec's `POST /api/analytics/exports` 202 says "poll the URL in the `Location` header until state=`done`" and declares `Location` and `Retry-After` response headers. `services/analytics/src/routes/analytics.ts` sets no header (zero hits for `setHeader`, `res.set`, `location` or `retry-after`; control: `setHeader('Location'` has hits in originate's `documents.ts`).
* **Status values and fields:** `exportService.ts` sets `pending`, `processing`, `completed` and `failed`; the spec's `AnalyticsExport` schema has `completed` in its status enum but also declares `url`, `sizeBytes` and `completedAt`, which the code does not send. The code sends `downloadUrl` and `expiresAt`. `WORKFLOWS.md` says `ready` and `url` (a presigned URL with a finite TTL).
* **The download:** `downloadUrl` is `data:<mime>;base64,<payload>` (`createDownloadUrl` in `exportService.ts`), so the file travels inside the status response; there is no separate download request. `pdf` and `xlsx` exports contain JSON text, and `pdf` is labelled `application/octet-stream` (a placeholder, per its own comment).
* **Request and 202 body:** the spec's request declares `from` and `to`; the code reads `period` (required) with `startDate` and `endDate`, and also accepts `xlsx`. The 202 body is `{ success, data: { id, status, type, format, createdAt } }`, not the bare object.

## KYC (`services/kyc`)

* **Steps:** the spec's `info.x-workflows` lists `POST /api/kyc/submit` and `GET /api/kyc/status`. `services/kyc/src/index.ts` registers `initiate`, `/:id`, `/user/:userId`, `/:id/document`, `/:id/selfie`, `/:id/complete`, `/:id/review`, `/:id/result` and `DELETE /user/:userId/data`. `GET /api/kyc/status` is read as `/:id` with id `status` and answers 404; `POST /api/kyc/submit` matches no service route (by reading the gateway's method map it would answer 405, because the path matches the spec's `/api/kyc/{id}`, which allows only GET; not executed). `initiate` answers 201 (not 202) with `verificationId`; statuses are lowercase `pending`, `in_progress`, `under_review`, `approved`, `rejected`.
* **The level never moves:** `WORKFLOWS.md` says `GET /api/users/me` shows the new `verificationLevel` after KYC and that a raised level unlocks higher-tier document types. A search of service source (tests excluded) finds `users.verification_level` written only by the gateway admin route, the social-login path in auth and originate's admin route; the kyc service has no access to the users table (0 hits for `FROM users`, `UPDATE users`, `INTO users` in `services/kyc/src`; control: `verification_level` has 5 hits in `services/auth/src/repositories/userRepo.ts`). So an approved KYC verification does not change a token's level by this reading. The seeded `PROPERTY_DEED` document type also needs no level (`creatorVerificationLevel: 'none'`), though the gate itself exists.

## Not repeated here

The create-document response shape (flat, not `DocumentDetail`), the `/anchor` 202 body, the verify `source` values and the error messages are recorded in the PR-2 pull request body as doc corrections, because there the code is plainly the intended behaviour; if you want them in the contract-corrections batch, say so.

Searched the board before filing: `kyc/submit`, `analytics exports`, `Retry-After` returned no ticket about these contract differences (KS-1327 is about KYC write races, KS-1372 about the login lockout). Control in the same session: `Connector keys are minted` returned KS-1433.

## Suggested direction (your call)

Per the ruling recorded on KS-1668 the docs lead and the code aligns; Kam decides which side moves. For the export, either send the headers and a real download, or change the spec and docs to the inline `data:` form; for KYC, remove the two steps from `x-workflows` and decide whether approval should raise the level.

nodes.body:
**BLUF:** Four more differences between the published spec and the code, found by two read-only verifiers during the KS-1807 PR-2 pass; I re-read each against the spec and the handler at develop `85cd24d81`. Read, not probed on a running stack. Correcting the spec is a product-source change (it is generated from `services/*/src/*.openapi.ts`) and is held this round, so this is findings only. This adds to the three items in my earlier comment on this ticket.

**1. `FlatAnchorRequest.contentHash` is stricter in the spec than in the code.** The spec pattern is `^[a-f0-9]{64}$` (lowercase only). The handler's schema (`services/anchoring/src/anchorSchema.ts`) is `/^[a-f0-9]{64}$/i`, which accepts upper case. A spec that is stricter than its server is the shape the code's own comment on `ACCEPTED_LIFECYCLE_VERBS` says it wants to avoid.

**2. `FlatAnchorRequest.documentId` has the length bounds but no `pattern` in the spec.** The spec gives `minLength: 1` and `maxLength: 128` and a description that says "doc-… external id or a UUID (anchorSchema.ts documentId pattern)", in prose. The code adds a regex on top of the same length bounds (`anchorSchema.ts`, `documentId`), so a value the spec accepts can still be refused 400.

**3. `DocumentCreateRequest` does not list `contentHash`.** The spec's properties are `title`, `documentType`, `data`, `onBehalfOf`, `documentUuid`, `userUuid` and `organizationUuid`. The create handler (`services/originate/src/routes/documents.ts`, `POST /`) reads `contentHash` from the body, and its own 400 for the unsupported `content` field says "send 'contentHash' (sha256 hex) or 'data' instead". A caller working from the spec is told to send a field it cannot find.

**4. Live routes the spec does not declare.** Searching the spec's path keys (control: `/api/documents` is declared): `POST /api/documents/{id}/sign`, `POST /api/documents/{id}/sign/request` (KS-1831, KS-1832 cover their behaviour, not their absence from the spec) and `/api/certifications/{id}/lineage` have no entry. `/api/certifications/{id}/verify`, `/api/admin/verification-queue` and `/api/admin/audit-logs` are also undeclared, and are covered by KS-1855.

**Also noted, code comment only (no contract difference):** the comment above `TRANSITIONAL_LIFECYCLE_VERBS` in `anchorSchema.ts` says "docs and the spec describe the vocabulary K advertises, and `certify` is no longer part of it". The spec's verb enum is generated from `ACCEPTED_LIFECYCLE_VERBS` (in `anchoring.openapi.ts`), which includes the transitional `certify`, so the published enum does list it. `docs/VOCABULARY.md` in the PR-2 pull request states this correctly.

**Not done:** no request against any box; no test written; whether Schemathesis flags item 1 (an upper-case hash the spec says is invalid) was not checked.

**BLUF:** Three more places where the published spec describes something the code does not do, found while re-checking the platform-k docs for KS-1807 (PR-2). The worst is billing `POST /api/billing/admin/credits`: the spec's request body is refused 400 by the handler. Read from code and spec at develop `85cd24d81`; not probed on a running stack. The spec is generated from `services/*/src/*.openapi.ts`, so correcting it is a product-source change and is held this round (findings only).

**1. `POST /api/billing/admin/credits`: the spec's request and the handler's do not match**

* Spec (`BillingAdminAdjustCreditsRequest`): `{ customerId, delta (integer), reason }`, `customerId` and `delta` required. The description says "Positive delta to grant; negative to deduct. Audit-logged." The 200 response is `BillingSuccess`, `{ success, message }`.
* Handler (`services/billing/src/routes/billing.ts`, `POST /admin/credits`): the Zod schema is `{ customerId: string, credits: positive integer }`. A request that follows the spec carries `delta` and no `credits`, so it fails validation and the handler answers 400. The handler only ever adds credits (`addCertificationCredits`); nothing deducts. It answers `{ customerId, creditsAdded, newBalance }`.
* "Audit-logged": the call writes an application log line (`[Stripe] Added credits`) and no audit record. Searching the billing service's non-test source for `audit` finds only the spec description (`billing.openapi.ts`) and text in the webhook handler (control: `logger.info` is found in 6 files of the same tree).
* Related, already tracked: KS-1850 (the handler admits `OWNER`, `ORG_ADMIN` and `SYSTEM_ADMIN`).

**2. The spec's second server is a deleted environment.** `servers[1]` is `https://secuura02-demo-api.kindtree-935b2ded.southeastasia.azurecontainerapps.io/api`, described as "Demo environment (Founders Hub, Azure Container Apps, southeastasia)". The Container Apps estate was deleted on 2026-07-31 (the project record says those URLs are dead); the live demo is the VM stack. Anyone using the spec's server picker for the demo calls a dead host.

**3. Seven gateway operations under `/api/admin/document-types` are not in the spec.** `services/api-gateway/src/routes/admin.ts` registers GET (list, by id, an id's documents), POST, PUT, PATCH `/:id/status` and DELETE on `/api/admin/document-types`, all behind `requireAdmin`. The published spec declares only `GET /api/document-types` (searched the path keys for `document-types`: one hit).

**Where the docs now say this:** `docs/QUICK-REFERENCE.md` (the `/api/billing/admin/credits` row) in the KS-1807 PR-2 pull request, which is docs only and not yet pushed.

**Not done:** no request against any box; no test written; I did not check whether Schemathesis or Akto currently flag item 1 (the spec-shaped request would be a natural negative-data failure).

title: api-gateway: a 401 or 403 from in front of the security service is cached as a 30 s key rejection; should an infrastructure 401/403 count as "could not answer"? (gate 31, F2)
description:
**BLUF:** A design question, not a defect found today. The gateway's `checkApiKey` treats any non-OK status from the key-validate call outside 5xx, 408 and 429 as a key rejection and negative-caches it for about 30 s (answering 401 `Invalid API key`). By the gate's reading, the real `/api/keys/validate` never answers 401 or 403 (`security/src/index.ts:775-779` skips JWT auth for that path; the handler near line 1800 answers 400, 503 or 200 with `valid: false`), so a 401 or 403 at the gateway would come from something **in front of** the security service (ingress or a WAF) and would make every key, valid ones included, answer 401 `Invalid API key` for 30 s. Pull request 1827 (KS-1788 item 3) now pins today's behaviour for a 403, which turns it into a tested contract. Should an infrastructure 401/403 count as "could not answer" (503, not cached) instead?

**Source.** QA gate 31 on pull request 1827 (KS-1788 item 3; tier 1, GO WITH NOTES, 2026-10-30), finding F2 (Note, a design question for Kam, not that pull request's defect). Verdict file (the coordinator's reference, local to her): `/Volumes/DevMASTER/WEDNESDAY/0_Brain/reference/2026-10-30_gate31-1827/verdict.md`. Related: KS-1788, where the 403 cell was asked for; KS-1174, which is about forwarding a distinct code per key failure and not about this classification; KS-1240, the original timeout work. Filed on Wednesday's word.

**The verdict text, quoted (F2, lines 56 to 59 of the verdict, unedited):**

* **F2 (Note, design question for Kam, not this PR's defect).** The cell freezes "any non-OK status outside {5xx, 408, 429} is a key rejection, negative-cached 30 s".
  * The real `/api/keys/validate` never answers 401 or 403. `security/src/index.ts:775-779` skips JWT auth for that path, and the handler at l.1800 answers 400 (schema), 503 (KS-1370) or 200 `valid:false`.
  * So a 401 or 403 at the gateway would come from something **in front of** the security service (ingress or WAF). Today that would answer every key, valid ones included, `401 Invalid API key` for 30 s.
  * Pinning today's behaviour is what the ticket asked for, so this is fine to merge. But this PR now makes it a pinned contract, so whether an infrastructure 401/403 should count as "could not answer" deserves a ruling.

**Board search before filing** (issues filter over title, description and comment bodies, archived included, 2026-10-30): random-token control 0 hits; positive control `checkApiKey` 1 hit (KS-1788). `couldNotAnswer` 0, `infrastructure 401` 0, `negative cache` 2 (KS-1788, KS-1207: neither asks this), `keys/validate` 23 (read: KS-1174, KS-1788, KS-1240 for ingress, WAF, status or "could not answer" text: none asks whether an infrastructure 401/403 is a rejection), `WAF` 8 (none about the key-validate call).

**Not measured by this filing:** the security service's routes (the statements about them are the gate's reading, not re-read here); what any ingress or WAF in front of the service answers in practice; whether one exists on any box.

title: DocumentKeyMigrationSweep reports "1 failed" on every revisit for the DbSeeder fixture upload, which has no blob by design
description:
## What happens

dev-ps (S `abbd542`, 29–30 Oct 2026) logs this at every revisit:

`DocumentKeyMigrationSweep: upload b7de5d6c-0000-4000-8000-1a2b3c4d5e6f (organisation 5) not migrated: blob not found … 0 migrated, 1 failed`

That GUID is the DbSeeder's cross-org fixture (`DbSeeder.cs:1538`), described there as "no physical blob backs this fixture". The sweep can never migrate it, so [PS-957](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-957/key-lifecycle-disablerevoke-erasure-dissolution-audit-docs-and-runbook)'s failure count is never zero on a seeded database, and a real failure is harder to see beside it.

## Fix

`CandidatesAsync` excludes any blob key that a `DocumentTransaction` with `ExternalRef == CardanoAnchorRefresher.SeedFixtureExternalRef` names. That is the existing "this is the seed fixture" marker, which the anchor refresher already honours.

## Acceptance

* A seeded fixture is no longer a candidate, and a real legacy blob still is (xUnit).
* dev-ps logs no "1 failed" after deploy.

title: S credits a shared platform-k document anchor's transaction to every event on it: a share and a transfer show "confirmed on chain" with the upload's transaction
description:
## What happens

platform-k keeps one anchor row per (document, network) ([KS-1384](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1384/one-anchor-row-per-document-id-network-a-repeat-post-apianchors-resets)). Because of that, `/share`, `/transfer-custody` and `/lifecycle-events` return the **document's** anchor id, not an anchor for the event. When that anchor confirms, S's refresher stamps the anchor's transaction on every S row holding the ref. On chain, though, that transaction records one thing only: label 674, `type: "document"`, the document's hash. Lineage repeats the claim: it reads K live for the edge's ref and shows "anchored".

**Seen live on dev-ps, 29 Oct 2026** (S `abbd542` ↔ Kintsugi `e3d8456ec`), document 19:

* Rows 108 (share) and 109 (rights-assign) now carry `b1cc72f9…`, block 4801203. That is the **upload's** transaction: type document, hash `00cf73f4…`.
* They got it through [PS-577](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-577/91-uat-anchors-are-stuck-reporting-failed-while-platform-ks-verify) corroboration. K failed `anchor_c09c1b1f-…` at 08:56:14 UTC. On its next tick S called `VerifyByHashAsync` once per row, the two calls 22 ms apart at 08:56:52. K's verify healed the document and answered with the same anchor id, confirmed, carrying the upload's transaction.

The same shape was seen on uat-ps through the ordinary poll: rows 80–83 all took the sign-cert version's transaction. uat-ps is out of scope here because it is behind dev-ps.

Evidence: [PS-895](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-895/question-in-simulated-anchoring-six-distinct-lifecycle-events-on-one) (30 Oct comment), [KS-1384](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1384/one-anchor-row-per-document-id-network-a-repeat-post-apianchors-resets) (30 Oct comment), and the review's 30 Oct section.

## Fix (plan approved by Stuart, 30 Oct)

A ref returned by `/share`, `/transfer-custody` or `/lifecycle-events` is the document's anchor. S stores it as `kdoc:<ref>`.

* The refresher reads it by the bare ref and never runs [PS-577](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-577/91-uat-anchors-are-stuck-reporting-failed-while-platform-ks-verify) corroboration for it.
* On confirmation it becomes `kdoc:<tx>` and leaves the poll. It is **never** given `AnchorTxHash`, so it keeps the [PS-1285](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1285/verify-page-record-the-anchors-read-back-identity-only-when-its) sibling link without claiming on-chain proof.
* Owning routes are unchanged: originate, version + anchor, certifications/issue, and the flat fallback.
* Lineage shows a new state, "recorded on platform-k — no separate on-chain record", and keeps the bare ref, so the k-live specs still resolve it on K.
* New setting `CardanoAnchor:LifecycleAnchorsPerEvent` (default false), to flip when [KS-1384](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1384/one-anchor-row-per-document-id-network-a-repeat-post-apianchors-resets)'s per-event anchors ship.
* A data migration repairs rows already stamped this way: a shared-route action whose transaction another row of the same document also holds.
* Also fixed: the refresher's "backfilled N txHash(es)" line counted park stamps. It now logs confirmed, parked and cleared separately.

## Acceptance

1. In the document-19 replay (xUnit), the share and transfer rows get no `AnchorTxHash` and make zero verify calls, while the upload confirms.
2. The sign, declare and flat-fallback rows still confirm on their own transactions.
3. After deploy, dev-ps rows 108 and 109 read `kdoc:b1cc72f9…` with no transaction hash, and a new share on dev-ps shows "recorded on platform-k" in Lineage.
4. A revisit that only parks rows logs no "backfilled".
