title: Docs claim rules the code does not apply: share checks no document access, ownerless documents skip the read check, a revoked key works 60 s at the gateway, the admin dashboard reads X-Tenant-Override, metering is certification-only
description:
**BLUF:** Five statements in the platform-k security docs describe a rule the code does not apply: document share checks no per-document access, a document with no recorded owner skips the read check, a revoked API key is still accepted by the gateway for up to 60 seconds, `GET /api/admin/dashboard` reads `X-Tenant-Override` from the raw header for an `ORG_ADMIN`, and the claim that agent document operations are metered holds only for certification operations. Read from code at `develop` `530f09112`; none of these was exercised against a running stack.

Found while re-verifying the platform-k docs for KS-1807 (PR-1). The docs and the code disagree on each; PR-1 describes what is built, names this ticket beside the passage, and does not write either behaviour as the intended one.

## Items

1. **Share has no per-document access check.** `POST /api/documents/{id}/share` (`services/originate/src/routes/documents.ts`): after the role-or-scope gate (`DOCUMENT_WRITE_ROLES` or `documents:share`) the handler runs `getDocument(id, tenantId)` and answers 404 only when the document is absent from the tenant; it never compares the caller with the owner, a recipient or an admin. `AGENT-DOCUMENT-OPERATION-RULES.md` R4 says "ownership checks still apply on read/share/revoke". Same class as KS-1688 (version) and KS-1814 (anchor; fixed), and as KS-1833/KS-1834 (lifecycle events).
2. **Ownerless documents skip the read check.** `GET /api/documents/{id}`: the refusal is guarded by `userId && document.owner?.id && document.owner.id !== userId && !isAdmin && !isRecipient`. `documentRepo` maps the owner as `row.owner_user_id || row.issuer_user_id || ''`, so a row with neither column set has `owner.id === ''` and the guard is false for every caller in the tenant. The inventory (§2.3) says reading needs owner, admin, recipient or creating connector. Not measured: how many rows have no owner.
3. **A revoked key keeps working at the gateway.** `services/api-gateway/src/middleware/auth.ts` caches a valid `sk_` key in `apiKeyCache` for 60 s (a rejection for 30 s); nothing outside tests deletes or clears the cache (zero hits for `apiKeyCache.delete` and `apiKeyCache.clear`; control: `apiKeyCache.set` has two). The security service's revoke is immediate. The rules doc R6 says keys are "revocable immediately", contract §5 says "takes effect on next validate", and the rotation grace default `API_KEY_ROTATION_GRACE_SECONDS=0` was ruled "instant revoke" (2026-08-07, KS-577).
4. `X-Tenant-Override` **is read raw by one admin route.** The inventory (§2.4) says the override is "honoured only for the super-admin list". The gateway applies that list when it sets the tenant GUC, but it also allow-lists the header through to the services (`TRUST_HEADER_ALLOW_LIST` in `services/api-gateway/src/utils/trustHeaders.ts`), and `GET /api/admin/dashboard` in `services/originate/src/routes/adminConfig.ts` reads `req.headers['x-tenant-override']` itself and, if it is a UUID, counts documents, users and verifications for that tenant under `runWithPlatformScope`; with no header it returns platform-wide totals. That router admits `ORG_ADMIN` (`requireRole('SYSTEM_ADMIN', 'ORG_ADMIN')`) and so does the gateway's `/api/admin/` proxy (`enforceAdminProxy`). By this reading an `ORG_ADMIN` can read counts for another tenant. Counts only; not exercised live.
5. **Metering covers certifications only.** The rules doc R7 says agent document operations are metered (KS-320). `charge_events` rows are inserted only by `services/originate/src/services/chargeEvents.ts`, which only `routes/certifications.ts` calls for writes; `documents.ts` and anchoring do not import it. Create, version, share, revoke, transfer-custody and anchor write none. Which operations should be metered is a product call, not a code reading.

Related and not repeated: KS-1433 (connectors cannot revoke; unenforced scopes), KS-1688, KS-1833, KS-1834, KS-1814.

Searched the board before filing: `x-tenant-override` 8 hits (none about the dashboard; KS-1704 is about a super-admin's override), `apiKeyCache` 0, `charge_events` 1 (KS-1401, RLS on the table, not coverage), `lifecycle-events` hits KS-1833 and KS-1834 (excluded above). Controls in the same session: `subjects:erase` returned KS-843.

## Suggested direction (your call)

Per the ruling recorded on KS-1668 the docs lead and the code aligns. Items 1 and 2 are access checks in originate; item 3 is a cache invalidation or a stated TTL; item 4 is to read the override from the verified request context, not the header; item 5 needs a ruling on what is metered first.

nodes.body: **BLUF:** Item 4 (`GET /api/admin/dashboard` reads `X-Tenant-Override` for an `ORG_ADMIN`) is now tracked as KS-2145, split out on 2026-11-09 so that it can be fixed and tested on its own. Re-read from code at develop `273de443c30c`: it still holds as written here, and an independent read by our QA gate on 2026-11-09 found the same route. This ticket keeps items 1, 2, 3 and 5; its state and priority are unchanged.

title: Scope vocabulary and enforcement drift: five scopes gate nothing or name missing routes, gateway requireScope ignores <resource>:*, mints never call validateScopes, * is mintable by every key-admin role (SCOPES.md vs code)
description:
**BLUF:** Six differences between what `SCOPES.md` (and the KS-540 inventory) say about scopes and what the code enforces. Five scopes in the vocabulary gate nothing or name routes that do not exist; the gateway's `requireScope` does not honour `<resource>:*` although the shared helper does; the key mints never call `validateScopes`; `*` can be minted by every key-admin role although the docs say super-admin only; and gates and mints use scope strings that are not in the 32-member `SCOPES` array. `anchors:read` and `documents:revoke` (minted but unenforced) are already tracked in KS-1433 and are not repeated here. Read from code at `develop` `530f09112`; the gateway and mint behaviour was not exercised against a running stack.

Found while re-verifying the platform-k docs for KS-1807 (PR-1). PR-1 rewrites `SCOPES.md` to describe what is built and marks each open question `UNDECIDED (KS-1807, 2026-10-30)`; this ticket is where the code side is decided.

## Items

1. **Declared, enforced nowhere.** `certifications:share`: `POST /api/certifications/{id}/share` exists in `services/originate/src/routes/certifications.ts` with no scope or role check (and is not in the published spec). `certifications:revoke`: the route checks the caller is the certification's issuer, no scope (not in the spec). `analytics:read`: the `/api/analytics` gateway mount is authentication only. `analytics:export`: `POST /api/analytics/exports` exists (in the spec) with no scope check. `users:write`: no reference in any source file outside `packages/shared/src/security/scopes.ts`.
2. **Names routes that do not exist.** `certifications:sign` (no `/{id}/sign` route in originate, not in the spec), `kyc:submit` (no `/api/kyc/submit`), `kyc:read` (no `/api/kyc/status`). The vocabulary entries are pinned by `packages/shared/src/__tests__/ks843-subjects-erase-scope.test.ts`, so removing them is a decision and a test edit.
3. **Gateway wildcard.** `services/api-gateway/src/middleware/scopes.ts` `requireScope` tests `userScopes.includes(s)` (exact) plus a lone `*`; the imported shared `hasScope` is shadowed by a local `const hasScope` in the same function. A key holding only `documents:*` is refused 403 on `GET /api/documents` and every other `/api/documents` method except create (the gateway's create handler in `routes/verification.ts` does accept `documents:*`). The KS-843 comment in the same file already calls the exact match "silent". No gateway test covers a `<resource>:*` key (control: the shared tests have 8 such cells).
4. **No validation at mint.** `services/security/src/index.ts` mint schema is `scopes: z.array(z.string()).default(['read'])`; originate `POST /api/admin/api-keys` (`services/originate/src/routes/adminConfig.ts`) stores the list as given; the shared `validateScopes` has no caller outside its own tests. The default `read` is not a vocabulary scope.
5. `*` **is not reserved.** `decideMint` in `services/security/src/provisioningPolicy.ts` allows every `KEY_ADMIN_ROLES` member (`SYSTEM_ADMIN`, `SUPER_ADMIN`, `ORG_ADMIN`, `ISSUER_ADMIN`, `ADMIN`) with any scope list, `*` included; only a provisioning key is refused wildcards. `SCOPES.md` says `*` is "reserved for super-admin keys".
6. **Out-of-vocabulary strings in use.** `webhooks:manage` (gates `/api/webhooks`), `users:create` (accepted by auth's `POST /api/users/stub`), `register` (legacy literal in the gateway's create handler), `metering:read` (minted onto the metering key by `services/tenant-provisioning/src/meteringKey.ts`; no gate reads it), `read`/`write` (mint defaults and the fixed set the admin portal sends), and the OAuth list (`verify:read`, `admin:read`, `admin:write` in `services/auth/src/services/oauth.ts`). The KS-540 inventory raised items 3, 4 and 6 as F-3, F-4 and F-5 on 2026-07-31; none is done.

Related and not repeated: KS-1433 (anchors:read, documents:revoke), KS-1777 (the flat 403 body of `requireScope`), KS-1653 (`certifications:write` admits `POST /api/users/stub`), KS-839 (OAuth `*`), KS-1535 and KS-1536 (which roles may mint keys).

Searched the board before filing: `certifications:share`, `certifications:revoke`, `analytics:read`, `users:write`, `kyc:submit`, `certifications:sign`, `metering:read` and `hasScope` each 0 hits; `wildcard` 4 hits (KS-839, KS-1584, KS-1156, KS-1210, none about the gateway helper); `validateScopes` 2 hits (KS-839, KS-1156). Controls in the same session: `subjects:erase` returned KS-843 and `documents:revoke` returned KS-1433.

## Suggested direction (your call)

Per the ruling recorded on KS-1668 (docs lead, code aligns), either make each declared scope gate its route, or take the entry out of the vocabulary and out of the docs; make `requireScope` call `hasScope`; call `validateScopes` at both mints; restrict `*` to the roles the docs name. Which of these is intended is open, and PR-1 says so in the docs.

title: POST /api/kyc/:id/review has no role or owner check: any signed-in caller can approve a verification and set its level, though the spec declares 403 "Reviewer role required" (four more admin-labelled routes ungated)
description:
**BLUF:** `POST /api/kyc/:id/review` approves or rejects a KYC verification and sets its `currentLevel` (up to `GOVERNMENT`), but it checks no role and no ownership. The only authentication in front of it is `jwtAuthenticate` on `/api` inside the kyc service and `authenticateToken(true)` on the `/api/kyc` gateway mount, so any signed-in caller who knows the id of a verification in state `under_review` can decide it. The published spec declares `403 Reviewer role required` on this operation. Four more routes that their own comments or the spec call admin-only have the same shape. Read from code at `develop` `530f09112`; nothing was probed against a running stack.

Found while re-verifying the platform-k docs for KS-1807 (PR-1, authentication, roles and scopes). Doc-versus-code difference: the spec (and the inventory's "they rely on gateway auth + ownership/tenant checks") says a gate exists; the code has none.

## The routes

1. **kyc review** — `services/kyc/src/index.ts`, handler for `POST /api/kyc/:id/review`. It parses `reviewVerificationSchema` (`status` approved or rejected, optional `reviewNotes`, optional `newLevel` NONE to GOVERNMENT), takes `reviewerId` from `req.user?.userId` (falling back to the string `admin`), then writes `verification.status` and, on approval, `verification.currentLevel = data.newLevel || verification.requestedLevel` and saves it. There is no `requireRole`, and nothing compares the verification's owner with the caller. Spec: `services/kyc/src/kyc.openapi.ts` declares the 403 with the description "Reviewer role required". Gateway: the `/api/kyc` mount in `services/api-gateway/src/routes/proxy.ts` is `authenticateToken(true)` plus the proxy. Not checked: whether the verification's `currentLevel` is read back into a user's token level elsewhere.
2. **governance** — `POST /api/governance/process-expired` in `services/governance/src/routes/governance.ts` (comment: "admin/cron endpoint"); spec `governance.openapi.ts` declares 403 "Admin role required". The gateway mount `/api/governance` uses `authenticateToken(false)` (the shape KS-736 tracks).
3. **transfer** — `POST /api/delegations/admin/process-expired` in `services/transfer/src/routes/delegations.ts` (comment: "admin trigger"). Mount is authentication only.
4. **staking** — `GET /api/stake/all` in `services/staking/src/routes/stake.ts` (comment: "List all stakes (admin)"); the handler pages `SELECT * FROM svc_stake_positions`. Mount is authentication only. Not checked: whether that table is tenant-scoped.
5. **wallet-connector** — `GET /api/wallets/sessions` in `services/wallet-connector/src/server.ts` (comment: "List active sessions (admin)"). Mount is authentication only.

For all five the service mounts no role gate (a census of `services/*/src` for `requireRole`, role comparisons and `isAllowedByRoleOrScope` finds none in kyc, governance, transfer, staking or wallet-connector; the same census finds originate's 73 hits, so the instrument fires).

## Evidence and how to confirm

Read at `develop` `530f09112`. A live check is one request per route with a token whose role is `OWNER` (the self-registration default); the expected answer by the spec is 403, and by this reading it is 2xx (or 404 for an unknown id). Not run.

## Suggested direction (your call)

Peter's ruling recorded on KS-1668: the docs lead and the code aligns to them; Kam decides which side moves. The aligned fix is a role gate on each route (the shared `requireRole` in `packages/shared/src/middleware/index.ts` is already mounted in billing, tokenisation and vc-issuer), and for the kyc review an owner-not-reviewer check as well. KS-1807's PR-1 documents the difference rather than the intended gate, and marks the passage so a test is not written against current behaviour.

Searched the board before filing: `Reviewer role required` 0 hits, `process-expired` 1 unrelated hit (KS-1762), `kyc/:id/review` 1 unrelated hit (KS-1327, a read-modify-write race). Control in the same session: `subjects:erase` returned KS-843.

nodes.body:
**BLUF:** Delivered: PR 1840 merged as b1216f1040cb on develop, deployed to kintsugi at b1fb543640e7 (2026-11-01). Verified by code read, not observed live. Left open: four routes the 2026-10-30 comment names as not covered and "reported for separate tickets" have no ticket on the board that I could find.

- **In the code at b1fb543640e7:** the shared `isPlatformRole` gates the five admin-labelled routes: `POST /api/kyc/:id/review` (`kyc/src/index.ts:30`; the review also refuses its own subject, `:1063`), `POST /process-expired` (`governance/src/routes/governance.ts:495`), `GET /all` (`staking/src/routes/stake.ts:451`), `POST /admin/process-expired` (`transfer/src/routes/delegations.ts:273`) and `GET /api/wallets/sessions` (`wallet-connector/src/server.ts:261`).
- **Not covered, from that comment:** `GET /api/kyc/:id`, `GET /api/kyc/user/:userId`, `DELETE /api/kyc/user/:userId/data` have no owner check, and `POST /api/kyc/initiate` takes the subject from the body. KS-1882 states that these four were reported separately and are not listed there.

**BLUF:** Pull request 1840 is ready to merge for this ticket after QA gate 45 (GO WITH NOTES): https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/1840. Nothing is merged or deployed.

* Head `a91b45726ef47099d6c0375536c748702daf14f0`, with develop `ddc644fb4869` merged in. Against develop it is 15 files: five route checks, five new test files (72 cells), three existing test files whose test user's role changed (no assertion changed), and the docs entry as two fragment files. The code and test files are byte-identical to the gated head `4b166a00d60b`.
* `POST /api/kyc/:id/review`, `POST /api/governance/process-expired`, `POST /api/delegations/admin/process-expired`, `GET /api/stake/all` and `GET /api/wallets/sessions` now answer 403 to any caller who is not SYSTEM_ADMIN or SUPER_ADMIN. The check is the shared `isPlatformRole`; its case fold admits lower-case `system_admin`. The review also refuses the verification's own subject, with both ids case-folded, and refuses an id that is missing or not a string.
* Red at develop in every service (kyc 18 of 24, the other four 9 of 12). With the change: kyc 58/58, governance 179/179, transfer 104/104, staking 78/78, wallet-connector 61/61. 59 of 59 mutants killed, plus 8 of 8 on the id fold.
* Pre-push hook on the merge-prep push: 13 of 16 legs ran, 3 skipped (legs 3, 4 and 8 need a local stack), nothing failed. That is not a full pass. develop has since moved by one file this PR does not touch, and the head still merges with it cleanly.
* Not run: the four platform suites, a running stack. Not covered: `GET /api/kyc/:id`, `GET /api/kyc/user/:userId` and `DELETE /api/kyc/user/:userId/data` have no owner check, and `POST /api/kyc/initiate` takes the subject from the body; reported for separate tickets. The docs conflict is gone: the entry is now its own fragment.

_Edited 2026-10-30 after QA gate 42: new head, and corrected counts. The first version said 73 cells and 9 of 14; at the first head the true figures were 65 cells and 9 of 12. Edited 2026-10-31 at merge prep: develop merged in, the docs entry is a fragment, and the suites were re-run on the merged tree._

**BLUF:** The effect of the missing check is narrower than the description reads. By code reading, a forged review changes the verification record held by the kyc service, not any user's token level. The missing role and owner check stands; what is not shown is a path from a forged review to a higher level in a token. Read from code at `develop` `530f09112`; not probed on a running stack.

The description left "whether a verification's `currentLevel` reaches a token" open. Checked now (found while re-verifying `WORKFLOWS.md` for KS-1807 PR-2):

- Writes to `users.verification_level` in service source (tests excluded) exist in three places only: the gateway admin route (`services/api-gateway/src/routes/admin.ts`), the social-login path in auth (`services/auth/src/routes/auth.ts`, sets `SOCIAL`), and originate's admin route (`services/originate/src/routes/adminConfig.ts`). Control: `verification_level` occurs 5 times in `services/auth/src/repositories/userRepo.ts`, so the search can find it.
- The kyc service touches no users table: `FROM users`, `UPDATE users` and `INTO users` return 0 hits in `services/kyc/src`.
- No other service reads a kyc verification's `currentLevel` (a search outside `services/kyc` finds `currentLevel` only in unrelated code: the anchoring Merkle builder and an auth upgrade-request type).

So the review writes `verification.status` and, on approval, `verification.currentLevel` on the kyc service's own record (what `GET /api/kyc/{id}` and `/result` return) and nothing more. The published spec still declares 403 "Reviewer role required", and the other four ungated admin-labelled routes in the description are unchanged by this. The priority is the coordinator's call; this comment only narrows the impact statement.

## What this is

This is the long-lived ticket for **round 10** of the Platform S UX/UI fixes. Branch: `project/platform-s-uxui-issues-r10`, cut from `develop` at `f1de017` (the round 9 merge, #1217) on 29 Oct 2026.

## How round 10 works

Stuart, 30 Oct 2026: *"Create a round 10 new long life ticket and merge this and subsequent PR's/fixes to this branch. SystemTest will be done at the end of this process. Any testing required by the PR will be focused only on that section"*

* **Every fix is its own per-ticket PR onto the round 10 branch.** Each one is merged onto the branch on Stuart's standing instruction above. That instruction covers merges **onto round 10 only**; it never covers merging round 10 into `develop`.
* **Each PR carries only the xUnit for its own area** (`dotnet test --filter …`). The full xUnit run is deferred, and each PR says so in its description.
* **At the end of the round:**
  * one full `dotnet test`;
  * one **full systemTest run** on a claimed stack slot (S slot N paired with K slot N);
  * then a **draft round 10 to develop PR**, with the results attached to it and to this ticket, for Peter's review.
  * That PR merges into `develop` only on an explicit instruction naming it.
* **Tickets** stay In Review while their work is only on round 10, and move to Done when round 10 reaches `develop`.

title: nft-certificate: the row-owner trim is asymmetric between the two read paths, and getWalletNFTCertificates still gets the raw ?walletAddress (gate 23, F2 and F3)
description:
**BLUF:** Two follow-ups from the gate on pull request 1819 (KS-1836), neither a regression. F2 (Low): `selectReadableCertificates` compares `cert.userId.trim()` with the owner, while `getUserNFTCertificates(ownerId)` matches `cert.userId === userId` exactly, so a row stamped `'user-A '` is returned to user-A on the `?walletAddress` path but not on the bare list. The trim never lets a different owner through; mutant Mc (drop the trim) survives every cell; no write path stamps a padded owner today. F3 (Info): `getWalletNFTCertificates` still receives the raw `?walletAddress` string (parameterised equality, no injection); removing that is a design choice, not a defect.

**Source.** QA gate 23 on pull request 1819 (KS-1836; tier 1, GO WITH NOTES, 2026-10-29), findings F2 and F3 only. F1 of the same gate (the foreign-selector log arm) is being worked separately under KS-1836 and is not part of this filing. Related: KS-1836. Verdict file (the coordinator's reference, local to her): `/Volumes/DevMASTER/WEDNESDAY/0_Brain/reference/2026-10-30_gate23-1819/verdict.md`.

**The verdict text, quoted (F2 and F3, lines 32 to 52 of the verdict, unedited):**

**F2 (Low, consistency). The row-owner trim is asymmetric between the two read paths.**

* **What happens:**
  * `selectReadableCertificates` compares `cert.userId.trim()` with the owner.
  * `getUserNFTCertificates(ownerId)` matches `cert.userId === userId` exactly, both in memory and in SQL.
  * So a row stamped `'user-A '` is returned to user-A on the `?walletAddress` path but not on the bare list. Attack cell A-M2 logged `padded-row/null-row -> ["n2"]`.
* **What does not happen:** the trim never lets a different owner through. It only matters for rows whose trimmed owner equals the caller.
* **Mutant:** Mc (drop the trim) survives every cell. No fixture has a padded owner.
* **Reachability:** no write path stamps a padded owner today; every row is `'user-id'`.

**F3 (Info). The wallet reader still receives attacker-controlled strings.**

* **What I saw:** `getWalletNFTCertificates` is called with the raw `?walletAddress` string, for example `" "`, `"%"` and `" addr_..."` (A-Q log lines).
* **No injection:** the query is parameterised equality (`wallet_address = $1`), not LIKE.
* **Side effects:**
  * The foreign wallet's rows are read and cached into `memNftCertificates`, which `loadFromDb` already fills at boot anyway.
  * In-process timing difference, a median of 15 calls:
    * foreign wallet with 0 rows: 1.59 ms;
    * foreign wallet with 2000 rows: 1.91 ms.
  * That is a weak size oracle at best. I measured it over loopback in-process, not over a network.
* **What would remove both:** querying by `ownerId` and narrowing by wallet in memory. That is a design choice, not a defect.
* The userId selector never reaches a service method. Every A-Q cell shows the user reader called only with `["user-A"]`.

**Where this lands.** Its own ticket and not a comment on KS-1836, because KS-1836 closes when a deploy round carries pull request 1819's merge, and these follow-ups outlive it. KS-1836 read whole: it holds neither F2 nor F3.

**Board search before filing** (issues filter over title, description and comment bodies, archived included, 2026-10-30): random-token control 0 hits; positive control `getUserNFTCertificates` 1 hit (KS-1836). `selectReadableCertificates` 1 hit (KS-1836); `getWalletNFTCertificates` 1 hit (KS-1836); `row-owner` 0; `userId.trim` 0; `padded` 20 hits, of which the first 15 titles were read and none is about the NFT read paths.

**Not measured by this filing:** nothing was run here; the timing figures in F3 are the gate's in-process loopback measurements.

title: api-gateway Dockerfile:35: the backup `rm -f` glob misses six name shapes, a backup-named directory fails the build, and the backups stay in the build context (gate 24, F1 to F3)
description: **BLUF:** The api-gateway Dockerfile line `RUN rm -f ./docs/openapi/*.pre-* ./docs/openapi/*.rollback-*` (`services/api-gateway/Dockerfile:35`, added by pull request 1820 for KS-1823) removes two backup-name shapes. Six other shapes still reach the final image (F1), the backups still enter the build context and the builder layer (F2), and a directory named like a backup fails the build (F3). Hygiene, not a stated exposure: the gate's runtime check found no reader of the backups (the only spec reader is `index.ts:590-605`, fixed path `docs/openapi/secuura-api.yaml`). **Source.** QA gate 24 on pull request 1820 (tier 1, GO WITH NOTES, 2026-10-29), findings F1, F2 and F3 of its verdict. The two shapes that actually sit on the demo host are covered, so this is not a regression. Related: KS-1823. Verdict file (the coordinator's reference, local to her): `/Volumes/DevMASTER/WEDNESDAY/0_Brain/reference/2026-10-30_gate24-1820/verdict.md`. **The verdict text, quoted (lines 32 to 66 of the verdict, unedited):** **F1 (Low, completeness). The glob removes two name shapes. Six other backup shapes still reach the image.** * **Where:** `services/api-gateway/Dockerfile:35`. * **What:** I planted these in `docs/openapi` in my clone and built with the head's Dockerfile. | Shape | Result | | -- | -- | | `x.pre-test` | REMOVED | | `x.rollback-test` | REMOVED | | `secuura-api.yaml.pre-ks508` (the real host shape) | REMOVED | | `secuura-api.yaml.rollback-2026-08-27-ks661` (the real host shape) | REMOVED | | `.z.pre-test` (a dotfile; busybox `*` does not match a leading dot) | **STILL IN IMAGE** | | `secuura-api.yaml.PRE-upper` (the glob is case-sensitive) | **STILL IN IMAGE** | | `sub/y.pre-test` (the glob covers the top level only) | **STILL IN IMAGE** | | `x.bak` | **STILL IN IMAGE** | | `x.orig` | **STILL IN IMAGE** | | `x~` | **STILL IN IMAGE** | * **Control:** all 10 shapes are present in the develop-Dockerfile image (`ls_develop_decoys.txt`). * **The .dockerignore does not cover any of them.** `Blockchain/Dev/.dockerignore` has `docs` then `!docs/openapi`, which re-includes the whole directory. Its `*.md` is root-only, which is why WORKFLOWS.md and TRACK2_OPENAPI_MIGRATION.md also ship. No `.dockerignore` sits beside the api-gateway Dockerfile. * **Scope:** the author's mail already states "the line removes two name shapes only". The two shapes that actually sit on the demo host are covered, so this is not a regression. * **Possible follow-up:** an allow-list (`COPY docs/openapi/secuura-api.yaml ./docs/openapi/`), or `.dockerignore` lines for these shapes. That would also keep them out of the build context and the builder layer (F2). * **Reproduce:** plant the files above, then run `docker build -f services/api-gateway/Dockerfile Blockchain/Dev`, then `docker run --rm --entrypoint ls -la /app/docs/openapi`. **F2 (Info, by design). The backups still enter the build context and the builder-stage layer.** * The rm runs in the `builder` stage. The final stage copies the post-rm directory (`COPY --from=builder /app/docs/openapi`, Dockerfile:71), so the final image is clean; the layer scan above shows 0 entries. * The files are still uploaded as build context, which matters for a remote `az acr build`. They also stay in the builder's `COPY docs/openapi/` cache layer on the build host, and in any `--target builder` image. * The .dockerignore route from F1 would close this too. **F3 (Low, robustness). A directory with a matching name breaks the build.** * **What:** I planted `docs/openapi/old.rollback-dir/` and built with the head's Dockerfile. * **Result:** `rm: './docs/openapi/old.rollback-dir' is a directory`, then `exit code: 1`. The build failed. * **Why it is Low:** it fails closed, and no such directory exists today. * **What does not fail:** a clean tree with no match. busybox `rm -f` on an unmatched literal glob gives rc 0, and the clean build passed. * **Possible fix:** `rm -rf`, or `find … -type f`. **Board search before filing** (issues filter over title, description and comment bodies, archived included, 2026-10-30): random-token control 0 hits; positive control `rollback-` 21 hits including KS-1823. `.pre-*` 1 hit (KS-1823); `old.rollback-dir` 0; `x.bak` 0; `rm -f ./docs/openapi` 0; `dockerignore` 14 hits, of which KS-1289 (Done) is the `tests` versus `__tests__` pattern, a different defect. **BLUF:** QA gate 133, run on pull request 1951 (KS 1868, nft-certificate catches), observed this ticket's defect in a probe and recorded it as pre-existing and out of scope for that pull request: with `isCardanoNFTReady()` false, `POST /mint` falls back to the mock mint and stores a `minted` row with a made-up transaction hash, even with `NODE_ENV=production`. This comment adds that observation and a line check. It changes nothing else on this ticket.

* **Gate wording, verbatim (G133-F7, section 8 of the gate's verdict):** "With `isCardanoNFTReady()` false, `POST /mint` falls back to mock minting and stores a `minted` row with a fabricated tx hash, even under `NODE_ENV=production`. There is no production guard in `mintOnCardano`'s mock branch (minting.service.ts:817-833). The behaviour is the same at base and head and is unrelated to this PR, but worth a card."
* **Line check, read from source and not run.** `Blockchain/Dev/services/nft-certificate/src/services/minting.service.ts` is the same 874 lines at develop `8150eeb3802b` and at the base of pull request 1951 (`1584c0f0ff80`). `mintOnCardano` starts at `:752` and `if (isCardanoNFTReady())` is at `:759`. The Cardano mock branch builds `mockTxHash` at `:817` with the expression this ticket quotes (`Buffer.from(uuidv4() + uuidv4()).toString('hex').slice(0, 64)`), logs "Minting Cardano NFT (MOCK)" at `:821` and returns it at `:829`. The only `NODE_ENV` reads in the file are at `:158`, `:272` and `:279`, all outside `mintOnCardano`. So the `:779-796` in this ticket's description (develop `d7ddfa1f6433`) is now `:817-833`.
* **Limit of the gate's measurement (from the verdict's first section).** The probe ran the real `nft.routes` router and the real minting service with the database module, the Blockfrost client package, global `fetch` and `../cardano` stubbed, so "Cardano not ready" came from the stub. Nothing ran against a real Cardano configuration, a real database or a booted service, and the gate did not test whether production can reach the not-ready state. This ticket's comment of 2026-10-30 reads the code for how production could reach it; that reading stands as written.
* **Board search before commenting** (control term "catch and log sites" returned KS 1868, so the run is valid): "mintOnCardano" 3 hits, "minting.service" 7, "mock mint" 2, "isCardanoNFTReady" 0, "mock minting" 0. This ticket is the one that carries the defect; KS 1930 and KS 1837 hit on the same file for other defects.
* Pull request 1951 is https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/1951. No code, push, state, priority or assignee change comes with this comment.

**Evidence for the two things this ticket lists as unread.** Read from code at develop `e43a289c1c7b` while checking `ARCHITECTURE.md` for KS-1807 PR-4; not run against a stack.

**What decides when mock mode applies.** `services/nft-certificate/src/cardano/index.ts`, `initCardanoNFT`: real minting is on only when both `BLOCKFROST_API_KEY` and `PLATFORM_WALLET_MNEMONIC` are set; if either is missing it logs "mock mode" and returns false, and `mintOnCardano` takes the mock branch.

**The production guard does not prevent it.** `services/nft-certificate/src/server.ts` calls `enforceProductionConfig` with `requiredEnvVars: ['DATABASE_URL', 'BLOCKFROST_PROJECT_ID', 'CARDANO_NETWORK']` and `requireRealProviders: true`. The service never reads `BLOCKFROST_PROJECT_ID` (that name appears in the service source only in that `requiredEnvVars` line; `BLOCKFROST_API_KEY` is read in `cardano/index.ts` and `services/blockchain-verifier.service.ts`, which is the positive control for the search), and `requireRealProviders` only refuses mock flags set to `true` (`DEMO_MODE`, `ENABLE_TEST_TOKENS`, the `ENABLE_MOCK_*` family; `packages/shared/src/validation/production-guard.ts`). So a production start with `BLOCKFROST_PROJECT_ID` set and no API key or mnemonic passes the guard and answers mints with fabricated hashes saved as `MINTED`.

**Also found in the same service.** It fetches the certification to mint for from originate with no `Authorization` header, in both branches (`minting.service.ts`, `fetchCertificationData`, around lines 145 to 170). In production a non-OK answer returns null. Outside production it falls back to hard-coded mock certification data and mints from that. Whether originate answers 401 to an unauthenticated read of that route was not traced.

Still unmeasured: which boxes run the mock branch, and what the portals show for such a record.

title: nft-certificate mintNFT fetches the certification with no Authorization header: production mints fail, other envs mint on fabricated data
description:
**BLUF:** Inferred from the code, not reproduced. `mintNFT` fetches the certification from originate with a bare `fetch` and no Authorization header, against a router that authenticates every request. In production that request should never succeed, so a mint ends in "Certification not found". Outside production the same failure falls through to a fabricated "Secuura Demo Issuer" certification, and the mint goes ahead on that.

## What I read (develop d7ddfa1f6433)

A non-ok answer logs and returns null (`:154`); an exception logs and returns null (`:167`). `mintNFT` then throws "Certification not found" (`:237-239`), after it has already saved the PENDING record (`:234`).
* `minting.service.ts:171-184` (not production): the same fetch at `:173`. A non-ok answer or an exception falls through to `:186-205`, which logs "Using mock certification data ... DO NOT USE IN PRODUCTION" and builds a certification with issuer "Secuura Demo Issuer" (`did:prism:demo123`), recipient "Demo Recipient" and a `documentHash` derived from the certification id, caches it (`:204`) and returns it.
* `minting.service.ts:140-143`: a cached certification is returned before any fetch, so once the fabricated entry is cached that id keeps the fabricated data without calling originate again.
* `Blockchain/Dev/services/originate/src/routes/certifications.ts:62-66`: `certificationsRouter.use(authenticate());`, with a comment that every route there requires an authenticated Bearer JWT.

## What I did not run or read

* No run, no box. Whether any box runs nft-certificate with `NODE_ENV=production`, what `ORIGINATE_SERVICE_URL` points at there, and whether a mint has ever been attempted: UNMEASURED.

title: POST /api/documents/:id/anchor answers status 'anchored' in its 202 body even when a mid-flight revoke kept the row revoked
description:
**BLUF:** after pull request 1814 (KS-1814), `POST /api/documents/:id/anchor` writes `status: 'anchored'` with `preserveTerminalStatuses: true`, so a revoke that lands while the anchoring call is in flight keeps `revoked` in the row. The handler still always answers `202` with `status: 'anchored'`; it never reads what `updateDocument` returned. The row is right; the response body misreports it. Found by QA gate 19 on pull request 1814 (finding 1814-2), measured over a mocked repository only.

**What was read and measured**

* The write: `updateDocument(id, tenantId, { blockchain, status: 'anchored' }, undefined, { preserveTerminalStatuses: true })` (`Blockchain/Dev/services/originate/src/routes/documents.ts:1584-1587` at the pull request 1814 head `277e5ba6b7ae`; `:1534-1537` at develop `d7ddfa1f6433`, where the write has no options at all). documentRepo's KS-521 CASE keeps `revoked` / `deleted` when that option is set.
* The answer: `res.status(202).json({ id, status: 'anchored', transactionHash, blockchain })` (`:1611-1613` at the head; `:1560-1562` at develop). It does not read `updateDocument`'s return value, which is `Promise<DocumentRecord | null>` (`services/originate/src/repositories/documentRepo.ts`).
* Gate 19's cell B6: a mocked `updateDocument` that returns a revoked record. The body still says `anchored`.

**Fix shape (the gate's):** answer from the returned record, or say plainly that the row's status was not updated. Whether the real repository's returned record carries the kept `revoked` status was not measured, so read that before choosing.

**Priority 3:** the response is wrong but the stored data is right, so it is not a data-integrity defect. A caller that trusts the 202 body over a read-back would believe a revoked document is anchored.

**Not done:** no request against any box; no test written. The race window (a revoke during the anchoring call) was not driven against a database.

title: GET /api/documents/:id/lifecycle-events lists any tenant document's events without the ownership 404 that GET /:id applies
description:
**BLUF:** originate `GET /api/documents/:id/lifecycle-events` (`Blockchain/Dev/services/originate/src/routes/documents.ts:2885-2907` at develop `d7ddfa1f6433`) checks authentication and the caller's tenant only, then returns every lifecycle event of the document (`listLifecycleEvents`, :2900). The ownership 404 that `GET /api/documents/:id` applies (:1142-1160) is missing, so a same-tenant caller who cannot read the document can read its events. Found in the KS-1814 sibling sweep. Read, not run.

**What I read**

* No owner, admin, recipient or creating-connector check between :2885 and :2907. `getDocument` scopes the lookup to the caller's tenant only.
* The response is `{ documentId, count, events }`: the events as stored, with their actions and payloads.

**Why it is not fixed in the KS-1814 pull request:** it is a read, and the anchor route's write predicate is the wrong shape for it. The natural fix is `GET /:id`'s read check (owner, admin, recipient or creating connector, else the same 404).

**Priority 3:** a read gap; it mutates nothing.

**Not done:** no request against any box; no test written; what the stored payloads contain for real documents is not measured.

title: POST /api/documents/:id/lifecycle-events: any tenant user can record a lifecycle event on any document and trigger its anchor emission
description:
**BLUF:** originate `POST /api/documents/:id/lifecycle-events` (`Blockchain/Dev/services/originate/src/routes/documents.ts:2757-2877` at develop `d7ddfa1f6433`) checks authentication, the action vocabulary, the payload's shape and the caller's tenant, and nothing about the caller's role or relation to the document. Any authenticated user in the tenant can record a lifecycle event on any document. The route then calls `emitLifecycleAnchor` (:2843), which posts to the anchoring service with the caller's bearer. Found in the KS-1814 sibling sweep. Read, not run.

**What I read**

* No `isAllowedByRoleOrScope`, no owner check and no creating-connector check between :2757 and :2877. `getDocument` scopes the lookup to the caller's tenant only.
* It writes an event row (`createLifecycleEvent`, :2809), records connector provenance for a connector caller, and calls `emitLifecycleAnchor` (:2843), then stores the anchor id on the event.
* `emitLifecycleAnchor`'s comment (:1349-1362) says anchoring is idempotent per (document, network): re-anchoring an already-anchored document returns its existing anchor id. For a document with no anchor row, whether the call submits a new transaction (and spends a fee) is UNMEASURED; I did not read anchoring's `POST /api/anchors` wallet path.
* The vocabulary includes `delete` and `restore` (`services/originate/src/lifecycleActions.ts:38-46`).

**Why it is not fixed in the KS-1814 pull request:** the anchor route's checks do not apply unchanged. A terminal-status refusal would break `restore` on a deleted document. Platform S sends this route under the owning organisation's connector key (KS-1688, comment of 2026-10-19), and which humans should be allowed is not settled, so it needs its own predicate.

**Priority 2:** the route mutates the document's record (an event row) and may cause an anchoring submission.

**Not done:** no request against any box; no test written; the fee question above is unmeasured.

title: POST /api/documents/:id/sign/request returns any tenant document's content hash and a signing nonce to any authenticated caller
description:
**BLUF:** originate `POST /api/documents/:id/sign/request` (`Blockchain/Dev/services/originate/src/routes/documents.ts:1223-1265` at develop `d7ddfa1f6433`) checks authentication and the caller's tenant only. For any document in the tenant it returns the document's `contentHash` and a signing nonce, and stores a signing request, even to a caller that `GET /api/documents/:id` refuses with its ownership 404 (:1142-1160). Found in the KS-1814 sibling sweep. Read, not run.

**What I read**

* No role, scope, owner, recipient or creating-connector check between :1223 and :1265. `getDocument` (:1236) scopes the lookup to the caller's tenant only.
* The response carries `hash` (the document's `contentHash`), `nonce`, `message` and `expiresAt` (:1253-1259), and `saveSigningRequest` (:1245) stores the nonce that `POST /:id/sign` accepts (filed separately).
* So a same-tenant user who is not the owner, an admin or the recipient learns a document's content hash that `GET /:id` cloaks from them, and can mint the nonce the sign route needs.
* Callers: the api-gateway mounts it with `authenticateToken(true)` and `blockPendingApproval` only (`services/api-gateway/src/routes/verification.ts:1027`).

**Why it is not fixed in the KS-1814 pull request:** it writes nothing to the document, so the anchor route's write predicate is the wrong shape. The natural fix is `GET /:id`'s read check, plus whatever the sign route's own signer policy decides.

**Priority 3:** a read gap. It mutates no document; it stores an in-memory signing request.

**Not done:** no request against any box; no test written.

title: POST /api/documents/:id/sign: any tenant user can sign any document, can turn a revoked document into signed, and no signature is verified
description:
**BLUF:** originate `POST /api/documents/:id/sign` (`Blockchain/Dev/services/originate/src/routes/documents.ts:1271-1346` at develop `d7ddfa1f6433`) checks authentication, the request body, the caller's tenant and the signing nonce, and nothing about the caller or the document's state. It then appends a signature and writes `status: 'signed'` (:1326-1329) through `updateDocument` with no options, so a revoked or deleted document is written back to `signed`. The signature itself is not verified: `isValidSignature` (:1313) accepts any string that starts `mock_signature_` or is longer than 50 characters, in every environment. Found in the KS-1814 sibling sweep. Read, not run.

**What I read**

* No role or scope gate, no owner or signer check and no terminal-status check between :1271 and :1346. `getDocument` (:1294) scopes the lookup to the caller's tenant only.
* The nonce (:1299-1311) ties the call to a `POST /:id/sign/request` for the same document id, and that route is open to any authenticated user in the tenant (filed separately).
* `updateDocument(id, tenantId, { signatures, status: 'signed' })` passes no `preserveTerminalStatuses`, so documentRepo's KS-521 guard (it keeps `revoked` and `deleted` only when asked) is off for this write.
* `isValidSignature = signature.startsWith('mock_signature_') || signature.length > 50` (:1313): no cryptographic check and no environment guard. KS-627 is the wallet-connector analogue (`POST /api/wallets/verify`), not this route.
* Callers: the issuer UI's Sign button posts here (`frontend/issuer/src/components/DocumentDetail.tsx:252`); the api-gateway mounts it with `authenticateToken(true)` and `blockPendingApproval` only (`services/api-gateway/src/routes/verification.ts:1026`). Platform S does not list this verb among the ones it sends (KS-1688, comment of 2026-10-19).

**Why it is not fixed in the KS-1814 pull request:** the anchor route's predicate (a write role or scope, then admin, owner or creating connector) does not apply unchanged here. A signer is not necessarily the owner or a write-role holder, so who may sign is this route's own policy question. A terminal-status refusal would apply, but on its own it does not close the route.

**Priority 2:** the route mutates a document (its signatures and its status).

**Not done:** no request against any box; no test written; whether any environment relies on the `mock_signature_` prefix today is not measured.

**BLUF:** The reach of `POST /api/documents/:id/sign` is wider than "any tenant user": a connector (`sk_`) key holding only `documents:read` gets through the gateway to it, and the connector token satisfies the handler's user check. Every Platform S per-org key is therefore in reach, not only signed-in humans. Found by QA gate 32 on pull request 1829 (KS-1807) and re-read against develop `530f09112`. Read from code, not probed on a running stack.

**What is new on this ticket**

* **Gateway:** the sign route has no mount of its own beyond `authenticateToken(true)` and `blockPendingApproval` (`routes/verification.ts`); it then falls into the `/api/documents` mount in `routes/proxy.ts`, which is `requireScope('documents:read', 'documents:write')` for every method except create. A key with either scope passes. The nine-scope set that `register-connector` mints for Platform S includes both.
* **Originate:** `getUserFromRequest` returns a user whenever `req.user.userId` is set. The connector token carries `userId: connector:<id>` (`generateConnectorToken` in auth `services/jwt.ts`), so a connector passes it. Nothing after that checks a role, scope, owner or the document's status, as this ticket already says.
* **Documented now:** `docs/security/AGENT-DOCUMENT-OPERATION-RULES.md` (operation matrix, *Request / submit a signature*) and `docs/SCOPES.md` (`documents:write` row) record both sign routes as ungated, with an UNDECIDED line on who may sign that points here and to KS-1832. That is in pull request 1829, which is docs only and has not been merged.

**Not done:** no request against any box; no test written. The priority on this ticket (High) stands.

**BLUF:** QA gate 19 on pull request 1814 (KS-1814, head `277e5ba6b7ae`) found that this ticket's defect also re-opens KS-1814's "a revoked document must not be anchored", through a chain of routes. Fixing this route (a terminal-status refusal, plus `preserveTerminalStatuses` on its write) is what closes that end to end. The gate traced the chain in source; it did not drive it.

**The chain** (develop `d7ddfa1f6433` for the sign routes, the pull request 1814 head for the anchor route):

1. The document is revoked (`status: 'revoked'`).
2. Any same-tenant user calls `POST /api/documents/:id/sign/request` (KS-1832) and then `POST /api/documents/:id/sign` with a `mock_signature_` value. The sign route checks no status and writes `{ signatures, status: 'signed' }` with no options (`documents.ts:1326-1329`), so the row now reads `signed`.
3. The owner or a platform admin then calls `POST /api/documents/:id/anchor`. The pull request 1814 refusal reads the row's status and refuses only `revoked` and `deleted`; `signed` is not terminal. The existing guard passes a document whose blob is absent or `anchor_failed`, so the route anchors it and writes `anchored`.

Pull request 1814's refusal is correct for the state it reads. The un-revoke happens at step 2, which is this ticket.

**Evidence class:** source reading only (gate 19, finding 1814-1). Nothing was run against any box.

title: Declare metadata.signatureHash and the signatureHash read-back fields in the published OpenAPI spec (the other half of KS-1454)
description:
**BLUF:** The published OpenAPI spec does not declare `metadata.signatureHash` on the anchor request, nor the `signatureHash` field on the two anchor reads. The anchoring-side pull request for KS-1454 adds all three in code; the spec declaration is the other half and nothing in that pull request does it. KS-1454's own text says Platform S switches `AnchorSignatureHash` on per environment only after K serves a spec that declares `FlatAnchorRequest.metadata.signatureHash`, so until this exists the field cannot be turned on. Ruled a follow-up ticket, not a hold on the pull request, by the coordinator (2026-10-30 00:11 AEDT).

* `docs/openapi/secuura-api.yaml` at develop be2cd084d0f1: 0 occurrences of `signatureHash`. Control: `identityCommitment`, an earlier anchor field, has 6.

* The code side, on the KS-1454 branch (commit d7d3a6e3ed4b): the request field in `services/anchoring/src/anchorSchema.ts` (64 lowercase hex, `sign` verb only, 400 otherwise); the read side in `anchorReadback.ts` (verify-by-hash carries it under `metadata.signatureHash` beside `documentType`) and in the by-id handler in `index.ts` (spread into the response beside the identity fields; `null` when absent).
* Where the spec comes from: `services/anchoring/src/anchoring.openapi.ts` exists, and the root `package.json` defines `generate-openapi` (line 50) and `check:openapi` (line 42: `generate-openapi --check` and `check:spec-examples`).
* The gateway's source: no request-body validation against the published spec that I could find (no validator package or option in `services/api-gateway/src`; control: `specPath` has 15 hits). The spec feeds the 405 method map, the edge auth gate and the docs routes. This is a source read only.

title: anchoring: the in-lock confirmed write omits the transaction hash, so a same-payload upsert can leave a confirmed row with a NULL hash
description:
**BLUF:** Inferred from the code, not reproduced. The in-lock `confirmed` write carries no `transactionHash`, the front-door upsert overwrites the stored hash on conflict, and guard 2 treats a row without a 64-hex hash as "no known submission". A same-payload upsert that lands during the roughly 27-minute in-lock confirmation poll could therefore leave the row `confirmed` with a NULL hash, and the queued call would build and submit a second transaction. Money-class; ruled High by Wednesday.

## What I read (develop 6d41673e0f79)

* `Blockchain/Dev/services/anchoring/src/anchorSubmission.ts:490-499`: the `confirmed` update sets status, confirmations, block number, slot, block hash, `confirmedAt` and `expectMetadataPayload`, and no `transactionHash`; the earlier `submitted` update (`:482`) does set it.
* `Blockchain/Dev/services/anchoring/src/index.ts:1454-1456`: the front-door insert is `ON CONFLICT (document_id, network) DO UPDATE SET status = EXCLUDED.status, transaction_hash = EXCLUDED.transaction_hash, ...`.
* `anchorSubmission.ts:430-432` (guard 2 re-reads the row inside the lock and returns "already" only if `knownChainSubmission` yields a hash) and `:244-251` (`knownChainSubmission` needs status submitting, submitted or confirmed AND a 64-hex `transactionHash`).
* The poll length comes from Seat R 61st's arithmetic on KS-1816 (27.2 to 28.2 minutes); I did not recompute it.

## What I did not run or read

* No reproduction, no database, no box. I did not read the compare-and-set in `anchorStatusUpdate.ts` or whether `expectMetadataPayload` would restore the hash on the `confirmed` write.

**BLUF:** A second way into the state this ticket describes, probed by Seat AA 5th and not run on a box: after a restart, a same-payload share that the overwrite guard declines builds and sends a second transaction, and the row then names the second one.

What was probed. Source: `/Volumes/DevMASTER/!CODING/Secuura/Blockchain/5_Project_History/2026-11-06_seatAA-5th/evidence/ks1384/probe_share3.lines`, measured at develop `c5c26b2835df`. It is an instrument, not a committed cell: the real submitter, the real `spendFromView` and `WalletView`, the real flat-anchor payload builder, a stand-in chain, and the upsert simulated from its SET list.
- `PROBE declined-share` (no restart): built 1, sent 1, and the row names the first transaction.
- `PROBE declined-after-restart` (the in-memory view and attempt families gone; the coins and the row kept): built 2, sent 2, spent coin a then coin b, and the row names the second transaction.

Why it belongs on this ticket (my reading of the code, not run). The front-door upsert in `Blockchain/Dev/services/anchoring/src/index.ts`, `ON CONFLICT (document_id, network) DO UPDATE SET` at lines 1590 to 1601 at develop `14ac61bd1a4c854c17539f1cd0f518631f998fbb`, sets `status`, `transaction_hash` and the other chain fields from the incoming row unconditionally. It did the same when this ticket was written (lines 1454 to 1456 at `6d41673e0f79`). AA 5th's reading: the attempt family is held in memory, so after a restart only the row is left to say a transaction exists, and the upsert has already overwritten its hash.

A fix shape AA 5th offered, not built and not decided here: when the upsert keeps the stored payload and the row is confirmed, keep its status and hash too.

Scope notes:
- Kam's card `secuura-ks1384-share-pays-second-tx-before-stage2-1106` = a ("Leave it until stage 2") covers admitted events. This probe is a share the guard DECLINES, which the card does not name.
- KS-1384 and KS-1171 are untouched. KS-1833 widens who can reach the front door (its description).
- No open pull request names this ticket: a GitHub search for open pull requests naming KS-1821 read 0, and the same search reads 45 open pull requests without the term. This ticket had 0 comments when I read it for this post.

title: MCP 1a: the agent as a named member of the organisation — Person.Kind (Human / Agent / System), agent members with no sign-in created with their application key from Settings → Integrations, kind-aware gates, supervising member, deactivation
description:
## Why

**Rulings (Stuart, 2026-10-29): an agent can only be registered as part of an organisation (any organisation, a personal one included), and the agent is a named member of that organisation.** Today every `Person` is assumed to be a human who signs in: the T&C filter, join flows, MFA enrolment, welcome, email sends and the Users list all assume it, and the one non-human member — system `Person` 4 (`webhook@secuura.ai`, `AspNetUserId` placeholder `"xx"`, system organisation 2, seeded in `DbSeeder.cs`) — is kept out of flows by a hard-coded email check (`AssignController.cs`). An agent member needs the same treatment as a first-class kind, not another literal.

## What

1. `Person.Kind` — a `TINYINT` discriminator on `Person` (`Human = 0`, `Agent = 10`, `System = 20`; ×10 spacing, `CHECK`, fluent config in `OnModelCreating`, no data annotations, the [PS-350](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-350/t1-identity-domain-model-ef-entities-migrations-enums>) conventions; `S2Constants.PersonKind`). Migration backfills `Human`, sets `System` for `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_PERSONID`; `__probe` migration zero operations ([PS-771](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-771/accepted-issuers-should-resolve-per-organisation-not-from-one>)). `AssignController`'s email literal becomes `Kind != Human`.
2. **The agent member row.** Created only from Settings → Integrations ("Add agent", `SsdAccountAdmin` / `SsdOrganisation`) **together with its first application key** ([PS-977](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-977/the-ssp-has-no-openapi-document-no-bearer-authentication-scheme-for>) item 2's `SdkApiKey`, which gains `AgentPersonId`): display name (its `FirstName`; `LastName` empty or the model family), a role from the **permitted tiers** (`SsdRegistrationUser` default; `SsdUser`, `SsdPowerUser` allowed; never `SsdAccountAdmin`, `SsdOrganisation` or `Administrator`), a **supervising member** (an active human member of the same organisation, default the creator). No `AspNetUsers` row and no password — decide whether `AspNetUserId` becomes nullable or keeps the `Person` 4 placeholder. **Email**: a generated address under a reserved pattern that is never mailed and never accepted at sign-up or sign-in (e.g. `agent-{PersonGuid}@agents.secuura.invalid` — settle the pattern on MCP 0), because `Person.Email` is the identity key across the platform and the SBCM's `onBehalfOf` requires one. Same `OrganisationId` as its key; `TCPrivacy` left null and never gated. A personal (unnamed) organisation's sole user may do all of this: they hold `SsdAccountAdmin` of their own organisation.
3. **Kind-aware gates and sends.** An agent member is never: offered or required T&C (`TcPrivacyEnforcementFilter` reads the signed-in person, which an agent never is — pin it anyway), put through join / approval (`JoinerRoleService`), MFA (`AdminMfaEnforcementMiddleware` — it can hold no admin tier), welcome, or sent any email (`obedenEmailSender` refuses a `Kind = Agent` recipient; the invitation, reset and notification paths skip it). It **is** subject to the lapsed-subscription gate ([PS-28](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-28/subscription-enforcement-is-ui-only-lapsed-orgs-can-access-gated>)) and `TierAccess` like any member. Sign-in with its email is refused as "Invalid login attempt." with no distinct message.
4. **Rights.** Everything an agent registers is owned by it (`OwnersId`); the supervising member is granted rights on each registration so a human can always open it. The Users list, Organisation documents and Assign rights treat the agent as a member; `Assign` lets admins add further holders as for anyone.
5. **Deactivation and moves.** `PersonDeactivation` / `PersonDeactivationPolicy` apply: deactivating an agent revokes every key bound to it and reassigns its documents through the normal path; deactivating the supervising member reassigns supervision to the organisation's main contact. An agent member cannot be moved to another organisation (the move path refuses `Kind = Agent`), and cannot be the main, legal or billing contact.
6. **Identity stamp.** No change: `ActorIdentityStamper` yields assurance `None` / source `None` for a `Person` with no evidence, which is inside the SBCM contract; the organisation's DID and trust level ride beside it. Whether the chain ever says "agent" is [PS-1420](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1420>).
7. **Docs.** `docs/role-classification.md` gains the agent member and its permitted tiers; `docs/IDENTITY-LAYER.md` one sentence on how an agent member anchors; USER-GUIDE / USER-MANUAL "Add an agent".

## Done when (xUnit, no stack)

* `PersonKindContractTests`: migration backfill, `Person` 4 is `System`, the `CHECK`, the permitted-tier set refuses an admin tier for an agent, the reserved email pattern is refused at Register / Login / ExternalSignup, no sender mails an agent, an agent cannot be main / legal / billing contact or be moved.

title: The ruled-retry cell (ks726:414) paraphrases the node's reply: with the real text it fails, and deleting the clause breaks no cell
description:
**BLUF:** The cell that pins the ruled retry after a node rejection, `ks726-write-ahead-tx-hash.test.ts:414`, feeds the guard a paraphrase of the node's reply (`"All inputs are spent"`). The node's real text, stored in `ks705-submission-idempotency.test.ts:48-50`, carries a second phrase, "already been included", and the `ALREADY_INCLUDED_REPLY` clause in `anchorSubmission.ts` turns the retry off for any text that contains it. No test pairs the real text with a write-ahead and an absent re-poll. I deleted the clause on develop `6d41673e0f79` and the whole anchoring suite's failing set stayed identical to the control; and when I gave the `:414` cell the real text, it failed. So the clause that makes the ruled retry unreachable for the real reply is unpinned, and the cell that should have caught it tests a text the node does not send.

**Source** (read at develop `6d41673e0f79`, `Blockchain/Dev/services/anchoring/src/`):

* `anchorSubmission.ts:112` `const ALREADY_INCLUDED_REPLY = /already been included/i;`, also listed among the patterns `isAlreadySubmittedError` matches (`:115-124`).
* `anchorSubmission.ts:637-641`: `refusedAndAbsent = found === 'absent' && known === writtenAheadTxHash && !ALREADY_INCLUDED_REPLY.test(message ?? '')`, then `if (!refusedAndAbsent) return;`. The comment at `:635-636` says "already been included" names this transaction as in the ledger and never reaches this branch's retry.
* `__tests__/ks726-write-ahead-tx-hash.test.ts:414` the cell "a 400 "All inputs are spent" after onSigned, the re-poll finds the hash ABSENT with DEFINITIVE evidence → scheduleRetry, no submitting rest"; its fixture at `:417` is `ConwayMempoolFailure "All inputs are spent"`. The control at `:452` uses `'this transaction has already been included'` (`:453`), a text that matches no reply recorded in the repo.
* `__tests__/ks705-submission-idempotency.test.ts:47-50`: "The node reply measured on demo, as Blockfrost surfaces it": `ConwayMempoolFailure "All inputs are spent. Transaction has probably already been included in a successfully applied block."`
* Phrase census at the pin: "already been included" appears in `ks705` (4 times), `ks726` (2), `anchorSubmission.ts` (3) and `Blockchain/Dev/env.example` (1); the long form "probably already been included" appears in `ks705` only, and `ks705` has no write-ahead, no `status_code` and no absent re-poll (per Seat W 7th's reading; I did not re-read every cell of that file). The KS-1171 files that use `onSigned` or the poll constants contain neither phrase.

**Measured by me** (develop `6d41673e0f79`, `services/anchoring`, vitest, Node v26.8.1; logs in `5_Project_History/2026-10-29_seatR-61st/evidence/anchoring/`, files `j_*`):

* Control, whole suite, nothing planted: 33 files, 456 cells, **1 failed** (`threadTokenMint … parameterises mint + spend with a deterministic per-seed policyId`, which is red on develop already).
* Control mutant M0, `&& false` appended to the conjunction: **4 failed**; the three extra reds are `ks726…:414`, `ks1171-b1-absent-boundary-is-inclusive` and `ks1171b-absent-needs-both-conditions`. So the suite does notice changes to this line.
* Mutant X, the `!ALREADY_INCLUDED_REPLY.test(message ?? '')` line deleted (an exact-once replace, restored afterwards with the file's blob read back equal to the staged blob): **1 failed**, and the failing set is byte-identical to the control's (`j_failset_control.txt`, `j_failset_x.txt`). X survives.
* Probe, three untracked copies of `ks726`, each run on that one cell and then deleted: (1) unchanged, short text: **passes**; (2) the line-417 fixture replaced with the `ks705` text, clause present: **fails**, `expected "vi.fn()" to be called 1 times, but got 0 times` (`scheduleRetry` never called); (3) the same real text with mutant X planted: **passes**. So for the node's real reply the clause is exactly what stops the retry.
* Reproduce: copy `ks726-write-ahead-tx-hash.test.ts`, replace line 417 with the string from `ks705:48-50`, run the cell with `vitest run <copy> -t "the re-poll finds the hash ABSENT with DEFINITIVE evidence"`.

**What this does and does not say:** it says the real reply makes the `:414` cell fail on today's code and that no cell would notice the clause going. It does not say which side is right: whether the clause should stay is a product question, and Seat W 7th's KS-1384 revision (section 3.2) proposes dropping it. Whether the node's refusal text at the two incidents of 28 and 29 October was this long form was not measured (the logs are cut; Seat W 7th lists it as unmeasured).

**Evidence:**

* `5_Project_History/2026-10-29_seatR-61st/evidence/anchoring/` : `j_control_whole_anchoring_suite.log`, `j_m0_conjunction_false.log`, `j_x_clause_deleted.log`, `j_probe_short.log`, `j_probe_long.log`, `j_probe_long_x.log`, `j_failset_*.txt`
* `5_Project_History/2026-10-29_seatW-7th/KS-1384-per-event-anchor-DESIGN-rev2.md`, section 3.2 (the code path) and 3.5 (the six cells; sub-agent B's reading, "not run" there, which this ticket now runs); section 16 item 4.

**Searched** (issues filter over title, description and comments, archived included; positive control `parseScopeString` 17 hits, a random token 0 hits): `ALREADY_INCLUDED_REPLY` 0 hits; `ks726-write-ahead-tx-hash.test.ts:414` 0 hits; `refusedAndAbsent` 1 hit, read: KS-1171 calls `refusedAndAbsent` the reader of the "absent" verdict and says nothing about the text clause; "already been included" 4 hits and "probably already been included" 4 hits, read: KS-726, KS-705 and KS-535 (all archived) record the reply, and KS-607 (Backlog) tabulates UAT anchors by the node's text `ConwayMempoolFailure "All inputs are spent"`, which is a different defect (GET /api/anchors and verify disagree on status). No ticket describes the paraphrased cell or the unpinned clause.

**Related:** KS-1384 (the revision that proposes dropping the clause), KS-1171 (the absence rule the retry depends on), KS-726 (the write-ahead; archived, so Linear refuses a relation to it: named here only).

title: POST /api/documents/:id/anchor has no role, owner or revoked-document check: any authenticated tenant user can trigger a re-anchor
description:
**BLUF:** Surface: originate `POST /api/documents/:id/anchor`, the retry route. I read the route and every layer in front of and behind it at develop `6d41673e0f79`. The only gates are authentication (a Bearer token and an active session), tenant scoping, and the refusal "Document is already anchored". There is no role gate, no owner check and no terminal-status guard. So any authenticated user in the tenant, including the public-signup `OWNER` role, which the share and transfer-custody gates exclude by design (`middleware/documentWriteRoles.ts:24-27`), can make originate call the anchoring service for a document whose blob is missing or `anchor_failed`; on success the route writes `status: 'anchored'` over the document, revoked or deleted ones included. This is a source reading. I ran no request against any box and did not execute the route.

**Route** (`Blockchain/Dev/services/originate/src/routes/documents.ts`, `:1437-1571`):

* `:1442` `getUserFromRequest` and a 401 when absent; `:1449` `getDocument(id, tenantId, req.db)` and a 404 when the document is not found in the caller's tenant.
* `:1458` the only state check: `if (document.blockchain && document.blockchain.status !== 'anchor_failed')` then 400 "Document is already anchored". A document with no blob at all passes it.
* `:1474-1478` it calls `${ANCHORING_SERVICE_URL}/api/anchors` with the caller's own `Authorization` header; `:1489` the body carries `...anchorIdentityFields(req.body)`, so the caller's request body supplies the identity fields (the comment above it, `:1488`, is "the re-anchor path carries S's identity too").
* `:1534-1537` `updateDocument(id, tenantId, { blockchain, status: 'anchored' })` with no options; `:1545` starts the confirmation poll; `:1560` answers 202.
* Within `:1437-1571` there is none of `ALLOWED_*_ROLES`, `DOCUMENT_WRITE_ROLES`, `hasAnyRole`, `requireRole`, `requireSelfOrRole` or `requireScope` (census of the file below).

**Siblings in the same file:** `POST /` (`:373`, `ALLOWED_CREATION_ROLES`), `transfer-custody` (`:1789`, `ALLOWED_TRANSFER_CUSTODY_ROLES`, declared `:1782`), `version` (`:2263`, `:2258`), `share` (`:2464`, `:2458`), `sign-cert` (`:2936`) and `sign-wallet` (`:3204`) each check a constant built from `DOCUMENT_WRITE_ROLES` (`middleware/documentWriteRoles.ts:37`: `ISSUER_ADMIN`, `ORG_ADMIN`, `SYSTEM_ADMIN`, `SUPER_ADMIN`; the file says at `:24` that `OWNER` is deliberately absent). `revoke` (`:2650`) is owner-only: `if (document.owner?.id !== user.id)` then 403 "Only the owner can revoke this document" (`:2677-2679`). The token census finds no gate in `sign`, `sign/request` or the lifecycle-events routes; I did not read whether they have another kind of check, so this ticket does not claim the retry route is the only route without one. W 7th's comparison, `GET /:id` (`:1078-1217`), is not a role gate either: its matches are the admin cross-tenant fallback terms.

**Layers in front** (read):

* originate `index.ts`: gateway provenance (`:219`), emitter-marker strip (`:223`), the multi-tenancy block (`:226-244`), request tenant resolution (`:259-262`) and `tenantGucContext()` (`:263`). They establish where a request came from and which tenant it is in; none checks a role or an owner.
* `documentsRouter.use(authenticate())` (`documents.ts:175`). `authenticate()` (`middleware/auth.ts:82-137`) verifies the RS256 token and the session; it sets the user and checks no role.
* api-gateway `routes/proxy.ts:657`: `requireScope('documents:read', 'documents:write')` on the whole `/api/documents` mount. `middleware/scopes.ts:34-36` lets JWT and email users straight through ("controlled by RBAC, not scopes"), and `:51` passes an OAuth or API-key caller on ANY ONE of the listed scopes or `*`, with no distinction by method. A search of the gateway's non-test source for `documents:write` and for a method-aware scope check found none for this path. Whether an OAuth or API-key principal reaches originate in a form originate accepts, I did not read (`utils/originateForward.ts`).

**Layer behind** (read): anchoring `index.ts:469` is `app.use('/api', jwtAuthenticate())`, authentication only. `POST /api/anchors` (`:475`) has no role gate; the only role reference near it is the connector branch (`:554`). [KS-1603](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1603/security-pre-existing-anchoring-post-apianchors-never-checks-who-owns) already tracks that anchoring does not check who owns `documentId`.

**Terminal status** (read): `documentRepo.ts:598` and `:621-622` make the status write `WHEN preserveTerminal AND status IN ('revoked','deleted') THEN status ELSE <new>`, and `preserveTerminalStatuses` defaults to false (documented at `:520-534`, KS-521: the async anchor pipeline "stomped a revoked set by the owner ... so a revoked document verified again"). The create path passes it (`documents.ts:1015`, `:1038`); the retry route does not. `revoke` writes the status only (`documents.ts:2705`), so a revoked document whose blob is absent or `anchor_failed` satisfies the route's entry condition.

**Cost, as logged:** each accepted anchor logs a submission with a fee. Seat D 42nd's demo log shows `"Anchor submitted to Cardano"` with `"fee":179449` (lovelace) in `5_Project_History/2026-10-29_seatD-42nd/evidence/demo/moved_logs.txt`. Whose wallet pays on each box, I did not verify here.

**Real callers:** Platform S uses this route in its normal flow; KS-1688's comment of 2026-10-19 describes "the anchor kick that follows it (`POST /{newId}/anchor`)" signed with the owning organisation's connector key. Any gate has to keep that principal working; `transfer-custody` shows one shape (a write role OR a scope, documented at `documents.ts:1589-1591`). I am not proposing the fix.

**Not run, not read:** no request to any box; the route was not executed; cross-tenant behaviour beyond the tenant-scoped `getDocument` and the RLS context was not exercised; the gateway's API-key and OAuth path into originate; `sign`, `sign/request` and the lifecycle-events routes, which show no role token.

**Evidence:**

* Source: develop `6d41673e0f79c0f02c2ec7b893cc960b6fa3ec10`, the files named above.
* Seat W 7th's section 16, item 9 (and item 10, the revival): `5_Project_History/2026-10-29_seatW-7th/KS-1384-per-event-anchor-DESIGN-rev2.md`, lines 496 and 497. Its claim was a lexical count "not verified against upstream middleware"; this ticket is that verification.
* My route census and reads: `5_Project_History/2026-10-29_seatR-61st/filings/board_search_i.txt` for the board search.

**Searched** (issues filter over title, description and comments, archived included; positive control `parseScopeString` 17 hits, a random token 0 hits): `documents.ts:1437` 0 hits; "/:id/anchor" 6 hits and "POST /api/documents/:id/anchor" 4 hits, read: [KS-1557](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1557/security-a-write-role-caller-can-make-another-organisations-bytes) (quotes the route name inside an error message), [KS-1385](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1385/ks-1175-follow-on-the-anchors-k-emits-for-share-transfer-custody) (lists the route among six sites that forward identity), [KS-520](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-520/anchoring-fabricates-a-tx-sim-hash-and-marks-the-document-anchored), KS-319, KS-535, KS-566 (archived, other defects); `anchorIdentityFields` 1 hit ([KS-1709](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1709/originate-the-certification-issue-route-swallows-a-non-ok-response), other defect); `DOCUMENT_WRITE_ROLES` 10 hits, read by title: [KS-1688](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1688/security-post-apidocumentsidversion-has-no-per-document-access-check) is the same class on `POST /:id/version` (a missing per-document check on the source document), KS-547 (archived) is a decision about `/certifications/issue`; `preserveTerminalStatuses` 5 hits: KS-1424's table of unguarded `updateDocument` callers lists `documents.ts:1408` and the sync writers, not this route's call at `:1534`. No ticket names this route's missing gate or its missing terminal-status guard.

**Related:** [KS-1688](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1688/security-post-apidocumentsidversion-has-no-per-document-access-check) (same class, the version route), [KS-1603](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1603/security-pre-existing-anchoring-post-apianchors-never-checks-who-owns) (the anchoring side), [KS-485](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-485/security-review-plan-methodology-and-handover-platform-k) (the security review plan).

title: The published did:jwk pattern admits values the runtime refuses (5,000 of 5,000 sampled); POST /api/anchors has no Schemathesis override
description:
**BLUF:** The published `did:jwk` pattern admits values the runtime refuses. In a seeded sample of 5,000 values that satisfy the published pattern, `identitySchema` refused 5,000 of 5,000 `did:jwk` values, against 0 of 5,000 for `did:key` and 0 of 5,000 for `did:web`. `systemTest/schemathesis/schemathesis.toml` has no `[[operations]]` entry for `POST /api/anchors`, so a Schemathesis positive-data sweep that generates a `did:jwk` for `actorDid` or `orgDid` is expected to meet a 400. Not measured against a stack: no sweep was run.

**Facts** (read at develop `6d41673e0f79`):

* `Blockchain/Dev/docs/openapi/secuura-api.yaml:1295` and `:1320` publish `pattern: ^did:(key|web|jwk):[A-Za-z0-9._:%-]+$` for both identity DID fields. `POST /api/anchors` is published at `:14619`. The yaml holds 0 `did:jwk` examples and 1 `did:key` example.
* Since KS-1175's private-key guard, the runtime refuses a `did:jwk` unless the payload is unpadded base64url of a JSON object with none of `d`, `p`, `q`, `dp`, `dq`, `qi`, `k` (`anchorSchema.ts:165-178`). A random string over the pattern's alphabet almost never decodes to a JSON object. The JSON-decodability half cannot be written as a JSON-Schema pattern at all, so some gap is irreducible.
* `systemTest/schemathesis/schemathesis.toml`: `[checks.positive_data_acceptance]` at `:128`; the file's per-operation entries scope some paths (for example `include-name = "POST /api/auth/login"`), and the only line that names an anchors operation is `include-name = "POST /api/anchors/thread-mint"` at `:424`; the mentions of flat `/api/anchors` at `:509-515` are in a comment. The global positive-data-acceptance list excludes 400.
* The description text on both fields states the rule and the 400; gate 16 records that it is generated from the imported member list and that `generate-openapi --check` goes rc 1 when a member is dropped.

**Measured:**

* By me, on develop `6d41673e0f79`: `tools/probe_didjwk_r61.ts` draws 5,000 values per method, seeded, length 1 to 40, uniform over the 67-character alphabet, keeps those that pass `DID_PATTERN`, and counts refusals by `identitySchema`: did:key 0 of 5000, did:web 0 of 5000, did:jwk 5000 of 5000. Positive controls in the same run: a public P-256 `did:jwk`, a `did:key` and a `did:web` are accepted; a private `did:jwk` is refused.
* By QA gate 16 on the KS-1175 guard's pull request head: the same sampling gave the same three figures.

**Fix-shape (gate 16 and Wednesday's addendum prefer (a); not ruled):**
