title: For one anchor id the anchor row reads failed while its document reads confirmed; a document read and a verify can settle it either way
description:
**BLUF:** On kintsugi, for anchor id `anchor_c09c1b1f-c639-49e3-8afc-f1fb31906732` (document `deb6d3c3-1d79-4993-82a1-7a49a75aae00`), the anchor row and the document disagree. The reconciler marked the anchor row `failed` at 2026-10-29 08:56:14Z (the 24 hour give-up). The document's stored blob reads `confirmed` against the upload transaction `b1cc72f9…` (block 4801203), written at 08:56:52Z after two `POST /api/verification/verify` calls. The code has two readers that can settle the same pair in opposite directions: a document read can write `anchor_failed`, a verify wrote `confirmed`. Only the verify-first order was observed.

**Measured** (Seat T 6th, kintsugi, read-only, 09:02:43Z and 09:04:53Z):

* Anchor row: status `failed`, error "transaction never appeared on chain within 24h (reconciler)", `created_at` 2026-10-28T08:55:38.299Z, `updated_at` 2026-10-29T08:56:14.459Z, `retry_count` 0. Its stored transaction `e1df3f61…` is not on the preview chain; the upload transaction `b1cc72f9…` is (Seat T 6th's earlier reading).
* Document (originate store, found through `documents.external_id`): row status `anchored`, `updated_at` 08:56:52.914Z; blob `blockchain.status` `confirmed`, `blockHeight` 4801203, txHash `b1cc72f9…`. originate log, 08:56:52.921Z: "KS-584: healed anchor state written back to document". audit_logs: two `verification.verify` requests answered 200 at 08:56:52.930Z and 08:56:52.951Z, and no request to the retry route `/anchor` for this document.
* Not measured: who sent the two verify calls, and why the once-a-minute document reads stopped at 05:53:39Z.

**Source** (read at develop `6d41673e0f79`; not exercised):

* Document read: `documents.ts:1167` calls `reconcileDocumentAnchorState` (`services/anchorStateSync.ts:353`). At `:399-400`, when the document is in flight and the anchor row's status is `failed`, it calls `markDocumentAnchorFailed`, which writes `status: 'anchor_failed'` and returns early only when the blob is already `confirmed` (`anchorStateSync.ts:173` onward). `documents.ts:1458` lets the retry route run for an `anchor_failed` blob.
* Verify: `routes/verification.ts` `confirmStalePendingAnchor` (`:426`) and `persistHealedAnchor` (`:496`), called at `:802-803` and `:1324-1325`; the log line above comes from `:504`.

**Evidence:**

* `5_Project_History/2026-10-29_seatT-6th/evidence/reread2_0902Z_t6.txt` (anchor row, document, logs, audit_logs, with controls)
* `5_Project_History/2026-10-29_seatT-6th/evidence/reread3_trigger_t6.txt` (the two verify calls and the gateway lines)

**Searched** (issues filter over title, description and comments, archived included; positive control `parseScopeString` 9 hits, a random token 0 hits): the phrase "anchor row failed" 0 hits; `anchorStateSync.ts:399` 1 hit, read: KS-772, in Seat T 6th's comments of 05:50Z and 09:09Z on the stuck row. They describe this same mechanism as stream comments, not as a ticket, and the 09:09Z comment says the same shape on another document can end either way and that only one outcome was measured; `markDocumentAnchorFailed` 10 hits, `confirmStalePendingAnchor` 6 hits and `persistHealedAnchor` 7 hits, read by title: they concern threadToken erasure (KS-1058, KS-1074), block heights (KS-1509, KS-1333), unpinned guard clauses (KS-1676), the simulated flag (KS-1661) and others, and none describes a failed anchor row beside a confirmed document. KS-1384 records this kintsugi row up to 2026-10-29 00:52Z, before the row failed.

**Related:** KS-1384 (the per-event anchor design under revision), KS-772 (the review stream whose comments record the kintsugi row), KS-1676.

Stuart says this case came through the ordinary poll, not verify.
- **The mechanism in code** (originate `routes/verification.ts`, read at develop `40c06084919d`): `confirmStalePendingAnchor` (line 426), when anchoring's chain index attributes a confirmed transaction to the same registration (`sameDoc`, lines 463-465), returns the stored blob with `txHash` replaced by the chain's transaction and `status: 'confirmed'` (lines 467-471). title: Please bring the platform-k docs up to date with current behaviour, so systemTest can be written to the docs rather than to the source
description:
## BLUF

Kamil, when you have the capacity, could you please update the platform-k documentation so that it describes how the platform is meant to behave today? The systemTest suites take their expected results from the docs, not from the platform-k source code, so up-to-date docs are what let the tests check the platform against its intended behaviour.

## Why this matters

* **The tests are written to the docs, on purpose.** A test whose expectation comes from the source can only confirm that the code does what the code does. It cannot catch a bug. When the expectation comes from the docs, a difference between the two is a real finding.
* **This follows the ruling already recorded under** [KS-1668](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1668/docs-record-kamils-linear-rulings-that-platform-k-docs-omit-or)**:** the docs lead and the code aligns to the docs. That ticket added your Linear rulings to the docs. This one asks for the wider pass that only you can do, because you know the intended behaviour best.
* **Where the docs are silent or out of date**, the test has no source for its expectation. It then either goes unwritten, or it is written against the code, which is the habit we are trying to avoid.

## What would help most

* Endpoint behaviour as it is meant to be: status codes, error bodies, auth and role requirements, and tenancy and ownership rules.
* Flows across services, such as originate, anchoring, certification, transfer and S↔K, including what happens when a step fails.
* Removing or marking anything retired, so a test does not keep asserting behaviour that is gone.
* Where the intended behaviour is not yet decided, a short line saying so is very useful. It tells us to wait rather than guess.

The order and the split into smaller pieces are entirely up to you. Child tickets per area are welcome if that suits you better.

## Done when

The platform-k docs describe current intended behaviour for the areas above, and anything still undecided is marked as such.

Thank you very much, Kamil. It makes a real difference to how much we can trust the test results.

title: KS-1709 follow-ups: non-JSON 2xx reads 'failed'; recertify unpublished with no fetch timeout; no re-anchor for a kept certification
description:
**BLUF:** Four loose ends from KS-1709, none introduced by it. QA gate 15 (1806-2, 1806-3) and Seat U 6th listed them in comments on KS-1709, and none has a ticket of its own: (1) an accepted 2xx from the anchoring service whose body is not JSON is reported as `failed`; (2) `POST /api/certifications/{id}/recertify` is not in the published spec; (3) its anchoring `fetch` has no timeout; (4) Platform K has no re-anchor for a kept certification.

**1. A non-JSON 2xx reads** `failed` (gate 15, 1806-2, measured at runtime). `upstream.json()` throws inside the `try` before `anchoringStatus = 'submitted'` is set (`certifications.ts:619-621` on the issue route; the same shape at `:1393-1395` on recertify, read only). On the issue route a 202 with an empty body gives 201 with `anchoringStatus: "failed"`, and a 200 with the text `ok` gives the same. In production the 202-empty case gives 503 with the provisional row deleted although anchoring had accepted the request (an orphan anchor; the gate records the production part as pre-existing). A 202 or 299 with a JSON id, and a 202 without `data.id`, give no key and `submitted`; a 409 gives `failed`. The published description says "a 4xx, a 5xx, an unreachable service or a timeout" and omits this case. The gate's likelihood note: low, since anchoring always answers JSON. The gate's fix-shape (not ruled): set `submitted` on `upstream.ok` before parsing (anchorId null when unreadable), or add "or an unreadable acceptance" to the description.

**2. Recertify is not published** (gate 15, 1806-3, read). `originate.openapi.ts:27` lists `/:id/recertify` among the endpoints not yet registered, and `secuura-api.yaml` has 0 matches for `recertify` (counted at develop `6d41673e0f79`). So the top-level `anchoringStatus` that KS-1709 added to the recertify 201 ships unpublished; `CertificationIssueResponse` covers the issue route only.

**3. Recertify's anchoring fetch has no timeout** (gate 15, 1806-3, read). The issue route's fetch carries `AbortSignal.timeout(10000)` (`certifications.ts:616`). The recertify fetch (`certifications.ts:1375-1395`) carries none, and the builder's own test header says so. The effective bound is the runtime's default fetch timeout, which nobody measured.

**4. No re-anchor for a kept certification** (Seat U 6th's KS-1709 wrap). A kept certification has `anchorId: null`. U 6th records that Platform K has no re-anchor for it; I did not search for one.

**Evidence:**

* `/Volumes/DevMASTER/WEDNESDAY/0_Brain/reference/2026-10-29_gate15-1805-1806/verdict.md`, findings 1806-2 and 1806-3
* the gate's probe output in the same folder: `evidence/probe/probe1806.out` (P1 to P10)
* Seat U 6th's wrap: `5_Project_History/2026-10-29_seatU-6th/HANDOVER.md`

The four items appear only as comments on KS-1709 (07:02Z) and KS-1175.

**Not measured:** the recertify default fetch timeout; items 2 and 3 are source readings at develop `6d41673e0f79`, not runs.

**Related:** KS-1709.

title: A kept (refused-anchor) certification reads anchored: true on GET /api/documents/{id}, and POST /anchor 400s "already anchored"
description:
**BLUF:** A certification whose anchor was refused is now kept and marked unanchored (KS-1709, Kam's 2026-10-23 ruling b: "keep it, but mark it unanchored"). Its blob carries `blockchain.status` `failed`. The documents surface still reads that blob as anchored: `GET /api/documents/{id}` answers `blockchain.anchored: true`, and `POST /api/documents/{id}/anchor` answers 400 "Document is already anchored", so the documents retry route cannot re-anchor it. The comparison dates from KS-1124 F4 (2026-09-28); the ruling turns it into a contradiction on a second read surface.

**What was measured** (QA gate 15, finding 1806-1, on the KS-1709 pull request head; documentRepo mocked, the real `documentsRouter`):

* A certification is a row in `documents`, so `GET /api/documents/{certUuid}` serves it. With the blob the KS-1709 cells assert (`status: 'failed'`, `anchoringStatus: 'failed'`, `anchorId: null`), GET answers `blockchain.anchored: true` and `POST /api/documents/{id}/anchor` answers 400 "Document is already anchored".
* Controls in the same probe: a blob with `status: 'anchor_failed'` gives `anchored: false` and POST 202; a null blob gives `anchored: false` and POST 202.
* `reconcileDocumentAnchorState` returns early on `anchorId: null`, so nothing heals it.

**Where** (read at develop `6d41673e0f79`):

* `Blockchain/Dev/services/originate/src/routes/documents.ts:1200`: `anchored: !!document.blockchain && document.blockchain.status !== 'anchor_failed'`.
* `documents.ts:1458`: `if (document.blockchain && document.blockchain.status !== 'anchor_failed')` then 400 "Document is already anchored".
* `Blockchain/Dev/services/originate/src/routes/verification.ts:99-100`: `FAILED_ANCHOR_STATUSES` is `['failed', 'anchor_failed']`, so the verify surfaces already read `failed` as failed.
* `Blockchain/Dev/services/originate/src/routes/certifications.ts:1204`: `POST /api/certifications/{id}/verify` builds `checks.blockchainAnchored` as `!!certification.blockchain`, which is true for a kept failed certification (Seat U 6th recorded this in its KS-1709 wrap; I read the line and did not run it).

**The gate's fix-shape (not ruled):** use one set, for example `FAILED_ANCHOR_STATUSES`, at both `documents.ts` sites. The regression test the gate proposed: the kept-certification blob gives GET `anchored: false` and POST `/anchor` 202.

**Evidence:**

* `/Volumes/DevMASTER/WEDNESDAY/0_Brain/reference/2026-10-29_gate15-1805-1806/verdict.md`, finding 1806-1
* the probe it names, in the same folder: `evidence/probe/_quarantine_2026-10-29/gate15-probe-docs.test.ts` and `evidence/probe/probe_docs.out`

**Searched** (issues filter over title, description and comments, archived included; positive control `parseScopeString` 9 hits, a random token 0 hits): `documents.ts:1200` 0 hits; `documents.ts:1458` 2 hits, read (KS-1709's description lists that line among three other sites with the same missing `else` for a non-ok anchoring response, which is a different defect; KS-772 comments describe the retry route's 400 for the stuck kintsugi document, and there is no ticket for this defect there); `FAILED_ANCHOR_STATUSES` 1 hit (KS-1640, chain-first verify blobs: a different surface); "Document is already anchored" 2 hits (KS-1650, the check is not network-bound; KS-282, archived, document versions); "status !== 'anchor_failed'" 3 hits (KS-1628, the deprecated verify route and placeholder hashes; KS-1158; KS-1004, archived); "keep it, but mark" and "kept certification": KS-1709 only. None of these describes this defect.

**Not measured:** I read the lines above at develop `6d41673e0f79` and did not re-run the gate's probe.

**Related:** KS-1709 (the ruling and the change), KS-1124 (where the `failed` blob began), KS-1640.

title: MCP 9 (decision): a distinct on-chain marker for an agent actor — the agent member already anchors as an unverified member of its organisation; naming it an agent on the chain needs an SBCM identity-block change (KS counterpart)
description:
## Decided so far (Stuart, 2026-10-29)

* **An agent can only be registered as part of an organisation** — any organisation, a personal (unnamed) one included.
* **The agent is a named member of the organisation**: a `Person` of kind `Agent` (MCP 1a / [PS-1421](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1421/mcp-1a-the-agent-as-a-named-member-of-the-organisation-personkind)), with no sign-in, holding a permitted tier, and the **actor** (`ActorPersonId`) and owner of everything it registers. This settles what the earlier draft of this ticket called option 3 ("agent as the actor") in the agent's favour: the objection was that every `Record*Async` and the `onBehalfOf` rule ([KS-566](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-566/ks-539-g-1-split-alignment-add-onbehalfof-to-revoke-drop-it-from>)) require a person with an email — an agent member **is** one.

## What the chain shows today for an agent member, with no contract change

`ActorIdentityStamper` stamps a person with no evidence as assurance `None`, source `None`, `actorVerified=false`, beside the organisation's DID, trust level and verification. A verifier reading only the chain therefore sees **"an unidentified member of organisation X at trust level Y"** — correct, and the same statement it makes for a human member who has never verified. It cannot tell an agent from such a human. `IdentityEvidenceSource` is `None | Platform | StripeIdv | EntraVerifiedId`; the DID-method set is `did:key|web|jwk`; the SBCM rejects off-contract values ([KS-1709](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1709/originate-the-certification-issue-route-swallows-a-non-ok-response>)).

## The remaining question

Should the chain itself say **agent**, so a verifier trusting only the anchor can see "produced by an AI agent vouched for by organisation X"?

**A. Not on the chain (the Phase 1 position).** The SSP's ledger, Lineage and Verify show the agent by name and kind; the anchor shows an unverified member of the organisation. No contract change; nothing for the SBCM to do. Cost: a chain-only verifier cannot distinguish an agent from an unverified human member.

**B. An agent marker in the identity block** — e.g. a new `actorSource` value (`OrganisationVouched`) or an `actorKind` field, plus a DID minted for the agent member by `ActorDidMinter` on the organisation's say-so with a defined semantics ("vouched for by organisation X at trust level Y", never a verified-human assurance). An SBCM contract change (KS ticket with Kamil), an `IdentityProfile` subject of kind `Agent` owned by the organisation, and the SSP side under **ID Integration** ([ID Integration](<https://linear.app/secuura/project/id-integration-ede91a2b6506>)). Existing anchors are never rewritten.

## Done when

* Stuart's decision (A or B) recorded here with the reason, and reflected in `docs/IDENTITY-LAYER.md` (the five statements) and `docs/mcp/MCP-AGENT-CONNECTOR.md`.
* If **B**: a KS ticket for the identity-block contract change is filed and linked here before any SSP code; the SSP side is split into tickets under ID Integration with this project's tickets related, since the identity layer owns subjects and stamps.
* If **A**: `docs/IDENTITY-LAYER.md` gains one sentence saying an agent member anchors as an unverified member of its organisation, and why that is the honest statement.

No code in this ticket.

title: MCP 8 (decision): hash-only registration — secuura_register_hash would need a DocumentStore row without a blob, and every reader assumes one
description:
## The question

The SBCM's MCP server registers by **hash only** (`secuura_hash_document` locally, then `secuura_register_document` with `contentHash`; "files never leave the device"). An SSP agent that produced a document locally may want the same: register the hash, keep the bytes.

## What the code says today (2026-10-29)

* **No hash-only registration path exists.** `IDocumentUploadService.StageUploadAsync` is the single minting path and it takes bytes (`IFormFile`); `NewTrackedDocumentStore` is private on purpose ([PS-478](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-478/entityhelpercreatedocumentstore-can-persist-a-chainless-document)) so the genesis transaction cannot be skipped. The Outlook status endpoint advertises `DocumentRegistration = false` with "register-from-hash … out of scope".
* Every `DocumentStore` assumes a stored blob: `FileGuid` is the blob key, a `DocumentKeys` row wraps its data key, `ApplyResultBlob`, download, view, watermark, sign, share and the derived-blob path all read it.
* The SBCM originate call itself only needs the hash, so the gap is entirely on the SSP side.
* Project See ([Project See](https://linear.app/secuura/project/project-see-636bf0aca9fb)) moves cryptography client-side; `SDK-ARCHITECTURE.md` §12.1 decision 8 already has `register` carry a client-computed `X-Secuura-Content-Sha256` as groundwork. Hash-only registration sits on the same line.

## Options to decide

1. **Not offered** — the SSP registers what it can later serve, verify and share; hash-only is the SBCM's job and an agent that wants it uses the SBCM's MCP server. Simplest; splits the agent story across two servers.
2. **A** `HashOnly` **document kind** — `DocumentStore` row with `FileGuid = null`, no blob, no `DocumentKeys` row; a `DocumentKind` column; every reader branches (download/view/watermark/sign/share refused with a stated reason; verify and lineage work). Large: a survey of every blob reader first, with a contract test that each one handles the kind.
3. **Register-then-attach** — hash-only row now, bytes attached later through a second tool, with the attached bytes required to match the hash. Option 2 plus a state.

## Done when

* Stuart's decision recorded here with the reason, and reflected in `docs/mcp/MCP-AGENT-CONNECTOR.md`.
* If option 2 or 3: this ticket is split into the reader survey (with the contract test) and the tool, both targeting `project/mcp-agent`; the survey lists every `FileGuid` / `DocumentKeys` / blob-store read site by file:line on the then-current `develop`.
* If option 1: `docs/mcp/README.md` states it and points at the SBCM's server for hash-only registration.

No code in this ticket. Related: Project See, SDK §12.1.

title: MCP 7: secuura_declare_document behind the annual allowance — the metered event is certify, not register (PS-283); surface allowance_exhausted to the agent
description:
## Why

[PS-283](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-283/enforce-annual-verified-document-allowance-tier-top-ups) (rewritten 2026-07-22 for v4 pricing) rules that the commercial event is **certification / verification of a document, not its upload**: the annual allowance (`ANNUAL_PROTECTED_DOC_ALLOWANCE_*`, Free 10 / Professional 5,000 / Business 50,000 / Enterprise fair-use, plus `TopUpCredit`) is consumed at the certify path. Today nothing enforces it anywhere — `BuildUsageStatsAsync` counts DocumentStore rows as a placeholder and `TopUpCredit.DocsConsumed` is never incremented.

So `secuura_register_document` (MCP 3) consumes **no** allowance, and an agent that wants its output **declared** is the first machine caller to hit the gate [PS-283](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-283/enforce-annual-verified-document-allowance-tier-top-ups) builds.

## What

1. `secuura_declare_document(documentId, textVersion?)` — the SDK's `documents.declare` adapter (`CertifyController.Confirm` → `DocumentCertification` + `RecordDeclareAsync`), role `TierAccess.Declare` (Power user and above; the acting-for person must hold it — an agent cannot escalate past the person it acts for). `secuura_declaration_text(documentId)` returns the legal text and version the agent must present before declaring, so a stale text is refused the way the web page refuses it.
2. **Allowance**: call [PS-283](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-283/enforce-annual-verified-document-allowance-tier-top-ups)'s shared resolver; when exhausted, the tool returns the SDK error `allowance_exhausted` with the verbatim `S2Constants` message and the renewal URL, and records nothing. `secuura_connector_info` (MCP 1) gains `allowance { used, remaining, periodEnd }` from the same resolver.
3. `ActionAssuranceGate` runs unchanged — if the acting-for person's assurance level is below what declare requires, the agent gets `assurance_required`, not a bypass.
4. Lineage and Verify already render `declare` rows; MCP 2's `producedBy` extras are added to the declare row too so a declaration made by an agent is visible as such.

## Done when

* xUnit: declare through the tool writes the same `DocumentCertification` row and `declare` transaction as the web Confirm; the allowance gate refuses the 11th declaration on a Free organisation with the verbatim message; a Power-user-less acting-for person is `forbidden`; the stale-text refusal matches the web.
* `systemTest/tests/functional/tier_document_limit.spec.ts` ([PS-283](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-283/enforce-annual-verified-document-allowance-tier-top-ups)'s waiting spec) gains an MCP sibling or is extended, run on a slot once at the end of the plan.
* `docs/mcp/README.md` tool table and `docs/PLATFORM-OVERVIEW.md` metering paragraph updated.

**Blocked by** [PS-283](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-283/enforce-annual-verified-document-allowance-tier-top-ups) (the resolver and the counter). PR targets `project/mcp-agent`.

title: MCP 6: OAuth 2.1 for hosted MCP clients (Claude.ai, ChatGPT connectors) — protected-resource metadata, PKCE, dynamic client registration over the SDK's authorize/token endpoints
description:
## Why

Header-based application keys (MCP 1) serve Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Cursor and CI agents. Hosted connectors — [Claude.ai](<http://Claude.ai>) custom connectors, ChatGPT connectors, the Claude API's MCP connector (`mcp_servers` + `mcp_toolset`) — discover and authenticate through the MCP authorization spec: OAuth 2.1 with a protected-resource metadata document (RFC 9728), authorization-server metadata (RFC 8414), PKCE, and dynamic client registration (RFC 7591). The SSP has no authorization server; the SDK's §5.3 authorize/token endpoints are **OAuth-shaped** so this can slot in, and `SDK-ARCHITECTURE.md` §15 Q1 left the library decision (Data Protection tokens vs OpenIddict) open.

## What

1. **Decide the library** on this ticket before starting, jointly with the SDK's item 2 owner: the hand-rolled Data Protection tokens cannot serve third-party dynamic registration cleanly; OpenIddict is the standards route. Record the decision on both tickets.
2. `GET /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource` for `/mcp` naming the SSP as authorization server; `GET /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server`; `POST /oauth/register` (DCR, gated by `AppSpecific:Mcp:AllowDynamicClientRegistration`, default false, with a per-IP limit) — **and, per the ruling that an agent can only be registered as part of an organisation (Stuart, 2026-10-29), a dynamically registered client is provisional**: it appears in Settings → Integrations as a pending connector, an `SsdAccountAdmin` / `SsdOrganisation` approves it for that organisation (name, scopes, redirect URIs shown), and only then can a member of that organisation authorise it. The authorize step refuses (`client_not_approved`) a client the person's organisation has not approved, so the same [Claude.ai](<http://Claude.ai>) or ChatGPT client is approved per organisation, never once for everyone; authorize + token with PKCE S256 only, refresh rotation, `resource` indicator (RFC 8707) bound to `/mcp`.
3. The authorize step runs the SSP's **existing** sign-in (Identity, Entra workforce, Google, Apple, GitHub, 2FA, T&C, join-pending) — no new identity provider. A consent page names the client and the scopes. **Who is the actor on this path is the design point to settle on MCP 0 before this ticket starts**, under the ruling that the agent is a named member of the organisation (Stuart, 2026-10-29). Recommended: the organisation admin's approval of a hosted client (step 2) creates or names **one agent member for that client in the organisation**; the token a person's consent mints acts as that agent member, and the consenting person is recorded as the supervising member on every registration it makes. The alternative, the consenting person as actor with the client as provenance only, would make the hosted path the one place an agent registers under a human's name. Either way `secuura_register_document` through this path writes `RegistrationChannel = Mcp` with `RegisteredViaSdkApiKeyId = null`, the OAuth client id in `producedBy.clientId`, and the approval record id as the credential, so MCP 4's counts and badges cover it.
4. Sessions are `SdkSession` rows (hashed refresh token, listed and revocable from the person's settings page; revoked by deactivation and `SessionInvalidator`).
5. The `WWW-Authenticate` challenge from MCP 1 points at the metadata document, so an MCP-1 deployment upgrades without a client change.

## Done when

* xUnit: metadata documents match the committed fixtures; PKCE `plain` refused; a token minted for another `resource` is refused at `/mcp`; a revoked session's token is refused within `ValidationInterval`; DCR 404 when disabled; an approved-in-organisation-A client is `client_not_approved` for a member of organisation B; revoking the approval refuses every session under it.
* A manual proof on dev-ps with one hosted client ([Claude.ai](<http://Claude.ai>) custom connector), recorded on the ticket with screenshots — the register-and-see path of MCP 5 driven by the hosted agent.
* `docs/mcp/claude-ai.md` and `chatgpt.md` added; `docs/session-revocation.md` extended to SDK/MCP sessions.
* Security review note on the PR: redirect-URI matching rule, consent-screen phishing resistance, DCR abuse limits.

PR targets `project/mcp-agent`. Blocked by [PS-977](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-977/the-ssp-has-no-openapi-document-no-bearer-authentication-scheme-for) item 2 and this ticket's library decision.

title: MCP 5: agent-facing setup guides (Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Cursor, generic HTTP) and the @mcp systemTest journey — register through /mcp on a slot, see it in My Documents, Lineage and Verify, anchored on the paired SBCM
description:
## Blockers (checked 30 Oct 2026)

This ticket cannot start until the MCP work it tests is on `project/mcp-agent`. None of it is built yet.

**Direct blockers**

* [PS-1414](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1414/mcp-3-the-registration-tools-secuura-register-document-secuura-get) — MCP 3: the registration tools (`secuura_register_document`, `secuura_get_registration`, `secuura_list_registrations`, `secuura_verify_hash`). Backlog, unassigned.
* [PS-1415](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1415/mcp-4-show-what-the-ai-registered-my-documents-badge-and-filter) — MCP 4: My Documents badge, Lineage genesis node, verify-result row, Agent pill, per-key count. Backlog, unassigned.

**Blocking** [PS-1415](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1415/mcp-4-show-what-the-ai-registered-my-documents-badge-and-filter) **in turn**

* [PS-1421](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1421/mcp-1a-the-agent-as-a-named-member-of-the-organisation-personkind) — MCP 1a: the agent as a named member of the organisation.
* [PS-1413](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1413/mcp-2-registration-provenance-on-the-ledger-the-agent-member-is-the) — MCP 2: registration provenance on the ledger.
* [PS-1414](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1414/mcp-3-the-registration-tools-secuura-register-document-secuura-get) (above).

**Branch:** `project/mcp-agent`, the PR target, does not exist on origin yet. No `docs/mcp/` and no MCP spec exist in the repo.

---

## What

Two halves: what an agent operator reads to connect, and the end-to-end evidence that the whole path works.

### Guides — `docs/mcp/`

Mirror the SBCM's `Blockchain/Dev/MCP Deployment/` set, for the SSP:

* `README.md` — generate an application key in Settings → Integrations (prefix shown, value shown once, never written anywhere), choose the acting-for person, the `X-Secuura-Api-Key` + `X-Secuura-Act-As` headers, the tool table, what the agent sees versus what a person sees.
* `claude-code.md` (`claude mcp add --transport http secuura https://<host>/mcp --header …`), `claude-desktop.md`, `cursor-ide.md`, `generic-http-agent.md`, `troubleshooting.md` (401 vs 403 vs 404-when-disabled vs 409 account gate vs 429).
* Every example names the key by placeholder; a `DocsNoSecretsContractTests`-style scan asserts no `sk_`-shaped literal appears under `docs/mcp/`.
* [Claude.ai](<http://Claude.ai>) and ChatGPT hosted connectors are listed as **Phase 2** (MCP 6) with the reason (OAuth 2.1 required).

### `@mcp` systemTest journey

`systemTest/tests/functional/mcp_agent_registration.spec.ts`, tagged `@mcp`, environmental stand-down when `/Health/Data` reports `mcp.enabled=false` (say so in the skip-kinds line, the `@k-live` pattern):

1. As `firstone@lhsg.com`, create an application key in Settings → Integrations (read the plaintext once from the page into the test's memory; never log it; `sameSecret` only).
2. Call `/mcp` over Streamable HTTP with the MCP TypeScript SDK (`@modelcontextprotocol/sdk` client, already a dependency on the SBCM side; add to `systemTest/package.json`): `initialize`, `tools/list` (pin the five names), `secuura_register_document` with a fixture PDF.
3. Sign in as the acting-for person: the document is in My Documents with the "Registered by agent" pill; Lineage genesis node reads "Registered (AI agent)"; Verify by hash shows the agent line and the identity line.
4. With the paired SBCM slot up (`@k-live` pairing rule): wait for `secuura_get_registration` to report `registered` with an `anchorTxHash`; if the SBCM slot is down, the anchor assertion stands down as environmental, counted in the skip-kinds line.
5. `secuura_list_registrations` with `scope: this_key` returns exactly the one document.
6. Revoke the key; the next call is 401.

POM in `systemTest/pages/`, strict TS, `getByTestId` only.

## Done when

* Guides merged; the no-secrets scan green.
* The spec is green on a claimed slot with the paired SBCM slot up, numbers posted on the PR and the ticket; the stand-down path is exercised once with `Mcp:Enabled=false` and reported.
* `docs/platform_s_testing_cheat_sheet.html` and `docs/platform_s_testing_architecture_flow_diagrams.html` gain an "MCP agent connector" area (by area, no counts, no ticket list — [PS-693](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-693/the-testing-docs-exact-test-count-and-mention-list-conflict-on-nearly)).
* `systemTest/package.json` quality gates (`format:check`, `typecheck`, `lint`, `knip`, `test:unit`) green.

PR targets `project/mcp-agent`. This spec is the browser evidence for MCP 1, 3 and 4.

title: MCP 4: show what the AI registered — My Documents badge and filter, Lineage genesis node, verify-result row, Users-list Agent pill, and a per-key count in Settings → Integrations
description:
## What

The human side of "show what was produced by the AI and registered with Secuura". Reads the actor's kind (`Person.Kind = Agent`, MCP 1a / [PS-1421](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1421/mcp-1a-the-agent-as-a-named-member-of-the-organisation-personkind)) and the provenance written by MCP 2; no new business logic. Because the agent member is the actor and owner (ruling, Stuart, 2026-10-29), its name already appears wherever an actor's does; this ticket adds the kind badge and the model / client detail.

1. **My Documents** (`Views/MyDocuments`, `_DocumentRowActions.cshtml`, `secuura/docgrid.js`): a pill on rows whose owner is a `Person` of kind `Agent` reading **"Registered by agent *{agent member's name}*"**, tooltip naming the organisation and the supervising member (no email). A grid filter "AI-registered" alongside the existing ones. Same pill family as the status badges (`badge-pill-shared-*`); contrast checked light and dark ([PS-1298](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1298/identity-standard-domain-verified-badge-colour-3b82f6-fails-wcag-aa>) lesson).
2. **Lineage** (`LineageService.BuildAsync`, `LineageGraphDto`, `lineage.js` `SHORT_ACTION`): the genesis node label becomes "Registered (AI agent)" when the actor's kind is `Agent` (actor kind, not `producedBy`); the event detail panel shows the agent's name as it shows any actor, plus model and client id from `producedBy`. `LineageEventDetailDto` gains `actorKind` and the `producedBy` fields.
3. **Verify result** (`Views/Verify/_VerifyResult.cshtml`, `DocumentVerificationResult`): the per-action row for the registration gains one line, "Registered by an AI agent (*{agent member's name}*), a member of" followed by the existing organisation line. The anonymous `/verify/credential` by-hash answer is **unchanged** ([PS-421](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-421/identity-close-verify-by-hash-existence-oracle-p2>) anti-enumeration: outcome only).
4. **Settings → Integrations** (the SDK key management page, [PS-977](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-977/the-ssp-has-no-openapi-document-no-bearer-authentication-scheme-for>) item 2): each key row shows "Documents registered: *n*" linking to My Documents filtered by that key (`RegisteredViaSdkApiKeyId`).
5. **Users list** (Organisation › Users and `Views/Person/PersonEdit.cshtml`): an agent member carries an "Agent" pill, its supervising member is shown, and the sign-in, MFA and T&C indicators that assume a human are suppressed for it (MCP 1a / [PS-1421](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1421/mcp-1a-the-agent-as-a-named-member-of-the-organisation-personkind) supplies the kind; this ticket draws it).
6. **Outlook** rows (`RegistrationChannel = Outlook`) get no badge in this ticket; whether to show the channel for every non-web registration is a product decision for the Outlook project.

Every new element carries `data-testid="<feature>-<element>-<role>"`, row-bound ones with the id inside the value (`mcp-badge-@row.Id`), no `data-testid-id`, no `@* *@` between attributes. Timestamps through `Helpers.UtcTimeTag`. No `DateTime.Now`.

## Done when

* xUnit: `TestIdCoverageContractTests` green with the new views; `HouseTimestampFormatContractTests` green; a `LineageService` test asserts the genesis node is labelled for an agent only when the actor's kind is `Agent`; a `_VerifyResult` render test asserts the line appears for an MCP-registered row and is absent for a web one, and that no email or name reaches it.
* Lineage, My Documents and Verify screenshots light + dark attached to the PR.
* `docs/USER-GUIDE.md` and `docs/USER-MANUAL.md` gain "Documents registered by an AI agent"; `docs/role-classification.md` gains the agent member (which tiers it may hold, from MCP 1a / [PS-1421](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1421/mcp-1a-the-agent-as-a-named-member-of-the-organisation-personkind)).
* a11y: the new pill passes the a11y sweep's contrast check on both themes.

Browser evidence: MCP 5's `@mcp` journey asserts the badge, the lineage label and the verify line end to end. PR targets `project/mcp-agent`.

title: MCP 3: the registration tools — secuura_register_document, secuura_get_registration, secuura_list_registrations, secuura_verify_hash as thin adapters over the SDK /api/sdk/v1 services
description:
## What

The four tools an agent uses to register what it produced and to see it afterwards. Each is a thin adapter: resolve the agent member (a `Person` of kind `Agent`, MCP 1a / [PS-1421](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1421/mcp-1a-the-agent-as-a-named-member-of-the-organisation-personkind)) from the MCP principal (MCP 1), apply the `TierAccess` role set the matching controller applies, call the **same service the SDK adapter calls** ([PS-977](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-977/the-ssp-has-no-openapi-document-no-bearer-authentication-scheme-for>) item 4), project the result. No business logic in the MCP layer.

| Tool | Input schema | Calls | Returns |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| `secuura_register_document` | `fileName`, `contentBase64` (≤ 5 MiB decoded, the `DocumentUploadOptions.ForRegister()` allow-list and cap unchanged), optional `title`, optional `sha256` (refused on mismatch, `hash-mismatch`, the SDK's `X-Secuura-Content-Sha256` rule), optional `agent { model, client }` (the name is the member's own) | `IDocumentUploadService.StageUploadAsync(file, agentMember, options, ct)` → `SaveChangesAsync` with `RollbackFileAsync` on failure, exactly as `OutlookApiController.UploadDocument` does; the agent member is actor and owner; its supervising member is granted rights (MCP 1a / [PS-1421](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1421/mcp-1a-the-agent-as-a-named-member-of-the-organisation-personkind)); provenance `Mcp` + key id + model / client (MCP 2) | `documentId`, `sha256`, `chainId`, `registration: pending|registered|unavailable`, `verifyUrl` |
| `secuura_get_registration` | `documentId` | owner / rights-holder / org-admin scope as `LineageController.Graph` | anchor state (`AnchorState`), `anchorTxHash`, `anchorNetwork`, `anchorConfirmedAt`, Cardanoscan link, `producedBy` block |
| `secuura_list_registrations` | `scope: this_key|agent`, `page`, `limit ≤ 100` — `agent` is every registration by this agent member across its keys; there is no `organisation` scope: an agent sees its own, and the organisation's humans see every agent's in the web app (MCP 4) | `DocumentStore` filtered by `RegisteredViaSdkApiKeyId` / `OwnersId`, `RegistrationChannel = Mcp` | ids, titles, hashes, anchor state, actor name |
| `secuura_verify_hash` | `sha256` | `ICardanoAnchorService.VerifyByHashAsync` + `IDocumentLifecycleResolver.ResolveByHashAsync` — the `/api/outlook/verify` shape, identity lines server-computed, **no names or emails** | the `DocumentVerificationResult` projection |

Rules:

* Tool names and descriptions follow the SBCM's `secuura_*` wording where the meaning is the same (`platform-k` `services/mcp-server/src/tools/*.ts`), so one agent prompt works on both.
* A key without `documents:write` scope, or an agent member whose role lacks `TierAccess.Register`, does not see `secuura_register_document` in `tools/list` and gets a tool error if it calls it anyway.
* Every mutating call returns the SDK's `ActionReceipt` fields (`SDK-ARCHITECTURE.md` §7.2) so the two surfaces agree.
* Errors are the SDK error model (§9), as MCP `isError` results, never exceptions to the client.
* **Rulings (Stuart, 2026-10-29): an agent can only be registered as part of an organisation, and the agent is a named member of that organisation.** Every document a tool registers is owned by the agent member inside the key's organisation (`DocumentStore.OrganisationId` = the agent's organisation = the key's, never another); `secuura_list_registrations` never crosses an organisation or an agent boundary.

## Done when (xUnit, no stack)

* `McpToolContractTests` pins the tool list and each input schema as a committed JSON fixture (`tests/.../mcp-tools.json`) — a tool added or a schema changed without updating the fixture fails the offline gate (the OpenAPI-pin idea from [PS-977](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-977/the-ssp-has-no-openapi-document-no-bearer-authentication-scheme-for>) item 5).
* Register through the tool produces a `DocumentStore` row identical to a web upload except `RegistrationChannel`, `RegisteredViaSdkApiKeyId` and the `producedBy` extras; `Sha256` matches; the genesis row's `ActorPersonId` and the row's `OwnersId` are the agent member, and the supervising member holds rights to it.
* A 5 MiB + 1 byte payload, a disallowed extension and a password-protected PDF are refused with the same messages the web Register page gives.
* `secuura_list_registrations` with `scope: this_key` never returns a row registered under another key; `agent` returns rows under any of this agent's keys and none of another agent's; no scope ever returns a row from another organisation.
* A registration lands with `OrganisationId` equal to the key's organisation; a key whose agent member has been deactivated is refused before any row is written.
* No test prints a key or token.

PR targets `project/mcp-agent`. The browser evidence for this ticket is MCP 5's `@mcp` journey, run once at the end of the plan.

title: MCP 2: registration provenance on the ledger — the agent member is the actor; producedBy extras (channel, credential, client, model) on the genesis row and a queryable registration-channel column, nothing new on the wire to the SBCM
description:
## Why

Nothing records who or what produced a document. `DocumentStore` and `DocumentTransaction` have no channel, source or client field; an Outlook upload is indistinguishable from a web upload; `ActorPersonId` is a non-null `int`, and until MCP 1a / [PS-1421](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1421/mcp-1a-the-agent-as-a-named-member-of-the-organisation-personkind) every `Person` it names is a human. "Show what was produced by the AI" needs a durable, queryable marker that does not touch the identity stamp or the SBCM contract.

## What

Implement the provenance model the design record (MCP 0) settles:

**Ruling (Stuart, 2026-10-29): the agent is a named member of the organisation**, a `Person` of kind `Agent` (MCP 1a / [PS-1421](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1421/mcp-1a-the-agent-as-a-named-member-of-the-organisation-personkind)). The genesis row's **actor is the agent** (`ActorPersonId`), as is the document's owner (`OwnersId`); the identity stamp runs on it as on any member (assurance `None`, the organisation's DID and trust level, all inside the SBCM contract), and `onBehalfOf` carries the agent member's own email, display name and `PersonGuid`. The agent's name is therefore `ActorName`, like any member's. What this ticket adds is the *channel and credential*, not the *who*.

1. **Genesis-row extras.** `TransactionService.RecordUploadAsync` gains an optional `RegistrationProvenance` argument that `BuildPayloadJson(tx, doc, extras)` merges as `producedBy { channel, credentialId, clientId, model }` under the `secuura` object in `PayloadJson` — no `agentName`, which would duplicate the actor. Web and Outlook callers pass `channel` only. `credentialId` is the organisation-owned credential (the `SdkApiKey`, or the organisation's OAuth client approval from MCP 6) — per the ruling that an agent can only be registered as part of an organisation (Stuart, 2026-10-29), there is no credential that is not an organisation's, so the block never needs an organisation id of its own: `DocumentStore.OrganisationId` is the owner. `PayloadJson` never leaves the SSP (CLAUDE.md), so this reaches no anchor.
2. **Queryable column.** Per MCP 0's decision: a `RegistrationChannel` `TINYINT` on `DocumentStore` (`Web=0`, `Outlook=10`, `SdkApi=20`, `Mcp=30`, ×10 spacing, `CHECK`, fluent config, no data annotations — the [PS-350](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-350/t1-identity-domain-model-ef-entities-migrations-enums>) conventions) **and** a nullable `RegisteredViaSdkApiKeyId` FK to `SdkApiKey` so Settings → Integrations can count per key. Migration backfills `Web` for existing rows; Outlook rows cannot be told apart after the fact and stay `Web` (say so in the migration comment). Run the `__probe` migration ([PS-771](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-771/accepted-issuers-should-resolve-per-organisation-not-from-one>)).
3. **Wiring.** `MyDocuments.MDImportFileUpload` → `Web`; `OutlookApiController.UploadDocument` → `Outlook`; the SDK `documents.register` adapter → `SdkApi`; the MCP register tool (MCP 3) → `Mcp` + key id + `clientId` / `model`, with `ActorPersonId` = the key's agent member.
4. **Wire guard.** A contract test over `CardanoAnchorService`'s originate body, flat anchor body and `LifecycleEventPayload` asserting none of `producedBy`, `agentName`, `model`, `clientId`, `channel` appears — the `LifecycleEventPayload` allow-list stays as it is. Adding any of them to the wire is a GDPR decision and a separate ticket with a KS counterpart.
5. **Erasure.** The agent block holds no PII (agent name and model are product strings; `clientId` is the SDK's stable app id), but confirm with the erasure path that `PayloadJson` extras are covered the way the rest of the row is.

## Done when (xUnit, no stack)

* `RegistrationProvenanceTests`: each caller writes its channel; MCP writes key id, client id and model and the genesis row's `ActorPersonId` is the agent member (kind `Agent`); web and Outlook write no credential block and their actor is the signed-in human; the genesis row's `PayloadJson` round-trips the block; `Sha256`, `ChainId`, identity stamp fields are unchanged by the addition.
* The wire-guard test above is green and fails when a field is added to any outbound body.
* `QuerySplittingContractTests` and `TestIdCoverageContractTests` unaffected (no view change here).
* `docs/VOCABULARY.md` gains a "provenance extras" note under the `upload` verb; `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` ledger section names the column.

Blocked by MCP 1a / [PS-1421](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1421/mcp-1a-the-agent-as-a-named-member-of-the-organisation-personkind) (`Person.Kind`). PR targets `project/mcp-agent`. No Playwright: a storage rule, asserted offline.

title: MCP 1: host the MCP endpoint in the SSP — ModelContextProtocol C# SDK, Streamable HTTP at /mcp, AppSpecific:Mcp:Enabled, SDK application key bound to an agent member, 401 not 302, per-credential rate limit
description:
## What

The transport and the front door, with no tools yet beyond `secuura_connector_info`.

* Add `ModelContextProtocol` + `ModelContextProtocol.AspNetCore` (pinned; `dotnet list ssd/ssd.csproj package --vulnerable --include-transitive` clean) and map a **Streamable HTTP** MCP endpoint at `/mcp` in `Startup`.
* `AppSpecific:Mcp` settings with `Enabled` default **false** (the `Outlook:Enabled` / `Sdk:Enabled` pattern): every `/mcp` route is 404 until a deployment turns it on. No deployed template states it in this ticket.
* **Authentication** through the SDK `SdkAuthenticationHandler` ([PS-977](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-977/the-ssp-has-no-openapi-document-no-bearer-authentication-scheme-for>) item 2): application key `X-Secuura-Api-Key`. **Rulings (Stuart, 2026-10-29): an agent can only be registered as part of an organisation, and the agent is a named member of that organisation** (MCP 1a / [PS-1421](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1421/mcp-1a-the-agent-as-a-named-member-of-the-organisation-personkind)) — every key is bound to one `Person` of kind `Agent`, and the resolved principal carries that agent member, the key id and the key's organisation (always the agent's own). `X-Secuura-Act-As` is **not** used on `/mcp`: a request that sends it naming anyone other than the key's agent member is **400** `act_as_not_applicable`, logged by key prefix, so an SDK client cannot make an agent register under a human's name. A key whose agent member is deactivated, or whose organisation is dissolved, is **403**. No cookie principal is ever accepted on `/mcp`, even when one is present.
* **Refusals in API shape**: unauthenticated → **401** with `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer resource_metadata="…"` (the MCP spec's discovery hint, so Phase 2 OAuth slots in without a client change) — never the cookie scheme's 302 to `/Identity/Account/Login`. Antiforgery exempt (`[IgnoreAntiforgeryToken]` or endpoint metadata). The MVC gate filters do not run on this endpoint, so the handler re-applies them itself (`SDK-ARCHITECTURE.md` §5.5): lapsed → 403 `subscription_lapsed`; T&C / join-pending / membership-changed / person-required → 409 `account_gate`.
* **Rate limit per credential** inside the handler (the global `UseRateLimiter` is per-IP and runs before auth, `Startup.cs`): a fixed window keyed on the key id, limits from `AppSpecific:Mcp:PermitLimit` / `WindowSeconds`, 429 with `Retry-After`. Precedent: `AssignRateLimiter` ([PS-887](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-887/assign-rights-lists-every-user-on-the-platform-all-organisations-full>)).
* `secuura_connector_info` **tool**: organisation display name, the agent member's display name and assurance pill text (no email), its supervising member's display name, scopes, rate-limit headroom, which tools this key may call. Mirrors the SBCM's `secuura_get_connector_info`.
* Health: `/Health/Data` gains `mcp.enabled`.

## Done when (xUnit, no stack)

* `McpEndpointContractTests`: 404 on every `/mcp` method when `Enabled=false`; 401 + `WWW-Authenticate` on no credential; a cookie-only request is 401; an `X-Secuura-Act-As` naming anyone other than the key's agent member is 400; a key whose agent member is deactivated is 403; a key whose organisation has been dissolved is 403 even if the agent row still exists; a valid key for an agent member whose role lacks `TierAccess.Register` reaches the server but `secuura_register_document` is absent from its tool list; the lapsed and account gates return the stated codes; the 429 path sets `Retry-After`.
* A startup contract test fails if the `/mcp` endpoint is ever reachable under the global `AuthorizeFilter`'s cookie redirect (assert the challenge scheme).
* Log lines name the key **prefix** only; `LoggingTemplateConventionTests` stays green; no test prints a key (`SameSecret`).
* `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` §7.5 and the MCP design record updated to "landed".

**Blocked by** [PS-977](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-977/the-ssp-has-no-openapi-document-no-bearer-authentication-scheme-for>) item 2 (the auth handler and `SdkApiKey`) and MCP 1a / [PS-1421](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1421/mcp-1a-the-agent-as-a-named-member-of-the-organisation-personkind) (the agent member a key binds to). PR targets `project/mcp-agent`.

title: MCP 0: design record — docs/mcp/MCP-AGENT-CONNECTOR.md (transport, auth reuse of the SDK application key, tool surface, provenance model, decisions)
description:
## What

Write the design record for the SSP's MCP server before any code: `docs/mcp/MCP-AGENT-CONNECTOR.md`, a documentation-only PR to `develop`, attached to the project as a Linear document (the [PS-971](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-971/sdk-phase-0-architecture-and-functional-definition-technical-marketing) pattern).

## Must cover

 1. **Why the SSP needs its own MCP server** when the SBCM already ships one (`platform-k` `Blockchain/Dev/services/mcp-server/`): the SBCM's registers directly into the SBCM and bypasses the SSP ledger, per-organisation encryption, lifecycle, shares and My Documents. Record the decision to **reuse its** `secuura_*` **tool names** and to diverge where the SSP has more to offer (acting-for person, lineage, shares).
 2. **Transport and hosting**: Streamable HTTP at `/mcp` inside `ssd/` with the official ModelContextProtocol C# SDK (NuGet `ModelContextProtocol` + `ModelContextProtocol.AspNetCore`; pin the version and check `dotnet list package --vulnerable`). Why not a sidecar Node process: one deployment, one auth handler, one ledger recorder, no second secret store.
 3. **Authentication**: the SDK application key (`X-Secuura-Api-Key` + `X-Secuura-Act-As`, `SDK-ARCHITECTURE.md` §5.2 / §5.4) is the Phase 1 credential; the Outlook token is a precedent, not a base (no scopes, no revocation, gate-skipping). The SDK user bearer token behind OAuth 2.1 is Phase 2 for hosted connectors ([Claude.ai](<http://Claude.ai>), ChatGPT need protected-resource metadata + PKCE + dynamic client registration; Claude Code, Claude Desktop and Cursor accept a header). State which MCP clients each phase serves.
 4. **Tool surface** with input schemas and the SDK adapter each one calls (§6.2 `documents.register`, `documents.get`, `documents.list`, `verify`): `secuura_register_document` (base64 bytes, title, optional `agent {model, client}` — the agent's name is the member's own, never supplied per call), `secuura_get_registration`, `secuura_list_registrations`, `secuura_verify_hash`, `secuura_connector_info`. Resources (`secuura://registrations/{id}`) optional; say whether Phase 1 ships them.
 5. **Provenance model** — settled by ruling (Stuart, 2026-10-29): **the agent is a named member of the organisation**, a `Person` of kind `Agent` (MCP 1a / [PS-1421](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1421/mcp-1a-the-agent-as-a-named-member-of-the-organisation-personkind)). The agent is the **actor** (`ActorPersonId`) and the **owner** (`OwnersId`) of every row it writes; the identity stamp runs on it as on any member (assurance `None`, source `None`, the organisation's DID and trust level — all inside the SBCM contract, nothing new on the wire), and `onBehalfOf` carries the agent member's own email, display name and `PersonGuid` ([KS-566](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-566/ks-539-g-1-split-alignment-add-onbehalfof-to-revoke-drop-it-from>) satisfied: it is a person with an email). The precedent is system `Person` 4 (`webhook@secuura.ai`, no sign-in, actor on webhook writes). Record **why not** the alternative (human actor, agent as metadata): it puts an agent's output under a human's name on the chain and makes every badge a side-table lookup. What is still recorded as extras: `producedBy {channel, credentialId, clientId, model}` on the genesis row via `BuildPayloadJson(tx, doc, extras)`, plus the queryable `RegistrationChannel` TINYINT (`Web`, `Outlook`, `SdkApi`, `Mcp`) and nullable `RegisteredViaSdkApiKeyId` (MCP 2). Nothing new crosses to the SBCM (`LifecycleEventPayload` allow-list unchanged); name the contract test that will pin it. Settle here too: the agent's **email** (a generated address under a reserved pattern that is never mailed — `Person.Email` is the identity key everywhere and the SBCM requires one), the **tiers an agent may hold** (recommended: `SsdRegistrationUser` default, `SsdUser` / `SsdPowerUser` allowed, never an organisation-admin tier), and the **supervising member** (a human nominated at creation, default the creating admin, granted rights to everything the agent registers so a person can always open it; reassigned when either is deactivated).
 6. **What people see**: My Documents badge + filter, Lineage genesis node, verify-result row, Settings → Integrations per-key count. What the agent sees: the list tool.
 7. **Gates the MCP path re-applies** that `[AllowAnonymous]` routes skip: `TierAccess.Register`, [PS-28](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-28/subscription-enforcement-is-ui-only-lapsed-orgs-can-access-gated>) lapsed, T&C / join-pending / membership-changed / person-required (`SDK-ARCHITECTURE.md` §5.5 already lists them for the SDK API) — and which of them do **not** apply to an agent member, which never signs in: T&C, join-pending, MFA enrolment, welcome. The lapsed-subscription gate and `TierAccess` apply to it as to any member.
 8. **Metering**: [PS-283](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-283/enforce-annual-verified-document-allowance-tier-top-ups>)'s ruling — certify, not upload, is the metered event — so `register` consumes no allowance and a `declare` tool waits for [PS-283](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-283/enforce-annual-verified-document-allowance-tier-top-ups>).
 9. **Security boundaries**: 401 + `WWW-Authenticate` not 302, antiforgery exemption, per-credential rate limit (the global limiter is per-IP and runs before auth), 5 MiB cap unchanged, keys named by prefix only, no key or token in any log.
10. **Phasing** matching the project description, and open questions for Stuart.

## Ruling to carry (Stuart, 2026-10-29)

**An agent can only be registered as part of an organisation.** The design record states it as a decision, not an option: the agent's credential (application key, later OAuth client) is an organisation-owned resource created, scoped and revoked by `SsdAccountAdmin` / `SsdOrganisation` in Settings → Integrations; it acts only for a named active member of that organisation; everything it registers is owned, listed, badged and counted under that organisation. No personal or unaffiliated agent, no cross-organisation agent. For the OAuth path this means an organisation admin approves a hosted connector's client before any member can authorise it. **Any organisation counts, a personal (unnamed,** `Name = NULL`**) one included** (Stuart, 2026-10-29): the rule is that an agent belongs to an organisation, not that the organisation must be named. The record states it with the consequence: a sole user in a personal organisation may register an agent through Settings → Integrations exactly as an account admin of a named one does, since that person holds `SsdAccountAdmin` of their own organisation.

**The agent is a named member of the organisation** (Stuart, 2026-10-29). The record states this as the model, not an option: an agent is a `Person` row of kind `Agent` in the organisation (`Person.Kind` discriminator `Human` / `Agent` / `System`, with system `Person` 4 becoming `System`), with no sign-in, no mailbox and no T&C, created with its first application key from Settings → Integrations by `SsdAccountAdmin` / `SsdOrganisation`, badged in the Users list, deactivated through `PersonDeactivation` with its documents reassigned like anyone's. The application key binds to the agent member; `X-Secuura-Act-As` names nobody else. It is the actor and owner of what it registers. The record lists the consequences for every place that today assumes a `Person` is a human (email sends, T&C and join gates, MFA, Assign rights, the Users list, the identity stamp) and names the ticket that makes each kind-aware (MCP 1a / [PS-1421](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1421/mcp-1a-the-agent-as-a-named-member-of-the-organisation-personkind)).

## Done when

* The document is on `develop` (docs-only PR, stated as such on the PR) and attached to [MCP Agent Connector](<https://linear.app/secuura/project/mcp-agent-connector-1b1e9ccb7b3a>).
* `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` §7.5 ("verification surfaces beyond the web app") gains a pointer to it.
* Each decision in (1), (3), (5), the organisation-only ruling (any organisation, personal ones included) and the agent-as-member ruling (email pattern, permitted tiers, supervising member) is written as a decision with its reason, not left as options.
* Every SSP file:line it cites exists on the `develop` tip at merge time.

No Playwright or stack applies: documentation only.

title: Connector KEK rotation: a retired slot, a re-seal sweep over StorageConnection secrets, a /Health count and a runbook, as PS-1375 gave every other at-rest key
description:
## Problem

[PS-1078](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1078>) (in #1200, `develop` bd88e41) seals every stored storage-connection secret (an organisation's OAuth refresh token) under a per-row data key wrapped by the **platform connector KEK** named in `StorageConnections:KekId` (`docs/storage-connector-model.md` §3). The row records which KEK and version sealed it (`StorageConnection.SecretKekId`, `SecretKekVersion`), and `StorageConnectionSecretProtector.OpenAsync` unwraps under that recorded key, so changing the setting strands nothing **while the old key still exists in the vault**.

That is the whole of its rotation story. Compared with the keys [PS-1375](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1375>) covered, the connector KEK has:

* **no retired slot** (no `…-retired` configuration, no optional fetch in any `setenv.sh`);
* **no sweep** that moves rows onto the current KEK. `DocumentKeyRotationSweep` enumerates `DocumentKey` rows only (§3 says so by design: the connector KEK is deliberately outside the organisation-key lifecycle). Nothing under `ssd/Services/DocumentKeys` or `ssd/Services/DocumentStorage` touches `StorageConnection` for re-sealing; `OrganisationDissolutionSweep` only clears secrets;
* **no** `/Health` **figure**: `HealthController` shows "Storage connector key" as present or absent, not how many rows are still under a key other than the current one;
* **no runbook** in `docs/runbooks/`.

So the only way to retire an old connector KEK today is to wait for every organisation's refresh token to be re-sealed by use (Box and OneDrive rotate on refresh, Dropbox never does) or to reconnect each store by hand. Deleting the old key from the vault before that locks each affected organisation out of its store: every blob read through that connection fails until an account admin reconnects.

## Ask

Give the connector KEK the same shape as the other at-rest keys:

1. **Configuration**: `StorageConnections:KekId` stays the current key; a sweep re-seals rows whose `SecretKekId`/`SecretKekVersion` differ from it. No retired *value* is needed in configuration, because the old key is a vault object, not a configured secret; what is needed is the rule "do not remove the old vault key until the count is zero".
2. **Sweep**: `StorageConnectionKekRotationSweep` (or a mode of the existing rotation sweep) that, for each `StorageConnection` with a secret under another KEK or version, opens it under the recorded key and seals it again under the current one, atomically with the row, honouring the atomic-persist rule for rotated refresh tokens (§2, Box). Gated by a flag per environment like `ConnectorKeyRotationEnabled`, off by default on UAT and production until a dump is taken.
3. `/Health`: "Storage connection secrets under a retired connector key" with the count, alongside the [PS-1375](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1375/rotation-tooling-for-the-at-rest-keys-retired-slots-in-deployments-re) rows.
4. **Runbook** `docs/runbooks/rotate-storage-connector-kek.md`: create the new vault key → set `StorageConnections:KekId` → deploy → sweep to zero → disable or delete the old vault key. Same order as the others.
5. **xUnit**: the sweep against EF InMemory with the local HKDF key store (`local:platform:` keys under two names), the Health row, and a contract test that the deployed templates still state the key blank until [PS-1409](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1409>) provisions one.
6. **Docs**: `docs/storage-connector-model.md` §3 and `docs/document-key-hierarchy.md` ("[PS-1078](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1078/per-organisation-storage-connections-encrypted-credential-store-oauth): platform keys") updated; the two testing HTML documents by area, not by count.

## Not in scope

Organisation-key rotation, BYOK and dissolution already never touch connection secrets (§3); keep it that way. Provisioning the first real KEK is [PS-1409](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1409>).

## Done when

Rotating the connector KEK on dev-ps with the runbook ends with the `/Health` count at zero and every connected organisation still reading its store without reconnecting, and `develop` carries the sweep, the Health row, the tests and the runbook.

title: Storage providers: provision the first provider's app credentials and the connector KEK in each secret store before any StorageProviders entry is enabled
description:
## Context [PS-1075]() (#1200, merged to `develop` 29 Oct 2026) ships customer-hosted storage with every provider **off** in every template and nothing provisioned in any secret store. Before `AppSpecific:StorageProviders:

:Enabled` goes `true` on dev-ps (then UAT, then production), the secret-store side has to exist. This ticket tracks that side; the provider tickets ([PS-1080]() OneDrive, [PS-1081]() Dropbox, [PS-1083]() Box, [PS-1379]() SharePoint) each name it as a prerequisite. No secret value belongs on this ticket. Key names and locations only. ## What `develop` reads (bd88e41) | Key | Kind | Today | | -- | -- | -- | | `StorageConnections:KekId` | id of a vault / KMS key in the **document-keys** store (never an organisation's key) | blank in `dep-az-dev`, `dep-aws-uat`, `dep-aws-secuura` templates; `local:platform:storage-connector` in `dep-ssd-local/docker-compose.yml` | | `AppSpecific:StorageProviders:onedrive:ClientId` / `:ClientSecret` (optional `:Authority`) | Entra app registration ("Secuura document storage") | named only; no `setenv.sh` fetch, no vault entry | | `AppSpecific:StorageProviders:dropbox:ClientId` / `:ClientSecret` | Dropbox app | same | | `AppSpecific:StorageProviders:box:ClientId` / `:ClientSecret` | Box custom app | same | | `AppSpecific:StorageProviders:sharepoint:ClientId`, `:CertificatePath`, `:CertificatePassword` | Entra app, certificate credential (PFX), never a client secret | same | | `AppSpecific:StorageProviders:s3:PrincipalArn` | Secuura's own role ARN, not a secret | blank; S3 uses STS AssumeRole from the instance role, no stored secret | `StorageProviderRegistration` registers a provider only when it is on **and** its credentials are present; `LiveConfigGuard` refuses a live boot with a provider on and the KEK or credentials unset, a placeholder or `local:`. `StorageProvidersConfigContractTests` pins that no value is in a tracked file. ## To do, per environment (dev-ps first) 1. **Owner of the app registrations** (the open question on `docs/storage-connector-model.md`, assigned to Stuart): the Entra storage app, the Dropbox app and its production approval, the Box app, and who rotates their secrets. 2. **Connector KEK**: create a key in the document-keys vault (dev-ps: the RBAC vault beside `secuura-ps-dev-kv`; AWS: KMS) and name it in `StorageConnections:KekId` in that environment's template. Terraform-owned like the document keys. 3. **Provider credentials in the store**: one entry per key above, following the pattern every other provider secret uses (dev-ps: `var.kv_secrets` in tfvars → Key Vault → `fetch_secret` in `ssd/dep-az-dev/setenv.sh` → `substitute "__X__"` → template placeholder; AWS: Secrets Manager via `setenv.sh`). The SharePoint PFX needs a file path the container can read plus its password, like `PdfSigning`. 4. **Redirect URIs** per slot and host for each OAuth provider (the [PS-915]() pattern: `:5122`/`:5222`/`:5322`/`:5422` and `dev-ps.secuura.net`). 5. **Local slots**: decide whether the store copy of `Docker.appsettings.Development.json` gets the same provider credentials (today the fake-cloud seam and the S3 emulator cover the journeys without any). This is the same shared-credential question as item 3 of the project description. 6. Switch the provider on in that environment's template only after its own proof, as the template comment says; `/Health` shows "Storage connector key" present and the provider usable. ## Done when Each enabled provider's credentials and the connector KEK come from the environment's secret store with no value in git, the runbook or README for that environment names the keys, and the project description's item 8 is closed.

title: Security (nit): decideMint's toUpperCase admits a dotless-i, a long-s and an array role as a key admin; plus the role-comparison sweep
description:
**BLUF:** `decideMint` (`services/security/src/provisioningPolicy.ts:96-97`, the `POST /api/keys` admission test) still compares `String(caller?.role ?? '').toUpperCase()` against the key-admin set, so a role spelled with U+0131 (dotless i) or U+017F (long s), or an array role, can be read as an admin role. KS-1591 fixed the same shape in `isPlatformRole` and `requireKeyAdmin` and deliberately left this site; this ticket tracks it, and the sweep of other role comparisons that KS-1591's description asks for, so that KS-1591 can close. Reachability is not established.

## Where

`services/security/src/provisioningPolicy.ts` at develop `5dccdcb29ec20393e80cbdb1e359a49caa633165` (the build on both boxes), read with `git show`:

* line 96: `const role = String(caller?.role ?? '');`
* line 97: `if (KEY_ADMIN_ROLES.has(role.toUpperCase())) {`

## What is measured and what is not

* Measured by the tier-2 gate on 2026-10-28 (the batch covering PRs 1775, 1776 and 1780, GO WITH NOTES): `decideMint` admits a role spelled with U+0131 or U+017F, and an array role, at PR 1776's head `8b92887a6fac`. The gate's note was filed on KS-1591 as a comment (`42e97e12`).
* Read by me, not run: lines 96 and 97 are unchanged at the deployed build. I ran no test of `decideMint` with those roles.
* Not established: whether any issuer, user-management path or seed can store or sign a token with such a role. That needs a token the auth service signs. KS-1591 said the same. Until someone measures it this is a nit; if any path can, it is a privilege escalation (admission to mint API keys) and should be re-rated at once.

## Recommendation

Not built. Apply the KS-1591 remedy here: fold ASCII letters only (`replace(/[a-z]/g, ...)`, as `isPlatformRole` now does) and refuse a role that is not a string, in the one shared definition so every caller inherits it. Cells: a dotless-i spelling, a long-s spelling and an array role each refused by `decideMint`; a control that every ASCII spelling admitted today is still admitted.

## Sweep candidates (not findings)

Method: `git grep -n -I "toUpperCase()"` at `5dccdcb29ec2` over `Blockchain/Dev/services` and `Blockchain/Dev/packages`, tests, `dist` and `node_modules` excluded, keeping lines that also contain "role" (case-insensitive). 14 lines. Controls: the `decideMint` line is in the result (1 line from `provisioningPolicy.ts`); a nonsense token over the same paths matches 0 files. Of the 14: 2 are comments, 2 are the sites KS-1591 fixed (`keyRevokePolicy.ts:144`, `security/src/index.ts:1104`), 1 is `decideMint`, and 9 are other candidates:

* `packages/shared/src/security/keyRevokePolicy.ts:85` and `:102` (`ORG_BOUNDED_ROLES`, `SCOPED_ADMIN_ROLES`; the same file KS-1591 changed at `:144`)
* `packages/shared/src/security/scopes.ts:288`
* `services/auth/src/routes/issuerCerts.ts:71`
* `services/auth/src/routes/users.ts:285` and `:377`
* `services/auth/src/services/password.ts:234` (whether it is a role comparison is unread)

title: OAuth /authorize: a repeated state or code_challenge answers 500, and POST accepts arrays
description:
**BLUF:** `GET /api/oauth/authorize` answers **500** `server_error` when `state` or `code_challenge` arrives as a repeated query parameter, the same class as the `scope` crash KS-1219 fixes. On POST, JSON arrays for the same two fields do not crash: an array `state` is coerced to a comma-joined string and echoed in the redirect, and an array `code_challenge` reaches `createAuthorizationCode` as an array. Low. Related to KS-1219, whose own recommendation ("by the same shape, any other non-string authorize parameter") PR 1797 closes for `scope` only. Raised on the tier-1 gate's note 1797-2 (gate 9, 2026-10-28), then measured here; the gate's wording ("repeated `state` / `code_challenge` still 500") holds for GET only.

Every figure below is from a loopback listener driving the real router with its collaborators mocked (the same harness as the ks1219 test), on PR 1797's branch with develop `92a02a356139` merged in. `oauth.ts` is blob `91aa664ac910`, which develop did not change; the lines involved are not touched by PR 1797. Nothing was run against a live box.

**Measured, GET** (client `client-1`, a confidential app, otherwise valid request):

1. `&state=xyz&state=second` answers **500** `server_error`; a single `state=xyz` answers 200 and serves the consent page.
2. `&code_challenge=aaa&code_challenge=bbb` answers **500** `server_error`; a single `code_challenge=aaa` answers 200.
3. `&code_challenge_method=S256&code_challenge_method=plain` answers 400 `invalid_request`. It is already refused, but by accident: the check at lines 361 to 367 is `PKCE_METHODS.has(codeChallengeMethod)`, which is false for an array.
4. `&scope=openid&scope=profile` answers 400 `invalid_request` (the KS-1219 fix, as the control).

**Cause, read from the file:** `generateConsentPage` calls `escapeHtml(params.state)` and `escapeHtml(params.codeChallenge || '')` (lines 1522 and 1523), and `escapeHtml(s: string)` is `s.replace(...)` (lines 1582 to 1584). An array has no `replace`, so the call throws and the handler's catch answers 500. The `as Record<string, string>` cast on `req.query` (line 492) does nothing at run time.

**Measured, POST with JSON arrays** (none of these is a 500):

1. `action: deny` with `state: ["a","b"]` answers 302 to `...?error=access_denied&state=a%2Cb`. The client's `state` comes back altered.
2. `action: approve` with `state: ["a","b"]` mints a code and answers 302 to `...?code=...&state=a%2Cb`.
3. `action: approve` with `code_challenge: ["x","y"]` answers 302, and `createAuthorizationCode` was called with `codeChallenge` equal to the array `["x","y"]` (`Array.isArray` true). **Not measured:** what the real pg driver and the column do with it, because the repository is mocked. It may store text, or it may fail.

**Scope is neither deduplicated nor bounded** (the gate's note 1797-3, pre-existing, measured here for a string scope, repository mocked): `openid openid profile openid` is stored as sent, 28 characters with the repeats; `openid,profile` is stored as `openid profile`; a 14,000-character scope made of one repeated token is stored as a 13,999-character string. Real column limits not measured.

**Not probed:** the other authorize parameters as arrays (`client_id`, `redirect_uri`, `response_type`, `email`, `password`, `action`, `mfaCode`).

**Fix shapes, not chosen here:** one check ahead of the resolver on both GET and POST that every authorize parameter is a string or absent, answering 400 `invalid_request` (the existing message, so no published message changes), as KS-1219's recommendation already describes; or per-field guards in the two handlers. A decision for whoever takes it: whether POST should refuse an array `state` or coerce it, and whether `scope` should be deduplicated and capped.

**Searched before filing** (Linear `issues` filter over title, description and comment bodies, archived included, team KS, 2026-10-28 21:2xZ): `repeated state` 0 hits, `repeated code_challenge` 0, `?state=` 0; `escapeHtml` 5 hits, read by title (KS 841, KS 799 and KS 798 are the consent page posting its own form, KS 488 a review stream, KS 163 a connector XSS), none is this; `code_challenge` 13 hits, read by title (PKCE, token-exchange and consent-page work, mostly Done, plus KS 836 and KS 782 in Backlog and KS 1677, the m365 callback), none is this; `array-valued` 5 hits (KS-1219 itself; KS 1671, the same species in the m365 callback, a different service; KS 839; KS 677; KS 256). The positive control `parseScopeString` found 3 (KS 1220, KS-1219, KS 839); a nonsense token generated at run time found 0 and was not recorded in this ticket.
