title: change-password publishes no 422: a weak new password is documented under 400 while the route answers 422
description:
**BLUF:** the published contract for `POST /api/users/me/change-password` lists **no 422** and documents a too-weak new password under **400** ("Wrong current password or new password too weak"), while the route answers **422** for a weak password. This is a pre-existing contract gap, found by the tier-1 gate on the KS-1467 services/auth change (finding 1799-7); KS-1467 was ruled to change no OpenAPI, so it did not touch it. Low. Related to KS-1467.

**What I read, at develop** `802eb2b8ecaf`**:**

1. `Blockchain/Dev/docs/openapi/secuura-api.yaml`, operation `/api/users/me/change-password`, response codes: 200, 400, 401, 403, 404, 415, 429, 500, 502, 503. There is no 422. The 400 description reads "Wrong current password or new password too weak".
2. The source of that text is `services/auth/src/auth.openapi.ts` line 1012: `400: { ...commonErrorResponses[400], description: 'Wrong current password or new password too weak' }`, and that operation's `responses` has no 422 entry.
3. The two sibling routes do publish it: reset-password has `422: ... 'New password too weak'` (a comment at `auth.openapi.ts` line 813 cites KS 255), and register has a 422 described "Weak password, or client-supplied `role` field (not permitted)".
4. The route throws `new ValidationError('New password is too weak', ...)` (`services/auth/src/routes/users.ts`, around line 993 at the pin), and `ValidationError` answers 422. The route-level cell for change-password in the KS-1467 PR drives the real route and reads status 422 for weak candidates.

**Not claimed:** I ran no schema-conformance tool against the yaml for this; the gate measured it on the wire (finding 1799-7). A wrong *current* password is a 400 and stays one.

**Fix shapes, not chosen here:** add `422: { ...commonErrorResponses[422], description: 'New password too weak' }` to the change-password operation and take "or new password too weak" out of the 400 text, then regenerate the yaml (`generate-openapi`, `check:openapi`). That changes the published contract, so it wants its own ruling; the KS-1467 ruling was no OpenAPI change. Since KS-1467 round 2 the 422 `details` is the published ZodIssue-compatible array, so documenting the 422 matches what the route sends.

**Searched before filing** (Linear `issues` filter over title, description and comments, archived included, team KS, 2026-10-28 15:5xZ): `new password too weak` 0 hits; `publishes no 422` 0; `no 422` with `change-password` 0; `change-password` with `422` 7 hits (KS-1467, KS-1005, KS-732, KS-501, KS-486, KS-485, KS-480), read: none records this gap; `too weak` with `yaml` 2 hits (KS 255, KS 141), neither covers change-password; the zero control `zzqq-no-such-token-r6c` 0 hits; the positive control (title `AppError resets`) found KS-1467.

title: systemTest: measure the PS-1350 Stripe key-file checks that need extra keys — a restricted rk_test_ key (L6), a second Stripe account (L8) and a saved CLI login (L2, L7)
description:
## BLUF

[PS-1350](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1350/systemtest-one-systemtest-only-key-file-switches-the-stripe-tests-on) made `systemTest/.env.stripe` the one switch for the Stripe system tests. It was proven with the team's `sk_test_` key on 28 Oct 2026: live checks L1, L3, L4 and L5 passed. Four of its live checks could **not** be measured, because each needs a credential that was not available:

* **L6:** a *restricted* test key (`rk_test_…`).
* **L8:** a test key from a *different* Stripe account.
* **L2 and L7:** a saved Stripe CLI login.

[PS-1350](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1350/systemtest-one-systemtest-only-key-file-switches-the-stripe-tests-on)'s acceptance criterion 4 is therefore only **partly met**. This ticket either measures the four checks or records the decision not to. Either way, [PS-1350](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1350/systemtest-one-systemtest-only-key-file-switches-the-stripe-tests-on) can close without them.

**Decision needed first (Peter):** supply the keys, or accept these as *not measured*. For L6, the third option is to stop accepting `rk_test_` keys (below).

## What an `rk_test_` key is, and why it matters here

A Stripe secret key comes in two kinds, each with a test-mode and a live-mode form:

|  | Standard secret key `sk_test_…` | Restricted key `rk_test_…` |
| -- | -- | -- |
| What it can do | Everything on the account, in test mode | Only the permissions ticked when it is created (for example "Webhook endpoints: write", "Events: read"), with everything else off |
| How to get one | Stripe dashboard → test mode → Developers → API keys (standard key, or *Create secret key*) | Same page → **Create restricted key**, then choose per-resource permissions |
| If it leaks | Whoever has it can do anything on the test account | It can do only what was ticked; for example, it cannot create charges or read customers |

**Why it helps testing.** The key in `systemTest/.env.stripe` sits on developer machines and, in time, on a server. The least-privileged key that still lets `stripe listen` forward webhooks is the safer one to hand out. That limits the damage from a leaked file, and the listener could not do anything beyond its job.

**What is unproven.** The listener (`ssd/dep-ssd-local/stripe-listen.sh`) and the gate (`systemTest/utils/external_mode_resolve.ts`) currently **accept** `rk_test_` keys. Nobody has checked that `stripe listen` works with one, or which permissions it needs. An `rk_test_` key could therefore be accepted by the file check and then fail at the listener, which is the confusing outcome the rule exists to prevent.

## The four checks

| \# | Check | What is needed | Expected |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| L6 | The listener with a restricted key | An `rk_test_` key on the **same** account as the app's test key | `stripe listen --print-secret` returns a `whsec_`; `stripe_checkout_sandbox` passes. Record the minimum permissions that work. **If none work:** narrow the accepted pattern to `sk_test_` only, in `stripe-listen.sh`, `external_mode_resolve.ts`, the parity test, `.env.stripe.example` and the docs |
| L8 | A key from a **different** Stripe account | A test key from another account | The listener starts but hears none of the app's checkouts. `stripe_checkout_sandbox` **fails** on its webhook timeout with the [PS-1350](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1350/systemtest-one-systemtest-only-key-file-switches-the-stripe-tests-on) §5.5 message: "Is systemTest/.env.stripe's key for the same Stripe account as the app's test key? ([PS-1350](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1350/systemtest-one-systemtest-only-key-file-switches-the-stripe-tests-on))" |
| L2 | No key file, but the CLI is signed in | A saved login of systemTest's own CLI (`npx stripe login` in `systemTest/`) | The listener still does **not** start (`stripe listen: skipped — no systemTest/.env.stripe …`) |
| L7 | Saved login on account X, key file on account Y | A saved login on one account, plus the key file holding another account's key | The listener follows the **file's** account, Y, never the saved login |

L2 and L7 are already covered offline: `StripeListenScriptTests` B1, B5 and B6 prove that no key means no CLI call, that the file's key overrides an ambient `STRIPE_API_KEY`, and that every call carries its own `--project-name ps-systemtest` and `--config`. These checks confirm that against the real CLI (`@stripe/cli` 1.53.1).

## Constraints

* **The key file is a person's step.** The [PS-1361](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1361/block-claude-code-sessions-from-printing-secret-files-hook-rule) hook stops a session creating, reading or merging `systemTest/.env.stripe` (working rules revision 11, §5). Peter places each key; a session checks it only with the exit-code check, which never prints the value: `bash -c '. <worktree>/ssd/dep-ssd-local/stripe-listen.sh; stripe_systemtest_key >/dev/null; echo $?'`.
* **Bring the slot up again after changing the key.** The app takes the listener's signing secret only when its container is created.
* **Sync the slot's Stripe products before any checkout check.** A freshly seeded slot has placeholder price ids, which Stripe refuses as "No such price" (found on [PS-1350](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1350/systemtest-one-systemtest-only-key-file-switches-the-stripe-tests-on), 28 Oct). Use Admin › Stripe products › Sync to Stripe. Not needed for L2.
* **Never** put a key, a `whsec_` value or a login token in this ticket, a PR, a commit or a log.
* **Remove the saved login afterwards** for L2 and L7 (`npx stripe logout` in `systemTest/`), so this Mac goes back to having none.

## Acceptance criteria

1. **Automated test proving the outcome:**
   * *If L6 works:* a parity case in `systemTest/tests-unit/stripe_key_readers.test.ts` and `StripeListenScriptTests` showing that `rk_test_` stays accepted, plus a passing `stripe_checkout_sandbox` run with the restricted key, recorded here.
   * *If L6 does not work:* the same tests changed so that `rk_test_` is **refused** (exit 2, "not a test key"), each seen red first.
   * L8: a `stripe_checkout_sandbox` run that fails with the §5.5 message, recorded here.
   * L2 and L7: the listener outcome against the real CLI, recorded here.
2. **Docs updated:** `systemTest/CLAUDE.md`, `docs/stack_slots_how_to.md`, `systemTest/.env.stripe.example` and the two `docs/platform_s_testing_*.html` files. Each says which key kinds are accepted, and the permissions if `rk_test_` works. Or record "no doc change" if all four simply confirm what is written.
3. **systemTest updated:** the gate (`utils/external_mode_resolve.ts`) and its tests, if the accepted pattern changes; otherwise "no systemTest change" and why.
4. **Not-measured is an outcome too.** For any check Peter decides not to run, this ticket records "not measured, by decision", with the date, and closes.

## Test classification (systemTest)

`@stripe` · `@area-billing` · `@role-account-admin` · `@crud` (checkout), and `@identity` · `@area-identity` · `@persona-kyc` (Identity, re-run with each key). Not `@smoke`.

## References

* [PS-1350](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1350/systemtest-one-systemtest-only-key-file-switches-the-stripe-tests-on)**:** the key file, the listener and the gate. See its "Live checks, 28 Oct" results and acceptance criterion 4.
* [PS-994](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-994/docker-stack-slots-and-any-deployments-sharing-one-stripe-account)**:** one Stripe account shared by slots; checkout is exercised only when no other slot listens.
* [PS-913](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-913/subscribe-createcheckoutsession-500-is-shown-to-the-user-as-nothing)**:** CreateCheckoutSession and "No such price". Its seed half is the product-sync constraint above.

title: Secrets stores (AWS Secrets Manager / Azure Key Vault): who can read and write, per user or group, and how often each key can be rotated
description:
## BLUF

* **The vaults are secure, and read and write can be granted separately, to one person or to a group**, on both AWS and Azure.
* **Gap 1. The dev-ps app-secrets vault can't be restricted per secret or per group.** It still uses Key Vault's older "access policy" model, which applies to the whole vault. The document-keys vault next to it already uses RBAC. Moving the app-secrets vault to RBAC fixes this.
* **Gap 2. Every secret value also exists outside the vaults:** in the gitignored `terraform.tfvars` and in the Terraform state file. Anyone who can read either has every secret, whatever their vault role says. This is how dev-ps leaked on 26 Oct ([PS-1364](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1364/rotate-the-dev-ps-secrets-exposed-on-26-oct-2026-tracking-checklist)).
* **Quarterly rotation:**
  * **Safe and easy today:** document keys, the identity key (raise the version) and the credential issuer key.
  * **Possible but manual, over two deploys:** the signing-certificate key and the platform-k connector key.
  * **Not on a schedule:** the remaining two (table 3).
* **Scheduled rotation is off everywhere.** `DocumentKeys:AutoRotateDays` is `0` in the dev-ps, UAT and production templates.

No secret value appears in this ticket. It names keys, secret names and where values live, never a value.

---

## 1. Where secrets live today (checked in tracked files)

|  | dev-ps | UAT | Production |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| Store | Azure Key Vault `secuura-ps-dev-kv` | AWS Secrets Manager `/secuura/uat/*` | AWS Secrets Manager `/secuura/prod/*` |
| Values come from | Terraform `var.kv_secrets` (gitignored `terraform.tfvars`) | Terraform `var.kv_secrets` (`aws_secretsmanager_secret_version`) | same as UAT |
| Also held in | Terraform state | Terraform state | Terraform state |
| What the app server may do | **Read only** (`Get`, `List`) | **Read only**: `secretsmanager:GetSecretValue` on its own prefix | **Read only**, same |
| What the Terraform operator may do | **Everything** (`Get, List, Set, Delete, Purge, Recover`) on every secret | Whatever their own IAM allows | same |
| Access model | Access policies: the whole vault, no per-secret control | IAM: per secret or per prefix | IAM: per secret or per prefix |
| Recovery window after delete | 7 days; purge protection **off** | 7 days | (check `main.tf`) |
| Document-keys vault | Separate vault: **RBAC**, premium/HSM, purge protection **on**; roles split (VM = Crypto User, admin identity = Crypto Officer) | KMS: key policy names only the instance role and the admin role, never the account root; the admin role has **no** `kms:Decrypt` | same as UAT |

Sources: `ssd/az-docker/az-secuura-DEV-docker/main.tf` (secrets vault access policies \~L271–L310; document-keys vault with RBAC \~L340–L420), `ssd/aws-docker/aws-secuura-UAT-docker/main.tf` (\~L216–L222, L357–L371), `ssd/aws-docker/aws-secuura-docker/main.tf` (\~L219–L225), `ssd/dep-aws-uat/README.md` ([PS-951](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-951/key-store-abstraction-key-vault-kms-wrap-unwrap-with-a-local-dev) paragraph).

---

## 2. Can read and write be separated, per user or per group?

**Yes, on both clouds.**

### Permission matrix

| What someone needs | AWS Secrets Manager (IAM action) | Azure Key Vault (RBAC role) |
| -- | -- | -- |
| See names only, no values | `ListSecrets`, `DescribeSecret` | **Key Vault Reader** |
| Read values | `GetSecretValue` (+ `kms:Decrypt` if the secret uses its own KMS key) | **Key Vault Secrets User** |
| Write or rotate a value | `PutSecretValue`, `UpdateSecret`, `RotateSecret` | **Key Vault Secrets Officer** (also reads), or a custom role with only `setSecret` |
| Delete or purge | `DeleteSecret` | Secrets Officer / Key Vault Administrator |
| Write **without** being able to read | Grant write actions and withhold `GetSecretValue`, or withhold `kms:Decrypt` on the secret's own key | Custom role with `secrets/setSecret/action` and not `secrets/getSecret/action` |

### Who you can grant to, and how narrowly

|  | AWS | Azure |
| -- | -- | -- |
| One person | IAM user, or an Identity Center user | Entra user |
| A group | IAM group, or an Identity Center group through a permission set | Entra group |
| An app or server | Instance role (what UAT and prod use) | Managed identity (what dev-ps uses) |
| Narrowest scope | One secret ARN, or a name prefix | One secret, **only in RBAC mode** |
| Just-in-time access | Identity Center session length + approval workflow | PIM: request, approve, expires |
| Second gate | A customer-managed KMS key on the secret, whose key policy decides who can decrypt | Not applicable; the vault role is the gate |
| Audit | CloudTrail logs every `GetSecretValue` / `PutSecretValue` | Diagnostic logs (send them to Log Analytics) |

**Limits:**

* **dev-ps app-secrets vault:** access policies are vault-wide, so nobody can be given one secret, and today's operator has full read, write and purge on all of them.
* **AWS:** the app secrets don't name their own KMS key, so they use the default AWS-managed key, and the extra `kms:Decrypt` gate is not available until each secret gets its own key.

### Suggested model (applies to both clouds)

| Who | Names | Read values | Write / rotate | Delete / purge |
| -- | -- | -- | -- | -- |
| App server identity | yes | **yes**, its own environment only | no | no |
| Operators group (day to day) | yes | no | no | no |
| Rotation operators (just in time, approved, time-limited) | yes | no | **yes** | no |
| Break-glass (two-person rule, [PS-1085](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1085/vault-access-governance-no-single-secuura-staff-member-can-use-or)) | yes | yes | yes | yes |
| Terraform pipeline identity | yes | no | yes, while values still come from Terraform | no |

---

## 3. Can each key be rotated every 3 months without breaking documents or sign-in?

| Key (config → secret name) | Protects | Quarterly? | How | Runbook |
| -- | -- | -- | -- | -- |
| Organisation document keys (KMS / Key Vault keys) | Documents | ✅ **Easy** | "Rotate key" button, or `DocumentKeys:AutoRotateDays = 90`. No document is rewritten and every one stays readable. | `rotate-organisation-key.md` |
| `Identity:DataEncryptionKey` → `identity-data-encryption-key` | KYC images, DID private keys | ✅ **Easy** (routine) | Raise `Identity:DataEncryptionKeyVersion`. No data moves. Replace the root key itself only after a compromise (retired slot + sweep). | `rotate-identity-data-encryption-key.md` |
| `Identity:IssuerSigningKeyBase64` → `identity-issuer-signing-key` | Verifiable credentials | ✅ **Easy** | List the old **public** key in `Identity:IssuerPublicKeysRetired`; credentials already issued keep verifying. | `rotate-identity-issuer-signing-key.md` |
| `AppSpecific:SigningKeyEncryptionKey` → `signing-key-encryption-key` | Stored signing certificates | ⚠️ **Manual, two deploys** | Old value into the retired slot → deploy → new value → `/Health` shows 0 → remove the retired value. **Production has no such key yet (**[PS-821](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-821/prod-appspecificsigningkeyencryptionkey-is-stated-nowhere)**).** | `rotate-signing-key-encryption-key.md` |
| `AppSpecific:CardanoAnchor:PlatformKCredentialKey` → `platform-k-credential-key` | Each org's platform-k connector key | ⚠️ **Manual, two deploys** | Same sequence. If the retired slot is skipped, the connector keys are **lost without any error**. | `rotate-platform-k-credential-key.md` |
| `AppSpecific:DocStorageKey` → `doc-storage-key` | Log email tags, older identity data | ❌ Not scheduled | Possible, but log tags stop matching across the change. Being retired ([PS-1385](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1385/retire-appspecificdocstoragekey-its-only-remaining-job-is-the-log)). | `rotate-doc-storage-key.md` |
| `AppSpecific:TemplateStorageKey` → `template-storage-key` | Legacy documents and certificates | ❌ Not scheduled | A one-time retirement, only once nothing is stored under it. | `rotate-template-storage-key.md` |

### Sign-in

| What | Affected by key rotation? | Note |
| -- | -- | -- |
| Passwords | No | Stored as hashes |
| Sign-in cookies | No | [ASP.NET](<http://ASP.NET>) Data Protection keys in `/var/dpkeys`. `Startup.cs` sets no `SetDefaultKeyLifetime`, so the framework rotates them itself every 90 days and keeps the old ones. It also sets no `ProtectKeysWith…`, so those keys sit **unencrypted** on the volume. |
| Entra / Google / Apple / GitHub client secrets, Stripe, Mailgun, DB password | Rotated at the provider | Issue the new one → deploy → revoke the old one. The provider allows two at once during the overlap. |

### What makes rotation slow

1. Secrets are read only at container start, so **every rotation needs a restart**, and config files are copied to the boxes by hand.
2. The ⚠️ keys need someone watching `/Health` between the two deploys.
3. AWS's built-in automatic rotation (a Lambda) suits database passwords, **not** our application keys, which need the retired-slot sequence above.

---

## 4. Pseudo code: reading and updating a secret programmatically

Rules for any script:

* never print, log or echo the value;
* read it into memory only;
* write a **new version** instead of overwriting;
* keep the previous version until the app is proven on the new one.

### Read (the app at start-up, or `setenv.sh`)

```
function readSecret(env, name):
    identity = currentIdentity()           # instance role (AWS) / managed identity (Azure); never a stored key
    if cloud == AWS:
        resp  = SecretsManager.GetSecretValue(SecretId = prefix(env) + "/" + name,
                                              VersionStage = "AWSCURRENT")
        value = resp.SecretString
    else:  # Azure
        client = SecretClient(vaultUrl(env), identity)
        value  = client.GetSecret(name).Value   # latest enabled version

    if value is empty:
        log("secret {name} missing or empty")   # the NAME only, never the value
        fail
    return value                               # held in memory; never written to disk or output
```

### Update / rotate (an operator in the rotation role, or a pipeline)

```
function rotateSecret(env, name, generate):
    newValue = generate()                      # e.g. 32 random bytes, base64; never typed or pasted

    if cloud == AWS:
        # stage the new value without making it live
        SecretsManager.PutSecretValue(SecretId = prefix(env) + "/" + name,
                                      SecretString = newValue,
                                      VersionStages = ["AWSPENDING"])
        # for a key with a retired slot, first write the CURRENT value into "<name>-retired"
        redeploy(env); waitUntil(health(env).ok)
        # promote: AWSPENDING -> AWSCURRENT; the old version becomes AWSPREVIOUS (kept, rollback-able)
        SecretsManager.UpdateSecretVersionStage(SecretId, "AWSCURRENT",
                                                MoveToVersionId = pendingVersionId,
                                                RemoveFromVersionId = currentVersionId)
    else:  # Azure
        client.SetSecret(name, newValue)       # creates a NEW version; older versions remain
        redeploy(env); waitUntil(health(env).ok)
        # rollback = disable the new version, so the previous one is latest again

    audit("rotated {name} in {env}")           # name, env, who, when; never the value
    newValue = null                            # drop from memory

# Keys with a retired slot (signing-key, platform-k credential, identity root):
#   1. write current value into "<name>-retired"     -> deploy
#   2. rotateSecret(name)                              -> deploy
#   3. wait until /Health "still under a retired key" == 0
#   4. delete "<name>-retired"                         -> deploy
```

**On dev-ps:** Terraform owns the values, so a value changed only in Key Vault is reverted by the next `terraform apply`. Until the values are moved out of Terraform, rotate there by editing `terraform.tfvars` and applying.

---

## 5. Open points (for decision; no work started)

| \# | Point | Related |
| -- | -- | -- |
| 1 | Switch the dev-ps app-secrets vault to RBAC (`rbac_authorization_enabled = true`) so access can be granted per secret and per group; turn purge protection on | [PS-1085](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1085/vault-access-governance-no-single-secuura-staff-member-can-use-or) |
| 2 | Take secret **values** out of Terraform (create the secret empty, set the value out-of-band), so they no longer sit in `tfvars` and state | [PS-1364](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1364/rotate-the-dev-ps-secrets-exposed-on-26-oct-2026-tracking-checklist) |
| 3 | Give AWS app secrets a customer-managed KMS key, to get the second `kms:Decrypt` gate |  |
| 4 | Decide whether to set `DocumentKeys:AutoRotateDays = 90` per environment | [PS-956](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-956/organisation-key-rotation-re-wrap-and-optional-document-re-encryption) |
| 5 | Production needs `SigningKeyEncryptionKey` before that key can be rotated at all | [PS-821](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-821/prod-appspecificsigningkeyencryptionkey-is-stated-nowhere) |
| 6 | Encrypt the Data Protection keys at rest (`ProtectKeysWith…`), or accept the risk with a recorded reason |  |
| 7 | Remove standing human read and write; just-in-time access with two people | [PS-1085](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1085/vault-access-governance-no-single-secuura-staff-member-can-use-or) |
| 8 | Turn on and keep vault audit logs (CloudTrail data events; Key Vault diagnostic settings) |  |

Related, cited by identifier only: [PS-1375](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1375/rotation-tooling-for-the-at-rest-keys-retired-slots-in-deployments-re) (rotation tooling), [PS-1385](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1385/retire-appspecificdocstoragekey-its-only-remaining-job-is-the-log) (`DocStorageKey` retirement), [PS-951](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-951/key-store-abstraction-key-vault-kms-wrap-unwrap-with-a-local-dev) / [PS-956](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-956/organisation-key-rotation-re-wrap-and-optional-document-re-encryption) (document keys).

title: ks597 integration guard (KS-1340): 127.0.0.1:6433, the shared stack's pgbouncer, is accepted, and the hostaddr refusal is case- and percent-encoding-literal
description:
**BLUF:** the guard that pull request 1790 gives the ks597 integration file (KS-1340) refuses the shared stack's Postgres ports 5432 and 6432 but not **6433**, the port docker-compose publishes for the shared stack's pgbouncer, which fronts the same shared database. `postgres://u:p@127.0.0.1:6433/db` is accepted, and so is `...:55412/db?port=6433`. Separately, its `hostaddr` refusal matches the lower-case key literally, so `?HOSTADDR=` and `?host%61ddr=` pass it. One guard and one logical path, so one ticket. Neither is a change to pull request 1790, which merges as gated (gate 8, 2026-10-29: #1790 GO). Filed on Wednesday's ANSWER of 2026-10-28 13:38:21Z; gate 8 findings 1790-1 and 1790-2.

## Where

`Blockchain/Dev/services/originate/src/__tests__/ks597-issuer-organization-id.integration.test.ts`: the `SHARED_STACK_PORTS` list (the port `5432` plus the `POSTGRES_EXTERNAL_PORT` default read from docker-compose.yml) and the `hostaddr` test in `disposableDsnTarget()`, at the head of pull request 1790 (`3a9b1c121f6d`). The port list is pre-existing (KS-1306); the pull request did not change it.

## 1. Port 6433

docker-compose.yml publishes the shared stack's Postgres on `127.0.0.1:${POSTGRES_EXTERNAL_PORT:-6432}` (line 156) and its pgbouncer on `127.0.0.1:${PGBOUNCER_PORT:-6433}` (line 262, container port 6432), the pooler every service connects through. The guard's list is `["5432","6432"]` (printed by the probe below). KS-296 records the labels (6432 = direct Postgres, 6433 = pgbouncer) and the compose stack-safety script's list in KS-1558's description already includes 6433.

Measured by running the pull request's own guard function, extracted from the file at its head and transpiled, beside the pg client (pg 8.20.0; no database and no socket: 0 connect calls, with a control reading 1):

```
DSN                                    guard                       pg dials
control: clean loopback, free port     ACCEPTED 127.0.0.1:55412    127.0.0.1:55412
control: shared postgres port 5432     REFUSED                     127.0.0.1:5432
control: shared published port 6432    REFUSED                     127.0.0.1:6432
pgbouncer published port 6433          ACCEPTED 127.0.0.1:6433     127.0.0.1:6433
6433 named only in the query string    ACCEPTED 127.0.0.1:6433     127.0.0.1:6433
```

Nothing was run against a pooler. Gate 8 found the same independently. Not measured: a stack started on another slot publishes pgbouncer and Postgres on other ports (KS-390's table lists 6533, 6633 and so on), and the list reads only the default; whether it should cover slot ports is a decision for whoever fixes this.

## 2. The hostaddr refusal is literal

The test is `/[?&]hostaddr(=|&|$)/`: lower case, not percent-decoded. Measured with the same probe: `?HOSTADDR=203.0.113.7` and `?host%61ddr=203.0.113.7` are accepted, and the pg client dials the authority (`127.0.0.1:55412`) for both. There is **no measured bypass**: pg ignores `hostaddr` in every spelling, and no consumer of the DSN in this file is libpq. The rule's stated reason is that libpq honours `hostaddr`; the gate states that libpq also decodes percent-escapes in a key, so the rule only partly meets that reason. I did not run libpq here.

## Fix shape (not chosen here)

Read the pgbouncer default from the compose file the way the Postgres one is read (`PGBOUNCER_PORT:-(\d+)\}:6432`), so the list cannot drift; and either decode and lower-case the query's keys before the `hostaddr` test, or refuse any query key outside a short allow-list.

## Also noted by the gate, not measured

Finding 1790-3: the same DSN is handed to the product as `DATABASE_URL` (Prisma), whose parser may read a duplicate or overriding query key differently from the pg client. Checking that needs a connection attempt.

## Board search before filing

Issues filter over title, description and comment bodies, archived included, run immediately before filing. `SHARED_STACK_PORTS`: 0 hits. `hostaddr` and `HOSTADDR`: only KS-1340 and KS-1793 (both mine; neither covers the spelling). `PGBOUNCER_PORT`: 3 hits (KS-1166, KS-390, KS-614) and `6433`: 6 hits (KS-1236, KS-1558, KS-296, KS-390, KS-490, KS-614); I read them: they concern slot ports, the VM firewall, a docs label fix and the compose stack-safety script's list, and none covers the ks597 guard's port list. Positive control `disposable`: 20 hits. Zero control: a fresh token never written to the board returned 0; the token is not recorded here so that it stays a control.

## Related

KS-1340 (pull request 1790, the guard). KS-1793 (the ks1263 guard with the same hole; unfixed). KS-1558 and KS-296 (where the role of 6433 is recorded).

## Provenance

Gate 8, findings 1790-1 and 1790-2 (`0_Brain/reference/2026-10-29_gate8-batch/verdict.md`), reproduced by running the pull request's own function on 2026-10-29. Probe: `5_Project_History/2026-10-28_seatT-5th/tools/guard_probe_followup_t5.js` in the project record.

title: smoke-test.sh is not remote-clean: 12 localhost:60xx checks, RUNBOOK 2.2's remote full run, and URL credentials echoed in "Smoke target:"
description:
**BLUF:** `scripts/smoke-test.sh` is still not remote-clean after PR 1793 made its `GATEWAY` honour `SMOKE_BASE_URL` (KS-1250). One remote full run would show all three problems below at once, which is why they are one ticket. Low. Related to KS-1250. Filed on the tier-2 gate's note (gate 8, 2026-10-28), after a search of the board (quoted at the end).

**Nobody runs this script against kintsugi, demo or any live box to reproduce or check any of this.** A full run anchors a real document, and that run is held for Kam (the KS-1250 hold). Everything below was read from the script or measured with a stub `curl` on a private PATH against a `.invalid` host.

1. **12 hard-coded** `http://localhost:60xx` **service-port checks remain in the full run** (sections 7 onward): lines 259, 263, 267, 275, 283, 292, 305, 307, 317, 319, 327 and 329 of `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/smoke-test.sh` at PR 1793's head `29989b01ab05`. PR 1793 moves only `GATEWAY`, so with `SMOKE_BASE_URL` set to a remote gateway those 12 checks still hit localhost, and the run mixes two environments while reading as a result for one.
2. **RUNBOOK section 2.2 still tells an operator to do a remote full run.** `Blockchain/Dev/deployment/azure/RUNBOOK.md` lines 139 to 143: `SMOKE_BASE_URL=https://<prod-gateway-fqdn> ../../scripts/smoke-test.sh`, under the heading "Bash smoke against production gateway", with no `--quick`.
3. **The** `Smoke target:` **line echoes credentials embedded in the URL verbatim.** Measured with a stub `curl` and `--quick`: `SMOKE_BASE_URL='https://alice:s3cr3t-token@smoke-target.invalid:9999'` (a fake credential) prints, as line 1 of the output, `Smoke target: https://alice:s3cr3t-token@smoke-target.invalid:9999`. A base URL carrying a token or basic-auth would be written to the terminal and to any CI log. The stub recorded 9 requests, all to `smoke-target.invalid`.

Also on this ticket: **no test cell uses an** `https://` **base** (the new suite uses `http://smoke-target.invalid:9999`), so the gate's mutant M11 survives.

Fix shapes, not chosen here: route the 12 service-port checks through a base the way `GATEWAY` is, or skip them with a printed line when the base is not localhost; make section 2.2 say `--quick` or say what a remote full run does not cover; print the target as scheme, host and port only.

**Searched before filing** (Linear `issues` filter over title, description and comments, archived included, team KS, 2026-10-28 13:4xZ): `remote-clean` 1 hit, KS-1250 itself; `smoke-test.sh` 11 hits, read: none is this follow-up (KS 1245 is the Done degraded-health fix, KS 1139 the arithmetic-under-errexit fix, KS 1101 a health-aggregation ticket); `SMOKE_BASE_URL` 2 hits, KS-1250 and a review comment on KS 1101 that repeats the same O-2 finding; `Smoke target` 1 hit, KS-1250; the zero control `zzqq-no-such-token-r6b` 0 hits.

title: ks1263 KS-1310 describe: the disposable-database guard reads new URL(dsn), so a ?host= or ?port= in the DSN query string passes it (same hole as KS-1340, on a guard that protects DDL)
description:
**BLUF:** the disposable-database guard in the third describe of `ks1263-multi-write-rolls-back.integration.test.ts` (the KS 1310 describe, which creates a trigger on `documents`) judges `new URL(DEFAULT_DB)`, the host and port the DSN's authority names. A `?host=` or `?port=` in the query string passes it while the pg client dials the remote host, or port 5432. It is the same hole as KS-1340, in a guard that protects schema DDL. Not fixed in pull request 1790, pull request 1792 or the KS-1600 pull request; Wednesday asked for this ticket (ANSWER 2026-10-28 12:23:51Z).

## Where

`Blockchain/Dev/services/originate/src/__tests__/ks1263-multi-write-rolls-back.integration.test.ts`, the `beforeAll` of the describe "KS-1310 ROUTE-LEVEL ...". At develop `d531abd5f34b` the block is lines 589 to 598: `new URL(DEFAULT_DB)`, hostname in `['127.0.0.1', 'localhost']`, port in 55410 to 55419, else it throws "KS-1310 installs a trigger (schema DDL) and therefore refuses any database that is not this seat's disposable one".

## Measured

The exact predicate of line 591 run beside the pg client on four DSNs (pg 8.20.0, pg-connection-string 2.12.0; constructing a Client opens no socket, so nothing was dialled):

```
DSN                                      guard accepts   pg dials
postgres://u:p@127.0.0.1:55412/db        true            127.0.0.1:55412
...@127.0.0.1:55412/db?host=203.0.113.7  true            203.0.113.7:55412
...@127.0.0.1:55412/db?port=5432         true            127.0.0.1:5432
postgres://u:p@203.0.113.7:55412/db      false           203.0.113.7:55412
```

A DSN that names no port is already refused here (`Number('')` is 0, outside the range), which is not true of the ks597 guard KS-1340 fixes. Probe script: `5_Project_History/2026-10-28_seatT-5th/tools/sibling_guard_probe_t5.js` in the project record.

## Why it matters, and its limit

The guard's own comment says a cell that writes DDL must be unable to reach a shared or real database. This describe runs `CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION` and `CREATE TRIGGER ... ON documents` against whatever `TEST_DATABASE_URL` names. The hole is reachable only if that variable carries such a query string (an operator mistake or an unusual DSN); it is not reachable by default, and nothing was run against a shared database to test it.

## Fix shape (the KS-1340 one; not chosen here)

Judge the host and port the pg client will dial, by asking the client (`new Client({ connectionString }).host` and `.port`), as pull request 1790 does for the ks597 guard, and keep the 55410 to 55419 range test on that answer. KS-1340 also refuses a DSN that names `hostaddr` (pg ignores it, libpq honours it).

Issues filter over title, description and comment bodies, archived included, run at 12:2xZ and again immediately before filing: `55410` gave 0 hits, `refuses any database that is not this` gave 0, `KS-1310 installs a trigger` gave 0. Positive control `disposable`: 19 hits at filing time (19 at the first run). Zero control: a fresh token never written to the board returned 0; the token is not recorded here so that it stays a control. No existing ticket covers this guard.

## Related

KS-1340 (the ks597 guard, pull request 1790). KS-1310 (added this guard; Done). KS-1499 (pull request 1792 edits the same file for other reasons and leaves this guard as it is).

title: The tenant-creation contract, TOKENISATION.md and the admin UI still describe a key file returned once at creation; the key service has not returned one since 2026-04-28
description:
**BLUF:** The published tenant-creation contract, `docs/TOKENISATION.md`, `docs/METERING-USAGE-API.md` and the admin UI all describe a vault key file that tenant creation returns once. The key service has not returned a key since 2026-04-28 (commit `1f1cba638`, "Audit Tier-0 ... B-5", which changed `generate-key` to persist the key wrapped server-side and answer only `{ keyId, keyHash }`), so since that commit the real service has not let `POST /api/tenants` carry a key file on success, and the admin UI's key-file dialog can never open. One logical path, three kinds of site; the checklist below names each. Low: it misleads readers and consumers, it does not break a request.

## Exercised (real entry modules, `pg` and JWT stubbed, no Docker)

* The real `generate-key` answers with the fields `algorithm, createdAt, keyHash, keyId, success, tenantId, tenantSlug, version`: no `keyFile`, no `key`.
* Tenant creation against that answer: `201` with body keys `meteringApiKey, success, tenant` (no `keyFile` key at all); with the key service refusing (403 `success: false`) the same `201` carries `keyFile: null`. So success and failure differ only as "key absent" versus "key null", and the admin UI treats both as "no key dialog".
* Files in the Platform K project folder: `5_Project_History/2026-10-28_seatY-4th/evidence/trace/generate_key_probe.json` and `tenant_create_real_shape.json`.

## Checklist (develop `2b7ef12fa564`, line numbers from there)

- [ ] **Published contract.** The `keyFile` property of the 201 of `POST /api/platform/tenants`: description "The tenant's vault key material (PII/encryption), returned once at creation; null if key generation failed (mint manually later)." Source `services/tenant-provisioning/src/tenant-provisioning.openapi.ts:385`, published in `docs/openapi/secuura-api.yaml` (regenerate it with `npm run generate-openapi`).
- [ ] **Docs.** `docs/TOKENISATION.md`: the key file format and the example response near `:312` to `:321`, the Key Security note at `:182`, the write-path example at `:201` (`"key": "<from vault_key_hash lookup>"`; no code does that lookup and a SHA-256 hash cannot give the key back), Key Lifecycle step 4 at `:382` to `:385` ("The key file is returned to the super-admin"), and the troubleshooting step at `:486`. `docs/METERING-USAGE-API.md:120` ("alongside the vault `keyFile`").
- [ ] **Code and UI.** `services/tenant-provisioning/src/index.ts:125` to `:139`: `requestKeyGeneration` is typed as returning `keyFile`, and the handler copies `keyResult.keyFile` (undefined on the real answer). `frontend/admin/src/pages/platform/ClientList.tsx:70` (`if (result.keyFile) setKeyFileJson(...)`) with the dialog at `:323` to `:332`, and the type at `frontend/admin/src/services/api.ts:1045`.

## A decision sits under this (not mine)

Either a way to deliver the tenant's key is restored or `keyFile` is retired from the contract, the docs and the UI. The design comment in `services/tokenisation/src/index.ts:126` promises "a separate admin-only, audited endpoint can return the wrapped envelope"; no such route exists (routes: health, tokenise, detokenise, generate-key, rotate-key, detect-pii, hash-key). Related: the gateway keeps a per-session tenant key that an administrator uploads (`POST /api/platform/tenant-key`), but no route returns a key to upload, and the gateway's tokenise and detokenise helpers have no caller in the tree (none at the commit that introduced them either).

## Not covered

The admin UI was read, not rendered; consumers outside this repository (the Extranet, other repositories, runbooks) are unmeasured; live data on the boxes is unmeasured.

## Board search before filing (Secuura-PK, `issues()` filter over title and description, archived included)

Literals: `requestKeyGeneration` (1 hit, KS-336, Done; the firing control), `zzqx-no-such-literal-9931` (0; the null control), `keyFile` (1 hit, KS-336, Done, the original design), `key file` (3 hits, none about tenant creation), `B-5` (KS-630, KS-612; neither concerns this), `TOKENISATION.md` (KS-525, KS-300; neither concerns this), `ClientList` (0), `vault key` (0), `keyPending` (0). None records that the key file is no longer returned.

Related to KS-1240 (not a blocker).

title: tenant-provisioning: the key service still writes a tenant's key row after the caller gives up, and neither the create rollback nor tenant delete removes it
description:
**BLUF:** The tokenisation service's `POST /api/generate-key` does not notice that its caller has gone: it still inserts the tenant's wrapped key row (`tenant_keys`) and an audit row afterwards. When tenant creation gives up (its fetch bound, a client disconnect) or rolls back, nothing removes that row. The create rollback deletes only `tenant_config`, `tenant_contacts` and `tenants`; tenant delete deletes `vault_entries`, `tenant_contacts`, `tenant_config` and `platform_document_registry`; tokenisation has no delete route. The result is an ACTIVE wrapped key for a tenant whose `vault_key_hash` is NULL, or for a tenant that no longer exists. Low: nothing reachable reads it today (see the vault-key trace on KS-1240).

## Exercised

A probe against the real tokenisation entry module (`pg` replaced by a recorder and the JWT middleware stubbed; no database, no Docker): the key INSERT slowed by 400 ms and the client aborting at 150 ms. Result, verbatim:

```
{ "clientOutcome": "client aborted: AbortError",
  "tenantKeysInsertsAtTheMomentTheClientGaveUp": 0,
  "tenantKeysInsertsOneAndAHalfSecondsLater": 1,
  "auditInsertsOneAndAHalfSecondsLater": 1 }
```

So the handler does not observe a client disconnect; the key row and the audit row land after the caller has left. File in the Platform K project folder: `5_Project_History/2026-10-28_seatY-4th/evidence/trace/generate_key_abort_probe.json` (the probe source is beside it as a `.txt`).

## Read (develop `2b7ef12fa564`)

* `services/tokenisation/src/index.ts`: the `generate-key` route is at `:220` and the key INSERT at `:238`; no `req.on('close')` handling and no delete route (routes: health, tokenise, detokenise, generate-key, rotate-key, detect-pii, hash-key).
* `services/tenant-provisioning/src/index.ts`: the rollback at `:322` to `:324` and the tenant delete list at `:520` name no `tenant_keys`. `tenant_keys` is written by tokenisation into the main database, tenant provisioning's `platformQuery` writes the platform database.
* `migrations/029_tokenisation_tenant_keys.sql`: `UNIQUE (tenant_id, version, status)`. A second `generate-key` for a tenant that already has an active version 1 would insert `(tenant_id, 1, 'active')` again and so answer 500 (read; not executed, it needs a real Postgres).

## Why it matters

* Tenant creation now gives up on a key service that is slower than 3 s (KS-1240 part 4). A key service that is slow but not hung still completes its insert, and the tenant ends up with a key row and a NULL `vault_key_hash`.
* The decision that keeps tenant creation answering 201 with a `keyPending` flag (KS-1240) leaves such tenants in place; a later attempt to generate their key by hand would meet the unique constraint above.
* A create that is rolled back after the key was written leaves a key (and its audit row) for a tenant that no longer exists.

## Options (not chosen here)

1. A platform-admin route on tokenisation that deletes a tenant's key rows, called by the create rollback and the tenant delete.
2. Make `generate-key` idempotent per tenant (answer with the existing active key's id and hash), so a retry or a late completion can be reconciled.
3. Have tenant creation read the hash back from the key service after a timeout instead of leaving it NULL.

## Not covered

A real Postgres (the unique-constraint rejection is read), live data (how many such rows exist on the demo or kintsugi boxes is unmeasured), and any other caller of `generate-key` (the search found tenant provisioning only).

## Board search before filing (Secuura-PK, `issues()` filter over title and description, archived included)

Literals: `requestKeyGeneration` (1 hit, KS-336, Done; the firing control), `zzqx-no-such-literal-9931` (0; the null control), `tenant_keys` (KS-311, KS-288, both Done and about earlier errors in these routes), `generate-key` (KS-476, KS-311, KS-310, KS-288, KS-175, all Done or Deployed To Prod), `rotate-key` (6 hits: KS-667, KS-476, KS-311, KS-310, KS-288, KS-175, all closed or deployed work on these routes), `wrapped key` (0), `vault key` (0), `key row` (6 hits, none about the key service), `keyPending` (0). None records this behaviour.

Related to KS-1240 (not a blocker).

title: KS-1240 gate follow-ups (#1785): exchange timeout still reads as a downstream 401; two http.request forwards unbounded; the non-OK 4xx validate branch has no cell
description:
**Three follow-ups from the tier-1 gate on #1785 (KS-1240 part 1, api-gateway). None blocks that merge.**

1. **A connector-exchange timeout still ends as a downstream 401.**
   * Where: `services/api-gateway/src/middleware/auth.ts`, `getConnectorBearer`, bounded at 5 s by #1785.
   * What happens: the base's fail-closed answer is kept. On a timeout the request goes on with no Bearer, and a Bearer-only upstream answers 401 for a key that was just validated. The client reads a transient fault as an auth failure.
   * Why it differs from the ticket: KS-1240's text suggests "a 503 on timeout".
   * Pinned today: the two "the exchange ..." cells in `ks1240b-front-door-key-exchange-timeout-answers-503-not-401.test.ts` pin the 401.
   * Why #1785 kept it: the gateway cannot tell whether a mount needs the connector Bearer. Gateway-local handlers serve `sk_` callers from `req.user` without it, so a gateway 503 would refuse requests that succeed today.
   * Related: auth's `/internal/connector-token` (`services/auth/src/routes/internal.ts:42`) has its own unbounded fetch to the security service, and answers 502 on any non-2xx from it.
2. **Two hand-built forwards are still unbounded.**
   * Where: `services/api-gateway/src/routes/proxy.ts:620` (`http.request` for `POST /api/documents/upload`) and `services/api-gateway/src/routes/verification.ts:900` (`http.request` for document create).
   * Read at #1785's head `e01a5094771d`: no `setTimeout`, timeout or abort in `proxy.ts` 600-660 or `verification.ts` 885-940.
   * The sibling at `verification.ts:559` has one: `proxyReq.setTimeout(originateForwardTimeoutMs, ...)`.
   * It is the same hang shape as KS-1240. Neither call is a `fetch(`, so #1785's census does not see them. Not executed.
3. **Test gap: the non-OK 4xx branch of** `checkApiKey` **has no cell.**
   * Three gate mutants survive with all 40 cells green:
     * F7: a 429 treated as a rejection.
     * F8: every non-OK status treated as unavailable, so a 4xx rejection becomes 503.
     * F18: a non-OK 4xx rejection not cached.
   * Unpinned: the `!resp.ok` branch for a status that is not 5xx, 408 or 429 (cache 30 s, answer 401), and the 429 classification.
   * Why it is harmless today: the security service rejects with 200 `valid:false`, and answers 400 only for a missing key. An edit that changes either branch would still go unseen.
   * Fix: one cell with a 403 stub and one with a 429 stub.

**Searched before filing.** Team KS, issue titles and descriptions including archived, plus comment bodies, 2026-10-28 \~10:30Z (issues / comments):

* No hits: "exchange timed out" 0 / 0, "proxy.ts:620" 0 / 0, "verification.ts:900" 0 / 0, "non-OK 4xx" 0 / 0, "checkApiKey" 0 / 0.
* "documents/upload": 2 issues. KS-1724 is about uncapped arrays and KS-1222 about the MIME screen; neither is this.
* "http.request": 4 issues (KS-1329, KS-1087, KS-1083, KS-955); none is about a missing timeout.
* Positive control "connector-token": 10 issues, KS-1240 among them. A freshly coined zero control: 0 / 0.

**Refs:** KS-1240; PR #1785 at head `e01a5094771d`; gate verdict `0_Brain/reference/2026-10-28_gate4-tier1/verdict.md`, findings 1785-1, 1785-3 and 1785-4. Filed on the coordinator's instruction (gate result, 10:26Z).

**BLUF:** Item 1 of this ticket (a connector-exchange timeout still ends as a downstream 401) is NOT built, on Wednesday's ruling of 2026-11-06, option C. The 401 stays as it is, logged and bounded at 5 s. The ticket stays open.

The caller has already set the connector principal and the x-user headers, so with no Bearer the request goes on. A Bearer-only upstream (originate documents, anchoring) then answers 401; a handler that serves an sk_ caller from req.user alone succeeds. The ticket itself records that second kind exists.
- **Three shapes were weighed, none built.**
  - A, a gateway-wide 503 when the exchange returns null: ruled out, because it would fail requests that succeed today.
  - B, a 503 only for mounts that need the connector Bearer: it needs a per-mount flag in the proxy table and a reviewed list of Bearer-only mounts, and it changes a status that outside connectors read, so it needs a ruling from Kam before anyone builds it.
  - C, leave the 401: chosen. It is logged with its true cause ("timed out after 5000 ms"), bounded at 5 s, and not cached, so the next request retries the exchange. The cost is the one this ticket names: a transient fault reads as an auth failure.
- **Read, not judged:** auth's own /internal/connector-token calls the security service with no signal (services/auth/src/routes/internal.ts:43), so after the gateway gives up at 5 s the auth handler keeps waiting.

* **(a) GitHub sign-in can take as long as production nginx allows.**
  * The GitHub adapter makes up to three calls in sequence (token, profile, emails), each bounded at 10 s by #1788, so one sign-in can take up to 30 s.
  * That equals production nginx's `proxy_read_timeout 30s` (`docker/nginx-gateway/nginx-production.conf:290-292`), which `location /api/auth/` (`:356-359`) inherits without overriding. If all three calls run just under 10 s, nginx answers 504 at 30 s while auth may still finish the sign-in for nobody, with the OAuth state already spent.

  * Options: one shared per-sign-in deadline across an adapter's calls (for example a single 20 s signal), or keep the per-call bound and document the case.
  * Found by reading the conf and the adapters; not run through nginx.
* **(b) The auth half of the connector-token exchange is still unbounded.** `services/auth/src/routes/internal.ts:43`: `/internal/connector-token` calls the security service's `/api/keys/validate` with no signal. #1785 stops the gateway waiting after 5 s, but the auth handler keeps waiting.
