title: No supported way to put a user in a second tenant on a local stack — needed for cross-tenant systemTest peers (split from KS-1674)
description:
**BLUF:** systemTest needs two ordinary (non-super-admin) users in two **different** tenants on a local slot, so the Schemathesis `object_level_authorization` check (BOLA/IDOR, WFC 906) can test cross-tenant isolation. On develop there is no supported route that does this. This ticket asks for that capability; how it is built is your call. The systemTest side is a separate ticket, blocked by this one.

## Why it is needed

[KS-1674](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1674/schemathesis-object-level-authorization-4310-never-runs-under) (PR [Secuura/Distributed_Secuura#1673](https://linear.app/secuura/review/ks-1674-schemathesis-object-level-authorization-runs-in-its-own-aec22065af81), merged as `5671d5115`) runs `object_level_authorization` with two OWNER peers in the **same** tenant (`systemTest/schemathesis/config/schemathesis_tests.yaml:650-668`). The ticket asked for peers across two tenants. Without them, cross-tenant exposure on findings such as [KS-1703](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1703/security-seven-get-by-id-routes-serve-any-authenticated-callers-object) is inferred, not measured.

## Why the existing routes do not work (read on develop `5f6899918`; nothing run)

1. **Self-registration lands in the default tenant.** `POST /api/auth/register` takes the tenant from `x-tenant-id` / `x-tenant-slug` (`services/auth/src/routes/auth.ts:217-218`), but the gateway strips client-sent trust headers (`services/api-gateway/src/index.ts:309-330`). A tenantless token is then given `DEFAULT_TENANT_ID` (`services/api-gateway/src/middleware/auth.ts:503`).
2. **Tenant from email domain at login is off, and would not persist.** `services/auth/src/routes/auth.ts:549-586` runs only when `MULTI_TENANCY_ENABLED=true` (defaults to `false` in `docker-compose.yml`). Its own comment says the `UPDATE users SET tenant_id` is a no-op under fail-closed RLS ([KS-458](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-458/rls-fail-closed-flip-guc-on-checkout-flip-the-consolidated-tenant)).
3. `X-Tenant-Override` **applies only to super-admin roles** (`services/api-gateway/src/middleware/auth.ts:515-521`). A super-admin can read every object, so it cannot act as a peer. (The override is also partly broken: [KS-1704](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1704/security-two-cross-tenant-isolation-regressions-fail-on-develop-a).)
4. **Invited stub then register keeps the stub's tenant** (`auth.ts:237-242`, [KS-74](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-74/pending-invite-ux-post-apicertificationsissue-accepts-holderemail-and)), but `POST /api/users/stub` takes the tenant from the caller's own verified token (`services/auth/src/routes/users.ts:398`). A caller can only mint stubs in a tenant they are already in.
5. **Not verified:** a connector token carries its own tenant (`services/auth/src/middleware/authenticate.ts:116`) and is accepted on `/api/users/stub`. If a connector can be issued for a second tenant, that may already be a route. Worth checking before building anything new.

## Acceptance criteria

1. A documented, supported sequence of API calls, runnable on a local slot without editing the database by hand, that (a) creates or selects a second tenant and (b) leaves a named, non-super-admin user (OWNER or another self-service role) whose verified token carries that tenant's id.
2. The user can log in and is scoped to that tenant on later requests (the gateway forwards its `x-tenant-id`, not the default).
3. The sequence is described here, or in the relevant service docs, so systemTest can call it from `systemTest/fixtures/provision-actors.ts`.

Raised from [KS-1674](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1674/schemathesis-object-level-authorization-4310-never-runs-under) at Peter's request (2026-10-26). The systemTest follow-up is assigned to Peter and blocked by this ticket.

title: Node 26's semver-major Readable.read() change truncates every synchronous cbor.encode() to its first byte on host test runs - images pin node:24 and are unaffected
description:
**Node 26.0.0 removed the behaviour** `cbor`**'s synchronous encoder depends on, so on a Node 26 host every** `cbor.encode()` **of a value longer than one byte returns only its first byte. Host-side test runs are affected; the deployed images are not. The failure mode is fail-closed.**

## The mechanism

Node commit `fadb214d95` / PR 60441, *"stream: readable read one buffer at a time"*, is listed **semver-major in the v26.0.0 changelog** (2026-05-05): `Readable.prototype.read()` with no size argument no longer concatenates the internal buffer, it returns one queued chunk. Deliberate, to avoid the cost of merging buffers — **so this is not a bug and no Node patch will restore the old behaviour.** *(Commit, PR and changelog entry identified via web search, not read at source.)*

`cbor`'s synchronous `encode()` / `encodeOne()` / `encodeCanonical()` are all `_encodeAll` (`encoder.js:595-602`):

```js
_encodeAll(objs) { const bs = new NoFilter({…}); this.pipe(bs); … this.end(); return bs.read() }
```

`NoFilter.read(size)` (`nofilter@3.1.0`, `lib/index.js:285`) delegates straight to `super.read(size)`. Its own documented contract is "no size argument → return all the data in the internal buffer", which is exactly what Node 26 withdrew.

## Measured on this host (Node v26.8.1, `cbor@9.0.2`)

| value encoded | returned | correct |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `['Signature1', …]` | `84` (1 B) | \~90 B |
| `'Signature1'` | `6a` (1 B) | `6a5369676e617475726531` |
| `Buffer.alloc(4,0xab)` | `44` (1 B) | `44abababab` |
| `Map{1:-8}` | `a1` (1 B) | `a10127` |
| `Map{1:1,3:-8,-1:6,-2:<32B>}` | `a4` (1 B) | \~45 B |

Not container-specific — **every** value whose encoding exceeds one byte is truncated. `7` and `Map{}` come back correct only because they are one byte already, which is what makes this quiet. Decoding a truncated value throws `Insufficient data`.

Scoped to the synchronous path: `cbor.encodeAsync` **is correct** (`83010203`) and **the decoder is healthy** (`decodeFirstSync('83010203')` → `[1,2,3]`).

## It is the runtime, proven with zero dependencies and a second runtime

Pure `stream.PassThrough`, 4 bytes written as 3 chunks, no packages involved:

|  | Node v26.8.1 | Node v24.22.1 |
| -- | -- | -- |
| 3 chunks, `read()` | `83` | `83010203` |
| 3 chunks + `end()`, `read()` | `83` | `83010203` |
| one 4-byte chunk, `read()` *(control)* | `83010203` | `83010203` |
| `read(4)` explicit size | `83010203` | `83010203` |

The control discriminates, so the zero is a real zero. Successive `read()` calls on Node 26 return `83`,`01`,`0203` in order — the bytes are all present, merely no longer concatenated. `read(readableLength)` is the documented approximation and was verified on Node 26.

Node 24 runs were in throwaway `docker run --rm node:24-alpine` containers from an image already present on the host; nothing was installed, downloaded or built. This laptop has **only** Homebrew `node@26` (v26.8.1) — no Node 24, no nvm/fnm/volta/asdf.

## Items

### (a) Remedy options — no choice made, this needs a ruling

1. **Pin the dev/test runtime to Node 24**, which is what every image already ships: tighten `engines.node` (today the root is `>=18.0.0`, which *permits* Node 26) and add a runtime file (`.nvmrc` / `.node-version`) so host runs match the images. There is currently **no** `.nvmrc` in the repo and `packages/shared` declares **no** `engines` **at all**.
2. **An upstream fix in** `cbor` **and/or** `nofilter` — have `_encodeAll` read the whole buffer (`read(readableLength)`, or drain in a loop and concatenate). Not filed upstream by this investigation; `cbor`/`nofilter` issue trackers were **not** searched.
3. ⚠ **Not an option: bumping** `cbor`**.** `cbor@10.0.12` **is broken identically — measured**, not assumed, against an on-disk copy under `@meshsdk/provider`: all four cases truncate the same way. **The open dependabot PR 635 (**`cbor` **9.0.2 → 10.0.12) does NOT fix this.**

### (b) KS-1727 is the first known symptom

`packages/shared/src/__tests__/wallet-signature.test.ts:47-49`, the file's only positive cell. `verifyMessageSignature` exits at `wallet.ts:372` (`CIP-8: failed to extract Ed25519 public key from COSEKey`) because the COSEKey the test hands it is the 1-byte `a4`. **Both** `wallet.ts` **and the test are correct**; the four negative cells pass only because all four assert `false`, which a verifier that always returns false satisfies. On Node 24, same cbor bytes from the same disk, the positive cell `RETURNS TRUE` **(**`wallet.ts:418`**)** and the negative exits at `:391` (payload mismatch), so the KS 278 payload binding is intact.

### (c) Related — flagged, not investigated

* **KS 1734** — `services/security`, 11 of 33 test files fail on the first run after `npm ci`; records Node v26.
* **KS 1729** — vc-issuer unit suite cold-run skips; records Node v26.
* **KS 1625** — the standing contradiction that admits a Node 26 host at all: declared Node floor `engines.node >=18.0.0` versus what the images actually ship.

None of these was examined for this cause. They are named because they share the runtime, not because a link was measured.

## Scope — deployed services are NOT affected

* **All 32 Dockerfiles pin** `node:24-alpine` (75 `FROM` lines, zero exceptions), `originate` included — the service hosting `/sign-wallet`. Node 24 encodes correctly, so no deployed route carries this. **No deployed route was called.**
* The only synchronous `cbor.encode` in tracked production source is `wallet.ts:397`; the other five occurrences are inside the test file. Two `decodeFirstSync` sites, both on the healthy decoder.
* Where it would bite on a Node 26 host, it **fails closed**: a real wallet supplies a properly-encoded COSEKey, so the failure lands at `:397` and surfaces as `Ed25519 signature verification failed` — valid signatures rejected, never invalid ones accepted. **Not a forgery surface.**

## Searched first

By symbol, file path and error string, titles + descriptions, `includeArchived: true`: `cbor.encode`, `nofilter`, `Readable.read`, `_encodeAll`, `encodeAsync`, `readableHighWaterMark` — **0 hits each**. `verifyMessageSignature` → 2 hits, KS-1727 and KS 1229 (Done). Control: the same instrument returns 25 hits for `node:24-alpine` and 3 for `Node v26`, so it can fire.

## UNMEASURED

* Whether the transitive `cbor` consumers (`services/anchoring`, `services/nft-certificate`, `frontend/issuer` lockfiles, `@meshsdk/provider`) call the synchronous encode internally — not traced.
* Whether `cbor` or `nofilter` upstream has a fix or an open issue for Node ≥26.
* Which other packages on this laptop depend on the same withdrawn `read()` contract — the repo-wide blast radius of Node 26 beyond CBOR.
* When host runs first moved to Node 26, and when KS-1727's cell began failing (develop was not bisected).

Evidence: `5_Project_History/2026-10-26_seatV-2nd/` — 8 probes, 19 output files, secret-scanned.

title: services/vc-issuer test files cannot use a top-level await: the enrolled type-check refuses it with TS1378 under module: commonjs, foreclosing the module-scope fix shape
description:
## BLUF

**A test file in** `services/vc-issuer` **cannot use a top-level** `await`**.** The service compiles
`module: commonjs` / `target: es2021`, and its enrolled test-file type-check
(`tsconfig.test.json`, read by `scripts/typecheck-tests/check.cjs`) therefore reports **TS1378**
for one. That forecloses a fix shape KS 1729 explicitly sanctions — doing an expensive import
once at module scope, so the cost falls at collection where there is no hook timeout.

Filed on the coordinator's ruling, facts only. **No fix is proposed here**: the trade-off is
named below and belongs to whoever owns the service's compile target.

## Measured

At develop `8661f5d418b23ffb0c63a2504d707eb12189b5ad`, adding one `await freshModules();` at
module scope in each of three test files, then running
`node scripts/typecheck-tests/check.cjs services/vc-issuer` from `Blockchain/Dev`:

**rc 1**, one error per file, verbatim:

```
src/__tests__/ks1020-presentation-lookup-exact-or-404.test.ts(91,1): TS1378: Top-level 'await' expressions are only allowed when the 'module' option is set to 'es2022', 'esnext', 'system', 'node16', 'node18', 'node20', 'nodenext', or 'preserve', and the 'target' option is set to 'es2017' or higher.
src/__tests__/ks1116-presentation-and-credential-reads-bound-to-the-creator.test.ts(192,1): TS1378: Top-level 'await' expressions are only allowed when the 'module' option is set to 'es2022', 'esnext', 'system', 'node16', 'node18', 'node20', 'nodenext', or 'preserve', and the 'target' option is set to 'es2017' or higher.
src/__tests__/ks1683-credential-list-and-by-hash-bound-to-the-creator.test.ts(134,1): TS1378: Top-level 'await' expressions are only allowed when the 'module' option is set to 'es2022', 'esnext', 'system', 'node16', 'node18', 'node20', 'nodenext', or 'preserve', and the 'target' option is set to 'es2017' or higher.
```

Without that line the same command is **rc 0** ("tsc examined 33 files, 19 of them under
`__tests__`; 0 errors: 0 in the baseline, 0 new; 0 stale baseline entries").

**Note the asymmetry:** vitest runs such a file fine — only the type-check refuses it. So the
pattern is available at runtime and unavailable under the gate.

## The config lines

`services/vc-issuer/tsconfig.json`:

* `"module": "commonjs"`
* `"target": "es2021"`

`services/vc-issuer/tsconfig.test.json` (what the ratchet reads) adds nothing relevant — it is:

```json
{
  "extends": "./tsconfig.json",
  "compilerOptions": { "noEmit": true },
  "include": ["src/**/*"],
  "exclude": ["node_modules", "dist"]
}
```

So the refusal comes from the **service's own** compile settings, inherited by the test config.
It is not specific to the ratchet, and it applies to every service enrolled the same way.

## The trade-off, named not resolved

* Raising `module`/`target` **only in** `tsconfig.test.json` would unblock the pattern without
  touching the service build, since that config is `noEmit` — but it makes the test program's
  module semantics differ from the shipped code's, which is the kind of divergence a type-check
  exists to prevent.
* Raising them in `tsconfig.json` keeps test and source aligned but **changes the service's**
  **emit**, which is a real change to shipped output.
* Leaving it means the module-scope shape stays unavailable and callers reach for a per-hook
  timeout instead — which is what KS 1729 did, deliberately, with the reason written in-file.

## Related, NOT a duplicate

**KS 1329** — `packages/shared` does not type-check `src/__tests__`. It is the only other open
issue naming `TS1378`, and it was read before filing rather than matched on the token:

* It concerns `packages/shared`, not `services/vc-issuer`.
* Its subject is test files being **excluded** from the type-check, hiding 10 errors.
* Its TS1378 appear as **probe artefacts** — it raises `module`/`target` in an out-of-repo probe
  precisely because that package's tests **already use** top-level `await`, and says leaving
  them at `commonjs` produces "9x TS1343 and 5x TS1378 that are artefacts of the probe".

That makes KS 1329 evidence the same constraint bites elsewhere, with the opposite symptom:
there the tests already use the pattern and are simply never type-checked; here they are
type-checked and the pattern is refused.

## Searched first

Exact substring over the title and description of all **705** open Secuura-PK issues:

* `TS1378` -> **1** (KS 1329, above).
* `top-level await` -> 0. `top-level 'await'` -> 0.
* `module: commonjs` -> 0. `"module": "commonjs"` -> 0.
* `tsconfig.test.json` -> 4 (KS 1554, KS 1494, KS 1090, KS 1000) — all about enrolment, none
  about this refusal.

Controls showing the instrument finds known tickets: `Hook timed out in 10000ms` -> 4,
`exceed vitest's 5 s default` -> 4, `ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT` -> 3.

## Found by

Seat S 2nd while building KS 1729 (pull request 1714), 2026-10-26. The module-scope shape was
built first, measured as above, and reverted in full — the three files were verified
byte-identical to develop afterwards. Measured on Node v26.8.1.

title: Rotate the dev-ps secrets exposed on 26 Oct 2026 (tracking checklist)
description:
**Status, 27 Oct 2026** (from Key Vault last-updated times, names only):

* **Rotated:** everything ticked below. Rows marked **delete/revoke the old** still have a live old value at the provider.
* **28 Oct 2026:** `azure-openai-key`, `stripe-test-secret-key`, `stripe-test-webhook-secret` (and `stripe-test-publishable-key`) rotated; `ciam-client-secret` removed from Key Vault (nothing reads it). Evidence in the comments.
* **Kept by Stuart's decision:** `dev-seed-password`. The seeded accounts' passwords were changed in the app instead (28 Oct 2026).
* `ciam-client-secret`**:** retired 28 Oct 2026, removed from Key Vault through Terraform; dev-ps restarted clean without it.
* **Group D:** all six rotated with [PS-1375](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1375/rotation-tooling-for-the-at-rest-keys-retired-slots-in-deployments-re>)'s tooling (27–28 Oct 2026); evidence per key is on [PS-1375](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1375/rotation-tooling-for-the-at-rest-keys-retired-slots-in-deployments-re>).

---

**What happened.** On 26 Oct 2026 a Claude Code session ran `terraform fmt -check -diff .` in `ssd/az-docker/az-secuura-DEV-docker/`. That also processed the gitignored `terraform.tfvars` and printed its values into the session transcript.

* **Where the values ended up:** the session transcript on Stuart's MacBook Pro (`~/.claude/projects/…/b6749c74-…jsonl`) and the model context. Nothing was committed, posted or logged elsewhere.
* **The guard against a repeat** is [PS-1361](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1361/block-claude-code-sessions-from-printing-secret-files-hook-rule) (#1159, on `develop`).
* **Scope:** **dev-ps only.** UAT and production use their own secret stores, which were not printed.

**How dev-ps reads these.** `ssd/dep-az-dev/setenv.sh` fetches each value from the Key Vault secret of the same name when the stack starts, renders the config, and the app reads it. So:

* **Terraform owns the values.** They come from `var.kv_secrets` in `terraform.tfvars` (`azurerm_key_vault_secret.app`). **Change the value in** `terraform.tfvars`**, then** `terraform apply`**.** A value changed only in Key Vault is put back to the old, exposed value by the next apply.
* **A new value takes effect only on the next dev-ps restart or deploy.** Make the change at the other end (provider, MySQL) first, then apply, then restart.
* This ticket names keys only. No value goes in a comment, PR or log.

**After each step, verify** (a Claude session can do this once you deploy):

* `/Health/Data` (via the VPN): database connected, mail provider, each sign-in provider configured, platform-k provisioning key accepted.
* The step's own check, listed under each group below.

## A. Issued by a provider: create a new one there, deploy, then revoke the old (no downtime)

Entra, Google, Stripe and Azure OpenAI all allow an old and a new secret to work at the same time.

- [X] `ciam-client-secret` (removed from Key Vault 28 Oct 2026, not rotated: nothing reads it since [PS-588](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-588/e483-workforce-only-retire-the-ciam-scheme-entirely))
  * **Where:** Entra CIAM tenant › app registration › Certificates & secrets.
  * **Check:** CIAM sign-in reaches the provider and comes back.
- [X] `azuread-workforce-client-secret` (rotated 26 Oct; **delete the old secret** in the app registration)
  * **Where:** workforce app registration › Certificates & secrets.
  * **Check:** "Continue with Microsoft" round trip.
- [X] `google-client-secret` (rotated 26 Oct; **delete the old secret** in the Google console)
  * **Where:** Google Cloud console › the dev OAuth client.
  * **Check:** the Google sign-in round trip.
- [X] `entra-vid-client-secret` (rotated 26 Oct; **delete the old secret** in the app registration)
  * **Where:** the Verified ID app registration (secpsdev tenant).
  * **Check:** a Verified ID Start no longer fails with an auth error.
- [X] `apple-private-key-base64` **and** `apple-key-id`, together (rotated 26 Oct; **revoke the old key** in Apple Developer)
  * **Where:** Apple Developer › Keys. A new key comes with a new key id.
  * **Check:** the Apple sign-in round trip, then revoke the old key.
- [X] `azure-openai-key` (rotated 28 Oct; a chat completion with the new key returned 200)
  * **Where:** Azure OpenAI resource › Keys. Switch dev-ps to key 2, then regenerate key 1.
  * **Check:** chat answers.
- [X] `mailgun-key` (rotated 26 Oct; **delete the old key** in Mailgun)
  * **Where:** Mailgun › API keys. Create the new key, deploy, then delete the old one.
  * **Check:** a test email is delivered.
- [X] `stripe-test-secret-key` (rotated 28 Oct; `GET /v1/balance` with the new key returned 200)
  * **Where:** Stripe (test mode) › API keys › roll (with overlap).
  * **Check:** the pricing / checkout page loads with no Stripe error.
- [X] `stripe-test-webhook-secret` (rotated 28 Oct; **not yet proven**: /Health "Last Stripe webhook accepted" moves off "never" on the next real event)
  * **Where:** Stripe › the dev-ps webhook endpoint › roll the signing secret (the old one stays valid for up to 24 h).
  * **Check:** a test event returns 200.
- [X] `exchange-rate-api-key` (rotated 26 Oct; delete the old key at the provider if it allows)
  * **Where:** the provider.
  * **Check:** display-currency rates refresh.
- [X] `platform-k-provisioning-key` (rotated 27 Oct, proven by ISS3 University registering; old key revoked on Kintsugi 27 Oct)
  * **Where:** a new one minted on **Kintsugi** by a platform-k admin; then revoke the old one.
  * **Check:** `/Health/Data` says the provisioning key is accepted. Existing organisations are unaffected; only new-organisation registration uses this key.

## B. Database passwords: change them inside MySQL first

MySQL reads `MYSQL_ROOT_PASSWORD` / `MYSQL_PASSWORD` only when its data volume is first created. A changed secret alone leaves the app unable to connect.

- [X] `mysqldump` dev-ps's `ssddb` first. (26 Oct, all databases, kept on the VM under `/home/ubuntu/db-backups/`)
- [X] (26 Oct) `mysql-user-password`: `ALTER USER` the app user (`mysql-user`) inside the dev-ps MySQL container, then update `terraform.tfvars`, apply, and restart, all in one window.
  * **Check:** `/Health/Data` shows the database connected, and the app log has no auth errors.
- [X] (26 Oct) `mysql-root-password`: same order.

## C. Simple: change the value, apply, restart

- [X] (26 Oct) `token-sign-key`: signs only the short-lived stream URLs in `SDViewDownload`. Anyone with a viewer open at that moment has to reload. Nothing stored depends on it.
- [X] (26 Oct) `entra-vid-callback-api-key`: our own value, sent with each Verified ID request. Only a verification in progress at the moment of the switch is affected.
- [X] (26 Oct) `dev-pfx-password`: **no application code reads it** (`Secrets:DevPfxPassword`). Rotate it, or remove it from the template and tfvars as dead config.
- [X] `dev-seed-password`: kept by decision; the seeded accounts' passwords were changed in the app (28 Oct). **Also a finding.** dev-ps's value equals the dev password the repo documents, against [PS-439](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-439/uat-seeded-accounts-fall-back-to-the-hardcoded-dev-password>)'s "no deployment shares a password with the repository". It is used only when seeding an empty database, so changing it does not change existing accounts. Do both:
  1. set a new value;
  2. change the seeded accounts' passwords in the app ([stuart@lhsg.com](<mailto:stuart@lhsg.com>), [firstone@lhsg.com](<mailto:firstone@lhsg.com>), [firsttwo@lhsg.com](<mailto:firsttwo@lhsg.com>) and the others).

## D. Keys that protect stored data: extra steps first, or data becomes unreadable

- [X] `platform-k-credential-key` (rotated 27 Oct 2026 with [PS-1375](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1375/rotation-tooling-for-the-at-rest-keys-retired-slots-in-deployments-re>)'s tooling: 12 connector keys re-encrypted, an anchor proven, the retired value removed — see [PS-1375](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1375/rotation-tooling-for-the-at-rest-keys-retired-slots-in-deployments-re>))
  * **Risk:** it encrypts each organisation's stored platform-k connector key. Rotating it without a retired slot strands them all silently.
  * **Order:** put the outgoing value in `PlatformKCredentialKeyRetired` → deploy → rotate.
- [X] `signing-key-encryption-key` (rotated 28 Oct 2026: 5 of 5 certificates re-encrypted, 0 failed; a document signed afterwards; retired value removed)
  * **Risk:** it encrypts the stored signing certificates.
  * **Order:** put the outgoing value in `SigningKeyEncryptionKeyRetired` → deploy → rotate. **Never overwrite it without that step.**
- [X] `template-storage-key` (rotated 28 Oct 2026: signing 0/0; migration 1/1 is a seed fixture with no file, accepted; an old document opened and signed with a personal and an organisation certificate afterwards)
  * **Risk:** it still decrypts any document not yet moved to an organisation key, plus some non-document secrets.
  * **Order:** first confirm dev-ps's migration figures are 0 remaining and 0 failures (`docs/runbooks/retire-template-storage-key.md` §1). Then see `docs/identity-key-rotation.md` for its other readers.
- [X] `doc-storage-key` (rotated 28 Oct 2026 after identity data left the fallback; the one fallback-era identity commitment no longer verifies locally; log tags changed)
  * **Risk:** the fallback root for identity crypto, and the log-pseudonym key (rotating it changes the pseudonym tags in logs).
  * **Order:** follow `docs/identity-key-rotation.md`.
- [X] `identity-data-encryption-key` (rotated 28 Oct 2026 as a ROOT rotation: 16 DID keys re-encrypted, 0 failed; retired root removed by decision, so 80 commitments under the exposed root no longer verify locally — anchored copies unchanged)
- [X] `identity-issuer-signing-key` (rotated 28 Oct 2026, compromised case: old public key NOT trusted, so the 9 earlier credentials verify as INVALID; a new declaration verified AUTHENTIC)
  * **Risk:** the issuer key for verifiable credentials.
  * **Not verified yet:** before rotating, check whether credentials already issued under the old key still verify afterwards.

## Not secret: no rotation needed

These were also printed, but they are not secrets:

* client ids and identifiers: `google-client-id`, `apple-client-id`, `apple-team-id`, `entra-vid-client-id`, `azuread-workforce-client-id`;
* Entra settings: `entra-vid-authority`, `entra-vid-verifier-authority`, `entra-vid-credential-type`, `entra-vid-accepted-issuers`;
* other values: `platform-k-base-url`, `stripe-test-publishable-key`, the `stripe-live-*` placeholders (`not-used-on-dev`), `health-allow-cidrs`, the SSH **public** key, `allowed_admin_cidrs`.

## Afterwards

- [ ] Consider deleting this session's transcript on the MacBook Pro once rotation is done. The values in it are dead by then, but it is the one remaining copy.
- [ ] Close this ticket with each step's verification reading.

nodes.body:
**Azure OpenAI and Stripe test keys rotated on dev-ps**, 28 Oct 2026. Stuart rolled the keys at both providers and updated the store `terraform.tfvars`.

**Apply**
- The plan showed only these four keys changing, plus the two pending `document_keys_audit` creates, which were not applied:
  - `azure-openai-key`
  - `stripe-test-publishable-key`
  - `stripe-test-secret-key`
  - `stripe-test-webhook-secret`
- Targeted apply of the four: 0 added, 4 changed, 0 destroyed.
- Value shapes checked without printing the values: `pk_test_`, `sk_test_` and `whsec_` prefixes are present; the OpenAI key is 84 characters.

**Restart and checks**
- `start-services.sh` exited 0, and the app container is up. `/Health` returns 200.
- A read-only Stripe `GET /v1/balance` with the new secret key returned **200**.
- An Azure OpenAI chat completion against `eddi-openai` / `gpt-35-turbo` (1 token) with the new key returned **200**.

**Not yet proven:** the new webhook signing secret. Only the next real Stripe event shows it working. `/Health` → "Last Stripe webhook accepted" should then move off "never". A refusal shows as "Last Stripe webhook refused".

**Still open on this ticket:** `dev-seed-password` was deliberately left unchanged.

**`ciam-client-secret` removed from dev-ps** on 28 Oct 2026, on Stuart's ruling.

**Removal**
- Targeted `terraform apply -target='azurerm_key_vault_secret.app["ciam-client-secret"]'`: 1 destroyed, nothing else touched.
- The secret was already absent from `terraform.tfvars`, so the plan had shown it as a pending destroy since then.
- `az keyvault secret show` → SecretNotFound, and it does not appear in the deleted-secrets list.

**Why this is safe**
- PS-588 retired the CIAM auth scheme, so nothing reads `AzureAdCiam:ClientSecret`.
- `ssd/dep-az-dev/setenv.sh` fetches it with `fetch_secret_optional`.

**Restart check**
- `start-services.sh` exit 0, with the expected `optional secret 'ciam-client-secret' not found … continuing without it` warning.
- The app container is up.
- `/Health` 200, `/Health/Data` 200, sign-in page 200.

**Not changed**
- Production's `setenv.sh` still requires the secret (`fetch_secret`). That belongs with PS-1378, production's template.
- `terraform.tfvars.example` still lists the key, and the dev-ps template still has the `__CIAM_CLIENT_SECRET__` placeholder. Both are repo tidy-up.
**Seeded account passwords on dev-ps: handled**, 28 Oct 2026 (Stuart). The `dev-seed-password` Key Vault secret was not part of this; it is only read when an empty database is seeded.

**platform-k provisioning key: DONE, 27 Oct 2026.** Stuart revoked the old key (exposed, created 20 Aug) around 02:20 UTC with the platform-admin `DELETE /api/security/keys/<id>`.

**Checked after the revoke:**
- **Health page (02:22 UTC):** Kintsugi reachable, last response at 02:22, 12 organisations registered, 0 pending or failed, 0 with a refused connector key, nothing waiting to anchor, 0 errors. The anchor-failed count is still 7, the same as before the rotation.
- **Real flow:** Stuart uploaded a document (dev-ps `DocumentTransaction` 97, `upload`, document 17). Kintsugi anchored it with that organisation's own connector key: `ExternalRef` set, no `AnchorFailedAt`. So the existing organisations' connector keys are unaffected by the revoke.

**Finding:** dev-ps's `platform-k-credential-key` (the key that encrypts the stored connector keys) is set to the old provisioning key's Kintsugi **id** string, not a generated random value. It works as encryption key material, which is why nothing broke, but it is not a generated secret, and it was in the exposed file. Rotating it is the PS-1375 work (retired slot `platform-k-credential-key-retired` first). The new value must be a generated 32-character secret (`openssl rand -base64 24`), never a Kintsugi id.

**platform-k provisioning key: Kintsugi key ids** — redacted 27 Oct 2026.

The old key's id was removed from this comment. dev-ps's `platform-k-credential-key` turned out to be set to that same string, so here it would have been an encryption key's value, not just a label. The new key's id is known to Stuart; record it only somewhere that is not also used as a secret.

**platform-k provisioning key (dev-ps): rotated and proven, 27 Oct 2026. Old key not yet revoked.**

- **New key:** created on Kintsugi by Stuart with a curl call: platform-admin `POST /api/security/keys`, scope `organizations:register`, no organisation, tenant Secuura Co. (`a0000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000099`). That is the tenant dev-ps's organisations are in.
- **Key Vault:** a targeted Terraform apply changed only `azurerm_key_vault_secret.app["platform-k-provisioning-key"]`, at 01:51 UTC. dev-ps restarted at 02:05 UTC.
- **Proof:** Stuart created a new organisation, "ISS3 University" (dev-ps org 17). At 02:08 UTC dev-ps registered it on Kintsugi: row `Provisioned`, Kintsugi org id `5e596a75-8c84-46a6-98a4-0e52a75789ae`. `/Health/Data` shows "Provisioning key accepted by K: accepted", 12 registered, 0 pending, 0 failed.
- **Still open:** revoke the old key on Kintsugi. A key with no organisation can't be listed through the API or the admin app, so its id has to come from Kintsugi's database (`svc_api_keys`, org-less, `organizations:register`, tenant Secuura Co., not the new key).

**Found while checking:** the `terraform.tfvars` from the secrets store differed from Key Vault on `platform-k-credential-key`, and lacked `ciam-client-secret`. A full apply would have changed the credential key and stranded all the stored connector keys. Nothing was applied except the targeted change above. Stuart has since copied in a tfvars matching Key Vault for both platform-k keys. `ciam-client-secret` is still missing from it; the app doesn't read that value, and it is Stuart's call. Rotating the credential key itself is PS-1375.

**platform-k provisioning key (dev-ps): handed to Kamil, 27 Oct 2026**

On the dev-ps side this is a one-secret change: the Key Vault secret `platform-k-provisioning-key`, managed by Terraform and last set on 20 Aug 2026. dev-ps uses it only to register a new organisation on Kintsugi. All 11 are already registered and none are pending, so the swap causes no outage.

The new key itself can't be created from Kintsugi's admin app:
- The API Keys page only makes `read`/`write` keys. A provisioning key needs scope `organizations:register`, no organisation, created by a platform admin through `POST /api/keys`.
- The new key must be in the same tenant as the old one, because dev-ps's organisations were registered into that tenant. The app doesn't show which tenant that is: either Secuura Co. (`…0099`) or the unlisted default tenant (`…0001`).
- Kintsugi has no in-place rotation, and an organisation-less key can't be listed, so the old key's id is only in Kintsugi's database (`svc_api_keys`).

**Ask for Kamil:** find dev-ps's current provisioning key (org-less, `organizations:register`), mint a replacement in the same tenant, and send it to Stuart privately. Revoke the old key only after Stuart confirms dev-ps is running on the new one.

**Then on dev-ps:** Stuart sets `platform-k-provisioning-key` in `terraform.tfvars`, then a targeted `terraform apply` and a restart. To prove it: a test organisation registers, and `/Health/Data` shows "Provisioning key accepted by K: accepted". After that, Kamil revokes the old key.

The 11 per-organisation connector keys are separate keys and are not part of this rotation.

**Group D, the six keys that protect stored data: ⛔ blocked on PS-1375.** No safe rotation is possible today:
- **No retired slots:** the signing-key and platform-k credential-key retired slots are not rendered by any deployment.
- **No re-encryption:** nothing re-encrypts stored data onto a new key (`Rotate()` has no callers).
- **Identity root:** rotating it strands everything stored, and the version bump derives from the same root.
- **Issuer key:** has no rotation procedure.

**Mitigation in place (#1044, checked on dev-ps):** all 23 document wrap records are under Azure Key Vault HSM keys that were never in the leaked file, so the exposed storage keys cannot decrypt any dev-ps document.

**What the remaining at-rest keys need to be misused:** the dev-ps database ciphertext. The database is not reachable outside the VM, and its passwords were rotated today.

**The exception:** `identity-issuer-signing-key`, which could forge dev-ps-issued credentials without the database.

**#16 / #17 `mysql-user-password` and `mysql-root-password`: ✅ rotated and proven (26 Oct 2026, 12:47 UTC).**

1. **Backup:** `mysqldump` of all databases first, to `/home/ubuntu/db-backups/dev-ps-all-20261026T124445Z.sql.gz` on the VM (≈1 MB, gzip-verified).
2. **Key Vault:** the new values went in by targeted terraform apply.
3. **MySQL:** `ALTER USER` on the box for the app user and root. The values were read from Key Vault with the VM's managed identity and fed to MySQL on stdin, never printed or put on a command line.
4. **Restart.** The first script stopped after its ALTER step: a `grep -v` with nothing left to print exited 1 under `set -e`. A second script checked first and restarted only once both new passwords were confirmed:
   - **Before the restart:** the app user and root accepted their NEW passwords and refused their OLD ones.
   - **After the restart:** the app user and root both connect (OK).
   - **App health:** `/Health/Data` shows Database connection ok (6 ms), 83 migrations applied, none pending, 0 errors in the buffer. The app container started 12:47 UTC on `4fb15e7`.

The same restart also brought in #10 / #12 / #13 / #14: exchange rate, token-sign, Verified ID callback, PFX.

**Stuart to check:**
- a share link opens in the viewer;
- a Verified ID Start shows a QR code.

**Remaining:** the six keys that protect stored data (group D), each needing a retired slot or migration check first.
**Deferred:** OpenAI, Stripe ×2, the platform-k provisioning key, the seed password.

**Simple keys done in one pass (26 Oct 2026).** Targeted apply of four Key Vault secrets; the plan showed each as `(sensitive value)`, nothing added or destroyed:
- `exchange-rate-api-key` (#10)
- `token-sign-key` (#12)
- `entra-vid-callback-api-key` (#13)
- `dev-pfx-password` (#14)

**Next:** a dev-ps restart. Then check that a share link opens in the viewer (token key), that a Verified ID Start shows a QR code (callback key), and that the log shows the exchange rates refreshed.

**#15 `dev-seed-password`: not changed on dev-ps, by Stuart's decision** ("I don't want to change anything on the dev-ps based on that"). Terraform shows no difference between `terraform.tfvars` and Key Vault for it.
- **Still open:** the seeded accounts on dev-ps keep the repo-documented dev password. This is the PS-439 concern ("no deployment shares a password with the repository").
- **Not acted on:** recorded so it is not lost.

**#10 `exchange-rate-api-key`: reversed. Stuart rotated it** (a new key is in the store). A targeted apply follows once the store copy is copied into the worktree; dev-ps then needs a restart.

**#11 `platform-k-provisioning-key`: ⏸ deferred.** A Kintsugi admin login was not available just now. **Still live**, with narrow impact: it can only register new organisations on Kintsugi.

**When picked up:**
- **Mint:** a Kintsugi platform admin runs `ssd/dep-ssd-local/commission-provisioning-key.sh --k-url https://kintsugi.secuura.net` (the account is `admin@secuura.com` unless Kintsugi was set up differently).
- **Revoke:** delete the old key on K after the new one shows "accepted".

**#10 `exchange-rate-api-key`: ⏸ deferred** (Stuart, 26 Oct 2026: "Leave exchange rate key"). **Still live.** Low impact if it is ever misused or rotated: a missing or rejected key only stops the display-rate refresh, and stored rates are served instead.

**#8 `stripe-test-secret-key` and #9 `stripe-test-webhook-secret`: ⏸ deferred** (Stuart, 26 Oct 2026: "Leave stripe"). **Both are still live**; rotate them later with an overlap: roll with the old key expiring in 7 days, and roll the webhook signing secret with its 24-hour overlap.

**#5 Apple key: ✅ proven.** Targeted apply of `apple-private-key-base64` and `apple-key-id`, then restart. **Stuart: "Continue with Apple" works.** The old key can be revoked in Apple Developer › Keys.

**#7 `mailgun-key`: ⏳ applied, not yet proven.**
- **Done:** a new dev-ps key (UAT already had its own) went to Key Vault by targeted apply, then restart.
- **Next:** a test email on dev-ps. Once one arrives, the old dev key is deleted in Mailgun.
- **Finding, separate:** a literal Mailgun key is committed in the tracked `ssd/dep-ssd-local/Docker.appsettings.template.json` (`MailGunKey`). It is in git history, so it is public to anyone with repo access, and should be replaced by a placeholder in a small PR.

**#5 Apple key:** the new key and Key ID are in Key Vault (targeted apply). Waiting on the restart and an Apple sign-in test, then the old key gets revoked.

**#6 `azure-openai-key`: ⏸ deferred (Stuart, 26 Oct 2026: "Leave eddie as it will be updated later").**
- **Why it is different:** the `eddi-openai` resource is shared by dev-ps, UAT, production and local stacks, and Azure OpenAI gives a resource only two keys.
- **Until then:** **the exposed key is still live.** Every environment on it moves to the spare key first; only then is the exposed key regenerated.

**#4 `entra-vid-client-secret`: ✅ proven.** Stuart started an Entra Verified ID verification on dev-ps as an account that had not verified before, and a QR code appeared, so Microsoft accepted the new client secret. The old secret can be deleted.

**#5 Apple key:** the new values are in the secrets store; the targeted apply and restart are next.

**Progress (26 Oct 2026)**

| # | Secret | State |
| -- | -- | -- |
| 1 | `ciam-client-secret` | ✅ **Removed.** Deleted at Entra (`ssdobeden` CIAM app) and taken out of `terraform.tfvars`. Nothing on develop reads it. The Key Vault copy goes at the next full apply. |
| 2 | `azuread-workforce-client-secret` | ✅ **Rotated and proven.** New dev-ps secret in the `secpsdev` workforce app; old one deleted. Targeted apply, then restart. **Stuart: "Continue with Microsoft" works.** |
| 3 | `google-client-secret` | ✅ **Rotated and proven.** Targeted apply, then restart. **Stuart: Google sign-in works.** The old Google secret can now be disabled and deleted. |
| 4 | `entra-vid-client-secret` | ⏳ **Rotated, not yet tested.** Targeted apply, then restart. Delete the old secret after a Verified ID Start succeeds. |
| 5 | Apple key (`apple-private-key-base64` + `apple-key-id`) | ▶ **In progress.** |

**How each one was done:** Stuart edits the store copy of `terraform.tfvars` and copies it into the worktree. The session then runs a targeted `terraform apply` of only those Key Vault secrets (each plan showed only `(sensitive value)`), and Stuart runs the restart.

**Restart finding, ticket to follow:** the `secuura-az-dev` systemd service cannot restart dev-ps.
- **Why:** under systemd, `setenv.sh` runs with no Azure login, so it fails at the first secret (`Please run 'az login'`). It has failed every time since 27 Aug.
- **The working restart:** `az vm run-command invoke … --scripts "export HOME=/root; cd /home/ubuntu/secuura-dk && az login --identity --output none && ./start-services.sh"`.
- **dev-ps after the restart:** up, on commit `4fb15e7`, with Google and Apple sign-in enabled.

title: governance GET /api/governance/proposals can still be silently unfiltered or under-validated (KS-1722 gate residue): misspelled filter names are dropped, no upper-case pin, NUL/control characters and unbounded length in proposerId
description:
## BLUF

**The KS-1722 fix (PR #1696, merged as develop** `18ffc05cda55`**) closed the blank and unusable filter values, but the proposals list can still be silently unfiltered or under-validated by four routes.** All four were **measured by the tier-1 gate on PR #1696** (round 1, GO WITH NOTES), not by the filer. They are one logical path, so this is one ticket. **Not fixed in #1696.**

## The four, as the gate measured them

1. **A misspelled filter name is dropped, and the list comes back unfiltered** (gate Minor 1).
   * `?proposerid=`, `?proposer_id=` and `?Status=` each return the **unfiltered** list.
   * So does a real filter that falls past **Express's 1000-parameter cap** on the query string.
   * Why, from the source: `ProposalListQuerySchema` (`services/governance/src/types/governance.types.ts`) is a plain `z.object`, not `.strict()`, so unknown keys are stripped rather than refused. A caller that misspells the filter it relies on gets everyone's proposals — the same trap KS-1722 closed for a blank value.
2. **No cell pins upper case** (gate Minor 2). A case-insensitive status check stayed **green on all 43 cells** of `ks1722-proposals-list-refuses-an-unusable-filter.test.ts`, including S2, the spec/runtime agreement cell. Nothing would catch `?status=ACTIVE` starting to be accepted.
3. **NUL and control characters in** `proposerId` **pass validation** (gate Note 3). The schema requires only a non-whitespace character. The service's existing NUL guard covers request **bodies** only, per the gate; it is `rejectNulBytes()` in governance `index.ts`.
4. `proposerId` **has no length limit** (gate Note 6). A **15 KB** value was accepted.

## Where

* `services/governance/src/types/governance.types.ts` — `ProposalListQuerySchema` and its value lists.
* `services/governance/src/routes/governance.ts` — `GET /proposals`.
* `services/governance/src/governance.openapi.ts` — the published query schema. S2 pins that it accepts exactly what the runtime accepts, so the two must change together. Then regenerate `docs/openapi/secuura-api.yaml`.
* Cells: `services/governance/src/__tests__/ks1722-proposals-list-refuses-an-unusable-filter.test.ts`.

## Fix shapes (none chosen here; the first is a behaviour decision)

* **Unknown keys:** `.strict()` would 400 a misspelled filter. It would also 400 any other extra parameter (a cache-buster, a client's own tag), which is a contract change and should be ruled first. A narrower option is to refuse only near-misses of the three known names.
* **The parameter cap:** whether a request past Express's limit should be refused rather than partly read.
* **Case:** pin the intended policy (lower case only, as today) with a cell: `?status=ACTIVE` → 400, and `?category=GENERAL` → 400.
* **Control characters and length:** add both to the `proposerId` rule (no C0 or DEL characters, plus a maximum matched to the platform's user-id length), in the runtime schema and the spec together.

## Related

* **KS-1722** — the change whose gate found these; it stays In Progress until deployed.
* **KS-1732** — the same route's other open defect: a failed DB read answers 200 \[\].
* **KS-1703** — visibility of proposals across callers; still Kam's ruling, and untouched by any of this.

## Searched first

Exact substring over the title and description of all **702 open** Secuura-PK issues:

* `proposerid` → KS-1722 only.
* `proposer_id=`, `ProposalListQuerySchema`, `misspelled`, `parameterLimit`, `1000-parameter`, `parameter cap`, `unknown query param`, `NUL in a query`, `no max length` → 0 each.
* `governance/proposals` → KS-1732, KS-1722, KS-1719, KS-1703, KS-188 (none of these four items).
* The generic phrasings (`case-insensitive`, `upper case`, `rejectNulBytes`, `control character`, `length limit`, `15 KB`) → other services only (anchoring, mcp-server, auth, the gateway limiter and others).

Control: `GHSA-27r3-jxmh-p828` finds KS-1732, KS-1731 and KS-1729.

## Found by

The tier-1 gate on PR #1696 (round 1: 0 Critical, 0 Major, 2 Minor, 4 Notes; Minors 1-2 and Notes 3 and 6 are recorded here). The verdict is on the coordinator's side at `0_Brain/reference/2026-10-26_gate-pr1696-ks1722/verdict.md`. Filed by Seat K on the coordinator's ruling, facts only.

nodes.body:
**BLUF:** Delivered: PR 1824 merged as 85cd24d81cb9 on develop, deployed to kintsugi at b1fb543640e7 (recorded deploy, 2026-11-01). Verified by code read at b1fb543640e7, not observed live (test cells). Left open: items 1, 3 and 4 are not part of PR 1824.

- **Item 2 is pinned:** `Blockchain/Dev/services/governance/src/__tests__/ks1722-proposals-list-refuses-an-unusable-filter.test.ts` has cells R8 (an upper-case status such as `?status=ACTIVE` answers 400 and never reaches SQL, :263) and controls R9 (an upper-case category answers 400, :270), under the comment at :258. The squash is test-only: no product file.
- **Left open, as the PR's own comment 98882ef7 records it:** item 1 (a misspelled filter name is dropped and the list comes back unfiltered), item 3 (NUL and control characters in `proposerId`) and item 4 (its unbounded length).

**BLUF:** Pull request 1824 (https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/1824) pins item 2 of this ticket and is ready for gate at tier 2 (head 310d26d1e2fc). It refs this ticket and leaves it open; the ticket's other items are not touched.

What changed: test only, zero product bytes. Five cells added to `ks1722-proposals-list-refuses-an-unusable-filter.test.ts`: three refuse an upper-case status, a capitalised status and a list with one capitalised part with a 400 before anything reaches SQL, and two controls refuse an upper-case and a capitalised category. They pin the policy at the tip, that `status` is lower-case only because `PROPOSAL_STATUS_LIST_PATTERN` has no `i` flag. A later change that makes the status filter case-insensitive turns the three status cells red on purpose and must change them in the same pull request. This is a decision pinned, not a claim that case sensitivity is the right policy.

Proof: the file goes from 43 of 43 to 48 of 48 at the untouched product; a one-line tamper adding the `i` flag at `governance.types.ts` line 353 (worktree only, never committed) turned 3 of 48 red and the restored file's sha256 equals the pre-tamper value. Whole governance suite 162 of 162 before, 167 of 167 after.

Not done: whether any external client sends a capitalised status (not measured; this repository's frontends, api-gateway and governance sources contain no caller that sends a status query); the other items of this ticket; the four platform suites, a running stack and Node 24 were not run.

title: governance: a failed database read answers as empty - GET /proposals returns 200 [] and the active-proposal cap fails OPEN (dbGetAllProposals swallows into [])
description:
## BLUF

**In** `services/governance`**, a FAILED database read answers as if the data were empty.** `dbGetAllProposals` catches every error and returns `[]` (`governanceService.ts:254-256`), and nothing above it checks. So:

* `GET /api/governance/proposals` and `GET /api/governance/proposals/active` answer **200 with an empty list** when the database fails. A caller cannot tell "no proposals" from "the read failed".
* **The active-proposal cap fails OPEN.** `createProposal` enforces `maxActiveProposals` by reading active and queued proposals through the same helper (`:495-497`). A failed read returns `[]`, the `>=` check is false, and the cap is not applied.

This is KS-1345's class (webhooks), which does not cover governance. **Not fixed in PR #1696**, which leaves `governanceService.ts` untouched.

## Where (develop `c2505d5c6fe0`; read from source, not run against a database)

`services/governance/src/services/governanceService.ts`:

* `:224-258` `dbGetAllProposals`, with `} catch (err: any) { logger.error('DB get all proposals failed', …); return []; }` at `:254-256`. The error is logged server-side; the caller gets `[]`.
* Its callers:
  * `:605` `getProposals`, used by the route `GET /proposals` (`routes/governance.ts:150`) and `GET /proposals/active` (`:168`). Both answer `200 { success: true, data: [], count: 0 }`, and neither route has an error path.
  * `:495` `createProposal` — the cap check at `:496`: `if (activeProposals.length >= governanceConfig.maxActiveProposals) throw new ConflictError(…)`.
  * `:977` `getGovernanceStats`.
  * `:1013` `processExpiredProposals` — a failed read expires nothing.

## The same shape elsewhere in the file (facts; consequences not traced unless stated)

Every `catch` in `governanceService.ts` that returns a value instead of rethrowing:

| line | helper | returns on failure |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `:218` | `dbGetProposal` | `undefined` (read by callers as "no such proposal") |
| `:254` | `dbGetAllProposals` | `[]` |
| `:264` | `dbGetParticipant` | `undefined` |
| `:274` | `dbGetParticipantByAddress` | `undefined` |
| `:312` | `dbGetAllParticipants` | `[]` |
| `:341` | `dbGetActiveDelegations` | `[]` |
| `:447` | `getTotalVotePower` | `0`, used at `:571` (`submitProposal`) and `:979` |
| `:1025` | `processExpiredProposals` | `0` |

The three save helpers (`:166`, `:186`, `:204`) and `verifyDbReady` (`:365`) rethrow. **What a** `0` **total vote power does to quorum is not traced.**

## Why it matters

* KS-1345 records that this exact shape once hid a real defect for its whole life: a query that always failed and always read as empty.
* Here the same failure can also lift an abuse limit (the cap), not just blank a list.
* Combined with a partial failure, a failed SELECT can disable the cap while the INSERT succeeds. In a full outage the INSERT fails too, at `dbSaveProposal`, which rethrows.

## Fix shape (not chosen here)

KS-1345's shape: let the read reject to the route, so it answers a constant 500 with the error logged server-side. Ruling-sensitive choices for whoever fixes it:

* whether a NOT-FOUND (`undefined`) must stay distinguishable from a FAILED read;
* whether the cap should refuse, rather than allow, when it cannot count.

## Related, NOT duplicates

* **KS-1345** — `GET /api/webhooks` swallows a failed list query into `200 []`. Same class, different service.
* **KS-1722** / PR #1696 — the proposals-list filter. Found while building it, and not touched by it.

## Searched first

Exact substring over the title and description of all **711** Secuura-PK issues, all states:

* `dbGetAllProposals` → KS-1722 only (the filter, not the catch).
* `governanceService.ts` → KS-1722 only.
* `DB get all proposals failed` → 0.
* `swallows a failed` → KS-1657 (originate anchors), KS-1345 (webhooks), KS-888 (`dbSaveApiKey`) — other services.
* `into 200 with an empty` and `return [];` → KS-1345 only.

KS-1345's description names only `routes/webhooks.ts:196` and `:412`. Control: `GHSA-27r3-jxmh-p828` finds KS-1723.

## Found by

Seat K while building KS-1722 (PR #1696), filed facts-only on the coordinator's ruling. Not measured against a running database.

title: Shell suites grade with `printf ... | grep -q` under pipefail: two unrelated suites failed a loaded preflight with "printf: write error: Broken pipe" (150 such lines in 29 files)
description:
## BLUF

Two unrelated shell suites each failed once inside preflight leg 14 of a pre-push, on the same tell, `printf: write error: Broken pipe`, while the machine was heavily loaded. Both grade a result with `printf '%s' "$out" | grep -qF ...` under `set -uo pipefail`. Both passed every time on a quiet machine (15 of 15 runs). **The failure was NOT reproduced under load, so the mechanism below is the explanation that fits, not a proven one.** The same line shape appears at 150 places in 29 files.

## What was seen

Two pushes ran their pre-push hook at the same time on one macOS laptop (12 CPUs). A Docker Desktop VM was at about 920% CPU and the load average read 98 / 100 / 98 at 00:45Z and my later readings of the 1-minute figure were 74 (00:52Z), 58 (01:12Z), 39 (01:13Z) and 6.65 (01:18Z), after Docker Desktop was restarted. Leg 14 took 947 s and 1007 s; the same leg took 553 s on an unloaded run earlier. Each push was a branch off develop `28dac5c12ba5` carrying a two-file change that touches neither suite. Both pushes were refused, `PREFLIGHT FAILED on leg(s) 14 - (13/16 legs ran)`, every other leg passing.

`check_shared_relink.test.sh` (push started 00:47:52Z, `shell suites: 90 passed, 1 failed, 1 skipped (of 92)`):

```
.../scripts/__tests__/check_shared_relink.test.sh: line 49: printf: write error: Broken pipe
  FAIL: F-6 inv: distroless nodejs is DENIED (exit correct, WRONG rule fired — wanted /a JavaScript runtime/)
        ::error::./services/thing/Dockerfile — re-link invariant (KS-921): final stage writes node_modules nowhere — but its base image is `gcr.io/distroless/nodejs22-debian12`, a JavaScript runtime, ...
  111 passed, 1 failed, 0 skipped
```

The captured output printed under the FAIL line contains the wanted text, so the rule fired and the grade was wrong. Line 49 is `if [ -n "$want_out" ] && ! printf '%s' "$out" | grep -qF -- "$want_out"; then`.

`ks1355_slot_blind_launchers.test.sh` (push started 00:49:30Z, `shell suites: 89 passed, 1 failed, 1 skipped (of 91)`):

```
.../scripts/__tests__/ks1355_slot_blind_launchers.test.sh: line 68: printf: write error: Broken pipe
FAIL CONTROL no slot named: the banner shows the historic 6882 and 6881
       want "yes yes"
        got "no yes"
ks1355_slot_blind_launchers: 22 passed, 1 failed
```

Line 68 is the helper `saw() { if printf '%s' "$2" | grep -qF -- "$1"; then echo yes; else echo no; fi; }`.

## Measured on a quiet machine

* `check_shared_relink.test.sh`, 10 consecutive runs, hermetic env (`env -i HOME PATH`), load about 4.5, tree `6bb63146affd` (develop `28dac5c12ba5` plus one two-file branch): **10 of 10 passed, 112 passed / 0 failed, 0 "Broken pipe".**
* `ks1355_slot_blind_launchers.test.sh`, 5 consecutive runs, same env, load 3.5 to 4.9, tree `b5767aa4c527` (tree identical to develop `28dac5c12ba5`): **5 of 5 passed, 23 passed / 0 failed, 0 "Broken pipe".**

## Not measured

The failure was not reproduced under load: no deliberate stress was run (it would have disturbed live pushes), so there is no measured failure rate under load. Only two failures were seen, one per suite, in one window. The mechanism is inferred from the shape: `grep -q` exits at its first match, a `printf` still writing to that pipe gets EPIPE, and `pipefail` turns the pipeline's status into failure, so a MATCH is graded as no match. It is a race between two processes, which fits "only when the machine is slow".

## The census, and its frame

`git grep -n -E 'printf [^|]*\| *grep -q'` at commit `28dac5c12ba5c00d9fc3ad04daee5230eff71619`, pathspecs `Blockchain/Dev/scripts` and `systemTest`, excluding `node_modules`: **150 lines in 29 files** (22 under `__tests__`, 7 product scripts); 26 of the 29 files mention `pipefail`. `check_shared_relink.test.sh` holds 13 of the lines, `ks1355_slot_blind_launchers.test.sh` 1. Not counted: 12 `echo ... | grep -q` lines (the sibling shape); other pipe-to-early-exit-reader shapes (`| head`, `| grep -m1`); any directory outside the two pathspecs. The count says nothing about which of the 150 can actually be hit: it is the number of lines with the shape.

## Siblings

* KS-1716 (In Progress): the same defect class in one script, `systemTest/scripts/check-package-format.sh`, where the large-input case silently dropped a package. Not these suites.
* KS-1149 (Backlog, archived): a different cause of a similar-looking push failure (`rc 141` after the gate PASSED; GitHub closes the idle ssh session). Not this one: here the hook itself refuses with `PREFLIGHT FAILED on leg(s) 14`.

## Searched before filing (board, title and description, archived included)

`check_shared_relink` (KS-956, KS-948, KS-937: the guard itself, not this flake); `ks1355_slot_blind_launchers` (KS-1558: gate follow-ups); `write error: Broken pipe` and `Broken pipe` (KS-1716 only); `grep -q` (KS-1716, KS-1624, KS-1134, KS-998, KS-912, KS-469); `pipefail` (8 hits, none about these suites); `EPIPE` (KS-1716, KS-1598); `SIGPIPE` (KS-1716, KS-1583, KS-1149). The terms `Broken pipe`, `EPIPE` and `SIGPIPE` all find KS-1716, so the search can see this class. No open ticket names either suite as flaking.

## Update 2026-10-26 02:20Z: a third suite, at moderate load, and a measurement that weakens the first explanation

**Third occurrence.** A third push was refused at leg 14 with the same tell. Push of the KS-1513 branch, started 01:53:06Z, ended `rc 1` after 1081 s: `shell suites: 90 passed, 1 failed, 1 skipped (of 92)`, FAILED `preflight_deps.test.sh`, which printed

```
.../scripts/__tests__/preflight_deps.test.sh: line 443: printf: write error: Broken pipe
.../scripts/__tests__/preflight_deps.test.sh: line 444: printf: write error: Broken pipe
FAIL KS-1638: that refusal SHORT-CIRCUITS — a red suite present, still not run
       want "HOOKCTL-REFUSED/1", got "OTHER/1"
preflight_deps: 60 passed, 1 failed
```

Lines 443 and 444 are consecutive `elif printf '%s' "$out" | grep -q '...'` verdict tests; in this cell the text for 443 (`could not derive the pre-push hook's own control`) sits at byte 1871 and the text for 444 (`de-slotted`) at byte 1821 of `$out`, so both match early and both pipelines failed, which sent the cell to the `OTHER` verdict. **This one was NOT in the 60 to 98 load window:** leg 14 took 662 s (against 553 s unloaded), and my readings of the 1-minute load average over the push were between 4.0 and 13.

**Quiet-box runs of this suite:** 6 of 6 passed on that exact tree (`716e26290155`, 61 passed / 0 failed, 0 "Broken pipe"), load about 6.

**What the measurement does to the explanation.** Using the suite's own `PREFLIGHT_FIXTURE_OUT` capture on the failing cell, `$out` is **2848 bytes**, 62 lines. That is far below the macOS pipe buffer (`st_blksize` 16384), so a single `write()` of it cannot meet a closed reader. The "large output, early match" form of the race is therefore NOT what happened here; for it to occur, bash 3.2's `printf` would have to deliver the string to `grep` in several small writes. I tried to reproduce that on the real captured output: 3 runs of 3000 iterations of `set -uo pipefail; printf '%s' "$out" | grep -q "could not derive the pre-push hook's own control"`, load about 8 to 10, **0 of 9000 reported no-match.** Not reproduced.

**Tally of pushes of mine that reached leg 14 since 00:43Z:** 6; refused by this tell: 3 (the KS-1391 and KS-1560 first attempts, and the KS-1513 push above); passed: 3 (the KS-1560 and KS-1391 second attempts, and KS-1289). A seventh push, KS-1716, ran no preflight leg. The refused ones were three different suites. So the suites are sometimes fragile on this machine under contention from several simultaneous preflights; the mechanism is unproven.

title: packages/shared wallet-signature.test.ts: the only positive cell fails on develop - verifyMessageSignature returns false for a valid CIP-8 signature
description:

```
AssertionError: expected false to be true // Object.is equality
 ❯ src/__tests__/wallet-signature.test.ts:49:63
    expect(verifyMessageSignature(ADDR, MSG, signature, key)).toBe(true);
```

`verifyMessageSignature` (`packages/shared/src/cardano/wallet.ts:352`) returns `false` for the signature the test builds with its own `makeWalletSignature(MSG)`.

**Why the other cells do not cover it:** this is the file's only positive cell. The other four all expect `false`: a different message, a tampered signature, the wrong public key, and malformed or empty inputs. * A branch merged with develop `28dac5c12ba5`, where neither file differs from develop: red again.

The detached `/sign-wallet` route (KS-278) runs `const signatureValid = verifyMessageSignature(walletAddress, …)`. **Not measured:** whether that route refuses genuine wallet signatures at runtime. nodes.body:
**Cause filed as KS-1739** — Node 26.0.0's semver-major `Readable.read()` change (`fadb214d95` / PR 60441) truncates every synchronous `cbor.encode()` to its first byte, which is why the COSEKey reaching `extractPublicKeyFromCOSEKey` is the 1-byte `a4`.

That ticket carries the remedy options (no choice made), this ticket as the first known symptom, and KS 1734 / KS 1729 / KS 1625 as related-but-not-investigated. **Nothing here is fixable in `wallet.ts` or in this test — both are correct** — so this ticket's state is left as it is and no code was changed.

Relation `related` created in both directions. Evidence unchanged: `5_Project_History/2026-10-26_seatV-2nd/`.

**Root cause established. It is the runtime, not the verifier and not the test — and it is an intentional Node 26 breaking change, so it will not be fixed by a Node patch. No code change proposed; no PR.**

## Which exit fires
Reproduced at develop `5f689991861b` on Node **v26.8.1**, the one file alone: **1 failed / 4 passed (5)**, 6.24 s. The verifier names its own exit in the run's stdout, so no instrumentation of `wallet.ts` was needed:

```
warn: CIP-8: failed to extract Ed25519 public key from COSEKey
```

That is `wallet.ts:372` — the **first** exit. Control flow never reaches the Sig_structure re-encode (`:397`), the SPKI import (`:405`) or `crypto.verify` (`:411`).

## Why key extraction fails
`extractPublicKeyFromCOSEKey` throws inside its own `try` and returns null. The input is bad before it ever gets there: the test's `coseKeyHex()` calls `cbor.encode(map)` and **gets back one byte**.

| value encoded | `cbor.encode` returned | correct |
|---|---|---|
| `Map{1:1,3:-8,-1:6,-2:<32B>}` (the COSEKey) | `a4` (1 B) | ~45 B |
| `Map{1:-8}` (protectedHeaders) | `a1` (1 B) | `a10127` |
| `['Signature1',…]` (Sig_structure) | `84` (1 B) | ~90 B |
| `'Signature1'` | `6a` (1 B) | `6a5369676e617475726531` |
| `Buffer.alloc(4,0xab)` | `44` (1 B) | `44abababab` |

`a4` is the CBOR "map of 4 pairs" header with its contents missing, so `decodeFirstSync` throws **`Insufficient data`**. Not Map-specific: **every** value whose encoding exceeds one byte is truncated to its first byte. `7` and `Map{}` survive only because they are one byte already — which is why four cells pass: all four assert `false`, and a verifier that always returns false satisfies them.

## The layer
`cbor`'s synchronous encode is `encoder.js:595-602`:

```js
_encodeAll(objs) { const bs = new NoFilter({…}); this.pipe(bs); … this.end(); return bs.read() }
```

`NoFilter.read(size)` (`nofilter/lib/index.js:285`) just delegates to `super.read(size)`. With 4 bytes written as 3 chunks, `nofilter` holds all of them — `length` 4, `slice()` and `toString('hex')` both `83010203` — but **`read()` returns `83`**. `cbor.encodeAsync` is correct (`83010203`): it does not use that path. The **decoder is healthy** (`decodeFirstSync('83010203')` → `[1,2,3]`).

## It is Node, proven with zero dependencies and a second runtime
Pure `stream.PassThrough`, no packages involved:

| | Node v26.8.1 | Node v24.22.1 |
|---|---|---|
| 3 chunks, `read()` | **`83`** | `83010203` |
| 3 chunks + `end()`, `read()` | **`83`** | `83010203` |
| 1 chunk of 4 B, `read()` *(control)* | `83010203` | `83010203` |
| `read(4)` explicit size | `83010203` | `83010203` |

The control discriminates, and successive `read()` calls on Node 26 hand back `83`,`01`,`0203` in order — the bytes are all present, just no longer concatenated.

Same `cbor@9.0.2` **bytes from the same disk**, the whole CIP-8 chain, only the runtime differing:

| | Node v26.8.1 | Node v24.22.1 |
|---|---|---|
| protectedHeaders / Sig_structure / COSEKey / COSESign1 | 1 / 1 / 1 / 1 B | 3 / 90 / 42 / 145 B |
| positive cell | `EXIT wallet.ts:372` — *Insufficient data* | **`RETURNS TRUE` (`wallet.ts:418`)** |
| negative cell (different message) | `EXIT wallet.ts:372` | `EXIT wallet.ts:391` (payload mismatch) |

On Node 24 the positive cell passes **and** the negative cell fails for the right reason, so the KS 278 payload binding is intact.

## It is deliberate upstream, not a bug awaiting a fix
Node commit `fadb214d95` / PR #60441 ("stream: readable read one buffer at a time"), listed as **semver-major in the v26.0.0 changelog** (2026-05-05): buffer merging was removed on purpose to save CPU, so each queued chunk returns on its own. `read(readableLength)` is the documented approximation — verified here on Node 26: `read()` → `83`, `read(p.readableLength)` → `83010203`. *(Commit/PR identified from the Node changelog via web search; not read at source.)*

Consequence: `cbor@9.0.2` relies on a contract Node 26 removed. **`cbor@10.0.12` is identical** — measured against an on-disk copy, all four cases truncated. So **the open dependabot PR 635 (`cbor` 9.0.2 → 10.0.12) does not fix this.**

## Scope — the live route is NOT affected
- The only synchronous `cbor.encode` in tracked production source is **`wallet.ts:397`** (the Sig_structure rebuild). The other five occurrences are inside this test file. Two `decodeFirstSync` sites, both on the healthy decoder.
- **All 32 Dockerfiles pin `node:24-alpine`** (75 `FROM` lines, no exceptions), `originate` included — the service hosting `/sign-wallet`. Node 24 verifies TRUE, so the deployed route does not carry this defect. **No deployed route was called.**
- A real wallet supplies a properly-encoded COSEKey, so on a Node 26 host the failure would move past key extraction to `:397` and surface as `Ed25519 signature verification failed`. It **fails closed** — valid signatures rejected, never invalid ones accepted. Not a forgery surface.

## Searched before filing
`cbor.encode`, `nofilter`, `Readable.read`, `_encodeAll`, `encodeAsync`, `readableHighWaterMark` — **0 hits each** (titles + descriptions, archived included). `verifyMessageSignature` → 2 hits: this ticket and KS 1229 (Done). The root cause is tracked nowhere.

Possibly the same cause, not investigated here: KS 1734 (`services/security`, 11 of 33 test files fail on first run) and KS 1729 both record Node v26. KS 1625 is the standing contradiction that lets this happen — root `engines.node` is `>=18.0.0`, which permits Node 26, while every image ships Node 24; `packages/shared` declares no `engines` at all.

## UNMEASURED
- Whether the cell ever passed on this host, and when it began failing — develop history was not bisected.
- Whether `cbor` or `nofilter` upstream has a fix or an open issue for Node ≥26.
- Whether the transitive `cbor` consumers (`services/anchoring`, `services/nft-certificate`, `frontend/issuer` lockfiles, `@meshsdk/provider`) call the synchronous encode internally — not traced; they are not direct call sites in tracked source.
- Whether other packages on this laptop depend on the same removed `read()` contract. The three `node:24-alpine` leg runs were in throwaway containers from an image already present; nothing was installed, downloaded or built.
- The repo-wide blast radius of Node 26 beyond CBOR.

Evidence (8 probes, 19 output files): `5_Project_History/2026-10-26_seatV-2nd/`.

Correction to the description's "on the Studio": every run cited here was on Kam's laptop, host `Kamils-MBP.localdomain` (MacBook Pro, `Mac14,5`), under Node `v26.8.1` (`/opt/homebrew/Cellar/node/26.8.1`). The description is left as written.

**One fact not in the description: the runtime.** Every run that reproduced this cell on this host was on **Node v26.8.1**. The host is `Kamils-MBP` ("Kamil's MacBook Pro"). The only Node installs here are Homebrew `node` and `node@26`, so **it has not been measured on Node 24**, the LTS line the repo's runtime rule names. Recorded because the verifier is crypto code, and a runtime difference is a candidate the description does not yet rule in or out. Not interpreted further.

Also red, same assertion (`wallet-signature.test.ts:49`), in Seat K's own clone on 2026-10-26: develop `1ae6f17d19a8` before any edit, and PR #1691's head `8cc4ec4c2190` (which merges develop `28dac5c12ba5`). That is 4 runs, before and after the KS-1723 lock refresh.

title: Request-body arrays are uncapped: a JSON array of failing elements costs time and memory linearly (1 MB -> 524,288 issues, 338 ms, +165 MB), and two 10 MB JSON limits multiply it
description:
## BLUF

A request body that is one large JSON array whose elements all fail validation makes `z.array(...)` build one issue object per element, with no cap, so the cost grows linearly with the body and is paid on the event loop. Measured on the zod 3.25.76 v3 entry that product code uses: 1 MB -> 524,288 issues, 338 ms blocked, +165 MB heap. Two JSON limits are 10 MB. Of 237 `z.array(` call sites, at most 232 show no length bound. This is the exposure-bounding work behind the 14-day baseline row for GHSA-mrhx-c7xc-m3w5 (KS-1723, Kam's card `secuura-ks1723-zod-msal-high-baseline-1026`, ruled a on 2026-10-26 09:55:48 AEDT); it does not clear that advisory.

## Measured

`z.array(z.string())` validating a JSON array of numbers (every element fails), `JSON.parse` then `safeParse`, one throwaway node process per case, `--expose-gc --max-old-space-size=1536`, one run each. Synthetic worst case, no concurrency.

| body | elements | issues | time blocked | heap delta | max RSS |
| -- | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- |
| 100 KB (express default) | 51,200 | 51,200 | 41 ms | +22 MB | 86 MB |
| 1 MB (gateway, mcp-server) | 524,288 | 524,288 | 338 ms | +165 MB | 274 MB |
| 10 MB (auth service, gateway uploads) | 5,242,880 | 5,242,880 | 4.5 s | +1,382 MB | 1,620 MB |

For comparison the v4 code that ships inside zod 3.25.76 (`zod/v4`; the advisory's class; an old unpatched copy): 100 KB +45 MB; 1 MB +438 MB heap, max RSS 550 MB; 10 MB aborted (rc 134) at the 1.5 GB heap cap. zod 4.6.5 and 4.6.7 were not tested.

## Where the limits are

* `Blockchain/Dev/services/api-gateway/src/index.ts:402`: `express.json({ limit: '1mb' })`.
* `index.ts:406`: `uploadBodyParser = express.json({ limit: '10mb' })`, mounted at `:407` (`/api/documents/upload`) and `:408` (`/api/nft/upload`).
* `Blockchain/Dev/services/auth/src/index.ts:85`: `express.json({ limit: '10mb' })`.
* `Blockchain/Dev/services/mcp-server/src/http-server.ts:29`: `express.json({ limit: '1mb' })`.
* 40 `express.json(` sites in services and packages; 12 name a limit; the rest take express's default of 100 KB.

## Sites (an upper bound)

Tracked product files under `services/*`, `packages/*`, `frontend/*`, excluding tests, `node_modules`, `dist`, `vendor`:

* `z.array(`: 237 lines in 46 files. 5 show a numeric `.max()` or `.length()` on the same line; 232 do not (multi-line chains are not resolved, so 232 is an upper bound).
* `.parse(req.body…)` / `.safeParse(req.body…)`: 118 sites.
* Unbounded, schema line -> parse line, read: `services/originate/src/routes/webhooks.ts:132` -> `:280`; `services/auth/src/routes/oauth.ts:1181` and `:1189` -> `:1201`; `oauth.ts:1301` -> `:1309`; `services/tokenisation/src/index.ts:54` -> `:62`.
* Bounded, for contrast: `services/referral/src/routes/rewards.ts:20` (`.max(50)`), `services/tokenisation/src/index.ts:89` (`.max(500)`), `services/security/src/index.ts:1605` (`.max(1000)`).

## Not measured

Whether each unbounded route is authenticated; behaviour under concurrent requests; the memory limits of the deployed containers; a request through the real gateway; zod 4.x numbers.

## Searched before filing

The board (title and description, archived included), by symbol and string, never by my own phrasing: `z.array(` (4 hits: KS-1696, KS-1600, KS-1514, KS-1210, each a different bug that contains the string), `uploadBodyParser` 0, `limit: '10mb'` 0, `express.json` (6 hits, none about a size cap), `handleArrayResult` 0, `zod 4` 0, `zod@4` 0, `zod v4` 0, `msal-node 7` 0, `@azure/identity` (1: KS-1379, lock re-resolution), `GHSA-mrhx-c7xc-m3w5` and `GHSA-xcx6-jx8p-x3h5` (KS-1723 only). Control: `GHSA-w9m9-85wc-3x92` returns KS-749, so the search can see an id. Filed new.

title: systemTest/schemathesis: test_symlinked_venv_is_refused_not_looped fails on Linux, because sys.executable keeps the symlink path and the KS-738 loop it asserts never occurs
description:
## BLUF

`tests/unit/runner/test_prevenv_bootstrap.py::TestReexecBehavesAsAProcess::test_symlinked_venv_is_refused_not_looped` fails on Linux at `origin/develop` `1ae6f17d19a8`. It expects exit 1 and the *"refusing to loop (KS-738)"* line; the script exits 0.

## Seen

Found during [KS-1719](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1719) (PR #1687), 2026-10-26. Python 3.14.9 linux/arm64 (official `python:3.14` image), `tests/unit` with `-n 4 --no-cov`:

* `origin/develop`: **1 failed, 4343 passed, 2 skipped**. This is the one failure.
* After PR #1687: 1 failed, 4359 passed, 2 skipped. The same single failure.
* Assertion: `AssertionError: expected the loop guard's exit 1, got 0` (`assert result.returncode == 1`).
* `scripts/venv_reexec.py:30-37` states the case the guard covers: with `<root>/venv` a symlink, *"CPython sets* `sys.executable` *to the RESOLVED target"*, so the venv-membership test never becomes true and the old prelude re-exec'd forever.
* Measured on Linux: a symlink `/tmp/x/python3` → `/usr/local/bin/python3.14`, run as `/tmp/x/python3 -c "import sys; print(sys.executable)"`, prints `/tmp/x/python3`, not the resolved target. No resolved-target path means no loop for the guard to refuse.

## Searched

Secuura-PK, all states, title and description: `test_symlinked_venv_is_refused_not_looped`: 0 hits. Control: `_free_active_proposal_slot` returned KS-1719, so the search can fire.

## Not established

* That the test passes on macOS. Not run there: the host Python was 3.14.7 when this was measured, below the suite's pin, so pytest exits before collecting.
* The experiment symlinked the interpreter *file*. The test stages a symlinked venv *directory* (`_stage_tree(tmp_path, venv="symlink")`). The same CPython behaviour is inferred for the directory case, not measured.
* Which hosts run `tests/unit` on Linux today. Not checked.

nodes.body:

It closes the first line under "Not established" (that the test passes on macOS), for that one machine. The other two stay open: the experiment symlinked the interpreter file, not the venv directory the test stages, and which hosts run `tests/unit` on Linux today has not been checked.
