Kam's card `secuura-ks2083-session-end-race-in-flight-1107` = a, "Merge with the wording corrected, and ticket the race High (recommended)", ruled 2026-11-08 at 20:32:11 +11:00. Evidence class: MEASURED AT RUNTIME, real route, real `authenticate()`, real session code, on a stand-in store; there is no Redis on the host. No state, assignee or priority of this ticket was changed.

**What gate 245 measured (PR 2075, KS-2083, head d2245bf37fe0):** deterministic, twice: PATCH role 200, role written, gateway check true, auth check true. The old token then raised a second account (200, the peer is ORG_ADMIN), and a following PATCH status suspended answered 200 with the session still active. Rates at 1 ms store latency, 20 rounds each, two runs: no traffic 0 and 0 (control); one client serial 2 and 5; one request every 50 ms 1 and 6; a burst of 40 in 40 ms 20 and 20; latency 0: 0 and 0. On develop, with status suspended and no PR: 0, 4, 4, 20, 0, the same race, so it is old behaviour (this ticket's description already says it affects every revoke path).

**Where (gate 245's tree):** `Blockchain/Dev/services/auth/src/services/session.ts` line 286 (read then write, not atomic), reached on every request from `Blockchain/Dev/services/auth/src/middleware/authenticate.ts` line 160; line 313 of the session file is the revoke it races. This ticket's description cites lines 270 to 294 of an earlier tree.

**Fix shape (gate 245, read only as to the fix):** make the activity write unable to resurrect a revoked record, for example an atomic check inside the store. Regression test the owner should add: a revoke between that read and that write, then assert both checks still say gone.

**Not measured:** real Redis, whose latency sets the real rate; the rates above belong to the stand-in's latency model, while the existence of the race does not. **For PR 2075:** its sentence "it closes the walk-around" is true for a serial request only; the seat raising that PR is correcting the wording.

**Source:** gate 245 verdict, finding F1 on PR 2075, `/Volumes/DevMASTER/WEDNESDAY/0_Brain/reference/2026-11-07_gate245-tier1-y-auth/verdict.md`. This seat re-read the verdict and ran nothing else.

title: auth: the OAuth refresh_token grant never checks the ORIGIN SESSION, so a revoked session's refresh token still redeems and mints a brand-new session (oauth.ts:988-1089)
description:
## BLUF

`POST /api/oauth/token` **with** `grant_type=refresh_token` **never reads** `decoded.sessionId`**, so revoking a user's sessions does not reach the OAuth refresh path.** A refresh token issued before a revocation still redeems, and mints a *brand-new* session. Measured by the gate on PR #1655 (KS-1407): after `revokeAllUserSessions` (n=1, `getSession` null), the same refresh token redeemed **200**, then **200 again**, leaving the account with **2 live sessions**.

Pre-existing; **outside** that PR's diff. Filed from gate BO1's note N1.

## Recommendation

Check the origin session on this grant (or introduce a per-user credential epoch) before minting. The oracle is already in the repo: the *interactive* `POST /api/auth/refresh` does a server-side session lookup at `routes/auth.ts:688-689`, so the two refresh paths disagree about whether a session must still exist. Wednesday or Kam should rule whether the fix rides with a KS-1407 follow-up or stands alone.

## Where

`services/auth/src/routes/oauth.ts:988-1089` — the `grant_type=refresh_token` branch. It verifies the JWT, checks the jti denylist, pins `user.status === 'ACTIVE'` at `:1067`, and mints a new session at `:1078`. It never consults the session named by the token it is redeeming.

## The measurement (gate BO1, probe C1)

Real `session.ts`, real `refreshDenylist.ts`, real `jwt.ts`, on the ks823 scaffold:

1. created a session and minted an OAuth pair bound to public client `pub-1`;
2. ran `revokeAllUserSessions` — returned n=1, and `getSession` then returned null;
3. redeemed the same refresh token: **200**. Redeemed again: **200**. Account left with **2 live sessions**.

* **Control in the same case:** a client-mismatch redeem was refused **400**, so the harness can produce a refusal.
* **Not run:** an authorization code issued before a revocation and exchanged after it. The code grant also mints a fresh session (`:969`), so it is plausibly a smaller sibling — unmeasured, stated as such.

## Consequence

Anyone holding an OAuth grant obtained before a password change, a password reset, an admin status change or a user erasure keeps a renewable foothold. It is the direct counterexample to KS-1407's premise that no session may outlive the password that minted it.

## Scope — what this ticket is NOT

**KS-1150 R-2 already covers the rotation/denylist half of this branch** ("the refresh grant does not rotate / denylist the presented token", `:836`/`:860`) and is still OPEN — its 2026-09-14 comment records R-1 landing as `b42e260c9897` with "R-2 / R-3 stay OPEN". **This ticket is the other half: the missing ORIGIN-SESSION check.** They are overlapping-but-distinct, not duplicates — a perfectly rotating implementation would still mint a new session for an account whose sessions were all revoked, because nothing reads `decoded.sessionId`. Do not close either as a duplicate of the other.

**Board search before filing:** `revokeAllUserSessions`, `updateSessionActivity`, `rotateSessionRefreshToken`, `decoded.sessionId`, "oauth refresh token revoked session", "session revoked refresh token still redeems". Nearest neighbours KS-1150 (the rotation half, above), KS-756 (the opaque session refresh handle, a different mechanism), KS-1280 (a revoked session's Bearer forwarded by originate, a different service). **Controls both ways:** a freshly generated token that was never published returned **0** hits, and `revokeAllUserSessions` returned **1** — so the search discriminates.

Related KS-1407, KS-1150.

nodes.body:
## Gate BS1 confirms this ticket's scoping, with TWO CONDITIONS

Gate BS1 (Opus, tier 1) reviewed the scoping of this ticket against KS-1150 R-2 while gating PR #1655, and **confirmed it is correct** — the origin-session half here, the rotation/denylist half on KS-1150. Verdict `0_Brain/reference/2026-10-20_gate-BS1-pr1655-ks1407-r2/verdict.md` (`sed '1d;$d' | shasum -a 256` = `8480cd2c56ef`, equal to its own trailer).

**Its two conditions, verbatim from the verdict (lines 136-137):**

> - (a) It must fail closed on a refresh token with no or unknown `sessionId`, or a legacy token walks around it.
> - (b) It does not cover the authorization-code sibling, which BO1 flagged as not run: a code issued before the change and exchanged after it mints a fresh session at `:969` with no origin session to check. That needs either a credential epoch or code invalidation, and it should be named in KS-1690 or KS-1692 rather than left implicit.

## What that adds to the work here
1. **The check must FAIL CLOSED.** A refresh token carrying no `sessionId`, or one naming a session that cannot be found, must be **refused** — not admitted on the grounds that there is nothing to check. Otherwise every token minted before the fix walks straight around it, which would make the fix cosmetic for exactly the population it exists to stop.
2. **The authorization-code sibling is NOT covered by this ticket and is named here, as the gate asked.** A code issued *before* a password change and exchanged *after* it mints a fresh session at `oauth.ts:969` with no origin session to consult. The gate's shape for it is a **credential epoch** or **code invalidation**. It is recorded rather than left implicit; whoever takes this ticket should decide whether to widen it or split that off.

Context: KS-1407's fix merged as `86df4f5a52cc`, so the premise "no session may outlive the password that minted it" is now true for the interactive paths and still false for this one.

title: Security: POST /api/documents/:id/version has NO per-document access check on its source - any write-role caller in the tenant can derive a new version from another organisation's document (the sibling of the certify path KS-1557/#1619 closed)
description:
## BLUF

`POST /api/documents/:id/version` **checks a ROLE, a SCOPE and the TENANT, and nothing about the caller's relationship to the source document.** Any write-role caller in the tenant can derive a new version from **another organisation's** document, and the derived row is a real child of it. This is the sibling of the path KS-1557 / pull request #1619 closed on `POST /api/certifications/issue`: the same defect class, the same service, still open on the versioning route. Measured on a scratch stack at develop `89956fe92956`. Facts only — no fix is proposed here.

## Where

`services/originate/src/routes/documents.ts`, the `'/:id/version'` handler:

* `:2219` — `const ALLOWED_VERSION_ROLES = DOCUMENT_WRITE_ROLES;`
* `:2246` — `isAllowedByRoleOrScope(req, ALLOWED_VERSION_ROLES, 'documents:write')` — role or scope only.
* `:2281` — `const source = await getDocument(id, tenantId, (req as any).db);` followed by a 404 when it does not resolve, and a `metadata.documentType` guard. **There is no owner / recipient / creating-connector test anywhere in the handler** — the check `callerMayCertifyDocument` applies on the certify path (`routes/certifications.ts:119-128`, call sites `:223` legacy and `:441` lineage) has no counterpart here.

## Measured (scratch Postgres 15 at migration 054, real `documents` + `certifications` routers, `secuura_app`, both `MULTI_TENANCY_ENABLED=false` and `=true` — identical results in both)

| cell | what was done | result |
| -- | -- | -- |
| G1 | **a FOREIGN organisation's connector** calls `/version` on organisation A's document | **201.** The minted row is a real child: its `parent_document_id` resolves to A's document. |
| G1 (same cell) | **the discriminating control** — that **same caller**, on that **same document**, through `POST /api/certifications/issue` with `parentDocumentId` | **403** `FORBIDDEN` |
| G2 | an **interactive write-role USER of another organisation** calls `/version` on A's document | **201** |
| G3 | **the bound** — a caller in **another tenant** calls `/version` on A's document | **404** `NOT_FOUND "Document not found in this tenant"` |

G1's two halves are the finding in one line: **the two sibling routes disagree about the same caller on the same document.** G3 bounds it — it does not cross the tenant, because `getDocument` is tenant-scoped.

## Board search before filing (symbol and path, each with a control)

* `callerMayCertifyDocument` → **2** hits (KS-1557, KS-1679); `isAllowedByRoleOrScope` → **2** (KS-1202, KS-1433). Both controls fire, so the instrument discriminates rather than returning everything.
* `ALLOWED_VERSION_ROLES`, `/:id/version`, `documents/:id/version`, `parent_document_id` → each returns the 12-hit fuzzy cap, and **none of the hits names this defect.** The nearest four, each a different thing: **KS-1538** (the legacy certify path — fixed), **KS-1557** (the lineage certify path — this route's sibling), **KS-1508** (`versionedById` is server-set — same route, different defect), **KS-1228** (a refused request still writes an `action_provenance` row — same route, different defect).
* **0 open hits for the source-access check itself.**

## Sequencing — this matters before anyone gates this route

The KS-1557 fix (shape (a′): `/version` records the creating connector on the document it mints, under the action value `create:connector`) **must land before any source-access gate is added here.** Otherwise a gate written with the same predicate would refuse `/version` on a version-minted document for exactly the reason certify refuses it today: a `/version`-created document has no creation provenance row of its own, so `wasCreatedByConnector` is false for the connector that actually made it. Measured on demo: **31 of 31** `/version`-minted documents have no such row.

## Open question, UNMEASURABLE from this project

**Does Platform S ever version a document it did not itself originate?** It decides the client-visible risk of closing this gap — if S does, closing it turns some S calls into 403. It cannot be answered from here: `Secuura/platform-s` returns 404 to this project's PAT (which sees exactly one repository), so no search of S's code is possible from Platform K's identity. **Stated as a question, not an assumption, and not asked of anyone here.**

## Not claimed

* No severity judgement beyond the priority on this ticket, and no fix design.
* The derived row carries the **caller's own** `newContentHash`, so this is not an alteration of the source document's bytes; the source gains a child it did not consent to, and the derived row presents as part of its lineage.
* Not measured: whether any such cross-organisation version exists in live data.

Found by Seat C 31st while measuring KS-1557 (Stuart's comment `16e8498d`) at develop `89956fe92956`, 2026-10-20.

nodes.body: @kamil.kreiser — your 00:13 note lists "whether Platform S ever versions a document it did not originate" as unmeasurable from your side: it is answered in my comment above (19 Oct 23:36 UTC). Short form: **no** — S versions only documents its own originate (or its own earlier `/version`) returned the id for, always under the owning organisation's connector key; the one edge is an S organisation merge (PS-492), which re-homes a document to the surviving organisation's key. So closing step 2 costs S nothing provided (a) the lineage-root / `create:connector` sequencing you describe holds, and (b) the merge edge is handled one of the two ways named there. Re-confirmed at S develop `61bdbd3`, 20 Oct.

## BLUF — measured interaction with the KS-1557 fix, and why this ticket's fix must come SECOND
The KS-1557 fix (a `create:connector` provenance row recorded for the connector that mints a document) **widens what the unauthorised versioner can do to the child it minted** — though it gives that caller **no new reach into the original document**. Measured by gate BN1 on a real Postgres, in both tenancy modes, on the develop arm and at the landing. Facts only; the policy question is not settled here.

## The chain, as measured
1. **User A** creates document **D** (`owner_user_id` = A's user).
2. **Org B's connector** calls `POST /api/documents/D/version` and gets **201 on both arms** — that is this ticket's defect, unchanged by KS-1557. The 201 body already echoes **A's title** on both arms.
3. The minted child **C** (whose `owner_user_id` is **A's user**, inherited from the source) now carries `create:connector` = **B's connector**.
4. **B certifies C:** lineage path **403 → 201**, legacy path **403 → 201**. The legacy path also moves the A-owned child C from `status: draft` to `certified` (on develop it stays `draft`).
5. **B reads C:** `GET /api/documents/C` **404 → 200**, and the body carries **A's data**.
6. **Reach into A's ORIGINAL D — unchanged:** B `GET D` is **404 on both arms**; B certify D is **403 on both arms**. D gains a child at step 2 on **both** arms, which is this ticket's pre-existing effect and not the KS-1557 fix's.

**So:** the fix gives B more over the row **B itself minted** (an A-owned row), and nothing more over **D**. Refusals on a version-minted document are unchanged on both arms for every other principal measured — a foreign connector, another organisation's user, a same-organisation non-owner, a same-organisation *other* connector and an unrelated recipient are all 403/403. A **human** of org B who versions gets no row and stays 403/403. Only the minter moves 403 → 201. (A recipient whose email is in the source's `recipientEmail`, which `/version` copies into the child, is 201/201 on both arms — pre-existing and unchanged.)

## Why this matters for the ORDER of the two fixes
The KS-1557 fix must land **first**, and a source-access gate on `/version` must come **after** it. If a gate were added here using the same predicate the certify path uses, it would refuse `/version` on a **version-minted** document for exactly the reason certify refused it before KS-1557: such a document had no creation provenance row of its own, so `wasCreatedByConnector` is false even for the connector that made it. Measured read-only on demo 2026-10-20: **31 of 31** version-minted documents had no such row before the backfill.

## What this does NOT establish
- **Whether step 2 should be refused at all** is the open question on this ticket, and it is not answered by the above.
- **Whether Platform S ever versions a document it did not originate** remains UNMEASURABLE from this project: `Secuura/platform-s` is 404 to this project's PAT. It decides the client-visible cost of closing step 2.
- Not measured on kintsugi.

Recorded here by Seat C 31st from gate BN1's note N1 on pull request #1654, 2026-10-20. The same point is carried as one line in that pull request's Known residue.

@kamil.kreiser — answering the open question from S's code at develop `355e6e6` (20 Oct), with the one edge that matters stated plainly.

**In the normal case, no: S only ever versions documents it originated itself, under the same organisation's key.** `CardanoAnchorService.PerVerb.cs`:
- `/version` is called for exactly two verbs, `watermark` and `sign-cert` (`VersionThenAnchorAsync`), always on `parentKId = doc.PlatformKTipDocId ?? doc.PlatformKRootDocId` — ids S only ever holds because its **own** originate or its own earlier `/version` returned them (`AnchorResultApplier`, `PerVerb.cs:204-205`). S has no other way to learn a K document id, so it cannot address another connector's or user's document.
- Every such call, and the anchor kick that follows it (`POST /{newId}/anchor`), is signed with **the document's owning organisation's connector key** — `OwnerOrgId(doc)` = `DocumentStore.OrganisationId`, the organisation that originated the document on K — plus `onBehalfOf` for the acting person. A recipient in another organisation who signs a shared document (PS-1126's grant) still produces a `/version` under the **owner's** key, never the recipient's. A cross-organisation rights-assign on S changes the holder, not the owning organisation, so the key is unchanged after a custody transfer too.
- **But the chain matters for your predicate:** S's second `/version` (sign-cert) is addressed to the document the first `/version` (watermark) minted. So the "document's own side" must be judged by the lineage root's creating connector, or `/version` must write the `create:connector` provenance you name under shape (a′) — exactly the KS-1557 sequencing you state. Gate this route with the per-document provenance arm as it stands today and **every S sign-cert after a watermark is refused**, the same shape as the certify regression measured on 19 Oct.

**The one edge where S versions under a different key than the originating one: an S organisation merge.** `OrganisationMergeService` (PS-492, an Administrator's tool) re-homes a dissolving organisation's documents to the surviving organisation (`doc.OrganisationId = targetOrganisationId`), and the dissolving organisation's K key is then erased through KS-695. Any later watermark or sign on those documents is signed with the **surviving** organisation's key, against a K document whose issuer organisation and creating connector are the dissolved one's. Under a strict "own side only" rule those calls would answer 403 and fall to S's flat anchor. S has no call that tells K about the merge today. Two ways to keep it working: K accepts the surviving organisation when the originating connector's organisation has been erased, or S gains a "transfer issuer" call to make before it versions — say which you prefer and S will file its half; it is rare (single-person organisation consolidation) and nothing in S's suite exercises it against K.

Everything else S sends with `/{id}` — share, transfer-custody, revoke, lifecycle-events, certify — follows the same rule: S's own K ids only, the owner organisation's key only. Nothing deployed on S since dev-ps `b7d414b`.

title: Make UAT a production replica for staging: its develop template diverges from production on DeployMode, RequireAdminMfa, DevTools, mail allow-list, anchoring keys and MySQL
description:
## Context

Ruled 2026-10-20: development and test happen on dev-ps; **UAT is staging, a replica of production** used for production-readiness testing before a release; production deploys only after that pass. UAT is behind `develop` today and is to be brought up to date shortly.

For UAT to be that replica, its configuration has to match production's except where a difference is deliberate and written down. On `develop` (`355e6e6`) the two tracked templates differ on these keys (names only, no values read beyond tracked placeholders and flags):

| Key | `dep-aws-uat` | `dep-aws-secuura` (production) |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `AppSpecific:DeployMode` | `dev` | `live` |
| `AppSpecific:RequireAdminMfa` | `false` ([PS-438](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-438/uat-admin-mfa-is-not-enforced-deploymodedev-leaves-requireadminmfa-at), 12 Aug) | not stated (live enforces anyway) |
| `AppSpecific:ShowDevTools` | `true` | `false` |
| `AppSpecific:ValidEmailDomains` | an allow-list, with `EmailOverride` to a UAT trap | empty (filtering off) |
| `CardanoAnchor:AnchorIdentity` | `false` | not stated |
| `CardanoAnchor:UsePerVerbEndpoints` | `true` | not stated |
| MySQL image (`docker-compose.yml`) | `mysql:8.4` | `mysql:8.0` |

The MySQL pin was ruled not a work item on 2026-09-02 (recorded on [PS-819](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-819/production-cannot-boot-or-sign-in-on-develop-sso-secrets-and-config)). Under the staging rule, though, production would come up on 8.0 while UAT tests on 8.4, so that ruling needs revisiting here.

## What to decide, key by key

For each row: does UAT move to production's value, does production move to UAT's, or is the difference kept deliberately, with the reason written in both templates' comments?

Two have known consequences:

* `DeployMode`: `dev` is what makes the seed accounts and their known password exist, and systemTest's `check:stack` requires it. A `live` UAT means randomly generated passwords and no suite run against UAT, which it is not used for anyway.
* `RequireAdminMfa`: [PS-438](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-438/uat-admin-mfa-is-not-enforced-deploymodedev-leaves-requireadminmfa-at) turned it off because systemTest cannot answer a TOTP challenge. [PS-581](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-581/give-systemtest-a-totp-path-so-the-second-factor-is-testable-at-all) wanted it stated `true`. On a production replica it should match production, which enforces.

## Done when

* Every row above is resolved in the templates (`dep-aws-uat`, `dep-aws-secuura`), and each deliberate difference carries a comment saying why.
* A contract test in `tests/ssd.UnitTests` compares the two templates and fails on an undeclared divergence, so the replica cannot drift silently.
* `CLAUDE.md` *Environment topology* drops its "divergence has to be resolved" sentence.
* UAT is redeployed from `develop` and `/Health/Data` on UAT reports the expected build commit.

No secret value appears anywhere in this work: key names and store paths only.

title: prism GET /api/credentials/:id returns any stored prism credential by id with no owner check (cluster-internal; not routed by the gateway)
description:
## BLUF

**prism has its own** `GET /api/credentials/:id` **that returns any stored prism credential by id, with no owner check.** It reads prism's own table (`svc_prism_credentials`), not vc-issuer's, and it is reachable only from inside the cluster: the gateway does not route `/api/credentials` to prism. KS-1116 bound vc-issuer's route of the same name; this one is untouched. Gate BH1 NOTE 6 on #1648 (census side-finding).

## What was measured (develop `c66b834ed451`, `services/prism/src/index.ts`)

* `:690` `app.get('/api/credentials/:id', …)` → `dbGetCredential(req.params.id)` (`:231`): `SELECT * FROM svc_prism_credentials WHERE id = $1`. The handler returns the credential or 404. There is no read of `req.user`, and no owner or tenant condition.
* Siblings on the same table, not examined for this ticket: `GET /api/credentials/subject/:did` (`:707`), `POST /api/credentials/revoke` (`:814`).
* Reachability: the gateway proxies only `^/api/did` to prism (`services/api-gateway/src/routes/proxy.ts:920`; control: the same search finds 6 vcIssuer mounts). `docker-compose.yml` has prism's host port commented out ("Was: - "6001:4001""). So a caller needs to be inside the cluster network, and must still pass prism's own bearer check on `/api`.

## Provenance

Gate BH1 (Opus, tier 1) on #1648, NOTE 6, 2026-10-20; re-read at develop `c66b834ed451` by Seat C 30th. Board search first: `svc_prism_credentials`, `dbGetCredential`, `prism/src/index.ts:690`, `prism GET /api/credentials` → 0 each (control: a never-written token → 0; `generateAccessToken` → 2).

title: Every API key without a connector id is the same principal (connector:api-key) within its tenant, so under KS-1116 those keys read each other's presentations and credentials
description:
## BLUF

**Every API key minted without a connector id authenticates as the SAME principal within its tenant,** `connector:api-key`**. Under KS-1116's "owner = the principal that created it", those keys therefore read each other's presentations and credentials.** Cross-tenant stays separated, because a key's tenant is fixed at mint. The shape predates KS-1116; KS-1116 is what makes the principal an ownership boundary. Gate BH1 NOTE 3 on #1648.

## What was measured (develop `c66b834ed451`)

* `services/auth/src/services/jwt.ts:289`, in `generateConnectorToken` (the sk\_-key → JWT exchange the gateway performs for an `x-api-key` caller): `userId: \`connector:${meta.connectorId || 'api-key'}\`\`. A key with no connector id gets the literal fallback.
* `services/security/src/index.ts:445-448`: `tenant_id` is written on every key INSERT and is immutable per key ("a key minted for tenant A never moves to tenant B"). So the collapse is per tenant, not global.
* vc-issuer (since #1648) stamps `created_by_user_id` from `req.user.userId` and compares it on read (`services/vc-issuer/src/ownership.ts`). It has no special case for the fallback: `git grep "api-key"` over `services/vc-issuer/src` → 0 files.
* **Precedent in the codebase:** originate already refuses the fallback principal for erase-connector — `isFallbackConnectorId` (`services/originate/src/services/connectorOrganisationErasure.ts:114`, used at `:146` and `:295`; KS-695, wording residue in KS-1579). There the fallback is treated as "not a distinct principal". vc-issuer treats it as one.
* Related, not this defect: KS-869 (merged) made a key's connector id persist across restarts. It does not change what a key minted WITHOUT one becomes.

## Open question

What should "the principal that created it" mean for a key with no connector id: the key itself (its key id), the fallback shared by every such key in the tenant (today), or not a principal at all (originate's erase-connector stance)?

## Provenance

Gate BH1 (Opus, tier 1) on #1648, NOTE 3, 2026-10-20; re-read at develop `c66b834ed451` by Seat C 30th. Board search first: `connector:api-key` → KS-869, KS-1579; `generateConnectorToken` → KS-1584, KS-1409, KS-1152; none owns the shared-principal question.

nodes.body:
**BLUF:** The sentence in this ticket's description, "Cross-tenant stays separated, because a key's tenant is fixed at mint", is true for vc-issuer, the service this ticket measures. It is not true for services whose notification stores key on the user id alone: there, every API key without a connector id is one principal across tenants. Two tickets record it, both measured by our QA gates.

* KS-2122 (High): the gateway's notification routes. Gate 246 measured, through the real `authenticateToken` with the security service's answer stubbed to a null connector id, that tenant B's key listed and deleted a notification row that tenant A's key had placed in that inbox. MEASURED AT RUNTIME by the gate.
* KS-2119 (Medium): the transfer service's `GET /api/notifications`. Gate 240 measured, in its cell O7, that a no-id key of tenant B read the reject notification of a transfer that a key had opened. MEASURED by the gate.

What this changes here: nothing in this ticket's own measurements for vc-issuer. The open question above (the key itself, the shared fallback, or no principal) also decides those two routes; KS-2119's comment records that a fix of that shared root would close both reads.

Not claimed: whether any live key without a connector id exists, or whether anyone reads those inboxes (UNMEASURED, and stated so in both tickets).

title: vc-issuer: after a revoke, the credential's creator can be refused GET /api/credentials/:id on the memory fallback - revoke() stores the row with no owner entry (fails closed)
description:
## BLUF

**After** `POST /api/credentials/:id/revoke`**, the credential's own creator can be refused** `GET /api/credentials/:id` **(404) whenever vc-issuer then falls back to memory.** `revoke()` writes the row into the in-memory store with no owner entry, so the KS-1116 bound reads it as owner-less. This fails CLOSED: a foreign caller is refused too, so the cost is availability, never a leak. Gate BH1 NOTE 2 on #1648.

## What was measured (develop `c66b834ed451`, `services/vc-issuer/src/repositories/credentialRepo.ts`)

* `revoke()` (`:288`) reads the row with `getById(id)` (`:292`) — from the database when it is available — and then calls `memoryStore.set(credential.id, revokedCredential)` (`:306`). It writes **no** `memoryOwners` entry.
* `getRecordById()` takes the owner from `memoryOwners.get(id) ?? OWNERLESS` on the memory path. So for any row this process did not itself `store()` or boot-load — one created on another replica, or after this process booted — and then revoked here, the memory copy is OWNERLESS.
* `mayRead()` refuses an OWNERLESS row under the interim reading (`ownerlessRowReadable()` returns false). With the database unavailable, or the SELECT throwing, the creator gets the unknown-id 404. Gate BH1 measured exactly that: its Q1 cell, "Alice 404".
* The foreign-caller half is pinned by cell Q1 in `ks1116-presentation-and-credential-reads-bound-to-the-creator.test.ts` (test-only follow-up to #1648). The creator's 404 is deliberately NOT asserted there, so that this ticket's fix does not have to edit a cell.

## Shape of a fix (not decided)

`revoke()` carries the owner it read — `getRecordById` instead of `getById`, writing `memoryOwners` alongside `memoryStore` — and a cell pins that the creator still reads her revoked credential on the memory path.

## Provenance

Gate BH1 (Opus, tier 1) on #1648, NOTE 2, 2026-10-20; re-read at develop `c66b834ed451` by Seat C 30th. Board search first: `memoryOwners`, `revoke() puts`, `Map-miss` → 0; `credentialRepo.revoke` → KS-1352 only, which is revoked-credential verification, a different defect.

title: Five tracked files cite DEPLOY-BLOCKERS.md as a repo document, including two product-code comments deferring a correctness condition to it, but the file is not in the repo
description:
## BLUF

**Five tracked files at** `develop` **cite** `DEPLOY-BLOCKERS.md` **as though it were a repo document. It is not in the repo, has never been in the repo, and two of the five citations are product-code comments that defer a correctness condition to it.** The file is real, but it lives in the coordinator's own notes outside this repository, so nobody working from a clone can open the authority those comments point at.

Measured at `develop` `292fe0b1642a`:

* `git ls-tree -r --name-only` returns **4,604** entries, of which **0** match `blocker` in any case. Control on the same listing: `DEV-PROCESS` matches **1**, so the zero is a real absence and not a broken instrument.
* `git log --all --diff-filter=ADR -- '*DEPLOY-BLOCKERS*'` is empty: it was never added and never deleted.
* Not under `2_Project_Files`, not elsewhere in the project folder.

## Recommendation

Pick one of two, then make the five citations consistent with it:

1. **Add an in-repo deploy-preconditions document** that the product-code comments can cite, leaving the coordinator's file as the working copy; or
2. **Keep the authority outside the repo and change the five citations to say so** — name it as an external document rather than a path a reader will look for in the tree.

**Do not copy the coordinator's file into the repo** as-is; which of the two above applies is a maintainer call, not an agent one. Nothing is blocked today: Seat D 22nd's deploy brief named the file by its absolute path and that seat worked from it.

## Detail

### The five citations at `develop` 292fe0b1642a

| File | Line | What it defers to the missing document |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `Blockchain/Dev/services/originate/src/routes/metering.ts` | 73 | *"DEPLOY-BLOCKERS step (3) asserts* `data.tenantId` *equals Platform S's key tenant"* |
| `Blockchain/Dev/services/originate/src/routes/metering.ts` | 77 | *"That is a DEPLOY gate, not a merge gate, and it is on DEPLOY-BLOCKERS.md"* |
| `Blockchain/Dev/services/originate/src/__tests__/ks1032-unconfigured-vouch-fails-closed.test.ts` | 24 | *"deploy condition lives in DEPLOY-BLOCKERS.md; it is not a condition on this code"* |
| `Blockchain/Dev/services/originate/src/__tests__/ks1041-gateway-provenance.test.ts` | 213 | *"the risk it named is real and is handled as a DEPLOY gate in DEPLOY-BLOCKERS.md"* |
| `Blockchain/Dev/docs/ENVIRONMENT-VARIABLES.md` | 120 | *"DEPLOY-BLOCKERS step (3) asserts* `data.tenantId` *equals Platform S's key tenant"* |
| `Blockchain/Dev/docs/DEV-PROCESS.md` | 255 | *"*`DEPLOY-BLOCKERS.md` *row 7 condition … is closed"* |

### Pre-existing, not introduced by the docs refresh

At the base of PR #1625 (`4a065fb7535`) **four** of those files already carried the citation (`ENVIRONMENT-VARIABLES.md`, both tests, `metering.ts`). PR #1625 added the fifth file (`DEV-PROCESS.md:255`). So this is a repo defect that the docs refresh widened by one, not a defect of that PR, and it is filed separately for that reason.

### Why it is worth fixing rather than tolerating

`metering.ts:73-77` is product code stating that a correctness property — the metering response's `data.tenantId` equalling Platform S's key tenant — is *not* checked at merge time because a deploy gate covers it. A reader auditing that code cannot reach the gate to confirm it says so, or that it is still current. Separately, that step-3 detector was independently measured **vacuous on kintsugi** during the 2026-10-19/20 deploy census (`DEFAULT_TENANT_ID` equals the tenant of all 14 `svc_api_keys` rows with `MULTI_TENANCY_ENABLED=false`, so the assertion passes whether the vouch works or not) — which is exactly the kind of thing an unreachable gate document lets persist.

### Board search before filing

`searchIssues` is fuzzy here and returns its 40-hit cap for every term, so absence was established with exact substring filters instead:

* `title contains "DEPLOY-BLOCKERS"` → **0** issues.
* `description contains "DEPLOY-BLOCKERS"` → **2** (KS-1594, KS-1582), both of which *cite* the file as the home of a deploy condition rather than owning this defect.
* Positive control: `description contains "admin_organisation_scopes"` → **3** issues (KS-1601, KS-1592, KS-1585), so the filter does match when there is something to match.
* Negative control: a freshly generated random token, deliberately not written into any ticket → **0** hits.

*Filed by the Platform K agent (Seat C 29th) during the KS-1668 review of PR #1625. Facts only; no code or document was changed by this ticket.*

title: m365 admin setup wizard sends a Secuura tenant id as organizationId - after KS-1673 the tenant choice is ignored
description:
**BLUF:** The admin M365 setup wizard sends a **Secuura tenant id** in the `organizationId` field — or the literal `'default'` when no tenant is selected. Since KS-1673 (merged 2026-10-20, #1633), the m365 service takes the organisation from the caller's login token and **ignores** that field. So the tenant a system admin picks in the wizard no longer decides anything: the connection, or the Teams webhook, lands in the admin's **own** organisation.

**Read statically at develop** `9207fe336797`**. Not driven.**

## What the wizard sends

| line | call | sent |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `frontend/admin/src/components/M365SetupWizard.tsx:94`, `:98` | `POST /api/m365/connections/init` | `organizationId: selectedTenantId \|\| 'default'` |
| `M365SetupWizard.tsx:171` | `POST /api/teams/webhook-config` | `organizationId: selectedTenantId \|\| 'default'` |

* `selectedTenantId` comes from `useTenantStore` (`M365SetupWizard.tsx:84`).
* The store is filled only for `super_admin` / `system_admin` / `SYSTEM_ADMIN` (`frontend/admin/src/components/Layout.tsx:107-112`, via `fetchTenants()`).
* Its values are **tenant** ids. A login token's `organizationId` is an **organisation** id. These are two different id spaces.

## What happens now (after KS-1673)

* **The field is stripped and ignored** on both calls. A system admin's new connection is owned by the admin's own organisation, whichever tenant the wizard shows as selected.
* **A token with no organisation gets 403** from both calls.
* **Tenant admins**, who previously got 400 because `'default'` failed the old UUID check, now succeed under their own organisation.
* **Rows written before KS-1673** carry a tenant id in `organization_id`. They now match no token, so they are owned by nobody. **Re-connecting is the remedy** (ruled 2026-10-20). Read-only measurement on 2026-10-19 found **0** connections and **0** Teams webhooks on kintsugi and on demo.

## Open question — not decided here

Whether a system admin may set up Microsoft 365 **on behalf of a customer organisation** is a product decision. It has gone to Kamil. Until it is ruled, the fail-closed behaviour above stands, consistent with KS-1673's no-bypass ruling. **No fix is proposed in this ticket.**

## How it was found

Gate AS1's note N1 on #1633 (KS-1673 PR A). Both frontend facts were re-read at develop by Seat R 56th before filing. Five Linear searches found no existing ticket: "M365SetupWizard", "m365 setup wizard organizationId", "wizard tenant id organizationId", "selectedTenantId m365", "m365 wizard default organization". The control search returned KS-1677. KS-1490 names the same file only because of a stale host URL.

**Measured by the security review of KS-1673 part B (gate AX1, 2026-10-20), on a real database engine and on mocks: what the rightful owner sees for a Teams webhook row the wizard wrote.**

| action by the owner (org A) | result |
| -- | -- |
| list | only A's own webhooks; the wizard's rows (no organisation, or `'default'`) are absent |
| notify | sent to A's own channels only; nothing to the wizard's rows |
| delete a wizard row by id | **200 `{"success":true}`, and the row stays active** |
| A's own webhook end to end: register → list → notify → delete → list | 201 / listed / sent / 200 / gone — the owner's own path works |

**Fail-closed: yes.** A wizard-written row is never listed, never notified, and cannot be deleted by anyone through the API — only directly in the database. Nothing is sent into a channel nobody can see.

**The usability problem this ticket should cover.** An operator who re-runs the wizard after deploy sees a success message — the wizard's "N Teams webhook(s) configured" counter is a count in the browser, not read back from the server — for a webhook that is then invisible and cannot be deleted. The review suggests three things:
- **(a)** stop the wizard sending `organizationId` at all — it is ignored now (`M365SetupWizard.tsx:171`);
- **(b)** decide between re-registering and a database backfill for any existing rows. Read-only measurement on 2026-10-19 found 0 on kintsugi and 0 on demo; the review did not re-check the data;
- **(c)** consider a delete that says whether anything was actually removed.

**Worth knowing:** a signed login token whose organisation is the literal text `'default'` would **own** the wizard's `'default'` rows. That is reachable only through a signed token, so it is not an attack. But it is why "goes dark" is not quite "unreachable".

title: m365: the OAuth callback lets any holder of a connection id rebind it - pending or already connected - state is the bare connection id, bound to no session (RFC 6749 10.12)
description:
> **Corrected 2026-10-20 (Seat R 56th).** This ticket first said only a **pending** connection was at risk. That was wrong: the callback has no status check, and the security review of #1633 rebound an **already-connected** connection. The title and this BLUF now say so. The original BLUF is kept below the line.

**BLUF:** The Microsoft 365 sign-in callback **trusts whoever completes it**, for **any** connection — **pending or already connected**. The OAuth `state` value it receives is simply the connection's own id, and nothing ties that value to the person who started the sign-in, or checks the connection's status. So anyone who holds a connection's id can finish the sign-in with a code from **their own** Microsoft account: the connection then holds their Microsoft tokens, and its organisation lists and syncs their content as if it were its own. A garbage code flips the connection to `error` instead. **Measured** by the security review of #1633 (see the 2026-10-20 comment).

**Read statically. Not driven live.** Read at develop `88b8ceb9f3041672d9575b40c09869d45ab1c111`, `services/m365-integration/src/index.ts`.

## What the code does

| line | what it does |
| -- | -- |
| `:1051` / `:1066` | `buildAuthorizationUrl` sets the OAuth `state` to `connection.id`. The state **is** the resource id. |
| `:543`–`:544` | `GET /api/callback` reads `state` and looks the connection up by that value **alone**: `memConnections.get(String(state))`. |
| `:553` | it exchanges whatever `code` arrived (`exchangeAuthCode(String(code), …)`) and, from `:555`, stores the resulting access and refresh tokens **on that connection**. |
| `:547`, `:577` | the connection id is written to the log, in the not-found line and the completed line. |

There is **no nonce**, **no PKCE** and **no check against the user or session that started the sign-in**. A search of `services/m365-integration/src` for `code_challenge`, `code_verifier`, `pkce` and `nonce` finds **0** occurrences. The same search for `state` finds 5, so the search does find what it looks for. Measured at #1633's head, which adds none of the four.

`GET /api/callback` cannot simply require our login. Microsoft's redirect does not carry it, which is why the route is unauthenticated and why the organisation binding in KS-1673 does not reach it.

## Class

OAuth `state` / login cross-site request forgery: **RFC 6749 §10.12**. The `state` value is meant to bind a callback to the user agent and session that started the request. Here it identifies a resource instead.

## Reach, bounded

* The connection id is `conn_<randomUUID>`, so it **cannot be guessed**.
* **KS-1673 PR A (#1633)** closes the routes that let any authenticated user **enumerate** connection ids. Before it, `GET /api/sites` and `GET /api/connections/:id` exposed them across organisations.
* A pending id is returned only to the user who started it (the `POST /api/connections/init` response). It also travels inside the authorization URL to Microsoft, and it is logged at `:547` and `:577`.
* **So once #1633 is merged, exploiting this needs a pending id to leak** — for example through a log, a referrer or a shared URL.
* Not measured on any deployed environment. KS-1673's read-only measurement found **0** connections on kintsugi and demo, so nothing is exposed today.

## What this ticket is not

* **Not KS-1673.** KS-1673 is about which organisation owns a connection. This is about whether the sign-in callback is bound to the session that started it. Different root cause, different fix, different tests.
* **No fix is proposed here.** The shape — a random per-sign-in `state` stored server-side, PKCE, or both — is a later decision.

## How it was found

Seat R 56th, 2026-10-20, reading the callback for the KS-1671 `code`-seam follow-up. Four Linear searches found no existing ticket:

* "m365 callback state"
* "OAuth state nonce"
* "callback connection id state"
* "m365 oauth csrf"

The control search ("m365 no connection is bound to its organisation") does return KS-1673, so the search can find what it looks for. The nearest existing ticket is **KS-1670**, which is about reflection — an unencoded connection id in the success redirect — not binding.

---

*Original BLUF, as first filed:*

**BLUF:** The Microsoft 365 sign-in callback **trusts whoever completes it**. The OAuth `state` value it receives is simply the connection's own id, and nothing ties that value to the person who started the sign-in. So anyone who holds the id of a **pending** connection could finish it with a sign-in code from **their own** Microsoft account. The connection would then hold their Microsoft tokens, and its organisation would list and sync their content as if it were its own.
