**⚠ Deploy precondition (Kam's, not code).** The Entra app must have this redirect URI registered: **the host the admin wizard is actually served from on that deployment**, followed by `/api/m365/callback`.
- On the Container Apps template, that is the default admin host (`https://<prefix>-admin.<env domain>/api/m365/callback`).
- **If a custom admin domain is bound** (`deployment/azure/configure-domain.sh` binds `admin.secuura.io`), users must reach the admin portal at the host named in `ENTRA_REDIRECT_URI`. Otherwise, that deployment must set `ENTRA_REDIRECT_URI`, and its Entra registration, to its custom admin host. The sign-in cookie only reaches the callback if both are the same host. (Gate BI1, note NB3.)
- On a VM, `ENTRA_REDIRECT_URI` must be the box's own public host. Kintsugi still redirects to `localhost:6882`; that is KS-1381.

**For the deploy round:**
- Migration **053** (`svc_m365_oauth_states`). The migrations image must be rebuilt; then check that the table exists on the schema itself.
- Rebuild m365-integration and api-gateway (its startup migrations changed).
- Sign-ins pending at deploy time are refused, and the user starts again.

**Residue for the next R seat: ONE test-only follow-up, not started** (gate BI1 notes NB1, NB2 and NB4):
- **NB1:** the PKCE verifier's secrecy has no test of its own. A verifier equal to the state, or derived from the connection id, passes every test. Two tests would close it:
  - none of the values a caller can see may hash to the challenge;
  - the verifier must be random across two sign-ins for the same connection.
- **NB2:** the bicep check matches the template's text. It does not evaluate the template, so an inverted `empty(apiPublicUrl)` condition survives.
- **NB4:** a stale line citation in `encryptedField.ts:61` (it should point to `tokenCrypto.ts:28`).

Low impact: the client is confidential, so redeeming a code still needs the client secret.

**BLUF: PR #1647, round 2, is pushed for a delta gate. ⚠ Deploy precondition: before Microsoft 365 sign-in can work on any Container Apps deployment, the admin host's `/api/m365/callback` must be registered as a redirect URI on the Entra app.** That registration is Kam's change. It is not in this PR.

**Why the redirect moved (the gate's first blocker).** The admin wizard starts the sign-in from the admin host, so the browser keeps the sign-in's cookie for the admin host only. The Container Apps template sent Microsoft back to the API host instead, and there the cookie would never arrive, so every real sign-in would have been refused. The redirect now uses the admin host, in `services.bicep` and `env.dev.json`. Admin nginx already forwards `/api/`.

**Kintsugi and demo** serve the portal and the API from one host each, so they are not affected by that split. Kintsugi does have Entra credentials, but its redirect URI is still the compose default `localhost:6882`, so sign-in there is broken with or without this PR. That is KS-1381's open item. On a VM, the redirect URI must be the box's own public address, registered the same way.

**Also in round 2:**
- Two PKCE checks: two sign-ins never share a verifier, and the verifier really reaches Microsoft's library.
- With the database up, the in-memory copy is never used as a fallback.
- The cookie is its own secret, never the state.
- Four stale references are updated.

Every one of 18 compile-safe deliberate breakages is caught by a test.

**BLUF: PR #1647 builds the fix for this ticket, and it is READY FOR GATE (tier 1). Not merged, not deployed.**

https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/1647

**One OpenAPI operation is removed: `POST /api/m365/connections/complete`.** Nothing called it, and it exchanged a raw code with no state and no status check, so it would have bypassed this fix. The Schemathesis and Akto collections will move. The spec goes from 311 to 310 paths.

**What changed.** The sign-in `state` is no longer the connection's id. Each sign-in gets an opaque single-use state, a browser-binding cookie and a PKCE verifier. Only the hashes of the state and the cookie are stored, and the verifier is encrypted.

The callback consumes the record keyed by **both** hashes in one statement. A caller without the cookie therefore cannot spend a real user's state; that is the lesson recorded on KS-819. The callback then refuses:
- an expired state;
- a connection that is no longer pending;
- an organisation mismatch.

Every refusal changes nothing, exchanges no code and returns one identical redirect. That also closes the "known id vs unknown id" difference.

**Measured, not assumed:**
- **The binding cookie survives the real path.** Measured live on a local stack: nginx, then the gateway, then m365, on a cross-site top-level redirect. A control with the cookies cleared read nothing.
- **Red-first:** develop fails 20 of the new route cells: 16 in the main suite and 4 in the no-database suite. All pass with the change.
- **Mutants:** 13 of the 13 compile-safe ones are killed, each type-checked on its own.

**For the deploy round:**
- New table `svc_m365_oauth_states`, via **migration 053**, plus the same create in the docker init scripts, the Azure init script and the gateway's startup migrations.
- **The migrations image must be rebuilt.** Check that the table exists on the schema itself; do not trust the runner's summary.
- Sign-ins pending at deploy time will be refused, and the user simply starts again. Kintsugi and demo hold no connections today.

**Separate, not in this PR:** KS-1682, a second route to the cross-organisation harm (refresh-token selection).

**BLUF: the security review on #1633 MEASURED this, and it is wider than this ticket says. Any connection can be taken over, not only a pending one. Priority stays Medium for now, because the id still has to leak first. Pre-existing, and unchanged by #1633.**

**Correction to my own description above.** It says "the id of a **pending** connection". That is wrong. The callback never checks the connection's status: it looks the connection up by `state` and overwrites its tokens whatever the status is. So an **already-connected** connection can be rebound. I wrote "pending" from what the OAuth flow is meant to do, not from the code.

**Measured by gate AS1** (adversarial review of #1633, 2026-10-20, Microsoft's sign-in library mocked, anonymous requests):

| cell | anonymous request | result |
| -- | -- | -- |
| C1 | `?code=evil&state=<A's connection id>`, the library returning the attacker's tokens | 302 `m365=success … tenant=ATTACKER-DISPLAY`. A's **next OneDrive call went out with the attacker's token**: A's organisation now reads the attacker's Microsoft account as its own. |
| C2 | the same with a garbage code | A's connection flips to `status: 'error'`. A's next `POST /api/sites` answers 400 "Invalid or disconnected connection". |

**Existence oracle.** The redirect `Location` for a **known** connection id differs from the one for an unknown id (`message=connection_not_found`). So this unauthenticated route also reveals whether a given id exists.

**On the code before #1633**, C1 and C2 behave identically. #1633 neither causes nor fixes this. What #1633 did change: it closed `GET /api/sites`, the route that disclosed connection ids across organisations. The review found **no** remaining cross-organisation route that discloses a connection id (`conn_<uuidv4>`). So reaching this still needs a leaked id.

**The review's own words on the design:** a connection id is still a bearer capability here, and calling the callback "unbound by design" is too strong. It could be bound with a single-use `state` value stored at init. That is the review's suggestion, recorded as such. **The fix shape remains a later ruling.**

title: m365: connections probably never persist or reload - svc_m365_connections is fail-closed RLS, read as secuura_app with no tenant GUC, and the save error is swallowed
description:
**BLUF:** m365-integration probably **never saves a Microsoft 365 connection to the database, and never reloads one**, and it does so without any visible error. Its table is under fail-closed row-level security. The service reads and writes it as a role without bypass, and never sets the tenant setting the policy checks. Every save fails and is swallowed as a single warning, and every reload returns nothing. So a connection lives only in the memory of the process that created it, and is lost on restart.

**The policy also matches on** `tenant_id`**, which for this table holds the Microsoft (Entra) directory id, not the Secuura tenant.** So even a correctly set tenant would never match a row.

Found while measuring KS-1673. **This ticket rests on reading the source plus two measured flags. Nothing was driven.** By Wednesday's ruling, nothing more was measured on any box for it.

## Facts

| fact | where |
| -- | -- |
| `svc_m365_connections` is in the consolidated tenant-policy table set | `migrations/038_rls_consolidate_policy.sql:42` |
| 038 creates `tenant_isolation`, `USING` / `WITH CHECK` on `tenant_id::text = current_setting('app.current_tenant_id', true)` (fail-open when unset) | `038:84-93` |
| 039 re-declares it **fail-closed** on the 038 table set (an unset setting admits nothing) | `migrations/039_rls_fail_closed.sql:2-8` |
| **Measured on both kintsugi and demo** (flags only): RLS enabled = t, forced = t, 1 policy | read-only count pass, 2026-10-19 |
| **Measured on both boxes:** m365's database role is `secuura_app`, `rolsuper` = f, `rolbypassrls` = f | same pass |
| m365 never sets the tenant setting: **0** hits for `app.current_tenant_id`, `set_config`, `tenant_scope_bypass` or `withTenant` in `services/m365-integration/src/` | develop `390cc0a317c9` |
| `dbSaveConnection` catches every error and logs one warn (`'DB save connection failed'`) | `services/m365-integration/src/index.ts:189` |
| `svc_m365_connections.tenant_id` holds the **Entra directory id**, not the Secuura tenant UUID | repo `BACKLOG.md` (an existing entry), and the connection's `tenantId` field |
| `svc_m365_connections` has **0 rows** on both boxes | same pass. Consistent with "never saves", but also consistent with nobody having connected, so it **does not prove it** |

**Compare:** `svc_teams_webhooks` has row-level security **disabled**, with 0 policies (measured on both boxes). The two m365 tables are inconsistent with each other. The Teams side has the cross-organisation exposure tracked in KS-1673.

## Not measured

* Whether an INSERT as `secuura_app` with no setting is actually refused on these boxes. This is a static reading of 039's intent; the flags are measured.
* The service log's count of `'DB save connection failed'` lines. I measured nothing more on the boxes, by ruling.

## Why it matters

* **Correctness:** M365 connections cannot survive a restart.
* **Interaction with KS-1673:** the connections that matter are the in-memory ones, so binding in-memory connections to an organisation is the whole fix there. A future fix to this ticket must keep that binding when rows start reloading. The `organization_id` column is already written and read.

## Searched before filing

"svc_m365_connections RLS", "m365 loadFromDb connections reload", "svc_teams_webhooks row level security", "secuura_app m365 FORCE". The negative control `qzxwvkplmrty` returned 0. KS-1673, KS-1670, KS-693, KS-1335 and KS-934 were read; none owns this.

nodes.body:
**BLUF: two readings of this ticket's premise disagree, and both are recorded here, not adjudicated. The code says `svc_m365_connections` is excluded from the fail-closed change. The measured flags on the boxes fit that reading AND this ticket's.**

**Reading 1 — the migrations (gate AS1 on #1633, re-read at develop `9207fe336797`).** `migrations/039_rls_fail_closed.sql` **excludes** `svc_m365_connections` from the fail-closed flip, in so many words:
- `:20-24`: "svc_m365_connections — its tenant_id column stores the MICROSOFT/ENTRA directory id … not the Secuura tenant UUID, so the GUC comparison can never match. Flipping it would break the M365 integration outright. Tracked as a follow-up data-model fix on KS-458."
- `:79`: "Fail-closed flip (038 set MINUS platform_document_registry + svc_m365_connections)".

So by the code, the table keeps 038's **fail-open** policy, where an unset tenant setting admits every row, and `loadFromDb` would re-warm connections after a restart. The review adds that `svc_sharepoint_sites` and `svc_synced_documents` are in neither 038 nor 039. It did not measure a live database.

**Reading 2 — this ticket.** It rests on `039:2-8` re-declaring the policy fail-closed "on the 038 table set". It also rests on a measurement on both kintsugi and demo: RLS enabled = t, forced = t, 1 policy, as `secuura_app` with `rolbypassrls` = f.

**What each instrument can and cannot tell.** The measured flags are enabled, forced and a policy count. They are the **same for a fail-open policy as for a fail-closed one**. What separates the two is the policy's `USING` expression, which was not read on either box. So the box measurement does not contradict reading 1, and the code does not contradict the flags. The disagreement is in this ticket's inference that 039 made the table fail-closed, and `039:79` says otherwise.

**Why it matters now.** Since #1633, sites and documents prove ownership through the in-memory connection map. An owner whose connection is in the database but not in memory sees its own sites and documents as not found. The review measured that state, and judged it **not** the normal state after a restart on one replica, by reading 1. It is reachable when the service runs on more than one replica.

**Not decided here.** Settling it needs a read of the policy's `USING` clause on a box, or a restart test. Neither was run tonight.

title: m365: no connection is bound to its organisation - any authenticated user can list every site's connectionId, then list and download another org's OneDrive files
description:
**BLUF:** In m365-integration, **nothing ties a Microsoft 365 connection to the organisation that owns it.** Any authenticated user, from any tenant, can do three things:

* list every registered SharePoint site **together with its** `connectionId` (`GET /api/sites`);
* use that id to list the files in **another organisation's OneDrive**, with that organisation's own access token (`GET /api/onedrive/files`);
* **download** one of those files into the synced-document store (`POST /api/onedrive/files/:id/sync`).

`POST /api/connections/init` takes the organisation from the **request body**, not from the caller's token. **Measured statically. Not driven live.** It only works where `ENTRA_*` is configured and a real connection exists. That is unmeasured for any deployed environment, and KS-693 shows a normal dev machine answers 503.

Found from gate AP1's note N5 on #1627 (KS-1671). Read by Seat R 55th at develop `a66cd6a4d1726794c816fd4fefec58c728d410e5` (`services/m365-integration/src/index.ts`).

## The chain

| step | route | what it does | org check |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| 1 | `GET /api/sites` (`:890-903`) | with no `connectionId` query, returns **every** entry of `memSites`; each `SharePointSite` carries `connectionId` (`:104-113`) | **none** |
| 2 | `GET /api/onedrive/files` (`:1082-1110`) | `memConnections.get(String(connectionId))` (`:1087`), then lists Graph `/me/drive/...` with `connection.accessToken` (`:1091-1093`) | **none** |
| 3 | `POST /api/onedrive/files/:id/sync` (`:1121`) | same lookup by id alone, then fetches the item's metadata **and** `/content` from Graph with that token | **none** |
| — | `GET /api/connections/:id` (`:722-743`) | returns `organizationId`, `tenantName`, `status` and `scopes` for any id | **none** |
| — | `POST /api/connections/init` (`:612-640`) | `organizationId` comes from `initConnectionSchema.parse(req.body)` (`z.string().uuid()`), not from the token | **none** |

`connectionId` is `conn_<randomUUID>` (`:616`), so it cannot be guessed. **Step 1 is what makes it enumerable**, as soon as any site has been registered on that connection.

## What I read to answer "does any middleware bind the connection to the caller's org?"

* **api-gateway** `routes/proxy.ts:949-957`: `/api/m365` and `/api/onedrive` are `authenticateToken(true)` followed by `proxy('m365', …)`. That checks identity only; nothing scopes by organisation.
* **m365**: `app.use('/api', jwtAuthenticate({ publicOps: ['POST /outlook/verify-hash'] }))` (`:606`) authenticates. I did not read its internals, because m365 never compares anything it sets to a connection's org. `requireM365` (`:259`) is a configuration gate (503 when unconfigured).
* **Census across all 22** `app.<verb>('/api…')` **routes in the file:** **0** read the caller's organisation from `req.user` or headers, and **0** compare `organizationId`. The census is a regex. I then read the five routes above by hand.

## Also from AP1 N5 (same route)

`GET /api/onedrive/files` interpolates a raw `folderId` into the Graph path (`:1090`: `/me/drive/items/${folderId}/children`), with no type check and no encoding. The handler's `try` → `next` means this cannot crash the process. Path text is passed to [graph.microsoft.com](<http://graph.microsoft.com>) under the connection's token.

## Priority: High, and why

It is a **cross-organisation read of customer files**: list, then download, using another organisation's Microsoft token. It is open to any authenticated user, and the enumeration needs only one registered site. Wednesday's rule for this class is High.

**What would lower it, and is not measured:** whether any deployed environment has `ENTRA_*` configured with live connections. Where it is not configured, every one of these routes answers 503 (KS-693). **Checking that means reading a live box, which I have not done.** The connection store is also in-memory and reloaded from the database (`loadFromDb`), so whatever a deployment holds is reachable once it is configured.

## Fix direction (not built)

* Bind each connection to the **caller's** organisation, taken from the verified token, never from the body.
* Every lookup by `connectionId` (or site id) must refuse a caller from a different organisation, with a 404 rather than a 403 so it does not leak that the id exists.
* `GET /api/sites` must filter to the caller's organisation.

This needs a tier-1 gate, with cross-org cells that use two organisations.

## Searched before filing

Searched "onedrive files folderId", "m365 connectionId org tenant isolation", "m365 connection ownership", "onedrive connection cross tenant" and "memConnections". The negative control `zkqvplmxhwrt` returned 0.

* **KS-1670** mentions `memConnections` only for the unencoded success redirect.
* **KS-748** and **KS-619** are about API-key and gateway tenant resolution, not m365 connections.
* The PS-1075..1084 storage tickets are Platform S design.

No ticket owns this.

nodes.body:
**BLUF:** Not run on kintsugi: needs two organisations' logins and Entra. Delivered: PRs 1633, 1637 and 1640 merged as 9207fe336797, f7d35d628cdc and 2b205beada00 on develop, deployed to kintsugi at ee1e1b832115 (kintsugi's REVISION head, read 2026-11-04 01:59Z). Left open.

- **Owed check:** the cross-organisation m365 connection check.
- **Why not run:** It needs two organisations' test logins and `ENTRA_*` configured for m365; neither is available.

**BLUF:** Delivered: PRs 1633, 1637 and 1640 merged as 9207fe336797, f7d35d628cdc and 2b205beada00 on develop, deployed to kintsugi at b1fb543640e7 (2026-11-01). Verified by code read, not observed live. Left open: the 2026-10-19 comment says this ticket is done only when deployed and checked live; the cross-organisation check is owed: live sweep owed (needs two organisations' test logins, and m365 needs `ENTRA_*` configured).

- **In the code at b1fb543640e7:** every org-owned m365 resource is bound to the caller's organisation, which comes from the signed token and never from the body or query (`m365-integration/src/index.ts:388-396`); `organizationId` is absent from the connection-init schema (`:361`); `GET /api/sites` refuses a token with no organisation instead of serving an empty 200 (`:947`).
- **Tracked in its own ticket:** the second route to the same harm, KS-1682.

**BLUF: a second route to this ticket's harm, filed separately as KS-1682 (High). Different root cause, not covered by the fix deployed here.**

This ticket binds each Microsoft 365 connection to its organisation. KS-1682 is about which refresh token a connection is handed in the first place. `exchangeAuthCode` takes the **first** refresh token in a process-wide MSAL cache, not the one for the account that just signed in. So once two organisations have connected within one process lifetime, the second organisation's connection stores the first organisation's refresh token. From its first token refresh it then reads the first organisation's Microsoft 365. No attacker is needed, and the organisation binding added here does not reach it.

Measured statically and on a real msal-node cache; not driven end to end. It is dormant today: 0 connections on kintsugi and demo. Details and the line table are on KS-1682.

**BLUF: all of KS-1673's code is now merged. Part A, part B and the test follow-ups are on `develop`. Nothing is deployed yet, so the ticket stays open: it is done only when deployed and checked live.**

The last piece merged as `2b205beada00a2f0fb3144e38198e471848132b6` on `develop` (#1640, squashed, one parent `c9ab6b36ff92`). The landed tree is `fc0a930ac613667f1f1e4cc73106777b86c1693f`, exactly the tree required before the merge. The review (gate BC1, the second round) found nothing further.

**What is now on `develop` for this ticket**
- **#1633** — Microsoft 365 connections, SharePoint sites, OneDrive and synced documents are bound to the caller's own organisation.
- **#1637** — Teams webhooks are bound the same way.
- **#1640** — the Teams tests now also run on a real database engine, so a widened filter can no longer pass unnoticed. The notify API description is corrected.

**Before deploy, two things to know.** Both are recorded on this ticket and on KS-1678.
- Existing connections and Teams webhooks created by the admin setup wizard will be **owned by nobody**, because the wizard saved a tenant id where the organisation id belongs. Re-connecting or re-registering is the remedy. There were **0** of either on kintsugi and demo when last measured.
- API keys with no organisation will be **refused** on the Teams routes. That is intended under the no-admin-bypass ruling.

**Related, still open:** KS-1677 (the Microsoft sign-in callback can take over a connection given its id) and KS-1678 (the admin setup wizard).

**BLUF: the last follow-up owed on this ticket is up for review, PR #1640. It is test-only, plus one corrected API description. Nothing is merged or deployed.**

https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/1640 — head `c210733f6592`, on `develop` `a4187f0f6`.

**What it closes.** Part B's Teams tests used a stand-in for the database. The stand-in could not see a query whose filter had been **widened** — for example, "this organisation's rows, *or* rows with no organisation". The security review wrote two such breakages that passed all 16 tests but leaked on a real database. This PR runs the four Teams queries — list, notify, delete, register — on a **real in-memory Postgres**. The table definition is read from the repo's own schema file each time, and ownership is checked against the database itself.

**How it was checked.**
- The review's two breakages, plus a third of mine (delete widened the same way), are now each **caught by exactly one new test**. The old 16 tests still pass under all three, which is the gap this PR closes.
- The old tests are unchanged.
- The service's full suite passes: 147 of 147.

**The API description** for sending a Teams notification no longer says it posts "to all configured webhooks", nor that other services call it. It now says what the route does: it reaches the caller's own organisation's webhooks, and a login token with no organisation is refused.

**One thing to know.** The in-memory Postgres reaches this service through another package's development tooling; this service does not declare it. If that ever changes, these tests **fail loudly** — that was checked by removing the package. They never skip silently.

**BLUF: part B is merged. Microsoft Teams webhooks are now bound to the caller's own organisation, like the rest of Microsoft 365 in part A. One test-only follow-up is still owed on this ticket. Nothing is deployed, so the ticket stays open.**

Merged as `f7d35d628cdcf1df88a6b55665f3cd2e5e2b7696` on `develop` (#1637, squashed, one parent `c129c63cf777`). The landed tree is `c1e36ae51acc351723c7021611ea5e73e68ac951`, exactly the tree required before the merge. The service's full test suite was run at that exact point: 139 of 139.

**What the security review found** (gate AX1, five notes, no blockers). It attacked as a second organisation, on a real database engine as well as on mocks. Another organisation's webhook URL or host appeared in **no** response body, header or log line, and **nothing** was sent to another organisation's channels on any refused request.

**A caller class that is now refused — please know this before deploy.** Any **API key whose record has no organisation** now gets **403** from notify, register and list, and an answer that changes nothing from delete. That is the intended fail-closed behaviour under the no-admin-bypass ruling. The review reasoned it from the code, not from live keys. For scale, the security service's code records a demo count of **18 of 39 keys with no organisation**, dated 2026-09-03.

**Still owed on this ticket:** a test-only follow-up. The tests' database stand-in cannot see a `WHERE` clause that has been widened. The review wrote two such breakages that pass all 16 tests yet leak on a real database engine. The follow-up adds tests on a real engine that catch both. It also corrects one sentence in the API description, which names a caller of notify that does not exist.

**BLUF: part B is built and up for security review, PR #1637. Microsoft Teams webhooks are now bound to the caller's own organisation, the same rule as part A. Nothing is merged or deployed yet.**

https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/1637 — head `1c26f26af047`, on `develop` `0f472ec20093`.

**What changes for a caller**
- **Listing** Teams webhooks returns only the caller's own organisation's. Each webhook carries its URL, and that URL is a secret: anyone holding it can post into that Teams channel. Before, the list returned **every** organisation's.
- **Registering** takes the organisation from the login token, not the request. The response now names the real owner.
- **Deleting** works only on the caller's own webhooks. Anything else gets the same answer as an id that does not exist.
- **Sending a notification** reaches only the caller's own channels. Before, one call posted a card — with the caller's own title, author and details — into every organisation's Teams channels at once.
- A login token that carries no organisation is refused, and nothing is written or sent.

**Before deploy:** every existing Teams webhook will be **owned by nobody**, because the admin setup wizard saved a tenant id where the organisation id belongs (KS-1678). The fix is to re-register them. **There are 0 Teams webhooks on kintsugi and 0 on demo.**

**Also in this PR:** the extra test the part A review asked for. A caller using its own connection with another organisation's site id never has that organisation's SharePoint site or library sent to Microsoft.

**How it was checked**
- 16 new tests. **12 fail on part A's code and pass here**; the other 4 check that the owner keeps access.
- Seven deliberate breakages of the fix were tried, and each is caught.
- The service's full test suite passes at the exact point it will land: 139 of 139.

**BLUF: PR A is merged. Microsoft 365 connections, SharePoint sites, OneDrive and synced documents are now bound to the caller's own organisation, on 14 routes. Teams is PR B, next. Nothing is deployed.**

Merged as `9207fe336797b136f3f12fb6da169fba7fd900b7` on `develop` (#1633, squashed, one parent `05ad5d3ac472`). The landed tree is `32e0b981e2b1adb25bffa08905b738e54b504a15`, exactly the tree required before the merge and re-derived independently on the moved `develop`.

**What the security review found.** It attacked as a second organisation with 20 id shapes, 6 body shapes and 13 token variants on every bound route. It found **no path to the first organisation's data**, and **zero** calls to Microsoft on every refused request. A "not yours" answer is identical to an "unknown id" answer in status, body and headers. No blockers.

**Existing rows — please read before this is deployed.** Existing `svc_m365_connections` rows written by the admin setup wizard carry a Secuura **tenant** id in `organization_id`. After deploy they will be **owned by nobody**: invisible to everyone, their real owner included. **Re-connecting is the remedy.** There were **0** such rows on kintsugi and demo on 2026-10-20. The wizard itself is filed as **KS-1678**.

**Recorded, not fixed here:**
- the unauthenticated sign-in callback — **KS-1677**, now measured by the review;
- an owner whose connection is in the database but not in this process's memory sees its sites and documents as not found — recorded on **KS-1675**;
- a review test for the documents/sync site lookup is added in PR B.

**BLUF: the first half of the fix is built and is at security review, PR #1633. Connections, SharePoint sites, OneDrive and synced documents are now bound to the caller's own organisation. Teams is the second half, PR B, still to come. Nothing is merged or deployed.**

PR: https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/1633 — head `76725fd4a5b7`, on `develop` `88b8ceb9f304`.

**What changes for a caller**
- The organisation comes from the caller's **signed login token**, never from the request body. `POST /api/connections/init` no longer reads `organizationId` from the body. A caller that still sends it gets a connection owned by **its own** organisation — not an error, and never the one it asked for.
- Asking for another organisation's connection, site or document gets **exactly the same "not found" answer** as asking for an id that does not exist. The two responses were compared byte for byte, and the "not yours" one contains neither the owner's organisation id nor its tenant name.
- Listing sites or documents with a token that carries **no organisation** is refused (403). It is no longer served an empty list that would read like "you own nothing".
- A connection with no organisation recorded is visible to **nobody**. So is a site whose connection is gone, including to the organisation that created it.
- **No exceptions for any role**, as ruled.

**The defect that mattered most, now pinned by tests:** a caller from organisation B asking to list or sync A's OneDrive gets "not found" and the service makes **no call to Microsoft at all**. That is measured two separate ways, because the service reaches Microsoft two separate ways. Before this change, the same request listed A's files using A's own Microsoft token.

**How it was checked**
- 33 tests. **22 of them fail on today's code and pass with the fix.** The other 11 check that each organisation's own access still works.
- Seven deliberate breakages of the fix were tried. Each one is caught. Removing the ownership comparison alone breaks every cross-organisation test.
- The full test suite of this service passes: 114 of 114.

**Two corrections to this ticket's description**
- **The service has 24 routes under `/api`, not 22.** I counted with a stated pattern and checked the count against today's code. Fourteen are now bound. Four are Teams, for PR B. Two are deliberately left alone: the health check, which reports totals only, and the Microsoft sign-in redirect, which cannot carry our login token.
- **The published API description said `organizationId` was required** on `connections/init`. It is corrected in the same PR.

**Not run, and why:** the four full-platform test suites, and three of the sixteen pre-push checks. All of them need the whole stack running, and this machine has no Docker. The PR lists exactly which ones.

**BLUF: the fix plan for this ticket is approved (Wednesday, 2026-10-20). It will ship as two pull requests on this one ticket, each with a full security review. No code has been written yet.**

**What was decided**
* **No exceptions for any role.** No admin, platform admin or super user can see another organisation's Microsoft 365 connections, sites, documents or Teams webhooks. If an operator ever needs that, it gets its own ticket and design.
* **Teams is in scope here.** It has the same root cause and the same fix.
* **Two PRs:**
  * **PR A:** connections, SharePoint sites, OneDrive and synced documents.
  * **PR B:** Teams webhooks. It follows PR A and reuses PR A's rule for where the organisation comes from.

**How the fix works**
* The caller's organisation comes from their signed login token, never from the request body.
* A connection is usable only by a caller from the same organisation.
* A "not yours" request gets exactly the same 404 as an unknown id, so nobody learns that the id exists.
* A caller with no organisation, or a connection with none recorded, sees nothing.

**Tests the fix must carry**
* Two organisations side by side. A cross-organisation request answers 404 and makes **no call to Microsoft Graph**, while the owner's request still works.
* For Teams, a test that another organisation's webhook URL never appears in the response at all, checked on the URL text, not just the row count.

**Separate issue found while measuring:** the m365 connections table may never save or reload a connection. That is KS-1675, not this ticket.

**BLUF: no customer data is exposed on either environment today. But on kintsugi every route in this chain is live, so the first organisation to connect Microsoft 365 there would be exposed at once. The defect is also wider than this ticket said: Microsoft Teams webhooks have the same missing org binding.**

**Measured 2026-10-19 13:47Z, read-only.** I checked only names and counts, sent no request to any m365 route, and wrote nothing on either box.

| | kintsugi | demo |
| -- | -- | -- |
| m365 running | yes | yes |
| Microsoft 365 configured (the three `ENTRA_*` settings) | **yes, so these routes are live** | **no, so they answer 503** |
| connections stored | **0** | **0** |
| Teams webhooks stored | **0** | **0** |

The counts used a database role that bypasses row-level security, with a non-zero control table. A zero therefore means empty, not hidden.

**The same defect in Teams:**
* `GET /api/teams/webhook-config` returns **every** organisation's active webhooks, **including the webhook URL**. That URL is a secret: whoever holds it can post into that Teams channel.
* `POST /api/teams/webhook-config` takes the organisation from the request body. `DELETE` and `POST /api/teams/notify` have no organisation filter.
* `svc_teams_webhooks` has no row-level security either.

**Scope correction to the description above:** none of m365's 22 routes checks the caller's organisation. A fix plan covering all of them, Teams included, is with Wednesday for a ruling. No code yet.

title: auth: no provider identity is ever stored - createUser and updateUser both drop social-id fields, so /social/link answers linked:true over nothing
description:
**BLUF:** The auth service never stores a provider identity (Google, Apple, GitHub, Microsoft personal). All three code paths that try to save one drop it silently, while the code that reads it back works. So no account can ever be found by the social account linked to it. `POST /social/link` answers `linked: true` with nothing saved, and its "already linked to another user" check can never fire. **Nothing is exposed today**, because an identity that is never stored authenticates nobody. **But the fix is security-sensitive.** The code warns that once ids persist, a risk that is latent today becomes live.

Measured by Seat R 55th at develop `4a065fb7535080190c407237f948d0af3538f2dd`. Line numbers come from a byte-identical copy of `services/auth` at `115797747cb6`. #1626 changed `routes/auth.ts` by +2/-2 at `:257` only, so they still hold.

## The three write sites, all dropped

| site | path | what happens |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `routes/auth.ts:1180` | social sign-in, **new user** | sets `newUser[`${provider}Id`] = profile.providerId` and passes it to `createUser`, whose INSERT names **no** social-id column |
| `routes/auth.ts:1249` | social sign-in, **existing account matched by email**, after the KS-795 gate | `updateUser(user.id, { [socialIdField]: providerId })`, and `updateUser` issues **no statement** for that field |
| `routes/auth.ts:1323` | `POST /social/link` (authenticated) | same `updateUser` call, then answers `{ success: true, linked: true }` |

**Why both writers drop it:**

* `updateUser`'s `fieldMap` (`repositories/userRepo.ts:801-824`) has 20 keys and **none** for a social id. A key that is not in the map is skipped, so a call carrying only a social id issues zero statements and returns the unchanged row. Control: the same read finds `walletAddress` once.
* `createUser` (`:668`): the 60 lines from its declaration mention **no** `google_id`, `apple_id`, `github_id`, `linkedin_id`, `facebook_id` or `microsoft_personal_id`.

## The columns and the reader exist

* `migrations/001_initial-schema.sql:534-539` adds `google_id`, `apple_id`, `github_id` and `microsoft_personal_id`.
* `userRepo.getUserBySocialId` (`:618`) reads them through the `SECURITY DEFINER` function `auth_find_user_by_social($1, $2)`.
* It is called at `routes/auth.ts:1039` (sign-in) and `:1317` (`/social/link`). It can only ever return null for an identity this app linked.

## What follows from that

* Every social sign-in resolves its account **by email**. A provider account whose email differs from the platform account can never sign in to it, even after a "successful" link.
* `/social/link`'s conflict check at `:1318` ("This social account is already linked to another user") cannot fire. So two users can each "link" the same provider account and both get `linked: true`.
* `/social/link` also raises `verificationLevel` to `SOCIAL` at `:1327` on the strength of a link that was never stored.

## ⚠ The fix is the dangerous part, and the code says so

`routes/auth.ts:1233-1240`, verbatim in substance: the link write's danger *"is LATENT rather than current: today* `updateUser` *has no social-id fields in its fieldMap, so the write is silently dropped. The moment that persistence defect is repaired, a pre-gate link write would attach an ATTACKER's provider identity to a SUSPENDED victim's account … That is why this reordering lands BEFORE the persistence fix, not after it."*

The KS-795 F-4 comment at `:1044-1050` also notes that the email-key rules start to matter *"the day the social-id persistence defect is fixed and this lookup starts finding rows"*.

So the fix must:

* keep every link write **after** the gate;
* re-check the `:1318` conflict path, which becomes live;
* decide what happens to accounts that were "linked" while nothing persisted (there are none in the database to migrate, by construction).

It should go through a tier-1 gate.

## Priority: Medium, and why

* **Not High:** nothing exploitable is live. The defect fails closed, and normal sign-in works through the email branch.
* **Not Low:**
  * A user-facing success answer is false: `linked: true` with nothing saved.
  * A verification level is raised over it.
  * The repair re-opens the KS-795 class unless it is done deliberately.

## Where it is already written down

* The repo's `BACKLOG.md` entry: "`userRepo.updateUser` silently drops EVERY social-id write — the account-linking it performs never reaches the database". It was widened on 2026-09-05 to say that `createUser` drops it too. That entry is the source; this ticket is its Linear home, because no Linear ticket owned it.
* The code comments at `routes/auth.ts:1233-1240` and `:1298-1301`.
* **KS-1460**, the discarding-`updateUser` sweep. Gate AO1's census on #1626 noted that at `:1249` and `:1323` `updateUserOrThrow` **would not catch** this, because no write is issued at all. See KS-1460's comment `73f91c88-be30-4865-92a7-98cc7a146017`.

Searched before filing:

* Phrases: "social id link updateUser drops", "socialIdField fieldMap", "social/link linked true", "verificationLevel SOCIAL unconfirmed".
* Negative control: `qvzkxmplorft` returned 0.
* The only hits were KS-1460 (the sweep, which cannot fix this) and KS-1617 (social sign-in diagnostics).

title: m365-integration: three more reflection sites from gate AM1 - an unencoded connectionId in the success redirect, and two uncapped error texts in JSON bodies
description:
**BLUF:** Gate AM1, reviewing #1622 (KS-1641 finding 2), found **three more places in** `services/m365-integration/src/index.ts` **that put text the service does not control into a response.** None is the crash #1622 fixes. One is an **unencoded** value in a redirect; two are **uncapped** error texts in JSON bodies, one of them an internal error message in a 500. All three need a valid session or a server-issued id to reach, so none is reachable by an anonymous request today.

Filed as one ticket because AM1 found them in one review pass. Measured by Seat R 55th at develop `115797747cb60009e781d80e9059dbbed69e1ac3`, file blob `1d9ea9df234832ceb8d04de116be10ee3bf421d3`. **Line numbers are develop's.** #1622 inserts 52 lines above them, so on that branch each is +52.

## The three sites

**1.** `:508` **—** `connectionId` **goes into the success redirect unencoded (AM1 N4).**

```ts
res.redirect(`…/admin/integrations?m365=success&connectionId=${connectionId}&tenant=${encodeURIComponent(connection.tenantName || '')}`);
```

`tenant` in the same template **is** encoded and `connectionId` is not. `connectionId` is `String(state)`, and it only reaches this line after `memConnections.get(connectionId)` hits. So it has to equal an id the server issued, and **it is not exploitable today.** It is fragile: if the id format ever admits `&`, `#` or `%`, the redirect's query changes shape. Fix: `encodeURIComponent(connectionId)`, the same as its neighbour.

**2.** `:742` **— an internal error message in a 500 body, with no guard at the site (AM1 N5).**

```ts
res.status(500).json({ success: false, error: { code: 'INTERNAL_ERROR', message: 'Token refresh failed', details: err?.message } });
```

This is the **KS-1410 class** (thrown text in a 500 body), but in a file KS-1410 does not cover. m365 reads `NODE_ENV` 5 times, **all at** `:1536` **or later** (the PII-key fatal-start block). There are **zero** `NODE_ENV` reads before `:742`, so nothing guards this site. The route is authenticated.

**3.** `:1026` **— Graph's own error text, passed back uncapped (AM1 N5).**

```ts
return res.status(resp.status).json({ error: (err as any).error?.message || 'OneDrive API error' });
```

This is **provider** text, not an internal error: it is the same kind of thing as the OAuth `error_description` KS-1641 capped. It is authenticated, uncapped, and it forwards Graph's status code unchanged.

## Why the third one matters beyond itself

The callback's `:515` already reflects MSAL's `err.message` into a redirect: encoded, uncapped, and reachable only with a valid `state`. KS-1641 calls that **a decision, not a cap**: bound the internal message, or map it to a code and keep the detail server-side. `:742` and `:1026` are the same decision in JSON bodies, so they should be decided together with `:515`, not capped one at a time.

## Neighbours read before filing

The search's negative control (`xkqvzzpholmdrf`) returned **0** hits, so the search does discriminate.

* **KS-1410** (In Progress): same class as site 2, but it lists **six files** by name, and m365 is not one of them.
* **KS-730** (Done): lists five files, with **0** m365 mentions.
* **KS-840**: about auth's own OAuth error envelope, not m365.
* **KS-1641**: owns `:465` (the cap, #1622) and the `:515` decision. These three are AM1's notes on that PR, carved out by Wednesday's ruling so they would not widen it.

## How to fix

Site 1 is a one-line change and can ship on its own. Sites 2 and 3 should wait for the `:515` decision on KS-1641, so that one rule covers all three.

Each fix needs a cell that sends **non-ASCII text across the boundary**. KS-1641's round 1 shipped a crash because every cell was ASCII; gate AM1's B1 is that crash.

title: renovate.json at the repo root: does Renovate for the systemTest pins conflict with the 2026-07-04 ruling "Dependabot, not Renovate" (KS-352 / KS-353)?
description:
## Found while

Aligning the docs with the rulings in the Linear tickets ([KS-1668](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1668/docs-record-kamils-linear-rulings-that-platform-k-docs-omit-or)).

## What is there

`renovate.json` is tracked at the repo root. It was last changed 2026-10-07 for [KS-1445](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1445/pin-systemtest-k6-to-the-latest-release-or-later-the-macs-native-k6-is) and [KS-1367](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1367/renovates-k6-rule-sees-only-the-dockerfile-from-not) ("Renovate sees the k6 pin"). It extends `config:recommended`, ignores `Blockchain/Dev/**`, runs before 6am on Monday, groups the observability stack images and the k6 runtime, and patches systemTest npm updates.

## The ruling it may conflict with

[KS-352](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-352/start-secuurash-rebuild-triage-npm-audit-vulnerabilities-across) and [KS-353](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-353/start-secuurash-rebuild-clear-npm-dependency-deprecation-warnings) (2026-07-04): "Dependabot, not Renovate". The repo docs and `.github/dependabot.yml` follow that ruling; the docs do not mention Renovate at all.

## Question for Kamil

1. Is Renovate allowed for the **systemTest** pins (everything outside `Blockchain/Dev/**`), with Dependabot kept for the platform, or should `renovate.json` go?
2. Whichever you choose, the docs should say it. I will write the answer into the docs under this ticket's number and the date.

## Related

[KS-1446](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1446/renovate-cannot-bump-base-image-watchsh-excluded-bases-blockchaindev) already asks whether Renovate may bump `base-image-watch.sh` (it is under `ignorePaths`) and says it needs Kamil's agreement; the answer to question 1 decides it.

## Not in scope

No change to `renovate.json` is proposed here. The docs-only PR for [KS-1668](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1668/docs-record-kamils-linear-rulings-that-platform-k-docs-omit-or) leaves this file alone.

title: KS-1633 follow-ups (PR #1623, gate AK1's nine notes): the row left behind when the reservation lands and the save fails (a design question), two surviving pool mutants, the untested provisionalWritten branch, two stale comments and a warn line that carries the DB error text
description:
## BLUF

**Gate AK1's nine notes on PR #1623 (KS-1633), in one checklist.** The PR merged **GO WITH NOTE, 0 blockers**, as develop `adb0dfd58fc582f24ab2a7db021a2027544f566c`, landed tree `e598e00e890284ae6b85a9fe0379eac3c28a72ca`.

**Rated Medium because of item (a)**, which is a design question rather than a defect with an obvious fix: it is asked here, not answered.

## (a) A row left behind when the reservation lands and the save then fails — THE DESIGN QUESTION

`POST /api/certifications/issue` now writes its `documents` row **before** it anchors. If that reservation **succeeds** and the authoritative `saveCertification` then **fails**, the request answers a failure to the client while a row remains, reading `certified` **with anchoring** `failed`**, no anchor id, and zero** `certification_events` **rows**.

It is **not** an orphan anchor — nothing was anchored, so the claimable shape the ticket was about does not arise. It is a certification the caller does not know exists, with no event behind it.

**The question, and it is genuinely open:** compensate it (the same delete the production-503 path uses), or document why not? Arguments both ways: compensating it is consistent with the 503 path and keeps "a failed request wrote nothing" true for one more case; **not** compensating it preserves evidence of a half-completed write that an operator may want, and every compensation is itself a write that can fail. **Whoever picks this up should decide and record the decision — it is not assumed here.**

## (b) Two surviving pool mutants — N1

Both of these **survive** the suite as merged:

1. the route passes **no** pool to `deleteCertification`;
2. `withTenant` **ignores** the pool it is handed.

The unit cell `ks1633-the-compensating-delete-uses-the-requests-pool.test.ts` pins that the route *hands over* `req.tenantPool`, and nothing pins that `withTenant` then *uses* it. **Cells needed that red both.** The honest constraint: no second tenant database was stood up for #1623 (no Docker on that machine, one scratch Postgres instance), so the cross-database path is covered by **no cell at all** — a real second database, or an injected pool whose `connect()` is observed, is what would close it.

## (c) The `provisionalWritten` branch is untested — N2

Nothing exercises the path where the reservation **failed** and the compensation is therefore skipped (`provisionalWritten === false`, which substitutes `1` for the row count). A regression that inverted that flag would either raise a **false** "removed no row" alarm or **suppress a real one**, and nothing would redden. **One cell: reservation made to fail, production + anchoring down, assert the 503 and that no "removed no row" line is logged.**

## (d) Two stale code comments — N5

`services/originate/src/routes/certifications.ts`:

* `:467` — *"Writing the row first removes the window rather than narrowing it."* **Wrong.** It narrows it: when the reservation itself fails, the anchor-then-fail path is unchanged.
* `:474` — *"the sub-second window before the second write"*. **Wrong.** The window is bounded by the anchoring timeout, `AbortSignal.timeout(10000)` — **up to 10 seconds**.

Both were corrected in the PR body before the merge and **deliberately left in the code**, because changing them would have moved the head the GO was pinned to. They are wrong in the merged tree today.

## (e) The ks1633 suite header — N6

`ks1633-certify-writes-its-row-before-it-anchors.integration.test.ts` at `:23`, `:31` and `:262` — the gate asked for the header's wording to be brought in line with the behaviour the cells now assert (the same "narrows / up to 10 s" corrections, and the narrowed ORPHAN claim).

## (f) The warn line carries the database error text — N7

`certifications.ts:530` logs `error: reserveErr.message` alongside `certId` and `tenantId` — the database's **own error text**, not ids alone. **Not new** (this file's warn lines already did this), but **PR #1623's body claimed "ids only" and that claim was wrong**; it was corrected in the body before the merge. Worth a decision here: either the claim goes (and the text stays, consistent with the file's other warns), or the text is dropped to match what the rest of this route promises. A database error message can carry row values.

## Searched before filing

Linear `searchIssues`, archived included: `reserveCertificationRow` **→ 0 hits**, `provisionalWritten` **→ 0 hits** (both symbols are new with #1623), and `KS-1633 follow-up compensating delete pool mutants` → 25 hits whose near neighbours are **KS-1633** itself and **KS-1664** (the `/recertify` sibling), neither covering these notes.

## Related

**KS-1633** (merged as `adb0dfd58fc5`) · **KS-1664** (`/recertify` has the same ordering and will need the same three lessons) · **KS-1612 / KS-1384** (what an orphan anchor allows) · **KS-1124 F4** (Kam's ruling on the stored anchor state, which AK1 confirmed still holds) · **KS-1090** (originate's tsconfig excludes its tests, so `tsc -p` cannot catch a type error in any cell above).

With A5b it is the only cell of 11 that fails, by `expect(repo.deleteCertification).not.toHaveBeenCalled()`; 0 TypeScript errors.
