title: Chain-first verify blobs hard-code `anchored: true` and drop anchoring's status/acknowledged, so a 'submitting' or failed anchor reads isAnchored: true (v1 + v2)
description:
## BLUF

**The chain-first verify branches build their blockchain blob with** `anchored: true` **hard-coded and no** `status`**, which makes the honest-anchor guard** `settled` **BY CONSTRUCTION.** An anchoring reply that is still in flight or has failed — `status: 'submitting'`, `acknowledged: false`, the KS-726 class — is therefore presented as `isAnchored: true`, in both the v1 and the v2 verify routes.

The code says so itself. `services/originate/src/routes/verification.ts:130-132`:

> *"KS-1628: a failed anchor is not an anchor, whatever else the blob says. The chain-first blobs carry* `anchored: true` *and no status, so they are unaffected; a stored blob that pairs* `anchored: true` *with a failed status was on-chain before this line."*

That comment reads as a reassurance. It is in fact the statement of the defect: *unaffected by the failed-status guard* is exactly the problem, because the guard is the thing that would have caught this.

Gate O1's Minor 2 on the twelve-PR batch, 2026-10-19T01:00:25Z. Pre-existing; not in those merges.

## The mechanism, measured

`isAnchoredHonestly` (`verification.ts:120`) decides the claim:

```ts
if (FAILED_ANCHOR_STATUSES.has(String(c.status))) return false;   // :133
const settled = c.anchored === true || c.status === 'confirmed';  // :141
```

* A **real stored** anchor row has no `anchored` boolean at all — the comment at `:136-139` says so: *"anchoring's vocabulary is pending | submitted | confirmed | failed … and there is NO* `anchored` *boolean on a real row."* For those rows only `status === 'confirmed'` earns the claim, and `'submitted'` deliberately does not, because *"the tx is in flight and may still fail — the KS-535 class."*
* A **chain-first** blob is built by hand with `anchored: true` and **no** `status` **key**. So `FAILED_ANCHOR_STATUSES.has(String(undefined))` is false — the failed guard cannot fire — and `settled` is true on the first disjunct, whatever anchoring actually reported.

**The four construction sites:**

| route | site |
| -- | -- |
| v1 | `services/originate/src/routes/verification.ts:717` |
| v1 | `services/originate/src/routes/verification.ts:1237` |
| v1 | `services/originate/src/routes/verification.ts:1259` |
| **v2** | `services/originate/src/routes/verificationV2.ts:233`, inside `chainOnlyMatch` |

The `status` argument the call sites pass does not rescue it: `verification.ts:758`, `:1297` and `verificationV2.ts:271` pass the **literal** `'anchored'`, and in any case the second argument is only consulted when there is no chain blob at all (`:149`).

**What bounds the severity.** `settled` is necessary but not sufficient: the claim also needs `typeof c.txHash === 'string'`, `REAL_TXHASH_RE` (64 hex) and `heightOk`. So the hash must already look like a real one, and it comes from the chain index. The defect is that **in-flight and failed anchors the index knows about still read as anchored** — not that an arbitrary blob does.

## Why High

On a document-authenticity platform, `isAnchored: true` is the product's central claim to a verifier. Presenting a `'submitting'` or failed anchor as anchored is the same family as KS-535 (a failed on-chain anchor reporting `status: anchored`) and KS-1634 (a simulated anchor returned unlabelled), and KS-1634 is High. The failure direction is always *over*-claiming, never under-claiming.

**Honest limit on this rating: I did not run a census.** I have not measured how many rows can reach these branches with a non-confirmed status today. The nearest evidence is KS-1634's census — 0 qualifying rows on both boxes at 2026-10-18, with kintsugi's 0 noted as contingent on one document row — and that census was for a different precondition. **A census is the first step on this ticket, and the rating should be revisited against it.**

## Recommendation

1. Carry anchoring's own fields into the chain-first blob instead of asserting the conclusion: pass `status` and `acknowledged` through, and let `isAnchoredHonestly` apply the same rules it applies to a stored row. Dropping `anchored: true` entirely is the cleaner shape, since no real row carries it — but `ks563` pins the current chain-first shape, so that is a deliberate change with a test to re-cut, not a one-liner.
2. A cell per site: a chain-first match whose anchoring status is `'submitting'` (and one that is `'failed'`) must read `isAnchored: false`. A mutant restoring the hard-coded `anchored: true` must red each of them.
3. Fold the **v2** site in with KS-1634's v2 work — it is the same four lines of construction, and splitting them across two tickets invites one to be done and the other forgotten.

## Dedupe

Over all **1,627** Secuura-PK issues including archived: `chainOnlyMatch` **→ 0 hits.** `anchored: true` → 4, each a different subject (KS-1634 the simulated-label defect, KS-1628 the route retirement, KS-834 a decision on verify auth, KS-535 the document-status variant, Done). `acknowledged` → 6, none about this presenter. `isAnchored` → 9; the nearest, KS-1637, is gate N1's residue about the removal pin reading only the router — a different mechanism, read and confirmed distinct. Positive controls on the same corpus: `verification` 360, `anchor` 313. Zero control: a nonsense token reads 0.

**Related:** KS-1634 (the same presenter, the `simulated` signal, and the v2 site it shares), KS-726 (the `status: 'submitting'` / `acknowledged: false` reply class this mis-presents; Done), KS-535 (the document-status variant; Done), KS-563 (which pins the current chain-first shape, so its cells are in scope for any change here).

---

*Filed by Seat R 51st on Wednesday's instruction of 2026-10-19T01:00:25Z, citing gate O1's verdict section "Minor 2". The Linear actor field is shared across the fleet, so authorship is this line, not the actor. Everything above the "Why High" section I verified in the source at develop* `37834600a543cb0276f427d969ac034d9df74fbd`*; the severity and the census limit are my own call, stated as such. Not fixed in these merges.*

title: Clear the 1,125 build warnings in ssd.sln (test project nullable context + xUnit analyzers)
description:
## Problem

VS Code shows 1K+ warnings building `ssd.sln`. On `develop` @ `818367a`, a clean `dotnet build ssd.sln --no-incremental` gives **1,125 unique warnings**: **1,124 in** `tests/ssd.UnitTests`, 1 in `ssd/`.

The cause: `tests/ssd.UnitTests/ssd.UnitTests.csproj` sets `<Nullable>enable</Nullable>`, while `ssd/` keeps nullable reference types **off on purpose** (CLAUDE.md). Full flow analysis in the tests flagged every deliberate `null` a test passes: 543 × CS8625, plus CS8767/8618/8602/8620/8603/8619/8613/8604/8600/8601/8605/8633. These are noise, not defects.

| Code | Count |
| -- | -- |
| CS86xx nullable (tests) | 912 |
| xUnit1012 — `[InlineData(null)]` into a `string` param | 189 |
| CS1998 — async test with no await | 10 |
| CS8601 in the two files with their own `#nullable enable` | 5 |
| xUnit2013 / 1031 / 2031 / 2000 | 8 |
| CA1416 — unguarded `File.SetUnixFileMode` | 1 |
| CS8632 — `ssd/Services/Transactions/ITransactionService.cs:81` | 1 |

## Plan (accepted)

1. Test csproj: `Nullable` `enable` → `annotations`, set in the csproj so it does **not** flow to the `ssd/` ProjectReference. (A command-line `-p:Nullable=annotations` *does* flow, and turns `ssd/` entity strings into required EF columns: 1,518 xUnit failures. That's the CLAUDE.md trap, confirmed. So do not do it that way.) Drop the two redundant `#nullable enable` lines.
2. xUnit1012: theory `string` params fed `null` → `string?`. Signature only.
3. Hand fixes: CS1998 → `void`; xUnit asserts → the overload the analyzer names; xUnit1031 → `await`; CA1416 → `!OperatingSystem.IsWindows()` guard (the `LocalOnlyScriptTests` pattern); CS8632 → `#nullable enable annotations` on `ITransactionService.cs` (the services pattern, metadata only).

## Offline result

* `dotnet build ssd.sln --no-incremental`: **0 warnings, 0 errors**
* `dotnet test tests/ssd.UnitTests`: **8,416 passed, 0 failed** (same total as before)

The testing HTML docs don't change: no test added or removed, and no tier or command changed.

## systemTest gate ([Secuura/platform-s#1080](https://linear.app/secuura/review/ps-1301-clear-all-1125-build-warnings-in-ssdsln-0-remaining-56be1f33dbac))

Slot 3, S `3c105f7` paired with K slot 3 (images from 15 Oct). Full detail is in the PR description.

| Run | App build | Result |
| -- | -- | -- |
| 1. Full suite, 3,028 tests | branch | **2,834 passed · 29 failed · 165 skipped** |
| 2. Attribution set, 186 tests | branch | 183 passed · 3 failed (all 26 NoTc pass) |
| 3. Same set | `develop`-equivalent (`ssd/` = `818367a`) | **186 · 0** |
| 4. Same set | branch, rebuilt | **186 · 0** |

None of the 29 run-1 failures is caused by this change:

* **26 NoTc** — `notc_user.json` is never refreshed ([PS-279](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-279/enforce-tandc-acceptance-gate-globally-repair-tcprivacy-accept)), and the project started 39 min after `global_setup`, past the 30-min timeout. All 26 pass with a fresh setup.
* **1** [KS-1402](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1402/auth-get-apiuserslookup-refuses-connector-tokens-so-every-platform-s) — named in the assertion.
* **2 flaky** — `testid_coverage_sweep:183` (60 s timeout) and `a11y_keyboard_journey:224`. Both pass on `develop` and on the branch in runs 3–4.

**Not exercised:** the Firefox leg ([PS-1199](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1199/systemtest-the-suite-has-no-firefox-leg-a-12-oct-smoke-19-routes-8), 104 environmental skips).

title: verifierVerificationLevel is still seeded, stored, served and admin-editable but enforced nowhere after KS-1628
description:
**After KS-1628, a document type's** `verifierVerificationLevel` **is still seeded, stored, served and admin-editable, but enforced nowhere.** Wednesday ruled (a) on KS-1628 PR 2: retire the gate with the route, and file this ticket. **The options below are for the owner to choose between; this ticket does not choose.**

## What happened

The only place the per-type verifier level was enforced was api-gateway's own handler for `POST /api/documents/:id/verify` (`routes/verification.ts`, the level check at develop `:596-608`): it read the document type's `verifierVerificationLevel` and refused a caller below it with 403 `INSUFFICIENT_VERIFICATION_LEVEL` (pinned by `ks1176` section E). KS-1628 retires that route.

**Still present, measured at develop** `83ed01af70fd`**:**

* seeded: `api-gateway/src/routes/admin.ts`, nine document types each carry a `verifierVerificationLevel`;
* stored and edited: originate `routes/adminConfig.ts:202`, `:234`, `:1768`;
* served: api-gateway `routes/platform.ts:895` and the document-types route (`routes/verification.ts`).

**Enforced:** nowhere. `meetsVerificationLevel` survives in `services/enforcement.ts:153`, but that is the CREATOR level on document create. The successor `POST /api/verification/verify` is public by design (KS-442).

**Real effect today:** none — the one enforcement point had 0 calls at the edge on kintsugi (\~30 days) and demo (\~38 days), measured read-only 2026-10-19. The risk is a **misleading control**: an administrator who sets a verifier level will reasonably believe it restricts who can verify a document of that type.

## Options for the owner

1. **Remove the setting** — drop `verifierVerificationLevel` from the type catalogue, the admin UI and the stores.
2. **Label it inert** in the admin UI ("not enforced since KS-1628") and leave the data.
3. **Re-introduce a verifier-level gate on a non-public verify route** (the public successor is public by design, so a gate there would contradict KS-442).

## Related

* **KS-1190** ("meetsVerificationLevel fails open on an unknown REQUIRED level") has two halves. Its **verify** half cites `routes/verification.ts:554-557`, which KS-1628 removes, so that half no longer applies; its **create** half (`POST /api/documents`) is unaffected.
* `VerificationRouteDeps.meetsVerificationLevel` is now unused by the routes and kept only so existing test doubles still type-check (comment in place; removable together with whichever option is chosen).

## Dedupe

`description: contains` over all issues: `verifierVerificationLevel` 1 (KS-1190), `verifier_verification_level` 1 (KS-1190), `meetsVerificationLevel` 3 (KS-1628, KS-1190, KS-1176), `verifier level` 0. None records the setting as inert. Control: a nonsense literal returns 0.

Filed by Seat R 49th from KS-1628 PR 2. Not built.

Option a reads: "Every row ruled as recommended; a board seat files and moves the tickets; the KS-607 demo rows still wait for a separate yes." This ticket is row A10 of the decision pack, ruled as recommended: option 1. title: tests/e2e callers of the retired POST /api/documents/:id/verify: rewrite against /api/verification/verify once the e2e package can run (KS-1628, KS-734)
description:

These** `tests/e2e` **callers of that route will fail against a stack that has the change, and none of them was run** — `Blockchain/Dev/tests/e2e` is a separate Playwright package that needs a live stack, which no preflight leg provides (KS-734 is the ticket for making it runnable). Wednesday ruled (b) on KS-1628 PR 2: leave them, name them, and file this ticket, because an unrun rewrite of assertions is a guess presented as a fix.

## The callers (at develop `83ed01af70fd`)

**Will fail when run:**

title: anchor_store.created_at is bound from the anchoring PROCESS's clock, not the database's — move it to a DB-side default (prerequisite for the #1568 gate's option (i))
description:
**Filed on Wednesday's instruction (2026-10-18T20:14:35Z), which ruled this OUT of #1568 round 3 and into its own ticket. Measured at develop** `83ed01af70fd5ed6cca9ac66f28ddcb8a1034105`**.**

## What

`anchor_store.created_at` has a DB default of `NOW()` (`migrations/001_initial-schema.sql:725`), but the main upsert **binds it explicitly** as parameter `$21` from `anchor.createdAt`, a `new Date()` taken in the anchoring service's own process (`Blockchain/Dev/services/anchoring/src/index.ts:1372`, the `INSERT INTO anchor_store … VALUES ($1…$22)`).

`documents.created_at` by contrast is the **database's** `NOW()` (`services/originate/src/repositories/documentRepo.ts`, the `INSERT INTO documents (… created_at, updated_at) VALUES (… NOW(), NOW())`).

So the two timestamps most likely to be compared with each other come from **two different clocks**.

## Why it matters

1. **It is the prerequisite for the #1568 gate's option (i)** — "the guard refuses when the stored anchor predates the claiming document". That rule is a direct comparison of these two columns, so under any skew it refuses legitimate updates. Round 3 deliberately avoided the comparison (migration 051 is an existence test at insert time, no clock), which is why this is not blocking — but option (i) cannot be made sound without this.
2. **Migration 051's one-off apply-time census does use the order**, and so inherits the caveat. A skew-induced false positive there costs a human one look at a listed row (the census is read-only and human-resolved), never a refused legitimate write — stated as narrowing in 051's header and in #1568's PR.
3. Any future reporting that orders anchors against documents has the same exposure.

## Scope

Stop binding `$21` and let the column's own `DEFAULT NOW()` apply (or capture `now()` inside the same statement). Roughly one line in the upsert plus its parameter list, and a cell asserting a freshly inserted `anchor_store` row's `created_at` comes from the server (e.g. it sits between two `now()` readings taken around the insert, and is unaffected by a skewed value supplied by the caller).

## Measured, and not

**Measured:** the `$21` binding and the `documents` `NOW()`, both read at the SHA above. **Not measured:** actual skew on any deployment. On compose the containers share the host kernel clock, so skew is expected to be \~0 (J 12th's reading); across hosts — the Container Apps shape — nothing guarantees it.

*Seat J 13th. Related: KS-1612, KS-1603, KS-1384.*

title: Declared Node floor (engines.node >=18.0.0 in 5 packages) contradicts what the repo needs (22.13+) and runs on (24) - decide the floor
description:
## BLUF

**The repo declares a Node floor it cannot run on.** Five `package.json` files declare `engines.node >=18.0.0`, but a shell suite on the push path already requires **Node 22.13+**, every Docker image builds on **Node 24**, and the preflight assumes a **Node 24** host. Nothing breaks today — the real runtimes are all 24 — but the declared floor tells a developer Node 18 or 20 is fine, and on either one that suite stops with a FATAL. **This ticket records the measurements and asks for a decision. It is deliberately NOT a fix:** the floor is a choice, not a defect with one right answer.

Filed by Seat R 48th on Wednesday's instruction (ANSWER of 2026-10-18T15:24:54Z), after it surfaced while raising PR #1580 (KS-1624 F1). All measurements at `develop` `6184eaa0af75c1e27eb69bbff67a7790ef494b5f`.

## Measurement 1 — what the repo DECLARES

A census of all **50** tracked `package.json` files:

| `engines.node` | files |
| -- | -- |
| `>=18.0.0` | `Blockchain/Dev/package.json`, `connectors/whatsapp-bot`, `services/mcp-server`, `services/tenant-provisioning`, `services/tokenisation` (**5**) |
| `>=24.11.0` | `systemTest/akto`, `systemTest/oxlint`, `systemTest/performance`, `systemTest/playwright` (**4**) |
| none | **41** |

There is **no** `.nvmrc`, `.node-version` or `.tool-versions` anywhere in the tree (0 files). So the only machine-readable statement of the platform's floor is `>=18.0.0` — and the repo's own test tooling already contradicts it with `>=24.11.0`.

## Measurement 2 — what the repo actually NEEDS

`Blockchain/Dev/scripts/__tests__/ks812_whatsapp_bot_default_api_target.test.sh` strips TypeScript types with `module.stripTypeScriptTypes`, available from **Node 22.13**. It says so in its header (line 24) and is guarded: the helper is at line 25, its first call at **line 40**, and on an older Node it exits **2** at **line 44** with `FATAL: this suite needs node 22.13+ (module.stripTypeScriptTypes)`. It runs in the full shell-suite runner. By grep it is the only script under `Blockchain/Dev/scripts`, `systemTest` or `.githooks` needing a Node newer than 18 — so 22.13 is the measured real minimum *for the tooling*, and it is above the declared floor.

## Measurement 3 — what the repo actually RUNS ON

* **Docker:** all **13** `FROM node:` lines in the tree are `node:24-alpine`. Every shipped service builds and runs on 24.
* **Preflight:** `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/preflight/lockfile-cleanroom.sh:49` and `:58` assume a host Node **>=24** on the CI path ("Host node >=24 lets us skip docker", "CI always runs node>=24 (host path)").
* KS-355 (Done) moved CI to Node 24.

## The decision this needs (options, not a recommendation)

1. **Raise the five floors to** `>=24` — matches every runtime and the systemTest packages; Node 18 and 20 are past end-of-life. This is the value KS-1398 already suggests (see below).
2. **Raise them to** `>=22.13` — the measured minimum for the tooling, the least restrictive honest value; leaves a gap between declared and shipped runtimes.
3. **Add a pin file** (`.nvmrc` / `.node-version`) as well as or instead of (1)/(2), so local tooling picks the right version automatically.
4. **Leave** `>=18.0.0` and accept that a developer on 18/20 gets a FATAL from one suite.

Whichever is chosen, `ks812`'s guard can stay as it is — it already fails loudly and names the version.

## Related, and why this is a separate ticket

**KS-1398** (Backlog) carries the same value as one row of a TypeScript 7 migration *suggestion*: `engines.node | >=18.0.0 ×5 | >=24 (Node 18 and 20 are past EOL)`. That row is the same field and the same direction as option 1. It is split out here because the floor is a decision that stands on its own today — it is a live contradiction on the push path, and it should not wait on whether a TypeScript 7 move is ever approved. If the TS 7 work goes ahead and settles the floor, this ticket closes with it.

## How this was searched before filing (dedupe)

Over **1,613** issues including archived, by symbol: `engines` (6 hits), `>=18` / `Node 18` (1: KS-1398), `stripTypeScriptTypes` / `strip-types` / `NO-STRIP-TYPES` (1: KS-355), `22.13` (0), `node:24` / `24.11` (39, broad), `nvmrc` / `node-version` / `tool-versions` (1: KS-355), `Node floor` / `Node version` / `engines.node` (5: KS-1427, KS-1398, KS-1102, KS-464, KS-355). Controls: `preflight` 169 hits, a nonsense token 0. Read KS-1398, KS-355, KS-1427, KS-1102 and KS-464: only KS-1398 records the declared floor, as noted above.

title: KS-1114 follow-up (PR #1576 gate F1): stale summary comment, btrim trims spaces only, and no index on documents.title
description:
## BLUF

> **⚠ EDITED IN PLACE 2026-10-19 by Seat R 48th, on Wednesday's instruction (ANSWER of 2026-10-18T14:05:18Z).**
> Nothing above or below was removed — each item below now carries its **state**, because two of the three read
> as actionable work when filed and are in fact open questions. That was a defect in how I filed them. The
> states were triaged against the live tip `8a9970511f22661d92f634058fae8c08c656124f`, not against the text.
>
> | item | state |
> | -- | -- |
> | **N3** | **brief-able** (Spark, briefed 2026-10-19) |
> | **N2** | **needs a ruling** — no forcing function |
> | **N5** | **needs a measurement, then a migration** — not a Spark shape |

Three notes the **gate F1** run recorded while gating **PR #1576** (KS-1114 follow-up, tier 1 FULL, Opus, 2026-10-18). The verdict was **GO WITH NOTE** and #1576 merged as `d900972f27134888567452c6dc9dabdf9b51659d`. **None of these is a finding against that change** — every one is either cosmetic or pre-existing. They are filed so they are not lost in a verdict file.

Raised by Seat R 48th after merging #1576, on Wednesday's GO of 2026-10-18T12:30:33Z. Verdict: `0_Brain/reference/2026-10-18_gate-F1-pr1576/verdict.md` (sha256/16 `53448c83acdb1797`, line 3 deleted; verified by me with a one-line-off control that differs). Note letters below are the verdict's own numbering.

## N3 — the summary comment at `verification.ts:1445` is now out of date (cosmetic)

**STATE: brief-able — with the Spark as of 2026-10-19.**
Re-measured at `8a9970511f2`: the line is still exactly at **:1445** and reads
`// Absent, another tenant's, draft, revoked and the sentinel all answer ONE not-found body.`
One product file, unambiguous from-text. A comment cannot go red behaviourally, so it takes a source-text
cell — which is the *right* instrument here rather than a proxy, because the artefact under test **is** a
comment. Precedent in the same directory: 14 of originate's 127 test files already read their own source
with `readFileSync`.

Verbatim: *"The summary line still reads 'Absent, another tenant's, draft, revoked and the sentinel all answer ONE not-found body'. It does not mention deleted or expired, although :1440-1441 does. This is cosmetic."*

#1576 widened the hidden set to `deleted` and `expired` and updated the comment at :1440-1441, but the summary line two paragraphs up still enumerates the old set. A reader who stops at the summary gets the wrong list. One-line edit; no behaviour.

## N2 — `btrim()` trims ASCII spaces only, so tab / newline / CR / NBSP still hit (recorded narrowing, not a regression)

**STATE: needs a ruling — do NOT brief this.**
It is a policy choice, not a change: widen to `btrim(d.status, E' \t\r\n\u00a0')`, **or** normalise on write
and say so at the column. There is also **no forcing function** — `documents.status` is NOT NULL and every
writer stores a fixed lower-case literal or the existing status, so no reachable input produces these
variants today. Briefing it would be asking a model to choose a policy nobody has chosen.

Verbatim: *"*`btrim()` *with no second argument trims ASCII spaces only. These variants stay HITs:* `"\tdeleted"`*,* `"revoked\t"`*,* `"\ndraft"`*,* `"expired\n"`*,* `"revoked\r"`*,* `"deleted<NBSP>"` *and* `" \trevoked\t "`*. They were HITs at 833984fc9 too, so nothing regresses. PG confirms it directly:* `btrim(E'\tdeleted')` *keeps the tab, and NBSP is kept. No writer stores such values. This is recorded, not a defect."*

**Why it is not urgent, stated so nobody re-litigates it:** `documents.status` is `VARCHAR(20) NOT NULL DEFAULT 'draft'` (`migrations/001_initial-schema.sql:104`), none of the 51 migrations alters it, and every writer stores a fixed lower-case literal or the existing status. So no reachable input produces one of these variants today. It becomes real only if some future writer stores a status it did not normalise — which is the thing to decide: either widen to `btrim(d.status, E' \t\r\n ')`, or normalise on write and say so in the column's comment.

## N5 — no index on `documents.title`, so the title lookup is a sequential scan (pre-existing)

**STATE: needs a measurement first, then a migration — not a Spark shape.**
Two reasons it is not brief-able. It wants a measurement before a decision (row count and query plan at
expected scale), and the change is a **migration**, not a source edit — which on this repo means the
baked-migrations-image path, with its own deploy discipline. Wrong shape for a one-file patch.

Verbatim: *"*`documents` *has no index on* `title`*, so the title lookup is a Parallel Seq Scan before and after the change. This is not introduced here."*

Worth sizing before the title lookup takes real traffic: it is an anonymous, unauthenticated endpoint, so a seq scan per request on a growing table is a capacity question as much as a latency one.

## Not in scope here

Gate note **N4** (the `ks1557` cross-tenant cell failing as `secuura_app` with `MULTI_TENANCY_ENABLED=true`, identically on untouched develop) was **added to KS-1557 as a comment** instead, because it is about that ticket's own integration suite. Gate note **N1** was a correction to the brief's NULL premise, not a defect — the previous predicate already hid NULL and the column cannot hold one — so there is nothing to carry.

## Suggested order

N3 is a one-line comment edit and can ride along with any other originate change. N2 is a decision before it is a change. N5 wants a measurement (row count and plan at expected scale) before anyone adds an index.

**PR #1579 is merged to `develop` as `385fc288fae831f2ca15b9d091c844f33285b784`.** N3 only — **N2 and N5 stay open here**, as marked. Nothing deployed.

**Gate G3** (tier 2, Sonnet): **GO WITH NOTE**, nothing security-shaped.

**The gate's S1 note — a coupling gap in the new suite (LOW, no new ticket, per Wednesday), and a correction to how I described it.** I wrote that the suite "compares the summary with the SQL predicate". **It does not.** It checks the SQL's status list against a *hardcoded* `draft, revoked, deleted, expired`, and the comment against *hardcoded* names — never the comment against the SQL. The gate proved the consequence by planting it: widen the SQL, update the test's hardcoded list, leave the comment stale, and **all five cells stay green** — which is exactly the defect #1579 repairs. Two related changes do fail loudly: widening the SQL *without* updating the list, and the `btrim` coupling (if N2 ever adds a second argument to `btrim`), though the latter with a generic message. The PR body and my earlier comment here are corrected in place.

**The shape of the missing cell, for whoever next touches this:** derive the expected names *from* the parsed `NOT IN (...)` list and assert the summary contains each one — then the comment is checked against the SQL itself, and a widening with a stale comment goes red. It is a one-cell, test-only change in the same file.

**Evidence on the tree that landed** (predicted commit `f7b69a3dd819`, tree `526bc67b37d39627a5d23c103bf60e64741fda2f` — the pair tree predicted for #1579/#1580 in either order): the suite **5/5**; originate in full **1393/1393, 112 suites, 0 failed**; `tsc` (TypeScript 5.9.3, real path) rc 0. The shell runner was not re-run: every shell-suite input subtree is identical to #1580's tree, which read 91/91. Five-point read 5/5 TRUE.

**N3 raised as PR #1579**, head `76de780c20421cf963d53273571776c1e2e8a97a`, on develop `6184eaa0af75`. Not merged, not deployed — it goes to a gate with KS-1624's PR. **N2 and N5 stay open here**, as marked.

The summary at `routes/verification.ts:1445` now names `deleted` and `expired`. A new 5-cell source-text suite reads the route's source: three CONTROLs prove the instrument finds the one summary line and the exact status list; two RED cells require the summary to name `deleted` and `expired`.

**Evidence (mine):** red-first **3 passed / 2 failed of 5** (the two RED cells exactly; the tip's :1445 names `deleted` 0 times); green **5/5**; originate in full **1393/1393, 112 suites, 0 failed**; `tsc --noEmit` rc 0. Push: `PUSH_RC=0`, preflight 13/16 (3, 4, 8 skipped, local stack not up), nothing failed. The full shell runner was not re-run: every shell-suite input subtree is identical to develop's, whose tree read 91/91 on the #1578 merge.

**Coupling to N2, for whoever rules it:** the suite's CONTROL matches `lower(btrim(d.status)) NOT IN (` literally. If N2 is ruled to widen `btrim`, that CONTROL fails loudly and has to move with the change — it will not silently pass.

Provenance: Spark READY round 2 of 2; canonical `8ff6ac7d8d41e635`; applied change lines byte-identical to it.


*Edited: I first wrote that the suite "compares the summary with the SQL predicate". It does not — both are checked against hardcoded names, never against each other. Gate G3's S1 note showed it; detail in the merge comment below.*

**Appendix, recorded here on Wednesday's instruction (ANSWER of 2026-10-18T12:47:28Z) — a missing `packages/shared/dist/` turns most of a service's suites into load failures that read as a regression.**

Measured by me at 12:4xZ while gating this batch, in a fresh clone of `develop`:

- First run of the full originate suite on the merge tree read **81 of 111 suites failed, 322 tests, 10 failed**. That is not ten defects — it is 71 suites failing to **load**, every one `TS2307: Cannot find module '@secuura/shared'`. `tsc --noEmit` said the same thing on 29 lines.
- The full shell runner read **89 of 90**, the one failure being `ks949_main_seed_idempotence`, which names its own cause: *"FAIL — packages/shared is not built (…/packages/shared/dist/index.js missing) — run: npm run build -w packages/shared"*.
- Cause: `@secuura/shared` declares `main: dist/index.js`, `dist/` is gitignored, and `npm ci` here runs no scripts, so a fresh clone has no `dist/` at all and nothing says so up front.
- After `npm run build -w packages/shared` (rc 0, 3 s, 29 files), **the same commit and the same tree** read originate **1387/1387, 0 suites failed**, `tsc --noEmit` rc 0 / 0 lines, and the shell runner **90/90, rc 0**.

**The tell, for whoever hits this next:** `suites_failed` far exceeding the count of failing cells, and a test total well below what the gate reported. Ten named failing cells with 81 broken suites behind them is a load failure wearing a regression's clothes — the natural response is to debug the service, which is the wrong direction.

**It is not only my clone.** Gate F2's own report (§7) records the same suite failing for the same reason: *"ks949_main_seed_idempotence: packages/shared dist missing at that moment"*. So two independent clones hit it on the same day, and in the gate's report it was summarised as "environmental", which is true but under-describes it.

**On where this belongs.** Item 1 of `2_Project_Files/BACKLOG.md` already records the *stale* `dist/` case, and KS-1517 (**Done**) covers the *stale* case for the type-check ratchet specifically. Neither covers a **missing** `dist/` across a service's whole suite set. BACKLOG item 1 is arguably the better long-term home, but that file is outside this seat's brief partition, so I have not edited it. If this warrants its own ticket rather than an appendix here, that is a call for Wednesday or Kam — my view is that it does, because two clones hit it in one day and a backlog line has no owner.

title: Gate E1 follow-ups: KS-1545 logs nothing for an upstream error status; KS-1613 step() has no second-slash cell
description:
## BLUF

Gate E1 (the Opus tier-1 gate on PR #1570 / KS-1613 and PR #1572 / KS-1545 step 1, 2026-10-18, with a Fable 5.1 trial gate on the same PRs) passed both, and left two follow-ups. **First**, a gap in KS-1545 step 1's coverage: `GET /api/platform/audit-log` now logs when reading the platform half **throws**, but an upstream that **answers** with an error status, or a first window that is not a list or is `null`, still drops the platform half with **no log line** — so for those cases an operator still cannot tell an empty platform half from a dropped one. Not a regression: nothing was logged there before either. Also a NIT: the timeout warn carries the internal upstream URL. **Second**, a test gap in #1570 (KS-1613) that the Fable trial gate found: `step()`'s own suite has no header with a second `/` after the denominator, though 7 of the 16 live headers carry one.

## Recommendation

A small test-first change, briefed to the Spark queue (Wednesday briefs it), gated like any other — or folded into KS-1545 step 2 if Kam's ruling there reshapes the route:

1. Check `r.ok` (and a first window with no list) at `routes/platform.ts:421-423`, and log the same one warn line (route, cause, `windowsRead`) for an error status, with a cell per shape: a 500 with a JSON body, a 401 `{"success":false,"error":"No token provided"}` on the first window (the H13 class), a first window that is not a list, and a JSON `null` body.
2. Decide whether the timeout warn should drop the internal URL's query (`?limit=&offset=`), or keep it and say so.
3. One cell in `scripts/__tests__/ks1547_preflight_step_header_denominator.test.sh` driving a header with a second `/` after the denominator (for example leg 8's `(/api/docs/openapi.json vs .yaml …)`), so `step()`'s own suite pins the non-greedy `${1#*/}`.

## Detail

* **MINOR M1:** `Blockchain/Dev/services/api-gateway/src/routes/platform.ts:421-423` **(the warn is only at** `:435`**, in the catch).** The gate's probe sent four upstream replies that empty the platform half without a throw: an HTTP 500 with a JSON body; an HTTP 401 `{"success":false,"error":"No token provided"}` on the first window; a first window whose body is not a list; a JSON `null` body. Each gave HTTP 200 with the `audit_logs` rows only and **no log line**, on develop and on the PR alike. `r.ok` is never checked, and a first window with no list is treated as an empty list. KS-1545's aim is met for connection refusals, timeouts, bodies that are not JSON and a later window that is not a list; not for an upstream that answers an error status.
* **NIT N3:** `platform.ts:435`**, the logged** `error` **text.** When the body is not JSON, V8's SyntaxError quotes up to 20 characters of the upstream body (longer bodies are cut to 10); the timeout text carries the internal upstream URL with `?limit=&offset=` (`Upstream timed out after 400ms: http://127.0.0.1:<port>/api/audit-log?limit=50&offset=0`). The caller's token, the request body, the rows and `err.cause` appear in no log call in any of the gate's 10 probe modes. Same expression as the KS-1510 precedent at `:1064`.
* **MINOR (#1570, test strength), from the Fable 5.1 trial gate:** `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/__tests__/ks1547_preflight_step_header_denominator.test.sh:56-97`**.** No cell drives a step header with a second `/` after the denominator, though 7 of the 16 live headers carry one (legs 3, 8, 10, 12, 13, 14, 16). The mutant `${1#*/}` -> `${1##*/}` on `preflight.sh:225` survives the suite 12/12 and is **not** equivalent: against the live headers it aborts those 7, i.e. every push. The Opus gate's reading of the same mutant (its PM4) is that only a different suite, `preflight_deps`, kills it; the two agree that `step()`'s own suite does not. Fable verdict: `/Volumes/DevMASTER/WEDNESDAY/0_Brain/reference/2026-10-18_gate-E1-pr1570-pr1572/fable/verdict.md`, sha256/16 `6af5896fb794a797` (line 3 deleted).

**Source:** the gate E1 verdict, `/Volumes/DevMASTER/WEDNESDAY/0_Brain/reference/2026-10-18_gate-E1-pr1570-pr1572/opus/verdict.md` (Wednesday's project), sha256/16 `cc91eb9abeaa70f0` computed with line 3 deleted. PRs: [#1572](<https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/1572>) (KS-1545 step 1), [#1570](<https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/1570>) (KS-1613 items 1+2).

**Why its own ticket, not KS-1621:** KS-1621 holds test gaps in originate's failed-anchor writer and api-gateway's document-types catch; the main item here is a product logging gap in the platform audit route, a different logical path. The #1570 test gap rides here because Wednesday ruled it into the same ticket as M1 (ADDENDUM 2026-10-18T11:24:40Z).

**Dedupe before filing:** over all 1,610 team issues including archived, 0 hits each for `Gate E1`, `platform.ts:42x`, `platform.ts:435`, `r.ok … not checked`, an audit-log error status, `Upstream timed out after`. Controls on the same data: the KS-1545 title phrase 1 hit (KS-1545), `Gate E2` 1 hit (KS-1621).

Filed by Seat R 47th on Wednesday's GO of 2026-10-18T11:21:08Z. Not built this session.

**BLUF:** PR 2033 is merged to develop as 45d2edc73aa989b95166c74253ab415c44ee168e, at 2026-11-06T03:27:00Z (read from the PR API). It adds the log line for a first audit-log window that answers 2xx without a list (comment d10b6188). The api-gateway deploy is owed, both boxes; demo is frozen. This ticket stays In Progress: item 2 (the timeout warn text) is undecided and item 3 (a scripts test cell) is another lane.

- What merged (PR API, four files): `Blockchain/Dev/services/api-gateway/src/routes/platform.ts` (+2 lines), the test `Blockchain/Dev/services/api-gateway/src/__tests__/ks1622c-platform-audit-log-logs-a-first-window-that-is-not-a-list.test.ts` (+133), and two Projects Documents fragments.
- Read at source by Seat S 27th (own shallow clone, read only, not run): the squash diff of `routes/platform.ts` is 2 added lines and 0 removed, a comment and one guard. The guard is `if (r.ok && collected.length === 0 && !Array.isArray(data?.entries))` and it writes one warn, "GET /api/platform/audit-log upstream answered a first window that is not a list", with the status and windowsRead, after the body is read. No other line of that file changes.
- Not on the Kintsugi pin Wednesday names (Seat D 56th's e174f5eb488a): in my clone that pin is an ancestor of this squash (rc 0) and this squash is not an ancestor of the pin (rc 1), so the pin does not carry this change. What Kintsugi actually runs, I did not read.
- Deploy owed: api-gateway, both boxes. Demo is frozen (Kam's card secuura-ks1401-058-merge-demo-billing-1104). Nothing is deployed by me or by this comment.
- NOT covered: I ran no test; the four platform suites were not run; no box, Kintsugi or demo state was read.

**BLUF:** PR 2033 (head `c3cb692fe4c7`, one commit on develop `85046e870`) is raised for a shape of this ticket's first item that was not fixed: a first window that answers 2xx with a body that is not a list. Nothing is merged or deployed.

- **The gap, measured on develop:** a first window answering 200 with `entries` a string, no `entries`, or a JSON `null` logged nothing, and the route answered 200 with the `audit_logs` rows only. The merge comment 832b5fc6 on this ticket said the four shapes gate E1 probed were fixed; for these three shapes that did not hold (cells F1 to F3 are red by assertion on develop).
- **The change:** one `warn` line after the body is read (route, status, `windowsRead`; never the body), only when `r.ok`, so an error status still logs exactly one line. A genuinely empty list stays silent. The response is unchanged.
- **Proof, run by Seat T 13th:** 3 of 6 new cells red on develop, 6/6 with the change; the four neighbouring audit-log files 33/33; nine tampers, 9 killed; api-gateway suite 158 files, 1660/1660.
- **Not covered:** Node 24, a real upstream, any box.
- **This ticket stays In Progress** (the pull request says `Refs`): item 2 (the timeout warn text) is undecided, item 3 (a scripts test cell) is another lane, and the api-gateway deploy is owed.

**BLUF: PR #1681 makes `GET /api/platform/audit-log` log a LATER paging window that answers an error status but still carries a list: the "fourth shape" recorded here on 2026-10-19. Not merged, not deployed.**

Before this, a second or later window answering 500 or 503 with an `entries` list was appended with no log line, so a degrading upstream looked healthy from the logs. One guarded line after the not-a-list throw now writes one warn with the status and `windowsRead`, never the upstream body.

- **Where:** PR #1681, branch `feature/ks-1622-log-a-later-audit-log-window-error-status` (the ticket's suggested branch name was already taken by merged #1629's branch), head `b5cc01ddcb2a`.
- **What changed:** 2 added lines in `api-gateway/src/routes/platform.ts` (a comment and the guard), one new test file with 6 cells. First-window behaviour, the throw and the catch are unchanged.
- **Env:** none touched.

**Scope, as a narrowing.** Whether such a window should also DISCARD the platform half is a separate product decision and is not decided here. Items 2 and 3 of this ticket (the timeout-URL warn text, the `step()` header cell) are not touched. The fix deliberately avoids the natural shape (dropping `collected.length === 0` from the first-window guard): that would make a later window that is not a list log twice, and the existing cell E3 pins one warn.

Two gaps in the drafted cells, measured: a later 4xx is not pinned (narrowing the guard to `status >= 500` leaves all six green), and the control "healthy read in three windows" actually reads one window. A probe that closes both is written and green; it is not in the PR. Details in the PR body. `Refs`, not `Closes`.

**BLUF: a fourth shape of this same gap is still unlogged after #1629, and it is not a regression. An upstream error status on a LATER paging window, whose body still carries an `entries` array, is appended to the platform half with no warning and no error. Measured on the merged code, not inferred from the diff.**

Read at `88b8ceb9f3041672d9575b40c09869d45ab1c111`, `services/api-gateway/src/routes/platform.ts`, inside the paging loop that opens at **`:480`** (`while (collected.length < overfetch)`):

- **`:491`** — the line #1629 added: `if (!r.ok && collected.length === 0) logger.warn(…)`. The `collected.length === 0` half means it fires on the **first** window only, which is exactly what item 1 of this ticket asked for.
- **`:493`** — the pre-existing not-a-list throw: `if (collected.length > 0 && !Array.isArray(data?.entries)) throw …`. It is reached only when the body is **not** list-shaped.
- **`:496`** — `collected.push(...rowsInWindow)`.

So a second or later window that answers, say, HTTP 500 with `{"entries":[…]}` passes `:491` (because `collected.length > 0`) and passes `:493` (because the body **is** a list), and its rows are pushed at `:496`. The caller gets HTTP 200 and an operator gets no line for it.

**Not a regression.** Before #1629 no error status was logged at any position, first window included. #1629 strictly improved the first window and changed nothing about later ones.

**Not fixed.** I am recording it rather than widening #1629's merged scope after its security review.

**If it is taken up,** the natural shape is to drop the `collected.length === 0` guard at `:491` so the warn fires at any position, and decide separately whether a later error status should also *discard* the platform half the way a not-a-list window does — those are two different behaviours and the second one is a product decision, not a logging one.

**BLUF: item 1 is fixed and merged. `GET /api/platform/audit-log` now writes one warning line when the upstream answers an error status on its first window, so an operator can tell a dropped platform half from an empty one. Items 2 and 3 of this ticket are untouched and stay open. Nothing is deployed.**

Merged as `88b8ceb9f3041672d9575b40c09869d45ab1c111` on `develop` (PR #1629, squashed, one parent `390cc0a317c9`). The tree that landed is `985fd9f982a8c4bc987258cb6a99086a72958a79` — the exact tree the security review required before the merge, re-measured on live `develop` afterwards. Two files: the route, plus a new 137-line test file.

**What changed, in one line of product code.** `services/api-gateway/src/routes/platform.ts` checks the upstream response status before it reads the body, and logs the route, the status and the number of windows already read. The four shapes gate E1 probed — an HTTP 500 with a JSON body, a 401 `No token provided`, a first window that is not a list, and a JSON `null` body — each used to give HTTP 200 with the `audit_logs` rows only and **no log line at all**.

**What this does NOT cover, stated plainly.** The guard is "nothing collected yet", so it is the **first** window only, which is what item 1 asked for. A **later** window whose status is an error but whose body still carries an `entries` array is appended with no warning. A later window that is not a list already throws and is logged by the existing catch. This is not a regression — before this change no error status was logged at any position — and it is not fixed here. I read the loop at the merged commit to confirm it rather than inferring it from the diff.

**Review residue (gate AR1, Sonnet, tier 2 — GO WITH NOTE, zero blockers, three notes).**
1. A non-JSON error body now produces **two** warning lines, the new one and then the catch. Both statements are true, so this is extra log volume, not a wrong reading.
2. The catch's message carries roughly ten characters of a non-JSON upstream body. That is V8's own `JSON.parse` text and predates this change.
3. No test pins that double-warning.

**Still open on this ticket, which is why the merge says `Refs` and not a closing keyword:**
- **Item 2** — whether the timeout warning should drop the internal upstream URL's `?limit=&offset=` query, or keep it and say so. Undecided.
- **Item 3** — one cell in `scripts/__tests__/ks1547_preflight_step_header_denominator.test.sh` driving a step header with a second `/` after the denominator, so `step()`'s own suite pins the non-greedy `${1#*/}`. 7 of the 16 live headers carry one.

Nothing was deployed and no environment was touched.

title: Security review — findings register (Platform S), successor to PS-175
description:
**BLUF:** This is the live index of platform-s security findings since the July review closed. It is the platform-s counterpart of [KS-485](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-485/security-review-plan-methodology-and-handover-platform-k), and it takes over from [PS-175](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-175/security-review-plan-methodology-and-handover-platform-s), which is archived and can no longer take comments. **A14 (High) is fixed on round 13 but not yet on** `develop`**, so dev-ps and UAT may still be exposed. A7 (Low) is partly open. A1–A6 and A8–A13 are fixed by #1064, on** `develop` **since 17 Oct 2026 (register corrected 5 Nov 2026).** Owner: Stuart. Peter owns systemTest coverage.

## Summary matrix

| Stream | Area | High | Med | Low | Open tickets | July review ticket |
| -- | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- |
| **A** | AuthN / AuthZ / tenancy & IDOR | **1** (A14, until it reaches `develop`) | 0 | **1** (A7, partly) | [PS-1286](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1286/auth-external-sign-in-entra-google-apple-github-a-cancel-at-google) | [PS-176](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-176/review-a-authn-authz-tenancy-and-idor) |
| B | Input validation, injection, upload & crypto | 0 | 0 | 0 | — | [PS-177](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-177/review-b-input-validation-injection-file-upload-and-crypto) |
| C | S↔K integration | 0 | 0 | 0 | — | [PS-178](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-178/review-c-sk-integration-security) |
| D | Payments & webhooks | 0 | 0 | 0 | — | [PS-179](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-179/review-d-payments-and-webhooks-stripepaypal) |
| E | Deployment, containers & CI/CD | 0 | 0 | 0 | — | [PS-180](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-180/review-e-deployment-containers-and-cicd-supply-chain) |
| F | Edge, WAF, DDoS & anti-automation | 0 | 0 | 0 | — | [PS-181](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-181/review-f-edge-waf-ddos-and-anti-automation) |

## Findings and actions

All paths are under `ssd/`. The evidence is at develop `7cb1a4e1` (2026-10-16), and the detail is on each ticket.

| ID | Sev | Problem | Action | Where | Ticket | Status |
| -- | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- |
| A1 | Med | Cancelling at Google, GitHub or Apple shows "sign-in failed, contact your administrator" | **Classify** a cancel from `Exception.Data["error"]` as well as from the message | `Services/Security/ExternalAuthFailureMapper.cs` | [PS-1286](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1286/auth-external-sign-in-entra-google-apple-github-a-cancel-at-google) | Fixed (PR #1064) |
| A2 | Med | The unit test pins a message the framework never produces | **Replace** the fixture with the real .NET 8 string | `tests/ssd.UnitTests/ExternalAuthFailureMapperTests.cs` | [PS-1286](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1286/auth-external-sign-in-entra-google-apple-github-a-cancel-at-google) | Fixed (PR #1064) |
| A3 | Med | A missing client secret is found only at the first sign-in | **Check** the secret at startup: refuse to start for Entra, log and skip for Google and GitHub | `Startup.cs` | [PS-1286](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1286/auth-external-sign-in-entra-google-apple-github-a-cancel-at-google) | Fixed (PR #1064) |
| A4 | Med | The failure log keeps the exception's message but loses its type and stack | **Pass** `ctx.Failure` to the logger as the exception | `Services/Security/ExternalAuthFailureEvents.cs` | [PS-1286](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1286/auth-external-sign-in-entra-google-apple-github-a-cancel-at-google) | Fixed (PR #1064) |
| A5 | Med | No external cookie means a silent bounce to Login, with no reason in the log | **Log** the reason and the provider, and **show** the generic message | `Areas/Identity/Pages/Account/Login.cshtml.cs` | [PS-1286](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1286/auth-external-sign-in-entra-google-apple-github-a-cancel-at-google) | Fixed (PR #1064) |
| A6 | Low | The cancel message names Microsoft for every provider | **Name** the provider the user chose, or none | `Services/Security/ExternalAuthFailureMapper.cs` | [PS-1286](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1286/auth-external-sign-in-entra-google-apple-github-a-cancel-at-google) | Fixed (PR #1064) |
| A7 | Low | /AdminLogs can't join the lines of one sign-in | **Keep** the request id (scopes or `TraceIdentifier`) | `Services/Diagnostics/InMemoryLoggerProvider.cs:39` | [PS-1286](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1286/auth-external-sign-in-entra-google-apple-github-a-cancel-at-google) | **Partly open:** #1064 puts `TraceIdentifier` in the external sign-in failure lines, but the provider still drops scopes (`BeginScope` returns `NullScope`), so other lines carry no request id |
| A8 | Low | The unlinked legacy `ExternalLogin` page shows the raw error and can throw a NullReferenceException | **Route** it through the shared mapper | `Areas/Identity/Pages/Account/ExternalLogin.cshtml.cs` | [PS-1286](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1286/auth-external-sign-in-entra-google-apple-github-a-cancel-at-google) | Fixed (PR #1064) |
| A9 | Low | The result of re-linking a login is ignored | **Log** the result when it fails | `Areas/Identity/Pages/Account/Login.cshtml.cs` | [PS-1286](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1286/auth-external-sign-in-entra-google-apple-github-a-cancel-at-google) | Fixed (PR #1064) |
| A10 | High | `SendDocsLinksAdmin/Create`, open to every tier, wrote a share link for any posted document id with no ownership check | **Apply** the Share page's direct-sharing rule, and answer not found | `SendDocsLinksAdmin` | This ticket's 17 Oct comment | Fixed (PR #1064) |
| A11 | High | `SendDocsLinksAdmin/Edit` re-pointed an own link at any document id | **Apply** the same rule | `SendDocsLinksAdmin` | This ticket's 17 Oct comment | Fixed (PR #1064) |
| A12 | Med | `/identity/credentials/panel/{id}` listed any document's credentials | **Apply** `DocumentReadAccess`; Administrators exempt | Identity credentials panel | This ticket's 17 Oct comment | Fixed (PR #1064) |
| A13 | Med | `DocumentTransactionsAdmin` let any Power user see every organisation's ledger | **Hold** non-Administrators to their own organisation | `DocumentTransactionsAdmin` | This ticket's 17 Oct comment | Fixed (PR #1064) |
| A14 | High | External sign-up used the posted address, so anyone with a provider account could link to and sign in to another person's account | **Read** the address from the external cookie only | `Areas/Identity/Pages/Account/ExternalSignup.cshtml.cs` | [PS-1572](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1572>) | Fixed on round 13 (PR #1380), **not yet on** `develop` |

**Done means:** each action is backed by an xUnit test that fails on today's code and passes after. These are rules, so they belong in xUnit, not Playwright.

## Next steps

| \# | Who | Step |
| -- | -- | -- |
| 1 | Stuart | Decide whether A7's remainder is worth doing: keep the request id on every /AdminLogs line, or accept that only the external sign-in failure lines carry it. |
| 2 | Peter | Check whether any systemTest spec relies on the old cancel copy, and update it. |

## Adding a finding

1. Raise the finding as its own ticket.
2. Add one row per finding to the table above: next ID in its stream, severity, problem, action (one verb in bold), file:line, ticket.
3. Update the counts in the summary matrix.
4. When a fix merges, set its rows to **Fixed (PR #n)**. Don't delete them.

## Background

The July review ([PS-175](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-175/security-review-plan-methodology-and-handover-platform-s), with streams [PS-176](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-176/review-a-authn-authz-tenancy-and-idor) to [PS-181](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-181/review-f-edge-waf-ddos-and-anti-automation) and G1–G4) and its project "Security Review — Platform S" were completed and archived on 22 Jul 2026. Its scope, threat model and methodology still apply. This register keeps its stream letters, so a new finding sits under the stream it would have belonged to. [PS-175](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-175/security-review-plan-methodology-and-handover-platform-s) is named here without a formal link, because a link to an archived ticket is silently dropped.

nodes.body: Merged to develop on Stuart's instruction (17 Oct): #1064 as `a98a220`.

**systemTest:** #1064's changes were run inside #1065 (full run 2,832 passed / 22 failed, join-seam 11/11). Nothing in this ticket's scope failed. Results: https://github.com/Secuura/platform-s/pull/1064#issuecomment-6231249783

**Correction (Stuart, 17 Oct 2026): no production hotfix is needed.** No production is live at the moment. Production will be deployed later, from develop, so A10–A13 reach it through #1064 like any other change. Disregard my earlier note about a release-branch hotfix.

**Production exposure, A10 (checked 17 Oct 2026):** `origin/release/production-Apr-4-26`, which production runs, has the same `SendDocsLinksAdmin/Create`.
- It has no ownership check: `DocumentStoreId = vm.SelectedDocumentId`, inserted as posted.
- The controller is limited to `Administrator` or `SsdManager`. `SsdManager` is the ordinary Power-user tier there, so any such user can mint a link to any organisation's document.
- That version also accepts a **client-supplied token**.

#1064 fixes develop only. Production needs a release-branch hotfix, which is Stuart's decision; nothing has been done there.

**New findings, 17 Oct 2026: four cross-organisation leaks.** They were found by the PS-1288 Q9 route audit, confirmed in the code, and fixed in https://github.com/Secuura/platform-s/pull/1064 (not merged yet).

| ID | Sev | Problem | Fix |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| A10 | **High** | `SendDocsLinksAdmin/Create`, open to every tier, wrote a share link for any posted document id with no ownership check and showed the token. Any signed-in user could mint a working view-and-download link to another organisation's document by id. | The Share page's direct-sharing rule (`DirectShareRights`), plus a "not found" answer. |
| A11 | **High** | `SendDocsLinksAdmin/Edit` re-pointed an own link at any document id. | The same rule. |
| A12 | Med | `/identity/credentials/panel/{id}` had no entitlement check; it lists any document's credentials when Identity is enabled. | `DocumentReadAccess` (Lineage's read rule); Administrators exempt. |
| A13 | Med | `DocumentTransactionsAdmin`: the DevTools-diagnostic policy admits SsdPowerUser in every environment, and every action bypassed the tenant filter. Any Power user could see every organisation's ledger, including recipient emails. | Non-Administrators are held to their own organisation. |

**Exposure:** UAT and dev-ps run develop. Production runs the older release branch, which is not checked here.

**Tests:** `CrossOrganisationLeakTests`, 5 cases red on develop.

title: auth social sign-in (Google / Microsoft / Apple): failures in a live environment can't be diagnosed — config is skipped silently, provider detail isn't logged, the raw provider response reaches the client — and Apple can't complete at all
description:
**BLUF:** If social sign-in were turned on in a live environment today, most failures would be hard to diagnose. A half-configured provider just vanishes. The provider's own explanation is thrown away. Logs from the gateway and the auth service can't be joined up. Separately, Sign in with Apple cannot complete at all, and its identity token is never verified. Nothing is exposed today, because the code itself notes that no deployment configures any provider (`routes/auth.ts:951-952`). That's why this is Medium. It should be fixed before any provider is switched on. Thank you, Kamil. The callback is already well defended: the state ordering, account gate, no-email refusal and the reasoning in [KS-722](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-722/security-social-sign-in-never-verifies-the-oauth-state-and-links-an) / [KS-795](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-795/ks-781-door-2-the-social-callback-account-linking-branch-mints-a) / [KS-819](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-819/ks-722-follow-up-the-oauth-state-is-consumed-before-the-request-is) all hold up. These findings are about **diagnosability and completeness**, not those decisions. Found by reading the code at develop `76698952a` (2026-10-16). Nothing was run against a live stack. Line numbers are against that commit, under `Blockchain/Dev/services/auth/src/`. ## Scope * **Microsoft is personal accounts only.** `/consumers` is hardcoded (`providers/social/microsoft-personal.ts:21, :25`) and there's no tenant setting. **Entra workforce sign-in is not implemented** in platform-k. Entra appears only in the KYC Verified-ID client. Whether workforce sign-in is wanted here is a product decision, not a defect. It's noted so nobody assumes it exists. * **No frontend uses social sign-in.** No file under `frontend/` calls `/api/auth/social`. ## Per-provider matrix | Check | Google | Microsoft (personal) | Apple | Entra workforce | | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- | | Implemented | Yes | Personal accounts only (`/consumers` hardcoded) | Partly | **No** | | Missing or half-set config | Skipped silently, not logged (`provider-factory.ts:39`) | Same | Same; no team ID, key ID or private-key config exists | n/a | | Redirect URI | `FRONTEND_URL` or a silent `localhost:8882` fallback (`:53`) | Same | Same | n/a | | Provider `?error=` | Generic 400 `OAUTH_PROVIDER_ERROR`; `error` logged, `error_description` dropped (`auth.ts:1011-1018`) | Same | **Unreachable**: Apple POSTs the response, only GET exists (`apple.ts:17`, `auth.ts:967`) | n/a | | State check | Yes, 403 `OAUTH_STATE_INVALID` (`auth.ts:1023-1026`) | Yes | Yes (once reachable) | n/a | | Nonce | None | None | None | n/a | | Token exchange failure | 400 that **includes the provider's raw response** (`google.ts:40`, `auth.ts:1032-1034`) | Same (`microsoft-personal.ts:39`) | Same (`apple.ts:38`) | n/a | | Client secret | Static (correct) | Static (correct) | Static; **Apple requires a signed ES256 JWT** (`apple.ts:30`) | n/a | | Identity source | userinfo over TLS (no ID-token check needed) | Graph `/me` over TLS | **ID token decoded without verification** (`apple.ts:42-44`) | n/a | | Email verified | From `verified_email` | **Hardcoded** `true` (`microsoft-personal.ts:58`) | From the token's `email_verified` claim | n/a | | Profile-fetch failure | Generic message, no HTTP status (`google.ts:50`) | Same (`microsoft-personal.ts:49`) | n/a | n/a | | Request ID on error logs | No: auth mints its own and ignores the gateway's (`requestLogger.ts:12`), and error and warn lines don't carry it | Same | Same | n/a | | User-facing result | Raw JSON from a browser redirect target (`auth.ts:1271`); no frontend | Same | Same | n/a | | Diagnostics endpoint | `GET /social/providers` lists names only (`auth.ts:921-924`) | Same | Same | n/a | ## A. Diagnosability (the question asked) 1. **Missing config is skipped silently.** * A provider whose `SOCIAL_

_CLIENT_ID` or `_CLIENT_SECRET` is unset returns `null` and is dropped with no log line (`providers/social/provider-factory.ts:39`). * When `FRONTEND_URL` is unset, the callback base quietly becomes `http://localhost:8882` (`:53`), so a deployed host would send providers a localhost redirect URI. * Nothing logs the enabled set at startup. 2. **The provider's explanation is discarded.** On `?error=`, only `error` is logged, trimmed to 200 characters (`routes/auth.ts:1011-1018`). `error_description` is not logged. That field is where providers say *which* thing is wrong, for example a redirect-URI mismatch or an unauthorised client. Not echoing it to the browser is right (errorHandler.ts §OAuthProviderError); not logging it is the gap. 3. **Profile-fetch failures lose the HTTP status.** Both read only "Failed to fetch … user profile" (`providers/social/google.ts:50`, `microsoft-personal.ts:49`). 4. **Request IDs don't join up across services.** * The gateway mints or forwards `X-Request-ID` (`api-gateway/src/index.ts:451`, `routes/proxy.ts:248`). * The auth service ignores the incoming header and mints its own (`middleware/requestLogger.ts:12`). * Neither the global error log (`middleware/errorHandler.ts:259-264`) nor the social `logger.warn` lines carry the ID. 5. **The only diagnostic surface is** `GET /social/providers`**.** It lists enabled names, never why one is disabled (`routes/auth.ts:921-924`). 6. **Browser-facing errors are raw JSON.** The callback is a browser redirect target, but it answers with JSON tokens or a JSON error (`routes/auth.ts:1271`) rather than redirecting to a frontend route with `?error=`. ## B. Security-relevant (the [KS-486](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-486/review-a-authn-authz-tenancy-and-idor) class) 7. **The provider's raw token-endpoint response reaches the client.** Each `exchangeCode` throws with `await tokenRes.text()` (`google.ts:40`, `apple.ts:38`, `microsoft-personal.ts:39`). The route then puts that message into the 400 it returns (`routes/auth.ts:1032-1034`). This is the same "log, never echo" principle that F-4 already applies to `?error=`. 8. **The Apple ID token is not verified.** * The payload is base64-decoded and `JSON.parse`d with no signature, `iss`, `aud` or `exp` check and no JWKS fetch (`apple.ts:42-44`). * It uses `base64`, not `base64url`. * It throws a TypeError if `id_token` is absent. 9. **No nonce is used by any provider** (`getAuthUrl` in all three). 10. `microsoft-personal` **hardcodes** `emailVerified: true` (`microsoft-personal.ts:58`). The auto-link path already distrusts it (`routes/auth.ts:1119-1129`, `mayAutoLinkByEmail`), but a newly created account is stored with `emailVerified: profile.emailVerified` (`routes/auth.ts:1166`), which is therefore always `true`. ## C. Apple cannot complete 11. **The callback route doesn't match Apple's response mode.** Apple is asked for `response_mode=form_post` (`apple.ts:17`), so Apple POSTs the callback. Only `GET /social/:provider/callback` exists (`routes/auth.ts:967`), so the handler is never reached. 12. **The client secret is static.** Apple requires an ES256-signed client secret JWT (team ID, key ID, `.p8` key) that expires within six months. The code posts `SOCIAL_APPLE_CLIENT_SECRET` as-is (`apple.ts:30`), and no team ID, key ID or private-key setting exists anywhere in the repo. ## Already recorded elsewhere (one line each) * Social IDs are never persisted (`routes/auth.ts:1135-1146`, `1180-1187`). It's recorded in the service's BACKLOG.md per those comments, but I couldn't find a Linear ticket for it. Happy to raise one if you'd like it tracked separately. ## Suggested done-when (your call on the shape) * Startup logs each provider as enabled, disabled or half-configured, with key names only and never values. An unset `FRONTEND_URL` in a non-local environment fails loudly. * `error_description` and profile-fetch status are logged server-side. Neither the provider's token response nor `error_description` reaches the client. * The incoming `X-Request-ID` is reused in auth and appears on error and social log lines. * Apple either works (POST callback, signed client secret, verified ID token) or is removed from `PROVIDER_MAP` until it does. * Each fix is backed by a test that fails on today's code and passes after.

nodes.body:
**BLUF:** Delivered: PRs 1604 and 1603 merged as 618d720ec370 and 9b90f8ac7753 on develop, deployed to kintsugi at b1fb543640e7 (recorded deploy, 2026-11-01). Verified by code read at b1fb543640e7, not observed live (it needs a provider failure on a configured sign-in). Left open: the ticket's other items, including Apple.

- **Items A.2 and A.3 are in the code:** `Blockchain/Dev/services/auth/src/routes/auth.ts:1061` logs the provider's `error_description` (capped at 200 characters) beside its error on the callback, and `Blockchain/Dev/services/auth/src/providers/social/google.ts:83-84` (and `microsoft-personal.ts`) log the refused token endpoint's status and bound the body, throwing an error that names the HTTP status. `ks1617-social-profile-fetch-failure-names-the-http-status.test.ts` pins A.3.
- **Left open, per the ticket's own done-when list and comment 97616cf7:** Apple's identity token is still decoded without a signature, `aud`, `iss` or `exp` check (`Blockchain/Dev/services/auth/src/providers/social/apple.ts:86-88`), and Apple cannot complete a sign-in; the startup provider status log and the `FRONTEND_URL` check are not part of these two PRs (not re-read in the code here).

**BLUF:** evidence for this ticket's "Apple's identity token is never verified", from the tier-1 gates on #1788 (KS-1240 part 2, the social sign-in timeouts). Not fixed there; it is out of that PR's scope. No new ticket is filed, because this one already covers it.

* **What the code does.** At #1788's head `7eeedb825c5c`, `services/auth/src/providers/social/apple.ts:86-89` reads `tokens.id_token` and decodes its middle segment with `JSON.parse(Buffer.from(tokens.id_token.split('.')[1], 'base64').toString())`.
  * The signature is never checked: no JWKS, no `aud`, `iss` or `exp` check.
  * `sub` and `email` from that payload become the profile.
* **What trust rests on.** TLS to appleid.apple.com alone. The token arrives on the service's own back-channel request to Apple's token endpoint, not through the browser.
* **Found by** reading the adapter (gate 5 finding 1788-7, carried into gate 7). Not executed against Apple.
* **Related:** the same gates' finding 1788-10 is filed as KS-1791, a provider's non-JSON 200 leaking text through the callback.

## Items A.2 and A.3 MERGED — and two things this ticket keeps

Both landed on gate Q1's GO, five-point 5/5 each, landed tree equal to prediction:

| item | PR | merged as |
|---|---|---|
| A.3 — the profile-fetch failure names the HTTP status | [#1603](https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/1603) | `9b90f8ac77532141624a2c5892a0b47074e01427` |
| A.2 — the callback logs the provider's `error_description` | [#1604](https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/1604) | `618d720ec3704251951ba19a4c7f1d85ebfc414d` |

Both `Refs`; this ticket stays open. A.3's five cells and A.2's three cells are in `services/auth`, which reads **1078** on the chained tree per the gate's run (it ran the integration suites my own evidence lacked).

## 1. A pre-existing disclosure this ticket should own: the token-endpoint error body

A.3's new text — `(HTTP 503)` on a profile-fetch failure — **does reach the user's browser.** I reported the brief's premise as wrong rather than answering the question as asked: `routes/auth.ts:1032-1035` re-raises the adapter's message as a `BadRequestError`, and `middleware/errorHandler.ts:293` writes `message: err.message` into the body with `res.status` at `:300`.

**Wednesday ruled it ships as is, and the reasoning is the finding:** the same 400 **already carries the provider's whole token-endpoint error body** — `google.ts:39-40` and **five sibling adapters** — which is **larger and pre-existing**. A.3 therefore adds strictly less than what is already disclosed there.

**That pre-existing body echo is now the open question on this ticket.** It was not touched by either PR. Worth deciding deliberately: a provider's raw token-endpoint error body in a 400 is a bigger surface than a status code, and nothing currently bounds it the way A.2 bounds `error_description` at 200 characters.

## 2. A.2's no-echo behaviour is RIGHT but NOT PINNED by #1604

I offered cell **A2-3**'s assertion that the raw response contains neither value as evidence that `error_description` is not echoed to a response. **The gate's reading is that A2-3 does not prove it** — A2-3 drives a cancel with **no description at all**, so the absence it observes is trivially true. The gate's own probe is what establishes the behaviour.

So: the behaviour is correct, `errorHandler.ts:190` documents the intent, and **there is no cell pinning it.** A follow-up, not a hold — but a cell that drives a callback *with* an `error_description` and asserts it is absent from the response body is the one that would notice if this ever changed.

## 3. Not in scope here, filed separately

**KS-1641** — a different service *does* echo the field: `services/m365-integration/src/index.ts:465` reflects unbounded provider `error_description` into a redirect URL, and all five of that file's admin redirects target a route the admin SPA does not have.

---

*Seat R 51st, 2026-10-19. Item A.1 and the rest of this ticket's scope are untouched. Nothing deployed.*

title: KS-1542 follow-up (PR #1554 gate): Map/Set/RegExp/Error print {}, {toJSON:()=>1} prints an accepted bound, String() throws before the catch, and a [1n] cell would kill the surviving catch mutant
description:
## BLUF

Follow-up to **KS-1542** (merged as `18de4b7ce` via PR #1554). The Opus gate found **no product defect against the stated goal**: every probed object shape is still REFUSED, and arrays and plain objects now print as JSON. It found **LOW message-fidelity items and one test gap**. All are capped at LOW because **no production caller passes** `originateForwardTimeoutMs`: `services/api-gateway/src/index.ts:898` builds the routes without it, so only tests or a future wiring can reach this message. Filed on Wednesday's ruling (GO of 2026-10-15T06:30:31Z).

Source: gate A verdict, `0_Brain/reference/2026-10-15_gate-A-pr1552-pr1554/verdict.md` in Wednesday's project, report sha256/16 `a99632143f942387`.

## The items (from the verdict; `services/api-gateway/src/routes/verification.ts` on develop after the merge)

1. **Information loss,** `:153-155`**.** `Map`, `Set`, `RegExp` and `Error` all print `{}`, losing both type and content, and they collide with a plain `{}`:
   * `new Map([['ms',800]])` printed `[object Map]` before;
   * `new Set([800])` printed `[object Set]`;
   * `/800/g` printed `/800/g`;
   * `Error('x')` printed `Error: x`.

   A config value from env, JSON or YAML cannot be one of these, so the impact is small. But for RegExp and Error it is a strict regression in wording.
2. **Collisions the new branch introduces,** `:155`**.**
   * An invalid `Date` prints `null`, the same text as a literal `null` refusal (it printed `Invalid Date` before).
   * `{toJSON: () => 1}` **prints** `1`**, the text of an ACCEPTED bound.** That breaks the PR's own stated invariant ("no refused bound may print what an accepted bound prints"); it printed `[object Object]` before.
   * `{toJSON: () => undefined}` prints `undefined` at runtime, although `shown` is typed `string`.
3. **Pre-existing, but the new catch looks like its cure and is not,** `:152`**.** `String(value)` runs BEFORE the object branch, so for `Object.create(null)` and a revoked Proxy, `String()` itself throws a `TypeError` that does not name `originateForwardTimeoutMs`. The value is still refused, but with the wrong message, and the try/catch at `:154-158` never gets the chance.
4. **Test gap.** Mutant M2 survived: the catch printing `String(value)` instead of `Object.prototype.toString.call(value)`. The only catch cell uses a plain-object cycle, where both give `[object Object]`. **A** `[1n]` **cell would kill it:** `String([1n])` is `1` (accepted text), and the type tag is `[object Array]`. The product comment names "a BigInt inside" as a reason for the catch, but no test covers it. Cells: `src/__tests__/ks1185-f1-workflow-approve-forward-bound-is-validated.test.ts:160-165`.

Also noted, not new: the message is unbounded (a 20,000-element array prints \~80 KB, before and after).

## Done when

The `{toJSON: () => 1}` case no longer prints an accepted bound's text, which is the PR's own invariant. A `[1n]` cell kills M2. The `String()` throw at `:152` either cannot happen or names the property. Item 1 is either pinned as acceptable or given a type-aware rendering.

title: package_format_gate.test.sh: five REAL-npm cells INTERMITTENT - red once in the full shell run (430/5), green twice run alone (435/0, develop and a branch)
description:
## BLUF

Five `REAL npm` cells in `systemTest/__tests__/package_format_gate.test.sh` went **red once** inside a full `npm run test:shell` run (**430 passed / 5 failed**), then **passed in both of two direct runs** (**435 passed / 0 failed**), one on develop and one on a branch. So the defect, if there is one, is **intermittent**, not "on develop". No harm today: these cells fail closed (a red refuses a push, it never lets one through). They are filed rather than dismissed because one red in three runs is not "flaky, proven", and a cell that reds without a code change will be read as a regression by whoever hits it next.

Filed by Seat R 45th (raise lane), 2026-10-15, on Wednesday's ruling (ANSWER 02:31:25Z, Q2 (ii)).

## The three runs

All three ran in one clone of `Secuura/Distributed_Secuura` on the same machine, with the same `node_modules` (`npm ci` rc 0, 1937 packages). Run 1 left `TMPDIR` to the runner's own handling; runs 2 and 3 set a short `TMPDIR=/tmp/r45ab` and unset git's local env.

| run | tree | how | package_format_gate |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| 1 | branch `762d044b0` (KS-1547: a one-line `preflight.sh` change; this suite does not read `preflight.sh`) | inside `npm run test:shell`, all 89 suites back to back, 02:15–02:24Z | **430 passed, 5 failed** |
| 2 | same branch, `762d044b0` | `bash systemTest/__tests__/package_format_gate.test.sh` alone, 02:25Z | **435 passed, 0 failed** |
| 3 | develop `e67e0dc1916b954a53c40db68ea81f0f905de641` | same, alone, 02:27Z | **435 passed, 0 failed** |

So the five did not reproduce on either tree when the suite ran on its own.

## The five cells, verbatim from run 1

```
FAIL REAL npm with a hanging postinstall: REFUSED as a timeout
       want "1/1", got "0/0"
FAIL ...no node_modules in the package, no stage
       want "no/0", got "yes/0"
FAIL ...so the listener was contacted and the script ran (the earlier 0 was the gate, not the fixture)
       want "1/yes", got "1/no"
FAIL the install's npm userconfig is the stage's private HOME, not the developer's ~/.npmrc
       want "1/0", got "0/0"
FAIL ...while it does see what npm and the shell need (PATH, npm_lifecycle_event, npm_config_cache)
       want "yes/yes/yes", got "no/no/no"
```

All five read `ok` in runs 2 and 3.

## What is and is not established

* **Established:** the five reds are not caused by the KS-1547 change. Runs 2 and 3 give the same result on its branch and on develop.
* **Not established:** the cause. Three readings fit, and I have not separated them:
  1. **Load or timing.** Every one of the five spawns a real `npm` and reads a timeout, a listener, or the staged env. Run 1 ran it as suite 60-something of 89 back to back, and the J-lane seat was live on the same machine.
  2. **Interference between suites.** Something an earlier suite leaves behind in run 1, such as a lingering listener, a port, an npm cache entry, or a leaked env var, could make the later suite misread.
  3. **The KS-1396 change.** KS-1396 (merged into develop as `e67e0dc1`) moved `systemTest` to TypeScript 7.0.2 and oxlint and removed ESLint there. It is the most recent change to this tree. **Named as a candidate only, not measured.** Runs 2 and 3 were on trees that already contain it and were green, so it is not enough on its own.

## What would settle it

Run the full `npm run test:shell` N times (N ≥ 5) on an idle machine and count the five cells. Then run `package_format_gate.test.sh` alone N times under a synthetic CPU load. If it reds only in the full run, the cause is interference between suites. If it reds alone under load, it is timing, and the fix is the cell's timeout margin.

## Related, not duplicates (searched first)

The search covered title and description, archived issues included, and was controlled: a fresh nonce returned 0 hits and `preflight_test_types_ratchet_leg` returned 3. `systemTest/__tests__/package_format_gate`, `hanging postinstall`, `REFUSED as a timeout`, `npm userconfig is the stage`, `npm_lifecycle_event`, `listener was contacted`, `no node_modules in the package` and `REAL npm` all returned **0**. `package_format_gate` returned **KS-1063** (Done, a different defect: a gate that examined nothing exits 0). `FORMAT_GATE_INSTALL` returned **KS-1583** (Backlog, the KS-998 item 1 gate's six Minors, a different defect).

KS-1605 Info 1 records two of this suite's cells failing when the fixture path holds a UUID: npm 11.5.1 refuses `npm config get userconfig` on a UUID-shaped value, giving 433/2. Measured against run 1 above:
