The UUID regex reads no on it. Control: the same regex fires on a path that does hold a UUID. The clone path holds none, and the suite mints none (`grep -ci uuid` on the suite = 0).
- **Five cells, not two.** Two of the five belong to Info 1's userconfig family: "npm userconfig is the stage's private HOME" and "...while it does see what npm and the shell need". The other three do not: the hanging-postinstall timeout, "no node_modules in the package, no stage", and "the listener was contacted".

title: Flow Sign step hides the signing error and shows the raw message (TSA URL included) — log it and use the Sign page's PS-891 wording
description:
## BLUF

When the flow engine's automatic **Sign** step fails, it logs nothing and shows the exception's raw text on the flow page. On 15 Oct 2026 (Stuart's local run on develop), Certify on `SDK-OVERVIEW.pdf` showed:

> Failed: PDF signing failed. TSA signing failed and fallback signing without TSA also failed. TsaUrl='[http://timestamp.digicert.com](<http://timestamp.digicert.com>)'.

Signing the same PDF from the Sign page also fails, so the PDF is the cause. But the flow path:

1. **Lost the real error.** `SignFlowOperation` catches `InvalidOperationException` and returns `Failed(ex.Message)` without logging. `PdfProcessingService.SignPdfBytesWithMaterial` also discards the fallback attempt's exception with a bare `catch`. No log line held the iText or certificate cause.
2. **Showed configuration detail to the user.** [PS-891](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-891/register-drop-zone-copy-omits-txt-accepted-and-viewable-by-decision-ps) removed exactly this from the Sign page (`Sign.cs` \~322-338).

## Status (16 Oct 2026)

| What | Where | State |
| -- | -- | -- |
| Fix | [Secuura/platform-s#1048](https://linear.app/secuura/review/flow-sign-step-log-signing-failures-and-show-the-sign-pages-sentence-8620d8cb94a7), merged into `project/platform-s-uxui-issues-r4` as `3236cca` | Merged |
| xUnit, this branch | `f0aaef4` (pre-push gate) | 8,111 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped |
| xUnit, round-4 with #1046 + #1048 + #1050 combined | round-4 tip `0c2bb31` (tree identical to the tested combination) | 8,141 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped |
| In the app, after the fix | — | **Not yet proven**: this is why the ticket is In Test. A signing failure in a Certify flow should show the fixed sentence on the flow page and log `Flow instance … failed to sign document …` with the exception. |
| systemTest on a slot | Belongs to the round-4 → `develop` PR #1030 | Not run |

Not in scope, left open: `WatermarkFlowOperation` has the same `catch (InvalidOperationException ex) → Failed(ex.Message)` shape (a follow-up is proposed). The "[PS-891](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-891/register-drop-zone-copy-omits-txt-accepted-and-viewable-by-decision-ps)" cited in the code comments looks miscited: Linear's [PS-891](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-891/register-drop-zone-copy-omits-txt-accepted-and-viewable-by-decision-ps) is a drop-zone copy ticket.

## Fix

* `SignFlowOperation` mirrors `Sign.cs`:
  * a `PdfOperationRefusedException` keeps its named sentence (`ex.UserMessage`), logged as a warning;
  * any other failure is logged as an error with the exception, and stores the fixed sentence "Signing failed. Please try again, and if it keeps failing, contact your administrator."
* `SignPdfBytesWithMaterial` keeps both attempts' exceptions, so the log shows why signing without TSA failed too.

## Acceptance

* **xUnit:** a generic signing failure stores the fixed sentence, never the TSA URL, and is logged with its exception; a refusal keeps its named sentence; the fallback wrapper carries both attempts' exceptions.

Found while reviewing [PS-1272](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1272/certify-flow-pauses-with-no-default-signing-certificate-is-set-for).

title: Certify flow pauses with "No default signing certificate is set for your organisation" although Organisation signing certificates shows a Default, Valid certificate — Continue does not pick it up
description:
## BLUF

**The reported defect was a timeline, not a bug.** The Certify flow's Sign step paused for "No default signing certificate…" at **07:29 JST on 15 Oct 2026**. The organisation's first (and only) certificate, FlindersUniversity, was uploaded by Iss One at **07:32 JST** (Certificates → Details: "Uploaded On 14 Oct 2026 at 22:32 UTC"). The first certificate an organisation uploads becomes its Default (`CertificateController.Upload`: `IsDefault = isFirstCertificate`). So the pause was correct when it happened, and a Continue after the upload picks the certificate up. Reproduced in the app on 15 Oct: Continue on instance 3 got past the certificate check.

**What was wrong is how Continue reported the result, and that is what shipped.** The engine returns `Advanced` whenever it settles a run, including one that paused again or failed. `FlowController.Continue` put every `Advanced` result in the **green success** banner. In the same reproduction, "Document not found or access denied." showed as a success message while the Sign step had failed. A Continue whose automatic step pauses or fails is now an error banner.

## Status

| What | Where | State |
| -- | -- | -- |
| Banner fix | [Secuura/platform-s#1046](https://linear.app/secuura/review/flow-a-continue-whose-automatic-step-pauses-again-or-fails-is-an-error-308fca3c6076), merged into `project/platform-s-uxui-issues-r4` as `e838385` | Merged |
| xUnit, this branch | `94500fa` | 8,120 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped |
| xUnit, round-4 with #1046 + #1048 + #1050 combined | round-4 tip `0c2bb31` (tree identical to the tested combination) | 8,141 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped |
| In the app, after the fix | — | **Not yet proven**: this is why the ticket is In Test |
| systemTest on a slot | Belongs to the round-4 → `develop` PR #1030 | Not run |

## What shipped

* `FlowAdvanceResult.StoppedOn`: `FlowService.DriveAsync` says which way the automatic step that stopped the drive ended (`Waiting` or `Failed`).
* `FlowContinueNotice` (`IsError`, `Text`): the banner rule. The wording is unchanged.
* `FlowController.Continue` uses it.

## Acceptance (revised 16 Oct 2026, to match the diagnosis)

* ✅ A Continue whose automatic step pauses again shows the pause reason in the **error** banner (xUnit: `FlowEngineTests`, `FlowControllerTests`, `FlowContinueNoticeTests`).
* ✅ A Continue whose automatic step fails shows the failure in the **error** banner (same tests, with `DocumentUnavailable`).
* ✅ A Continue that completes or moves the flow on keeps the green banner and its wording.
* ✅ With a Default, Valid certificate in place, Continue on a Sign step paused for a missing certificate gets past the certificate check (`FlowEngineTests.Sign_pauses_on_no_default_certificate_and_resumes_after_one_is_added`, and observed in the app on 15 Oct).
* ⬜ **In-app proof of the banner after the fix:** a Continue that re-pauses or fails shows the amber banner. Needed to move to Tested Not Deployed.

The original acceptance asked for an xUnit check that the Sign step's certificate lookup matches the Certificates page, and a Playwright spec for "pause → set a default → Continue → Certified". Both were written for a certificate bug that did not exist: the two paths read the same organisation through the same query (`SignFlowOperation.cs` \~117-122, `CertificateController.cs` 61, `OrganisationCertificateProvider.GetValidCertificatesForOrgAsync`). They are dropped here, not deferred.

## Found along the way (separate tickets)

* [PS-1273](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1273/flow-sign-step-hides-the-signing-error-and-shows-the-raw-message-tsa): the flow's Sign step hid the real signing error and showed the raw message, TSA URL included.
* [PS-1274](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1274/signing-fails-on-a-pdf-whose-cross-reference-table-itext-had-to): `SDK-OVERVIEW.pdf` could not be signed at all ("Append mode requires a document without errors").
* **Local data:** document 5's stored file (`test-02-letter.pdf`, registered 21 Sep) is not on this Mac's disk, so the Continue on 15 Oct failed instance 3 at Sign. That is an environment issue, not a product one.

## Original report (15 Oct 2026)

A Certify flow on `test-02-letter.pdf` showed **Sign: waiting**, with "No default signing certificate is set for your organisation. Add or choose one on the Certificates page, then press Continue.". Meanwhile Organisation signing certificates showed FlindersUniversity as **Default** and **Valid** (13 Feb 2026 – 13 Feb 2027, `C=AU, O=Secuura, CN=FlindersUniversity`). Steps: Register 21 Sep 14:24; Note skipped; Watermark skipped 15 Oct 07:29; Declaration done 15 Oct 07:29; Sign waiting. Stuart's local run on `develop` under VS Code.

nodes.body: **Covered by the round-4 develop PR run** ([#1030](https://github.com/Secuura/platform-s/pull/1030)), at r4 tip `0c2bb31`, which includes this ticket's PR. Full systemTest on slot 2 gave **2,732 passed / 33 failed / 166 skipped / 5 did not run**, and join-seam passed 11/11. Every failure is attributed on #1030: NoTc session age (re-run 26/26), Stripe listener absent, K defect KS-1402, and load timeouts that passed on a solo re-run. None is attributable to this change.

**Review of this ticket against `develop` at `d93a121`** (the build Stuart is running under VS Code). There's no PR or code for this ticket yet, so this checks the analysis above.

**What holds on develop**
- **Same organisation, same rule.** The Sign step and the Certificates page both look up the acting person, then use that person's organisation. Both apply the same rule: same organisation, not deleted, within the valid-from and expiry dates, flagged Default. The services involved are all per-request, and only one certificate provider is registered (`SignFlowOperation.cs:113-122`, `CertificateController.cs:61`, `OrganisationCertificateProvider.GetValidCertificatesForOrgAsync`).
- **Continue really re-runs a paused step.** `FlowGraph.IsReady` admits Waiting.

**What's different on develop**
- **The PS-1214 declarer route is only on the round-4 branch.** On develop, the step checks only owner, rights holder, or a live share. That candidate doesn't apply to this run.

**How to narrow it down**
If Continue re-runs the step as someone who isn't the owner, the rights holder or a share holder, the stored message changes to "…owner or rights holder". So if the no-certificate text stays after Continue, only two things fit. The banner Continue showed tells you which (`FlowController.cs:377-382`):
- **Green banner repeating the no-certificate sentence:** the step re-ran and found no valid Default certificate for the organisation of the person who pressed Continue. That's a data question: the presser's `Person.OrganisationId` compared with the certificate's `OrganisationId`.
- **Amber banner:** Continue was refused before the step ran, which is why the old text stayed. The banner will say one of three things:
  - "Only the person who started this flow or an organisation administrator can continue it." (`MayResume`)
  - "The flow's definition changed after this document started it." Editing Certify under Flow → Manage while an instance is running moves the definition on (`FlowVersioning.NextVersion`). After that, the instance can only be cancelled, never continued. Here the edit would have to be after 07:29 GMT+9 on 15 Oct.
  - "The document is no longer available."

Each time the step runs, the app logs `Flow instance {id} step sign (sign) -> Waiting: …`. If that line doesn't appear after Continue, the step never ran.

Two queries against that run's database would settle it. Its connection string is in a secrets file, which wasn't opened.

```sql
SELECT Id, OrganisationId, IsDefault, IsDeleted, NotBefore, NotAfter FROM OrganisationCertificate;
SELECT i.Id, i.OrganisationId, i.StartedByPersonId, i.DefinitionVersion, d.Version, r.ActorPersonId, r.FailureReason, r.Changed
FROM FlowInstance i JOIN FlowDefinition d ON d.Id = i.FlowDefinitionId
JOIN FlowStepRun r ON r.FlowInstanceId = i.Id AND r.StepKey = 'sign' WHERE r.Status = 'Waiting';
```

The `'Waiting'` filter assumes the status is stored as text; drop it if nothing comes back.

**Gaps in the acceptance criteria**
- **The proposed xUnit test would mostly pass today.** `FlowEngineTests.Sign_pauses_on_no_default_certificate_and_resumes_after_one_is_added` already covers pause → add a Default → Continue → Completed. But it uses a fake certificate provider (`FakeCerts`), so the real `OrganisationCertificateProvider` query is never compared with the Certificates page's query. The new test should run both against one database.
- **A minor wording problem.** When Continue re-runs the step and it pauses again, the engine returns `Advanced`, so the pause reason appears in the green success banner. That reads as if the flow moved on.

**Investigation paused (Stuart, 15 Oct): he will test this elsewhere.** Nothing has been committed or merged for this ticket.

**What's established from the round-4 code:**
- The Sign step and the Certificates page use the same organisation (the acting person's) and the same valid-dates rule.
- Continue re-runs a Waiting Sign step.

**Still open as candidates:**
- which person the step runs as: the PS-1214 declarer route, the person who started the flow, or the person pressing Continue;
- a Continue refused by `MayResume`, which leaves the old pause text showing;
- the data.

**The VS Code run's data:** it isn't in the native `ssddb`, which holds no organisation certificates and has no activity since 8 Oct.

title: Akto suppressions and exclusions: one cites the wrong ticket (KS-442 → KS-510), and two coverage trade-offs (VOLATILE_PATH_RE, 8 built-in data-exposure templates) have no ruling or owner
description:
**BLUF:** the [KS-1478](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1478/akto-image-2371-2383-release-v2383-2026-10-13-testing-image-has-no) audit of every rule that stops an Akto result from counting checked each one against the ticket it cites. Most stand and are no wider than their ruling: [KS-308](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-308/akto-scans-report-100percent-skipped-tests-testing-container-cant), [KS-323](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-323/akto-after-ks-314-drive-connectivity-skip-bucket-to-0-confirm-mongo)/324, [KS-397](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-397/are-apidocument-types-and-apioauthscopes-intentionally-public-or)/364, [KS-719](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-719/security-put-apiprivacysettings-and-apisettingsnotifications-accept), [KS-708](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-708/security-akto-add-user-id-bola-high-on-get-apiplatformaudit-log) (narrower than the ruling), [KS-1397](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1397/the-gateway-answers-every-request-with-server-nginx-aktos-unwanted)/1421 (narrower, fails closed, **seen firing live on 2026-10-14** on `POST /api/certifications/issue`), [KS-709](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-709/akto-reports-a-pass-for-a-test-that-executed-nothing-clean-0-not), [KS-417](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-417/akto-spec-consistency-guard-for-the-endpoint-scoped-known-fp-allowlist)/425/524 and [KS-1416](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1416/akto-the-three-code-injection-sqli-scans-run-0-sqlnosql-templates-akto). **Three do not.** The citation fix was made and then **backed out at Peter's instruction (update the app only, log issues)**. Re-verified against `develop` 3c0a52221 on 2026-10-14.

## 1. Wrong citation: `/api/identity-credentials/types`

`systemTest/akto/src/core/endpointFalsePositives.ts:148` (and the docblock at `:117-119`) suppresses `REMOVE_TOKENS` on this endpoint, citing [KS-442](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-442/make-the-verify-family-public-5-ops-gateway-relax-spec-security-ks-424). [KS-442](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-442/make-the-verify-family-public-5-ops-gateway-relax-spec-security-ks-424)'s ruling (Kam, 2026-07-11) covers **only the five verify operations** and says *"reference reads stay protected"*. The ticket that actually registered this endpoint as public by design is [KS-510](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-510/akto-register-get-apiidentity-credentialstypes-as-by-design-public) (Done, 2026-07-23), resting on the spec's `security: []`. The test comment `tests/unit/core/endpointFalsePositives.test.ts:34` carries the same citation.

## 2. `VOLATILE_PATH_RE` drops whole paths from HAR replay with no ruling

`src/setup/harSpec.ts:26`: `/\/(analytics|dashboard|realtime|metrics)\b/i` means those endpoints get **no real HAR sample**, so authz templates skip them for **every** template, not just the similarity ones ([KS-357](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-357/akto-drive-authz-precondition-skips-0-complete-attacker-role-auth)). Today's feed excluded **19** volatile endpoints of 141 GET endpoints. Kamil's [KS-708](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-708/security-akto-add-user-id-bola-high-on-get-apiplatformaudit-log) analysis (2026-08-28) warns that this exact mechanism *"removes the audit log from the scan"* and that the `analytics` paths *"already make"* that trade, *"worth asking whether they should be making it either"*. No ticket reviews it, and its scope is wider than any ruling.

## 3. 8 Akto built-in data-exposure templates are loaded but never selected

`tests/aktoSetup.test.ts:329-338` (`KNOWN_CATALOG_DRIFT.loadedNotInCatalog`): `SENSITIVE_DATA_EXPOSURE_{ADDRESS,CREDIT_CARD,EMAIL,IP_ADDRESS,JWT,PHONE_NUMBER,SSN,VIN}`. Its own comment calls this *"a REAL, previously-unrecorded coverage observation … a coverage decision … deliberately not folded into* [KS-717](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-717/akto-test-id-catalog-and-the-loaded-template-library-drift-silently)*'s drift fix"*. Today on 2.38.2 the library is again 208 = 199 bundled + 9 built-ins, so it is unchanged. No ticket owns the decision.

## Also stale

`endpointFalsePositives.ts:206` quotes `routes/admin.ts:1437`; the quoted code is now at `:1487` / `:1523`. Staleness detection for similarity entries is already [KS-761](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-761/similarity-undiscriminating-fp-entries-have-no-staleness-detection-a), so it is not duplicated here.

## Acceptance criteria

1. The `/api/identity-credentials/types` entry and its test cite [KS-510](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-510/akto-register-get-apiidentity-credentialstypes-as-by-design-public) (with "spec `security: []`, no Kam ruling"), not [KS-442](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-442/make-the-verify-family-public-5-ops-gateway-relax-spec-security-ks-424). **A test demonstrates it:** a unit test that every `public-by-design` entry's cited ticket is one whose text names that endpoint (or a recorded reason), red on the [KS-442](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-442/make-the-verify-family-public-5-ops-gateway-relax-spec-security-ks-424) citation.
2. `VOLATILE_PATH_RE`: a recorded decision (Kamil's input sought, per the [KS-708](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-708/security-akto-add-user-id-bola-high-on-get-apiplatformaudit-log) discussion): narrow it, scope it to the similarity templates as [KS-708](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-708/security-akto-add-user-id-bola-high-on-get-apiplatformaudit-log) Option B did for the tolerance, or accept it with a reason. Report the number of endpoints it excludes in the run's coverage section so the trade is visible.
3. The 8 data-exposure templates: enable them (and measure the tier-budget cost and any false positives on a platform that legitimately returns emails and addresses), or record why not, with the decision recorded where the catalog selection lives.
4. The stale `admin.ts:1437` pointer is corrected or replaced by a symbol reference.

nodes.body:
**Raw results for item 3, as promised** (no classification). This is the first `test:security` run with the 19 built-ins: slot 3 of the Mac, KS-1608 commit `4ce20980e`, Akto 2.41.6, 2026-10-27, Full OWASP scan `6ae0a02a2695a009eb32f225`.

**All 19 executed.** Each recorded 355 results against the 355-endpoint collection. They are passive and read the 81 authenticated HAR samples fed that run. The `settings: plan: PRO` concern did not apply: the self-hosted engine ran them.

| Template | Vulnerable | Not applicable (filter not matched) |
|---|---|---|
| `SENSITIVE_DATA_EXPOSURE_EMAIL` | **4** | 351 |
| `SENSITIVE_DATA_EXPOSURE_IP_ADDRESS` | **3** | 352 |
| the other 17 (address, AWS ×8, credit card, database, JWT, phone, secret, SSN, token, username, VIN) | 0 | 355 each |

**The 7 flagged results**, one each, verbatim from the run artifact:
- EMAIL: `GET /api/auth/me`
- EMAIL: `GET /api/users/me`
- EMAIL: `GET /api/users/admin/list`
- EMAIL: `GET /api/security/audit`
- IP_ADDRESS: `GET /api/platform/audit-log`
- IP_ADDRESS: `GET /api/security/audit`
- IP_ADDRESS: `GET /api/sessions`

**What this does to the gate:** these 7 are the run's only vulnerable results, and they fail `test:security` (`assertNoVulnerabilities`: "vulnerable results 7"). The `develop` control on slot 4 (Akto 2.38.5, without these templates) had 0 vulnerable in the same scan.

**A report detail you may also want to weigh in on:** these templates declare `severity: dynamic_severity`, which Akto decides per finding (public endpoint HIGH, private LOW, otherwise MEDIUM). The harness maps only the four fixed severities, so the HTML report shows **0 in every severity tile next to "7 Vulnerable"**. The gate still fails, but a reader cannot see how serious each one is.

**The decision we'd value from you:** for each of EMAIL and IP_ADDRESS, is returning that data on those endpoints by design (and so a recorded, ruled exception like KS-1397's), or exposure to fix? And are the other 17 worth keeping in the scan at all?

**@kamil.kreiser, your opinion please on item 3 (Akto's built-in sensitive-data templates).**

**BLUF:** under KS-1608 we've started including Akto's active built-in `SENSITIVE_DATA_EXPOSURE_*` templates in `test:security`. They can be taken straight back out, so this is a request for your view rather than a done deal. Would you keep them, keep some, or drop them?

**What they are.** At Akto 2.41.6 there are **19** of them (8 at 2.38.x):
- personal data: address, credit card, email, phone number, SSN, username, VIN;
- credentials: JWT, token, secret, AWS access key;
- infrastructure: AWS ARN / DocDB / DynamoDB / RDS / S3 / SQS URLs, database, IP address.

Each is a **passive** check: it sends no request, and reads responses already captured from our HAR feed for a value of that data type. Severity is decided per finding: HIGH on a public endpoint, LOW on a private one, MEDIUM otherwise. Akto seeds them itself at start-up, which is why our catalog (built from the template library) never selected them.

**Why your view matters.** The platform legitimately returns some of these, for example a login response carries a JWT and a profile carries the user's own email. So some findings will be by design, and a few could be real exposure. Your read of which data types count as exposure here would decide whether they stay, and whether any need a ruling like the KS-1397 `Server: nginx` one.

**What we'll have for you.** The first `test:security` run that includes them is in progress on slot 3 (KS-1608, commit `4ce20980e`). Its per-template results and any findings will go on this ticket, as each template's raw result (no interpretation), so you're judging real output.

**To remove them:** drop the built-in source in `generate-test-ids` and restore the `KNOWN_CATALOG_DRIFT` exemption. That's one small commit.

*Note: these templates declare `settings: plan: PRO`; whether the self-hosted engine runs them at all is being measured in the same run.*

title: Cockpit: statusline.sh:85 does shell arithmetic on rate_limits.seven_day.resets_at, so an ISO-8601 value kills the whole statusline — the lane-V pane renders none and ctx% is unreadable from inside a session
description:
Filed on Wednesday's instruction of 2026-10-13 11:39:04Z, after Seat V 9th could not satisfy a context-based wrap threshold because its pane shows no statusline. **This is a root cause with a one-line fix, not just a symptom report.** The file is at the workspace root (`Setup and System/statusline.sh`), outside any project folder, so this seat read it and did not edit it.

## The defect

`Setup and System/statusline.sh:85`

```sh
week_resets=$(printf '%s' "$input" | jq -r '.rate_limits.seven_day.resets_at // empty')   # :79
...
secs_left=$((week_resets - now_ts))                                                       # :85
```

`:85` performs **shell arithmetic directly on** `resets_at`, which assumes the field is epoch-seconds. When Claude Code supplies it as an **ISO-8601 string**, the arithmetic aborts:

```
/Volumes/DevMASTER/Setup and System/statusline.sh: line 85: 2026-10-17T00: value too great for base (error token is "17T00")
```

The script then exits **rc 1 having printed nothing**, so Claude Code has no statusline to render — and `ctx:NN%`, computed 30 lines earlier at `:54`, is lost with it.

## Truth table, measured by piping synthetic JSON to the real script

| `rate_limits.seven_day.resets_at` | rc | rendered |
| -- | -- | -- |
| ISO string `2026-10-17T00:00:00Z` | **1** | **nothing** |
| epoch integer | 0 | `[Secuura/Blockchain] Opus 5 \| Ultrathink \| ctx:37% \| 7d:89% renews:3d 11h \| azure:-` |
| field absent | 0 | `… ctx:37% \| 7d:89% \| azure:-` |
| `rate_limits` absent entirely | 0 | `… ctx:37% \| azure:-` |

So three of four shapes are fine and exactly one kills it. **The same ISO input against the global fallback** `~/.claude/statusline-command.sh` **returns rc 0** and renders `Opus 5 | ctx:200k used:37% | 7d:89%`, so the defect is specific to the project script.

## The observable effect, measured across panes

`tmux capture-pane -p -t <pane> -S -` and a count of lines matching `ctx:[0-9-]`:

| pane | cockpit name | `ctx:` lines | last value |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| `%0` | wednesday | 1 | `ctx:74%` |
| `%83` | Secuura/Blockchain-K | 1 | `ctx:26%` |
| `%84` | Secuura/Blockchain-J | 1 | `ctx:21%` |
| `%82` | **Secuura/Blockchain-V** | **0** | **none** |
| `%1` | fleet-monitor | 0 | none (not a session pane) |

Three session panes render a figure and lane V's renders none, so the instrument discriminates. Wednesday read K at 23% and J at 16% about ten minutes earlier and this seat read 26% and 21%, so those are live values rather than stale screen text. **Which shape of** `resets_at` **a given pane receives is what decides it; that is not established here, and the fix makes it moot.**

## Why it matters beyond one cosmetic row

`ctx:NN%` is the **only** instrument for the context window. A seat whose statusline dies has no way to read it:

* both statusline scripts take the JSON on **stdin** and persist nothing (`statusline.sh:54` and `statusline-command.sh:7` both read `.context_window.used_percentage`; the only cache in the project script is `/tmp/.claude_azure_user_cache`, for `az account show`);
* the rendered line is not in the pane's scrollback — zero `ctx` hits over the full history;
* nothing under `~/.claude` holds it.

A seat in that state either guesses or substitutes a different number. This one substituted the **session token budget** ("\~2.6% of 15M remaining") for the context window, which is a different quantity entirely, and Wednesday had to correct it. Her words: *"A seat once read the budget as 3% and died at 100% of its window hours later."* So a dead statusline row removes the guard against a seat dying mid-merge.

## Fix

Convert before subtracting, and never let this block the render. Both halves matter:

1. Parse `resets_at` as a date when it is not numeric — e.g. `date -j -f '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ' "$week_resets" +%s` on macOS — or skip the countdown when it does not parse.
2. **Guard the arithmetic** so a future field-shape change degrades the countdown rather than deleting the statusline: test `case $week_resets in (*[!0-9]*) ... esac` before `$(( ))`, and have the script emit its base line regardless. A statusline is a diagnostic; it must not be the thing that fails silently.

A self-test with the four rows of the truth table above would have caught this.

## Proposed and NOT done

A project-local `statusLine` wrapper in `.claude/settings.local.json` that tees stdin to a file, making `ctx%` readable from inside a session. **Wednesday ruled against it for now** (11:39:04Z): that file is shared by every seat in the project folder, and J 10th and K 10th were live in it at 89% weekly usage. It is recorded here as the option, not as a pending action. Fixing `:85` is the smaller and better change and needs no shared-settings edit.

## Priority

Filed **Medium** as instructed. An argument for higher exists and is recorded rather than acted on: the failure is silent, it disables the only context instrument, and it is latent for every seat whose harness sends an ISO `resets_at`. That call is not this seat's.

## Provenance

* Measured by Seat V 9th, 2026-10-13, pane `Secuura/Blockchain-V` `%82`. Everything above is a reading, not a quotation, except Wednesday's sentence about the earlier seat, which is quoted as hers.
* Deduped before filing: 327 distinct issues over 5 search terms with comments and archived included; 0 near hits. `statusline.sh`, `resets_at`, `value too great for base` and `context_window.used_percentage` each → 0. Fresh-nonce negative control `v9c-f4d2b8ff74cb` → 0; positive control `cockpit` → 2 (KS-939, KS-907).

title: KS-998 item 3 gate follow-ups (#1545): the three Minors of the Opus gate, the ks884 S10 fixture collision, and three Info as text
description:
Follow-ups from the Opus tier-1 QA gate on pull request #1545 (KS-998 item 3 + the four Minors of the #1540 gate), verdict **GO WITH NOTE**: 0 Major, 3 Minor, 9 Info. Head under test `50f0552ce011ac9d8c4caddf67bc747a7fed2d5b`, report sha256/16 `4cb85c41ae671c0e`. Same shape as KS-1583, which carries the #1532 gate's follow-ups.

Scope: developer tooling only (the pre-push hook and the package-format gate). **Nothing here deploys.** Cells first, then the fix, per the gate's note that each item is "a few lines plus one cell".

### Minor 1 — a package-level `.npmrc` redirects the install to a host the lock check never allowed

`systemTest/scripts/check-package-format.sh:485` copies `.npmrc` into the stage and `:494` runs `npm ci` with npm's default `replace-registry-host=npmjs`, while `_check_lock_sources` (`:351`) validates only `resolved`. Measured (gate shape B1): a lockfile whose every entry is `https://registry.npmjs.org/…` with an integrity passes the check, a `systemTest/<pkg>/.npmrc` carrying `registry=https://<other host>/` arrives on the same branch, and npm then fetches the tarball from that host — **1 GET to the attacker's listener — and its postinstall runs**. Control B3, same lock without the `.npmrc`: the fetch goes to [registry.npmjs.org](<http://registry.npmjs.org>). No `systemTest/*/.npmrc` exists today.

Fix (both candidates measured at 0 GETs on B1): do not copy `.npmrc` into the stage, **or** refuse (`lockbad`) when a package `.npmrc` sets `registry`, `*:registry`, `replace-registry-host`, `strict-ssl`, `proxy`, `https-proxy`, `ca` or `cafile`. **And** pass `--replace-registry-host=never`, so npm fetches exactly the URL that was checked. One cell: the gate's B1.

Also correct the "nothing is fetched or run" sentences, which this defeats: `check-package-format.sh:153` and `:350`, `systemTest/CLAUDE.md:494`, `Blockchain/Dev/CONTRIBUTING.md:401`.

### Minor 2 — "already on the remote" trusts local tracking refs, and treats "the remote has it" as "it was judged"

`.githooks/pre-push:120` runs before step 1 for every ref. Measured: a **stale** tracking ref (branch deleted or force-moved at the remote since the last fetch) lets a RED commit the remote no longer has land with rc 0 under a note saying it is already on the remote (gate rows R22, R22b, R23; develop refuses all three, and the `fetch --prune` controls are refused on the head too). Separately, fast-forwarding an existing branch onto an already-pushed RED commit lands with no gate and no preflight (R20, R21), where develop judges `remote_sha..tip`. 4 of 789 tracking refs in the project clone are already stale.

Fix: apply the `onremote` skip **only to refs the remote does not have yet** (`_jr_rsha` empty or zero), **after** step 1, so existing-branch updates keep their `remote_sha..tip` judgement. Correct the stale-ref comment at `.githooks/pre-push:116-119` (which claims a stale ref can "never" lead to a pass) and the docs (`CONTRIBUTING.md:417`, `systemTest/CLAUDE.md:530`). Cells: R20 and R22.

### Minor 3 — two surviving mutants are test gaps

* **X14** (ancestor-config names listed from HEAD instead of the pushed commit) survives the gate and hook suites (435/0, 74/0). CASE 48 cannot kill it, because it keeps `.prettierrc` at both commits. Distinguishing cell: the pushed commit has `.prettierrc` and **HEAD has deleted it** (head rc 0, X14 rc 1) — the gate shipped `tools/x14_cell.sh`.
* **Y07** (the `~/.npm` fallback appended even when `npm_config_cache` is set) survives. Cell: `npm_config_cache=X` set with `HOME/.npm` present, asserting **exactly one** `npm_config_cache=X` in the install environment.

### Item 5 — `ks884` S10 is non-deterministic on the #1545 hook: a fixture SHA collision (found by Seat K 10th at the pre-squash measurement, not by the gate)

`Blockchain/Dev/scripts/__tests__/ks884_pre_push_tag_named_develop.test.sh` cell **S10** fails about half the time on the #1545 hook blob `b63a7a46dd647cac1419` and never on develop's `454605d8`: head tree 4/10, predicted merge tree 6/10 (**10/20**), develop tree **0/16**. The blob is identical in head and predicted tree, so the merge is not implicated. It prints no `not ok` line; it prints `FAIL S10 … landed=1 ks991=0 preflight-ran=0`.

Cause, proven by a harness-only probe printing both tips — **7 FAIL runs had** `s4_tip == s10_tip`**, 3 pass runs differed, 10/10 with no exception**: cell S4 pushes `docs/stale` to the fixture origin, then S10 clones that origin and builds `docs/stale10` with the same parent (`origin/develop`), the same tree (both run `echo more >> docs/readme.md`), the same message (`docs only`) and the same identity. A commit SHA depends only on the committer timestamp once those match, so within one clock second the two commits are byte-identical; S10's clone then holds `refs/remotes/origin/docs/stale` pointing **at** S10's own commit, and `pre-push:120`'s `git for-each-ref --contains "$_tip" "refs/remotes/<remote>/"` matches, because a ref contains itself.

**The hook is correct — this is not a gate bypass.** The commit genuinely is already on the remote, by SHA. The defect is the S10 fixture reproducing S4's commit. On develop the collision still happens but is invisible, because develop has no `onremote` skip. The Minor 2 fix above does **not** cure it: `docs/stale10` is a new ref, so `_jr_rsha` is zero and the skip still applies.

Fix (tested, one line, **test fixture only, no shipped file**): at `…/ks884_pre_push_tag_named_develop.test.sh:128`, inside the `s10_out` block, `echo more >> docs/readme.md` becomes `echo s10-distinct >> docs/readme.md`. Fixed: **0 runs with any FAIL out of 14**, 0 dead. Control, the unfixed suite in the same loop and conditions: **S10 FAIL in 7 of 14**. Keep an apostrophe out of that comment — inside the `s10_out="$( … )"` substitution it breaks the parse (rc 2).

### Info, as text only

1. **Info 1** — two gate cells fail when the fixture path contains a UUID: npm 11.5.1 refuses `npm config get userconfig` when the value holds a UUID-shaped string (@npmcli/redact treats it as a token), so the suite reads 433/2 on a scratchpad with a UUID and 435/0 through a UUID-free `TMPDIR`. Have the stub derive the userconfig from `node -p 'require("os").homedir()'`, or assert on `HOME` alone.
2. **Info 2** — credentials in *values*, and names the six patterns miss: userinfo in `npm_config_registry`, `npm_config_proxy`, `npm_config_https_proxy` and `HTTPS_PROXY` reaches every install script verbatim, and so does `npm_config_otp`. Add `otp` to the credential patterns and add one doc sentence on credentials in values (`CONTRIBUTING.md:403-405` and `systemTest/CLAUDE.md` do not say it).
3. **Info 5** — `FORMAT_GATE_LOCK_ALLOW` without a trailing slash (`https://npm.example.com`) accepts `https://npm.example.com.evil.example/…`. The default has the slash. Document "end the prefix with `/`".

Evidence for item 5: `5_Project_History/2026-10-13_seatK-10th/measurements/ks884_S10_finding.txt` (plus the failing and passing run logs beside it). Gate evidence for Minors 1-3 and the Info: the verdict and `evidence/` under the gate's own folder.

**BLUF:** Delivered: PR 1553 merged as 53b429ed6b4b on develop, deployed to kintsugi at b1fb543640e7 (recorded deploy, 2026-11-01). Verified by code read at b1fb543640e7, not observed live (a shell test). Left open: the ticket's other items are not landed.

- **Item 5 is in the code:** `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/__tests__/ks884_pre_push_tag_named_develop.test.sh:128` makes the S10 build commit differ from the S4 commit, so a SHA collision cannot skip their checks.
- **Left open, as the ticket's comment a122fb34 of 2026-10-27 records it (not re-read in the code here):** Minor 1 (the package `.npmrc` registry redirect, all three parts), Minor 2, and Minor 3 (partial).

## Read at source, item by item. **Minor 1 is NOT landed — none of its three parts is on the tree. Minor 2 is NOT landed. Minor 3 is partial. Item 5 IS landed. So this ticket STAYS OPEN and NO state was moved.**

Read at develop `885d69b06f5fce7c8f58effea68623ecb25407b1`. The brief that sent me here listed this ticket as "possibly done, UNVERIFIED" on the strength of a stage `.npmrc` note at `check-package-format.sh:111`. **That note is a comment, not the fix** — section 1 below.

## Minor 1 — the package `.npmrc` registry redirect: **all three parts OPEN**

The ticket asks for (a) stop copying `.npmrc` into the stage **or** refuse when it sets `registry`/`*:registry`/`replace-registry-host`/`strict-ssl`/`proxy`/`https-proxy`/`ca`/`cafile`; **and** (b) pass `--replace-registry-host=never`; **and** (c) correct four "nothing is fetched or run" sentences.

| part | measured at my tip |
| -- | -- |
| the stage copy | `check-package-format.sh:485` still reads `for f in package.json package-lock.json npm-shrinkwrap.json .npmrc; do` — **`.npmrc` is still copied** |
| `--replace-registry-host=never` | `:494` reads `npm ci --no-audit --no-fund --no-update-notifier --fetch-retries=0 --fetch-timeout=20000`. The string `replace-registry-host` occurs **0 times in the whole 919-line script** (rc 1; the same instrument returns 3 for `setpgrp` and 48-odd for the lock terms, so it fires) |
| an `.npmrc` refusal | `lockbad` exists at `:476`, `:657` and `:807`, but its reason text at `:807` is *"the lockfile has a source the gate will not install from: ${LOCK_REASON}"* — that is **KS-1583's Minor 3** (validating each lock entry's `resolved`), not an `.npmrc` check |
| the four sentences | `:153` still reads *"… naming the entry, and NOTHING is fetched or run."* and `:350` still reads *"… is refused. Nothing is run and nothing is fetched."* — **unchanged**, and these are two of the four the ticket names |

**And the suite confirms the behaviour is still the one the ticket describes.** `package_format_gate.test.sh` CASE 40's Q12 cell (`:1232-1238`) asserts the opposite of the first fix candidate, by design for KS-1583: *"a package .npmrc is copied into the stage the install runs in"*, expecting **1**. So Minor 1's candidate (a) is not merely unbuilt — a live cell currently pins the copy. Whoever takes this has to move that cell too, which is worth knowing before starting.

## Minor 2 — "already on the remote": **OPEN**

The fix asks for the `onremote` skip to apply **only to refs the remote does not have yet** (`_jr_rsha` empty or zero) and to run **after** step 1.

At my tip, `.githooks/pre-push:120`:

`if [ -n "$(git for-each-ref --contains "$_tip" "refs/remotes/${_remote}/" 2>/dev/null)" ]; then _jr_skip=onremote; return 0; fi`

is **unconditional** and sits **before** the `_jr_rsha` read at `:122` (`if [ -n "$_jr_rsha" ] && [ "$_jr_rsha" != "$ZERO" ] && …`). So neither half of the fix is in. The note text at `:347-348` is also unchanged.

## Minor 3 — **partial, and neither mutant has a discriminating cell**

* **X14.** `CASE 48` exists (`:1614`), but its header is *"MINOR 4 (X14, X15)"* — the **#1540** gate's Minor 4, which is the cell this ticket says **cannot kill X14**. Re-read at my tip, CASE 48 writes `.prettierrc` as `A` at the pushed commit and `B` at HEAD (`:1618`, `:1623`) — it **keeps `.prettierrc` present at both commits**, which is exactly the condition under which this ticket records X14 as surviving. The distinguishing shape it asks for — *the pushed commit has `.prettierrc` and HEAD has DELETED it* — is not there, and **`tools/x14_cell.sh` is not in the tree** (0 paths match `x14`).
* **Y07.** No cell asserts **exactly one** `npm_config_cache=` in the install environment. CASE 43 (`:1416-1445`) checks membership through `has_env`, which is a presence test, not a count; `npm_config_cache` appears in its "the install DOES see" loop at `:1430`. The strings `Y07` and `exactly one` occur **0** times in the suite.

## Item 5 — the ks884 S10 fixture collision: **LANDED**

`Blockchain/Dev/scripts/__tests__/ks884_pre_push_tag_named_develop.test.sh:128`:

`echo s10-distinct >> docs/readme.md   # K10: must differ from the S4 commit, or the two share a SHA`

That is the one-line fix this ticket specifies, with the reason in the comment, and the apostrophe-free wording the ticket warns about. The sibling `echo more >> docs/readme.md` lines at `:64` and `:166` are untouched, which is correct — only S10 needed to differ from S4.

## Not established

* **I ran nothing** — no suite, no gate, no mutant. Every row is a source read: a string present or absent at a line, with a firing positive control and a zero control on the same file each time.
* Whether moving the Q12 cell would disturb anything else in CASE 40.
* The remaining two of Minor 1's four sentences (`systemTest/CLAUDE.md:494`, `Blockchain/Dev/CONTRIBUTING.md:401`) — I checked the two in the script only.
* Infos 1, 2 and 5 of this ticket, which it carries "as text only" and which I did not verify.

## Conclusion

**Not Done.** Of this ticket's four work items, one (item 5) is on the tree and three are not. The brief's "possibly done" reading came from a comment at `:111` describing what the stage copies; the fix Minor 1 asks for is the opposite of that behaviour.

**Assignee** set to the board account with this comment, per the board rule for an unassigned ticket I write on.

*Seat G 24th, 2026-10-27, on Wednesday's 05:40:47Z go-ahead for the "read at source" pair. Board seat: nothing built, no suite run, NO state change, nothing archived.*

**Item 5 is merged to develop as `53b429ed6b4bf4d23c0721bf573b9df1c858bc06` (PR #1553). This ticket stays open for items 1–4, 6 and 7. One note from the gate, recorded here rather than changed in the merged head:**

- **The `:128` comment undersells its own line.** It reads "must differ from the S4 commit, or the two share a SHA". With dates pinned to one second, the gate measured the unfixed S10 commit as byte-identical to **both** S4's commit and cell 1's (`docs/tagged`): one SHA, `eceba002…`, in all three clones. The code is right. The two merged lines together close a **three-way** collision, cell 1 = S4 = S10, and either line alone would have left a pair. Only the wording of K 10th's comment is narrower than what it guards. Gate verdict F2, non-blocking.
- **The gate's optional suggestion (F4): a permanent fixed-timestamp run.** The cure is "distinct content per cell", and nothing stops a future cell from reusing `echo more >> docs/readme.md` off `origin/develop` with "docs only", which would bring the race back silently and only about half the time. One extra run of this suite with `GIT_AUTHOR_DATE` and `GIT_COMMITTER_DATE` pinned to one value makes any such collision **deterministic**. Under that pin, develop went red 5/5 and the cure stayed green 5/5. Not built; it is a suggestion for whoever picks this up.
- Also measured by the gate, harmless (F3): the three local `side` tags (`commit-tree`, never pushed) are still byte-identical within a second. `pre-push:120` only consults remote-tracking refs, so they cannot trigger the skip. Pinned runs confirm there is no effect.

Gate report: `0_Brain/reference/2026-10-15_gate-pr1553/verdict.md` in Wednesday's project, sha256/16 `6aad7fad2eeccd01` (recomputed independently).

**BLUF: item 5 is raised as [PR #1553](https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/1553), head `91809ebe6b8cb8e0cb7b836440c9d9b705283be7` on develop `e67e0dc1`. It is waiting for its gate. Items 1–4, 6 and 7 are not in it, and this ticket stays open.**

- **Item 5 needed TWO lines, not one.** K 10th's line at `:128` (S10 → `s10-distinct`) cures S10: red in **0 of 54** cured runs, against 8/14 on develop. But the first 14+14 loop also showed **S4** red in both arms with the same `landed=1 ks991=0 preflight-ran=0` signature. A harness-only probe proved the partner over 40 runs, with 100% correlation: every S4 red had S4's tip equal to **cell 1's** (`docs/tagged`), contained in `refs/remotes/origin/docs/tagged`; every pass had them differ. It is the same mechanism, one cell earlier. On Wednesday's ruling, the cure widens by one line at `:113` (S4 → `s4-distinct`).
- **Result, 14+14 interleaved, both lines:** FIXED **0/14 runs with any red**; develop 11/14 (S10 ×10, S4 ×1). 0 dead runs. On its own push the suite ran 10/0 in-hook, shell suites 88/88.
- Test-only, two lines, hook untouched. The link is `contributes`, so the merge will not close this ticket.
Mention-instrument control for the #1545 team notes: this sentence names no user, so its bodyData must carry zero suggestion_userMentions nodes. Posted by Seat K 10th.

title: Security: nothing binds the forwarded `identity` block to the authenticated caller — any authenticated caller can anchor any DID at the highest trust level
description:
## BLUF

Facts only, no fix shape. From the pull request 1549 Opus gate (verdict `40bdc24d2e1f07dc`, its **INF-2**). Wednesday ruled it gets its own Medium ticket and is **not** in 1549's fix round: Kam's ruling ("Latest event's identity wins") decides **whose** identity is stored, not **who may assert** one.

## Facts

* anchoring checks the `identity` block's **shape** only. `services/anchoring/src/anchorSchema.ts:109-118` says so outright: K proves SHAPE by regex/enum/type and **never SEMANTICS**.
* Nothing compares the block to the authenticated caller: the DID, `actorLevel`, `actorVerified`, `orgDid`, `orgTrust` and `orgVerified` are taken as sent.
* The gate's case "different actor, max claims" (`evidence/identity_edges.log`): all seven fields were anchored as sent.
* anchoring's direct `POST /api/anchors` has accepted this since **KS-1175**. Pull request 1549 (KS-1385) forwards the block from **six more originate sites**, each called with the end user's or a connector's bearer — so any authenticated caller of those originate routes can now place an asserted identity on chain through them.
* Measured by the gate, not re-measured here. Related: **KS-1603** (who may write an anchor row at all) — a different question from who may assert an identity.

*Filed by Seat J 9th on Wednesday's instruction. Not fixed here.*

nodes.body:
**BLUF: @stuart.jamieson — ruled on the fix shape: bind at the ORGANISATION level, which is your proposal. It is the only shape that does not break what KS-1175 delivered. Unscheduled, and no date.**

Your 14 October fact is what decides this, so it is worth restating as the reason rather than just the input: for every Platform S call the `identity` block is **by design** an assertion by the connector about a person who has no K identity at all. S registers organisations with K, never people, so there is no K user and no K DID that the block could be bound to.

That rules out the shape that looks most obvious from K's side:

- **Binding `identity` to the authenticated caller's own DID would blank every S identity**, because the caller is an organisation key and the subject is a person it is speaking for. It would turn KS-1175 off for your whole integration while appearing to harden it.
- **Binding at the organisation level does not.** The assertion stays the connector's to make, and what gets checked is that the organisation it names is the organisation whose key signed the call — which is a claim K can actually verify.

**What is ruled:** the shape. **What is not:** when it is built. It is not scheduled, it is not in a current review round, and I am not giving you a date for it. The exposure it closes is real but it is bounded by the fact that a caller can only assert under its own key.

Nothing needed from you on this one.

@kamil.kreiser — one fact to keep in front of any fix shape here, from S develop `aeae5ca`: **for every Platform S call the `identity` block is, by design, an assertion by the connector about a person who has no K identity of their own.** It is S's own ledger snapshot of the acting person at the time of the row (`IdentityAnchorFields.From(tx)`: `actorDid`, `actorLevel`, `actorVerified`, `orgDid`, `orgTrust`, `orgVerified`, the DID from S's identity profile, the level from S's KYC record), sent under the document owner's organisation key with the person as `onBehalfOf`. S registers organisations with K, never people, so there is no K user or K DID the block could be bound to; the authenticated caller is the organisation's connector, and the organisation is the party attesting. A fix that binds the block to the caller's **own** DID or trust level would therefore refuse or blank every S identity (every block S sends is "a different actor" from the caller), which is the PS-870 / KS-1175 feature undone. What would fit S is binding at the **organisation** level — the block's `orgDid` / `orgTrust` must belong to the calling connector's organisation, and `actorDid` must be an actor that organisation has registered or asserted through `onBehalfOf` — with the actor's level taken on the connector's word, as it is today. Happy to measure whichever shape you pick against a slot pair before it merges.

title: ks742-keys-tenancy-route-contract.test.ts: the 10 s beforeAll hook lapses under fleet load, SKIPS all 21 cells, and then throws a misleading TypeError in afterAll
description:
Found while building KS-1598 round 1, not while looking for it: `npx vitest run` in `services/security` came back **2 failed / 341 passed**, and neither failure was in anything I had touched. Recorded here rather than left in a session log, per the workspace never-skip rule. **Nothing is being called flaky on a hunch — the measurements are below.**

## Where

`Blockchain/Dev/services/security/src/__tests__/ks742-keys-tenancy-route-contract.test.ts`

* `beforeAll` at `:108`
* `afterAll` at `:125`, which is where the confusing message comes from

## What happens

Under load the `beforeAll` exceeds its hook timeout:

```
Error: Hook timed out in 10000ms.
 ❯ src/__tests__/ks742-keys-tenancy-route-contract.test.ts:108:3
```

`server` is then never assigned, so `afterAll` dereferences it:

```
TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'close')
 ❯ src/__tests__/ks742-keys-tenancy-route-contract.test.ts:125:47
      await new Promise<void>((resolve) => server.close(() => resolve()));
```

**The run reports** `1 failed` **with** `21 skipped`**.** Zero cells executed. The headline failure a reader sees is the `TypeError` about `close`, which points at teardown and says nothing about the hook that actually lapsed. In the full suite the same load shows up differently again — a 5 s per-test timeout on the repo-walk cell at `:521` and a `fetch failed / ECONNRESET` at `:597` — so the same root cause wears three different faces.

## Measured, with the load named

| run | scope | load average (1 min) | result |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| 1 | full security unit suite | **11.12** | 2 failed / 341 passed — the `:521` timeout and the `:597` ECONNRESET |
| 2 | this file alone | \~11 | **1 failed, 21 SKIPPED** — the `beforeAll` lapse, 0 cells executed |
| 3 | this file alone | — | 21 passed, rc 0 |
| 4 | full security unit suite | **8.21** | 31 files / **343 passed**, rc 0 |
| 5 | full security unit suite | 8.21 | 31 files / **343 passed**, rc 0 |

Other seats on this machine were running their own vitest and jest suites throughout. So: the file passes alone, the suite passes twice at the lower load, and the failures appear only at the higher load. The failing hook is in a file my change does not touch, and the failure is a **hook timeout** — a function of wall time, not of content.

## Why it matters

A 0-executed run is reported as a *failed file*, not as a run that never started. A reader (or a gate) comparing "31 files / 343" against "1 failed / 21 skipped" has to notice the word `skipped` to tell the difference between a regression and a file that never booted. That is the same class of trap as a mutation kill whose red cells carry empty messages.

It also makes the suite's verdict depend on who else is on the box, which is exactly what a push-time gate must not do.

## Fix shapes, none chosen here

* Give the hook an explicit budget sized for fleet load (the convention in this repo for the 5 s-default class is a per-file `testTimeout`/`hookTimeout`), rather than leaving it on the default.
* Make `afterAll` tolerate an unassigned `server` so the reported failure names the hook that lapsed instead of the teardown that could not run.
* Optionally: assert in `afterAll` that `beforeAll` completed, so a 0-executed run says so in its own words.

## Related, and NOT duplicates

* **KS-1155** — `packages/shared` tree-walking guards exceed vitest's 5 s default under fleet load. Same class, different files.
* **KS-1328** — `services/kyc` `db.retry.test.ts`, same class.
* **KS-1521** — the budget wording and the governance source-text pin. Touches the timeout convention, not this file.
* **KS-743** and **KS-742** concern the route contract this file tests, not its harness.

## Provenance

* Deduped before filing: 325 distinct issues read across 6 search terms with comments and archived included; the token `ks742-keys-tenancy-route-contract` hit **KS-743** and **KS-1521**, both of which were read and neither of which covers the hook timeout. Fresh-nonce negative control `v9b-bf367a4ef9ff` → 0 hits; positive control → 1.
* Logs: `5_Project_History/2026-10-13_seatV-9th/logs/sec_unit.log` (the red), `ks742_alone_1.log` (the 21-skipped run), `ks742_alone_2.log`, `sec_unit_2.log`, `sec_unit_3.log` (343/343).
* Filed by Seat V 9th, 2026-10-13.

Node v26.8.1, not Node 24. Evidence and the full table are in the PR body.

**One precision that points straight at the fix, measured after filing.** This file runs under `services/security/vitest.config.ts`, which sets **no `testTimeout` and no `hookTimeout`** — so it is on vitest's defaults (5 s per test, 10 s per hook). Its sibling `vitest.integration.config.ts` in the same service **already sets `testTimeout: 60_000` and `hookTimeout: 60_000`**, with `fileParallelism: false`, and the comment above it says why: these suites need a real migrated PostgreSQL.

So the service already contains the answer for DB-backed suites; `ks742-keys-tenancy-route-contract.test.ts` simply is not one of them. Its name ends `.test.ts`, not `.integration.test.ts`, so the unit config picks it up (control: `vitest.config.ts:15` excludes `**/*.integration.test.ts`, and the integration files are a separate, non-empty set).

That gives whoever takes this a choice that is now a fact rather than a guess:

1. give the file its own `hookTimeout` sized for fleet load, the smallest change; or
2. if the hook really is booting a server and touching a database, the file belongs on the integration config's budgets, under which it would have **60 s** rather than 10 s.

title: KS-1598 follow-up (pull request 1548 gate i6): the admin-scope route's `upper(role) = $3` carries the same libc fold as the status guard, and users.role has no CHECK
description:
Filed from the pull request 1548 (KS-1598) Opus gate, report hash `20fb01665917ef45`, verdict `GO WITH NOTE` at 0 Major / 1 Minor / 6 Info. This is the gate's **i6**, recorded as PRE-EXISTING and deliberately NOT touched by KS-1598 round 1, so that the `COLLATE "C"` decision is taken for both folds or for neither rather than half-applied by accident.

## Where

`Blockchain/Dev/services/security/src/index.ts` — the target query of `PUT /api/keys/admin-scopes/:userId`:

```sql
SELECT 1 FROM users
 WHERE id = $1::uuid AND tenant_id = $2::uuid
   AND upper(role) = $3
   AND lower(status COLLATE "C") = 'active'
 LIMIT 1
```

The status half now folds under `COLLATE "C"` (KS-1598 round 1). The role half beside it still folds under the database's default libc collation.

## Measured, on my own PostgreSQL 15.14 under en_AU.UTF-8, with controls

| stored `role` | `upper(role) = 'ADMIN'` (default) | `upper(role COLLATE "C") = 'ADMIN'` |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `ADMIN`, `admin`, `Admin` | true | true |
| `admın` (U+0131 DOTLESS I), `ADMıN` | **true** | **false** |
| `SUPER_ADMIN`, `ISSUER_ADMIN` | false | false |

* Codepoint verified: `ascii(substr(...))` = **305** = 0x131, so these are not ASCII rows in disguise.
* The gate measured the same under `en_US.UTF-8`, so this is not one locale's quirk.
* `users.role` **has NO CHECK constraint.** Probe: `pg_constraint` for `users` with a definition matching `%role%` returns **(none)**. Control, with the same probe: a definition matching `%status%` returns `users_status_vocabulary`, so the probe is not blind. That is the difference from the status column, whose vocabulary is bounded at migration `046:60` — **nothing bounds the spelling of** `role` **at the database level.**

## Why it is Info and not a defect to hotfix

* Reaching it needs a direct database write. Code read: the application's writers put literal role strings in. No route accepts an arbitrary `role` string for this column.
* It was **not** measured at the route. The gate measured the SQL predicate in isolation.
* It is pre-existing: KS-1598 introduced neither half.

## The decision this ticket asks for

Either apply `upper(role COLLATE "C")` beside the status fold, or state why the two columns are treated differently. The second is defensible — `status` is bounded by a CHECK and `role` is not — but it should be written down rather than left as an accident of which finding came first.

Minimal change if it is taken: `AND upper(role COLLATE "C") = $3`, plus one cell per fold (a U+0131 role spelling must be 404) in `ks1570b-admin-scope-route.integration.test.ts`, which already carries the equivalent U+0130 cells for `status`.

## How this differs from KS-1591 — they are NOT the same finding

**KS-1591** is `String(role).toUpperCase()` in **JavaScript**, in `packages/shared/src/security/keyRevokePolicy.ts` (`isPlatformRole`), judging the **caller's claimed** role out of a token, and it admits a dotless-i, a long-s and an array as `SUPER_ADMIN`.

**This ticket** is `upper(role)` in **SQL**, against the **stored target row's** role, under the database's collation. Different site, different language's fold, different principal, different threat. Both should fold explicitly, and neither fix reaches the other.

## Provenance

* Verdict: `0_Brain/reference/2026-10-13_gate-pr1548/verdict.md`, report hash `20fb01665917ef45` (recipe: delete line 2, sha256 the rest, first 16 hex). Recomputed independently; one appended byte gives `c67118e9d49d7c81`.
* Deduped before filing: 325 distinct issues read across 6 search terms with comments and archived included, 0 near hits on two or more distinctive tokens. Fresh-nonce negative control `v9b-bf367a4ef9ff` → 0 hits; positive control `admin_organisation_scopes` → 1. The `U+0131` token hit **KS-1591**, which is why the section above exists: the dedupe found the sibling and it was read rather than assumed to be the same thing.
* Filed by Seat V 9th, 2026-10-13.

nodes.body:
**Widened by one codepoint, from the pull request 1548 round-2 gate (report `6a41c4bef88d1e55`, finding i4).** This ticket as filed named U+0131 (dotless `ı`) as the codepoint whose `upper()` lands in ASCII. The gate enumerated **every codepoint** rather than sampling, and there are **two**:

| codepoint | `upper()` under the default collation | under `COLLATE "C"` |
|---|---|---|
| **U+0131** LATIN SMALL LETTER DOTLESS I | `I` | unchanged |
| **U+017F** LATIN SMALL LETTER LONG S | `S` | unchanged |

Under `COLLATE "C"` the count of non-ASCII codepoints folding into ASCII is **0**.

**The conclusion on this ticket does not change.** Neither codepoint can spell `ADMIN` except through U+0131, which is what the ticket already records; `ADMIN` contains no `S`, so U+017F cannot reach this particular comparison. It matters for two reasons anyway:

1. **The same one-token change shuts both.** `upper(role COLLATE "C")` is the whole fix, and it is the same shape as the `lower(status COLLATE "C")` that merged as `3c0a522216258040f32d400ede433e48e683f734`. So the decision this ticket asks for — fold both, or write down why a CHECK-bounded column and an unbounded one differ — is now a decision about two codepoints rather than one, at no extra cost.
2. **U+017F reaches any role or vocabulary word containing `S`.** `SUPER_ADMIN`, `ISSUER_ADMIN` and `SYSTEM_ADMIN` all contain one. This ticket's comparison is against the literal `'ADMIN'`, so it is unaffected — but any sibling comparison against a role spelled with `S` is not, and `users.role` still has **no CHECK** to bound the spelling (probe: `pg_constraint` for `users` matching `%role%` → `(none)`; control, same probe matching `%status%` → `users_status_vocabulary`).

Related and still not the same finding: **KS-1591** is the JavaScript `String(role).toUpperCase()` on the **caller's claimed** role in `packages/shared`, which already records the long-s among its three admitted spellings. This ticket is SQL `upper()` against the **stored target row**. Two sites, two languages, two principals — and now the same two codepoints, which is a reason to settle them together rather than evidence they are one ticket.

Facts only; no state change asked for here.

title: KS-1594 follow-up (pull request 1547 round-2 gate): the non-string and null organizationId rules at originate's admin mint are pinned for one caller class only
description:
Filed from the round-2 Opus delta gate on pull request 1547 (KS-1594), report hash `ccbe317fcbf769f3`, verdict `GO WITH NOTE` at 0 Major / 1 Minor / 6 Info. 1547 merged to `develop` as `92d1316ffe31cb13b3f7e843e7891225383b2f84`. This ticket carries the Minor plus two Info items the gate asked to be recorded. **The implementation is correct today** — every item below is test coverage or a pre-existing difference, not a live defect.

## 1. The Minor: three mutants survive the 23 cells (test coverage)

`Blockchain/Dev/services/originate/src/__tests__/ks1594-admin-mint-provisioning-and-org-bound.integration.test.ts:292-293` — all four `c17` shapes use `tok('SYSTEM_ADMIN')`, so the "400 for a non-string `organizationId`" rule is pinned for a **platform** caller only. No cell anywhere in the file sends `organizationId: null`: the gate's `grep -i` found 0 such calls, against 16 `mint(` calls found by the same instrument as its control.

The three gate mutants that therefore survive:

| mutant | what it does | behaviour it restores |
| -- | -- | -- |
| R9 | narrows the 400 guard to platform callers | an ORG_ADMIN sending `organizationId: [A2]` is silently treated as absent and gets 201 bound to its own org — the round-1 m2 behaviour |
| R1 | moves the 400 guard after the (a) and (c) decisions | an ORG_ADMIN sending a non-string gets 403, not 400 |
| R7 | makes `organizationId: null` a 400 | breaks the ruled "null and absent behave the same" |

**Why it is a Minor, not a Major.** The matrix the gate ran over the real route found 0 of 900 non-string cases that were not 400, and 0 of 342 null/absent pairs that differed in status or stored org. None of the three survivors creates a false pass: in each, every FALSE PASS category stays at 0 and the deviations are status codes or own-org rows.

### The fix (the gate's own minimal fix, two cells)

1. `ORG_ADMIN(A1)`, `permissions: ['organizations:register']`, `organizationId: [A2]` → **400** and **0 rows** written.
2. `organizationId: null` with `permissions: ['read']` → the **same status and the same stored org** as with the field absent, for **SYSTEM_ADMIN** and for **ORG_ADMIN(A1)**.

Both cells must red R9, R1 and R7 respectively. Run in both tenancy modes, as the existing 23 are.

## 2. i5 — UNTESTED, carried verbatim from the gate

In the gate's own words:

> a forged `x-tenant-id` sent directly to the router is honoured; KS-1032 closes it on the merged tree by reading only, not tested end to end

What the gate measured on the gated head: `ORG_ADMIN(A1)` + `organizations:register` + `organizationId: A1` with a forged `x-tenant-id: T2` sent **directly to the router** returns **201, stored in tenant T2**, bound to A1. It is pre-existing — `develop` at `026c2d16` gave 201 too, and the security route would have refused it as cross-tenant. The gate's harness mounts the router **without** `index.ts`'s middleware, which is why it cannot answer the real question.

**The claim that is untested:** that KS-1032, now on `develop`, shuts this. The reading is that `gatewayProvenance` strips trust headers whenever `GATEWAY_VOUCH_SECRET` is unset (fail closed), and that the KS-458 resolution reads `x-tenant-id` only on a vouched request. **Nobody has run it.**

**The instrument that would settle it:** an end-to-end request through originate's **real middleware stack** on `develop` `92d1316f` — `GATEWAY_VOUCH_SECRET` unset, a forged `x-tenant-id: T2` — expecting the key to be stored in the **caller's own tenant**, not T2. Until that runs, "KS-1032 shuts it" is a reading, not a measurement.

## 3. i4 — pre-existing difference between the two doors

A malformed `permissions` value (a bare string, a nested array, `[null, …]`, an object) is a **400** at `services/security/src/index.ts`, because zod parses `scopes: z.array(z.string())`. At originate the same input falls back to `['read']` or is stored inertly. 720 cells in the gate's door comparison sit in this bucket; 200 agree, 395 differ on allow/refuse and 125 on refusal code.

**It is not an escape:** the classifier found **0** non-platform rows whose stored scopes are provisioning-capable. It is a divergence in refusal behaviour between two doors that are now identical on all 1680 well-formed shapes.

Decide whether originate should reject a malformed `permissions` with 400 to match security, or whether the fall-back is intended. That choice is not made here.

## Provenance

* Verdict: `0_Brain/reference/2026-10-13_gate-pr1547-r2/verdict.md`, report hash `ccbe317fcbf769f3` (recipe: delete line 2, sha256 the rest, first 16 hex). Recomputed independently; a one-byte perturbation gives `80f78858246cf02d`.
* Deduped before filing: 253 distinct issues read across 5 search terms with comments and archived included. 0 near hits. Fresh-nonce negative control `v9nonce-1fe0a1cf6ffe` → 0; positive control `svc_api_keys` → 18 issues. The nonce is fresh for this filing precisely because a token already written into a description stops being a control.
* Filed by Seat V 9th, 2026-10-13.

title: Two ungated tenant reads that KS-1032's fail-closed ruling does not cover: metering prefers req.tenantId over a verified req.user.tenantId, and extractTenantContext's header read is ungated in multi-tenant mode
description:
## BLUF

Two findings from the **pull request 1546 Opus gate** (verdict `34fb8ee6b4650ac6`, head `ad366066`), recorded as **facts with no fix shape**. Both are hardening **beyond** Kam's KS-1032 ruling ("Fail closed, deployed only after the secret is set"), which is why they are a ticket and not code in that pull request. Neither is exploitable while the provenance strip works: the gate found **0 forged-versus-bare differences across all 147 declared routes** (its cells GA5, GB3, GC7).

**Nothing here is ruled and nothing is commissioned.**

## Fact 1 — metering scopes by `req.tenantId`, not by the verified `req.user.tenantId`

* `services/originate/src/routes/metering.ts` resolves the tenant with `reqTenantId(req)`, which reads `(req as any).tenantId` and falls back to `DEFAULT_TENANT_ID`.
* On a box with `GATEWAY_VOUCH_SECRET` **unset or MISMATCHED**, the gateway still attaches a connector Bearer JWT carrying the key's `tenantId` (minted by auth `/internal/connector-token`), and `authenticate()` accepts it and sets `req.user`. But the handler never consults `req.user.tenantId`.
* Because the headers were stripped, the KS-458 block had already set `req.tenantId` to the default. **Measured result: 200, reading the DEFAULT tenant's usage** (gate cells GA1, GC5). A **401** happens only when the gateway's token exchange failed (GA2).
* So on such a box a partner reads **another tenant's** usage totals whenever Platform S's key tenant differs from DEFAULT. **Whether that is true on Kintsugi or demo is UNMEASURED.**
* The gate recorded a possible direction (its M1 option (c)): have `reqTenantId` prefer a verified `req.user.tenantId` when `authenticate()` set the user. **Recorded as the gate's option, not as a decision.**

## Fact 2 — `extractTenantContext`'s header read is ungated in multi-tenant mode

* Enumerating every writer of `.tenantId` in `services/originate/src` and `packages/shared/src` gives exactly **three**: `originate/src/index.ts:251` (the KS-458 resolution), `originate/src/routes/metering.ts:65`, and `packages/shared/src/db/tenant-context.ts:91`.
* The third assigns straight from the **raw** `req.headers['x-tenant-id']` read at `tenant-context.ts:67`, with no provenance check.
* `resolveRequestTenantId` prefers an already-attached `req.tenantId` over its own gated header arm. So with `MULTI_TENANCY_ENABLED=true` the attached arm wins and carries an ungated header value: **KS-1032's part (c) is a second line in single-tenant mode only**, and the strip is the only line in multi-tenant mode.
* `MULTI_TENANCY_ENABLED` is `${MULTI_TENANCY_ENABLED:-false}` in `docker-compose.yml`. **Whether it is on for any live box is UNMEASURED.**
* Related: with `MULTI_TENANCY_ENABLED=true` and `NODE_ENV=production`, `extractTenantContext` answers **400 on every request** once the headers are stripped ("Missing tenant context", `tenant-context.ts:68-73`). Read statically, not run.

## What was already done about the texts

Pull request 1546's fix round corrected the comments and operator docs that misdescribed the above (gate findings M1, m2, m3) — `routes/metering.ts`, `utils/requestTenant.ts`, the C2 cell comment, `.env.example`, `env.example`, `docs/ENVIRONMENT-VARIABLES.md` and `services/originate/src/index.ts`. **Only the texts. No behaviour was changed**, deliberately: gating `extractTenantContext` is outside Kam's ruling.

## Dedupe

Literal `containsIgnoreCase` over title **and** description (NOT `searchIssues`, which is fuzzy — it returns hits for a nonsense term, so it cannot be a membership test). Terms and counts: `reqTenantId` 1, `extractTenantContext` 2, `req.user.tenantId` 0, `GATEWAY_VOUCH_SECRET` 4; **negative control** `zzqq-no-such-term-at-all` **0**, so the instrument discriminates.

Near-misses read and rejected:

* **KS-1084** — the gateway's own Authorization-only calls send **no** `x-tenant-id`, so originate defaults them. That is the header being **absent**; Fact 1 is about a **present and verified** `req.user.tenantId` being ignored in favour of `req.tenantId`. KS-1084's own stated unknown ("whether originate's `authenticate()` sets the tenant from the forwarded JWT on these routes") is partly answered here for metering.
* **KS-1091** — the cross-tenant JWT probe on originate's direct path, explicitly **not commissioned and not ruled**; about the strip, not these two reads.

No relation link added, because neither is the same defect.

Filed by Seat J 9th from the pull request 1546 gate round 1. Contributes to KS-1032; does not resolve it.
