## Residue of the pull request 1546 round-2 review — 2 Minor + 4 Info, facts and file:line only

Pull request 1546 merged as `d53d80cbb2d50a5525c3d881a2da7a31eba67fb5`. The round cap was 2 of 2, so this residue is ticketed rather than fixed there. **No fix shape beyond "the text matches `routes/metering.ts:57-77`".** Review hashes: `34fb8ee6b4650ac6` (round 1), `4e98f3e1a91a1741` (round 2, GO WITH NOTE, 0 Major / 2 Minor / 6 Info).

### n1 (Minor) — the Major's false sentence survives in the rationale file the boot comment points to

* **`services/originate/src/utils/gatewayProvenance.ts:64-73`**, untouched by the round-1 commit. Lines 69-73 still say, *"Blast radius, measured rather than assumed: … so a SINGLE-TENANT deploy answers exactly as before … where it is on, the tenant is lost until the secret is set."* Lines 64-66 describe the deploy gate with no tenant assertion.
* `services/originate/src/index.ts:208-211` points readers at this file ("The full rationale … lives in utils/gatewayProvenance.ts"), so this is the text a developer is sent to.
* It contradicts the corrected `routes/metering.ts:57-77` in the same pull request, which says the claim *"holds ONLY where S's key tenant is already DEFAULT … UNMEASURED"*.
* Measured by the round-2 review: **R2-GA1** (secret unset, Platform S with Bearer) → 200, `data.tenantId = DEFAULT`; **R2-GA6** (a legitimate gateway-shaped human whose JWT tenant and `x-tenant-id` are both T_HUMAN) → 200, `data.tenantId = DEFAULT`. So the sentence is false for **every** caller whose tenant is not DEFAULT, not only for Platform S. Round-1 develop control: develop honours the header tenant.
* "Measured rather than assumed" is not true of the sentence it labels.

### n2 (Minor) — two more operator texts still describe unset as fail-open

* **`docs/ENVIRONMENT-VARIABLES.md:122-124`**, two lines below the new "Unset FAILS CLOSED" prose, tells operators to look for a boot line `[gateway-provenance] DISABLED — …honoured from ANY caller…` and to "check that line to know which state a box is in". **The merged head never emits that line.** Its unset boot line is `[gateway-provenance] FAIL-CLOSED — GATEWAY_VOUCH_SECRET is unset, so identity/tenant/role headers are DROPPED…` (`utils/gatewayProvenance.ts:187`). The head's own cells assert the message does **not** contain "honoured from ANY caller" (`ks1032-unconfigured-vouch-fails-closed.test.ts:166`, `ks1041-gateway-provenance.test.ts:233`). An operator told to grep for "DISABLED" finds nothing, and the doc quotes a fail-open statement as the current state.
* **`deployment/azure/services.bicep:126-128`** ("Empty is valid and fail-OPEN …"), **`:129`** (`@description` "Empty => provenance check inert"), **`:685`** and **`:823-824`** ("the documented fail-open"). That Container Apps estate was deleted 2026-07-31, so the practical risk is low; it is still a template in the tree contradicting shipped behaviour.
* **Honest note:** round 1's m3 listed five sites and missed both of these, because it scoped its grep. Round 2 grepped the whole `Blockchain/Dev` tree.

### i1 (Info) — line references made stale by the round-1 commit itself

* `utils/requestTenant.ts:17-18` and the pull request body name the three `.tenantId` writers as `index.ts:251`, `metering.ts:65`, `tenant-context.ts:91`. At the merged head they are **`index.ts:252`** and **`metering.ts:83`** — moved by **my own comment insertions**, by +1 and +18 lines. `tenant-context.ts:67`/`:91` is still correct.
* Also loose wording of mine: "`index.ts:251` (this function)" — that line *calls* the function, it is not the function.

### i2 (Info) — "the only 401 shape" is narrower than stated

* `routes/metering.ts:69`, the pull request body's table and both env templates say 401 arrives "only when the token exchange failed". **R2-GA7:** secret unset with an *invalid* Bearer also gives **401**, handler not run. It does not affect the deploy check, which asserts tenant rather than status.

### Two corrections to texts I wrote, recorded here so they are not rediscovered as new

* **i3 — attribution.** The texts I wrote file the multi-tenant-production **400** under "measured by the gate (GA1/GA2/GC5)". Round 1 never measured it; it was a static read, and round 2 measured it (`extractTenantContext`, "Missing tenant context", under `NODE_ENV=production` + `MULTI_TENANCY_ENABLED=true`, with a vouched control answering 200 on T_CONN and a development-mode arm answering 200 on DEFAULT). The claim is now true; **my attribution of it was wrong**. Also "on **every** request" is overstated: `GET /api` answers 200 and `/health` 503 in both states, because they mount ahead of the block.
* **i4 — a wrong sentence in my own cell file.** My comment in `ks1032-second-lines-hold-without-the-strip.test.ts` says restoring the vouch header "would be a different scenario (a caller who holds the secret)". That is **inaccurate**: the verdict is recorded before the restore and nothing downstream re-reads `x-gateway-vouch`, which is why the review's extra mutant x1 (the wrapper also restores the vouch header) survives all 71 cells. Harmless, but it is a false reason given for a real choice.

*Recorded by Seat J 9th after the merge. Contributes to KS-1032, which stays open; no behaviour change is proposed here.*

title: KS-1119 follow-ups (pull request 1542, Opus gate): the hash-match flag is not the lookup predicate, crossTenantLookup never retries the registry by hash, and four pre-existing verify disclosures
description:
## BLUF

Facts recorded from the Opus tier-1 gate on [pull request 1542](<https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/1542>) (KS-1119, merged as `026c2d1614065c79fc8d96007ac0d80f19fb9363`), filed at Wednesday's instruction. **Two items are KS-1119 residue; four are PRE-EXISTING and measured identical on develop and on the merged head, recorded here so nobody reads them as covered by that merge.** No fix shape is proposed for the two items that touch which registration answers — they need the KS-584 / KS-590 review first.

Measured at develop `405e33a1061310662b10245c5154c3d75c49f0f4` and at the merged head.

## A. KS-1119 residue

**A1 — leg (b) compares the exact stored hash, while the lookup matches three forms.** `services/originate/src/routes/verification.ts:1212`. The lookup accepts the bare digest, the `sha256:`-labelled form and a mixed-case spelling; the flag derived at :1212 compares only the exact stored value. Measured consequence under `MULTI_TENANCY_ENABLED=false`: a document stored as `sha256:<hex>` with a request `contentHash` of `sha256:sha256:<hex>` answered `verified:true` before the merge and answers `verified:false, documentExists:true, hashValid:false` after it. It refuses rather than admits; no caller in this repository sends that shape; the single-label and bare-digest controls still answer verified. Mutant M2 survives on the merged head and the shape above is what reaches it — the pull request body's "no reachable trigger" was wrong and has been corrected in place.

**A2 —** `crossTenantLookup` **never falls back to the registry by hash when the tenant the documentId points to has no hash match.** Consequence, measured under multi-tenancy: the exact right hash sent with the documentId of a document in ANOTHER tenant answered `verified:true` naming the wrong document before the merge, and after it answers "This document hash is not registered" — which refuses correctly but states something false, because the hash IS registered. **No fix shape here: a retry changes WHICH registration answers, so it belongs to the KS-584 / KS-590 review.**

## B. PRE-EXISTING, identical before and after the merge

**B1 — the documentId-only answer hands any caller the stored** `contentHash`**.** `verification.ts:1344`. Under multi-tenancy this crosses tenants: a caller holding only a documentId receives the document's content hash, which is the value the whole verify contract treats as the integrity secret.

**B2 —** `{documentId: X, hash: <hash of document Y>}` **answers** `verified:true` **naming Y.** The documentId is ignored when the hash matches. **This is the one a relying party reading only the** `verified` **field would trust**: it asked about X, the answer is true, and the document described is Y.

**B3 — KS-1590 is wider than verify-file.** The same unnormalised comparison also makes `/verify`'s hash-only cross-tenant answers depend on the spelling the caller sent. Added as a comment on [KS-1590](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1590) rather than restated here.

**B4 — the registry by-hash query has** `LIMIT 1` **with no** `ORDER BY`, so which tenant's registration answers an outsider is arbitrary and may change between identical calls. **Related but NOT the same query as** [KS-584](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-584), whose quoted SQL is the `documents`-table lookup and does carry `ORDER BY d.certified_at DESC NULLS LAST`; this one is `platform_document_registry` and carries no ordering at all. Recorded against the live [KS-590](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-590) because KS-584 is archived. **No fix shape: same reason as A2.**

## Dedupe

300 distinct issues read over six `searchIssues` terms with `includeComments` and `includeArchived`, then literal `containsIgnoreCase` matching on eight distinctive tokens. Positive control `platform_document_regist` found in 12 issues, so the pipeline demonstrably sees descriptions. Nine near hits were read one by one: KS-1119 (the parent), KS-1590 (B3's home), KS-584 and KS-590 (the documents-table variant of B4, distinguished above), KS-1118, KS-1133, KS-1129, PS-547, PS-514 — none covers A1, A2, B1 or B2. `verification.ts:1344` and "three-form" matched zero issues.

A first run's control token was the string `KS-1590` itself, which appears in no description and so could never fire; that run's near-hit list was discarded rather than reported.

title: Lifecycle vocabulary: add a `timestamp` verb (a signature's RFC 3161 timestamp added after signing)
description:
From platform-s [PS-1209](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1209/timestamping-as-one-service-three-tsas-in-order-and-an-automatic-retry) phase 2 (Stuart, 2026-10-13).

## What S now does

When every timestamp authority (DigiCert, GlobalSign, Sectigo) fails at signing time, platform-s saves the signature without a timestamp. A background retry then adds the timestamp later:

* **Detached** `.p7s`**:** an RFC 3161 token is added as an unsigned attribute. The document's bytes are unchanged; the `.p7s` is replaced.
* **PDF:** a DocTimeStamp is appended as an incremental update. This is a **new file and a new hash**.
* **Office:** a XAdES `SignatureTimeStamp` is added. This is also a **new file and a new hash**.

S records each one as a new lifecycle event with the verb `timestamp`. The actor is the platform itself, with no person.

## Why this ticket

K's vocabulary has no `timestamp`. Today S therefore **never sends** these events: `TransactionAction.IsNeverAnchored` excludes the verb everywhere rows are picked to anchor, the same way the read verbs are excluded.

The consequence: for PDF and Office, the current signed copy on S (the timestamped one) has a hash K has never seen. Verify on S still recognises it from S's own ledger. But K's lineage stops at the signed copy, and an on-chain check of the timestamped copy finds nothing.

## Ask

Add `timestamp` to the lifecycle vocabulary (`LIFECYCLE_VERBS` / the anchor `documentType` enum), as a **byte-changing** verb.

* **PDF / Office:** a new K version with `parent_document_id` = the signed copy, the same shape as `sign-cert`.
* **Detached:** the content hash is unchanged. A flat anchor is enough. Optionally record the new `.p7s` hash in metadata (compare [KS-1454](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1454/anchor-schema-accept-and-anchor-platform-ss-signaturehash-the-plain)'s `signatureHash`).

Once K accepts the verb, S will:

* move `timestamp` from never-anchored to anchored;
* route the byte-changing cases through the per-verb path with versioning;
* adopt it in `CardanoAnchorService.PlatformKAnchorVerbs`.

That will be a follow-up PS ticket.

## Payload

The only non-PII fields S would send are the `timestamp` verb, the content hash, and (for detached) the `.p7s` hash. The issuing authority's name (e.g. "DigiCert SHA256 RSA4096 Timestamp Responder 2026 1") is a service, not a person, and could go in metadata if K wants it.

Kam's words, verbatim:

> Build all three after KS-1454, inside the KS-1384 project

Card `secuura-s-signing-contract-additions-1019`, option **(a)**. Ruled on the live board 2026-10-19 between 18:22 and 18:23 AEDT; recorded 18:28.

"All three" is:
1. KS-1575 — record a signature against an existing K document without creating a new version;
2. KS-1575's `metadata.rowHash` ask;
3. **KS-1596** — the `timestamp` verb (a signature's RFC 3161 timestamp added after signing).

So the `timestamp` verb is accepted, and it is scheduled: after KS-1454, inside the KS-1384 project rather than as a standalone vocabulary change.

**Nothing is built by this comment** — no code, schema or vocabulary change. This records the ruling only.

**BLUF: @stuart.jamieson — received, with Kam, not scheduled. No date. First reply on this ticket, so recording what it asks and why it is not an isolated decision.**

The ask: a **`timestamp` verb** in the lifecycle vocabulary, for an RFC 3161 timestamp added to a signature *after* signing — making a new version for PDF and Office files, and a flat anchor for a detached signature.

Why it is not being answered on its own merits yet:

- It adds a verb to the **published lifecycle vocabulary**, which is a contract change on a public route rather than an internal addition.
- It lands in the same decision as the other signing-contract asks (KS-1575, and the signature-hash work), and all of them depend on how events map to anchor rows — the KS-1384 question Kam has just ruled the shape of but not the schedule.

Deciding the verb in isolation risks a vocabulary that then has to change again when the per-event anchor project starts, so they go to Kam together.

**Nothing is being built on this.** No date. When it is decided it lands here as a comment.

title: KS-759 follow-up: nothing pins that originate's connectorContext reads stay type-checked — a cast reintroduced at either site is invisible to every suite (facts only)
description:
## BLUF

**Facts only, no fix shape chosen.** Pull request 1543 (KS-759) deletes the `as unknown as { tenantId?; organizationId? }` casts in both `connectorContext` functions, so the compiler now checks those reads. **Nothing keeps it that way.** A cast reintroduced at either site would compile, lint and pass every suite, exactly as the original did. Filed on Wednesday's instruction (ruling 3 on KS-759: no guard cell in that PR; a facts-only P3 afterwards if a guard is worth a ticket).

## The measurement that shows the gap

Same deletion of both fields from originate's `JwtPayload` (`services/originate/src/middleware/auth.ts`), same `npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json`:

| tree | result |
| -- | -- |
| develop `a7cffc8d` (casts present) | **rc 0, zero errors anywhere in originate** |
| pull request 1543 head `502b164e` (casts removed) | **rc 2, exactly four TS2339**, at `routes/gdpr.ts` 472 / 477 and `routes/platformOrganizations.ts` 54 / 56 |

So the protection exists only while the code stays as 1543 leaves it. Re-adding the cast restores the first row, and no suite runs a check that would notice: the change is type-only, so every runtime cell is green either way.

A related fact from the first row: with both fields deleted, **nothing else in originate fails to compile**. These two functions are the only places originate reads either field off a `JwtPayload`.

## Why a source-text guard is not enough

A grep for `as unknown as` near those reads passes when the offending line is commented out, and misses a differently-shaped cast (`as any`, an intermediate variable, a `Record<string, unknown>` widening). This repo has been bitten by that class before — KS-1319, a wiring pin that passed on a commented-out line.

## Shapes worth weighing (not chosen)

* A **tsc-level cell**: a test-only file that reads `user.tenantId` / `user.organizationId` off a `JwtPayload` value under `// @ts-expect-error` *with the fields deleted*, run by the type-check ratchet. Note originate is **not** in the test-file type-check ratchet's default list today (that list is auth, api-gateway and vc-issuer).
* Make `connectorContext` take an already-typed payload, so there is nothing to cast — a wider change that touches the callers.
* Or accept the gap: it is a typing guarantee, and the values themselves are unchanged by any cast.

## Related

\[\[KS-759\]\] the parent · \[\[KS-764\]\] where `tenantId` was declared on `JwtPayload` · \[\[KS-1319\]\] the commented-out-line class

title: verify-file's cross-tenant registry lookup compares the sha256:-prefixed hash against platform_document_registry.content_hash with no normalisation, so it never matches a bare-hex registration (measured; facts only, no fix)
description:
## BLUF

`POST /api/verification/verify-file` searches `platform_document_registry` with the `sha256:`**-prefixed** hash, by exact equality and with no normalisation. The registry stores whatever the registering caller passed, verbatim. **So where registrations carry a bare hex hash, verify-file's entire cross-tenant path is unreachable** — a file certified in another tenant answers "not found" rather than being found through the registry.

**Facts only. No fix shape, no severity rating, and I have not measured which format real rows carry in any environment** — I have no box access. Filed on Wednesday's instruction, as a side reading from the KS-1119 proof.

## The two lines

* **The search**, `services/originate/src/routes/verification.ts:528-537` inside `crossTenantLookup`: when `documentId` is empty, the registry is queried as
  `SELECT * FROM platform_document_registry WHERE content_hash = $1 LIMIT 1` with `$1 = hashToVerify` — **exact equality, no** `sha256:` **handling on either side.**
* **The caller**, `:663`: `crossTenantLookup('', fileHash)`, where `fileHash` is built at `:639` as
  `` `sha256:${crypto.createHash('sha256').update(fileBuffer).digest('hex')}` `` — **always prefixed**. (`hashNorm`, the unprefixed form, is computed on the next line and is *not* what is passed.)
* **The write**, `registerInPlatformRegistry` (`:487-509`): stores `doc.contentHash` verbatim, with no normalisation either. The format in the table is therefore whatever the registering caller supplied.

Contrast: the *tenant-DB* query a few lines later (`:553-566`) is careful about exactly this — it strips the prefix into `searchHash` and matches `content_hash = $1 OR = $2 OR = $3` across all three forms. The registry query above it does not.

## The measurement

From the KS-1119 probe, on a local scratch PostgreSQL 15 with `MULTI_TENANCY_ENABLED=true`, as `secuura_app` (`rolsuper=false`, `rolbypassrls=false`), 3/3 cells in each run. The **only** difference between the runs is the format stored in `platform_document_registry.content_hash`:

| registry row stored as | verify-file reached the cross-tenant path? |
| -- | -- |
| `sha256:<hex>` | **yes** — the registry hit, and the lookup continued into the tenant DB |
| bare `<hex>` | **no** — the registry search found nothing, `crossTenantLookup` returned `null` |

Control in both runs: a file with no registry row at all answers `verified:false`, so the instrument can tell a miss from a hit.

*(The prefixed run is also how \[\[KS-1119\]\]'s second instance was found — that is a different defect and lives there. This ticket is only about the format mismatch making the path unreachable.)*

## What is NOT established

* **Which format real rows carry**, on Kintsugi, on the demo VM, or anywhere else. That reading is on the deploy-time census list with KS-1119's.
* Whether `v1 /verify` is affected the same way. It is **not**, on the path I measured: when a `documentId` is supplied the registry is searched by `document_id` first, so the format never arises; and when only a hash is supplied, that hash is whatever the *caller* sent, which may or may not carry the prefix. I did not measure the hash-only-no-documentId shape.
* Whether this is intended. It may be that every registration is expected to be prefixed, in which case the bug is on the write side or nowhere.

## Related

\[\[KS-1119\]\] — the proof this fell out of · \[\[KS-584\]\] and \[\[KS-590\]\] — which registration a hash resolves to (a different question; this ticket is about whether the row is found at all) · \[\[KS-598\]\] — the registry upsert collapsing registrations per `(hash, tenant)`.

**BLUF:** At develop `07a2d62be6a0` the single-form registry read this ticket describes is unchanged, and gate 192 measured both directions on PostgreSQL 15 (G192-F4, base = head, pre-existing): a bare registry row is found by `/verify` and missed by `verify-file`, and a prefixed registry row is found by `verify-file` and missed by `/verify`. This matches the ticket's third comment (the same form dependence on `/verify`).

Source: /Volumes/DevMASTER/WEDNESDAY/0_Brain/reference/2026-11-05_gate192-ks1986-pr2004/verdict.md, finding G192-F4 (lines 46 to 56), cells `S-NO-LOCAL-ROW` and `G-NO-LOCAL-ROW-PREFIXED-REGISTRY`; /Volumes/DevMASTER/WEDNESDAY/0_Brain/reference/2026-11-05_gate192-ks1986-pr2004/ready_2004.txt, FILING CANDIDATES (c).

* Lines now, in `Blockchain/Dev/services/originate/src/routes/verification.ts`: `verify-file` builds `fileHash = sha256:<hex>` at line 905 and calls `crossTenantLookup('', fileHash)` at line 941; `/verify` calls `crossTenantLookup(documentId || '', computedHash)` at line 1415, with `computedHash` the supplied hash, or `sha256:<hex>` when only document data is sent (lines 1164 to 1167 and 868 to 871). The registry read is lines 787 to 790, `content_hash = $1 ORDER BY created_at ASC, id LIMIT 1` (the ORDER BY came with KS-1561's D4), with `$1` unchanged.
* The write side is as this ticket says: `registerInPlatformRegistry` inserts the hash as given (lines 746 to 757). In `Blockchain/Dev/services/originate/src/routes/documents.ts`, line 679 sets `hash = clientHash || generateContentHash(data)`, lines 794 to 798 pass it on, and lines 577 to 582 accept a client `contentHash` with an optional `sha256:` prefix, so both forms can enter the registry. Gate 192 reports that `generateContentHash` returns bare hex (not re-read here).
* Of the registry readers this seat read, v2 `crossTenantRowsByHash` (`Blockchain/Dev/services/originate/src/routes/verificationV2.ts` lines 314 to 345) and PR 2004's `readCrossTenantOriginals` (`Blockchain/Dev/services/originate/src/routes/verification.ts` lines 602 to 612) bind the hash, the bare form and the prefixed form; v1 `crossTenantLookup` is the single-form one.
* Letter case is a separate gap: an original stored with an upper-case hash is invisible to the originals read (filed as KS-1996).

Not measured: which form production registry rows hold (the gate did not measure it; the census this ticket mentions is still owed); any deployed multi-tenant environment; no test and no service was run by this seat (Seat S 19th), and the code facts are reads of a depth-1 clone at `07a2d62be6a0`.

## Wider than verify-file: `/verify`'s hash-only cross-tenant answers also depend on the spelling the caller sent

Recorded from the Opus tier-1 gate on [pull request 1542](https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/1542) (KS-1119, merged `026c2d1614065c79fc8d96007ac0d80f19fb9363`). Facts only; no fix shape, because a change here alters **which** registration answers and that belongs to the KS-584 / KS-590 review.

This ticket is written against `verify-file`. The same unnormalised comparison sits on the `/verify` path too: the registry lookup compares the `sha256:`-prefixed hash with no normalisation, so a cross-tenant hash-only answer depends on the form the caller happened to send. A registration stored as bare hex is unreachable from a `sha256:`-labelled request and vice versa — on `/verify`, not only on `verify-file`.

Measured identical on develop `405e33a1061310662b10245c5154c3d75c49f0f4` and on the merged head, so **the KS-1119 merge did not change it and must not be read as covering it.**

Filed alongside this as [KS-1597](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1597), which carries the other three pre-existing observations from the same gate — including that the `platform_document_registry` by-hash query has `LIMIT 1` with no `ORDER BY` at all, which is a different query from the `documents`-table one quoted on KS-584.

@kamil.kreiser — the format question you could not measure, answered from the S side for every document S registers: **S's registrations are bare hex.** Originate is called with `contentHash = tx.ContentHash.ToLowerInvariant()` — 64 lowercase hex characters, no `sha256:` prefix — and `POST /api/documents` stores `clientHash` verbatim (`documents.ts`, `const hash = clientHash || …`) before handing the same value to `registerInPlatformRegistry`. So on Kintsugi and demo-pk every `platform_document_registry` row written for a Platform-S document carries a **bare** hash, and by your measurement `verify-file`'s cross-tenant path cannot find any of them. S itself is not a caller of `verify-file` and is unaffected on its own verifies: S posts `providedHash` to `/api/verification/verify` (and to v2 when enabled) after stripping any prefix and lower-casing, so its hash is in the form the tenant-DB query already handles. title: KS-1564 follow-ups (pull request 1537 round-2 gate): the ks1564 source guard is satisfied by a parenthesised argument, an alias and a COMMENTED-OUT guard; describeFailure's trailing-dot trim is quadratic; the three Playwright cells have never run
description:
## BLUF

Three carried items from the **round-2 (delta) gate** on pull request 1537, Sonnet tier 2, **GO WITH NOTE, 0 Major / 2 Minor** — reports `de22859410b28af3` (round 1) and `465eec274ce18e10` (round 2). Neither Minor blocked the merge. Filed before the squash on Wednesday's instruction.

**The through-line: the ks1564 cells pin TEXT, and the browser run is what pinned BEHAVIOUR.** That is fine while the browser run exists; it is not fine as the standing regression guard, because five mutants walk straight past it.

---

## A. The source guard can be satisfied wrongly

`packages/shared/src/__tests__/ks1564-admin-api-keys-page-sends-no-default-org.test.ts` — the `fetchApiKeysArgs` regex and `racesAreGuarded`. **Five mutants SURVIVED 9/9**, each one a real way to break the page while the guard stays green:

| mutant | what it does | why nothing reds |
| -- | -- | -- |
| **N3** | the race guard line turned into a **comment** | cell 5 is a text-position check; the behaviour is then unguarded |
| **N6b** | `fetchApiKeys(String(orgId) \|\| ['default','org'].join('-'))` plus any other plain call | the argument regex is `[^()]*`, so an argument **containing parentheses** is not seen and the call is skipped |
| **N7** | alias call — `const f = fetchApiKeys; f('x')` | no parenthesis follows the name, so the scrape misses it |
| **N9** | the **organisations-loader** guard deleted | no cell pins it at all |
| **N10** | the Generate **in-flight** guard (`submitRef`) deleted | no cell pins it at all |

Killed, for contrast: N1, N2, N4, N12 (cell 5) and N5, N11 (cell 4); the comment-only control stayed green. One conservative false red: N8, a *comment* quoting `fetchApiKeys(orgId || 'x')`, reds cell 4 — harmless.

**Also worth recording:** the round-2 brief expected cells 4 **and** 5 to red on the old code. Only **cell 5** does. The old code already called `fetchApiKeys(orgId)`; cell 4 only reds a bad call *shape*. Nothing is wrong in the product — the expectation was half wrong, and a red-first claim built on it would have been overstated.

### Shape

Parse with a TypeScript AST, or strip comments first and match the argument by **balanced** parentheses rather than `[^()]*`. Add a cell for the organisations-loader guard and one for `submitRef`. Each new cell red-first against the mutant it is meant to catch — N3, N6b, N7, N9, N10 respectively.

### This class has a precedent, and it is \[\[KS-1319\]\]

"walkTimeouts guard: **the wiring pin passes on a commented-out line**" — same failure mode (a source scrape a comment satisfies), different guard, already Done. N3 is that class recurring in a second guard, which is the argument for doing A as a parser change rather than another regex.

---

## B. `describeFailure`'s trailing trim is quadratic

`frontend/admin/src/pages/ApiKeys.tsx:99` — `message.replace(/[.\s]*$/, '')`. Backtracking is quadratic on a long run of dots or whitespace **followed by another character**. Measured in node (V8, the browser's engine):

| input | time |
| -- | -- |
| 20k spaces + `"x"` | 230 ms |
| 40k spaces + `"x"` | 947 ms |
| 80k spaces + `"x"` | **3.84 s** |
| **control:** 80k plain letters | **0.27 ms** |

A server error message of that shape would freeze the tab. **Exposure is low** — the messages come from the platform's own services — but that text can still echo user input, so it is not structurally impossible.

### Shape

Trim in a linear way: `message.replace(/\s+$/, '').replace(/\.+$/, '')`, or a manual end-scan. A cell with an 80k-space input and a wall-clock bound would red the current code.

---

## C. The three Playwright cells have never been run

`tests/e2e/tests/sysadmin-exhaustive.admin.spec.ts` cells 3.8b.1-3.8b.3. **Not run in round 1, not run in round 2, not run by the author.** A QA pass needs the Docker stack. The gate read them against the code and they look right (`openApiKeysTab` waits for `GET /api/platform/tenants`, takes the first tenant id from `body.data.tenants ?? body.tenants`, opens `platform/clients/<id>?tab=api-keys`; `App.tsx:53-54` and `ClientDetail.tsx:54,355` render `<ApiKeys />` for that tab; every testid it uses was exercised against a stub) — but **reading is not running**.

**One concrete way the cleanup cell can red on the real stack:** 3.8b.1 revokes the key it minted by finding its row *on the current table page*. The page lists **10 per page in server order**. If the organisation already holds more than 10 keys and the new one is not on page 1, the revoke locator fails. Unknown without the real stack.

---

## What the browser run DID establish (so nobody re-does it)

Both round-1 Majors are **fixed**, proven in a browser against a stub, each with a control build of the old head that **reproduces the bug**: the stale-list overwrite (round-1 reproduction now ends on Beta; the old head still shows Alpha), A-B-A-B-B switching, Refresh in flight, a late error after a newer success, unmount mid-request, and the organisations-loader-versus-tenant-switch case. Double-click mints **one** POST (old head: two). No `window.alert`, no fake key on failure, XSS rendered as literal text.

Note the limit the gate itself drew: the organisations-loader guard **line** is not exercised even by that run, because the real route remounts the component — consistent with N9 showing no cell pins it.

---

## Related

\[\[KS-1564\]\] the parent · \[\[KS-1319\]\] the same guard class, already Done · \[\[KS-1155\]\] the walkTimeouts budget this PR's `walkTimeouts.setup.ts` touch belongs to.

**BLUF:** Delivered: PR 1734 merged as bc958363c549 on develop, deployed to kintsugi at b1fb543640e7 (recorded deploy, 2026-11-01). Verified by code read at b1fb543640e7, not observed live (a test file). Left open: items B and C are not part of PR 1734.

- **Item A is in the code:** `Blockchain/Dev/packages/shared/src/__tests__/ks1564-admin-api-keys-page-sends-no-default-org.test.ts` reads the admin-page guard off the TypeScript AST (header :17-48), so a guard line turned into a comment (N3) and an argument containing parentheses (N6b) now go red.
- **Left open, as the ticket's comment 4f3c8357 records it:** item B (`describeFailure`'s trailing-dot trim is quadratic) and item C (the three Playwright cells have never run).

**Item A is READY FOR GATE as PR #1734, head `b6c678248c98d55f935add0fb3f6a563a0749e5f` (read from origin). Items B and C are NOT done, so this ticket stays open.**

All five mutants the round-2 gate recorded as surviving 9/9 now red, each on the cell meant to catch it. Measured twice on a fresh worktree at base `c3eb63c9d23b`, 2026-10-27, Kamil's MacBook Pro (Mac14,5, 12 cores), node v26.8.1, vitest 4.1.12, TypeScript 5.9.3.

| mutant | before | after | cell |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| N3 — guard line turned into a comment | green | **RED** | 5 |
| N6b — argument containing parentheses | green | **RED** | 4 |
| N7 — alias call | green | **RED** | 4 |
| N9 — organisations-loader guard deleted | green | **RED** | 6 (new) |
| N10 — Generate `submitRef` guard deleted | green | **RED** | 7 (new) |
| N1, N2, N4, N12 | RED | RED | 5 — still killed |
| N5, N11 | RED | RED | 4 — still killed |
| comment-only control | green | green | unchanged |

Each mutant was applied to a **copy** of `frontend/admin/src`, with the guard pointed at the copy by a new `KS1564_ADMIN_SRC` override. `ApiKeys.tsx` is never edited. The copy's sha256 is asserted to change for every mutant, and an anchor occurring other than exactly once aborts the run rather than reporting a result.

**Shape: the AST, not a third regex** — the option this ticket names first. N3 is the KS 1319 class recurring in a second guard, which is the ticket's own argument for parsing; `ks781-p3-3-body-parser-order.test.ts` in the same package already uses the compiler API. `racesAreGuarded` is replaced by `latestRequestWins`, which decides the order from node positions and serves **both** loaders, so cell 6 is the same claim as cell 5 rather than a second implementation. `fetchApiKeysValueUses` is new; an import, a re-export, a declaration, another object's property and a *same-name* destructure are not escapes, while a *renaming* destructure is.

**Figures.** This file 9/9 → 13/13 ran, rc 0 both. Whole `packages/shared` 1035 → 1039 tests ran (1034 → 1038 passed), 54 files both, 53 passed both.

**Two corrections to this ticket's own record, measured:**

1. **The ticket says five mutants survived; on my tree only three do as written.** N6b and N7 survive only when the bad call is **added beside** the real `fetchApiKeys(orgId)` call. My first attempt replaced it, and cell 4 then reded through its own `expect(calls.length).toBeGreaterThan(0)` sanity assertion — a red for the wrong reason, not a detection. This ticket's own N6b wording ("plus any other plain call") is what resolves it, and with additive mutants all five survive exactly as recorded. Worth stating because a red-first claim built on the substitutive form would have been overstated.
2. **N8's false red is gone, deliberately.** This ticket records N8 — a comment quoting `fetchApiKeys(orgId || 'x')` — as a conservative FALSE red on cell 4. It is now green: stripping comments is the fix this ticket prescribes, so removing that false positive and killing N3 are the same change. Control C4 pins both halves.

**Not covered by this PR:** item B (the quadratic trailing trim at `ApiKeys.tsx` `describeFailure`) and item C (the three Playwright cells, which need the Docker stack). Neither is touched. No browser run here — `frontend/admin` has no unit tier (KS 1391), so cells 5, 6 and 7 pin the **order of the guard statements in the source** and cannot show a stale answer being dropped or a second click minting nothing. The four platform suites (Schemathesis, Akto, Playwright, Performance/k6) are UNMEASURED and not claimed as a pass.

**Also measured, and relevant beyond this ticket:** nothing in the repository type-checks this file — `packages/shared/tsconfig.json` excludes `src/__tests__` and `check:test-types` (`package.json:44`) covers only auth, api-gateway, vc-issuer, security and m365-integration. It was type-checked separately, rc 0, with a planted `TS2322` inside `rootDir` as the control that fires. `npm run lint -w packages/shared` is rc 1 before and after on the pre-existing `no-control-regex` error (`BACKLOG.md:884`); zero lint lines name this file.

Per the repo-local `secuura-test-discipline` skill section 4, the two platform-k HTML docs are updated in the **same commit** (flow section 60, plus a cheat-sheet entry): this change moves cell counts, a run command and red-first ratios, so the escape clause does not apply.

*Posted by the Platform K build seat. `gh` ran under the project's own token as `kksecura`.*

title: KS-1582 follow-up (pull request 1536 gate m-a, m-b, N1): pin the transaction-local timeout and its value, pin the ::text tenant compare, and handle a pg client error while checked out
description:
## BLUF

**The follow-up to pull request 1536 (KS-1582): two coverage Minors and one pre-existing note from its Sonnet delta gate** (verdict sha256/16 `7306c470a243195b`, GO WITH NOTE, 0 Major). The code change behaved correctly in every probe, so these are gaps in the PR's own cells. Facts only, from the gate's report. Filed on Wednesday's GO.

## m-a: nothing pins that the timeout is transaction-local, or its value

* Where: `services/referral/src/__tests__/ks1582-referrer-wallet-read-gate-cells.integration.test.ts`, cell P (its connection probe reads only the tenant GUC) and cell B1 (`expect(ms).toBeLessThan(8_000)`). Code under test: `services/referral/src/db.ts:210` (`SET LOCAL statement_timeout = ${WALLET_READ_TIMEOUT_MS}`), the constant at `:199`.
* The gate's mutants **Z1** (`SET statement_timeout = 3000` before `BEGIN`), **Z4** (`SET` without `LOCAL` inside the transaction) and **Z3** (the value 7000) all leave the PR's 20 integration cells and 3 unit cells green.
* Z1 and Z4 would leave a permanent 3 s `statement_timeout` on a pooled connection that every other referral query also uses.
* Fix asked for:
  * in P's probe, also read `current_setting('statement_timeout')` and assert `'0'` for each distinct pid (the gate's T1 does this; its control T0 shows the probe can see a leak);
  * tighten B1 to a window around the bound, for example more than 2500 ms and less than 4500 ms.

## m-b: the stated reason for `::text` (no cast error) is not pinned

* Where: `ks1582-tenant-bound-in-sql.integration.test.ts`, which exercises only the exact tenant and one other uuid tenant; code at `db.ts:212` (`tenant_id::text = $2`).
* The gate's mutant **Z7** (`tenant_id = $2::uuid`) passes every PR cell. With it, a token whose `tenantId` is not a uuid (`not-a-uuid`, an array, a number) makes generate answer **5xx** for a signed-in user, where develop answers 201. The head answers 201 for all 13 shapes the gate tried.
* Fix asked for: one cell of the gate's M2 shape (a non-uuid, an array and a number `tenantId` under the app role answer 201 with no wallet), or a non-uuid tenant added to the bypass file's RED cell.

## N1 (pre-existing, the same on develop `c855cfc2`): an unhandled `pg` client error

* When the database kills the backend mid-read (or on a failover), the checked-out `pg` client emits an `error` event that nothing listens for. vitest reports `Uncaught Exception: Connection terminated unexpectedly`, while the request itself correctly answers 500 and the next one works.
* The identical pattern exists in `queryWithTenantGuc` in `packages/shared`.
* In production an uncaught exception exits the process, per `packages/shared/src/utils/gracefulShutdown.ts`.
* Not introduced or worsened by KS-1582: a statement timeout is an ordinary query error, not a connection error.
* Fix asked for: a `client.on('error', …)` while a client is checked out, in shared code (outside KS-1582's scope).

## Notes carried, no action asked

* N2: a read slower than 3 s now fails closed (500). That is the intended trade, and the bound is a product decision.
* N3: B1 takes about 12 s on a red run and about 3 s on a green one.

nodes.body:
**The pull request 1539 gate found the SAME defect on a second code path — adding it here rather than filing a duplicate.**

This ticket's **N1** is "a checked-out `pg` client with no `'error'` listener", and names `queryWithTenantGuc` in `packages/shared`. The 1539 gate (verdict `91e8da4021c40661`, finding **m3**) measured the same class in **`services/security/src/db.ts:59-72`** — both `transaction()` and `queryWithTenantGuc` there.

What it measured, which is more than N1 had:

* On the **head**, through PR B's new route (its probe B6): a backend killed under a checked-out client raises an **uncaught** `Connection terminated unexpectedly`.
* On **develop**, through the **ordinary mint path**: the same uncaught error, 1 of 1. So this is **pre-existing** and not introduced by PR B — it adds a caller, not the class.
* In production an uncaught exception **exits the process** (`packages/shared/src/utils/gracefulShutdown.ts:24`, "uncaughtException … always exits").

So the fix N1 asks for should cover **both** sites: attach an `'error'` listener while a client is checked out (or `release(err)` to destroy it) in `packages/shared` **and** in `services/security/src/db.ts`.

Dedupe note, because it matters for whoever picks this up: Linear's `searchIssues` is **fuzzy** and returned 12 hits for a deliberately nonsensical control term, so it cannot be used as a membership test. This was deduped with a literal `containsIgnoreCase` filter instead, controlled both ways (0 for the nonsense term, non-zero for a real one). `client.on('error'` matches **only** this ticket.

Recorded by Seat V 7th from the pull request 1539 gate.

**Dedupe check against KS-1188 — recorded so the next seat does not redo it.**

KS-1188 was the single near-miss this ticket's dedupe printed, because both texts carry the literal string `connection terminated unexpectedly`. **KS-1188 does not cover N1, so N1 stays here.**

- KS-1188's findings are auth-side: an unpinned route-level 503 on the routes calling `getUserById` (F1), an unpinned key set on the classifier log line (F2), and a backup code burnt before the caller is told to retry (F3, a product decision).
- Its measurements were taken, in its own words, with "the DB, the DEK store and the logger stubbed and witnessed. There was no live stack." No `pg` client appears anywhere in it.
- N1 here is a real checked-out `pg` client emitting an unhandled `error` event when the backend is killed mid-read, which in production exits the process via `packages/shared/src/utils/gracefulShutdown.ts`.
- So the shared string is an *injected fault message* in KS-1188 and the *uncaught exception's own text* here. That is why the dedupe matched. It is not a shared defect.

**No relation link added, deliberately** — a `related` edge would assert a kinship the two tickets do not have.

Checked by Seat V 7th after pull request 1536 merged as `06d0109c837dc41abb1163d7a9a1388a44b021e2`.

title: security's own audit INSERT can never succeed on a repo-built database (previous_state/new_state undefined; encrypted details into jsonb) — POST /api/audit persists nothing, silently
description:
## BLUF

**On a database built from the repo,** `services/security`**'s own audit INSERT can never succeed, and** `dbSaveAuditLog` **swallows the error.** So `POST /api/security/audit` (`/api/audit` in the service) never persists its rows to `audit_logs`; they live only in the service's in-memory cache. **Measured** on a scratch PostgreSQL 15 built from `docker/init/*` and `run-migrations.sh`. Facts only, no fix. Found while building KS-1570 PR B, which avoids the path and does not change it.

## Two independent causes (develop `2cdf1d7a`)

1. **Columns that no schema source defines.**
   * `dbSaveAuditLog` (`services/security/src/index.ts:122-146`) inserts into `previous_state` and `new_state`.
   * Neither column exists in `docker/init/01-schema.sql:390` (`CREATE TABLE audit_logs`) or `migrations/001_initial-schema.sql:347`, and no later migration adds them (git grep: 0 hits in docker/ and migrations/).
   * Only `prisma/schema.prisma:524-525` declares them.
   * Measured error: `column "previous_state" of relation "audit_logs" does not exist`.
2. **Encrypted text into a** `jsonb` **column.**
   * `details` is written as the output of `encryptDetails` (a `v1:…` ciphertext string). The column is `jsonb` in both schema sources.
   * The service's boot widens it to TEXT (`runDbBootTasks`, the `ALTER TABLE audit_logs ALTER COLUMN details TYPE TEXT` block). That boot step runs as `secuura_app`, which by design has no DDL rights (`docker/init/01-create-app-role.sh`; KS-92's runtime-DDL class), and it logs a failure as "non-fatal".
   * So on a fresh database the column stays `jsonb`. Measured error once cause 1 is avoided: `invalid input syntax for type json`.
   * When PII_ENCRYPTION_KEY is unset, the details are plaintext JSON and cause 2 does not apply. Cause 1 still does.

## What is not known

Whether the Kintsugi and demo databases happen to have these columns, or a widened `details` (for example from a `prisma db push`, or an earlier owner-run boot). That needs a read-only check by a deploy seat:

```sql
SELECT column_name, data_type FROM information_schema.columns
WHERE table_name = 'audit_logs' AND column_name IN ('details','previous_state','new_state');
```

## Why it matters

The security service's audit endpoint reports success while persisting nothing (it fails open, silently). The gateway (`api-gateway/src/middleware/audit.ts:313`) and tokenisation (`services/tokenisation/src/index.ts:198`) write `audit_logs` with their own statements and are not covered by this ticket.

## Not decided here

The fix shape. Options: add `previous_state`/`new_state` and the TEXT widening as an owned migration; or drop the two columns from the INSERT and stop the runtime DDL.

nodes.body:
**A THIRD cause, from the pull request 1539 gate (verdict `91e8da4021c40661`, finding n2) — this ticket's fix is incomplete without it.**

This ticket records two reasons `dbSaveAuditLog` cannot succeed on a repo-built database (`previous_state` / `new_state` undefined, and the encrypted-details `jsonb` widening failing as `secuura_app`). The gate measured a third, independent of both:

* Callers build **`id: 'audit_<uuid>'`**, and **`audit_logs.id` is `uuid`**.
* As `secuura_app` that insert fails on its own, even with the two missing columns present: *"column id is of type uuid but expression is of type text"* (the gate's `results/ks1586_psql.txt`, step 2).

So a fix that only adds the two columns and widens the jsonb column will still leave `POST /api/audit` persisting nothing. All three causes have to go.

Recorded by Seat V 7th; not fixed here. PR B deliberately avoids this path with its own INSERT and plain-JSON ids, which is why its atomicity cell can prove the rollback.

title: KS-1570 PR A follow-up (pull request 1535 gate m1-m3, n1-n3): 503 on an infrastructure fault, EXPECTED_TABLES drift, PR B write-time checks, three nits
description:
## BLUF

**The follow-up to pull request 1535 (KS-1570 PR A): three Minors and three Nits from its Opus gate**, plus the inputs that PR B must honour. Verdict sha256/16 `908a786016f5c2f2`. Facts only, from the gate's report; line numbers at 1535's head `335dfd78`. The Major (M1) is its own ticket. Filed on Wednesday's GO.

## Minors

* **m1:** a scope read that hits a database **infrastructure** fault answers a generic **500**, not the retryable **503** that the KS-888 classifier gives the same fault on save.
  * Where: `services/security/src/index.ts:1181` (mint, through the catch at `:1323` → `errorHandler`) and `:1419-1421` (revoke, `next(err)`).
  * Measured with the app role cut off (connection limit 0, backends terminated): head 500/500; develop's save path 503/503. Fail-closed holds either way.
  * Fix: run the scope-read error through the same SQLSTATE 08/53/57 + socket classifier, and answer 503 `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE`.
* **m2:** `scripts/rls/verify-fail-closed.sh:53` has `EXPECTED_TABLES` without `admin_organisation_scopes`. The script's own selector picks the table up (measured), so every verification run prints a `DRIFT` line. Fix: add the table.
* **m3 (PR B's input, not a defect of 049):** "rows are written only by a platform role" is an application convention.
  * Measured as `secuura_app`:
    * an INSERT into its own tenant under the GUC succeeds;
    * WITH CHECK refuses another tenant;
    * a self-set `app.tenant_scope_bypass` inserts into any tenant. That is the repo-wide model, the same as 041.
  * There are no foreign keys: `user_id` is not checked against `users`, and `organization_id` is not checked against that tenant's `organizations`.
  * **PR B must** validate at write time that the user exists with role ADMIN in that tenant and that each organisation belongs to the tenant, decide on purging rows when a user is deleted or changes role, and keep the writer platform-only and audited.

## Nits

* **n1:** a stale docstring at `services/security/src/__tests__/ks1533-key-mint-organisation-arm.test.ts:80` ("UNDECIDED POLICY, KS-1535"). The cell itself is rewritten correctly. Reword to RULED (KS-1570).
* **n2:** the comment at `ks1570-admin-organisation-scope.integration.test.ts:19` and the PR body's M6 overstate.
  * "Read under the platform bypass, another tenant's rows would count" is true only if `WHERE tenant_id = $1` is also removed.
  * The gate's G1 (bypass only, WHERE kept) survives every cell. It is equivalent in behaviour.
  * The GUC property is pinned by no cell. Reword, or add a log- or `pg_stat_activity`-based pin.
* **n3 (pre-existing):** `services/security/src/db.ts:27-33` sets no `statement_timeout`, so a scope read blocked by a lock waits.
  * Measured: ACCESS EXCLUSIVE held 4 s, the client aborts at 2 s, nothing is minted while locked, and after release the A2 mint is refused and the A1 mint completes. It never allows.
  * Optional: a statement timeout. Referral got one in KS-1582.

## Also from the gate's NOT-tested list, for the deploy seat

The deploy seat must confirm that `secuura_app` has SELECT on `admin_organisation_scopes` on Azure. Otherwise every organisation-naming ADMIN mint and revoke answers 500: fail closed, but an outage of that feature.

title: KS-998 item 1 gate follow-ups (#1532): the six Minors of the Opus gate, and the Info that matters
description:
## BLUF

**The Opus tier 1 gate on pull request #1532 (KS-998 item 1) returned GO WITH NOTE: 0 Major, 6 Minor, 7 Info.** This ticket carries the six Minors and the Info that matters, so they are findable after #1532 merges. Facts only, from the gate's report.

* **Report:** `0_Brain/reference/2026-10-13_gate-pr1532/verdict.md` in the Wednesday tree, sha256/16 `85bf04b8ef22923b` (recomputed by the report's own recipe, placeholder replaced: equal; a one-byte change breaks it).
* **Head it is bound to:** `3dbfdf7e36443a8665b6a106e2d8ccbb6763cd44`. Instruments: macOS, `/bin/bash` 3.2.57, node v24.7.0, npm 11.5.1.
* **None of the six hides a formatting red or lets a push pass without a check.** (1) fails closed; (2) and (3) are properties of `npm ci` that the gate now triggers automatically.

## Where each rides (Wednesday's rulings, 2026-10-13)

* **Minors 1, 2, 4, 5, 6:** the stacked **item 2** pull request (same functions), each with its cell.
* **Minor 3:** a **third pull request stacked on item 2**, so item 2 stays reviewable: the lock-source allowlist AND a scrubbed install environment, lifecycle scripts still running as ruled. A plan mail comes first.

## The six Minors

1. **The final rename races (**`check-package-format.sh`**, the** `mv` **into place).** The `[ -e node_modules ]` guard is not atomic with the `mv`; BSD `mv` onto an existing directory moves the source INSIDE it, and onto a symlink to a directory moves it into the target. `_rm_stage` can then delete a `node_modules` the gate did not make. Measured with a PATH `mv` shim: a hollow in-progress tree was deleted; a symlink arrival had our tree written into the outside target; a complete tree arrival left `node_modules/node_modules`. **Two real gate processes on one package REFUSED a correct push in 4 of 5 trials** (`mv` loses its own rename race: ENOTEMPTY). It fails closed and what can be lost is a regenerable, gitignored tree, but it falsifies "deletes only what it made". **Fix:** `rename(2)` (via `node -e 'fs.renameSync'`), which refuses a non-empty or symlink target; map that to `raced`, not `mvfail`; drop a marker file into the staged tree before the rename and require it at `$dir/node_modules/` before any move-back.
2. **The watchdog and the TERM path kill npm's pid, not its process group.** A dependency's postinstall child outlives the gate (ppid 1) on the watchdog, on SIGTERM and on SIGKILL; only a Ctrl-C to the whole group removes it. esbuild's `install.js` fallback (`downloadDirectlyFromNPM`: `https.get`, no timeout, hard-coded registry) is the process that would be orphaned against a silent registry. **Fix:** start npm in its own process group (`set -m` in bash 3.2, or `perl -e 'setpgrp; exec @ARGV'`) and signal the group: TERM, then KILL, in both the watchdog and the cleanup. Same class as KS-1331 (a different script: `run-shell-suites.sh`).
3. **The gate does not check lock sources.** A lock entry whose `resolved` points at a non-registry host is fetched, and its postinstall runs on the push (measured: 1 GET at the listener, INSTALLED, a sentinel written outside the repo; a tampered integrity was refused with EINTEGRITY). Lifecycle scripts see `NPM_TOKEN`, `GH_TOKEN`, `SSH_AUTH_SOCK` and other `*TOKEN` names from the environment, and `~/.npmrc` is in scope; `--fetch-retries=0` and `--fetch-timeout` reach lifecycle children through `npm_config_*`. This is what a manual `npm ci` does too; the difference is that it now runs automatically on push, including for a package selected by a stale base or a merge the developer did not author. **Today's four lockfiles are clean:** 411/411, 344/344, 269/269 and 217/217 entries are `registry.npmjs.org` with an integrity hash. **Ruled YES:** every non-link entry must have `resolved` starting `https://registry.npmjs.org/` and a non-empty `integrity`; every `link` must resolve inside the repo; otherwise refuse with a named reason and run nothing; AND scrub the install's environment to a minimal set (`PATH`, `HOME`, what npm needs; no `*TOKEN`, no `SSH_AUTH_SOCK`).
4. `m23b` **("no EXIT trap") is NOT equivalent, contrary to the item 1 table.** On bash 3.2 the EXIT trap is what cleans up on untrapped fatal signals other than QUIT. SIGUSR1 mid-install: head kills npm and removes the stage; with the EXIT trap removed, npm stays alive and the stage stays. Same for SIGALRM and SIGPIPE. The other four survivors (`m13a`, `m23`, `m25`, `m35`) were re-derived by the gate and are equivalent. **Fix:** one cell that sends SIGUSR1 or SIGALRM mid-install and expects no orphan and no stage.
5. **Four mutants survive that are test gaps, not equivalents.** `Q8` (the post-move `-x` → `-e`): no cell has a non-executable prettier. `Q11` (the hollow re-check dropped): a raced-in hollow tree would be reported as a *formatting failure* instead of the environment refusal, the KS-991 confusion. `Q12` (`.npmrc` not copied to the stage): no fixture has a package `.npmrc`. `Q13` (the six-digit length guard dropped): a 20-digit `FORMAT_GATE_INSTALL_TIMEOUT` overflows and refuses at once with "timed out after 99999999999999999999s"; head exits 2 naming the variable. **Fix:** one cell each.
6. **SIGQUIT to the gate alone leaves npm and the stage.** It is not trapped and bash 3.2 does not run the EXIT trap for it: rc 131, the hung npm alive, one stage left (the next run sweeps the stage). **Fix:** add QUIT to the trap list.

## The Info that matters

* **Info 2 (pre-existing, KS-1483):** a branch deletion (`git push origin :todelete`) and a tag push were both REFUSED because HEAD's branch touched an uninstallable package: the hook computes the changed set from `@{upstream}..HEAD`, not from the pushed refs. The develop control refuses the same two pushes (KS-1063 NOTHING CHECKED), so it is not a regression of #1532. **KS-998 item 2 with KS-1483 fixes it** (per-ref judging; a deleted ref is skipped before anything runs).
* **Info 3:** `_rm_stage` with an EMPTY `STAGE_PREFIX` would delete a relative single-component directory under the cwd (demonstrated on the extracted function). Unreachable today: the prefix is assigned once, never empty, and `set -u` aborts if unset. **Defence in depth:** `[ -n "$STAGE_PREFIX" ]` and require an absolute `$d`.
* **Info 5:** `-x` is true for a *directory* named `.bin/prettier`, so it is INSTALLED and then reported as a formatting failure with rc 126. npm never produces this. Cheap: `[ -f ] && [ -x ]`.
* **Info 6:** an invalid `FORMAT_GATE_INSTALL_TIMEOUT` blocks every push, including pushes that touch no systemTest file (validation exits 2 before selection), and the hook's wrapper then says "fix the files named above", which is wrong for it. Loud and self-inflicted; the wrapper's wording is the defect.
* **Info 7:** esbuild's install-script network fallback, exercised under the sandbox: with `@esbuild/darwin-arm64` removed, `install.js` tries `npm install` and then a direct download. **70.4 s** with npm defaults, **0.43 s** with `npm_config_fetch_retries=0`, and that value IS inherited from the gate's `npm ci` (measured through a postinstall). Both paths verify the binary with a sha256 before use.

## NOT tested by the gate (carried as unmeasured)

Linux (GNU `mv` has the same move-into-directory behaviour, so Minor 1 is expected to apply, not measured); preflight legs 3, 4, 8 and the full A/B; a real pty Ctrl-C (emulated); a silent registry against esbuild's direct download (reasoned from the code); the `--no-update-notifier` request census (not repeated).

## Related

KS-998 (the parent, stays In Progress: item 2 and KS-1483 are unbuilt), KS-1483 (item 2 folds it in). Same class as KS-1331 (process-group signalling), in a different script. Pull request #1532, head `3dbfdf7e3644`.

## Read at source, item by item. **Five of the six Minors have landed WITH a labelled cell. Minor 5 is 3 of 4 — Q11 has no cell. So this ticket STAYS OPEN and NO state was moved.**

Read at develop `885d69b06f5fce7c8f58effea68623ecb25407b1`. `systemTest/scripts/check-package-format.sh` is 919 lines; `systemTest/__tests__/package_format_gate.test.sh` is 1,640 lines and carries **48** `# --- CASE` headers. Zero control on both files: 0. Positive control on the suite: 395 `check ` calls.

## The six Minors

| Minor | in the script | its cell | state |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| **1** rename race | `:290` `node -e '…renameSync…'` catching the error code; `raced` in the state list at `:468`; the marker-before-rename rule documented `:133-138` | **CASE 35** (`:1014`, header *"the final rename RACES (Minor 1)"*) — control, a COMPLETE tree arriving, a `.arrived-first` assertion, *"ours was NOT nested inside it"*, and a no-`.format-gate-moved`-marker check; **CASE 46** covers the move-back | **landed** |
| **2** process group | `:274` `exec perl -e 'setpgrp(0, 0); exec @ARGV …'` via `_run_grouped`, used at `:494` | **CASE 37** (*"npm runs in its OWN PROCESS GROUP …(Minor 2)"*) and **CASE 41** (*"no perl -> the install is REFUSED by name, never run ungrouped (Minor 2)"*) | **landed** |
| **3** lock sources + env scrub | `:224` `LOCK_ALLOW="${FORMAT_GATE_LOCK_ALLOW:-https://registry.npmjs.org/}"`; `_check_lock_sources` `:345-347`; `_build_install_env` `:412-414` with `env -i` at `:494` and a private `HOME` | **CASE 43** (*"the install runs under an ALLOW-LIST environment with a private HOME (Minor 3, second half)"*) plus the lock cases around `:1331-1338` | **landed** |
| **4** `m23b` / fatal signals | — (trap behaviour) | **CASE 38** (`:1184`, *"every fatal signal cleans up, not only TERM/INT/HUP (Minor 4; mutant m23b)"*) — `for sig38 in USR1 ALRM PIPE` at `:1188`, so SIGUSR1 **and** SIGALRM are both driven | **landed** |
| **5** four surviving mutants | Q13's guard at `:210` (`[ "${#FORMAT_GATE_INSTALL_TIMEOUT}" -gt 6 ]`); Q12's copy at `:485`; Q8's `_prettier_ok` at `:343` | **CASE 40** (`:1223`) carries **Q8** (`:1224`), **Q12** (`:1232`) and **Q13** (`:1239`), Q13 with a 20-digit, a 7-digit and a 6-digit boundary cell | **3 of 4 — see below** |
| **6** SIGQUIT | `:465` `trap '_fg_cleanup; exit 131' QUIT      # bash 3.2 does not run the EXIT trap for SIGQUIT (gate review, Minor 6)` | **CASE 39** (`:1201`), with a control proving SIGQUIT is deliverable to a job started that way (a plain sleep dies rc 131) | **landed** |

## The one gap: **Q11 has no cell**

CASE 40's header is *"the survivors of the gate review's mutation pass that were test gaps (Minor 5)"* and it names **Q8, Q12 and Q13 only**. `Q11` does not occur anywhere in the suite.

**The guard Q11's mutant removed does exist** — `check-package-format.sh:785`, inside `run_install`'s `raced)` outcome:

`_prettier_ok "$dir" || unready="hollow"`

That is the post-move hollow re-check: without it a raced-in hollow tree would be reported as a *formatting failure* rather than the environment refusal (the KS-991 confusion this Minor names). **Nothing asserts it.** `raced` occurs **0** times in the suite — measured against a firing control of 395 `check ` calls in the same file — so CASE 35's race cells drive the complete-tree and symlink arrivals but not a **hollow** arrival, which is the one that reaches `:785`.

By this ticket's own definition — *"Fix: one cell each"* for Minor 5's four — Minor 5 is **not** complete, so the ticket is not Done.

## One more fact, not claimed as blocking

**Info 6's wrapper wording is unchanged.** `.githooks/pre-push:330` still reads:

`echo "[pre-push] systemTest formatting gate FAILED — fix the files named above." >&2`

which is the sentence Info 6 calls the defect (it is wrong for an invalid `FORMAT_GATE_INSTALL_TIMEOUT`, which refuses before selection). **I am not treating this as blocking the ticket:** the "Where each rides" section assigns only the six Minors to pull requests; the Info items are carried here so they are findable. Stating it so the next reader does not have to re-measure. **Info 3** (`:307` `[ -n "$STAGE_PREFIX" ] && [ -n "$TREE_PREFIX" ] || return 1`) and **Info 5** (`:343` `_prettier_ok() { [ -f … ] && [ -x … ]; }`) **have** landed, with **CASE 44** covering both.

## Not established

* **I ran nothing.** No suite, no mutant, no gate. Every row above is a source read at the tip: a line present or absent, and a labelled CASE present or absent. "Landed" here means *the shape and a labelled cell exist*, not *the cell was observed to pass or to red against its mutant*.
* Whether CASE 35's existing race shims could be extended to a hollow arrival, or whether Q11 needs its own fixture. Not my call.
* Which pull request carried each Minor. The ticket's plan put 1, 2, 4, 5, 6 on the item-2 PR and Minor 3 on a third stacked PR; I verified the **tree**, not the route.

## Searched

Not a filing, so no dedupe was needed; the reads above are the instrument. For completeness, the same paginated board search used elsewhere this session returns `pre_push_stack_legs_comment` → 2 and `KS-1047` → 6, with positive controls `KS-1531` → **18** and `fetchApiKeys` → **4** and a zero-control token → **0**.

**Assignee** set to the board account with this comment, per the board rule for an unassigned ticket I write on.

title: GET /api/keys has no tenant-level mode: organisation-less keys cannot be listed, so the Admin Dashboard cannot show or revoke them
description:
## BLUF

`GET /api/keys` **can list only keys that carry an organisation id. An API key minted with no organisation (a tenant-level key) is never returned by any list call**, so the Admin Dashboard cannot show it and cannot offer its revoke (the page revokes by the key id it read from the list). **This is design work, not a defect:** the exclusion is deliberate in the handler. It matters now because the unqualified mint is the only mint an unscoped `ADMIN` will be allowed after KS-1570, and because Admin Dashboard change KS-1564 therefore leaves the "no organisation" option out of its dialog.

## Recommendation

Decide whether the list gets a tenant-level mode. No action is needed on KS-1564, KS-1570 PR A or PR B for this; none of them depends on it. Facts only.

## Detail (read at develop `343a7b4e`, not run)

* `services/security/src/index.ts:1319-1322`: `organizationId` is REQUIRED on `GET /api/keys`; a missing one answers 400 `organizationId required`.
* `index.ts:1356-1358`: a key is returned only when `wantedOrg !== null && normaliseOrgId(k.organizationId) === wantedOrg`. The comment at `:1347-1353` says the null case is intended: "null must not equal the stored null of every org-less, tenant-level key". So a key stored without an organisation never equals any non-null query.
* The mint allows it: `organizationId` is optional (`index.ts:627`), and an unqualified mint is allowed under the 2026-09-03 ruling (comment at `index.ts:1169-1175`). `tenant-provisioning`'s metering key is minted this way (`meteringKey.ts:45`, no `organizationId`).
* Revoke of such a key works today when the caller has the key's id (`keyRevokePolicy.ts:208`, org-less keys stay revocable). Only the list is missing, so the id has to come from somewhere other than this endpoint.
* A list for "keys in my tenant with no organisation" would also have to keep the tenant filter of KS-742 (`index.ts:1359`) and the role check, and would be a published-spec change (`security.openapi.ts` lists `organizationId` as required).

## Not covered

No dashboard behaviour was run; no key counts were taken on any environment (no box access).

## Dedupe (2026-10-13, Seat J 6th)

`searchIssues` with comments and archived included, five terms, 266 distinct issues; positive control: the term `default-org` found KS-1564, KS-1565, KS-1578. Near hits read: KS-1574 (the list has no organisation arm for ORG_ADMIN or ISSUER_ADMIN: a different gap on the same handler), KS-1570, KS-1533, KS-764, KS-779. None describes a tenant-level list mode.

Related: KS-1564, KS-1570, KS-1574 (same handler).

title: KS-695 follow-up: distinguishing code for a key revoked by erasure (S's ask, KS-695 comment 7221c520)
description:
## BLUF

Platform S asked K for a distinguishing code or status for an API key that was revoked **by erasure**, so S can read that fact instead of inferring it. **This is design work, not a defect, and nothing in the merged change (pull request 1497, squash** `343a7b4e`**) depends on it.** Nobody has decided whether to build it.

## Recommendation

Decide first whether K builds it. If yes, it is a small design: see "What K does today". No action needed for the erasure itself.

## The ask, verbatim

Stuart, ticket KS-695, comment `7221c520-c6fb-4343-aedd-7bffbfdc9b75`, 2026-10-12T23:00:58Z:

> **One ask of K:** a distinguishing code or status for a key revoked *by erasure* — on the POST (for example a 401 whose `error.code` says so) or on the status GET — would let S drop the inference in (2) and read the fact directly. Until then the attempt-count rule is what S will use. Nothing here blocks part ii's gate; S's change is small and I will note on this ticket when it is on develop.

The inference in (2), same comment: *"A 401 'Invalid API key' on this route counts as 'already erased, Confirmed' only when S has already recorded at least one attempt on that organisation's erasure (the row's attempt counter is non-zero)."* S's side of this is PS-1201 (point 4) and platform-s pull request 972 (In Review at 2026-10-13T00:52Z, per the ticket).

## What K does today (read at develop `343a7b4e`, not run)

* The erasure revokes the calling key last: `UPDATE svc_api_keys SET is_active = false` (`services/originate/src/services/connectorOrganisationErasure.ts:440`), the same write the security service's rotate makes (`services/security/src/index.ts:186`). Nothing on the row records why the key is inactive.
* A repeat call is refused at the gateway before the originate route runs: a presented `sk_` key that fails `validateApiKey` is answered `401 {"code":"UNAUTHORIZED","message":"Invalid API key"}` (`services/api-gateway/src/middleware/auth.ts:367-368`). That branch has no sub-code, so it cannot say why validation failed.
* The status GET (`GET /api/platform/organizations/erase-connector/:organisationGuid`, `routes/platformOrganizations.ts:152`) has a connector-role guard in originate. I did not trace the gateway mount of that path, so I do not know whether the same revoked key reaches it; if it does not, "a code on the status GET" would need a credential other than the revoked key.
* So any distinguishing code needs (a) a durable marker of the reason at the revoke, written in the erasure transaction, and (b) a gateway change, because the refusal happens at the gateway. Neither exists. A new `error.code` on that 401 is also a client-visible change to a shared door.

## Not covered

No S behaviour was read (K cannot read S's code); everything about S is Stuart's text above. No live check on any box.

## Dedupe (2026-10-13, Seat J 6th)

`searchIssues` with comments and archived included, five terms, 196 distinct issues. Positive control: the term `PlatformKErasureClient` found 4 issues (PS-1201, PS-699, PS-700, PS-701). Zero literal hits in title or description for "revoked by erasure". Near hit: PS-1201, the S-side counterpart, not a duplicate.

Related: KS-695 (the erasure), PS-1201.

title: KS-695 erase-connector round 6 gate follow-ups (pull request 1497): description wording for whitespace-only ids, an R3 cell for the second read, a stale cell title, an inaccurate header sentence, a legacy-key divergence
description:
## BLUF

Five facts from the Opus delta gate on pull request 1497 round 6 (report sha256/16 `0d886f63f692f62a`, head `c48d71638f330eb3a603a6e123471c4a1bbdf93e`) that are not defects in the merged change but are worth fixing or recording. One checklist; split an item out when someone picks it up. The code was deliberately NOT touched while the pull request was at the gate. Each item below was checked by me against the source (the lines are the ones read), except where it says it is the gate's measurement.

- [ ] **1. The published description understates the refusal (gate Minor m-1, cell V1).** `services/originate/src/originate.openapi.ts:3728` and the regenerated yaml `docs/openapi/secuura-api.yaml:31211` say a key "with an empty or absent id" authenticates as `connector:api-key` and is refused. The predicate is `isFallbackConnectorId(id) = id.trim() === '' || id === 'api-key'`, so a key whose stored connector id is **only whitespace** (a space, TAB, U+00A0, U+FEFF, U+3000, U+2028) is refused too: the gate measured 403 with nothing written on the real route in both tenancy modes, and 200 `completed` when both refusals were removed. Those ids are NOT the fallback principal: the gateway keeps a whitespace-only string as it is (`connectorId || 'api-key'`), so each is its own principal. Wording-only options: add "blank or whitespace only" to the description and the yaml, or narrow the predicate to `''` and the label. The pull request body was corrected; every real connector id is `platform-s:<guid>`.
- [ ] **2. Add an R3 cell beside R2 (gate N-1).** Mutant X2 (the second guard read moved to just BEFORE the blanking UPDATE, after the count) **survives the real-Postgres file** `ks695-ask3-erase-connector-fallback-principal.integration.test.ts` in both modes (gate: 8/8 green). Reason: R2 holds `LOCK TABLE documents IN ACCESS EXCLUSIVE MODE`, so the erase stalls at the count, and a read placed anywhere after the count still sees the key. X2 is killed by the three unit statement-order cells and by the gate's R3: `LOCK TABLE documents IN EXCLUSIVE MODE` lets the count run (a read takes ACCESS SHARE) and stalls the UPDATE itself; the key and root commit there; the code answers 403, X2 answers 200. This is the gate's measurement; I did not re-run X2.
- [ ] **3. A stale unit-cell title (gate N-2).** `__tests__/ks695-ask3-erase-connector-refusals.test.ts:279` says a key with a NULL id and one with an empty id "already got 403 from the ownership comparison and still does". After round 6 the 403 for those keys comes from the fallback refusal (the gate's direct resolver call gets `OrganisationErasureFallbackPrincipalError` for both); with both refusals removed the status is still 403, through the ownership mismatch. The cell pins the status, not the reason. Reword the title.
- [ ] **4. An inaccurate header sentence (gate N-4).** `services/originate/src/services/connectorOrganisationErasure.ts:220`: "a key that was deleted or rotated away". A rotation only deactivates or shortens the old key: `retirePriorStatement` in `services/security/src/index.ts` is an `UPDATE svc_api_keys SET is_active = false` (grace 0) or an `UPDATE ... SET expires_at = LEAST(...)`, and the security service source contains no `DELETE FROM svc_api_keys` (checked; the search found the two `UPDATE`s as its control). The guard reads inactive keys, so a rotated key IS seen. Only a DELETED key escapes it (the gate's cell C5: 200, 2 blanked, reachable only by a DBA delete).
- [ ] **5. A legacy key's connector id can differ between memory and the database (gate N-5; read from code only, NOT run).** The security service upserts `connector_id = COALESCE(EXCLUDED.connector_id, svc_api_keys.connector_id)` (`services/security/src/index.ts:401`, with a KS-869 comment that a pre-KS-869 row holds NULL and the next save backfills it) and validates from the in-memory key (`connectorId: apiKey.connectorId || null`, `:1299`, `:1569`); the boot load reads rows (`SELECT * FROM svc_api_keys`, `:535`). So a pre-KS-869 key that is live in memory with id X while its row holds NULL would authenticate as `connector:X`, while the erasure's guard, which reads rows, would not see it as carrying X. It closes on the next save or a reload. A census of Kintsugi's keys is the deploy seat's read-only item; nothing here was run against a box.

## Recorded in the verdict, no action asked

* **N-3.** A colliding key alone, with no document, can turn another organisation's erasure into a terminal 403 (the same availability property the first guard always had); minting a named connector id is platform- or provisioner-only since KS-1533 arm 1.
* **N-6.** The added guard read costs 4.2 to 6.5 ms with 50,000 keys in one tenant (a sequential scan, no index on `connector_id`), twice per erasure; negligible against the 25 s budget.

Related: KS-695.
