Five-point check 5/5; the landed tree is the tree I tested (`9bdd15e27bc783c25554fa00bedae0e6273cfc9f`), and I re-measured `services/tenant-provisioning` there at **21/21 in 5 files** rather than carrying the author's figure, because the PR's evidence said "delta 0, the landing tree" and that had stopped being true — develop had moved seven commits.

**This ticket stays open**, and the link is `Refs`, because the PR pins the ORDER BY *text*, not the paging *behaviour* this ticket's own test spec asks for (>200 rows sharing one `created_at`, read in two windows, no id duplicated or missing). The query-plan check is also still owed.

## Residue 1 — the same missing tie-break on the gateway's `audit_logs` reads, but a *different* consequence

I was asked to record that "the same tie-break gap exists on the gateway's `audit_logs` query". It does — and the consequence is **milder than a paging hazard**, which is worth stating so nobody sizes it wrongly:

| site | query | paged? |
|---|---|---|
| `services/api-gateway/src/routes/platform.ts:447-453` | `SELECT … FROM audit_logs ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT $1` (`overfetch`) | **no OFFSET** |
| `services/api-gateway/src/routes/admin.ts:1542` | `SELECT * FROM audit_logs ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT 1000` (CSV export) | **no OFFSET** |

Neither uses OFFSET, so there is **no window boundary** and therefore none of the duplicate-or-skip behaviour this ticket is about. What they do have is a nondeterministic **cut**: among rows tied on `created_at`, *which* ones fall inside the `LIMIT` is not promised to be stable between two calls. For the CSV export that means two exports a second apart can differ by a tied row; for `platform.ts` the overfetch is then merged with the platform half and sliced in JS, so the same instability reaches the page the UI renders. Both want `, id DESC` for the same reason — just not for the same failure.

## Residue 2 — the index note I was handed is wrong for one provisioning path and right for the other, and the divergence is the real finding

The note said "there is no index on `platform_audit_log`". Measured:

| path | indexes on `platform_audit_log` |
|---|---|
| **migrations** (`migrations/003_platform_tenancy.sql:49` creates the table) | **ZERO** — no `CREATE INDEX` naming that table anywhere under `migrations/` |
| **docker-init** (`docker/init-platform/01-platform-schema.sql`) | **three** — `idx_platform_audit_actor (actor_id)` `:131`, `idx_platform_audit_action (action)` `:132`, `idx_platform_audit_time (created_at DESC)` `:133` |

Counts: 0 hits under `migrations/`, 3 under `docker/` — so the zero is a real absence, not a failed search.

**So a migrations-provisioned database — which is the deployed path — has no index on this table at all, while a docker-init local stack has three.** That is a schema divergence between the two provisioning paths, and it is the kind that hides: a developer profiling this query locally gets an index-backed plan that production does not have. It also means the ticket's own framing ("`idx_platform_audit_time` is on `created_at` alone") describes the *local* schema, not the deployed one.

Two things follow, and I have not done either:
1. The deployed schema should be read directly to confirm the absence on the live boxes (the DDL is the prediction, not the measurement).
2. Whichever index is added should be `(created_at DESC, id DESC)`, to cover the ordering this PR just introduced rather than only its first column.

---

*Seat R 51st, 2026-10-19. Residue 1 and 2 were handed to me as notes from gate O2; I read the source and the schema before writing them here, which is why both are stated differently from how I received them. Measured at develop `37834600a543cb0276f427d969ac034d9df74fbd`. Nothing deployed.*

title: One role vocabulary, seven divergent lists: platform_admin is a super-role to the gateway and an ordinary tenant user to the key policy
description:
## BLUF

**The same question — "is this caller a platform role?" — is answered by at least seven separate hard-coded lists that do not agree.** The one that matters most: `platform_admin` is accepted as a super-role by the api-gateway in six places, and is **absent** from the key policy's `PLATFORM_ROLES`, so `decideTenantAccess` treats it as an ordinary tenant user.

Found while building KS-1533 arm 1 (the mint's organisation arm). It is **not** folded into that ticket: arm 1 is one call site, this is a repo-wide vocabulary problem. KS-1535 records the *policy* question of which roles may cross an organisation boundary; **this ticket is the engineering problem that there is no single answer to consult.**

## The seven lists, read at source

```
services/api-gateway/src/routes/platform.ts:65       SUPER_ROLES           super_admin SUPER_ADMIN platform_admin SYSTEM_ADMIN
services/api-gateway/src/middleware/auth.ts:515      SUPER_ADMIN_ROLES     super_admin SUPER_ADMIN SYSTEM_ADMIN platform_admin
services/api-gateway/src/routes/admin.ts:577         PLATFORM_SCOPE_ROLES  SYSTEM_ADMIN system_admin super_admin SUPER_ADMIN platform_admin
services/api-gateway/src/routes/proxy.ts:1094,1227   (two inline lists)    …include platform_admin, ORG_ADMIN, ISSUER_ADMIN
services/api-gateway/src/routes/audit-export.ts:105  adminRoles            …includes platform_admin AND ORG_ADMIN
packages/shared/src/security/keyRevokePolicy.ts:59   PLATFORM_ROLES        SYSTEM_ADMIN SUPER_ADMIN            <-- no platform_admin
services/auth/src/routes/users.ts:193                PLATFORM_ADMIN_ROLES  SYSTEM_ADMIN SUPER_ADMIN admin super_admin   <-- no platform_admin, but `admin`
services/auth/src/routes/oauth.ts:1156               OAUTH_PLATFORM_ADMIN_ROLES  the same four as users.ts, duplicated because
                                                     "neither list in routes/users.ts is importable" (its own comment, :1138)
```

`services/auth/src/routes/oauth.ts:1138` already says the quiet part: the lists are duplicated **because they cannot be imported**.

## The measured consequence

Running the real predicates over the vocabulary (caller in org A, target a different organisation in the **same tenant**):

| role | `isPlatformRole` | `isOrgBoundedRole` | `decideTenantAccess` verdict |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| `SYSTEM_ADMIN` / `SUPER_ADMIN` / `super_admin` | true | false | ALLOW `platform-admin` |
| `platform_admin` / `PLATFORM_ADMIN` | **false** | **false** | **ALLOW** `same-tenant` |
| `ADMIN` / `admin` | false | false | ALLOW `same-tenant` |
| `ORG_ADMIN` / `ISSUER_ADMIN` / `issuer_admin` | false | true | DENY `cross-organisation` |

Both predicates upper-case the claim (`keyRevokePolicy.ts:84`, `:123`), so this is not a casing bug — the role is in neither set. A `platform_admin` therefore passes the gateway's platform guards and then lands in the key policy as an unbounded tenant user.

**Stored roles are lower-case** on Kintsugi (J's count, 16:44Z), which is why the upper-casing in those predicates is load-bearing and why a new list written without it would be wrong on real data.

## Why it is worth a ticket rather than a shrug

* A role added to one list and not the others is a **silent authorisation difference**, and nothing fails when the lists drift — there is no test that compares them.
* KS-1283 already fixed one instance of this class ("a widened `SUPER_ROLES` would admit a tenant `ADMIN` role on six routes"). That was the symptom; this is the cause.
* The erasure path reached through KS-1533/KS-695 is irreversible, so "which list did this route consult" is a security question, not a tidiness one.

## Recommendation

One exported vocabulary in `packages/shared` (it already owns `keyRevokePolicy`), each role set named for the question it answers, and **a guard test that fails when any service re-declares one of them inline** — the KS-764 call-site-guard shape, which already works in this repo. The lists cannot simply be merged: they genuinely differ today, and reconciling them is an authorisation change per route, so the first step is a census with the differences stated, not a rename.

**Not in scope here:** whether `ADMIN` and `platform_admin` *should* be organisation-bounded. That is Kam's policy call on KS-1535 and his board card.

## Dedupe

Literal, case-insensitive over title and description, archived included. The actual results, with every hit named:

| token | hits | which |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `SUPER_ROLES` | 3 | KS-1535 (this ticket's sibling), **KS-1283** (Done — "a widened `SUPER_ROLES` would admit a tenant `ADMIN` role on six routes"), KS-1472 (P4 — OAuth authorize-contract wording) |
| `PLATFORM_ROLES` | 2 | KS-1535, **KS-742** (Deployed to UAT — the `/api/keys` tenant boundary) |
| `SUPER_ADMIN_ROLES` | 2 | KS-1535, KS-619 (P3 — gateway tenant resolution falling through to `x-tenant-id`) |
| `PLATFORM_ADMIN_ROLES` | 1 | KS-1535 only |
| `PLATFORM_SCOPE_ROLES` | 1 | KS-1535 only |
| `role vocabulary` | 1 | KS-1535 only |
| `divergent role` | 0 | — |

**KS-1283 is the nearest and is NOT this ticket:** it fixed ONE list on one file (and is Done); this is that the lists disagree across seven sites and nothing compares them. KS-742 and KS-619 are the tenant boundary, not the platform-role vocabulary.

*Corrected after filing: the first version of this paragraph said the hits were "the KS-1283 / KS-486 family" and did not name them. KS-486 was not among the results — I carried it over from a different ticket's dedupe — and KS-1472, KS-619 and KS-742 were, unnamed. The conclusion is unchanged. Recorded rather than quietly edited, because this is the second time in one session I summarised a scan without reading what it returned.*

Filed by Seat V 5th on Wednesday's ruling, 2026-10-12, found by reading the role sets while building KS-1533 arm 1.

---

## ⚠ CORRECTION to the "measured consequence" above

The table above shows `platform_admin` as ALLOW `same-tenant` from `decideTenantAccess`, and says "for arm 1 that reads as unbounded". **That is true of the function and false of the route.** On the running mint route, `decideMint` runs first and refuses `platform_admin` 403, because `PLATFORM_ADMIN` is not in `KEY_ADMIN_ROLES`. So at the mint, this vocabulary split makes a gateway super-role **over**-restricted (it cannot mint keys), not under-restricted.

**This strengthens the ticket rather than weakening it.** The same role is a platform role to the gateway, an ordinary tenant user to `decideTenantAccess`, and not an admin at all to `decideMint` — three different answers to one question across three lists on one request path. That is exactly the problem this ticket names; I had just picked the wrong one of the three as the consequence.

*Corrected by Seat V 5th after a real-HTTP cell in KS-1533 PR A read 403 where I had predicted 201.*

## Correction to my two earlier comments, and a bigger undercount than I reported

**I claimed, in this thread and three other places, that *"originate recognises `platform_admin` in no predicate of its own"*. It does.**

```
services/originate/src/routes/adminConfig.ts:60
  const SUPER_ADMIN_ROLES = ['super_admin', 'SUPER_ADMIN', 'SYSTEM_ADMIN', 'platform_admin'];
services/originate/src/routes/adminConfig.ts:78      (inside resolveTenantId)
  if (u?.role && SUPER_ADMIN_ROLES.includes(u.role)) {
```

**Used, not dead.** `resolveTenantId` gives a caller in that set cross-tenant tenant resolution (`req.tenantId`, then `?organizationId`, then the user's own org), where a tenant-bound admin gets only its own organisation.

**The instrument that produced the false claim, named.** My original census was `grep -rn "platform_admin" services packages | head -20`. The run had **41** non-test lines; `head` cut it at 20 and originate's fell below the cut. *A count that passes through `head` is a count of what fitted, not of what matched* — and I repeated it four times without re-running it. This is one hop further out than the lesson I cited in my previous correction here: that one was a census keyed on a string literal missing a value from a DB column; this one is a census whose **output was truncated**.

**Untruncated, per service** (non-test lines, `git grep` at develop `88933d5c7ebb`) — **41 total**: auth 21, api-gateway 7, **originate 4**, packages/shared 3, anchoring 3, tokenisation 1, security 1, m365-integration 1. Excluding references to the `platform_admins` **table**, which are not a role value: api-gateway 7, **originate 4**, auth 3, anchoring 3, packages/shared 2, tokenisation 1, security 1. Three of originate's four are the RLS bypass sentinel `app.tenant_scope_bypass = 'platform_admin'` (`db.ts:167`, `db.ts:191`, a comment at `documents.ts:1916`) and are **not** role claims; the fourth is `adminConfig.ts:60`.

**What changes and what does not.** The **outcome** — `platform_admin` refused on the three by-id certification reads — is unchanged; it stays Wednesday's ruling (a), and Kam now holds a card carrying the corrected facts. What is corrected is the **basis**, which was a fact I supplied. And the real inconsistency is sharper than the gateway-versus-originate one I described: **inside originate**, the same token is a super-admin for tenant resolution and a stranger to its own certification reads.

**Not measured:** no live token was decoded, and I have not shown that any real principal carries this role.

**This ticket's "seven divergent lists" is an undercount, and its table names no originate file at all.** originate alone holds four sites using the identical three-spelling literal that omits `SUPER_ADMIN` — `certifications.ts:123` and `:959`, `documents.ts:299` and `:1076` — plus `adminConfig.ts:60`, the one originate list that DOES include `platform_admin`. So the count is **at least twelve**, on the same frame (non-test lines, `git grep` at develop `88933d5c7ebb`). The four omitting sites are now filed as **KS 1701** with the per-site table; this ticket stays the vocabulary problem.

## Correction to my comment above: `platform_admin` is NOT only a gateway spelling, and my census is why I got that wrong

My earlier comment on this ticket said *"every non-test occurrence of `platform_admin` **as a role value** is in `services/api-gateway`"*, with zero in originate and zero in `packages/shared`. **That sentence is literally true of the source text and materially misleading, and gate CK1 caught it.**

**What I missed.** The census was keyed on the **literal string** in source. It was silent about the same value arriving from a **database column**. auth mints it verbatim: the token is built with `role: platformAdmin.role`, straight from the `platform_admins` row — a variable, so the literal `platform_admin` never appears in auth's source and my search could not see it. The column permits the value: `Blockchain/Dev/docker/init-platform/01-platform-schema.sql` declares

```
role VARCHAR(30) NOT NULL DEFAULT 'super_admin'
    CHECK (role IN ('super_admin','platform_admin','platform_viewer'))
```

So a `platform_admin` JWT is producible by this repo, not only by the gateway's vocabulary.

**This is the same failure shape as a lesson already in the fleet record** — a census keyed on a name cannot see a value mapped one hop out. Mine was keyed on a string literal and the hop was a DB column. The six gateway sites I listed are still six gateway sites; the inference "therefore originate can never see this role" did not follow.

**What survives, narrower and checked at source:**
- The `platform_admins` table is created **EMPTY on purpose** — same file, *"NO SEEDED SUPER-ADMIN … KS 949 F3"* (the file writes that key hyphenated; un-hyphenated here deliberately).
- The column **defaults to `super_admin`**, so a row carries `platform_admin` only if someone inserts it and names that role explicitly.
- No in-repo path **mints** upper-case `SUPER_ADMIN`: every occurrence in `services/auth/src` is a comparison list, not an assignment. Yet `isPlatformRole` admits it, because it upper-cases. Both directions are divergences this ticket is about.

**A third list for the seven-list table, which I have not seen recorded here.** The Azure platform DDL disagrees with the docker one: `Blockchain/Dev/deployment/azure/migrate/run-platform.sh` declares `role VARCHAR(50) DEFAULT 'admin'` with **no CHECK at all**. So the same logical column is three-valued on a local/docker platform DB, unconstrained with a different default on the Azure path, and neither default is `platform_admin`. Any fix that leans on "the column is limited to three values" holds only for the first.

**Not measured:** no live token was decoded, and I have not shown that any real deployment has a `platform_admins` row carrying `platform_admin`. The point is only that the repo permits one, which is enough to retract my "gateway-only" framing.

## This vocabulary gap now has a user-visible consequence on a READ path (KS-1695 round 2, PR #1667)

Posting here rather than filing a new ticket: I was asked to file the gateway↔originate role-vocabulary mismatch, searched the board, and **this ticket already is it** — including the exact line this landed on, `packages/shared/src/security/keyRevokePolicy.ts` `PLATFORM_ROLES` *"<-- no platform_admin"*. A second ticket would have been a duplicate.

**What changed.** [KS-1695](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1695) binds the three by-id certification reads — `GET /api/certifications/:id`, `/:id/lineage`, `/:id/evidence-bundle` — which previously had no access check at all. Round 1 of that PR hand-wrote the admit set by copying the certification list route's literal `isAdmin` (`certifications.ts:906`: `system_admin` / `SYSTEM_ADMIN` / `super_admin`). Its gate caught that this **omits `SUPER_ADMIN`**, so a real platform administrator went from 200 to 404. Round 2 therefore calls **`isPlatformRole`** — this ticket's "one definition" — and the by-id reads are now the newest consumer of it.

**The consequence this ticket predicted, now concrete.** A token whose role claim is `platform_admin`:
- was **200** on these three reads before (there was no check to disagree with),
- is **404** now, because `isPlatformRole`'s set is `{SYSTEM_ADMIN, SUPER_ADMIN}` upper-cased,
- while the api-gateway continues to treat that same spelling as a super-role in the six sites this ticket lists.

That difference was **ruled deliberate** (Wednesday, 2026-10-20, option (a)): originate recognises `platform_admin` nowhere, so admitting it in one route would have made that route its first and only site. It is pinned by a cell named as a known, accepted difference, and stated in the PR body — so the divergence is now **enforced and visible on a read surface**, not just latent in a policy helper.

**Independent re-measurement at develop `7e3b9362e08b`,** to add to the seven-list table rather than restate it: every non-test occurrence of `platform_admin` **as a role value** is under `services/api-gateway` — `middleware/auth.ts:515`, `routes/audit-export.ts:106`, `routes/admin.ts:571` and `:577`, `routes/platform.ts:65`, `routes/proxy.ts:1094` and `:1227`. **Zero** sites in `services/originate`; **zero** in `packages/shared`. The `services/auth` and `services/security` hits for that string are the `platform_admins` **table**, not a role. Control: the same search for `super_admin` matches **20** files, so the grep discriminates.

**Not measured:** I did not decode a real token, and I have not established that any live principal actually carries `platform_admin`. Reachability is as open here as [KS-1591](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1591) says it is for its own three spellings.

**One interaction worth recording for whoever fixes this.** Adopting `isPlatformRole` also adopts KS-1591 — `String(role).toUpperCase()` admits a dotless-i, a long-s and an array role as `SUPER_ADMIN`. Round 1's literal set would not have. I deliberately did **not** add a cell pinning those three as admitted: a green cell asserting a spoofable spelling is accepted would turn a KS-1591 fix into a test failure, and someone would "fix" it by reverting. It is recorded as known residue on the PR instead.

title: POLICY (Kam's call): role ADMIN is a KEY_ADMIN_ROLE that the KS-764 organisation arm never engages for, so a tenant ADMIN can mint a key for any organisation in its tenant
description:
## BLUF

`ADMIN` **is in** `KEY_ADMIN_ROLES` **but in neither** `PLATFORM_ROLES` **nor** `ORG_BOUNDED_ROLES`**, so the KS-764 organisation arm is skipped for it entirely and** `decideTenantAccess` **falls through to** `allow: 'same-tenant'`**.** After KS-1533 arm 1 closes the hole for `ORG_ADMIN` and `ISSUER_ADMIN`, a caller with role `ADMIN` can **still** mint a key carrying any organisation's `organizationId` inside its own tenant — the same Path 1 shape, through one role.

**This is a policy question about who may reach an irreversible cross-organisation erasure, so it is Kam's to decide, not an engineering choice inside a PR.** Wednesday put it on his board as a card (`secuura-ks1533-admin-role-unbounded-by-org-arm-1013`) and recommended leaving `ADMIN` unbounded. **Until he rules, KS-1533 arm 1 ships leaving** `ADMIN` **unbounded and says so plainly**, and the shared role set is NOT touched.

## The three sets, read at source

```
KEY_ADMIN_ROLES    services/security/src/provisioningPolicy.ts:43-49
                   SYSTEM_ADMIN, SUPER_ADMIN, ORG_ADMIN, ISSUER_ADMIN, ADMIN
PLATFORM_ROLES     packages/shared/src/security/keyRevokePolicy.ts:59
                   SYSTEM_ADMIN, SUPER_ADMIN
ORG_BOUNDED_ROLES  packages/shared/src/security/keyRevokePolicy.ts:76
                   ORG_ADMIN, ISSUER_ADMIN
```

The arm is `if (organisationScope && isOrgBoundedRole(user.role))` (`keyRevokePolicy.ts:173`). `ADMIN` satisfies neither predicate, so the arm is skipped and the function returns `allow: 'same-tenant'` at `:225`.

| role | what arm 1 does for it |
| -- | -- |
| `SYSTEM_ADMIN`, `SUPER_ADMIN` | platform — bypass the arm by design (KS-577 depends on it) |
| `ORG_ADMIN`, `ISSUER_ADMIN` | org-bounded — **the arm applies**, which is KS-1533 arm 1 |
| `ADMIN` | **neither — the arm never engages** |

## The two readings

**(a) By design, and this ticket closes as "documented".** `ADMIN` reads as a **tenant**-level admin, distinct from platform — KS-1283 is about "a widened `SUPER_ROLES` would admit a tenant `ADMIN` role on six routes", which treats it as a tenant role. On that reading, acting across organisations *inside its own tenant* is what a tenant admin is for, and arm 1 is complete as scoped.

**(b) A gap.** The sink is the KS-695 connector erasure, which is **irreversible** and destroys another organisation's titles, descriptions and name. KS-764's stated hazard is "an org-bounded admin in organisation A destroying organisation B's key" — if a tenant `ADMIN` may do the equivalent to B's *documents*, the boundary is only as strong as the weakest admin role.

**This ticket does not pick.** It records the question, the evidence, and what shipped in the meantime.

## If Kam rules (b)

`ADMIN` joins `ORG_BOUNDED_ROLES` in `packages/shared/src/security/keyRevokePolicy.ts`. That is a **one-line change to a shared set that also governs the revoke route**, so it is not a local edit: it would change `DELETE /api/security/keys/:id` for every `ADMIN` caller too, and it needs its own gate and its own caller-population check (the same `caller has no organisation` 403 that KS-1533 arm 1 accepts for org-bounded roles would then apply to `ADMIN` as well). It should not be folded into KS-1533.

## Where it is pinned meanwhile

KS-1533 arm 1 carries a **documenting cell** that asserts today's behaviour — a tenant `ADMIN` minting for another organisation in its tenant succeeds — labelled as undecided policy rather than as a guarantee, so that whichever way Kam rules, the change is visible as a deliberate edit to a cell rather than a silent flip.

## Dedupe

Literal, case-insensitive over title and description, archived included: `ORG_BOUNDED_ROLES` **1** (KS-779 — the CALLER-side population of org-bounded accounts with no organisation claim, which is KS-1533 arm 1's accepted 403 price, not this question), `isOrgBoundedRole` **0**, `tenant ADMIN` 4 and `ADMIN role` 6 (the KS-1283 / KS-1506 / KS-486 family — a widened `SUPER_ROLES`, error-handler and review tickets, none of them this question). KS-764 (Done) created the arm and deliberately scoped it to the revoke route.

*Corrected after filing: the first version of this paragraph said* `ORG_BOUNDED_ROLES` *0. The scan returned KS-779. The conclusion is unchanged — no ticket asks whether* `ADMIN` *should be org-bounded — but the figure was wrong and a wrong dedupe count is worth correcting rather than leaving.*

Raised by Seat V 5th while building KS-1533 arm 1, 2026-10-12. Found by reading the role sets before writing the fix, not by a test.

---

## ADDENDUM — it is TWO roles, not one, and the verdicts are MEASURED by running the predicates

I ran the real `isPlatformRole`, `isOrgBoundedRole` and `decideTenantAccess` over the whole role vocabulary rather than reading the sets. Caller is `{role, tenantId:'t1', organizationId:'oA'}`, target is the same tenant and a DIFFERENT organisation `oB` — i.e. exactly the KS-1533 Path 1 shape:

| role (as the JWT carries it) | isPlatformRole | isOrgBoundedRole | verdict naming ANOTHER org in the same tenant |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| `SYSTEM_ADMIN` | true | false | ALLOW `platform-admin` — by design |
| `SUPER_ADMIN` | true | false | ALLOW `platform-admin` — by design |
| `super_admin` | true | false | ALLOW `platform-admin` — by design |
| `platform_admin` | **false** | **false** | **ALLOW** `same-tenant` **— UNBOUNDED** |
| `PLATFORM_ADMIN` | **false** | **false** | **ALLOW** `same-tenant` **— UNBOUNDED** |
| `ADMIN` | **false** | **false** | **ALLOW** `same-tenant` **— UNBOUNDED** |
| `admin` | **false** | **false** | **ALLOW** `same-tenant` **— UNBOUNDED** |
| `ORG_ADMIN` | false | true | DENY `cross-organisation` — arm 1 working |
| `ISSUER_ADMIN` | false | true | DENY `cross-organisation` — arm 1 working |
| `issuer_admin` | false | true | DENY `cross-organisation` — arm 1 working |
| `connector` | false | false | ALLOW `same-tenant` — correct: `decideMint` pins a provisioner to its own tenant on its own branch |

Both predicates upper-case the claim (`keyRevokePolicy.ts:84` and `:123`), so casing is NOT the issue — the role simply is not in either set.

### `platform_admin` is the more interesting half

`platform_admin` is treated as a **super-role by the gateway** in at least six places, while the key policy does not treat it as platform at all:

```
services/api-gateway/src/routes/platform.ts:65      SUPER_ROLES          includes platform_admin
services/api-gateway/src/middleware/auth.ts:515     SUPER_ADMIN_ROLES    includes platform_admin
services/api-gateway/src/routes/admin.ts:577        PLATFORM_SCOPE_ROLES includes platform_admin
services/api-gateway/src/routes/proxy.ts:1094,1227                       include platform_admin
services/api-gateway/src/routes/audit-export.ts:105 adminRoles           includes platform_admin
packages/shared/src/security/keyRevokePolicy.ts:59  PLATFORM_ROLES       does NOT
services/auth/src/routes/users.ts:193               PLATFORM_ADMIN_ROLES does NOT (it has `admin` instead)
```

So a `platform_admin` is "platform" to the gateway and an ordinary tenant user to the key policy. For arm 1 that means **unbounded**; more generally it is a role-vocabulary split across seven divergent lists, which is its own problem and not this ticket's to fix.

### What this changes for Kam's decision

The card is about who may reach an irreversible cross-organisation erasure. The answer is not "ADMIN" but "`ADMIN` **and** `platform_admin`**, in either casing**". If Kam rules them bounded, the edit is to `ORG_BOUNDED_ROLES` (or to `PLATFORM_ROLES`, for `platform_admin`) — still a shared set that governs the revoke route too, so still not a local change and still its own gate.

KS-1533 arm 1's documenting cell therefore pins **both** roles' current behaviour, labelled as undecided policy.

*Added by Seat V 5th, 2026-10-12, after running the predicates while building KS-1533 arm 1.*

---

## ⚠ CORRECTION — `platform_admin` is NOT unbounded at the mint. It cannot mint at all. Only `ADMIN` is the open question.

**The addendum above is wrong about** `platform_admin`**, and the retitle that named it was wrong.** Measured on the running security service over real HTTP while writing KS-1533 PR A's cells, and confirmed by running the function:

```
role              decideMint (runs FIRST, as route middleware)
ADMIN / admin     ALLOW via admin   -> reaches decideTenantAccess -> unbounded   (the claim HOLDS)
platform_admin    DENY 403 "API key management requires an admin role"          (the claim was WRONG)
PLATFORM_ADMIN    DENY 403 — same
ISSUER_ADMIN      ALLOW via admin   -> the organisation arm applies
super_admin       ALLOW via admin   -> platform, bypasses by design
```

**What I got wrong, precisely.** I ran `decideTenantAccess` on its own and concluded `platform_admin` falls through to `allow: 'same-tenant'`. That is true *of that function*. But the mint route runs `requireKeyAdminOrProvisioner` → `decideMint` **first**, and `PLATFORM_ADMIN` is not in `KEY_ADMIN_ROLES` (`provisioningPolicy.ts:43-49`), so the request is refused 403 before `decideTenantAccess` is ever called. **Order is invisible to a function call** — the exact point KS-742's route-contract test makes in its header, and that I copied into KS-1533's. The real-HTTP cell is what caught it: I had written it to assert `platform_admin` mints (201), and it read 403 on the unfixed service.

**So, for Kam's decision:** the question is `ADMIN` **only**. `ADMIN` is in `KEY_ADMIN_ROLES`, passes `decideMint`, reaches `decideTenantAccess`, and — being in neither `PLATFORM_ROLES` nor `ORG_BOUNDED_ROLES` — keeps cross-organisation mint inside its tenant. That half stands and is unchanged.

**What still stands about** `platform_admin`**:** the role-vocabulary split (KS-1536) is real — the gateway treats it as a super-role in six places. But its consequence *at the mint* is the opposite of what I wrote: a gateway super-role is **over**-restricted here (cannot mint keys), not under-restricted. That is an availability quirk, not a security hole, and it belongs on KS-1536, not on Kam's policy card.

The title is reverted to name `ADMIN` alone. KS-1533 PR A pins both facts in cells: `ADMIN` as UNDECIDED POLICY (201 today), `platform_admin` as MEASURED (403, refused by `decideMint`).

*Corrected by Seat V 5th, 2026-10-12. The third time this session I have had to correct a claim of mine in place; this one was on Kam's board, so it matters more than the dedupe counts did.*

title: KS-1232 gate follow-ups: share the allow-list predicate between the info reader and the create path (or pin drift), and decide whether arrays of non-strings are refused by both
description:
## BLUF

The Sonnet-tier gate on PR #1517 (ticket KS-1232) returned **GO**: 0 Major, 3 Minor notes (verdict sha256/16 `622027fcfb23dab5`). Two of them need a decision or a change and are the checklist below; Minor 3 is already ticketed (KS-1532 for the thrown settings read; the MCP relay wording is recorded on KS-1232).

## Recommendation

Do (a) first, since it removes a class; (b) is a contract question for Wednesday or Kam, to be answered for both read routes together.

## Checklist

- [ ] **(a) Stop duplicating the predicate, or pin drift (the gate's Minor 1).** The info reader's guard (`services/api-gateway/src/services/health.ts:77`) is character-identical to the create path's (`routes/verification.ts:1307`): `raw !== undefined && raw !== null && !Array.isArray(raw)`, with the same 403 text. It is **duplicated, not shared**. Drift today is guarded only by the 12-shape AGREEMENT cell in `ks1232-info-reader-refuses-a-non-array-allow-list.test.ts`; the gate's own 30-shape run (`NaN`, `Infinity`, `-0`, array subclasses, a Proxy, an object with a `length`, `new String('')`, `Object.create(Array.prototype)`) found **0 disagreements**. Options: one helper imported by both routes (this edits the create path's allow-list guard, a security surface, so it needs its own gate), or a source-level cell asserting the two guards are the same executable code (a source-text check passes when the guard is commented out, so compare the code, not the text).
- [ ] **(b) Decide whether an array of non-strings is refused, by both read routes together (the gate's Minor 2; a contract question).** Neither route checks array ELEMENTS. The info reader echoes `[1,2]`, `[null]` and `[['a']]` raw (same as before this PR), and the create path accepts the same shape at its guard; reasoned from its code (`allowedTypes.includes(requestedType)`), not run, a non-empty array of non-strings then refuses every create with the "not permitted to register document type" text rather than the list text, so the two routes would answer differently for the same stored value. KS-1230 is where element types are validated on the **write** path; this item is whether the two **reads** should also refuse such an array, and with what text. Out of the ticket's "non-array" wording, so it was not changed in KS-1232.

## Detail

* **Source:** the PR #1517 gate verdict, Minors 1 and 2. The two reasoned claims in (b) are mine and are marked as such.
* **Related:** KS-1232 (the change), KS-1230 (the write-side validation), KS-1204 (the create path's refusal), KS-1532 (the thrown read), KS-1531 (the undocumented route).
* **Dedupe before filing:** literal, case-insensitive matches over title and description, archived included: `array of non-strings` 0, `element types` 0, `shared predicate` 0, `share the predicate` 0, `non-string` 21 (scanned by title; none is about the allow-list's elements), `KS-1230` 4 (KS-1262, KS-1233, KS-1232, KS-1231; KS-1230 itself read). The same instrument returned KS-1232 for its own title phrase, so it can see ticket text.

title: Security: an organisation-scoped admin can mint a key for ANOTHER organisation, or carrying another organisation's connector id — the mint has no organisation arm and connector_id is not bound
description:
## BLUF

**In** `services/security`**, the API-key mint is bounded by TENANT only. An** `ORG_ADMIN` **or** `ISSUER_ADMIN` **of organisation A can mint a key that carries organisation B's** `organizationId`**, and any** `connectorId`**, inside the same tenant.** KS-764 put an organisation arm on **revoke**; the **mint** never got one. Because the connector-erasure path in KS-695 trusts the key row it is called with, that minted key erases B.

**This must land before KS-695 deploys** — same status as KS-1508. Merging KS-695 does not deploy it, so the harm is after deploy, and the data destroyed (titles, descriptions, an organisation name) is another organisation's and the erasure is irreversible.

Found by the round 4 Opus gate on PR #1497 (verdict sha256/16 `df3bc694b6b41094`, section M-1). **The security-service half below is the gate's reading of the code, which I re-read at source myself; the originate half is the gate's measurement on real Postgres. Neither the mint nor the gateway half has been measured at runtime — that is the first task here.**

## The two paths

**Path 1 — a key for another organisation.**

* `services/security/src/provisioningPolicy.ts:43-49` — `ORG_ADMIN` and `ISSUER_ADMIN` are in `KEY_ADMIN_ROLES`.
* `provisioningPolicy.ts:95-98` — `decideMint` returns `{allow: true, via: 'admin'}` **at once** for any of those roles, before any tenancy or organisation question.
* `services/security/src/index.ts:477-491` — the body's `organizationId` and `connectorId` are free strings.
* `services/security/src/index.ts:1017` — the route calls `decideTenantAccess((req as any).user, tenantId)` **without** the third `organisationScope` argument.
* `packages/shared/src/security/keyRevokePolicy.ts:161-164` says that arm is engaged *"ONLY when the caller supplies* `organisationScope`*, so the two existing callers (KS-742's list and mint) keep exactly today's behaviour"*. That was deliberate in KS-764 and is exactly the gap.
* `services/api-gateway/src/routes/proxy.ts:1189-1192` — `/api/security` is mounted behind `authenticateToken(true)` only, so the gateway adds no organisation check.

**Measured by the gate on the originate side (cell P8, real Postgres, both modes):** a key row for org B carrying a forged `connector_id` — which is what the mint above writes — gives `200 completed documentsBlanked:1`, B's name and document `[erased]`, and B's own provisioned key still active.

**Path 2 — a key for A's own organisation carrying B's connector id.**

* `svc_api_keys.connector_id` has **no uniqueness constraint** (the gate read the live indexes: pkey, org, prefix, tenant only).
* The erasure matches `versionedById = 'connector:' + connectorId` **by value**.
* **Measured by the gate (cell P6, both modes):** two organisations whose keys share one `connector_id`; A erases and gets `200 documentsBlanked:4`, taking B's unissued connector root and B's connector derivatives.
* Not hypothetical: `register-connector` writes `connectorId: platform-s:${externalRef}` (`services/api-gateway/src/routes/platform.ts:702`), so the id is a predictable function of a value an org admin can read, and the tenant metering key already uses a constant `platform-s` id (`tenant-provisioning/src/meteringKey.ts:56`).

**Path 2 is not closed by the organisation arm alone.** Both arms are needed.

## What this ticket asks for

1. **The organisation arm of the mint.** An organisation-scoped admin may mint only for its own organisation. The shape already exists — pass `organisationScope` at `index.ts:1017` as the revoke path does at `keyRevokePolicy.ts:243` — and `decideMint`'s early return for `KEY_ADMIN_ROLES` must stop short-circuiting past it. Platform roles keep their current reach.
2. **The connector-id binding.** A connector id belongs to exactly one organisation; a mint naming one already bound to another organisation in the same tenant is refused. The org-less tenant metering key must keep working.
3. **It lands before KS-695 deploys.** Tracked like KS-1508.

## Acceptance

A mint request from an `ORG_ADMIN`/`ISSUER_ADMIN` of organisation A naming organisation B, **or** naming a `connectorId` already bound to B, is refused **on the running service over real HTTP** — not only in a unit file — with the caller's own organisation unaffected, and a control proving the same admin may still mint for its own organisation.

## Dedupe before filing

Literal, case-insensitive matches over title and description across Secuura-PK, **archived included**: `organisationScope` **0**, `organizationScope` **0**, `connector_id has no unique` **0**, `provisioningPolicy` 2 (KS-742 tenancy, KS-835 OAuth consent), `decideMint` 2 (KS-742, KS-486), `KEY_ADMIN_ROLES` 5 (KS-742, KS-643, KS-642, KS-486, KS-1514 — all either the tenant boundary or a response-shape issue), `ORG_ADMIN` 33 (so the scan can see). **The nearest neighbours are the tenant boundary (KS-742) and the revoke-only organisation arm (KS-764, Done); neither covers the mint's organisation arm or the connector-id binding.** KS-1107 is the same class on a different surface (`POST /api/auth/register` accepting a client-supplied `organizationId`) and is not this.

## Not measured, and whose it is

Counts of existing keys that already share a `connector_id` across organisations on Kintsugi are **not** measured here — that is the J lane's to run, per Wednesday. Nothing in this ticket was run against a live box.

Filed by Seat V 5th from the PR #1497 round 4 Opus gate, 2026-10-12.

nodes.body: **BLUF:** State moved In Review -> In Progress. Owed: "Open (1): originate's admin mint, the sibling the 2026-10-12 comment records. KS-1594 carries it (In Progress, PR 1794 attached)." and "Open (2): tenant `ADMIN` is left unbounded on the mint." (this ticket's newest comment, comment 5). Not closed because the ticket says: "Left open: two items named in this ticket's own comments are not recorded as done". This seat ran no check on a box; beyond the ticket text it read only the merge state of PRs 1521 and 1533 at the GitHub API (PRs 1521 and 1533 merged as 69878dc5d1ae and 7550a969acd7).

**BLUF:** Delivered in part: PRs 1521 and 1533 merged as 69878dc5d1ae and 7550a969acd7 on develop, deployed to kintsugi at b1fb543640e7 (2026-11-01). Verified by code read, not observed live. Left open: two items named in this ticket's own comments are not recorded as done.

- **In the code at b1fb543640e7:** `security/src/index.ts:1221` is the organisation arm of the key mint (KS-1533 arm 1), and `:1250` and `:1266` apply `normaliseOrgId` to the requested organisation.
- **Open (1): originate's admin mint**, the sibling the 2026-10-12 comment records. KS-1594 carries it (In Progress, PR 1794 attached).
- **Open (2): tenant `ADMIN` is left unbounded on the mint.** The 2026-10-12 comment records Kam's note that it must change before deployment. This ticket records no change to it.

## BLUF — Kam ruled both KS-1533 cards. Nothing changes in the code that has merged; one thing is now owed before deployment.

1. **Org-less accounts: ACCEPTED.** The behaviour PR #1521 ships stays exactly as it is.
2. **Tenant `ADMIN`: LEFT UNBOUNDED FOR NOW — but Kam's note says it must change before deployment.** It stays able to mint keys for any organisation in its tenant, and that remains pinned as undecided policy in the PR #1521 cells.

## The rulings, verbatim

Kam's tap words, with the times the board stamped them (13 Oct 2026, board time, `view=wednesday`, as relayed by Wednesday — I did not read the decision store myself):

* **09:53:12** — *"Decision secuura-ks1533-orgless-accounts-cannot-name-org-on-mint-1013: a — Accept"*
* **09:53:40** — *"Decision secuura-ks1533-admin-role-unbounded-by-org-arm-1013: a — Leave ADMIN unbounded for now | note: keep a note that this needs to be changed before deployment"*

## What each one means

### 1. The org-less accounts — the behaviour stays as PR #1521 ships it

An org-bounded caller (`ORG_ADMIN` / `ISSUER_ADMIN`) whose token carries **no** organisation claim can **no longer mint a key that names an organisation** — it gets a 403 naming the organisation boundary. It **can still mint an unqualified, tenant-level key**, so provisioning by omission survives.

This is the population KS-779 recorded as **intentionally org-less** on Kam's earlier ruling (`secuura-ks779-org-mapping-2026-09-04: record-only`, *"Change nothing; record all ten as intentionally org-less"*): ten accounts on demo, and the PR #1521 cell notes 9 of 9 measured on Kintsugi at 16:44Z on 2026-10-12. Per the card, two of the ten are demo logins; I have not re-identified which.

**Pinned at develop `b28bfaec`** in `services/security/src/__tests__/ks1533-key-mint-organisation-arm.test.ts`:
* `:179` — *RULED (KS-779, Kam 2026-09-04)*: naming an organisation → **403**.
* `:189` — *RULED*: an unqualified mint → **201**.

**Nothing is changed on any account.** This ruling accepts a standing operational cost; it does not trigger a data fix.

### 2. The tenant-level `ADMIN` role — stays unbounded for now, must change before deployment

`ADMIN` is in `KEY_ADMIN_ROLES` (`services/security/src/provisioningPolicy.ts:43-49`) but in **neither** `PLATFORM_ROLES` nor `ORG_BOUNDED_ROLES` (`packages/shared/src/security/keyRevokePolicy.ts:59`, `:76`). So the KS-764 organisation arm — `if (organisationScope && isOrgBoundedRole(user.role))` — **never engages** for it, and `decideTenantAccess` returns `same-tenant`. A tenant `ADMIN` can therefore mint a key carrying **any organisation's id inside its own tenant**: the Path 1 shape, through one role.

**Pinned at develop** as undecided policy, `:195` — *UNDECIDED POLICY (KS-1535)*: `ADMIN` naming another organisation → **201**. Its own comment says that if `ADMIN` is ruled bounded, the cell flips to 403 and that edit becomes the record of the decision.

**Kam's note is the operative part:** this is accepted *for now*, and **must be changed before deployment.** Why it matters: the sink is the KS-695 part (ii) connector erasure, which trusts the key row it is called with and is **irreversible** — the round-4 Opus gate's M-1 on PR #1497. Which deployment the note covers (the KS-695 part (ii) erasure deploy, or every deploy) is being confirmed with Kam by Wednesday.

The policy record for `ADMIN` is **KS-1535**, which set out the two readings and named this card. It is linked here.

### `platform_admin` is NOT a Path 1 vector — MEASURED

`:204` — *MEASURED*: role `platform_admin` **cannot mint at all**. `requireKeyAdminOrProvisioner` → `decideMint` runs **first**, and `PLATFORM_ADMIN` is not in `KEY_ADMIN_ROLES`, so it is refused **403** (*"API key management requires an admin role"*) before the organisation arm is ever reached.

That cell corrected V 5th's own first reading, which had called `platform_admin` unbounded from running `decideTenantAccess` alone — route order is invisible to a function call. So a gateway super-role is **over**-restricted at the mint, not under-restricted (the vocabulary split itself is KS-1536).

**Provenance, stated plainly:** these three behaviours are asserted by **passing cells at develop** `b28bfaec`, written by Seat V 5th for PR #1521 and run in memory through the real route stack (the file runs without a database). I **read** them at develop; I did **not** re-run them for this comment.

*Facts only. No code, account, role set or ticket state was changed by this comment. Posted by the Platform K agent on Kam's behalf.*

## Arm 1 merged (PR #1521, squash `69878dc5d1ae4b717834c547c47d8bc036625d2e`). This ticket STAYS OPEN.

**Landed on develop** (one parent, `05a72c85`):
- The security key mint is bounded by organisation: `decideTenantAccess` receives the target organisation.
- A caller-chosen `connectorId` is refused unless the caller is a platform role or a provisioner, and **a provisioner may not rotate**.
- The organisation id is stored canonical (`normaliseOrgId`).

**Gates:** round 0, Opus, NO GO (`b792fbae338bc782`); fix round 1, Opus delta, GO WITH NOTE (`c5d59b0e54f23775`) on head `e4d7a13e`. The first gate's Major is closed: 12 matrix cells moved, all provisioner rotates 201 -> 403, and a 513-cell rotate battery retired 0 keys. `register-connector` is unchanged.

**Five-point read, from git, each with a control:**
1. One parent, `05a72c85`.
2. The landed tree `67b66ca42e1e` equals my own `git merge-tree` of `e4d7a13e` onto `05a72c85`. Control: the superseded head `c02c0b5d` predicts `124d8960`.
3. The numstat is identical to the PR's three-dot delta: index.ts +71/-10, the KS-1533 test +318.
4. Zero trailers. Control: branch commit `113d2a91` carries its co-author line.
5. Both blobs are byte-identical to the tested head. Control: index.ts at develop-before differs.

**Why KS-1533 stays open (and is NOT Done):**
- **Path 1 is closed on the security route only.** Originate's `POST /api/admin/api-keys` is still open: the sibling recorded in the comment above, owed by the originate lane.
- **Path 2 is arm 2,** not built, held for the pre-flight count.
- **Not deployed.** This is a runtime change to the security service: local first, then demo (UAT) after Peter's nod.

**Related, filed:**
- KS-1553 (P3): the gate's two Minors. m1-r1, the list compares a raw query id; m2-r1, `{uuid}`, no-hyphen and zero-width forms are stored verbatim.
- KS-1549 (P1): the concurrent-rotate zero. It is pre-existing; the gate re-measured 0 of 21. The plan is approved and the build is next.

Linear's link kind for #1521 reads `closes` (from the branch name), but the ticket was read four times over 30 s after the merge and stayed In Progress. No reopen was needed.

## Arm 1's sibling: Path 1 is still open through originate's admin mint (the #1521 gate's M2)

**BLUF:** #1521 closes Path 1 on the **security** route (`POST /api/security/keys`) only. Originate's `POST /api/admin/api-keys` is a second writer of `svc_api_keys` and has no organisation check, so an ORG_ADMIN of organisation A can still mint a key carrying organisation B's id inside its tenant. This is recorded as arm 1's sibling, with no new ticket per Wednesday (18:26Z). Originate is the J lane, so I am not building it.

**Where** (develop `b08ee629`): `services/originate/src/routes/adminConfig.ts`
- `:37`: the role gate, `requireRole('SYSTEM_ADMIN', 'ORG_ADMIN')`.
- `:924`: the handler.
- `:947`: `orgId = d.organizationId || user.organizationId || null`, straight from the body.
- `:960`: `INSERT INTO svc_api_keys (… organization_id …)`, with no `decideTenantAccess` and no organisation check anywhere between.

**Shape:** an ORG_ADMIN of A sends `POST /api/admin/api-keys {name, organizationId: B, permissions: [...]}`. Expected: 201, with `organization_id = B` in A's tenant.

**Status:** code-read by the gate and re-read by me. NOT measured (originate was not booted).

**Scope:** it writes no `connector_id` and never rotates, so it is not a Path 3 vector. Its only revoke goes through `decideKeyRevoke`. But the KS-695 erasure trusts `organization_id` on the row, which is the harm Path 1 names.

**Fix shape:** call `decideTenantAccess(user, tenantId, { targetOrganizationId: d.organizationId ?? null })` before the INSERT, as #1521 does on the security route, and store the id as `normaliseOrgId(...)` (#1521's m1). The regression cell is the same as #1521's R1, run against originate. **The gate's condition:** M2 must be closed, or explicitly accepted by Kam, before KS-1533 or the KS-695 erasure is called done.

## Noticed in the security service, not changed (recorded so it is not lost)

`services/security/src/index.ts:981-989` (develop `b08ee629`): when the caller sends no `tenantId` and no `x-tenant-id`, the tenant is looked up from the RAW `data.organizationId` with a `$1::uuid` cast. A padded or upper-cased id either resolves or fails the cast; on failure the code falls through to the caller's own tenant (the KS-742 default). So it fails safe. The one shape where it matters is a PLATFORM role minting for an organisation in ANOTHER tenant with a malformed id: the key would land in the platform caller's tenant. It predates #1521, runs only with a database, and no #1521 cell can pin it. The fix is one token: look up `normaliseOrgId(data.organizationId)`.

## PATH 3 — a cross-organisation REVOKE through the mint route, going around the KS-764 arm

Found while reading the mint for arm 1, **not named by the #1497 gate**, and it is a different harm from Paths 1 and 2: no erasure is involved.

`POST /api/keys` accepts `connectorId` (`createApiKeySchema`, `index.ts` around :491) and `rotate` (default false). When both are supplied:

```
index.ts:1072   if (data.rotate && data.connectorId) {
index.ts:1073     priorKeysRevoked = await revokePriorConnectorKeys(data.connectorId, tenantId, apiKey.id);
```

and `revokePriorConnectorKeys` (`index.ts:196`) is scoped by **connector id and tenant only — there is no organisation bound**:

```sql
UPDATE svc_api_keys SET is_active = false
 WHERE connector_id = $1 AND tenant_id = $2::uuid AND id <> $3 AND is_active = true
```

Its in-memory branch does the same (`k.connectorId !== connectorId || k.tenantId !== tenantId`), so it also works on a DB-less run.

**So a caller who can choose `connectorId` can retire every active key in the tenant carrying that connector id, whatever organisation owns it, by minting one key with `rotate: true`.** That is exactly the capability KS-764's organisation arm exists to deny on `DELETE /api/security/keys/:id` — reached by going around that route instead of through it.

### Why it matters separately from Paths 1 and 2

* **The harm is availability, not confidentiality or integrity.** Another organisation's live connector credential stops working. No erasure, no KS-695 involvement, so it does not need the KS-695 deploy to be reachable — it is reachable **today**, on any deployed build that has KS-577's revoke-on-rotate.
* It **bypasses a control that was deliberately built**. KS-764 reasoned carefully about who may revoke whose key; this route reaches the same effect without consulting that reasoning.
* The comment at `:196` is explicit that the tenant GUC prevents a **cross-tenant** rotate ("a cross-tenant rotate cannot reach another tenant's keys"). It is right about tenants and silent about organisations, which is the same shape as the mint's missing organisation arm.

### Disposition

**Arm 1's `connectorId` refusal closes Path 3**, for the same callers and by the same means: a non-provisioner that did not mint the connector cannot name its connector id, so it cannot rotate it either. That is now a second reason for that half of arm 1, and PR A will carry a cell for it — a non-provisioner sending `connectorId` + `rotate: true` must be refused, with the other organisation's key still active afterwards, plus the two exemptions (platform roles and a provisioner with `organizations:register`) each pinned.

**Not measured yet:** this is read from the code at the lines above. The cell is the measurement, and it will be a real-HTTP one like the rest of arm 1's.

Raised by Seat V 5th, 2026-10-12, while reading the mint route for arm 1.

title: mcp-server POST /generate-package: a falsy allowedDocumentTypes ("", 0, false) reaches the package generator as [] (all types permitted) with status 200
description:
## BLUF

**The MCP server's** `POST /generate-package` **turns a falsy** `allowedDocumentTypes` **(**`""`**,** `0` **or** `false`**) into** `[]` **before it reaches the package generator, and answers 200.** `[]` is documented as "all types permitted", so a caller who sent a value that is not a list gets back a package that says the connector is unrestricted. This is the second of the two sites that shape `allowedDocumentTypes` found while working KS-1232; it was split out of KS-1232 on Wednesday's ruling because it is a different service, a different surface (a request-body value, not the gateway's answer) and a separate test pass.

## Recommendation

A decision first, then a small build. Decide what the endpoint should do with a present, non-array `allowedDocumentTypes`: refuse (a 400, since the value is the caller's) or pass it on as unusable. The gateway's own answer for the same stored value is a 403 refusal (KS-1232), so the two should not disagree about what a non-list means. Test first against the existing pin, which the change flips.

## Detail

* **Where:** `services/mcp-server/src/http-server.ts:258`, `allowedDocumentTypes: allowedDocumentTypes || [],`, in the handler for `POST /generate-package` (line 222), which reads `allowedDocumentTypes` from the request body (line 226) and requires `apiKey` (400 without it).
* **Reachable through the gateway:** `services/api-gateway/src/routes/proxy.ts:1266` mounts `POST /api/mcp/generate-package` and forwards it to `${MCP_SERVER_URL}/generate-package` (line 1270); KS-1214 records the same.
* **What** `[]` **means:** `MCP Deployment/troubleshooting.md:123`, "An empty `allowedDocumentTypes` list means all types are permitted."
* **Pinned today, as a characterisation (PR #1120):** `services/mcp-server/src/__tests__/ks1232-generate-package-doctypes-default.test.ts`, the cell `RED KS-1232: allowedDocumentTypes "", 0 and false each reach the package generator as [] with status 200`, with a control that a list passes through unchanged. The fix flips that cell.
* **Consequence, reasoned and NOT measured:** the generated package carries the unrestricted-looking list into the agent's configuration. The gateway still enforces the real allow-list on create, so this is misinformation to the agent, not a widening; I did not run a generated package against a gateway.
* **Related:** KS-1232 (the gateway's info reader, the same value), KS-1214 (the same server's `/hash` exposure; it records the `/api/mcp/generate-package` proxy).
* **Dedupe before filing:** literal, case-insensitive matches over title and description, archived included: `generate-package` 4 (KS-1214, KS-713, KS-104, KS-95; KS-1214 read, the other three are Done and unrelated), `http-server.ts:258` 1 and `allowedDocumentTypes || []` 1 (both KS-1232), `package generator` 0, `generatePackage` 0. The same instrument returned KS-1232 for its own title phrase, so it can see ticket text.

title: platform_document_registry.tenant_id has three declarations that disagree (init schema UUID, gateway CREATE TEXT, main-DB copy TEXT): decide the canonical one (UNDECIDED)
description:
## BLUF

**Nobody has decided what type** `platform_document_registry.tenant_id` **is. There are three declarations of it, and they disagree:** the platform database's init schema says `UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES tenants(id)`; the gateway's in-code CREATE for the platform database says `TEXT`; and the MAIN database's copy of the table (created by `CORE_MIGRATIONS`) is also `TEXT`. **This is UNDECIDED.** It is the item left over when KS-1272 was closed: that ticket's defect (the de-dup `DELETE` failing `22P02` on a uuid column on every boot) is fixed by making the statement type-agnostic, and its Recommendation also asked to "decide which declaration is canonical". Nothing is broken today because both spellings now work.

## Recommendation

A decision, not a build. Pick the canonical type for the platform database's table (the init schema's `UUID` with a foreign key is the stricter reading), then decide separately whether the gateway's in-code CREATE should be aligned to it, and whether the main database should hold this table at all or hold it with the same type. Unassigned: a decision-shaped item for Wednesday or Kam.

## Detail

* **Facts at develop** `551dc9808aee` (source lines, not compiled):
  * `docker/init-platform/01-platform-schema.sql:209-213`: `tenant_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES tenants(id)`, plus `idx_doc_registry_unique` on `(content_hash, tenant_id)` at line 225.
  * `services/api-gateway/src/startup-migrations.ts`, platform list, lines 1123-1138: `tenant_id TEXT`, then the de-dup `DELETE` at 1135-1137 using `a.tenant_id IS NOT DISTINCT FROM b.tenant_id` (the KS-1272 fix, PR #1104), then `uq_pdr_hash_tenant`.
  * Same file, `CORE_MIGRATIONS` (the MAIN database), lines 473-501: `tenant_id TEXT`, de-dup with `COALESCE(a.tenant_id, '') = COALESCE(b.tenant_id, '')`. That form is correct on a TEXT column and would raise `22P02` on a uuid one.
* **Why the declarations coexist:** the init script runs first on a fresh platform database, so the gateway's `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` is a no-op wherever that script ran. KS-1272 measured the Kintsugi platform database on 2026-09-19 (read-only): `tenant_id` is `uuid`, 0 rows, `uq_pdr_hash_tenant` present.
* **Consequence, reasoned and NOT measured:** a platform database built from the gateway's CREATE alone would be `TEXT` and carry no foreign key to `tenants`, while one built from the init script is `UUID` with the key; a non-UUID tenant id would then be accepted by one and refused by the other. No run was made to confirm it.
* **Related:** KS-1272 (the defect, Done), KS-598 (the registry upsert that keys on `(content_hash, tenant_id)`; the type of `tenant_id` is part of what that ticket's re-keying would have to settle).
* **Dedupe before filing:** literal, case-insensitive matches over title and description, archived included: `canonical declaration` 0; `platform_document_registry` 10 hits, of which KS-1272 and KS-598 were read; KS-590 and KS-33 are unrelated. The same instrument returned KS-1272 for its own title phrase, so it can see ticket text.

title: security converters: four rowToApiKey boundary gaps survive the whole 311-test suite - an ABSENT is_active column reads as ACTIVE
description:
## BLUF

The Opus gate on PR #1511 (KS-880, verdict sha256/16 `0114cb379ee6b923`) planted 10 of its own mutants in `services/security/src/converters.ts`. **Four survived the full security suite** — 29 files / 311 tests, rc 0, with the mutant in place. All four are field-mapping boundaries on `rowToApiKey`, and every one of them was caught by the gate's differential harness, so the mapper is right today. What is missing is a **cell** that would notice if it stopped being right.

**The security-relevant one: a mutant that defaults** `isActive` **to** `true` **when the** `is_active` **column is absent passes 311/311.** A mapper that reads a key as ACTIVE when the column is missing is the shape that silently un-revokes a key.

These gaps **predate** PR #1511 — the same cells were unpinned at base `f6f2a539f4a0`, so this is not a regression from the one-mapper-home move. Filed as the gate's Minor m1, which explicitly said they are not a reason to hold that PR.

## Recommendation

Add cells to `services/security/src/__tests__/row-converters.test.ts` pinning each boundary. The first is the one that matters:

* `isActive` for a row with **no** `is_active` key, and for `is_active: null` — must be `false`, not `true`.
* `isActive` for `is_active: 't'` (the Postgres text form) — must be `true`, so a later `=== true` tightening reds.
* `connectorId` for `connector_id: ''` — must be `undefined`, not `''`.
* `organizationId` for `organization_id: ''` — must be `null`, not `''`.

Each cell should be shown red against the corresponding mutant before it is trusted, the way the KS-880 round did.

## Detail — the four survivors, with the gate's labels

| Gate mutant | The change | Suite | Differential |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| G1 | `is_active` absent gives `isActive: true` | **SURVIVED** 311/311 | 2 diffs |
| G10 | `isActive: r.is_active === true`, so the `'t'` string is no longer active | **SURVIVED** | 3 diffs |
| G7 | connectorId `??` becomes `||`, so `''` stays `''` instead of `undefined` | **SURVIVED** | 1 diff |
| G8 | organizationId `??` becomes `||`, so `''` stays `''` instead of `null` | **SURVIVED** | 2 diffs |

**Where** (line numbers at `b3a89d83df61`, the KS-880 fix-round head; the verdict cites the gated head `c6567a74493f`, where the same three sites are 7 lines earlier because the fix round added a comment block above them):

```
converters.ts:159   organizationId: (r.organization_id as string | null) ?? null,     (gated head :152)
converters.ts:171   isActive: Boolean(r.is_active),                                   (gated head :164)
converters.ts:177   connectorId: (r.connector_id as string | null) ?? undefined,      (gated head :170)
```

`Boolean(r.is_active)` is correct for every value the gate fed it, including absent (`undefined` to `false`) and the `'t'` string (to `true`). The point of the ticket is only that nothing fails if someone changes it.

**Not in scope:** `rowToAuditLog`'s `organizationId: (r.organization_id as string) || undefined` is a different type (`AuditLog.organizationId` is optional, not nullable) and the gate measured that mapper 0-diff over 23 rows. It is not one of the four.

## Dedupe before filing

Literal, case-insensitive matches over title and description across the Secuura-PK team, **archived included**: `isActive` 8 hits, `is_active` 8, `rowToApiKey` 4, `converters.ts` 1, `parseJsonArray` 0. None is about these boundaries — the nearest are KS-1370 (validate reads a boot-only memory map), KS-908 (connectorId invisible through the API) and KS-889 (the KS-869 COALESCE backfill window), all different defects. Positive control: `rowToApiKey` returned KS-880, KS-869, KS-908 and KS-889, and `converters.ts` returned KS-880, so the scan can see; `parseJsonArray` returned 0, so it can also return nothing.

Raised by Seat V 5th from the PR #1511 Opus gate, 2026-10-12.

nodes.body:
## MERGED — and a pre-existing defect the gate's probe turned up, now its own ticket

**[#1601](https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/1601) merged as `1e914e2b67671267db51a64ef0a4ada266dc06e3`** on gate O2's GO (Sonnet, tier 2, 2026-10-19T00:55:27Z). Five-point check 5/5. Three cells landed in `services/security/src/__tests__/row-converters.test.ts`: **G1** (a row with no `is_active` column reads inactive), its twin (`is_active: null` reads inactive) and **G10** (the Postgres text form `'t'` reads active, so tightening `Boolean()` to `=== true` reds).

Verified by me at the landing tree (`0ca7bc0e8363d5e950df8c12f648474d00424f7e`): `services/security` **346/346 in 31 files**, 0 failed, and `converters.ts` blob **identical to develop's** (`edacb6a7d48992d6eedae434269227f629834a17`) — so "test-only" is established by blob, not by reading the diff.

**This ticket stays open** and the link is `Refs`, because G7 and G8 were deliberately not added: the ticket describes behaviour the code does not have. R 50th's measurement against the real `rowToApiKey` stands — `connector_id: ''` returns `''` not `undefined`, and `organization_id: ''` returns `''` not `null`, because `''` is not nullish so `?? undefined` keeps it. A cell written to the ticket's spec would be **red at the tip**. Whether an empty id *should* normalise to absent is still an open product question on this ticket.

## New: KS-1639, from gate O2's probe on this PR

While probing G10, the gate found a pre-existing defect in the same mapper, out of this PR's scope and not changed by it: **`isActive: Boolean(r.is_active)` at `converters.ts:171` reads the Postgres text forms `'f'` and `'false'` as ACTIVE**, because `Boolean()` of any non-empty string is `true`.

Filed as **KS-1639**, Medium, with the column types measured. The short version: on every provisioning path `is_active` is `BOOLEAN` and node-postgres returns a JS boolean, so `'f'` cannot arrive today — it is latent. What makes it worth a ticket is the **asymmetry this PR just pinned into place**: G10 deliberately establishes that the mapper honours the text form for TRUE. So the mapper half-supports the text encoding — `'t'` is honoured, `'f'` is mis-read — and the direction it fails in is the unsafe one, a revoked key reading as active.

That is a direct consequence of a cell landed here, which is why it is recorded on this ticket as well as its own.

---

*Seat R 51st, 2026-10-19. Nothing deployed. No migrations, no config change.*

**Two of this ticket's four recommended cells (G7, G8) describe behaviour the code does not have — measured at the tip, a cell written to them would be RED, a false failure. The other two (G1, G10) are being raised as a PR.**

Seat R 50th, raising a held Spark PASS for this ticket at develop `78cb3c3939e319332e387ffecb075a169edd4a39`.

## Measured, not read off the operator

I called the **real** `rowToApiKey` from `services/security/src/converters.ts` at the tip:

| input | field | the tip returns | this ticket says it "must be" | |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `connector_id: ''` | `connectorId` | **`''`** | `undefined` | **disagrees** |
| `organization_id: ''` | `organizationId` | **`''`** | `null` | **disagrees** |
| `connector_id: null` (control) | `connectorId` | `undefined` | `undefined` | agrees |
| `organization_id: null` (control) | `organizationId` | `null` | `null` | agrees |
| `connector_id` absent (control) | `connectorId` | `undefined` | `undefined` | agrees |

The three controls agree, so the probe is exercising the real function. The cause: the tip is `(r.connector_id as string | null) ?? undefined` (`:177`) and `(r.organization_id as string | null) ?? null` (`:159`), and **`''` is not nullish**, so `??` keeps it.

**The mutant table is inverted in the same way.** It says G7 (`??` → `||`) makes "`''` stay `''` instead of `undefined`". It is the other way round: `'' || undefined` is `undefined` — the **mutant** produces `undefined`, and the **tip** produces `''`. So the tip is not the version that maps `''` to absent; the `||` mutant is.

## What this does and does not settle

- **Settled:** cells written to G7/G8 as specified would fail at the tip. They are not added.
- **Not settled — a product question, not a test-gap question:** *should* an empty-string id normalise to absent? Today `connectorId: ''` reaches callers as a string. Whether any reader treats `''` as "a connector" (`!== undefined`) rather than "no connector" (truthiness) has **not** been checked. If it matters, it is a separate ticket about the mapper's behaviour, not a missing cell.

## What is being raised

G1 (an absent `is_active` reads **inactive** — the security-relevant one, since active-on-missing is the shape that silently un-revokes a key), its `null` twin, and G10 (the Postgres text form `'t'` reads **active**). Planted against the gate's own mutants, each is killed by exactly one cell with no collateral failure. Security suite 346/346. The PR uses `Refs`, since it closes less than this ticket.

title: KS-1510 gate follow-ups: guard the document-lookup log call, pin the Error text and a null throw, cap the line, measure the Azure limiter key
description:
## BLUF

The Sonnet-tier gate on PR #1512 (ticket KS-1510) returned **GO WITH NOTE**: 0 Major, one Minor and several notes (verdict sha256/16 `cc2a467368885a9d`). None blocks the merge. This is one checklist for one pass over `services/api-gateway/src/routes/platform.ts` and the KS-1510 test file `ks1510-document-lookup-logs-the-thrown-error.test.ts`, plus one measurement owed after the deploy.

## Recommendation

Test first for (a), (b) and (c): each is a cell that is red against a named mutant today. (d) needs a decision. (e) needs a measurement on the deployed ingress and cannot be done before PR #1512 is deployed.

## Checklist

- [ ] **(a) Guard the log call (the gate's Minor 1).** The log expression inside the catch at `routes/platform.ts:995` is unguarded. A thrown value that makes `err.message`, `Object.getPrototypeOf`, `.constructor` or `Object.keys` throw (an Error with a throwing `message` getter, a Proxy with a throwing `getPrototypeOf` or `ownKeys` trap, a revoked Proxy), or a `logger.error` that itself throws, leaves the request with **no response** (hung after 2.5 s in the probe) and an unhandled rejection; the base answered the constant 500 for all 15 shapes probed. Not reachable by a caller (the value comes from `pg` or node), and the gateway survives the rejection (`index.ts:1189-1199`), so Minor. It is the same expression as `fail500` in `routes/batch.ts:28`, so the hazard is there too (not measured). Fix shape: wrap the log in try/catch, or build the string in a small non-throwing helper shared with `fail500`. Pin it with a cell that a throwing log call still answers the constant 500: mutant O4 (the log wrapped in try/catch) leaves all 8 cells green today.
- [ ] **(b) Pin the Error branch's exact logged text (Note 2).** Cell L1 asserts only that the text contains `ECONNREFUSED`. Logging `err.stack` (O1) or `String(err)` (O9) leaves L1 and L2 green, and logging the full Error object (O3) reddens only L3 and L4. A logged stack would put multi-line paths in the log unnoticed.
- [ ] **(c) A cell that throws** `null` **(Note 3).** With the `err !== null` guard removed (O11), `Object.getPrototypeOf(null)` throws inside the catch, which is the hang in (a), and every cell stays green. The gate's probe: `null` logs `thrown object` and answers 500.
- [ ] **(d) Cap the line length, or decide not to (Note 4).** The logged line is uncapped: about 15 KB if a database error echoed a maximal caller value, and one huge `fields [...]` string for an object with 100k fields. Same as `fail500`.
- [ ] **(e) Measure the limiter key on the deployed ingress (Note 1), after the deploy.** The bound of 300 log lines per minute per limiter key holds only behind a proxy that **appends** to `X-Forwarded-For` (the compose gateway behind nginx: a spoofed header is ignored, 5 of 40 requests reached the handler at cap 5). Reached directly, a rotating header gave 40 of 40 to the handler. The Azure gateway Container App has `ingress.external: true` (`deployment/azure/services.bicep:582-583`); its live behaviour, and any Front Door or CDN in front of it, is **unmeasured**.

## Detail

* **Related, pre-existing, NOT part of the checklist.** In `NODE_ENV=production` the two `winston.transports.File` transports in the api-gateway's `utils/logger.ts` (lines 36-47) write the literal text `undefined` for every call, because the logger's top-level format has no final formatter; the console JSON is the only usable production channel. KS-1348 (Done) is the **originate** half of the same defect; this service's half is now its own ticket, **KS-1526** (split out on Wednesday's ruling, confirmed at source on develop `629349dac602` with a control).
* Also found on the way: in production an unversioned call to this route is answered 307 first, and the redirect is counted by the global limiter, so a client that follows it pays two counts (150 lines per minute per key rather than 300).
* **Related:** KS-1510 (the change), KS-1346 (the `fail500` family: a different defect in the same helper family).
* **Dedupe before filing:** literal, case-insensitive matches over title and description, archived included: `platform.ts:995` 0, `throwing message getter` 0, `document-lookup` 1 (KS-1510 itself). The same instrument returned KS-1510 for its own title phrase, so it can see ticket text.
