title: Decide production VC verification: no DID resolver is wired anywhere, so with NODE_ENV=production /credentials/verify refuses every Ed25519 credential
description:
**BLUF: with** `NODE_ENV=production`**,** `POST /api/credentials/verify` **answers** `verified: false` **for EVERY Ed25519 credential, including a genuine unrevoked one, because nothing in the tree supplies the verifier a** `didResolver`**. The refusal is deliberate in code; a working production verify has never been built. DECISION NEEDED: is production VC verification intentionally off until go-live (then say so, and pin it with a test), or is wiring the resolver work to schedule? The same wiring would close KS-1383.**

## Measured (2026-10-12, develop `c63cec1f6070`)

In-process, on the real `POST /api/credentials/verify` handler and the real shared verifier, with `NODE_ENV` set per call (the verifier reads it at call time). **Not** a booted production app.

| case | `NODE_ENV=development` | `NODE_ENV=production` |
| -- | -- | -- |
| genuine, never revoked | `verified: true` | `verified: false`, `No DID resolver configured; cannot verify Ed25519 proof in production` |
| revoked, as issued | `false`, `Credential has been revoked` | `false`, the same resolver error plus `Credential has been revoked` |
| revoked, id never issued | `false`, `no issuer record` | `false`, the resolver error plus `no issuer record` |
| revoked, another LIVE credential's id | `true` (KS-1383) | `false`, the resolver error only |
| same, with a tampered `credentialSubject` | `true` (KS-1383) | `false`, the resolver error only |

So in production there is no bypass, and also no credential that verifies. Rows: `5_Project_History/2026-10-12_seatJ-4th/evidence/probe.env.txt`.

## From the code (read)

* `packages/shared/src/vc/verifier.ts:409-411`: `// In production, this MUST fail. In dev, allow pass-through.` then `if (process.env.NODE_ENV === 'production') errors.push('No DID resolver configured; cannot verify Ed25519 proof in production')`. In the file since its first commit, `e50dbde98` (2026-02-18).
* `verifier.ts:67` declares `didResolver` in the config; `:385` and `:447` use it. A search of the non-test, non-doc tree finds **no caller that supplies one**: `services/vc-issuer/src/routes/credentials.ts:339-346` passes the revocation resolvers only.
* No test names the production message, and I found no document saying production verification is deliberately off.

## What I can and cannot establish

* **Can:** the refusal is by design (the guard and its comment), and a working production verify path does not exist.
* **Cannot:** whether leaving it unbuilt is an accepted decision for the current phase. That is the decision this ticket asks for.

## NOT measured

A booted production app (vc-issuer will not boot without `DATABASE_URL` and `PRISM_AGENT_URL`); any deployed production environment; the demo VM; `POST /api/presentations/verify` in production mode (it calls the same shared verifier, per the code, but I did not run it); behaviour with a resolver wired.

## Priority, and why P3

It fails closed, so nothing unsafe is accepted; there is no production environment today (Platform K has no public domain yet); and its fix is the same wiring as KS-1383, which is High. It becomes a go-live blocker for any use of the VC verify routes.

## Board search before filing (Secuura-PK, archived included, titles, descriptions and comments, literal)

`No DID resolver configured`: 2 (KS-1375 description, as an aside "pre-existing, read, not driven"; KS-1383 only through my own comment of 2026-10-12). `verifier.ts:410`, `cannot verify Ed25519 proof in production`, `PRISM_AGENT_URL`: 1 each, all KS-1383 via that same comment. `production verif`: 2, both closed review tickets. Positive control `statusListResolver`: 4. Negative control: 0. **No open ticket tracks this as a question.** Related, not duplicates: KS-1383 (the id/proof binding), KS-1375, KS-625 (`/presentations/verify` never checks the holder signature: the opposite failure, a claim of validity with no check).

title: Timestamping: the opentimestamps and blockchain types still report verified true, and /verify accepts a forged proof with no stored row (KS-753 gate m2)
description:
**ACTION (owner: the timestamping build lane, with a policy decision first):** decide what an `opentimestamps` or `blockchain` timestamp may claim when nothing external ever checked it, then make creation and `/api/timestamps/verify` agree with that decision, the way KS-753 and KS-1404 did for `rfc3161`. Options to rule between: (a) report `verified: false` on creation and on verify for these two types until a real attestation check exists; (b) require a stored row and honour its `verified` column on verify (KS-1404's shape for rfc3161); (c) stop advertising the types in `supportedTypes` (`index.ts:185`) until they are real. Tests first, with a planted-red mutation per branch.

**Symptom (gate evidence P7, P8).**

* **P7:** creating an `opentimestamps` or `blockchain` timestamp answers `verified: true` and persists `verified = true`. Both types are placeholders by design (the proof is generated locally, `generateMockOpenTimestampsProof` / blockchain at `index.ts:689` and `:705`).
* **P8:** a **forged** `opentimestamps` JSON proof (the right hash plus one attestation) with **no stored row** returns `verified: true` from `/verify` (`index.ts:616-621`; the `blockchain` case at `:625` is the same shape: hash match plus `chain` and `slot` fields). Nothing checks an attestation against anything.
* KS-1404 closed this same forgery path for `rfc3161` only.

**Why P2.** This is "a mock timestamp reported as verified" by KS-753's own wording, on an evidentiary path (Tier 1). It is **not a regression** from PR #1502 and did not block it; the PR declared these types out of scope.

**Data, handled separately.** Rows of these types already stored as `verified = true` are a data question. A backfill is approval-class (Kam), and the count must come first, read-only per environment, classified by the proof's SHAPE rather than the `(mock)` name (the name missed 1 of 5 mocks in the gate's test). Wednesday is handing the count SQL to the deploy seat.

Source: the Opus QA gate of PR #1502 (KS-753), verdict sha256/16 `5e1fcf87edc4e8a4`, finding m2. Wednesday ruled on 2026-10-12 (12:20Z) that this is filed as P2. PR #1502 head `5daf8830dc46`; line numbers below are at that head.

title: Timestamping: a TSA reply flagged mock must force eidasQualified false, so requireEidas refuses it (KS-753 gate m1)
description:
**ACTION (owner: the timestamping build lane):** in `services/timestamping/src/index.ts`, `createTimestamp` (line 469 at the PR #1502 head), derive `eidasQualified` from the mock flag as well as the token, so a mock reply can never count as qualified:

```ts
eidasQualified = tsaResult.token && tsaResult.mock !== true ? tsaResult.eidasQualified === true : false;
```

Add the cell first and watch it fail: a stubbed TSA reply `{ token, mock: true, eidasQualified: true }` must answer `eidasQualified: false`, and with `requireEidas: true` it must answer **503**. Today it answers 201.

**Symptom (gate evidence P2).** With that input the route answers `201`, `verified: false`, `eidasQualified: true`; with `requireEidas: true` it answers **201 rather than 503**. The mock flag now decides `verified` (the line after, `if (tsaResult.mock === true || !tsaResult.token) verified = false;`) but not `eidasQualified`, so a mock reply could still pass the `requireEidas` gate. The PR's own "flag decides" cell uses exactly this input and asserts only `verified`.

**Not reachable today.** The real fallback hard-codes `eidasQualified: false` (`tsa/qualified-tsa.ts:333`), so the combination cannot occur until the TSA module changes or a second mock source appears. This is defence in depth, one line plus one cell.

title: GET /api/security/keys: the declared 200 body is {keys:[...]} but the handler answers {success,data}; organizationId's uuid format is declared and not enforced (KS-747 residuals)
description:
Filed by Seat V 4th on Wednesday's ruling (L11, 2026-10-12): the two residual findings on `GET /api/security/keys` that KS-747 did NOT cover, as ONE ticket, so KS-747 can close as "declare the parameter".

KS-747's fix (#1318, squash `f28cd1fbc7a5`) declared `organizationId` as a required uuid query parameter. It is on develop, deployed, and confirmed on the SERVED spec of Kintsugi (bytes equal to the yaml at the deployed commit; the parameter reads required, in query, format uuid). These two things remain:

## 1. The declared 200 body is `{keys: [...]}`; the handler answers `{success, data: [...]}`

Read at the deployed commit `65d7722f83a6`: `services/security/src/security.openapi.ts` registers `ApiKeyListResponse = z.object({ keys: z.array(ApiKeySchema) })` for the 200, and `services/security/src/index.ts` `app.get('/api/keys', ...)` ends `res.json({ success: true, data: keys })`. So the two cannot both be right. Peter measured the consequence on all four KS-1353 sweeps (slot 3, head `d9ce1403d`, seed 1353): `response_schema_conformance` **31 of 31** own-test 200s fail with `"keys" is a required property`, and one more inside a stateful chain, 32 calls in all (KS-747, comment of 2026-09-28T12:31Z). KS-908's merge note also records the `keys`-vs-`data` naming as pre-existing drift.

Decision needed: which side is the contract. The house envelope elsewhere is `{success, data}`, which argues for changing the DECLARED schema to match the handler, not the handler (consumers already read `data`). Not decided here.

## 2. `organizationId` is declared `format: uuid`, and nothing enforces it

The handler checks only `if (!organizationId)`; a value that is not a uuid is accepted and simply matches nothing. Peter's sweeps record **5** `negative_data_rejection` failures on this operation, and KS-747's own merge note flagged it as "U-1" (declaration and enforcement are separate) and left it unfiled. Decision needed: enforce the format (400 on a non-uuid) or stop declaring it.

This is one instance of the class **KS-1022** (the id-format contract seam).

## Not established by me

I did not observe either finding LIVE: the one authed GET I was cleared to make was refused 403, because the only QA credential (role OWNER) is not in `KEY_ADMIN_ROLES`. Both are read from source at the deployed commit and from Peter's sweep data.

Related: KS-747, KS-908, KS-1022, KS-1361 (Done; the sweeps' baseline), KS-1015.

nodes.body:
**BLUF:** as suggested above, both `GET /api/security/keys` baseline entries now cite **this ticket** on develop (KS-983, PR #1563, merge `fe0656b60`, 2026-10-16), with the cause measured that day and Kamil's verbatim words from this ticket (`systemTest/schemathesis/config/baseline_kamil.py["KS-1514"]`).

- They still pass the gate **only as known failures**; nothing is hidden, and the expiry is unchanged (2026-12-31).
- Re-run on 2026-10-16: `response_schema_conformance` fired and resolves here. `negative_data_rejection` did not fire on that seed, which means not sampled, not fixed.
- When this ticket's fix lands, remove both entries. The proposed acceptance criteria above still apply.

**BLUF:** both `GET /api/security/keys` pairs are still firing today, and the Schemathesis baseline still attributes them to **KS-747 (Done)** rather than to this ticket.

**Measured on 2026-10-16** (slot 2, develop `a92f46e14`, Schemathesis 4.31.1):
- `response_schema_conformance::GET /api/security/keys`: the handler answered `{"success":true,"data":[]}` where `ApiKeyListResponse` requires `keys`. This is the first half of this ticket.
- `negative_data_rejection::GET /api/security/keys`: fired again. This is the second half (the uuid format is declared but not enforced).
- KS-747's own fix is in place: `organizationId` is now declared (commit `f28cd1fbc`). So the baseline's reason for both entries, *"organizationId undeclared"*, no longer describes the cause.

**Suggestion, gently:** when convenient, re-cite both baseline entries to KS-1514 with a reason that matches the measured cause, so they have a live owner (the KS-1015 finding 2 pattern).

**Proposed acceptance criteria:**
- `GET /api/security/keys` 200 matches `ApiKeyListResponse` (or the spec changes to the envelope the handler returns).
- A non-uuid `organizationId` is rejected with 400.
- A test demonstrates the fix: Schemathesis `response_schema_conformance` and `negative_data_rejection` stop firing for this operation on a full sweep, and a targeted unit/contract test pins both behaviours.
- Both baseline entries are removed.

## Facts comment — scope of these two items, 2026-10-13

Recorded while planning **KS-1553** (Wednesday's ruling of 2026-10-13). **Nothing else on this ticket is changed**, and no code has been written for either item.

### Item 1 (the declared `{keys: […]}` body vs the handler's `{success, data}`) stays its OWN ticket

It is the only part of this ticket that changes the **spec**, and it is a contract decision — which side is right — rather than a validation fix. Folding it into KS-1553's PR would turn a small change into a published-contract change and pull in the Schemathesis pre-merge tier. Confirmed still true at develop `d19b7a70`: `ApiKeyListResponseSchema` registers `keys: z.array(ApiKeySchema)` (`services/security/src/security.openapi.ts:413-416`, used for the 200 at `:828`) while `app.get('/api/keys', …)` ends `res.json({ success: true, data: keys })`.

### Item 2 (the declared-but-unenforced `format: uuid` on `organizationId`) is DEFERRED, and here is the reason

Enforcing it — a 400 for a non-uuid — **cannot ship on its own, because it would break a page that works today, and the break would be silent.**

Measured 2026-10-13 on a scratch PostgreSQL 15 with the service connected as `secuura_app`, against the real routes, every arm with a control:

* The **Admin Dashboard** hard-codes `organizationId: 'default-org'` on both operations — the list (`frontend/admin/src/services/api.ts:358-360`, called with no argument from `pages/ApiKeys.tsx:75`) and the mint (`pages/ApiKeys.tsx:92`).
* That path **works end to end today**: the mint answers **201** and stores `default-org` verbatim, and the list answers **200 and returns that key**. Controls: a different organisation id returns 0 keys (so the filter is real), and the UPPER-CASE form returns 0 (which is KS-1553 (a)).
* With the format enforced, the **list** would 400 — and `request()` (`api.ts:84-91`) turns any non-2xx into `{ok:false}`, after which `fetchApiKeys` returns `[]`. The page would show **zero keys with no error shown to the user**. The **mint** would 400 too, and the Create-Key button would stop producing a key.

**Sequencing.** Item 2 is bundled into a deferred PR together with **KS-1553 (b)** and the frontend fix (**KS-1564**), because none of the three is safe alone. That PR needs a deploy seat for the frontend surface and waits on Platform S's answer about the id form it sends (asked on KS-1553, comment `2087528f`).

**KS-1553's PR 1** is deliberately scoped to normalising the list query with no 400, so it closes KS-1553 (a) without touching this item — and it carries the Admin Dashboard's exact shape as a regression pin.

Also filed today: **KS-1564** (the frontend hard-coding, the source) and **KS-1565** (count the existing non-canonical rows, read-only, no backfill).

*Facts only; no change to this ticket's description, state or priority.*

| -- | -- |
| Prerequisite, once per machine | `brew install stripe/stripe-cli/stripe` then `stripe login` (browser pairing, test mode) |
| How to know it worked | one `stripe listen:` line in the dock_run log, *forwarding …*, or *stripe CLI not available or not logged in*; `up-slot.sh` echoes it after health |
| Without the CLI | `/idv` still completes through the return-path fallback (`docs/identity-provider-configuration.md`); the stack is unchanged |
| Opt out (to prove the fallback) | `./dock_run --no-stripe` / `./up-slot.sh N --no-stripe` or `STRIPE_LISTEN=0` |
| Inspect / stop | `./stripe-listen.sh status` / `stop` (`~/.secuura-dev/stripe-listen-<project>.*`) |
| Several slots | every listener receives every event of the account; the slot that does not own the session logs "unknown session" and answers 200 |

Also in `CLAUDE.md` (platform-s), *Local Development with Docker* › *Stripe test webhooks reach the local stack (*[PS-958](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-958/a-stripe-identity-result-that-stripe-cannot-deliver-by-webhook-is)*)*.

**Unblock steps (a person's step, test mode only):**

1. `brew install stripe/stripe-cli/stripe`, then `stripe login` once on this Mac (needs a browser and the Stripe account).
2. `ssd/dep-ssd-local/up-slot.sh 3` so the listener starts; confirm the log line says *forwarding*.
3. Exercise Stripe checkout (subscription purchase) and Stripe Identity (`/idv`) through the UI; record results here.

**Related.** [PS-1019](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1019/the-return-path-reconcile-marks-an-untouched-stripe-identity-session) (Stripe Identity return-path reconcile marks an untouched session) is still a tracked `test.fixme`; [PS-958](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-958/a-stripe-identity-result-that-stripe-cannot-deliver-by-webhook-is) added the listener; the [PS-966](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-966/systemtest-the-hosted-continue-with-link-on-an-open-hosted-kyc-row-has)/[PS-815](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-815/identity-integrationspects138-provisioning-twice-creates-no-duplicate) sets covered the return path only. Two full-suite reds on earlier slot runs were attributed to the slot's Stripe identity config (no `stripe listen`), so a green Stripe path would also clear those.

**Not affected by the round-3 merge (#965):** nothing in #965's description touches Stripe; not re-verified in the code.

## Stripe add-ons: "one change per press" (handed over from [PS-1442](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1442/systemtest-recorded-once-per-press-declare-share-save-re-grant-extend) row 8, 2 Nov 2026)

[PS-1442](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1442/systemtest-recorded-once-per-press-declare-share-save-re-grant-extend) added browser tests that each control fixed by [PS-1398](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1398/double-submit-9-more-controls-can-record-an-action-twice-on-a-double) records once per press. The subscription add-ons were left to this ticket (Peter, 2 Nov 2026). [PS-1442](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1442/systemtest-recorded-once-per-press-declare-share-save-re-grant-extend) implements nothing for them.

**What the docs promise** (`docs/USER-MANUAL.md:280`):

> Adding, removing or changing the quantity of an add-on is one change however many times its button is pressed: the page waits under *Processing, please wait* until it has been made, and Stripe is asked to make it once ([PS-1398](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1398/double-submit-9-more-controls-can-record-an-action-twice-on-a-double), 30 Oct 2026).

The fix is PR #1234. Its body names "A Stripe test-mode double click" as proof debt for the end-of-round run, and it added no systemTest spec.

**What a test needs, as found on** [PS-1442](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1442/systemtest-recorded-once-per-press-declare-share-save-re-grant-extend)**:**

* **A live test-mode subscription.** The dev-seed fixture on organisation 1 has an empty `TransactionId` (`stripe_commerce.spec.ts` header), so its Add / Remove buttons have no Stripe subscription behind them. A new account must subscribe through the hosted checkout first, as `stripe_checkout_sandbox.spec.ts` does, gated by `externalAreaGate('stripe-billing', ['sandbox'])`.
* **No other slot running a Stripe listener.** On 2 Nov 2026, slot 2's `global_setup` reported "stripe listen also running for ssd-slot3 — checkout is not exercised ([PS-994](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-994/docker-stack-slots-and-any-deployments-sharing-one-stripe-account))", so checkout stood down `[env]`. `systemTest/.env.stripe` held a test key.
* **Page-object work.** `pages/stripe_portal_page.ts` has the selectors `addonAddBtn`, `addonRemoveBtn`, `addonBuyBtn`, `activeAddonCard` and `availableAddonCard`. It has no Add, Remove or quantity action methods, and no quantity selector. How these controls behave under a live subscription (confirmation step, form submit or script call) was **not measured**.
* **Harness to reuse.** `utils/held_request_probe.ts` from [PS-1442](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1442/systemtest-recorded-once-per-press-declare-share-save-re-grant-extend) (on [PS-1442](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1442/systemtest-recorded-once-per-press-declare-share-save-re-grant-extend)'s branch, not yet on `develop`). It holds the first request in flight, raises the second press from inside the page, and reports whether the second press really happened. For a script-submitted form, the browser abandons the first navigation when the second starts, so assert on the resulting state, not on the first press's answer (measured on [PS-1442](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1442/systemtest-recorded-once-per-press-declare-share-save-re-grant-extend)'s Deactivate test).

**Acceptance (in addition to the above):** a Playwright test per control (Add, Remove, quantity). It presses twice with the first request held, asserts the second press was raised, and asserts one change in the portal's active add-ons or totals. Tagged `@stripe @area-billing @regression @validation`, carrying `(PS-1398)` in its title and an `issue` annotation. It stands down `[env]` where checkout is not `sandbox`. Docs: a line in `docs/platform_s_testing_cheat_sheet.html`'s once-per-press row.

title: versionedById is caller-controlled but is now an erasure selector: reserve it as a server-set key on create, /version, /sign-cert and /sign-wallet
description:
## BLUF

`metadata.versionedById` is meant to be set by the server (`user.id`), but any writer can set it, and KS-695 part (ii) now uses it to decide which documents an organisation's erasure irreversibly blanks. Reserve it as a server-set key.

## Recommendation

Strip `versionedById` from caller-supplied `data` on create, and make the three version paths ignore a caller's value, so it can only come from `user.id`. Review the neighbouring keys that share the same spread (`versionAction`, `versionedAt`, `parentDocumentId`) in the same change.

## Detail (read by me in the tree at develop `8d34fbf0890a`, 2026-10-12)

* **Create:** `services/originate/src/routes/documents.ts:600` builds `data` as `{ ...rawData, ... }` from the request. `stripReservedMetadataKeys` (`repositories/documentRepo.ts:158`) removes only `blockchain`, `signatures` and `walletAddress`, so a caller-supplied `versionedById` is stored as metadata.
* **/version, /sign-cert, /sign-wallet:** `documents.ts:2106`, `:2840` and `:3034` set `versionedById: user.id` and then spread the caller's `...metadata` AFTER it, so the caller's value wins.
* **Why it matters now:** the Opus gate on PR #1497 reproduced it through the real create route and the real erase route as `secuura_app`: organisation A's connector created a document with `data.versionedById = "connector:platform-s:<B's GUID>"` (201), B's erase answered `completed`, and A's title read `[erased]` (irreversible). Gate verdict: `WEDNESDAY/0_Brain/reference/2026-10-12_gate-pr1497/verdict.md`, finding M1. PR #1497 bounds the selector by the issuer, which stops that outcome, but that is a seatbelt on one consumer; this ticket is the root.
* The connector id is `platform-s:<Organisation GUID>`, which is the externalRef, so it is knowable.

## Done when

- [ ] A caller-supplied `versionedById` is not stored by create and is overridden by `user.id` on the three version paths; one red-first cell per route (four routes, four claims).
- [ ] Platform S does not rely on sending it (confirm with Stuart; a round-trip of a K document's `data` into a new create must not carry it).
- [ ] Measured: how many existing documents carry a `versionedById` that is not the creating connector's (a read-only count), and a recorded decision on them.

## Sequencing (Wednesday's ruling, 2026-10-12, after the second Opus gate on #1497)

**This ticket must LAND BEFORE KS-695 DEPLOYS.** With PR #1497's selector bounded by the issuer, a NULL-issuer document can still be claimed for another organisation by any writer through `versionedById` (a create without `organizationUuid`, or any `/version`, whose metadata is spread after `versionedById` and whose source has no organisation check), so the erasure's reach is only as trustworthy as this field. The gate's evidence: A's `/version` of A's own document with `metadata.versionedById` = B's connector is blanked by B's erasure and is not reached by A's.

## Not claimed

That any caller has done this. Exploiting it needs organisation A's own writer to plant B's id (a bug in a round-trip, or on purpose); B cannot do it alone. Raised by the Opus gate on #1497; filed by Seat J 3rd on Wednesday's instruction.

* Note 1: the cells pin the `!== undefined` gate, not every rewrite. The gate's own mutants: `!= null` is caught by exactly one cell (`null`); `typeof x === 'string'` by three (`null`, `0`, `false`; the `''` cell passes it). Every shape tried was caught by at least one cell.

**BLUF: this ticket's drop-log gate has the same truthy-only blind spot KS-1679 just closed for its own two keys, and nothing records it here. Facts only — no code change, no PR, nothing claimed about priority.**

Found while raising **[#1671](https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/1671)** (KS-1679, gate BF1 N1), which adds one cell planting `''`, `null`, `0`, `false` for `certificationId` and `certifiedAt`. The same reasoning applies to **`versionedById`**, and I am recording it here rather than widening that PR.

## The shape, re-read at live develop `561a6c5b528289f4d7ecd19f9c069501e925e9ea`

All four dropped-key log gates in `services/originate/src/routes/certifications.ts` are byte-identical in form:

```
:648  if (droppedVersionedById !== undefined) {
:651  if (droppedParentDocumentId !== undefined) {
:654  if (droppedCertificationId !== undefined) {     <- KS-1679 covers these two
:657  if (droppedCertifiedAt !== undefined) {         <-
```

**This ticket's gate is `:648`.** The shipped code is **correct** — `!== undefined` is the right test, because the question is *"was a value supplied"*, not *"is it truthy"*.

## Why a cell is still missing

A falsy plant is dropped from the stored row **either way**: the destructure at `:647` removes the key regardless of its value. So **the row cannot distinguish the two readings — only the log line can.** A mutant changing `:648` to a bare truthiness test (`if (droppedVersionedById) {`) therefore keeps every existing cell green while silently dropping the log for `''`, `0`, `false` and `null`.

## Measured, not inferred

I checked whether any existing cell already plants a falsy value for **`versionedById`**:

- `ks1508-versionedbyid-is-server-set.test.ts` (12 cells)
- `ks1508-a-planted-versionedbyid-is-not-stored.integration.test.ts` (3 cells)

**No cell plants a falsy literal for either key**, and the planted constants are all non-empty string literals, i.e. truthy:
`PLANTED = 'connector:platform-s:' + GUID_B`, `OTHER_ORG_CONNECTOR = 'connector:platform-s:9999…'`, `FOREIGN_ID = 'doc-another-organisations-document'`.

**What my probe could and could not see:** it is a source-text scan for a falsy literal at the key, plus a read of each planted constant's definition. It would **not** catch a falsy value reaching the key through a variable I did not resolve. Paired with a positive control — the same probe on KS-1679's file, which hits its `for (const planted of ['', null, 0, false])` loop at `:171` — so the negative result is a measurement, not an empty result set.

I also scanned this ticket's comments for any truthiness/falsy term before writing: **no hits**, against a positive control on KS-1679 where the gap *is* recorded (its 2026-10-19 20:05Z comment). So this is not a duplicate.

## What would close it
One cell on this ticket's own key, in the shape #1671 uses: plant `''`, `null`, `0`, `false`, assert the key is absent from the stored row **and** logged exactly once, with a `[key, planted, …]` prefix on every expectation so a failure names the pair. **One caveat from building it:** a single looped cell short-circuits — I measured that a tamper breaking all four falsy values reports only the **first** pair (`["certificationId", ""]`), 1 failed / 13 skipped. It names the individual value, but it will not list every broken pair at once.

**Not assigned, not prioritised, no PR.** Recorded so it has a home on the ticket that owns the line.

## Merged to develop (squash `b2085e99ff1c`, PR #1516). NOT Done: it stays In Progress until deployed.

**BLUF:** `versionedById` is now server-set on all FIVE routes that let a caller write it (create, `/version`, `/sign-cert`, `/sign-wallet`, and `POST /api/certifications/issue` with `parentDocumentId`, which the ticket did not list). Opus gate: GO WITH NOTE at head `770d0f3de074` (verdict sha256/16 `020f335956fb7b09`), 0 Major, 1 Minor, 8 Notes. Merged on Wednesday's head-bound GO of 2026-10-12 16:40Z; develop was `f39104e71688`, the path overlap with the landed commit was 0, and the landed tree equals the predicted tree.

**Still open, honestly:**
- **N-3: rows that already exist are not healed**, and #1497's selector still reads them (every ROOT row carrying the key was caller-planted). Bounding that selector arm is for the #1497 round, not for this ticket. Kintsugi (read-only): 0 root rows carry the key; one derived row, `313180f3-5850-48a7-9d82-f085cac6c6d4`, could not be classified (QA box).
- **N-4:** on `/certifications/issue` the dropped value is still echoed in the 201 response, kept in the certification's own `certification_metadata` and covered by two content hashes. Disclosure only. Follow-up **KS-1537** (P3 checklist: the Minor on the published spec, the two HASH cells the gate says no shipped test pins, the fifth surface on real Postgres, N-4).
- **N-6:** a pre-existing authorisation gap on the legacy certify path, unrelated to this change. Filed as **KS-1538** (P2).

title: Mount the audit-export router behind authenticateToken (it answers 401 to every caller), then settle its three unfiled residuals
description:
## BLUF

**Action (owner: the K lane): mount the audit-export router behind** `authenticateToken`**; today it answers 401 to every caller.** `app.use('/api/admin/audit', auditExportRouter)` (`services/api-gateway/src/index.ts:808` at develop `361537eed238`) has no `authenticateToken`, and the router reads `req.user`, which only that middleware sets. So the platform audit export, the goal of KS-745, is unreachable as shipped. It is the same shape as the batch family tracked in KS-1243 (`/api/batch/*`, 401 to every caller); KS-1243 names only the batch routes.

## Recommendation

1. **Tests first:** a platform-admin JWT reaches the export and gets the entries; an anonymous request gets 401; a tenant ADMIN gets 403 if the router gates on role (read its own guard first).
2. **Then mount it with** `authenticateToken(true)`**.**
3. **Then decide the three residuals below** (they were read at source, not measured, and were never filed).
4. KS-745 stays In Progress until this is done: its PR fixed the route the export calls, and its own comment says the goal is still unmet.

## Detail

* **The PR's three unfiled residuals (from its own text):** (1) the list route ignores the export's `type`; (2) the list defaults `limit` to 50, so an export caps at 50 entries; (3) a date-only `to` looks like it drops that day.
* **Evidence:** the Tier-1 gate on KS-745's PR proved the export unreachable as shipped (KS-745's latest comment). I read the mount line at the tip. I re-measured the sibling `/api/batch/verify` today with a valid human token and a valid `x-api-key`: 401 both times. I did NOT drive the audit export itself, and I did not measure `/api/notifications`, which is mounted the same way two lines above (`index.ts:807`).
* **Searched first** (Linear, includeArchived, title and description): `audit-export`, `audit export`, `/api/admin/audit`, `auditExportRouter`. No ticket mentions the audit export's mount. Nearest: KS-745 itself, KS-1243 (batch only), KS-1410 (`err.message` in 500 bodies; a different subject).

Related: KS-745, KS-1243.

## BLUF

**Steps 1-2 are built and at merge: [#1608](https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/1608), head `ce638c916fc7d550479ceb4e6f612998a1c14774`, gate V1 GO WITH NOTE.** One line — `app.use('/api/admin/audit', authenticateToken(true), auditExportRouter);` — plus a 5-cell suite that drives the real gateway app over HTTP.

**⚠ A correction to my own framing, which gate V1 caught: this is NOT defence in depth. It switches a DEAD export ON.** The gate measured it directly — a `SUPER_ADMIN` token gets **401 on develop and 200 on the branch**. I had written in #1608's body that the middleware was "defence in depth, not a change in whether unauthenticated callers get in". The second half is true for an *anonymous* caller; the first half is wrong, and it was the sentence a reviewer would quote. #1608's body is corrected in place and says so.

**⚠ The now-live export has four faults, filed as KS-1645 (Medium). They must be repaired before this export is deployed.** Merging to `develop` is fine; nothing is deployed, so there is no live exposure yet.

## The ticket's own question, answered from source

This ticket asks to mount the router behind `authenticateToken` and then **settle** whether any caller loses access.

- **`authenticateToken` is already imported** — `services/api-gateway/src/index.ts:27`.
- **`true` means REQUIRED, and it is the parameter's default** — `authenticateToken(required: boolean = true)` at `services/api-gateway/src/middleware/auth.ts:361`.
- **Before this change the mount had no auth middleware at all** — `index.ts:811` read `app.use('/api/admin/audit', auditExportRouter);`.
- **No caller loses access it should keep.** For an *unauthenticated* request the router already refused without `req.user` — `ks1410-batch-and-audit-export-500-never-answer-err-message`'s control C1 asserts *"no req.user still answers 401 UNAUTHORIZED on batch and on the audit export"* — so for an anonymous caller only **where** the 401 is produced moves. Cells that mount the router directly are unaffected (`ks745-audit-export-calls-the-list-route.test.ts:24` does exactly that; `ks1410`'s suite likewise; both green in the full run). **Gate V1 re-measured this independently and confirmed that only bare-router unit tests call the export.**
- **The e2e callers are a different path.** `tests/e2e*` call `/api/admin/audit-logs`; the export router is `/api/admin/audit/export`. Control for that search: `api/admin/api-keys`, a route that **does** have callers, returns 11 files.
- **`middleware/audit.ts:85` does not interact.** That list is `EXCLUDED_PREFIXES`, and its own comment says why — *"Audit endpoints themselves are excluded so the act of querying audit doesn't generate new audit rows."* It suppresses **audit-row writes**, not authentication. `/api/admin/audit` was in it before this change and is unchanged by it.

## What was measured, and by whom

**By me**, in a scratch clone at develop `9512cc70d8c4ad8a1214b17a39d7c48456feb531` (this branch's base):

- **Red-first** with `src/index.ts` reset to **develop's blob**, the tamper asserted to have landed (the mount line read back without the middleware): **3 failed / 2 passed of 5 executed** — the failures are exactly the three RED cells (A1 JSON export, A2 CSV export, A3 403-not-401 for a non-admin). 5 cells executed, so a real red and not a load failure. The two CONTROL cells (A4 anonymous → 401 with zero upstream hits, A5 connector-JWT-as-Bearer → 401, zero upstream hits) pass either way, by design — they are what stop A1-A3 passing on a route that let everyone through.
- **Restore proved by blob, three ways:** the working tree's `index.ts` = `94d34512ee…` = a fresh application of the canonical patch = **the patch's own declared post-image `94d34512e`**; develop's `4817a72ac…` = **its declared pre-image**; the new suite = `365ff76230…` = the patch's `365ff7623`.
- **Whole `api-gateway` suite: 1122 / 1122 in 115 files**, against **1117 / 114** measured by me at develop in the same clone — exactly the 5 new cells in 1 new file, the figure predicted before the run.
- `tsc --noEmit` and the real `tsc` emit both rc 0. **ESLint 0 errors** on both touched files; `index.ts`'s two warnings (`117:3` no-namespace, `929:7` unused eslint-disable) are **pre-existing**, proved by running the same ESLint over develop's blob through `--stdin`. Positive control: a stdin file with a bad expression reports 1 error, rc 1.
- Push preflight, in-hook: `PUSH_RC=0`, **13 of 16 legs ran with 3 SKIPPED** (legs 3, 4, 8 — no local stack on this box). **That is not a pass.**

**By gate V1** (Opus, tier 1, the batched five, round 1 of 2) and **not reproduced by me**: the 401→200 `SUPER_ADMIN` measurement, the caller census, the four export faults now in KS-1645, and the suites on the chained landing tree.

**Not tested by anyone:** #1608 end to end against a **real** security service.

## Scope — why the link is a reference and not a resolution

This is **steps 1-2 only**: the mount and its pinning suite. The ticket's remaining settle question stays open here, and KS-1645 now carries the export's correctness as a separate, blocking condition on deploying it.

title: KS-811 gate findings (#1491): the 403-code scan reads comments, and the global CSRF middleware answers unpublished CSRF_* 403s on the same path
description:
Filed by Seat V 4th as the single P3 follow-up required by Wednesday's head-bound GO on PR #1491 (KS-811 second ask), 2026-10-12T09:55:43Z. Gate verdict `2026-10-12_gate-pr1491/verdict.md`, sha256/16 `2331702dc31cc79e`. 0 Major.

The merged work is sound and stays merged: one new test file, no product file touched, and the gate derived the emitted 403 set (`FORBIDDEN` plus the four enforcement codes) and the published set independently and they matched the author's. This ticket carries the two residuals the gate named.

## Finding 1 (Minor) — the scan reads comments, so commented-out code can red or green a cell

The derivation in `ks811-post-documents-403-code-set-agrees.test.ts` scans source text without
stripping comments. Consequences the gate demonstrated:

* a commented-out `403` on the route turns three cells red, so a purely documentary edit breaks the suite;
* nearby unrelated code can be misattributed to the handler under test.

Closing step: strip comments before deriving the set (or parse rather than text-scan), then re-run the
gate's mutation set to confirm the three cells no longer answer to a comment.

## Finding 2 (Note) — the asserted set holds at handler level only

The global CSRF middleware answers unpublished `CSRF_*` 403s on this path for cookie-only requests.
So "the 403 code set of `POST /api/documents`" is true of the handler, not of the front door: a
cookie-only caller can receive a 403 whose code is not in either set the test compares.

Closing step: decide whether the published set should include the `CSRF_*` codes reachable on this
path, or whether the test's scope sentence should say handler-level explicitly. Either is acceptable;
leaving both unstated is not.

## Known blind spots — already stated in the test file header, recorded here so they are not re-found

Three of the gate's eleven mutations stayed green: the helper, the variable and the `Object.assign`
form. The file header names them. They are not regressions and are not in scope for this ticket

title: ks963 wallet ordering guard (KS-806 round 4): the purity pin on canonicalWalletAddress is a deny-list, and the allow-list matches names only
description:

Two Minors from the Sonnet-tier delta gate on #1476 round 4 (verdict `/Volumes/DevMASTER/WEDNESDAY/0_Brain/reference/2026-10-12_gate-pr1476-r4/verdict.md`, sha256/16 `f70196195b8ce128`), filed at the priority Wednesday asked for (P3). An impure helper that uses none of them, or a `console.log` inside it, stays green. 2. **Minor-2, the allow-list matches names only:** nothing ties the `canonicalWalletAddress` name used in `routes/wallet.ts` to the export in `utils/walletEmail.ts`, so a local impure function with the same name declared inside `wallet.ts` shadows the pure one and stays green. **MERGED: #1643 squash `513371a34be58af9e740b82ea26795155c7bd0b4`. Minor-2 is pinned. This ticket stays open: Minor-1 is untouched.**

BLUF: merged on Wednesday's head-pinned GO after gate BD1 (tier 2, round 1 of 2): **GO WITH NOTE, 0 blockers, 3 notes.** Landed tree `54dc22e920569148070ee579fc173753432f6dd4` with exactly one parent, `2b205beada00a2f0fb3144e38198e471848132b6`, equal to BD1's `merge-tree`, Wednesday's and my own. One file, +10/-1. `Refs KS-1500`; the attachment reads `linkKind=contributes`, `status=merged`, and this issue stayed In Progress at the merge.

## What landed for this ticket

The first of the two commits, `737389ca6587e0fbfa5211d2a10fe89512369b9f`: a cell pinning that `routes/wallet.ts` imports `canonicalWalletAddress` from `../utils/walletEmail` **and** declares no binding of that name, read through the comment-and-string-blanked source so a mention in a comment cannot satisfy it.

**Still open, and not addressed:** Minor-1 — the purity pin is a deny-list (it rejects a fixed token set), so an impure helper using none of those tokens still passes. Your recommended closing step, an allow-list matched structurally, is not done.

**Suite:** auth 1,095 -> 1,096 by cell name, 99 files, rc 0 both sides, 0 new reds. The +1 is this ticket's cell. The push gate's `typecheck-tests: auth` leg reports 42 errors, 42 in the baseline, **0 new**.

## The mutant matrix was corrected before the merge, on gate BD1 note N2

**Three of the four `T` mutants I first reported as kills do not compile, so those readings are withdrawn.** Measured with `tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json` in `services/auth`, each planted into `routes/wallet.ts` and restored byte-identically, against a clean baseline of rc 0 / 0 errors:

| mutant | compiles? | status |
| -- | -- | -- |
| T1 import dropped + a local impure fn declared | **yes** | SURVIVED unedited, **KILLED** edited |
| T3d a local binding declared in **another** function, import kept and still used at `:188` | **yes** | SURVIVED unedited, **KILLED** edited |
| T2 import re-pointed at `../utils/cip8` | **no — `TS2305`** | withdrawn, not a valid mutant |
| T3 import kept + a **top-level** fn of that name | **no — `TS2440`** | withdrawn, not a valid mutant |
| T4 import dropped, no local fn | **no — `TS2304`** | withdrawn, not a valid mutant |
| K1 `INSERT` template + decoy `//` comment | **yes** | SURVIVED unedited, **KILLED** edited |
| K2 decoy **block** comment containing a backtick | **yes** | SURVIVED unedited, **KILLED** edited |
| K3 lookup replaced by a different statement | **yes** | **KILLED by both** (the positive control) |

A mutant that cannot compile is a change that could never ship, so a cell "catching" it proves nothing. `T3d` is seat-written to replace `T3` compile-safely: it declares a local binding of the name in a different function, keeping the top-level import in place and still used, which avoids both the `TS2440` conflict and the `TS6133` unused-import that a same-scope shadow causes.

**Two things stated rather than implied.** First, **the import-source half's independence is UNMEASURED**: `src/utils/walletEmail.ts` is the only module in the service exporting `canonicalWalletAddress`, so no compile-safe tamper can re-point the import without adding a module. `T3d` establishes the no-local-binding half; `T1` breaks both at once. Second, **my own false-kill detector was blind here**, and that is worth knowing: it flags a kill whose failure text carries a `TS####` code, but this cell reads `wallet.ts` as *text* rather than importing it, so a non-compiling mutant yields an ordinary assertion failure and no TypeScript diagnostic ever appears. For a source-scan test the mutant must be type-checked separately — the detector cannot see it.

**One disagreement with the gate, with my measurement.** BD1's N2 lists `T2` among its compile-safe proofs. My reading is that `T2` cannot compile: `src/utils/cip8.ts` exports neither `canonicalWalletAddress` nor `syntheticWalletEmail` (0 matching export lines, against 2 in `walletEmail.ts`), and planting it gives `TS2305` on both names. I have therefore marked it withdrawn, which claims less rather than more.

**PR #1643 is up: Minor-2 is pinned — `wallet.ts` must import `canonicalWalletAddress` from `../utils/walletEmail` and declare no binding of that name. Test-only, zero product bytes. Minor-1 stays open.**

BLUF: https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/1643, head `de44e3d3ccfcefd58abe5295a1f8a2571e765bc4`, **two commits** on develop `2b205beada00a2f0fb3144e38198e471848132b6`; this ticket's is the first, `737389ca6587e0fbfa5211d2a10fe89512369b9f`. Raised byte-for-byte from the held Spark pass `KS-1500-WALLETIMPORTPIN-1`. One file, +10/-1 across both commits. `Refs`, not a close keyword. Gate pending, not merged.

## Scope — Minor-2 only, and Minor-1 is untouched

- **Closed by this:** Minor-2. `PURE_BEFORE_LOOKUP` matched the **name** `canonicalWalletAddress`, and nothing tied that name to the pure export in `utils/walletEmail`. A local impure function of the same name declared inside `routes/wallet.ts` shadowed the pure one and the guard stayed green. The new cell pins both halves: the import comes from `../utils/walletEmail`, **and** `wallet.ts` declares no binding of that name — read through the comment-and-string-blanked source, so a mention in a comment cannot satisfy it.
- **Still open:** Minor-1 — the purity pin is a **deny-list** (it rejects a fixed token set: await, query, fetch, require, import, process, fs, db, assignment), so an impure helper using none of those tokens, or a `console.log`, still passes. Your recommended closing step, an allow-list matched structurally, is **not** done here.
- Nothing in `services/auth` product code changed.

**T2 and T3 are why both halves of the assertion are load-bearing**: T2 re-points the import while declaring no local function (a "no local binding" check alone would pass it), T3 keeps the import and adds a local function (an "imports it" check alone would pass it). Both are killed.

## Shared evidence for both commits

**Red-first here is a TAMPER, not a failing test on develop** — these cells pin guards that are correct today. So each half was reproduced: plant the tamper in `routes/wallet.ts`, show the **unedited** test stays green (the gap), then show the **edited** test reds. `mutate.py` asserts each target line's exact text before planting, restores the file and checks its sha256, and flags any kill whose failure text carries a `TS####` code as a false kill. Unmutated control green both rounds (25 cells unedited, 26 edited).

Both tamper lines were re-taken **byte-identical** at develop `2b205beada00a2f0fb3144e38198e471848132b6` before being trusted — `wallet.ts:34` (the import) and `wallet.ts:200` (the `SELECT * FROM auth_find_user_by_wallet($1)` template) — with a line-33 control that does not match.

| tamper | unedited | edited |
| -- | -- | -- |
| T1 import dropped + a local impure `canonicalWalletAddress` (the checker's own) | SURVIVED | KILLED |
| T2 import re-pointed at another module, no local function | SURVIVED | KILLED |
| T3 import kept **and** a local function added | SURVIVED | KILLED |
| T4 import dropped, no local function | SURVIVED | KILLED |
| K1 lookup swapped for an `INSERT`, SELECT text only in a decoy `//` comment (the checker's own) | SURVIVED | KILLED |
| K2 decoy **block** comment that itself contains a backtick | SURVIVED | KILLED |
| K3 the lookup replaced by a different statement | **KILLED** | KILLED |

**K3 is the positive control.** It is killed on the *unedited* test too, which is what makes the six SURVIVED readings a real coverage gap rather than an inert suite. Without it the round would be unfalsifiable.

**Suite, by cell name:** `auth` baseline at develop **1,095 / 1,095** (99 files, rc 0) -> patched **1,096 / 1,096** (99 files, rc 0). +1 cell, 0 vanished, **0 new reds**. The `ks963` file goes 25 -> 26 cells. The push gate's `typecheck-tests: auth` leg examined 150 files, 99 under `__tests__`, and reports 42 errors — 42 in the baseline, **0 new**.

**Order independence**, which matters because both commits touch one file: either order gives tree `54dc22e920569148070ee579fc173753432f6dd4`, and each alone gives a different tree (`dc51264410f3af98f28d02175d596829cdad1d39`, `3a3e0e7929085994e957b22058b1e944733112b1`), so the check is not vacuous.

**Preflight on push, verbatim in the PR body, ending `PREFLIGHT INCOMPLETE — 13/16 legs ran, 3 SKIPPED. Nothing failed.`** That is **not a pass**: legs 3, 4 and 8 need a running local stack and there is no Docker on this machine.

Closing step: assert `relforcerowsecurity` for all three tables, or add an other-tenant INSERT/UPDATE refused on each of `shares` and `custody_events`.
2. **F2 (Minor), the SETUP guard is an ordinary cell, not a** `beforeAll`**.** A run that excludes it (`-t ROLLBACK`, `it.only`, a single-cell watch run) executes the rollback cells as a superuser and exits 0 (gate run 11: 2 passed, 9 skipped, exit 0). Closing step: also assert the role inside the existing `beforeAll`, or document in the file header that it must be run whole.
3. **F5 (Note), env-variable shape differs from KS-597.** KS-597's suite also accepts `APP_DB_USER` / `APP_DB_PASSWORD` to compose the app DSN; this suite needs `TEST_APP_DATABASE_URL` outright. Harmless, but someone with the KS-597 env set meets the refusal and has to read its message. Closing step: accept the KS-597 pair as a fallback, or name the difference in the refusal message.
4. **N1 (Note), no CI job runs the originate integration config.** A grep of `origin/develop` for `jest.integration`, `test:integration` and `TEST_DATABASE_URL` finds nothing under `.github`, so this gate and its predecessors are a manual instrument (as before; GitHub Actions is retired for this repo). Closing step: a decision, not code: either record the manual run command in `docs/DEV-PROCESS.md` §Manual CI-gate equivalents, or accept and say so.

Also from the gate (F3, F4): the role probe names only `withTenant`'s connection (a future route opening a different pool would not be probed); the RLS control is positive-controlled and cleans up in `finally`. No action.

Refs KS-1311.

title: Wallet login: a suspended account stored under a mixed-case address can be evaded by logging in with the lower-case form (needs a case-insensitive lookup, a migration)
description:
## BLUF

Residual declared on #1476 (KS-806) and confirmed by its Opus delta gate (round 3), filed at the priority Wednesday asked for. A wallet account whose `wallet_address` was stored before #1476 in a NON-canonical casing and has since been SUSPENDED refuses its own casing (401), but the same wallet logging in with the lower-case form gets a NEW ACTIVE account (200). Suspension can be evaded through the double-account path.

## Recommendation

A separate PR with a migration: replace `auth_find_user_by_wallet` (migration 039, exact equality) with a case-insensitive lookup (or add a functional index on `lower(wallet_address)` and look up on the lower-cased argument), and canonicalise the stored column for existing rows in the same migration. Then the lookup in `routes/wallet.ts` needs no presented-casing-first loop. Until then #1476's raw-casing-first lookup keeps a legacy row reachable by its own casing, which is the part it can fix without a migration.

## Detail

* **Why it exists:** CIP-8 verification compares the claimed and signed address case-insensitively (`utils/cip8.ts`), so one wallet can present several casings, but `auth_find_user_by_wallet` is `WHERE wallet_address = p_wallet_address` (exact). #1476 stores new rows in the canonical lower-case form and looks up the presented casing first, then the canonical form; a legacy row in a casing the wallet does not present is not found by any lookup there.
* **Effect (gate probe D5 and the residual cell):** legacy row `L` (mixed case, SUSPENDED). Login with the mixed-case form: 401 (the suspension holds). Login with the lower-case form: no row found, a new row `N` is created, ACTIVE, 200.
* **Related, declared in #1476:** `/link` stores the raw casing (`routes/wallet.ts`), so one wallet can also become two accounts there; `/status/:walletAddress` is not canonicalised. The same migration fixes the lookup side of both; the write side of `/link` should canonicalise.
* **Not caused by #1476:** before it, every casing was a separate account anyway; #1476 closes the double account for rows it creates and leaves this one for legacy rows.

Provenance: Opus delta gate on #1476 round 3, verdict `/Volumes/DevMASTER/WEDNESDAY/0_Brain/reference/2026-10-12_gate-pr1476-r3/verdict.md`; filed by Seat V 3rd on Wednesday's instruction. Related: KS-806, KS-1486 (concurrent first logins), KS-1460.

## BLUF

Six Minor notes from the Sonnet-tier gate on PR #1489 (KS-1305), all in `scripts/prisma-generate.cjs` and its test. The script is developer tooling. They were left out of that PR because a change to the gated head voids the GO. Filed as ONE ticket; one small tier-2 PR later.

## Recommendation

One small PR, test first: guard the signal paths, make the staging directory safe to reuse, and make the "client exists" check mean "this run produced it". None of it matters in the normal run; all of it is the edge cases of a script that creates and deletes a directory.

## Detail (line numbers at head `80be89ee`)

1. `:68-75`**, SIGINT and SIGTERM skip the** `finally`**:** `node_modules/.generate` is left behind (rc 130 / 143), and SIGTERM also orphans the prisma child. The next run cleans it. Install signal handlers that remove the staging directory and kill the child.
2. `:66-69`**, a symlinked** `.generate`**:** the link is removed but its **target's** `schema.prisma` is overwritten. Needs write access to `node_modules` already. Refuse a `.generate` that is a symlink, or `lstat` first.
3. `:79`**, a stale client passes the check:** OK is printed when prisma exits 0 and writes nothing, if a client from an earlier run is present. Compare the client's mtime (or a hash) against the start of the run, or remove the old client first.
4. `:65`**,** `.generate` **being a file** gives an uncaught stack trace with rc 1 instead of a message.
5. `:86`**,** `path.relative` **from another cwd** prints `../../..` noise in the OK line.
6. **Test gap:** no cell for prisma **killed by a signal** (`spawnSync` returns `status: null`; the script maps it to 1, but nothing pins that). The gate's mutant that returned 0 for a signal-killed prisma survived.

Refs KS-1305.

nodes.body:
**PR #1578 is merged to `develop` as `6184eaa0af75c1e27eb69bbff67a7790ef494b5f`.** Items 2 and 4 only — **this ticket stays open** for its other items, starting with signals skipping the cleanup. Nothing deployed.

**Gate G2** (tier 2, Sonnet) returned **GO WITH NOTE**. It measured more staging shapes than the suite pins: a directory symlink, a file symlink, a **dangling** symlink and a regular file are all refused with rc 2, as are a self-loop symlink and a FIFO; an absent `.generate` and a plain directory both still generate.

**Uncovered but measured correct:** the **file-symlink** and **dangling-symlink** shapes have no cell in `ks1497_prisma_generate_refuses_a_bad_staging_dir.test.sh`. They pass today because `lstat` reports a symlink regardless of what it points at — which is exactly the property a future refactor to `stat` would silently lose. Two more cells, same fixture shape as the existing ones; a natural add to whichever PR next takes an item from this ticket.

**Evidence on the tree that landed** (predicted commit `747e2f0bcd80`, tree `8cda8b91829d44b22cdcf28b653c106be6378c87` — the same tree both gates and I predicted for #1577/#1578 landing in either order): `ks1497` **7/7**; full shell runner **91/0/0 of 91**, rc 0 in 505 s. Five-point read 5/5 TRUE.

**Still not covered, as stated when raised** (neither is a regression): the `lstat`/`mkdirSync` check-then-act window, and a symlinked `node_modules` *above* `.generate`.

**Raised as PR #1578**, head `972286126bc69fad209ef4c270aca94f4d8f4c9f`, on `develop` `8a9970511f2`. Not merged, not deployed — it goes to a gate next.

**⚠ This does NOT close the ticket.** It is **items 2 and 4 only**. The other items — signals skipping the cleanup, and the rest of the KS-1305 gate notes — are untouched and stay open here. The narrowing is stated in the PR body as well, so it cannot be lost.

**What was wrong.** `scripts/prisma-generate.cjs` copies the schema into `<svc>/node_modules/.generate`, runs `prisma generate` against it, then removes the directory — and never checked what `.generate` already was. A **symlink**: `mkdirSync(…, {recursive:true})` succeeds on the existing link, the schema is written **into the link's target**, and the cleanup removes only the link, leaving the written file behind. A **plain file**: `mkdirSync` throws an uncaught `EEXIST`, so the operator sees a stack trace instead of a message.

**What landed.** Thirteen lines: an `lstatSync` before the `mkdirSync` (tolerating `ENOENT`, re-throwing anything else), then two guards calling the script's existing `fail()`, so both cases stop with a `generate:` message and **exit 2 before anything is written**. A stale *real* directory from an interrupted run is still reused and removed, unchanged.

**Evidence, run by me:**

- **Red-first** (test section only, product untouched): **2 passed / 5 failed**. The two passes are CONTROL cells; the five failures are the symlink and file cases. One demonstrates the defect directly rather than by proxy — `nothing is written into the symlink's target` wanted `0` and **got `1`**: at the tip the schema really is written through the link.
- Control that the tip lacks the change: `symbolic link` and `is not a directory` each occur **0** times in the script at `develop`, and the suite file does not exist there.
- **Green** (product section applied): **7 passed / 0 failed**; both strings occur once; `node --check` parses.
- **Full shell-suite runner on the committed head: 91 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped (of 91)**, `SHELL_RC=0`. The count rises 90 → 91 because this adds the 91st suite, which is the cheapest proof the runner actually picked it up.
- Push preflight **13 of 16 legs ran, 3 SKIPPED (3, 4, 8 — local stack not up), nothing failed**; `PUSH_RC=0`. Not a 16/16 pass.

**The suite drives the real script**, not a test-only path: it goes through `PRISMA_GENERATE_SVC_DIR` / `PRISMA_SCHEMA_SRC`, which already exist on `develop` (3 occurrences each, checked against a control reading 0). Two of its 7 cells are CONTROLs that must pass before and after — no `.generate` at all still generates and cleans up, and a stale real `.generate` is still reused — which is what stops the guard being a blunt refusal.

**Two residuals, named rather than left to be found later.** Neither is covered, and neither is a regression (both are true of `develop` today): (1) the `lstat` and the `mkdirSync` are separate syscalls, so a `.generate` created between them is still mkdir'd — the window narrows, it does not close; (2) the guard inspects `.generate` itself, so a symlinked **`node_modules` above it** still lands the schema in the target tree.

**Provenance.** Held Spark READY; canonical patch byte-verified `eeaac686abb7b2da`, 5467 B, equal to the concatenation of its two section files (`cmp` rc 0). Each section `git apply -p1 --check` rc 0 at the live tip, strict, no options. The new suite is committed with mode `100755`.

title: A real-Postgres twin of the KS-1267 transfer-custody cells: the mocked flip ignores its arguments and cannot commit or roll back (PR 1486 gate note)
description:
## BLUF

A real-Postgres twin of the two KS-1267 cells in `ks1228-a-refused-request-writes-no-provenance-row.test.ts` (`/transfer-custody`: the owner flip throws, and the custody INSERT returns no row). Found by the Sonnet-tier gate on PR #1486; left out of that PR because a change to the gated head voids the GO. Not a regression.

## Recommendation

One small tier-2, test-only PR using the faithful local Postgres recipe (`5_Project_History/2026-10-12_seatJ-2nd/RECIPE-faithful-local-postgres.md`) and the existing KS-1263 route-level harness, which already drives the real `/transfer-custody` route over a real database (the KS-1310 describe there seeds a document, an owner and a holder and installs a trigger as a fault vehicle). Assert on real rows: after a flip that fails there is no `action_provenance` row for the document, no `custody_events` row and the owner is unchanged; after a flip that succeeds there is one provenance row, one custody row and the owner is the NEW holder.

## Detail

The unit cells use a mocked transaction client whose `$executeRaw` **ignores its arguments** and has **no commit or rollback model**. The gate found two mutants of `routes/documents.ts` that therefore stay GREEN (31/31):

1. **Recording after the flip but before the COMMIT** (inside the transaction): a failed commit would leave a provenance row for a transfer that did not happen, and nothing can see it.
2. **The flip writing the WRONG owner** (its `SET` pointed at `fromHolderId`): the mock never looks at the value.

A twin against a real database closes both, because it reads the rows back. Also: the title of cell 3, "the custody INSERT returns no row: 500, no row, and the owner is never flipped", over-states what it asserts. The mock cannot show the owner, so the cell asserts only the WRITE ORDER (the flip statement is never issued). The PR body and squash body say so; the title is left as merged.

Refs KS-1267, KS-1263, KS-1310.

title: KS-968 follow-ups: the integration suite's loopback guard can be bypassed by ?host=, an untested rethrow, and four smaller gaps
description:
## BLUF

Gate notes on #1485 (KS-968, Opus, GO WITH NOTE, no Major). The first is a safety property of a suite that TRUNCATES `users`: its guard against reaching a non-loopback database can be bypassed. The rest are small.

## Recommendation

One small PR: fix the guard (validate the parsed connection config, or reject any query string), pin the rethrow, move the two lookups inside the named try, and either type-check the integration file or add it to `tsconfig.test.json`'s include. Wiring the suite into any gate is the same open question as KS-1487.

## Detail (line numbers at `ebdb123d5`; they drift)

1. **Loopback guard bypass** (`services/auth/integration/ks968-platform-admin-seed-with-both-rows.integration.ts` lines 29-36): the guard checks `new URL(RAW).hostname`, but `pg-connection-string` lets `?host=` and `&port=` override it. The gate measured both: a URL with host `127.0.0.1:1` plus `?host=<socket>&port=56488` ran 6/6 against another target, and `?host=192.0.2.1` dialled that address. The suite truncates `users` and `pii_subject_keys`, so it must never be able to reach a non-loopback database.
2. **The rethrow is untested** (`userRepo.ts:1654`, `throw remediationErr`): a mutant where the catch no longer rethrows (m5) passes the integration (6/6) and unit (31/31) suites while logging the false "SUSPENDED" warn.
3. **Not every failed remediation gets the new error line:** the `getUserById` / `getUserByEmail` lookups at `userRepo.ts:1589-1590` sit outside the named try, so a database fault there logs only the generic "Failed to seed demo user".
4. **The integration file has 4 tsc errors** (lines 114, 147, 163) under `tsconfig.test.json`; nothing type-checks it and nothing runs it automatically (it is outside `src/`, so the KS-1000 ratchet does not see it).
5. **"Otherwise unchanged" is not exact for a legacy plaintext email row:** when the email row has no lookup hash, develop suspended BOTH rows (no collision happened); head leaves the id row ACTIVE.
6. **Pre-existing, noted:** a whitespace `ADMIN_USER_PASSWORD` is seeded as a real password; two legacy plaintext duplicates of the address suspend only one (`LIMIT 1`); the H5 rewrite (`:1706`) and `createUser` (`:1758`) also swallow 23505 but only a race reaches them.

Provenance: Opus QA gate on #1485, verdict `/Volumes/DevMASTER/WEDNESDAY/0_Brain/reference/2026-10-12_gate-pr1485/verdict.md` (sha256/16 `cb7d6fa23d5bdb5b`), Minor 1 to 5 and the pre-existing notes; filed by Seat V 3rd on Wednesday's instruction. Related: KS-968, KS-966, KS-1487, KS-1000.

title: api-gateway: no cell pins the verification limiter above the audit middleware, and the production unversioned verification 307s are counted by no limiter (a decision)
description:
## BLUF

Two notes from the Opus gate on PR #1483 (KS-1479), neither a defect in that PR:

1. **N1, a test gap.** Moving the verification limiter **below** the audit middleware (`index.ts:570`) turns **0 cells** red, and would start auditing every `429` (one audit row per throttled verification request). The position is harmless today, but nothing guards it.
2. **N2, a decision carried from KS-1469.** In production the unversioned `/api/verification*` `307`s are now counted by **no** limiter (the gate sent 305 of 305 through): the limiter sits after the redirect by design (so a followed redirect counts once), and `READ_ONLY_PATHS` exempts `/api/verification` from the global limiter. None reaches a handler, so a `307` flood costs only the redirect, but it is unbounded.

## Recommendation

* **N1:** pin the order with a behavioural cell: drive the real app with the audit middleware's `query` stubbed, send a throttled verification request, and assert that no audit row is written for the `429`. Tests first; a tamper that moves the block below the audit middleware must turn it red. Priority Low.
* **N2:** an owner decision, not a fix: is an unbounded `307` flood acceptable, or should the unversioned redirect be counted by the global limiter (drop the `/api/verification` prefix from `READ_ONLY_PATHS` for the unversioned spelling only)? Either answer should be written next to the limiter block and pinned.

## Detail

* Source: the Opus gate on PR #1483 (KS-1479), 2026-10-12, notes N1 and N2 (`WEDNESDAY/0_Brain/reference/2026-10-12_gate-pr1483/verdict.md`; its tamper "limiter moved below the audit middleware": 0 red).
* **Searched first** (Linear, includeArchived): none for the limiter's position relative to the audit middleware.

Related: KS-1479, KS-1469.

title: api-gateway: every per-IP limiter keys on the last X-Forwarded-For hop (trust proxy 1), so a caller that reaches the gateway without nginx rotates that hop and gets a fresh bucket each request
description:
## BLUF

`index.ts:108` sets `app.set('trust proxy', 1)`, so every IP-keyed control in the gateway (the global limiter at 300 per minute, the verification limiter, the login limiters, the brute-force guard) keys on the **last** `X-Forwarded-For` hop. The Opus gate on PR #1483 (KS-1479) **reproduced against the gateway directly** that rotating that last hop gets a fresh bucket each time, identically on base and on #1483, so the per-IP bound is only as strong as who can set the last hop. Pre-existing, not caused by KS-1479. **Whether it is reachable in practice depends on whether anything reaches the gateway without nginx appending the hop; that part is unmeasured.**

## What the repo's own configs say (READ, not measured)

* `docker/nginx-gateway/nginx.conf:133`, `nginx-production.conf:296` and `nginx-demo.conf:334` all set `proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-For $proxy_add_x_forwarded_for`, which **appends** nginx's `$remote_addr` to whatever the client sent. Through that nginx, the last hop is the address nginx saw (and on demo, `nginx-demo.conf:100-107` resolves it from `X-Forwarded-For` only for trusted source addresses with `real_ip_recursive on`). A client behind it can prepend hops but cannot choose the last one.
* The gate's reproduction sent the header **straight to the gateway**, with no nginx in front. So the exposure is any path that reaches the gateway without that nginx: a published gateway port, another container on the compose network (the comment at `nginx-demo.conf:89` already names this for nginx's own rate limit), or an ingress that passes the header through.
* The related finding on how the IP is derived at all is **KS-618** (archived, Backlog, P2): on demo every IP-keyed control saw the Docker bridge address because two proxy hops met `trust proxy 1`; its recommended fix (an explicit trusted-subnet list rather than a hop count) is also the fix shape here. Its nginx realip half appears to be in `nginx-demo.conf` now; whether it is deployed on demo and Kintsugi is not known to me.

## Recommendation

1. **Measure first, read-only, after the Kintsugi window:** through the real public front door, send several `GET /api/credentials/abc` (answered 401 by the gateway's own gate, after the global limiter) with different client-supplied `X-Forwarded-For` first hops and read the `RateLimit-Remaining` header each time. If it keeps decrementing across them they share one bucket (the edge fixes the hop); if it resets, the hop is client-controlled at the real ingress. This needs no credential and writes nothing but limiter counters. Also check the compose files and VM firewalls for any published gateway port.
2. **If any path reaches the gateway without nginx:** replace the hop count with an explicit trusted-proxy list (KS-618's recommendation), so `X-Forwarded-For` is honoured only from the nginx peer.
3. Add a cell that sends a forged last hop to the real app with `trust proxy` configured as intended. Priority P2 as Wednesday ruled; it may drop to P3 if step 1 shows the edge appends the hop.

## Detail

* Source: the Opus gate on PR #1483, 2026-10-12, note N3 and its XFF probe (`WEDNESDAY/0_Brain/reference/2026-10-12_gate-pr1483/verdict.md`, `evidence/`): "the key is the last hop; rotating the last hop bypasses the limit, as on develop; rotating the first hop with the last fixed does not". Edge configuration was not checked by the gate.
* **Searched first** (Linear, includeArchived, literal title and description): `X-Forwarded-For`, `trust proxy`, `last hop`, `XFF`, `x-real-ip`, `set_real_ip_from`, `spoof`: nearest is KS-618 (above); nothing covers a client-chosen last hop.

Related: KS-618, KS-1479, KS-946, KS-1469.

nodes.body: Priority changed P2 to **P3** by Seat K 4th, on Wednesday's instruction (09:05Z) and for the reason in the measurement comment above: at the real Kintsugi front door a client-supplied `X-Forwarded-For` hop does not move the bucket (ten requests, `RateLimit-Remaining` 1999 to 1990 with no increase), and no compose file publishes `api-gateway`. The exposure is a caller reaching the gateway without nginx, which I could not find; demo and the VMs' own firewalls remain unmeasured.

## Measured since filing (2026-10-12, Seat K 4th, read-only)

**1. The real front door, measured on Kintsugi at 09:03Z (the window had closed).** Ten unauthenticated `GET`s to `https://secuura02-kintsugi.southeastasia.cloudapp.azure.com/api/credentials/abc`, each answered `401` by the gateway's own gate **after** the global limiter, so `RateLimit-Remaining` shows the bucket: three with no `X-Forwarded-For`, three with a different client-supplied single hop (`203.0.113.11` to `.13`), one with two client-supplied hops, then three with no header again. **`RateLimit-Remaining` fell strictly 1999, 1998, 1997, 1996, 1995, 1994, 1993, 1992, 1991, 1990, with no increase at all.** A client-supplied hop did not move the bucket; the edge, not the client, decides the key. Evidence: `5_Project_History/2026-10-12_seatK-4th/live/xff_probe.py` and `xff_probe_rows.json`. Writes: none beyond in-memory limiter counters; no credential was used. **Demo was not probed** (off-limits until its window closes).

**2. Published ports, from the compose files in the tree.** No compose file publishes `api-gateway` (`docker-compose.yml`, `.production.yml`, `.staging.yml`, `.e2e.override.yml`, `.cache.yml`, `.ci.yml`, `.isolation.yml`). Only `nginx-gateway` publishes (`${GATEWAY_PORT:-6882}:80` in `docker-compose.yml`). Positive control: the same parser sees 8 port-publishing services in `docker-compose.yml` (postgres, redis, pgbouncer, cardano-mock and others) and nginx's mapping.

**What this changes.** The gate's reproduction is real but is **direct-to-gateway only**: through the front door that the stack actually exposes, a caller cannot choose the last hop. What remains is (a) a caller that reaches the gateway without nginx: the compose network (other containers; the services call each other directly, and the #1470 gate found no service code that reads a gateway URL), a VM firewall or a port mapping added outside the repo's compose files, which I cannot see; and (b) demo, where the edge may differ and which is unmeasured. **I would rate it P3 rather than P2** and keep the explicit trusted-proxy list as hardening, but the priority is Wednesday's call and I have not changed it.

**Still unmeasured:** the VMs' own firewall and any compose override on them; demo; whether KS-618's realip half is deployed (the monotonic count above is consistent with a per-client key, but a quiet bridge address would look the same over ten seconds, so it does not prove it).

title: ks1061 mock-completeness guard: negative twin for a wrong helper path, a two-factories-in-one-file cell, and the pre-existing blind spots (KS-1159 gate notes)
description:
## BLUF

Four Minor notes from the Sonnet-tier gate on PR #1482 (KS-1159), all in `services/originate/src/__tests__/ks1061-shared-mock-completeness.test.ts`. They were left out of that PR because a change to the gated head voids the GO. None is a regression; none blocks anything. Filed as ONE ticket so they are searchable.

## Recommendation

One small tier-2, test-only PR, test first: the two missing cells (they are the survivors of the gate's own mutations), then decide whether the pre-existing blind spots are worth widening the guard for.

## Detail

1. `VIA_HELPER` **has no negative twin for a wrong helper path or name** (`~:55`). Loosening the pattern to a bare `require(` stays green (10/10). Add a fixture that calls `require('./somewhere/else').makeSharedMock(` or a differently named helper and must be NAMED as an offender.
2. `ROOT_MOCK` **has no two-factories-in-one-file cell** (`~:54`). Dropping the `/g` flag stays green (10/10). Add a fixture with two factories in one file, one compliant and one partial: `declared` and `viaHelper` must be 2 and 1.
3. **The claim "T6b/T6c/T7 are red on develop's patterns" was false** (PR text, corrected on the PR and in the squash body): develop already has those widenings; only T8 was red there. Recorded here so the corrected statement is the one that is searched.
4. **Pre-existing blind spots, none present in the corpus today:** the guard does not see `setMock`, `unstable_mockModule`, an aliased `jest` (`const j = jest; j.mock(...)`), or a non-literal module name. Comments containing the pattern, spreads and block-body factories read as conservative false-reds, which is the safe direction.

Refs KS-1159, KS-1061, KS-1000.

title: Wallet login: two simultaneous first logins for one address issue a token for an id that is not in the database (4 of 5 rounds)
description:
## BLUF

Pre-existing on develop, found by the Opus gate on #1476 (KS-806) and filed at the priority Wednesday asked for. Two concurrent FIRST wallet logins for the same address both succeed with 200, only one row is created, and in 4 of 5 measured rounds one of the two responses carries an access token for a user id that does **not exist** in `users`. `userRepo.createUser` returns the object it was given, not the row `ON CONFLICT ... DO UPDATE` actually stored, and `getOrCreateWalletUser` trusts it.

## Recommendation

Make the wallet create path read back the stored row (or `RETURNING` it) and use THAT id, or fail and retry the lookup when the returned row's `wallet_address` does not match. Add a concurrency cell against a real Postgres (Seat J's native recipe). This is the same "fabricated object, not in the table" class KS-806 names; #1476 removes the collision between different wallets but not this race between two requests of the same wallet.

## Detail

* **Measured** (gate probe P4, real Postgres 15 built from the repo's init SQL + 49 migrations, app role `secuura_app` under RLS, the real route, real `/register`, real `userRepo`, real 039 lookup): 5 rounds of `Promise.all([login(A), login(A)])` for a fresh address A. Every round: both statuses 200, exactly 1 row. `idsInDb` per round: `[true,true]` (same id) once, then `[false,true]`, `[true,false]`, `[true,false]`, ... so in 4 of 5 rounds one returned id is not in the table. The token for that id then works until something looks the user up.
* **Where:** `services/auth/src/routes/wallet.ts` `getOrCreateWalletUser` (lookup, then `userRepo.createUser(user)` with a fresh `uuidv4()`), and `userRepo.createUser`'s upsert on `email_lookup_hash` returning its input.
* **Not caused by #1476:** the same shape exists on develop; with the old 8-character email the collision made it worse (every second wallet), with the new email it only happens for a true double submit of one address.
* Evidence: `/Volumes/DevMASTER/WEDNESDAY/0_Brain/reference/2026-10-12_gate-pr1476/logs/probe_head.out` (line 4) and `gateprobe1476.test.ts` (cell P4).

Provenance: Opus QA gate on #1476, verdict `/Volumes/DevMASTER/WEDNESDAY/0_Brain/reference/2026-10-12_gate-pr1476/verdict.md` (sha256/16 `b4615b4a35be26fb`), Minor-4; filed by Seat V 3rd on Wednesday's instruction. Related: KS-806, KS-1460 (`updateUser` callers that discard the result), KS-1052.
