title: pre-push gate: pushing a branch that is not checked out skips the preflight, because the hook diffs HEAD and not the pushed commits
description:
**BLUF.** `.githooks/pre-push` decides whether to run the preflight from `HEAD` (`git diff --name-only "@{upstream}" HEAD` at `:80`, `"$_b" HEAD` at `:184`), and the preflight then tests the working tree. The refs git hands the hook on stdin are read only for the force-push check (`:48-69`). So `git push origin some-other-branch`, with a clean `HEAD` on another branch, skips the preflight for a `Blockchain/Dev` change in the branch actually pushed. The push lands with no `[pre-push]` output. Pre-existing; identical in the tip's hook, `302d8d081` and the KS-884 fix. Found by the KS-884 ref matrix (scenario S15).

**Recommendation.** Make the hook judge what is pushed, not what is checked out. Read the stdin lines (`<local ref> <local sha> <remote ref> <remote sha>`) and:

1. Compute the changed set per pushed ref from `<local sha>` against its base, not from `HEAD`.
2. Because the preflight tests the working tree (HEAD), also FAIL CLOSED: when a pushed `<local sha>` is not `HEAD` and it changes `Blockchain/Dev`, refuse with a clear message ("check out what you push, or push with the bypass deliberately"), rather than run the wrong tree. Running the preflight in a temporary worktree of the pushed sha is the heavier alternative.
3. Handle the shapes the stdin loop already skips: branch deletes (`<local sha>` all zeros), brand-new remote branches, tags (`refs/tags/...`), and multi-ref pushes (`--all`, several refspecs).
   Add a test cell per shape (red against today's hook for the unchecked-out branch). Not built here; this is the larger of the two KS-884 follow-ups because it changes what the hook refuses.

**Detail.**

* Measured 2026-10-12 by Seat F 17th. Scenario S15: `b-other` carries a `Blockchain/Dev` change, `HEAD` is back on a clean branch at `origin/develop`, then `git push origin b-other` to a local bare remote. Result SKIP for the tip's hook, `302d8d081`'s hook and the KS-884 fix; the saved push output is only git's two `To ...` / `* [new branch]` lines, so nothing tells the pusher the gate did not run.
* Why it is more than a corner case: `git push origin <name>` from a different checkout is an ordinary shape (a seat pushes a sibling branch, or a script pushes a ref), and the result reads like a green push.
* Evidence: `5_Project_History/2026-10-12_seatF-17th/ks884_ref_matrix.sh` (S15) and `ks884_matrix_full_OLD.txt`, `ks884_matrix_full_CURRENT_302d8d0.txt`, `ks884_matrix_full_FIXED.txt`.
* Related: KS-884 (PR #1474). Not caused or changed by it.

nodes.body:
## BLUF

**This ticket's BLUF is stale, and its own Recommendation item 2 is already in the code.** The hook no longer *skips* the preflight for a branch that is not checked out — it **REFUSES the push**, with very nearly the message this ticket asked for. Measured today at develop `ce98606212e4e0dce8212d4541ffff2484f2217b` while I was trying to land #1597's author-corrected commit. Item 1 (judge the pushed sha, not `HEAD`) and item 3 (the skipped ref shapes) are a different matter and I have **not** measured them.

## Detail — what the hook does now

`.githooks/pre-push:351-359` at `ce98606212e4`:

```sh
if [ -n "$changed" ] && [ "$_tip" != "$_head_c" ]; then
    echo "[pre-push] REFUSED — this push sends ${_lr} ($(_short "$_tip")), which changes Blockchain/Dev" >&2
    echo "           (or cannot be shown not to), but HEAD is ${_hd}." >&2
    echo "           The preflight tests the CHECKED-OUT tree, so it cannot vouch for what you are pushing." >&2
    echo "           Check out what you push (git checkout <branch>) and push again," >&2
    echo "           or push with the bypass deliberately (git push --no-verify) and say so on the PR." >&2
    exit 1
fi
```

That is this ticket's item 2 almost verbatim — *"refuse with a clear message (**check out what you push, or push with the bypass deliberately**)"*.

**Observed, not inferred.** Pushing `refs/heads/feature/ks-1634-…` while the worktree sat detached at develop, 2026-10-19T04:33:28Z: refused in **6 seconds**, before any leg ran — no `PREFLIGHT` line in the log at all. The `ALLOW_FORCE=1` non-fast-forward check *passed* first (`[pre-push] ALLOW_FORCE=1 — proceeding with a non-fast-forward push, deliberately.`), and then this guard refused. **The remote ref did not move.**

So the BLUF's *"The push lands with no `[pre-push]` output"* is no longer true for the `Blockchain/Dev`-changing case this ticket is about. Whoever picks this up should **re-measure scenario S15 before writing any code**: what remains open here is item 1 (the changed set is still computed from `HEAD`, not from the pushed `<local sha>`) and item 3 (deletes, new remote branches, tags, multi-ref pushes) — not the refusal.

## One behaviour worth a decision while this ticket is open

The guard's predicate is `[ -n "$changed" ] && [ "$_tip" != "$_head_c" ]`, and `$changed` is computed **from the push's base**, not from **the ref the push replaces**. So a force-push whose tree is **byte-identical to the ref it overwrites** — nothing new reaching `Blockchain/Dev` at all — is refused on the same footing as one that rewrites the service.

That is exactly the case I hit: `8ec96bbac643` → `8f3310c6ed85`, trees **both** `b64be7e50092c55af3d6670f065c2a75601ec584`, and `git diff` between the two commits is **0 bytes** (control: the same reader on that commit against develop returns 223,355 bytes, so it is not a broken reader). The two commits differ only in their author and committer lines. Nothing the preflight could test has changed, yet neither worktree can satisfy the hook: at the branch, leg 14 reds on the pre-fix `ALLOW_FORCE` leak (KS-1638, fixed only in `ce98606212e4` and later); at develop, this guard refuses.

**Not asking for a change here** — recording the shape, because an author-only amend is a real operation and it currently has no path through the hook that is not `--no-verify`. If item 1 lands (judge the pushed sha against the ref it replaces), this case resolves by itself.

Measured by Seat R 52nd (lane Secuura/Blockchain-R), 2026-10-19. Related: KS-1638 (merged `ce98606212e4`), KS-1643, KS-1634.

**Staying open after #1545.** Item 3 of KS-998 merged to `develop` as `0662f7213cc08d962b745fa6998fc2a3f47499a5`. Taking the three recommendation sentences in order, against what is now on develop:

1. *"Compute the changed set per pushed ref from `<local sha>` against its base, not from `HEAD`."* — **on develop**, from item 2 (#1540, `405e33a1061310662b10245c5154c3d75c49f0f4`). The hook reads the ref lines git hands it and judges each pushed sha: `remote_sha..tip` when the branch exists at the remote, else the upstream, else the merge-base with the trunk.
2. *"Also FAIL CLOSED: when a pushed `<local sha>` is not `HEAD` and it changes `Blockchain/Dev`, refuse."* — **on develop**, also from #1540, and the remedy wording is now pinned by a cell (mutant X15, killed by name: *"…remedy is 'check out what you push'"*).
3. *"Handle the shapes the stdin loop already skips: deletes, brand-new remote branches, tags, multi-ref pushes; a cell per shape."* — **on develop**. The Opus gate on #1545 re-measured these against real bare remotes: deletion lands silently (R31), a tag is judged by its commit (R4/R4c/R4d), a detached-HEAD push runs the preflight with a banner (R32), a three-ref push with one RED ref is refused (R30), and an unborn HEAD is refused with the corrected wording (R35).

**Why it does not close yet.** #1545 also added the "already on the remote" skip (`.githooks/pre-push:120`), which runs *before* the per-ref base diff. That is Minor 2 of the Opus gate on #1545, and it partially re-opens sentence 1's guarantee for shapes this ticket exists to cover — the hook does not judge every pushed ref while that skip can pre-empt it. Measured by the gate on this exact code, which is now develop:

- **R20 / R21** — fast-forwarding an existing branch onto an already-pushed RED commit: `rc 0`, the branch moves, **no gate and no preflight**. Develop before #1545 refused both, judging `remote_sha..tip`.
- **R22 / R22b / R23** — a **stale** tracking ref (the remote branch was deleted after a squash merge, or force-moved): a RED commit the remote **no longer has** lands with `rc 0` under a note saying it is already on the remote. The `fetch --prune` controls are refused, so the skip is the cause. 4 of 789 tracking refs in the project clone are already stale.

Both shapes need the RED commit to have reached the remote once (`--no-verify`, a clone without `core.hooksPath`, or a web edit), which is why the gate rated it Minor rather than Major.

**The cure is tracked on KS-1605** (item 2 there): apply the `onremote` skip only to refs the remote does not have yet (`_jr_rsha` empty or zero), *after* step 1, so existing-branch updates keep their `remote_sha..tip` judgement — plus the correction of the comment at `.githooks/pre-push:116-119`, which currently claims a stale ref can "never" lead to a pass. Cells R20 and R22.

So: sentences 1-3 are delivered, and this ticket should close when KS-1605 item 2 is on develop, not now. Nothing here deploys — developer tooling only.

BLUF: KS-1483 is folded into KS-998 item 2, pull request 1540 (head c6d103ffc4692cb075287eb8143715989abeafab). The hook now reads the ref lines git hands it and judges each pushed sha, instead of deciding from HEAD; a pushed sha that is not HEAD and changes Blockchain/Dev is refused with a message saying to check out what is pushed; a deleted ref is skipped, a tag is judged by its commit.

The pull request is not linked to this ticket automatically because the branch name carries only the KS-998 id. Ticket state unchanged; the pull request is awaiting the gate.

## Cross-reference from KS-998 item 2: the formatting gate's half of this defect will be fixed there; the PREFLIGHT half stays here

Facts only, from the KS-998 items 1+2 planning pass (Seat K 8th, 2026-10-13). This ticket already states
the defect precisely — `.githooks/pre-push:80` diffs `HEAD` and the pushed ref lines (`:48-69`) are read
only for the force-push check. I was about to file a duplicate P3 for the same thing and the board
search stopped me; recording the relationship instead.

- **KS-998 item 2** (ruled variant A′, Opus tier) makes the hook **keep `local_sha` per pushed ref** and
  archive that sha for the systemTest formatting gate. That fixes the **formatting gate's** half of
  "judges HEAD, not what is sent". It does **not** touch the preflight's changed set (`:80`, `:184`),
  which is this ticket's.
- Measured while planning: `all_changed` (`:80`) feeds **both** the Blockchain/Dev filter that decides the
  preflight **and** the systemTest filter that decides the formatting gate, so once item 2 lands the two
  would be computed from different bases (pushed shas vs `HEAD`) unless this ticket lands with or after
  it. Worth sequencing deliberately rather than discovering the divergence later.
- Related and not the same: KS-1482 (rename-out shows only the new path) and KS-1422 (a stale
  `origin/develop` makes the formatting gate select a package the author never touched).

title: api-gateway: dot-segment and extra-segment spellings (/abc/., /./abc, /abc/%2e ...) are forwarded verbatim without the spec method and auth gate; whether any reaches an upstream handler is unmeasured
description:
## BLUF

A request whose path differs from a spec path by a **dot segment or a percent-encoded dot/space/slash segment** is not matched by the gateway's spec method and auth gate, so the gate has no opinion and the request is **forwarded to the upstream verbatim**. The Opus gate on PR #1472 (KS-1469) measured this on base and on the merged tree; **I reproduced it independently on the merged develop tip** `d38302a9a27e` (the real app over real HTTP, a recording stub for every upstream, `NODE_ENV=test`). Unchanged by KS-1469.

| unauthenticated `GET` | gateway | upstream saw |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `/api/credentials/abc` (canonical) | **401** | nothing |
| `/api/credentials/abc/` (KS-1469 fixed this one) | **401** | nothing |
| `/api/credentials/abc/.` | **200** | `/api/credentials/abc/.` |
| `/api/credentials/abc/./` | **200** | `/api/credentials/abc/./` |
| `/api/credentials/./abc` | **200** | `/api/credentials/./abc` |
| `/api/credentials/abc/..` | **200** | `/api/credentials/abc/..` |
| `/api/credentials/abc/%2e`, `/%20`, `/%2F` | **200** | the same raw path |
| `/api/./credentials/abc`, `/api/zzz-not-in-spec/.` (controls) | **404** | nothing |

**What this does and does not show.** It shows the gateway's gate is skipped and the raw path is forwarded (the stub answers 200). It does **not** show an exposure: whether a real upstream router (Express in vc-issuer, originate, ...) ever routes `/abc/.` or `/./abc` to a handler is **not measured**. By reading, Express does not collapse dot segments, so most of these should 404 at the upstream; the per-route `authenticateToken` and the upstream's own auth are the layers behind the gate. So this is a skipped defence-in-depth layer with an unmeasured tail, not a demonstrated bypass.

## Recommendation

Two steps, the first before the second:

1. **Measure** (read-only, in process): for each service router behind a `bearerAuth` spec op, send these spellings to the real router and record whether any reaches the handler. If none does, close this as defence-in-depth.
2. **If any does, or to close the class:** do not widen the spec regexes. Add a front-door normaliser in the family of KS-858's `normaliseRepeatedSlashes` that answers `400` (or rewrites) any path containing a dot segment, raw or percent-encoded, so the gate and the router can never see different paths. Tests first, a cell per spelling above, the canonical and the not-in-spec controls kept. Priority P3.

## Detail

* Source: the Opus gate on PR #1472, "Not changed, and not checked" (`WEDNESDAY/0_Brain/reference/2026-10-12_gate-pr1472/verdict.md`; rows 12 to 22 of `evidence/probe_head.out`), plus my independent run above.
* **Searched first** (Linear, includeArchived, literal title and description): `dot-segment`, `dot segment`, `normaliseRepeatedSlashes`, `path spelling`, `%2e`: nearest are KS-858 (the repeated-slash class, fixed) and KS-983 (no systemTest suite drives a path-spelling variant), neither covers dot segments.

Related: KS-1469, KS-1461, KS-858, KS-983.

**A measured data point (2026-10-30), facts only.**

- **What:** the Schemathesis integration cell `test_status_compliance::TestStatusCodeServerErrors::test_no_crash_on_invalid_input` sent `GET /api/documents/..%2F..%2Fetc` and got **200**. The cell expects a 4xx: `AssertionError: KS-1042: GET /documents/<'..%2F..%2Fetc'> returned 200, expected a 4xx`.
- **Where:** platform-k slot 1, Peter's Mac, run `pre-merge-2026-10-30T10-03-47Z-slot1`. The platform is `develop` `4c14143b3` unchanged; the branch, KS-1609, changes only `systemTest/` and docs.
- **Not established:** which handler answered, or what the body held. The cell asserts the status code only.
- So this shows that an encoded dot-segment spelling under `/api/documents/` is answered 200. It does not show that the request reached a different upstream route than intended.

**BLUF:** A dot-segment spelling on develop gets a **200**. `GET /api/documents/..%2F..%2Fetc` answered 200 where the test expects a 4xx, in every run, 4 of 4, including on clean develop. This ticket says whether any such spelling reaches an upstream handler is unmeasured; this shows one gets a success response. Which handler produced the 200, and what it returned, has **not** been measured.

**Where and when**
- **Develop control:** clean develop worktree at **`5f689991861b3b9be295797a437ef18b6f55a492`**, built **2026-10-26 12:20:09 UTC**, platform-k slot 2 on Peter's Mac. Pre-merge sweep 12:23-12:40, seed 2391897950.
- **The other three runs:** platform-k slot 1, build `65ced3173`, which is develop `5f6899918` plus a systemTest-only commit from KS-1641 (no product code differs). Built 2026-10-26 11:17:45 UTC. They were the pre-merge sweep at 11:38-11:56 and the two targeted re-checks at 12:18 and 12:20.
- Every container was healthy with RestartCount 0, and image revision labels matched each build.

**Test:** `systemTest/schemathesis/tests/test_status_compliance.py::TestStatusCodeServerErrors::test_no_crash_on_invalid_input`, failing with:

> `AssertionError: KS-1042: GET /documents/<'..%2F..%2Fetc'> returned 200, expected a 4xx | assert 400 <= 200`

The request is authenticated (ISSUER_ADMIN), sent to `/api/documents/..%2F..%2Fetc`.

**Not measured:**
- whether the gateway or an upstream normalised the path, and which route answered (for example the document list);
- the response body.

Both are needed to tell whether this is harmless routing or a path reaching a handler it shouldn't.

*Added on Peter's instruction, 2026-10-26.*

**BLUF:** the dot-segment and `%2F` spellings this ticket measured at the api-gateway also act one layer earlier, at the nginx gateway. There, two encoded-slash dot segments take a request out of `/api/` altogether. `GET /api/documents/..%2F..%2Fetc` answers **200 with the issuer portal's HTML** instead of a gateway 4xx. A KS-1042 live test found it on 2026-10-21 (slot 1, develop `280fdbcd1`).

| Authenticated `GET` (ISSUER_ADMIN) | Answer |
| -- | -- |
| `/api/documents/..%2Fetc` (one level) | **400** `VALIDATION_ERROR` "Invalid document id in path…". The request stays in `/api/` and the gateway refuses it. |
| `/api/documents/..%2F..%2Fetc` | **200** `text/html`, the SPA's `index.html` |
| `/api/documents/..%2F..%2Fnope-ks1042` | **200** `text/html`, the same page |

**Inference, not verified in nginx's logs:** nginx decodes `%2F` and resolves the dot segments before matching a `location`. So `/api/documents/../../etc` normalises to `/etc`, misses `location /api/` (`docker/nginx-gateway/nginx.conf:184`) and falls through to the SPA location.

**What this does not show:** any exposure. What came back is the public SPA shell. Not measured: whether a crafted spelling can reach a different `/api/` upstream than its prefix suggests (for example `/api/<a>/..%2F<b>/…`). That is the useful next probe, alongside this ticket's step 1.

**Acceptance criteria (in addition to this ticket's own)**
1. **Automated test:** `systemTest/schemathesis/tests/test_status_compliance.py::TestStatusCodeServerErrors::test_no_crash_on_invalid_input` (KS-1042) drives `..%2F..%2Fetc`. It is **red today** on the 200 and goes green when the edge refuses the request with a 4xx. The front-door normaliser this ticket proposes, answering 400, would do it.
2. **Docs updated:** none expected. If the nginx config changes, update its own comments.
3. **systemTests updated:** nothing beyond the KS-1042 test above.

## Step 1 of the recommendation, measured on the real stack (2026-10-12 09:05Z, Seat K 4th, read-only)

**Result: no dot-segment or extra-segment spelling returned anything but a refusal to an unauthenticated caller on Kintsugi.** 27 unauthenticated `GET`s through the public front door (`https://secuura02-kintsugi.southeastasia.cloudapp.azure.com`), no credential, three bearerAuth mounts, nine spellings each (canonical, `/`, `/.`, `/./`, `/..`, `/%2e`, `/%20`, `/%2F`, and a `./` before the last segment): `/api/credentials/abc`, `/api/referrals/abc`, `/api/governance/proposals`. **All 27 answered `401 UNAUTHORIZED`**: no 2xx, no 3xx.

* **The instrument could have shown a bypass:** controls in the same run: `/health` answered `200`, and `/api/zzz-not-in-spec` and `/api/zzz-not-in-spec/.` answered `404 NOT_FOUND`.
* **What the 401s tell us.** Kintsugi does not yet run KS-1469, so the gateway's spec gate still skips the trailing-slash spelling; that spelling (`/api/credentials/abc/`) was also `401`. So the refusal comes from the layer behind the gate (the per-route `authenticateToken` and the upstream's own auth), which is the layer this ticket asked about: it held for every spelling tried. I cannot tell from the status alone which of the two answered.
* **Limits, stated:** three `GET` mounts only. Not tried: the other optional-auth mounts (`nft`, `billing`, `certifications`), any method other than `GET`, or any authenticated caller (an authenticated caller with a valid token is not a bypass of anything). Demo is unmeasured (off-limits). The stub-based reproduction in this ticket showed the gateway forwards these spellings verbatim; this shows that, on this stack, forwarding them does not yield an unauthenticated 2xx.
* Evidence: `5_Project_History/2026-10-12_seatK-4th/live/dotseg_probe.py` and `dotseg_probe_rows.json`.

**Re-rating.** I filed this at P3 as "a skipped layer with an unmeasured tail". With the tail measured on three mounts I am lowering it to **P4**: defence in depth, not a demonstrated bypass. The front-door normaliser recommended above is still the clean way to close the class, and the measurement should be repeated for the remaining mounts and methods before this is closed rather than kept open indefinitely. Seat K 4th changed the priority on its own ticket; Wednesday can restore it.

Another measured fact for this ticket, from the Opus gate on PR #1483 (KS-1479), note N4: `/api/v1/v2/verification/../verification/verify` is forwarded upstream with the **literal `..`** in the path. It is the same class as the spellings above, and it is now **counted** by the verification limiter (the gate's 25 bounded spellings include `/./` and `/../` inside the tail). Whether the spec gate or nginx normalises it before the gateway is unchecked by the gate; the question this ticket already asks (does any real upstream router route a dot-segment path to a handler?) covers it. The recommended front-door normaliser would close it too.

title: updateDocument atomicity follow-ups: two blob writers still decide from a prior read, plus a type guard and test nits (KS-1124 gate)
description:
## BLUF

PR #1471 (KS-1124 option A) made every blob write that goes through `updateDocument` atomic. Its Opus gate (GO WITH NOTE, head `4a822bd8c244`, no Major) and Wednesday's GO list what it does not cover. Filed as ONE ticket so none is rediscovered. **None is a regression and none blocks #1471.**

## Recommendation

Fix the first two together in one tier-1 PR (they are the same defect class #1471 closed, in the two places it did not reach), test first with a forced interleaving on a real Postgres as K1-K10 do (recipe: `5_Project_History/2026-10-12_seatJ-2nd/RECIPE-faithful-local-postgres.md`). Take the guard and the nits with it or as a small tier-2 PR after.

## Detail

1. `anchorStateSync.ts:178-212`**,** `markDocumentAnchorFailed` decides from a read taken before the `UPDATE`: the `confirmed` guard (`:180`) and the `txHash` / `blockHeight` / `network` / `anchoredAt` carry (`:190-196`). A confirm write landing between the read and the write can be downgraded to `anchor_failed` with its `txHash` erased. Same family as KS-1004. (Line numbers at the PR head.)
2. `routes/certifications.ts:563` replaces `certification_metadata` wholesale, outside `updateDocument`. It drops `threadToken` from the authoritative blob, and the KS-550 heal then copies that loss into `metadata`.
3. **Hardening,** `documentRepo.ts:632/640/661/669`**.** The replace branch has no `jsonb_typeof(supplied) = 'object'` guard. A future `blockchain: null` would store `[{…}, null]` (`'{}'::jsonb || 'null'::jsonb` gives `[{}, null]`), where the old code stored `null`. No current caller can reach it (`verification.ts:393` guards `!healed`).
4. **Test nits in** `ks1124-blockchain-blob-writes-are-atomic.integration.test.ts`**.** (a) K9 (`:218-224`) seeds `anchored`, which `mapDbStatus` round-trips, so it cannot detect a status write-back; seeding `deleted` or `certified` would pin the "status not supplied keeps the stored status" semantics (only K1 reds on that mutant today). (b) `waiting()` (`:93`) counts lock waits cluster-wide, with no `datname` or `pid` filter; on a shared server a parallel job could satisfy it and make a forced interleaving vacuous. (c) `documentRepo.ts:697-702`: the returned record carries `threadToken` and the status from the first read; presentation only.
5. **Pre-existing, outside KS-1124's scope, and the largest.** Every `updateDocument` rewrites `certification_metadata` to `{ signatures, blockchain }`, which erases `issuerName`, `certificationId` and `certifiedAt` written by `certifications.ts:563` and the admin backfill. `signatures` and `data` also remain read-then-write: a concurrent sign and anchor write can drop a signature. Consider splitting this into its own ticket when it is picked up.
6. **Left in place on purpose:** the pollers' `carriedForward` (`anchorStateSync.ts:111-113`) is now redundant with the SQL carry; it was kept to keep #1471 off `anchorStateSync`. It can go with item 1.

Refs KS-1124, KS-1074, KS-1004, KS-550.

title: No gate executes the DB-backed integration suites: the default test run ignores them and CI is retired
description:
## BLUF

**No gate executes the DB-backed integration suites.** Five `*.integration.test.ts` files exist at develop `65d7722f83a6` (originate: `ks597-issuer-organization-id`, `ks597-b-caller-org-externalref`, `ks1263-multi-write-rolls-back`, `rightsHolders.tenant-scope`; auth: `auth.integration.test.ts`). Each is red-proved, and none runs unless someone types `npm run test:integration` against a Postgres. The cells that pin RLS attribution and multi-write atomicity therefore protect nothing automatically.

## Recommendation

Add one opt-in-but-loud step to the author's final check: run each service's `test:integration` against a throwaway Postgres built the repo's documented way, and list it in `docs/DEV-PROCESS.md` under the manual CI-gate equivalents. It must print a visible SKIP line with the reason when no database is reachable, never a silent pass. A faithful local recipe that needs no Docker is in `5_Project_History/2026-10-12_seatJ-2nd/RECIPE-faithful-local-postgres.md` (init SQL, then all main-DB migrations, then the `secuura_app` role).

## Detail

* **Why none runs:** `services/originate/jest.config.js:8` ignores `\.integration\.test\.ts$` by pattern ("the default run stays unit-only + mock-DB"); the pre-push preflight runs each workspace's `test` script, which is that default run; GitHub Actions is retired for this repo; `docs/DEV-PROCESS.md` §Manual CI-gate equivalents does not list the integration config. `grep` for `test:integration` finds it only in `services/originate/package.json`, the jest configs and `docs/TESTING.md`.
* **Found while:** verifying KS-980 and KS-1306 (the RLS integration suite), where the merge comment already said the config "still runs only on demand".
* **Not in scope:** KS-1307 (a PR body that quoted a subset as a full run) is about reporting, not about whether the suites run at all.
* PR #1471 (KS-1124) adds a sixth suite of this kind, so the gap grows by one if it merges as is.

Refs KS-980, KS-1306.

nodes.body:
## Measured 2026-10-13: the originate integration files are NOT safe to run in parallel, which any gate for this ticket must handle first

**BLUF:** `npm run test:integration` runs the files in parallel (jest's default; `jest.integration.config.js` sets no `maxWorkers`), and several files create and drop triggers on the SHARED tables `documents`, `organizations` and `svc_api_keys`. Running them concurrently produces failures that are not product defects. `--runInBand` is green. A gate that runs them has to run them in band (or the files have to stop doing DDL on shared tables).

**Evidence (my own runs, a throwaway Postgres as `secuura_app`, 8 integration files, 88 cells):**
- In a parallel run the #1497 bounds file's table-wide slow triggers (a BEFORE UPDATE statement trigger that sleeps) slowed every other file's writes: the KS-1508 file (`ks1508-a-planted-versionedbyid-is-not-stored`) failed 5 cells on its create (a 500) in single-tenant mode. The round-4 gate's N-7 ("14 failures, all Exceeded timeout of 30000 ms", read as an environment blip) was most likely the same effect.
- I scoped those triggers to the file's own tenant (AFTER statement triggers with a transition table, #1497 round 5). That removed 4 of the 5; ONE failure remained in a later parallel single-tenant run (a 500 on a create while another file ran its trigger DDL), and the pool-mode parallel run was 88/88 once and 30 failed once (that second run started right after a run polluted by the gate's scratch files, so I do not count it).
- `--runInBand`: 88/88 in single-tenant AND pool mode.
- Other files with the same shape (created/dropped triggers on shared tables, from the grep of what each file installs): `ks695-ask3-erase-connector.integration.test.ts` (`ks695_fail_revoke` on `svc_api_keys`), the bounds file's `ks695sb_skip_revoke*`. I did not audit the rest.

**Recommendation:** if these suites are ever gated, run them with `--runInBand` (cheap, no code change), and say so in `jest.integration.config.js`; the longer-term fix is no DDL on shared tables from a test (a per-test tenant plus a row-level or tenant-keyed trigger, or a dedicated database per file).

Context: found while finishing #1497 round 5. Not a product defect; nothing was skipped.

title: The developer portal page documents POST /api/verification/verify-batch, which no service and no spec implements (CSRF carries exclusions for it)
description:
## BLUF

`services/api-gateway/src/docs/developer-portal.html:294` lists `POST /api/verification/verify-batch` ("Verify mul\[tiple documents\]") as a public endpoint. **Nothing serves it.** The OpenAPI spec (310 paths) declares `verify` and `verify-file` for the unversioned and v2 families but no `verify-batch`; no router in `services/originate` or any other service registers `/verify-batch` under verification (the only `verify-batch` code is the separate MCP server's own root-level `/verify-batch` in `services/mcp-server`). So a developer who follows the portal gets a 404, and `csrf.ts` carries CSRF exclusions for `/api/verification/verify-batch` and `/api/v2/verification/verify-batch` that cover a route nothing implements.

## Recommendation

Owner decision, then one of: (a) implement the route and add it to the spec, so the page and the exclusions are true; (b) remove the row from the portal, and drop both CSRF entries in the same change (a dead exclusion is a latent hole: a future route at that name would be silently CSRF-exempt). Priority Low. Until then the two CSRF entries are PINNED by cells (KS-1469) so they cannot vanish or change unnoticed; that pin is deliberately not a statement that the route exists.

## Detail

* Found while resolving the m1 note from the Opus gate on PR #1466 (the `/api/v2/verification/verify-batch` exclusion was pinned by no cell). Evidence, from a repo-wide search at develop `b4a245fba1ca`: spec path scan (310 paths, none `verify-batch`); `git grep` for verify-batch in non-test code finds only the portal row, the two `csrf.ts` entries, and the MCP server; a control with the same grep shape finds the real `/verify` and `/verify-file` routes.
* Other rows on that page were NOT checked against the code.
* **Searched first** (Linear, includeArchived, literal title and description): `developer-portal`, `developer portal`, `verify-batch`: no ticket about this page's rows.

Related: KS-1469, KS-1461, KS-1165.

title: ks963 wallet ordering guard: three blind spots in the source scan (template interpolation, tagged/bracket/optional calls, raw-body SELECT pin)
description:
## BLUF

Gate notes on #1469 (KS-1131 items 3 and 4, head `8f2145e1f`, GO WITH NOTE, no Major). The new `assertWalletNothingWrittenBeforeLookup` is a **source-scan guard, not a behavioural test**, and it has three blind spots. All Minor; none blocks the merge. Item 1 is the only one that is a coverage regression against the old cell.

## Recommendation

Fix 1 and 3 in one small test-only PR (recurse into `${}`; read the blanked body for the SELECT pin). Leave 2 unless a real write ever lands in one of those shapes; a behavioural test of `getOrCreateWalletUser` against a stubbed pool would retire the whole class and is the better long-term answer.

## Detail (line numbers at head `8f2145e1f`; they drift)

1. **Template interpolation** (`ks963-preauth-rethrow.test.ts` lines 251-263, `blankCommentsAndStrings`): the quote branch blanks a whole template literal, `${...}` included. Planting `` const _s = `${await query("INSERT ...")}`; `` before the lookup: the OLD cell was RED (its `await` regex saw it), the NEW cell is green. A small coverage regression for an exotic shape. Fix: recurse into `${}` and keep its contents unblanked.
2. **Call shapes the regex cannot see** (line 290, `(?<![\w$.])` plus a dotted-name pattern): a tagged template (`` await query`INSERT ...` ``), a bracket call (`(userRepo as any)["createUser"]({})`) and an optional invoke (`(query as any)?.(...)`) all stay green. Measured green on OLD too except the interpolation case. Very low risk; the bracket and optional shapes are caught only when the literal `createUser(` appears.
3. **The SELECT pin reads the raw body** (line 296, `expect(body.slice(0, lookup)).toContain('SELECT * FROM auth_find_user_by_wallet')`): a `// SELECT * FROM auth_find_user_by_wallet` comment satisfies it, so swapping the real query text for an INSERT while leaving that comment stays 22/22 green. The OLD cell had the same gap; this PR did not introduce it.

Not a defect, recorded so nobody "fixes" it: any harmless call before the lookup (`walletAddress.toLowerCase()`, `logger.debug(...)`) reds the cell, as does renaming `getOrCreateWalletUser` or turning it into an arrow function. That is the allow-set contract the test's own docblock states (fails closed).

Provenance: Sonnet-tier QA gate on #1469, verdict `/Volumes/DevMASTER/WEDNESDAY/0_Brain/reference/2026-10-12_gate-pr1469/verdict.md` (read 2026-10-12); filed by Seat V 3rd on Wednesday's instruction. Related: KS-1131, KS-963, KS-1155 (the load-timeout class that shares this file's neighbourhood).

nodes.body:
**MERGED: #1643 squash `513371a34be58af9e740b82ea26795155c7bd0b4`. Item 3 is pinned. This ticket stays open: items 1 and 2 are untouched, and the gate found residue inside item 1's shape.**

BLUF: merged on Wednesday's head-pinned GO after gate BD1 (tier 2, round 1 of 2): **GO WITH NOTE, 0 blockers, 3 notes.** Landed tree `54dc22e920569148070ee579fc173753432f6dd4`, one parent `2b205beada00a2f0fb3144e38198e471848132b6`. One file, +10/-1. `Refs KS-1468`; attachment `linkKind=contributes`, `status=merged`; this issue stayed In Progress at the merge.

## What landed for this ticket

The second commit, `de44e3d3ccfcefd58abe5295a1f8a2571e765bc4`: the SELECT pin now walks every raw match of `SELECT * FROM auth_find_user_by_wallet` and requires at least one to sit immediately after a backtick in the comment-and-string-blanked body, so only a real template literal counts. **It adds no cell** — it strengthens the existing assertion, which is why the suite's +1 belongs to KS-1500.

## Still open

- **Item 1** (template interpolation blanked wholesale) and **item 2** (tagged-template, bracket and optional-invoke shapes) are not addressed.
- **Gate BD1 N1, residue inside item 1's shape:** a decoy *template literal* — `void \`SELECT * FROM auth_find_user_by_wallet\`;` — satisfies the new pin while the real query is an `INSERT`. It compiles and survives both test versions. That is item 1's blind spot rather than a regression introduced here, but it means the new pin is not sufficient on its own.
- **N3, residue:** the pin requires a backtick immediately before the query text, so refactoring the lookup to a quoted string would red the cell. Reasoned by the gate, not run.

## The mutant matrix was corrected before the merge, on gate BD1 note N2

**Three of the four `T` mutants I first reported as kills do not compile, so those readings are withdrawn.** Measured with `tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json` in `services/auth`, each planted into `routes/wallet.ts` and restored byte-identically, against a clean baseline of rc 0 / 0 errors:

| mutant | compiles? | status |
| -- | -- | -- |
| T1 import dropped + a local impure fn declared | **yes** | SURVIVED unedited, **KILLED** edited |
| T3d a local binding declared in **another** function, import kept and still used at `:188` | **yes** | SURVIVED unedited, **KILLED** edited |
| T2 import re-pointed at `../utils/cip8` | **no — `TS2305`** | withdrawn, not a valid mutant |
| T3 import kept + a **top-level** fn of that name | **no — `TS2440`** | withdrawn, not a valid mutant |
| T4 import dropped, no local fn | **no — `TS2304`** | withdrawn, not a valid mutant |
| K1 `INSERT` template + decoy `//` comment | **yes** | SURVIVED unedited, **KILLED** edited |
| K2 decoy **block** comment containing a backtick | **yes** | SURVIVED unedited, **KILLED** edited |
| K3 lookup replaced by a different statement | **yes** | **KILLED by both** (the positive control) |

A mutant that cannot compile is a change that could never ship, so a cell "catching" it proves nothing. `T3d` is seat-written to replace `T3` compile-safely: it declares a local binding of the name in a different function, keeping the top-level import in place and still used, which avoids both the `TS2440` conflict and the `TS6133` unused-import that a same-scope shadow causes.

**Two things stated rather than implied.** First, **the import-source half's independence is UNMEASURED**: `src/utils/walletEmail.ts` is the only module in the service exporting `canonicalWalletAddress`, so no compile-safe tamper can re-point the import without adding a module. `T3d` establishes the no-local-binding half; `T1` breaks both at once. Second, **my own false-kill detector was blind here**, and that is worth knowing: it flags a kill whose failure text carries a `TS####` code, but this cell reads `wallet.ts` as *text* rather than importing it, so a non-compiling mutant yields an ordinary assertion failure and no TypeScript diagnostic ever appears. For a source-scan test the mutant must be type-checked separately — the detector cannot see it.

**One disagreement with the gate, with my measurement.** BD1's N2 lists `T2` among its compile-safe proofs. My reading is that `T2` cannot compile: `src/utils/cip8.ts` exports neither `canonicalWalletAddress` nor `syntheticWalletEmail` (0 matching export lines, against 2 in `walletEmail.ts`), and planting it gives `TS2305` on both names. I have therefore marked it withdrawn, which claims less rather than more.

**PR #1643 is up: item 3 is pinned — the SELECT pin is now read through the blanked body, so a decoy comment cannot satisfy it. Test-only, zero product bytes. Items 1 and 2 stay open.**

BLUF: https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/1643, head `de44e3d3ccfcefd58abe5295a1f8a2571e765bc4`, **two commits** on develop `2b205beada00a2f0fb3144e38198e471848132b6`; this ticket's is the second, `de44e3d3ccfcefd58abe5295a1f8a2571e765bc4`. Raised byte-for-byte from the held Spark pass `KS-1468-SELECTPINBLANKED-1`. One file, +10/-1 across both commits. `Refs`, not a close keyword. Gate pending, not merged.

## Scope — item 3 only

- **Closed by this:** item 3. `assertWalletNothingWrittenBeforeLookup` pinned the lookup with `expect(body.slice(0, lookup)).toContain('SELECT * FROM auth_find_user_by_wallet')` against the **raw** body, so a comment repeating that text satisfied it and the real query could be swapped for an `INSERT`. The pin now walks every raw match of the statement and requires at least one to sit immediately after a backtick in the comment-and-string-blanked body, so only a real template literal counts.
- **Still open:** item 1 (`blankCommentsAndStrings` blanks a whole template literal including `${...}`, so `\`${await query("INSERT …")}\`` before the lookup is invisible — the one actual coverage regression against the old cell) and item 2 (tagged-template, bracket and optional-invoke call shapes). Neither is addressed here.
- **This commit adds no new cell** — it strengthens the existing assertion, which is why the Spark's own run reported 25 cells before and after. The suite's +1 comes from the KS-1500 commit.

**K2 is the sharp tamper for this one:** a decoy **block** comment that itself contains a backtick before the statement text. A naive "is there a backtick before the match" check would be satisfied by it; the cell is not. **K1** is the checker's own tamper (an `INSERT` template with the SELECT text kept only in a `//` comment).

## Shared evidence for both commits

**Red-first here is a TAMPER, not a failing test on develop** — these cells pin guards that are correct today. So each half was reproduced: plant the tamper in `routes/wallet.ts`, show the **unedited** test stays green (the gap), then show the **edited** test reds. `mutate.py` asserts each target line's exact text before planting, restores the file and checks its sha256, and flags any kill whose failure text carries a `TS####` code as a false kill. Unmutated control green both rounds (25 cells unedited, 26 edited).

Both tamper lines were re-taken **byte-identical** at develop `2b205beada00a2f0fb3144e38198e471848132b6` before being trusted — `wallet.ts:34` (the import) and `wallet.ts:200` (the `SELECT * FROM auth_find_user_by_wallet($1)` template) — with a line-33 control that does not match.

| tamper | unedited | edited |
| -- | -- | -- |
| T1 import dropped + a local impure `canonicalWalletAddress` (the checker's own) | SURVIVED | KILLED |
| T2 import re-pointed at another module, no local function | SURVIVED | KILLED |
| T3 import kept **and** a local function added | SURVIVED | KILLED |
| T4 import dropped, no local function | SURVIVED | KILLED |
| K1 lookup swapped for an `INSERT`, SELECT text only in a decoy `//` comment (the checker's own) | SURVIVED | KILLED |
| K2 decoy **block** comment that itself contains a backtick | SURVIVED | KILLED |
| K3 the lookup replaced by a different statement | **KILLED** | KILLED |

**K3 is the positive control.** It is killed on the *unedited* test too, which is what makes the six SURVIVED readings a real coverage gap rather than an inert suite. Without it the round would be unfalsifiable.

**Suite, by cell name:** `auth` baseline at develop **1,095 / 1,095** (99 files, rc 0) -> patched **1,096 / 1,096** (99 files, rc 0). +1 cell, 0 vanished, **0 new reds**. The `ks963` file goes 25 -> 26 cells. The push gate's `typecheck-tests: auth` leg examined 150 files, 99 under `__tests__`, and reports 42 errors — 42 in the baseline, **0 new**.

**Order independence**, which matters because both commits touch one file: either order gives tree `54dc22e920569148070ee579fc173753432f6dd4`, and each alone gives a different tree (`dc51264410f3af98f28d02175d596829cdad1d39`, `3a3e0e7929085994e957b22058b1e944733112b1`), so the check is not vacuous.

**Preflight on push, verbatim in the PR body, ending `PREFLIGHT INCOMPLETE — 13/16 legs ran, 3 SKIPPED. Nothing failed.`** That is **not a pass**: legs 3, 4 and 8 need a running local stack and there is no Docker on this machine.

title: api-gateway: an untyped create never meets the catalogue's DOCUMENT rules (enforcement.ts:101), plus two KS-1203 follow-ups (PR #1465 gate notes)
description:
## BLUF

Three notes from the Opus QA gate on PR #1465 (KS-1203 option A, merged as `a2f575a642638d64493997d0f68747a1d1f03dc6`), left out of that PR on purpose because a change to the gated head would have voided the GO. **Note 1 matters most:** an untyped `POST /api/documents` never meets the type catalogue's `DOCUMENT` rules, so the type's own requirements are skipped for exactly the body KS-1203 is about. It is pre-existing and outside the ruled scope. The gate graded it Minor; I filed it at Medium because it is an authorization-shaped gap.

## Recommendation

One small tier-1 PR, test first:

3. **Tell operators about the new 403.** `MCP Deployment/troubleshooting.md:119-123` does not say that an untyped create from a restricted connector is checked as `DOCUMENT`. A connector operator who hits the new 403 has no hint.

title: packages/shared: one test imports services/demo-service and needs cors, so the suite cannot pass on a member-only install
description:
**BLUF:** one test file in `packages/shared` needs another workspace member's dependency, so the package's suite cannot pass on an install that provides only `packages/shared`'s own closure. It passes on a full `npm ci` at `Blockchain/Dev`, where `cors` is hoisted from `services/*`.

**Measured** (2026-10-12, Seat F 17th; clean-room copy of develop `a31b77577` with no `node_modules`; node v24.7.0):

* `npm ci` run inside `packages/shared` is an implicit-workspace install from the root lock (npm's prefix there is `Blockchain/Dev`). A stock one has no vitest at all, so to see this I made vitest resolvable in that install (a variant lock carrying the KS-1317 vitest declaration). Then `npm test`: `Test Files  1 failed | 48 passed (49)`, `Tests  945 passed | 4 skipped (949)`.
* The one failing file is `src/__tests__/ks781-p3-3-body-parser-order.test.ts`: `Error: Cannot find package 'cors' imported from .../services/demo-service/src/app.ts` (`app.ts:14`), thrown from the file's `KS-832 ACCEPTANCE BAR` suite, whose 4 tests are then skipped.
* Control, same develop on a full `npm ci` at `Blockchain/Dev`: `node_modules/cors` present, `Test Files 48 passed (48)`, `Tests 945 passed (945)`, `tsc --noEmit -p packages/shared` rc 0. In the member-only install `node_modules/cors` is absent.
* `cors` is declared by 21 of the `services/*/package.json` files (`demo-service` among them) and not by `packages/shared`, so nothing in `packages/shared/package.json` tells a reader the suite depends on it.

**Why it matters:** the dependency is invisible and works only through hoisting, so the failure appears only when someone runs the package's tests without the full install. It is lower urgency than it looks: since the KS-1317 guard, a member-only `npm test` stops early with a message naming the full install, so this is reached only when someone supplies vitest another way.

**Suggested shapes (not prescribed):**

* Move the test to where its dependency is declared (`services/demo-service`), or to a root-level guard suite that is only run after a full install.
* Do not declare `cors` in `packages/shared`: the 25 service Dockerfiles (of the 29 that reference `packages/shared`; the other four are frontends) copy `/shared` (with its `node_modules`) from the `shared-builder` stage into the runtime image, so any new dependency there ships in every image. That is the cost that made the Spark's vitest declaration for KS-1317 the wrong shape.

**Where:** `Blockchain/Dev/packages/shared/src/__tests__/ks781-p3-3-body-parser-order.test.ts` (the boot of the demo-service app, around line 5601), `Blockchain/Dev/services/demo-service/src/app.ts` line 14.

Found while raising KS-1317. Filed unassigned in Backlog on Wednesday's instruction, 2026-10-12.

title: originate migrate-tenant-data: a non-Error throw logs as [object Object], and the per-tenant error is a bare string (PR #1460 gate notes)
description:
## BLUF

Two **Minor** notes from the Opus QA gate on PR #1460 (KS-1334's fifth site, merged as `ba697cf3d4218383491391ed8fd280a2486d6f86`). Both sit in the per-tenant catch of `POST /api/admin/migrate-tenant-data`. They were left out of #1460 on purpose: a change to the gated head would have voided the GO. Neither blocks anything; filed so they are not lost.

## Recommendation

Fix both in one small tier-2 PR, test first:

1. **A non-Error throw logs as** `[object Object]`**.** `services/originate/src/routes/adminConfig.ts:2164` is `error: err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err)`. `String({})` gives `[object Object]`, which tells an operator nothing. `fail500` (`:103`) already formats a thrown string or object properly; extract that into one helper and use it at both sites.
2. **The per-tenant error is a bare string where the route's other errors use** `{ code, message }`**.** `:2166` pushes `{ tenant, error: 'TENANT_COPY_FAILED' }`. Either change it to `{ tenant, error: { code: 'TENANT_COPY_FAILED' } }` for consistency, or leave it and say in the route's comment why. There are no consumers of this route's response (no spec entry, no frontend, no doc), so the change has no known blast radius.

## Detail

* **Source:** Opus gate on PR #1460, verdict `GO WITH NOTE`, 0 Major, 0 blocking Minor. Verdict file sha256/16 `eecd5bade92e7d75` (Wednesday's `reference/2026-10-12_gate-pr1460/verdict.md`).

title: KS-1236 follow-ups: the approve level check and write are not atomic, and the local level order duplicates the shared one
description:
## BLUF

Gate notes on #1457 (KS-1236, head `13d3bf195`, merging 2026-10-12). Both are minor and neither blocks it. Item 1 closes a milliseconds-wide race; item 2 removes a duplicated list and a wrong comment.

## Recommendation

Do 2 as a comment-and-import fix. Do 1 only if the race matters: it needs a conditional UPDATE in the repo layer. Item 3 is an observation for a ruling.

## Detail

1. **Not atomic:** the approve pre-check (`users.ts`, the KS-1236 block) reads the subject's level and the write (`userRepo.updateUserPlatformScope`) is a separate statement. A raise that lands between them can still be lowered. Close it with a conditional UPDATE (`... WHERE verification_level < target`).
2. **Duplicate order:** the module-level `LEVEL_ORDER` that #1457 hoists omits `NONE` and `SOCIAL`, and its comment says they "cannot be compared". The canonical order is `VERIFICATION_LEVEL_ORDER` in `packages/shared/src/verification/policy-engine.ts` (`NONE < BASIC < SOCIAL < STANDARD < ...`). The outcome is safe today because the zod schema limits targets to STANDARD and above, which rank above both. Replace the local list with the shared one and fix the comment.
3. **Observation:** a refused stale request stays PENDING until a reviewer rejects it, and submit refuses any new request from that subject ("already pending") meanwhile. Consider an auto-close or a hint in the 400.

Provenance: independent Opus gate, 2026-10-12, minor findings 4, 5 and 6; found by Seat V 3rd while merging. Related: KS-1236, KS-1194, KS-1050.

title: KS-1006 follow-ups: two inaccurate statements in the merged change, and the passwordless no-secret MFA state
description:
## BLUF

Gate notes on merged #1456 (KS-1006, squash `44afaf482`): two statements in the change are inaccurate, and one gap is real. Items 1 and 2 are comment-only; item 3 needs a ruling.

## Recommendation

Fix 1 and 2 in one small PR. Rule on 3 before building anything: default is leave it (the account state is not produced by normal enrolment).

## Detail

1. `services/auth/src/routes/users.ts`**, the KS-1006 comment in** `POST /me/mfa/disable`**:** it says an account with no stored secret "can still disable through POST /api/auth/mfa/disable (password or backup code)". That overclaims. A passwordless (wallet or social) account with `mfa_enabled`, no secret and no backup codes can use neither route; the `routes/mfa.ts` else-branch needs a valid TOTP or backup code.
2. `services/auth/src/__tests__/ks1006-mfa-disable-refuses-when-no-secret-is-stored.test.ts` **header:** it calls the base "a latent shape, not a live bypass". That understates it. `decryptMfaSecret` (`repositories/userRepo.ts:172-189`) returns `undefined` when the DEK is missing or destroyed, or when decryption fails, so on the base a decrypt fault let any six-character string disable MFA.
3. **Gap:** such an account (MFA on, secret unreadable, no backup codes, no password) now has no way to turn MFA off. Options: admin-assisted reset, a re-enrol path, or leave.

Provenance: independent Opus gate on #1456 and #1457, 2026-10-12, minor findings 1 and 2; found by Seat V 3rd while merging. Related: KS-1006, KS-732, KS-938.
