title: Admin › Add user & organisation creates a support account with a predictable password and emails it in plain text
description:
## Summary

`AdminController.AdminAddUserOrgAsync` (`ssd/Controllers/AdminController.cs`, around lines 620–740) creates a second Identity user for every new organisation, the "support" account. That account is a problem in three ways:

1. **Its password is predictable.** Line 655 builds it from a hard-coded literal in source plus the sanitised `WhiteLabel` value. Every organisation created this way on a deployment gets the **same** password, and anyone who can read the repository knows it. The value is not repeated here.
2. **It holds strong roles.** It gets `SsdAccountAdmin` and `SsdPowerUser` (lines 669–670). Its email is confirmed programmatically, so it can sign in immediately.
3. **The password is emailed in plain text.** Line 731 adds `Support Pw: …` to the "New Org Signup" email sent to `AppSpecific:DefaultEmail`.

The username is also predictable (`assurance+<sanitised org name>@<whitelabel>.com`, line 628). The username and the password together are a working credential for every admin-created organisation.

Found in passing while working on [Platform S UX/UI Issues](https://linear.app/secuura/project/platform-s-uxui-issues-a455be6e5a82) Phase 13. It was not fixed there: this is a security change, not UX.

## Suggested shape (for whoever owns it)

* Decide whether the support account is still needed at all.
* If it is:
  * Use a random per-account password, or better, no password: an invitation or reset link.
  * Never put a credential in an email, a log or a ticket.
* Rotate or disable the existing support accounts on every deployed environment (dev-ps, UAT, prod). Any organisation created through this action carries one.
* Add an xUnit contract that no email body built in `ssd/Controllers/**` concatenates a password variable.

## Environment

* platform-s, project branch `project/platform-s-uxui-issues` (the code is the same on develop).
* Found 12 Oct 2026.

nodes.body:
**Partly addressed by #976** (round 3, Phase 16, PS-1191). Admin → Add User + Org now sends its "new organisation" notice from a template that has no support-account lines, so **that email no longer carries the support account's password**.

**Still open here:**
- The support account is still created, with a password built from a fixed pattern in the code (~`AdminController.cs:655`).
- Existing support accounts on the deployed environments still need rotating or disabling.

title: Epic: attested enclave lane (Option B) — org keys released only to a verified build
description:
## Why

Some operations need plaintext with no human present: automatic flow sign and watermark steps (`SignFlowOperation`, `WatermarkFlowOperation`), emailed attachments (`ShareAttachmentBuilder`), the Outlook attach, and the verify page's upload fallback. Browser-side encryption ([PS-1086](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1086/epic-browser-side-document-encryption-option-a-keys-never-reach)) cannot serve these. Under today's design and the [PS-948](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-948/organisation-document-encryption-keys-system-generated-or-customer) programme they run in the ordinary app process, where anyone who controls the app can read the plaintext.

Option B runs that code inside attested confidential compute. The vault releases an organisation's key **only** to a measured, approved image (Azure Secure Key Release with attestation; AWS KMS with Nitro Enclave attestation conditions). Staff who can deploy the ordinary app, or read its memory, then get nothing.

The decision tree suggests A + B with B deferrable. No ticket for B existed. Raised in the Project See key-handling review, 10 Oct 2026; see *Combining A and B…* §1.

## Blocked on

* Decision 1 confirming A + B, and the open question in *Combining A and B…*: does any customer need the unattended features under E2E, or can they simply be off? If they can be off, park this epic.
* [PS-949](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-949/design-document-key-hierarchy-scope-and-vault-choice)'s vault choice. Azure Secure Key Release needs Key Vault Premium or Managed HSM with an exportable key and a release policy; the AWS route needs KMS key-policy conditions on enclave attestation.

## Scope (child tickets once unblocked)

1. **Platform choice per cloud.** dev-ps (Azure): confidential containers / confidential VMs with Microsoft Azure Attestation and a key release policy. UAT and prod (AWS): Nitro Enclaves, with a KMS key policy conditioned on `kms:RecipientAttestation:ImageSha384` (and PCRs as decided). Or a decision to move the lane to one cloud.
2. **Enclave workload:** the existing iText sign / watermark code and the attachment builder packaged as a minimal enclave image, reachable only from the app over an authenticated channel, with no outbound network except the vault/KMS and the ciphertext store.
3. **Release policy ownership (the trust anchor):** who may change the attestation policy or the approved image measurement. A Secuura staff member who can change the policy to approve a debug image can defeat the lane, so changing it needs two people outside the deploy path ([PS-1085](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1085/vault-access-governance-no-single-secuura-staff-member-can-use-or)), raises an alert, and — ideally — is visible to the customer org.
4. **Reproducible builds:** the enclave image is built reproducibly so a third party can check the published measurement matches the published source.
5. **Per-organisation switches:** each unattended feature is off by default for an E2E org; turning it on records the org admin's consent and routes that operation through the lane (decision 7).
6. **Signing:** the enclave supplies a digest to [PS-947](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-947/hash-only-remote-signing-endpoint-deferred-pades-signing)'s endpoint, so the signing key never enters the enclave or the app ([PS-946](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-946/move-pdf-signing-keys-into-azure-key-vault-hsm)).

## Done when

* Unblocked decisions are recorded, or the epic is explicitly parked with the reason.
* Child tickets exist for each scope item.
* The independent cryptographic review (decision 12) covers the attestation policy and the release-policy ownership, not only the code.

## Acceptance (for the epic)

* Proven on dev-ps: the org key is released to the approved enclave image, and refused to (a) the ordinary app identity and (b) the same image built with debug enabled or a one-byte change. Both refusals observed and recorded with the date.
* Changing the release policy or approved measurement needs two people and raises an alert, observed.
* `docs/` states in plain words what the lane protects against (staff and infrastructure access to plaintext and keys) and what it does not (a malicious change approved through the two-person policy path).

**Why no Playwright test is listed on the epic:** the subject is where code runs and which identity a key is released to; the user-facing journeys are unchanged. Each child that adds a consent switch or changes a flow step carries its own spec, and the epic's proof is the observed release and refusal above.

title: Epic: browser-side document encryption (Option A) — keys never reach Secuura
description:
> **Storage-side inputs from** [PS-1076](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1076/design-storage-connector-model-for-organisation-chosen-storage) **(agreed 27 Oct 2026),** `docs/storage-connector-model.md` **§7, §9, §10.**
>
> * **Browser writes.** The browser writes to a customer store through the **separate register-reference method** ([PS-949](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-949/design-document-key-hierarchy-scope-and-vault-choice) §5) plus an **optional provider capability that issues a short-lived upload target**: an S3 presigned PUT, a Graph upload-session URL, or a Dropbox temporary upload link.
> * **No tokens in the browser.** The browser never holds a refresh or access token. Providers without such a target stay relay-only. Whether Box has one is for this epic to establish.
> * **Recipients.** Presigned delivery to recipients becomes useful only with the key carried separately (Decision 5).
> * **Enclave scope.** An attested enclave needs read-only access to ciphertext, a scope the connection model must offer.

## Why

This is the only option in Project See under which **Secuura staff cannot read a document**, because Secuura never holds a key that can decrypt it. The server-side key programme ([PS-948](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-948/organisation-document-encryption-keys-system-generated-or-customer)) and the signing-key move ([PS-946](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-946/move-pdf-signing-keys-into-azure-key-vault-hsm)) are foundations, but by their own text they do not deliver this: the app can still ask the vault to unwrap.

[PS-947](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-947/hash-only-remote-signing-endpoint-deferred-pades-signing) already defers "the browser-side preparation and injection" to "a separate ticket once the library choice is made". That ticket did not exist. This epic is it, plus the encryption and key-handling it depends on.

Raised in the Project See key-handling review, 10 Oct 2026. Background: the feasibility doc, the decision tree, and *Combining A and B, bring-your-own-storage, and signable objects* (all on the Project See page).

## Blocked on decisions (decision tree)

Build cannot start until these are recorded, because each one changes the key structure:

* **1 / 2** — the customer promise and opt-in per organisation (suggested: A + B, opt-in per org).
* **3** — who can recover a document if its owner can't (org escrow, customer-managed key, or none). This is the decision that determines whether *any* Secuura component can ever hold an unwrap path.
* **3a** — Secuura-hosted ciphertext or customer-hosted (bring-your-own-storage).
* **4** — how user keys are created and unlocked (passkeys / WebAuthn PRF vs a separate passphrase), given most users sign in with Entra, Google, GitHub or Apple.
* **5** — how external recipients get the key (URL `#fragment` vs recipient accounts).
* **8** — whether a browser-supplied hash is acceptable for the provenance chain and Cardano anchors.
* **9** — front-end build pipeline and libraries (pinned, SRI), given the current ES5/jQuery front end.
* **11** — what happens to existing server-readable documents.

## Scope (child tickets to be filed once the decisions above are recorded)

1. **Client crypto foundation:** a built, pinned, SRI-protected crypto bundle; WebCrypto AES-GCM; CSP tightened so only that bundle can run crypto.
2. **User / org key unlock** per decision 4, with the org-recovery path per decision 3. Wrapped keys are stored server-side; unwrapping happens only in the browser.
3. **Encrypt on upload:** the browser hashes the plaintext, encrypts, and uploads ciphertext (to Secuura storage or the customer's store per 3a). The provider interface takes ciphertext or a reference ([PS-949](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-949/design-document-key-hierarchy-scope-and-vault-choice) / [PS-950](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-950/route-every-document-blob-readwrite-through-idocumentstorageprovider)).
4. **Decrypt to view / download** in the browser (PDF.js is already in use).
5. **Share links:** recipient decryption per decision 5.
6. **Browser watermarking** with parity tests against the iText output.
7. **Browser signature preparation:** placeholder, byte-range hash, call [PS-947](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-947/hash-only-remote-signing-endpoint-deferred-pades-signing)'s digest endpoint, inject the CMS.
8. **Feature switches:** the operations that need plaintext with no human present (automatic flow steps, emailed attachments, Outlook attach, verify upload fallback, password-protected PDFs) are off for an E2E organisation unless routed through the Option B enclave lane.
9. **Honest product wording** ([PS-945](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-945/register-page-remove-inaccurate-end-to-end-encrypted-claim)) for the tier, including the remaining caveat that Secuura serves the JavaScript.

## Done when

* Decisions 1, 2, 3, 3a, 4, 5, 8, 9 and 11 are recorded on the decision tree.
* Child tickets exist for each scope item, each with its own acceptance and test plan.
* An independent cryptographic review is booked before launch (decision 12).

## Acceptance (for the epic)

* For an E2E organisation, no request from browser to server carries document plaintext or an unwrapped document key: proven by a network-capture systemTest over upload, view, download, share and sign, asserting request bodies are ciphertext or digests only.
* The server holds no key that can unwrap an E2E organisation's document keys, unless decision 3 explicitly chose org escrow held outside Secuura — stated in `docs/` in plain words.
* `docs/` states the remaining trust assumption (Secuura serves the code) and the mitigations (pinned bundle, SRI, CSP).

**Playwright:** each child carries its own spec. The epic's own proof is the network-capture spec above, suggest `systemTest/tests/functional/e2e_no_plaintext_on_wire.spec.ts`, which fails on `develop` today because upload posts the plaintext file.

title: Vault access governance: no single Secuura staff member can use or grant use of customer keys
description:
## Why

The key programme ([PS-948](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-948/organisation-document-encryption-keys-system-generated-or-customer) and children, [PS-946](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-946/move-pdf-signing-keys-into-azure-key-vault-hsm)) puts keys in a vault as non-exportable. That stops Secuura staff **extracting** a key. It does not stop staff **using** one: the app's managed identity can unwrap DEKs and sign digests, and anyone who can act as that identity, or grant themselves the same data-plane role, can decrypt documents or sign as a customer.

No ticket today says who at Secuura may hold those rights. Without that, "keys are in a vault" is a storage claim, not an access claim.

Raised in the Project See key-handling review, 10 Oct 2026.

## Scope

* **Vault tier consequence (feeds** [PS-949](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-949/design-document-key-hierarchy-scope-and-vault-choice)): on Azure Key Vault (Premium or Standard, RBAC model), a subscription Owner or User Access Administrator can assign themselves a data-plane role such as Key Vault Crypto User at vault scope. On **Managed HSM**, data-plane access is governed by the HSM's own local RBAC, which control-plane Owners cannot grant. Record this in the [PS-949](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-949/design-document-key-hierarchy-scope-and-vault-choice) vault decision as a security property, not only a cost line.
* **Security domain / recovery material (Managed HSM):** the security domain is protected by an M-of-N quorum of RSA keys. Decide who holds the shares; no single Secuura person may hold a quorum. Record where shares are kept and the recovery drill.
* **Role inventory:** list every principal with control-plane or data-plane rights on each key vault / HSM / KMS key, per environment (dev-ps, UAT, prod). Humans: none standing on data-plane in UAT and prod.
* **Just-in-time elevation:** human data-plane or role-assignment rights only through time-boxed, approved elevation (Entra PIM on Azure; an equivalent approval flow on AWS), with a second approver.
* **Separation of duties:** a person who can deploy the app image (ECR/ACR push, `deploy-from-ecr.sh`) must not also be able to change vault RBAC or key policies, and vice versa.
* **App identity scope:** the app's managed identity / instance role gets only the operations it needs (wrap, unwrap, sign) on the keys it needs — no key management, no `get` on key material, no role assignment.
* **Alerting:** any role assignment, access-policy or key-policy change, key disable/delete/purge, or security-domain operation raises an alert to a channel that the person making the change cannot silence.
* **AWS:** the same controls for KMS on `dep-aws-uat` / `dep-aws-secuura` — key policies that name the instance role and a restricted admin role, not blanket account-root delegation to IAM, and CloudTrail alerts on `PutKeyPolicy`, `CreateGrant`, `DisableKey`, `ScheduleKeyDeletion`.
* **Break-glass:** a documented, two-person, audited emergency path, with a post-use review.

## Out of scope

* Stopping the **running app** from decrypting. While the app can unwrap, someone who controls the app's code can too. That is solved only by browser-side encryption or attested confidential compute ([PS-1086](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1086/epic-browser-side-document-encryption-option-a-keys-never-reach) for Option A, [PS-1087](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1087/epic-attested-enclave-lane-option-b-org-keys-released-only-to-a) for Option B). This ticket narrows the human paths around the app; it does not remove the app path.

## Done when

* The [PS-949](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-949/design-document-key-hierarchy-scope-and-vault-choice) design records the vault tier with the RBAC consequence above.
* A role inventory per environment exists in `docs/` (principals and roles named, no secrets), and shows no standing human data-plane access in UAT or prod.
* JIT elevation, separation of duties and alerting are configured in Terraform (or the AWS equivalent) and proven by an observed alert from a test role assignment, with the date and environment.
* The break-glass runbook is merged beside [PS-957](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-957/key-lifecycle-disablerevoke-erasure-dissolution-audit-docs-and-runbook)'s runbooks.

## Acceptance

* An `az role assignment list` / `az keyvault role assignment list` (or Managed HSM local RBAC listing) and the AWS key policies for each environment are attached as observations, dated, showing the app identity's operations and no standing human data-plane role in UAT or prod.
* A test role assignment on dev-ps triggers the alert, and the alert reaches a channel the assigner does not administer — observed, not inferred.
* The app identity cannot perform key management or role assignment: an attempted `RotateAsync`/`DisableAsync`-equivalent or role assignment using only the app identity is refused, observed.
* No key material, security-domain share, password or `*.tfvars` value appears in the ticket, PR, docs or logs. Principals and roles are named; secrets are not.

**Why no Playwright test applies:** this is cloud identity and access configuration. Nothing changes in the app's UI or routes; the proof is the observed role listings, the refused app-identity operations and the triggered alert above.

title: Signing formats: a detached signature is bound on chain by content hash only — state the residual risk and the closure path (KS-1454 + PS-607 + PS-1053)
description:
Found in review of [Secuura/platform-s#946](https://linear.app/secuura/review/ps-1042-document-signing-formats-sign-every-supported-file-type-0c53c669149d) (2026-10-10). Verified on `project/document-signing-formats` @ `5a21dfe`. **A decision and documentation ticket**, plus whatever the decision makes buildable.

## What is true today

* **The anchor is not keyed to K's document.** A detached sign has `SignedFileGuid` null, so the per-verb `sign` case takes the flat `/api/anchors` path (`CardanoAnchorService.PerVerb.cs`). The flat anchor's `DocumentId` is `ToHyphenatedGuid(tx.ChainId)` (`CardanoAnchorService.cs:83`): **S's transaction id, not K's document id**.
  * The signature therefore sits outside K's lifecycle for that document.
  * Its anchored hash is the content hash, which the upload's anchor also carries, so **K's verify-by-hash can show two anchors for the same hash**.
* **The signature's own hash is not on chain yet.** `metadata.signatureHash` rides on the sign anchor only once [KS-1454](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1454>) is deployed on the paired K **and** `CardanoAnchor:AnchorSignatureHash` is switched on. It is off in every template.
* **The ledger is linked by id, not by hash.** `ChainIntegrityChecker` checks `PreviousChainId == previous.ChainId` (`:95`–`121`). No row carries a hash of its predecessor, so the `signatureSha256` in a row's `PayloadJson` ([PS-1059](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1059/signing-formats-protect-the-detached-p7s-verify-its-recorded-hash-on)) is **not tamper-evident** against a database rewrite.
* **Consequence**, as the design doc's own caveat says (`docs/signing-formats-design.md:146`–`155`): a substitute signature minted with a platform-held key ([PS-607](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-607/rotate-existing-personal-signing-certificates-onto-the-isolated-key): `SigningKeyEncryptionKey` is set nowhere), plus a rewrite of the `.p7s` blob, `DocumentSignature.SignatureSha256` and the Sign row's payload, **passes all three** [PS-1059](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1059/signing-formats-protect-the-detached-p7s-verify-its-recorded-hash-on) **integrity checks**.

## To decide and do

1. **Anchor keying:** should a detached sign anchor against K's document (a K-side "attest / sign without version" verb, or `lifecycle-events`) rather than as a flat anchor keyed by S's tx id? That would be a platform-k change, raised as a KS ticket to Kamil, not edited from S. Also how Verify should present two anchors for one hash.
2. **The closure is** [KS-1454](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1454/anchor-schema-accept-and-anchor-platform-ss-signaturehash-the-plain) **+** [PS-607](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-607/rotate-existing-personal-signing-certificates-onto-the-isolated-key) **+** [PS-1053](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1053/signing-formats-investigate-signing-in-the-browser-key-stays-with-the)**:** hash on chain, signing keys isolated, keys held by the signer. Sequence them, and make sure the design doc states this as the closure, with what each one removes.
3. **A ledger row-hash chain** (each row carries the hash of its predecessor plus its own payload)? A bigger change across all verbs, so decide whether it is in scope or whether the K anchor is the tamper-evidence. Record the decision either way.
4. **Docs:** update the design doc's "what protects it" section and the testing docs with the residual risk as stated above, until each piece lands.

nodes.body:
**Progress on the decisions (2026-10-13):**
- **3, row-hash chain:** built as PS-1204, [#975](https://github.com/Secuura/platform-s/pull/975).
- **4, docs:** the same PR updates the design doc's "what protects it" section with the residual risk and the closure table (PS-1204 → KS-1454 → KS-1575 → PS-607 → PS-1053), and updates both testing docs.
- **1, anchor keying:** KS-1575 is with Kamil. It also now asks K to accept `metadata.rowHash`, so the newest ledger hash can be pinned outside S.

**Still open on S:** switch the detached `sign` case in `CardanoAnchorService.PerVerb.cs` over to K's document, and decide how Verify presents the result. Both wait on KS-1575 shipping, so this ticket stays open, blocked by it.

**Decisions (Stuart, 2026-10-13)**

1. **Anchor keying: key a detached signature to K's document.** The flat anchor keyed by S's transaction id is retired once K supports this. It needs a platform-k change (a sign-without-new-version verb, or a `lifecycle-events` sign event on the document), raised as a KS ticket for Kamil. S switches the detached `sign` case in `CardanoAnchorService.PerVerb.cs` over when that verb ships on the paired K. Verify should then show one document with a signature event, not two anchors for one hash.
2. **Ledger row-hash chain: in scope, built.** Each `DocumentTransaction` row carries the hash of its predecessor plus a hash of its own payload, and `ChainIntegrityChecker` checks the hashes as well as the ids. Existing rows get a backfill migration. This touches every verb, so it gets its own ticket.
3. **Closure unchanged:** KS-1454 puts the signature hash on chain, PS-607 isolates the signing keys, and PS-1053 has the signer hold the key. The row-hash chain is added to that list: it makes `signatureSha256` in `PayloadJson` tamper-evident against a database rewrite that leaves the chain's hashes alone.
4. **Docs:** the design doc's "what protects it" section and the testing docs state the residual risk until each piece lands.

title: Per-device session revocation: sign out ends only this device, plus an active-sessions list
description:
## Background

[PS-1037](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1037>) (PR #943, on `project/platform-s-uxui-issues`) made sign-out revoke the session on the server. It does this by **rotating the user's security stamp**, which is now re-checked every minute (`SessionClaimCarryOver.ValidationInterval`). "Account → Sign out of all devices" does the same rotation.

This ticket is the follow-up recorded in `docs/session-revocation.md` § "What it costs".

## Current behaviour

* **Signing out on one device signs the user out on every device.** A stamp rotation invalidates all of the user's auth cookies, not just the one in front of them.
* Each auth cookie is a self-contained ticket. The server keeps no list of sessions, so it can't revoke one session on its own or show the user where they are signed in.

## Proposal

1. **A server-side ticket store.** Implement `ITicketStore` and set it as `CookieAuthenticationOptions.SessionStore` for `IdentityConstants.ApplicationScheme`.
   * The cookie then carries only a session key.
   * The ticket lives server-side: a MySQL table, e.g. `UserSession(Key, UserId, CreatedUtc, LastSeenUtc, ExpiresUtc, UserAgent, IpHash, RevokedUtc)`, with sliding-expiry renewal.
2. **Plain sign-out deletes or revokes only this session's row.** It no longer rotates the stamp.
3. **"Sign out of all devices" still rotates the stamp** and revokes every row for the user.
4. **New "Active sessions" page in Account settings.** It lists each session (device / browser, approximate location or IP hash, signed in, last seen) and has a per-row "Sign out this device". New testids: `manage-sessions-row-<id>`, `manage-sessions-revoke-btn-<id>`.
5. **Password change, 2FA disable and similar** keep their current stamp behaviour, which ends every session.

## Things to decide or check

* **Storage and sweep:** expired rows need a background sweep. Estimate the row volume per active user.
* **GDPR:** IP and user agent are personal data. Store a hash or a truncated value, and include these rows in erasure.
* **Data Protection:** the session key cookie must still be protected. Check the multi-container behaviour; the dpkeys volume is already shared.
* **Migration:** existing self-contained cookies stay valid until they expire. There is no forced re-login, or the change forces one deliberately.
* **Interaction with** `SessionClaimCarryOver`**:** a refreshed principal must be written back to the store.
* **External IdP sign-out:** the federated round-trip in `Logout.cshtml.cs` is unchanged.

## Tests

* **xUnit:** ticket store round-trip, revoke one session versus all, sweep, and the claim carry-over writing back to the store.
* **systemTest:** extend `session_invalidation.spec.ts`. Two contexts for one persona (`SignOutUser`):
  * signing out in context A leaves context B signed in;
  * "Sign out this device" from B ends A only;
  * "Sign out of all devices" ends both.

title: Correct the failed-run message in run-migrations.sh (:187-188): it still names the applied-counts-skips defect that PR #1436 fixed
description:
**ACTION (owner): change the failure message at** `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/run-migrations.sh:187-188` **so it stops naming a defect the runner no longer has.**

**What the code says.** Read at develop `4aa5cb38bd52449b08e08a77bc6bebca04751c2b`, which contains PR #1436 (the KS-808 fix, squash `ae9bf6828f88`):

* Line 188 is printed on **every** failed-migration run. It sits inside the `failed_count > 0` branch that opens at `:180`, and reads: `applied=N-counts-skips defect is KS-808. Exit 3 - the code this`. With `:187`, the sentence says the applied=N-counts-skips defect is still open.
* That counting was changed by PR #1436. `:121`, `:147` and `:173-174` now count a skip on its own (comments marked `KS-808 (2)`), and `:176` prints `Summary: applied=$applied_count failed=$failed_count skipped=$skipped_count`.
* So at runtime the script tells an operator about an open defect that the code no longer has.

**Scope.** Text only: the two `echo` lines at `:187-188`. No behaviour change; the exit code (3) and the counting stay as they are.

**How it was found.** gate77 finding N-1436-1, graded Minor by the gate, recorded during the merge of PR #1436. Board search by symbol before filing, team-scoped, title or description: the filename returns 8 tickets (KS 808, KS 1296, KS 1443, KS 1305, KS 1401, KS 1376, KS 1054, KS 1031), none of which owns these two lines; the exact phrase `applied=N-counts-skips` returns 0; `:187-188` returns 0; a fabricated control term returns 0.

title: Signing formats: investigate signing in the browser (key stays with the signer)
description:
Part of [PS-1042](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1042/epic-sign-every-supported-file-type-embedded-where-the-format-allows). **An investigation: report and recommend, no build.**

## Why

Today every signature is made **on the server**:

* PAdES for PDF (iText);
* separate CAdES `.p7s` files ([PS-1043](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1043/signing-formats-p1-detached-signing-baseline-signformatpolicy));
* Office package signatures ([PS-1046](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1046/signing-formats-p4-ooxml-embedded-signing-engine-for-docxxlsx-spike)).

All three use a person or organisation certificate whose PFX the user uploaded to the platform. So the platform holds the signing key, and "who signed" rests on our access control rather than on the signer holding the key. Signing in the browser would keep the key with the signer. That is what qualified and advanced e-signature schemes expect, and what Project See's browser lane ([PS-947](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-947/hash-only-remote-signing-endpoint-deferred-pades-signing): a hash-only remote signing endpoint, HSM) assumes.

## The shape every format shares

None of the three formats needs the document in the browser. Each one splits the same way:

1. **Prepare (server):** compute exactly what gets signed.
   * PAdES: the ByteRange digest.
   * CAdES: the DER of the signed attributes, which carry the document's hash.
   * Office signature: the canonicalised SignedInfo, which carries the manifest digests.
2. **Sign (browser or device):** a raw RSA or ECDSA signature over that digest, using the signer's key.
3. **Finalise (server):** insert the signature value and certificate, add the timestamp, store the result and record it on the ledger, `DocumentSignature` and K, exactly as now.

The investigation should confirm this split for each engine, and find what in the current code (DetachedCmsSigner, OoxmlPackageSigner, PdfProcessingService's iText path) needs to become two calls.

## Questions to answer

1. **Where the key can live, and what a web page can reach.** Compare these on security, user experience, browser and OS support, and cost:
   * a non-extractable WebCrypto key generated in the browser, with its certificate issued by us or by a CA;
   * smartcards and USB tokens. Browsers give JavaScript no PKCS#11 or OS-certificate-store access, so this needs a local agent or extension (EU DSS's NexU, Web eID, vendor agents);
   * the Windows or macOS certificate store, through the same route;
   * remote or cloud signing: the CSC API for remote QES providers, and our own HSM ([PS-947](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-947/hash-only-remote-signing-endpoint-deferred-pades-signing));
   * WebAuthn / passkeys. These are not X.509 document signatures, but could they authorise a server-side or HSM signature? Where does that leave legal standing?
2. **Certificates and trust.** Who issues the signer's certificate in each option? How does this interact with today's PFX upload, Office's "recoverable versus valid", Acrobat's AATL and the C2PA trust list ([PS-1047](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1047/signing-formats-p5-c2pa-embedded-signing-engine-for-images))?
3. **Per format:**
   * the PAdES deferred-signing flow in iText 7.2 (`SignDeferred` / external container);
   * CAdES signed attributes built server-side and signed in the browser;
   * the Office SignedInfo signed in the browser, and how that fits the `SignedXml` engine;
   * the signing-certificate attributes and XAdES SigningCertificate need the certificate **before** the hash, so the certificate has to reach the server first.
4. **Security.**
   * What stops the server presenting a different hash from the document the signer reviewed? (The review step, showing the hash, a two-phase confirm.)
   * Replay and binding of the prepare→sign→finalise round trip.
   * CSRF and session handling.
   * What the ledger records about where the key was.
5. **Flows.** Does the flow engine's automatic sign step still make sense, or does a browser-signed step become a gated human step?
6. **Effort and sequencing** against [PS-1047](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1047/signing-formats-p5-c2pa-embedded-signing-engine-for-images) and [PS-947](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-947/hash-only-remote-signing-endpoint-deferred-pades-signing).

## Second question: Project See (the server never sees the plaintext)

[Project See](<https://linear.app/secuura/project/project-see-636bf0aca9fb>) ([Project See](https://linear.app/secuura/project/project-see-636bf0aca9fb)) asks for more than key custody: Secuura should never see the unencrypted file. The three-step split above assumes **Prepare (server)**, which means the server reads the plaintext. So, for each key option and each format, also answer:

* **Can prepare and finalise run on hashes alone, with the server never holding the plaintext?**
  * **Separate** `.p7s` **(CAdES):** probably yes. The browser already hashes the file for Verify, and the signed attributes need only that hash.
  * **Office signature (OOXML):** the browser would compute the per-part digests and the server would build SignedInfo from them. Is that feasible, and what does the browser need to parse?
  * **PAdES:** the ByteRange digest covers the PDF *with* a signature placeholder added. Either the PDF is restructured in the browser (a JS PDF library), or the server sees the file. With [PS-1057](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1057/signing-formats-make-embedding-into-pdf-and-into-office-files)'s `EmbedPdf` off, a PDF signs detached and this case goes away.
* **Where** [PS-946](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-946/move-pdf-signing-keys-into-azure-key-vault-hsm) **sits.** HSM-held keys stop a signing key ever being exportable from the platform, but Secuura still holds the key. That fixes exposure, not custody. State which goal each option meets: custody, never-sees-plaintext, both, or neither.
* **Out of scope here:** watermarking. Project See's feasibility note already says watermarking ciphertext is impossible.

Related: [PS-947](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-947/hash-only-remote-signing-endpoint-deferred-pades-signing) (hash-only remote signing endpoint) and [PS-946](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-946/move-pdf-signing-keys-into-azure-key-vault-hsm) (signing keys in Key Vault / HSM). This investigation should answer [PS-947](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-947/hash-only-remote-signing-endpoint-deferred-pades-signing)'s design questions rather than duplicate them.

## Deliverable

A written comparison and a recommendation on this ticket and in `docs/signing-formats-design.md`, plus a proposed phase plan. Include a tiny proof of concept only if one question can't be answered without it, for example a WebCrypto signature over a CAdES signed-attributes digest that a stock verifier accepts.

title: Docs: the .docx one-pagers are four refreshes behind their Markdown sources
description:
`docs/ONE-PAGER-BUSINESS.docx` and `docs/ONE-PAGER-TECHNICAL.docx` are Word renderings of the two Markdown one-pagers. They were committed once (PR [Secuura/Distributed_Secuura#413](https://linear.app/secuura/review/fixanchoringkyc-db-probe-retry-with-backoff-no-more-boot-race-latch-ks-8ce336617d30)) and have **not been regenerated since**, while the Markdown has moved on through roughly four doc refreshes.

## Why this matters

They are **committed artefacts that are shared with people outside the repo** — a buyer or a technical evaluator reads the `.docx`, not the Markdown. So the drift is not cosmetic: the Word versions currently state things the platform has moved past, including (at least):

* **"Certify"** rather than **Declare** — the attestation verb was renamed on the wire and in storage ([PS-612](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-612/rename-the-certify-verb-to-declare-across-s) / [KS-661](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-661/rename-the-certify-lifecycle-verb-to-declare)).
* **Google / Apple / GitHub SSO listed as *planned*** — all three are shipped (`Startup.cs`).
* No mention of the **confirmed-anchor verification rule** ([PS-575](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-575/persist-per-action-anchor-confirmation-so-s-knows-which-actions)/576), organisation lifecycle, `did:web`, ID Verify, or **Flow**.

## Why it keeps happening

Nothing couples the `.docx` to its source. Markdown is edited, the `.docx` silently rots, and the next reviewer flags it again (this has now been noted across several sessions without being actioned).

## Options

1. **Regenerate on demand and stop committing them** — remove the `.docx` from the repo, gitignore them, and generate when someone needs one. Removes the whole failure mode.
2. **Regenerate now and add a contract test** that fails when a one-pager's `.md` is newer than its `.docx`, the way other house rules are pinned.
3. **Regenerate now, accept the drift risk**, and treat it as a manual step at release time.

Option 1 or 2 is preferable; option 3 is what we have today and it has not held.

**Note:** regeneration should be done by whoever made the originals, or with an agreed tool — a different converter will change the formatting, which is why previous sessions left them rather than rebuilding them unilaterally.

title: Docs: flow-design.md §1.2 describes the deleted Workflow controllers in present tense
description:
Spun out of [PS-1050](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1050/docs-role-classification-said-flow-and-lineage-were-unbuilt) (the role-classification correction) — deliberately **not** fixed there, because it needs a judgement call from the doc's author.

## The problem

`docs/flow-design.md` §1.2 ("What already exists, and is reused rather than rebuilt") states in the **present tense**:

> **The surface is stubbed.** `WorkflowController` (`/Workflows`, `ssd/Controllers/WorkflowController.cs:11-23`) and `WorkflowAdminController` (`/WorkflowAdmin`, `ssd/Controllers/WorkflowAdminController.cs:10-22`) render one "coming soon" view …

**Both files no longer exist.** Flow replaced them ([PS-839](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-839/flow-07-the-flow-sidebar-section-and-routes-replacing-the-workflows)) and the routes now 301 via `LegacyWorkflowsRedirect` / `LegacyWorkflowAdminRedirect` in `ssd/Controllers/FlowController.cs`. The `file:line` references resolve to nothing, and a reader who greps for them finds no such files.

## Why it was left alone

§1.2 reads as a **design record** — it describes the pre-Flow baseline that the Flow design was reasoning against, which is legitimately historical. Rewriting it could destroy useful context about why Flow was shaped as it was.

## The decision needed

Pick one, from whoever owns the doc:

1. **Mark it historical** — a one-line "as at design time (Sep 2026); these controllers were removed in [PS-839](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-839/flow-07-the-flow-sidebar-section-and-routes-replacing-the-workflows)" note, leaving the body intact. Cheapest, preserves the reasoning.
2. **Update to present tense** — describe what replaced them, and drop the dead `file:line` refs.
3. **Leave as-is** — if the convention is that design docs are frozen at authoring time. If so, worth stating that convention somewhere, because the next reviewer will flag this again.

Low urgency: it misleads only a reader who follows the references, and the surrounding doc is otherwise accurate about Flow.

title: A bare `slot-literal-ok:` marker DOES exempt a quoted value in all five slot guards — the closing quote satisfies the "has a reason" test, contradicting systemTest/CLAUDE.md:1169
description:
**BLUF:** the platform rule says a bare `slot-literal-ok:` marker exempts nothing, but on a **quoted value** (JSON, or any line where the marker is not last) the value's own closing quote satisfies the "has a reason" test, so **a bare marker DOES exempt**. Measured in all five harness guards' shared regex shape. Found while fixing KS-1450; not introduced by it.

## The rule it contradicts

`systemTest/CLAUDE.md:1169`, verbatim:

> A deliberate exception carries `slot-literal-ok: <reason>` on the same line; a bare marker exempts nothing.

## The defect

Every implementation tests for "marker, optional whitespace, then one non-whitespace character":

```
no_hardcoded_slot_literals.test.sh   grep -vE 'slot-literal-ok:[[:space:]]*[^[:space:]]'
playwright/.../no-hardcoded-slot-literals.test.ts:79    const MARKER = /slot-literal-ok:\s*\S/
performance/.../noHardcodedSlotLiterals.test.ts:49      const MARKER = 'slot-literal-ok:'
schemathesis/.../test_no_hardcoded_slot_numbers.py:50   _OPT_OUT = "slot-literal-ok:"
akto/tests/unit/config/noTypedSlotValues.test.ts        (same shape)
```

`[^[:space:]]` / `\S` is satisfied by **any** non-space character, including `"`. So:

```
  "reason": "x 6982 slot-literal-ok:",      -> EXEMPTED   (wrong: the reason is empty)
const p = 6982; // slot-literal-ok:          -> reported   (right)
```

Driven both ways in one call against the same regex. The only reason this has never shown up is that every existing marker sits in a `#` or `//` comment at true end-of-line, where nothing follows the colon — which is also why the suites' own controls pass: each plants its bare-marker fixture into a comment, never into a quoted value. `test_no_hardcoded_slot_numbers.py:263` asserts "the bare marker does not \[exempt\]" and passes for exactly that reason.

## Why it matters now

KS-1450 is the first change to put `slot-literal-ok` markers inside JSON string values (the six `accepted.*.reason` entries of `systemTest/schemathesis/config/schemathesis-baseline.json`). Before it, that file carried **zero** markers, so the gap was latent. It is recorded as a named limitation in KS-1450's PR Test Evidence rather than fixed there, because a one-guard fix would make the five guards disagree about what a bare marker means.

## Suggested fix

Require a reason character that is not structural, e.g. tighten the class to `[^[:space:]",]` (and the JS/Python equivalents) in **all five** implementations in one change, so they stay in agreement.

**Blast radius, measured before proposing it:** exactly **2** existing marker lines repo-wide would lose exemption, and **neither needs it** — `systemTest/schemathesis/tests/unit/test_no_hardcoded_slot_numbers.py:50` (`_OPT_OUT = "slot-literal-ok:"`, a constant; the line holds no slot literal) and the shell guard's own bare-marker control line (its port is computed, not typed). So nothing that passes today would go red.

Each implementation should also gain a control that plants the bare marker into a **quoted value**, not only into a comment — the absence of that control is what hid this.

## Provenance

* Both-way measurement and the blast-radius count: Seat R 16th, 2026-10-08, during KS-1450.
* The rule: `systemTest/CLAUDE.md:1169`.
* The guard: KS-1386 (Done, Peter).

POST /api/nft/ipfs/upload: the spec doesn't mark the request body required, so a bodyless POST is "valid" and its 400 fails positive_data_acceptance
description:
## BLUF

`positive_data_acceptance` fails on `POST /api/nft/ipfs/upload`. The pair is **not** in `schemathesis-baseline.json` at `develop` b280b74ff, so it is untriaged. It is [KS-591](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-591/positive-data-acceptance-recurs-at-scale-734-failures-across-64-ops-ks)**'s class** (positive_data_acceptance at scale), on an operation [KS-591](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-591/positive-data-acceptance-recurs-at-scale-734-failures-across-64-ops-ks) doesn't name. It was raised separately, not appended, because Peter's rule is that only Backlog/Todo tickets are updated, and [KS-591](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-591/positive-data-acceptance-recurs-at-scale-734-failures-across-64-ops-ks) is In Progress.

## Evidence (re-verified from source at `develop` b280b74ff, 2026-10-07)

* **Spec** (`Blockchain/Dev/docs/openapi/secuura-api.yaml`): `POST /api/nft/ipfs/upload` has a `requestBody`, but `requestBody.required` is **unset**. Under OpenAPI an empty body is therefore spec-valid. Compare `POST /api/auth/wallet/authenticate`, where `required: true`.
* **Runtime:** a request with **no body** is answered `400 {"code":"BAD_REQUEST","message":"Validation error","details":[{"path":["data"],"message":"Required"} …]}`.
* **Live result:** Schemathesis 4.29.4, `pre-merge`, slot 2 on Peter's Mac, stack built from the [KS-1445](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1445/pin-systemtest-k6-to-the-latest-release-or-later-the-macs-native-k6-is) branch (no service changes), run `pre-merge-ks-1445-2026-10-07T14-30-16Z-slot2`, test case `P8GPsj`. Reproduce with `curl -X POST -H 'Authorization: Bearer …' http://localhost:6982/api/nft/ipfs/upload`.
* **Counts are a floor:** it fired in that run and not in the run before it on the same commit.

## Fix direction

The runtime clearly requires a body (`data` is required), so declare `requestBody.required: true` in the route's OpenAPI source. Then run `npm run generate-openapi`, restart or recreate api-gateway (it serves the spec), and check whether sibling `nft` operations have the same omission.

## Done when

- [ ] The spec marks the body required, and a bodyless POST is no longer generated as a positive case.
- [ ] The pair stops firing, or is baselined against this ticket.

Found while running [KS-1445](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1445/pin-systemtest-k6-to-the-latest-release-or-later-the-macs-native-k6-is)'s pre-merge gate.

title: Security: POST /api/notifications still creates a notification for ANY userId (BOLA) — its owning ticket KS-486 is closed and archived
description:
## BLUF

The notification BOLA recorded in Review A ([KS-486](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-486/review-a-authn-authz-tenancy-and-idor), row 1: "`POST /api/notifications` takes `userId` from body … any authenticated user pushes spoofed `security`/`system` notifications with an `actionUrl` to any user") is **still live on** `develop`. [KS-486](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-486/review-a-authn-authz-tenancy-and-idor) is **Deployed to UAT and archived**, so the defect has **no open owner**. This ticket is that owner. It was raised separately, not appended to [KS-1015](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1015/sweeps-2026-09-08-28-checkoperation-pairs-have-no-live-owner-18), because Peter's rule is that only Backlog/Todo tickets are updated, and [KS-1015](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1015/sweeps-2026-09-08-28-checkoperation-pairs-have-no-live-owner-18) is In Progress.

## Evidence (re-verified from source at `develop` b280b74ff, 2026-10-07)

* **Create:** `services/api-gateway/src/routes/notifications.ts:242`. `POST /` reads `userId` from `req.body` (`:244`) and stores the row under that user. There is no self-or-admin check against the caller's token.

title: No malware scanning anywhere in the upload path — arbitrary bytes under an allowed extension are accepted, encrypted, anchored and served back byte-identical to external recipients, on all three deployed environments
description:
## BLUF

Secuura accepts a file, encrypts it, hashes it, anchors it, and later hands **the same bytes** to external recipients over a share link. At no point is the content scanned for malware. There is no antivirus service in the local, UAT or production stacks, and the only acceptance check is the **file extension** — so a document carrying a macro-bearing `.docx`, a malicious PDF, or any arbitrary payload named `.pdf` passes through intact and is redistributed with the platform's own assurance language attached to it.

Raised partly as a **decision**: scanning may be deliberately out of scope, and plenty of platforms push it to the recipient's endpoint. But it is not written down anywhere I can find, and the product's framing ("verified", "unaltered", "genuine") invites a recipient to read a Secuura link as safer than an email attachment. Found 7 Oct 2026 on slot 4.

## Evidence

**1. No scanner exists in any environment.** `grep -i -E "clamav|clamd|virus|malware|scan"` across `ssd/dep-ssd-local/docker-compose.yml`, `ssd/dep-aws-uat/docker-compose.yml` and `ssd/dep-aws-secuura/docker-compose.yml` returns **nothing**. The running slot-4 stack is `nginx`, `obeden-ssd`, `db`, `mailpit`, `phpmyadmin` — no scanning sidecar, no queue, no hook.

**2. Acceptance is extension-only** — measured today, consistent with `PS-974`:

| Uploaded | Result |
| -- | -- |
| `liar.pdf` — the 16 ASCII bytes `not a pdf at all` | **registered** (id 9) |
| `header-only.pdf` — `%PDF-1.4` and nothing else | **registered** (id 10) |
| `double.pdf.exe` — a valid PDF renamed | refused: *"File extension '.exe' is not allowed…"* |

So the gate stops a file **called** `.exe` and admits **any bytes whatsoever** called `.pdf`. The allowed set is ten extensions including `.doc`, `.docx`, `.xls`, `.xlsx` — the macro-bearing Office formats — see `PS-1034`, which also asks whether that list is intended.

**3. The bytes come back unchanged.** A view-only share of a PDF streams the original bytes to an anonymous recipient (`application/pdf`, byte-identical). `PS-902` records that an Office file is handed over in full on the same path. Nothing in between inspects content.

**4. Anchoring lends it credibility.** The file is hashed and anchored, and the recipient is shown *"This is the registered document — matches Secuura's record exactly and has not been altered."* That sentence is true and is about **provenance**. A non-expert reader will hear it as **safety**.

## What I did NOT do, and why

**I did not run an EICAR test.** The standard way to prove "nothing scans this" is to upload the EICAR test string — 68 harmless bytes every scanner detects by agreement. Peter runs **BitDefender** on the host, which would quarantine the fixture mid-test, fire an endpoint alert, and prove nothing the above does not already establish. The absence of any scanner in the compose files plus the successful `liar.pdf` upload settles it without creating a quarantine event on a developer machine.

If you want empirical confirmation before deciding, the right place is a UAT box with the host AV accounted for, not a laptop. Happy to run it there.

## The decision to make

1. **Is scanning in scope at all?** Legitimate answers include "no — recipients' endpoints scan, and we say so", or "yes — at ingest".
2. **If no:** say so where it matters. The recipient page and the Verify result should not let "unaltered" be read as "safe". One sentence — *"Secuura confirms this document has not changed since it was registered. It does not scan for viruses."* — closes the gap at zero cost, and is the cheapest resolution of this ticket.
3. **If yes:** ingest-time scan (ClamAV sidecar is the usual shape, and would be a container beside the app in each compose file), with a decision on what happens to a positive — refuse at Register, or quarantine and flag — and what the owner and any existing recipients are told.
4. **Either way:** `PS-1034` asks whether `.doc` / `.xls` / `.xlsx` belong in the allowed list. Macro formats are the classic delivery vehicle, and that question is really part of this one.

## Why it matters

* The platform is a **distribution** channel to third parties outside the organisation, which is the case malware scanning exists for. The recipient has no relationship with the sender's security posture.
* The assurance language is the aggravating factor. "Verified", "Integrity verified", "has not been altered" are all accurate about provenance and all read as reassurance.
* GDPR Art. 32 (appropriate technical measures, proportionate to risk) and Art. 5(1)(f) integrity and confidentiality: [https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2016/679/oj](<https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2016/679/oj>) · UK GDPR/DPA 2018: [https://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/2018/12/contents](<https://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/2018/12/contents>) · Singapore PDPA 2012 s.24: [https://sso.agc.gov.sg/Act/PDPA2012](<https://sso.agc.gov.sg/Act/PDPA2012>)
* OWASP ASVS 4.0 **V12.4 / V12.5 — File Storage**: files obtained from untrusted sources should be scanned by antivirus to prevent serving known-malicious content: [https://owasp.org/www-project-application-security-verification-standard/](<https://owasp.org/www-project-application-security-verification-standard/>) · CWE-434 Unrestricted Upload of File with Dangerous Type: [https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/434.html](<https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/434.html>)
* Enterprise buyers ask this in security questionnaires. "We do not scan, and here is why" is a fine answer; "we have not considered it" is not.

## Priority note

Set **High** because it spans every deployed environment and the mitigation for option 2 is a single sentence of copy. Downgrade to Medium if the ruling is that scanning is out of scope and the disclosure wording is all that is wanted — the exposure is real but it is the recipient's endpoint that is the last line either way, and no Secuura-side boundary is being crossed.

## Reproduce

1. Sign in and go to `/Register`.
2. Create a file containing any bytes you like and name it `probe.pdf` — e.g. `printf 'not a pdf at all' > probe.pdf`.
3. Press **Choose files** (`verify-browse-btn` equivalent on Register) and register it → it is accepted, encrypted and appears in `/MyDocuments`.
4. Share it view-only to an external address, open the link anonymously, and fetch the document — the bytes returned are byte-identical to what was uploaded.
5. Confirm no scanner is involved: `docker ps` on the slot shows no scanning container, and `grep -i clamav ssd/dep-*/docker-compose.yml` returns nothing.

## Acceptance

* A written ruling on whether ingest scanning is in scope, recorded in `docs/` (suggest `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` or a new `docs/file-safety.md`) rather than only in this ticket.
* **If out of scope:** the recipient page and the Verify result state that Secuura confirms provenance, not safety; the wording is reviewed so "unaltered" cannot be read as "scanned".
* **If in scope:** uploads are scanned before the `upload` chain row is written; a positive result is refused at Register with a clear message and never anchored; the behaviour is documented and covered by a test.

**Playwright test — disclosure route only. NO malware sample in the suite.**

**Ruled out (Peter, 7 Oct): no Playwright test that uploads a malware sample, including EICAR.** A test artefact that every scanner detects by design would be quarantined by endpoint protection on developer machines (BitDefender here) and on any CI runner, so the spec would fail for reasons unrelated to the product, intermittently, and would alarm whoever's machine caught it. The suite must not carry one, and no fixture generating one at runtime either.

*If the ruling is **out of scope** (disclosure):* a spec — suggest `systemTest/tests/functional/file_safety_disclosure.spec.ts` — asserting the agreed wording is present. This is pure text assertion, no sample of any kind:

1. The recipient page `/SDViewDownload/v/{token}` contains the scanning-disclaimer sentence, for both a view-only and a view-and-download share.
2. The Verify result modal contains it, on **both** the verified and the no-matching-record outcome — so the reassurance and the refusal both carry it.
3. The wording is driven from one constant shared with the view, so copy and test cannot drift.
4. **Control:** the existing verdict text is unchanged.

All of 1–3 fail on `develop` today; no such sentence exists anywhere.

*If the ruling is **in scope** (scanning):* verify the wiring **without** a malicious sample:

* an integration or unit test with the scanner client **stubbed** to return a positive verdict, asserting Register refuses, no `upload` chain row is written, and nothing is anchored — this is where the behaviour belongs anyway, per `CLAUDE.md`'s "a rule belongs in the xUnit suite";
* a deployment/contract check that the scanner service is present and reachable in each environment (a health-endpoint assertion), so a silently-absent scanner cannot pass as a working one — which is the actual failure mode worth guarding;
* a Playwright test only for the **user-visible** half: that a refused upload shows a clear message, exercised with the stub rather than with real malware.

Any genuine end-to-end check against a live scanner is a manual, one-off verification on a stack host with the host AV accounted for — recorded as evidence on this ticket, not automated into the suite.

## Related

`PS-974` (Backlog) — extension-only validation, no MIME or content sniff; the mechanism underneath this ticket. · `PS-1034` — the allowed-extension list is undocumented and includes the macro-bearing Office formats; the question there and the decision here should be answered together. · `PS-891` (Todo) — Register accepts structurally invalid PDFs. · `PS-902` — Office files handed to view-only recipients in full.

## Environment

platform-s `develop` **2d9a6639** · platform-k `develop` **2c27ddfee** · slot 4 (S `:5422`, K `:7182`). 7 Oct 2026. Compose files read at the worktree's `develop`; upload behaviour driven black-box through the UI with the server responses captured. No malicious or test-malware sample was created at any point.

nodes.body:
**Fix for the crash above: [#1405](https://github.com/Secuura/platform-s/pull/1405), open onto round 13 and not merged.** Stuart, 5 Nov 2026: "Fix the crash".

- `_NoMalwareScanNote` moves to `Views/Shared/`, and `_VerifyResult` names `_SignatureChecks` by full path. What the note says doesn't change.
- A new test fails on any bare partial name in those two views that isn't in `Views/Shared/`. It failed against the old layout.
- Focused xUnit: 1,865 passed, 0 failed.
- On slot 2 rebuilt from `e1614b2`, the six specs that failed all pass, with no further `_NoMalwareScanNote` errors and no 5xx on a Flow route.

The full xUnit and full systemTest haven't been run on this commit.

**Defect found by round 13's full systemTest on `a6bad9e`, from [#1390](https://github.com/Secuura/platform-s/pull/1390). Not on `develop`: the file exists only on round 13.**

`ssd/Views/Verify/_VerifyResult.cshtml` (lines 246 and 268) calls `Html.PartialAsync("_NoMalwareScanNote")` by bare name, and the note lives in `Views/Verify/`. `Views/Flow/_FlowVerifyIntegrity.cshtml:37` renders `_VerifyResult` by full path, so inside a Flow request the bare name is searched in `Views/Flow/`, `Views/Shared/` and `Pages/Shared/`, and isn't found.

App log, slot 2, during the run: `InvalidOperationException: The partial view '_NoMalwareScanNote' was not found`, 8 times up to the moment I checked. The stack frames are in `_VerifyResult`.

**Why xUnit didn't catch it:** `NoMalwareScanDisclosureTests` reads the view source. It never renders the view from another controller.

**Likely affected, not yet confirmed one by one:** Verification-flow failures in the run, including `flow_verify:262`, `a11y_seeded_states:144`, `busy_overlay:342` and `k_live/flow_completion:189`.

No change has been made while the suite is running.

description:

title: start-secuura.sh --rebuild leaves ~30 untagged images per slot per rebuild (and interrupted rebuilds pin them)
description:
Raised from platform-s ([PS-1012](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1012/dep-ssd-local-systemtest-make-stack-slots-safe-across-two-dropbox>)) rather than fixed from there, because `Start_Up/start-secuura.sh` is platform-k's.

## What happens

`docker compose` names each built image `<compose project>-<service>`: `platform-k-*` for slot 1, `secuura_slot2-*` for slot 2, and so on. `start-secuura.sh --rebuild` builds every service again (the serial per-service `docker compose build` from [KS-345](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-345/start-secuurash-rebuild-hangs-on-the-full-33-service-compose-bake)). Each rebuild moves those tags to new images, and the previous image of each service is left untagged as `<none>`. That's about 30 images per slot per rebuild, some of them 0.6–2.2 GB. Nothing in the script prunes images or the build cache. A grep of `start-secuura.sh` for `prune`, `rmi` and `image rm` finds nothing.

**The worse case is an interrupted rebuild.** On 2026-10-02 the Pro had 29 `<none>` images, every one held by a container in K slot 1's project (`platform-k`) that was `Created` **but never started**: `secuura-auth`, `secuura-api-gateway`, `secuura-originate` and others. Docker won't prune an image a container uses, so those stayed until someone removed them by hand (Stuart did).

## Measured (MacBook Pro, Docker Desktop, 2026-10-07)

* `docker system df`: images 20.7 GB, of which 1.76 GB is reclaimable. The **build cache is 39.6 GB, of which 22.65 GB is reclaimable**, mostly entries last used in the previous two days by slot rebuilds.

## Suggested fix (for Kamil's judgement)

The platform-s side is doing this in [PS-1012](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1012/dep-ssd-local-systemtest-make-stack-slots-safe-across-two-dropbox) / [Secuura/platform-s#909](https://linear.app/secuura/review/ps-1012-stack-slots-safe-across-two-dropbox-synced-machines-994c737d0439):

* **Label every build with its owner:** for compose, a `labels:` entry under each service's `build:` such as `com.secuura.slot-image=<project>-<service>`, or one label per project.
* **Before rebuilding,** run `docker image prune -f --filter label=…` scoped to this compose project. Without `-a`, this removes only dangling, unused images from earlier builds of this slot. It never touches another slot, platform-s, a tagged image, or an image a container still uses.
* **After an interrupted rebuild,** remove that slot's `Created`-but-never-started containers, so they stop pinning old images.
* **Don't prune the build cache automatically.** It's shared by every slot on both platforms, so pruning it makes everyone's next build cold. Documenting a manual `docker builder prune --filter until=168h -f` is enough.

title: Akto full scan reports three LOW HEADER_ALL_KEYS_INVALID_VALUES results (wallet-status ×2, GET /api/settings/notifications) that no ticket or allowlist covers — classify them: by-design or a finding
description:
## BLUF

The one `test:security` run on 2026-10-07 reported three **LOW** results from `HEADER_ALL_KEYS_INVALID_VALUES` on two public routes. No ticket covers them and no allowlist mechanism can express them. They are probably expected for public routes that ignore request headers, but that is **not established**, and today they fail the Full OWASP workflow on their own because the gate fails on any severity, LOW included.

## Measured (slot 1, Mac, Akto 2.37.1, 2026-10-07, run `security`, full OWASP summary `6ac60a95a141e9203079d8bf`, 50,450 result docs)

| Result |  |
| -- | -- |
| Template | `HEADER_ALL_KEYS_INVALID_VALUES`, category INPUT, severity LOW, CWE-20, nature INTRUSIVE |
| Docs for the template | 350; **90 executed** (a captured exchange); **3 flagged** (raw `vulnerable: true`); 347 not |
| Flagged 1 | `GET /api/auth/wallet/status/dt-seed-7` |
| Flagged 2 | `GET /api/auth/wallet/status/STRING` (the `{walletAddress}` placeholder) |
| Flagged 3 | `GET /api/settings/notifications` |

**What the template does** (read from the library file): it selects a 2xx, non-error response, replaces **every request header value** with invalid values, and flags the result when an attempt still returns 2xx with a body more than 90% identical to the original and the same schema.

**What the data shows.** Each flagged result has 4 attempts. Attempts 0–2 returned **400** (102-character body, 0% match). **Attempt 3 returned 200** (50 characters for wallet-status, 83 for settings/notifications) with a **100% match** — that attempt is what tripped the template. The altered request carried 3 headers for wallet-status (`host`, `x-akto-ignore`, `authorization`) and 2 for settings/notifications (`host`, `x-akto-ignore`). Which values attempt 3 used was **not examined**.

## Why this needs a ticket

* The two routes are already known to be public: `wallet/status` is public by necessity and cannot be allowlisted ([KS-1009](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1009/security-get-apiauthwalletstatus-returns-userid-role-to-any-anonymous); Kamil, PR #802, quoted in `endpointFalsePositives.ts`: "the registry has no representation for a parameterised route"), and `GET /api/settings/notifications` keeps optional auth by ruling ([KS-719](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-719/security-put-apiprivacysettings-and-apisettingsnotifications-accept), quoted in the same file from `routes/admin.ts`: "The GET above keeps optional auth so anonymous readers still get the documented defaults").
* No existing allowlist mechanism fits. `KNOWN_FALSE_POSITIVE_ENDPOINT_TESTS` admits two ruled kinds with compile-time bounds (`public-by-design` only for `REMOVE_TOKENS`; `similarity-undiscriminating` only for three templates — Kamil's [KS-708](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-708/security-akto-add-user-id-bola-high-on-get-apiplatformaudit-log) bound), and a LOW from an INPUT template is neither. The wallet-status URL also carries a path parameter the registry cannot express.
* The gate (`assertNoVulnerabilities`) fails on any severity. So even after [KS-1009](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1009/security-get-apiauthwalletstatus-returns-userid-role-to-any-anonymous)'s HIGH is fixed, any of these LOWs that recurs will keep the Full OWASP workflow red.

## Not established

* **Whether it is a real input-validation gap (CWE-20) or expected** for routes that never read the headers being altered. For `settings/notifications` the altered headers do not include `authorization`, so "it ignores a bad token" does not explain it.
* **Why it was not reported before.** The 2026-10-05 full runs on slots 2 and 4 listed only the nginx LOW ([KS-1421](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1421/akto-security-tier-fails-every-run-on-the-accepted-server-nginx-low)). This stack's collection also carried authenticated samples for these URLs (a `feed-har` added them, 343 → 349 endpoints). Not shown to be the cause.
* Related, not claimed: [KS-1207](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1207/security-an-unknown-sk-key-on-an-optional-auth-mount-skips-the) (In Progress, Kamil) covers an unknown key on an optional-auth mount skipping the Bearer check.

## Proposed next steps (smallest first)

1. Re-run **only** this template on those three URLs with a targeted Akto `CUSTOM` run (`apiInfoKeyList`; the technique used for [KS-1421](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1421/akto-security-tier-fails-every-run-on-the-accepted-server-nginx-low)) and read attempt 3's actual request: which headers, which values.
2. Classify each: by design, or a finding. Kamil's call for the platform side.
3. If by design: accept it by a **narrow** rule with the ruling quoted verbatim (the [KS-1421](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1421/akto-security-tier-fails-every-run-on-the-accepted-server-nginx-low) pattern), and a control showing another endpoint or template still fails. Extending the allowlist's compile-time bound needs Kamil's ruling first. If a finding: a platform ticket for Kamil.

## Done means

1. Each of the three results has a recorded classification, with the attempt-3 evidence.
2. If by design: the Full OWASP workflow no longer fails on them, a control still fails, and Console = Akto = HTML agree on the known-FP and vulnerable counts.
3. If a finding: it is ticketed for the owner and the test keeps failing honestly.

Found while verifying [KS-1440](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1440/akto-image-23610-2371-release-v2371-2026-10-06-both-local-tags) (PR [Secuura/Distributed_Secuura#1411](https://linear.app/secuura/review/ks-1440-akto-23610-2371-with-the-ks-1416-ks-1421-and-ks-724-fixes-it-5f3e7f62426b), merged; history entry PR [Secuura/Distributed_Secuura#1412](https://linear.app/secuura/review/docs-project-history-for-the-2026-10-07-akto-2371-batch-one-pr-merged-06305b942330)). Nothing was changed for this finding.

title: Connector keys are minted `anchors:read` and `documents:revoke`, but neither scope is enforced anywhere — anchor reads are scope-ungated and revoke has no scope check
description:
## Summary

`register-connector` mints Platform S connector keys with nine scopes, including `anchors:read` and `documents:revoke`. Neither scope is checked anywhere in the request path. So a connector key's anchor reads are not scope-gated at all: a key minted WITHOUT `anchors:read` would still read anchors. And `documents:revoke` has no effect: the revoke route checks ownership only. That breaks the deny-by-default rule ([KS-539](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-539/k-define-governing-rules-for-document-operations-by-agents) R2: scopes are the authority) for these two scopes. This is a code read; nothing has been probed live yet.

+++ Evidence (read at source, `develop` `f556373b9`, 2026-10-06)

**Minted:** `services/api-gateway/src/routes/platform.ts:485-489` (`S_CONNECTOR_SCOPES`) includes both `'documents:revoke'` (:486) and `'anchors:read'` (:487). Vocabulary: `packages/shared/src/security/scopes.ts:42` and `:76`.

`anchors:read` **— enforced nowhere:**

* `api-gateway/src/routes/proxy.ts` gates only the two anchor WRITES: `POST /api/anchors` and `POST /api/anchors/batch` carry `attachScopes, requireScope('anchors:write')` (:852-863).
* The catch-all `router.use('/api/anchors', authenticateToken(true), proxy('anchoring', …))` (:865-868) has no `requireScope`, so every anchor read reaches anchoring with authentication only.
* A search of `services/*/src` and `packages/shared/src` (tests excluded) finds `anchors:read` only in the minting list and the vocabulary — no check in anchoring either.

`documents:revoke` **— enforced nowhere:**

* The other document verbs check their scope through `isAllowedByRoleOrScope(...)`: create and version `documents:write` (`documents.ts:372`, `:1983`), transfer `documents:transfer-custody` (`:1599`), share `documents:share` (`:2172`).
* The revoke route (`documents.ts:2344` onward) has no scope check. It gates on `document.owner?.id !== user.id` → 403. A connector principal is never the owner, so connectors cannot revoke at all. Your own [KS-566](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-566/ks-539-g-1-split-alignment-add-onbehalfof-to-revoke-drop-it-from) finding, 2026-08-26, verbatim: *"A connector principal cannot revoke at all"*.

### Not verified

* No live probe yet with a connector key minted without `anchors:read`. Whether anchoring further limits reads per tenant was not checked.
* Severity therefore not asserted beyond "the scope is not checked".

### Related, deliberately not duplicated

* Whether connectors should be able to revoke at all is the open question you put to Stuart on [KS-566](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-566/ks-539-g-1-split-alignment-add-onbehalfof-to-revoke-drop-it-from) (2026-08-26, Kam's ruling "ask Stuart to reconcile [PS-616](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-616/s-shipped-ps-569-ahead-of-ks-566-so-lifecycle-event-and-flat-anchor) first"). This ticket does not reopen that. It only records that the minted scope is dead either way: if the answer is "no", stop minting it; if "yes", the route needs the scope check plus an owner-gate change.
* Duplicate check, Platform K + Platform S, 2026-10-06: no ticket names either scope's enforcement. [KS-71](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-71/q6-scope-aware-rbac-in-originate-sk-connector-role-can-post) (Done) built scope-aware RBAC for create. [KS-858](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-858/security-class-a-scope-gate-mounted-as-an-exact-route-above-a-catch) (Deployed) is a different class: scope-gate bypass by path spelling.

### Suggested direction (your call)

1. Gate anchor reads with `requireScope('anchors:read')` for key callers (as `/api/documents` does with `documents:read`), or stop minting the scope.
2. Resolve `documents:revoke` per the [KS-566](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-566/ks-539-g-1-split-alignment-add-onbehalfof-to-revoke-drop-it-from) answer.

systemTest coverage follows on Peter's side: [KS-571](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-571/systemtest-schemathesis-ks-539-agent-document-operation-rules) item 3 (R2, deny-by-default) / [KS-568](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-568/systemtest-schemathesis-sk-connector-identity-regression-coverage-ks).

+++

Refs: [KS-480](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-480/sk-k-side-support-consistent-userorg-ownership-credential) / [KS-539](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-539/k-define-governing-rules-for-document-operations-by-agents) (rules R2) · [KS-566](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-566/ks-539-g-1-split-alignment-add-onbehalfof-to-revoke-drop-it-from) (revoke question) · [KS-571](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-571/systemtest-schemathesis-ks-539-agent-document-operation-rules) / [KS-568](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-568/systemtest-schemathesis-sk-connector-identity-regression-coverage-ks) (systemTest) · [KS-486](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-486/review-a-authn-authz-tenancy-and-idor) (Review A). Raised by agent on Peter's behalf.

title: systemTest: pin originate's unhandledRejection posture (split from KS-572) — waits on KS-1427's ruling
description:
## Summary

Split from [KS-572](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-572/systemtest-schemathesis-pin-the-ks-546-unhandledrejection-posture) on 2026-10-06. [KS-572](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-572/systemtest-schemathesis-pin-the-ks-546-unhandledrejection-posture) pins what [KS-546](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-546/unhandledrejection-posture-api-gateway-survives-logalert-everything) actually shipped:

* `UNHANDLED_REJECTION_MODE=survive` on the api-gateway only, in compose and bicep;
* the real [KS-529](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-529/gateway-intermittent-502-bad-gateway-to-healthy-upstreams-under-sweep) guard, no longer a copy;
* the live malformed-body run with `RestartCount` unchanged;
* the gateway's boot line `unhandledRejection mode: survive`.

What [KS-572](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-572/systemtest-schemathesis-pin-the-ks-546-unhandledrejection-posture) **can't** pin yet is originate. `services/originate/src/index.ts:72-77` registers its own listener that logs and doesn't exit, so originate survives rejections, yet the gateway comment cites it as fail-fast. [KS-1427](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1427/unhandledrejection-posture-as-shipped-differs-from-ks-546s) asks Kamil which is intended.

## Waiting on

[KS-1427](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1427/unhandledrejection-posture-as-shipped-differs-from-ks-546s) (Kamil, Backlog): survive or fail-fast for originate, and whether `setupGracefulShutdown` gets callers.

## Test (once ruled)

* **If survive:** assert originate declares it in config (`UNHANDLED_REJECTION_MODE=survive`). Extend [KS-572](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-572/systemtest-schemathesis-pin-the-ks-546-unhandledrejection-posture)'s "no other service declares survive" config assertion to an explicit allow-list of gateway + originate.
* **If fail-fast:** a live leg triggers an unhandled rejection in originate (only if a black-box trigger exists; otherwise a container-level check of the boot-logged mode) and asserts the process exits and restarts with the trace logged.
* **If** `setupGracefulShutdown` **gets callers:** sample one non-gateway service's boot log for `unhandledRejection mode: exit`.
* Red against the current shape, green after. Appears on all three surfaces (console, Schemathesis results, HTML report).
