**BLUF:** Delivered: PR 1655 merged as 86df4f5a52cc on develop, deployed to kintsugi at ee1e1b832115. Verified by git at ee1e1b832115, not observed live. Left open: N-1382-2 and gate note N1, as comment 4d6333ed records.

- **In the deployed tree:** 38 of the squash's 41 added non-test lines are present verbatim at ee1e1b832115 (control: 8 of them were already present at its parent), so the change both password doors make (revoke the account's other sessions, fail closed when the session store cannot revoke) is in the deployed source, with later edits to 3 lines.
- **Still open:** N-1382-2 is untouched, and gate BS1's note N1 is a residual gap (comment 4d6333ed).

## BLUF
**MERGED to `develop` as `86df4f5a52cc36b40276b441900627bf0a4c5de5` (squash of PR #1655), verified at source.** Both password doors now revoke the account's sessions and both fail closed when the session store cannot revoke. Gate BS1 (Opus, tier 1, DELTA round 2 of 2) returned GO WITH NOTE, 0 blockers, 5 notes. **KS-1407 stays OPEN: N-1382-2 is untouched, and gate note N1 is a real residual gap.** Not deployed.

## Verified at source, not from the merge response
- merge sha `86df4f5a52cc36b40276b441900627bf0a4c5de5`; **tree `2346900a5105fe24f8b3777a73123dd6df80a2a5`**, equal to the landing the gate and the GO both predicted and to my own `merge-tree` figure;
- **exactly ONE parent**, `f4259b8ed3875316a269d3228031c198eec39edd`, which was `develop` at the GO;
- 8 files, **+775/-3**; subject 82 characters; **0 attribution trailers**; `develop`'s tip is now this commit.

## What landed
`revokeAllUserSessions` returns **0 without throwing** when the store is unreachable, while `createSession` throws in the same condition. The first landing therefore wrote the password, burned the single-use reset token and answered 200 while revoking nothing, and the old sessions validated again once Redis recovered. Both routes now confirm the revocation is possible **before** the write and **re-assert after** it, because a pre-write check alone is a check-then-act.

Route-local, using the already-exported `isRedisAvailable`, so `revokeAllUserSessions` keeps its contract for its two other callers. The refusals differ on purpose: reset leaves the token unburned; change-password says the password **WAS** changed.

**Change-password revokes the caller's own session**, so the client must sign in again. No in-repo client calls either route — measured, with controls.

## Residual, and why this ticket does not close
- **N-1382-2** untouched: the e2e case posts to `/api/auth/change-password`, a route that does not exist.
- **Gate note N1 (MEDIUM), my own declared gap A5:** a revocation that **throws** after the write is fail-closed on reset (500, token kept, the retry works) but only half fail-closed on change-password — the password **is** written, an old session is **ACTIVE** after recovery, and the caller is told only "unexpected error". My `.catch(() => 0)` arm reds **0 of the 23** cells; the gate's own probes kill it. Recorded on KS-1692 with the gate's fix shape, for a later tier-1 round.
- **N2 (LOW-MEDIUM):** `session.ts:323`'s unguarded `del` can orphan the remaining sessions mid-loop. Also on KS-1692.
- **N4 (mine, trivial):** change-password's post-write 503 advises signing in again although that path leaves the caller's own session alive, and two of my comments cite `:317-318`/`:156` where the head has `:316`/`:155`. Both ride the KS-1692 round, on the gate's instruction, rather than a new PR.
- Tickets filed from the gate's notes: **KS-1690**, **KS-1691**, **KS-1692**.
- **The four platform suites did not run** (no local stack, no Docker for this seat) and **no real Redis was driven** — the gate's probes used a fake too.

## Next
An auth deploy carries this; it has not happened.

## BLUF
**Gate BO1 returned NO GO on the first head with one blocker, and it was right. Round 2 is pushed to the same PR #1655, head `893506989ae7c656e69408d4a6489b052b728e33`, READY FOR DELTA GATE, tier 1.** The reset route failed OPEN when the session store could not revoke: `revokeAllUserSessions` returns **0 with no throw** when Redis is unreachable, so the route wrote the password, burned the single-use token and answered 200 — and the old sessions validated again once Redis recovered. Both routes now fail closed on **both** sides of the write. Three tickets filed from the gate's notes. Nothing deployed.

## Recommendation
Delta-gate `893506989ae7c656e69408d4a6489b052b728e33`. This is round 2 of 2 under the cap, so a second NO GO ships nothing and goes to Kam. Merge on a GO naming that head; then an auth deploy, which has not happened.

## The blocker, and why my first body under-stated it
I had documented the case where the revocation **throws**. The real failure is quieter: `services/auth/src/services/session.ts:317-318` is `if (!redisAvailable) return 0;` — a silent zero. The route logged `sessionsRevoked: 0`, indistinguishable from an account that had no sessions. **The same module throws in the same condition elsewhere** (`createSession`, `:156`), and that inconsistency is the root.

## The fix
Route-local, fail closed before the write **and** re-asserted after the revoke:
- **before the write** — store unavailable → 503, nothing written, the reset token **not** burned;
- **after the revoke** — re-assert, because the pre-write check alone is a check-then-act and the store dropping inside that window reproduces the defect exactly. Reset leaves the token **unburned** so a retry finishes the job; change-password says the password **WAS** changed, because telling that caller it failed would send them back to a password that no longer works.

`isRedisAvailable()` was already exported and `ServiceUnavailableError` already existed, so **`services/session.ts` is untouched** — deliberately. `revokeAllUserSessions` has exactly two other product callers (the user-erasure subscriber at `userErasedSubscriber.ts:50` and the admin status change at `routes/users.ts:838`), and changing its contract changes both; that is a wider ruling and is filed as KS-1692.

## Evidence
- **9 new cells** over two new files pin both halves of the failure mode, which no cell covered before. Each file carries a healthy-store positive control, and change-password carries an inverted-want control on the wording.
- **Red-proof, 5 arms**, each anchor proved unique, type-checked (an arm that will not compile is inadmissible, not a result), restored by content with a sha256 assert:
  - **A1′** the exact pre-fix product (guards *and* imports reverted) → **7 of 9 red**;
  - **A2** pre-write guards removed → 7 of 9;
  - **A3** only my **post-write re-assert** removed → **4 of 9 red**, which is what justifies that addition by measurement rather than argument;
  - **A4** the message reworded to claim failure → the inverted-want control fires;
  - **A5** `.catch(() => 0)` → **nothing red**, a negative arm that documents a real gap: these cells do not cover a *throwing* revoke.
- **Whole `services/auth` suite: 103 files / 1119 tests / 0 failed, 0 skipped.** Baseline on a clean checkout of the base: 99 files / 1096 tests / 0 failed. +23 cells, **0 vanished**. `tsc` rc 0.
- **Four cell files now declare a healthy session store, one line each, with no assertion changed** — proved by identical `expect(` and cell counts before and after. Two of them (`ks1005`, `ks1052`) **predate this PR** and were found by running the whole suite rather than by reading the route: 6 cells there pin the happy path of both doors without declaring the store's state. Neither is a defect in those tests; the product now has a precondition it did not have.
- Preflight, quoted as printed: `PREFLIGHT INCOMPLETE — 13/16 legs ran, 3 SKIPPED. Nothing failed.` Legs 3, 4, 8 need a local stack. Leg 16 type-checks auth's test files: **154 examined, 42 errors, 42 baselined, 0 new**.
- Push rc 0, 623s, a **fast-forward** `8e5308a87..893506989` — `origin` was proved an ancestor beforehand, so the hook's non-fast-forward refusal was satisfied, not bypassed.
- Landing on live develop predicted **`2346900a5105fe24f8b3777a73123dd6df80a2a5`**, merge-tree rc 0, exactly 8 files. Develop moved 6 commits during the round; its advance is 9 files with **0 overlap** with mine (negative control 9).

## Tickets filed from the gate's notes
- **KS-1690** (Bug, High) — the OAuth `refresh_token` grant never reads `decoded.sessionId`, so a revoked session's refresh token still redeems and mints a new session (gate measured 200 twice, 2 live sessions). Scoped to the origin-session half: **KS-1150 R-2 already covers the rotation/denylist half of that branch and is still open.** Overlapping but distinct; neither should be closed as a duplicate of the other.
- **KS-1691** (Bug, Medium) — an in-flight request resurrects a revoked session, which is then missing from `user_sessions:<id>` so a second revoke returns 0 and cannot reach it.
- **KS-1692** (Bug, High) — the silent zero as it reaches the erasure subscriber and the admin path.

## Still not covered
- **The four platform suites did not run** (no local stack, no Docker for this seat). This touches a runtime surface, so that is a real gap.
- **No real Redis was driven** — the gate's probes used a fake too.
- **N5** (a login straddling the write) is reasoned, not run, and left as residue.
- **N-1382-2** untouched, which is why this stays `Refs`.
- No migration, schema or config change.

## BLUF
**N-1382-1 is BUILT and raised as PR #1655 (https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/1655), head `8e5308a87e14d4a4796e5f838de30dae0838a5bf`, READY FOR GATE, tier 1.** Both password doors now revoke the account's sessions. **The behaviour change a reviewer must agree to: change-password revokes the caller's OWN session, so the client must sign in again.** Nothing is deployed. N-1382-2 stays open, so this is `Refs`, not a close.

## Recommendation
Gate it as tier 1 — it is a session and credential surface, and it does not merge on a green run alone. Merge on a GO naming head `8e5308a87e14d4a4796e5f838de30dae0838a5bf`; then an auth deploy, which has not happened.

## What changed
| door | file | placement | why there |
|---|---|---|---|
| change-password | `services/auth/src/routes/users.ts` (+3/-0) | after `updateUserOrThrow` | the write throws if it did not land, so a revocation can never follow a non-write |
| reset-password | `services/auth/src/routes/auth.ts` (+4/-1) | after the write, **before** `consumeResetToken` | a revocation that throws leaves the single-use token **unburned**, so the user can retry instead of holding a changed password and a dead token |

`revokeAllUserSessions` is account-wide and nothing spares `req.sessionId`, so the caller's own access token stops validating after a successful change. That is deliberate. The alternative (`getUserSessions` + `revokeSession` minus the caller's own) needs two functions the existing session mock does not provide; it was neither built nor ruled.

If the revocation throws (a Redis fault) **after** the password was written, the request answers an error although the password did change. Reset: the token is unburned, so a retry works. Change-password: the user retries with the new password as the current one.

## Evidence
- **Red-first, reproduced here rather than quoted: 6 failed / 14 run** — 3 of 7 in each new cell file, the three RED assertion cells, with all 8 CONTROL cells green and 0 load-failure signatures. Green after: **14 passed / 14 run, 0 skipped**. `tsc --noEmit -p services/auth` rc 0.
- **`services/auth` suite, both ends measured on real trees:** baseline **99 files / 1096 tests / 0 failed** on a clean checkout of the base; after **101 files / 1110 tests / 0 failed**. +14 cells, **0 vanished**.
- **13 mutation arms, 13 killed, 0 survivors, so no cell was added.** Including two that pin *which* account is revoked (revoke a different account id reds R1 on both doors). Each arm proved its anchor unique before tampering, type-checked (a mutant that will not compile is inadmissible, not a survivor), and restored by content with a sha256 equality assertion.
- **Who this breaks: nobody, measured.** No in-repo client calls either route. `me/change-password` has 8 hits, every one the route, the generated spec, the OpenAPI registration or a test; `auth/reset-password` has **zero** call sites under `frontend/` or `sdk/`. Controls: the same search shape finds `auth/login` in 6 files under `frontend/` and 105 repo-wide. `frontend/admin/src/pages/Profile.tsx:49` `handleChangePassword` posts to `/api/auth/password/reset-request` — it emails a reset link and never calls this route. Both SDKs expose no password or session surface. **Equally: no in-repo client exercises this behaviour at all.**
- Pre-push preflight, in-hook: **`PREFLIGHT INCOMPLETE — 13/16 legs ran, 3 SKIPPED. Nothing failed.`** Legs 3, 4 and 8 need a local stack that was not up. Quoting it as the gate printed it, including its own line *"This is NOT a pass."* Leg 16 type-checks auth's test files against the ratchet baseline: **152 files examined, 42 errors, 42 baselined, 0 new**.

## Not covered
- **The four platform suites (Schemathesis / Akto / Playwright / Performance k6) did not run** — they need the local stack, and this seat is held off Docker on this machine. This does touch a runtime surface, so that is a real gap, stated rather than skipped.
- **No real Redis was driven.** Both cell files replace the session service, so what is pinned is that the call is made, once, for the right account, at the right point in the sequence — not that Redis actually drops the sessions.
- **N-1382-2 untouched** — the e2e case at `tests/e2e/tests/security-bad-actor.prelaunch.spec.ts:1155,1182` posts to `/api/auth/change-password`, a route that does not exist.
- No migration, no schema change, no config or environment value.

The two patches are a local-model (Spark) pass applied byte-for-byte from each run's canonical `patch.diff`; the measurement above is mine.

title: Cross-tenant guard fails open for tenantless tokens (connector on /lookup and /stub; access tokens likewise)
description:
## BLUF

**The cross-tenant 404 on** `GET /api/users/lookup` **and** `POST /api/users/stub` **is skipped entirely when the caller's token carries no tenant claim.** Filed from gate54a's finding **N-1374-1** on PR #1374 (KS-1402). **Not reachable through the token exchange today** — read in the code, the exchange always issues a tenant claim — so this is a latent fail-open, not a live hole. It is filed so the guard's shape is fixed rather than left depending on a property of a different component.

## What the gate measured

* **P5: 200 at the head.** A token with no tenant claim reaches the handler and the cross-tenant branch does not fire.
* **P5b: 200 at the base too.** So this is **not a regression introduced by PR #1374** — the behaviour predates it. PR #1374 only widens which token *types* reach the route; it does not change the tenant guard.
* The guard lives at `Blockchain/Dev/services/auth/src/repositories/userRepo.ts:759`, and it has applied to `POST /api/users/stub` since **KS 564**. `GET /api/users/lookup` joins it with PR #1374.
* **Access tokens are in scope too**, not just connector tokens: the guard keys on the presence of a tenant on the caller, not on the token type.

## Why it is not reachable today

The token exchange always issues a tenant claim. That was established **by reading the exchange code, not by exercising it** — so "unreachable" is a code reading, and a change to the exchange (or any other issuer, including a test-only or future path) could make it reachable without anything here changing.

## Fix shape

**Fail closed when the caller has no tenant**: refuse rather than fall through to the unscoped read. The route-level 404-not-200-empty convention should be preserved, so a tenantless caller gets the same 404 a cross-tenant caller gets, and the absence of a tenant is never the thing that widens a read.

## Provenance

* gate54a on PR #1374, finding N-1374-1. Report: `2026-10-05-ks1402-1374-g54a/report.md`.
* Duplicate search before filing (all 571 KS issues, title + description, searched locally): `tenantless` **0 hits**; `cross-tenant` 22; `fails open` 8; `no tenant claim` 1. Must-hit controls `connector` **86** and `tenantId` **24**, impossible-token control `zzqqxx` **0** — so the 0 is a measurement. The two closest neighbours were read and are **different mechanisms**: KS-1091 is an `x-tenant-id` header honoured on originate's direct path; KS-1119 is a `crossTenantLookup` hash fallback in verification.
* **Who builds this is not decided here.**

title: systemTest: run real iOS / Android device legs across Docker slots without collisions (device per slot, or a lease when one must be shared)
description:
## Split from [PS-997](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-997/spike-systemtest-has-no-real-device-leg-and-the-ios-simulator-android), 2 Oct 2026

[PS-997](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-997/spike-systemtest-has-no-real-device-leg-and-the-ios-simulator-android) covered two different things, so it has been split. [PS-997](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-997/spike-systemtest-has-no-real-device-leg-and-the-ios-simulator-android) is now the spike: whether and how Playwright tests the real iOS and Android UIs, how tests find controls on each platform, and how one spec serves several languages. **This ticket** is the infrastructure part, moved here unchanged below: running device legs safely when several Docker slots run at once.

This work only starts if [PS-997](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-997/spike-systemtest-has-no-real-device-leg-and-the-ios-simulator-android)'s decision (its Work item 1, repeated below) is that a real-device leg is wanted in the unattended estate. It also depends on [PS-995](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-995/docker-stack-slots-cant-run-systemtest-in-parallel-unattended) (PR #905) for `config/run_partition.ts`.

### What the [PS-997](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-997/spike-systemtest-has-no-real-device-leg-and-the-ios-simulator-android) spike found that bears on this ticket

| Finding | Effect here |
| -- | -- |
| Two iOS simulators can be booted side by side, and each slot can be given its own by UDID; an Android emulator is chosen by serial | **One device per slot may remove the need for a lease.** Live run 3 below would confirm it; the lease (Work item 2) is then only needed where two slots must share one device |
| A fresh simulator (shut down, erase, boot) takes 23–25 s | A practical per-run clean-up for Work item 4 |
| Safari keeps cookies per host, not per port, so a cookie set on one slot is sent to every slot | Confirms Work item 4 is needed whenever a device is shared |
| `xcodebuild` waits 600 s after any failed test unless `-collect-test-diagnostics never` is passed | Any device leg that calls `xcodebuild` must pass it, or a failure stalls the run for ten minutes |
| The iOS leg runs through `xcodebuild` (XCUITest), started from Playwright; Android through Playwright's `_android` | The lease and per-slot device choice belong in those two fixtures |

---

## BLUF

Every `npm test` runs Playwright's **emulated** phones (`mobile-iphone-*` on WebKit, `mobile-pixel-*`), and they are slot-isolated like the rest of the suite. Nothing drives a **real** iOS Simulator or Android emulator. Those checks were done by hand in [PS-995](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-995/docker-stack-slots-cant-run-systemtest-in-parallel-unattended) (1–2 Oct 2026), and they found real things: the Android dev-cert gap below, and [PS-920](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-920/ios-phone-width-pass-iphone-17-pro-ios-27-safari-sign-in-inputs) came from a manual iOS pass.

A real simulator or emulator is a single machine-wide resource. The moment two slots drive one unattended, they collide. That is exactly the "exclusive" situation [PS-995](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-995/docker-stack-slots-cant-run-systemtest-in-parallel-unattended) measured **not** to exist for `@identity` / `@stripe`, which is why [PS-995](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-995/docker-stack-slots-cant-run-systemtest-in-parallel-unattended) deliberately built no lease. This ticket is where one would be needed.

## What is true today (verified in [PS-995](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-995/docker-stack-slots-cant-run-systemtest-in-parallel-unattended), S `ae71ec1d`)

| Fact | Evidence |
| -- | -- |
| Emulated phones run in every `npm test`, per slot | `playwright.config.ts` mobile twins; failures attributed per slot across 8 multi-slot isolation runs ([PS-995](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-995/docker-stack-slots-cant-run-systemtest-in-parallel-unattended) comments) |
| Real devices exist on this Mac and run without a permission prompt | iOS "PS iPhone" (Simulator, mobile Safari) and Android `Pixel_9` / `Pixel_Tablet` AVDs, booted and driven unattended overnight |
| iOS: slot pages render over trusted TLS | `localhost:5N22` in mobile Safari; the Secuura dev CA is in the System keychain |
| Android: the dev cert does **not** cover the emulator's host alias | `https://10.0.2.2:5222` → `NET::ERR_CERT_COMMON_NAME_INVALID`; it works via `adb reverse tcp:5N22 tcp:5N22` + `https://localhost:5N22` |
| A device beside a running suite does not interfere | Round 4: 3 Android sign-ins (correct password) + 3 iOS page loads on slot 2 during its full suite → 20 failed = baseline. Slot 1 was paused 16.5 min meanwhile, then resumed, and finished at baseline |
| The per-slot password tripwire holds on a real device | Android, slot 3: slot 1's password → "Login attempt failed."; slot 3's own password → dashboard (BUILD `133aa256`) |
| One simulator / emulator per machine | a booted device and its `adb` port are host-global. Two slots' runs would share one browser state, one keyboard and one screen |
| Android tab order: email → "Forgot password?" → password | observed driving the form with TAB. A common pattern, noted for the a11y estate, not a defect claim |

## Work

1. **Decide scope** (Peter): is a real-device leg wanted in the unattended estate, or does it stay a manual / exploratory pass ([PS-920](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-920/ios-phone-width-pass-iphone-17-pro-ios-27-safari-sign-in-inputs) style)? If manual, close this ticket with the decision recorded in `systemTest/CLAUDE.md`. *(Now decided on* [PS-997](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-997/spike-systemtest-has-no-real-device-leg-and-the-ios-simulator-android).)
2. **If automated, a machine-wide device lease** (the design [PS-995](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-995/docker-stack-slots-cant-run-systemtest-in-parallel-unattended) drafted and did not build):
   * one lease per device (UDID / AVD name) under `~/.secuura-dev/`, held by the runner PID plus a heartbeat, and reclaimed only when the holder is dead or silent, never by age;
   * a second slot's device leg **queues or refuses**, naming the holder's slot, worktree, PID and start time;
   * taken only by the device project(s), never by the rest of `npm test`, which stays fully parallel across slots;
   * `config/run_partition.ts`'s contract already refuses an exclusive tag without `utils/exclusive_lease.ts`. The device tag would be the first legitimate entry, and the lease module the precondition that unlocks it.
3. **Android TLS without** `adb reverse` **hand-steps:** either `make-dev-cert.sh` adds `10.0.2.2` to the SAN, or the device leg sets up `adb reverse` for its own slot's ports only (never another slot's).
4. **Per-slot hygiene on a shared device:** clear the browser's cookies / storage between slots' legs, so slot N's session can never be presented to slot M. The per-slot password tripwire would refuse it, but it should not get that far.

## Testing

### Offline (tests-unit, red first, run unslotted AND under `STACK_SLOT=1..4`)

| Area | Cases |
| -- | -- |
| Lease: exclusion | two slots cannot hold the same device at once · two **different** devices can be held by two slots at once |
| Lease: refusal | the refusal names the holder's slot, worktree, PID and start time · exit code and message are stable (pinned wording) |
| Lease: waiting | `--wait` (or its env equivalent) queues, then takes the lease when released · a wait has a ceiling and says so when hit |
| Lease: liveness | a dead holder (PID gone) is reclaimed · a stale heartbeat is reclaimed · a live, long-running holder with a fresh heartbeat is **not** reclaimed, however old · PID reuse: a live PID with a stale heartbeat is reclaimed |
| Lease: release | released on normal exit · released when global setup throws · released on SIGINT/SIGTERM (child-process cell) |
| Lease: races | two contenders reclaiming one dead lease at the same moment → exactly one wins (child processes, repeated ≥ 50×) |
| Who takes it | the device project(s) take it · `npm test`'s other projects, `test:k-live`, the seams and `test:unit` never do · `--project=<device>-slotN` does, `--project=main-slotN` does not |
| Partition | the device tag may be in `EXCLUSIVE_TAGS` only while `utils/exclusive_lease.ts` exists (the existing contract) · the full run still equals its two halves |
| Android ports | the slot's `adb reverse` set is exactly its own app (and Mailpit, if used) ports, derived from `STACK_SLOT`, never another slot's · teardown removes only its own reversals |
| Device hygiene | the leg clears device browser state before it starts and after it ends (asserted through the driver interface, not a live device) |
| Slot isolation guards | the new modules pass `slot_resource_matrix`, `no_hardcoded_slot_literals` and `unit_suite_slot_independence` |

### Live acceptance (Docker slots on this Mac; record branch, SHA, slot and device for every result)

1. **One slot, one device, the baseline.** A full device leg on slot 2 against the PS iPhone, then the Pixel 9. All device tests pass or skip with a named reason; record counts and duration.
2. **Two slots, one device, contention.** Start the device leg on slots 2 and 3 at the same moment against the **same** simulator. Exactly one holds the lease; the other queues (with `--wait`) or refuses, naming the holder. No test from either slot runs on the device while the other holds it (verified from both logs' timestamps). Both runs' non-device projects run in parallel throughout.
3. **Two slots, two devices.** Slot 2 on the PS iPhone, slot 3 on the Pixel 9, at the same moment. Both run, neither waits, and each result names its own slot's port only.
4. **Dead holder.** Kill slot 2's runner (`kill -9`) mid-leg. Slot 3's queued leg takes the lease within the heartbeat window and completes. The device is left clean (no slot-2 session in its browser).
5. **Misrouted device.** Point slot 3's device leg at slot 2's port. Refused at the first sign-in by the per-slot password tripwire, with nothing changed on slot 2 (diff slot 2's DB counts before and after, as [PS-995](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-995/docker-stack-slots-cant-run-systemtest-in-parallel-unattended) did).
6. **Android TLS.** With the chosen fix (SAN or scoped `adb reverse`), slot pages load in Chrome with no interstitial on every slot 1–4. Remove the fix and the test fails naming the cert, not timing out.
7. **Four slots, full suites, two devices.** Four `npm test` runs at once, two of them with device legs on two devices. The device legs serialise per device; everything else is parallel. Run it at least three times before calling it fixed ([PS-995](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-995/docker-stack-slots-cant-run-systemtest-in-parallel-unattended) practice). Compare the failure sets against the single-slot baseline, test for test.
8. **Gate.** The full systemTest suite on a claimed slot, `npm run quality`, `npm run test:unit` unslotted and per slot, `dotnet test`. Post the counts (passed / failed / skipped, and every failure attributed) on the PR and here.

### Evidence to attach

Per run: slot, device (name + UDID / AVD), SHA, start/end times, counts, the lease holder/queue log lines, and screenshots of the device at the first and last device test. For runs 2 and 4: both slots' timestamped logs side by side, showing no overlap on the device.

## Done when

A real-device leg runs unattended on two slots at once; one slot's device leg waits for (or refuses on) the other; live runs 1–7 are recorded here with counts; and the result is trustworthy. Or the decision to keep devices manual is recorded in `systemTest/CLAUDE.md` and this ticket is closed with it.

---

## Verified against develop `cc2af114` — 5 Oct 2026

Still valid, and the starting point is now precise: **there is no real-device leg at all today, and what looks like one is emulation.**

`playwright.config.ts:206-231` builds the three `a11y-webkit-*` projects on `devices['iPhone 13']` — a Playwright **descriptor** (WebKit, 390×664, touch, mobile UA), with the comment at `:214` noting that a missing WebKit binary is detected by `utils/webkit_availability.ts` and fixed with `npx playwright install webkit`. The phone twins in `config/mobile_projects.ts` are the same thing: descriptors, not hardware.

So nothing in the suite competes for a physical device yet — which means this ticket is **design-before-code**, and its shape depends on what [PS-997](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-997>) (the spike, In Progress) concludes about feasibility and locators. Worth holding until that reports.

**Two constraints already known, from** [PS-995](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-995/docker-stack-slots-cant-run-systemtest-in-parallel-unattended) **and the local environment:**

* The iOS Simulator and the Android emulator are **one per machine**, while slots are up to four — so either a device per slot (not possible for the Simulator) or a machine-wide lease. [PS-995](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-995/docker-stack-slots-cant-run-systemtest-in-parallel-unattended) deliberately declined to build a lease for `@identity` / `@stripe` after measuring that nothing collided between slots; a real device is the first case where one is genuinely unavoidable.
* Four slots is already the Docker Desktop ceiling, and three suites below 16 GiB SIGKILL the app ([PS-761](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-761/three-stacks-running-suites-at-once-sigkill-the-app-in-the-docker-vm)). A device leg adds load on top of that, so the lease design should assume it cannot simply run everywhere at once.

**Related:** [PS-1002](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1002>) — the twin expansion is per-project, so whatever a real-device leg looks like must not inherit the same "every spec runs again on the same account" problem.

## Shared acceptance — phone and device legs (added 6 Oct 2026)

Shared with [PS-1002](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1002>) (phone twins re-run state-changing tests on the same account). Both cover the mobile projects (`config/mobile_projects.ts`, `playwright.config.ts`). Neither is done until these hold, in addition to its own acceptance:

1. **One contract.** [PS-1002](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1002/phone-twins-re-run-state-changing-tests-on-the-same-account-the-seal)'s `@shared-state` contract (`tests-unit`, with its allow-list) also covers this ticket's device projects. A device project is checked by the same contract, not a second one.
2. **No shared account.** No twin or device leg re-runs a state-changing test on an account that another project uses at the same time.
3. **Tests cover every slot.** Each ticket's red-first offline tests run unslotted and under `STACK_SLOT=1..4`, with identical results.

**This ticket's part:** points 1 and 2 — every device project this ticket adds passes [PS-1002](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1002/phone-twins-re-run-state-changing-tests-on-the-same-account-the-seal)'s contract, alongside `slot_resource_matrix`, `no_hardcoded_slot_literals` and `unit_suite_slot_independence`.

## Acceptance (this ticket's own, alongside the shared points above)

* Work item 1 is answered before any code: [PS-997](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-997/spike-testing-platform-s-on-real-ios-and-android-from-playwright)'s conclusion is quoted here, and if the answer is "manual", the decision is written into `systemTest/CLAUDE.md` and this ticket closes on it with no lease built.
* If automated: one lease file per device (UDID / AVD name) under `~/.secuura-dev/`, held by the runner PID plus a heartbeat, reclaimed only when the holder is dead or silent — **never by age**.
* A second slot's device leg queues or refuses, naming the holder's slot, worktree, PID and start time, with a stable exit code and stable wording.
* The lease is taken by the device project(s) only. `npm test`'s other projects, `test:k-live`, the seams and `test:unit` never take it, and remain fully parallel across slots.
* The device tag enters `EXCLUSIVE_TAGS` only once `utils/exclusive_lease.ts` exists — `config/run_partition.ts`'s existing contract already refuses otherwise, and this would be its first legitimate entry.
* Android TLS needs no hand-steps: either `10.0.2.2` is in `make-dev-cert.sh`'s SAN, or the leg sets up `adb reverse` for **its own slot's** ports only and removes only its own reversals.
* Any `xcodebuild` invocation passes `-collect-test-diagnostics never`, so a failure cannot stall the run for ten minutes.
* Live runs 1–7 above are recorded here with branch, SHA, slot, device (name + UDID / AVD), counts and durations; runs 2 and 4 carry both slots' timestamped logs side by side showing no overlap on the device.

**Why a Playwright journey cannot demonstrate this, and what does instead.** The subject is the test harness, not a product surface — there is no page on which a lease is visible, and the failure this ticket prevents (two slots driving one simulator) destroys the very run that would be asserting it. A spec cannot be its own control here. The demonstrating tests are:

1. `systemTest/tests-unit`**, red first, run unslotted and under** `STACK_SLOT=1..4` **with identical results** — the full matrix in the *Testing* table above, with the load-bearing cases being: two slots cannot hold one device at once; two different devices can be held at once; a live holder with a fresh heartbeat is **not** reclaimed however old; two contenders reclaiming one dead lease (child processes, ≥ 50 repetitions) leave exactly one winner; the refusal's wording and exit code are pinned.
2. **The project-scoping assertion:** `--project=<device>-slotN` takes the lease, `--project=main-slotN` does not. This is the one that would otherwise regress silently and make every slot serialise.
3. **A** `docker` **/ process observation, not a spec, for the contention claim:** live run 2's two logs, showing the queued slot's first device action timestamped after the holder's last one — the measurement [PS-995](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-995/docker-stack-slots-cant-run-systemtest-in-parallel-unattended) used for its own isolation claims.
4. **Control that must keep passing:** a full `STACK_SLOT=N npm test` with no device leg selected is unchanged in counts and parallelism from the pre-change baseline — the lease must not leak into the ordinary suite.

Feedback is very welcome. ## The identifier to use > **Give every element one key, for example** `login-email-input`**.** > **Put the key in** `data-testid`**, and use the same key to look up the element's visible name in the user's language.** > That single key is the identifier that covers all test coverage, in every language, and gives screen-reader users a correct name to hear. ### Examples in both languages The key and the `data-testid` never change between languages. Only the name changes, and it is looked up from the key. | Element | Key = `data-testid` (every language) | English name | French name | A French screen reader says, roughly | | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- | | Email field | `login-email-input` | "Email address" | "Adresse e-mail" | "Adresse e-mail, champ de texte" | | Sign-in button | `login-submit-btn` | "Sign in" | "Se connecter" | "Se connecter, bouton" | | Theme toggle (icon only) | `theme-toggle-btn` | "Switch to dark theme" | "Passer au thème sombre" | "Passer au thème sombre, bouton" | | Cancel on each subscription row | `admin-subs-cancel-link-42` | "Cancel subscription for Acme Ltd" | "Annuler l'abonnement de Acme Ltd" | "Annuler l'abonnement de Acme Ltd, lien" | ```mermaid flowchart LR K["One key per element
login-email-input"] --> T["data-testid
login-email-input
(same in every language)"] K --> F["fr.json
Adresse e-mail"] K --> E["en.json
Email address"] T --> P["Playwright: web,
emulated and real Android"] F --> N["Visible and spoken name
in the user's language"] E --> N N --> I["iPhone and
cloud device tests"] N --> C["Claude's exploratory
testing"] N --> A["Screen readers and
accessibility checks"] ``` **Why the key has to produce two things:** iPhone test tools cannot see `data-testid` or any other HTML attribute (12 tried), so they find elements by name. Playwright finds them most reliably by `data-testid`. One key feeding both keeps the two in step, so nobody maintains two identifiers. The spike proved it in two languages: the same test found "Email address" in English and "Adresse e-mail" in French from the same key, 4 of 4 runs. ### How accessibility and screen readers are supported **BLUF:** blind users never hear the key or the `data-testid`, because screen readers ignore them. They hear each element's **role, name and state**, in the page's language. That name is the same one the iPhone tests and Claude use to find the element. So the key gives screen-reader users correct, unique, translated names, and any test that finds an element by its name proves that name exists before a person ever hears it. ```mermaid flowchart LR K["Key

BLUF: Thank you, Stuart. I am okay with this. Before we enhance our FE code any further,   I think we should so a proof-of-concept (POC) branch.

There is no point developing code that we then have to rewrite completely later on. Let's get it right first time, so the POC should prove the approach before we add additional code.
Filed as PS-1205 (related, not blocking): unique accessible names for repeated per-row actions. English only, starting with Admin › Subscriptions "Cancel".

## Product-owner review (Stuart), 13 Oct 2026

Checked against platform-s `develop` `3e2ff5c` and `project/platform-s-uxui-issues` (PR [#965](https://github.com/Secuura/platform-s/pull/965), open). For Peter (peter@obeden.com): this answers the product-side questions in section 6, items 2 and 3. Scope, F1 and F2 remain yours.

**Summary:** the rule *every element has a test id, a role and a unique accessible name* is endorsed. **Localisation is not on the roadmap now**, so platform-s stays English-only and nothing under `ssd/` changes for this spike. Decision #3 is already made and implemented (PS-881). Some figures and tickets below need correcting.

### Answers

| # | Question | Answer |
| -- | -- | -- |
| 3 / F3 | Cookie-checkbox fix in `Services/`? | **Done already.** PS-881's fix landed via [#962](https://github.com/Secuura/platform-s/pull/962) on the project branch: `MenuMasterService.cs:249` now reads `for="SAT_OperationalCookiesOptIn"`. It reaches `develop` with #965. |
| F4 | Is localisation on the roadmap? | **Not now.** English-only. The test estate may still carry name keys over an English-only `t()` string file in systemTest; that costs the product nothing. The `UiKey` tag helper, `IUiText`, `RequestLocalization`, `fr.json` and a dynamic `lang` are deferred until a product decision. |
| F2 | iOS finds controls by role + name | No product objection. It is your call as test-estate owner. It stays consistent with PS-52 because `data-testid` remains mandatory everywhere. |
| F8, F9 | Legal scope; PDFs and emails | Business decisions, not answered here. |

### Corrections to the spike

| # | Spike says | Source says |
| -- | -- | -- |
| 1 | Suggested ticket 1 (cookie label) and ticket 2 (xUnit: every `label for` resolves to an id) | Both already exist: PS-881 and `tests/ssd.UnitTests/LabelForTargetContractTests.cs`, on the project branch via #962 and heading to develop with #965. Drop them from section 2.3. |
| 2 | "126 known gaps" in names | The total of 126 entries in `systemTest/config/a11y_known_debt.ts` on develop is correct, but only **25 are name or label** findings (9 `name`, 16 `label`). The other 101 are axe findings, **63 of them `color-contrast`** (PS-921). On the project branch it is 67 entries: 64 contrast and **3 name/label**. The headline should read "25 name/label gaps on develop, 3 after #965". |
| 3 | Repeated names ("Cancel" on every row) are counted | Nothing checks name **uniqueness** today. The sweeps flag missing names (`nameless-control`, `unlabelled-control`, `dangling-label-for`) only, so a repeated name is in no count. Your suggested ticket 6 is the right home for that check. |
| 4 | Taxonomy "Add" (`PersonEdit.cshtml:320`) is likely to repeat | It is the single button in a modal, so it does not repeat. "Add department / Add job title" would be nicer, but it is not a uniqueness defect. |
| 5 | "One key per element" | The spike's own examples use more than one key per element. The theme toggle's testid is `theme-toggle-btn`, but its text key is `theme-toggle-dark`, and it needs a light/dark pair. The Cancel link has `admin-subs-cancel-link` for its name and `admin-subs-cancel-short` for its visible text. Better wording: **one test-id key, plus one or more text keys**. |

Confirmed as written: `MenuMasterService.cs:246-247` is still dangling **on develop**; `_HeadAssets.cshtml:7` hard-codes `lang="en"`; there is no localisation anywhere in `ssd/`; Login markup is at `Login.cshtml:54-71`; every subscription row's link is named just "Cancel" (`AdminSubscriptions.cshtml:101-104`, and the `title` does not count as the name).

### For whenever localisation *is* decided: the proposed product code needs these changes

| Proposed | Problem | Instead |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `JsonUiText.Get` throws `KeyNotFoundException` | A missing key turns into a 500 while the page renders | Fall back to `en` and log. Enforce completeness in the xUnit language-file check |
| `lang="@CurrentUICulture.TwoLetterISOLanguageName"` | Without `UseRequestLocalization`, the culture is the process culture. Nothing in `ssdDockerfile` or the compose files sets `LANG`, so in our containers that is likely the invariant culture, which renders `lang="iv"` | Ship it only together with request localisation. While English-only, the hard-coded `lang="en"` is correct |
| `SupportedCultures = supported` | Changes `CurrentCulture`, not just the UI culture: about 40 view-level `ToString("dd MMM yyyy")`-style calls in `Views/` and `Areas/` format without `InvariantCulture` (e.g. `Dashboard.cshtml:263`, `SettingsUserEdit.cshtml:71`), and decimal model binding changes (e.g. `StripeProduct.SGPrice/UKPrice/EUPrice/USPrice`). The central PS-677 helpers in `Helpers.cs` are already pinned to `InvariantCulture` | Set `SupportedUICultures` only, and keep formatting invariant |
| `fr` in the supported list | The default providers include `Accept-Language`, so any French browser would get a half-translated page (a WCAG 3.1.2 failure) | Add a language only when its file is complete |
| `@addTagHelper *, ssd` in `Views/_ViewImports.cshtml` | Login and Register are Razor Pages under the Identity area, which has its own `Areas/Identity/Pages/_ViewImports.cshtml` | Register it there too |
| `data-testid` emitted by the tag helper | `TestIdCoverageContractTests` **and** `LabelForTargetContractTests` both read `.cshtml` source; the spike names only the first | Both must learn `ui-key` |

### Follow-on on the product side

I'm filing one product ticket, related to this one: unique accessible names for repeated per-row actions (Admin › Subscriptions "Cancel" first), English-only, with the visible word kept first (WCAG 2.5.3). Its acceptance relies on your uniqueness check (suggested ticket 6).

*No code was changed for this review. It is a review of the ticket against source, so no suite was run.*

title: auth GET /api/users/lookup refuses connector tokens, so every Platform-S transfer-custody 401s and falls back to a flat anchor — KS-739's users:read ruling cannot take effect
description:
## BLUF

**No Platform-S rights-assign or rights-reassign reaches** `POST /api/documents/{id}/transfer-custody` **successfully.** originate resolves `newHolderEmail` by calling auth's `GET /api/users/lookup` with the **caller's** `Authorization` header, and `/lookup` accepts only access tokens (`authenticate()`). Platform-S authenticates per Organisation with a **connector** token, so auth answers 401 *"Invalid token"*, originate passes it through ([KS-739](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-739/transfer-custody-maps-a-401403-from-userslookup-to-502-bad-gateway-the)'s 4xx rule), and S degrades to a flat `/api/anchors` anchor. No `custody_events` row is written and `documents.owner_user_id` never moves.

[KS-739](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-739/transfer-custody-maps-a-401403-from-userslookup-to-502-bad-gateway-the) (Done, archived) ruled 2026-09-02 that *"Platform S provisions* `users:read` *on its connector key; K does not widen* `ALLOWED_LOOKUP_ROLES`*"*. That ruling cannot take effect: the scope check sits behind an authenticator that rejects the token type before any scope is read. A missing scope would answer **403**; what S receives is **401 Invalid token**.

## Code (platform-k `develop` `0736d8b78`)

* `services/originate/src/routes/documents.ts:1665-1671` — email-only path: `fetch(${AUTH_SERVICE_URL}/api/users/lookup?email=…, { headers: { Authorization: <caller's header> } })`.
* `services/originate/src/routes/documents.ts:1708-1730` — a 4xx from the lookup is passed through; 401 → *"The credential on this request was rejected by the user lookup. Re-authenticate and retry."* ([KS-739](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-739/transfer-custody-maps-a-401403-from-userslookup-to-502-bad-gateway-the)).
* `services/auth/src/routes/users.ts:266` — `userRoutes.get('/lookup', authenticate(), …)` — access tokens only.
* `services/auth/src/routes/users.ts:357-359` — "[KS-564](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-564/share-lifecycle-events-and-certificationsissue-all-fail-on-recipient) *(Option A): this ONE route also accepts a connector token — see authenticateAccessOrConnector. Every other route keeps plain authenticate()."* — `/stub` was widened; `/lookup` was not.
* Platform-S side: `ssd/Services/CardanoAnchor/CardanoAnchorService.PerVerb.cs` `TransferCustodyAsync` sends `{ newHolderEmail, reason }` + `onBehalfOf` with `Authorization: Bearer <connector access token>` (`CardanoAnchorService.cs:1527`).

## Measured — local pair, slot 3, 2026-10-01

platform-s `f370236c` (+ [PS-992](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-992/systemtest-the-date-sort-contract-has-asserted-nothing-since-ps-914) systemTest changes only) ↔ platform-k `0736d8b78`, fresh databases, 33/33 K containers up, `/health/deep` 200, S provisioning key accepted, 10/0/0 organisations registered.

**4 of 4** transfer-custody calls refused, identical body, under Organisation 3's connector key:

```
transfer-custody status=401 body={"success":false,"error":{"code":"UNAUTHORIZED","message":"The credential on this request was rejected by the user lookup. Re-authenticate and retry. Upstream said: Invalid token"}} … using /api/anchors fallback.
```

* 09:21:55Z — 2 calls ([PS-992](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-992/systemtest-the-date-sort-contract-has-asserted-nothing-since-ps-914)'s date-sort seed: two documents delegated to a same-org colleague).
* 09:22:55–09:31:06Z — 2 calls during `npm run test:k-live` (`verb_matrix.spec.ts` rights-assign + rights-reassign on K document `7af2374a-dd61-47e7-be50-122dcb5e412b`).

In the same window, Organisation 3's connector token **succeeded** on `originate` (201) and on lifecycle events (`rights-unassign`, `delete`) — so the key is valid; only the auth-service lookup refuses it.

## Why nothing went red

The platform-s `@k-live` cell "rights-assign and rights-unassign each reach K" asserted only that the S edge carries an anchor K resolves as not-failed — which the flat fallback also satisfies. It passed (17 passed / 1 skipped) while both custody calls 401'd. [PS-992](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-992/systemtest-the-date-sort-contract-has-asserted-nothing-since-ps-914) tightens that cell to assert the custody transfer K records — `GET /api/documents/{id}` `owner.id` must move off its pre-assign value (measured: it reads `""` before and after today's refused transfers). The cell is **red until this ticket ships**, deliberately, and turns green once K records the transfer. Platform-S's `TransferCustodyAsync` carries a comment naming this ticket.

## Options (Kamil's call — no K code changed)

1. **Widen** `/lookup` **to** `authenticateAccessOrConnector()`, as [KS-564](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-564/share-lifecycle-events-and-certificationsissue-all-fail-on-recipient) did for `/stub` — makes [KS-739](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-739/transfer-custody-maps-a-401403-from-userslookup-to-502-bad-gateway-the)'s `users:read` ruling effective (the connector key then needs that scope).
2. **originate resolves the holder with its own service credential**, not the caller's header — removes the dependency on the caller's token type.
3. **Platform-S sends** `newHolderId` — requires S to know the K user id of the recipient (S-side; it does not today).

Whichever is chosen, a recipient with no K account still gets the typed 404 `RECIPIENT_NOT_FOUND` ([KS-739](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-739/transfer-custody-maps-a-401403-from-userslookup-to-502-bad-gateway-the) measurement A) — worth confirming the S holder exists in K once the 401 is gone.

## Related

[KS-739](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-739/transfer-custody-maps-a-401403-from-userslookup-to-502-bad-gateway-the) (Done, archived — ruling this ticket shows cannot take effect) · [KS-564](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-564/share-lifecycle-events-and-certificationsissue-all-fail-on-recipient) (Option A connector scoping) · [PS-681](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-681/systemtest-k-live-every-share-and-rights-verb-times-out-waiting-for) (Done — Stuart's original 502 report) · [PS-992](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-992/systemtest-the-date-sort-contract-has-asserted-nothing-since-ps-914) (platform-s: the k-live cell that hid this).

**BLUF:** Yes, Kintsugi wrote one custody event for every accepted call: seven events for your document, at the seven times you listed, to the second. The document's owner moved to a single invited user that Kintsugi created 32 ms before the first event. None of the seven events recorded an anchor. I cannot confirm that the invited user's address is firsttime@lhsg.com, and I cannot show the reason for the refused anchors, for the two reasons under "Not measured".

All times are UTC, with AEDT (UTC+11) in brackets. Each figure says how it was read. Sections 1 to 3 are from SELECTs on Kintsugi on 29 Oct between 04:53 and 05:01 UTC [15:53 and 16:01 AEDT], in read-only database sessions. Section 4 is from the box's REVISION records, read at 05:04 UTC [16:04 AEDT].

**1. The invited user**
- Kintsugi holds one user created inside the 26 Oct 03:00 to 03:20 UTC window: status `invited`, role `user`, created 2026-10-26 03:09:24.532 [14:09:24 AEDT], in Kintsugi's default tenant. It was created 32 ms before the first custody event.
- It is the recipient of all seven events and the owner of the document now. It owns no other document.
- Its address is not shown here. See "Not measured".

**2. The custody events** (the K document you name, `427c4864-fde0-4713-9e36-7e50d0097a49`, is stored on Kintsugi as the document's external id)

| # | created (UTC) | [AEDT] | from | to |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | 2026-10-26 03:09:24.564 | [14:09:24] | none | the invited user |
| 2 | 03:10:24.746 | [14:10:24] | the invited user | the invited user |
| 3 | 03:11:24.832 | [14:11:24] | the invited user | the invited user |
| 4 | 03:12:24.896 | [14:12:24] | the invited user | the invited user |
| 5 | 03:13:25.046 | [14:13:25] | the invited user | the invited user |
| 6 | 03:14:25.113 | [14:14:25] | the invited user | the invited user |
| 7 | 03:15:25.262 | [14:15:25] | the invited user | the invited user |

- Count: 7, all inside 03:09:00 to 03:16:00 UTC; the gaps between them are 60, 60, 60, 60, 60 and 60 seconds. Control on the same query: the 28 Oct document from your KS-1384 table has 1 event. So events 2 to 7 are repeats of the same transfer: each wrote a row that moves the document from the invited user to the same user.
- Ownership: the document's owner is the invited user. That user did not exist before 03:09:24.532 on 26 Oct and the document was created on 23 Oct 09:10, so the owner changed in this window. The document's `updated_at` is 03:15:25.262, the time of event 7, and its status is still `draft`.
- All seven events have an empty "transferred by" and an empty anchor transaction. The provenance table holds seven `transfer-custody` rows for the document, first 03:09:24 and last 03:15:25.
- Kintsugi's audit trail holds seven `POST …/transfer-custody` requests answered 201, at the same seven times.

**3. The anchors**
- Kintsugi's audit trail holds seven `POST /api/anchors` requests answered 400, each 8 to 37 ms after a transfer-custody request. Those seven are the only `anchors.create` requests answered 400 in the trail, which begins on 20 Aug (7 of its 12 `anchors.create` rows). The trail records no error text for them.
- Kintsugi's anchor table holds 0 rows for this document; control: 1 row for the 28 Oct document.
- So no anchor was created for any of the seven transfers, and the transfer route answered success each time. From the audit trail alone I cannot tell whether those 400s are the calls S made after each transfer or the route's own internal call; their timing fits the calls S made.

**4. Which build**
Kintsugi ran develop `1ae6f17d19a8` for all seven events (deployed 26 Oct 00:46:20 UTC [11:46:20 AEDT], replaced 26 Oct 07:55:24 UTC [18:55:24 AEDT], read from the box's REVISION records). Your comment names `bcc51903d`, which was the build before that. Kintsugi now runs `5dccdcb29ec2`.

**Not measured**
- Whether the invited user's address is firsttime@lhsg.com (as you gave it). Kintsugi stores addresses encrypted. Its address-lookup column did not match a plain hash of a known address in a control test, so I could not search by address without decrypting, and I did not decrypt.
- The reason for the refused anchors, and whether the transfer route's own anchor call also met a 400 `Invalid DID`. Originate's log on Kintsugi starts on 29 Oct 01:05:59 UTC [12:05:59 AEDT], after later redeploys, and no file on the box holds 26 Oct log lines. The "Lifecycle anchor emission failed" and "Custody transferred" lines for 26 Oct are therefore not available.

Update, 03:17 UTC: **S stopped the loop at 03:15:58 UTC.** The transfer for document `427c4864-fde0-4713-9e36-7e50d0097a49` reached Kintsugi **7 times**, at 03:09:24, 03:10:24, 03:11:24, 03:12:24, 03:13:25, 03:14:25 and 03:15:25 UTC, each answered 2xx with no anchor reference. Nothing more will arrive from S for it. On Stuart's instruction S's row was given a local marker and parked. A count of `custody_events` for that document over 03:09–03:16 UTC would show whether K wrote one row per call. The S fix is filed on the S side. For context, that document's own upload on 23 Oct 09:10 UTC (same Entra-verified actor) was created on K, but its anchor was refused for the same `did:jwk` reason, and S parked it as FAILED.

@kamil.kreiser — **live custody transfer on dev-ps against Kintsugi `bcc51903d`, 26 Oct 2026 03:09 UTC: K accepted it, but returned no anchor reference.** Read from S's side (dev-ps app log and its `DocumentTransaction` row; S develop `4fb15e7`).

- **What ran:** stuart@obeden.com assigned S document 15 (K document `427c4864-fde0-4713-9e3…`) to firsttime@lhsg.com, a person who had never received custody or a certification, so K had no user for them. S row 96, chain id `5008820d82c743fd971cbc4d99729a20`.
- **K's answer to `POST /api/documents/{id}/transfer-custody`: 2xx**, with no `transfer.anchorId` / `transfer.anchor.id` in the body. S logged `transfer-custody OK but no ref in payload for tx 5008820d…; using /api/anchors fallback`. So the old 404 `RECIPIENT_NOT_FOUND` and the 500 are gone on Kintsugi. **Please confirm from your side:** an invited stub for firsttime@lhsg.com in `users`, and the `custody_events` row(s) with the owner moved.
- **Why no anchor reference, as far as S can tell:** the assigner is Entra-verified, so S's identity block carries a `did:jwk` `actorDid`. S's flat fallback (`POST /api/anchors`) was then refused 400 `Invalid DID — expect did:key:… or did:web:…` at `identity.actorDid` (the KS-1175 widening). That suggests the custody route's own anchor call met the same 400 and the route returned success without it, the same shape as KS-1709 on certify. Can you confirm from originate's log?
- **The S-side problem this exposes, which matters for your tables:** S's background drain re-sends any row that has no K reference on every pass, with no limit. For this row it has re-sent the same transfer-custody **once a minute: 03:09:24, 03:10:24, 03:11:24 …, 4 calls by 03:13 UTC**, each answered 2xx by K and each followed by a refused flat anchor. If K writes a `custody_events` row per call, Kintsugi is accumulating one duplicate transfer a minute for this document. A count of `custody_events` for that document would tell us. It continues until S stops it (I'm asking Stuart now) or K accepts `did:jwk`. It is the only row in that state on dev-ps.

The S fix (do not re-send a side-effecting verb K has already accepted; park the row instead) will be an S ticket.

**#1620 measured end to end, 19 Oct 12:13–12:31Z, slot 4, K develop `115797747` (fresh DB, 54 migrations), S develop `b7d414b`:** the PS-992 cell's rights-assign to `firsttwo@lhsg.com` — a person this K had never seen — now answers **201**: S logs `'rights-assign' → transfer-custody ref anchor_ff9fea6c-…`, K's `users` gains one **invited** stub (2 → 3), `custody_events` holds 1 row with `transferred_by_id` NULL, and originate's log has no 22P02 beyond its startup probe. Zero `RECIPIENT_NOT_FOUND` in the run. The cell then fails on its custodian read-back (`GET /api/documents/{id}` → 404 to the k-live client after ownership moved), the shape already filed to Peter on PS-1299 — so on this build the transfer half is green and the read half is the estate's.

On PS-1091 reading Canceled: that was done **because** the K side changed, not on the assumption it would not — it was cancelled at 09:55Z quoting Kam's (a) verbatim, with the note that #1620 makes S's pre-transfer stub call unnecessary and that Kintsugi keeps answering 404 until it takes #1614 + #1620 together. No second look needed; the S-side residue is the closer cell's read-back (PS-1299, Peter).

Read #1620 merged at `a0da739b6` and KS-1662's fix at `115797747`. Stuart's slot-1 K was rebuilt at `115797747` today (originate image 11:34Z carries the stub path), so the next S run against it will exercise the mint for real; the dev-ps pairing stays as you describe — 201 locally, 404 on Kintsugi — until the round.

## BLUF

**The invited-stub holder is merged — not deployed.** PR #1620 landed on `develop` at
`a0da739b6954d42333640ea190d877f031803c7f`. A custody transfer naming a recipient Platform K has
never seen now **mints an invited stub user and records the transfer**, instead of answering
`404 RECIPIENT_NOT_FOUND`. That completes the build half of Kam's ruling. **Nothing is live**, so
Platform S still sees the old 404 on every environment until a deploy round carries this.

## Recommendation

1. **Deploy needs a rebuild, and both KS-1402 changes should travel together** — the 500 fix with
   migration `052` (merged earlier at `80868551e679`) and this stub holder. A box with one and not
   the other is a state no suite covers. Rebuilding **either** the `migrations` image **or** the
   `api-gateway` image lands `052`; afterwards check `custody_events.transferred_by_id` reads
   `is_nullable = YES` — the runner prints `applied=N failed=0` even when it ran a stale image, so
   the column is the evidence, not the summary line.
2. **This ticket stays In Progress** until it is deployed and live-checked.
3. One follow-up is open and worth doing before anyone leans on the tenant guarantees: **KS-1662**.

## Detail

**What landed.** On the email path's zero-row case only, the route calls auth's
`POST /api/users/stub` with the caller's credential forwarded — the shape `certifications/issue`
already used for `holderEmail`, which is the precedent Kam's card names. auth stays the only writer
of `users`, so its PII encryption, the email lookup hash, the cross-tenant rule and the
claim-on-registration flow are not duplicated. **No auth change, no new scope, no migration**:
Platform S's connector key already passes that endpoint's gate.

**What is deliberately different from Kintsugi.** Kintsugi answers 404 for an unknown recipient;
Platform K now answers 201. Recorded separately on this ticket with a case-by-case table — only that
one branch diverges.

**Gaps in the shipped coverage, stated rather than left to be discovered (KS-1662):**
- The route's **tenant predicates are not independently proven**. `users` is FORCE RLS for the
  application role, so dropping a predicate still leaves the suite green — RLS hides the row anyway.
  A cell without RLS is needed before anyone treats those predicates as tested.
- The non-2xx fallback has no cell (it fails safe).

- That omission is deliberate and recorded on the line above it (`:477-478`): "−users:read (Stuart ③ — on-behalf-of resolution is K-side, §6)".
- A provisioning-key caller may not override the set: `if (byConnector && body.scopes !== undefined)` → 403 "A provisioning key may not override the minted scope set" (`:529-535`). So KS-739's "Platform S provisions `users:read` on its connector key" has no mechanism on the S side.
- The lookup's own gate is role or scope (`services/auth/src/routes/users.ts:282-295`): `ALLOWED_LOOKUP_ROLES` is `ISSUER_ADMIN`, `ORG_ADMIN`, `SYSTEM_ADMIN`, `SUPER_ADMIN` (`:180`), which a connector token is not, and the scope is absent. That is your CELL 2: 403.

**Not measured live** — this is from the code; I have not run a pair against `2d85b84e1` yet, and Kintsugi still publishes the 28 Sep spec (`f28cd1fbc`), so it does not have #1374 either.

What would finish it, your call:

1. Add `users:read` to `S_CONNECTOR_SCOPES`. Scopes are fixed on the key row at mint, so every already-registered Organisation keeps its old set until its key is rotated (platform-admin only) — the same shape as the `subjects:erase` cutover in KS-843. It also reverses the §8 sign-off quoted above, so it wants a recorded ruling.
2. Option 2 from the description: originate resolves `newHolderEmail` with its own service credential instead of the caller's header. No scope change, no re-mint, and it keeps "on-behalf-of resolution is K-side".

Either way the Platform-S `@k-live` rights-assign cell (PS-992) stays red until K records the transfer; S's `TransferCustodyAsync` needs no change for either option.

**KS-1402 is fixed on develop, and here is exactly what changed and what is still unverified.**

Kam ruled this on 2026-10-02 (live board, card `secuura-ks1402-lookup-refuses-connector-tokens`), option (a): *"Widen /lookup to accept a connector token, as /stub already does (KS 564)."*

`GET /api/users/lookup` now authenticates through `authenticateAccessOrConnector()`, the same door `POST /api/users/stub` has used since KS 564. The token type is no longer the gate; the route's own role/scope check runs afterwards, so **`users:read` is the effective permission**, and a cross-tenant lookup still answers 404 rather than 200-empty.

Merged as **#1374**, squash `2d85b84e1012961c880daa3de70d8491fc0a2ff9`, on develop.

Four cells pin it (`services/auth`, `npx vitest run` — `npm test` there is watch mode):

| cell | at base | at head |
|---|---|---|
| connector token WITH `users:read` reaches the handler | 401 | **200** |
| connector token WITHOUT `users:read` | 401 | **403** |
| interactive ACCESS token still works (control) | 200 | 200 |
| tenant-A connector reading a tenant-B-only email | 401 | **404** |

Red-first at the base: 3 failed / 1 passed of 4. Green after: 4/4. Suite 77 → 78 files, 836 → 840 tests, 0 new reds.

A connector token without a tenant claim would skip the cross-tenant 404 on this route. Read in the code, the token exchange always issues a tenant claim, so this was not reached in testing; it is tracked in KS-1406.

**@stuart.jamieson — one thing needs checking on the S side, and it is the difference between a fix and a half-fix.** Whether Platform-S's connector key actually carries `users:read` is **not measurable from Platform K**. If it does, the transfer-custody call now succeeds. If it does not, S moves from **401 Invalid token** to **403** — still a refusal, but the correct one, and the scope is then the thing to fix. UNMEASURED from here.

Not done on this PR: no live sweep (skill §5f), no S↔K pair run, no Schemathesis/Akto/Playwright/k6, no deploy. The `authenticate.ts` audit-label change this PR carries is **covered by no test** — reverted alone the suite stays green — so its route-neutrality is argued and measured in the PR body, not test-guarded.

Re-measured 2 Oct on a second pair (platform-s `d04829b` ↔ platform-k develop `88e8877a2`, clean build, slot 3): the refusal is unchanged. Platform-S logged `transfer-custody status=401 … rejected by the user lookup … Upstream said: Invalid token` 5 times in a full suite run and 2 times in `test:k-live` alone, all under organisation 3's connector key, while originate, lifecycle events and shares under the same key succeeded. The `verb_matrix` rights-assign cell fails on the custodian assertion as designed (PS-992). Code re-read at `88e8877a2`: `services/auth/src/routes/users.ts:266` still guards `/lookup` with `authenticate()`.

title: 13 new advisories block every push: axios 1.18.1 ×12 (7 high — SSRF, proxy bypass, ReDoS, prototype pollution; runtime in services/kyc) and dompurify 3.4.13 — all fixed in range (axios 1.20.0, dompurify 3.4.16)
description:
## BLUF

**The push preflight fails legs 6 and 7 on** `develop`**'s own dependencies again, so no push on this repo succeeds until this lands.** Thirteen advisories published on 2026-09-30 are absent from `scripts/audit/audit-baseline.json`: **twelve against axios 1.18.1 (7 high)** and one against dompurify 3.4.13 (low). **No lock changed to cause this.** No `axios`/`dompurify` line in any lock moved between `377989cf3`, where both legs were rc 0 on 2026-09-30 \~02:45Z, and `4f18c59a8`.

**Every one is fixed inside the declared ranges, so this is a lock refresh, not a manifest bump.** That was checked against each advisory's `vulnerable_versions`, not inferred. `frontend/issuer` already pins axios 1.20.0 / dompurify 3.4.16 and is flagged by neither leg.

Measured at `develop` `4f18c59a8`, twice (2026-09-30 \~22:55Z and 23:11Z, identical ID sets), on Stuart's Mac: `npm run audit:gate` rc 1 (`24 distinct advisories reported, 26 baselined` → 13 NEW); `npm run audit:locks` rc 1 (`1611 distinct packages pinned — 18 advisories match, 6 already baselined` → 12 NEW).

## The thirteen, and the fix version measured for each

Each advisory's `vulnerable_versions` comes from the npm bulk-advisory endpoint, the same data the gates read, and was checked with `semver.satisfies` against both the pinned version and the candidate fix.

| advisory | sev | summary (from the gate) | vulnerable | 1.18.1 | 1.20.0 |
| -- | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- |
| `GHSA-r4gj-5m52-g5wh` | high | `maxRedirects: 0` not enforced by fetch adapter → redirect-based SSRF | `>=1.17.0 <1.20.0` | VULN | ok |
| `GHSA-mghh-pgcx-3jjj` | high | ReDoS in `shouldBypassProxy`, reachable via untrusted redirect `Location` | `>=1.15.0 <1.20.0` | VULN | ok |
| `GHSA-3pq3-5fj3-cg6v` | high | HTTP/2 adapter bypasses configured DNS lookup and proxy controls | `>=1.13.0 <1.20.0` | VULN | ok |
| `GHSA-542g-h47m-68v8` | high | DoS via unhandled `error` in HTTP/2 session init | `>=1.13.0 <1.20.0` | VULN | ok |
| `GHSA-c29m-xwm3-cm6r` | high | ReDoS in `fromDataURI` data: URL parser | `>=1.16.1 <1.20.0` | VULN | ok |
| `GHSA-x97p-jq2g-jp4f` | high | prototype-pollution gadget in `toFormData` options | `>=1.15.1 <1.20.0` | VULN | ok |
| `GHSA-m8m8-qj5v-23w3` | high | Node HTTP adapter prototype-pollution gadget → request socket hijack | `>=1.15.2 <1.20.0` | VULN | ok |
| `GHSA-44g4-m2mj-wpvx` | moderate | CIDR-form `NO_PROXY` entries ignored → proxy exclusion bypass | `>=1.15.0 <1.20.0` | VULN | ok |
| `GHSA-vh66-26gq-q6x8` | moderate | prototype-pollution gadget in fetch adapter alters outbound requests | `>=1.7.0 <1.20.0` | VULN | ok |
| `GHSA-9fr6-4gfg-395g` | moderate | prototype pollution in default instance overrides HTTP method | `>=1.0.0 <1.20.0` | VULN | ok |
| `GHSA-j8rh-479h-cp32` | moderate | header injection via inherited headers after minimal interceptor | `>=1.0.0 <1.20.0` | VULN | ok |
| `GHSA-4hqw-qxg8-jxx2` | moderate | fetch adapter header injection via inherited FormData `getHeaders` | `>=1.12.0 <1.20.0` | VULN | ok |
| `GHSA-p98j-92pf-mc4p` | low | **dompurify** `IN_PLACE` hook leaves detached event handlers armed → DOM XSS | `>=3.4.13 <=3.4.15` | 3.4.13 VULN | 3.4.16 ok |

## Where, and why a lock refresh reaches it — measured

| lock | pinned | declared range | leg |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| `services/kyc` | axios 1.18.1 | `^1.8.2` (`dependencies`) | 7 |
| `frontend/admin` | axios 1.18.1 | `^1.6.5` | 7 |
| `frontend/verifier` | axios 1.18.1 | `^1.6.2` | 7 |
| `Blockchain/Dev` root (workspace) | axios 1.18.1 (one copy, hoisted) | admin/issuer/verifier/kyc as above + `@meshsdk/provider` `^1.7.2` | 6 |
| `Blockchain/Dev` root (workspace) | dompurify 3.4.13 | `frontend/issuer` `^3.4.13` | 6 |
| `frontend/issuer` | axios **1.20.0**, dompurify **3.4.16** | — | not flagged |

Every range admits axios 1.20.0 and dompurify 3.4.16, `@meshsdk/provider`'s `^1.7.2` included, so the root lock can stay on a single copy.

`services/kyc` **is runtime exposure, not build-tree only.** axios is in `dependencies`, the image installs with `npm ci --omit=dev` (`services/kyc/Dockerfile:63`), and `src/providers/microsoft-entra-client.ts` imports it for outbound calls. The redirect-SSRF and proxy-bypass rows are the ones to read against that client. Reachability was **not** assessed here. The frontends' exposure (browser bundle vs build tree) was not measured either.

## Done means

1. axios ≥ 1.20.0 in `services/kyc`, `frontend/admin`, `frontend/verifier` and the root lock, and dompurify ≥ 3.4.16 in the root lock. Each lock is regenerated **containerised** (`node:24-alpine`; host npm 11.5.1 dies with `edgesOut`, see [KS-1379](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1379/pr-1339s-standalone-locks-were-re-resolved-from-bare-manifests-1000)), with a no-target control run as [Secuura/Distributed_Secuura#1358](https://linear.app/secuura/review/ks-1380-15-locks-agree-with-packagesshared-on-types-esc-4199-pg-8231-020075b0edd2) did so that every move is attributable.
2. Legs 6 and 7 green at the PR head with **no** baseline row for any of the thirteen.
3. The `services/kyc` suite and image build at the head, since it is the runtime consumer.

## Reproduce

```bash
cd Blockchain/Dev
npm run audit:gate    # leg 6
npm run audit:locks   # leg 7
```

Found on 2026-09-30 while verifying [Secuura/Distributed_Secuura#1358](https://linear.app/secuura/review/ks-1380-15-locks-agree-with-packagesshared-on-types-esc-4199-pg-8231-020075b0edd2) ([KS-1380](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1380/develop-does-not-build-since-ks-1378-1339-analytics-billing-and)) for Stuart. [KS-1395](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1395/two-advisories-published-after-ks-1378-block-every-push-again-undici), the previous batch, is closed. This is the next one.
