title: Suggested: move platform-k (outside systemTest + observability) to TypeScript 7.0.2 — five current tools fail on TS 7 (tested), so they would be replaced first
description:
**Owner:** Kamil; the order of work is his call. **Raised:** 2026-09-30, split from [KS-1396](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1396/platform-k-systemtest-observability-typescript-702-oxlinttsgolint). **Base:** `develop` @ `4f18c59a8`.
**Companion ticket:** [KS-1396](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1396/platform-k-systemtest-observability-typescript-702-oxlinttsgolint) (Peter) covers `systemTest/` + `observability/`. The two tickets reference each other and never overlap.

## 1. Summary

**Suggestion (Peter, 2026-09-30): move the rest of platform-k to TypeScript 7.0.2**, the version systemTest and observability are moving to on [KS-1396](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1396/platform-k-systemtest-observability-typescript-702-oxlinttsgolint). This ticket covers the rest of platform-k: 43 `package.json` files, 38 of them on TypeScript 5.x. Whether and when to move is Kamil's decision.

**We can't just change the TypeScript version number and keep our current tools.** Five of the tools we use today **stop working** when TypeScript 7 is installed. This was tested, not assumed (§2). Those tools have to be replaced (or, for tsup, fixed) before TypeScript 7 can go in. The replacements were tested too, and they work.

## 2. Why the tools have to change

### In plain English

The `typescript` package on npm has always contained two things:

1. **The compiler** (`tsc`): you run it to check and build code.
2. **A library**: other tools load it *inside their own code* to compile or check TypeScript for you. Our test runner, our script runner, our linter and our SDK bundler all work this way.

**TypeScript 7 is a rewrite, and it ships only the compiler. The library is gone.** In the `typescript@7.0.2` package the library exports exactly **2** things: `version` and `versionMajorMinor`. In 6.0.3 it exports **2,248**. Microsoft says a new, *different* library will come with TypeScript 7.1, and gives no date. The tools that depend on the old library would then have to be rewritten against the new one.

So any tool that loads TypeScript as a library crashes when TypeScript 7 is installed. It asks for functions that no longer exist. Nothing in our config can fix that, because the code the tool needs is not in the package.

### Proof: the same test on TypeScript 6 and TypeScript 7 (2026-09-30)

**Method:**

* Two fresh projects on Node 24.18.0, identical apart from the TypeScript version.
* Each tool at the version we use today.
* The same two-file source in each: one module and one test.
* Tools installed with `--legacy-peer-deps`, because npm refuses to install ts-jest next to TypeScript 7 at all.
* **TypeScript 6.0.3 is the control:** every tool must pass there, so that a failure on 7 can only be caused by 7.

| Tool (version we use) | What we use it for | Where | Its declared TypeScript support | **TypeScript 6.0.3** | **TypeScript 7.0.2** |
| -- | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- |
| **typescript-eslint** 8.71 (parser) | Linting TypeScript | `Blockchain/Dev` workspace root | `>=4.8.4 <6.1.0`: **excludes 7** | ✅ lints | ❌ `typescript-eslint does not support TS 7.0.` |
| **ts-jest** 29.4 + jest 29.7 | Running unit tests | governance, originate, referral, vc-issuer | `>=4.3 <7`: **excludes 7** (npm refuses the install) | ✅ 1/1 passed | ❌ `does not expose the JavaScript compiler API required by ts-jest` |
| **ts-node** 10.9 | Running `.ts` scripts | referral, vc-issuer, staking, `connectors/whatsapp-bot`, `deployment/cardano` | `>=2.7`: claims open support | ✅ ran | ❌ `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'fileExists')` |
| **ts-node-dev** 2.0 | Dev server with reload | governance | `*`: claims open support | ✅ ran | ❌ same `fileExists` crash (it runs ts-node underneath) |
| **tsup** 8.5 (`--dts`) | Building the SDK's type declarations | `sdk/javascript` | `>=4.5.0`: claims open support | ✅ `.d.ts` written\* | ❌ `TypeError … (reading 'useCaseSensitiveFileNames')`; no `.d.ts` |

\* **tsup has a second, separate problem.** Its d.ts step injects a `baseUrl` option that TypeScript 6 already rejects as deprecated (`TS5101`) and TypeScript 7 removes entirely. The control passed only with `"ignoreDeprecations": "6.0"`. tsup's JS build works on both versions; only the type-declaration step fails.

**Result: 5 of 5 tools pass on TypeScript 6 and fail on TypeScript 7.** Two of them say so up front in their declared ranges. The other three *claim* support but crash when run.

### Proof: the replacements work on TypeScript 7

| Replacement | Replaces | Loads the TypeScript library? | **TypeScript 7.0.2** |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| **oxlint 1.86 + oxlint-tsgolint 7.0.2003** | typescript-eslint | No. Its own parser, plus TypeScript 7's Go compiler for type-aware rules | ✅ lints ([KS-1396](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1396/platform-k-systemtest-observability-typescript-702-oxlinttsgolint) spike: 4 harnesses, 9/9 planted checks) |
| **Vitest 5.0.3** | ts-jest + jest | No (not a dependency or peer) | ✅ 1/1 passed |
| **tsx 4.23.15** | ts-node, ts-node-dev | No (not a dependency or peer) | ✅ ran |
| **tsc 7.0.2** itself | — | — | ✅ type-checks the same source clean |

## 3. Options (Kamil's call)

| Option | What it means | Trade-off |
| -- | -- | -- |
| **1. Replace the tools, then TypeScript 7.0.2** (this plan) | typescript-eslint → oxlint; ts-jest → Vitest; ts-node / ts-node-dev → tsx; fix or replace tsup's d.ts step | Same TypeScript version as [KS-1396](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1396/platform-k-systemtest-observability-typescript-702-oxlinttsgolint). The most work, but every replacement is proven above |
| **2. Keep the tools, run two TypeScripts side by side** | TypeScript 7 for `tsc`; TypeScript 6 installed under the name `typescript` for the tools. ts-jest's own error message recommends this | Two compilers in one tree, which can disagree. **Unproven:** the TypeScript 7 package name ts-jest suggests, `@typescript/native`, **does not exist on npm** (checked 2026-09-30); `@typescript/typescript6` does (6.0.2). Needs its own proof first |
| **3. Stay on TypeScript 6.0.3 for now** | Bump 5.x → 6.0.3, which every current tool supports; revisit when the tools support TypeScript 7.1's new library | The least work now, a second migration later. Leaves platform-k on two TypeScript versions (6.0.3 here, 7.0.2 in systemTest/observability) |

## 4. Scope

**In scope: everything in platform-k except** `systemTest/` **and** `observability/`**.** That is 43 tracked `package.json` files: the `Blockchain/Dev` workspace (services, packages, frontends, sdk, tests, connectors, deployment) and `secuura-website-package`.

**Out of scope:** `systemTest/` and `observability/` → [KS-1396](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1396/platform-k-systemtest-observability-typescript-702-oxlinttsgolint).

## 5. The work, in the proposed order (Option 1)

1. **Linting:** `Blockchain/Dev` root typescript-eslint → oxlint + tsgolint.
2. **Tests:** Jest / ts-jest → Vitest in governance, originate, referral and vc-issuer. [KS-1051](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1051/develop-is-red-on-the-servicesoriginate-jest-suite-and-nothing-catches): originate's Jest suite is already red on `develop`. Also `sdk/javascript` Vitest 1 → 5, and the rest of Vitest 4 → 5.
3. **Scripts:** ts-node / ts-node-dev → tsx in the six packages above.
4. **SDK types:** fix or replace tsup's d.ts step (both problems in §2).
5. **TypeScript 5 → 7.0.2**, in batches that each build clean with `Start_Up/start-secuura.sh --rebuild` ([KS-1380](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1380/develop-does-not-build-since-ks-1378-1339-analytics-billing-and) shows how easily lock drift breaks a clean build). Review [KS-920](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-920/shared-ships-the-typescript-compiler-and-a-267-mb-dev-tree-into-all-24) alongside this: `/shared` ships the TypeScript compiler into 24 runtime images, and TypeScript 7's compiler is a native per-platform binary.
6. **Playwright → 1.63.0** in the `Blockchain/Dev` root (^1.61.1; workspace-root lock), `tests/e2e` (^1.40.0, **npm-deprecated**) and `tests/e2e-v2` (1.58.2; `RUNBOOK.md:26` ties it to a cached chromium). Settle [KS-1393](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1393/repo-hygiene-31-spec-files-under-blockchaindevtests-that-no-playwright) row 1 (with [KS-1390](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1390/the-e2e-v2-harness-is-platform-ks-only-browser-portal-and) / [KS-734](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-734/the-e2e-playwright-suite-cannot-run-from-a-clean-checkout-testse2e-is)) first, because some of these test corpora may be retired.
7. **Other currency items:**

| Item | Now | Target |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `secuura-website-package` ESLint | ^8.56.0 (**EOL, npm-deprecated**) | Off ESLint 8, or retire the package ([KS-1393](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1393/repo-hygiene-31-spec-files-under-blockchaindevtests-that-no-playwright) row 3) |
| `@types/node` | ^20.x ×31, ^22.0.0 ×3 | The 24 line, matching the `node:24-alpine` runtime ([KS-872](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-872/packagesshared-project-tsc-is-red-on-develop-cryptojsonwebkey-is-gone) shows the cost of drift) |
| `engines.node` | `>=18.0.0` ×5 | `>=24` (Node 18 and 20 are past EOL) |
| dotenv | ^16.3.x ×22 | 18.0.4, with a test. In 18, a bare `config()` follows `DOTENV_CONFIG_PATH` (measured on [KS-1396](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1396/platform-k-systemtest-observability-typescript-702-oxlinttsgolint)) |
| vite / @vitejs/plugin-react | ^5 to ^8 / ^4 to ^6 | 8.3.1 / 6.1.1 |
| prettier | ^3.2.4 | 3.9.9 |
| `.claude/skills/secuura-test-discipline/SKILL.md:463-465` | Describes the 400-line cap as ESLint `max-lines` | Reword once linting moves |

## 6. Done when

* Each batch builds clean from `--rebuild`, and its packages' own gates pass.
* Lock changes are scoped to the target packages. [KS-1379](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1379/pr-1339s-standalone-locks-were-re-resolved-from-bare-manifests-1000): an unscoped re-resolve moved \~1,000 non-target entries.
* The preflight (`Blockchain/Dev/scripts/preflight/preflight.sh`) is green, including `audit:locks`.
* A live Docker sweep on a slot passes.
* If Option 1 is chosen: every `package.json` in scope declares TypeScript 7.0.2, the same version as [KS-1396](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1396/platform-k-systemtest-observability-typescript-702-oxlinttsgolint).

## 7. Reference: toolchain inventory for this scope

**Sources:** versions from the 43 tracked `package.json` files in scope on `develop` @ `4f18c59a8`; latest from `npm view`, 2026-09-30. *(assumed)* marks general practice, not a fetched EOL date.

| Package | In use | Latest | Support / EOL |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| Node.js (runtime) | `node:24-alpine`; `engines >=18.0.0` ×5 | 24.x LTS line | Node 18 and 20 past EOL *(Node schedule, not re-fetched)* |
| typescript | ^5.3.2 ×19, ^5.3.3 ×14, ^5.7.0 ×3, ^5.3.0, ^5.1.6 | 7.0.2 | No LTS *(assumed)* |
| eslint | ^10.7.0 ×14, ^8.56.0 | 10.11.0 | v8 EOL + npm-deprecated; v9 EOL 2026-08-06 |
| typescript-eslint | ^8.64.0 | 8.71.0 | Excludes TS 7 |
| @eslint/js / globals | ^10.0.1 / ^17.7.0 | 10.0.1 / 17.12.0 | Current |
| @playwright/test | ^1.61.1, 1.58.2, ^1.40.0 | 1.63.0 | 1.40.0 npm-deprecated |
| vitest | ^4.1.11 ×15, ^4.1.9 ×9, ^1.0.4 | 5.0.3 | Latest major only *(assumed)* |
| jest / ts-jest | ^29.7.0 ×4 / ^29.4.11 ×4 | 30.5.2 / 29.4.14 | ts-jest excludes TS 7 |
| ts-node / ts-node-dev | ^10.9.2 ×5 / ^2.0.0 | 10.9.2 / 2.0.0 | Fail on TS 7 (§2) |
| tsx | ^4.23.1 ×19 | 4.23.15 | Current; works on TS 7 |
| tsup | ^8.0.1 | 8.5.1 | d.ts fails on TS 7 (§2) |

title: Repo hygiene: 31 spec files under Blockchain/Dev/tests that no Playwright config covers, 708 branches on the remote, and a duplicated website package a major React version behind
description:
## BLUF

Three separate bits of accumulated debt, none urgent, all cheap to decide and none of which anyone will notice until it misleads someone. Grouped because they are one afternoon together and three tickets apart. Measured on `develop` `8ba2da02d`, 29 Sep 2026 — branch count taken from the GitHub API, not the local clone, which is shallow here.

| \# | Where | Seen | Suggest |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| 1 | `Blockchain/Dev/tests/*.spec.ts` | **31 spec files** sitting directly in that directory, covered by no Playwright config. The repo has exactly three configs — `systemTest/playwright` (`testDir: ./tests`), `tests/e2e-v2` (`testDir: ./tests/tierN`), `tests/e2e` (`testDir: ./tests`) — and none of them resolves to `Blockchain/Dev/tests/` itself. Names read as exploratory leftovers: `admin-sidebar-collapse-{test,fresh,final}.spec.ts`, `issuer-portal-{quick,full,detailed,complete}.spec.ts`, several near-identical variants of one check | Delete, or move the ones worth keeping into `tests/e2e-v2/tests/tierN/` where a config can see them |
| 2 | The remote | **708 branches** (`gh api repos/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/branches --paginate`), of which 706 are neither `main` nor `develop`. The oldest carry no commit since March; ten are Dependabot branches whose PRs are open and stale | Prune merged and abandoned branches. Worth agreeing a rule — delete-on-merge, plus a sweep for anything with no commit in N months |
| 3 | `secuura-website-package/` | A hand-off bundle whose `source/` duplicates `Blockchain/Dev/frontend/website/` under the **same package name** `@secuura/website` v1.0.0, drifted to React 18 / Vite 5 / eslint 8 against the live copy's React 19 / Vite 8 / eslint 10; `diff -rq` over the two `src/` trees reports 19 differing files. Nothing outside itself references it — no compose service, no CI, no script | Decide: is it a deliverable that should be generated from `frontend/website` on demand, or dead weight? Either way it should not be a second copy of a shipped app under the same name |

## Why it matters

Each one is a small lie the repository tells a reader.

* **Row 1** — 31 files named `*.spec.ts` look like test coverage. They are not run by anything, cannot fail, and sit next to `tests/e2e`, `tests/e2e-v2` and `tests/connectors`, which are real. Someone counting specs to answer "how well is the admin portal covered?" gets a wrong answer. Same class as `KS-718`, where gitignored snapshots meant a fresh clone wrote its own expectations and passed.
* **Row 2** — 706 stale branches makes `git branch -r` useless for finding live work and slows every clone and fetch. It also hides the ten stale Dependabot branches behind noise.
* **Row 3** — two packages with the same name and different major versions of React is the shape that produces "it works in my build" confusion. `.planning/codebase/STRUCTURE.md:94` is the only place that mentions it, so nothing in the live docs explains why it exists.

None of this is a defect in the running platform, which is why Low.

## Suggested shape

1. Row 1 is a judgement call per file, but the duplicated-variant names (`-quick`, `-full`, `-detailed`, `-complete`, `-fresh`, `-final`) suggest most can go. Anything worth keeping earns a home under a config; anything else is deleted in one commit.
2. Row 2: agree the retention rule first, then sweep once. GitHub's automatic delete-on-merge setting would stop the recurrence.
3. Row 3: if the bundle is a customer deliverable, generate it from `frontend/website` at release time and stop tracking the copy. If it is not, delete it.

## Acceptance

* Every `*.spec.ts` in the repo is either reachable from a Playwright config or gone.
* Branch count is back to something a person can read, and the rule that keeps it there is written down.
* `@secuura/website` names exactly one package.

## Note to Kamil — please scan before fixing

Suggest doing row 1 together with `KS-1390` (the e2e-v2 harness is in no gate) and `KS-734` (the `tests/e2e` corpus cannot install from a clean checkout) rather than separately — all three are about which Playwright corpus is real, and the answer to "which of these three trees survives" settles all of them at once. Row 2 is independent and can go any time.

## References

`Blockchain/Dev/tests/*.spec.ts` (31 files) · `systemTest/playwright/playwright.config.ts` · `Blockchain/Dev/tests/e2e-v2/playwright.config.ts` · `Blockchain/Dev/tests/e2e/playwright.config.ts` · `secuura-website-package/source/package.json` vs `Blockchain/Dev/frontend/website/package.json` · `.planning/codebase/STRUCTURE.md:94` · related: `KS-1390`, `KS-734` (In Review), `KS-1038` (Backlog), `KS-718` (Done).

## Environment

Distributed_Secuura `develop` **8ba2da02d**, 29 Sep 2026. Static review — file counts and the package comparison read from the tree at that commit; the branch total came from the GitHub API because the local clone is shallow and its own count differs. Nothing was executed and nothing was deleted.

title: ci.yml's contract job cannot work — all three Aiken steps use `contracts/secuura` from the repo root, where no such directory exists; deploy-demo.yml has the same steps correct
description:
## BLUF

`.github/workflows/ci.yml` builds and tests the Aiken contracts with `cd contracts/secuura`, relative to the repo root. There is no `contracts/` at the repo root — the project is at `Blockchain/Dev/contracts/secuura` — and the workflow sets no `working-directory` and no `defaults.run.working-directory`. All three steps are wrong the same way: `aiken build` (`:205-208`), `aiken check` (`:210-213`), and the artifact path `contracts/secuura/plutus.json` (`:219`). The job would fail on the first `cd`. Latent today because Actions executes nothing on this repo, and wrong the moment it returns. The fix already exists in the tree: `deploy-demo.yml` does the identical steps with `working-directory: Blockchain/Dev/contracts/secuura`. Verified on `develop` `8ba2da02d`, 29 Sep 2026.

## What was seen

Aiken appears in exactly two workflows, and they disagree.

**Broken —** `.github/workflows/ci.yml`:

```yaml
      - name: Build contracts
        run: |
          cd contracts/secuura        # :207  — no such directory from the repo root
          aiken build

      - name: Run contract tests
        run: |
          cd contracts/secuura        # :212
          aiken check

      - name: Upload contract artifacts
        with:
          path: contracts/secuura/plutus.json   # :219
```

`grep -n "working-directory\|defaults:" .github/workflows/ci.yml` returns nothing, so there is no job-level default to rescue the relative path.

**Correct —** `.github/workflows/deploy-demo.yml:84-100`, same steps:

```yaml
      - name: Build contracts
        working-directory: Blockchain/Dev/contracts/secuura
      - name: Run contract tests
        working-directory: Blockchain/Dev/contracts/secuura
      - name: Upload contract artifacts
        with:
          path: Blockchain/Dev/contracts/secuura/plutus.json
```

So this is a straight port of a fix that was already made once, into the file that did not get it.

## Why it matters

The contracts are the best-covered thing in platform-k and the least exercised. Measured on this commit: **10 validators, 13 test modules, 378 test blocks**, including property/fuzz modules built on `aiken-lang/fuzz` v2.2.0 (`contracts/secuura/aiken.toml:20-23`). The only routes to running them are:

* `ci.yml` — broken as above, and dispatch-only anyway (`on: workflow_dispatch`, header *"CI/CD PIPELINE (DISABLED — DEPLOY VIA CURSOR)"*).
* `deploy-demo.yml` — correct, but fenced behind an explicit opt-in input because it targets the Azure Container Apps estate that was deleted in the 2026-07-08 cost pivot (`:35-39`, `:52-70`).
* `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/deploy-contracts.sh:45,76,87` — by hand, as a deploy prerequisite.

`KS-637` (Backlog, High) already records that the nightly Internal Audit has failed 40 runs straight and that *"the Aiken tests run nowhere else"*. This ticket is the narrower, immediately-fixable half: even if a runner came back tomorrow, the general-purpose job would still fail on the `cd`, so the contract tests would still not run. On-chain validators are the one area where a regression is unrecoverable after deploy — `KS-246` (Backlog) holds the external Aiken audit as the mainnet-readiness gate, and an audit is worth much less if the suite it rests on has no working automated home.

## Suggested shape

1. Port `deploy-demo.yml`'s shape into `ci.yml`: `working-directory: Blockchain/Dev/contracts/secuura` on both run steps, and `Blockchain/Dev/contracts/secuura/plutus.json` as the artifact path. Three lines.
2. Consider a job-level `defaults.run.working-directory` if other steps in that job are also root-relative — worth a read of the whole job rather than patching three lines blind.
3. While there: `contracts/secuura/TESTING.md` instructs the reader to `cd /Volumes/KK_DEV_Local/NEW STRUCTURE/…`, a former machine's absolute path, and recommends `aiken test` where every script and workflow in the repo uses `aiken check`. Same defect class — a documented path that cannot work anywhere but one laptop.
4. Add a contracts row to the manual-gate table in `Blockchain/Dev/docs/DEV-PROCESS.md:77-143`, which has none, so `aiken check` has a named local home while Actions is down.

## Acceptance

* `ci.yml`'s contract job reaches `aiken check` from a clean checkout — provable today by running the same commands locally from the repo root, without needing a runner.
* `TESTING.md` contains no machine-specific absolute path and names `aiken check`.
* `DEV-PROCESS.md` lists the contract command with its measured wall-clock, like the 13 rows already there.

## Note to Kamil — please scan before fixing

Recommend one grep across `.github/workflows/` for every root-relative `cd ` and every `path:` in an upload step, rather than fixing this instance alone. The repo moved to the `Blockchain/Dev/` layout at some point and `deploy-demo.yml` was evidently updated while `ci.yml` was not, so other files may carry the same stale assumption — and none of them can fail visibly while Actions is retired, which is exactly the condition in which this class accumulates.

## References

`.github/workflows/ci.yml:198-219` · `.github/workflows/deploy-demo.yml:79-100` · `Blockchain/Dev/contracts/secuura/` (10 validators, 13 test modules, 378 test blocks) · `contracts/secuura/aiken.toml:20-23` · `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/deploy-contracts.sh:45,76,87` · `contracts/secuura/TESTING.md` · `Blockchain/Dev/docs/DEV-PROCESS.md:77-143` · Aiken docs: [https://aiken-lang.org/](<https://aiken-lang.org/>) · related: `KS-637` (Backlog), `KS-246` (Backlog), `KS-552` (Done — the Container Apps pivot that fenced deploy-demo.yml).

## Environment

Distributed_Secuura `develop` **8ba2da02d**, 29 Sep 2026. Static review — the two workflow files were read and compared at that commit; nothing was executed and no runner was invoked. GitHub Actions on this repo answers every job with *"The job was not started because recent account payments have failed…"*, so the defect cannot surface until billing is restored.

title: No frontend declares a `test` script — six package.json files, none with one, so the issuer's vitest setup and its 12 component assertions are unreachable from any runner
description:
## BLUF

`Blockchain/Dev/frontend/` has nine directories, six of them with a `package.json`, and **not one declares a** `test` **script**. The root workspace runner is `"test": "npm run test --workspaces"` (`Blockchain/Dev/package.json:17`), so it cannot reach them. The issuer went further than the others — it has `vitest` + `@testing-library/react` + `jsdom` in devDependencies, a `test:` block in `vite.config.ts:8-12`, and two real spec files carrying 12 assertions — and none of it can be run without typing a `vitest` invocation by hand. This is unit/component coverage only; the portals themselves are covered by the e2e-v2 browser tier, which has its own problem (`KS-1390`). Read from the tree on `develop` `8ba2da02d`, 29 Sep 2026.

## What was seen

Every `scripts` block under `Blockchain/Dev/frontend/*/package.json`:

| Frontend | `scripts` | Test files present |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `admin` | `dev`, `build`, `preview`, `lint` | 0 |
| `issuer` | `dev`, `build`, `preview`, `lint`, `check:bundle` | **2** (`blockchain-card.test.tsx`, `provenance-timeline.test.tsx`) |
| `verifier` | `dev`, `build`, `preview`, `lint` | 0 |
| `website` | `dev`, `build`, `preview`, `lint` | 0 |
| `outlook-addin` | `dev`, `build`, `preview`, `lint` | 0 |
| `demo-overlay` | `build`, `dev` | 0 |
| `status`, `gmail-addon`, `shared` | no `package.json` | 0 |

So the two issuer specs are dead weight: present, maintained-looking, and executed by nothing. `frontend/issuer/vite.config.ts:8-12` configures the vitest environment for them, which makes it look deliberate rather than abandoned — the missing piece is one line in `package.json`.

## Why it matters

* **It is a silent zero.** `npm run test --workspaces` at `Blockchain/Dev` looks like it covers the workspaces, and `frontend/*` is a workspace glob (`package.json:6-10`). A reader has no signal that the frontend leg of that command is empty.
* **It is the same class already ticketed one layer down.** `KS-634` (Backlog) — *"No CI gate runs the services' unit suites — a 73-test suite sat dead on develop and every PR stayed green"* — and `KS-652` (Backlog) — *"1219 tests across 23 services are ungated"*. Those are about services having suites nothing runs; this is frontends having no suite to run, plus one that exists and cannot be reached. Same failure mode, opposite end.
* **The precedent for cost is in the repo.** `KS-649` had 31 auth tests dead since 6 Aug because two suites failed at module load and reported "no tests"; `KS-718` had golden-master snapshots gitignored, so a fresh clone wrote its own expectations and passed. Tests that cannot fail are worse than absent — they read as coverage.
* Four shipped admin pages import types from `frontend/admin/src/__mocks__/` (`DocumentTypes.tsx:20`, `DocumentTypeDetail.tsx:22`, `VerificationQueue.tsx:11`, `Workflows.tsx:12`) — a `__mocks__` directory on the production path, in an app with no test framework to justify the name. Worth a look in the same pass.

## Suggested shape

1. Add `"test": "vitest run"` to `frontend/issuer/package.json` so the 12 assertions that already exist can run and fail. One line; it is the whole fix for the unreachable half.
2. Decide for the other five whether a unit tier is wanted at all. "No unit tests for admin/verifier, the browser tier covers them" is a legitimate answer — but it should be written down rather than inferred from an absence, because today the two states are indistinguishable.
3. If the answer is none, make `npm run test --workspaces` honest: `--if-present`, or a note in `Blockchain/Dev/package.json` saying the frontend leg is intentionally empty.
4. Rename or relocate `frontend/admin/src/__mocks__/` if it is production data, so the name stops implying a test fixture.

## Acceptance

* `npm test -w frontend/issuer` runs and reports 12 passing assertions.
* A planted failure in one of those specs turns the command red (the `KS-718` lesson — prove the suite can fail before trusting it).
* The intended unit-test posture for the other frontends is stated in the repo, whatever it is.

## Note to Kamil — please scan before fixing

Suggest checking the same shape across every workspace in one pass rather than ticket by ticket: which `package.json` files declare `test`, which declare it and are never invoked by a gate, and which have test files with no script. `KS-634` / `KS-652` already hold the services half, so a single audit would close the family. The `sdk/javascript` and `sdk/python` client SDKs are a third instance — no tests at all, and not workspace members, so nothing would reach them even if they had some.

## References

`Blockchain/Dev/package.json:6-10`, `:17` · `Blockchain/Dev/frontend/*/package.json` · `frontend/issuer/vite.config.ts:8-12` · `frontend/issuer/src/__tests__/` · `frontend/admin/src/__mocks__/` · related: `KS-634` (Backlog), `KS-652` (Backlog), `KS-649` (Done), `KS-718` (Done), `KS-1390`.

## Environment

Distributed_Secuura `develop` **8ba2da02d**, 29 Sep 2026. Static review — the scripts blocks above were read from the tree at that commit; nothing was executed.

title: The e2e-v2 harness is platform-k's only browser, portal and accessibility coverage — 222 tests, runnable by hand, named in no gate and absent from the gate inventory
description:
## BLUF

`Blockchain/Dev/tests/e2e-v2/` holds **24 spec files and 222 tests** across four tiers — including every browser journey and the only accessibility coverage platform-k has — and it is wired into nothing. It is not in `.githooks/pre-push`, it has no row in the "Manual CI-gate equivalents" table that `KS-685` commissioned, and the workflow its own README points at (`.github/workflows/e2e-tests.yml`) does not exist on `develop`. Meanwhile the suite people *are* pointed at, `systemTest/playwright`, is API-only: 3 spec files, 11 tests, no browser. So the documented estate says platform-k has a Playwright tier, and the thing that actually opens a browser is the one nobody is told to run. Counted on `develop` `8ba2da02d`, 29 Sep 2026. Nothing was executed — this is about wiring, not results.

## What is there

Measured from the tree, not from the docs:

| Tier | Specs | Tests | What it covers |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| `tier1-api` | 12 | 174 | API over HTTP |
| `tier2-smoke` | 5 | 43 | Smoke journeys |
| `tier3-e2e` | 4 | 40 | **Real browser journeys** — issuer, admin, verifier |
| `tier4-a11y` | 3 | 6 | **axe on admin, issuer and verifier** |
| **Total** | **24** | **222** |  |

It is runnable today. `Blockchain/Dev/tests/e2e-v2/package.json` declares `test`, `test:api`, `test:smoke`, `test:e2e`, `test:a11y`, `install:browsers` and `report`, and `playwright.config.ts` defines the four matching projects (`api`, `smoke`, `e2e`, `a11y`). `@axe-core/playwright` is a devDependency there.

## What is missing

1. **No gate names it.** `grep -rn "e2e-v2" .githooks/pre-push Blockchain/Dev/docs/DEV-PROCESS.md` returns nothing. The manual-gate table at `DEV-PROCESS.md:77-143` maps *former CI job → local command* for 13 rows and has no row for e2e-v2, and none for accessibility at all.
2. **Its README cites a workflow that does not exist.** `Blockchain/Dev/tests/e2e/README.md:4` sends the reader to `.github/workflows/e2e-tests.yml`; `git ls-tree origin/develop .github/workflows/e2e-tests.yml` is empty.
3. **The plan doc under-reports it.** `Blockchain/Dev/docs/E2E-TESTING-PLAN.md:324` still says *"only the verifier portal has a tier-4 spec. Issuer + admin coverage is a follow-up."* That follow-up is `KS-44`, which is **Done** — there are three tier-4 specs in the tree today. The row understates the coverage that exists.

## Why it matters

* It is the whole UI answer. Without it the honest statement about platform-k is that no browser opens anywhere in the estate — `systemTest/playwright/playwright.config.ts:12-18` says so itself, and `DEV-PROCESS.md:141` spells it out: *"Despite the name, this suite drives no browser… Read a green here as '12 API assertions passed', not as 'the portals work'."*
* It is the whole accessibility answer. There is no `eslint-plugin-jsx-a11y` anywhere in the repo and no axe inside any frontend, so `tier4-a11y` is the only thing that would catch a regression against WCAG 2.2 / EN 301 549 — relevant to the same obligations the platform-s side tracks. WCAG 2.2: [https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG22/](<https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG22/>) · EN 301 549 v3.2.1: [https://www.etsi.org/deliver/etsi_en/301500_301599/301549/03.02.01_60/en_301549v030201p.pdf](<https://www.etsi.org/deliver/etsi_en/301500_301599/301549/03.02.01_60/en_301549v030201p.pdf>) · EAA Directive 2019/882: [https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/dir/2019/882/oj](<https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/dir/2019/882/oj>)
* An ungated suite rots quietly. `KS-557` / `KS-560` are the precedent — the tier reported 126 failures, of which only 11 were real, and the cause was a harness defect that had gone unnoticed. `systemTest/CLAUDE.md:358` keeps that lesson as a standing rule.
* Actions being retired makes this the *only* route to the coverage, not a redundant one.

## Suggested shape

1. Give e2e-v2 a row in the `DEV-PROCESS.md` manual-gate table: the exact command, the pass criterion, and a measured wall-clock — matching the 13 rows already there.
2. Decide the tier split deliberately. `tier4-a11y` is 6 tests and needs only a running stack; it is the cheapest thing in the estate to make routine. `tier3-e2e` is slower and flakier (single-session collisions, `E2E-TESTING-PLAN.md` § "Worker-session collisions") so it may belong in a nightly/manual tier rather than a per-push one.
3. Fix the two stale pointers: the dead workflow reference in `tests/e2e/README.md:4`, and the tier-4 row in `E2E-TESTING-PLAN.md:324` that `KS-44` has already overtaken.
4. Say in `systemTest/CLAUDE.md` where the browser tier actually lives, so "Playwright" stops meaning two different things in the same repo.

## Acceptance

* `DEV-PROCESS.md`'s gate table has an e2e-v2 row (or rows) with a command and a measured time.
* A named person can run the a11y tier from the runbook without reading source.
* No document points at `.github/workflows/e2e-tests.yml`, and the tier-4 row reflects the three specs that exist.

## Decision needed before fixing — naming the three Playwright estates

Worth settling the naming in the same pass: `systemTest/playwright` (API-only, 11 tests) and `Blockchain/Dev/tests/e2e-v2` (browser, 222 tests) are both "Playwright", and a third corpus sits at `Blockchain/Dev/tests/e2e` (`KS-734`, In Review — not a workspace member, cannot install from a clean checkout; `KS-1038`, Backlog — races its own lockout). Three Playwright estates with one name is the reason a reader can believe the portals are covered when the suite in the gate never opens a browser. One decision about which survives, which is gated, and what each is called would close this ticket and shrink two others.

## References

`Blockchain/Dev/tests/e2e-v2/package.json` · `playwright.config.ts:29-73` · `Blockchain/Dev/docs/DEV-PROCESS.md:77-143`, `:141` · `Blockchain/Dev/docs/E2E-TESTING-PLAN.md:316-345` · `Blockchain/Dev/tests/e2e/README.md:4` · `systemTest/playwright/playwright.config.ts:12-18` · `systemTest/CLAUDE.md:358` · related: `KS-1076` (Urgent, Todo — no Playwright e2e on a PR since 7 Sep), `KS-734` (In Review), `KS-1038` (Backlog), `KS-44` (Done), `KS-637` (Backlog), `KS-685`.

## Environment

Distributed_Secuura `develop` **8ba2da02d**, 29 Sep 2026. Static review — no stack started, no suite executed; all counts measured from the tree at that commit. GitHub Actions executes nothing on this repo (billing), so no workflow is a live alternative to the local route.

nodes.body:
**BLUF:** Hi Kamil, thanks for picking this up. While grounding a plan for this ticket I found six more things that bear on it. Each one was re-checked from source on `develop` **`8c810023f`** (29 Sep), not taken from memory. The most important is #1: once e2e-v2 is named in a gate, a bare local run of it hits slot 1's gateway without saying so. Nothing was edited or run. These are notes for you to take or leave as you see fit.

**1. e2e-v2 has no slot awareness, so a local run naming no slot targets slot 1.**
- `playwright.config.ts:3` defaults `GATEWAY_URL` to `http://localhost:6882`.
- `fixtures/api-client.ts:17` and `:22` do the same for the API and issuer bases.
- Nothing under `tests/e2e-v2` reads `SECUURA_STACK_SLOT` or `STACK_SLOT` (0 matches).

On a shared machine that means another ticket's stack. The systemTest harnesses refuse this case (KS-1016), and e2e-v2 would be the one browser suite that doesn't.

The good news is that `systemTest/slot-target.sh:99` already exports a slot-derived `GATEWAY_URL`, and that's the first variable e2e-v2 reads. So wrapping the gate command, e.g. `systemTest/run-in-slot.sh <N> npm --prefix Blockchain/Dev/tests/e2e-v2 run test:a11y`, would target the right stack and hold the per-slot lock with no typed port. A small refusal guard in the config would cover the bare `npm run` case. That's your call.

**2. The runbook the acceptance line relies on is itself stale.** "Run the a11y tier from the runbook without reading source" needs these fixed first.
- `RUNBOOK.md`:
  - `:16` lists tier 4 as 2 tests; there are 6.
  - `:189` says a11y is "admin/verifier-only"; issuer is covered too.
  - `:63-72` give the decommissioned Container Apps demo URLs.
  - `:48` hand-rolls `docker compose up -d` rather than `Start_Up/start-secuura.sh`.
- `README.md`:
  - 8 lines still carry the dead secuura01 `yellowground-ae96b9b1` URLs, which KS-333 repointed elsewhere.
  - `:24` says "3 Tiers"; there are four.
  - Its credentials table names the retired admin password, which may already fall under KS-965's documentary cleanup if it isn't one of its 55 files.
- `tests/tier4-a11y/README.md`:
  - `:11` says to install axe at `Blockchain/Dev`; it's in e2e-v2's own `package.json` and lock now.
  - `:71-73` describe `button-name` / `color-contrast` as demoted under KS-45; no spec passes `knownIssueRules` any more.
  - `:26` runs against `GATEWAY_URL=https://secuura.com`, a domain we don't own. That's the KS-669 class, in a README rather than the spec.

**3. The admin a11y test needs `TEST_ADMIN_PASSWORD`, and no e2e-v2 doc says so.** `fixtures/api-client.ts:61` leaves it empty when unset. That's deliberate (KS-964, no published fallback), so this is a docs gap rather than a code bug. But anyone following the runbook will get a failed admin login and nothing telling them why. The variable is documented only in `systemTest/playwright`'s docs.

**4. Stale suppression in `tests/tier4-a11y/_axe.ts:15`.** `// @ts-expect-error — package is not yet in the e2e-v2 lockfile`. It is in the lockfile now (`package-lock.json:16`). Nothing type-checks e2e-v2 (see #5), so this has never surfaced. Under a real `tsc` it would likely become an "unused @ts-expect-error" error.

**5. e2e-v2 has no quality gates of its own.**
- The package has no tsconfig, Prettier config or ESLint config.
- The repo-level `Blockchain/Dev/eslint.config.mjs` only targets `services/`, `packages/`, `sdk/`, `scripts/` and `frontend/`.

So a gate row for e2e-v2 would run specs that nothing lints or type-checks. Worth deciding whether a minimal `typecheck` belongs in the same change.

**6. A timing measurement can't use a current build yet (KS-1380).** The acceptance asks for a measured wall-clock, but `develop` still doesn't build: `packages/shared` locks `@types/express-serve-static-core` 4.19.9 and `@types/pg` 8.23.1, while analytics, billing and governance still lock 4.19.8 / 8.20.0. Until KS-1380 lands, a timing run would need a stack built at `8af6ab821`, as other slots have been, and the evidence should say so.

**Smaller count notes:**
- The gate table in `DEV-PROCESS.md` has 14 rows at this commit, not 13.
- `.github/workflows/e2e-tests.yml` is also cited at `docs/REVIEW_NOTES.md:276` and `CHANGELOG.md:73`, as well as `tests/e2e/README.md:4`. The CHANGELOG line is history and probably wants to stay.

**Related, already tracked:** KS-1393 row 1 (31 uncovered specs; its note already suggests doing it together with this ticket and KS-734), KS-965 (retired admin credential in docs), KS-669 (URLs on domains we don't own), KS-1380 (build).

Happy to help with any of it if useful. Thank you!

title: Sourcing systemTest/slot-target.sh with no slot named silently exports slot 1's targets — and preflight leg 13 + the pre-push hook depend on that, so it cannot be fixed in systemTest alone
description:
## BLUF

**No action is needed today, and nothing is broken on the trunk.** This asks for your view on one coordinated change that sits across your files and systemTest.

`systemTest/slot-target.sh`, sourced with **no** slot named, silently exports slot 1's targets. Every harness now refuses an unslotted local run in its own code, so the export itself is the last place a slot is silently defaulted. It can't simply be made to refuse, though: **preflight leg 13 and the pre-push hook source it with no slot, on purpose**, and leg 13's positive control would then refuse every push.

Found by the [KS-1386](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1386/systemtest-api-explorer-hard-codes-slot-1s-gateway-6882-a-slot-n) systemTest slot audit (2026-09-29). Re-checked against `develop` @ `8ba2da02d`, code and docs, not from memory.

## What happens today

* `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/stack_env.sh` resolves `SECUURA_STACK_SLOT="${SECUURA_STACK_SLOT:-${STACK_SLOT:-1}}"`: an unnamed slot becomes **1**.
* `systemTest/slot-target.sh:51` records whether a slot was actually requested (`SECUURA_SLOT_REQUESTED`), then sources `stack_env.sh` and exports slot 1's `SECUURA_GATEWAY_URL`, `API_BASE_URL`, `SECUURA_BASE_URL`, `SECUURA_API_URL`, `PERF_BASE_URL`, the `AKTO_*` set and `SECUURA_ARTIFACT_SUFFIX=-slot1`. `SECUURA_SLOT_REQUESTED` is only used by `retarget()`.
* The TypeScript harnesses still refuse an unslotted local run, because `SECUURA_STACK_SLOT` itself is never exported. Akto and Schemathesis read several of these exports directly, though. [KS-1386](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1386/systemtest-api-explorer-hard-codes-slot-1s-gateway-6882-a-slot-n) is adding their own entry-point guards so they no longer depend on this.

## Why it can't be fixed in systemTest alone

* `.githooks/pre-push:273-285` ([KS-691](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-691/pre-push-preflight-cannot-run-from-a-git-worktree-legs-1-and-6-fail)) sources it deliberately, `|| true`, so the stack-dependent legs probe *this* slot's gateway rather than preflight's own `localhost:6882` default. When the developer's shell names no slot, that is the slot-1 export.
* `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/preflight/preflight.sh:589-630` (leg 13, [KS-786](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-786/stack-env-and-slot-target-read-the-values-they-unit-test-out-of-the)) **measures** the variables `slot-target.sh` exports under `env -i`, **with no slot named**, and has a positive control: an empty list refuses the leg. If `slot-target.sh` refused (exported nothing) when unslotted, that control would fire and **every push would be refused.**

So the three pieces have to move together, and the hook and preflight are yours.

## A possible shape (entirely your call)

1. `slot-target.sh`: when `SECUURA_SLOT_REQUESTED` is empty and `CI` is not truthy, export nothing target-bearing and print a one-line notice, or `return 2`, matching the refusal the TS harnesses use (`systemTest/fixtures/slot-required.ts:76-91`).
2. **Leg 13:** measure the export set with an explicit slot (e.g. `SECUURA_STACK_SLOT=1` inside the `env -i` subshell) rather than relying on the unslotted default. Its purpose, the full clear-list, is unchanged.
3. **Pre-push:** when no slot is named, say so and let the stack-dependent legs report SKIPPED (the [KS-1046](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1046/preflight-passed-is-printed-identically-whether-13-legs-ran-or-10-the) verdict), rather than probing slot 1.

Related: [KS-1355](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1355/stack-tooling-is-not-slot-derived-end-to-end-stack-guard-lists-a) (stack tooling not slot-derived end to end), [KS-786](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-786/stack-env-and-slot-target-read-the-values-they-unit-test-out-of-the) (leg 13's origin), [KS-691](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-691/pre-push-preflight-cannot-run-from-a-git-worktree-legs-1-and-6-fail) (why the hook sources it).

## Not done here

No change to `slot-target.sh`, the hook or preflight on the [KS-1386](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1386/systemtest-api-explorer-hard-codes-slot-1s-gateway-6882-a-slot-n) branch. Peter's ruling (2026-09-29): raise it for you rather than change your files.

Thank you, and apologies for another slot ticket. This one felt worth raising because the obvious fix would have quietly blocked every push.

## Shared acceptance — slot derivation group (added 6 Oct 2026)

This ticket is one of five platform-k tickets that must all take slot values from `stack_env.sh` and never fall back to slot 1: [KS-1355](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1355>), [KS-1381](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1381>), [KS-1389](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1389>), [KS-1382](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1382>), [KS-1162](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1162>). None of them is done until these hold, in addition to its own acceptance above:

1. **One guard.** A single static guard in `check-stack-safety.sh` fails on any literal published port of any slot 1–4 outside `stack_env.sh`. The first ticket to land creates it; the others extend it; nobody adds a second guard. Bite-checked: plant a literal, see it red, remove it.
2. **No silent default.** A local run with no slot named refuses and prints an example command; it never falls back to slot 1 (preflight, `slot-target.sh`, the `Blockchain/Testing` entry points, the smoke scripts). Any change to `stack_env.sh`'s own slot-1 default re-runs every test in this group.
3. **One preflight change.** [KS-1355](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1355/stack-tooling-is-not-slot-derived-end-to-end-stack-guard-lists-a) (spot 4, `preflight.sh:94`) and [KS-1389](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1389/sourcing-systemtestslot-targetsh-with-no-slot-named-silently-exports) (leg 13, `preflight.sh:589-630`) land in one PR, or one after the other, each re-running the other's checks.
4. **The workflow question.** [KS-1162](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1162/three-retired-github-workflows-bake-slot-234-port-literals) decides first whether the three workflows are deleted or made to derive their ports. If deleted, [KS-1382](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1382/blockchaintesting-five-auditdasttenant-isolation-entry-points-default)'s "explicit `TARGET_BASE` is used unchanged" criterion has no CI caller left; if derived, their `TARGET_BASE` comes from `stack_env.sh` too.
5. **Tests cover every slot.** Slots 1–4, hermetic: identical results unslotted and under each slot's environment.

**This ticket's part:** points 2 and 3 — `slot-target.sh` refusing when unslotted is point 2; leg 13 is coordinated with [KS-1355](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1355/stack-tooling-is-not-slot-derived-end-to-end-stack-guard-lists-a)'s spot 4. This ticket had no acceptance section of its own, so these points are its acceptance, together with the three steps of its possible shape.

title: observability/ reaches the platform by slot 1's container names (documented), and both .env examples suggest the nginx stub_status on :6882, a port that does not exist on the container network
description:
## BLUF

`observability/` is **slot 1 only by a documented decision**, and that decision stands. This ticket records what would need to change to make it slot-aware, so the work is ready when [KS-984](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-984/no-service-exposes-metrics-the-secuura-services-scrape-job-has-never)'s `/metrics` lands. It also covers **one real error to fix now**: both example env files suggest a gateway status URL on a port that does not exist inside the container network.

Found by the [KS-1386](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1386/systemtest-api-explorer-hard-codes-slot-1s-gateway-6882-a-slot-n) systemTest slot audit (2026-09-29). Re-checked against `develop` @ `8ba2da02d`, code and docs, not from memory.

## 1. The concrete error (small, fix any time)

* `observability/.env.example:47` and `observability/config/alerting.env.example:55` both say:
  `# SECUURA_NGINX_STATUS_URI=http://secuura-nginx-gateway:6882/stub_status`
* **6882 is the host-side port of the gateway's** `6882:80` **publish.** Inside the container network only **80** exists. The compose default already uses it (`docker-compose.yml:331`: `${SECUURA_NGINX_STATUS_URI:-http://secuura-nginx-gateway:80/stub_status}`), and `prometheus/prometheus.yml:48-52` explains why the old `:6882` scrape job was removed for exactly this reason.
* Anyone who uncomments the example gets an nginx exporter that cannot connect. **Fix:** change both examples to `:80`.

## 2. Where observability assumes slot 1 (documented, for when [KS-984](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-984/no-service-exposes-metrics-the-secuura-services-scrape-job-has-never) lands)

| Where | What | Documented as |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `scripts/observability.sh:57` | `docker inspect secuura-nginx-gateway` to discover the platform network | override `SECUURA_PLATFORM_NETWORK` |
| `scripts/observability.sh:96-100` | `docker exec "${SECUURA_PG_CONTAINER:-secuura-postgres}"` to read DB credentials | "SLOT 1 ONLY, deliberately" (`:88-90`) |
| `scripts/observability.sh:137-138` | `docker inspect "${SECUURA_REDIS_CONTAINER:-secuura-redis}"` | same limitation |
| `docker-compose.yml:296, 311, 331` | exporter defaults name `secuura-postgres`, `secuura-redis`, `secuura-nginx-gateway` | same |
| `prometheus/prometheus.yml:82-92` | `secuura-services` static targets `secuura-auth:4003` … labelled `slot: slot1` | "⚠ SLOT 1 ONLY" (`:74-78`) |
| `loki/alloy.river:84-92` | default `slot = "slot1"` for **every** container, then more specific rules override | README "Which stack slot am I looking at?" |

The README states the position clearly ("What is NOT per-slot: application metrics"), and the reasoning in `prometheus.yml:74-78` is sound: slot discovery needs either a Docker socket inside Prometheus or a generated targets file plus per-slot `docker network connect`, and neither is worth it while the job collects nothing ([KS-984](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-984/no-service-exposes-metrics-the-secuura-services-scrape-job-has-never)).

**One small thing worth considering, independent of** [KS-984](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-984/no-service-exposes-metrics-the-secuura-services-scrape-job-has-never)**:** `alloy.river`'s default labels non-platform containers (Akto, observability's own, a k6 container without its label) as `slot1`. A neutral default such as `unslotted` would stop those logs appearing under slot 1 in the picker. That matches the rule the [KS-1386](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1386/systemtest-api-explorer-hard-codes-slot-1s-gateway-6882-a-slot-n) systemTest fix adopts: an unslotted run is labelled `unslotted`, never `slot1`.

## Suggested shape (when [KS-984](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-984/no-service-exposes-metrics-the-secuura-services-scrape-job-has-never) is picked up)

* Derive container names from `STACK_PREFIX` (`Blockchain/Dev/scripts/stack_env.sh:58-64`: `secuura` on slot 1, `secuura-s<N>` above) rather than typing `secuura-<svc>`.
* Revisit the static scrape job together with [KS-984](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-984/no-service-exposes-metrics-the-secuura-services-scrape-job-has-never)/[KS-985](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-985/eight-dashboards-show-a-slot-picker-that-filters-nothing-latent-today), as `prometheus.yml:74-78` already proposes.

## Not done here

No code changed. The observability stack was not started; this is a read of the files at `8ba2da02d`.

nodes.body: **BLUF:** Delivered: PR 1387 merged as 32e058975d4e on develop; no deploy surface (docs/tests/example env files only: observability/.env.example, observability/config/alerting.env.example, Blockchain/Dev/scripts/__tests__/prometheus_targets.test.sh and two Projects Documents HTML files, the squash's only files). Verified by code read: `observability/.env.example:48` and `observability/config/alerting.env.example:56` at b1fb543640e7 both set SECUURA_NGINX_STATUS_URI to http://secuura-nginx-gateway:80/stub_status, the one error this ticket said to fix now. Left open: the rest of the ticket records what a slot-aware observability/ would need, ready for when KS-984's /metrics lands, and the finding appended on 2026-10-07 (npm run down exits 1 with no message when slot 1's secuura-redis or secuura-postgres container is absent) is recorded there with no commit after PR 1387 naming KS-1388 on the deployed history.

## Appended 2026-10-07 (posted at Peter's instruction) — a consequence of §2: `npm run down` fails whenever slot 1's platform isn't running

**BLUF:** the credential lookups in §2 (`scripts/observability.sh:96-100` Postgres, `:137-138` Redis) run **before** the action switch, under `set -euo pipefail` (`:25`). So `npm run down` exits 1, **with no error message**, whenever slot 1's `secuura-redis` or `secuura-postgres` container isn't present. The stack keeps running. Stopping it needs neither credential.

**Observed on Peter's Mac, 2026-10-07**, with observability started from the KS-1445 worktree:
- Slot 1 had been stopped by another session.
- `npm run down` → `bash scripts/observability.sh down` → exit 1, and all 9 `secuura-obs-*` containers were still up.
- `bash -x` shows the run stopping inside `resolve_redis_password`, called at file scope via `_pg_dsn="$(resolve_pg_dsn)"` (`:115`) and the Redis equivalent, after `docker inspect secuura-redis` finds no container. The `down)` branch (`:257-259`) is never reached.

**Workaround used:** the `down` branch's own command, run directly from `observability/`:
```bash
docker compose -f docker-compose.yml --profile phase2 down
```
It removed all 9 containers and kept the 3 data volumes, as `down` normally does.

**Fix direction (suggestion, not done):** resolve the platform credentials only for the actions that start containers (`start` / `up` / `phase2`), or make the lookups non-fatal for `down` / `status` / `logs`. Stopping the stack should never depend on the platform being up.

No code changed. Re-verified against the script at `develop` b280b74ff before posting.

title: A clean image build of platform-k develop fails: services/governance does not compile (TS2742 on router's inferred type) — a new slot cannot start until the image exists from an older build
description:
## Seen (2026-09-29, develop `0aa9b52c6`; origin/develop `b4461d1e2` is three commits ahead, none touching governance)

Starting a fresh stack slot with no cached images (`Start_Up/start-secuura.sh` via platform-s's `up-slot.sh 4`) fails at the governance image:

```
docker compose -p secuura_slot4 build --progress=plain governance
#19 1.611 src/routes/governance.ts(19,7): error TS2742: The inferred type of 'router' cannot be
      named without a reference to '@secuura/shared/node_modules/@types/express-serve-static-core'.
      This is likely not portable. A type annotation is necessary.
#19 ERROR: process "/bin/sh -c npm run build" did not complete successfully: exit code: 1
```

Reproducible: the same `docker compose build governance` fails the same way on a second run. Slots 1–3 on this machine start only because they hold `secuura_slot{1,2,3}-governance` images built up to two weeks ago; slot 4 had no image and could not be built. A new developer machine, or a slot torn down with `--rmi all` (the test-discipline teardown), hits this.

The first attempt on the same slot failed one image earlier — `nft-certificate` at `npm ci --ignore-scripts` — and that one built cleanly on retry, so it was transient; governance is not.

## Suggested fix

`services/governance/src/routes/governance.ts:19` — give `router` an explicit type (`const router: Router = express.Router()`), the usual TS2742 remedy when a workspace package (`@secuura/shared`) carries its own `@types/express-serve-static-core`. Worth a `tsc --noEmit` over every service in the PR gate so a non-portable inferred type cannot land again.

## Impact on platform-s

Blocks pairing an S slot with a fresh K slot for the gate run on platform-s PR #889 (the S↔K remediation branch); recorded there and on [PS-928](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-928/k-live-goes-red-on-the-second-full-run-on-a-slot-the-anchor-refresher). Related: [KS-955](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-955/a-fresh-clone-cannot-run-the-four-platform-suites-and-fails-in-a-way) (a fresh clone cannot run the suites).

nodes.body:
@kamil.kreiser — the rebuild evidence, as asked. Read it before deciding; on your own criterion it does **not** close this ticket.

- **Command:** `./Start_Up/start-secuura.sh --rebuild` (Stuart, by hand, from his `~/obd-dev/platform-k` clone, clean on `develop` at **`78cb3c393`**), slot 1, 2026-10-18 22:45:40Z → 23:02:58Z. The script builds **serially**, one `docker compose --progress=plain -f docker-compose.local.yml build <service>` per service with `COMPOSE_BAKE=0`; it passes **no `--no-cache`**, so the layer cache was warm from the 15 Oct build — not a cold build. `governance` built 22:53:14Z → 22:54:38Z (image `2f87233cfc20`), then the script went on to `issuer-frontend`; all 33 services came up healthy, `/health/deep` 200, migrations `applied=0 skipped=51`.
- **The variable you named:** inside `platform-k-governance:latest` there is exactly **one** copy of `@types/express-serve-static-core`, at `/shared/node_modules/…`, version **`4.19.9`** — no nested second copy. That is the repository-lockfile layout you describe as the one in which the pre-fix tip also builds clean.

So this build shows that develop at `78cb3c393` (which carries `b45b69171`) builds under the single-copy layout; it cannot distinguish "the explicit `Router` type removed the error class" from "this layout never produces it". The sentence in our document is corrected accordingly: fixed on develop, proven only in the non-reproducing layout. Leave the ticket where you judge it; nothing on S waits on it.

**BLUF: @stuart.jamieson — your document says this is fixed and proven by a clean rebuild of develop on 19 Oct across 33 services, and asks us to close it. I am not closing it on that, and I would rather tell you exactly why than close it quietly. Could you paste the rebuild evidence here? Then it closes on your measurement rather than on nobody's.**

**Why your claim is not yet this ticket's evidence.** The ticket's acceptance is a clean *image* build of develop. The last work recorded here is explicit that the clean image build **was never run on our side** — the Docker daemon was down on the machine doing the work — and that is still true today: there is no Docker on the machine I am on, so I cannot reproduce your result or contradict it.

**And there is a reason not to assume it.** When the TS2742 failure was examined, it only reproduced when the two nested `@types/express-serve-static-core` copies were pinned to **different** versions. With the repository's own lockfiles both resolve to `4.19.9`, and in that layout **the pre-fix tip builds clean too**. So a green build of develop is consistent with two different worlds: the fix removed the error class, or the lockfile state was never going to produce it. A green build alone does not distinguish them, which means closing on "it builds now" could close a ticket whose symptom is still live for anyone whose install hoists differently.

**What would settle it,** and any one of these is enough:

1. The **exact command** you ran (`docker compose build`, a specific Dockerfile target, or something else) and **which develop SHA**.
2. Whether the 33 services were built **from a cold cache** — a warm layer cache can skip the compile step that fails.
3. If you have it, the resolved `@types/express-serve-static-core` versions in the image that built, since that is the variable the failure turns on.

Paste that and I will record it as the evidence and close the ticket against it. If you would rather not spend the time, say so and I will leave it In Progress with this comment as the reason — that is a better outcome than a ticket closed on an unverified claim.

No date, and nothing else is blocked on this.

**PR #1581 is merged to `develop` as `b45b69171b362da0233842cdd14c161c2f9266c2`.** `governance.ts:19` now reads `const router: Router = Router();`. Nothing deployed; the ticket stays In Progress.

**What gate H2 showed about TS2742 — stated exactly, because it decides whether this ticket's symptom is closed.** H2 reproduced TS2742 **without Docker**, but **only by pinning the two nested `@types/express-serve-static-core` copies to DIFFERENT versions**: in that layout the tip fails and this head builds clean, so **the change removes that error class**. **With the repository's real lockfiles both copies are `4.19.9` and the tip builds clean too.** So whether the ticket's original image-build failure is closed stays **"not reproduced with the real lockfiles"**. The clean `docker compose build governance` was not run (no Docker daemon in my environment) — that remains the real check, e.g. at the next governance deploy.

**Low note from H2:** the new `ks1387` suite goes red if a trailing comment is ever added to the declaration line (it matches the line literally).

**Evidence on the tree that landed** (predicted commit `4a87bcb052fa`, tree `f33b620c79e8` — byte-identical to the PR head's own tree, develop having not moved since the gate), in two environments: the new suite **3/3**; governance in full **119/119**; `tsc` (TypeScript 5.9.3) rc 0. Five-point read 5/5 TRUE.

**Raised as PR #1581**, head `6b4bcaec11fa4aea156a11bbaa23b56b09126b63`, on develop `385fc288fae8`. Not merged, not deployed.

`services/governance/src/routes/governance.ts:19` — `const router: Router = Router();`. Byte-checked: the applied file differs from the tip **only on that line** (the Spark patch's blank-line churn around it is a no-op; lines 18 and 20 are byte-identical).

**This ticket's own symptom is NOT reproduced, and I want that to be plain.** The clean image build was **not run** — the Docker daemon is down here. Governance's local `npm run build` is rc 0 **at the tip as well as with the change**, because this install hoists `@types/express-serve-static-core` to the root and has no copy nested under `packages/shared` — the layout that triggers TS2742. So a local pass is **not** evidence the image build is fixed. The real check is `docker compose build governance` from a clean cache; worth running at the next governance deploy.

Evidence (mine): red-first **2/1** (the annotation cell); green **3/3**; governance in full **119/119**; `tsc` rc 0; push preflight 13/16, nothing failed.

Clean build confirmed, 2 Oct. `SECUURA_STACK_SLOT=3 ./Start_Up/start-secuura.sh --rebuild` at develop `88e8877a2`: **35 of 35 services built, 0 failed**, including `governance`, `analytics` and `billing`; the stack came up with 33 containers running (32 with a healthcheck, all healthy) and the two one-shot jobs (`migrations`, `demo-overlay`) exited 0; gateway `/health` and `/health/deep` both 200. The first pass was cut off by my session's time limit at service 32 during a slow package download, so the last four were built on a second pass with the first 31 from cache — no service failed in either pass.

The fault this ticket records is gone (fixed by KS-1380, `6cf5c3629`). Safe to close from the Platform-S side.

One thing worth knowing for slot users: before the rebuild, slot 3 started in under a minute on images dated 15 Sep while its owner marker read `develop @ 88e8877a2`. The marker records the checkout, not what the images were built from.

Re-read at develop `88e8877a2` (2 Oct): KS-1380's fix has merged (`6cf5c3629`), and `services/analytics`, `services/billing`, `services/governance` and `packages/shared` now all lock `@types/express-serve-static-core` 4.19.9 and `@types/pg` 8.23.1. That removes the cause recorded here. I have not re-run the clean image build, so this is from the lock files only; the ticket can close once one clean build of those three services is confirmed.

Definitive list, every service built one at a time from `0aa9b52c6` with Docker's disk cleared: **three fail** — `governance` (TS2742), `analytics` (TS2742 ×4) and `billing` (`src/db.ts:45` TS2345, the `@types/pg` `Pool` from `/app` vs `/shared`); the other 20 images build cleanly. None of the three is on Platform-S's path, so for the PR #889 gate run I tagged the 28 Sep 08:43 slot-1 images as the slot-4 images for exactly those three and built everything else fresh — recorded on the run so the evidence says which K each service ran.

It is wider than governance. Building every service for a fresh slot one at a time (2026-09-29, `0aa9b52c6`), so far:

* `analytics` — `npm run build`: TS2742 on `app` (`src/index.ts:34`), `router` (`src/routes/analytics.ts:20`), `dashboardRouter` (`src/routes/dashboard.ts:12`), `healthRouter` (`src/routes/health.ts:7`) — all "cannot be named without a reference to `@secuura/shared/node_modules/@types/express-serve-static-core`".
* another service in the same pass — `src/db.ts:45`: TS2345 `import("/app/node_modules/@types/pg").Pool` is not assignable to `import("/shared/node_modules/@types/pg").Pool` — the same shape: `/shared` (built from `packages/shared` inside the image) carries its own `@types/*` that no longer match the service's.
* `nft-certificate` and `transfer` failed once each for a different reason (Docker's disk was full mid-build: `chmod: … No space left on device`); both build after reclaiming space, so they are not part of this.

Two observations for whoever picks it up: (1) the images that exist on this machine from a 28 Sep 08:43 build are fine, and the only 29 Sep commit touching dependencies is KS-1378 (`2cb858335`, morgan / nodemailer / ip-address / undici bumps) — a duplicate-`@types` drift between `packages/shared` and the services is the shape a lockfile bump produces; (2) `Blockchain/Dev/.dockerignore` excludes `node_modules` and `services/*/node_modules` but not `packages/shared/node_modules`, so a host that has run `npm install` inside `packages/shared` would ship that directory into the `COPY packages/shared/ ./` layer — not the case on this machine, but it is a second way to get exactly this error. The full per-service list follows when the loop finishes.

title: Organisation merge moves DocumentStore.OrganisationId with no K call — the documents' K estate stays under the old organisation's connector while S now signs and reads back with the new one
description:
## Finding (S↔K compatibility review, 2026-09-29, develop `477eb57`)

`OrganisationMergeService` re-homes every live document of the moving members:

```
ssd/Services/OrganisationMergeService.cs:315-325
  foreach (var doc in documents) { doc.OrganisationId = targetOrganisationId; … }
```

There is no platform-k call in that service beyond reading the `PlatformKOrganisation` row (`:155-158`). `DocumentStore.OrganisationId` is what selects the connector key for every later anchor and read (`CardanoAnchorService.cs:1411-1412`, `OwnerOrgId(doc)`), and K scopes document reads and per-verb writes to the key's organisation (the [KS-480](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-480/sk-k-side-support-consistent-userorg-ownership-credential) model; originate refuses a foreign `organizationUuid` with 403 — [PS-801](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-801/the-local-platform-k-refuses-every-s-originate-with-403-forbidden)).

So after a merge, every later event on a moved document (share, declare, delete, note…) is sent under the **target** organisation's key against a K document owned by the **source** organisation's connector. What K does then (403, or an anchor attributed to the wrong org) was not verified live in the review — `docs/org-recognition-configuration.md` already notes the conflict.

## Decide / do

1. Rule the intended semantics with Kamil: does a merge transfer the K documents (a K-side re-home under the target connector), or does S keep anchoring under the source key for pre-merge documents (a per-document connector, not per-org)?
2. Until ruled, the merge tool should say on its preview that K-side lineage of moved documents stays with the source organisation.

## Verify

Paired slot: originate under org A, merge A → B, then `note` the document; the event must anchor (not 403) and Verify must still resolve the document.

Related: [PS-492](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-492/e483-task-9-administrator-merge-tool-consolidate-stranded-per-user) (merge tool), [PS-690](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-690/adopt-org-owned-documents-ownership-model-for-single-vs-multi-user) (org-owned documents), [PS-319](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-319/sk-consistent-organisationuser-ownership-dr-credential-reconciliation), [PS-801](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-801/the-local-platform-k-refuses-every-s-originate-with-403-forbidden).

## Acceptance

* The intended semantics are **ruled with Kamil and recorded here** before code: does a merge transfer the K-side documents (a K re-home under the target connector), or does S keep anchoring pre-merge documents under the source key (a per-document connector rather than per-organisation)?
* What K actually does today when S sends a per-verb write under the target organisation's key for a document owned by the source organisation's connector is **measured, not inferred** — 403, or an anchor attributed to the wrong organisation. The review did not establish this, and `docs/org-recognition-configuration.md` only notes the conflict.
* Until the ruling lands, the merge tool's **preview** states plainly that the K-side lineage of moved documents stays with the source organisation. That is a small, shippable mitigation and should not wait for the ruling.
* Once ruled, `OrganisationMergeService` implements it: either the K call that re-homes the documents is made (and its failure handled — a merge must not half-complete), or `OwnerOrgId(doc)` resolution (`CardanoAnchorService.cs:1411-1412`) stops depending on `DocumentStore.OrganisationId` for pre-merge documents.
* `docs/org-recognition-configuration.md` is updated to state the outcome rather than the conflict.
* Related tickets are cross-checked so this does not land against a different model: [PS-690](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-690/adopt-org-owned-documents-ownership-model-for-single-vs-multi-user) (org-owned documents), [PS-319](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-319/sk-consistent-organisationuser-ownership-dr-credential-reconciliation), [PS-801](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-801/the-local-platform-k-refuses-every-s-originate-with-403-forbidden) (local K's 403 on originate), [KS-480](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-480/sk-k-side-support-consistent-userorg-ownership-credential).

**Playwright test that demonstrates the fix** (required): add `systemTest/tests/k_live/organisation_merge_lineage.spec.ts`. This is the S↔K path, so it belongs in `k_live`; nothing there covers merge today, and `organisation_dissolution.spec.ts` (functional) is the nearest existing spec and does not cross to K. The ticket's own *Verify* line is the journey — written out as assertions, against a slot paired with K slot N:

1. originate a document under organisation **A**, confirming it resolves on K under A's connector;
2. merge A → B through the admin merge tool (`admin-org-merge-form`, `admin-org-merge-confirm-input`, `admin-org-merge-confirm-btn`), with the moving member's document in the preview (`admin-org-merge-person-docs`);
3. emit a further verb on that moved document — `note` is the cheapest — and assert it **anchors and resolves on K**, and that Verify still resolves the document. **This is the assertion that fails on today's** `develop`, where S sends under B's key against a K document owned by A's connector and the event is refused or misattributed. Record which of the two it actually is, since that is the measurement this ticket is missing;
4. assert the merge **preview** carried the lineage warning (step 2's mitigation), so the warning cannot be quietly dropped once the ruling lands;
5. **control (passes today and must keep passing):** a document originated under B **before** the merge still anchors a later `note` under B's key and still resolves on Verify — so the fix cannot be satisfied by breaking the ordinary same-organisation path;
6. **control:** the merge's existing S-side outcomes are unchanged — members moved, documents re-homed, the blockers (`admin-org-merge-blockers`) still refusing what they refuse today.

If the K slot is not up, the spec must stand down as an **environmental** skip with a named reason (the [PS-944](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-944/systemtest-a-spec-that-stands-down-on-an-environmental-condition-must) rule); a 14-environmental-skip `@k-live` run proves nothing about this path, and the S↔K claim would then have to be evidenced another way.

title: protect / unprotect / restore are in both vocabularies and routed, but nothing in S ever records them — the three recorders have no callers
description:
## Finding (S↔K compatibility review, 2026-09-29, develop `477eb57`)

* K accepts `protect`, `unprotect`, `restore` on the flat anchor and `/lifecycle-events` ([KS-556](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-556/add-protectunprotectrestore-to-the-ks-134-lifecycle-verb-vocabulary); `services/anchoring/src/anchorSchema.ts:18`, `services/originate/src/lifecycleActions.ts:38`).
* S mirrors them (`CardanoAnchorService.cs:767-789`) and routes `restore` to `/lifecycle-events` and `protect` / `unprotect` to the flat anchor (`CardanoAnchorService.PerVerb.cs:89-123`).
* `TransactionService` has `RecordProtectAsync` / `RecordUnprotectAsync` / `RecordRestoreAsync` (`ssd/Services/Transactions/TransactionService.cs:254-261`) and **no caller outside that service and its tests** (grep of `ssd/`).

So [PS-615](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-615/adopt-ks-556-protectunprotectrestore-were-anchoring-unlabelled-for-15) adopted the verbs on the wire and nothing emits them. Either the protect/unprotect UI (PDF protection in `BaseController`) should record them, or the recorders and the routing cases are dead code to remove along with the vocabulary rows, on both platforms.

## Verify

Whichever way: `LocalOnlyVerbCoverageTests` / `k_verb_matrix.ts` stay green, and either a protect action produces a `protect` row that anchors, or the three verbs are gone from `TransactionAction.cs`, the mirror and `K_VERB_MATRIX` with a KS ticket to drop them from K.

Related: [PS-615](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-615/adopt-ks-556-protectunprotectrestore-were-anchoring-unlabelled-for-15), [PS-499](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-499/s-can-emit-three-verbs-platform-k-rejects-protect-unprotect-restore), [KS-556](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-556/add-protectunprotectrestore-to-the-ks-134-lifecycle-verb-vocabulary), [PS-228](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-228/evaluation-roadmap-make-the-documenttransaction-ledger-the-source-of).

## Acceptance

* The ruling is recorded here first: **wire the verbs up** (the protect / unprotect UI in `BaseController` records them) or **remove them** — recorders, routing cases, `TransactionAction.cs` entries, the `CardanoAnchorService.cs:767-789` mirror, and `K_VERB_MATRIX` — with a KS ticket raised to drop them from K's `anchorSchema.ts:18` and `lifecycleActions.ts:38`.
* Whichever way, there is **no verb that S can route but never emits**: the set S mirrors and the set S can produce are the same set, asserted rather than assumed.
* `LocalOnlyVerbCoverageTests` and `k_verb_matrix.ts` are green, and under the removal branch they are green *because the verbs are gone*, not because the matrix was edited to agree with itself.
* The relationship to [PS-615](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-615/adopt-ks-556-protectunprotectrestore-were-anchoring-unlabelled-for-15) is stated: that ticket adopted the verbs on the wire, and this one resolves that nothing emits them. Neither K nor S is left mid-way.

**Which test demonstrates it depends on the branch.**

**Under the removal branch, no Playwright test applies** — the work deletes unreachable code, so there is no behaviour for a browser to observe and a journey would only assert that protect/unprotect still works as it does today. The demonstrating tests are **xUnit**, red first:

1. a source/dead-code contract that `RecordProtectAsync`, `RecordUnprotectAsync` and `RecordRestoreAsync` (`TransactionService.cs:254-261`) have **no caller outside the service and its own tests** — red on today's tree, which is the finding; after removal it is satisfied by their absence;
2. a contract that `TransactionAction`, the `CardanoAnchorService` mirror and `K_VERB_MATRIX` agree on exactly one set of verbs, so a verb cannot be routable without being emittable again;
3. **control (green today, must stay green):** every verb S *does* emit still routes to the endpoint it routes to now (`restore` would have gone to `/lifecycle-events`, `protect` / `unprotect` to the flat anchor — the remaining verbs' routing must be untouched).

**Under the wire-it-up branch**, the S→K hop becomes real and a journey is then the right tool: add `systemTest/tests/k_live/protect_verbs.spec.ts` (new — `verb_matrix.spec.ts` covers the emitted verbs and would need the new ones adding to its matrix instead, which is also acceptable; say which). Against a slot paired with K slot N: applying PDF protection from the `BaseController` surface produces a `protect` `DocumentTransaction` that **resolves on K**, removing it produces `unprotect`, and a restore produces `restore` — **none of which happens on today's** `develop`, where the recorders are never called. Control: the verbs that already anchor (`share`, `certify`, `share-revoke`) still anchor exactly once each, so the new emissions have not disturbed the working path.

title: Ledger gap: share expiry leaves no DocumentTransaction and no K event — expiry is checked at access time only and no sweep exists
description:
## Finding (S↔K compatibility review, 2026-09-29, develop `477eb57`)

A share link that passes `ExpiresAt` stops working, but nothing records that it lapsed:

* Expiry is evaluated when a recipient opens the link (`ssd/Controllers/SDViewDownload.cs:276-280`) and logged locally as an `Expired` access-log row; no `DocumentTransaction` is written.
* No hosted service sweeps expired links. `Startup.cs:1217-1233` registers `CardanoAnchorRefresher`, `ConsentRetentionJob`, `DomainLinkageRecheckJob`, `PlatformKOrgRegistrar`, `PersonErasureSweep`, `OrganisationDissolutionSweep` — nothing for shares.
* The vocabulary has `share-expiry-change` (an edit) but no "share expired" verb, so K's chain never learns a share lapsed, while `share-revoke` is anchored.

## Options

1. A `share-expire` verb (non-mutating, `/lifecycle-events`), written by a sweep when `ExpiresAt` passes — needs a K-side vocabulary addition first (the [PS-499](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-499/s-can-emit-three-verbs-platform-k-rejects-protect-unprotect-restore) / [KS-1172](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1172/add-note-and-verified-to-the-lifecycle-vocabulary-lifecycle-verbs) ordering).
2. Or rule that expiry is a property of the `share` event already on chain (`expiresAt` is in the local payload only — `TransactionService.BuildPayloadJson`) and document that on `docs/VOCABULARY.md`.

Decision first; the sweep is small once ruled.

Related: [PS-228](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-228/evaluation-roadmap-make-the-documenttransaction-ledger-the-source-of) (ledger as source of truth), [PS-235](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-235/ledger-gap-ps-231-follow-up-record-share-email-expiry-token-rotate) (share edit verbs), [PS-231](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-231/ledger-gap-share-edits-permissionexpiryemailtokenresend-not-recorded).

## Acceptance

* The ruling is recorded here first: option 1 (a `share-expire` verb written by a sweep) or option 2 (expiry is a property of the `share` event already on chain). The sweep is not written before the decision.
