* Either way, `docs/VOCABULARY.md` states the outcome explicitly, so the next reader cannot infer from the absence of a verb that expiry was overlooked.
* **If option 1:** a hosted sweep is registered alongside the six already in `Startup.cs:1217-1233`, it writes exactly one `DocumentTransaction` per link whose `ExpiresAt` has passed (idempotent — a second tick writes nothing), the verb routes to `/lifecycle-events` as non-mutating, and the K-side vocabulary addition is raised as a KS ticket and lands first (the [PS-499](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-499/s-can-emit-three-verbs-platform-k-rejects-protect-unprotect-restore) / [KS-1172](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1172/add-note-and-verified-to-the-lifecycle-vocabulary-lifecycle-verbs) ordering).
* **If option 2:** `expiresAt` is confirmed present in what crosses to K on the `share` event, or the doc says plainly that it is local-only and why that is sufficient. No sweep, no verb.
* xUnit either way: `LocalOnlyVerbCoverageTests` stays green, and the sweep (if built) is pinned for the boundary — a link expiring exactly now, one expired and already recorded, one revoked before it expired (no expire row).
* The existing recipient-facing behaviour is untouched: an expired link still fails at access time and still writes its `Expired` access-log row.

**Playwright test — which branch it applies to.** Under **option 1** the S→K hop is the subject, so add `systemTest/tests/k_live/share_expiry_anchor.spec.ts` (new; nothing in `tests/k_live/` covers expiry — `share_edit_matrix.spec.ts` covers the *edit* verbs). Against a slot paired with K slot N it must:

1. create a share on a freshly uploaded document with an expiry already in the past (or the shortest the UI allows, then wait out the sweep tick), and assert a `share-expire` row appears for that document on S **and** resolves on K — **this is the assertion that fails on today's** `develop`, where no transaction is written at all and K's chain never learns the link lapsed;
2. assert the recipient opening the lapsed link still gets the refusal and still produces the `Expired` access-log row — **control, passes today and must keep passing**, because the sweep must not change what a recipient sees;
3. **control:** `share-revoke` on a separate share still anchors exactly once, so the new verb has not disturbed the verb that already worked.

Under **option 2 no Playwright test applies** — there is nothing new to observe in a browser or on the chain, and inventing a journey would assert current behaviour. The verifiable criterion is then the `docs/VOCABULARY.md` statement above plus the `LocalOnlyVerbCoverageTests` / `k_verb_matrix.ts` pair staying green with no "share expired" entry.

title: KS-1175 follow-on: the anchors K emits for share / transfer-custody / lifecycle-events carry no documentType and drop Platform-S's identity block — only originate and the flat anchor anchor identity
description:
## Found by

The S↔K compatibility review of 2026-09-29 (platform-k `0aa9b52c6`, platform-s `477eb57`).

## The gap

[KS-1175](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1175/anchor-originate-lifecycle-event-schemas-accept-and-anchor-platform-ss) (merged `cbae988db`, `910687394`) accepts the `identity` block on `POST /api/anchors` and anchors it beside `documentType` / `occurredAt` (`services/anchoring/src/anchorSchema.ts:128-151, 261-315`). Platform-S sends that block on **every** write once `CardanoAnchor:AnchorIdentity` is on — flat anchors, originate, version, certifications, share, transfer-custody and lifecycle-events (`ssd/Services/CardanoAnchor/CardanoAnchorService.cs:1606-1631`).

On K, three of those routes never carry it to the anchor:

* `POST /api/documents/{id}/lifecycle-events` reads only `action` and `payload`; an `identity` key in the body is ignored (`services/originate/src/routes/documents.ts:2440-2545`).
* `POST /{id}/share` and `POST /{id}/transfer-custody` likewise.
* All three anchor through `emitLifecycleAnchor`, whose body is `{documentId, contentHash, network}` — no `metadata.documentType`, no `identity` (`documents.ts:1275-1297`).

Result: for every non-mutating verb (delete, share-revoke, the share-\* edits, rights-unassign, note, certified, verified, share, rights-assign/reassign) the chain record has no verb and no actor/organisation identity, whatever S sends. Only `upload` (originate) and the flat-anchor fallback carry them.

## Ask

1. Carry `identity` (and the verb as `metadata.documentType`) from the share / transfer-custody / lifecycle-events request bodies into the `emitLifecycleAnchor` call, so the anchor records them — subject to the per-document-anchor ruling on the companion ticket (a reset row would not keep them anyway).
2. Declare `identity` on `DocumentShareRequest`, `TransferCustodyRequest` and `LifecycleEventRequest` in `originate.openapi.ts` so S's [PS-614](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-614/check-ss-verb-vocabulary-against-platform-ks-openapi-enum-at-gate-time) gate can see it (today S's `k_openapi_vocabulary.test.ts` only checks `onBehalfOf` placement).
3. Echo what was anchored on the lifecycle-event response, so S's read-back ([PS-870](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-870/6-send-the-identity-record-to-platform-k-on-every-anchored-verb) item 5) works on these verbs too.

## Verify

Paired slot with `AnchorIdentity=true` on S: a `share-revoke` on an originated document → the anchor read (`GET /api/anchors/{id}`) returns `identity.actorDid` and `metadata.documentType = share-revoke`. Today it returns neither.

Related: [KS-1175](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1175/anchor-originate-lifecycle-event-schemas-accept-and-anchor-platform-ss), [PS-870](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-870/6-send-the-identity-record-to-platform-k-on-every-anchored-verb), [PS-864](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-864/epic-id-status-stored-and-shown-throughout-the-system-actor-and), the [PS-895](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-895/question-in-simulated-anchoring-six-distinct-lifecycle-events-on-one) companion ticket (one anchor per document).

nodes.body:
**BLUF:** A share event's anchor payload carries no `issuerOrgId` and no `environment`. By a read of originate's chain-fallback verify, an answer built from such an anchor then shows the issuer organisation and the certifier organisation id as null. The key sets were probed by Seat AA 5th; the code I read at develop; nothing was run end to end. No action is asked of anyone here: this records the reading.

Key sets. `PROBE payload-keys` in `/Volumes/DevMASTER/!CODING/Secuura/Blockchain/5_Project_History/2026-11-06_seatAA-5th/evidence/ks1384/probe_share3.lines`, measured at develop `c5c26b2835df` with the real flat-anchor payload builder:
- Upload payload keys: `algorithm`, `certId`, `documentId`, `environment`, `hash`, `identityCommitment`, `issuerOrgId`, `network`, `orgDid`, `orgTrust`, `timestamp`, `type`, `version`.
- Share payload keys: the same list without `environment` and without `issuerOrgId`.

Code. `Blockchain/Dev/services/originate/src/routes/verification.ts` at develop `14ac61bd1a4c854c17539f1cd0f518631f998fbb`, in the chain-first fallback (comment at lines 948 and 949): line 988 reads `issuer: chain.metadata?.issuerName || chain.metadata?.issuerOrgId || null` and line 997 reads `certifierOrganizationId: chain.metadata?.issuerOrgId ?? null`. AA 5th's reading is that both come out null for a share's anchor. I did not run it.

What I could not tell. Whether this sits inside the scope of the merged pull requests 1549, 1568 and 1607 on this ticket or is a separate gap: I did not read those diffs. I also did not check whether the share path writes `issuerName` into the metadata by another route.

Related: the probe also shows a second admitted share building a second transaction. That behaviour is ruled to stay until stage 2 (card `secuura-ks1384-share-pays-second-tx-before-stage2-1106` = a) and is not part of this comment.

**BLUF:** Not run on kintsugi: needs a custody transfer. Delivered: PRs 1549, 1568 and 1607 merged as 8cbadd8d403f, 04a4a33938f0 and 7e2f8157cec2 on develop, deployed to kintsugi at ee1e1b832115 (kintsugi's REVISION head, read 2026-11-04 01:59Z). Left open.

- **Owed check:** the holder-update check named in the 2026-10-19 comment.
- **Why not run:** It needs a Platform S custody transfer, a write this sweep does not make.

**BLUF:** Delivered: PRs 1549, 1568 and 1607 merged as 8cbadd8d403f, 04a4a33938f0 and 7e2f8157cec2 on develop, deployed to kintsugi at b1fb543640e7 (2026-11-01). Verified by code read, not observed live. Left open: live sweep owed (write): the holder-update check named in the 2026-10-19 comment on this ticket needs a write on kintsugi.

- **In the code at b1fb543640e7:** `anchorOverwriteGuard.ts:148` names the four frozen issuer fields (`issuerOrgId`, `orgDid`, `orgTrust`, `orgVerified`), and `index.ts:1701` in the anchoring service logs `KS-1385 (b): applied the update and kept the first-anchored issuer fields` when a holder's update is applied.
- **What the three PRs cover:** 1549 anchors the latest event's identity at the six ruled sites, 1568 carries the guard to originate's anchors and no-issuer rows, 1607 keeps the first-anchored issuer fields on a holder's update.
- **Follow-up with its own ticket:** KS-1644 (the two Info items from gate U1).

**BLUF:** The 2026-10-13T12:23Z correction on this ticket ("INF-1, corrected": "There is no `signatureHash` in the anchored payload") was accurate when written and does not hold as of develop ed12d4e08d43, because pull request 1811 (KS 1454, p1 and p2) added `signatureHash` to the anchored payload. This comment records what I read and measured. It changes nothing in the ruling on this ticket and recommends nothing.

- **Instrument 1, `git grep -n signatureHash` at develop ed12d4e08d43, non-test source in `services/anchoring/src` and `services/originate/src`:** `anchorSchema.ts` 5 hits (the request field at :266, the `sign`-only refinement at :301 to :305, and the payload builder at :366, which spreads `signatureHash` under `secuura` beside `documentType`); `anchorReadback.ts` 4 hits; `services/originate/src/routes/documents.ts` 2 hits at lines 911 and 912, which are a code COMMENT repeating the older statement ("There is NO `signatureHash` in the anchored payload"). That comment is also out of date at this commit.
- **Instrument 2, reading `services/anchoring/src/index.ts` at the same commit** (the upsert starts at :1456, `metadata_payload = CASE` at :1504): the stored `metadata_payload` is replaced by the incoming one only when the ownership guard, `content_hash` equality and `anchor_type` equality all hold (:1504 to :1524). An admitted overwrite by the issuer's organisation takes the whole incoming payload (`ELSE EXCLUDED.metadata_payload`, :1522). An admitted overwrite by anyone else keeps the four `ISSUER_FIELDS` (`issuerOrgId`, `orgDid`, `orgTrust`, `orgVerified`, at `anchorOverwriteGuard.ts:148`) and takes the rest of the incoming payload (:1512). `signatureHash` is not among those four. So, read from the SQL, an admitted later event whose payload carries no `signatureHash` leaves the stored row without one, which is the 2026-10-13T10:49Z statement applied to a payload that now carries the field.
- **Not measured:** no database was run, so what `GET /api/anchors/:id` and the database-source verify return after a later event is reading, not measurement. QA gate 18 recorded the same point (its finding 1811-4).
- **Unchanged:** the ruling on this ticket ("Latest event's identity wins", quoted in the SQL comment above :1504). The same SQL comment names KS 1384 (one row per `(document_id, network)`) as the structural question and leaves it untouched; so does this comment.

**BLUF: @stuart.jamieson — the merge is already recorded above, so this is the part that was missing: what the deploy actually waits on, in plain words. Five conditions, and only one of them is ours to clear unilaterally. No date, deliberately.**

You asked when this rides Kintsugi. Nobody has written the full precondition list on a ticket before, which is why the answer has read as vague. Here it is.

1. **Your own dev-ps deploy.** The order you set still holds: Kintsugi takes K only after dev-ps is running S `aeae5ca` or later. Your document records that deploy as pending with you, so this one is not a K action and we are not treating it as one.
2. **Kam has to have seen the KS-1570 round.** The standing deploy-blocker is "not until the tenant-level ADMIN bound is merged *and* Kam has seen it". The merge half is done — all five pieces landed on 13 Oct. The second half is his, and it is in front of him.
3. **The KS-1032 vouch secret** has to be in place on the target box.
4. **Migrations 050 and 051 each need their own census on the box they are applied to.** They are data migrations over the live anchor table, so a census run on develop proves nothing about Kintsugi. That is the deploy seat's work at apply time, not something that can be pre-cleared from here.
5. **A new one, and it is the reason we would not deploy today even if 1–4 were clear.** On develop a Platform S custody transfer currently answers **500**; on Kintsugi it answers 404. A deploy right now would therefore regress you from 404 to 500. That fix is in progress as its own piece of work. We would not have found this by looking at the deploy list — it came out of your own 14 and 15 October measurements on KS-1402.

**What is true today:** the ruling is on develop, it is not on any box, and this ticket stays In Progress until it is and the live check is done. Nothing is being asked of you here beyond item 1, which you already own.

The migration-census detail sits on KS-1612 rather than being repeated here.

**BLUF: Kam's (b) on card `secuura-ks1385-cert-holder-can-rewrite-issuer-fields-1018` ("Holder may update, but not the issuer fields") is MERGED to develop as `7e2f8157cec2`, the squash of #1607 at `243d324d4dd7`. It went through two Opus gates: T1 GO WITH NOTE, then delta gate U1 GO. Nothing is deployed, so this ticket stays In Progress (runtime work). The deploy and the live check are owed.**

## What changed
- **The four fields hold.** When the anchor guard admits an update for anyone other than the issuer's organisation (today the custodian's organisation, Kam's (c)), `issuerOrgId`, `orgDid`, `orgTrust` and `orgVerified` keep their first-anchored values, and the rest of the holder's payload applies. A field the first anchor did not carry stays absent.
- **The issuer's own later events are unchanged:** latest event wins.
- **It is not a refusal:** `POST /api/anchors` still answers 202 with the same body, and the server logs one info line.
- **The chain carries the same values,** because the Cardano submitter encodes the stored row.
- **Who the guard admits is unchanged,** byte for byte.
- **No migration and no trigger.** A trigger cannot see the caller, so it would have frozen the issuer too.

## What the gates measured
- **T1, booted, round 1:**
  - verify-by-hash, `GET /api/anchors/:id` and the encoded metadatum all carry the issuer's four fields beside the holder's actor; all four controls hold; develop shows the bug;
  - its two Minors became round 2: a stored payload of an odd shape failed the write, a refused caller's included; and the log split was pinned only by source text.
- **U1, booted, round 2:**
  - those Minors are closed on all 10 stored shapes, for both an admitted holder and a refused caller (the refused caller is byte-identical to develop, 10/10);
  - the log decision is tested on the real returned row;
  - on the landing tree: shell suites 91/91, anchoring integration 89/89, unit 379/380 (`threadTokenMint`, KS-562), `tsc` 0.

## One consequence Kam has seen (Wednesday put it on his panel)
On rows with no issuer organisation, which is every certification, the four fields are frozen permanently after the first anchor, even against a holder's correction. That is what option (b) chose.

## Follow-up
**KS-1644** (Low): U1's two Info items. An INCOMING `secuura` that is not an object still raises (no route builds one), and `dbPersistAnchor`'s own row handling is pinned by source text alone.

*Seat J 13th.*

**BLUF: #1568 is held at its review cap at `767ab575818f`, NOT merged and nothing deployed. Round 2 returned NO GO. #1568 would have delivered Kam's no-issuer ruling (b) and carried both of his rulings to originate's real anchors. A third round needs Kam, on card `secuura-ks1612-third-round-after-cap-1018` (default: hold, and re-plan around KS-1384).** Kam's rulings stand as ruled. They are simply not live for originate's anchors yet. This ticket stays In Progress.

**MAJ-A, in one paragraph.** Some anchor records have no document behind them at all. Originate's hash-only `POST /api/anchoring/submit` creates one on every call. Migration 050 only compares documents with documents, so it cannot see these. Another tenant, or on a single-tenant box simply another organisation, can register a document whose external id is that anchor's id; the id is public through verify-by-hash. The new external-id lookup then allows the overwrite, and the anchored identity is rewritten silently. Develop keeps it.

**The gate's three ways forward (findings, not built):**
* **(i)** The guard refuses when the stored anchor predates the document claiming it.
* **(ii)** 050 also refuses an external id that is already an anchor id.
* **(iii)** KS-1384, a tenant column on the anchor table.

Full detail is on KS-1612.

**BLUF: #1568 round 2 is pushed (head `767ab575818f`), ready for its final gate.**

* It still delivers Kam's (b) and (c) to originate's real anchors and to certifications.
* It closes the cross-tenant hole round 1's gate found, at the database, via migration 050 (detail on KS-1612).
* Nothing is merged or deployed, so this ticket stays In Progress.

**BLUF: Kam's ruling on no-issuer rows (card `secuura-ks1385-null-issuer-certifications-1015` = b, "Apply (c) to them too") is built in #1568 (head `16e71610366b`), ready for its gate. Nothing is merged and nothing is deployed.**

* **The change:**
  * A document with no issuer organisation is no longer refused before the custody rule runs.
  * The custodian's organisation can now update its anchored identity. Every certification is such a row, so the holder's organisation can do so for a certification issued to it, as the card said.
  * Anyone else is still refused.
* **The same PR fixes KS-1612**, the reason neither of this ticket's rulings reached originate's real anchors until now.
* The ticket stays In Progress: it closes only once this is tested, merged and deployed.

## Round 2 built and pushed — Kam's custody ruling (c), head `80daaa78a2c7adf7196a41cdf240376d8c2bf75a`

**Kam ruled card `secuura-ks1385-custodian-may-update-anchor-identity-1013` = c, verbatim: *"Issuer, or anyone in the custodian's organisation"*** — 2026-10-14 11:15:54, Kam's own live-board message. (The decision record's `ruled_ts`, 11:17:07, is when Wednesday's tool recorded the ruling on the card, a record of Wednesday's act, not of his.)

Facts only. Pull request 1549, branch `feature/ks-1385-anchor-identity-latest-event-wins`. Nothing merged, nothing deployed. In the Opus delta gate next.

### What changed
- **One constant:** `CUSTODY_OPTION` `'a'` → `'c'` in `services/anchoring/src/anchorOverwriteGuard.ts`. Every other changed line in that file is a comment.
- **develop merged in twice** (`e67e0dc1` → `ea799fd4`; then `53b429ed`, the ks884 cure, → `80daaa78`). File overlap 0 of 17 against develop's 179, with a planted control reading +1. The landed tree equals the `merge-tree` prediction.
- **Cells re-pinned to (c).** C0 now drives a colleague in the custodian's organisation who is *not* the custodian user. (a) and (b) both refuse that caller and only (c) admits it, so the cell cannot pass under the wrong option. A third organisation is still refused.

### What it does, measured
A three-arm matrix (develop / round 1 / round 2), each arm running its own guard bytes against real Postgres:
- The **only** row that changes is a colleague in the custodian's organisation on a document with an issuer. Refused in round 1, admitted in round 2.
- Round 1's five scenarios are identical between rounds.
- A third organisation stays refused.

Mutation: 27 mutants, 27 killed, including two that make (c) look right while shipping (b).

### KNOWN LIMIT — kept as built on Wednesday's ruling (2026-10-15T02:17:54Z)
A document with **no issuer organisation** is refused before the custody check runs. On those rows (c) does not apply, and the stored payload is kept, which is develop's behaviour.

```
CONTROL  issuer set,  custodian-org colleague, (c): {"allow":true,"reason":"caller-shares-custodian-organisation"}
PROBE    issuer NULL, custodian-org colleague, (c): {"allow":false,"reason":"document-has-no-issuer-organisation"}
PROBE    issuer NULL, custodian USER,          (b): {"allow":false,"reason":"document-has-no-issuer-organisation"}
```

Two product write sites produce that shape:
- `services/originate/src/repositories/certificationRepo.ts:199` — the certification INSERT writes no `issuer_organization_id` and sets `owner_user_id` to the **holder**. So every certification row is this shape.
- `services/originate/src/repositories/documentRepo.ts:432/458` — the issuer is a sub-select, NULL whenever the claimed organisation is not in that tenant.

Applying (c) to those rows would let a holder's organisation rewrite the anchored identity of a certification issued to it. That is the false-attribution risk this guard exists to stop. Kam's card was about custody on documents that have an issuer. Wednesday is putting the certification case to him as its own card, defaulting to "keep as built". Cell C-f pins the limit.

### Platform S — read against Stuart's comment of 2026-10-14T00:42Z
His point 1 holds under (c) as it did under (a): S signs every per-document call with the **owner** organisation's key, so every S event is admitted as the issuer's. (c) only adds callers from a custodian's organisation, and S sends none. **No S change follows from (c).** His point 2 (a possible false "Mismatch" on S's Verify page until KS-1384) is unchanged by this round. His KS-772 request belongs to the deploy round.

Linear link stays `contributes`. This ticket closes only once tested, working **and** deployed.

**Fix round 1 of 2 built and pushed — head `b1801721d56b35d7982cbe5b103c740113aa70b9`** (pull request 1549, two commits on `feature/ks-1385-anchor-identity-latest-event-wins`). Facts only; the round is in gate, nothing is merged and nothing is deployed.

**The gate's NO GO (report hash `40bdc24d2e1f07dc`) answered item by item.** Ruled principle: overwrite only when the guard positively confirms a legitimate event of this document; otherwise keep the stored payload exactly as develop does. Every condition added can only *reduce* the set of overwrites, so the worst case of this round is develop's behaviour.

- **MAJ-1** — `anchorOverwriteGuard.ts` reads the owning document from `documents` (same database) and allows the overwrite only when the row is in the caller's tenant **and** the caller's organisation is the document's issuer. Otherwise the payload is kept.
- **MAJ-2** — the payload is kept on a content-hash mismatch. No 409, no update-both, no response-shape change, plus one operator log line naming the document and both hash prefixes.
- **MIN-1** — compare-and-set in the submitter on the payload it signed, as its own commit, guarding all three writes that claim a transaction.
- **MIN-2** — cells for transfer-custody, share and revoke. They kill **k04, k05, k06 and g08**, all four of which survived at the gate.
- **MIN-3** — the payload is kept when `anchor_type` differs, so a batch item no longer wipes a single anchor's attestation.

All three keep-conditions ride in **one CASE** in the upsert, so they are atomic with the write they gate.

**Three measurements that changed the design, recorded because they are not obvious from the code:**

1. **The tenant bound is explicit SQL, not RLS.** `documents`' tenant policy carries an `app.tenant_scope_bypass = 'platform_admin'` escape, and the `secuura` role is `rolsuper` + `rolbypassrls` — so a GUC-only read would have been **vacuous**. Anchoring runs as `secuura_app`, which is neither, so RLS is live in production; but a guard whose correctness depends on which role is configured is not a guard. The GUC is set as well, and a cell proves the read works under FORCE RLS as `secuura_app`, with a zero-rows-without-the-GUC control.
2. **`users` carries a second, permissive policy whose qual is literally `true`**, and Postgres ORs permissive policies — so tenant isolation on `users` is open for SELECT by construction. The custody LEFT JOIN therefore carries its own tenant bound. A mutant that dropped it **survived** the first mutation pass; cell `C-e` now kills it.
3. **`anchorDocumentSchema` accepts two `documentId` shapes** (`anchorSchema.ts:160-163`): a uuid **or** `doc-<digits>-<alnum>`, which is Platform S's flat form. So the non-uuid branch is half the contract, not an exotic case, and `id = $1::uuid` on it would raise 22P02 and answer 5xx for an anchor that works today.

**CUSTODY — the stated limit.** Kam holds card `secuura-ks1385-custodian-may-update-anchor-identity-1013`. Custody is recorded as a **user** (`documents.owner_user_id`), not an organisation; there is no custodian-organisation column and it is derivable in one join via `users.organization_id`. **Option (a), issuer only, ships here.** The limit: after a transfer-custody, an event raised by the new custodian's organisation keeps the prior payload rather than overwriting it. Options (b) and (c) are each one condition, and cells `C-b` / `C-c` exercise both for real today by passing the option explicitly — so "one condition away" is measured, not asserted.

**INF-1, corrected.** The previous pull request body and two code comments said "`documentType` and `signatureHash` are overwritten". **There is no `signatureHash` in the anchored payload** — zero hits in anchoring and originate non-test source apart from those comments. What actually travels is the whole `secuura` object plus the seven identity fields and `documentType`. The correction is named in the code so it outlives this round.

**Measured:**
- anchoring integration **3 files / 29 tests**; originate unit **107 suites / 1352 tests**; `tsc --noEmit` **0 errors** in both (positive control: a planted type error gives rc 2).
- **Red-first matrix across three trees** over five scenarios. This round is the only column correct in all five rows: head `aca6efb0` falsifies in four, develop fails Kam's ruling in the first. In two rows the guard *allows* and the payload is still kept, which is what shows the hash and `anchor_type` conditions do their own work rather than riding on the ownership guard.
- **Mutation: 24 mutants, 24 killed, 0 survived**, each by a named cell with a non-empty message, with a load-failure guard so a compile break is never scored as a kill. Every file asserted byte-identical afterwards.

**Not run, stated plainly:** the four platform suites, and the pre-push preflight did not complete — its own words, with `PUSH_RC=0`: *"PREFLIGHT INCOMPLETE — 13/16 legs ran, 3 SKIPPED. Nothing failed. legs 3 4 8 — local stack not up … This is NOT a pass."* The api-gateway was not booted, so MAJ-1's route *through the gateway* still rests on the gate's reading of `proxy.ts` / `scopes.ts`. No real Cardano. The anchoring unit lane is 370 passed / 1 failed — `threadTokenMint.test.ts`, pre-existing, already in `BACKLOG.md`, and that file's only import is `vitest` with zero references to anything this round touches.

**No migration, no schema change, no environment variable.** Adjacent and deliberately untouched: **KS-1384** (whether there should be one anchor row per `(document_id, network)` at all), **KS-1603**, **KS-1604**.

## Built to Kam's ruling — pull request 1549, head `aca6efb0`, at the Opus gate

**Kam ruled card `secuura-ks1385-anchor-identity-needs-ps895-ruling-1013` = b, verbatim: *"Latest event's identity wins"*.**

### What changes
* Platform S's top-level `identity` block is now forwarded to the anchor at **six** originate sites: `POST /api/documents` (create), `POST /api/documents/:id/anchor`, `emitLifecycleAnchor` (share, transfer-custody, revoke, lifecycle-events), originate's own `POST /api/anchors`, `POST /api/certifications/issue`, and `POST /api/certifications/:id/recertify`. Until now originate's `.passthrough()` schemas let the key through validation and then dropped it.
* **Site 5, `POST /api/anchoring/submit`, is deliberately excluded** (Wednesday, 2026-10-13T08:48:09Z): a hash-only contract that S does not send an identity to.
* anchoring's `anchor_store` upsert now updates `metadata_payload` on conflict. Before, the **first** anchored verb's payload was kept for the life of the row, so forwarding identity from a later verb would have shown the uploader's identity beside a share's transaction hash.

### ⚠ The consequence, which is Kam's ruling and not an oversight
**An earlier verb's identity is OVERWRITTEN by a later verb on the same `(document_id, network)` row — and `metadata.documentType` and `signatureHash` are overwritten the same way**, because they travel in the same payload. After deploy, `GET /api/anchors/{id}` for a document with several anchored verbs returns the **latest** verb's identity, documentType and signatureHash. `content_hash` is **not** updated — unruled, left alone. PS-895 (per-document vs per-event anchoring) stays open on Platform S's board and is the structural answer.

### Evidence
* Measured on real Postgres against develop's **own** upsert SQL: after a create then a share on one document, develop's row carries the share's transaction hash beside `did:key:zUPLOADER`; this branch carries `did:key:zSHARER`. `content_hash` unchanged in both — the control.
* 28 cells across three files, a two-directional red-proof, and a mutation pass of **14 mutants, 14 killed by name, 0 survived**. Two of those were found by the pass itself: sites 6 and 7 had **no** cell until it showed deleting either spread survived everything.
* Suites on the predicted merge onto develop `d53d80cb`: originate 109/109 suites, 1361/1361 tests; tsc 0 errors. Schemathesis, Akto, Playwright and k6 **not run** (local stack down).

**Not deployed.** develop deploys are held by DEPLOY-BLOCKERS' KS-1570 row; this rides the next permitted deploy. This ticket stays open until deployed and checked live.

*Seat J 9th.*

**Correction to this ticket's title and scope, measured 2 Oct: originate drops the identity block too.**

I wrote "only originate and the flat anchor anchor identity". That is wrong for originate. On a paired slot (platform-s `d04829b`, `AnchorIdentity` on, ↔ platform-k develop `88e8877a2`, clean build) an upload through `POST /api/documents` came back from `GET /api/anchors/{id}` with **no** identity block, although S sent one.

In code at `88e8877a2`: originate's auto-anchor body is built at `services/originate/src/routes/documents.ts:857-865` as `{documentId, contentHash, network, environment, issuerOrgId, issuerName, certId}`, and no non-test file under `services/originate/src` mentions `identity` or `identityCommitment`. That matches open item 1 in Kamil's 22 Sep comment on KS-1175 ("the seven originate-fronted endpoints forward no `identity`").

So the scope here is all seven originate-fronted routes (`POST /api/documents`, `/{id}/version`, `/{id}/anchor`, `/{id}/share`, `/{id}/transfer-custody`, `/api/certifications/issue`, `/{id}/lifecycle-events`), not three. Until they forward the block, Platform-S's identity reaches the chain only on its direct `POST /api/anchors` calls, which with per-verb endpoints on is the fallback path. Platform-S side: PS-870.

title: One anchor row per (document_id, network): a repeat POST /api/anchors resets the existing row to pending and nulls its transaction hash — so Platform-S's per-event anchoring collapses to one anchor per document (PS-895 companion)
description:
## Found by

The S↔K compatibility review of 2026-09-29 (platform-s `477eb57`, platform-k `0aa9b52c6`; origin/develop `b4461d1e2` is three commits ahead, none touching this). Companion to [PS-895](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-895/question-in-simulated-anchoring-six-distinct-lifecycle-events-on-one), which asked the question from the S side after seeing six lifecycle events on one document share one External Ref, and one on-chain transaction for register + declare on dev-ps.

## What the code does

`dbPersistAnchor` upserts on the composite key and rewrites the chain columns from the **new** request:

```
services/anchoring/src/index.ts:1334-1372
  INSERT INTO anchor_store (...)
  ON CONFLICT (document_id, network) DO UPDATE SET
    status = EXCLUDED.status, transaction_hash = EXCLUDED.transaction_hash,
    block_hash/block_number/slot/fee/confirmations/confirmed_at = EXCLUDED.…,
    error_message, retry_count, simulated, updated_at = EXCLUDED.…
  RETURNING id
```

`metadata_payload` and `content_hash` are **not** in the update list, so the first event's label and hash stay on the row. Every `POST /api/anchors` builds the anchor with `status: 'pending'` and a null hash (`index.ts:463-560`), so on a conflict the existing row goes back to `pending` with `transaction_hash = NULL`, and `processAnchor(persistedId)` runs again (`:535`).

K's own share, transfer-custody, revoke and lifecycle-event routes all go through `emitLifecycleAnchor`, which posts only `{documentId, contentHash, network}` to that same flat endpoint (`services/originate/src/routes/documents.ts:1275-1297`). So every non-mutating verb S records re-enters the same row for the document.

Migration 031 records the one-row-per-(document, network) decision. `anchorSubmission.ts:383-386` (guard 1) reads the row's `transaction_hash` to avoid a second fee-paying transaction — the upsert has just nulled it.

## What this means for the S↔K contract

* Platform-S's user-facing promise (`docs/USER-MANUAL.md` §1, §7) is that every declare, sign and share event is anchored. K anchors **one row per document version per network**; later events reset and re-process it.
* For every verb S routes through `/lifecycle-events`, `/share` or `/transfer-custody`, the chain record carries **no** `documentType` **and no** `identity` — `emitLifecycleAnchor` sends neither, and the lifecycle-events handler reads only `action` and `payload` (`documents.ts:2440-2545`). That is a [KS-1175](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1175/anchor-originate-lifecycle-event-schemas-accept-and-anchor-platform-ss) gap; filed separately.

## Decisions needed (Kamil)

1. Is one anchor per (document, network) the intended contract? If yes, S will label its External Ref column "anchor for version X" and group events ([PS-895](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-895/question-in-simulated-anchoring-six-distinct-lifecycle-events-on-one) item 2), and the USER-MANUAL wording changes.
2. If events should each anchor, the upsert key needs an event dimension and `emitLifecycleAnchor` needs the verb.
3. Either way: **what happens on the reset.** Trace whether `processAnchor` after a conflict mints a second Cardano transaction for the same document (guard 1 cannot see the previous hash any more), or is caught by another guard. Not verified live in the review; [PS-895](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-895/question-in-simulated-anchoring-six-distinct-lifecycle-events-on-one)'s dev-ps observation was one transaction for two events.

## Verify

* Unit: a second `POST /api/anchors` for the same `(documentId, network)` returns the existing id **and** either leaves a confirmed row's `transaction_hash` intact (per-document contract) or creates a distinct row (per-event contract) — whichever is ruled.
* Live on a paired slot: originate → declare → share on one document; count anchor rows and Cardano transactions; quote both on this ticket.

Related: [PS-895](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-895/question-in-simulated-anchoring-six-distinct-lifecycle-events-on-one) (the S-side question), [KS-1175](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1175/anchor-originate-lifecycle-event-schemas-accept-and-anchor-platform-ss) (identity block), [PS-870](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-870/6-send-the-identity-record-to-platform-k-on-every-anchored-verb).

**BLUF:** Question 2: one row, as S expects. On kintsugi, `anchor_store` holds 1 row for document `d7163cda-a6f8-40cb-bceb-28dc0d325dbb`, status `confirmed`, naming the share's transaction `2b6a4172…`. The upload's `1a70dd41…` is in 0 rows of the table.

* **The read:** read-only, 2026-11-06 08:34:59Z. Transactions were matched on their first 8 hex characters. Content hash `4abd0a4d…7efb` is on that 1 row and on no other. Controls: 50 rows in the table; a document id that cannot exist reads 0; a content hash that cannot exist reads 0.
* **Its limit:** this is one table at one moment, with no history and no chain read. It does not show how `1a70dd41…` left the row. The account of that in the earlier comment on this ticket comes from the code and a stand-in run, and this read does not test it.
* **Against the earlier comment:** that comment said, not read on the box, that K's row would no longer name `1a70dd41…`. This read shows that for the transaction hash. It did not read the row's payload.

**BLUF:** Question 1: stage 1 leaves this in place. It did not add it and was not built to stop it, because its shared-coin rule covers repeat attempts of one payload and a share carries a new payload. So today an admitted share pays for its own transaction on the same row, and stage 2 is what gives each event its own row. Question 2 is a box read and comes separately; the unique key on `(document_id, network)`, migration 031, allows one row. This comment decides nothing about that spend.

* **The path:** the share route calls `emitLifecycleAnchor`, which posts to `POST /api/anchors`. The upsert sets the row back to `pending` with a null hash, and `processAnchor` runs again. Read at `07a2d62be6a0` and originate `5fc5569ed96a`. The files on this path are unchanged at develop `35bcfa000b44`.
* **Why it pays again:** every post stamps its own `timestamp`, so the payload differs and no earlier attempt counts as the same one. Measured on the real submitter and wallet view, with a stand-in chain and the upsert simulated from its SET list: a share whose payload replaces the stored one built a second transaction on a second coin, and the row ended naming the second hash. The same code path existed before stage 1, by read.
* **Your two transactions fit that:** the emitter posts `documentId`, `contentHash`, `network` and your `identity` block, and not `environment` or `issuerOrgId`. A payload built from that body has exactly the differences you list. Stored issuer fields are kept on a later event only for a caller outside the issuer's organisation, so by inference this caller was in it.
* **After the share:** by code the row holds the share's hash and payload, so K's row no longer names `1a70dd41…`. Not read on the box.
* **What K has said:** comment 616db2a5 describes stage 1 as stopping "a refused or retried event" from paying twice, for "the same request". It did not say a new event pays. The route's code comment says "idempotent — reuses the document's existing anchor", which holds for the anchor id and not for the transaction. **Thanks, Stuart. Our approach for KS-1384, in two stages. No date yet: we will update this ticket as each stage makes progress.**

**Stage 1: make today's one-anchor-per-document model safe (in build now).**
- The reconciler stops giving up too early: it judges a row by its last update, not its creation time, and it no longer fails a row because the chain provider was unreachable (KS-1808, KS-1810).
- Anchoring stops a refused or retried event from paying twice or getting stuck: every attempt anchoring makes for the same request spends the same wallet coin, so at most one of them can land on chain.
- A sweep ends a stranded row honestly as `failed` instead of leaving it pending, and never mints.
- The retry route checks anchoring's own row first: an attempt still in flight answers 409 and nothing new is posted.
- The reconciler change can ship on its own; the other three deploy together on each box, after a wallet check.

**Stage 2: one anchor per lifecycle event (the fix for what you describe above).**
- Each event (upload, version, share, transfer, and so on) gets its own anchor row and its own transaction, so S can name the transaction for each event rather than the document's first one.
- This needs a database migration and a backfill, and it follows stage 1.

- `tx 84c4d91e… 'share' → share ref anchor_c09c1b1f-… (parent deb6d3c3-…)`
- `tx 20b5a812… 'rights-assign' → transfer-custody ref anchor_c09c1b1f-… (parent deb6d3c3-…)`
- After that, every refresher tick logs `status poll made 2 platform-k read(s) for 3 row(s) — 1 answered by a read already made this tick`. The two rows share one ref, so one read answers both.

**What this shows**
1. **One anchor per (document, network), confirmed live.** `/share` and `/transfer-custody` both go through `emitLifecycleAnchor` → `POST /api/anchors` → `dbPersistAnchor`'s `ON CONFLICT (document_id, network)` and return the existing row's id (`services/anchoring/src/index.ts`, the KS-281 upsert, at `061c3a4f6`). S therefore has no separate on-chain reference for the transfer.

All three rows on document 19 are still unconfirmed **23 minutes** after the last action. That fits the description: each repeat resets the row to `pending` with `transaction_hash` NULL and re-processes it. **Not verified (needs K data, Kamil):** for `anchor_store` where `document_id = 'deb6d3c3-1d79-4993-82a1-7a49a75aae00'` on preprod/preview, please give:
- the row's current `status`, `transaction_hash` and `retry_count`;
- how many Cardano transactions anchoring submitted for that document between 08:55 and 09:20 UTC (question 3 above: did the reset mint a second fee-paying transaction?).

**For S, if one-anchor-per-document is the intended contract (decision 1):** S needs to change. Today it shows one tick per action and records the share and the transfer under one ref. When the row eventually confirms, both rows will be stamped with whatever transaction the row last carried, so the earlier action is attributed to the later action's transaction. That is the KS-1119 / KS-1561 false-attribution shape on the S side. It is PS-895's question, now answered live.

Will add the final state when the rows confirm or park.

**Kam has ruled: design now, merge after the Kintsugi round lands.**

Kam's words, verbatim:

> Design now, merge after the Kintsugi round lands

Card `secuura-ks1384-schedule-per-event-anchors-1019`, option **(b)**. Ruled on the live board 2026-10-19 between 18:22 and 18:23 AEDT; recorded 18:28.

What that means for this multi-PR project:

- Per the card, the small **interim ownership check** on the flat-anchor route goes ahead now, on its own, and is not held behind this project — that is **KS-1603**, already in flight on its own seat.

**Nothing is built or merged by this comment.** This records the ruling and the sequencing.

**BLUF: @stuart.jamieson — Kam ruled the shape of this on 2026-10-09: option (a), one anchor per lifecycle event. That ruling never reached this ticket, which is why your document still records KS-1384 as unruled. That is our miss. The shape is settled and it is the one you prefer. WHEN the work starts is still with Kam — a card is on his panel today. No date.**

## Kam's ruling, 2026-10-09 10:06:00 AEDT

Option (a), verbatim:

> One anchor per lifecycle event

So the structural answer is the one you have argued for on both this ticket and KS-1612 — a row per event rather than one row per `(document_id, network)` — and not a narrower guard on the existing single row.

## What is ruled, and what is not

**Ruled:** the target shape. One anchor row per lifecycle event, which is also what removes the overwrite you had to word around in PS-1285 and closes KS-1603's exposure for good rather than guarding it.

**Not ruled:** when it starts. This is a multi-PR project, not a patch — a migration and backfill on the live anchor table with three source rules, five code writers to bind to the tenant, six SQL files and two services (the sizing is in `4384fa9a` on this ticket). Scheduling work of that size against a deploy round that is already queued is Kam's call, and it is in front of him now.

**Deliberately not stated:** a start date or a landing date. Anything merged to `develop` rides the next deploy round, and that round has conditions outside our control.

## Your measurement is recorded and it holds

Your `750da63c` of 2026-10-18 answers the one residual the round-3 write-up left open — whether an id chosen outside K is predictable enough to be squatted. At S develop `7cb1a4e`: a fresh v4 GUID per ledger row from `Guid.NewGuid()` in `TransactionService.BuildBaseTransaction`, 122 bits from the platform CSPRNG, no counter and no time component, and never known outside S before the anchor exists. We are not treating that as an open risk.

## Interim

The small ownership check on the flat-anchor route (KS-1603) is tracked separately and does not wait on this project. If Kam schedules KS-1384 to start now, that check is subsumed; if he holds the project, the check still protects your existing rows. Either way nothing is being asked of you here.

@kamil.kreiser — on the "reverse order" residual you record above ("an id chosen outside K, such as S's hyphenated ledger chain id on a flat anchor, is only as unpredictable as its source, which K cannot measure"): the S measurement, at S develop `7cb1a4e`.

- **The id is a fresh v4 GUID per ledger row**: `Guid.NewGuid().ToString("N")` in `TransactionService.BuildBaseTransaction`, hyphenated for the wire (`ToHyphenatedGuid`). 122 random bits from the platform CSPRNG, no counter, no time component, no derivation from the document or the organisation.
- **It is never known outside S before the anchor exists.** S writes the row and dispatches the anchor in the same request (`TryAnchorAsync`) or on the refresher's next tick (≤ 30 s locally); the id is visible only inside S, to signed-in members of the owning organisation, on pages that render after the row is written. It is not in any S email, share link or public URL.
- So pre-registering a `documents` row under one of S's flat-anchor ids requires guessing a v4 GUID inside a window of seconds. For S's ids the "reverse order" residual is theoretical; migration 051's forward refusal covers the case that matters for S.

That does not change S's preference (this ticket's tenant column is still the answer that needs no reasoning about id entropy), but it lets you record the S source as measured rather than unmeasurable. The S flat-anchor write site is the one you list as unguarded, `originate/src/routes/anchors.ts:109` via `POST /api/anchors/` — S sends it only under the owner organisation's connector key, for its own rows, one id per event.

**BLUF: #1568 round 3 did NOT take this, and the reason is scope, not merit. Platform S prefers it, I agree it is the structural answer, and it should be planned as its own piece of work rather than squeezed into a review round.**

**Stuart's position, from his KS-1612 comment of 2026-10-18T11:42:31Z, verbatim:** *"S's preference is unchanged: (iii) KS-1384, one anchor row per event with a tenant column, which also removes the overwrite S had to word around in PS-1285."*

**Why round 3 took the smaller option instead.** Kam allowed #1568 exactly one more round (card `secuura-ks1612-third-round-after-cap-1018` = (a); a further NO GO stops for him). Round 3 therefore closes the round-2 gate's MAJ-A with one predicate — migration 051, which refuses a `documents` row that claims an id an `anchor_store` row already holds and that no document owns. Ruled by Wednesday 2026-10-18T20:14:35Z.

**What this ticket is, as sized against the writer census I ran at develop `83ed01af70fd5ed6cca9ac66f28ddcb8a1034105`:**

* a hot-table migration on `anchor_store` plus a backfill with **three distinct source rules** — document anchors from `documents`, certification anchors from `documents.id`, and orphan/flat anchors that have **no recorded first caller at all** (→ NULL → correctly frozen against cross-tenant updates);
* **every writer must bind the tenant** — there are five: `anchoring/src/index.ts:1372` (the main upsert), `anchoring/src/index.ts:1755`, `anchoring/src/anchorStatusUpdate.ts:114`, `originate/src/routes/anchors.ts:109` (unguarded), `demo-service/src/seed/index.ts:162`; plus six migration/init writers (001, 003, 007, 031, `docker/init/06-consolidate-anchors.sql`, `deployment/azure/migrate/init.sql`);
* a new refusal path in the upsert's `DO UPDATE` (`WHERE anchor_store.tenant_id = EXCLUDED.tenant_id`, NULL-tenant legacy rows refused — fail closed);
* and the guard's per-organisation rule still needed **on top**, because a single-tenant box puts two organisations in one tenant.

That is multiple PRs across two services, a seed and six SQL files — not a round.

**What it would close that 051 does not.** KS-1603 (the unconditional columns on both upserts). The **reverse order** residual 051 names: 051 refuses a document claiming an id an anchor already holds, but cannot stop a document being pre-registered under an id that can be *predicted* before the anchor exists — and an id chosen outside K, such as S's hyphenated ledger chain id on a flat anchor, is only as unpredictable as its source, which K cannot measure. With a tenant column the anchor row carries its own owner and none of this is inferred from `documents` at all.

*Seat J 13th. Nothing deployed. Related: KS-1612, KS-1603, KS-1630.*

title: Local tooling and config still fall back to slot 1: commission-provisioning-key.sh mints on :6882 and seed-seam-accounts.sh seeds :5122 unless told otherwise; host CardanoAnchor BaseUrl, the local template and a committed .claude allowlist pin slot 1
description:
## BLUF

The container runtime is slot-derived ([PS-830](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-830/a-platform-s-stack-on-slot-n-calls-platform-k-on-slot-1): `docker-compose.override.yml` sets `AppUrl`, `WebSiteUrl*`, `StatusListBaseUrl` from `HTTPS_PORT` and the K URL from `K_GATEWAY_URL`), but **two local scripts default to slot 1's stacks when run without an explicit target**, so from a slot-N worktree they act on whichever session owns slot 1: `commission-provisioning-key.sh` mints against K `:6882`, and `seed-seam-accounts.sh` seeds personas into S `:5122`. Slots are dynamic and several sessions share this host; a default should be the invoking worktree's slot (from its `dep-ssd-local/.env`, as `up-slot.sh` / `slot-env.sh` already do) — or a refusal — never slot 1. Lower-risk leftovers are listed after.

## The spots (platform-s `develop` + [PS-914](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-914/data-testid-coverage-audit-scan-every-page-and-ui-element-razor-views) branch, 29 Sep 2026)

**Act on another session's stack**

| File:line | Default | Should be |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `ssd/dep-ssd-local/commission-provisioning-key.sh:37`, `:51` (help) | `K_URL="http://localhost:6882"` unless `--k-url` / `--slot` | the slot in this worktree's `.env` ([PS-852](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-852/per-slot-provisioning-key-k-provisioning-key-in-the-slots-dep-ssd) added `--slot`; the no-flag default is still slot 1) |
| `ssd/dep-ssd-local/seed-seam-accounts.sh:58` | `BASE_URL="${BASE_URL:-https://localhost:5122}"` | this worktree's `HTTPS_PORT` (its `--reset` already refuses without a `.env`; the plain seed does not) |

**Fall back to slot 1 (not slot-aware)**

| File:line | Value |
| -- | -- |
| `ssd/Models/CardanoAnchorSettings.cs:11`, `ssd/appsettings.json:172` | `BaseUrl = "http://localhost:6882"` — the host `dotnet run` path |
| `ssd/dep-ssd-local/Docker.appsettings.template.json:353–356, 424, 533` | `AppUrl` / `WebSiteUrl*` / `StatusListBaseUrl` on `:5122`, CardanoAnchor `BaseUrl` on `:6882` (overridden per slot at runtime — the template documents slot 1 as if it were the value) |
| `ssd/dep-ssd-local/docker-compose.override.yml:63, 69–73` | `${K_GATEWAY_URL:-…:6882}`, `${HTTPS_PORT:-5122}` — silent slot-1 fallback when a slot's `.env` lacks the key |
| `.claude/settings.local.json:32–39` | committed permission allowlist entries that `curl http://localhost:6882/api/…` — slot 1's K |

## Verified from the code and docs (29 Sep, re-read)

* `commission-provisioning-key.sh:37` sets `K_URL="http://localhost:6882"`; only `--slot` (`:78–84`, derives `6882 + 100*(N-1)`) or `--k-url` changes it. **The supported path is safe:** `up-slot.sh` reaches it through `k-pairing.sh:154`, which always passes `--slot "$n"`, and `docs/stack_slots_how_to.md:417, 608` document `--slot N`. The slot-1 default bites only on a direct call without `--slot` — which the script accepts silently.
* `seed-seam-accounts.sh:58` `BASE_URL="${BASE_URL:-https://localhost:5122}"`; its ownership guard (`:49`, `:151`) covers `--reset` only, so a plain seed from a slot-N worktree with no `BASE_URL` exported seeds slot 1's stack.
* `.claude/settings.local.json` is tracked (last changed `163995ae`, 29 May).
* Container runtime confirmed slot-derived: `docker-compose.override.yml:63, 69–73` read `K_GATEWAY_URL` / `HTTPS_PORT`, which `slot-env.sh:55, 126` writes per slot.

## Fix shape (Stuart's call)

Make both scripts read the slot from the invoking worktree's `.env` (or refuse, printing the `--slot N` form), the way `up-slot.sh` does. Consider making the compose fallbacks refuse instead of defaulting, and move the `.claude` allowlist entries to a per-developer file. A `UpSlotScriptTests`-style contract test ("no script under `dep-ssd-local/` defaults to a literal slot port") would hold it.

## Acceptance — comprehensive slot unit tests in the same PR

Slots are dynamic: a developer picks, drops and re-picks them at will, several sessions share one host, and slot numbers are never fixed. A script that defaults to a fixed slot mints a key on, or seeds personas into, another session's stack — and nothing errors. That makes this a high-risk area, so the PR is not done without unit tests covering **every slot 1..4, not only slot 1 or the author's**:

* `tests/ssd.UnitTests/UpSlotScriptTests.cs` (or a sibling, driving the scripts in bash the way it already does) extended: for a worktree `.env` on each slot 1..4, `commission-provisioning-key.sh` with no `--slot` / `--k-url` targets that slot's K gateway, and `seed-seam-accounts.sh` with no `BASE_URL` targets that slot's app; with no `.env` and no flag, each refuses — never a fixed-slot default.
* `StackSlotContractTests` extended: `docker-compose.override.yml` has no fixed-slot fallback that a slot's `.env` could silently fall through to (or, if fallbacks stay, the test proves `slot-env.sh` always writes every key they read, for every slot).
* A static contract test: no script under `ssd/dep-ssd-local/` and no tracked config carries a literal published port of ANY slot 1..4 (the same rule `systemTest/tests-unit/no_hardcoded_slot_urls.test.ts` now applies to the suite) — bite-checked: plant one, see it red, remove it.
* Hermetic: identical results unslotted and with any slot's variables in the environment.

**Why no Playwright test here.** Nothing in this ticket renders. The subject is what a shell script and a Compose file *resolve to* before any container starts, so the verifiable criteria are the bash-driven xUnit contract tests named above plus one observation per slot: from a worktree whose `dep-ssd-local/.env` names slot N, `commission-provisioning-key.sh --dry-run` (or its printed target) names `6882 + 100·(N−1)` and `seed-seam-accounts.sh` names that slot's `HTTPS_PORT` — captured for N = 1..4, with the no-`.env` refusal captured too. A browser journey could not distinguish "minted on my slot" from "minted on slot 1", which is the entire defect.

## Not in this ticket

`systemTest/` — fixed on the [PS-914](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-914/data-testid-coverage-audit-scan-every-page-and-ui-element-razor-views) branch (`a37f594e`: slot-derived Mailpit/app hints, `K_DEFAULT_API_URL` removed, a guard over every slot's ports). platform-k → [KS-1355](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1355/stack-tooling-is-not-slot-derived-end-to-end-stack-guard-lists-a) / [KS-1381](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1381/slot-1-urls-hard-coded-outside-ks-1355s-four-spots-the-three-frontends) (Kamil), [KS-1382](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1382/blockchaintesting-five-auditdasttenant-isolation-entry-points-default) (Kamil). Deployed-environment dirs (`dep-aws-*`, `dep-az-*`) are not slotted. `tests/ssd.UnitTests` literals are fixtures (transport-policy / erasure-client cases), not defaults.

## Environment

Audited 29 Sep 2026 on Peter's Mac while pairing slot 2 for the [PS-914](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-914/data-testid-coverage-audit-scan-every-page-and-ui-element-razor-views) gate run.

title: Slot-1 URLs outside KS-1355's four spots: m365's Entra redirect URI defaults to :6882 (compose + three code fallbacks), bootstrap leaves FRONTEND_URL / CORS_ORIGINS / LLM_BASE_URL at slot 1, 20 service .env.examples and two smoke scripts pin slot 1, and dead VITE_* compose values name :6882
description:
## BLUF

On a slot-N stack, **platform-k's M365 integration builds its Entra OAuth redirect URI on slot 1's gateway** (`http://localhost:6882/api/m365/callback`) unless someone sets `ENTRA_REDIRECT_URI` by hand — the compose default and three fallbacks in `services/m365-integration/src/index.ts` all name `:6882`. And `bootstrap-env.sh` **derives only** `DATABASE_URL` **/** `REDIS_URL` **per slot**, so a fresh slot-N `.env` keeps slot 1's `FRONTEND_URL`, has no gateway origin in `CORS_ORIGINS`, and keeps `LLM_BASE_URL` on slot 1's Ollama — all three had to be edited by hand on slot 2 today. This is the remainder after [KS-1355](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1355/stack-tooling-is-not-slot-derived-end-to-end-stack-guard-lists-a) (compose `FRONTEND_URL` / `CORS_ORIGINS` defaults, `preflight.sh:94`, `start-local.sh`, `dev-reload.sh` — excluded here). Slots are dynamic; each value should derive from `stack_env.sh`'s exported ports.

## The spots (platform-k `develop` `0aa9b52c6`, tracked files, re-read line by line 29 Sep)

**Runtime — the M365 callback points at slot 1**

| File:line | Value |
| -- | -- |
| `Blockchain/Dev/docker-compose.yml:888` | `ENTRA_REDIRECT_URI=${ENTRA_REDIRECT_URI:-http://localhost:6882/api/m365/callback}` |
| `Blockchain/Dev/services/m365-integration/src/index.ts:481, 595` | `process.env.ENTRA_REDIRECT_URI \|\| \`${process.env.FRONTEND_URL || '[http://localhost:6882](<http://localhost:6882>)'}/api/m365/callback\`\` |
| `Blockchain/Dev/services/m365-integration/src/index.ts:993` | `… \|\| 'http://localhost:6882/api/m365/callback'` |

**Bootstrap — derives two URLs per slot, not the rest** (`scripts/bootstrap-env.sh:229` `DATABASE_URL`, `:240` `REDIS_URL`; nothing writes these)

| Template (`env.example` is canonical since [KS-1081](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1081/config-drift-two-tracked-env-templates-disagree-by-39-vars-bootstrap); `.env.example` is its fallback) | Key | Slot-1 value |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `Blockchain/Dev/env.example:146` | `CORS_ORIGINS` | `:6100–:6102` only — no gateway / website origin on any slot |
| `Blockchain/Dev/env.example:372` | `LLM_BASE_URL` | `:11434` (Ollama is offset per slot in `stack_env.sh`) |
| `Blockchain/Dev/.env.local.example:117` | `FRONTEND_URL` | `:6882` (lines 23–63 also document every social-login callback on `:6882`) |
| `Blockchain/Dev/.env.example:92, 95, 190` (fallback template) | `FRONTEND_URL`, `API_BASE_URL`, `CORS_ORIGINS` | `:6882`, `:6881` |
| `Blockchain/Dev/services/*/.env.example`, `services/billing/env.example` — **20 files** | `DATABASE_URL` `:6432`, `REDIS_URL` `:6379`; api-gateway `CORS_ORIGINS`; m365 `ENTRA_REDIRECT_URI`; billing `API_GATEWAY_URL` | slot 1 |

**Scripts — default to slot 1**

| File:line |  |
| -- | -- |
| `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/auth-matrix-smoke.sh:31` | `API_URL="${API_URL:-http://localhost:6882}"` |
| `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/smoke-test.sh:15` | `GATEWAY="http://localhost:6882"` — no override |
| `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/setup-dev-environment.sh:323–324`, `start-environment.sh:241` | print slot-1 URLs whatever the slot (display only) |

**Dead config — inert, but a slot-1 literal that reads as live**

`Blockchain/Dev/docker-compose.yml:1841, 1876, 1910–1912` set `VITE_API_URL` / `VITE_ORIGINATE_URL` / `VITE_ANALYTICS_URL` to `http://localhost:6882/…` in the issuer, verifier and admin frontends' **runtime** `environment:`. Those images are static Vite builds (`RUN npm run build`, then nginx — `frontend/{issuer,verifier,admin}/Dockerfile`), `import.meta.env.VITE_*` is fixed at build time, and no build arg or `.env` supplies it, so the bundles use their relative `'/api'` fallback — correct on every slot. The values are never read; delete them so nobody takes them as the source of truth.

## Fix shape (Kamil's call)

Pass `GATEWAY_PORT` into compose for `ENTRA_REDIRECT_URI` and drop the three `:6882` fallbacks in m365 (fail if neither `ENTRA_REDIRECT_URI` nor `FRONTEND_URL` is set); have `bootstrap-env.sh` write `FRONTEND_URL`, `API_BASE_URL`, `CORS_ORIGINS` (gateway + website origins) and `LLM_BASE_URL` from `stack_env.sh` as it does `DATABASE_URL`; source `stack_env.sh` in the two smoke scripts; remove the dead `VITE_*` lines. [KS-1355](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1355/stack-tooling-is-not-slot-derived-end-to-end-stack-guard-lists-a)'s proposed `check-stack-safety.sh` pin could take a "no literal slot port outside `stack_env.sh`" rule to hold all of it.

## Acceptance — comprehensive slot unit tests in the same PR

Slots are dynamic: a developer picks, drops and re-picks them at will, several sessions share one host, and slot numbers are never fixed. A value right for the slot it was checked on is wrong on every other — and the failure is silent (a request lands on someone else's stack, or an OAuth callback on the wrong gateway). That makes this a high-risk area, so the PR is not done without unit tests that prove every changed value **for every slot 1..4, not only slot 1 or the slot the author used**:

* `scripts/__tests__/bootstrap_env_slot_ports.test.sh` extended: for `SECUURA_STACK_SLOT` = 1, 2, 3, 4, a fresh bootstrap writes `FRONTEND_URL`, `API_BASE_URL`, `CORS_ORIGINS` (gateway + website origins) and `LLM_BASE_URL` on that slot's ports from `stack_env.sh` — and no other slot's port appears in the output.
* A render test (`docker compose config` per slot) asserting `ENTRA_REDIRECT_URI` resolves to that slot's gateway, and a unit test that `services/m365-integration` has no `:6882` fallback left (no-`ENTRA_REDIRECT_URI`, no-`FRONTEND_URL` case refuses rather than defaulting).
* The two smoke scripts target the named slot's gateway for 1..4 and refuse locally when no slot is named.
* A static guard (e.g. in `check-stack-safety.sh`) failing on any literal published port of ANY slot 1..4 outside `stack_env.sh` — bite-checked: plant one, see it red, remove it.
* Tests are hermetic: run unslotted AND under each slot's environment with identical results (the offline-suite rule), never spawned with the shell's slot variables leaking in.

## Not in this ticket

[KS-1355](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1355/stack-tooling-is-not-slot-derived-end-to-end-stack-guard-lists-a)'s four spots. `Blockchain/Testing/**` `TARGET_BASE` defaults → [KS-1382](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1382/blockchaintesting-five-auditdasttenant-isolation-entry-points-default) (the Internal Audit Harness, Kamil). The build break → [KS-1380](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1380/develop-does-not-build-since-ks-1378-1339-analytics-billing-and). `docker-compose.production.yml` (deployed, not slotted).

## Correction history

First filed 29 Sep 08:29 UTC with the `VITE_*` values as the headline ("the frontends call slot 1's gateway"). Re-checked against the Dockerfiles the same morning: they are build-time variables never supplied at build, so that claim was wrong and is now listed as dead config; the template counts and canonical-template references were also corrected.

## Environment

Peter's Mac, fresh K worktree at `0aa9b52c6`, slot 2, 29 Sep 2026. Found while pairing platform-k slot 2 for the platform-s [PS-914](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-914/data-testid-coverage-audit-scan-every-page-and-ui-element-razor-views) run.

## Shared acceptance — slot derivation group (added 6 Oct 2026)

This ticket is one of five platform-k tickets that must all take slot values from `stack_env.sh` and never fall back to slot 1: [KS-1355](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1355>), [KS-1381](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1381>), [KS-1389](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1389>), [KS-1382](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1382>), [KS-1162](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1162>). None of them is done until these hold, in addition to its own acceptance above:

1. **One guard.** A single static guard in `check-stack-safety.sh` fails on any literal published port of any slot 1–4 outside `stack_env.sh`. The first ticket to land creates it; the others extend it; nobody adds a second guard. Bite-checked: plant a literal, see it red, remove it.
2. **No silent default.** A local run with no slot named refuses and prints an example command; it never falls back to slot 1 (preflight, `slot-target.sh`, the `Blockchain/Testing` entry points, the smoke scripts). Any change to `stack_env.sh`'s own slot-1 default re-runs every test in this group.
3. **One preflight change.** [KS-1355](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1355/stack-tooling-is-not-slot-derived-end-to-end-stack-guard-lists-a) (spot 4, `preflight.sh:94`) and [KS-1389](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1389/sourcing-systemtestslot-targetsh-with-no-slot-named-silently-exports) (leg 13, `preflight.sh:589-630`) land in one PR, or one after the other, each re-running the other's checks.
4. **The workflow question.** [KS-1162](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1162/three-retired-github-workflows-bake-slot-234-port-literals) decides first whether the three workflows are deleted or made to derive their ports. If deleted, [KS-1382](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1382/blockchaintesting-five-auditdasttenant-isolation-entry-points-default)'s "explicit `TARGET_BASE` is used unchanged" criterion has no CI caller left; if derived, their `TARGET_BASE` comes from `stack_env.sh` too.
5. **Tests cover every slot.** Slots 1–4, hermetic: identical results unslotted and under each slot's environment.

**This ticket's part:** points 1, 2 and 5 — the static guard in this ticket's acceptance is the point-1 guard, shared with [KS-1355](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1355/stack-tooling-is-not-slot-derived-end-to-end-stack-guard-lists-a)'s `docker-compose.yml` pin (both tickets edit that file), and the two smoke scripts follow point 2.

No commit under this key changes them.

## The slot-derivation group's shared static guard now EXISTS — created by KS-1355, and this ticket extends it

Facts only, from the KS-1355 build (Seat K 8th, 2026-10-13). KS-1355 is the first of the five to
land, so by this ticket's own acceptance point 1 — *"the first ticket to land creates it; the
others extend it; nobody adds a second guard"* — it created the guard.

**Where it is:** `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/check-stack-safety.sh`, section **3c**. The file went
from 100 to 105 invariants.

**Its scope is deliberately NARROW, and stated in the guard itself:** scripts that run the
**platform** compose stack with `up` / `run` / `restart` / `down`. It does **not** yet cover the
env templates, the 20 service `.env.example` files or the two smoke scripts this ticket lists.
**That widening is KS-1381's**, and the guard's own comment says so by name. Do not add a second
guard.

**What it asserts today:**
- Every declared platform launcher sources `stack_env.sh` — `Start_Up/start-secuura.sh`,
  `Blockchain/Dev/stop-secuura.sh`, `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/start-local.sh`. It replaced a
  `for f in "$START" "$STOP"` loop that covered two of them, which is how `start-local.sh`
  brought the platform stack up slot-blind with the gate green.
- `LAUNCHER_EXCEPTIONS` — each entry `path|reason`, with a ticket. Current entries:
  `start-environment.sh` and `stop-environment.sh` (**KS-1550**), `observability.sh` (KS-200,
  standalone stack), and two Akto side-stack scripts.
- A **census**: a NEW tracked script that runs the platform compose and is in neither list fails
  the gate.
- Both directions of the list: an exception that is **no longer** a launcher is reported stale,
  and an exception with **no reason** is refused.

**Measurement worth having before you extend it:** a naive text match for a compose
`up|run|restart|down` hits **19** tracked `.sh`, of which **7 are false positives** — the only
mention is a comment or a line that *prints* a compose command to the operator
(`check-slot-credentials.sh`, `setup-dev-environment.sh`, `stack_guard.sh`,
`verify-slot-credential-isolation.sh`, `systemTest/__tests__/slot_target.test.sh`, and two Akto
scripts). Filtering comments and printer lines (`echo`/`printf`/`say`/`print_info`/…) gives the
real candidate set of **8**. An exception list padded with false positives is one nobody reads.
The detector lives in the guard; a copy is at
`5_Project_History/2026-10-13_seatK-8th/tampers/detect2.sh`.

## This ticket's "Dead config" section is CONFIRMED by independent measurement

Measured during the KS-1355 build **before** reading this ticket, and it agrees with what is
written here — so both readings are controls on each other:

- The issuer, verifier and admin images build in stage 1 (`RUN npm run build`) and stage 2 is
  nginx serving static `dist/`.
- **No** frontend Dockerfile declares an `ARG` or `ENV` for any `VITE_*` — zero matches across
  `Blockchain/Dev/frontend/*/Dockerfile`.
- Source reads `VITE_API_URL` in **10** files, `VITE_ORIGINATE_URL` in **2**, and
  `VITE_ANALYTICS_URL` in **ZERO**.

So the five values are dead config, as this ticket says. KS-1355 did **not** touch them: they are
**named exceptions** in both of its guards, each carrying KS-1381 as the reason, so they stay
visible rather than silently tolerated. No duplicate ticket was filed.

## Also relevant to this ticket's acceptance

- **`env.example:146`** (this ticket's bootstrap table) **is done** — KS-1355 commented it out
  with a pointer to `docker-compose.yml:503`, whose default now derives from `GATEWAY_PORT` /
  `WEBSITE_PORT` and also carries the `:6103` origin the old line omitted. Measured on the way:
  `bootstrap-env.sh` really did copy that line into a generated slot-2 `.env`, so it was a live
  defect and not only a template smell.
- **Group point 3** (one preflight change): KS-1355 did spot 4, `preflight.sh:94`. **KS-1389's
  leg 13 is not built**, so there were no KS-1389 checks to re-run; whichever lands second
  re-runs the other's.
- **Group point 5** (slots 1–4, hermetic): KS-1355's render proof covers all four slots and
  clears ambient slot variables.


The guard landed in PR https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/1526 (KS-1355), head `f0278d3b267b7a09374690810a6a578b71e87b57`.

title: develop does not build since KS-1378 (#1339): analytics, billing and governance images fail `tsc` — packages/shared now locks @types/express-serve-static-core 4.19.9 / @types/pg 8.23.1, those three services still lock 4.19.8 / 8.20.0
description:
## BLUF

A clean build of platform-k `develop` at `0aa9b52c6` fails: `Start_Up/start-secuura.sh --rebuild` stops with *"Build FAILED for: analytics billing governance — not starting containers"*, so no stack comes up. The previous clean build on this Mac, at `d9ce1403d` (28 Sep), succeeded. Between the two, no `package.json` or Dockerfile of those three services changed; what changed is [KS-1378](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1378/five-new-advisories-block-every-push-bump-morgan-nodemailer-ip-address) **(**[Secuura/Distributed_Secuura#1339](https://linear.app/secuura/review/ks-1378-bump-morgan-nodemailer-ip-address-and-undici-off-five-815a0a16d4c7), `2cb858335`**)**, which refreshed `packages/shared/package-lock.json` and several services' locks — but not these three.

## Evidence

`packages/shared/package-lock.json` (top-level `node_modules/@types/*`):

|  | before `2cb858335` | after | `services/analytics` lock at `0aa9b52c6` |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| `@types/express-serve-static-core` | 4.19.8 | **4.19.9** | 4.19.8 |
| `@types/pg` | 8.20.0 | **8.23.1** | 8.20.0 |
| `@types/express` | 4.17.25 | 4.17.25 | 4.17.25 |

Each service image copies the built `/shared` (with its own `node_modules`) beside the service's `node_modules`, so `tsc` sees two copies of the same declarations:

```
analytics  src/index.ts(34,7): error TS2742: The inferred type of 'app' cannot be named without a reference to '@secuura/shared/node_modules/@types/express-serve-static-core'. This is likely not portable.
           (also routes/analytics.ts:20, routes/dashboard.ts:12, routes/health.ts:7)
billing    src/db.ts(45,32): error TS2345: Argument of type 'import("/app/node_modules/@types/pg/index").Pool' is not assignable to parameter of type 'import("/shared/node_modules/@types/pg/index").Pool'.
           (plus TS2742 on index.ts:33, routes/billing.ts:26, routes/webhooks.ts:29)
governance same TS2742 family
```

`#1339`'s file list refreshes the locks of queue, security, timestamping, prism and others; `services/analytics`, `services/billing` and `services/governance` are not in it.

**The mismatch is wider than the three that fail (re-checked from every lock at** `0aa9b52c6`**).** Eleven service locks still carry `@types/express-serve-static-core` 4.19.8 / `@types/pg` 8.20.0 against shared's 4.19.9 / 8.23.1: analytics, billing, governance (fail) and **kyc, nft-certificate, referral, staking, tenant-provisioning, tokenisation, transfer, wallet-connector** (built fine in the same run — none of their exported types is inferred across the boundary today, so they are latent, one annotation-less `const app = express()` away from the same error). `services/shared` locks 4.19.8 and `vc-issuer` a third `@types/pg` (8.21.0). At the last good commit `d9ce1403d`, `packages/shared` itself locked 4.19.8 / 8.20.0 — every lock agreed, which is why that build passed. All 35 images were attempted in this run; exactly these three failed.

## Likely fix (Kamil's call)

Refresh the failing three — and the eight latent ones — to the same `@types/express-serve-static-core` / `@types/pg` versions `packages/shared` now pins (or pin those `@types` in shared to what the services use). A check that every service lock agrees with `packages/shared` on the `@types` it re-exports would stop the next bump doing this — [KS-953](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-953/class-editing-api-gatewaysrcindexts-silently-reddens-packagesshared) is the same class (a change in one package silently reddening another).

## Reproduce

```bash
git worktree add --detach <path> origin/develop      # 0aa9b52c6
cd <path> && SECUURA_STACK_SLOT=<N> ./Start_Up/start-secuura.sh --rebuild
```

## Environment

Peter's Mac, Docker Desktop 8 CPU / 31.3 GiB, fresh K worktree at `0aa9b52c6`, slot 2, 29 Sep 2026 \~09:25–09:50 BST. Found while bringing up a paired K for the platform-s [PS-914](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-914/data-testid-coverage-audit-scan-every-page-and-ui-element-razor-views) gate run. Not caused by that work (no platform-k change on it).
