title: ARCHITECTURE.md §6.1 still says the SSP authenticates to the SBCM with "a JWT obtained from POST /api/auth/login" — that is the break-glass path; the per-organisation connector key (x-api-key) is the norm
description:
## Finding (SDK Phase 0 assessment, [PS-971](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-971/sdk-phase-0-architecture-and-functional-definition-technical-marketing) §13 finding 8, SSP develop @ `1800ab3`)

*Terms: the SSP is the Secuura Services Provider (*`platform-s` */* `obeden-ssd`*); the SBCM is the Secuura Block Chain Manager (*`platform-k`*). Identifiers, routes and paths are quoted as the code has them. ARCHITECTURE.md itself still uses the older names "Platform S" and "Platform K".*

`docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` §6.1 opens: "Platform S talks to Platform K over REST with a service (or per-user) **JWT** obtained from `POST /api/auth/login`", and the §6.1 sequence diagram labels the SSP→SBCM hop "AnchorOrOriginate (JWT)". §7.4 of the same document correctly describes the current model — one provisioning `sk_` key per instance, one connector key per organisation sent as `x-api-key`, the login-derived bearer kept **only** as break-glass and alarmed when used — so the document contradicts itself. Still true at `477eb57`: #880 ([PS-933](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-933/docs-re-sync-with-develop-chain-confirmed-verification-domain-linkage)) left §6.1 and its diagram label untouched.

The code: `CardanoAnchorService.SendWithAuthRetryAsync` (`ssd/Services/CardanoAnchor/CardanoAnchorService.cs:1414-1480`) uses the document owner's organisation key when `UseConnectorKeyAuth` is on and falls back to the shared bearer only when the owner has no key; `ApplyAuth` (`:1517-1535`) sends `x-api-key` alone for a connector key, or `Authorization: Bearer` + CSRF cookie/header for the break-glass path. UAT, dev-ps and the local stack all run `UseConnectorKeyAuth = true`.

## Do

* Rewrite the §6.1 opening and the diagram label: connector key as the norm, bearer as break-glass with a pointer to §7.4 and `docs/platform-k-dr.md`.
* While there: §6.1's "per-user" JWT wording refers to the retired per-user account tier (the §7.4 "Superseded" note) — drop it.
* Check `docs/ONE-PAGER-TECHNICAL.md` and `docs/platform-s-platform-k-integration.pdf`'s summary paragraph for the same sentence.
* Documentation-only PR; say so in the body.

## Why it matters for the SDK

`docs/sdk/SDK-ARCHITECTURE.md` decision 1 (the SDK never calls the SBCM, because the connector key is an SSP-side secret) rests on the connector-key model; ARCHITECTURE is the document that model is cited from.

## Acceptance

* `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` section 6.1's opening sentence no longer says the SSP talks to the SBCM with a service (or per-user) **JWT** obtained from `POST /api/auth/login`. It states the **per-organisation connector key, sent as** `x-api-key`, as the norm, and the login-derived bearer as **break-glass**, with a pointer to section 7.4 and `docs/platform-k-dr.md`.
* The section 6.1 sequence diagram's SSP-to-SBCM label no longer reads "AnchorOrOriginate (JWT)". Prose and diagram say the same thing — #880 ([PS-933](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-933/docs-re-sync-with-develop-chain-confirmed-verification-domain-linkage)) left both untouched, which is how the self-contradiction with section 7.4 survived.
* The "per-user" JWT wording is dropped: it refers to the retired per-user account tier that section 7.4 already marks *Superseded*.
* The new statement matches the code as read at `477eb57`: `SendWithAuthRetryAsync` (`CardanoAnchorService.cs:1414-1480`) uses the document owner's organisation key when `UseConnectorKeyAuth` is on and falls back to the shared bearer only when the owner has no key; `ApplyAuth` (`:1517-1535`) sends `x-api-key` alone for a connector key, or `Authorization: Bearer` plus the CSRF cookie and header for break-glass. UAT, dev-ps and the local stack all run `UseConnectorKeyAuth = true` — say so, so the reader knows the norm is the norm everywhere deployed.
* `docs/ONE-PAGER-TECHNICAL.md` and the summary paragraph of `docs/platform-s-platform-k-integration.pdf` are checked for the same sentence, and the outcome of that check is recorded here — corrected, or confirmed clean. Not left open.
* Section 6.1 and section 7.4 no longer contradict each other, read end to end rather than only at the edited sentence.
* `docs/sdk/SDK-ARCHITECTURE.md` decision 1 — the SDK never calls the SBCM, because the connector key is an SSP-side secret — still cites section 6.1, and now cites a sentence that actually supports it.
* **Documentation-only PR, and the description says so explicitly**, standing in for the full systemTest run (the CLAUDE.md rule: the omission must be visible and deliberate, never silent).

**Why no Playwright test applies, and what replaces it.** Nothing in the product changes. This is prose and a diagram label; there is no behaviour to exercise, no route, no control, and no assertion a browser could make that would differ before and after. Writing a journey here would assert the existing connector-key behaviour, which is already covered by the `@k-live` specs and is not what this ticket touches. The verifiable criterion is instead:

1. **The named file states X.** `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` section 6.1 (prose and diagram label) describes the connector key as the norm and the bearer as break-glass, verified by reading it — and the PR diff shows both the sentence and the diagram label changed, not just one. The diagram label is the half most likely to be missed, because #880 missed exactly that.
2. **A grep that must come back empty** across `docs/`: no remaining claim that the SSP authenticates to the SBCM by `POST /api/auth/login` as the normal path, and no remaining "per-user" JWT wording. Paste the grep and its empty result in the PR — that is what makes "checked ONE-PAGER-TECHNICAL too" an assertion rather than a claim.
3. **Control:** the code is **not** edited. `CardanoAnchorService` and `UseConnectorKeyAuth` are untouched, and `dotnet test` is green at the same counts as `develop` — evidence that a documentation fix stayed a documentation fix.

If a docs-contract test is wanted so this cannot drift again, the cheapest shape is an xUnit assertion that section 6.1 does not contain the login-endpoint claim — worth considering, since this is the second time the sentence has outlived the model it describes.

title: docs/outlook-addin/PS-345-authenticated-features.md still says the add-in signs in through "Entra CIAM" — the CIAM scheme was deleted (PS-588); the Microsoft scheme is Entra workforce on /common
description:
## Finding (SDK Phase 0 assessment, [PS-971](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-971/sdk-phase-0-architecture-and-functional-definition-technical-marketing) §13 finding 7, SSP develop @ `1800ab3`)

*Terms: the SSP is the Secuura Services Provider (*`platform-s` */* `obeden-ssd`*); the SBCM is the Secuura Block Chain Manager (*`platform-k`*). Identifiers, routes and paths are quoted as the code has them.*

`docs/outlook-addin/PS-345-authenticated-features.md` describes the add-in's auth bridge as "the user signs in via the existing **Entra CIAM** / Identity flow", names "CIAM redirect URIs" and "the Entra CIAM app's allowed redirect/reply URLs" in the deployment notes, and its test flow says "S login (CIAM)".

On the SSP's `develop` the CIAM scheme no longer exists: [PS-588](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-588/e483-workforce-only-retire-the-ciam-scheme-entirely) deleted it from code, [PS-587](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-587/e483-single-microsoft-entry-point-via-common-delete-home-realm) moved Microsoft sign-in to the **Entra workforce** tenant on the `/common` authority (`ssd/Startup.cs:96-146`; the Login page's `EntraStart` / `EntraWorkforceLogin` / `EntraLogin` handlers at `ssd/Areas/Identity/Pages/Account/Login.cshtml.cs:241-298, :391-410`), and [PS-750](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-750/restore-uat-sign-in-on-develop-ciam-is-retired-in-code-and-uat-cannot) stripped `AzureAdCiam` / `EntraS1` from the deploy templates. [PS-933](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-933/docs-re-sync-with-develop-chain-confirmed-verification-domain-linkage) (#880) re-synced ARCHITECTURE and the one-pagers for exactly this change but did not reach the Outlook folder — still true at `477eb57`.

## Do

* Replace every CIAM mention in that file with the workforce scheme (`S2Constants.cs:56-79` holds the scheme names), and re-state which redirect URIs the Dialog needs against the workforce app registration.
* Sweep the rest of `docs/outlook-addin/` (`DEPLOYMENT.md`, `PS-342-foundation-spike.md`) and `outlook-addin/README*` for the same word; `grep -rn CIAM docs/outlook-addin outlook-addin --include=*.md`.
* Documentation-only PR; say so in the body.

## Why it matters for the SDK

`docs/sdk/SDK-ARCHITECTURE.md` §5.3 reuses the Outlook add-in's "sign in through the SSP's existing login" pattern for the SDK's PKCE flow and names the workforce scheme; the Outlook doc is the reference an implementer will read next.

## Acceptance

* `grep -rn CIAM docs/outlook-addin outlook-addin --include=*.md` returns **nothing** — the sweep named in *Do* is complete, not just the one file.
* `docs/outlook-addin/PS-345-authenticated-features.md` names the **Entra workforce** scheme on the `/common` authority, using the scheme constants as `ssd/S2Constants.cs` has them, and no longer says "Entra CIAM", "CIAM redirect URIs", "the Entra CIAM app" or "S login (CIAM)".
* The deployment notes state which redirect/reply URIs the Office Dialog needs **against the workforce app registration**, not a CIAM one.
* Nothing outside `docs/` and `outlook-addin/*.md` changes: `git diff --stat` on the PR shows no `.cs`, `.cshtml`, `.js` or `appsettings*` file.
* Cross-check: the scheme named here matches what `docs/sdk/SDK-ARCHITECTURE.md` §5.3 says, so the two docs cannot be read against each other.

**Why no Playwright test applies**: this ticket changes **documentation only** — there is no route, control or copy string in the running application that the edit touches, so no browser journey can observe it, and the PR is a documentation-only PR which under the `develop` gate states that explicitly instead of carrying a suite run. The verifiable criterion is the `grep` above returning empty plus the named sentences reading as the workforce scheme. A `DocsCiamRetiredContractTests`-style xUnit test asserting that no file under `docs/outlook-addin/` contains the string `CIAM` would make the rule permanent, and is the right place for it if we want the sweep to stay swept.

title: The SSP has no OpenAPI document, no bearer authentication scheme for external callers and no [ApiController] surface outside the test seam — the SDK API (Phase 1) has to add all three
description:
## Finding (SDK Phase 0 assessment, [PS-971](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-971/sdk-phase-0-architecture-and-functional-definition-technical-marketing) §13 finding 6, SSP develop @ `1800ab3`)

*Terms: the SSP is the Secuura Services Provider (*`platform-s` */* `obeden-ssd`*); the SBCM is the Secuura Block Chain Manager (*`platform-k`*). Identifiers, routes and paths are quoted as the code has them.*

Everything on the SSP is cookie-authenticated MVC or Razor Pages behind a global `AuthorizeFilter` (`ssd/Startup.cs:972`) and a global `AutoValidateAntiforgeryToken` (`:1001`). For a machine caller there is:

* **no OpenAPI / Swagger** — `ssd/ssd.csproj` references neither Swashbuckle nor NSwag; nothing describes any route;
* **no bearer / API-key authentication scheme** — no `JwtBearer` package, no custom handler; sign-in is Identity cookies plus Entra workforce, Google, Apple and GitHub;
* **no** `[ApiController]` outside `TestSeamController` (a policy-gated test hook).

The one precedent is `OutlookApiController` (`ssd/Controllers/OutlookApiController.cs:34`): a `ControllerBase` under `/api/outlook`, `[AllowAnonymous]` at the class, a hand-checked `Authorization: Bearer` Data-Protection token carrying only the email (`ssd/Services/Outlook/OutlookAddinTokenService.cs:44`), 404 unless `AppSpecific:Outlook:Enabled`. It works, but it is bespoke to one add-in and undocumented by any spec.

## What resolves it — SDK Phase 1 (`docs/sdk/SDK-ARCHITECTURE.md` §14, items 1–5)

1. `AppSpecific:Sdk` settings, `Enabled` default `false`.
2. `SdkAuthenticationHandler` — user bearer token and application key + `X-Secuura-Act-As`; `SdkApiKey` and `SdkSession` tables; authorize / token endpoints (PKCE through the SSP's existing login; library decision Data Protection vs OpenIddict on the ticket); key management in Settings → Integrations.
3. `SdkCallLog` + action filter + retention + `/AdminSdkCalls`.
4. Controllers under `/api/sdk/v1` as thin adapters over the existing services.
5. Swashbuckle generating `docs/sdk/openapi/secuura-sdk-v1.yaml`, pinned by a contract test (file in git == what the running app emits).

This ticket is the finding and the parent for the Phase 1 tickets; split it into the five above once Phase 0 ([PS-971](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-971/sdk-phase-0-architecture-and-functional-definition-technical-marketing)) is reviewed. Every Phase 1 PR targets the `project/sdk` branch. Whether `/api/outlook/*` later moves onto the same handler and spec is a separate decision (project *Outlook Add-in → Platform S*).

## Acceptance

This ticket is the **finding and the Phase 1 parent**, so its own acceptance is that the finding is recorded accurately and split — not that any API ships here.

* Each of the five Phase 1 items above exists as a child issue under this one, each with its own done-when, and each targeting the `project/sdk` branch.
* The finding is re-verified against the SSP `develop` tip at split time, not left at `1800ab3`: `ssd/ssd.csproj` still references no Swashbuckle/NSwag, there is still no `JwtBearer` package or custom bearer handler, and `grep -rn "\[ApiController\]" ssd/` still matches only `TestSeamController`. If any of those has changed, the ticket is corrected rather than split as written.
* The `OutlookApiController` precedent is stated as a precedent and **not** silently adopted: the decision on whether `/api/outlook/*` moves onto the SDK handler and spec is recorded as out of scope here, with the project it belongs to named.
* `docs/sdk/SDK-ARCHITECTURE.md` §14 items 1–5 and the child issues say the same thing — no item exists in one and not the other.
* The library decision for item 2 (Data Protection vs OpenIddict) is written down on its child ticket before that ticket starts.

**Why no Playwright test applies**: there is nothing to drive in a browser. The subject is the **absence** of a machine-callable surface — an OpenAPI document, an authentication scheme and `[ApiController]` classes — and this ticket adds none of them; it records the gap and splits it. A Playwright journey signs in with cookies and clicks a UI, which is exactly the surface that already exists and is not in question.

The verifiable criteria instead are the greps above, plus the contract test that item 5 must bring with it: an xUnit test asserting that `docs/sdk/openapi/secuura-sdk-v1.yaml` **as committed** is byte-identical to what the running app emits from Swashbuckle, so a route added without regenerating the spec fails the offline gate. Item 2's child ticket carries its own xUnit coverage for the handler (a valid application key plus `X-Secuura-Act-As` authenticates as the acted-upon user; an expired or wrong-audience token is refused; the surface is 404 when `AppSpecific:Sdk:Enabled` is `false`, matching the Outlook gate's behaviour). Key material is named by config key only — `AppSpecific:Sdk` — and no test may print a key or token value.

title: The system-default PDF signing certificate is never loaded — PfxSigningKeyProvider.LoadFromPkcs12 has no caller, so the "system default" fallback in PdfProcessingService would sign with a null chain
description:
## Finding (SDK Phase 0 assessment, [PS-971](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-971/sdk-phase-0-architecture-and-functional-definition-technical-marketing) §13 finding 4, SSP develop @ `1800ab3`)

*Terms: the SSP is the Secuura Services Provider (*`platform-s` */* `obeden-ssd`*); the SBCM is the Secuura Block Chain Manager (*`platform-k`*). Identifiers, routes and paths are quoted as the code has them.*

On the SSP, `PdfProcessingService` resolves a signing certificate in the order personal certificate → organisation certificate → **system default** (`ssd/Services/PdfProcessing/PdfProcessingService.cs:375-394`, fallback used at `:620-623`). The system default is meant to come from `PfxSigningKeyProvider` (`PdfSigning:PfxPath` / `PfxPassword`), but:

* the provider's constructor does not load a PFX, and
* `PfxSigningKeyProvider.LoadFromPkcs12` (`ssd/Services/PdfProcessing/PfxSigningKeyProvider.cs:54`) **has no caller** anywhere in `ssd/` (`:34-45` shows the constructor).

So the fallback branch would receive a null chain. It is **dormant today** only because `Sign.SignDoc` redirects to certificate selection when no certificate is chosen (`ssd/Controllers/Sign.cs:179-373`) and the Flow engine pauses on a missing organisation certificate (decision 6, `docs/flow-design.md`) — no live path reaches the fallback. The `PdfSigning` configuration block (`ssd/appsettings.json`, CLAUDE.md "PDF Processing and Digital Signatures") therefore documents a capability that does not work.

## Decide, then do one of

1. **Remove the fallback**: delete the system-default branch, `PfxSigningKeyProvider`, `PdfSigningOptions.PfxPath/PfxPassword` and the CLAUDE.md / appsettings block; make "no certificate" an explicit refusal in the service with a verbatim message constant; **or**
2. **Make it work**: load the PFX at startup (fail fast on a bad path/password in `DeployMode=live`, log and disable otherwise), and pin it with a test that signs with only the system default configured.

Either way, an xUnit test that asserts the fallback branch cannot yield a null chain.

Related: [PS-946](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-946/move-pdf-signing-keys-into-azure-key-vault-hsm) (move PDF signing keys into Azure Key Vault / HSM) — if that lands first, the system-default concept moves with it.

## Effect on the SDK

`documents.sign` in `docs/sdk/SDK-ARCHITECTURE.md` requires a resolvable personal or organisation certificate and returns `validation` (`details.rule = no-certificate`) otherwise; `documents.certificates()` exists so an app can choose.

## Acceptance

* The decision — remove the fallback, or make it work — is recorded here before any code, including whether [PS-946](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-946/move-pdf-signing-keys-into-azure-key-vault-hsm) (signing keys into Key Vault / HSM) should land first and take the system-default concept with it.
* **If removed:** the system-default branch (`PdfProcessingService.cs:375-394`, used at `:620-623`), `PfxSigningKeyProvider`, and `PdfSigningOptions.PfxPath` / `PfxPassword` are gone; "no resolvable certificate" becomes an explicit refusal in the service carrying a **verbatim message constant**; and the `PdfSigning` block is removed from `ssd/appsettings.json` and from CLAUDE.md's *PDF Processing and Digital Signatures* section, so the configuration stops documenting a capability that does not exist.
* **If made to work:** the PFX is loaded at startup — fail fast on a bad path or password when `DeployMode` is `live`, log and disable the fallback otherwise — and `LoadFromPkcs12` acquires its caller.
* Either way, **the fallback branch cannot yield a null chain**, asserted directly rather than inferred from the fact that nothing reaches it today.
* The reason it is currently dormant stays true or is restated: `Sign.SignDoc` redirects to certificate selection when none is chosen (`Sign.cs:179-373`), and the Flow engine pauses on a missing organisation certificate (`docs/flow-design.md` decision 6). If either of those changes, the fallback becomes live — note that dependency.
* No PFX password value appears in any log line, error message, test name or assertion output. The key is named (`PdfSigning:PfxPassword`) and its location stated; the value is not read in the course of this work.

**Why a Playwright journey does not apply, and what replaces it.** There is **no live path that reaches the fallback** — that is the ticket's own finding, and it is why the null chain has never been observed. A browser journey therefore cannot exercise the branch at all, and a spec that tried would be asserting the two guards in front of it (certificate selection, the Flow pause), not this code. The demonstrating tests are **xUnit**, in `tests/ssd.UnitTests`:

1. the resolver invoked with **no** personal and **no** organisation certificate: under the remove branch it returns the explicit refusal carrying the message constant, and `PfxSigningKeyProvider` no longer exists to be called; under the implement branch it returns a loaded chain. Either way it **never returns null** — red on today's code, where the fallback hands back an unloaded provider;
2. a source/dead-code contract that `LoadFromPkcs12` either has a caller in `ssd/` or is absent — so this cannot silently return (`knip` covers the TypeScript side only, so this needs an xUnit assertion);
3. under the implement branch: startup with a bad `PfxPath` under `DeployMode=live` fails fast; the same under a non-live mode logs and leaves the fallback disabled rather than half-loaded;
4. under the remove branch: a contract that the `PdfSigning` section is absent from `ssd/appsettings.json` and from every deployment template, so the dead configuration cannot be reintroduced;
5. **controls (green today, must stay green):** signing with a resolvable **personal** certificate and with a resolvable **organisation** certificate are unchanged, and `Sign.SignDoc` still redirects to certificate selection when none is chosen. The existing `SigningKeyProtectorTests` stay green.

The one journey-level control worth keeping is the existing `systemTest/tests/functional/sign_form.spec.ts` and `person_certificate_manage.spec.ts` passing unchanged — evidence that the two guards in front of the fallback still behave as before, not evidence about the fallback itself.

title: Upload validates the file extension only — no MIME / content sniff, so any bytes named *.pdf are stored and served as application/pdf
description:
## Finding (SDK Phase 0 assessment, [PS-971](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-971/sdk-phase-0-architecture-and-functional-definition-technical-marketing) §13 finding 3, SSP develop @ `1800ab3`)

*Terms: the SSP is the Secuura Services Provider (*`platform-s` */* `obeden-ssd`*); the SBCM is the Secuura Block Chain Manager (*`platform-k`*). Identifiers, routes and paths are quoted as the code has them.*

On the SSP, `DocumentUploadService.StageUploadAsync` decides whether a file is acceptable from `Path.GetExtension(file.FileName)` against the allow-list (`.txt .pdf .doc .docx .xls .xlsx .gif .jpg .jpeg .png`) and the 5 MB cap (`ssd/Services/DocumentStorage/DocumentUploadService.cs:82-86`; the list at `ssd/Controllers/MyDocuments.cs:191-192`). **Nothing inspects the content.** The MIME type used on download is derived from the same extension (`Helpers.ResolveMime`, `ssd/Helpers.cs:353-367`).

Consequences:

* A file whose bytes are not what the extension says is stored, and later served with the extension's content type — to a share recipient, through the Outlook add-in (`GET /api/outlook/documents/{id}/content`) and through the in-app viewer.
* The password-protected-PDF probe and the watermark / sign paths assume a `.pdf` *is* a PDF; iText failures surface late and as generic errors rather than as a validation refusal at register time.
* Every future caller (the SDK API's `documents.register`, `POST /api/outlook/documents/upload`) inherits the gap unless it is closed once, in the service.

## Proposed

* In `StageUploadAsync`, after the extension check, sniff the leading bytes (PDF `%PDF-`, OOXML / OLE2 zip and CFB magic for Office types, the image magics) and refuse a mismatch with a new `UploadError.ContentMismatch` and a plain message; treat `.txt` as "must be valid UTF-8 / ASCII text".
* Store the sniffed type beside the extension so `ResolveMime` can prefer it.
* xUnit: one fixture per allowed extension with matching and mismatched bytes; the mismatch cases must be red before the change.
* Both testing HTML docs: the Documents area gains "content sniff on register".

## Effect on the SDK

`docs/sdk/SDK-ARCHITECTURE.md` §12 says the SDK API should sniff and refuse mismatches as `validation` before staging; the right place is this service so every surface of the SSP benefits.

## Acceptance

* `StageUploadAsync` refuses a file whose leading bytes do not match its extension with a new `UploadError.ContentMismatch` and a plain message, for every extension on the allow-list (`.txt .pdf .doc .docx .xls .xlsx .gif .jpg .jpeg .png`) — not only `.pdf`.
* A `.txt` whose bytes are not valid UTF-8 / ASCII text is refused by the same path.
* The sniffed type is stored beside the extension and `Helpers.ResolveMime` prefers it, so a download's content type can no longer be driven by a renamed file.
* The refusal lives in the service, so `POST /api/outlook/documents/upload`, `GET /api/outlook/documents/{id}/content` and the SDK's `documents.register` inherit it without a second check.
* xUnit: one fixture per allowed extension with matching and mismatched bytes; the mismatch cases are red before the change.
* Both testing HTML docs gain "content sniff on register" under the Documents area.

**Playwright test that demonstrates the fix** (required): extend `systemTest/tests/functional/upload.spec.ts`. The surface is part of the subject here — the refusal has to reach the person who dropped the file, not only the service. Against a live stack, signed in as the seeded AccountAdmin, it must:

1. attach a file named `<runId>-fake.pdf` whose bytes are plain text (no `%PDF-` header) to `upload-file-input`, submit with `upload-submit-btn`, and assert the row in `upload-queue-root` reports a content-mismatch refusal **and** that no document of that name appears in `mydocs-table` — **this is the assertion that fails on today's** `develop`, where those bytes are accepted, stored, and later served as `application/pdf`;
2. repeat for a file named `<runId>-fake.docx` carrying PDF bytes, so the check is not hard-coded to the PDF magic;
3. **control (passes today and must keep passing):** a genuine PDF uploaded under a unique name is accepted, appears in `mydocs-table` and opens in the viewer — the sniff must not begin refusing real files;
4. **control:** a disallowed extension is still refused by the existing extension check with the existing wording, so `ContentMismatch` does not displace the message people already see.

It deletes every document it creates ([PS-806](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-806/systemtest-specs-leave-uploaded-documents-behind-non-pdf-document)). The xUnit fixtures stay the primary pin for the per-extension magic table; this spec exists because a mismatch must surface as a validation refusal at register time rather than as a late iText error.

nodes.body:
**Test classification (systemTest) for the 13 Oct evidence above**

| | |
| -- | -- |
| Area | `@area-documents` |
| Feature | `@upload` |
| Type | `@validation`, `@bva` (empty / damaged / not-a-PDF / no-extension) |
| Roles | every role that can register: `@role-power`, `@role-user`, `@role-account-admin`, `@role-issuer`, `@role-admin` (the Registration user too) |
| Core smoke | no |

**Acceptance:** a file named `*.pdf` whose bytes are not a PDF is refused on Register with a sentence in the damaged-PDF message's voice, and nothing is stored. The empty and damaged cases keep their current messages (controls). If such a file does exist (registered before the fix), View says it can't show it, and Certify, Watermark and Sign are not offered.

**Still reproduces on `develop` bb92be69 (slot 3, 13 Oct 2026 ~15:30 UTC, UI only), and here is what the user sees now.** The damaged-PDF check from #963 (Phase 14) catches a real but broken PDF, but **not a file that isn't a PDF at all**.

Register, as `e2e-power@e2e.invalid`, three files side by side:

| File | Content | Register result |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `malformed-….pdf` | the `fixtures/malformed_pages_array.pdf` bytes | ❌ "This PDF is damaged and can't be registered. Try re-saving it from your PDF tool." ✓ |
| `empty-….pdf` | 0 bytes | ❌ "This file is empty (0 bytes), so there is nothing to register." ✓ |
| `not-really-….pdf` | 34 bytes of plain text | ✅ **"Done"**, listed as a Registered document |

For the plain-text "PDF" afterwards:
* **View** opens the PDF viewer on a blank page reading "Page 1/?", with an "Unable to load PDF." toast (the console shows `InvalidPDFException`).
* **Certify**, plus Watermark and Sign in the Actions menu, are all still offered, and Certify starts ("Not started · Certify"). That is PS-1030's shape: an operation offered on a file it can never complete.

Suggested acceptance addition: Register refuses a file whose bytes don't start with `%PDF-` when its extension is `.pdf`, in the same voice as the damaged-PDF message ("This file is named .pdf but isn't a PDF…"). Checked before posting: no open PR or branch mentions PS-974.

title: The subscription document allowance is enforced nowhere — upload, declare, sign and share never check the tier; the portal's usage figure is a plain document count
description:
## Finding (SDK Phase 0 assessment, [PS-971](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-971/sdk-phase-0-architecture-and-functional-definition-technical-marketing) §13 finding 2, SSP develop @ `1800ab3`)

*Terms: the SSP is the Secuura Services Provider (*`platform-s` */* `obeden-ssd`*); the SBCM is the Secuura Block Chain Manager (*`platform-k`*). Identifiers, routes and paths are quoted as the code has them.*

The commercial metric — protected documents per subscription year (Professional 5,000, Business 50,000, Enterprise fair use; Free 10, internal only; `ssd/S2Constants.cs:289-307`) — is **not enforced anywhere** on the SSP:

* Upload (`MyDocuments.MDImportFileUpload`), declare (`CertifyController.Confirm`), sign (`Sign.SignDoc`) and share (`Senddocs.Create`) never read the tier or an allowance.
* The portal's "protected documents this year" is the count of stored, non-deleted documents, explicitly a placeholder pending [PS-283](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-283/enforce-annual-verified-document-allowance-tier-top-ups) (`ssd/Controllers/StripeController.cs:1060-1080`).
* The `SsdSubscription == Subscribed` gate on the people/settings pages is not a paid gate: loading `/Welcome` flips the flag (`ssd/Controllers/HomeController.cs:299-300`).

## Existing specification

[PS-283](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-283/enforce-annual-verified-document-allowance-tier-top-ups) — *Enforce annual verified-document allowance (tier + top-ups)* — already specifies the fix (resolver for tier + remaining allowance, subscription-year window, enforce at certify, consume `TopUpCredit`, real usage panel, activate `tier_document_limit.spec.ts`). It is in Backlog but was **archived on 2026-08-12**, so it takes no comments or relations and is invisible in the project views. It is blocked by [PS-384](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-384/ps-380-phase-1-re-pricing-core-constants-schema-seed-sync) (allowance constants + `TopUpCredit` schema).

This ticket exists so the gap is visible. **Resolution is either to unarchive** [PS-283](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-283/enforce-annual-verified-document-allowance-tier-top-ups) **and do it there, or to carry its body here** — not to write a second design. Do not duplicate the work.

## Effect on the SDK

The SDK API adds no gate of its own (decision 3 in `docs/sdk/SDK-ARCHITECTURE.md`: no behaviour the SSP does not have). It returns `details.allowance` on receipts so an app can show usage. Open question §15.6 asks whether the SDK API should be the first surface to enforce, or whether the web UI goes first.

## Acceptance

**First, the routing decision — this ticket must not grow a second design.** Either [PS-283](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-283/enforce-annual-verified-document-allowance-tier-top-ups) is unarchived and the work happens there (in which case this ticket closes with that recorded, and nothing below applies here), or [PS-283](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-283/enforce-annual-verified-document-allowance-tier-top-ups)'s body is carried across to this ticket. State which, here, before any code. [PS-283](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-283/enforce-annual-verified-document-allowance-tier-top-ups) is also blocked by [PS-384](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-384/ps-380-phase-1-re-pricing-core-constants-schema-seed-sync) (allowance constants + `TopUpCredit` schema), so that sequencing is part of the decision.

If the work lands here, done means:

* A resolver returns, for an organisation, its tier and its **remaining** allowance over the subscription-year window — not a count of stored documents.
* Enforcement happens at **certify**, as [PS-283](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-283/enforce-annual-verified-document-allowance-tier-top-ups) specifies, with `TopUpCredit` consumed before a refusal.
* The portal's "protected documents this year" reads the real usage figure, replacing the placeholder at `StripeController.cs:1060-1080`.
* The constants in `S2Constants.cs:289-307` (Professional 5,000, Business 50,000, Enterprise fair use, Free 10) are the single source for the limits — no second copy.
* The non-paid `SsdSubscription == Subscribed` gate is left alone or fixed on its own ticket: `/Welcome` flipping the flag (`HomeController.cs:299-300`) is a separate defect and must not be conflated with allowance enforcement.
* xUnit for the resolver and the certify gate: at the limit, one over, with a top-up available, across a year boundary, and Enterprise (fair use — pin whatever "unlimited" resolves to rather than leaving it implicit).

**Playwright test that demonstrates the fix** (required): **activate** `systemTest/tests/functional/tier_document_limit.spec.ts`. That file already exists and is named in [PS-283](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-283/enforce-annual-verified-document-allowance-tier-top-ups)'s own plan as something to switch on — it is the pre-built home for this, so no new spec is needed. Against a live stack:

1. for an organisation on a tier whose allowance the test can reach, certify documents up to the limit and assert the last one succeeds; then certify one more and assert it is **refused with a message naming the allowance** — **this is the assertion that fails on today's** `develop`, where certify never reads the tier and the (N+1)th document is protected like any other;
2. assert the Subscription portal's usage figure matches the number actually certified in the window, not the count of stored documents — the two diverge as soon as the test deletes one, which is the cheapest way to show the placeholder is gone;
3. with a `TopUpCredit` present, the refused certify now succeeds and the credit is consumed — so the top-up path is exercised, not just the ceiling;
4. **controls (pass today and must keep passing):** upload, declare, sign and share of a document **within** allowance are unchanged in behaviour; and a Free-tier organisation can still do everything it can do today up to 10 — the gate must not start refusing work that is inside the entitlement.

A tier whose allowance is 5,000 is not reachable in a journey, so the spec must drive a seeded low-allowance tier (Free, 10) or a test-only allowance override, and say in a comment which it is — asserting a 5,000-document boundary through a browser would be dishonest about what was measured.

*Scope flag: this ticket is explicitly a visibility record for a gap whose design lives on an archived ticket. If the answer to the routing decision is "unarchive* [PS-283](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-283/enforce-annual-verified-document-allowance-tier-top-ups)*", the acceptance above is* [PS-283](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-283/enforce-annual-verified-document-allowance-tier-top-ups)*'s, not this one's.*

title: PR #1339's standalone locks were re-resolved from bare manifests: ~1,000 non-target moves, incl. runtime bullmq/msgpackr 2 and @azure/identity/msal-node 6
description:
Raised from **gate41's finding N-1339-2** (Major, non-blocking) on PR #1339 (KS-1378, the four-package advisory bump). Wednesday ruled this a ticket rather than a fold-in for round 2, because the only mechanism the gate's own fix-shape offers is `npm install --package-lock-only`, and host npm 11.5.1 dies with `Cannot read properties of null (reading 'edgesOut')` on this machine — measured by Seat B 43rd even on a bare `package.json` in an empty temp dir, so it is the host npm build and not the workspace layout.

## What happened

#1339's 13 standalone `package-lock.json` files were regenerated **from their bare manifests** rather than from their committed locks. That resolved every dependency afresh, so about **1,000 versions moved that the bump did not target**. All are inside their declared ranges, so nothing is a range violation — but nothing exercises them either: the suites run from the **root** lock, which moved **0** non-target versions.

## The moves that matter (gate-measured)

* `services/queue`: **bullmq 5.76.2 → 5.81.5**, pulling **msgpackr 1 → 2** — runtime.
* `services/m365-integration` and `packages/shared`: **@azure/identity 4.13.1 → 4.13.3**, pulling **@azure/msal-node 5 → 6** — runtime.
* `services/originate`: minimatch 3 → 10, plus dev-only eslint-cache majors.

## Fix-shape, quoted verbatim from gate41's report

> Fix-shape: regenerate each standalone lock FROM its committed lock (`npm install <pkg>@<ver> --package-lock-only`), or declare the drift and add a standalone-install smoke (build + boot) per service.

## The condition attached to #1339 merging without this

Wednesday's ANSWER to Seat B 44th, 2026-09-29T03:54:40Z: the two runtime moves above **get a clean standalone** `npm ci` **plus that service's own suite in the next gate**, so what ships untested by the root-lock suites is tested once. **Merged is not deployed:** no deploy carries these until this ticket is done or Kam says otherwise.

## Blocked on, and why it is not just "run the command"

`npm install` in any form is unavailable on this host. Seat B 43rd's workaround for #1339 was `node:24-alpine` (npm 11.19.0), mounted at `/src` — **never** `/dev`, which clobbers the container's `/dev/null` and dies rc 127 before starting. Whoever takes this needs either that container route explicitly permitted, or a working host npm.

## Neighbours (cross-reference only)

KS-1290 (an npm command inside a workspace member moves platform discriminators silently) and KS-1154 (the root lock carries only the darwin rollup binary) are the same family — lockfile regeneration doing more than it was asked to — but neither covers this drift.

Discovered 2026-09-29 by gate41 on PR #1339; ticketed by the Platform K build seat under Wednesday's ruling.

title: validate route follow-ups from the KS-1370 gate: usage_count lost update, a cache-miss read fault mislabelled, and D1 pins no write
description:
Three gate40 findings on the merged KS-1370 change (#1338, squash `8af6ab8216007462e596daed6b0adcd1e87e34ee`). One logical path: the `POST /api/keys/validate` route in `services/security`. Each item is copied verbatim from the gate40 report (`2026-09-29-batch1338-g40/report.md`, sha256 prefix `372924904c1f`). Facts only; none of the three blocks anything that shipped.

- [ ] **N-1338-3 (Minor, TICKET — MEASURED AT RUNTIME; LOST-UPDATE-CANDIDATE):** the seat's "`usage_count` written from a stale copy is a lost update" is **narrowed by half (ii) but not closed**. Two processes validating one key in sequence (B, B2, B, B2): **head 0 → 4 (exact); base 0 → 2 (the stale-copy loss)**. Twenty CONCURRENT validates (10 on each process): **head 0 → 12 (run 1: 11); base 0 → 9 (run 1: 10)**. The remaining loss is a read-modify-write race: `usage_count = $3` is written from a value read one statement earlier. Fix-shape: `SET usage_count = usage_count + 1, last_used_at = GREATEST(last_used_at, $2)`. Regression cell: two instances × N concurrent validates on the real DB, asserting usage_count == N. Usage is telemetry, not an auth decision, so this is a ticket, not a block.
- [ ] **N-1338-4 (Minor, TICKET — MEASURED AT RUNTIME; pre-existing, unchanged by this PR):** a failed read on a cache MISS answers **200** `valid:false, 'Key not found'` (plus a warn line). The same fault on a cache HIT now answers **503**. Both are refused, and through the gateway both become a 30 s cached 401, so this is **coherent with "A revoked key is never honoured"**. But the miss branch mislabels a database fault as an unknown key, and auth's connector-token returns 401 there instead of 502. Fix-shape: give the cache-miss branch the same 503 on a failed read (a product decision; outside card-2's scope). Cell: miss + read fault → 503.
- [ ] **N-1338-5 (Minor, TICKET — PROBED; NOT-PINNED):** D1 asserts the answer and the eviction but **not that no write was issued**. The base's vanished-row RESURRECTION therefore has no cell. The head prevents it structurally (early return), but nothing pins that. Cell: in D1, assert the mock recorded no INSERT/UPDATE (`state.usageSql.length === 0`).

Adjacent, not duplicated: KS 1174 covers the gateway collapsing every API-key failure into 401, which is the gateway half of N-1338-4's symptom, not the security route's miss branch.

Refs KS-1370

## MERGED as `af788a4c8be68f9f1f452a4c211b6a150573cd5a` — and the gate CORRECTED my residue reading

[#1602](https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/1602) merged on gate Q1's GO WITH NOTE, five-point 5/5, landed tree equal to its prediction. `Refs`, so this ticket stays open.

**The gate measured the thing nobody had measured.** On its own PostgreSQL 18.3: **every `GREATEST`/NULL arm behaves correctly**, and **20 clients × 25 uses give 500 of 500** with the new statement against **31 of 500** with develop's. My own evidence could not include that — this box has no PostgreSQL and the Docker daemon is down — and the PR said so plainly rather than implying coverage. The drafter's earlier 20-client figure was *carried*; the gate's is *measured*.

## My residue reading was wrong in three ways. The gate's is the one to keep.

I posted earlier that the shared upsert clobbers on **mint, revoke and rotate**, and that `:1494` **widens** the row-versus-API divergence. Corrected:

1. **The `usage_count = EXCLUDED.usage_count` overwrite (`:425`, value at `:436`) fires on REVOKE ONLY.** Mint and rotate insert **fresh ids**, so there is nothing to overwrite. And revoke **reads the row fresh at `:518`** — so what is lost is only the uses **between that read and the save**, not the accumulated count. My reading overstated both the scope and the size.
2. **That same overwrite also moves `last_used_at` BACKWARDS** — which neither I nor Wednesday had named, and which is the more interesting half, because the new statement's `GREATEST` exists precisely to stop that happening on the validate path.
3. **`:1494` serves the SAME number as before.** Only the stored row changed, and it is now correct. **My "this widens the divergence" claim is withdrawn** — it is in the landed commit message as withdrawn, so the record does not carry it.

**What stands from my reading:** the in-memory count is still written back by that upsert on the revoke path, and dropping `usage_count` from its DO UPDATE list is **not** available as a remedy — for the reason the comment at `:479-483` gives for `is_active`: revoke persists *through* that upsert and the KS-764 call-site guard pins that shape. The shapes that would work remain `usage_count = GREATEST(svc_api_keys.usage_count, EXCLUDED.usage_count)`, or not carrying the column in the DO UPDATE list at all — each needing its own cell and call-site guard.

**So this ticket's remaining work, as measured rather than as I first described it:** the revoke-path window at `:425`/`:436`, including the backwards `last_used_at`, with a cell.

---

*Seat R 51st, 2026-10-19. I am recording the correction rather than quietly replacing my earlier comment, because the earlier reading is already in this thread and a reader needs to know which one survived measurement. Nothing deployed.*

## RAISED as #1602 — and two residue sites this PR deliberately does not touch

**[#1602](https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/1602)**, head `70dc59643b5aaa089606e51a43d2948ab5c671b2`, `Refs` (not a close-link), tier 1, at gate. `services/security/src/index.ts:499` becomes `SET last_used_at = GREATEST(last_used_at, $2), usage_count = usage_count + 1` and the params drop `k.usageCount`, so the increment happens in the database. Red-first put exactly the new W3 cell red against develop's product file with the other 9 green; `services/security` 347/347 after (develop's 346 + 1); tsc 0; ESLint 0 against a stdin probe reading 1.

**This ticket stays open.** Two sites still read the process-local count, and neither is in #1602.

## Residue 1 — the shared upsert writes the process-local count straight back

`apiKeyInsertStatement` (`services/security/src/index.ts:421-437`) sets `usage_count = EXCLUDED.usage_count` at **`:425`**, with `k.usageCount` as the value at **`:436`**. That statement is the one `dbSaveApiKey` uses for **mint and revoke**, and the KS-1549 **rotate** transaction uses it too.

So after #1602: 20 concurrent validates correctly leave the row at 20, and then **the next revoke or rotate writes that process's own count over it** — perhaps 3 — and the 20 is gone. #1602 does not remove the lost update; it **narrows it from the hot path to a rare one**. That is a real improvement, and it is also why "the count lives in the database" is true of validate's writes rather than of the key's lifetime.

**Dropping `usage_count` from that upsert is NOT available as the fix**, for exactly the reason the comment at **`:479-483`** gives for `is_active`: the revoke route persists its revoke *through* that same upsert (`apiKey.isActive = false` then `dbSaveApiKey(apiKey, { rethrow: true })`), and the KS-764 call-site guard pins that shape. Removing the column from the DO UPDATE list would be the same mistake one field over.

The shapes that would work, neither of them a one-liner:
- `usage_count = GREATEST(svc_api_keys.usage_count, EXCLUDED.usage_count)` — monotonic, so a stale in-memory copy can no longer lower the stored count; or
- stop carrying `usage_count` in the DO UPDATE list at all, and let only the usage statement move it — which needs a guard proving mint still seeds it and revoke still persists.

Either wants its own cell and its own call-site guard. **Not in #1602.**

## Residue 2 — the API serves the count from memory, so #1602 WIDENS the visible divergence

`index.ts:1494` maps `usageCount: k.usageCount` into the key-list response out of `memApiKeys`, never from the row.

Before #1602 the row and the response were wrong *together* — both process-local. After it the **row is right** (it counts every process's uses) and the **response still counts this one's**. So anyone comparing the admin key list against `svc_api_keys` will now see a mismatch that did not exist before.

**That is not a regression #1602 introduces** — it is a pre-existing memory-first read becoming visible because the row is finally correct. It is called out in the PR body in one line for exactly that reason, so nobody reads the mismatch as new breakage. The fix is to read the count from the row on that route, which is again a separate change.

## One thing in this ticket's brief that nobody has measured

`GREATEST` ignoring NULLs — a first use with `last_used_at` NULL, and a NULL `$2` against a stored value — **is measured by nobody so far**, and the PR body says so plainly rather than implying otherwise. This seat has no PostgreSQL (`psql`, `pg_ctl`, `postgres`, `initdb` all absent) and the Docker daemon is not running; starting it was ruled against, as a host-level change under two other live sessions. The drafter's concurrency figure — 20 concurrent clients leaving `usage_count` at 20 with the new statement and 1 with the old, on PostgreSQL 18.3 — is **carried from the SCREEN_11 report, re-run by nobody.** The tier-1 gate measures both arms on its own scratch PostgreSQL.

---

*Seat R 51st, 2026-10-19. Both residue sites were found while answering the gate's own question about whether anything still reads the in-memory count; they are source reads at develop `37834600a543cb0276f427d969ac034d9df74fbd`, not inferences. Nothing deployed.*

title: Security: certifications ends RLS FORCE with no tenant_isolation policy on every fresh database, permanently
description:
**Found by the gate39 QA pass over PR #1332 (N-G39-1, Major). Facts only.**

## What is wrong

On a **fresh bare database**, `public.certifications` ends with row-level security **ENABLED and FORCED but with no** `tenant_isolation` **policy**. RLS with no policy is **default-deny**, so the table is unreadable and unwritable by the application role — and unlike the defect #1332 fixed, **this does not heal on a later boot**. It is permanent for the life of that database.

Measured across all four head paths (gateway runner boot 1 and boot 2, `scripts/run-migrations.sh`, and both combined): identical, `4c59e2ebdc37`. The **merge-base differs** (`fd91b0ab5a48`) and **does** carry `CREATE POLICY tenant_isolation ON public.certifications` — so the merge-base heals it and the current tip does not. An app-role `INSERT` carrying the tenant GUC is **refused**.

## Why it changed

`migrations/038a_ks1054_core_tables_before_039.sql` (added in #1332) creates `certifications` **before** 039 runs. 039 then finds the table present and applies its RLS `ENABLE`/`FORCE` block to it — but the branch of 039 that creates the `tenant_isolation` policy does not cover it on that path. Before #1332, `certifications` did not exist when 039 ran, so 039 skipped it entirely and a later boot created it with its policy intact.

## A FALSE CLAIM IN THE MERGED CODE, filed here deliberately rather than separately (N-G39-4)

`038a_ks1054_core_tables_before_039.sql` lines **16-17** describe this exact condition — `certifications` with RLS forced and no `tenant_isolation` policy — as one of the things the migration **fixes**. **It does not fix it; it is the cause of it.** The same header's claim that the schema equality is "proved … across … the docker/init seeded path" is also **wider than true**: the equality holds for `certifications` only, and fails for `oauth_apps` and `svc_webhooks` because of a pre-existing docker/init DDL difference (extra indexes and the `svc_webhooks_app_id_fkey` foreign key). Both header claims need correcting in the same change that fixes the policy, so the file does not keep asserting a fix it does not deliver.

## Fix shape (from the gate)

A migration numbered **after 039** that applies 039's `tenant_isolation` block to `certifications`, plus a **real-PostgreSQL cell driven as the application role** (`secuura_app`) asserting that an `INSERT` carrying the correct tenant GUC succeeds and one carrying a foreign tenant is refused. A source-text assertion is not sufficient here: the defect is a runtime default-deny, and only a driven app-role probe distinguishes "policy present" from "policy absent but table reachable as owner".

## Scope

Not fixed in #1332 — that PR was round 2 of 2 under the class cap and shipped GO WITH FINDINGS with this as named residue. No board ticket covered it before this one (searched by symbol: `certifications` + `tenant_isolation`, `tenant_isolation policy certifications`, `038a`, `certifications RLS force default-deny`, `certifications no tenant_isolation` — zero title-relevant results; three positive controls each returned their expected ticket first, so the search was working).

Refs KS-1054

title: Security: a revoked credential resubmitted with any other id verifies TRUE — neither verify route wires a didResolver, so the proof's id binding is never checked outside production
description:
**BLUF — the gate measured this at runtime on the merged code (gate38 finding N-1330-1, Major). A credential revoked through** `POST /api/credentials/:id/revoke`**, resubmitted with any other** `id`**, answers** `verified: true` **with** `checks.status: true`**.** Measured at the PR head and at the merged END.

This is not a defect of #1330 against its ruling — an edited id *is* an unknown id, and pass-through for unknown ids is the open card's default. It is filed because the measured cost of that default is **wider than the card prices it**.

**The mechanism, as the gate read and drove it:**

* Both revocation resolvers key on the caller-supplied `credential.id`, and the stored-record arm abstains on `found: false` (`services/vc-issuer/src/services/revocationResolvers.ts`; `packages/shared/src/vc/verifier.ts` :478-:484).
* **Neither verify route wires a** `didResolver`, so an Ed25519 proof gets a structural check only unless `NODE_ENV === 'production'` (`verifier.ts` :372-:396, read).
* The proof payload **does** cover `id`, so a wired didResolver would catch the edit.
* In production every Ed25519 credential already fails with `No DID resolver configured…` (pre-existing, read, not driven).

**Why it matters more than the card says.** The card `secuura-ks1352-unknown-credential-id-verify-policy` (open, `ruled_ts` null) prices its option a as "a revoked credential whose record was lost still verifies true" — an accident. The measured behaviour is deliberate and trivial: **any holder of a revoked credential can un-revoke it on a development-mode stack by editing one field.**

**Fix-shape (the gate's, quoted):** "wire the issuer's DID resolver on both verify routes so the proof binds `id` (then an edited id fails signature), or key revocation on a proof-bound value."

**Regression cell (the gate's, quoted):** "revoke R1, submit `{...doc, id: 'urn:x'}`, expect `verified: false`."

**Relation to the shipped work.** #1330 (squash `9caa42ad05f145251db820ba43eaf7941316668f`) is what makes revocation reachable at all; before it, verify consulted no authority. This finding is the remaining hole in the id-keyed approach. The unknown-id policy question itself is KS 1368; this ticket is the measured cost that should inform it.

**Board search before filing, with controls:** `didResolver`, `revocationResolvers`, `id-edit`, `edited id`, `No DID resolver` all returned **0**; the positive control `statusListResolver` on the same literal query shape returned **1** (KS-1352), and a nonsense control returned 0.
