**BLUF:** KS-1383 is a duplicate of this ticket and is being closed on that ground: same root cause (neither verify route wires a didResolver, so the proof never binds the credential id) and the same fix shape. Its content is carried here in full so nothing is lost with it. The facts this ticket did not hold: a revoked credential resubmitted with another LIVE credential's id also verifies true on both verify routes, and a forged subject also verifies. Both come from gate43's finding N-1341-1 (Major, not blocking). This comment changes no state or priority on KS-1375.

What KS-1383 held, in full:
* Credential verification is not bound to the credential's own proof. A revoked credential resubmitted carrying another live credential's id verifies true on both verify routes. A forged subject also verifies. Pre-existing: it reproduces at the merged head of PR 1341 and at develop before it.
* No DID resolver is wired, so the proof is not validated on these routes (structurally checked only, outside production). PR 1341's fail-closed change covers ids that no authority holds, which is why it is partial against its ruling's phrase "closes the id-edit trick": an id that is held by a live credential is not an unknown id.
* Provenance: the ruling card for the unknown-id policy said a separate proof-binding ticket (wire the issuer's DID resolver) was coming and goes ahead either way. KS-1383 searched the board by symbol and found it was never filed; the only match for didResolver was this ticket. Adjacent but not this: KS-624 (prism issues VCs with random bytes as the proof), KS-625 (presentations verify never checks the holder signature), KS-627 (wallet CIP-8 and COSE verification).
* Not measured: the production path was not driven (the vc-issuer app refuses to boot without DATABASE_URL and PRISM_AGENT_URL), so the finding is measured on the structural path only. The fix shape was left blank on purpose: it needs a decision on where the resolver lives and what it costs a stack with no network to an issuer's DID document.

Evidence, in full. Gate43 (the batch of PRs 1341 to 1345), finding N-1341-1, Major, not blocking. Report: `/Volumes/DevMASTER/!CODING/Testing Agent MAIN/projects/secuura/reports/2026-09-29-batch1341-g43/report.md`, lines 8, 53, 405, 425 and 440. Probe output, all under `/Volumes/DevMASTER/!CODING/Testing Agent MAIN/projects/secuura/reports/2026-09-29-batch1341-g43/evidence/`: `07_probe1341_P1341_idswap.stdout` and `07_probe1341_P1341_idswap.stderr`; `07_probe1341_RBDEV_idswap.stdout` and `07_probe1341_RBDEV_idswap.stderr`; `07_probe1341_P1341_idswap_prod.stdout` and `07_probe1341_P1341_idswap_prod.stderr`. In the first probe's stdout the revoked credential reads verified false, and the credential carrying another live credential's id reads verified true twice.

**BLUF:** Our QA gate 273 measured the mechanism this ticket names: on develop `93028c8151ec`, with the config the two vc-issuer verify routes pass (no DID resolver), a structurally valid credential with ANY proofValue that starts with `z` verifies `verified: true` when NODE_ENV is not `production`. Wednesday ruled it High; gate 273 found it while reviewing PR 2108 (KS-1973), and it is not caused by that PR. This ticket already carries the same root cause; this comment adds the measurement and the open question.

What the gate measured, verbatim: "Context, pre-existing and NOT this PR's (identical on develop, measured): with that production-shaped config, a structurally valid credential with any `z…` proofValue verifies `verified:true` when NODE_ENV ≠ production (:413-418 pass-through)." The gate's line numbers are at PR 2108's head.

READ ONLY by the board seat, at develop `93028c8151ec`, `Blockchain/Dev/packages/shared/src/vc/verifier.ts`: a proof value starting `zDEV_` or `zHMAC_` has its own branch (lines 355 and 364); any other `z` value takes the Ed25519 branch at line 383; with `didResolver` unset the `else` at line 407 runs, and only `process.env.NODE_ENV === 'production'` adds an error (lines 410 to 412). The constructor (lines 90 to 96) sets only `checkStatus`, `checkExpiration` and `checkBlockchain`.

UNMEASURED: whether any running box runs the vc-issuer or the verifier with NODE_ENV not `production`. A read-only check of NODE_ENV on those services on Kintsugi AND on the demo is owed to the next deploy seat; the board seat read no box. A prior reading exists on KS-658: 26 of 26 Node services on the live demo VM had NODE_ENV=development, measured 2026-08-17 and not re-read since, so it may be stale. Also UNMEASURED here: whether a forgery would also need an id with a stored, unrevoked record (PR 1341 made the routes fail closed on an unknown id; KS-1975 says the revocation resolvers behave that way).

Related: KS-1975 (the `zDEV_` default key, and gate 177's forged Ed25519-form proof measurement), KS-1522 (production refuses every Ed25519 credential, a decision), KS-1383, KS-658, KS-1973 (PR 2108).

Delivered: PR 1341 merged as dcaf22533 on develop (verify fails closed when no authority holds a record for the id), in the kintsugi deploy b1fb543640e7 (2026-11-01). Verified by git log (the squash names KS-1375 and is reachable from b1fb543640e7); the behaviour was not run here. Left open: the ticket's merge comment says a live sweep against a running environment is still owed and the ticket stays open, and that the change is partial against "closes the id-edit trick": a revoked credential resubmitted with another live credential's id still verifies true, which is carried by KS-1383 (Backlog); production verification with no DID resolver is KS-1522 (Backlog). A live sweep needs credentials issued and revoked on the box, which is not a read-only probe.

Merged to `develop` as PR #1341, squash `dcaf22533400c09fa32527fef9723d3404d8b426`, tree `27e89a1dc1b0`. Verified at source: develop equals the squash by ls-remote, the commits API reports that tree, and a contents-API blob read on each changed path equals the head's blob. The landed subject is within the 92-character limit.

QA recorded one Major finding that does not block this merge: a revoked credential resubmitted with ANOTHER LIVE credential's id still verifies true on both verify routes, at this head and at develop (pre-existing — the proof is not verified on these routes, as no DID resolver is wired). Fail-closed covers ids no authority holds, so the change is partial against 'closes the id-edit trick'. A separate ticket carries the proof-binding work.

This changes runtime code, so a live sweep against a running environment is still owed and this ticket stays open. Nothing was deployed by the merge.

title: Akto scans are now paced to fit the platform's rate limit — test times went up; which way should we go?
description:
## BLUF

Kamil, when you have a moment: **we need your decision on how the platform's rate limit should treat our Akto scans.** To stop 429s being counted as passes, the scans are now slowed to 1,500 requests/min using Akto's own rate limit (systemTest only, no platform code changed). Coverage is honest, but **pre-merge went from 47 s to 19 m 28 s, and the security tier now takes about an hour.** Six options are below, most of them gateway-side, which is yours. Once we've agreed one, either of us can make the change. **Reducing test coverage is not an option.** Thank you.

+++ What was added, and what it costs (measured)

**The pacing** ([KS-1286](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1286/akto-image-2222-2356-latest-paired-local-pair-verified-2026-09-28-and) branch; [KS-709](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-709/akto-reports-a-pass-for-a-test-that-executed-nothing-clean-0-not) for the false passes it fixes)

* Akto reads a per-account `globalRateLimit` from its Mongo once a minute. `systemTest/akto/tests/tierPacingSetup.ts` sets it per tier: **pr unthrottled; pre-merge and security at 1,500/min** (0.75 × the platform's 2,000/min, derived in `src/setup/aktoRateLimit.ts`), restored to unthrottled afterwards. `AKTO_GLOBAL_RATE_LIMIT=N` overrides it.
* Before any setup login, the harness also waits (≤61 s, probing `GET /api/auth/me`) for the 60-second window to have room, since back-to-back tiers were having their setup logins refused ([KS-1362](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1362/back-to-back-tiers-setup-logins-land-in-the-platforms-spent-60-second)).

**Measured on slot 2 of the Mac, 2026-09-28, Akto 2.35.6**

| tier | unpaced | paced at 1,500/min |
| -- | -- | -- |
| pr | 29 s — 8,702 results, 129 refused | (left unpaced) |
| pre-merge | **47 s** — only 1,057 actually tested, **8,129 refused** | **19 m 28 s** — 192 refused |
| full OWASP scan | 423.8 s — **8,730 of 50,162 refused** | **\~27 min — 0 of 50,306 refused** |
| whole security tier | — | **60 m 52 s** |

Two things to expect at any pace: Akto overshoots its setting by about 10%, and it releases each minute's allowance as a \~5 s burst, so the first minute of a paced run still sees a few refusals.

**The platform side as it stands** (read-only)

* Global limiter: `api-gateway/src/index.ts:472-485` — 60 s window, `max = RATE_LIMIT_MAX_REQUESTS || (non-prod ? 10000 : 300)`; `.env.example:205` sets **2000**. Keyed per address, and every caller on the host shares `192.168.65.1` ([KS-618](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-618/client-ip-is-invisible-platform-wide-on-demo-every-ip-keyed-control)).
* Skip rules: `middleware/rateLimitSkip.ts` — read-only paths; an operator override `DISABLE_RATE_LIMIT=true` in non-prod envs; and a `Bearer test_token_` bypass when `ENABLE_TEST_TOKENS=true` in `development`/`test`.
* nginx (`nginx-demo.conf:171-172`, VM demo) adds `limit_req` at 50 r/s (api) and 5 r/s (auth).

+++

+++ The options, as I see them

1. **Keep things as they are** — harness-side pacing only; no platform change. *Cost:* pre-merge \~20 min and security \~1 h locally. The limiter stays exactly as deployed.
2. **Raise** `RATE_LIMIT_MAX_REQUESTS` **for local stacks only** (e.g. back to the code's non-prod default of 10,000, or a figure you choose), leaving demo and production alone. The harness would pace to the new figure automatically, since it derives its rate from this value. *Cost:* local stacks stop matching the demo's limiter, so a limiter regression would be less likely to show locally.
3. **Use the existing operator override** — `DISABLE_RATE_LIMIT=true` on local non-prod stacks during scans. *Cost:* the global limiter is out of the picture entirely, including the verifier rate-limiting test's realism; easy to leave on by accident.
4. **Key the limiter per authenticated principal** (user or token) instead of per address — so the scanner's personas, k6 and a human each get their own budget. *Cost:* a real design change with security implications; overlaps [KS-618](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-618/client-ip-is-invisible-platform-wide-on-demo-every-ip-keyed-control).
5. **A dedicated, higher budget for a scanner identity in non-prod only** (e.g. a service account or a signed header, gated like the existing test-token bypass). *Cost:* a new bypass surface that has to be airtight to non-prod.
6. **Tune the harness further, no platform change** — pace closer to 2,000 (e.g. 0.85×) to save a few minutes at the price of a few more first-minute refusals, or pace fewer tiers. *Cost:* marginal gains; the limiter still sets the floor.

+++

## Where I'd love your guidance

1. Which option (or combination) fits how you want the limiter to behave?
2. Should local stacks match the demo's limits exactly, or is a looser local limit acceptable for testing?
3. Is \~20 min for pre-merge and \~1 h for security acceptable as a local gate, or is it worth a platform change to bring those down?

Once we've agreed a direction, either of us can make the change — whichever is more convenient. The one thing that isn't on the table is reducing test coverage: every option above keeps the same templates, tiers and endpoints, and changes only how fast they run or how the limit is set. No platform code has been touched so far.

## Checklist item added after the merge of PR #1347 (squash `8c810023f9c9`)

- [X] **N-1347-11 — the residue of the target-keyed pacing.** Closed by PR #1349, merged to `develop` as squash `691bb93e5c530c845ba0926ab0f369d5dc502720`: `isLocalScanTarget()` now reads `OVERRIDE_APP_URL` first and falls back to `SECUURA_API_URL`, the same precedence `systemTest/akto/src/scan/scanOptions.ts:98` uses for the host the scan attacks. With `RATE_LIMIT_MAX_REQUESTS=10000` reaching the harness (a raised local `.env`), a scan aimed at a remote stack through `OVERRIDE_APP_URL` alone was paced at 7500/min and is now paced at 1500, and an `OVERRIDE_APP_URL` pointing at localhost is paced at 7500. Without that raised value, and without `AKTO_PLATFORM_REQUESTS_PER_MINUTE`, every target is paced at 1500, as before. Checked by unit tests only (9 cells: 4 that fail on the previous code, 5 controls); no Akto scan was run against any stack, and the demo's own `RATE_LIMIT_MAX_REQUESTS` has not been read.

nodes.body:
**BLUF:** Paced `pre-merge` runs still lose 4 to 8 percent of results to 429s. There are three possible readings and none is settled. Controlled re-run owed, not yet run. This comes from reading code at develop `cd773edc2bb8` and the figures already on this ticket; no stack and no Akto run sit behind it.

**Reading 1, overlap with other traffic.** The limiter is keyed per address, so other callers on the host can spend the same budget. It is not needed to explain the highest figure: the 2026-10-07 comment says nothing else was on the slot for the run with 1,671 refused, which is more than the 939 of 2026-10-06, when a preflight may have overlapped. It is not ruled out for 2026-10-06. Settled by: the gateway columns of `npm run scan:pacing`, all requests against Akto's per minute, on a slot with nothing else on it.

**Reading 2, the 10,000 budget not applying per scan as the harness assumes.** `services/api-gateway/src/index.ts` has one limiter, per address, per 60 s window, not per scan, and the harness paces the tier as one budget. If the gateway had been at 2,000 while Akto paced at 7,500, refusals would be nearer the 70 percent measured unpaced than 4 to 8 percent. That is an inference; no stack's environment was read. Settled by: the `RateLimit-Policy` header on a captured 429, which should read `10000;w=60`.

**Reading 3, Akto bursting above its rate within the minute.** `aktoRateLimit.ts` already records this as operating fact 3: each minute's allotment leaves as a burst of about 5 s, and a run's first gateway window catches two. The headroom is still 0.75, so the loss would scale with the pace. At 1,500/min the measured refusals were 192 and 290 results; five times those is 960 and 1,450. The figures at 7,500/min are 944 (2026-10-05, "all in one ~2 s burst"), 939 and 1,671. Settled by: the per-minute rows of `npm run scan:pacing`; this reading predicts every refusal in the first minute or two of the run and none after.

**The point against reading 3.** The `security` tier's full OWASP scan refused 393 of 50,450 at the same pace, well below that scaling, although it sends about one request per result where `pre-merge` sends about four. The code does not explain that. So reading 3 is a lead, not a finding.

**Not measured.** The wall-clock of a paced run since PRs 1347 and 1349.

**What settles all three.** A disposable slot with nothing else on it, `npm run test:pre-merge`, then `npm run scan:pacing`. Controlled re-run owed, not yet run. The pacing does not change until a run supports it.

Delivered: PRs 1347 and 1349 merged as 8c810023f and 691bb93e5 on develop, both in the b1fb543640e7 tree (2026-11-01); they change env.example and the systemTest Akto harness, so there is no deployed surface. Verified by code read at b1fb543640e7, not observed live: env.example sets RATE_LIMIT_MAX_REQUESTS=10000 with a 60000 ms window. Left open: the ticket asks which way to go on how the platform's rate limit treats Akto scans, and no ruling is recorded in its comments. The newest two comments (2026-10-06 and 2026-10-07) report the paced pre-merge runs still receive 429s on about 4% and 8% of results (1,671 of 21,031 on 2026-10-07), so the pace and the limit are described as not yet fitting.

## Data point: rate-limited (429) counts on Akto 2.37.1, slot 1, 2026-10-07

Kamil, for your open pacing question; nothing assumed. All runs paced at 7,500/min (0.75 × the local 10,000/min):

| Tier | Result docs | Refused (429) |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `pre-merge` | 21,031 | **1,671** (about 8%) |
| `security`, full OWASP scan alone | 50,450 | 393 |
| `pr` (unthrottled) | 8,727 | 11 |

For comparison, earlier `pre-merge` runs: 944 on slot 2 on 2026-10-05 (Akto 2.36.10, all in one ~2 s burst) and 939 on slot 1 on 2026-10-06. This run therefore has about 1.8× the refusals, and I cannot separate the image bump from pacing: I have only this one `pre-merge` run on 2.37.1, nothing else was on the slot during it, and the per-minute breakdown (`npm run scan:pacing`) was not captured. The testing engine itself is unchanged between the two images (the `apps/testing` git tree is identical).

## First paced scan since #1347 / #1349: still 939 rate-limited results at 7,500/min

**BLUF.** Kamil, thank you for #1347 and #1349. One thing worth knowing, no action assumed: the first paced Akto run since your change still hit the platform limiter on about 4% of results, so the pace and the limit don't quite fit yet.

>>> Evidence (Akto `pre-merge`, local slot 1, 2026-10-06 ~14:21Z, run `pre-merge-ks-571-2026-10-06T14-20-45Z`)

* **Pacing, from the run log:** `Akto engine rate limit set to 7500 req/min (platform budget 10000/min, 75% headroom)`. The harness waited 65 s for Akto's watcher to apply it, then restored "unthrottled" at the end.
* **Verdict:** PASS — 0 vulnerable.
* **Buckets:** clean 7,953 · authz-precondition 644 · not-applicable 10,716 · not-on-stack 772 · connectivity 7 · **rate-limited 939**.
* **HTTP:** `429 939` of 21,031 non-vulnerable results (also 400 347 · 404 5,587 · 415 38).
* So **939 results (≈4.5%) weren't exercised**, even with the engine at 75% of the platform budget.

**Not measured / not ruled out:**
* The run's wall-clock time (not captured), so I can't say whether the ~20 min / ~1 h concern is settled.
* **Other traffic on slot 1:** a repo pre-push preflight was running on the same machine around then, and its spec-auth and path-resolvability legs probe the slot-1 gateway. I can't rule out that it overlapped the scan and used part of the budget. A clean re-run with nothing else on the slot would settle it.

**Possible readings, your call:** overlap with that other traffic; the 10,000/min budget not applying per scan as the harness assumes; or Akto bursting above its configured rate within the minute. A clean re-run, and measuring where the 429s cluster, would tell them apart.

>>>

Refs as KS-NNN text. Posted by agent on Peter's behalf; edited the same day to state the possible overlap.

Merged to `develop` as PR #1347, squash `8c810023f9c9ac060a7aff24f0933ae3b8734479`, tree `e889329f530b`, parent `8ba2da02d980`. Verified at source: develop equals the squash by ls-remote, the commits API reports that tree, and a contents-API blob read on all six changed paths equals the head's blob. The landed subject is 92 characters.

The squash subject was composed rather than taken from the PR title, because the title had become false at round 2: it said "raise the local templates" (plural) when only `env.example` is raised, and "read the platform limit" without the condition. The landed subject states the condition: `env.example` goes to 10000, and the Akto harness reads it only when `SECUURA_API_URL` is local.

Round 2 closed the three findings a review raised against round 1: the production-compose template is back to its own value, the harness no longer reads a local limit for every scan, and the derived rate is floored at 1 so it can never be zero — zero means unthrottled in that harness.

One residue remains and is recorded as a checklist item below: a scan aimed at a remote stack through `OVERRIDE_APP_URL` alone, with `SECUURA_API_URL` local or unset, still paces at the local figure. The demo's own limit was not read at any point, because its environment file is not in this repository.

This ticket stays In Progress. Nothing was deployed by the merge.

Second correction, to our comment above. Two things in it were wrong, and a review of the change found them. *(Edited after a later review: two statements in the first version of this comment were themselves imprecise, and they are corrected in place below rather than in a third comment.)*

First: we wrote "Demo and production limits are unchanged". That held for deployments already running, but not for a host seeded afterwards. Blockchain/Dev/docker-compose.production.yml:16 tells an operator to copy .env.example to .env, and that file's own default is RATE_LIMIT_MAX_REQUESTS:-100. The first round raised .env.example to 10000, so a production-compose host seeded from it after that change would have run at 10000. No running environment was affected, and nothing was deployed, but the statement was wrong about the seeding path.

Second: we said the Akto harness now takes the platform limit from RATE_LIMIT_MAX_REQUESTS. It did, for every scan — including a scan pointed at a remote stack. The harness's configuration loader reads the local Blockchain/Dev/.env whatever stack is being scanned, so a local value of 10000 would have paced a remote scan at 7500 where it had previously paced at 1500. We cannot state the demo's own limit here: its environment file is not in this repository, and the only figures the repository carries are deployment/azure/services.bicep:681, which sets 2000 for the Azure `dev` environment and 100 for every other one. An earlier version of this comment gave "2000" as the demo's limit, which was not something we had read.

Both are fixed at head 18bc5123ce90, merged as PR #1347 (squash 8c810023f9c9):
- Blockchain/Dev/.env.example is back to 2000, with the reason recorded in the file. Only Blockchain/Dev/env.example is raised to 10000; scripts/bootstrap-env.sh reads that one as canonical. So env.example seeds local stacks, .env.example seeds production-compose, and the two no longer move together.
- The harness reads RATE_LIMIT_MAX_REQUESTS only when SECUURA_API_URL resolves to a local host (an unset value is local, because the default is always a localhost port). A remote SECUURA_API_URL paces at the 2000 default. AKTO_PLATFORM_REQUESTS_PER_MINUTE is an explicit override for a remote stack whose real limit an operator knows; its name is deliberately not defined by either env template, so it cannot be picked up from a local .env the way the previous value was.
- A platform limit of 1 previously derived 0, which this harness treats as unthrottled. The derived rate is now floored at 1.

One case is NOT covered, and an earlier version of this comment implied otherwise by saying "any other target paces at the 2000 default". The host the scanner actually attacks is OVERRIDE_APP_URL if set, falling back to SECUURA_API_URL (systemTest/akto/src/setup/scanOptions.ts:98), while the check above reads SECUURA_API_URL only. So a scan aimed at a remote stack through OVERRIDE_APP_URL alone, with SECUURA_API_URL local or unset, still paces at the local figure. That configuration also logs in to the local stack, so such a scan is already misconfigured, but the pacing is wrong in it and the gap is real. It is recorded on this ticket as a checklist item, with the one-line fix.

Two further things to be plain about. The .github/workflows/internal-audit.yml CI stack copies env.example, so CI now runs at 10000. And a remote stack reached through a localhost port-forward or tunnel reads as local; the explicit override is the answer there, and the change does not try to detect that case.

Hi @kamil.kreiser

I added this yesterday as a temporary fix, as I did not want to update the codebase

* systemTest/akto/src/setup/aktoRateLimit.ts:60

## BLUF
Thanks Peter, this is a clear write-up. **Our recommendation is option 2 plus one guard:** raise `RATE_LIMIT_MAX_REQUESTS` on **local stacks only** (to the code's own non-prod default of 10,000, which you cite at `api-gateway/src/index.ts:472-485`), leave demo and production exactly as deployed, and **add one dedicated limiter test that runs at the demo's limit** so a limiter regression still shows up locally. Coverage is unchanged; only local pacing and one config value move.

## Recommendation, answering your three questions
1. **Which option:** 2, plus the limiter test above. The harness already derives its pace from this value, so it speeds up on its own.
2. **Should local stacks match demo exactly?** A looser local limit is acceptable **for scanning**, provided one test pins the demo behaviour: at the demo figure (2,000/min), requests beyond it are refused with 429, and the read-only skip paths still skip. That keeps the realism you were worried about losing in option 2, without paying for it in every scan.
3. **Is ~20 min / ~1 h acceptable as a local gate?** No. That is slow enough that people start skipping the gate, which costs more coverage than it protects. A config change is worth it.

## Why not the others
- **3 (`DISABLE_RATE_LIMIT=true` during scans):** removes the limiter from the picture entirely and is easy to leave on by accident.
- **5 (a scanner identity with a higher budget):** a new bypass surface that has to stay airtight to non-prod; not worth it when a config value does the job.
- **4 (key the limiter per principal):** probably the right long-term design, and it overlaps KS-618 (every caller shares one address). It is a separate piece of work with security implications, so we suggest a ticket for it, not this change.
- **6:** marginal gains; the limiter still sets the floor.

## Detail
No platform code is proposed to change; demo and production limits are untouched. If you agree, either side can make the change, as you offered: the local `.env` value, and the one limiter test.

title: api-gateway failed-login lockout is inert: createBruteForceProtection installs recordFailure, but no production code ever calls it — it can never block
description:
## Summary

For when you have a moment, Kamil. The gateway's failed-login lockout (`createBruteForceProtection`, `api-gateway/src/middleware/security.ts:146-192`) looks as though it never engages: it only blocks once `recordFailure()` has run, and nothing outside its own unit test seems to call it. The auth service's per-account lockout is still doing its job, so this is about the edge layer only. Either wiring it up or retiring it would be fine; whichever you prefer. Thank you.

+++ Evidence, and the two options

**What the code shows** (read-only, 2026-09-28)

* `security.ts:173-189` attaches `req.bruteForce = { recordFailure, recordSuccess }` and calls `next()`; nothing on the login's response path calls either helper.
* Searching `services/api-gateway/src` for `recordFailure` outside `middleware/security.ts` finds only `__tests__/security.test.ts:261`, which checks the helper exists.
* So `attempts` is never incremented, `blockedUntil` is never written, and the `429 "Too many failed attempts"` branch can't be reached.

**What the logs show**

* Slot 2's gateway, six hours of traffic including failed logins: **0** `BRUTE_FORCE_LOCKOUT`, **0** `BRUTE_FORCE_BLOCKED`.
* The lockout that does work is the auth service's (`services/auth/src/services/accountLockout.ts`: (email, /24), 5 failures in 15 min → 15-min lock). It answers **401** (`routes/auth.ts:339-342`).

**Why it came up:** [KS-1362](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1362/back-to-back-tiers-setup-logins-land-in-the-platforms-spent-60-second) first put some refused setup logins down to this lockout; on a closer look they were the global request window. It seemed worth recording that this layer isn't active, so no one leans on it.

**Options**

1. Wire it: call `recordFailure` / `recordSuccess` from the login proxy's response handling (401 / 2xx), with a test that shows a block after `freeRetries` failures.
2. Retire it: remove the middleware, its `bruteForce` config in `config/services.ts`, and the doc line at `security.ts:8`.

[KS-618](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-618/client-ip-is-invisible-platform-wide-on-demo-every-ip-keyed-control) (every IP-keyed control is shared behind one address) applies either way.

**Done means:** a test red on today's code shows N+1 failed logins from one address aren't blocked at the gateway; after the change they are — or the middleware and its claims are gone.

+++

title: Security: validate reads API keys from a boot-only memory map, so a revoked key keeps authenticating AND its usage write rewrites is_active = true over the revoke
description:
**BLUF — measured from the source path at develop** `0d156d12`**, and it is worse than a multi-replica write-back concern: it is also a live authentication bypass on a single process.**

`POST /api/keys/validate` in `services/security/src/index.ts` resolves the key from an **in-memory map first** and reads the database **only on a cache miss**:

* `:1326` `let apiKey = Array.from(memApiKeys.values()).find(k => k.keyHash === keyHash);`
* `:1328-1334` the code's own comment states the map "is populated **only at boot** from svc_api_keys".
* `:1335` the DB fallback (`security_find_api_key_by_hash`) runs **only** `if (!apiKey)`, and `:1347` warms the cache.

So once a key is in memory, this process never re-reads its row. Two consequences follow, and the second is the one the KS-888 validate brief raised:

**1. A revoked key keeps authenticating.** `:1358` `if (!apiKey.isActive)` is evaluated against the **stale memory copy**. If the row is set inactive by anything this process did not do — the revoke route on another replica, an operator UPDATE, a future admin tool — this process answers `valid: true` until it restarts.

**2. The usage write then UNDOES the revoke for everyone.** `:1369` `await dbSaveApiKey(apiKey);` and the upsert at `:316-318` is `ON CONFLICT (id) DO UPDATE SET last_used_at = EXCLUDED.last_used_at, usage_count = EXCLUDED.usage_count, is_active = EXCLUDED.is_active`. `EXCLUDED.is_active` comes from the in-memory `k.isActive`, which is still `true`. So a validate on a stale copy writes `is_active = true` over a persisted revoke. The revoke is lost in the database, not merely missed locally.

**What is measured and what is not.** Every line above is read at `0d156d12` and quoted. The control flow is decisive on its own: memory-first, DB-on-miss-only, boot-only population, and the upsert asserting `is_active` from that copy. What is **NOT** done is a driven two-process run demonstrating the lost revoke end to end — that needs two memory maps over one database and is the natural first step for whoever takes this.

**Why it is not KS-888.** KS-888 is about what happens when the usage write *fails* (mint refuses, revoke answers 503, validate logs and continues — all shipped or pinned). This is about the write *succeeding* and carrying a stale field. The pin for validate's log-only behaviour is PR #1334; it does not touch this and must not be read as covering it.

**Board search before filing, with controls:** `EXCLUDED.is_active`, `populated only at boot`, `security_find_api_key_by_hash`, `stale memory`, `revoked key still validates` all returned **0**; positive controls on the same literal query shape returned `memApiKeys` 4, `dbSaveApiKey` 3, `is_active` 2, and the nonsense control 0. The four `memApiKeys` hits (KS-1174, KS-889, KS-888, KS-869) were each read and none covers this: they are the gateway's 401 collapsing, the connector_id backfill window, the KS-888 save-failure family, and connector_id persistence.

**Shapes worth considering (not a recommendation).** Narrowest: drop `is_active` from the upsert's SET list, so a usage write can never assert liveness. That closes consequence 2 and leaves consequence 1. Wider: re-read the row (or invalidate the cache entry) before answering, which closes both and costs a query per validate on a deliberately unauthenticated hot path.

nodes.body: **BLUF:** State moved In Review -> In Progress. Owed: "a revoke in one security replica refusing the key in another." (this ticket's newest comment, comment 7). Not closed because the ticket says: "It needs a key minted and revoked (writes) and a second security replica; no permitted login covers it". Kam ruled on 2026-11-04 12:42 AEDT (card `secuura-observation-owed-closeout-1104`, option **a**): "Run one live-check sweep on kintsugi, then close what passes"; this ticket is named in that card. This seat ran no check on a box; beyond the ticket text it read only the merge state of PR 1338 at the GitHub API (PR 1338 merged as 8af6ab821600).

**BLUF:** Not run on kintsugi: needs an API key minted and revoked. Delivered: PR 1338 merged as 8af6ab821 on develop, deployed to kintsugi at ee1e1b832115 (kintsugi's REVISION head, read 2026-11-04 01:59Z). Left open.

- **Owed check:** a revoke in one security replica refusing the key in another.
- **Why not run:** It needs a key minted and revoked (writes) and a second security replica; no permitted login covers it.

Delivered: PR 1338 merged as 8af6ab821 on develop (validate answers on the stored revoke and its usage write cannot revive one), with KS-1377's PR 1602 counting key usage in the database, in the kintsugi deploy b1fb543640e7 (2026-11-01). Verified by code read at b1fb543640e7, not observed live: services/security/src/index.ts carries both halves, the usage-only write at line 471 and :1904 and the stored-row check on a cache hit at :1820 to 1862 (stored-revoked beats cached-active). Left open: the ticket's merge comment says NOT Done, live sweep owed: a cross-replica revoke and the EXECUTE grant on the deployed database. Both need a second replica or database access and a revoke on the box, which is not a read-only probe, and neither was run here.

Merged 8af6ab8216007462e596daed6b0adcd1e87e34ee (PR #1338, services/security/src/index.ts); offline gates green; NOT Done per secuura-test-discipline §5f — live sweep owed (torn-down rebuilt stack, all containers verified up), unverified: a revoke in one security replica refused by another within the gateway's 60 s valid cache, the secuura_app role's EXECUTE on security_find_api_key_by_hash on the deployed database, and a security-DB fault's 503 -> 401 path through the gateway

---

**For the record, measured by the gate at the base (VANISHED-ROW-RESURRECTED-AT-BASE):** at the base a stale instance honours a DELETED key (200 `valid:true`) AND its usage upsert **re-creates the row** (`is_active true, usage 1`) as secuura_app under the key's tenant GUC. Any delete, including migration 019's, was undone by one validate on a stale replica. The merged head closes it (`Key not found`, evicted, no row). My own PR body called this path "defensive, not live" — that was true of today's DELETE sites but understated the base defect, and the gate's measurement is the accurate account.

**PR #1338 raised** — `feature/ks-1370-validate-reads-stored-revoke-b42-1` at head `42f8a5abc65ef9a6bc20c07797786089f2b9cd93`, base `develop`. Not merged; holding for the QA gate. Nothing deployed.

**Reproduced first, on a real PostgreSQL 18.3 (unix socket only), at develop `0de108577e61`.** Two module instances with separate in-memory key maps, driven through the real `POST /api/keys/validate`:
- a stale instance validated a key revoked by another process → `valid: true`
- after its usage write the row read `is_active` false → **true**, `usage_count` 1 → 2
- controls both ways: a never-revoked key validated; a third instance booted after the revoke refused it and the row stayed `false`, so the database held the revoke and the stale cache alone is the difference

**Both halves fixed, per the ruling on this ticket (option a):**
- (i) validate's usage write is now a usage-only `UPDATE ... SET last_used_at, usage_count`. The shared upsert keeps `is_active` because the revoke route persists through it and the KS 764 guard pins that shape.
- (ii) on a cache hit validate re-reads the stored row through the reviewed `security_find_api_key_by_hash` carve-out and decides on it, refreshing the stale entry.

**The failed-read case, per the second ruling (option a):** a failed stored read with a database configured returns 503 "Unable to verify key"; memory-only deployments answer from memory and are unchanged.

**Two shapes that follow from the rulings rather than adding to them:**
- A revoke is sticky in **both** directions — revoked if either the cache or the store says revoked. Refreshing blindly from the store would have undone KS 888's rule that a revoke whose save failed still blocks the key in that process. Cell R2 of the KS 888 file caught it, and that cell now passes unchanged.
- A row that has vanished reads `Key not found` and the cache entry is evicted. This is a defensive path: nothing outside migration 019 deletes from `svc_api_keys`.

**Evidence:** `services/security` 26 files / 275 tests, 0 failed · KS 888 validate file 19/19 (baseline 19/19; 5 declarations = 7 executed cases moved and re-pinned, reason in the mock, no pin weakened) · 9 new cells, 5 of them red at the base tip · KS 764 guard 15/15 untouched · tsc rc 0 · eslint rc 0 · 16/16 real-PostgreSQL arms with the product file restored byte-identical · push preflight 12/15 legs, 3 skipped, nothing failed.

**Not covered, stated:** the drill runs as a superuser, so RLS is bypassed and it cannot discriminate the fail-closed path that justifies the SECURITY DEFINER carve-out — the gate should drive the stored read as a non-superuser app role. `usage_count` written from a stale copy is a lost update, named as a candidate and not fixed. Runtime change on validate, so the §5f live sweep is owed.

**REPRODUCED on a real PostgreSQL. Facts only — no product change, no state change.**

**Instrument:** a driven two-instance repro. Two instances of `services/security/src/index.ts` are loaded with separate CJS module caches, so each holds its **own `memApiKeys`** (the map is exported as a test seam at `:160`). `SECURITY_DISABLE_BOOT=1` suppresses `app.listen` and `initDb`; `initDb()` is then called explicitly per instance, and each instance's real Express `app` is served on an ephemeral loopback port and driven through the real `POST /api/keys/validate` route. One PostgreSQL **18.3**, unix socket only (`listen_addresses = ''`, 0 inet sockets verified with `lsof`), schema built by the repo's own file migrations.

**Commit under test:** worktree at develop `215cc6875e2bac0b6d6b38918572384fbfcbdb77` (the local HEAD adds only an unrelated test-file change; `services/security/src/index.ts` is byte-identical to develop's, sha256 `7f29bb85765e7985`).

**Anchors re-read at this commit and unchanged from the filing:** `:1326` resolves the key from `memApiKeys` first; `:1328` states the map is "populated only at boot"; `:1335` reads the DB only on a cache miss; `:1358` tests the cached `isActive`; `:1369` `await dbSaveApiKey(apiKey)`; `:316-318` `ON CONFLICT (id) DO UPDATE SET ... is_active = EXCLUDED.is_active`.

**Sequence and results.** Instance B boots while the key is active, so its cache holds `isActive: true`. The revoke is then persisted (`is_active = false`). Then:

| step | result |
|---|---|
| CONTROL — key never revoked, validated in B | `valid: true` |
| revoke persisted | DB `is_active = false` |
| **(1) B validates the revoked key** | **`valid: true`** — the key still authenticates |
| **(2) DB row after B's usage write** | **`is_active = true`**; `usage_count` 1 → 2 |
| CONTROL — a THIRD instance booted AFTER the revoke | `valid: false`, reason `Key revoked`; DB stays `false` |

**Both halves of the report are confirmed.** A revoked key keeps authenticating in any process that cached it before the revoke, and that process's usage write then **rewrites `is_active = true` over the persisted revoke**.

**What the controls establish.** The first control shows the harness can answer `valid`, so answer (1) is not a harness artefact. The third-instance control shows the database genuinely held the revoke and that a fresh boot refuses the key — so the difference is the stale cache alone, not the database.

**Scope of what was driven.** The revoke was applied as the persisted row state that the revoke route's `dbSaveApiKey` produces, rather than through that route's admin-authenticated handler; instance B — the subject of the report — was driven end to end through its real route. The two instances share one process with separate module caches rather than being two OS processes; the separation under test is the memory map, which is genuinely separate.

**An earlier run of this instrument was INVALID and is withdrawn:** `initDb()` had not been called, so `loadFromDb()` returned early, no key was cached, and every answer read `Key not found` — **including the control**. A control that fails alongside the subject is the tell, and it is why that run was not reported.

**A dependency the gate38 report records, from the other side (finding N-1334-1, facts only).**

PR #1334 (squash `215cc6875e2bac0b6d6b38918572384fbfcbdb77`) pinned validate's log-only behaviour with a test-only change. The gate's note on it: *"the pin binds validate's usage write to the `INSERT … upsert` shape, so a KS 1370 fix would red 5 of its cells."*

So whoever fixes this ticket should expect `services/security/src/__tests__/ks888-failed-mint-save-issues-no-key.test.ts` to go red — specifically the V1 ×3 / V2 / V3 cases that assert the current upsert shape — and should update those cells as part of the fix rather than reading the red as a regression. The narrowest fix shape named on this ticket (dropping `is_active` from the upsert's SET list) is exactly the kind of change that would do it.

Nothing to do here now; recorded so the coupling is not discovered by surprise.

Filed at Urgent, corrected to **High** on the same day it was filed. The evidence is a source-path reading at develop `0d156d12` — memory-first lookup, boot-only population, DB read only on a cache miss, and `is_active` asserted from that copy in the upsert — every line quoted in the description. What is **not** done is a driven two-process run showing a persisted revoke actually lost. High matches KS-1352, the sibling finding that a revoked credential verifies. A driven repro is what would justify raising it to Urgent, and it is the natural first step for whoever takes this.

title: api-gateway crashes under load: onProxyReq calls setHeader after the proxied request's headers were sent — uncaught exception, 13 restarts, 502s on /api/auth/login
description:
## Summary

When you get a chance, Kamil — this one does hurt under load. During the [KS-1354](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1354/bump-systemtest-k6-210-230-grafanak6-v220-v230-released) k6 runs, the api-gateway process exited on an uncaught exception thrown from its own proxy hook, and Docker restarted it 13 times in about five minutes. nginx answered 502 while it was down. The hook calls `setHeader` on a request whose headers were already sent, and nothing guards or catches that. A small guard plus an error path would likely settle it; your call on the shape. Thank you.

+++ Evidence, impact and a suggested direction

**The throw** (31 occurrences in the gateway log)

```
Uncaught exception {"error":"Cannot set headers after they are sent to the client"}
  at ClientRequest.setHeader (node:_http_outgoing:684:11)
  at ProxyServer.onProxyReq (/app/dist/routes/proxy.js:254:26)
  at ProxyServer.emit (/app/node_modules/eventemitter3/index.js:184:35)
  at ClientRequest.<anonymous> (/app/node_modules/http-proxy/lib/http-proxy/passes/web-incoming.js:133:16)
  at tickOnSocket (node:_http_client:1116:7)
```

`dist/routes/proxy.js:254` is the hook's first statement, `proxyReq.setHeader('X-Request-ID', requestId)` — source `Blockchain/Dev/services/api-gateway/src/routes/proxy.ts:246` (mapped by reading the compiled file in the running container). None of the hook's later header writes (vouch `:276`, policy headers, `Authorization`, the [KS-453](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-453/did-endpoints-getpatchdelete-apididdid-return-502-on-malformed-did) body re-stream) checks `proxyReq.headersSent` either.

**Where:** local slot 1, api-gateway built from develop `63db8a383` ([KS-1354](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1354/bump-systemtest-k6-210-230-grafanak6-v220-v230-released) changes no service code); Apple M2 Max, four stacks up. Load: k6 `scalability` (12:54–13:15Z) then `auth-spike` (13:15–13:17Z, 150 VUs on `POST /api/auth/login`). First crash 13:12:11Z; `restartCount=13`, last start 13:17:36Z; healthy afterwards.

**What callers saw**

| Signal | Value |
| -- | -- |
| nginx, `POST /api/auth/login` during auth-spike | **11,362 × 502** + 6,123 × 429 |
| scalability | thresholds 6/6, but **14.8 %** `http_req_failed`, 65,192 failed checks |
| auth-spike | INVALID — all 17,788 logins failed |
| auth service, same second as the first crash | `DB getUserByEmail failed … timeout exceeded when trying to connect` |

The auth DB-pool timeout looks like the trigger; the gateway turning it into a process exit is the defect.

**Ruled out:** slots sharing a database (each has its own Postgres + pgbouncer network), and the harness/k6 version (the trace is inside api-gateway; other k6 scenarios pass).

**Suggested direction**

1. Return early from the hook when `proxyReq.headersSent` (or the request is destroyed).
2. Let the proxy's error path answer 502/503 rather than letting a handler throw reach `uncaughtException` (the class [KS-1242](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1242/t-1-authenticatetoken-is-an-async-express-4-middleware-with-no-catch-a) describes for `authenticateToken`).
3. A regression test driving `onProxyReq` with an already-sent `proxyReq`, red on today's code.

**Reproduce:** `BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_PASSWORD=… systemTest/run-in-slot.sh 1 bash -c 'cd systemTest/performance && npm run test:scalability'`, then `npm run test:auth-spike`; watch `docker inspect secuura-api-gateway --format '{{.RestartCount}}'` and `docker logs secuura-api-gateway | grep "Cannot set headers"`.

**Related:** [KS-1242](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1242/t-1-authenticatetoken-is-an-async-express-4-middleware-with-no-catch-a) (async middleware without a catch — same class, different site) · [KS-744](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-744/gateway-500s-on-every-proxied-route-for-a-token-lacking) (unguarded header set in `auth.ts:377`) · [KS-1362](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1362/back-to-back-tiers-setup-logins-land-in-the-platforms-spent-60-second) (back-to-back tiers' setup logins refused inside a spent request window — the 429 side of busy runs) · [KS-1354](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1354/bump-systemtest-k6-210-230-grafanak6-v220-v230-released) (where it was found) · [KS-491](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-491/review-f-edge-waf-ddos-and-anti-automation) (Review F — availability under load).

+++

## Checklist item added after the merge of PR #1342 (squash `67c73393dfa0`)

- [ ] **N-1342-1 (Major, not blocking):** under keep-alive agent saturation (more than 128 requests in
  flight to one upstream), a **body-parsed** POST whose headers were already sent is delivered to the
  upstream with its `Content-Length` and **zero body bytes**. The guard skips the re-stream, so the
  upstream waits and the client gets a TCP reset at exactly 60.0 s, with **no 502 and no log line**.
  At develop before #1342 the same request **crashes** the process, so the merged change is strictly
  better — this is residue, not a regression. The raw-stream `/api/auth/login` route is unaffected
  (140/140 delivered). Evidence: `evidence/runs/probe1342b.log` and `probe1342c.log` in the gate43
  batch #1341-#1345 report directory.

nodes.body: Delivered: PR 1342 merged as 67c73393d on develop, deployed to kintsugi at b1fb543640e7 (2026-11-01). Verified by code read at b1fb543640e7, not observed live: services/api-gateway/src/routes/proxy.ts:256 returns early when `proxyReq.headersSent` is true, inside the onProxyReq hook (control: the hook is present, 3 hits in proxy.ts). Left open: the ticket carries an unchecked checklist item, N-1342-1 (Major, not blocking): under keep-alive saturation (more than 128 requests in flight to one upstream) a body-parsed POST whose headers were already sent is delivered with its Content-Length and zero body bytes, and the client gets a TCP reset at 60 s with no 502 and no log line. The merge comment also says a live sweep against a running environment is owed. Neither is a read-only probe, so this check did not run them.

Merged to `develop` as PR #1342, squash `67c73393dfa07c741f359c59b893cb24a89d5152`, tree `449ae9c6c10e`. Verified at source: develop equals the squash by ls-remote, the commits API reports that tree, and a contents-API blob read on each changed path equals the head's blob. The landed subject is within the 92-character limit.

QA recorded one Major finding that does not block this merge: under keep-alive saturation (more than 128 requests in flight to one upstream), a body-parsed POST whose headers were already sent is delivered with its Content-Length and zero body bytes, and the client gets a TCP reset at 60.0 s with no 502 and no log line. At develop the same request crashes the gateway, so this change is strictly better. The raw-stream login route is unaffected (140/140 delivered). Added below as a checklist item.

This changes runtime code, so a live sweep against a running environment is still owed and this ticket stays open. Nothing was deployed by the merge.

title: Native KYC in dev: the mock assessor can never reject or send for review, uploads are not checked for file type, and the KYC empty states skip the shared _EmptyState partial (PS-593's unfiled follow-up)
description:
**BLUF: three product gaps that** [PS-593](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-593/systemtest-close-the-identityverify-coverage-gaps-left-by-ps-442) **recorded on 2026-08-19 and proposed as one follow-up ticket, which was never filed. Re-checked in the code on 2026-09-28 (**`develop` `8e83e9be`**): all three are still true. The first two block browser tests that cannot otherwise be written truthfully.** [PS-593](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-593/systemtest-close-the-identityverify-coverage-gaps-left-by-ps-442) is Done, so this is raised as a new ticket rather than a comment there. ## 1. Rejected and UnderReview cannot be produced in dev * `ssd/Services/Kyc/MockKycProvider.cs:29` hard-codes `RequiresManualReview = false`, and the mock rejects only when a check has status Failed. * Every check the UI can create is written Passed (`KycService.cs` `SubmitDocumentAsync` / `SubmitSelfieAsync`, score 0.95). * So neither outcome is reachable through `/identity/verify`. No browser test covers a rejected verification (`kyc-granted-level` stays None) or the `kyc-under-review` state, and [PS-964](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-964/identityverify-an-underreview-verification-is-resumed-by-the-start) (UnderReview has no way out) cannot be exercised. * Suggested shape (your call): a failure-injecting assessor registered in dev only (never a deployed environment), selected for example by a reserved document type or region, so a test can ask for Rejected or UnderReview deliberately. ## 2. No server-side file-type check on identity uploads * `KycVerificationController.ReadImageAsync` (\~`:715-722`) rejects only null, empty and over-8MB files. It does not look at content type or magic bytes. * `accept="image/*"` on the inputs is a browser hint; a direct request bypasses it. [PS-593](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-593/systemtest-close-the-identityverify-coverage-gaps-left-by-ps-442) recorded that a `.txt` uploaded as `document-front.png` is accepted and hashed. * Suggested shape: check the content type and the leading bytes against the image formats you accept; refuse with the same "Please attach … as an image under 8MB." message. ## 3. KYC empty states do not use the shared partial * `Views/KycVerification/Index.cshtml` (`kyc-history-empty`) and `Details.cshtml` (`kyc-checks-empty`) render a plain `

`; neither uses `_EmptyState` (confirmed: no reference in either view). * The shared partial carries `role="status"`, so screen readers announce it; these do not. The empty-state sweep cannot cover them for the same reason. ## Acceptance * **Item 1 — dev only, and provably so.** A verification can be driven to `Rejected` (granted level `None`) and to `UnderReview` on demand through a failure-injecting assessor selected by something explicit (a reserved document type or region). The selection is gated on more than `DeployMode == "dev"` — per `CLAUDE.md`, `"dev"` covers internet-facing UAT, so it must be ANDed with its own opt-in flag, the way `DevToolsAllowAccountAdmin` is. An xUnit contract test asserts no tracked deployment template enables that flag. * **Item 2 — server-side type check.** `ReadImageAsync` validates content type **and** leading magic bytes against the accepted image formats, and refuses with the existing message. The `.txt`-renamed-`document-front.png` case from [PS-593](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-593/systemtest-close-the-identityverify-coverage-gaps-left-by-ps-442) is refused rather than accepted and hashed. * **Item 3 — empty states.** `Views/KycVerification/Index.cshtml` and `Details.cshtml` render their empty states through the shared `_EmptyState` partial, keeping `kyc-history-empty` and `kyc-checks-empty`, so both gain `role="status"` and are announced. * The companion unit-test ticket ([PS-970]()) covers the service side of item 1; that work must not be duplicated here. **Playwright test that demonstrates the fix** (required — items 2 and 3 are surfaces, and item 1 exists precisely to unblock browser coverage): extend `systemTest/tests/functional/kyc_verification_guards.spec.ts` for the upload refusal and `systemTest/tests/functional/empty_states.spec.ts` for the partial, and add the two outcome cases to `kyc_verification.spec.ts` once the injecting assessor exists. Against a live stack, as the worker's KYC persona: 1. post a **text file renamed** `document-front.png` to `POST /identity/verify/{id}/document`; assert the response refuses it with the "Please attach … as an image under 8MB." message and that `kyc-checks-empty` is still present — no check row was created; 2. post a **real image**; assert it is accepted and a check row appears — so the new validation is not simply refusing everything; 3. drive a verification to **Rejected** via the injected failure; assert `kyc-granted-level` reads `None` and the row's status is Rejected; 4. drive one to **UnderReview**; assert `kyc-under-review` is rendered (this is also the state [PS-964]() needs reachable, and [PS-961]()/[PS-962]() sit on the same page); 5. with no history and no checks, assert `kyc-history-empty` and `kyc-checks-empty` each resolve via `getByRole('status')` — the partial's contribution, and the reason the empty-state sweep cannot cover them today. **Which assertions fail on** `develop` **today:** 1 (the `.txt` is accepted and hashed — `ReadImageAsync` checks only null, empty and the 8MB ceiling), 3 and 4 (unreachable: `MockKycProvider.cs:29` hard-codes `RequiresManualReview = false` and every UI-created check is written `Passed`), and 5 (both views render a plain `

`, confirmed — neither references `_EmptyState`). **Control assertions that pass today and must keep passing:** 2 above, plus the existing happy path in `kyc_verification.spec.ts` — document + selfie + complete still reaches **Approved** with a granted level. A failure-injecting assessor that leaks into the default path would break this, which is exactly the regression worth guarding. **And one assertion that must stay negative on a deployed environment**, since "dev only" is a claim this ticket makes: the injection trigger produces no effect when the opt-in flag is off. That belongs in the xUnit contract test above rather than in a spec — the suite only ever runs against a slot, so it cannot prove anything about UAT.

title: /identity/verify: an UnderReview verification is resumed by the start page but its Details page treats it as closed — no way out, and the suite's reset helper would hang
description:
**BLUF: the two definitions of "open" disagree about UnderReview. The start page redirects a person with an UnderReview verification to its Details page, but Details does not count UnderReview as open, so it offers neither the evidence form nor Cancel — the person is sent to a page they cannot leave except by navigating away. Not reachable today (the mock assessor never returns UnderReview), so Low; it becomes live the moment a real assessor can send a verification for manual review.**

Found by the [PS-863](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-863/systemtest-role-kyc-specs-share-one-login-across-parallel-workers-so-a) code-vs-test review, `develop` `8e83e9be`, re-checked 2026-09-28.

## Where

* `ssd/Services/Kyc/KycVerificationLifecycle.cs:29-31` `IsOpen`: Pending **or InProgress or UnderReview**. `OpenVerificationForAsync` uses it, so `Index` resumes an UnderReview row (`KycVerificationController.cs:138-139`).
* `KycVerificationController.cs:508` `BuildDetailsAsync`: `IsOpen = verification.Status is KycStatus.Pending or KycStatus.InProgress` — UnderReview excluded, so Details renders the `kyc-under-review` notice with no abandon form.
* `KycService.AbandonAsync` → `RequireOpenVerificationAsync` refuses UnderReview anyway (`KycService.cs:414-415`).
* The systemTest reset helper `ensureNoOpenVerification()` (`systemTest/pages/kyc_verification_page.ts:109-122`) waits for the start form or an abandon button; on an UnderReview row neither appears, so it would time out. Its own comment records this as a known limit.
* `MockKycProvider.cs:29` hard-codes `RequiresManualReview = false`, which is why this is unreachable today.

## Fix (your call)

Decide what an UnderReview row means to the person: either the start page should not resume it (show the start page with its status in history), or Details should present it as a waiting state with a clear way back. Then make `IsOpen` / `IsResumable` and `BuildDetailsAsync` agree.

## Acceptance

* The decision is **recorded on this ticket in one sentence**: either the start page stops resuming an UnderReview row (shows the start page, with the status in history), or Details presents it as a waiting state with a clear way back. Everything below depends on which.
* `KycVerificationLifecycle.IsOpen` / `IsResumable` and `BuildDetailsAsync` **agree** about UnderReview. Today `IsOpen` (`:29-31`) counts Pending, InProgress **and** UnderReview, while `BuildDetailsAsync` (`:508`) counts only Pending and InProgress — the disagreement *is* the defect, so one definition, used by both, is the fix.
* `KycService.AbandonAsync` → `RequireOpenVerificationAsync` (`:414-415`) is consistent with the chosen answer. If Details is to offer a way back, abandoning an UnderReview row must be permitted; if the start page stops resuming it, the current refusal is correct and stays.
* No person can reach a page with no exit. Whichever branch is taken, an UnderReview row either is not landed on, or is landed on with an abandon control or the evidence form present.
* `systemTest/pages/kyc_verification_page.ts:109-122` — `ensureNoOpenVerification()` — no longer has a state that hangs it. Its own comment records the limit today (it waits for the start form or an abandon button and an UnderReview row shows neither, so it times out); after this, either that state is not reachable from the start page or the abandon button exists. The comment goes when the limit does.
* **xUnit covers the lifecycle rule** — the primary gate here, since this is a rule, not a surface: a table-driven test over all statuses asserting `IsOpen`, `IsResumable` and the Details `IsOpen` flag agree, so a future status added to one list and not the other is red immediately. [PS-970](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-970>)'s UnderReview service case is the companion and should land first or alongside.

**Playwright test — required, but blocked, and the block must be stated not worked around.** UnderReview is **not reachable** in dev today: `MockKycProvider.cs:29` hard-codes `RequiresManualReview = false`, so no journey through `/identity/verify` can produce the row this ticket is about. Once [PS-965](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-965>)'s dev-only failure-injecting assessor exists, extend `systemTest/tests/functional/kyc_verification.spec.ts` (the `role-kyc` project, per-persona since #887) to assert, as that worker's own persona:

1. drive a verification to **UnderReview** via the injected review outcome;
2. navigate to `/identity/verify` and assert the landing matches the ruling — either the start page with its own form, or `/identity/verify/{id}`;
3. on whichever page is landed on, assert there **is a way forward**: the start form, or on Details an abandon control — `kyc-under-review` is rendered **and** an exit exists beside it;
4. assert the row is still listed in `kyc-history` with status UnderReview, so "give them a way out" was not implemented by quietly closing the review.

**Which assertion fails today:** 3. With the row forced into UnderReview, Details renders `kyc-under-review` with neither the evidence form nor Cancel — the person is on a page they can only leave by navigating away, which is the whole ticket. Assertion 2 is the one that encodes the decision and so cannot be written before it is made.

**Control assertions that pass today and must keep passing:** a Pending or InProgress verification is still resumed by the start page and still offers the evidence form and Cancel on Details — `OpenVerificationForAsync` exists for that and the fix must not disable resuming in general; and a settled (Approved / Rejected / Expired) row still offers no evidence form, which is correct.

Do **not** write the spec against a faked UnderReview row to unblock it — that tests the fake. Until [PS-965](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-965>) lands, the xUnit lifecycle test is the gate, and this ticket should say so on its PR rather than attach a run that never exercised the state.

nodes.body: **Parked. Stuart's decision, 5 Nov 2026:** native KYC has had no assessor since `64525ac`, so this waits until one returns. The evidence routes on hosted rows are fixed separately under PS-965.

title: PR template still says to dispatch pre-merge-platform-suites.yml and has no Test Evidence block; CONTRIBUTING's Test Evidence template has drifted from DEV-PROCESS
description:
## Summary

For when you have a moment, Stuart. Two small bits of drift in the merge-flow paperwork you own, spotted while preparing the [KS-1354](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1354/bump-systemtest-k6-210-230-grafanak6-v220-v230-released) PR. The PR template still suggests dispatching the retired `pre-merge-platform-suites.yml` and has no Test Evidence block. And the Test Evidence templates in `CONTRIBUTING.md` and `DEV-PROCESS.md` have drifted apart. Nothing has been changed. Thank you.

+++ Evidence (develop `63db8a383`, 2026-09-28) and what "done" could look like

**1.** `.github/pull_request_template.md` **and the adopted merge flow**

* It asks authors to dispatch `pre-merge-platform-suites.yml`. Root `CLAUDE.md` (*Merge flow*), `Blockchain/Dev/docs/DEV-PROCESS.md` and [KS-441](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-441/akto-ci-scan-throughput-21-s-local-vs-10-min-in-the-isolated-pr-akto) say not to: Actions is retired, and the gate is a local four-suite run.
* It has no Test Evidence block (touched / ran / NOT run / migrations+config), which the merge flow relies on. `grep -ci 'Test Evidence' .github/pull_request_template.md` → **0**.

**2. The two Test Evidence templates**

`DEV-PROCESS.md` says it uses the same wording as `CONTRIBUTING.md`, but:

* `grep -c 'Cross-cutting guards' Blockchain/Dev/docs/DEV-PROCESS.md` → **2**
* `grep -c 'Cross-cutting guards' Blockchain/Dev/CONTRIBUTING.md` → **0**

`CONTRIBUTING.md` also lacks DEV-PROCESS's Schemathesis "failing SET + diff vs develop" wording.

**Why here:** it belongs to the process [KS-685](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-685/define-the-work-test-commit-manual-merge-process-while-ci-is) set up (now Deployed to UAT), so there was no open ticket to add it to.

**Related:** [KS-1049](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1049/a-prs-test-evidence-must-state-whether-the-preflight-ran-the-hook) (Kamil — Test Evidence should say whether the preflight ran; the template would be its home) · [KS-1012](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1012/the-require-pr-gates-ruleset-survived-the-actions-retirement-7) (the `require-pr-gates` ruleset outlived Actions).

**Done when**

- [ ] The PR template no longer mentions dispatching the retired workflow.
- [ ] The PR template seeds the Test Evidence block, including a preflight-ran line ([KS-1049](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1049/a-prs-test-evidence-must-state-whether-the-preflight-ran-the-hook)).
- [ ] `CONTRIBUTING.md` and `DEV-PROCESS.md` share one Test Evidence template (one canonical copy; the other points at it).

+++

title: Spec: 85 of 145 request bodies are not marked `required: true`, so Schemathesis sends "valid" empty bodies the handlers reject — 17 ops, 35 cases per sweep, 15 of them baselined against Done KS-255
description:
## Summary

One for the spec when convenient, Kamil. 85 of the spec's 145 request bodies aren't marked `required: true`, so Schemathesis reasonably sends "valid" requests with no body at all, and 17 operations answer 400 (35 cases per sweep). It isn't a blanket fix: 23 operations happily accept an empty body. So the likely shape is marking `required: true` where the Zod schema rejects an absent body. 15 of these pairs are still baselined against [KS-255](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-255/fix-tighten-openapi-request-schemas-add-400-responses-for-12-endpoints), which is closed, so this would give them a live home. Thank you.

+++ Full evidence

**Sweep 4** (slot 3, seed 1353, 4.28.0, toml loaded): 85 operations with a non-required `requestBody`; 40 were sent a no-body positive case (237 cases); **17 operations / 35 cases** failed `positive_data_acceptance`.

| `POST /api/nft/verify/asset` | 1 | 400 | [KS-255](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-255/fix-tighten-openapi-request-schemas-add-400-responses-for-12-endpoints) (Done) |
| `POST /api/nft/verify/transaction` | 2 | 400 | [KS-255](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-255/fix-tighten-openapi-request-schemas-add-400-responses-for-12-endpoints) (Done) |
| `POST /api/onedrive/files/{id}/sync` | 5 | 400 | [KS-255](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-255/fix-tighten-openapi-request-schemas-add-400-responses-for-12-endpoints) (Done) |
| `POST /api/referrals/generate` | 2 | 400 | [KS-255](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-255/fix-tighten-openapi-request-schemas-add-400-responses-for-12-endpoints) (Done) |

Example, `POST /api/billing/checkout/custom` (all four sweeps): body `null` → 400 `"path":["quantity"],"message":"Required"`.

**Direction:** mark `requestBody.required: true` where the handler's Zod schema rejects an absent body, at the generator (`*.openapi.ts` → `npm run generate-openapi`). Optionally, a spec-lint rule: a body whose schema has a non-empty `required` list must itself be `required: true`.

Related: [KS-255](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-255/fix-tighten-openapi-request-schemas-add-400-responses-for-12-endpoints) (Done) · [KS-591](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-591/positive-data-acceptance-recurs-at-scale-734-failures-across-64-ops-ks) · [KS-1015](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1015/sweeps-2026-09-08-28-checkoperation-pairs-have-no-live-owner-18) (finding 2) · [KS-1361](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1361/schemathesis-baselinejson-lags-the-linear-registers-37-of-90-failing).

nodes.body:
**One more operation in this class: `POST /api/identity-credentials/issue`** (not in this ticket's list or KS-1705's).

**Evidence is attached to this ticket** (Resources: *"Evidence: POST /api/identity-credentials/issue, failed vs passed run (2026-10-26)"*). The file holds every case Schemathesis sent to this operation in both runs: request, response and every check result. Credentials are redacted; nothing else is edited. It includes the failing case, the control's passing stateful case, and every no-body request from both runs.

**Measured 2026-10-26** on Peter's Mac, Schemathesis 4.32.1, `pre-merge`, platform-k slot 1, run `pre-merge-ks-955-2026-10-26T16-33-38Z-slot1`, seed 1833334654. That run was on the KS-955 branch, which does not touch the spec or this service.

- The published spec does not mark this operation's request body required (`requestBody.required` is unset). Schemathesis therefore treats a request with no body as valid.
- In the stateful phase it sent exactly that and got a 400. It reported ST202 `positive_data_acceptance` (case `a5Fnkw`):

```
curl -X POST -H 'Authorization: [Filtered]' http://localhost:6882/api/identity-credentials/issue
→ 400 {"success":false,"error":{"code":"BAD_REQUEST","message":"Validation error: Required, Required"}}
```

## Failed run against passing run: every request this operation received

I compared the KS-955 run (failed) with a develop control the same day (passed). The control ran on platform-k slot 2, built from develop `ec3313a80`, seed 1543992972, run `pre-merge-2026-10-26T17-19-41Z-slot2`.

Every case Schemathesis sent to this operation, read from each run's own `schemathesis-output.ndjson`. Requests are grouped by phase, generation mode, whether a body was sent, and the status returned:

| Phase | Mode | Body | Status | KS-955 run (failed) | Control (passed) |
| -- | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- |
| coverage | negative | body | 400 | 48 | 48 |
| coverage | negative | body | 401 | 1 | 1 |
| coverage | negative | **no body** | **400** | 1 | 1 |
| coverage | positive | body | 201 | 22 | 22 |
| coverage | positive | body | 415 | 2 | 2 |
| examples | positive | body | 201 | 1 | 1 |
| examples | positive | body | 401 | 2 | 2 |
| fuzzing | negative | body | 400 | 1 | 3 |
| fuzzing | negative | body | 401 | 1 | 0 |
| fuzzing | positive | body | 201 | 4 | 3 |
| **stateful** | **positive** | **no body** | **400** | **1 → ST202 (case `a5Fnkw`)** | 0 |
| stateful | positive | body | 201 | 0 | 1 |

**What this shows:**

- The API answered the same request the same way in both runs. A request with no body got **400** every time (coverage phase, both runs). A valid body got **201** every time.
- The **only** difference is what the stateful phase generated. In the KS-955 run it sent a positive case with **no body**, and because the spec does not require a body, Schemathesis expected a 2xx and flagged the 400. In the control it sent a body and got 201.
- The handler is right to refuse an empty body; the spec is what needs changing. The failure depends on the seed: the same item also appeared in develop runs on 2026-10-21.

**Suggested fix (this ticket's direction):** mark `requestBody.required: true` for this operation in its `*.openapi.ts`, then `npm run generate-openapi`.

**BLUF:** one more operation belongs to this class, not in the table above: `POST /api/timestamps/verify`. Peter asked for it to be added here.

**Measured on 2026-10-16** (slot 2, develop `a92f46e14`, Schemathesis 4.31.1, `pre-merge`): `positive_data_acceptance::POST /api/timestamps/verify` fired. A bodyless request (`curl -X POST …/api/timestamps/verify`, no `-d`) answered **400** `"hash: Required"`. It is the only one of that run's 82 failing pairs that is **not** in `config/schemathesis-baseline.json`; the hand-run baseline gate showed it, since KS-752 still skips the gate.

**Verified from source:**
- `services/timestamping/src/timestamping.openapi.ts:458-463` registers the body with **no `required: true`**.
- The two sibling routes in the same file do mark it (`:309`, `:347`).
- The handler parses with zod (`services/timestamping/src/index.ts:413`), and `TimestampVerifyRequest` requires `hash`, `proof` and `timestampType`.

So the fix is exactly this ticket's direction: `required: true` at the generator, then `npm run generate-openapi`.

**Proposed acceptance criterion for this operation:** after the fix, a test demonstrates it. A targeted Schemathesis `positive_data_acceptance` run on `POST /api/timestamps/verify` no longer fires, and the spec-lint rule suggested above (a body whose schema has a non-empty `required` list must itself be `required: true`) would catch it. Thank you.

**One more operation in this class, 2026-10-07 (KS-1414 runs; platform-k slot 3, Mac, Schemathesis 4.29.4, seed 1414):** `negative_data_rejection::POST /api/documents/{id}/revoke`, **1** case in `full-ks-1414-2026-10-07T11-40-31Z-slot3`, on a stack rebuilt from `develop` `2c27ddfee`. Only the body was negative, no body was sent, and the platform answered 200. The spec's `requestBody` for this operation is not `required` (read from `secuura-api.yaml`), so the sent request was valid, which is this ticket's mechanism. The KS-1414 classifier counts it under "no body (KS-1364 class)": 2 such cases in that run. It wasn't drawn in the two earlier runs that day, so this is a sample, not a measurement. Thank you, Kamil. Posted by agent on Peter's behalf.

## 2026-10-05 (KS-1408 sweeps, Schemathesis 4.29.3): five more operations in this class

**BLUF.** Since this ticket is in progress, Kamil, here's what the 4.29.3 sweeps added to its class: two more operations that **reject** an absent body the spec allows, and three that **accept** an absent body which Schemathesis's `negative_data_rejection` treats as invalid. None of the five specs marks `requestBody.required`. Thank you.

>>> Evidence (slot 4, `develop` `46c3e20cf`, seed 1408)

**Rejects a no-body positive case (`positive_data_acceptance`, 400):**

| Operation | `requestBody.required` | 4.28.0 | 4.29.3 | re-run |
| -- | -- | -- | -- | -- |
| `POST /api/identity-credentials/issue` | not set | 0 | 1 | 1 |
| `PUT /api/nft/admin/platform-fee` | not set | 0 | 1 | 1 |

**Accepts a no-body "negative" case (`negative_data_rejection`, 2xx):**

| Operation | `requestBody.required` | 4.28.0 | 4.29.3 | re-run |
| -- | -- | -- | -- | -- |
| `POST /api/did` | not set | 0 | 1 | 1 |
| `PATCH /api/webhooks/{id}` | not set | 0 | 1 | 2 |
| `POST /api/documents/{id}/revoke` | `false` | 0 | 3 | 0 |

The second group is the mirror image. The published contract permits omitting the body, so these aren't the platform accepting invalid input against the spec. Whether each body *should* be required is this ticket's per-operation decision, same as the 23 operations already noted that accept an empty body.

Run directories: `systemTest/schemathesis/output/reports/full-ks-1408-2026-10-05T09-32-24Z-slot4`, `…T10-23-55Z-slot4`.

title: OAuth rotate-secret: the 200 response omits the declared `id` — first reached by a sweep on 2026-09-28
description:
## Summary

When you get a chance, Kamil. On the one sweep that reached it, a successful `POST /api/oauth/apps/{id}/rotate-secret` returned a 200 without the `id` the published schema lists. It only shows up when a sweep happens to draw a valid app id (1 of 6 sweeps), so a small create-rotate-check test would be a steadier guard than the sweep. Adding `id` to the rotate response, or a rotate-specific schema if the narrower shape is intended, would settle it. Thank you.

+++ Full evidence

| Sweep | Cases | Statuses | Failing |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| 1: 4.27.5 | 27 | 401×5, 400×22 | `positive_data_acceptance` ×22 |
| 2: 4.28.0 | 27 | 401×5, 400×22 | `positive_data_acceptance` ×22 |
| 3: + deps | 49 | 401×31, 400×7, **200×11** | `positive_data_acceptance` ×7, `response_schema_conformance` **×11 (11 of 11 200s)** |
| 4: toml loaded | 27 | 401×20, 400×5, 404×2 | `positive_data_acceptance` ×5; no 200 reached |

(Cases exclude undeclared-method probes.)
