title: KS-962 seed-idempotence suite skips all 27 cells on hosts without Postgres binaries — would an opt-in Docker runner help it run anywhere?
description:
## Summary

No rush at all on this one, Kamil. The [KS-962](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-962/the-api-gateway-user-seed-throws-42p10-on-every-boot-and-has-never) seed-idempotence suite (`ks949_main_seed_idempotence.test.sh`) skips all 27 of its cells on any machine without Postgres binaries, and it does so honestly and loudly, exactly as designed. The only gap is that on such hosts the guard never runs. An opt-in Docker runner might let it run anywhere, but it's your suite, so whichever approach you'd prefer is the one to go with. Happy to help build or test it.

+++ Details and options

**Observed 2026-09-28** during the [KS-1353](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1353/bump-systemtest-schemathesis-pin-4275-4280-first-minor-since-427x-9) preflight: `SKIP — no PostgreSQL binaries (initdb pg_ctl postgres psql) found; … 0/27 cells run`. Shell suites 59 passed, 0 failed, 1 skipped (of 60).

**What the suite needs** (read from the file): the Postgres binaries (via `KS949_PG_BIN`, then the Homebrew / Debian paths); Node ≥18, tsx and a built `packages/shared`; and auth's path includes the native `argon2`, so a macOS `node_modules` can't simply be mounted into Linux.

**One possible shape:** an opt-in container runner (Postgres 15 + Node, repo mounted read-only, `node_modules` in a named volume), off by default (e.g. `KS949_PG_DOCKER=1`). The suite already searches `/usr/lib/postgresql/15/bin`, so it would need no change itself.

**Other options, equally welcome:** connect to an already-running Postgres instead of `initdb`; reuse the stack's own `postgres` container; or document `brew install postgresql@15` as a prerequisite. (Not suggested: wrapping `pg_ctl` into a container, because Postgres's 0700 data-dir check is fragile across Docker Desktop's bind mounts.)

No defect was found; this is a coverage gap on Postgres-less hosts. Related: [KS-962](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-962/the-api-gateway-user-seed-throws-42p10-on-every-boot-and-has-never) · [KS-1353](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1353/bump-systemtest-schemathesis-pin-4275-4280-first-minor-since-427x-9).

+++

title: Stack tooling is not slot-derived end to end: stack_guard lists a project twice under mixed marker labels, dev-reload.sh / start-local.sh bypass stack_env.sh, and compose defaults FRONTEND_URL / CORS_ORIGINS to slot 1
description:
## Summary

For when you have a moment, Kamil; it matters most on a busy host. A few pieces of stack tooling still assume slot 1 instead of deriving from `SECUURA_STACK_SLOT`, so on slots 2–4 they can double-report a stack, miss its containers, carry slot-1 URLs, or preflight the wrong gateway. Each fix is small and follows the existing `stack_env.sh` pattern. The four spots are below. Thank you.

+++ The four spots, evidence and fix shapes

1. `stack_guard.sh` `list_other_stacks` **(lines 105–111)** reports one line per label tuple (`sort -u` on `project|owner|branch`), so a project with one `owner=unknown` container (the [KS-1011](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1011/ks-666-stack-marker-reads-unknown-for-ownerbranchcommitstarted-at) case) shows up twice. *Fix:* group by project and append an `unknown` count; add a case to `scripts/__tests__/stack_guard.test.sh`.
2. `dev-reload.sh` **(**`:45` `CONTAINER="secuura-$SVC"`**) and** `start-local.sh` don't source `stack_env.sh`, so they only find slot 1's containers and stamp `unknown` markers on anything they create. *Fix:* source `stack_env.sh` and use `${STACK_PREFIX}` (or retire `start-local.sh` if unused); extend `check-stack-safety.sh` so every script running `docker compose up|run|restart` must source it.
3. `docker-compose.yml` **defaults** `FRONTEND_URL` (`:767`) and `CORS_ORIGINS` (`:503`, `:2179`) to slot 1's ports. *Fix:* derive them from the exported `GATEWAY_PORT` / `WEBSITE_PORT`, so an unedited `.env` is right on every slot; pin it in `stack_env.test.sh` or `check-stack-safety.sh`.
4. **The** [KS-380](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-380/harden-the-pre-release-gate-required-checks-on-develop-preflight) **preflight's PROVISIONED legs** default to `:6882` (`preflight.sh:94`). On a slot-N worktree they probe slot 1 unless `GATEWAY_URL` is passed. *Fix:* derive from `SECUURA_STACK_SLOT` via `stack_env.sh`, and fail loudly with an example command when no slot is named locally.

**Seen 2026-09-28** (Peter's Mac, `develop` `d9ce1403d`), bringing up slot 4 with slots 2 and 3 running:

```
Other Secuura stacks running on this host (NOT affected by this operation):
  secuura_slot2 — owner peterdouglas, branch feature/ks-1286-…
  secuura_slot3 — owner peterdouglas, branch feature/ks-1353-…
  secuura_slot3 — owner unknown, branch unknown
```

The `owner unknown` container came from a bare `docker compose` call in the [KS-1353](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1353/bump-systemtest-schemathesis-pin-4275-4280-first-minor-since-427x-9) worktree at about 09:33 UTC. That's the same mechanism as spot 2, reached by hand, and slot 3 was restored through `start-secuura.sh` afterwards.

**Verify:** the guard prints a mixed-label project once; `SECUURA_STACK_SLOT=N ./scripts/dev-reload.sh api-gateway` finds `${STACK_PREFIX}-api-gateway`; an untouched `.env` renders slot-N URLs (`docker compose config`); the preflight probes slot N; `check-stack-safety.sh` goes red on a revert of any of the four.

Related: [KS-1011](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1011/ks-666-stack-marker-reads-unknown-for-ownerbranchcommitstarted-at) (unknown markers; PR [Secuura/Distributed_Secuura#1181](https://linear.app/secuura/review/ks-1011-markerwarn-start-secuurash-warns-loud-and-named-on-unknown-bc1340b4bef0) warns in `start-secuura.sh` only) · [KS-666](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-666/prevent-destructive-rebuilds-of-the-shared-vm-stack-from-destroying) (slot design) · [KS-1034](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1034/check-stack-safetysh-resolves-the-wrong-repo-root-inside-a-git-hook) · [KS-1373](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1373/schemathesis-full-run-named-slot-3-but-871-of-its-requests-incl) (the same slot-derivation theme, harness side).

+++

## Shared acceptance — slot derivation group (added 6 Oct 2026)

This ticket is one of five platform-k tickets that must all take slot values from `stack_env.sh` and never fall back to slot 1: [KS-1355](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1355>), [KS-1381](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1381>), [KS-1389](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1389>), [KS-1382](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1382>), [KS-1162](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1162>). None of them is done until these hold, in addition to its own acceptance above:

1. **One guard.** A single static guard in `check-stack-safety.sh` fails on any literal published port of any slot 1–4 outside `stack_env.sh`. The first ticket to land creates it; the others extend it; nobody adds a second guard. Bite-checked: plant a literal, see it red, remove it.
2. **No silent default.** A local run with no slot named refuses and prints an example command; it never falls back to slot 1 (preflight, `slot-target.sh`, the `Blockchain/Testing` entry points, the smoke scripts). Any change to `stack_env.sh`'s own slot-1 default re-runs every test in this group.
3. **One preflight change.** [KS-1355](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1355/stack-tooling-is-not-slot-derived-end-to-end-stack-guard-lists-a) (spot 4, `preflight.sh:94`) and [KS-1389](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1389/sourcing-systemtestslot-targetsh-with-no-slot-named-silently-exports) (leg 13, `preflight.sh:589-630`) land in one PR, or one after the other, each re-running the other's checks.
4. **The workflow question.** [KS-1162](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1162/three-retired-github-workflows-bake-slot-234-port-literals) decides first whether the three workflows are deleted or made to derive their ports. If deleted, [KS-1382](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1382/blockchaintesting-five-auditdasttenant-isolation-entry-points-default)'s "explicit `TARGET_BASE` is used unchanged" criterion has no CI caller left; if derived, their `TARGET_BASE` comes from `stack_env.sh` too.
5. **Tests cover every slot.** Slots 1–4, hermetic: identical results unslotted and under each slot's environment.

**This ticket's part:** points 1, 2 and 3 — the spot-3 pin in `check-stack-safety.sh` is a natural home for the point-1 guard, and spot 4 is coordinated with [KS-1389](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1389/sourcing-systemtestslot-targetsh-with-no-slot-named-silently-exports)'s leg 13.

All are ancestors of the kintsugi deploy b1fb543640e7 (2026-11-01). Verified by git log (each squash names KS-1355 and is reachable from b1fb543640e7); the behaviour was not run here. ## Correction to my own box-render claim — it was too strongly worded (the conclusion is unchanged)

My merged comment, PR #1526's body and the squash body all say, of `GATEWAY_PORT`, `WEBSITE_PORT`,
`FRONTEND_URL` and `CORS_ORIGINS`, that **"no record in the K lane's reach names any box's values"**.
A wider sweep I had started earlier and only read after the merge shows that is too strong.

**What the records actually say.** Searching all of `5_Project_History` (not just the D-seat
records and kintsugi handovers I used before the commit) finds the four names in 2299 / 868 / 249 /
353 files. Almost all are push logs, `history.md` copies and scratch repo trees — the repo's own
text, not box readings. Two are real deploy records, and **both describe the retired Container Apps
estate, not the VM**:

- `history.md` **2026-05-02** — "Demo + Dev `CORS_ORIGINS` expanded to include `outlook.office.com`,
  `outlook.office365.com`, `outlook.cloud.microsoft`, plus the per-env outlook FQDN", with a config
  table row "`CORS_ORIGINS` | full list incl. outlook.office.* … | matched to demo". Applied through
  `services.bicep` / `deploy.sh`.
- `history.md` **2026-06-29 (KS-344)** — m365's `FRONTEND_URL` was unset on demo and was **set to
  the admin portal host in `services.bicep`** (env-only, no image rebuild), verified live as
  `secuura02-demo-m365` carrying `FRONTEND_URL=https://secuura02-demo-admin…`.

Both are **Container Apps** configuration, and those 24 apps plus `secuura02-demo-env` were
**deleted on 2026-07-31**. `services.bicep` has no bearing on the current VM, where
`DEPLOYMENT-ARCHITECTURE.md:105` makes the box's own `.env` authoritative.

**The precise claim, restated:** no record names the **current VM's** values for those four keys.
The records that do exist describe the **retired** Container Apps estate and were applied by a
mechanism that no longer runs.

**Why this does not change the conclusion, and mildly improves it.** The VM's values are still
UNMEASURED, so the next deploy round must still diff `docker compose config` before and after on
each box — that condition stands unchanged. And it cuts slightly in the safe direction: this
platform's deploy history shows these keys being set **explicitly** when they matter, and an
explicit value **wins** over the compose default, so a box that carries one is unaffected by this
change. The unslotted render also remains byte-identical to the base
(`2daa06e430f2e651…`), which is the stronger guarantee for any box naming no slot.

Disclosed rather than left standing, because the loose wording is in a merged squash body where it
cannot be edited. Nothing to re-do; the measurement that mattered (`env.example` cannot reach a box)
is unaffected and had its own positive controls.

title: Hash-only remote signing endpoint (deferred PAdES signing)
description:
## Why

For Secuura never to see the unencrypted file, the browser has to prepare the PDF itself. Secuura then signs **only the digest**. Today `PdfProcessingService.SignDocumentAsync` loads and decrypts the whole document server-side and signs it with iText `PdfSigner.SignDetached`.

This endpoint is the server half of standard deferred/remote PAdES signing:

1. **Client:** adds a signature field and placeholder (`/ByteRange`, `/Contents`), then computes the SHA-256 of the byte ranges.
2. **Server (this ticket):** receives that digest. It builds the CAdES/CMS `SignedData`:
   * signed attributes: content-type, message-digest, signing-certificate-v2
   * signs with the org or personal key
   * adds a TSA timestamp token, which is also taken over a hash
   * returns the DER-encoded CMS
3. **Client:** injects the CMS into `/Contents`.

The server never receives the document, only 32 bytes.

## Scope

* **API endpoint**, e.g. `POST /api/sign/digest`, authenticated.
  * Inputs: document id, digest (hex/base64), digest algorithm, certificate choice (personal, org or system, the same rules as today), reason, location.
  * Returns: the CMS blob plus the certificate chain for the visible appearance.
  * **Format-agnostic (Project See follow-up, 29 Sep 2026):** the endpoint signs a digest and returns a CAdES `SignedData`. It must carry **no PDF assumptions**: no byte-range semantics, no `/Contents` sizing, no PDF-specific inputs. The same CMS is what a detached CAdES signature in an ASiC container needs for non-PDF objects ([PS-987](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-987/signable-object-abstraction-embedded-padesooxml-wrapped-asic-detached)). The client decides whether to inject it into a PDF or package it.
* **Same authorisation and gates as** `Sign.cs` `SignDoc`:
  * owner / rights-holder / org-admin
  * `IActionAssuranceGate`
  * Entra verified-signer enforcement
  * the "already signed" check
* **CMS building**: use BouncyCastle, which is already a dependency via iText, or iText's `IExternalSignatureContainer` / `PdfPKCS7`.
* **Key access**: go through the signing abstraction from [PS-946](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-946/move-pdf-signing-keys-into-azure-key-vault-hsm), so this works with the current PFX providers now and with Key Vault later.
* **TSA**: reuse `PdfSigningOptions.TsaUrl` / `RequireTsa` behaviour, including the fallback rules.
* **Ledger**: record the Sign transaction. The ContentHash comes from the client-reported final hash, which the client submits after injection, so the endpoint also needs a "complete" call (`POST /api/sign/complete`) carrying the final SHA-256.
* **Replay/abuse**:
  * bind each digest request to a short-lived, single-use signing session per document
  * rate-limit
  * log every signature issued

## Proving it before the browser work exists

* Add a server-side test harness that does the client role with iText: prepare the placeholder, hash, call the endpoint, inject. Assert that the result validates in `PdfSignatureVerificationService` and in Adobe Reader.
* xUnit: CMS structure, signed attributes, the message-digest match, TSA present/absent, and authorisation refusal cases.

## Out of scope

* The browser-side preparation and injection (a separate ticket once the library choice is made).
* Any PDF-specific behaviour in the endpoint itself. Byte-range logic stays entirely on the client so the CMS is reusable for wrapped (ASiC / detached CAdES) signatures over non-PDF objects.
* Moving the keys themselves ([PS-946](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-946/move-pdf-signing-keys-into-azure-key-vault-hsm)).

## Done when

* The endpoint produces a signature that validates in Adobe Reader and in our verifier when driven by the harness.
* Authorisation parity with `SignDoc` is covered by tests.
* An xUnit test signs an arbitrary non-PDF digest and the returned CMS validates as a detached CAdES signature over that content, proving the endpoint is not PDF-bound.
* Full systemTest run attached to the PR and this ticket.
* Peter reviews, with a deep review for security/crypto.

## Acceptance

* `POST /api/sign/digest` accepts a document id, a digest, a digest algorithm and a certificate choice, and returns a DER-encoded CAdES `SignedData` plus the certificate chain — and **nothing in its request or response names a byte range,** `/Contents`**, a page or any other PDF concept**. A reader of the endpoint's signature cannot tell it was built for PDFs.
* The CMS carries the three signed attributes named above (content-type, message-digest, signing-certificate-v2), its message-digest equals the digest that was submitted, and a TSA token is present when `PdfSigningOptions.RequireTsa` is on and absent-with-the-documented-fallback when it is off.
* Authorisation parity with `Sign.cs` `SignDoc` is exact: owner / rights-holder / org-admin, `IActionAssuranceGate`, Entra verified-signer enforcement and the already-signed check all refuse through this endpoint the same way they refuse through the MVC action — one refusal case each, asserted, not asserted collectively.
* A digest request is bound to a short-lived, single-use signing session for that one document: replaying the same session token is refused, and a session issued for document A cannot sign a digest presented for document B.
* `POST /api/sign/complete` records the Sign transaction with the client-reported final SHA-256, and a missing or mismatched complete call leaves no half-written ledger row.
* The harness round trip holds: placeholder → hash → endpoint → inject produces a PDF that `PdfSignatureVerificationService` reports as valid, and that Adobe Reader also accepts (recorded as an observation with the Reader version, since it is a manual check).
* Private key material is reached only through the [PS-946](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-946/move-pdf-signing-keys-into-azure-key-vault-hsm) abstraction, and no key, passphrase or digest-session secret appears in any log line, error message or test failure — config keys are named (`PdfSigning:PfxPath`, `PdfSigning:PfxPassword`), values never are.

**Why no Playwright test applies**: the subject here is a **server-side cryptographic endpoint with no screen**. It is reached by a machine caller, its inputs are 32 bytes and its output is a DER blob; the browser half that would eventually call it is explicitly out of scope on this ticket. Per the platform convention, a rule belongs in the xUnit suite — and every claim above is a rule. A browser journey could only prove that `/Sign` still works, which is a regression control the existing `sign.spec.ts` / `sign_form.spec.ts` already provide and which the full-suite gate run already covers.

The criteria that stand in for it, all in `tests/ssd.UnitTests`:

1. **CMS structure and attributes** — parse the returned `SignedData` and assert each signed attribute, the digest algorithm, and that the message-digest attribute equals the submitted digest.
2. **Tamper test that must throw** — flip one bit of the submitted digest and assert the resulting CMS does **not** validate against the original content.
3. **Format-agnostic proof** — sign the SHA-256 of an arbitrary **non-PDF** byte array and assert the returned CMS validates as a detached CAdES signature over exactly those bytes. This is the test that fails today, because today's only signing path is `PdfProcessingService.SignDocumentAsync`, which loads and decrypts a whole PDF.
4. **Control that must keep passing** — the existing `PdfProcessingService.SignDocumentAsync` tests and the `/Sign` MVC path stay green and unchanged, proving the endpoint was added beside the current signer rather than in place of it.
5. **Authorisation refusals** — one test per gate listed above, each asserting a typed refusal rather than an empty or partial response.

Context: Project See feasibility review, and [Combining A and B, bring-your-own-storage, and signable objects](<https://linear.app/secuura/document/combining-a-and-b-bring-your-own-storage-and-signable-objects-58bd00082339>) §3.

nodes.body:
PS-1053 (Document Signing Formats) is investigating browser and device signing. Its design is this ticket's: prepare on the server, a raw signature over a digest in the browser or device or HSM, then finalise on the server, for PAdES, detached CAdES and the Office package signature.

Its brief now also carries Project See's question: whether prepare and finalise can work from hashes alone, so the server never holds the plaintext. Its findings and phase plan should answer this ticket's design questions, so they aren't investigated twice. Pick this one up once PS-1053's recommendation is in.

Note from the signing-formats work: with PS-1057's `EmbedPdf` off, a PDF signs as a detached CAdES `.p7s`. That signature needs only the file's hash, which the browser already computes for Verify. The deferred PAdES path is then needed only where an embedded PDF signature is wanted.

Cross-link from the SDK project (PS-971, 2026-09-29): the SDK architecture v0.2 (§12.1, PR [#890](https://github.com/Secuura/platform-s/pull/890)) defines `documents.sign` with a `digest` server mode that is exactly this ticket's digest + complete pair — single-use signing session per document, `SignDoc`'s authorisation and gates, final hash reported on complete. It proposes the endpoints live under the SDK route family (`POST /api/sdk/v1/documents/{id}/sign/digest` and `…/sign/complete`) so they are built once and serve the web, Flutter, iOS and Android bindings as well as the browser. Open question 7 on PS-971 asks Stuart whether to re-scope this ticket that way; no change made here.

title: Move PDF signing keys into Azure Key Vault / HSM
description:
## Why

Signing private keys currently live in the app's own storage and are decrypted into application memory to sign:

* **System default certificate**: a PFX on disk at `PdfSigningOptions.PfxPath` (`PfxSigningKeyProvider`).
* **Organisation certificates**: `EncryptedPfxData` and `EncryptedPassword` in the DB, decrypted by `SigningKeyProtector` (`OrganisationCertificateProvider`).
* **Personal certificates**: same pattern (`PersonCertificateProvider`).

Anyone with the DB plus app secrets can extract every signing key. Moving keys into Key Vault, or a managed HSM with non-exportable keys, means the app asks the vault to sign a digest and never holds the private key.

This is worth doing whichever Project See option we choose, and it's the foundation for the hash-only signing endpoint.

## Scope / approach

* Introduce a signing abstraction that takes a **digest** plus a key reference and returns a signature. iText supports this via `IExternalSignature`.
* Implement it against Azure Key Vault (`CryptographyClient.SignAsync`, RS256/ES256). Evaluate Key Vault Premium or Managed HSM for FIPS 140-2 L3 non-exportable keys.
* Consider the AWS equivalent (KMS/CloudHSM) for the `dep-aws-*` deployments.
* **Import path for uploaded org and personal PFX**: import the key into the vault on upload, and store only the key id plus the certificate chain in the DB.
* **Migration** for existing `EncryptedPfxData` rows: import them, then wipe the local copy once verified.
* The system default certificate moves to the vault as well.
* Local/dev: keep a file-based provider behind config so stacks without Key Vault still work.
* Update `LiveConfigGuard` checks as needed.

## Open questions

* Key Vault Premium (HSM-backed) or Managed HSM? This is a cost versus compliance call.
* Do any customers need qualified (eIDAS/QSCD) signatures? That would affect the HSM choice.

## Done when

* No private signing key material is stored in the DB or on disk in deployed environments.
* Sign, watermark-then-sign and the automatic flow sign step all sign via the vault.
* xUnit coverage for the provider abstraction and the migration.
* Full systemTest run attached to the PR and this ticket.
* Peter reviews, with a deep review for security/crypto.

## Acceptance

* The two **open questions** are answered before the build starts, in writing on this ticket: Key Vault Premium or Managed HSM, and whether any customer needs qualified (eIDAS / QSCD) signatures. The second one can change the HSM choice, so it cannot be left until after the vault is provisioned.
* A signing abstraction exists that takes a **digest plus a key reference** and returns a signature, implemented as iText's `IExternalSignature`, and `PfxSigningKeyProvider`, `OrganisationCertificateProvider` and `PersonCertificateProvider` all sit behind it. No caller holds a private key.
* In a deployed environment, **no private signing key material is in the database or on disk**: an `az keyvault key show` / `az keyvault key list` observation for the key, plus a query showing `EncryptedPfxData` and `EncryptedPassword` are null for every migrated row, plus the absence of a PFX at the path `PdfSigningOptions.PfxPath` used to name. All three stated as observations with the environment and the date.
* All three signing paths go through the vault: `/Sign`, watermark-then-sign, and the automatic flow sign step. Each is named separately, because they are three call sites and a partial migration is the likely failure.
* The **PFX import path** works: uploading an org or personal PFX imports the key into the vault and the database keeps only the key id and the certificate chain. The uploaded bytes are not persisted anywhere after import.
* The **migration** of existing `EncryptedPfxData` rows imports, verifies by signing a test digest and comparing against a signature made the old way, and only then wipes the local copy. A failed verify leaves the old row intact.
* The **local/dev file provider** still works on a stack slot with no Key Vault, and `LiveConfigGuard` refuses it in a live deployment — a config that would run the file provider live fails startup rather than signing with a disk key.
* No passphrase, key, PFX password or vault secret appears in any log, error, test name or failure message. `PdfSigning:PfxPassword` and `AppSpecific:SigningKeyEncryptionKey` are named as keys; neither value is ever read into a ticket, a PR or output. Note that `AppSpecific:SigningKeyEncryptionKey` is in no tracked deployment template today, so the migration must state where it is provisioned before it runs.

**Why no Playwright test applies**: this is **key-management infrastructure**. The change is which component holds a private key and where the signing operation happens — inside the vault instead of in process memory. Nothing a browser can observe changes: `/Sign` looks and behaves exactly as it does today, and it must, or the ticket has regressed. Driving a browser here would assert only that signing still works, which is a regression control the existing specs already provide.

The criteria that stand in for it:

1. **xUnit on the abstraction**: a digest-plus-key-reference signature verifies against the certificate; an unknown key reference is a typed failure; the personal / organisation / system certificate-selection rules are unchanged from today's behaviour, asserted case by case.
2. **xUnit on the migration**: verify-before-wipe, resumability, and a forced verify failure leaving the original row untouched.
3. **Contract test on the live guard**: a live `DeployMode` plus the file provider fails `LiveConfigGuard`.
4. `az` **observations** for the three no-key-on-disk claims above — these are the only way to prove the goal of the ticket, and a PR without them has not shown it.
5. **Control that must keep passing**: `sign.spec.ts`, `sign_form.spec.ts`, `cross_user_signing.spec.ts`, `pdf_output.spec.ts` and `watermark_queue.spec.ts` are all green today and must stay green on the slot the gate runs on, together with the existing `PdfSignatureVerificationService` tests — a document signed through the vault must verify identically to one signed before the change.

Context: Project See feasibility review.

nodes.body:
**Key-handling review (10 Oct 2026)**

1. **The PFX import path exposes keys at upload.** As scoped, an org or personal PFX and its password are posted to the app, then imported into the vault. For that moment the private key and password are in app memory, where staff with app access could capture them. Options, best first: the customer imports straight into the vault (or a key is generated in the HSM and only a CSR leaves it, so the private key never exists outside the HSM); or the browser wraps the key for a vault import key, like PS-955's BYOK flow. Recommend generating keys in the HSM with a CSR as the default, and treating PFX upload as a legacy path with a stated warning.
2. **Using a key is the remaining risk.** Once keys are in the vault they can't be exported, but the app identity can still sign any digest. Add to acceptance: every signature issued is logged with document, actor and purpose and reconciled against the vault log (same pattern as the PS-957 comment), and the app identity has sign-only rights (PS-1085).
3. **The existing-row migration also passes keys through memory**: it decrypts `EncryptedPfxData` in-process to import it. That is unavoidable for legacy rows, but the migration should run as a one-off, audited job with a short-lived identity, not inside the serving app.

title: fail500 family: a non-Error throw is logged as [object Object], so its content is lost from the log
description:
## BLUF

The `fail500` family helper logs a **non-Error** throw as `'[object Object]'`, so the thrown object's content is **lost from the log** — the body stays correctly constant, but the diagnosability the helper exists to preserve is gone. Measured at runtime by the gate29 probe on the routes #1290 converted.

## Detail

`fail500(res, context, err)` logs `err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err)`. `String({...})` is `'[object Object]'`. So:

* an **Error** throw logs its message — correct;
* a **string** throw logs itself — correct;
* an **object** throw logs `[object Object]` — the content is gone.

At the merge-base neither kind leaked, because `err.message` on a non-Error is `undefined`; the helper is what made the log the only place the detail could live, and for objects it does not live there either.

**Fix shape:** in the family helper, log `err` itself, or `JSON.stringify` / `util.inspect` it for non-Errors.

**Family:** this is the same helper shape merged for KS730 in `routes/gdpr.ts` and `routes/systemErrors.ts`, so a fix belongs in all of them rather than in `webhooks.ts` alone.

## Also not pinned by the shipped cell (gate29 N-1290-3, measured: all green at head)

* (a) **non-Error throws** (string / object) on the three routes part B converted;
* (b) **rotate-secret throwing AFTER** `newSecret` **exists** — a rejected `$executeRaw` UPDATE, with the real `encryptField` and the key loaded. The gate probe drove this (S1) and measured the new secret **absent** from the 500 body and from every logger call, with a positive control — so today's behaviour is safe, but **no committed cell pins it**;
* (c) the **secret's absence from every log level** as an assertion.

## Done when

- [ ] the family helper preserves a non-Error throw's content in the log, in every file carrying the helper
- [ ] a cell pins a non-Error throw on at least one converted route
- [ ] a cell pins rotate-secret throwing after `newSecret` exists, asserting the secret is absent from the body and from every logger call

## Provenance

Gate29 report `2026-09-26-batch1290-g29/report.md` (sha256 `c3a273b3a582c088d3d088a3ac21a954c562ac8735cc679ec7979c12553f1e52`, measured by this seat), notes **N-1290-2** and **N-1290-3**; carries gate28's **N-1288-6**. Filed by the merging seat on that GO's instruction.

## Board search before filing

Literal match over **1335 issues (includeArchived) and 3780 comments**. Control token `b31nonce-9wq4tx-never-written` -> 0, while known terms returned hits, so the search discriminates in both directions. `[object Object]` -> 3 (KS-1341, which is this seat's own gate28 record that it was NOT filed; KS-744, a gateway/verificationLevel issue; KS-440 Done) — **none is this defect.**

Refs KS-1341

**Recorded for the reviewer, measured rather than asserted:** this file logs through `../utils/logger` (`gdpr.ts:22`), the service's own winston logger, which performs no redaction in any environment; the redacting logger in `packages/shared` is not on this path and keys off field names, so it would not reliably help even if it were. Consequently a thrown object now reaches the log with its contents — on a subject-data surface, where that object may carry the data subject's own identifiers. This is the intended effect of the ticket rather than a fault in the patch, but it is a real widening and the decision on it belongs above this seat. No ticket filed.

**Part A raised as [#1296](https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/1296), head `eff979b3d493b973aaa4f91defe2c58f960c3f11`. READY FOR QA. Not merged; nothing merges without a signed GO naming that head.** Facts only.

The redacting logger in `packages/shared` is not on this path, and would not reliably help if it were: it keys off the field NAME, and after `inspect()` the secret sits inside a string value under the key `error`, so a thrown object carrying an SSN and no email survives its rules. title: Multi-tenancy docs: eight non-blocking overstatements and Polish notes left by #1286's gate (N-1286-3..10)
description:
## BLUF

Eight non-blocking notes from the gate28 review of PR #1289's batch-mate #1286 (merged `7475697ce65e`), all in `Blockchain/Dev/docs/MULTI-TENANCY.md` (MT) and `Blockchain/Dev/docs/RLS-FAIL-CLOSED-PLAN.md` (RP). None was made worse by #1286's corrections; all were left deliberately because that PR's GO said to change nothing else.

## The notes, as the gate recorded them

* **N-1286-3** — "writes **every**" is overstated, at `MT:27` and `RP:47`. Provisioning writes the rest; the sentence describes the 8 seeded ids.
* **N-1286-4** — "the only tenant isolation that exists" is overstated, at `RP:54-55`. 21 service files also filter on `tenant_id`. #1286's new sentence about `MULTI_TENANCY_ENABLED` does not strengthen the claim, but does not fix it either.
* **N-1286-5** — `RP:60`, "plus any table not split per-tenant-DB", is still unmarked (it was `:57` in round 1).
* **N-1286-6** — "The deliberate exception" at `MT:32` is incomplete: it omits migration 039 §3's `secuura_auth_lookup` path.
* **N-1286-7** (Polish) — `MT:43`, "**This is the flag that actually gates per-tenant databases**, and it is off everywhere." Gating is TRUE; "off everywhere" is TRUE for the repository and **UNVERIFIABLE for live app settings** (no `az` in the gate). It re-widens the "in the repository" qualifier the neighbouring sentence had just added.
* **N-1286-8** (Polish) — `MT:40`, "a distinction the first version of this correction got wrong", is change-log prose about the correction itself. It will puzzle any reader who never saw the first version. Its home is the commit message, where it already is.
* **N-1286-9** (Polish) — `MT:44-47`, "ON in dev and demo": all three cites are exact, but "ON in dev and demo" is the whole set the deploy script can deploy, which is an understatement rather than a scope statement.
* **N-1286-10** (Polish) — `MT:152-153`, the onboarding cite is accurate enough; the granularity is loose (`:245-274` with the INSERT at `:271`, where the measured shape is `:245-257`, `platformQuery(` at `:271`, the INSERT at `:272`, close at `:275`).

## Done when

- [ ] N-1286-3 and N-1286-4's overstatements are narrowed to what the code does, at all four cites
- [ ] N-1286-5's caveat is marked
- [ ] N-1286-6 names the 039 §3 `secuura_auth_lookup` exception
- [ ] N-1286-7's "off everywhere" carries the same "in the repository" qualifier as its neighbour
- [ ] N-1286-8's self-referential sentence is removed from the reference document
- [ ] N-1286-9 and N-1286-10 are tightened or explicitly accepted as-is

## Provenance

Gate28 report `2026-09-26-batch1286-g28/report.md` (sha256 `760c86711baee5a5282ed9ddc6f172a34dbe7321e1f7f52c4574243ff6794909`, measured by this seat), the #1286 section. Filed by the merging seat on that GO's instruction; the gate files nothing.

## Board search before filing

Literal match over **1332 issues (includeArchived) and 3776 comments**: `MULTI-TENANCY.md` -> 2 (KS-1336 the parent, KS-300 Done); `RLS-FAIL-CLOSED-PLAN.md` -> 5 (KS-1336, KS-300, KS-174, KS-172, KS-160). None carries these eight notes. Control token `b31nonce-zqx7vk-never-written` -> 0, and the two doc paths returning 2 and 5 show the search is not blind in either direction.

Refs KS-1336

title: entrypoint-corpus guard: a parenthesised return of a guarded call reads `guarded:false`, and the file's own rule-3 comment claims both return shapes are covered
description:
**BLUF: the guard reads** `guarded:false` **for call shapes the file's own comment says it covers.** Its rule-3 comment states *"Both return shapes are covered: a concise arrow body, and an explicit* `return`*"* — yet `return (() => g())` and `() => (() => g())`, when called, both read `guarded:false`, while the truth and `develop` both read **true**. `(() => g()).call(null)` reads false as well, and is not named anywhere.

This is the residue of a capped round. Nothing shipped for it; the pull request that attempted it stays open and its disposition sits with the repository owner.

## What is wrong, precisely

The defect is **parenthesisation**. A guarded call wrapped in parentheses — whether returned explicitly or as a concise arrow body — is not recognised, so a correctly-guarded call site is reported as unguarded. The reading is wrong in the **unsafe-looking** direction: it accuses safe code.

Three shapes, measured at runtime:

| shape | guard reads | truth / develop |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `return (() => g())` then called | `guarded:false` | true |
| `() => (() => g())` then called | `guarded:false` | true |
| `(() => g()).call(null)` | `guarded:false` | true |

The third came from a call-shape table the round was commissioned to make **"read as the truth or be NAMED"**. It does neither: it reads false and is unnamed.

**Evidence produced by the gate:** `evidence/1268/probe_readings_head.jsonl`, rows 23, 40 and 41.

## Why this is its own ticket

It is the same defect **class** as the round's first attempt, which is why the round capped. The fix is a reader change: recognise a parenthesised expression as transparent when deciding whether the inner call is guarded, and either read `.call`/`.apply` invocation forms as the truth or name them as unsupported. **A guard whose own comment claims coverage it does not have is worse than one with a stated limit**, because the comment is what the next reader trusts.

## Not in this ticket

The round's other work — the `entrypoint-corpus.test.ts` change at blob `8a4ce36a3a96` — is sound and is being re-raised separately by its author. This ticket is only the reader defect.

## Board search before filing

Searched over **486 open issues** on this team, matching literally against identifier + title + description: `guarded:false`, `parenthesised`, `rule-3`, `concise arrow` — **0 open hits each**. `entrypoint-corpus` returned 3 (KS-1155, KS-1142, KS-1140), none of them this reader defect. Controls: a fresh nonsense token **0**, `ssrf-guard` **2**, so the instrument discriminates in both directions.

Refs KS-1316

title: k6 runner: the pre-suite path is taken from URL.pathname, so a checkout directory containing a space fails ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND
description:
## BLUF

`systemTest/performance/runner/cli.ts:162` resolves the pre-suite step with
`new URL('../../fixtures/pre-suite.ts', import.meta.url).pathname`. `URL.pathname` **is**
**percent-encoded.** A checkout whose directory contains a space yields `.../Testing%20Agent%20MAIN/...`,
which is passed to the spawn as a literal path, and the run dies with
`ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND … %2520 …` (the `%25` is the second round of encoding).

**This is not hypothetical on this fleet.** The QA gate's own checkout lives at
`/Volumes/DevMASTER/!CODING/Testing Agent MAIN/` — a path with **two spaces**. Any performance run
driven from a checkout like that cannot start its pre-suite step.

Found as a develop-own finding during the tier-2 gate on #1268 (report lines 214-219). **Not built**
**there**, and not built here: it is develop's, not that PR's.

## Measured at `00de57baeb405d0081fe8b6f192bd40d35acef61`

```
$ node -e "const u=new URL('../../fixtures/pre-suite.ts','file:///Volumes/Dev/Testing%20Agent%20MAIN/x/runner/cli.ts');
           console.log(u.pathname); console.log(require('url').fileURLToPath(u));"
/Volumes/Dev/Testing%20Agent%20MAIN/fixtures/pre-suite.ts     <- .pathname, what the code uses
/Volumes/Dev/Testing Agent MAIN/fixtures/pre-suite.ts         <- fileURLToPath, correct
```

`cli.ts:162` **is the only** `.pathname` **use of an** `import.meta.url` **URL in the package.** The fix-shape
already has precedent **in the same directory**, so this is a consistency fix rather than a new idea:

* `runner/actor_manifest.ts:60` — `dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url))`
* `runner/paths.ts:12` — `path.dirname(url.fileURLToPath(import.meta.url))`
* `gate/cli.ts:31` — the same

## Done means

1. `cli.ts:162` uses `fileURLToPath(new URL('../../fixtures/pre-suite.ts', import.meta.url))`.
2. **A regression cell in the gate's own shape: run the CLI from a copy of the tree whose path**
   **contains a space**, and assert the pre-suite step resolves and spawns. A cell that only asserts
   the string has no `%20` would pass for a path that is wrong in some other way.
3. A sweep for any other `.pathname` on an `import.meta.url` URL across `systemTest/`, so the fix is
   the class and not the one line. ~~Measured today: **1** occurrence, this one.~~ **CORRECTED 2026-09-26 (gate29, and the PR agrees): the count is 3, not 1.** Measured by `git grep` over the clone at develop: `systemTest/performance/runner/cli.ts:162` (**fixed** by PR #1291, squash `3f70224a069b`), `systemTest/akto/tests/preSuiteSetup.ts:36` and `systemTest/playwright/global-setup.ts:42` — the last two remain open on this ticket. The original figure came from a sweep scoped to the performance package, while this DoD names `systemTest/`. Two wider sweeps add nothing to the class. The same class ALSO exists in 2 files under `Blockchain/Dev`, outside this ticket's scope — filed as KS-1347.

## Why it was not fixed in the round that found it

It is **develop's own defect**, not #1268's. #1268 touches `packages/shared`; folding an unrelated
`systemTest/performance` fix into it would widen a fix round past its declared scope and past the
files its gate reviewed.

## Search before filing

`searchIssues`, KS team, `includeArchived: true`, every page literal-matched client-side:
`preSuiteStep` **0**, `cli.ts:162` **0**, `%2520` **0**. `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` returns 3 (KS-691,
KS-149, KS-1148 — all unrelated: worktree preflight, vc-issuer tooling, CI-runner gaps).
`pre-suite.ts` returns 7, all about the step's own behaviour rather than path encoding.
Controls: `performance` **37** literal hits and `runner` **44** (the matcher fires); a nonce token
never written anywhere **0**.

No fleet STOP count is quoted because none was produced — measured, with a control: those log lines appear 0 times here and 4/1/4 times in a `Blockchain/Dev` push made the same night.

**This ticket stays open.** The playwright site (`systemTest/playwright/global-setup.ts`) and the DoD 2 real-CLI cell are untouched.

The resulting tree equals the batch's declared END_TREE `0cc6669f3a6ed3ac2841e9cf17c6229e890e0250` exactly.

**This ticket stays In Progress — one of three sites is fixed.**

🔴 **A CORRECTION TO THIS TICKET'S OWN DoD 3.** It reads "Measured today: 1". **That is false; the count is 3**, and both the gate and the PR agree. The ticket's sweep was scoped to the performance package ("the only `.pathname` use ... in the package") while DoD 3 names `systemTest/`. Measured at develop by `git grep` over the clone:

| site | state |
|---|---|
| `systemTest/performance/runner/cli.ts:162` | **FIXED** by #1291 |
| `systemTest/akto/tests/preSuiteSetup.ts:36` | open, on this ticket |

The description above has been corrected in place, marked as a correction.

**DoD 2, the gate's note:** the existing real-CLI cell **reds only on a spaced checkout**, so on a checkout without a space it cannot witness the defect. #1291's cell sidesteps that by building its own temp directory containing a space — which is why it red-proves from any checkout — but it reconstructs the resolution rather than crossing the CLI's own process boundary, so **DoD 2 is approximated, not met.**

**One follow-up filed, searched first: KS-1347** — the same `import.meta.url).pathname` class exists in **2 files under `Blockchain/Dev`** (4 lines), outside this ticket's stated scope: `scripts/openapi-examples/proxy/server.ts:31` and `services/auth/src/__tests__/ks732-mfa-disable-proof.test.ts:293,296,316`. It also records that **neither `ks860` nor `ks879` walks `systemTest/`**, so that tree has no raw-control-byte or loopback-bind guard and nothing structural would have caught this class there.

**One immaterial difference from this ticket's text:** it says the spawn dies with `%2520`; on this machine (node v24.7.0, the package's pinned tsx) both the unit run and the direct CLI show a single `%20`. The encoding count depends on the tsx/node pair and does not affect the fix.

Facts only.

**Raised at PR [#1291](https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/1291)** — head `2c9022c519bd26e9b58acddeed817f4413d92449`, base `develop` `179a4f32ec0643689b55a8d7207e63f6ec3d3831`. **READY FOR QA.** Not merged. Facts only.

**The fix.** `systemTest/performance/runner/cli.ts` built the pre-suite step path from `new URL(...).pathname`. A URL pathname is **percent-encoded**, so a checkout directory containing a space handed `tsx` a path with `%20` and the step died `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND`. `fileURLToPath` decodes. `+4/-1`.

**The red is the defect verbatim:** expected `…/Testing Agent MAIN/systemTest/fixtures/pre-suite.ts`, received `…/Testing%20Agent%20MAIN/systemTest/fixtures/pre-suite.ts`.

**Measured** in a worktree detached at develop, `npm ci` in the package (standalone lockfile): strict apply rc 0; **RED 1 failed / 2 passed / 3** (the declared cell, on its assertion); **GREEN 3/3**; whole performance unit suite **BARE 64 files / 1114 tests** -> **PATCHED 65 / 1117**, 0 failed either side, **0 new reds**; **`npm run lint` rc 0** (`tsc` x2 + eslint).

**The cell builds its own temp directory containing a space** rather than relying on the checkout's path — which is why it red-proves the defect even from a checkout without one. The corollary matters for anyone re-running it: **a green run on a space-free checkout is not evidence the defect is absent.**

🔴 **Scope — this closes ONE of THREE occurrences.** The pattern was measured **3x** on develop. This PR converts `runner/cli.ts:162`. **Not in this PR:** `systemTest/akto/tests/preSuiteSetup.ts:36` and `systemTest/playwright/global-setup.ts:42`, in other packages with their own installs and suites. The PR body carries `Refs` with no closing keyword for that reason.

🔴 **This ticket's "Done means 2" is approximated, not met.** That step asks for a cell that runs **the CLI itself** from a spaced copy. This cell reconstructs the resolution in a probe module, so it pins the defect and would catch its return, but it does not cross `runner/cli.ts`'s own process boundary. Stated rather than claimed closed.

**Provenance.** `runner/cli.ts` is **byte-identical** to the local model's (Ornith) product hunk. The **test file is that output plus the package's own `eslint --fix`** — formatting only, one hunk, 15 lines, 3,481 -> 3,524 bytes. The model's diff was byte-identical to its reviewed golden, but the package's own `npm run lint` was **rc 1 on it: 6 prettier errors in the new cell**, while both `tsc` stages passed. That was raised as a STOP and the formatter applied on an explicit ruling, rather than shipping a package whose own `lint`/`quality` scripts are red. The push log bears that out: the pre-push **format-gate** for this package reads `format:check OK, 1 package(s) checked, 0 failed`.

**One correction to my own artefact:** I first wrote the platform fleet-STOP figures into the PR body as boilerplate. **They do not apply** — the pre-push hook filters by path and this change touches no `Blockchain/Dev/` path, so the platform preflight did not run at all. The PR body has been corrected to state what actually ran. A missing gate is not a passing gate.

title: Per-tenant DB readiness: the dormant per-tenant-database path, and the five tickets that each break it
description:
## BLUF

**Every tenant shares one database today.** Isolation comes from a `tenant_id` column plus
fail-closed RLS. A per-tenant-database path exists in the code and is **switched off**. This is the
parent for the five tickets that each break that path in a different way, so the work has one place
rather than five.

**Nothing is built by this ticket.** It exists because Kam ruled option (c) on KS-1304 — *"Leave it*
*until per-tenant databases are actually planned. Nothing changes. The ticket keeps the measurement for*
*whoever builds per-tenant databases"* (2026-09-26 07:19) — with the note **"start planning the**
**database"**. This ticket is the artefact that carries that ruling onto the board.

## Measured at `00de57baeb405d0081fe8b6f192bd40d35acef61` (develop's tip), by this seat

Re-measured here rather than carried over from the planning document, which read an older tree.

1. **The flag is set in 0 config files.** `PROVISION_PER_TENANT_DB` occurs in exactly **two source**
   **files** — `packages/shared/src/db/tenant-pool-manager.ts:152` and
   `services/tenant-provisioning/src/index.ts:245` — and in **no** `.env`, `.example`, `.yml`,
   `.yaml` or `.json` config file. *Control: 25 config files do mention* `DATABASE_URL`*, so the*
   *config-file search is not blind.*
2. **Every tenant is seeded onto the shared database, and the code says so in its own comment.**
   `services/api-gateway/src/startup-migrations.ts:1116-1144` writes all eight `tenant_config` rows
   with the same `db_name`, `db_host` and `db_port`, derived from `DATABASE_URL`. The comment at
   `:1116-1117` reads: *"Ensure all tenants have a tenant_config entry pointing to the shared*
   *'secuura' database. On Azure there is a single DB; per-tenant DBs are not provisioned."*
3. **The docs state the opposite.** `docs/MULTI-TENANCY.md:13` — *"Each client (tenant) receives an*
   *isolated PostgreSQL database"* — and `:16` — *"Each tenant has its own PostgreSQL database*
   *(*`secuura_tenant_{slug}`*)"*. `docs/RLS-FAIL-CLOSED-PLAN.md:35` — *"Real isolation is per-tenant*
   *databases."* **The second of those is internally contradictory**: the two lines immediately above
   it say RLS is *"permanently on its fail-open branch — inert today"*, so that document simultaneously
   says isolation comes from per-tenant databases and that the mechanism which would route to them is
   not in use. A reader of either doc will overestimate the isolation that exists.

A docs PR correcting both files is raised separately and links here.

## The five tickets, and why each blocks switching the path on

* **KS-1304** — `documents.ts` mixes a tenant-pool read with a default-pool write. Ruled (c): left
  until per-tenant databases are planned. `adminConfig.ts` carries 9 of the 11 `withTenant(` sites.
* **KS-1235** — auth's tenant-pool statements carry no tenant GUC.
* **KS-1055** — per-tenant databases never receive the file migrations. Measured on that ticket: a new
  tenant database comes up with RLS forced on and **zero policies**, so the app can read nothing.
* **KS-1054** — migration-runner ordering and exit status.
* **KS-598** — the MULTI_TENANCY registry upsert silently collapses. **KS-598 keeps KS-772 as its**
  **parent** (Stuart's review stream — re-parenting it would silently remove an item from a human's
  queue) and is linked here as *related* instead.

## What this ticket is NOT

* It does not choose between building the opt-in dedicated-database tier and deleting the dormant path
  and hardening RLS. **That decision is Kam's**, and it turns on whether a named customer or contract
  needs physical separation (data residency, per-tenant restore or deletion, customer-held keys) or
  whether this is defence in depth.
* It carries **facts only**. The planning document's recommendations and phasing are deliberately not
  reproduced here, so the board does not record a plan as though it were agreed.

## Search before filing

`searchIssues`, KS team, `includeArchived: true`, every page literal-matched client-side:
`per-tenant DB readiness` **0**, `tenant database readiness` **0**, `dedicated database tier` **0**;
`PROVISION_PER_TENANT_DB` returns **3** — KS-1055, KS-1304, KS-1235, i.e. the children, **no parent**;
`per-tenant database` returns 2, both children. Controls: `tenant` **49** literal hits and
`multi-tenancy` **8** (the matcher fires), a nonce token never written anywhere **0**.

title: pre-push fixture guard: re-land GUARDGAPS with a call-site reader that passes the aborting `||` / `if` / `&&` shapes and flags multi-line `$(` and group openers
description:
**BLUF: the fixture guard's round-2 work was measured correct in cells 7 and 8 and shipped nothing, because cell 9's reader flags shapes that DO abort and passes shapes that swallow the abort — wrong in both directions.** This ticket re-lands the work with a reader that discriminates, and it resolves a contradiction in the earlier hold text.

## What is on `develop` today

Guard blob `52c852203edc2d7b64c3e23bc2ab3f077cf07cc6` at 6 cells, with three gaps all open: unanchored abort counts, a `repo_state` blind to the worktree, and no call-site pin. **Reach is 0 today** — all 12 of 12 call sites are bare — so nothing is currently mis-scored; the guard simply cannot see a regression.

## What the reader must do

Through the real guard, cell 9 currently **FLAGS** the named aborting shapes:
`bf || true` · `false || bf` · `if bf; then :; fi` · `bf && :`
and **PASSES** the named swallowing shapes: a multi-line `x=$(` / call / `)` and `( : noop` / call / `)`.

That is backwards. `build_fixture` aborts with an explicit `exit 2`, so only a **subshell** call site swallows it; `|| true`, `if` and `&&` do not.

## Scope

Re-land the anchored counts (cell 7), the widened `repo_state` (cell 8) and cells 11-12 from blob `5189cf31a098a62c485367beedb78def2428d787`, with `c9_scan` **admitting** `bf || true`, `false || bf`, `if bf; then :; fi` and `bf && :`, and **flagging** a previous line ending in `$(` / `(` or holding an unclosed `(`. Cell 10 computes `c9_scan`; cell 12 asserts on a subject copy.

## The contradiction to resolve, named by the gate to the filer

The earlier hold asked for a **strict whitelist** AND for the `||` shapes to be **unflagged**. Those two contradict each other. **The admitting whitelist is the one to pick** — that is the gate's own note to whoever picks this up.

## A limit worth carrying forward rather than rediscovering

Do not attempt to track shell nesting by counting parentheses. A paren-depth counter over lines called 11 of 12 real call sites offending, because a subshell can close with `) > "$WORK/c0.out" 2>/dev/null` and a multi-line `$( … )` can end with `)"`. A guard that half-parses shell is worse than one with a declared limit: read one line of context and write the limitation down.

## Evidence produced by the gate

`evidence/reader1253/reader_rows.json` · `evidence/reader1253/guard_*.stdout` · `behav_*.stdout` · `evidence/g1253/garms_rows.json`.

## Board search before filing

Searched over **483 open issues**, matching literally against identifier + title + description rather than by fuzzy search: `c9_scan`, `call-site reader`, `5189cf31a098`, `GUARDGAPS`, `admitting whitelist` — **0 open hits each**. Controls as above: a fresh nonsense token **0**, `run-shell-suites.sh` **16**.

Refs KS-1297

title: packages/shared does not type-check src/__tests__, hiding 10 errors — add a test-inclusive tsc leg and fix them
description:
## BLUF

`npx tsc -p . --noEmit` in `packages/shared` returns **rc 0**, and always has. That is not health: `tsconfig.json` carries `"exclude": ["node_modules", "dist", "src/__tests__"]`, so **the package's own type-check never sees a test file**. Under a program that does include them there are **10 errors across 6 files**. The exclusion is the defect; the 10 are its consequence.

Filed from KS-1179's TYPECHECK-DEBT item on the coordinator's ruling (one ticket, not two: a single test pass proves it, because the new leg goes green only once the errors are gone).

## The 10, measured

| file | errors |
| -- | -- |
| `src/__tests__/ks781-p3-3-body-parser-order.test.ts` | 2x **TS2345** (`Express` not assignable), 1x TS2741 |
| `src/security/ssrf-guard.ts` | 1x **TS2349** (see below), 1x TS7006 — **TS7006 fixed in KS-1179** |
| `src/__tests__/openapi-operation-ids.test.ts` | 1x TS2352 |
| `src/__tests__/openapi-415-injection.test.ts` | 1x TS2352 |
| `src/__tests__/ks914-pinned-address.test.ts` | 2x TS6133 (unused `vi`, unused `safeOutboundRequest`) |
| `src/__tests__/walkTimeouts.test.ts` | 1x TS5097 (`.ts` import extension) |

⚠ `ks781-p3-3-body-parser-order.test.ts`**'s three are blocked until PR #1268 merges.** That PR is open and changes the same file; two branches on one file needs a declared merged-blob equality target. Do them after it lands.

## TS2349 — carried here because it does NOT fix cleanly

`mod` is `typeof https | typeof http` and calling the union of their overloads is the error. Four shapes were measured and **each relocated it**:

| attempt | result |
| -- | -- |
| no change | **TS2349** not callable |
| cast the callee `(mod.request as typeof https.request)` | **TS2769** no overload matches — `agent` is `https.Agent \| http.Agent` |
| callee cast + `agent: agent as https.Agent` at the call site | errors 10 -> 8, clean, **but the emit changes**: `agent,` expands to `agent: agent,` |
| callee cast + the assertion on the declaration | emit identical again, **TS2352** — the two Agent types "neither sufficiently overlaps" |

The only remaining shape is `as unknown as https.Agent`. **It was refused deliberately:** in an SSRF guard, a type the compiler stops checking is the risk to avoid. The honest fix is narrowing at the branch (`isTls ? https.request(...) : http.request(...)`), which **duplicates the call and changes the emit** — a real change to the request path, and not something a type error alone justifies. Decide it here, with the guard's owner.

## Method, so this is reproducible

A probe config **outside the repo**, extending the package's own `tsconfig.json` and overriding only:

```json
{ "compilerOptions": { "noEmit": true, "module": "esnext", "target": "ES2022" },
  "include": ["<pkg>/src/**/*.ts"], "exclude": [] }
```

`module`/`target` are raised only because the tests use top-level `await`; leaving them at the package's `commonjs` produces **9x TS1343 and 5x TS1378 that are artefacts of the probe**, not of the tree.

**Controls, because two earlier probes gave wrong answers:**

* **A** — the probe must SEE the file: `--listFilesOnly | grep <file>` returns 1.
* **B** — the probe must REPORT an error in it: planting `const x: number = "not a number";` takes it from **10 -> 11**, the new one naming the file and line. *(First read of this control grepped for the variable name and found 0 — tsc prints the file and line, not the identifier. The probe was fine; the grep was not.)*
* A probe adding `types: ["vitest/globals","node"]` reported **2 errors, both TS2688** — its own type-resolution failure silencing everything else. A probe that reports almost nothing looks like a clean tree.
* The same 10 reproduce under `moduleResolution: node` (the package's own) as under `bundler`, so they are not a resolution artefact. *(A duplicate-*`@types/node` *theory was raised and withdrawn: the tree holds 30 copies at three majors, but this program loads exactly one.)*

## Definition of done

- [ ] `packages/shared` type-checks `src/__tests__` — a leg or script that fails on a type error in a test file, with a positive control proving it can fail
- [ ] the 10 above resolved, or each recorded with the reason (TS2349 is a decision, see above)
- [ ] the ks781 three done after #1268 merges

⚠ **The leg touches the push gate**, which is not in the KS-1179 lane. That is why this is a separate ticket rather than more of that PR.

## Board search before filing

Literal match over **1,318 issues (includeArchived) and 3,718 comments**: `tsconfig` -> 67 total / 30 open · `src/__tests__` -> 178 / 93 · `TS2345` -> 5 / 4 (KS-1313, KS-1179, KS-932, KS-872 — the F-3 lineage and L6's, none this subject) · `TS2349` -> **0** · `type-checks` -> 23 / 14. **No open issue is about the exclusion itself.** Controls: `readYaml` -> 13 total / 11 open, fires; a fresh token never written anywhere -> **0**.

Refs KS-1179

title: kyc verification writes are a whole-row read-modify-write: two timers, or a timer and an admin review, can still race
description:
## BLUF

`services/kyc` persists a verification by reading the **whole row**, mutating the object, and writing the **whole row** back through an upsert whose `ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE SET` names `status`, `current_level`, `documents`, `liveness_completed`, `liveness_score`, `checks`, `overall_score`, `risk_level`, `reviewed_by`, `review_notes`, `updated_at` and `completed_at`. Nothing serialises those writers. So any two of them overlapping — two mock timers, or a timer and an admin review — can still lose one side's changes.

KS-849's fix (re-reading inside each mock timer) **narrows the window from 1500/3000 ms to the read-modify-write's own microseconds, and that is all it can do.** It does not make the write atomic.

## The part KS-849 explicitly does NOT close, measured

The 3000 ms auto-approve timer at `services/kyc/src/index.ts` sets `status = 'approved'` and `currentLevel = requestedLevel` **itself**. So after the re-read:

* **FIXED** — every field the timer does not own survives an admin review landing inside the window: `reviewedBy`, `reviewNotes`, `documents`, `livenessCompleted`, `livenessScore`, and checks that are no longer `pending`.
* **NOT FIXED** — an admin **rejection** through `POST /api/kyc/:id/review` inside those 3 seconds is **still overwritten to** `approved`, and a `newLevel` supplied by the reviewer is still replaced by `requestedLevel`.

This correction matters because the KS-849 ticket's own fix-shape text ("re-read the verification inside the timer") reads as though it addresses the admin-overwrite case. **It does not**, and the ticket should not be read that way.

## Where it is pinned rather than left to be rediscovered

PR for KS-849 adds `services/kyc/src/__tests__/ks849-mock-timer-stale-write.test.ts`, whose cell **S3 asserts** `status === 'approved'` **after a rejection**, with a comment stating this is not fixed and is tracked here. A later reader cannot mistake the limit for closed.

## Fix shapes, not chosen here

1. A **single-statement partial UPDATE** per writer, naming only the columns that writer owns, instead of the whole-row upsert. Removes the class for non-overlapping column sets; two writers to the *same* column still race.
2. **Row locking** (`SELECT … FOR UPDATE` inside a transaction) around read-modify-write.
3. Move the mock auto-approve **off the request path** entirely, which removes the 3 s window but not the class.

Both (1) and (2) are behaviour changes to a persistence path and want their own gate, which is why this is a ticket rather than part of KS-849.

## Scope

The mock/demo path gates the timers (`KYC_PROVIDER === 'mock'`), but **the whole-row upsert is not mock-gated** — `/review`, `/complete`, `/document` and `/selfie` all write through it in every mode. So the timers are the reachable trigger today; the class is wider than the trigger.

## Board search before filing (team Secuura-PK, 1,316 issues **including archived**, 3,705 comments; literal match on titles, descriptions and comments)

* `auto-approve` → 0 titles/descriptions, 2 comments · `autoApprove` → 0 · `row locking` → 0 · `read-modify-write` → 0 titles, 1 comment · `stale write` → 0.
* `partial UPDATE` → 1 (KS-938, TOTP seed retention — unrelated).
* `svc_kyc_verifications` → KS-851 (column ordinal drift, a different defect) and KS-386 (archived, image payload).
* `KYC_PROVIDER` → KS-849 itself and KS-626 (archived, Entra callback).
* **Controls that fire:** `KS-1155` → 4 titles / 7 comments; `KS-849` → 1 / 1; a nonsense token `zzqx-l8-never-written-anywhere-7731` → **0 / 0**. So the search discriminates. (That token is now spent by appearing here.)

Nothing on the board describes this class in kyc.

Refs KS-849

title: childSuiteCounts reads a child KILLED by its own 180 s spawnSync timeout as a PASS - a lookalike summary pair is accepted as {7,0}
description:
**BLUF:** `childSuiteCounts` **can report a clean pass for a child process that was killed.** When a child is terminated by its own 180 s `spawnSync` timeout *after* it has already logged a summary-shaped pair, the reader takes that pair as the verdict and returns `{7,0}`. The kill is invisible to it. **Measured on both sides** - at PR #1245's head `65eb964271b0d6895e90fe8f5ffcbbbb9a484050` **and** on `develop` `4db87c3e4b98b8e366c3dd60d5f399917bad5086` - so this is a property of the code on the mainline, not of one branch.

This is the residue of a capped round. Nothing shipped for it; the pull request that attempted it stays open and its disposition sits with the repository owner.

## The lookalike that is accepted

A child that logs

```
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  7 passed (7)
```

and is then killed still presents that pair to the reader. `childSuiteCounts` returns `{7,0}` - seven passed, zero failed - and nothing downstream can tell that outcome apart from a genuine completion. **A verdict composed separately from the work reproduces here exactly:** the summary text is not evidence that the run finished.

## Three residues, one test pass, one ticket

1. **KILLED-AFTER-LOOKALIKE** - the defect above.
2. **CALLSITE-STILL-TEXT** - the call site still reaches the summary through text. The shape asked for is a pure `countsFromSpawn(result)` sitting behind `childSuiteCounts`, fed a synthetic spawn result, so the decision is made from the spawn outcome rather than from scraped output.
3. **JOINED-CLAIM** - the sentence *"measured to hold on the JOINED text"* should be dropped. It is not true: **10 real shapes are misread on joined text, 3 of them silently.** A claim about where a reader is safe, which is false, is worse than no claim.

## Fix shapes, any one of which closes the first residue

* **Refuse when the spawn says so:** `result.error` or `result.signal` set, or `result.status` not `0`/`1`.
* **Require vitest's trailing** `Start at` **/** `Duration` **block**, which a killed child never reaches.
* **Use the JSON reporter** instead of parsing human output.

## Cells the next attempt should carry

* The **H1 stdout capture** returns `null`.
* A spawn result of `{status 143, ETIMEDOUT}` **throws** rather than yielding counts.

Signal 143 is SIGTERM; a status of 143 with `ETIMEDOUT` is precisely the killed-child case, and it is the discriminating fixture.

## Reusable from the capped attempt - do not rebuild these

The round-2 **stdout-only reader**, the **whole-run cells**, and the `{3,2}` **row** are sound and are the parts to start from.

## Not covered

Preflight legs 3, 4 and 8 were not run for that attempt (no local stack). They are owed by nothing here; recorded so the absence is not mistaken for a pass.

## Board search before filing

Searched over **481 open issues** on this team, matching literally against identifier + title + description rather than by fuzzy search: `countsFromSpawn`, `KILLED-AFTER-LOOKALIKE`, `CALLSITE-STILL-TEXT`, `JOINED-CLAIM`, `ETIMEDOUT`, `status 143`, `capturedChildOutput` - **0 open hits each**. `spawnSync` returned 2 (KS-1111, KS-1098), neither about this reader. A fresh nonsense control token returned **0** and `childSuiteCounts` returned **1**, so the instrument discriminates in both directions.

**Not duplicates, deliberately:** KS-1313 is the parent this residue falls out of, and KS-1226 is its own parent. Both stay open and neither is closed by this ticket.
