title: A PTY harness so SIGINT can be asserted for run-shell-suites.sh in the foreground, in both the standalone and in-hook environments
description:
**BLUF: there is currently no way to assert that** `run-shell-suites.sh` **handles SIGINT, because every available harness either backgrounds the runner or runs with SIGINT already ignored - and bash discards the signal in both cases.** A pseudo-terminal harness is the only route to closing that gap. Nothing is broken today; the runner's INT/TERM arms exist and are correct. What is missing is the ability to *prove* the INT arm, and today that is recorded as UNREACHABLE rather than tested.

## The two measured rules that create the gap

Both measured on `/bin/bash` 3.2.57, which is the only bash on this drive - there is no Homebrew bash cellar and every local project image is busybox/Alpine with no `bash` at all.

1. **A signal IGNORED ON ENTRY to bash cannot be trapped.** `trap '...' INT` is silently not installed and `trap -p INT` comes back empty. **The in-hook preflight runs with SIGINT ignored**, so an INT arm inside the hook cannot exist at all.
2. **bash ignores SIGINT in any ASYNCHRONOUS (background) job**, whatever the parent's disposition: `trap -p INT` empty, the signal discarded, rc 0. The identical trap in the **foreground** gives rc 130.

Between them, SIGINT-to-pid is unassertable by any harness that backgrounds the runner, which is what a test harness naturally does in order to hold its pid.

## Current state, so this is not read as a defect report

The runner's signal arms were built and accepted on the ruling that each arm **probes its own reachability** and either asserts all four properties or reports UNREACHABLE naming the rule above. That is the right behaviour given the constraint. TERM is assertable and is asserted. INT is not, and says so.

## What this ticket asks for

One harness that runs `run-shell-suites.sh` **in the foreground of a pseudo-terminal** so a real SIGINT can be delivered to it and its disposition observed, usable from:

* a standalone run, and
* the in-hook environment, where the parent's disposition is the thing being worked around.

Candidate mechanisms, none chosen here: `script -q` (present on macOS and on Linux with different argument orders), a small `openpty`/`forkpty` helper, or Python's `pty` module driving the runner. The acceptance criterion is the discriminating one: **the same harness must give rc 130 on a foreground INT and must show the arm reporting UNREACHABLE when the signal is ignored on entry** - a harness that only ever produces one of those has not measured anything.

## Proposed tier

**Tier 2.** It is test-infrastructure with no runtime surface, but it is the only path to converting a standing UNREACHABLE into an assertion, and the rules above will otherwise be re-derived by whoever next touches the runner's signal handling.

## Board search before filing

Searched, over 479 open issues on this team, matching literally against identifier + title + description: `pseudo-terminal`, `pseudoterminal`, `SIGINT`, `script -q`, `openpty`, `forkpty`, `PTY harness` - **0 open hits each**. A fresh nonsense control token returned **0** and `run-shell-suites` returned **14**, so the instrument discriminates in both directions.

Note for anyone re-running this search: the bare term `pty` is useless here - it is a substring of "empty" and returned **69** open hits on this corpus. Use a word boundary or a longer term.

Refs KS-1302

title: Seat push tooling reuses one push-log name per worktree, so a push record is overwritten and the earlier STOP-count evidence is lost
description:
## BLUF

`push24.sh` (and its predecessors `push22/23.sh`) name the push log by the **worktree basename**: `<worktree>-push.out`. A seat that pushes twice from the same worktree **overwrites the first push's log**, and with it the in-hook evidence — the fleet STOP counts, the leg-by-leg preflight output and the `FIXTURE BUILD FAILED` check for that push.

Confirmed by the tier-2 gate on #1255 (report `2026-09-26-batch1249-t2b`, finding **N-1255-a**, READ): `raise/s-b28-cells-push.out` held a push from `15:50:24Z` to `15:57:03Z`, overwritten again afterwards — **#1255's own push record is gone.** Non-blocking; nothing shipped wrongly, and the counts were quoted into the PR from the run at the time.

## Why it matters

A PR's Test Evidence block quotes the STOP counts from that push's log. If the log has been overwritten by a later push from the same worktree, the evidence behind a merged PR is no longer re-readable — the claim survives and its source does not. That is an evidence-integrity gap, not a correctness one, which is why it is non-blocking and still worth closing.

## Fix shape (the gate's)

Name the push log by the **head sha** (or append `-push-<n>`), never reused. Same for the `.start`, `.end`, `.rc` and `-stubs.txt` siblings, which share the defect.

## Done when

- [ ] two pushes from one worktree leave two distinct logs, both readable afterwards
- [ ] the naming includes something that cannot repeat (head sha preferred)
- [ ] a control: push twice from one worktree and assert both files exist with different names

## Board search before filing

Literal match over 1,310 issues incl. archived and 3,687 comments: `push24.sh` → 0; `-push.out` → 0; `push log` → 4 total / 3 open (KS-1201, KS-1047, KS-948), each about other things (login_stub orphans, the hook's leg naming, an unrelated script) — **none about log-name reuse.** No existing home. Controls: `withTenant` → 12, `ZZZNOSUCHSYMBOLZZZ` → 0.

Raised from the #1255 merge (develop `4db87c3e4b98b8e366c3dd60d5f399917bad5086`).

title: Published spec descriptions carry internal ticket keys ("KS-1275:", "KS-1118 F-3", "KS-1133 — HASH ALIAS ORDER") — the owner's call
description:
## BLUF

The **served** OpenAPI description text now carries internal ticket keys. #1252 added `"KS-1275:"` and `"KS-1118 F-3"` to two descriptions in `originate.openapi.ts`, and they are published into `docs/openapi/secuura-api.yaml` and served from `/api/docs`.

**This is a pre-existing style, not a new one** — `"KS-1133 — HASH ALIAS ORDER"` was already in the same file's v2 verify description before #1252.

Recorded by the tier-2 gate on #1252 (report `2026-09-26-batch1249-t2b`, finding **N-1252-b**, READ) as Polish and explicitly **the owner's call**.

## The decision, stated plainly

Ticket keys in a published description are useful to us and meaningless to an integrator reading the contract. Two defensible positions:

* **Keep them.** They make the reason for a wording discoverable, and the convention is already established in this file.
* **Strip them.** The published contract is customer-facing; internal identifiers belong in the source comment, not the served text. The source comment above each description can carry the key instead.

**No change should be made on a seat's own judgement** — hence a ticket rather than a fix. If the answer is "strip", it is a sweep across the spec (three known instances and possibly more), not a one-line edit.

## Scope, measured

Instances found in the published description text: `KS-1275:` and `KS-1118 F-3` (added by #1252), `KS-1133 — HASH ALIAS ORDER` (pre-existing). A full sweep of `originate.openapi.ts` description strings has not been done and is part of the work if the ruling is to strip.

## Done when

- [ ] a ruling is recorded: keep, or strip
- [ ] if strip: every instance in the published description text removed, the key moved to the adjacent source comment, and the yaml regenerated
- [ ] if keep: the convention written down where the next editor will find it, so it is a decision rather than an accident

## Board search before filing

Literal match over 1,310 issues incl. archived and 3,687 comments: `HASH ALIAS ORDER` and `SPEC-PROSE` searched alongside `originate.openapi.ts` (30 total / 11 open) and `docs/VOCABULARY.md` (13 / 7) — the path hits are about spec content generally, none about **internal keys in the published text**. No existing home. Controls fire as above.

Raised from the #1252 merge (develop `49bc69abae1528d8da76018aaa68b04749e5d93b`).

title: ks781 LEG F: a guard DEFINED but never called inside the parser continuation still reads guarded true (over-reports)
description:
## BLUF

Pre-existing limit of LEG F's guard walk, recorded by the tier-2 gate on PR #1248 (KS-1143 GF-2, merged `fa25c9b10fb4`). **A guard that is DEFINED but never CALLED inside the parser's continuation still reads** `guarded: true`**.**

This **over-reports**, which is the **unsafe** direction: the leg says something inspects the parsed body when nothing does. It is the same asymmetry KS-1143's own GF-1 was about, one step further in.

## Mechanism

GF-2 moved the walk's start from the whole wrapper body to the parser call's **continuation** — the function-valued arguments of the parser call. Inside that continuation the walk still hits on a **call node whose callee name is a known guard**. It does not establish that the call is reached: a guard call sitting in a branch that never executes, or bound and shadowed, is indistinguishable from one on the path.

Not introduced by #1248 — the predicate it replaced had the same property over a wider region, so GF-2 narrowed the region without changing this. Recorded so the remaining looseness has a name.

## Relationship to what is already open on KS-1143

KS-1143 stays In Progress for the **indirect-invocation false negative**, which is the *opposite* direction (under-reports: a continuation passed by NAME is not followed, so a genuinely mounted guard reads unguarded). **This one over-reports.** Two different directions, two different risks; they are not the same defect and should not be closed by one change without saying which each fix addresses.

## Done when

- [ ] a fixture where the guard call inside the continuation is unreachable reads `guarded: false`, **or**
- [ ] a line in the file records why reachability is deliberately out of scope for a text-level walk, so the limit is stated rather than latent

## Board search before filing

Literal match over **1,305 issues (includeArchived) and 3,677 comments**: `CONT-DEFERRED` -> 1 (KS-1143, this finding's own record) · `parserContinuations` -> **0** · `defined but never` -> 1 (KS-1143) · `never called` -> 17 total / 5 open, each read and none this subject (KS-1291 a stale comment, KS-1185, KS-843, KS-1143 itself). **Searched those four terms, 0 open hits for this defect.** Controls: `readYaml` -> 8 hits, fires; `zzz-nonexistent-token-l6-control` -> 0.

## Provenance

Tier-2 gate `QA/Secuura-batch1243`, non-blocking, recorded at the merge of #1248.

Refs KS-1143

nodes.body:
**Fix round 1 of 2 pushed to [#1268](https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/1268)** —
new head `5ac42fafeee11dec596e7e7d833ac82b8b478790`, a fast-forward on the existing branch (the author
has wrapped). Not merged; nothing merges without a signed GO naming the head. Facts only.

The gate's blocking finding: the walk read `guarded: false` on the alias shape the file's own comment
named while asserting it read `true`. Cause — the invoked-name set recorded only a **direct**
`name(...)` call, so an alias, `.call`, `.apply`, `.bind()()`, a `new Promise` callback and a returned
arrow all left the name out and the binding read as a definition the walk would not enter. Nine shapes
flipped correct → wrong, every one **under**-reporting.

**Three rules, each proved independently load-bearing by its own arm:** a bound function expression is
a definition only when its binding is referenced nowhere else; `NewExpression` arguments are treated
like call arguments; a function expression returned from an invoked one escapes and is descended.

⚠ **The third rule is beyond the gate's two stated shapes, and it is here because of a measurement:**
with the first two only, **W18 (`mk()()`) still read `false`** — the returned arrow has no binding, so
the binding rule cannot see it. The gate's own regression set requires W18 to read `true`.

**The limit is held.** W9 still reads `false` and new **W19** pins that an arrow merely stored and
never called still reads `false`, so the escape rule cannot widen until everything reads `true`.

**Test evidence** — base the worktree CONTAINS `4db87c3e4b98`, no merge-in:
`packages/shared` **BARE 947 → PATCHED 953**, 0 failed both · `tsc --noEmit` rc 0, zero `error TS`.
Red proofs, 5 arms, all behaved, zero LOADFAIL, each red set asserted **exactly**: reverting rule 1
reds W14/W15/W16; rule 2 reds W17; rule 3 reds W18; all three together reproduce the previous head
exactly (W14–W18); removing the narrowing reds **W9 and W19**, so both controls are live.
Push gate `28/0 · 6/0 · 49/0 · 60 of 60`; preflight **12/15 legs ran, 3 skipped (3, 4, 8 — no local
stack), nothing failed** — not quoted as a pass.

**KS-1318's and KS-1142's proven work is untouched, verified by blob:** `entrypoint-corpus.test.ts` is
byte-identical to the adopted head, and zero changed lines mention the tag set.
**K1b is not built** — non-blocking, not pinned, reach 0.

## BLUF

**[PR #1268](https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/1268) is open, head `a8e0fca70ed4`, base `develop` at `4db87c3e4b98`. READY FOR QA.** Built as the **first** done-when option — the syntactic fix — not the recorded-limitation line.

## Why the fix, having first proposed the line

I initially proposed the recorded limitation, arguing that reachability is a control-flow property a text-level walk cannot decide. That is true of reachability in general and it is **not** what this finding is about. The finding is narrower: whether a **nested function expression** is invoked *within the continuation's own body* is syntactic — it is immediately invoked, handed to a call, or bound to a name called there. The walk no longer descends into an uninvoked nested function expression; the continuation itself is always entered, because the parser invokes it.

## The cells

| cell | shape | reads |
|---|---|---|
| **W9 🔴** | `const later = () => g(req,res,next); next();` | `guarded: false` (was `true`) |
| W10 CONTROL | the same arrow, `later();` | `guarded: true` |
| W11 CONTROL | `(() => { g(...); })();` | `guarded: true` |
| W12 CONTROL | `[1].forEach(() => { g(...); });` | `guarded: true` |
| W13 | `if (false) { g(...); }` | `guarded: true` — **still not decided**, pinned as such |

**Under develop's walk with these cells present: exactly ONE red, W9.** Every control is green at **both** ends, so none is satisfied by a walk that merely stopped entering nested arrows.

## The control earned its keep

**W11 caught a real defect in the first version of the walk.** An IIFE parses as a call whose callee is a `ParenthesizedExpression`, so the `invoked` flag did not survive the parentheses and the arrow read as a definition — `guarded: false` where it should be `true`. **W9 alone would have passed over it.**

## Not closed

W13's class — reachability of a *statement* — is control flow and stays undecided, now pinned by a cell rather than left in prose. KS-1143's indirect-invocation false negative is the opposite direction and remains out of scope, as ruled.

---

**Evidence.** `packages/shared` **941/941 bare -> 947/947 patched** (48 files, +6 = exactly the new cells), `vitest run --no-file-parallelism` at develop `4db87c3e4b98`, load 17.67 / 10.00. `tsc -p . --noEmit` rc 0. Push gate: `PREFLIGHT INCOMPLETE — 12/15 legs ran, 3 SKIPPED. Nothing failed.` (legs 3, 4, 8, local stack not up — not quoted as a pass); fleet STOP count 28/0, 6/0, 49/0, shell suites 60 of 60. **No product file is touched.**

**Note:** this PR carries KS-1318, KS-1142 and KS-1316 together — KS-1318 and KS-1316 are the same file and KS-1142 reads it. A NO GO on one holds the three; that cost was agreed before building. Ticket stays In Progress.

title: KS-980 N-5: an anonymous Docker volume was left behind by a disposable test Postgres
description:
Raised as a non-blocking finding by the review of PR #1242 (merged as `33ccff807eb2`).

**What it is.** A disposable Postgres container used for the integration cells was removed, but its **anonymous volume** `0ec12181` was not, and remains on the host.

**Why it matters.** `docker rm -f` removes the container, not its anonymous volume. Volumes accumulate silently across sessions and are invisible to a `docker ps -a` check, so a teardown that looks complete is not.

**What a fix looks like.** Tear down with `docker rm -f -v`, or prove the volume gone as part of the teardown check rather than proving only the container gone.

Refs KS-980

title: KS-980 N-3: a squash body named a base commit that is not an ancestor of the squash
description:
Raised as a non-blocking finding by the review of PR #1242 (merged as `33ccff807eb2`).

**What it is.** The PR body's base line named `d9515f4a06e0`, which is **not an ancestor** of the merged result. The actual base at merge time was `e68e2f0e837df86da527d775a3a49c631b0f5b17`, and the squash's parent is that commit.

**Why it matters.** The base line is how a reviewer reconstructs what a change was measured against. A base that is not an ancestor cannot be the one the work was tested on, so any figure quoted against it is unverifiable after the fact.

**What a fix looks like.** Take the base from the same read that pins the head, at the moment the evidence is produced, rather than from an earlier draft of the body.

Refs KS-980

title: KS-980 N-2: the PR body claimed a 14/14 full run over 2 suites when the integration config runs 3
description:
Raised as a non-blocking finding by the review of PR #1242 (merged as `33ccff807eb2`).

**What it is.** The PR body reported a full run as **14/14 over two suites**. `jest.integration.config.js` matches **three** suites. The number quoted is therefore not the full run it is presented as — it is a subset, described with the words of a complete one.

**Why it matters more than the number.** A count is a claim about what executed. A subset reported as a full run makes coverage look wider than it is, and the next reader has no way to tell from the body alone.

**What a fix looks like.** Quote the runner's own ratio and name the suites it covered, or say plainly which suite was excluded and why.

Refs KS-980

title: originate documents.ts is the first router to mix a tenant-pool READ with a default-pool WRITE — on a dedicated-DB tenant it fails closed
description:
## BLUF

At #1239's head the `/share` and `/transfer-custody` handlers **read** through `req.db` (the tenant pool set by `extractTenantContext`) and **write** through `withTenant`, which always uses `tenantManager.getDefaultPool()`. **On a tenant whose config resolves to a dedicated database those are two different databases.**

`documents.ts` **is the first router to do this.** Every other non-test `withTenant` call site — 9, all in `routes/adminConfig.ts` — sits under `adminConfig.ts:30` `(req as any).db = prisma // Always shared DB`, so that router reads and writes one database by design.

## Reach, measured

* A pool other than `getDefaultPool()` **is** reachable in code: `getPool` returns a dedicated `Pool` when `perTenantDbEnabled` (`PROVISION_PER_TENANT_DB === 'true'`) **and** the tenant's config resolves elsewhere.
* `PROVISION_PER_TENANT_DB` **appears in 0 tracked config files** — compose, deployment and bicep; bicep sets only `MULTI_TENANCY_ENABLED`. So it is **latent and gated on a variable no template sets**.

## Behaviour on a dedicated-DB tenant, by reading

It **fails closed** rather than misplacing rows: `/share`'s target subquery runs in the default DB → NULL → `SHARE_TARGET_NOT_FOUND` → 404. `/transfer-custody`'s INSERT names a `document_id` absent from the default DB's `documents` → 23503 → rollback → 500.

**That is the right failure direction**, and it is why this is Minor rather than Major. It is still a router whose read and write disagree about which database it is talking to.

## NOT claimed

**Live proof NOT RUN** — no slot was available, and no per-tenant-DB tenant was provisioned. The reach above is static: read from `tenant-context.ts:93`, `tenant-pool-manager.ts:152/201-260` and `db.ts:308`, not executed.

## Related, and NOT a duplicate

**KS-1235** concerns **auth**'s `db.ts` sending tenant-scoped statements through `getPool(tenantId).query()` with **no tenant GUC** under fail-closed RLS. Same neighbourhood — tenant pool versus default pool — but a different service and a different mechanism (a missing GUC there, a read/write pool mismatch here). Read in full before filing.

## Fix shape

`withTenant` checks out from `getPool(tenantId)` (or takes the request's pool). Cell: a manager stub whose `getPool(t) !== getDefaultPool()` must see **both** writes on `getPool(t)`'s client.

## Board search before filing (team Secuura-PK, 1,291 issues incl. archived, 3,644 comments, literal match on titles, descriptions and comments)

* `PROVISION_PER_TENANT_DB` -> 5 total / 3 open (**KS-1235**, KS-1055, KS-1054); `getPool(` -> 2 / 1 (KS-1235). **KS-1235 read in full — related, not a duplicate** (see above).
* `getDefaultPool` -> 1 total / **0 open**. `tenantPool` -> **0**.
* Control that fires: `PROVISION_PER_TENANT_DB` -> 5. Nonsense control -> **0**.

`Refs KS-1263`; does not close it. Ruled TICKET (Minor) by the tier-1c gate, explicitly **not** part of #1239's round 2.

title: k6 readYaml adoption: the unit suite that proves it is run by no gate, and three coverage gaps the new self-read cells leave
description:
## BLUF

PR **#1236** (KS-1110, merged `2208acc0638a`) routed both k6 unit tests through `readYaml()`, so a malformed scenarios file fails them **without printing its content** — measured: the old path printed the whole file. The gate recorded **four** non-blocking findings alongside it. They are one file and one fix pass, so they are items of one ticket rather than four, per Kam's 2026-09-07 rule.

## The four items

1. **READYAML-UNGATED — the one that undoes the rest.** **No pre-push leg and no PR workflow runs this unit suite.** The cells that prove the property exist, and nothing executes them. A regression here is caught only if someone runs the suite by hand.
2. **READYAML-CANARY.** The canary that proves the old path leaked file content was measured for items A and B; it is not retained as a standing cell, so the property "a malformed file does not print its content" has no permanent witness.
3. **READYAML-ROUTING.** An **indented or dynamic** parser import would pass the new self-read cells — they read the file's own source for a top-level import, so a `js-yaml` import that is indented, conditional or dynamic is invisible to them.
4. **READYAML-SHAPES.** The shapes covered are those the two tests use; other config shapes are unasserted.

## Why item 1 leads

The other three are ordinary coverage limits. Item 1 is different in kind: it means the suite's verdict is **never produced** in the normal flow. That is the "a verdict nobody runs" shape the repo already tracks elsewhere — and it makes items 2-4 moot in practice, because even a perfect cell that nothing runs protects nothing.

## NOT claimed

Not a live failure. `systemTest/performance` reads 1088/1089 at the merged tree, and the single red is the pre-existing path-dependent `PRESUITE-URLPATH`, identical at base, head and end — not this PR.

## Board search before filing (team Secuura-PK, 1,286 issues incl. archived, 3,631 comments, literal match on titles, descriptions and comments)

* `readYaml` -> 5 total / 3 open (**KS-1117**, KS-1110, KS-485). **KS-1117 read in full and is NOT a duplicate** — it is js-yaml 5.2.3 rejecting a BOM followed by `#`, a parsing defect in the loader itself.
* `scenarios.yml` -> 18 total / 5 open; `sheddingCeiling` -> 2 total / 1 open (**KS-1110**, the merged ticket this comes from).
* Controls that fire: `KS-1229` -> 5; `consumeResetToken` -> 3; nonsense control -> 0.

`Refs KS-1110`; does not close it (item C is separately open there).

## Provenance

Tier-2c QA gate `2026-09-25-batch1218-t2c` (report sha256 `70dc4c987f04…`), raised as a **non-blocking** finding and recorded at the merge. Filed on the coordinator's instruction after the batch landed; it did not hold the merge.

- **New, non-blocking, raised by the gate against the merged work:** MULTILINE-IMPORT (the routing check reads indented, re-exported, required and dynamic imports, but not a **multi-line** import — which this package's own formatter produces for a long import line), CANARY-IN-PACKAGE, and T2C-ROUTING-HOME (proving the loaders themselves call `readYaml`, currently homeless).

The disclosed limit already in the code stands: a parser reached through a **computed** specifier still evades the routing check — under-reporting, the safe direction.

**Items 2-4 BUILT and RAISED — PR #1243, head `0c89e2b503d9333829c277c50ad3b1a33f03cb96`.** https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/1243

**Item 2 (READYAML-CANARY)** — now a standing cell. The raw parse runs in a **child process** on purpose: importing the parser into the suite would correctly trip the routing cell, and a child is also what a reader of a real failure sees. It asserts the unwrapped parser's error carries the file's sentinel and `readYaml`'s carries none of it, with both halves proven to have printed so a dead child cannot pass on absence.

**Item 3 (READYAML-ROUTING)** — the check was `line.startsWith('import') && line.includes(needle)`. It is now `parserImportSites()` in `tests/unit/support/readYamlRouting.ts`, reading four import positions: static (at any indent), re-export, `require()` and dynamic `import()`. A **positive control** feeds it each spelling alone and a mention-only set that must stay empty — the thing the gate recorded as missing.

**Item 4 (READYAML-SHAPES)** — the cells index `scenarios[name].thresholds['http_rate_limited']` through two optional hops; the shapes are now asserted, including that the root is not an array and the rules are arrays of strings, so they cannot pass vacuously.

**Item 1 (READYAML-UNGATED) is NOT delivered and stays open.** Wiring this suite into a gate edits the pre-push hook or the preflight. That is outside the scope this work was commissioned under, so it is stated rather than quietly dropped — and it remains, as this ticket says, the item that makes the other three moot in practice.

**Red-proof:** routing narrowed back to the old predicate -> the positive control reds; detector blinded to `[]` -> the positive control reds; `readYaml` rethrowing the parser's own error -> the canary reds; parsed arrays flattened to strings -> READYAML-SHAPES reds. Baseline 21/21 between arms; restores sha256-asserted.

**Disclosed limit:** a parser reached through a **computed** specifier (`import(base + '-yaml')`) still evades the routing check — under-reporting, the safe direction.

**Verification:** `npm run test:unit` 63 files / 1097 passed / 0 failed (base 63 / 1089 / 0); `npm run lint` rc 0 (both tsconfigs); `npm run format:check` rc 0.

title: vc-issuer credentialRepo.store() falls back to memory SILENTLY when the database is unavailable — the caller is told it was stored
description:
## BLUF

`credentialRepo.store()` **in vc-issuer writes to the in-memory map and returns SILENTLY when the database is unavailable.** The caller is told the credential was stored. Nothing is logged, so there is no artefact anywhere that the write did not reach PostgreSQL — and on restart the credential is simply gone.

**Pre-existing, and deliberately NOT counted against PR #1231** (merged 2026-09-25 as `b83f986fd3e4`). That PR made the *table-absent* fallback LOUD — two WARNs per store. **This is the sibling path it did not touch:** `store()` then `if (!isDbAvailable()) return;` with no log at all. Raised by the tier-2b QA gate as **P-1** and ruled by the coordinator to be tracked separately rather than folded into #1231's scope.

## Why it matters, stated without overclaiming

A silent success on a durability-critical write is the failure mode that cannot be investigated after the fact: there is no line to grep, no counter, no artefact. The credential is served from memory for the life of the process and then disappears. Every other symptom (a verifier 404, a revoke that finds nothing) surfaces far from the cause.

**What is NOT claimed here:** that this is currently happening in any deployed environment. It is a code path, found by reading, with the trigger condition (`isDbAvailable()` false) unmeasured in Azure or on kintsugi.

## UNMEASURED — stated rather than glossed

Carried verbatim from the gate's findings on #1231, because they bound what this ticket knows:

* **Azure reach UNMEASURED.** Whether this path is reachable in the deployed environment was not measured; the Azure role and the table's state were not read.
* **The least-privilege SELECT is UNMEASURED.** Whether the runtime role can even perform the existence check that gates the fallback is unknown.
* The **kintsugi log observation** owed against KS-1281 would, if done, also say whether the loud sibling path fires there. That observation has not been made.

So the *severity* of this ticket rests on an unmeasured reach. **Measure the reach before choosing a fix shape** — if the path is unreachable in every deployed environment, a log line is the whole fix; if it is reachable, the question is whether a silent memory write is acceptable at all for credentials.

## Fix shapes, not chosen here

1. **Log it** — match what #1231 did for the table-absent path: a WARN naming the credential id and the reason. Smallest change; makes the event investigable.
2. **Refuse it** — treat a store with no database as an error the caller must handle, rather than a success. Correct if credentials must be durable, and a behaviour change that needs its own decision.

(1) is strictly an improvement and does not foreclose (2).

## Board search before filing (team Secuura-PK, 1,284 issues incl. archived, 3,620 comments, literal match on titles, descriptions and comments)

* `isDbAvailable` -> 14 total / 7 open (KS-1120, KS-1018, KS-953, KS-871, KS-851, KS-843, KS-577). Read for overlap; all concern other services or other call sites.
* `credentialRepo` -> 7 total / 5 open. The two nearest were read in full and are **NOT** duplicates: **KS-1121** is `getById` resolving by SUBSTRING (a disclosure defect, different function); **KS-1120** is presentations test-coverage gaps from #966.
* `vc_credentials_store` -> 3 total / 2 open (KS-1281, KS-1121). `services/vc-issuer` -> 30 total / 14 open. `memory fallback` -> 13 total / 5 open, none on this path. `falls back to memory` -> 0.
* Controls that fire: `KS-1281` -> 1; `consumeResetToken` -> 2. So the search discriminates.

## Provenance

Tier-2b QA gate `2026-09-25-batch1225-t2-r1` on PR #1231, finding **P-1**, at head `bd1d2daec2bf`. Filed at the merge of #1231 onto `develop` `b83f986fd3e47b66054d23a350e5aef6d80d0550`, on the coordinator's instruction. `Refs KS-1281`; it does not close it.

nodes.body:
**BLUF:** At develop `07a2d62be6a0`, `store()` in vc-issuer has a second memory-only branch that this ticket does not name: when the database INSERT throws, the catch logs "DB write failed for credential — kept in memory" and returns without throwing. The branch this ticket names (`isDbAvailable()` false, now warned) is the first of the two. A credential left in the second state is the one KS-1993 describes: it has no database row, and every revoke of it answers 503 "Retry the revoke."

Source: `Blockchain/Dev/services/vc-issuer/src/repositories/credentialRepo.ts` lines 68 to 101 at develop `07a2d62be6a0` (read in a depth-1 clone by Seat S 19th); KS-1993.

* `store()` writes the credential into `memoryStore` at line 69 before either branch.
* `isDbAvailable()` false: the warning "Credential stored in memory only — the database is unavailable" at lines 80 to 83, then a return (lines 73 to 85). This is the branch this ticket names and PR 1267 changed.
* INSERT throws: the catch at lines 95 to 100 logs "DB write failed for credential — kept in memory" with the credential id and the thrown message (an unguarded `err?.message` read, which KS-1959 names), then the function returns without throwing.
* In both branches the credential has no database row and `store()` raises no error to its caller.

Wednesday ruled (2026-11-05, ANSWER to Seat S 19th, 23:40:08Z) that one test pass would prove both fall-backs, so the second branch is recorded here and not as a new ticket.

Not measured: whether either branch is reached in any deployed environment; what the issuing route answers when `store()` takes the INSERT-failure branch (that route was not read); no test and no service was run by this seat.

**BLUF:** The owed log read on kintsugi found the fallback warning 0 times, but the window is short: it covers only the container started in today's deploy. Delivered: PR 1267 merged as 6d5c009b5731 on develop, deployed to kintsugi at ee1e1b832115 (kintsugi's REVISION head, read 2026-11-04 01:59Z). Left open: whether the `isDbAvailable()` false trigger is ever reached is still unmeasured.

- **Probe (read-only `docker logs`, 2026-11-04 02:13Z):** `secuura-vc-issuer`, started 01:41:20Z, 148 log lines, 0 lines with `Credential stored in memory only`.
- The earlier containers' logs were replaced by the deploy, so this read says nothing about before 01:41Z.

**BLUF:** Delivered: PR 1267 merged as 6d5c009b5731 on develop, deployed to kintsugi at b1fb543640e7 (carried deploy record of 2026-11-01, not re-measured today). Verified by code read, not observed live: `Blockchain/Dev/services/vc-issuer/src/repositories/credentialRepo.ts:80` now logs a warning, 'Credential stored in memory only', where store() used to fall back silently (shape 1, log it, as scoped). Left open: observation owed. The 2026-09-25 merge comment says the ticket's own UNMEASURED section stands: whether the isDbAvailable() false trigger is reached in any deployed environment, Azure or kintsugi, and whether the privilege role can perform the existence check at all, both need a deployed read; the kintsugi log observation owed against KS-1281 has not been made.

**Merged to `develop` as squash `6d5c009b57319e8145bd4497547ca86dc6f58ffd`** (PR #1267, head `71f6f4d73cbde5b32f1564c9171eb1b705f77880`). **Staying In Progress, as the gate addendum directs.**

- **What landed:** `store()` no longer keeps a credential in memory silently when the database is unavailable — the path now warns, so a caller can tell a persisted credential from one that exists only in this process. Two files: the `ks1295` test and `credentialRepo.ts`.
- **⚠ This merge carried a THREE-WAY merged blob, not the head's own, and that mattered.** `credentialRepo.ts` was changed on `develop` after this pull request forked, so the head's blob would have **reverted** that earlier correction. The merge took the 3-way result `c93152727c3977bbbf853a556c8ad55a7faa2794` instead. Verified independently **before** merging: re-running the 3-way merge from develop's blob (`13570cde`), the merge-base's (`8a46bbf7`) and the head's (`94fae265`) reproduced `c93152727c39` exactly, and the merged text was measured to keep develop's corrected wording — 0 occurrences of the withdrawn "auto-created" claim, against 2 in the head's own blob. Confirmed again after the merge: `credentialRepo.ts` at develop reads `c93152727c39`.
- **Base-invariant at the merge:** squash tree == the tree predicted before the merge ran, parent == the develop predicted over, 2 paths touched, both equality targets equal with modes preserved.
- **Why it does not close:** the ticket's own UNMEASURED section still stands — whether the `isDbAvailable()` false trigger is reached in any deployed environment was not measured, in Azure or on kintsugi, and this merge does not measure it.

**PR [#1267](https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/1267) raised — READY FOR QA.** Head `71f6f4d73cbde5b32f1564c9171eb1b705f77880`, base `develop` `4db87c3e4b98`. Not merged.

**Shape (1) only, as scoped: LOG it.** A WARN on `credentialRepo.ts:50` naming the credential id and the reason, matching what #1231 did for the table-absent path. **Shape (2) — refusing the write — is NOT built here**; it is a behaviour change needing its own decision, and (1) does not foreclose it.

`loadFromDb()`'s identical early return at `:207` is a startup read, not a store, and is untouched. The file's bare silent returns go **2 → 1**.

**Three cells, in a new file.** `credentialRepo.test.ts` mocks `isDbAvailable` as a module-scope `vi.fn(() => false)` and so **cannot produce the database-AVAILABLE arm** — without which "the WARN does not fire" would be untested.

- **W1** database unavailable → exactly one WARN carrying `credentialId` and a reason; **no SQL issued at all**, so the WARN provably came from this branch; the credential is still retrievable from memory.
- **W2** database available → no such WARN, **and the INSERT is proven to have been issued** with the expected parameters. That control is the point: without it W2 would also pass on a `store()` that did nothing, or if the WARN text had been misspelled out of existence.
- **W3** two stores → two WARNs, in credential order.

**Red proof:** reverted to develop, **W1 and W3 go RED, W2 stays GREEN** — correct, because W2 asserts an absence true on both sides. It is the control, not a result.

vc-issuer **129/129 → 132/132**, `tsc --noEmit` rc 0, the new file type-checked separately under `exclude: []` (0 errors in it). Push preflight **12/15, 3 skipped (legs 3, 4, 8)**; not quoted as a pass.

⚠ **This PR does not measure the reach, and the ticket's severity rests on it.** Whether `isDbAvailable()` is ever false in the deployed Azure environment, and whether the least-privilege role can perform the existence check at all, remain **UNMEASURED** — both need a deployed read. The kintsugi log observation owed against KS-1281 has still not been made. A WARN is an improvement regardless; it is not evidence the path fires anywhere.

Ticket stays In Progress.

title: Nothing runs `tsc -p packages/shared` — the push preflight has no project type-check leg, so a type error is invisible (KS-872 acceptance, second half)
description:
## BLUF

`npx tsc -p packages/shared --noEmit` is **not run by anything**. Not by the push preflight's fifteen legs, not by vitest (which does not type-check), not by any remaining CI. A type error in `packages/shared` is therefore red in `tsc` and **invisible everywhere the team actually looks**.

KS-872 was filed when exactly that happened: `crypto.JsonWebKey` vanished in `@types/node` 26.1.0 and the project tsc went red on develop with nobody noticing. That ticket's acceptance has two halves. The fix is one; **this is the other** — *"either the preflight gains a shared project type-check leg, or a ticket says explicitly why it should not."*

## Measured today (2026-09-25, at develop `6ab9d5021e96`)

`npx tsc -p packages/shared --noEmit` exits **rc 0**, zero output, on a clean `npm ci` at `Blockchain/Dev`. A planted `const x: number = 'not a number'` gives **rc 2 / TS2322**, and removing it returns rc 0 — so the check is live, and the original error genuinely does not reproduce.

**Why it is green is the point, and it is fragile.** `npm ci` NESTS `packages/shared/node_modules/@types/node@20.19.43` (the package declares `^20.11.5`) beside the hoisted `@types/node@26.1.0`. The nested 20.x still carries `crypto.JsonWebKey` at `crypto.d.ts:513`; in 26.1.0 that interface moved to `webcrypto.JsonWebKey` (`crypto.d.ts:3630`). **Nothing pins that nesting.** A hoist change, a dedupe, or a lockfile refresh can remove it, and the error returns — to a check that still nobody runs.

## Ask

Add a `packages/shared` project type-check leg to the push preflight (`.githooks/pre-push`), **or** record here why it should not exist. If it is added it needs a planted-error control, like every other leg — a type-check that cannot fail is the failure mode this ticket is about.

## Searched before filing

Six terms, `includeArchived: true`, every page literal-matched on the title: `type-check leg` (50 fuzzy / **0** literal), `tsc` (50 / **12**), `preflight leg` (50 / **8**), `project type-check` (50 / **0**), `packages/shared tsc` (50 / **0**), `noEmit` (50 / **1**). **KS-872 itself has zero relations, zero inverse relations and zero children.**

Nearest, and all a different class:

* **KS-892** and **KS-933** — both *Duplicate/ARCHIVED* — say the project tsc is VACUOUS for `src/__tests__` because the tsconfig excludes it. That is *"the tsc does not cover enough"*, not *"no leg runs the tsc"*. Named rather than linked: archived issues refuse relations.
* **KS-1000 / KS-1122 / KS-848 / KS-1090** — the same excludes-`__tests__` class in auth, vc-issuer, kyc and api-gateway.
* **KS-910 / KS-1040** — preflight *leg* tickets, but legs 12 and 4.

**No open home; filed new.**

---

*Filed by Seat L3, 2026-09-25, on Wednesday's ruling (ANSWER Q1b). Carries the second half of KS-872's acceptance;* `.githooks/` *is in no seat's lane this round.*

title: Lockfile edits move platform discriminators silently: an npm command inside a workspace MEMBER rewrites the ROOT lock (0 version changes, 12 lines of dev/devOptional churn), and an isolated resolve on darwin/arm64 strips os/cpu/libc markers (26 entries from frontend/issuer, 30 libc lines from services/mcp-server incl. the musl markers node:24-alpine needs, 103 entries on a full root re-resolution) — cause side of KS-1154; push-gate leg PROPOSED for Kam
description:
## BLUF

Two measured hazards in how this repo's lockfiles get edited on a developer host. Both produced wrong bytes in a working tree on 2026-09-25 before a per-file check caught them; neither is visible in `git diff --numstat` as anything but a small diff.

**TRAP 1 — an npm command run inside a workspace MEMBER rewrites the workspace ROOT lock, not the member's own lock.** `Blockchain/Dev/package.json` declares `workspaces: ["packages/*","services/*","frontend/*"]`, so `services/originate`, `services/mcp-server` and the frontends are members — while each also carries its own tracked standalone `package-lock.json`, which is what `scripts/audit/audit-locks.mjs` reads (43 of the 45 tracked locks). Measured: `npm install --package-lock-only --ignore-scripts` run **inside** `services/originate` left `services/originate/package-lock.json` **byte-unchanged** and instead rewrote `Blockchain/Dev/package-lock.json` — 12 lines, eleven `lightningcss-*` platform binaries plus `magicast` flipping `devOptional` → `dev: true`, with **0 packages added, 0 removed, 0 version-changed**. `npm update @hono/node-server` inside `services/mcp-server` moved **nothing at all**. So the in-place route silently misses its target and dirties a file the change must not touch.

**TRAP 2 — resolving a standalone lock in an isolated copy STRIPS platform discriminators for every host but the one resolving.** The isolated route writes the right file, but re-resolves optional platform deps for the current host (Darwin/arm64) and drops the rest. Measured, same session, npm 11.5.1 / node 24.7.0:

| lock | collateral |
| -- | -- |
| `frontend/issuer/package-lock.json` | **26 entries removed** — `emnapi/runtime` plus **25** `rollup/rollup-<platform>` **binaries** |
| `frontend/admin`, `frontend/verifier` | 1 entry removed each |
| `services/mcp-server/package-lock.json` | **30 lines of** `libc` **blocks deleted** — ten `"libc": ["glibc"]` / `["musl"]` markers |
| `Blockchain/Dev/package-lock.json` (full re-resolution) | **103 entries removed** — esbuild 75, rolldown 13, lightningcss 10, cbor-extract 5. **103 of 103 carry an** `os`**/**`cpu` **constraint; 0 do not.** |

**Every service Dockerfile is** `node:24-alpine`**, i.e. musl**, so removing a `"libc": ["musl"]` discriminator is not cosmetic. And the frontends are built in Linux containers, so removing `rollup-linux-*` breaks their build.

*(npm scope sigils are omitted above —* `rollup/rollup-linux-x64-gnu` *means the scoped package; the symbols stay searchable.)*

## Relation to KS-1154 — read both; they are cause and symptom

**KS-1154** (Backlog) is *"Root package-lock.json carries only rollup-darwin-arm64 — npm ci on ubuntu installs no Linux rollup binary…"*. That is **one symptom**: a binary already absent from the root lock. This ticket is the **mechanism that keeps removing them**, in both directions and across every lock, plus TRAP 1, which KS-1154 does not mention at all.

KS-1154's own "Ancestors" paragraph states the link in its own words: *"The lock has lost a platform binary set three times now; the regen-on-one-host shape is what keeps re-creating it."* Its ancestors KS-653 and KS-376 (both Done, archived) are the two earlier recurrences. KS-1154's guard proposal is a **lockfile cell pinning the rollup set**; this ticket's proposal below is a **push-gate leg covering every discriminator in every lock**, which would have caught all three past recurrences and this one.

**Not a duplicate, and KS-1154 should not be closed by this:** KS-1154 has its own "Done when" (add `rollup-linux-x64-gnu`, green the advisory job's step 6). This ticket does not add that binary.

## The proven workaround, in use now

Both scripts live at `5_Project_History/2026-09-25_seatB-25th/raise/` and were used to build the KS-530 and KS-528 lock changes:

* `lockresolve21.sh` — copies a member's two manifests into an isolated dir **outside every workspace**, resolves there, copies the lock back. Fixes TRAP 1. Its header carries the measurement.
* `splice_lock21.py` — takes **only** the named packages' entries from npm's own output (authoritative `version` / `resolved` / `integrity` / inner pins) and splices them into the pristine lock; every other byte stays pristine. Fixes TRAP 2. It refuses if the two locks hold different keys for those packages.

Result on the two PRs built with them: **added 0 / removed 0 / version-changed N** in every lock touched, and `libc` / `os` / `cpu` / `devOptional` counts identical before and after in all seven files.

## PROPOSAL — needs Kam, not this ticket's author

**A push-gate leg: a lockfile change must not move a platform discriminator.** Per changed `package-lock.json`, compare the before/after count of `os`, `cpu`, `libc` and `devOptional` markers; refuse the push on any delta that the change does not declare. **This is a gate change, so it is Kam's call** — recorded here as a proposal, not a decision, and deliberately not built. Evidence that it works: the check read `libc` **10 → 0** on the bad `services/mcp-server` lock and **10 → 10** after the splice. It is a guard that failed when it should have.

## What was searched before filing

The whole KS board, **1,279 issues including archived**, literal substring match on title + description for: `workspace member` (3 hits, none related), `package-lock` (36), `libc` (1 — KS-366, Done/archived, a currency review), `musl` (**0**), `os/cpu` (**0**), `optional binar` (4), `platform binar` (5), `rollup-` (1 — KS-1154), `esbuild` (13), `lightningcss` (**0**), `arborist` (**0**), `devOptional` (2), `lock-regen` (6), `package-lock-only` (9). Controls: `gate` matched **930** issues (the reader fires); a symbol that cannot exist matched **0** (it does not invent). **The only candidate was KS-1154**, related above.

## Also recorded from the same session

* A **full re-resolution of the root lock does not fix** either advisory pin it was tried for: `node_modules/ip-address` stays 9.0.5 and `@prisma/dev/node_modules/@hono/node-server` stays 1.19.11, with and without `overrides`. So a regen is not a fix and is destructive — see the 103-entry row above.
* `npm install --package-lock-only` is **inert for a version bump** on npm 11.5.1: it prints `up to date` and moves nothing. `npm update <pkg>` is what moves it. A command that reports success while doing nothing.
* Resolving a workspace root **from bare manifests with no** `node_modules` crashes npm: `TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'edgesOut')` at `#loadPeerSet` (`@npmcli/arborist/lib/arborist/build-ideal-tree.js:1314`) — peer-dependency resolution, reproducible. With `node_modules` present it completes. Not a repo defect; a constraint on how any future measurement must be run.

## Done when

- [ ] `docs/DEV-PROCESS.md` carries both traps and names the two scripts as the way to edit a lockfile
- [ ] the two scripts live somewhere durable in the repo rather than in one seat's record folder
- [ ] the push-gate leg is decided by Kam — built, or recorded as declined with the reason

title: cardano/transaction.ts: add_json_metadatum_with_schema throws on any metadata string over 64 bytes — KS-721's identityCommitment (≥69 bytes) has never been anchorable on a real chain
description:
## BLUF

`Blockchain/Dev/services/anchoring/src/cardano/transaction.ts:107` attaches every anchor's metadata with `txBuilder.add_json_metadatum_with_schema(label, JSON.stringify(metadataPayload), CSL.MetadataJsonSchema.BasicConversions)`. With the lockfile-pinned `@emurgo/cardano-serialization-lib-nodejs` **15.0.3** (`Blockchain/Dev/package-lock.json`), that call **throws for ANY string value over 64 bytes**: `Max metadata string too long: 65, max = 64`. This is Cardano's own metadata rule (text strings and byte strings in transaction metadata are capped at 64 bytes each), surfaced by CSL at tx build.

**Consequence for KS-721:** the `identityCommitment` accepted since 2026-08-31 (#763, `436f37bed`) has the form `<label>.v<N>:<64 lowercase hex>`, whose regex minimum is **69 bytes** (`a.v1:` + 64). Platform-S's real value (`identity-commitment-l2.v1:<64 hex>`) is **90 bytes**. So every non-mock anchor carrying a commitment would fail at `buildAnchorTransaction` before submission — **the field has never been anchorable on a real chain through this code.** Nothing has hit it yet because: (a) the mock branch (`cardano/index.ts:234-238`) hands `JSON.stringify(payload)` to the mock provider and never touches CSL, which is why KS-721 could only be proven in mock mode ("no chain write was possible", history.md); (b) S ships `CardanoAnchor:AnchorIdentity = false` (PS-870), so S has never sent the field; (c) K's own originate→anchoring hops forward only `documentId`/`contentHash`/`network`. Every real preview anchor confirmed to date is all-short (64-hex hash, doc ids, ISO timestamps, verbs), so the demo's 194 confirmed anchors are unaffected.

**Consequence for KS-1175:** `actorDid`/`orgDid` (≤512 bytes) inherit the same limit. The KS-1175 PR fixes this at the tx-build boundary (see below) and `Refs` this ticket; this ticket is filed separately because it is a separate fix (KS-721's latent defect), per the one-ticket-per-fix rule.

## Measurement (2026-09-20, Seat A 15th, at develop `dc061f2bb6dff9180a0724b1d1d5c50b9a0173fa`)

Instrument: `5_Project_History/2026-09-20_seatA-15th/boot/csl_probe.cjs` — pure wasm against the worktree's hoisted CSL 15.0.3; no chain, no port, no wallet. Both directions:

| input | `encode_json_str_to_metadatum(…, BasicConversions)` |
| -- | -- |
| 64-char string | OK (78 bytes) |
| 65-char string | THROWS `Max metadata string too long: 65, max = 64` |
| minimal KS-721 commitment `a.v1:<64 hex>` (69) | THROWS |
| S's `identity-commitment-l2.v1:<64 hex>` (90) | THROWS |
| 512-char `did:web:…` | THROWS |
| array of 2 × 45-char strings | OK (107 bytes) |
| an all-short realistic anchor payload (hash/documentType/occurredAt/timestamps) | OK (305 bytes) |

And through the exact call `transaction.ts:107` makes — a `TransactionBuilder` built from fabricated protocol params: 69-byte commitment THROWS, 64-byte string OK. Wednesday reproduced the same table independently at 22:00 AEST (her `csl_probe2.js`).

`transaction.ts:107` is the **single** attach point for BOTH labels (674 single, 675 batch); `index.ts:744` (`json_metadata.secuura` off Blockfrost) is the single chain reader. No other encoder/decoder exists under `services/anchoring/src` (grep, non-test).

## Fix (shipping in the KS-1175 PR, as its own named test block)

A pure helper `services/anchoring/src/cardano/cardanoMetadatum.ts`: `toCardanoMetadatum(payload)` replaces any string > 64 UTF-8 bytes with an ARRAY of ≤64-byte chunks split on character boundaries (byte count, never `.length`); `fromCardanoMetadatum(md)` joins an all-string array back. Consequence to document: an independent chain reader (Cardanoscan / raw Blockfrost) sees a long value as an array — the standard Cardano convention for >64-byte metadata strings.

A CSL version bump (it changes the on-chain encoder for every anchor — its own ticket if ever). KS-721 itself stays archived (`Deployed to UAT`); this ticket `Refs KS-721`.

title: POST /api/certifications/:id/verify forwards a revoked session's Bearer to originate: the gateway's session check never runs on this route
description:
## BLUF

`POST /api/certifications/:id/verify` (api-gateway `routes/verification.ts:784`, mounted with no `authenticateToken`) forwards whatever `Authorization` the caller sent to originate's `GET /api/documents/:id` (`:788`). Measured in-process: a **REVOKED** session's JWT, alone or beside a valid connector key, reaches originate as that user's Bearer, because the gateway's session check never runs on this route. On `POST /api/documents/:id/verify` (`:488`, `authenticateToken(true)`) the same revoked JWT alone is refused 401 `SESSION_INVALIDATED`. What originate does with that token is **NOT measured**.

## Recommendation

Measure originate's `GET /api/documents/:id` with a revoked session's JWT. That sets the severity, which the gate graded Minor pending that measurement.

## Detail

* Surfaced by the #1070-#1076 gate (`2026-09-19-batch1070-1076-tier1-r1`, finding N76-2).
* Pre-existing, not introduced by that batch: api-gateway product bytes are identical at develop `51dbedd39` and at every head of the batch. `verification.ts` is unchanged at develop `f9c28a8b8`.
* How the gate measured it: in-process, the real gateway app with loopback doubles; not against a live stack or a real session store.
* Related: KS-834, the pending decision on whether this route stays public. KS-834's text says a caller who sends a token "is still scoped downstream"; this finding is that a *revoked* session's token passes the gateway here unchecked.
* Also related: the revocation property established on the authenticated mounts (KS-1207, KS-1215).
* Board search before filing (Secuura-PK, archived included):
  * literal title/description contains `certifications/:id/verify`: KS-834, KS-815 (archived, a control-byte guard);
  * `certifications/{id}/verify`: 0; `verification.ts:78`: 0;
  * `api/certifications/`: 38, none about Bearer forwarding;
  * `searchIssues("certifications verify")`, literal re-match: KS-834, KS-815.
  * None records the revoked-session forwarding.

title: Hosted verification: "Back" from the Entra page lands on `/identity/verify/{id}` (the attempt's own page) instead of the selection page — PS-800's Back routing regressed, or an open attempt left by an earlier failed spec is being resumed
description:
## BLUF

`hosted_verification_routing.spec.ts` › *Back from the Entra page lands on the selection, and the attempt is closed rather than left InProgress* ([PS-800](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-800/back-or-a-failure-inside-a-hosted-id-verification-entra-stripe-lands)) failed on 18 Sep: after clicking Back on the Entra page the browser landed on `/identity/verify/41` — a specific verification's page — where [PS-731](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-731/ps-730-phase-0-one-returnsurfaces-resolver-for-retval-replacing-twelve)/[PS-800](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-800/back-or-a-failure-inside-a-hosted-id-verification-entra-stripe-lands) say Back must return to `/identity/verify`, the selection page. It passed on 17 Sep against the same S code, so this is either a routing regression that arrived with the day's K change, or — the lead I'd check first — an **open verification (#41) left behind by an earlier failed spec in the same run**, which `KycVerificationController`'s "still-open verification worth resuming" logic then routes Back into. Either way it's worth a quick look: if a leftover attempt can hijack Back, a real user who abandoned one hosted attempt would see the same thing.

## Evidence

* Run: `STACK_SLOT=2 npm test`, 18 Sep 09:15 BST, project `role-kyc`. `expect(page).toHaveURL(/\/identity\/verify$/)` received `https://localhost:5222/identity/verify/41` (24 polls over 10 s, stable).
* Artefacts: `systemTest/reports/test-results-2026-09-18T08-15-20-705Z-slot2/tests-functional-hosted_ve-3e0b1-rather-than-left-InProgress-role-kyc-slot2/` — `trace.zip`, `test-failed-1.png`, `error-context.md`.
* In the **same session** (run 3, 08:30 BST) `kyc_verification.spec.ts` › *attaching a document and a selfie records both checks* failed with a "Page not found" after the document POST — i.e. a native KYC attempt was started and not cleaned up. The `role-kyc` account is dedicated and shared by both specs ([PS-608](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-608/systemtest-kyc-verification-specs-are-not-parallel-safe-gotostart)), so an attempt one spec leaves open is exactly what the other spec's Back would resume.
* Code lead: `ssd/Controllers/KycVerificationController.cs:459` "The caller's still-open verification worth resuming, if any. [PS-800](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-800/back-or-a-failure-inside-a-hosted-id-verification-entra-stripe-lands): a hosted provider…"; the Entra page's Back is the [PS-731](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-731/ps-730-phase-0-one-returnsurfaces-resolver-for-retval-replacing-twelve) return.
* Not related to PR #866 (markup/POMs only); surfaced because that branch ran the full suite five times.

## Why it matters

* [PS-800](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-800/back-or-a-failure-inside-a-hosted-id-verification-entra-stripe-lands) fixed exactly this: Back or a failure inside a hosted verification must not strand the person on the attempt's page or leave it InProgress. If an older open attempt can redirect Back, the fix has a gap for the "abandoned once, tried again" path.
* If it is only suite state, the spec needs a precondition (abandon any open attempt before `makeEntraAttempt`) so `role-kyc` is not order-dependent — that half is a `systemTest/` change (Peter can take it).

## Acceptance

* Either: with an open native attempt on the account, Back from a hosted attempt still lands on `/identity/verify` (product), **or** it is confirmed that resuming the open attempt is the intended behaviour, documented on [PS-800](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-800/back-or-a-failure-inside-a-hosted-id-verification-entra-stripe-lands), and the spec resets state first (suite).
* ✅ **DONE (suite half) —** [PS-863](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-863/systemtest-role-kyc-specs-share-one-login-across-parallel-workers-so-a), PR #887, merged 29 Sep 2026 (`ab2b810f`). `hosted_verification_routing.spec.ts` passes in a full run regardless of what `kyc_verification.spec.ts` left behind. Each Playwright parallel slot now signs in as its own KYC persona (`fixtures/kyc_pool_test.ts`), so no spec can leave an open attempt on another's person. The spec passed in all six K-paired full runs on 28 Sep. **The product half above (should Back ever resume an older open native attempt?) is still open for Stuart.**

**Playwright test that demonstrates the product half** (required): extend `systemTest/tests/functional/hosted_verification_routing.spec.ts` — the file whose [PS-800](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-800/back-or-a-failure-inside-a-hosted-id-verification-entra-stripe-lands) case found this, and now parallel-safe per persona since #887, so it can set up the precondition deliberately instead of inheriting it. Against a live stack, as that worker's own KYC persona:

1. **start a native verification and leave it open** (post nothing, or post one document and stop) — the precondition that used to arrive by accident from `kyc_verification.spec.ts`;
2. then start a **hosted (Entra)** attempt and click Back on the Entra page;
3. assert `await expect(page).toHaveURL(/\/identity\/verify$/)` — the selection page, not `/identity/verify/{id}`;
4. assert the hosted attempt is **not** left `InProgress` — the [PS-800](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-800/back-or-a-failure-inside-a-hosted-id-verification-entra-stripe-lands) half — and that the older native attempt is still listed in `kyc-history` with its own status, so "land on the selection page" is not achieved by silently closing the person's other work.

If the ruling instead is that resuming an older open attempt **is** intended, the same spec inverts: step 3 asserts the URL is `/identity/verify/{thatAttemptId}` and the Details page offers a way out — an abandon control or the evidence form — so the person is never stranded. Either way the stranding is what the spec must make impossible; which of the two URLs is correct is Stuart's decision, and the spec should be written after it, not before.

**Which assertion fails on** `develop` **today:** step 3 in the first form. Measured 18 Sep on slot 2 — `expect(page).toHaveURL(/\/identity\/verify$/)` received `https://localhost:5222/identity/verify/41`, stable over 24 polls across 10 s. With the suite half fixed, that landing is now reproducible on purpose rather than by order, which is exactly what makes the product half testable.

**Control assertions that pass today and must keep passing:** the existing [PS-800](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-800/back-or-a-failure-inside-a-hosted-id-verification-entra-stripe-lands) case with **no** older open attempt — Back from the Entra page lands on `/identity/verify` and the attempt is closed — and the rest of the `role-kyc` project, green in all six K-paired full runs on 28 Sep. The fix must not be "never resume anything", which would break the deliberate resume path `OpenVerificationForAsync` exists for.

xUnit companion: once the ruling is made, pin it on `KycVerificationLifecycle` / `OpenVerificationForAsync` — which statuses are resumable, and from which entry point. That rule runs with nothing up. The Playwright spec is still required because the defect is a *navigation outcome* across two pages and a provider round-trip; `KycVerificationController.cs:459`'s "still-open verification worth resuming" comment is correct in isolation and only misbehaves in the journey.

## Environment

platform-s `develop` e1ad1f2a (+ PR #866) · platform-k `develop` 8b9c3f022 · slot 2 · 18 Sep 2026.

Every `@role-kyc` spec used to sign in as the one `e2e-kyc` account. `hosted_verification_routing.spec.ts` and `kyc_verification.spec.ts` ran on different workers, so while this spec pressed Back, the other file could hold an open native verification on the **same person**. `/identity/verify` then correctly resumed into that neighbour's `/identity/verify/{id}`, which matches the evidence above: #41, plus a native attempt in the same session that 404'd after its document POST. PS-863's comment of 16 Sep records the same shape on slot 4 (`/identity/verify/3`).

The acceptance's product alternative: with an open native attempt on the **same** account, should Back from a hosted attempt land on `/identity/verify`, or is resuming the open attempt intended (and documented on PS-800)? Real users, unlike the suite, can have one of each. Stuart's decision.

title: api-gateway vitest suite is not isolation-safe: --no-isolate reds 10 of 30 runs non-deterministically at develop
description:
**From the #1040 / KS-1125 batch gate, finding N40-1: Minor, pre-existing (measured AT DEVELOP).**

## What's wrong

The api-gateway suite passes only because vitest isolates each file. With `--no-isolate`, it reds **10 of 30 runs, non-deterministically**, at develop, before any of the batch's PRs. Files leak module state, `process.env` changes and globals into each other. KS-1125's new file adds to the pattern (N40-2: unrestored `process.env` deletes and a global it never removes), though isolation contains it.

## Why it matters

A suite that needs isolation to pass hides order-dependent bugs, and switching to a faster pool or a shared worker would turn them into flaky reds.

## What to do

Run the suite with `--no-isolate` repeatedly and bisect the leaking files. Restore env and globals in each file's `afterAll`, and add a CI-equivalent local check that runs the suite un-isolated.

title: Connector allow-list still fails OPEN when Redis closes or errors at runtime, on a read error (catch {}), or on LRU eviction of platform-settings
description:
**From the #1038 / KS-1233 batch gate, finding N38-1: Major, pre-existing. Not #1038's regression.**

## What's wrong

KS-1233 (#1038, merged `e51686bed`) stops `platform-settings` expiring on a TTL. But a **missing** key is still read as "no restriction". The allow-list therefore still **fails open** on every other way the key can go missing or unreadable:

* a runtime Redis close or error (the gate's row R6, measured over a stateful fake);
* a read error swallowed by a bare `catch {}`;
* LRU eviction of the key.

In each case every restricted connector becomes unrestricted.

## Why it matters

It is the same fail-open class KS-1233 fixed for the TTL trigger. A connector allow-list should fail **closed** when the configuration cannot be read.

## What to do

Make the reader fail closed. A missing or unreadable `platform-settings` should refuse restricted connector operations (or fall back to a persisted source), not grant everything. Add cells for the close, error and eviction paths. Check the other readers in the gate's reader census (section C) for the same class.

title: Spec-example guard E7: the 40-char floor means a 38-39-char secret-shaped value is never a finding (sk_<uuid>, pk_<uuid>, 39-char random tokens)
description:
**From the #922 tier-2 gate, round 2 (F11, Minor, pre-existing), 2026-09-18.** #922 neither causes nor widens it.

## What's wrong

E7 returns before it reads `BENIGN_SHAPES` for any value under 40 chars (`HIGH_ENTROPY_RE = /^[A-Za-z0-9+/=_-]{40,}$/`, `contract.mjs`; `rules-example.mjs:87-88`). So a 38-39-char value is never an E7 finding at all, deny list or not. That covers `sk_<uuid>`, `pk_<uuid>`, any 1-2-letter prefix plus a uuid, and a 39-char random secret-shaped value; the gate probed no finding at round 1 or at head. **No other rule (E1-E9) covers a short random token in a field that is not id-named or password-named.**

## Why it matters

Real-world key formats shorter than 40 chars would pass the only name-blind secret rule the published-spec guard has.

## What to do

Decide the floor from the key formats the platform and its integrators actually use (measure them), or add a second, shorter rule for secret-shaped prefixes. Pin the boundary with cells either side.

---

title: Spec-example guard E7: the secret-name deny list in PREFIXED_UUID_RE is a denylist - tok_/sess_/sid_/pass_/refresh_/access_/csrf_/nonce_/invite_/reset_/totp_/hmac_/oauth_/creds_ + v4 are still admitted
description:
**From the #922 tier-2 gate, round 2 (F9, Polish, TICKET), 2026-09-18.** #922 merged as `570ea002d`.

## What's wrong

`PREFIXED_UUID_RE` (`scripts/spec-examples/check/contract.mjs`) refuses secret-NAMED prefixes with a **deny list**. The gate probed that `tok_`, `sess_`, `sid_`, `pass_`, `refresh_`, `access_`, `csrf_`, `nonce_`, `invite_`, `reset_`, `totp_`, `hmac_`, `oauth_` and `creds_`, each followed by a lower-case v4 uuid (43-44 chars, so E7 reaches them), are still admitted. They were admitted at round 1 too.

**Not a blocker today**, measured by the gate:

* the pre-existing bare-uuid shape already exempts the same uuid unprefixed;
* the minter census has **0** uuid-minted prefixed credentials;
* the spec holds exactly 1 prefixed value, the anchor id.

## What to do

The robust fix is an **ALLOW list of the minted prefixes** (the census's 13 benign ones: `anchor` `audit` `batch` `ce` `conn` `did` `event` `evt` `int` `req` `site` `sync` `ts`) in place of the deny list. Then a new record prefix is a reviewed addition, and a new credential name needs no foresight. Pin each allowed prefix with a guard-driven cell and red-proof the list. The same family as KS-1252.

---

Filed from the gate report `2026-09-18-ks679-922-30c773ee8-tier2-r2` (F9).

nodes.body:
**#1227 is MERGED** to `develop` as `7f06f3d4044d`. tier-2b QA gate `2026-09-25-batch1225-t2-r1`, GO WITH FINDINGS. The PR carries this ticket and KS-1252.

**Ticket stays In Progress — deliberately.** The **14 credential names are refused (CLOSED)**, but **the allow-list shape stays OPEN by ruling**: this ticket's own recommendation was not available from the lane that built the PR, so the deny-list approach shipped and the allow-list question is still yours to answer.

**The residual that makes the shape matter:** the thirteen minted prefixes are pinned by a typed list, so a newly minted prefix is not checked against the deny list. That is the failure mode an allow list would not have.

**Suites:** new suite 6/2 at base -> 8/0 at head -> 8/0 merged (bash 3.2.57); `run-shell-suites` 58/58 -> 59/59 on the batch end.

Base-invariant: head == the GO's pin, three-dot diff == the PR's own paths, every blob and mode == the gate's equality targets, squash verified at origin afterwards.*

## The recommended ALLOW list is a TWO-FILE change and cannot land from the scripts side alone — measured at develop `6ab9d5021e96`

This ticket recommends replacing `PREFIXED_UUID_RE`'s deny list with **an ALLOW list of the minted
prefixes**. Measured before writing it: that change **reddens two rows** in
`Blockchain/Dev/packages/shared/src/__tests__/ks256-spec-example-contract.test.ts`, which imports
`scripts/spec-examples/check/contract.mjs` directly and asserts on both patterns.

Three candidates, run through the tip's own `BENIGN_SHAPES` and `HIGH_ENTROPY_RE`, against that file's
19 `BOUNDARY_ROWS`, its 20 `SECRET_NAMED` rows, its 5-row under-40 prefix table and its
`refused === ['key']` assertion, all copied verbatim:

| candidate | `ks256` ROWS | prefix table | `refused===['key']` | the 14 probed prefixes | spec's `anchor_…` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **current (control)** | 0 mismatches | 0 | OK | **14/14 still admitted** | benign |
| **A — the ALLOW list this ticket recommends** | **2 mismatches** | 0 | OK | 0/14 (closed) | benign |
| **B — keep the deny shape, add the 14 as EXACT prefixes** | **0 mismatches** | 0 | OK | **0/14 (closed)** | benign |

The current row is the harness's positive control: it reproduces `ks256`'s expectations exactly while
showing this defect fully open, so the instrument can both pass and fail.

**The two rows candidate A reddens**, both in `ks256-spec-example-contract.test.ts`'s `BOUNDARY_ROWS`:

- `['len12', 'abcdefghijkl_<v4>', false]`
- `['credit', 'credit_<v4>', false]`

Each asserts that a **non-secret-named** prefix stays benign. An allow list refuses both by
construction, because neither `abcdefghijkl` nor `credit` is a minted prefix.

### What ships now, and what is still owed

**Shipping as a declared NARROWING:** candidate **B** — the 14 prefixes the gate probed (`tok_`,
`sess_`, `sid_`, `pass_`, `refresh_`, `access_`, `csrf_`, `nonce_`, `invite_`, `reset_`, `totp_`,
`hmac_`, `oauth_`, `creds_`, each + a lower-case v4) move from silent to an E7 finding, with the 13
minted prefixes, `key_`'s by-design refusal, all 19 `BOUNDARY_ROWS`, all 20 `SECRET_NAMED` rows and the
published spec's findings **unchanged**. `credit_` survives because `contract.mjs`'s own comment already
records that `cred` is refused as an **exact** prefix only — and `creds_` is not `credit_`.

**Still owed, and why this ticket stays open:** the ALLOW list remains the robust shape — a new record
prefix should be a reviewed addition, and a new credential name should need no foresight. Landing it
means changing `packages/shared/src/__tests__/ks256-spec-example-contract.test.ts` in the same pass, so
it is a two-file change spanning the `scripts/` and `packages/shared/` families and belongs to a single
seat that owns both.

### Not claimed

The three candidates were compared on the regexes and on E7's verdict, not by executing
`ks256-spec-example-contract.test.ts` itself — the row expectations above are read from that file at the
tip and evaluated against the guard's exports. Nothing in `packages/shared/` was edited.

title: Spec-example guard: eslint runs `rules: {}` on scripts/**/*.mjs and the ks256 test is type-checked by nothing, so 'rc 0' on the guard checks nothing
description:
**Found by the #922 tier-2 gate (F6) on 2026-09-18, and seen again in the KS-679 round-2 evidence.** Pre-existing: #922 doesn't change it.

## What's wrong

1. **eslint checks nothing on the spec-example guard.** The Dev-root flat config gives `scripts/**/*.mjs` `"rules": {}` (`npx eslint --print-config scripts/spec-examples/check/contract.mjs`). So "eslint rc 0" on `contract.mjs` is a check that cannot fail. The gate planted a `no-unused-vars` + `no-var` control through `--stdin --stdin-filename`: it fires on the three `.ts` files and **not** on `contract.mjs`.
2. **The ks256 test is type-checked by nothing.** `packages/shared/tsconfig.json` excludes `src/__tests__`. `tsc --listFilesOnly` lists `ks256-spec-example-contract.test.ts` 0 times (control: `fixtures.ts` 1), and vitest doesn't type-check.
3. Context: the guard runs only in local pre-push preflight leg 1 (`check:openapi` then `check:spec-examples`). GitHub Actions is retired for this repo, so nothing else runs it.

## Why it matters

KS-679 round 2 (`30c773ee8`) put a new `PREFIXED_UUID_RE` and 44 cells into exactly these two files. Their evidence is the vitest run and a 17-row tamper table. A reader who sees "eslint 0/0, tsc rc 0" in a Test Evidence block would take both as real checks, and neither is.

## What to do

* Give `scripts/**/*.mjs` a real rule set (at least `eslint:recommended`) and fix what it flags.
* Type-check `src/__tests__` with a test tsconfig. Note that `extends` inherits `exclude`, so that config needs `exclude: []`.
* Add a planted-violation control for each, so each check can be seen to fail.

---

title: N-2: a 2xx whose body is not exactly top-level 'degraded' — including 200 {status:'unhealthy'} — still reads up
description:
#1037 reads a 2xx body as degraded only when it is **exactly** top-level `"degraded"`. Any other 2xx body **still reads up**, including **200** `{status:'unhealthy'}`.

Pre-existing: develop already read it as up, and #1037 neither introduced it nor fixed it. It's a real correctness gap, though. A service reporting itself unhealthy on a 200 is shown as healthy.

## What to do

Decide the vocabulary the aggregates accept (`ok`/`up`/`healthy`, `degraded`, `unhealthy`/`down`), and treat an unrecognised or unhealthy body on a 2xx as at least degraded rather than up.

---

title: T-1: authenticateToken is an async express-4 middleware with no catch — a throw after the await can kill the process
description:
`authenticateToken` in the api-gateway is an **async express-4 middleware with no catch**. Express 4 does not await a middleware's returned promise, so any future throw after the `await` becomes an **unhandled rejection**.

## Why it matters, and why it is not urgent

**Not request-reachable today** — the gate could not reach it, and it is identical at develop. Graded **Major *if* reached**.

The consequence depends on a setting most deployments do not set:

* `UNHANDLED_REJECTION_MODE` **unset =** `exit`**, the default** → the process **exits 0**, and later requests get `ECONNREFUSED`;
* under `survive` → only that one request hangs.

`survive` **is set in only two places:** `docker-compose.yml:441` and `deployment/azure/services.bicep:617`. `deploy/docker-swarm/docker-stack.yml` **and any bare** `node dist/index.js` **run in** `exit` **mode** — so the harshest behaviour is what an unconfigured deployment gets.

## What to do

Wrap the await, or adopt an async-middleware wrapper that forwards rejections to `next`. Worth doing for the whole gateway, not just this one middleware.

---
