## BLUF
For the audit trail's owner: the case-sensitivity half of this ticket is now the only part of the gateway's path-spelling class that is **deliberately left unfixed**, and it is yours to decide. PR #1466 (KS-1461) folds the other gateway checks and leaves `middleware/audit.ts` alone on purpose. Nothing was built here.

## What changed since this was filed
- `middleware/pathFold.ts` (`foldAsciiCase`, ASCII only) is on develop (KS-801, squash `672352369b8a`). If you decide the audit prefix test should ignore case, `audit.ts:210-212` can use it as the other gateway checks now do; the open design question stays as written above (whether `action` should be normalised, and what an unrouted 404 should write).
- Routing stays case insensitive on purpose. Making it case sensitive instead turned a `403` into a `200` on a scope-gated route (measured on KS-801), so please do not take that route to make `/API/...` consistent.

## One fact toward your edge check
This ticket asks which spellings the edge forwards. Measured on Kintsugi on 2026-10-12 (a `POST` with a `text/plain` body, no credentials): `/api/oauth/apps` reaches the gateway (`415`), while `/API/oauth/apps`, `/Api/oauth/apps` and `/API/documents` get a static `405 Not Allowed` page from nginx before the gateway. A lowercase `/api` prefix with a cased tail was not probed live. So on Kintsugi the unaudited `/API/` write you describe is not reachable through the edge; it is reachable wherever the gateway is exposed without a case-sensitive edge.

## Also related, filed separately
KS-1457 (three finish-time reads in `audit.ts` still use `req.path` rather than `auditPath`; one-line fixes, Backlog).

title: api-gateway meetsVerificationLevel fails open on an unknown REQUIRED level: an off-canonical document-type level admits every authenticated caller
description:
## BLUF

The api-gateway's `meetsVerificationLevel` fails OPEN when a document type's *required* level is a string outside the known order. `indexOf` returns -1 for the requirement, and every user index is `>= -1`, so any authenticated caller passes: every human level, and a connector key.

* An anonymous caller is still refused (`enforceDocumentTypeRules` answers 401 for any non-`none` level with no user).
* So a document type stored with an off-canonical level, e.g. `standrd`, admits every authenticated principal to create it (`POST /api/documents`) and to verify it (`POST /api/documents/:id/verify`).
* This is a READ-only chain. Nothing has been measured against a stored catalogue.

## Recommendation

Not built; Backlog. **Do not make it fail closed yet.** Two measurements come first; without them, a fail-closed fix could lock out every document type whose stored level string is off-canonical:

1. **The level strings actually stored in the catalogue:** `document_type_configs` in each tenant DB, and the gateway's Redis document types. Any value outside `none, basic, social, standard, enhanced, high, government` (after lowercasing) is exposed today.
2. **Who can create or edit a document type:** the auth guards on originate's admin-config router and on the gateway's template clone. That sets how reachable an off-canonical value is.

KS-1176 (the connector-key fix) deliberately leaves this behaviour unchanged, and its PR carries a cell that pins it as it is at base, so the fix cannot move it silently.

## Detail

**The comparison** (`services/api-gateway/src/services/enforcement.ts` at develop `e0f41a8fafd64fa31524390cfeab320e822f3d15`):

* `:39-47` `VERIFICATION_LEVEL_ORDER = ['none','basic','social','standard','enhanced','high','government']`.
* `:53-57` `meetsVerificationLevel(userLevel, requiredLevel)` returns `ORDER.indexOf(user) >= ORDER.indexOf(required)`, both lowercased. An unknown requirement makes `reqIdx` -1, so the result is true for every user index, including -1.
* **Creation:** `:143-151` compares `creatorVerificationLevel`. With no user, `:136-141` refuses any non-`none` string with 401, so anonymous callers are not affected.
* **Verification:** `routes/verification.ts:554-557` compares `verifierVerificationLevel` when it is not `none`, with the same -1 semantics.

**Where the level strings come from (READ):**

* originate `routes/adminConfig.ts:156-172`: `POST /document-types` checks only `name` and `code`, then inserts `creatorVerificationLevel` (default `basic`) and the other three levels as given. No level validation was found.
* api-gateway `routes/platform.ts:880-894`: the template clone inserts `creator_verification_level` / `verifier_verification_level` from `platform_document_type_templates` rows as stored. Validation was not traced.
* The gateway's Redis catalogue has a writer at `services/redis.ts:511` (`setDocumentType`). **Untraced: how the Redis catalogue is filled from those database rows**, and so whether an off-canonical DB value reaches the gateway's comparison unchanged.

**Found by** the KS-1176 census (seat A, 2026-09-17). Wednesday's ANSWER at 19:52:15Z ruled it a separate ticket, not built, with the KS-1176 fix leaving it unchanged.

### Dedupe before filing

Searched with the board's `searchIssues` (includeArchived, includeComments), keeping only literal, case-insensitive matches in title, description or comments:

* `meetsVerificationLevel`: 2 fuzzy, 2 literal (KS-1176, PS-519).
* `creatorVerificationLevel`: 3 fuzzy, 3 literal (KS-1176, PS-519, KS-364 archived).
* `reqIdx`: 0 fuzzy, 0 literal.
* `document-types`: 121 fuzzy, 13 literal (KS-1176, PS-519, and archived catalogue, Akto and conformance tickets: KS-388, KS-397, KS-364, KS-40, KS-510, KS-357, KS-118, KS-39, KS-37, KS-465, KS-144).

None is about an unknown required level. Related: KS-1176.

title: Audit log (KS-871 gate R-3/R-5): H29 attemptedEmail is never written for proxied logins; production rows are v1.* on base and #1011 round 2 changes them
description:
## BLUF

Two pre-existing audit-log gaps, recorded by the tier-1 QA gate on PR #1011 (KS-871) round 1 as R-3 and R-5. Both were re-read against #1011's round-2 head `6dc8256448b50de6a15519001a4f7032ace1ae19`. Neither is built.

* **R-3: H29** `attemptedEmail` **is never written for a login through the gateway.**
  * The audit middleware reads the email from `req.body`. The gateway does not parse bodies on `/api/auth` (a proxied prefix), so the field is absent from every login audit row, on base and on round-1 head, in test and in production mode.
  * #1011 round 2 does not change this (READ).
  * The other half of R-3: on base, a login refused 429 by the login rate limiter is audited as `unknown.create` with path `/`. The gate MEASURED its D3 shape writing `auth.login` / `/api/auth/login` instead. Round 2 uses that shape, so this half moves if #1011 merges (not measured at `6dc825644` itself).
* **R-5: in production mode the audit trail on base already spells mounted and proxied routes** `v1.*`**.**
  * In production mode (`NODE_ENV=production`) the gateway answers the measured `/api/...` writes with a 307 to their `/api/v1/...` spelling. So `v1.login` / `/api/v1/auth/login` is written where a canonical row would be `auth.login` / `/api/auth/login`.
  * **#1011 round 2 changes these rows.** It captures the canonical path at entry, which is the gate's D3 shape, and the gate measured D3 turning those production rows canonical.
  * If #1011 merges, production audit rows change spelling. Anything reading `v1.*` action names would see the change.

## Recommendation

Not built; Backlog. Two things for the owner, neither a fix decided here:

1. **R-3 (H29):** decide whether the attempted-email capture should work at all for proxied logins, and where the email should come from. Today the code expects a parsed body that the gateway deliberately does not parse on `/api/auth`.
2. **R-5:** before or when #1011 merges, check whether anything outside the repo reads audit `action` values. The gate did not test this (its NOT TESTED item 6: "the blast radius of `v1.*` actions is argued, not measured"). Candidates are the security service's audit reader, dashboards and any SIEM export. If nothing depends on `v1.*`, R-5 needs no work.

## Detail

**Source:** gate report `Testing Agent MAIN/projects/secuura/reports/2026-09-17-ks871-1011-0a1f8900c-tier1-r1/report.md` (section Records, R-3 and R-5). The census covered 1115 requests over 119 audited routes on the real app with an in-memory sink, in test and production modes. The D3 comparison is `evidence/compare_production_base_d3.out`.

### R-3: H29 `attemptedEmail`

* `services/api-gateway/src/middleware/audit.ts` at round-2 head `6dc825644` (unchanged from develop `e0f41a8fa` on these lines):
  * `:287-291` sets `attemptedEmail` only when `req.path === '/api/auth/login' && req.body && typeof req.body === 'object'`.
* `services/api-gateway/src/index.ts` at develop `e0f41a8fa`:
  * `:400-404` `proxyPaths` includes `'/api/auth'`;
  * `:413` `shouldParseBody` returns false for those prefixes;
  * `:416` the JSON body parser runs only when `shouldParseBody` is true.
  * So `req.body` is never populated for a proxied login.
* **Measured by the gate:** `details.attemptedEmail` absent on 7 + 3 login rows, for every login spelling, on every tree, in both modes.
* **Unchanged by round 2 (READ):** round 2's `audit.ts` diff touches `deriveAction`'s path source and `details.path` only. The two other finish-time `req.path` reads, the login user-id extraction (`:261`) and the warning-log path (`:333`), are also untouched.
* **The 429 half.** Production mode, same client IP, requests 5 to 7 answered 429 by the login rate limiter:

| Tree | Audit row for a 429 login |
| -- | -- |
| Base | `unknown.create`, resource type `unknown`, path `/`, success false |
| Round-1 head | `auth.login` (test mode) / `v1.login` (production mode) |
| Gate's D3 shape | `auth.login`, resource type `session`, path `/api/auth/login`, success false |

### R-5: the production trail is `v1.*` on base

* **Gate record:** in production mode, 441 base rows equal round-1 head rows and differ from D3, for proxied and mounted admitted routes (`v1.login`, `v1.upload`, `v1.erasures` and so on).
* Example from `compare_production_base_d3.out`, a proxied login answered 200:
  * base: `v1.login`, resource type `v1`, path `/api/v1/auth/login`
  * D3: `auth.login`, resource type `session`, path `/api/auth/login`
* **Re-read against round 2:** `audit.ts` at `6dc825644` vs its merge-base `1125607e9`:
  * `:224` `const auditPath = req.path;` is captured when the middleware runs. It is mounted at the app root after the `/api/v1` strip (`index.ts:570`).
  * That value feeds `deriveAction(req, auditPath)` (`:244`) and `details.path` (`:294`).
  * These are the same two uses as the gate's D3 counterfactual edit (`evidence/d3_apply.py`). So R-5's "a canonical-path fix changes production rows too" now describes #1011 round 2 itself.
  * MEASURED on D3; READ-equivalent for round 2; NOT measured at `6dc825644` (its round-2 gate was being drafted when this was filed).
* develop `e0f41a8fa`'s `audit.ts` is byte-identical to `1125607e9`'s (`git diff --quiet` rc 0), so "base" above is current develop.

### Dedupe before filing

Searched with the board's `searchIssues` (includeArchived, includeComments), keeping only literal, case-insensitive matches in title, description or comments:

* `attemptedEmail`: 1 fuzzy, 1 literal (KS-871, in comments).
* `H29`: 1 fuzzy, 1 literal (KS-871, in comments).
* `middleware/audit.ts`: 101 fuzzy, 3 literal (KS-871; KS-661 and KS-28, both archived and unrelated).
* `v1.`: 105 fuzzy, 35 literal. None is about audit action names; the nearest is KS-1177, a different v1 verify-route defect.

None covers R-3 or R-5. Related: KS-871.

## Update from the KS-1457 work (PR #1481) and its Sonnet-tier gate, 2026-10-12

* **The cause stated here is confirmed, re-read at develop `d38302a9a27e`:** `index.ts:385` lists `/api/auth` in `proxyPaths` and `index.ts:399-402` skips the gateway's body parsing for it, so `req.body` is undefined when the audit row is written at `'finish'`. `details.attemptedEmail` is never written for `/api/auth/login` in production, throttled or not. The gate's production-shaped harness (same gating, the real login limiter) confirmed it on head and base.
* **R-3's "other half" and the two other finish-time `req.path` reads:** KS-871 (#1011) fixed the row's path and the 429 row's shape. PR #1481 (KS-1457) fixes the remaining finish-time reads (the login user-id lift and the write-failed warning's path, plus the email read) by using the path captured at entry. Of those, only the warning's path was live in production; the email read and the user-id lift are latent while the body is unparsed and the proxy streams the response. PR #1481's cell B4 passes only because its test parses bodies globally.
* **New, from the gate:** if someone enables parsing for `/api/auth/login` to make this field work, `audit.ts:290-292` stores the lower-cased email with **no length cap**, so each throttled attempt could store an unvalidated string up to the body limit (1 MB), and the only cap on audit rows is the global limiter (300 per minute per IP). **Cap the length when it is turned on.**
* **Follow-ups for KS-1457's tests (its head cannot change):** reword the header comment at `ks1457-audit-finish-reads-use-the-entry-path.test.ts:15-17` and cell B4, and make B4 mirror the `proxyPaths` gating, so they state what is live.
* I filed this as a new ticket (KS-1488) before noticing this one; KS-1488 is closed as a duplicate of KS-1189.

## BLUF
PR #1011 (KS-871) merged as `523f283c6cd2550263ec9869dc5ee722be40df4e`, and its round-2 QA gate measured both halves of this ticket:
- **R-5 is CLOSED by that merge.** Production audit rows for mounted and proxied routes are now written canonically (e.g. `auth.login` / `/api/auth/login`, not `v1.login` / `/api/v1/auth/login`). The census over the real app measured 574 production rows changed, all toward canonical, 0 regressions.
- **R-3 has MOVED, not closed.** The login rate limiter's 429 row is now `auth.login` in both test and production mode. The **H29 `attemptedEmail` is still never written** for a login through the gateway.

## Recommendation
This ticket's remaining scope is H29 alone, plus the unmeasured consumer check below. Not built.
1. **H29:** decide whether attempted-email capture should work for proxied logins at all, and where the email should come from. The gateway deliberately does not parse bodies on `/api/auth`.
2. **Consumers:** check whether anything outside the repo groups audit rows by `action` (the security service's reader, dashboards, a SIEM export). The rename from `v1.*` has already shipped to develop.

## Detail
- Gate report: `Testing Agent MAIN/projects/secuura/reports/2026-09-17-ks871-1011-6dc825644-tier1-r2/report.md` (Round-1 carry-forward, census, Merge-seat ADDENDUM).
- **R-3 (login 429):** base wrote `unknown.create` at `/`; the merged code writes `auth.login` at `/api/auth/login`, in both modes. H29: `middleware/audit.ts` still sets `attemptedEmail` only from a parsed `req.body`, which `index.ts`'s `shouldParseBody` skips for `/api/auth`. The merge did not touch either line.
- **R-5 (production `v1.*`):**
  - base → merged tree in production mode: 574 of 1115 census rows changed, every one toward canonical.
  - Canonical rows went from 527 / 1101 to 1101 / 1101.
  - Routes whose row is the same whatever the request spelling went from 109 to 119 of 119.
  - Response status sequences are identical.
- The out-of-repo blast radius of the action rename is NOT TESTED by the gate.

title: Security: an absolute-form request target bypasses the KS-843 erasure door's scope/role gate (a connector without subjects:erase reaches originate)
description:
## BLUF

An absolute-form request target (`POST http://<any host>/api/gdpr/erasures`, and `/api/v1/` in production) **bypasses the KS-843 erasure door's scope/role gate**: it answers **200, and originate receives the POST, for a connector WITHOUT** `subjects:erase`. The origin-form control answers 403 with no upstream hit. The `GET` status read and the user role are bypassed the same way. A credential is still required: no credential or an invalid token answers 401. **Pre-existing:** base == head. Found by the tier-1 QA gate on PR #1011 (KS-871); **not caused by that PR**.

## Recommendation

Treat as Urgent until two conditions are measured (below). One of them is already READ as true: originate does not re-check the scope. title: workflow-approve persists the instance approved before the forward, so a refused forward strands it: re-approve and reject answer 400, no re-forward path, the kept document unusable until TTL (KS-1087 gate F2)
description:
## BLUF

`POST /api/workflow-instances/:id/approve` persists the instance `approved` (`services/api-gateway/src/routes/verification.ts:970-972`) BEFORE it forwards the pending document to originate. So after any refused forward the workflow is stranded:

* a retry answers 400 "Workflow already completed" and never forwards (originate hits 0);
* reject answers 400;
* there is no re-forward path;
* the kept pending document stays unusable (403 `PENDING_APPROVAL`, relayed) until its Redis TTL.

The persist-before-forward predates PR #1008. Before #1008 the same input also reached `approved` and silently deleted the pending document; #1008 (merged `f7c2f4acb28875e3665a61c8eaaad5c54bd3aa55`) keeps the document and answers 502, which makes the strand visible and recoverable in principle.

## Recommendation

A design call beside KS-1087 item 2, not a fix round on #1008. Two shapes:

* persist `approved` only after originate answers 2xx; or
* add a re-forward / retry path for an `approved` instance whose pending document still exists.

Regression test (the gate's): a stateful store, originate 401 then 201 → the second attempt forwards and deletes exactly once.

## Detail

After any refused forward the instance is `approved`, re-approve/reject 400, no re-forward path, and the kept document is unusable until its TTL. nodes.body:
## BLUF
Record from the tier-1 QA gate on PR #1010 (KS-1183, merged as `1125607e9`), for whoever designs this ticket's fix. After a lost 201, the gateway answers **502 with the pending document kept while originate's copy exists**. A caller retry answers **400 "Workflow already completed"**, so a retry makes **no duplicate**. **Any re-forward path this ticket adds must send a `documentUuid`, or it will mint a second document.** No state change here.

## Recommendation
If the fix is "re-forward an approved instance whose pending document still exists", make the forward idempotent. Send a stable `documentUuid` (for example the pending document id), so that originate's KS-596 idempotency answers 200 with the existing row instead of creating another.

## Detail
Measured by the gate (report `Testing Agent MAIN/projects/secuura/reports/2026-09-17-ks1183-1010-c3213b04e-tier1-r1/report.md`, section 5, Record R1), at the head and on the merged tree:
- `O-late-201-persist-then-lost+retry`: 502 at 804 ms, pending document KEPT, originate created 1, instance `approved`. The caller's retry answered 400 "Workflow already completed", and originate hits stayed at 1.
- Base: 200 + delete at 1,503 ms. No residual, but no bound either.
- Worse than the base only in one band. If originate takes 15–30 s, the base answered a truthful late 200, while the head now answers 502 though originate's copy exists. If originate is slower than the proxy (over 30 s in production), the base already answered nginx 504 plus a later delete, so the head is not worse. Any bound under the proxy's forces that trade.

Read at source by the gate (`services/originate/src/routes/documents.ts:616-648`): originate is idempotent only on a caller-supplied `documentUuid` (KS-596: same hash → 200 with the existing document; a different hash → 409). The gateway's forward payload in `routes/verification.ts` is `{ title, documentType, description, contentHash, data }` and carries **no** `documentUuid`.

Nothing deployed.

title: Organisation verification: submitting evidence sends no notification to any Administrator (join requests do), and the automated domain-linkage failure is logged as "Rejected"
description:
## BLUF

The `/organisation/verify` flow is clear and works: linkage check gives a precise reason ("The domain does not serve /.well-known/did-configuration.json"), Start verification → Attach document ("Document received") → Submit ("Submitted for review. An administrator will decide it."). Two small gaps for the people on the other end. Found 16 Sep 2026, develop `d36ff71e`, as Account Admin of Trimming Test Ltd.

## What was seen

1. **No email to a platform Administrator** when evidence is submitted. Mailpit shows nothing to any admin address after submit; by contrast a join request emails the organisation's admins within seconds ("Someone is waiting to join…", `JoinRequestAdminNotifyCooldownMinutes`). An Administrator learns of pending organisation verifications only by opening the queue (`/OrganisationVerificationAdmin`). May be intended — flagging as a question.
2. Audit row after a failed *automated* linkage check reads `DomainVerified · Unverified · Rejected`. "Rejected" reads as a human decision; "Not verified" / "Check failed" would match the inline message and avoid alarming the applicant.
3. ~~(Observation) Trust-level badge propagation could not be tested without the Administrator decision — deferred with the admin path.~~ **Resolved 17 Sep — tested and working, see the addendum below.**

## Addendum 17 Sep 2026 — Administrator decision → badge (pass), plus two small observations

The full loop was run on the rebuilt slot 3 (S `4e256ece`, K `f8c7aaa39`) and it works end to end — nice to see:

| Step | Actor | Outcome |
| -- | -- | -- |
| Start DocumentVerified → attach `mobile-doc-1.pdf` (incorporation, SG) → Submit | Account Admin of Trimming Test Ltd | Pending → "Document received." → "Submitted for review. An administrator will decide it." |
| Queue → Review (verification 1) → Approve (notes filled) | Administrator in a **different** organisation (the real reviewer path, not the [PS-454](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-454/organisations-cannot-verify-themselves-no-org-identity-flow-trust-is-a) self-decision guard) | "Approved at DocumentVerified."; Details shows "Already decided — Approved, granted DocumentVerified" |
| Badge | Account Admin, same session | `/organisation/verify` current level DocumentVerified, one Approved history row; dashboard chip flips to **"Organisation ID verified · Trimming Test Ltd · since 17 Sep 2026"** (`data-testid="dashboard-org-identity"`, `data-verified="true"`) |

So item 3 above is closed. Two small things noticed on the way, both minor and both fine to fold into whatever tidy-up this ticket becomes:

4. **The reviewer cannot open the evidence.** The Details page says so itself ("Documents are stored encrypted. Retrieval for inspection is not wired to this screen yet — decide from the metadata and any out-of-band review for now."). Honest and clear, but it does mean a trust level is granted on file name, type and country alone. If the retrieval is planned elsewhere, a pointer here is enough; if not, this is probably the more valuable half of the ticket.
5. **One hand-rolled timestamp** on the decided line in `ssd/Views/OrganisationVerificationAdmin/Details.cshtml:78` — `$" on {v.CompletedAt.Value:dd-MMM-yyyy HH:mm} UTC"` renders "on 17-Sep-2026 13:16 UTC", while the queue's Started column two clicks earlier uses `Helpers.UtcTimeTag` ("17 Sep 2026 at 14:14", localised). The [PS-677](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-677/one-house-datetime-format-26-aug-2026-at-1427-everywhere-millisecond) house rule is that every displayed timestamp goes through the `Helpers` (`UtcTimeTag` / `FormatUtcTimestamp`); this one slips past `HouseTimestampFormatContractTests` because it is an interpolation rather than `ToString("dd-MMM…")` — the test may want a second pattern. Cosmetic, one-line fix.

## Re-checked 12 Oct 2026 on `develop` 3e2ff5cf: items 1 and 4 still reproduce

Slot 4 (S `:5422`, K `:7182`; app-reported build commit **3e2ff5cf**), black-box through the UI, mail read in Mailpit's web page. Applicant: a freshly self-registered user (`explore-new1@example.test`); reviewer: Administrator `stuart@lhsg.com`.

* Linkage check against an unresolvable domain → "Domain linkage not verified: The domain does not serve /.well-known/did-configuration.json." ✓ (clear).
* Start → **Attach document** ("Document received.") → **Submit for review** ("Submitted for review. An administrator will decide it.") ✓.
* **Item 1 still reproduces:** no email to any Administrator after submit.
* **Item 4 still reproduces:** the review page still reads "Retrieval for inspection is not wired to this screen yet — decide from the metadata and any out-of-band review for now."
* Approve → "Approved at DocumentVerified."; the applicant's page shows **Current trust level DocumentVerified** ✓. **No email to the applicant** about the decision either.
* New on this pass: in the queue, the **Organisation** column is **blank** for a self-registered applicant, because the auto-created organisation has no name ([PS-1140](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1140/self-registered-user-the-auto-created-organisation-has-no-name-blank)).

## Why it matters

* `docs/USER-MANUAL.md` §10 "Organisation verification — decide an organisation's verification after it has submitted evidence… This decision sits with an Administrator": a decision nobody is told about waits indefinitely. Consistency with the join-request notification design (`docs/org-recognition-configuration.md`).
* GDPR Art. 12 (transparent communication about processing of the applicant's evidence — timelines), PDPA 2012 s.20.
* WCAG 2.2 SC 3.3.3 (wording of error/status messages).

## Suggested shape

* On submit: one email to Administrators with the same cool-down pattern as join requests; applicant already gets an on-page confirmation — an email to them too is reasonable.
* Audit wording: "Not verified (automated check)" for linkage failures; keep "Rejected" for human decisions.

## Acceptance

* Playwright: submit evidence → Mailpit contains one Administrator notification; audit row wording per above.

**Playwright test that demonstrates the fix** (required): extend `systemTest/tests/functional/organisation_verification.spec.ts` (it already drives this flow; a new file would duplicate its fixtures) with a case that, against a live stack, asserts:

1. as Account Admin, start a `DocumentVerified` verification via `org-verify-level-select` → `org-verify-document-type-select` → `org-verify-evidence-input` → `org-verify-document-submit-btn`, then poll **Mailpit** and assert **exactly one** notification addressed to a platform Administrator exists for that submission, identified by the organisation name in its subject or body. This is the assertion that **fails on today's** `develop` — Mailpit holds nothing for any admin address after submit;
2. submitting a **second** document within the cool-down window does **not** produce a second admin email, matching the join-request `JoinRequestAdminNotifyCooldownMinutes` pattern the ticket compares against — also unverifiable today, since there is no first mail;
3. run the domain-linkage check against a domain that serves no `/.well-known/did-configuration.json`, then assert `org-verify-history-status` for that row reads the automated wording ("Not verified" / "Check failed") and **not** the literal `Rejected`. Red today;
4. after an Administrator in a different organisation approves via `org-verify-admin-approve-btn`, assert `org-verify-admin-already-decided` renders its timestamp through the house helper — a `<time class="secuura-local-time" data-testid="local-time">` element rather than the hand-rolled `17-Sep-2026 13:16 UTC` string at `OrganisationVerificationAdmin/Details.cshtml:78`. Red today (item 5).

**Control assertions that pass today and must keep passing:** the applicant still sees "Submitted for review. An administrator will decide it." in `org-verify-msg`/`org-verify-current-level`, the reviewer queue still lists the pending row with `org-verify-admin-review-link`, and after approval `dashboard-org-identity` still carries `data-verified="true"` — the whole loop in the 17 Sep addendum already passes, and adding a notification must not disturb it.

**xUnit companion** (the cheaper half): item 5's class of defect is a *rule*, so widen `HouseTimestampFormatContractTests` to catch interpolated formats (`{x:dd-MMM-yyyy HH:mm}`) as well as `ToString("…")` calls — that is what stops the next one, and it runs in two minutes with nothing up. Item 3's wording is likewise a resolver-level string worth pinning there.

## Regulatory, accessibility & mobile references (with links)

GDPR Art. 12: [https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2016/679/oj](<https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2016/679/oj>) · UK GDPR/DPA 2018: [https://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/2018/12/contents](<https://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/2018/12/contents>) · Singapore PDPA 2012 s.20: [https://sso.agc.gov.sg/Act/PDPA2012](<https://sso.agc.gov.sg/Act/PDPA2012>) · eIDAS 910/2014 (organisation identity assurance context): [https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2014/910/oj](<https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2014/910/oj>) · WCAG 2.2 SC 3.3.3: [https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG22/](<https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG22/>) · DIF Well-Known DID Configuration (the linkage spec the page cites): [https://identity.foundation/.well-known/resources/did-configuration/](<https://identity.foundation/.well-known/resources/did-configuration/>) · `docs/USER-MANUAL.md` §10, `docs/org-recognition-configuration.md`, `docs/identity-integration-design.md`.

## Note to Stuart — please scan before fixing

Strongly suggested: list every "something is waiting for an Administrator / Account Admin" event (join request, organisation verification, identity verification queue, connector key refused, anchor failed) against who is notified and how, in one table, and fix the gaps together so similar issues do not become several tickets and follow-ons.

title: Personal-data exposure audit: who sees whose email address on every end-user surface — one decision per audience, one contract test per surface
description:
## BLUF

A scan of the non-admin views, `wwwroot/js` and email templates (16 Sep 2026, develop `d36ff71e`) finds \~20 places that render a person's email address; about 11 of them show it to an audience that has no need for it (an anonymous link recipient, every Account Admin on the platform, colleagues and cross-org rights holders on the lineage graph). The rest are owner- or admin-facing and correct. This parent holds the inventory and the rule; each child fixes one surface with its own Playwright contract so a regression names the surface. Admin/DevTools pages are out of scope by design.

## The rule (proposed — Stuart to confirm)

| Audience | May see |
| -- | -- |
| Document owner / sender | everything they entered: recipient emails, assignee emails |
| Account Admin (own organisation) | own members; joiners' emails on join requests |
| Rights holder in another organisation | names + organisations; not the owner's recipients' emails |
| Colleague in the same organisation (lineage, org documents) | names + roles; recipient email in the evidence panel only if they own/hold the document |
| Anonymous link recipient | issuing organisation name, document identity; **no personal email** |
| Verify / Outlook add-in result | organisation, never a person |

## Inventory (scan)

| Surface | Sites | Audience | Verdict |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| `Views/SDViewDownload/ViewDownload.cshtml` (:237, :253, :285 `mailto:`) | 4 + 3 | anonymous | change → child B |
| `wwwroot/js/lineage.js` (:170, :280, :350, :865, :977, :1000) + `Views/Lineage/View.cshtml:89` label "Verifier" | 6 | org members, cross-org holders | change → child C |
| `Views/Assign/Assign.cshtml` "To" select (built in `AssignController`) | all users | any Account Admin | change → child A ([PS-887](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-887/assign-rights-lists-every-user-on-the-platform-all-organisations-full)) |
| `Views/Shared/_DocumentRecipientsDrawer.cshtml`, `Views/Home/Dashboard.cshtml` "From/With", `OutlookApiController` verify result | 2 + 2 + 1 | holder in another org; Outlook user | decide → child D |
| Share / rights emails built in `SendDocs*` / `Assign*` | sender line "by Name on date (email)" | recipients | copy only → folded into child B |
| `Views/SendDocsLinksAdmin/Index.cshtml` (5), `All.cshtml` (1), `Views/Assign/List.cshtml` (1) | owner | keep |  |
| `Views/Settings/SettingsUserEdit.cshtml` (2), `Views/Shared/_OrgJoinRequestsSection.cshtml` (3) | Account Admin, own org | keep |  |
| `wwwroot/templates/Email/{EmailConfirmation,EmailChangeConfirmation,Support,Contactus}.txt` | the recipient's own address | keep |  |

## Children

* **A** — [PS-887](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-887/assign-rights-lists-every-user-on-the-platform-all-organisations-full) Assign rights directory (re-parented)
* **B** — [PS-878](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-878/privacy-sharing-and-lineage-surfaces-show-more-personal-data-than-the) anonymous link page + email copy (re-parented; lineage part moves to C)
* **C** — lineage graph & export: covered inside [PS-878](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-878/privacy-sharing-and-lineage-surfaces-show-more-personal-data-than-the)'s description; if Stuart prefers a separate PR, split out
* **D** — recipient drawer, dashboard "From", Outlook verify result (new)

Order: A, then B and C in parallel (different files, different POMs), D last.

## Acceptance (parent)

* All children Done.
* `@privacy` Playwright group: for each audience above, one spec asserting the page contains no `@` the audience is not entitled to (POMs `assign`, `sdview`, `lineage`, `dashboard`, `outlook`).
* `docs/USER-MANUAL.md` §6 gains a "who can see what" table matching the rule.

**Playwright test that demonstrates the fix** (required, expanding the `@privacy` bullet above): this is the **parent**, so its spec is the matrix the children's individual specs cannot be — suggest one new file, `systemTest/tests/functional/privacy_email_audience_matrix.spec.ts`, tagged `@privacy`, parametrised over the six audiences in the rule table above. Each child fixes its own surface in its own spec (`sdview_identity_lines.spec.ts`, `lineage_identity_lines.spec.ts`, `assign_form.spec.ts`, `outlook_identity_lines.spec.ts`); this one asserts the **rule** across all of them, so a surface that regresses names itself. Assert:

1. For each audience row, load the surfaces that audience reaches and assert the page's rendered text and every `href` contain **no email address outside that row's allowance** — collect the addresses with a single regex over the DOM and diff against the allowed set, rather than checking for the mere presence of `@`, which produces false positives on hashes and DIDs.
2. Drive it with **three organisations and a genuinely external recipient address**, because four of the eleven wrong cases in the inventory are only visible to a cross-organisation or anonymous viewer. A single-org fixture would report green on surfaces that are still exposed.
3. The assertions that fail on `develop` today are the eleven inventory rows marked **change** or **decide**: the anonymous `/SDViewDownload/v/{token}` page (`ViewDownload.cshtml` :237 / :253 / :285), the six `lineage.js` sites plus the "Verifier" label at `View.cshtml:89`, the `/Assign` "To" select, and the recipient drawer / dashboard "From" / Outlook verify result. Name them in the spec so a partial landing is legible.
4. **Controls that pass today and must keep passing** — these are the inventory's **keep** rows, and they are the whole risk of a privacy sweep, which tends to over-redact: the owner's own `SendDocsLinksAdmin` Index (5 sites) and `All` (1), `Assign/List` (1), `SettingsUserEdit` (2), `_OrgJoinRequestsSection` (3), and the four email templates that show the recipient their **own** address. Each must still render its address to its entitled audience.
5. **Verify / Outlook result** shows the issuing **organisation** and never a person — the one surface the inventory records as already right, and therefore the shape the others are being moved towards.
6. A regression that reaches the DOM but not the visible text must still fail: assert over `innerHTML` as well as `innerText`, since `mailto:` and `title`/`aria-label` attributes are where an address most easily survives a visual fix.

Alongside this, the parent's durable gate is an **xUnit contract test** rather than the journey: a static sweep of `Views/**`, `wwwroot/js/**` and `wwwroot/templates/**` for `.Email` / `RecipientEmail` / `mailto:`, with an explicit allow-list of the **keep** sites above. That is the same shape as `TestIdCoverageContractTests`, runs in the two-minute suite, and is the only thing that will catch a twelfth surface appearing — which is exactly what the note to Stuart anticipates. The Playwright matrix proves the rendered audiences; the contract test holds the inventory.

## Regulatory, accessibility & mobile references (with links)

**Privacy / data protection** — EU GDPR Art. 5(1)(c) minimisation, 5(1)(f) integrity, 25(2) privacy by default, 32 security: [https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2016/679/oj](<https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2016/679/oj>) · UK GDPR + DPA 2018: [https://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/2018/12/contents](<https://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/2018/12/contents>) · ICO guide: [https://ico.org.uk/for-organisations/uk-gdpr-guidance-and-resources/](<https://ico.org.uk/for-organisations/uk-gdpr-guidance-and-resources/>) · Singapore PDPA 2012 s.18, s.24: [https://sso.agc.gov.sg/Act/PDPA2012](<https://sso.agc.gov.sg/Act/PDPA2012>) · PDPC: [https://www.pdpc.gov.sg/](<https://www.pdpc.gov.sg/>) · OWASP ASVS 4.0 V4: [https://owasp.org/www-project-application-security-verification-standard/](<https://owasp.org/www-project-application-security-verification-standard/>) · Platform decision [PS-869](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-869/5-decision-the-on-chain-identity-record-did-level-source-and-verified) ("names and emails never" on chain)

**Accessibility / mobile** — masked or moved emails also shorten node labels and rows: WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.10 Reflow, 2.5.8 Target Size: [https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG22/](<https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG22/>) · EN 301 549: [https://www.etsi.org/deliver/etsi_en/301500_301599/301549/03.02.01_60/en_301549v030201p.pdf](<https://www.etsi.org/deliver/etsi_en/301500_301599/301549/03.02.01_60/en_301549v030201p.pdf>) · EAA 2019/882: [https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/dir/2019/882/oj](<https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/dir/2019/882/oj>) · W3C WAI mobile mapping: [https://www.w3.org/TR/mobile-accessibility-mapping/](<https://www.w3.org/TR/mobile-accessibility-mapping/>) · Apple HIG: [https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/accessibility](<https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/accessibility>) · Material 3: [https://m3.material.io/foundations/accessible-design/overview](<https://m3.material.io/foundations/accessible-design/overview>)

**Platform-s** — `docs/VOCABULARY.md`, `docs/USER-MANUAL.md` §6, `docs/role-classification.md`, `docs/ui-test-selectors.md`, `CLAUDE.md` › Project.

## Note to Stuart — please scan before fixing

The inventory above is the scan. Strongly suggested: re-run the grep (`\.Email\b`, `RecipientEmail`, `mailto:` across `Views/**`, `wwwroot/js/**`, `wwwroot/templates/**`) before starting the children and fold any new hit in, so similar issues do not become several tickets and follow-ons.

**Child A (PS-887) merged to `develop`** — [#1061](https://github.com/Secuura/platform-s/pull/1061), `7cb1a4e`, 16 Oct 2026.

The Assign list is now the caller's own organisation only, and anyone elsewhere is reached by typed email. It also closed an id-enumeration oracle in the Assign POST that wasn't in the inventory: every target that cannot hold rights now gets one sentence, whatever the reason.

Per this parent's order (A → B, C → D), **B and C (PS-878) are next**, then D (PS-898).

For the parent's rule table, the one ruling taken on A: **uniform refusal, no invite** (Stuart, 16 Oct). A successful assignment still shows the address is an eligible user, but it hands over a real document and emails the target, so it is never a silent probe.

**A surface to add to the inventory: Organisation Users › Add New User lets an Account Admin test whether ANY email exists on the platform** (found 13 Oct 2026, `develop` bb92be69, slot 3, UI only).

As `firstone@lhsg.com` (Account admin of First One PTE Ltd), Add New User (`/personedit?id=0&orgId=3`), with first and last name filled in:

| Email typed | Result |
| -- | -- |
| `e2e-basic@e2e.invalid` (a member of the admin's own organisation) | "User with this email already exists" (expected) |
| `STUART@LHSG.COM` (the platform Administrator, **another organisation**; case changed) | "**User with this email already exists**" |
| an unused address | saved |

So the form answers "does this person have an account anywhere on Secuura?" for any address, across tenants and case-insensitively. That's the same disclosure PS-1151 records for the sign-in page, here reachable by every Account Admin without any lockout budget.

**Suggested row for the rule table:** Account Admin, Add user → may learn that an address is **already a member of their own organisation**. For an address belonging to another organisation, the answer should not reveal it. For example, a neutral "We couldn't add this person — if they already use Secuura, ask them to request to join your organisation" for both the exists-elsewhere and unusable cases.

**Test classification (systemTest):** `@area-people` · `@person` · `@validation`, `@role-access` · actor `@role-account-admin`, target an address in another organisation (`@role-admin`'s seed account) · not core-smoke. **Acceptance:** the Add-user response for an address in another organisation is indistinguishable from the response for an address the platform won't accept for other reasons. The own-organisation duplicate keeps its specific message (control).

Checked before posting: no ticket, branch or PR covers the Add-user path (PS-1151 is sign-in; PS-887 is the Assign directory).

title: Document row keeps the originating persona's email (createdOnBehalfOf.email) after platform-s has erased them
description:
## Found by

[PS-875](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-875/11-end-to-end-journey-and-docs-one-persona-acts-through-every-verb-the)'s `@k-live` chain half (platform-s PR #856, 2026-09-16), whose privacy assertion first read K's **document** row for an S-originated document and found:

```json
"createdOnBehalfOf": { "email": "firstone@lhsg.com", … }
```

This is the `onBehalfOf` platform-s sends on originate ([PS-746](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-746/ks-566-has-shipped-on-platform-k-develop-revert-the-ps-616-interim) / [KS-1016](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1016/test-anchor-read-honesty-hardcodes-docker-exec-secuura-postgres-fails) territory), stored on K's document record. The spec now reads the **anchor** record, which carries no email — so this is **not** a [PS-869](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-869/5-decision-the-on-chain-identity-record-did-level-source-and-verified) breach (nothing personal is on chain).

## Why it matters

Platform-s implements the right to erasure ([PS-382](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-382/security-reachable-right-to-erasure-dsar-for-identitykyc-data), [PS-690](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-690/adopt-org-owned-documents-ownership-model-for-single-vs-multi-user)): after `PersonGdprErasureService` runs, S holds no email for the person, and every S surface renders the actor from the immutable identity snapshot (DID, level, source) only. K's document row is a second, off-chain place the persona's email persists, outside S's erasure and outside K's anchoring rule. Anyone with the K account's read scope on the document sees it.

## Suggested work

1. Decide whether `createdOnBehalfOf.email` is needed on the document row at all, or whether the S-side `actorDid` / the K account id suffices (S already sends the [PS-869](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-869/5-decision-the-on-chain-identity-record-did-level-source-and-verified) `identity` block once [KS-1175](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1175/anchor-originate-lifecycle-event-schemas-accept-and-anchor-platform-ss) lands).
2. If it stays: give K an erasure hook S can call (or a scheduled sweep S can trigger) that blanks `createdOnBehalfOf.email` for a given email/DID, and have S's `PersonGdprErasureService` call it (a PS follow-up).
3. Either way, note it in K's data-retention statement.

## Acceptance

* An S-erased persona's email no longer resolves anywhere on K's document read API.
* platform-s's `identity_status_chain.spec.ts` can extend its no-`@` assertion from the anchor record to the document row.

nodes.body: Code check, 2026-09-29 (K `0aa9b52c6`): `createdOnBehalfOf` on the document read is not a column — it is read from `action_provenance` (`services/originate/src/services/provenance.ts:249-262`, `email_enc` decrypted). The connector erasure by `externalRef` blanks `email_enc`, `display_name_enc` and `email_hash` on every `action_provenance` row for that ref (`services/originate/src/services/gdprService.ts:1430-1445, 1478-1483`). So if S's `PersonGdprErasureService` → `POST /api/gdpr/erasures` had completed for the persona before the spec read the document, the email should already read `null`. Two candidate explanations for the PS-875 observation: the S erasure bridge had not run (or not confirmed) for that persona at read time, or the K under test predated #790. Worth a live re-check on a paired slot before any K change: erase, poll `/api/gdpr/erasures/{externalRef}` to `completed`, then read the document.

title: v1 verify family refused for cookie-bearing callers in production (versioning redirect runs after CSRF) while v2 passes
description:
## BLUF

In `NODE_ENV=production`, a cookie-bearing browser caller that sends no `X-XSRF-TOKEN` gets through on the v2 verify family but is refused on v1. The v1 call is redirected 307 to `/api/v1/verification/verify` by `versioning.ts`, which is production-only and mounted AFTER CSRF. The re-POST then meets `403 CSRF_TOKEN_MISSING`, because `/api/v1/` is not in `excludedPaths`. Pre-existing on the v1 side. PR #1001 (part of KS-1165) exempted v2, which turned "both refused" into "different" in production.

## Recommendation

Owner decision on the intended behaviour, then one of these:

* exempt the v1 verify family under its `/api/v1/verification/verify` spelling too;
* run the versioning redirect before CSRF;
* publish the difference in the spec if it is intended.

Pin the choice with a production-import cell (`NODE_ENV=production`).

## Detail

Found by the tier-1 QA gate on PR #1001 (KS-1165) at `3925d4c072b940eb91de462b7b92eabfe8889c75`, 2026-09-16. Report: `Testing Agent MAIN/projects/secuura/reports/2026-09-16-ks1165-1001-3925d4c07-tier1-r1/report.md`, section 7, F-2. The measurement, verbatim:

**F-2 — In NODE_ENV=production the v1 and v2 verify families diverge for cookie-bearing, header-less callers**

* Evidence class: MEASURED AT RUNTIME on a TRUE production import, replicated twice, plus the base-csrf run.
* Severity: **Minor**.
* Target: **TICKET** (pre-existing v1 routing/exemption interplay), noted against **KS-1165 DoD box 1**.
* SHIPS-WITH.
* Oracle: **P**roduct consistency (`csrf.ts:90-97` says the v1 verify family is exempt, but in production the redirected path is not). Also the PR title's claim "as v1's are", and box 1's "or the difference is published in the spec" (it is not).
* At head in production, cookie + allowed Origin + no X-XSRF-TOKEN:
  * `POST /api/v2/verification/verify` → **200** upstream (PT-1).
  * `POST /api/verification/verify` → **307 Location** `/api/v1/verification/verify` (PT-5; `versioning.ts:45-58` is production-only and mounted at `index.ts:530`, AFTER CSRF).
  * The re-POST the browser makes → **403** `CSRF_TOKEN_MISSING` (PT-6; `/api/v1/` is not in `excludedPaths`, as in M17).
* Controls:
  * PT-7: the same v1 alias with no cookie → 200.
  * PH-6 (hybrid): a valid double-submit token → 200.
  * Development PH-1: v1 → 200 with no redirect.
* At base in production, **both** families refuse this caller (v2 403: PT-1 red at base-csrf; v1 307→403 unchanged). So #1001 turns "same (both refused)" into "different" in production. Outside production they are the same at head (M1 = M3 = 200).
* Likelihood (READ ONLY; no browser):
  * The verifier portal calls `${VITE_API_URL || '/api'}/verification/verify` via `safeFetch`, which sends `credentials:'include'`, echoes `X-XSRF-TOKEN` when `document.cookie` holds it, and retries once on 403.
  * A same-site portal therefore probably passes on v1.
  * The refused shape is a cookie-holding caller that does not echo the header (cross-site cookie jar, or plain `fetch` with credentials), which is the caller class KS-1165 exists for, but on v1.
* Fix-shape (prose): exempt the v1 verify family under its `/api/v1/` spelling too, or run the versioning redirect before CSRF. The owner decides and publishes the difference if it is intended.

Not measured (report section 10): v1 `verify-file` in production (the 307 → alias path for octet-stream). F-2 is stated for `/verify` only.

Relation: KS-1165 DoD box 1 ("the v1 / v2 verify families behave the same for cookie-bearing callers, or the difference is published in the spec") is PARTIAL because of this. KS-1165's remaining close depends on this ticket existing plus its F-1 follow-up PR.

Dedupe before filing (seat A, 2026-09-16): literal matches over Linear `searchIssues` (archived and comments included), title + description + comments:

* `versioning.ts`: 0 of 117 results;
* `CSRF_TOKEN_MISSING`: 11 of 90 (KS-1165, KS-119, KS-188, KS-35, KS-428, KS-430, KS-46, KS-781, KS-798, KS-799, KS-841), none about the production versioning redirect running after CSRF;
* `/api/v1/verification`: 0 of 95;
* "versioning redirect": 0 of 113.
  Filed new.

nodes.body: A note from the KS-1469 work (PR #1472, merged `0ae2339e612367d99341b772a21799e1016c6fc1`), for whoever owns the v1/v2 verify decision here. The merged CSRF change judges the exclusion on the path the `/api/v1/` alias gives it, stripped one level. That is the "exempt the v1 verify family under its `/api/v1/verification/verify` spelling" option below, generalised to every excluded path: `/api/v1/x` is now excluded exactly when `/api/x` is, and nothing is excluded that the canonical spelling does not already exclude (`/api/v1/auth/loginx`, `/api/v1/v1/auth/login` and `/api/v1/documents` stay `403`). Measured in `NODE_ENV=development` only; the production 307 followed by CSRF on the re-POST was not measured by me or by the gate. If the intended behaviour is the opposite (publish the difference), that change needs reverting here.

title: api-gateway: connector-key principals (verificationLevel 'api_key') fail meetsVerificationLevel against 'none' — every Platform-S originate 403s once the doc-type catalogue is seeded
description:
**BLUF:** `meetsVerificationLevel('api_key', 'none')` **returns false because** `'api_key'` **is not in** `VERIFICATION_LEVEL_ORDER` **(**`indexOf` **→ -1, and** `-1 >= 0` **is false). So once the document-type catalogue is seeded, every** `POST /api/documents` **from a Platform-S connector key is refused with** `INSUFFICIENT_VERIFICATION_LEVEL` **— even though** [KS-388](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-388/k-freeze-documenttype-as-a-strict-enum-originate-flat-anchor-metadata) **seeded** `SSD_DOCUMENT` **as "deliberately friction-free" with** `creatorVerificationLevel: 'none'`**. Fix is a few lines in** `services/api-gateway/src/services/enforcement.ts`**; this is the K-side root cause of** [PS-519](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-519/originate-403s-under-connector-keys-k-wants-a-verification-level-api).

## Symptom

Platform-S app log, on every upload under a connector key (135–142 occurrences per full S suite run):

```
CardanoAnchor: originate POST status=403 body={"success":false,"error":{
  "code":"INSUFFICIENT_VERIFICATION_LEVEL",
  "message":"This document type requires NONE verification. Your current level is API_KEY."}}
```

S then falls back to flat `/api/anchors`, which succeeds — so the anchor badge goes green but **no K document exists**: no content-hash resolution for `/api/verification/verify`, no lineage root, no lifecycle events. S's `@k-live` suite fails 11/14 on this alone.

Reproduced 2026-09-16 on Peter's Mac, slot 4 pair: platform-k `0b25f823f` (develop, fresh worktree, fresh volumes) ↔ platform-s `2fa69634` and again `d36ff71e` (develop). Two full S suite runs, 12 failures each, 11 of them this.

## Builds under test

| Platform | Branch | Commit (full SHA) | Slot |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| platform-k | `develop` | `0b25f823f6660ac52b665f14055799ff0c3b616d` | 4 — gateway `:7182`, `secuura_slot4`, fresh worktree + fresh volumes |
| platform-s (run 1) | `develop` | `2fa696340967313fef214bfe1232f17a69cec410` | 4 — `https://localhost:5422`, `ssd-slot4` |
| platform-s (run 2) | `develop` | `d36ff71e5d347089c5cff08a0892bd8cb0e45385` | 4 — same slot, `--rebuild --reset`; `/Health/Data` `build.Commit` matched |

## Cause

`Blockchain/Dev/services/api-gateway/src/services/enforcement.ts`

* `:39` `VERIFICATION_LEVEL_ORDER = ['none','basic','social','standard','enhanced','high','government']`
* `:53-57` `meetsVerificationLevel(userLevel, requiredLevel)` = `ORDER.indexOf(user) >= ORDER.indexOf(required)`
* `middleware/auth.ts:276` sets `verificationLevel: 'api_key'` on every connector-key principal.

`'api_key'` is not in the order → `indexOf` = `-1` → `-1 >= 0` is false → a connector key fails even `none`. Any other unknown level string fails the same way.

The check is only reached when `resolveDocumentType` finds the type. On an unseeded K it returns null and `:110-127` (the [KS-388](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-388/k-freeze-documenttype-as-a-strict-enum-originate-flat-anchor-metadata) fallback) passes through — which is why the failure appears and disappears between rebuilds, and why [PS-519](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-519/originate-403s-under-connector-keys-k-wants-a-verification-level-api) saw the suite "green 2h earlier against the previous K". `routes/admin.ts:283-303` seeds `SSD_DOCUMENT` with `creatorVerificationLevel: 'none'` and says why: *"deliberately friction-free … gating either would break those paths."* The ordering bug defeats that intent. Confirmed on the live K: `GET /api/document-types` lists `SSD_DOCUMENT`, `creatorVerificationLevel: none`.

## Fix (either; the first is narrower)

1. In `meetsVerificationLevel`, an unknown `userLevel` satisfies `requiredLevel === 'none'` only — treat `indexOf === -1` as index 0 when the requirement is `none`, and still refuse any higher requirement, so a connector key cannot originate a `STANDARD`-gated type by accident.
2. Or place `'api_key'` explicitly in the order — but where a machine credential ranks against human KYC levels is a product decision, not a bug fix.

Either way the message should stop rendering `NONE` as harder to meet than `API_KEY`.

## Verification

* Unit: `meetsVerificationLevel('api_key','none') === true`; `meetsVerificationLevel('api_key','standard') === false`; an arbitrary unknown string behaves the same as `'api_key'`.
* Live: S upload under a connector key against a **seeded** K → originate `201`; S `@k-live` `chain_match.spec.ts` green; `POST /api/verification/verify` resolves the document by content hash.

## Related

* [PS-519](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-519/originate-403s-under-connector-keys-k-wants-a-verification-level-api) — the S side (surface K's `error.code` instead of the "revoked or wrongly scoped" guess); its open question "deliberate tightening or seed drift?" is answered here: neither.
* [KS-388](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-388/k-freeze-documenttype-as-a-strict-enum-originate-flat-anchor-metadata) — the catalogue seed that arms the check.

**Not shown:** I can't see whether kintsugi's document-type catalogue is seeded, which is the condition in this ticket's title. Your side can read that. S's app log for that hour was lost when dev-ps restarted at 02:51 UTC, so the evidence is the ledger and the chain.

Verified by code read, not observed live: `Blockchain/Dev/services/api-gateway/src/services/enforcement.ts:63` ranks an unrecognised verification level as none (`userRank = userIdx === -1 ? 0 : userIdx`), which is how a connector key's api_key level now compares. Left open: observation owed. The merge comment of 2026-09-16 keeps the ticket open until a live Platform-S upload under a connector key is run against a seeded K: live sweep owed (write), not run on kintsugi.

PR #1014 merged. A connector key's `api_key` verification level (any unrecognised level) now ranks as `none`, and the connector document-type allow-list resolves `documentType || type`. **This ticket stays In Progress.**

`Merged fa887f382b212b8da4a0a4a556bacb05ea34daaa; offline gates green; NOT Done per secuura-test-discipline §5f — live sweep owed (torn-down rebuilt stack, all containers verified up), unverified: the live Platform-S upload under a connector key against a seeded K, a real originate, and the production platform-settings shape`

## Recommendation

No action needed now. The live sweep is batched into the Sunday QA pass. Three findings from the round-2 gate are filed as separate Backlog tickets (see Detail); one of them is built next as a follow-up PR.

## Detail

**The merge** (Wednesday's GO 2026-09-16 22:41:29Z, spf/dkim/dmarc pass; tier-1 round-2 delta gate GO WITH FINDINGS at `9ba0caf78b8ddb737541df38303b776c982521d2`, no Blocker; F-1 closed: 0 disallowed types admitted on head and merged, 32 at round 1):

* Squash `fa887f382b212b8da4a0a4a556bacb05ea34daaa` at 22:44:35Z, pinned with `--match-head-commit 9ba0caf78…`.
* Verified at origin: develop tip = the merge commit; one parent = `7e89318bcedbc9a35757d4298ace54a6a23020bd` (#1016); tree `5748a1d68318ed2e310a360fb79e7a1ebc63c785` = the merge-tree prediction; 3 files = the PR's.
* The GO's equality targets hold: `enforcement.ts` `be466fbf4`, `verification.ts` `28fb58343`, `ks1176-connector-key-level-ranks-as-none.test.ts` `43cebf8d7`. The verification.ts blob differs from the PR head's by design: #1016 landed first in the same file, ~900 lines apart.
* Reports: round 1 `Testing Agent MAIN/projects/secuura/reports/2026-09-17-ks1176-1014-616c766a5-tier1-r1/report.md`; round 2 `…/2026-09-17-ks1176-1014r2-9ba0caf78-tier1-r2/report.md`.

**Records assigned to merge time (fix-round mail, 21:09:01Z):**

* The workflow-bypass connector row.
* `PROPERTY_DEED` ranks at `none`: a product question, not answered here.
* The "nothing beyond anonymous" premise was vacuous, because anonymous is 401 first. Round 2 reworded the why-comment to "an unrecognised level ranks as none, the lowest authenticated level" (R-c, now CLOSED).
* KS-1190 already names `verification.ts:554-557` (the unknown-REQUIRED fail-open, left as it was at base).
* The tenant spoof is stripped by the app chain.
* No level marker is sent on the forward.
* `x-api-key` is not declared on the spec operation.
* Two catalogue sources exist, and the seed is off in production.

**Records from round 2:**

* **R-10:** the allow-list matches exactly, while enforcement matches case-insensitively and by id. That is fail-closed: 23 false refusals on head (e.g. `ssd_document`, `dt-seed-7`), 10 at base; no legitimate shape is newly refused against base.
* **R-g, extended:** `type` is not declared in `DocumentCreateRequest`; the 403 text does not mention the allow-list refusal.
* PR #1016's `ks1072-…test.ts(124,10)` TS18046 shows on develop under a test-including program. It is #1016's record (KS-1180), not this PR's.

**Filed from round 2 (Backlog, not built by this merge):** N-1 (served `data.documentType` unchecked, Major, pre-existing), N-4 (untyped body from a restricted connector stored as DOCUMENT, Minor, pre-existing), and N-2 + N-3 together (a STRING allow-list substring-matches; no both-present precedence cell, Minor). N-2/N-3 is built next as a tier-1 follow-up PR.

## BLUF
PR #1014 round 2 is at head `9ba0caf78b8ddb737541df38303b776c982521d2` and awaits its QA delta gate. The round-1 QA gate found that a connector restricted to certain document types could name any type through the `type` field instead of `documentType`, and this change had widened that. Round 2 fixes it in the same PR: the allow-list now reads the same key enforcement reads.

## Recommendation
No action needed. This ticket stays open: a live sweep is owed after merge.

## Detail
- **Fix:** `services/api-gateway/src/routes/verification.ts`, the connector allow-list resolves `documentType || type`.
- **Measured in-process at the new head:**
  - a connector restricted to `DOCUMENT` naming `SSD_DOCUMENT` via `type` is refused 403 (201 at round 1);
  - the same via `documentType` is refused 403;
  - `DOCUMENT` via `type` still passes;
  - an untyped body behaves as before.
- **Suites:** api-gateway 49 files / 428 tests pass; packages/shared 44 / 851 pass; tsc rc 0. A seven-row tamper table in the PR body reds exactly as predicted.
- **The round-1 gate's other findings are separate tickets, not built:** KS-1195 (per-key rate limiter), KS-1196, KS-1197, KS-1198.

## BLUF
PR #1014 (https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/1014) is open for this ticket at head `616c766a57a51238450c99bbf1d59bb109e3841c`, awaiting its tier-1 QA gate.
- **The fix:** in `meetsVerificationLevel` (`services/api-gateway/src/services/enforcement.ts:53-64`), an unrecognised user level such as a connector key's `api_key` now ranks as `none`. It satisfies a `none` requirement and nothing higher. This is the narrower of the two fix shapes in this ticket.
- **What it restores:** a connector-key `POST /api/documents` on `SSD_DOCUMENT` passes enforcement. Every type above `none` still refuses a connector key.

## Recommendation
No action needed. This ticket stays open after the merge: the live half of its verification (a Platform-S upload under a connector key against a seeded Platform K, then `POST /api/verification/verify` resolving it) is still owed.

## Detail
- **Measured in-process, at the PR head** (the real router and the real enforcement, with a mocked document-type catalogue):
  - a connector key creating `SSD_DOCUMENT` passes enforcement (403 before the fix);
  - a connector key creating a `standard` type is still refused 403 `INSUFFICIENT_VERIFICATION_LEVEL`;
  - the verifier gate on `POST /api/documents/:id/verify` still refuses a connector key on a standard-gated type.
- **Unit cells:**
  - `api_key` vs `none` → true; `api_key` vs `basic` / `standard` → false;
  - an arbitrary unrecognised string behaves exactly as `api_key`;
  - every known level pair is unchanged (225 rows).
- **Not changed, and filed separately:** an unknown REQUIRED level still passes every authenticated caller. That is KS-1190. The PR pins today's behaviour so it cannot move silently.
- **Not changed:** three other level-order copies with no production callers (auth and shared `requireVerificationLevel`, shared `policy-engine`) and the issuer frontend's upload pre-check. The PR records them.
- **Suites at the head:** api-gateway 49 files / 423 tests pass; packages/shared 44 / 851 pass; tsc rc 0. A six-row tamper table in the PR body reds exactly as predicted.

title: Anchor / originate / lifecycle-event schemas: accept and anchor platform-s's non-PII actor + organisation identity fields (actorDid, actorLevel, actorSource, actorVerified, orgDid, orgTrust, orgVerified) beside identityCommitment
description:
## What platform-s needs

Follow-on to [KS-721](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-721/anchor-schema-accept-and-anchor-platform-ss-opaque-identitycommitment) (which accepted `metadata.identityCommitment`). Platform-S now needs the Cardano record to **show** who acted and at what identity level, for the actor and their organisation — readable, not only committed. The S-side ruling on what is allowed in clear is [PS-869](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-869/5-decision-the-on-chain-identity-record-did-level-source-and-verified) (decision) under epic [PS-864](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-864/epic-id-status-stored-and-shown-throughout-the-system-actor-and); the field list there is the contract:

| Field | Type | Pattern / values |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `actorDid` | string ≤ 512 | `^did:(key|web):[A-Za-z0-9._:%-]+$` |
| `actorLevel` | integer | `1`, `2`, `3` — NIST 800-63A IAL alignment |
| `actorSource` | string | `platform` | `stripe` | `entra-verified-id` |
| `actorVerified` | boolean |  |
| `orgDid` | string ≤ 512 | as `actorDid` |
| `orgTrust` | string | `unverified` | `domain` | `document` | `kyc` | `government` |
| `orgVerified` | boolean |  |
| `identityCommitment` | string ≤ 128 | already accepted ([KS-721](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-721/anchor-schema-accept-and-anchor-platform-ss-opaque-identitycommitment)); the `vN` will move to `v2` |

All optional; all non-PII (DIDs are pseudonymous, levels and sources are enumerations, no dates, no names, no emails). Consistent with [KS-240](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-240/strict-by-default-on-chain-minimisation-strip-issuername-any-human) — no free text, nothing recoverable to a natural person.

## Suggested work

1. Accept the block as `metadata.identity` (or flat under `metadata` — say which) on **every** endpoint S anchors through: `POST /api/anchors`, `POST /api/documents` (originate), `POST /{id}/version`, `POST /{id}/anchor`, `POST /{id}/share`, `POST /{id}/transfer-custody`, `POST /api/certifications/issue`, `POST /{id}/lifecycle-events`. Today `anchorSchema.ts` strips unknown keys, so S will not send until K is live (the [PS-612](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-612/rename-the-certify-verb-to-declare-across-s) ordering).
2. Carry it into the on-chain record beside `documentType` / `occurredAt` / `identityCommitment`.
3. Return it in provenance / verify / anchor-status responses so S can render "on chain: Level 2, entra-verified-id" beside its local snapshot and flag any mismatch.
4. **State which existing request fields reach Cardano metadata**: `holderEmail`, `recipients[].email`, `newHolderEmail`, `onBehalfOf.email` / `displayName`. S sends these today; the requirement is that no PII is stored on the blockchain. If any of them is written to chain metadata, file the defect and link it here.

## Finding: KS-721's commitment could never reach a real chain (KS-1284, filed 2026-09-20, `Refs KS-721`)
Cardano metadata caps every string at **64 bytes** and has **no boolean type**; CSL 15.0.3 throws at tx build (`Max metadata string too long: 69, max = 64`; `bools not allowed in metadata`). `identityCommitment` (≥69 bytes) therefore failed at `cardano/transaction.ts` on every non-mock anchor — proven in mock mode only, never hit because S has never sent it. The PR adds a codec at the two chain boundaries only: strings >64 bytes are anchored as arrays of ≤64-byte chunks (the Cardano convention), the two verified flags as `"true"`/`"false"`; K's readers undo both; the DB row and both read-backs keep the logical typed form. For every payload anchored to date the codec is a byte-identical no-op (pinned by test). An independent chain reader (Cardanoscan / raw Blockfrost) sees the array / string forms.

Records: `5_Project_History/2026-09-20_seatA-15th/`.

## Wire shape as platform-s will send it (PS-870, built 2026-09-16 behind `CardanoAnchor:AnchorIdentity`, default off)

On **every** anchored write — `POST /api/documents`, `/{id}/version`, `/{id}/share`, `/{id}/transfer-custody`, `/api/certifications/issue`, `/{id}/lifecycle-events`, `POST /api/anchors` — a **top-level** `identity` object:

```json
"identity": {
  "actorDid": "did:key:z6Mk…",         "actorLevel": 2,          "actorSource": "stripe",
  "actorVerified": true,
  "orgDid": "did:web:acme.example",     "orgTrust": "domain",     "orgVerified": true,
  "identityCommitment": "identity-commitment-l2.v1:<64 hex>"
}
```

- Absent fields are omitted (never `null` / `""`); a row with no snapshot sends no `identity` key at all.
- `actorLevel` ∈ {1,2,3}; `actorSource` ∈ {`platform`,`stripe`,`entra-verified-id`}; `orgTrust` ∈ {`unverified`,`domain`,`document`,`kyc`,`government`}.

- Read-back: S records whatever the anchor GET returns under `identityCommitment` and `identity` into `DocumentTransaction.AnchorIdentityJson` on confirmation, so returning them on `GET /api/anchors/{id}` is what makes the local-vs-chain comparison possible (PS-871).

S will not turn the switch on for an environment until its K confirms this contract — a K that strips the key makes anchors look identity-evidenced while carrying nothing.

title: api-gateway collapses every API-key failure into 401 'Invalid API key' — forward the security validate reason as a distinct code, and answer 503 when the security service is unavailable
description:
## BLUF

**A Platform S connector cannot tell a dead key from an unavailable security service.** The api-gateway collapses every API-key failure — revoked, expired, unknown, security-service 5xx, security-service unreachable, non-JSON reply — into one response: `401 {code:'UNAUTHORIZED', message:'Invalid API key'}`. The security service's own `reason` is computed and then discarded.

Platform S is building a `KeyInvalid` state (PS-740) so a rotated-away key is *seen* rather than reported as an anchor backlog. Because of this collapse it has to be built as a persistence heuristic (two refusals ≥ 60 s apart) rather than a definitive classification, and it can never be made exact without a change here.

## Measured on `develop` @ `48e65c43` (2026-09-15)

**Security computes the reason** — `services/security/src/index.ts`, `POST /api/keys/validate`, all HTTP 200:

| line | condition | response |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `:1314-1316` | hash miss in `memApiKeys` and DB fallback empty **or thrown** | `{ valid:false, reason:'Key not found' }` |
| `:1318-1320` | `!apiKey.isActive` | `{ valid:false, reason:'Key revoked' }` |
| `:1322-1324` | `expiresAt < now` | `{ valid:false, reason:'Key expired' }` |

**The gateway throws it away** — `services/api-gateway/src/middleware/auth.ts`:

| line | what happens |
| -- | -- |
| `:219` | security non-2xx → `null`, negative-cached 30 s |
| `:225` | `if (!data?.valid) → null` — `reason` **is never read** |
| `:240` | fetch throws (unreachable, DNS, reset, hang — `:214` has no timeout/AbortSignal) → `null` |
| `:265` | every `null` → `401 { code:'UNAUTHORIZED', message:'Invalid API key' }` |

So `'Key revoked'`, `'Key expired'`, `'Key not found'`, a security 500, and a security outage are **byte-identical to the caller**. A second transport-shaped 401 exists too: when the connector-bearer exchange fails (`:179-203`) the request goes downstream with no Bearer and answers `401 'No token provided'`.

Also: `:1309-1311` swallows a DB error in the validate fallback and reports `'Key not found'` — a cache-miss during a DB outage reads as an unknown key.

## Ask

1. **Forward the reason as a distinct error code** at `auth.ts:265`: `API_KEY_REVOKED`, `API_KEY_EXPIRED`, `API_KEY_NOT_FOUND` (the `ErrorResponse` schema's `code` enum would gain three values). Status can stay 401.
2. **Answer 503** `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE`**, not 401, when the security service is unreachable or errors** (`:219`, `:240`) — that is the platform's own fault, not the caller's credential, and it must not be negative-cached as if it were.
3. Give the validate fetch at `:214` a timeout.
4. (Docs) `docs/S-K-OWNERSHIP-CONTRACT.md` §5 still says a rotate leaves the *"old key untouched"* and tells the admin to revoke by hand — stale since KS-577 (#880) retires prior keys as part of the mint. The OpenAPI 401 prose (32× "Missing or invalid Bearer token") documents no API-key body at all; the three strings above appear nowhere in the spec.

## Why it matters to the S↔K re-key cluster

KS-577 is merged with instant revoke by default, and KS-889's 39-key re-mint and KS-576's bulk re-key are waiting on S being able to survive a rotation. S's side of that (PS-740) lands as a heuristic because of this ticket; with (1) and (2) it becomes exact and the heuristic is deleted. Until then, a security-service outage on K will look to S like every connector key dying at once — and S's design deliberately keeps presenting the key so that false positive costs nothing, but it is still a lie on the dashboard.

Filed from PS-740's planning pass. Cited in prose, no `Refs` trailer.

title: Guard 3's re-poll reads a MIXED window as ABSENT — one early "not found" then an unreachable chain still schedules a retry that can re-mint a written-ahead transaction (#805 tier-1 r3 residue)
description:
## BLUF

After #805 (KS-726) merged as `48e65c435` on 2026-09-15, `reconfirmKnownSubmission` treats a bounded re-poll as `'unknown'` **only when NO attempt reached the chain** (`polled === 0`). A window in which at least one attempt answered "not found" (a Blockfrost 404) and every remaining attempt THREW (5xx / 402 quota / DNS) still reads `'absent'`, guard 3 calls it a definitive rejection, and the ordinary retry mints a second fee-paying transaction for a document whose first — the hash just written ahead — may be on its way to a block. This is the same class as the F1 the merge closed (an unreachable chain read as absent), one neighbour over: the fix weights **whether** the chain ever answered, not **when**.

Measured by the tier-1 delta gate (round 3) at `a4d182bf9` and on the merged tree — report `/Volumes/DevMASTER/!CODING/Testing Agent MAIN/projects/secuura/reports/2026-09-15-ks726-805-a4d182bf9-tier1-r3/report.md` §5 (cells R3a/b/c, R3b-2nd): with the answer early / middle / late in a 3-attempt window, `polled 1 / errored 2` each time → `'absent'` → `scheduleRetry` 1; R3b's second call minted TX_B (`minted [TX_B]`, `signedHashes [TX_A, TX_B]`, row `confirmed`/TX_B). Grade: **TICKET, ships-with** — the gate's, endorsed by the coordinator; filed by the merge seat as the ADDENDUM required.

## Why the early 404 is a likely FALSE negative in exactly the case that matters

The retry is wrong only when TX_A is in fact accepted while the node says "inputs spent" for it — a same-hash duplicate submit, the two-process race the module's NOT HANDLED list already names. In that premise TX_A entered the mempool seconds before the 400; Blockfrost's `/txs/{hash}` answers 404 until the tx is in a block **and** indexed; the production poll's first attempt lands \~10–12 s after the 400, the second \~15–17 s later, the third \~22 s later. So an early "not found" says little, and a rule that accepts any single answer as definitive is weakest at the start of the window — where a fresh transaction is most likely to be unindexed.

## Blast radius (round 2's units, the gate's reading)

Severity **HIGH** — a duplicate fee-paying transaction (\~181,825 lovelace) and an unrecorded on-chain anchor for the document (TX_B is a valid anchor; TX_A is the orphan; no data loss, no false "anchored" claim). Likelihood **LOW** — {a same-hash duplicate submit} ∧ {TX_A unindexed at every answered attempt} ∧ {the provider unreachable from the first unanswered attempt through attempt 30, \~27 min}. Blast radius one document per occurrence. The gate did not accept "rarer than F1": by its arithmetic the residue's outage-start window is of the same order as the closed case's; both hang on a long provider outage (or a 402 quota exhaustion, a sustained state that naturally arrives mid-poll) beginning within tens of seconds of a duplicate submit.

## Where it lives (at `48e65c435`)

* `services/anchoring/src/cardano/confirmation.ts` — `waitForConfirmation` reports `polled` / `errored` counts only; nothing says WHEN the last answer came.
* `services/anchoring/src/anchorSubmission.ts` — `reconfirmKnownSubmission`: the `confirmation.polled === 0` → `'unknown'` arm (after the `confirmed` return, before the `'absent'` return); guard 3's `refusedAndAbsent` reads `'absent'` as definitive.
* The shipped cells that pin today's rule: `__tests__/ks726-gate-f1-unreachable-chain.test.ts` — "a mixed window (throw, not found, throw) reads ABSENT … → retry" is a deliberate pin of the commissioned "any attempt" semantics and must be REWRITTEN, not deleted, by whoever changes the rule.

## Fix-shape (prose — the gate's, for the owner to weigh; not a committed artefact)

Have `waitForConfirmation` also report `lastAnsweredAttempt` (or the elapsed ms at the last answered attempt), and have `reconfirmKnownSubmission` treat `'absent'` as definitive **only when the last answer is late enough for a mempool transaction to be in an indexed block** — e.g. `polled >= 2`, or an answer ≥ 60 s after the 400 — else `'unknown'` (rest in `submitting` for the reconciler). Regression cells: (404, throw ×29) → `'unknown'`, `scheduleRetry` 0, the row rests; CONTROL (404 ×k spanning ≥ 60 s, then throws) → `'absent'` → retry; the existing all-404 and all-throw cells unchanged. **The cost to weigh:** a genuinely absent transaction whose late attempts threw would now rest \~24 h for the reconciler instead of retrying in \~15 s — the (c) ruling's own concern — so this is a design decision for the ticket owner, not a bug fix, which is why the builder did not make it under KS-726.

## Two smaller records the gate carries, stated here so they are not lost

* (8j) the `confirmed`-before-`polled === 0` ordering in `reconfirmKnownSubmission` is unpinned by any shipped cell; the cell to add if wanted: an injected `{ confirmed: true, polled: 0 }` → row `confirmed`, no `'unknown'` log.
* (8k) `getTransaction` returns `null` when no Blockfrost client is configured (`cardano/provider.ts`), which the `polled` counter reads as "the chain answered"; pre-existing, unreachable through the production submitter without a real 64-hex hash on the row.

## Symbol search before filing (the `issues` filter over title + description + comments, `includeArchived:true`, 1,160 issues; controls 1/0 as expected)

`reconfirmKnownSubmission` → 1 (KS-726 itself, the merge seat's own comments) · `lastAnsweredAttempt` → 0 · `mixed window` → 0 · `reads 'absent'` → 0 · `unreachable chain` → 1 (KS-671, the /health chain-path mechanism — different) · `polled` → 8 (KS-726's comments, wrap comments on the review parent, and KS-683's consumer re-poll — a different mechanism; the rest archived and unrelated). No open ticket owns this.

## Related

KS-726 (the parent finding; merged as `48e65c435`, PR #805) · the gate report above (§5, §7).
