## RULED by Kam — option (c), both conditions

> **Decision `secuura-ks1171-when-is-an-anchor-absent`: c — Both conditions (strictest, fewest double submissions)**

— Kam, live board, **2026-09-25 12:49:07 AEST**. Card id: `secuura-ks1171-when-is-an-anchor-absent`.

This is the design decision the ticket deliberately refused to make for itself: *"a design decision for the ticket owner, not a bug fix, which is why the builder did not make it under KS-726."* It is now made.

## The rule, as it will be built

A transaction may be declared **ABSENT** — and therefore retried — only when **BOTH** hold:

1. **at least 2 answered polls**, AND
2. **an answer that arrived at least 60 s after the node's 400**.

Anything short of both keeps today's behaviour: the row rests in `submitting` for the reconciler, `'unknown'` rather than `'absent'`, and `scheduleRetry` is not called.

Kam's parenthetical names the trade he accepted: *strictest, fewest double submissions*. The cost the ticket flagged is accepted with it — a genuinely absent transaction whose late attempts threw now rests ~24 h for the reconciler instead of retrying in ~15 s. Fewer duplicate fee-paying transactions was judged the better side of that trade.

- `services/anchoring/src/cardano/confirmation.ts` — `waitForConfirmation` also reports `lastAnsweredAttempt` (the ticket's own fix-shape).
- `services/anchoring/src/anchorSubmission.ts` — `reconfirmKnownSubmission`'s `confirmation.polled === 0` gate becomes the two-condition test above; guard 3's `refusedAndAbsent` then reads a verdict that means what it says.
- `src/__tests__/ks726-gate-f1-unreachable-chain.test.ts` — its mixed-window cell is a **deliberate pin of the commissioned "any attempt" semantics**, so it will be **REWRITTEN to the new rule, never deleted**, exactly as the ticket instructs whoever changes the rule.

Ruled, not yet built. It ships as its **own PR, tier 1**, after the three already in flight from this lane (KS-975 item 2, KS-976 item 1, KS-1129 anchoring site). Nothing in this comment is a code change.

*Delivered by Seat L2 (security + anchoring lane), 2026-09-25, before building, so a reader arriving at this ticket lands on the ruling rather than on the open question.*

title: userRepo.ts: ILIKE search on encrypted PII columns can never match — :1017 and :1061 compare ciphertext to a pattern
description:
## BLUF

`services/auth/src/repositories/userRepo.ts` runs a text search over columns that hold ciphertext. `listUsersInner` (`:1017`) and `countUsersInner` (`:1061`) both push `(email ILIKE $n OR first_name ILIKE $n OR last_name ILIKE $n OR display_name ILIKE $n)` with the pattern `%<search>%`. Every one of those four columns is written through `encryptPiiCol` (`:832-840` — the `encryptedCols` map: `first_name`, `last_name`, `display_name`, `phone_number`, `email`, `mfa_secret`; `:671`, `:703-705`, `:712`, `:847`, `:856`), with AAD bound to the user id, so the stored value is a per-row ciphertext and an `ILIKE` over it answers a different question from the one asked: a search for a known user's name or address returns nothing, without an error, and looks like "no such user". It is the runtime form of the trap KS-968's schema comment now warns about at the column (`docker/init/01-schema.sql`, the `users.email` comment landed by PR #905): comparing ciphertext to a literal or a pattern never errors and never matches.

The file's own docblock at `:562-568` records the rule for equality — `getUserByEmail` moved to an HMAC lookup against `email_lookup_hash` "rather than LIKE/LOWER on the encrypted blob — the encrypted column is non-deterministic so direct equality doesn't work" — and the two search sites were left on the old shape. Measured and recorded by s232 on KS-968 (comment `1079a310`, 2026-09-14) while landing #905; filed by the merge seat s228 on Wednesday's ADDENDUM 2026-09-14 11:00:17Z. Board searched first — every KS issue incl. archived, titles + descriptions + comments: `ILIKE` 1 hit (KS-968's own comments), `userRepo.ts:1017` 1 (the same), `userRepo.ts:1061` 0, `searchUsers` 0, `listUsers` 2 (KS-968; KS-703 archived, a NUL-byte 500 — unrelated). No existing home.

## Where it hurts

* Any admin or tenant user-list with a `search` term (`listUsersInner` / `countUsersInner` are the search arm of the users listing; both take `search`, `role`, `tenantId`). The count and the page disagree with reality in the same direction, so the UI shows an empty, internally consistent result.
* Rows still holding legacy plaintext (the migration-window fallback the docblock describes) WOULD match — so the search "works" on exactly the rows that should not exist any more, and silently stops working as rows are backfilled. A test seeded with plaintext passes; production does not.

## Fix-shape (for the owner)

Pick one, and say which in the PR:

1. **Searchable-hash columns per searched field** — the `email_lookup_hash` pattern (`lookupHash(normalised)`) extended to `first_name` / `last_name` / `display_name`, with an exact-or-prefix match on the hash instead of a substring `ILIKE` (a substring search over a keyed hash is not possible; the product decision is whether prefix/exact search is enough).
2. **Resolve the search through the existing hash for email only** and drop the name columns from the predicate, documenting that the listing searches by exact email.
3. **Drop the search arm** and remove `search` from both signatures and their callers.

Whichever lands, the docblock at `:562-568` should name the search sites as covered.

## Regression cell

Seed one user through `createUser` (so the columns are ciphertext, not plaintext), then call `listUsersInner` with `search` = that user's display name (and separately the email) and assert the user is returned and `countUsersInner` reads 1; a control search for a name no user has reads 0. On develop today the first two assertions red (0 rows) — the cell is red-first by construction.

## Definition of done

- [ ] A search for a known, encrypted-at-rest user's name or email returns that user through both `listUsersInner` and `countUsersInner`, or the search arm is removed with its callers.
- [ ] The regression cell above green; the docblock at `:562-568` names the search sites.
- [ ] KS-968's schema comment stays true (the column is never compared to a literal or a pattern).

title: start-secuura.sh never waits for five default-profile, healthchecked services — demo-service, mcp-server, pgbouncer, tenant-provisioning, tokenisation — "All 27 containers are healthy" can print while they are still booting
description:
## BLUF

`Start_Up/start-secuura.sh`'s health wait, `--status` report and timeout diagnostic all iterate `EXPECTED_SUFFIXES` — 27 names (the [KS-312](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-312/cut-midnight-zk-selective-disclosure-remove-service-privacy-ui) cut of the original list). The compose files declare **33** default-profile, long-running containers. Six are not on the list. One is `stack-marker` ([KS-666](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-666/prevent-destructive-rebuilds-of-the-shared-vm-stack-from-destroying) label carrier, correctly excluded). The other **five are real services with healthchecks and** `restart: unless-stopped` that the script has never waited for:

| service | healthcheck | in the wait list |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `demo-service` | yes | no |
| `mcp-server` | yes | no |
| `pgbouncer` | yes | **no** — and every service's `DATABASE_URL` goes through it |
| `tenant-provisioning` | yes | no |
| `tokenisation` | yes | no |

So `✓ All 27 containers are healthy` and `Containers: 27/27 running` can print while any of these is still starting or already `unhealthy`; the post-start checks that depend on them (anything through pgbouncer, tenant provisioning, tokenisation) then race the boot. Not new — measured the same on `develop` before [KS-1096](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1096/start-secuurashs-health-wait-status-and-dbredis-checks-probe-slot-1s); [KS-1096](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1096/start-secuurashs-health-wait-status-and-dbredis-checks-probe-slot-1s) only made the list slot-correct and added the test that exposed the gap.

## How it was found

`Blockchain/Dev/scripts/__tests__/start_secuura_expected_services.test.sh` ([KS-1096](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1096/start-secuurashs-health-wait-status-and-dbredis-checks-probe-slot-1s), PR [Secuura/Distributed_Secuura#959](https://linear.app/secuura/review/ks-1096-derive-start-secuurashs-probe-names-and-dbredis-ports-from-the-7856c22cafff)) derives the set the script should wait for from the compose files — every `container_name: ${STACK_PREFIX:-secuura}-<svc>` (40) − `profiles:`-gated (5: cardano-mock, cardano-devnet, guardian, queue, ollama) − `restart: "no"` one-shots (2: migrations, demo-overlay) = 33 — and asserts equality with `EXPECTED_SUFFIXES`. To make that green without deciding platform-k base-code behaviour on Peter's ticket, the five above (plus `stack-marker`) sit in the test's `KNOWN_UNWAITED` list, each annotated "as above — script-behaviour call for Kamil". **This ticket is that call.**

## Decision needed (Kamil — platform-k base code)

Either:

1. **Wait for them.** Add the five suffixes to `EXPECTED_SUFFIXES` (`Start_Up/start-secuura.sh`, the `EXPECTED_SUFFIXES=(` block; the count comment says 27 → 32) and delete their five lines from `KNOWN_UNWAITED` in the test. The wait treats `health=none` as healthy, so a service without a healthcheck costs nothing; these five have one, so the wait becomes real. Or —
2. **Deliberately not wait**, per service, with the reason written next to it in `KNOWN_UNWAITED` (e.g. "demo-service is only reachable via a deleted gateway location, [KS-487](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-487/review-b-input-validation-injection-upload-xssssrf-and-crypto) B-6") — the test then keeps the exception honest, failing if the service is ever removed.

Red→green either way: the test is green now only because of the exceptions; removing a line from `KNOWN_UNWAITED` makes it red until the script waits for that service.

## Where

* `Start_Up/start-secuura.sh` — `EXPECTED_SUFFIXES=(` block (27 entries).
* `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/__tests__/start_secuura_expected_services.test.sh` — `KNOWN_UNWAITED` (6 entries).
* `Blockchain/Dev/docker-compose.yml` — the five services' `healthcheck:` blocks.

Live context: on the [KS-1096](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1096/start-secuurashs-health-wait-status-and-dbredis-checks-probe-slot-1s) slot-2/slot-4 runs the summary reads `33 running, 30–31 healthy` while the wait reported 27/27 — the gap is these services plus the two one-shots.

> Wait for all five

**Recorded, not built here.** The build is a later Claude round — this ticket sits past the local model's counter, so nothing was implemented under this comment.

*Delivered by Seat B 24th, 2026-09-25, under Wednesday's confirmation.*

title: Three retired GitHub workflows bake slot-2/3/4 port literals (6982/7182/6732…) into CI env — a stack slot applied to a non-local build, typed per slot
description:
## BLUF

The CLAUDE.md Key Rules added under [KS-1096](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1096/start-secuurashs-health-wait-status-and-dbredis-checks-probe-slot-1s) (2026-09-14) make two things MUST: **a stack slot applies to a build on the developer's local host only**, and **every slot value is calculated from slot 1** (`base + 100*(N-1)`) in `stack_env.sh` / `slot-target.sh`, never typed per slot. Three GitHub workflow files break both — they hardcode slot-2/3/4 ports into CI job env and `with:` inputs:

| file | lines hitting | example |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `.github/workflows/pr-platform-suites.yml` | 37 | `GATEWAY_PORT: "6982"` … |
| `.github/workflows/nightly-platform-suites.yml` | 34 | header `offsets — schemathesis 6882 · playwright 6982 · perf 7082 · akto 7182`; `POSTGRES_EXTERNAL_PORT: "6532"` |
| `.github/workflows/pre-merge-platform-suites.yml` | 14 | `GATEWAY_PORT: "7182"`, `POSTGRES_EXTERNAL_PORT: "6732"`, `REDIS_EXTERNAL_PORT: "6679"`, `TARGET_BASE: http://localhost:7182` |

Measured by `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/__tests__/slot_is_local_host_only.test.sh` ([KS-1096](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1096/start-secuurashs-health-wait-status-and-dbredis-checks-probe-slot-1s) PR [Secuura/Distributed_Secuura#959](https://linear.app/secuura/review/ks-1096-derive-start-secuurashs-probe-names-and-dbredis-ports-from-the-7856c22cafff)): 85 hits across the three files; 0 in `Blockchain/Dev/deployment/`, the compose files, `docker/`, or any Dockerfile. All three workflows are **retired** — GitHub Actions is off for this repo (Kam, 2026-08-27); `pre-merge-platform-suites.yml` is `workflow_dispatch`-only and `nightly-platform-suites.yml` has its `schedule:` commented out — so nothing runs today. They are exempted in that test's `KNOWN_EXCEPTIONS` against this ticket; **the exemption comes out when this closes.**

## Fix direction

Either:

1. **Derive, don't type.** One step per job sources `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/stack_env.sh` with `SECUURA_STACK_SLOT=N` and exports `GATEWAY_PORT`/`POSTGRES_EXTERNAL_PORT`/`REDIS_EXTERNAL_PORT` into `$GITHUB_ENV`; every literal goes. If CI genuinely needs parallel stacks, the slot is a job-level *input*, and the ports are still derived. Or —
2. **Delete the three dormant workflows.** Actions is retired and every retired job maps to a local runner in `Blockchain/Dev/docs/DEV-PROCESS.md` §Manual CI-gate equivalents; dead YAML that contradicts a MUST rule is a liability. Needs Kam's nod.

Red→green: remove the three paths from `KNOWN_EXCEPTIONS` in `slot_is_local_host_only.test.sh`; the test is red before the fix and green after.

Found while adding that test under [KS-1096](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1096/start-secuurashs-health-wait-status-and-dbredis-checks-probe-slot-1s).

## Shared acceptance — slot derivation group (added 6 Oct 2026)

This ticket is one of five platform-k tickets that must all take slot values from `stack_env.sh` and never fall back to slot 1: [KS-1355](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1355>), [KS-1381](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1381>), [KS-1389](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1389>), [KS-1382](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1382>), [KS-1162](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1162>). None of them is done until these hold, in addition to its own acceptance above:

1. **One guard.** A single static guard in `check-stack-safety.sh` fails on any literal published port of any slot 1–4 outside `stack_env.sh`. The first ticket to land creates it; the others extend it; nobody adds a second guard. Bite-checked: plant a literal, see it red, remove it.
2. **No silent default.** A local run with no slot named refuses and prints an example command; it never falls back to slot 1 (preflight, `slot-target.sh`, the `Blockchain/Testing` entry points, the smoke scripts). Any change to `stack_env.sh`'s own slot-1 default re-runs every test in this group.
3. **One preflight change.** [KS-1355](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1355/stack-tooling-is-not-slot-derived-end-to-end-stack-guard-lists-a) (spot 4, `preflight.sh:94`) and [KS-1389](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1389/sourcing-systemtestslot-targetsh-with-no-slot-named-silently-exports) (leg 13, `preflight.sh:589-630`) land in one PR, or one after the other, each re-running the other's checks.
4. **The workflow question.** [KS-1162](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1162/three-retired-github-workflows-bake-slot-234-port-literals) decides first whether the three workflows are deleted or made to derive their ports. If deleted, [KS-1382](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1382/blockchaintesting-five-auditdasttenant-isolation-entry-points-default)'s "explicit `TARGET_BASE` is used unchanged" criterion has no CI caller left; if derived, their `TARGET_BASE` comes from `stack_env.sh` too.
5. **Tests cover every slot.** Slots 1–4, hermetic: identical results unslotted and under each slot's environment.

**This ticket's part:** point 4 — record the delete-or-derive decision here before [KS-1382](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1382/blockchaintesting-five-auditdasttenant-isolation-entry-points-default) closes, and whichever way it goes, the three paths leave `KNOWN_EXCEPTIONS` and the point-1 guard covers `.github/workflows/`.

nodes.body:
**BLUF: one more reason to pick option 1 or 2. Once KS-1386 lands, the retired Akto jobs here would be refused at start-up, not just carry the wrong literals. Nothing runs these workflows today, so there's no urgency. This is a note for whoever picks the ticket up.**

**What changes (re-checked against `origin/develop` @ `8c810023f` and the KS-1386 branch @ `f11159053`):**

* **On `develop` today:** Akto falls back to `http://localhost:9091` when `AKTO_DASHBOARD_URL` is unset. See the `env('AKTO_DASHBOARD_URL', 'http://localhost:9091')` default in `systemTest/akto/src/config/env.ts`.
* **On KS-1386:** there is no default URL any more. A run that names no slot must set both `SECUURA_API_URL` and `AKTO_DASHBOARD_URL`, or it is refused with `No stack slot named, and AKTO_DASHBOARD_URL is not set — there is no default URL.` (`src/config/validate.ts`, `assertUrlsResolved`). CI stays exempt from the *slot* refusal, but not from needing a URL.
* **The Akto jobs here set only `SECUURA_API_URL`.** Examples: `pre-merge-platform-suites.yml:207`, `pr-platform-suites.yml:455`, `nightly-platform-suites.yml:437`. None names a slot or sets `AKTO_DASHBOARD_URL`, so each would stop at config load.
* **The Playwright, Performance and Schemathesis jobs are unaffected.** They pass their target URL explicitly (`API_BASE_URL`, `PERF_BASE_URL`, `--base-url`).

**How it fits the two fix directions:**

1. **Derive, don't type:** name the slot per job (`SECUURA_STACK_SLOT=N`) and let the harness derive both URLs. That removes the literals and satisfies the new check in one move.
2. **Delete the dormant workflows:** unaffected.

Thank you. No action is needed until this ticket is scheduled.

title: redis healthcheck passes REDIS_PASSWORD as a `-a` argv — readable via `docker inspect` / `docker events` / `ps` by anyone on the host
description:
## BLUF

`Blockchain/Dev/docker-compose.yml:228` defines the redis container's healthcheck as

```
test: ["CMD", "redis-cli", "-a", "${REDIS_PASSWORD:-secuura_redis_dev}", "ping"]
```

Compose renders `${REDIS_PASSWORD}` into the container's **config** at create time, so the plaintext password is exposed on every surface that shows the healthcheck command: `docker inspect <redis>` (`.Config.Healthcheck.Test`), `docker events` (each `exec_create: redis-cli -a <password> ping`, every healthcheck interval), and `ps` inside the container while the probe runs. Any account that can talk to the Docker socket reads it without touching `.env`.

Work-stream **B** (crypto & secrets — [KS-487](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-487>), Done 2026-09-14, so filed as a sibling rather than appended). Pre-existing; not introduced or changed by [KS-1096](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1096/start-secuurashs-health-wait-status-and-dbredis-checks-probe-slot-1s).

## Measured — 2026-09-14, slot 4, Peter's Mac

Recording `docker events` for the [KS-1096](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1096/start-secuurashs-health-wait-status-and-dbredis-checks-probe-slot-1s) slot-4 deploy window (07:03–07:16 UTC, 431 events) captured the bootstrap-generated slot-4 `REDIS_PASSWORD` in clear, once per healthcheck tick, as the `exec_create` action string on `secuura-s4-redis`. The recording was deleted; no value is quoted here or in the PR/ticket. The same value is visible at any time via `docker inspect secuura-s4-redis --format '{{.Config.Healthcheck.Test}}'`.

## Why it matters

* Since [KS-731](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-731/local-slots-share-one-postgresredis-credential-pair-any-slot-can-read) the password is per-clone and generated, so a leak is no longer "the shared literal everyone knows" — it is the actual credential for that stack's Redis (sessions, rate-limit state, cache).
* Anyone reproducing a run with `docker events` / `docker inspect` in a log, a PR, or a support bundle ships the password with it. The `secuura-test-discipline` "never read a secrets file" rule is bypassed by a command that reads no file.
* The VM demo stack (`/home/secuura/secuura/Dev`) uses the same compose file, so the demo Redis password is exposed the same way to anyone with socket access there.

## Fix direction

Keep the password out of argv. Options, in order of preference:

1. `test: ["CMD-SHELL", "redis-cli ping"]` with `REDISCLI_AUTH` supplied via the service's `environment:` — `redis-cli` reads the password from `REDISCLI_AUTH` and it never appears in the command. (Environment is still readable via `docker inspect .Config.Env`, so pair with 2 if that surface matters.)
2. Mount the password as a file/secret and `test: ["CMD-SHELL", "REDISCLI_AUTH=$(cat /run/secrets/redis_password) redis-cli ping"]`.
3. Auth-less liveness: `redis-cli ping` unauthenticated answers `NOAUTH` when the server is up — the same signal `start-secuura.sh` already treats as "responding" ([KS-260](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-260/start-secuurash-verification-false-negatives-redis-noauth-counted-as)). Cheapest, and sufficient if the healthcheck only needs liveness.

Check whether `pgbouncer`/`postgres` healthchecks (`pg_isready -h localhost -p 6432`, no password — fine) or any other service put a credential on a command line: grep `docker-compose.yml` + `docker-compose.local.yml` for `-a `, `--password`, `PGPASSWORD=`, `:${…PASSWORD` inside `test:` / `command:` / `entrypoint:`.

**Red→green:** a static check (`check-stack-safety.sh` shape, or `check_slot_credentials.test.sh`) that greps rendered `docker compose config` for any `*PASSWORD*` value inside `healthcheck.test`, `command` or `entrypoint` — red on develop, green after; plus `docker inspect … .Config.Healthcheck.Test` on a running stack showing no credential.

## Where

* `Blockchain/Dev/docker-compose.yml:228`
* Surfaces: `docker inspect` (Healthcheck.Test), `docker events` (exec_create), in-container `ps`.

Found during the [KS-1096](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1096/start-secuurashs-health-wait-status-and-dbredis-checks-probe-slot-1s) slot-4 verification ([Secuura/Distributed_Secuura#959](https://linear.app/secuura/review/ks-1096-derive-start-secuurashs-probe-names-and-dbredis-ports-from-the-7856c22cafff)).

title: Add an OAuth marker to sessions minted by the OAuth grants (so a future deploy-step denylist can be selective) — the current forward-only window is accepted (Kam 14:53)
description:
## BLUF

**Kam ruled 2026-09-14 14:53 AEST (via Wednesday, ADDENDUM 04:53:30Z): (B) marker-only — add the OAuth session marker now; the current forward-only launder window is ACCEPTED, no deploy-time cutoff.** This supersedes his 14:45 ruling `denylist-at-deploy` (ADDENDUM 04:46:19Z), which this ticket was first filed under (title then: "Deploy step: denylist every OAuth refresh jti minted before #983/#984 (the forward-only launder window)", High) — rescoped after the merge seat measured that the pre-fix jtis are not enumerable (below). Priority Medium: no longer a deploy blocker. **The build is the next auth lane's; the deploy stays Kam's.**

**The accepted window, stated:** a refresh token minted at the OAuth grant BEFORE #983 (M31 `b9f541e6b`) / #984 (M32 `2c3315f37`) landed carries neither `client_id` nor `authMethod`, so #986's guard (`routes/auth.ts:677`, M33 `9864379e5`) cannot recognise it and it still launders at `POST /api/auth/refresh` until it expires. **Expiry mechanism:** the refresh JWT's own `exp` — `JWT_REFRESH_EXPIRES_IN`, default `'7d'` (`services/auth/src/services/jwt.ts:44`, `env.example:107`) — so the window closes by itself at most 7 days after the deploy that carries M31–M33 (the last pre-fix mint is at that deploy). Population unmeasured (the AUTH4 gate, report §3.7). Accepted by Kam 14:53.

## What was measured (develop M34 `b42e260c9`, END tree `cf700ee32`, read verbs only, 2026-09-14 04:4x Z)

1. **The denylist exists and is jti-keyed:** `services/auth/src/services/refreshDenylist.ts:21` `refresh_denylist:${jti}` in Redis; `denylistRefreshJti(jti, ttlSeconds)` `:28` (`setex`; fail-loud `Refresh denylist requires Redis` `:34`); `isRefreshJtiDenylisted(jti)` `:46`. Readers `routes/auth.ts:693` and `routes/oauth.ts:1047`; writers `routes/auth.ts:718` (rotation) and `:762` (logout); 0 writers in `routes/oauth.ts` (= R-2 on KS-1150).
2. **A refresh token's jti is minted in memory and never persisted:** `jwt.ts:231` `jti: crypto.randomUUID()`; no `oauth_*` token table in `migrations/`; `refresh_tokens` (`001_initial-schema.sql`) is not written by the OAuth grants.
3. **No marker distinguishes an OAuth-minted session:** both OAuth grants call `createSession(user, req.ip, req.get('user-agent'), undefined, 'browser')` — the code grant at `routes/oauth.ts:965`, the refresh grant at `:1074`; the interactive logins pass `data.clientType ?? 'browser'` (`routes/auth.ts:284`, `:441`, `:590`) or `'browser'` (`:1247`, `wallet.ts:362`); `ClientType = 'browser' | 'native' | 'api'` (`services/session.ts:107`). The Redis `Session` (`sess:<id>`, `user_sessions:<userId>`) carries `clientType`, ip, user-agent, device, expiry, activity — nothing that says "minted by the OAuth grant", and no jti.
4. **Therefore a selective deploy-step denylist ("every pre-fix OAuth refresh jti, interactive untouched") had no enumerable target set** — the fact that turned 14:45 into 14:53.

## The work (one test pass proves it — Kam's 2026-09-07 rule)

* **Mark every session the OAuth grants create.** The builder's design; the two shapes the code already offers: (i) a new `ClientType` value (`'oauth'`) passed as `createSession`'s fifth argument at `routes/oauth.ts:965` and `:1074` — note the KS-43 cohort-aware eviction in `createSession` buckets by `clientType` (`session.ts:178–230`), so a new value needs its own eviction policy decided, not inherited by accident; or (ii) a dedicated field on `Session` (e.g. `mintedBy: 'oauth'` + the `client_id`), leaving `clientType` and the eviction cohorts untouched. Either way the marker is written at mint and readable on `getSession` / `getUserSessions` (`session.ts:256`, `:329`).
* **Make it queryable at deploy time:** a read that lists a user's OAuth-minted sessions (and, if a future cutoff is ever wanted, all of them — `user_sessions:<userId>` is per-user; a global enumeration needs a set of OAuth session ids or a SCAN, decided by the builder and stated).
* **Do NOT add a cutoff** — the window is accepted (14:53). The marker exists so that a FUTURE deploy-step denylist can be selective; it does nothing for tokens already in the wild, which is why the window is accepted rather than closed.
* **Test pass:** red-first at the parent (an OAuth-grant session carries no marker / `clientType 'browser'`) → green at head (the code grant's and the refresh grant's sessions carry the marker, read back through `getSession`); an interactive login's session carries no marker (control); the KS-43 eviction cohorts behave as decided for the new value (a cell per policy); `auth.integration` OAuth cells unchanged; the ks1151 / ks1150 / ks823 / ks835 suites unchanged.

## Search before filing (every KS issue incl. archived, 1,146 issues, title + description + comments, literal; `5_Project_History/2026-09-14_s225/item6/symbol_search.log`)

`denylistRefreshJti` → KS-1151 / KS-823 / KS-486 (archived), KS-485, KS-329 (PQ hybrid — other subject), **KS-756 (Backlog, live: "Wire up the opaque refresh token that** `createSession` **already mints" — a symbol neighbour, not this work; named, not related)**; `isRefreshJtiDenylisted` → KS-486 only; `JWT_REFRESH_EXPIRES_IN` → KS-1151 comments; `forward-only` → KS-1151 + KS-550 (unrelated); `denylist-at-deploy` → 0. No existing work item; KS-1156 §C carries the window as a record — this ticket is the work and links to it.

**Related:** KS-1150 (R-2: the OAuth refresh grant rotates/denylists nothing — the same denylist, the other route; open), KS-1156 (the AUTH4 records; §C the window). **Named, no relation (archived):** KS-1151 (#986, M33), KS-823 (#983, M31), KS-835 (#984, M32).

## Definition of done

The marker is on develop with the red-first / green / control cells above; `getSession` returns it; the KS-43 eviction policy for the new value is decided and tested; no cutoff added; the accepted window's end date (the M31–M33 deploy + `JWT_REFRESH_EXPIRES_IN`) written on this ticket by whoever deploys. KS-1156 §C and KS-1150 R-2 are not closed by this ticket.

Filed 2026-09-14 by the merge seat s225 on Wednesday's ADDENDUM 04:46:19Z (Kam 14:45); rescoped the same seat on ADDENDUM 04:53:30Z (Kam 14:53).

nodes.body:
**Gate BT1's note N1 is closed by cells, not by a product change. PR #1665 is up at head `a404df30d1cdc82a236321930353e634213ffce4` — three new route/service cells plus three controls, in a new file. No product file is touched.**

BT1's words were the specification: *"C2 and C3 pin 'unmarked' only at the service layer. No route-level cell pins that a non-OAuth grant stays unmarked, that the marker survives a rewrite, or that a caller cannot forge it."* The marker exists to be an enumerable target set for a selective denylist, and each of the gate's three mutants breaks that set differently:

| cell | pins | the set breaks how |
|---|---|---|
| **X1** | a PASSWORD login passes **no** marker argument at all | false positive — the denylist takes out interactive logins |
| **X2** | `rotateSessionRefreshToken` preserves the marker | false negative — a long-lived OAuth session ages out and is never revoked |
| **X3** | the `authorization_code` grant ignores `req.body.mintedBy` | the set becomes caller-controlled |

Mine, marked as mine: **X1b** (the same login with a `deviceId` and `clientType`, so the marker is not a side effect of the optional arguments — it reds alongside X1, so it is not decoration), **XC1** (the harness reaches BOTH handlers and both mint, so an "unmarked" verdict is not a route that never ran) and **XC2** (an unmarked session stays unmarked across the same rotation, so X2 is not reading a marker the rotation invents).

**Red-proof.** Each mutant on a snapshot, `tsc --noEmit` **rc 0 before anything ran** (`services/auth` sets `noUnusedLocals` and `noUnusedParameters`, so a TS6133 arm would measure the compiler rather than the cells), the cell red by assertion, the product restored by sha256 equality. M-X1 reds X1 + X1b only; M-X2 reds X2 only; M-X3 reds X3 only — no collateral in any arm.

**BT1's claim re-measured rather than carried: each of the three mutants passes all 7 pre-existing cells (7 passed / 0 failed per arm).** So these cells are the only thing in the repository that catches these three regressions.

**Suite:** baseline with the new file withheld `104 files / 1126 passed, 0 failed, rc 0`; with it `105 files / 1132 tests`, reaching `1132 passed, 0 failed, rc 0`.

⚠ **One thing a reviewer will see and should not misread.** The auth suite is non-deterministic under load. Three consecutive runs of the same tree, no source change between them: **2 failed, then 10 failed, then 0 failed**. Eight of the ten sat at 5002–5766 ms — vitest's 5000 ms default, which `services/auth` does not override — across six repo-walking / import-graph guards this PR does not touch (`ks949`, `ks1186`, `ks1188`, `ks999`, `s130-f6`, `ks488`); `ks949` alone passes 31/31. I am not calling it pre-existing, because the withheld baseline was 0 failed: added load makes it trip more often. **My six cells failed 0 times in all three runs.** It is in the PR's Known residue and in a new `BACKLOG.md` entry carrying every figure — the same class as KS-1155 and the existing `services/kyc` entry, so a third service.

Scope unchanged: Kam's 2026-09-14 marker-only ruling still holds and nothing here builds or plans the selective denylist query. This is `Refs`, so the ticket stays open.

## BLUF
**MERGED to `develop` as `610570e5a75790d8ebf4264c4aec3ec8bebc0609` (squash of PR #1657), verified at source.** Both OAuth grants now mint their session with `mintedBy: 'oauth'`. Gate BT1 (Opus, tier 1, round 1 of 2) returned GO WITH NOTE, 0 blockers, 4 notes. **KS-1157 stays OPEN** — the deploy-step denylist is not built, and gate note N3 changes what building it will take. Not deployed.

## Verified at source
- merge sha `610570e5a75790d8ebf4264c4aec3ec8bebc0609`; **tree `0cd4627ead0ecf22546e4423f3fba825038c7b7d`**, equal to the landing the GO declared for the post-#1655 case and to my own `merge-tree` figure, computed independently before merging;
- **exactly ONE parent**, `86df4f5a52cc36b40276b441900627bf0a4c5de5`, which is my KS-1407 merge — so the two landed in the order the GO required;
- 4 files, **+250/-2**; subject 65 characters; **0 attribution trailers**.

## The note that matters for the rest of this ticket
**Gate BT1 N3:** the OAuth `refresh_token` grant never reads the session its token names. The gate's probe got **200 against an empty store**, minting a fresh *marked* session for a non-existent `sess-old`. **A denylist that selects sessions by `mintedBy` alone therefore would not stop a refresh-token holder.** The marker is necessary and not sufficient; KS-1690 (the origin-session check) has to land before or with the denylist. The earlier comment on this ticket has been edited in place to say so.

## Also residual
- **N1 — a cell gap of mine, not a defect in the code.** Three compile-clean mutants pass all 7 of my cells: a password-login session marked `'oauth'` at the route; `rotateSessionRefreshToken` deleting the marker; the code grant taking the marker from `req.body.mintedBy`. My seven arms all died, but they were the wrong seven to prove *non-OAuth stays unmarked*, *the marker survives a rewrite*, and *the marker is not forgeable*. Queued as one later test-only PR (tier 2), each cell required to red on its own mutant.
- **N2** — my "8 arms" figure counted the red-first run as an arm; it is 7 mutation arms plus that run. Corrected in place above.
- **N4** — the `setex`/reader line numbers in the PR body are pre-patch, each +2 at the landing.
- **Sessions already in Redis carry no marker**, by design: the forward-only window accepted in the 2026-09-14 ruling.
- **The four platform suites did not run** (no local stack, no Docker for this seat) and no real Redis was driven.

## BLUF
**The "mark every session" bullet is BUILT and raised as PR #1657 (https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/1657), head `a7de040ab040f460c83f5784ae132a2667ed80c6`, READY FOR GATE, tier 1.** Both OAuth grants now mint their session with a dedicated optional `mintedBy: 'oauth'`. Marker-only per Kam's ruling of 2026-09-14 14:53, with the forward-only window accepted. Nothing deployed. `Refs` — the deploy-step denylist is not built, so this ticket stays open.

## Recommendation
MERGED as `610570e5a75790d8ebf4264c4aec3ec8bebc0609`, tree `0cd4627ead0e`, on Wednesday's head-pinned GO after gate BT1. **The remaining work is NOT just the selective denylist query.** Gate BT1's note N3 measured that the OAuth `refresh_token` grant never reads the session its token names — 200 against an empty store, minting a fresh *marked* session for a non-existent `sess-old`. **So a denylist selecting sessions by `mintedBy` alone would not stop a refresh-token holder** until that grant checks its origin session, which is KS-1690. Sequence KS-1690 before, or together with, the denylist.

## What changed — 6 product lines over 3 files
| file | change |
|---|---|
| `types/index.ts` (+2/-0) | an optional `mintedBy?: 'oauth'` on `Session` |
| `services/session.ts` (+2/-0) | `createSession` takes a 6th parameter and spreads it **only when given** |
| `routes/oauth.ts` (+2/-2) | both grants pass it — the `authorization_code` and `refresh_token` branches of `POST /token` |

Interactive login, wallet and social callers pass nothing, so their sessions carry **no `mintedBy` key at all** — not the key with an `undefined` value. It is a field of its own rather than a value written into `clientType` (the ticket's shape ii, not shape i), so the KS-43 per-cohort LRU caps and the single-session policy for `'api'` are untouched.

## Scope, so this is not misread as closed
- The deploy-time query that would list a user's OAuth-minted sessions is **not built**.
- **Sessions already in Redis carry no marker.** The window is forward-only by construction — the accepted half of the ruling, not an oversight.

## Evidence
- **Red-first reproduced here, not quoted: 4 failed / 7 run** at the untouched product tip (R1-R4), all three CONTROL cells green, 0 load-failure signatures. **Green after: 7/7, 0 skipped.** `tsc` rc 0.
- **`services/auth` suite, both ends measured on real trees:** baseline **99 files / 1096 tests / 0 failed** on a clean checkout of this branch's own base; after **100 files / 1103 tests / 0 failed**. +7 cells, **0 vanished**.
- **7 mutation arms (M1-M7), all killed, plus the red-first run → no cell added at the time.** Each grant's omission reds its own cell; storing nothing reds R3+R4; an always-present key reds C2; marking every session reds C2+C3; writing the marker into `clientType` reds R3+R4; a wrong stored value reds R3+R4. Two arms from the pass's table are **inadmissible** here rather than survivors: `noUnusedLocals`/`noUnusedParameters` make them TS6133, so they would measure the compiler — re-formed into compile-safe equivalents reaching the same assertions.
- ⚠ **Both `createSession(..., 'oauth')` call sites are byte-identical lines** (`oauth.ts:969` and `:1078`). A one-line anchor would hit whichever came first while the *other* grant's cell reddened anyway — a wrong plant that looks right. Both oauth arms use **two-line** anchors on the distinguishing preceding comment, and every anchor was count-asserted unique before any write.
- **Can the new field leak or break a reader? Measured.** A session is **one opaque JSON string** under `sess:<id>` via `setex` — **not a hash**, so there is no key-enumeration surface. All three readers do **partial** casts, including the one outside `services/auth`: `packages/shared/src/security/session-validation.ts:105` casts to two fields. **No `SessionSchema` exists anywhere** (control: `.strict()` is in 11 files repo-wide, so the search finds the construct) and nothing enumerates a session's keys (control: `Object.keys` in 138 files). Worth recording for whoever builds the denylist: that shared validator returns `null` on a parse error and its own docstring says the gateway and originate then **fail OPEN**, so a reader broken by a malformed record would weaken auth rather than block traffic.
- **No interaction with #1655 (KS-1407), measured on the real branches:** `git merge-tree --write-tree` rc 0 with a single line of output, file sets **disjoint** (intersection 0, negative control 8), and **`services/session.ts` is not in #1655's set at all**.
- Preflight, quoted as printed: `PREFLIGHT INCOMPLETE — 13/16 legs ran, 3 SKIPPED. Nothing failed.` Legs 3, 4, 8 need a local stack. Leg 14 shell suites 91/91; leg 15 `13 code guards passed`, `23 / 23 services`; **leg 16 type-checks auth's test files: 151 examined, 42 errors, 42 baselined, 0 new.** Push rc 0, 590s.

## Not covered
- **The four platform suites did not run** — no local stack, no Docker for this seat. This touches a runtime surface, so a real gap.
- **No real Redis driven.** The cells pin the shape written and read back, not Redis's behaviour.
- **No existing session was re-marked** — nothing migrates them, by design.
- **The selective denylist is not proven possible**, only that the field it selects on is now written.
- No migration, schema, config or dependency change.

## A correction against myself
My first mutant run reported **6 survivors**, and that was my parser, not the code: the cell file uses nested describes, so a red line reads `× <file> > <describe> > RED ... R1:`, and my label regex anchored with `re.match` at the start of a segment beginning with the describe. Every label was dropped, and a verdict computed from labels alone read SURVIVED on arms whose own tally said 1-2 cells failed. Fixed, proved against a real captured red line, **and the verdict now cross-checks against the failed count — labels and tally disagreeing is reported as a parser failure, never as a survivor.** Without that cross-check, "6 mutants survive this patch" would have gone out as a measurement.

The patch is a local-model (Spark) pass applied byte-for-byte from the run's canonical `patch.diff`; the measurement is mine.


---
*Edited in place on 2026-10-20 after gate BT1, on Wednesday's post-merge instruction, rather than stacking a second comment. Two changes only: the arm count (BT1 **N2** — "8 arms" counted the red-first run as an arm; the evidence records 7 mutation arms M1-M7, all killed, plus that run), and the Recommendation, which understated the remaining work (BT1 **N3**). Nothing else was altered.*

## Rescoped (merge seat s225, 2026-09-14 04:5x Z): High "deploy-step denylist" → Medium "OAuth session marker" — Kam's 14:53 ruling supersedes his 14:45

- **14:45 AEST (Wednesday's ADDENDUM 04:46:19Z):** `denylist-at-deploy` — this ticket was filed as "Deploy step: denylist every OAuth refresh jti minted before #983/#984 (the forward-only launder window)", High, related KS-1150 / KS-1156.

description:
## BLUF

The open Records the AUTH4 tier-1 gate read or measured while gating PR #983 r2 (KS-823), PR #984 r2 (KS-835), PR #986 (KS-1151) and PR #987 (KS-1150 R-1) on 2026-09-14 — **none a finding at Minor or above against any of the four deltas; all four verdicts GO WITH FINDINGS, OVERALL GO WITH FINDINGS.** Filed as ONE ticket on Wednesday's brief to the merge seat (03:44:52Z, ITEM 5) so each record is searchable by symbol/path and none is rediscovered as new. #983 r2 landed as M31 `b9f541e6b`, #984 r2 as M32 `2c3315f37`; #986 / #987 follow on their stack seat merge-ins.

Report: `/Volumes/DevMASTER/!CODING/Testing Agent MAIN/projects/secuura/reports/2026-09-14-ks823-835-1151-1150-AUTH4-5b0f4dd58-9b020ff82-ac1c119b5-b6ed60f3b-tier1-r1/report.md` (246 lines, 13:28 AEST; §2 d, §3.5, §3.7, §8, §9). Measured on develop M29 `4569dd889` (the report's own numbering calls it "M24" — it did not count Kam's five merge commits).

**Search before filing (every KS issue incl. archived, 1,145 issues, title + description + comments, literal match;** `5_Project_History/2026-09-14_s225/item5/symbol_search.log`**):** `MACHINE_AUTH_METHODS` → comments only (KS-1150 `0d94fde8`, KS-835); `validateScopes` → **KS-839 (Backlog, live) is the existing home of the H-wildcard record — it is NOT re-filed here, only related**; `scopes.ts:125` → comments only; `requireScope` → 16 issues, none this record; `JWT_REFRESH_EXPIRES_IN` → 0; `ks1151` → KS-1150's comment only; `forward-only window` → 0; `oauth_app` → 21 issues, the H-limiter ancestor among them is **KS-164 (Done, archived — named here, no relation)**: "API-key clients aren't rate-limited — `rateLimitEnforce.ts:21`". Controls: a known title hits 1, a nonsense term 0.

**Not this ticket:** R-2 / R-3 (the OAuth refresh grant rotates/denylists nothing; OPEN on KS-1150 — its own DoD) · H-wildcard (KS-839) · KS-1152 (L5 records) · KS-1153 (L7 records) · KS-1150's own #982 records.

## The records, each with its symbol/path

### A. From #984 r1/r2 (KS-835) — READ, open, UNEDITED at `06aafd51c` (report §2 c–d)

1. **H-limiter.** `services/api-gateway/src/middleware/rateLimitEnforce.ts:61` `MACHINE_AUTH_METHODS = new Set(['api_key','oauth_app'])` — nothing mints `'oauth_app'`; an OAuth-minted token now carries `authMethod: 'oauth'` (KS-835), so the machine-client limiter's label set and the mint's label do not meet. Archived ancestor: KS-164.
2. **The stale** `scopes.ts:125-126` **docblock.** `services/api-gateway/src/middleware/scopes.ts:125-126` still says "KS-835 records that OAuth-minted tokens carry the `email` label too" — no longer true after #984; the comment describes the pre-fix world. Still there at `ac1c119b5`.
3. **H-mounts "eight" is seven.** `services/api-gateway/src/routes/proxy.ts`: `requireScope(` ×6 (`:375 :394 :568 :575 :764 :770`) + `requireScopeOrRole(` ×1 (`:731`) = SEVEN scope-gated mounts. "eight" remains in the PR #984 body (2 hits), two KS-835 comments and the gateway test `ks835-oauth-token-scope-gate.test.ts:59` comment. Polish.
4. **H-wildcard** (`validateScopes`, `services/auth/src/services/oauth.ts:352` `if (allowed.includes('*')) return requested;`) — **home: KS-839**; listed here only so the AUTH4 index is complete.

### B. From #986 (KS-1151) — MEASURED, test-quality Polish against the PR's OWN tests, not the guard (report §3.5)

* **R-C1 (T5):** the shipped suite records `world.sessionLookups` (`:64`, `:82`) but no cell asserts it (30 `expect(` lines, 0 on `sessionLookups`) — the "before `getSession`" claim is pinned by the comment and the PR text, not by the suite. Described regression cell: C3 of `evidence/__qa1151_launder.test.ts` (assert `getSession` = 0 on the refusal). Tamper T5 (guard moved below `getSession`): the builder's 5 cells STAY GREEN; the gate's C3/C6/C7 go red.
* **R-C2 (T6/T7):** every OAuth fixture in the shipped file carries `client_id` (cells 1/2 both claims, cell 3 `client_id` only), so the `authMethod === 'oauth'` arm has NO earning cell — it can be dropped (T6) or case-broken (T7) and the suite stays green. Described regression cell: C7 (re-sign minus `client_id`, keep the label → 401).
* **R-C3 (Polish, message text):** the guard's 401 body is `InvalidCredentialsError`'s default `"Invalid email or password"` (C1/C2/C6/C7), while a garbage/access token reads `"Invalid token"` (C8). The route's other two `InvalidCredentialsError` sites (`:663` absent token, `:687` no session) say the same words, so it is the route's own idiom and `logger.warn` carries the reason for operators — but an integrator whose OAuth SDK hits this route by mistake is told about an email and a password. Not a defect in #986; a wording the owner may want to unify.
* File: `services/auth/src/__tests__/ks1151-auth-refresh-refuses-oauth-token.test.ts`; guard: `services/auth/src/routes/auth.ts` after `verifyRefreshToken`, before `getSession` (`client_id !== undefined || authMethod === 'oauth'` → 401).

### C. THE FORWARD-ONLY WINDOW — escalation candidate, deployment-side, Kam via Wednesday (report §3.7; NOT a grade on #986)

A refresh token minted at the OAuth grant BEFORE #983/#984 land carries NEITHER `client_id` NOR `authMethod` and therefore passes the guard and still launders at `/api/auth/refresh` until it expires (`JWT_REFRESH_EXPIRES_IN` default `'7d'`, `services/auth/src/services/jwt.ts:44`). The deployed population is UNMEASURED (both round-1 reports, both PR bodies and this pass agree — no environment was probed). The instrument that closes the window is deployment-side (denylist the pre-deploy OAuth refresh jtis, or force re-authorisation at deploy). Also by design: a refused OAuth token is NOT denylisted by the sibling (C3 proves it stays alive at its own grant) — its replay protection is the OAuth grant's own `isRefreshJtiDenylisted` read (`oauth.ts:923`), which rotates/denylists nothing on success → R-2, open on KS-1150.

## §8 FINDINGS INDEX (evidence class · severity · target · SHIPS-WITH or TICKET) — verbatim

* **None at Minor or above against any of the four deltas.**
* R-C1 · MEASURED (T5) · Polish/test-quality · #986 · described regression cell C3 (assert `getSession` 0 on the refusal) — SHIPS-WITH as a follow-up test, not a blocker.
* R-C2 · MEASURED (T6/T7) · Polish/test-quality · #986 · described regression cell C7 (label-only token → 401) — SHIPS-WITH as a follow-up test.
* R-C3 · MEASURED · Polish/message text · #986 (route idiom, pre-existing) · owner's call.
* FORWARD-ONLY WINDOW · RULED consequence · deployment-side · Kam via Wednesday (escalation candidate, not a finding against #986).
* R-2 / R-3 · READ · open · KS-1150 (TICKET stays open after #987).
* #984 r1 Records: H-limiter · stale `scopes.ts:125-126` docblock · H-wildcard · H-mounts "eight" (seven) · READ · open · KS-835 / a follow-up ticket.
* Brief-precision (Wednesday's): END-state test FILES = 55 on M20 / 59 on M24, not 54; the oauth.ts `:852/:958` sites are `:848/:954` at `ac1c119b5`; the launcher's develop arm refuses at M24 (GUARDED) — the merge seat re-pins deliberately.

## §9 CLOSING — what the gate wants acted on — verbatim

1. Merge seat: the ADDENDUM at the top, re-pinned on the develop you land on (M24 or later); expected END tree `055e65485` on M24, auth 59/734.
2. Kam (via Wednesday): the forward-only window (§3.7) — decide the deployment-side instrument (denylist pre-deploy OAuth refresh jtis / forced re-auth), population unmeasured.
3. Owner (s221 or successor): two described regression cells for the ks1151 file (C3 ordering, C7 label-only); R-2 / R-3 on KS-1150; the four #984 Records.
4. Nothing else. No environment was touched; nothing was pushed, commented, filed or merged; scratch quarantined by rename under my scratchpad (`gate.KgDanL/quarantine/`, 20 items); the checkout and the builder's four worktrees read porcelain 0 at start and close.

## Definition of done

One test pass, per Kam's 2026-09-07 rule: A.1–A.3 edited (the limiter's label set decided, the docblock rewritten, "eight" → seven in the test comment; the PR body and ticket comments are history and stay), B's two described cells added to the ks1151 file (C3, C7) and R-C3 decided, C ruled by Kam (deployment-side; recorded here or on its own ticket if it becomes work). A.4 closes with KS-839; R-2/R-3 close with KS-1150.

Filed by the merge seat s225 on 2026-09-14 after #984's squash (M32 `2c3315f37`), before KS-835's archive, so KS-835's closing comment can name it.

title: packages/shared tree-walking guards exceed vitest's 5 s default under fleet load — 5 cells at load 32, 9 at load 25–49, 5,243 ms alone at load 27; assertions hold (green solo / with testTimeout raised / at load 11) — a load class that costs a re-run on every merge
description:
## BLUF

`packages/shared`'s repo-tree-walking guard cells exceed vitest's 5 s default `testTimeout` when the box carries the fleet's load (several seats' suites + QA gates at once). The assertions hold every time — the same cells pass solo, or with `--testTimeout` raised, or on the same tree minutes later at a lower load. So a red `Test timed out in 5000ms` in these files on a loaded box is a **load class**, not a product finding — but a merge seat cannot tell that from the run alone without a solo re-run or a raised-timeout re-run, which costs minutes on every merge. Filed so the class has a name and a home (KS-1053 names it only as context for the `services/auth` ks949 cell, a different suite).

## The measurements (all 2026-09-14, all on trees where the guard files are blob-identical to develop)

* **s224 (quoted as s224's, from its STACK READY mail 02:54:51Z):** `packages/shared` 43 files / 835 — **830 passed / 5 failed at load 32**, every failure `Test timed out in 5000ms` in the tree-walking guards (`crypto-agility.guard.test.ts`, `entrypoint-corpus.test.ts:180` the CENSUS cell, `ks727-errorhandler-class-guard.test.ts:905`, `ks764-key-revoke-call-site-guard.test.ts:263`, `ks860-test-listeners-bind-loopback.test.ts:463`); **1 at load 34**; the same cells green solo (**5,243 ms alone at load 27** — over the 5 s budget even solo, under that load).
* **s220 (the merge seat, PRED(985)** `3239e7207`**,** `item11/suite985/`**):** run at load 25–49 — **835: 822 passed / 9 failed / 4 skipped**, all nine timeouts: `crypto-agility.guard.test.ts` (5 s), `ks256-spec-example-contract.test.ts` (5 s, the positive-control cell), `ks727-errorhandler-class-guard.test.ts` ×4 (5 s: the CONTROL enumeration, the 🔴 corpus-is-the-shared-derivation cell, its CONTROL, the ROOTS-pinned cell), `ks764-key-revoke-call-site-guard.test.ts` (5 s, CALL_SITES), `ks781-p3-3-body-parser-order.test.ts` ×2 (a 10 s **hook** timeout in KS-832's ACCEPTANCE BAR + LEG C 5 s), `threadToken.test.ts` (**30 s**, `parameteriseMintPolicy` different-seeds — a crypto cell, not a walk). Solo re-runs at load 47–49: four files green; `ks727` and `ks781` still one timeout each. With `--testTimeout 120000 --hookTimeout 120000` at load ~20: `ks727` **94/94**, `ks781` **231/231**. The full suite again with the raised timeouts at load 11: **43 / 835 / 0**.
* **s203 (KS-1053's context line, 2026-09-13):** three `Test timed out in 5000ms` in the same guards at load ~20.
* Not the same subject as KS-1053 (the `services/auth` ks949 cell, 5.7–6.0 s on a 5 s budget under load, mechanism unestablished) — related as the neighbouring load-class record.

## What this costs today

Every merge-seat run of `packages/shared` on a loaded box is a coin-flip red that has to be re-run solo or with the timeout raised before it can be read (the s220 protocol did both). The tree walks themselves are the guards' point (they read the whole `services/` + `packages/` tree by design); their budget is the default 5 s.

## Fix shapes (the owner's call)

3. `threadToken.test.ts`'s 30 s cell is a different shape (CPU-bound crypto); its own budget line.

- [ ] the tree-walking guard cells carry an explicit timeout budget that a loaded box meets (measured: a full `packages/shared` run at load ≥ 30 reads 0 timeouts), or the walk is shared and the cells fit the default
- [ ] the merge-seat protocol no longer needs a solo re-run to read a `packages/shared` result on a loaded box

title: Root package-lock.json carries only rollup-darwin-arm64 — npm ci on ubuntu installs no Linux rollup binary, so frontend/demo-overlay and frontend/outlook-addin die at vite build (npm/cli#4828); the advisory workspace-suites job stays red at step 6 on every PR until the lock carries rollup-linux-x64-gnu
description:
## BLUF

*(npm scope sigils are omitted throughout —* `rollup/rollup-linux-x64-gnu` *means the scoped package; the symbols stay searchable.)*

`Blockchain/Dev/package-lock.json` records exactly ONE rollup platform binary — `node_modules/rollup/rollup-darwin-arm64` (the lock was generated on macOS arm64); `rollup-linux-x64-gnu` appears only inside an `optionalDependencies` list (lock line 19376), never as an installed entry. So `npm ci` on `ubuntu-latest` installs no Linux rollup binary, and the two vite-6 frontends — `frontend/demo-overlay` and `frontend/outlook-addin` (rollup 4.60.4) — die at `vite build` with `Error: Cannot find module … rollup-linux-x64-gnu`. Upstream: npm/cli#4828 (npm's optional-platform-dependency flaw). Measured live by the L9 gate on PR #887's advisory job (`pr` run 34786655660 / job 103803259738, step 6): the four vite-8 frontends (rolldown) and all 26 service/package builds green; these two red. **Consequence:** `pr-platform-suites.yml`'s `Workspace unit suites (advisory, non-blocking)` job stays red at step 6 on EVERY PR until the lockfile carries `rollup-linux-x64-gnu` — advisory, blocks nothing, but the job cannot say anything useful until then. A macOS pass is not runner evidence for this job.

The gate's TICKET line, verbatim: *"the rollup-linux-x64-gnu lockfile matter — Blockchain/Dev/package-lock.json -> node_modules/rollup/rollup-* (only rollup-darwin-arm64 installed; rollup-linux-x64-gnu only in an optionalDependencies list at :19376); frontend/demo-overlay, frontend/outlook-addin; pr-platform-suites.yml workspace-suites step 6; npm/cli#4828 — a KS or KS-1148 (c)."*

Report: `/Volumes/DevMASTER/!CODING/Testing Agent MAIN/projects/secuura/reports/2026-09-14-L9-940-941-942-887-ks1075-1077-1078-961-tier2-r1/report.md` (§2 the live job; §4b(iv) the mechanism — `git grep -o -E '"node_modules/rollup/rollup-[a-z0-9-]+"' 3aee3deed -- Blockchain/Dev/package-lock.json` → `rollup-darwin-arm64` only; findings register R-4). First recorded by s215 as an adjacent finding in KS-1148's comment (2026-09-13T22:32Z): "a DIFFERENT class from (a)/(b), so not added to the checklist".

**Why its own ticket, not KS-1148 (c):** KS-1148's class is *the runner never installs or builds* — its fix is an install/build step per job. This job DOES install and build; the defect is the lock's CONTENT, and `npm ci` on Linux cannot install a binary the lock does not carry. One fix, one file, a different owner's action — the 2026-09-07 one-ticket-per-fix rule. Related: KS-1148 (the runner-gap class this was first noted under), KS-961 (#887, the advisory job that surfaces it).

**Ancestors (archived — named, not related):** KS-653 (Done — root-workspace `npm run build` broken for 5 of 6 vite frontends: the same npm/cli#4828 class on rolldown's `darwin-arm64` binding; fixed by regenerating the root lock's optional native bindings) and KS-376 (Done — the esbuild platform-binary subtree inconsistent in the same lock, same class). The lock has lost a platform binary set three times now; the regen-on-one-host shape is what keeps re-creating it.

## Fix shape (the builder's call)

* Make the root lock carry ALL rollup platform binaries (as it once did for esbuild's 25/26 variants): a lock regeneration that records every `rollup/rollup-*` optional binary (npm ≥ 10 records all platforms when run with `--package-lock-only` from a clean state; or add `rollup/rollup-linux-x64-gnu` as an explicit optionalDependency at the root so the lock pins it), then verify on a Linux `npm ci` (the advisory job itself is the instrument: step 6 green for `demo-overlay` and `outlook-addin`).
* Regression guard: a lockfile cell that asserts the `rollup/rollup-*` entry set covers `darwin-arm64` AND `linux-x64-gnu` (the two hosts that build this repo), so a future macOS regen cannot drop the Linux binary silently.

## Done when

- [ ] `Blockchain/Dev/package-lock.json` carries `node_modules/rollup/rollup-linux-x64-gnu` (and keeps `rollup-darwin-arm64`)
- [ ] `pr-platform-suites.yml` `Workspace unit suites` step 6 builds `frontend/demo-overlay` and `frontend/outlook-addin` green on a Linux runner (read from the live job at the fixing PR's head)
- [ ] a guard cell pins the platform-binary set, red-first on the current lock

title: A push whose pre-push gate runs past ~6 min dies with rc 141 after the gate PASSED — GitHub closes the idle SSH session git opened before the hook; the launcher's core.sshCommand has no keepalive
description:
## BLUF

**A Platform K push whose pre-push gate runs longer than ~6 minutes dies with** `rc 141` **(SIGPIPE) and** `Connection to github.com closed by remote host.` **— after the gate has PASSED.** git opens the SSH session to read the remote refs BEFORE the pre-push hook runs, holds it through the hook, then writes the pack; GitHub closes the idle session during a long gate, and the pack write hits a dead socket. Nothing lands, nothing is refused, and the only tell is one line above `push rc=141`. The repo's `core.sshCommand` (written by `Launch_Claude.command`) carries no keepalive, and `~/.ssh/config` has none for [github.com](<http://github.com>). Measured 2026-09-14 on three pushes from the same box through the same hook shape.

## Measured (2026-09-13/14 UTC, darwin arm64, OpenSSH default keepalives = none)

| push | branch | gate duration | outcome |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| #903 | `kamilkreiser/ks-991-stale-local-develop` | 5 min 05 s (14 legs) | landed, rc 0 |
| #918 | `feature/ks-926-wire-unreachable-guards` | 5 min 44 s (15 legs) | landed, rc 0 |
| #925 attempt 1 | `feature/ks-1046-preflight-passed-…` | 6 min 17 s (15 legs, stacked) | gate PASSED (`PREFLIGHT INCOMPLETE — 12/15 legs ran, 3 SKIPPED. Nothing failed.`), then `Connection to github.com closed by remote host.` — **rc 141, origin unchanged** |
| #925 attempt 2 | same head, `GIT_SSH_COMMAND` = the same key + options + `-o ServerAliveInterval=30 -o ServerAliveCountMax=20` | 4 min 35 s | landed, rc 0, `push_protocol.py verify` PROTOCOL-CLEAN |

So the idle cutoff sits between ~5:45 and ~6:15 of hook time, and the gate is only growing (leg 15 landed on two branches today; the shell suites are 30). `push_protocol.py verify` on attempt 1 read the tracking ref UNCHANGED = origin — a push that touched nothing; the failure is the transport, not the tree.

## Where

* `Launch_Claude.command:130` and `:135` — the two `core.sshCommand` lines the launcher writes into `2_Project_Files/.git/config` (`ssh -i <key> -o IdentitiesOnly=yes -o StrictHostKeyChecking=accept-new`); no `ServerAliveInterval`.
* `.githooks/pre-push` → `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/preflight/preflight.sh` — the gate whose duration crosses the cutoff.
* Records: `5_Project_History/quarantine/2026-09-14-s214/push3-ks1046/` (`push.out` line 893, `verify1.out`, `INCIDENT_sigpipe_idle_ssh.txt`, `attempt2/`).

## Fix shape

Append ` -o ServerAliveInterval=30 -o ServerAliveCountMax=20` to the launcher's `core.sshCommand` value (the launcher is the owner; the fix is carded to Kam as `secuura-launcher-ssh-keepalive`). Until it lands, a seat whose gate is long retries with the same options on `GIT_SSH_COMMAND` for that one push — never an edit to the repo's `.git/config`. A control for the fix: a push whose hook is padded past 7 minutes lands with keepalives and dies without them.

## Why it matters

The failure prints no refusal and no `To github…` line; a seat reading only the gate's verdict reports a push that never happened. The two seats that pushed today with 5-minute gates were under the cutoff by chance.

nodes.body:
**BLUF:** Two more pushes ended rc 141 on 2026-11-09 with the keep-alive options set, after 1,224 s and 1,205 s. So the keep-alive on the SSH command did not prevent this drop at about 20 minutes, which is new against the 2026-10-26 comment above, where the same options carried a 13 min 45 s push to success and two roughly 38-minute hooks held the session. Facts only; read from the two seats' own records, nothing re-run.

**The two drops.** The seats' push driver runs `git -c core.sshCommand="ssh -i <key> -o IdentitiesOnly=yes -o StrictHostKeyChecking=accept-new -o ServerAliveInterval=15 -o ServerAliveCountMax=120" push origin <branch>` with `GIT_SSH_COMMAND` unset (the push line is 209 in one copy of the driver and 210 in the other).

* Seat T 19th, first push of the KS-2109 branch: push start 21:26:22Z, push end 21:46:46Z, rc 141, elapsed 1224 s. The push output has `Read from remote host github.com: Can't assign requested address` and then `client_loop: send disconnect: Broken pipe`, at lines 1953 to 1954 of 3,900, in the middle of the hook's output. The driver's `ls-remote` returned nothing. The second attempt through the same driver verified.
* Seat T 20th, push of the KS-2132 branch: push start 23:34:20Z, push end 23:54:25Z, rc 141, elapsed 1205 s. The push output has `Connection to github.com closed by remote host.` and then `client_loop: send disconnect: Broken pipe`, at lines 2860 to 2861 of 3,901, in the middle of the hook's output. The hook then ran on to its verdict (`PREFLIGHT INCOMPLETE — 13/16 legs ran, 3 SKIPPED. Nothing failed.`) and the push ended 141 afterwards. `ls-remote` returned nothing.

Each drop cost a full hook run and a turn in the push queue.

**Differences from the 2026-10-26 runs, none of them tested.** Those used the one-command `GIT_SSH_COMMAND` form; these use the driver's `-c core.sshCommand` form with the same options. The hooks here ran about 20 minutes; the earlier success ran 13 min 45 s and the two hooks that held ran about 38 minutes (rc 1, not 141). The first drop's error text is a local socket error, the second's is the remote side closing. Host load and the number of seats pushing at the same time are not recorded.

**Not known.** Why the session ended in these two runs and not in the 38-minute ones.

**Records.** `/Volumes/DevMASTER/!CODING/Secuura/Blockchain/5_Project_History/2026-11-09_seatT-19th/evidence/d5/push/real/push.out` and `/Volumes/DevMASTER/!CODING/Secuura/Blockchain/5_Project_History/2026-11-09_seatT-20th/evidence/e1/push/real/push.out`, each beside its status and push.rc records in the same directory; the driver copies are `/Volumes/DevMASTER/!CODING/Secuura/Blockchain/5_Project_History/2026-11-09_seatT-19th/tools/pushlock_t19_newbranch_v3.sh` and `/Volumes/DevMASTER/!CODING/Secuura/Blockchain/5_Project_History/2026-11-09_seatT-20th/tools/pushlock_t20_newbranch_v3.sh`.

**Measured 2026-10-25/26 (UTC) on the same box and the same hook, with the idle cutoff isolated and with the per-command keepalive.** Facts only.

**Idle cutoff, isolated.** `git push --dry-run` to the real origin through a scratch `core.hooksPath` whose `pre-push` only sleeps 690 s (no keepalive; sends nothing, writes no ref). Connection opened 23:17:01Z. ssh printed `Connection to github.com closed by remote host.` at 23:23:05Z (the modification time of the file it was written to) = **364 s**. git then ended `rc=141` at 23:28:34Z, when the hook returned. This sits inside the 5:45 to 6:15 bracket in the description.

**Real pushes that ended rc 141 with nothing on origin (no keepalive):**
* KS-1391 branch, 22:16Z to 22:27:13Z (about 11 min). The hook refused (`PREFLIGHT FAILED on leg(s) 6 7 14`), git printed `error: failed to push some refs`, then `push rc=141`.
* KS-1723 lock refresh, first attempt, 22:58:56Z to 23:14:10Z (15 min). The gate PASSED (`PREFLIGHT INCOMPLETE - 13/16 legs ran, 3 SKIPPED. Nothing failed.`), then `push rc=141`; `git ls-remote origin refs/heads/feature/ks-1723-lock-refresh` returned nothing.

**With the per-command keepalive** (`GIT_SSH_COMMAND="$(git config core.sshCommand) -o ServerAliveInterval=15 -o ServerAliveCountMax=120" git push -u origin <branch>`, for that one command; `.git/config` not edited): the same commit and the same hook, started 23:17:27Z and ended 23:31:12Z (13 min 45 s), **landed, rc 0**. Proof: PR #1688, merged as `28dac5c12ba5c00d9fc3ad04daee5230eff71619`. Two later pushes with the same form ran 2272 s and 2364 s (about 38 min) and ended `rc 1` with the hook's own `PREFLIGHT FAILED on leg(s) 14` and git's `error: failed to push some refs`, not 141, so the ssh session stayed up for those 38 min.

**The launcher's keepalive did not apply to this session.** The repo-local value read at about 01:35Z on 2026-10-26 is `ssh -i ".../3_Access_Keys/github_deploy_rw" -o IdentitiesOnly=yes -o StrictHostKeyChecking=accept-new`, with no `ServerAlive*`, although `Launch_Claude.command` lines 130 and 135 carry `-o ServerAliveInterval=30 -o ServerAliveCountMax=20`. Reading the launcher (lines 129 to 141): it writes `core.sshCommand` only in its first two branches (the agent holds the identity; or `SECUURA_ALLOW_ONDISK_KEY=1` with the key file present). In the third branch, the one that prints `[F-02] No SSH identity available for git (keychain not seeded, on-disk fallback off).`, it writes nothing and the message says `git will use whatever core.sshCommand is already in the repo config`. This session's launch (2026-10-25T21:55:16Z) printed that F-02 warning; the 2026-10-26 daily note records the same F-02 for two other seats launched that morning.

This issue was archived on 2026-10-05T02:48:32Z (history actor: the board account; not an automatic archive) while in Backlog. It was unarchived on 2026-10-26 to record the above and left in Backlog.

**Launcher edited by s220 on Kam's 11:09 ruling (`delegate`); takes effect at each seat's next launch.** `Blockchain/Launch_Claude.command` (project root, outside the repo) — the two `core.sshCommand` values it writes into `2_Project_Files/.git/config` now carry ` -o ServerAliveInterval=30 -o ServerAliveCountMax=20`:
- line 130 (agent-backed): `ssh -o IdentitiesOnly=yes -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no -o ServerAliveInterval=30 -o ServerAliveCountMax=20`
- line 135 (on-disk key): `ssh -i "$DEPLOY_KEY_ONDISK" -o IdentitiesOnly=yes -o StrictHostKeyChecking=accept-new -o ServerAliveInterval=30 -o ServerAliveCountMax=20`

Backup beside it: `Launch_Claude.command.pre-0914-keepalive` (sha256 `9b3017215b4d5093…`, byte-identical to the pre-edit file); edited file sha256 `35413bab27864a0e…`; `diff` = exactly the two lines; `bash -n` rc 0. Verified without relaunching: `ssh -G github.com -o ServerAliveInterval=30 -o ServerAliveCountMax=20` prints both options (a bogus option is refused — the instrument discriminates); `GIT_SSH_COMMAND="<the line-135 value>" git ls-remote origin develop` rc 0 → M20 `a53343502` in 2 s (control: the current repo-local config, rc 0 in 3 s). The repo-local `core.sshCommand` is unchanged until the next launch rewrites it — a push from an already-running seat still runs without keepalives. Reason: this ticket's measurement (s214) — a pre-push gate over ~6 min dies on GitHub's idle SSH cutoff (rc 141) with the gate PASSED.

title: CI-runner environment gaps (one class, two jobs): `Security Scanning` runs `audit:contract` with no install, so `audit-locks.mjs` dies on `Cannot find package 'semver'` (7 of 59 cases red); `PR Security Gates` runs the shell suites with no build, so `ks949_main_seed_idempotence` aborts on a missing `packages/shared/dist` — the jobs' setup, not the code
description:
## BLUF

Two CI jobs run test code whose runtime prerequisites the job never installs or builds. Both reds are **environment gaps on the runner**, not defects in the code under test — each suite is green locally on a tree that has a root `node_modules` and a built `packages/shared`. Recorded here as ONE ticket because one fix pass (an install/build step per job) proves both, and because both were surfaced by the same lane on the same day. **Fixing either is a** `.github/workflows/` **edit — Kam-class; nothing here is changed by the seat that filed this.** Filed on Wednesday's ADDENDUM of 2026-09-13T21:58Z; board searched first (`packages/shared is not built` 0 hits · `npm run build -w packages/shared` 0 · `Cannot find package 'semver'` 1 — the closed ticket that gave `scripts/audit/` its own `package.json`, Done + archived · `CI-runner environment` 0 · nonsense-token control 0).

## Checklist

- [ ] **(a)** `Security Scanning` **→ job** `Dependency Audit` **→ step** `Audit-contract suites`**:** `scripts/audit/audit-locks.mjs` **cannot start.**
  * Evidence: PR #940's run 34426409872 / job 102712486541 / step 7 — the first run where this step printed anything (PR #940 dropped `bash -e` from that step). `ℹ tests 59 · pass 52 · fail 7`; the seven reds are every `audit-locks:` case in `scripts/audit/gate-exit-codes.test.mjs` (`:91`, `:104`, `:113`, `:180`, `:192`, `:201`, `:208`), each "got 1" where 3 / 2 / 0 was expected. The `:192` case's assertion captured the child's output verbatim: `Error [ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND]: Cannot find package 'semver' imported from /home/runner/work/Distributed_Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/Blockchain/Dev/scripts/audit/audit-locks.mjs` (Node.js v24.20.0).
  * Mechanism: the job deliberately runs **no install** — the comment above its `npm audit` step says advisories resolve straight from the lockfile so no `npm ci` is needed. That is true for `npm audit` and false for the next step's test suite: `audit-locks.mjs:50` imports `semver`, which is declared only in `scripts/audit/package.json` (a standalone member, intentionally outside the workspaces list; its own description names exactly this failure on any tree without a root install). Locally the hoisted root `node_modules` supplies it → 59/59.

- [ ] **(b)** `PR Security Gates` **→ job** `Code Security Gates` **→ step 11** `All shell test suites`**:** `packages/shared` **is never built.**

The suite's own guard at `ks949_main_seed_idempotence.test.sh:113` refuses to run without `packages/shared/dist/index.js`, exactly as designed.
