*Original comment, unchanged below:*

**BLUF: `services/security` has the same gap as this ticket's two services. Its tests are never type-checked, and two of its test files hold type errors that nothing reports. Found while raising KS-1568. Nothing here is fixed.**

**Why nothing reports them:**
* `services/security/tsconfig.json` excludes `src/__tests__`.
* security is not one of the three services the test type-check ratchet covers (`scripts/typecheck-tests/check.cjs`: auth, api-gateway, vc-issuer).

So `tsc -p` for the service sees no test file at all.

**Measured.** I used a scratch config that extends the service's own and sets `exclude: []`. The program contains every test file, and `--listFilesOnly` counts the KS-1568 test once.

Develop `4a065fb75350` plus the KS-1568 branch: **rc 2, 2 errors**, both in existing files:

* `src/__tests__/ks952-rate-limit-scope-route.test.ts:249`: `TS2339 Property 'error' does not exist on type '{}'`
* `src/__tests__/ks952-rate-limit-scope.test.ts:313`: `TS1343 The 'import.meta' meta-property is only allowed when the '--module' option is 'es2020' … 'nodenext'`

**Controls:**
* With the KS-1568 test removed, the count is still **2**, so neither error is from KS-1568.
* A deliberate `TS2322` planted in the KS-1568 test file shows up as one more error.
* The vitest suite is **354/354**. Both files run fine, because vitest does not type-check.

**Not done:** no ratchet baseline for security, no fix to either file, no other service checked. This comment only adds a third service to the inventory.

## BLUF

**Still true in originate today, and the exclusion has GROWN since this ticket was written.** Re-measured at develop `a0da739b6954d42333640ea190d877f031803c7f` while building KS-1633. **No new ticket filed — this ticket already carries the measurement and the two shapes, so this is an update to it rather than a fourth sibling** (KS-892, KS-1122 and KS-848 are all closed as Duplicate in this family).

## What changed since the description

The description records originate excluding `src/__tests__` **and** `src/**/*.test.ts`. It now excludes **three** patterns:

```
"exclude": ["node_modules", "dist", "src/__tests__", "src/**/*.test.ts", "src/**/*.integration.test.ts"]
```

`src/**/*.integration.test.ts` has been added since. It matters because it is a **second, independent** mechanism: a reader who moved tests out of `src/__tests__` to get them type-checked would still be excluded by the glob.

## Re-measured, with the same control shape this ticket used

| arm | `tsc --noEmit -p services/originate` |
| --- | --- |
| `const plantedTypeError: number = "this is a string, not a number";` in a **test** file (`ks564-certification-issuer-uuid.test.ts`) | **rc 0, 0 `error TS`** |
| the **same** statement in a **non-test** file (`src/utils/principalId.ts`) — the control | **rc 2, 1 `error TS`** |

`--listFilesOnly` on the project: **0** files under `__tests__` in the program, against a control of **1** for `src/routes/certifications.ts`. Both files restored byte-identically afterwards.

## The one thing worth adding: what it costs a reader at the bench

**The jest signature of a type error in a test file is `Tests: 0 total`.** Not a red, not a named failure — a `Test suite failed to run` block followed by a tally of zero. It reads like "there was nothing to run", and a seat scanning for `failed` counts sees none. It cost me two throwaway probes today before I recognised it. So the practical cost of this gap is not only that `tsc` cannot fail — it is that the error's eventual appearance is in a shape that does not look like an error.

**Worth noting for sequencing:** the test-file type-check ratchet shipped under KS-1000 / KS-1487 gates `services/auth`, `services/api-gateway` and `services/vc-issuer`. **originate is not in that list**, so this service has neither the tsconfig coverage nor the ratchet.

## Both shapes from the Recommendation still apply unchanged

A `tsconfig.test.json` that includes the tests plus a script that runs it, or including the tests in the main config. **No fix in this comment and none attempted** — I was building KS-1633 and this is not that ticket.

## BLUF

**PR #1507 merged to `develop` as `36f0f56f3698` (2026-10-12 13:35Z): preflight leg 16 now gates `services/api-gateway` as well as `services/auth`.** A type error in a gateway test file is now refused at push time instead of being found later by hand. **This ticket stays In Progress:** `services/originate` (the other service) and R2-4 remain. Nothing is deployed; per the GO it lands in deploy round 3 (a push-time gate, so no image carries it).

## Recommendation

1. Expect a refusal with `TS2307` on `@secuura/shared/...` after a develop that changed the shared package's exports: it means a stale build. Run `npm run build -w @secuura/shared` (4.5 s here). **`npm ci` does not rebuild it** in this repo (`.npmrc` sets `ignore-scripts=true`). KS-1517 (raised to P3) is to make the leg detect this and say so.
2. Follow-ups are in **KS-1520** (P3, a checklist): pin that a gateway failure fails the default run, run its cells without an install, correct the "test file" failure sentence, fix the header.
3. V's ratchet-hardening PR (#1506) conflicts with this one on a `CLAUDE.md` sentence and lands second.

## Detail

* **The hole it closes, measured:** with a `TS2322` planted in a real gateway test file, the unchanged leg answered rc 0 `OK — 1 service(s)` (the push accepted); the new leg answers rc 1 and names the file and the code.
* **Cost, as the Opus gate measured it:** about **+5.4 s per push**, serial: leg 16 +2.7 s and leg 14 +2.7 s (the leg's own suite now type-checks the gateway too). The "+3 s" in the PR's first text counted leg 16 only.
* **Gate:** Opus tier, GO WITH NOTE, 0 Major (verdict sha256/16 `550ec6716d11d27b`).
* **Verified at source:** one parent, landed tree `ec5badba2f1b` equals the gated prediction, three blobs equal the gated head. On that tree: the changed suite 26/0 twice, the real leg `OK — 2 service(s)`, api-gateway 114 files / 1100 tests, 0 failed.
* **Not run:** Schemathesis, Akto, Playwright, k6; the hook that pushed this head printed `13/16 legs ran, 3 SKIPPED`, "NOT a pass".

## BLUF

**PR #1504 merged to `develop` as `cc2939bbf352` (2026-10-12 12:42Z): the api-gateway's test files are now type-checked against a baseline that can only shrink.** This is the **api-gateway half of R2-2 only**. **This ticket stays In Progress:** `services/originate` (the other service) and R2-4 remain.

## Recommendation

1. Next, as its own PR with an Opus gate: add `services/api-gateway` to preflight leg 16's default list, so the pre-push hook runs this baseline. Today it does not; only `npm run check:test-types` and the new cell in the gateway's own suite do, and both are run by hand.
2. KS-1489 (fingerprint-keyed baseline entries) must land after this and convert `baseline-api-gateway.txt` as well as auth's.

## Detail

* **What landed:** `services/api-gateway/tsconfig.test.json` (byte-identical to auth's), `scripts/typecheck-tests/baseline-api-gateway.txt` (35 errors in 14 file+code entries across 13 files), one gate cell in the gateway suite, and `npm run check:test-types` now runs both services. No product code.
* **Gate:** Sonnet tier, GO WITH NOTE, 0 Major (verdict sha256/16 `796c6635e6b36741`). It re-ran 6 of my 8 tampers and added 8 of its own; 6 of those 8 were caught.
* **What the ratchet does not guarantee** (inherited from the auth mechanism, named in the squash): the baseline is keyed by file + code + count, so (1) a same-code swap or a `// @ts-ignore` beside a new error of that code in the same file passes; (2) `// @ts-nocheck` on a test file with no baseline entry silences it; (3) `--init` after deleting the baseline admits new errors silently. "Can only shrink" is stronger than the checker guarantees.
* **Follow-up:** KS-1517 (P4): a stale `packages/shared` build made the gateway checker report two false `NEW` `TS2307` errors; nothing checks that build.
* **On develop at the merge:** `npm run check:test-types` rc 0 for both services; the 23-cell leg-16 suite 23/23; api-gateway 113 files / 1086 tests, 0 failed, twice.
* **Not run:** Schemathesis, Akto, Playwright, k6; the hook that pushed this head predated leg 16 (it printed 12/15, "NOT a pass").

## BLUF
A measurement for this ticket's class from the KS-1205 gate (PR #1463): **the api-gateway's `tsc` configuration skips `src/__tests__`, and with tests included it reports 30 errors that no gate sees.** The same 30 errors appear on base, on the PR head and on the merged tree, and **none is in a file KS-1205 added or changed**.

## Detail
- The default `tsc --noEmit` is rc 0 on all three trees. With test files included the same command gives 30 errors; the set is identical on all three trees.
- A type error planted in a test file returns rc 0 under the default config (the gate's zero control: a planted error gave rc 2 only when tests were included).
- So a "tsc rc 0" line in a Test Evidence block says nothing about a gateway test file. Source: Opus gate verdict on #1463, section 3 and note N3.

**Merged a37fb11d3a673f4a9f021e0bd7435b78dca8ba33 (PR #1305) on the gate32 GO of 2026-09-27T13:05:46Z.** develop's tree equals the GO's declared END tree `977c6a48635341fe9d29f48a0c7e83c843dd9895`.

**NOT Done — this ticket stays In Progress.** **R2-2 (the tsconfig half) and R2-4 (the record) are still open.** What merged is R2-3 only: the cells pin that the gateway vouch reaches originate and none of the other seventeen service keys.

**PR #1305 open at head `7aab743e13f45d10a43650e07f25abffccb6441e`, base `develop`, awaiting the QA gate.** Nothing is merged, and this covers **R2-3 only** — it is `Refs`, not a close.

Patch produced by a local model under a Wednesday brief, re-verified independently.

What it does: one NEW api-gateway test file, no product change. The merged mint-scope test pins two of the eighteen service keys that must never receive the gateway vouch header, so an allow-list widening sparing those two stays green. The new cells drive the real `createProxyRoutes` with every service pointed at one recorder and pin, per non-originate key, that no vouch arrives; a control proves originate does receive it and that the factory reads exactly eighteen keys. Renamed at raise — the builder's filename described this ticket's *other* half.

**Still open on this ticket:** the tsconfig half (R2-2) and the record (R2-4). That is why there is no closing keyword.

Measured at develop `94c9c7aa9be7`, in this session:
- the READY's closing code fence was glued to its last `+` line; stripped, and a full diff of the READY's raw block against what was applied is exactly those three backticks and nothing else
- strict apply, no recount and no fuzz; a corrupted hunk count is refused rc 128 (a new file cannot be controlled by a path tamper, so the count is corrupted instead)
- RED under a product tamper at `services/api-gateway/src/routes/proxy.ts:275`: **2 failed / 2 passed of 4**, both failures being the two declared cells on their assertions; restore verified byte-identical to the tip blob
- GREEN at head: 4 of 4
- api-gateway suite: bare **82 files / 754 tests** → patched **83 / 758**, 0 new reds
- `packages/shared` 48 files / 945 tests, rc 0
- tsc over a program proven to contain the new file (619 files, 83 test files): 29 pre-existing errors, the same SET as the tip, 0 naming this file
- api-gateway lint rc 0, 36 problems, 0 errors, unchanged from the tip
- push gate: `pre_push_hook_base` 28/0, its fixture guard 6/0, `run_shell_suites` 49/0, shell suites 60 of 60, 0 `FIXTURE BUILD FAILED`, 12/15 legs ran (3 skipped, no local stack)

vc-issuer has the same shape: its tsc program excludes src/__tests__ (measured with --listFilesOnly, Seat B 6th); a tests-included tsc there shows 3 pre-existing TS2339 in credentialRepo.test.ts (the #1084-#1091 gate).

title: Prod: tracked config still names the cutover host aws-ps.secuura.net — a fresh box would issue its TLS cert and set nginx server_name for the wrong domain
description:
`ps.secuura.net` has been the live production hostname since the AWS cutover, but the tracked `ssd/dep-aws-secuura/` files still carry the interim `aws-ps.secuura.net` used during Phase A of `ssd/aws-docker/MIGRATION.md`:

| File | Lines | Value |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `Docker.appsettings.template.json` | 277-280 | `WebSiteUrl`, `WebSiteUrlTnC`, `WebSiteUrlPP`, `AppUrl` = `https://aws-ps.secuura.net/…` |
| `deploy-from-ecr.sh` | 38 | `DOMAIN="${DOMAIN:-aws-ps.secuura.net}"` — certbot issues for THIS name on first deploy |
| `local-nginx.conf` | 47, 56, 59-60 | `server_name aws-ps.secuura.net`; `ssl_certificate …/live/aws-ps.secuura.net/…` |

(`StatusListBaseUrl` at `:373` already says `https://ps.secuura.net`, so the file disagrees with itself.)

The running box presumably has hand-edited copies (UAT's were "reconciled back into git" in `1c4ab13`; prod's never were). The consequence lands on the replacement box Stuart said is coming: `deploy-from-ecr.sh` would issue a Let's Encrypt cert for `aws-ps.secuura.net` (which must resolve to the box for http-01 to pass — if the record is gone, issuance fails and the stack stays down), nginx would serve the wrong `server_name`, and every absolute link in email templates would point at the old host.

## Work

* Replace all `aws-ps.secuura.net` occurrences in the three files with `ps.secuura.net`; `README.md` if it mentions the cutover host.
* Before deploying: compare checksums of the box's `/home/ubuntu/secuura-dk/` files against git to find any other drift and reconcile it into git, as `1c4ab13` did for UAT.
* Confirm the DNS record for `aws-ps.secuura.net` can be retired (or keep it as a CNAME if anything still links to it).

## Verify

`openssl s_client -connect ps.secuura.net:443 -servername ps.secuura.net </dev/null | openssl x509 -noout -subject` → CN = [ps.secuura.net](<http://ps.secuura.net>) on the new box; `grep -rn aws-ps ssd/dep-aws-secuura` returns nothing.

## Acceptance

* `grep -rn aws-ps ssd/dep-aws-secuura` returns **nothing** — all occurrences in `Docker.appsettings.template.json` (`WebSiteUrl`, `WebSiteUrlTnC`, `WebSiteUrlPP`, `AppUrl`), `deploy-from-ecr.sh`'s `DOMAIN` default and `local-nginx.conf`'s `server_name` / `ssl_certificate` paths now read `ps.secuura.net`, and `README.md` no longer names the cutover host.
* The file no longer disagrees with itself: `StatusListBaseUrl` and the four URL keys all name the same host.
* **Reconciliation recorded before any deploy.** The running box's `/home/ubuntu/secuura-dk/` files are compared against git by checksum **through SSM** (port 22 is closed), every difference is listed here, and the ones that belong in git are committed — the same treatment `1c4ab13` gave UAT. "No drift" is an acceptable outcome only if the checksums are quoted.
* A decision is recorded for the `aws-ps.secuura.net` DNS record: retired, or kept as a CNAME because something still links to it. Note that `deploy-from-ecr.sh` needs the name it is issuing for to resolve to the box — so if the record is gone *and* the default is still `aws-ps`, http-01 issuance fails and the stack stays down. That is the failure this ticket prevents.
* On the new box: `openssl s_client -connect ps.secuura.net:443 -servername ps.secuura.net </dev/null | openssl x509 -noout -subject` → **CN = [ps.secuura.net](<http://ps.secuura.net>)**, and nginx answers on that `server_name`.
* **A deployment-template contract test** instead of a Playwright spec — **Playwright is the wrong tool here**: the environment this concerns does not exist yet and is not reachable from the suite. Add a case to the existing `DeployTemplateContractTests` in `tests/ssd.UnitTests` asserting that **no tracked file under** `ssd/dep-aws-secuura/` **contains the string** `aws-ps`, and that the four URL keys and `StatusListBaseUrl` name the same host as `deploy-from-ecr.sh`'s `DOMAIN` default. It runs offline in the two-minute xUnit leg and stops the drift coming back; `SeedPasswordContractTests` and `LiveConfigGuard` are the precedents for pinning a template this way.
* An email sent from the new box carries absolute links to `https://ps.secuura.net/…` — the consequence the template keys actually produce.

title: Prod: prove the boot unit restores the stack after a reboot, and confirm the retired Azure Key Vault holds no last-copy secrets before it is deleted
description:
Two operational checks that belong with the production stand-up and have never been done.

## 1. Reboot survival ([PS-788](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-788/dev-ps-does-not-survive-a-vm-restart-the-boot-unit-cannot-read-key)'s shape)

`ssd/dep-aws-secuura/secuura-aws-prod.service` runs `start-services.sh` as `ubuntu` (`Type=oneshot`, no retry), exactly like dev-ps's unit. dev-ps stayed down 17 hours after a VM restart because the unit's user had no CLI session and Docker's `restart: unless-stopped` recreated the shredded config bind-mount as a directory. On AWS the instance role is ambient to every user, so the first defect should not apply — but [PS-788](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-788/dev-ps-does-not-survive-a-vm-restart-the-boot-unit-cannot-read-key) itself says "whether their boot path has ever been exercised is unknown… worth a reboot test". The second defect (config mount → directory) is cloud-independent: `docker-compose.yml` gives the app `restart: unless-stopped` and `start-services.sh` shreds `Docker.appsettings.Development.json` after start.

Work: on the new production box, `sudo reboot`; `/Health/Data` must answer within two minutes with no human involved. If it does not: `journalctl -u secuura-aws-prod`, then apply [PS-788](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-788/dev-ps-does-not-survive-a-vm-restart-the-boot-unit-cannot-read-key)'s fix shape (`restart: "no"` for the app service or `ExecStartPre=docker compose down`, plus a retry) to `dep-aws-secuura` AND `dep-aws-uat` in the same change.

## 2. Retired Azure Key Vault `kv-secuura-prod-sg` ([PS-591](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-591/retired-azure-uatprod-infrastructure-still-exists-and-still-bills-ps))

[PS-591](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-591/retired-azure-uatprod-infrastructure-still-exists-and-still-bills-ps)'s "before deleting anything" list: the two retired Key Vaults "plausibly hold the last copy of some values". Before [PS-591](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-591/retired-azure-uatprod-infrastructure-still-exists-and-still-bills-ps) deletes `secuura-ps` / `kv-secuura-prod-sg`, list its secret NAMES (never values) and confirm each is either present under `/secuura/prod` in Secrets Manager or genuinely dead. Record the name-level comparison here; do not copy any value through a session.

## Verify

Reboot test passes; [PS-591](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-591/retired-azure-uatprod-infrastructure-still-exists-and-still-bills-ps) has the name-level reconciliation attached before deletion.

## Acceptance

**1. Reboot survival — observed, with the state quoted**

* `sudo reboot` on the new production box, then with **no human involvement**: `/Health/Data` answers **200 within two minutes**, `docker ps` shows the app, db and nginx containers **Up**, and the app container's `RestartCount` is **0** once health holds. A single 200 is not enough on its own — a health probe can pass mid-`up` — so confirm a stable uptime and no recreation underneath it.
* `journalctl -u secuura-aws-prod` for the boot window is read and quoted either way. A pass must show the unit **succeeding**, not the stack arriving by some other route.
* If it does not come up, [PS-788](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-788/dev-ps-does-not-survive-a-vm-restart-the-boot-unit-cannot-read-key)'s fix shape is applied to **both** `dep-aws-secuura` **and** `dep-aws-uat` in the same change: `restart: "no"` for the app service (or `ExecStartPre=docker compose down`) so the daemon cannot restart the container ahead of the unit and leave Docker recreating the shredded config bind-mount as a **root-owned directory**, plus a retry so one transient failure does not become dev-ps's 17 hours. The second defect is cloud-independent — it does not depend on the AWS instance role being ambient — so it must be checked even if the unit succeeds.
* **UAT gets the same reboot test**, since [PS-788](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-788/dev-ps-does-not-survive-a-vm-restart-the-boot-unit-cannot-read-key) says that boot path has never been exercised either; the result is recorded here per box.

**2. Retired Key Vault** `kv-secuura-prod-sg`

* A **name-level** comparison is attached to [PS-591](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-591/retired-azure-uatprod-infrastructure-still-exists-and-still-bills-ps) **before** it deletes anything: every secret NAME in the retired vault listed beside either its `/secuura/prod` counterpart in Secrets Manager or an explicit "dead, nothing reads it". **Names only — no value is listed, read, copied or passed through a session.** If a name has no counterpart and is not provably dead, deletion is blocked until it does.
* The comparison is on [PS-591](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-591/retired-azure-uatprod-infrastructure-still-exists-and-still-bills-ps) (as its "before deleting anything" list asks) **and** referenced from here, so the gate is visible from the ticket that would do the deleting.

**No Playwright spec — it is the wrong tool here:** a reboot of an EC2 box and a secret-store reconciliation are not journeys, the production host is not reachable from the suite (port 22 is closed; inspection is read-only through SSM), and no browser assertion can distinguish "the unit brought it up" from "a person did". The verifiable criteria are the post-reboot `docker ps` / `RestartCount` / `/Health/Data` observation with the journal quoted, and the name-level vault reconciliation. The **offline** companion, if the compose change is made, is an xUnit contract case asserting that **no deployment** `docker-compose.yml` **gives the app service a** `restart:` **policy the boot unit does not own** — pinning [PS-788](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-788/dev-ps-does-not-survive-a-vm-restart-the-boot-unit-cannot-read-key)'s second defect so it cannot return to either AWS directory.

nodes.body:
**The reboot question is answered for AWS, on UAT (2026-09-11), and production's unit has the same defect.** First reboot of the rebuilt UAT box: the app did not come back. Not PS-788's first cause — the AWS CLI works as `ubuntu` because the instance role is ambient — but the other two: (1) every deploy runs as root via SSM and leaves `health-allow.conf` root-owned, so the unit running as `ubuntu` died in `setenv.sh` with "Permission denied"; (2) Docker's `restart: unless-stopped` had already recreated the shredded config bind-mount as a root-owned directory and the app exited 127.

Fix on UAT (PR #811 `11e8eb8`): `secuura-aws-uat.service` runs as **root** and does `ExecStartPre=-docker compose down` before `start-services.sh`. Second reboot: app answered within 105 s unattended.

`ssd/dep-aws-secuura/secuura-aws-prod.service` is byte-for-byte the same shape (`User=ubuntu`, no ExecStartPre) — apply the identical change under this ticket, and note prod's `local-nginx.conf` has no `health-allow.conf` include, so defect (1) would surface on a different root-owned file instead.

title: Prod: every existing external login is CIAM (psauthsecuuarademosg) — count the real users and decide how they reach the workforce scheme before cutover
description:
[PS-750](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-750/restore-uat-sign-in-on-develop-ciam-is-retired-in-code-and-uat-cannot) Finding 4 for UAT: all 12 external logins were `LoginProvider = Entra` (CIAM) and seven accounts had no password, so retiring CIAM stranded them. Production has the same structure with **real users**, and nobody has counted them.

The callback re-links by exact email match: `Login.cshtml.cs:525-558` finds the `IdentityUser` by email and `AddLoginAsync` adds an `EntraWorkforce` row beside the existing `Entra` one — so a user whose Microsoft account email equals their platform email carries across on first sign-in; everyone else is stranded unless they hold a password. Production ships no `LocalLogin: "Dev"` (`dep-aws-secuura` template has no such key), so the password form does not render there at all — the bridge UAT used is not available.

## Work

1. Read-only query on the production DB (via SSM, no values copied out): `SELECT LoginProvider, COUNT(*) FROM AspNetUserLogins GROUP BY LoginProvider;` and the list of users with `PasswordHash IS NULL` — the same shape as [PS-750](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-750/restore-uat-sign-in-on-develop-ciam-is-retired-in-code-and-uat-cannot) Finding 4. Record the numbers here.
2. For each password-less CIAM user: does a Microsoft work/personal account exist under the same email? If yes, no action; if no, decide (a) a password reset via the Identity forgot-password flow, (b) an Administrator-provisioned password, or (c) an alternative provider (Google) — with `RequireAdminMfa` in force for admins on live.
3. Keep the `AzureAdCiam` section (`TenantId` still suppresses the old CIAM `tid` as an org signal — `EntraPrefillService.cs:238`); delete the dead `ciam-client-secret` and `entra-s1-secret` fetches (`setenv.sh:106`, `:120`) and their placeholders (template `:64`, `EntraS1-*`) — no C# reads either — and remove both keys from the prod `kv_secrets` map (30-day recovery window on prod).
4. Confirm the workforce registration lists `https://ps.secuura.net/signin-oidc-workforce` before the first production sign-in attempt (sub-issue on AzureAdWorkforce).

## Verify

Every user in the Finding-4-style list has a confirmed route in, and a previously-CIAM user signs in via Microsoft and lands on their existing account (an `EntraWorkforce` login row appears beside the `Entra` one).

## Acceptance

* **The numbers are recorded here before any cutover**, read-only through SSM with nothing copied out: `SELECT LoginProvider, COUNT(*) FROM AspNetUserLogins GROUP BY LoginProvider;` and the count of users with `PasswordHash IS NULL`, in the [PS-750](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-750/restore-uat-sign-in-on-develop-ciam-is-retired-in-code-and-uat-cannot) Finding-4 shape. "All CIAM" is not a finding until it has a count against it.
* **Every password-less CIAM user has a confirmed route in**, listed by **email** (never display name): no action where a Microsoft work/personal account exists under the same email — which is what makes `Login.cshtml.cs`'s exact-email re-link add an `EntraWorkforce` row beside the `Entra` one — and otherwise an explicit choice of forgot-password, an Administrator-provisioned password, or Google. `RequireAdminMfa` is in force for admins on live, so an admin's route must satisfy it.
* It is stated explicitly that **production ships no** `LocalLogin: "Dev"`, so the password form does not render there at all: the bridge UAT used is unavailable, and any plan that assumes it is wrong.
* **Passwords are never printed.** An Administrator-provisioned password is recorded as "provisioned" with the key and store it came from, never as a value, in no comment, script output, ticket or PR.
* The `AzureAdCiam` section **stays** (`TenantId` still suppresses the old CIAM `tid` as an org signal). The two dead REQUIRED fetches `ciam-client-secret` and `entra-s1-secret` and their template placeholders are removed, and both keys are dropped from the prod `kv_secrets` map — noting the 30-day recovery window on prod, so the deletion is reversible within it. A grep over `ssd/**/*.cs` showing no reader is part of the evidence.
* The workforce registration lists `https://ps.secuura.net/signin-oidc-workforce` **before** the first production sign-in attempt ([PS-820](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-820/prod-azureadworkforce-has-no-delivery-path-blank-clientidclientsecret) owns the registration; this ticket owns the ordering).
* A previously-CIAM user signs in via Microsoft and lands on their **existing** account, with an `EntraWorkforce` row appearing beside the `Entra` one — observed, not inferred.
* **No Playwright spec — it is the wrong tool here:** the subject is production's own `AspNetUserLogins` rows and a real Microsoft tenant, neither reachable from the suite, and a slot's database has none of those users. The equivalent **local** mechanism — the exact-email re-link on the external callback — is already covered by the join-seam specs (`external_logins.spec.ts`, `external_join_seam.spec.ts`), so extend those **only** if this work changes the re-link logic; it should not. The verifiable criteria are the recorded counts, the per-user route list, the grep showing no C# reader, and the observed sign-in above.

title: Prod: decide the platform-k target and enable the connector-key tier — CardanoAnchor is off, the connector keys are unlisted in vars.tf, and no K instance is named
description:
Production's platform-k integration is dormant: `ssd/dep-aws-secuura/Docker.appsettings.template.json:294-327` has `CardanoAnchor.Enabled: false`, `DefaultNetwork: "preprod"`, and none of `UseConnectorKeyAuth` / `UsePerVerbEndpoints` / `OrgRegistrationEnabled` (all default `false` in `CardanoAnchorSettings.cs`, so anchors would go out under the retired shared identity if it were switched on). `setenv.sh:156-158` fetches `platform-k-base-url` / `-credential-key` / `-provisioning-key` optionally, but `ssd/aws-docker/aws-secuura-docker/vars.tf:48-55` does not list them, so a tfvars built from the example produces no pairing.

## Decisions needed (Stuart + Kam)

* Which K instance production anchors to (demo-pk is UAT's; Kintsugi is dev-ps's) and on which Cardano network — `DefaultNetwork` drives the explorer link ([PS-504](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-504/s-named-the-wrong-cardano-network-a-hard-coded-preprod-explorer-link)).
* A production provisioning key (`sk_…`, scope `organizations:register`) issued by a K admin (`docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:453-480`: one key per S instance).
* `platform-k-credential-key` (32 chars) — MUST be settled before the first registration; changing it later strands every stored connector key unless `PlatformKCredentialKeyRetired` is set first ([PS-303](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-303/review-g2-per-user-platform-k-credential-storage-platformkaccount)). The templates carry no `__…_RETIRED__` token; add one before any rotation on prod.

## Work

Template: `Enabled: true`, `UseConnectorKeyAuth: true`, `UsePerVerbEndpoints: true`, `OrgRegistrationEnabled: true`, correct `DefaultNetwork` — mirroring UAT `:390-511` with the production values; `vars.tf` + `terraform.tfvars.example` list the three keys; secrets under `/secuura/prod`. `LiveConfigGuard.cs:185-190` refuses plaintext http to K in live mode — the base URL must be https.

## Verify

`/health/anchoring` 200 Healthy on production; one Organisation reaches `Status = Provisioned` with a K-side id; one document's anchor confirmed on the chosen K.

## Acceptance

* **The K instance is named here**, with the decision's author and date — not demo-pk (UAT's) and not Kintsugi (dev-ps's) — together with the Cardano network, since `DefaultNetwork` drives the explorer link and a wrong value produced [PS-504](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-504/s-named-the-wrong-cardano-network-a-hard-coded-preprod-explorer-link).
* The template states `Enabled: true`, `UseConnectorKeyAuth: true`, `UsePerVerbEndpoints: true`, `OrgRegistrationEnabled: true` and the correct `DefaultNetwork`, mirroring UAT's block with production's values. Leaving the three flags unstated means they default `false`, which would send anchors out under the retired shared identity — that is the failure this guards.
* `vars.tf` **and** `terraform.tfvars.example` list all three `platform-k-*` keys that `setenv.sh` already fetches, so a tfvars built from the example produces the pairing instead of silently none. **Key names only — no value on this ticket, in the repo or in any session.**
* A **production provisioning key** (`sk_…`, scope `organizations:register`) is issued by a K admin for this S instance — one key per S instance, per `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`. Recorded as "issued", never quoted.
* `platform-k-credential-key` is **settled before the first registration**. Changing it later strands every stored org connector key unless the outgoing value is listed in `PlatformKCredentialKeyRetired` first ([PS-303](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-303/review-g2-per-user-platform-k-credential-storage-platformkaccount)) — and the templates carry no `__…_RETIRED__` token today, so **add that placeholder now**, before any rotation is possible on prod. The ordering is the criterion: add the retired slot, deploy, then rotate.
* The K base URL is **https** — `LiveConfigGuard` refuses plaintext http to K in live mode.
* On the box: `/health/anchoring` reports **200 Healthy**; one Organisation reaches `Status = Provisioned` with a K-side id; one document's anchor is **confirmed** on the chosen K, with the explorer link resolving on the network named above.
* **xUnit config-contract test rather than a Playwright spec** — **Playwright is the wrong tool here**: the chosen K instance and the production box are not reachable from the suite, and the only local equivalent is slot N's own K. Extend `DeployTemplateContractTests` so that a template with `CardanoAnchor.Enabled: true` **must** state all three of `UseConnectorKeyAuth`, `UsePerVerbEndpoints` and `OrgRegistrationEnabled` (no silent `false` default), must state `DefaultNetwork`, must use an `https` base URL, and must carry the `PlatformKCredentialKeyRetired` placeholder — and that every `platform-k-*` fetch in `setenv.sh` has a matching `vars.tf` entry. Red before the change, green after, in the offline two-minute leg; `SeedPasswordContractTests` and `LiveConfigGuard` are the precedents. The S↔K *behaviour* is already covered locally by the `@k-live` project against slot N's K and needs nothing new here.

nodes.body: Confirmed unchanged at develop `477eb57` (2026-09-29): `ssd/dep-aws-secuura/Docker.appsettings.template.json:295` `Enabled: false`; none of `UseConnectorKeyAuth` / `OrgRegistrationEnabled` / `UsePerVerbEndpoints` stated (all default false); `ssd/aws-docker/aws-secuura-docker/vars.tf` and `terraform.tfvars.example` list no platform-k variables. Production anchors nothing. Two new inputs for the decision: the identity block (PS-870, `AnchorIdentity`) and the v2 verify switch (PS-611, `UseVerifyListV2`) are both off by default and would need stating in the same template when this is picked up.

title: Prod: Entra Verified ID needs its own authority (did:web:ps.secuura.net) in a Secuura-owned tenant, its own registration, and the seven secrets wired
description:
`docs/entra-verified-id-runbook.html` (Tenancy) is explicit: **production gets its own authority in a Secuura-owned tenant** — the DID's signing key is what tells a holder's wallet that the verifier is Secuura, and it must not live in the personal directory (`efc17e5f-…`, sole Global Administrator outside the project) that dev-ps and UAT borrow. Microsoft supports only one authority per tenant ([PS-708](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-708/give-the-dev-ps-entra-tenant-its-own-azure-subscription-and-its-own) comment 2026-09-08), so this cannot share dev-ps's tenant either. [PS-708](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-708/give-the-dev-ps-entra-tenant-its-own-azure-subscription-and-its-own)'s comment says "the production authority needs its own ticket (not created)" — this is that ticket.

Tracked state: `ssd/dep-aws-secuura/Docker.appsettings.template.json:335-345` is blank literals with `Enabled: false`; no `entra-vid-*` fetch in `setenv.sh`.

## Work (person-work first, repo last)

1. A Secuura-owned Entra tenant with an Azure subscription (free account route per `docs/sso-tenant-configuration.md`; do NOT transfer the subscription hosting anything live).
2. Key Vault in it with **Permission model: Vault Access Policy** (RBAC is unsupported by Verified ID), signing key granted `Key: Sign` to the two Verified ID service principals — codify the two access policies in terraform as `az-secuura-DEV-docker/main.tf:278-305` does, or the next plan strips them.
3. Onboard Verified ID: trusted domain `https://ps.secuura.net`, DID `did:web:ps.secuura.net`. Publish `did.json` + `did-configuration.json` via `WellKnownController` — template needs `Identity:WellKnownDocumentsPath: "/ssd-storage/.well-known/"` (dev-ps template `:664`) and the two files dropped on the box's `ssd-storage` bind mount. Confirm `https://ps.secuura.net/.well-known/did.json` resolves publicly (`/.well-known` is excluded from the 404→302 rewrite since [PS-684](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-684/entra-verified-id-azure-tenant-setup-and-config-values-needed-before)).
4. App registration in that tenant with application permission `VerifiableCredential.Create.PresentRequest` (`410607a4-…` on `3db474b9-…`) + admin consent, verified by reading back `appRoleAssignments`; client secret with a rotation schedule.
5. Decide `CredentialType` and `AcceptedIssuers` for production (which issuing tenant's `VerifiedEmployee` is trusted — the dev issuer is Obeden's `2fefc32a-…`).
6. Repo: replace the blank block with the seven `__ENTRA_VID_*__` placeholders (dev-ps template `:607-631`) + optional fetches; secrets under `/secuura/prod`; `entra-vid-callback-api-key` fresh, ≥32 chars.
7. Rollout order (runbook): all seven real → `Enabled: true` → real presentations verified → only then `EnforceSigningVerification: true` ([PS-676](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-676/enabling-entra-verified-id-instantly-hard-blocks-all-document-signing): enabling enforcement blocks signing for every unverified user).

## Verify

A real cross-tenant presentation completes on production and the wallet shows the `ps.secuura.net` verifier identity.

## Acceptance

* A **Secuura-owned** Entra tenant with its own Azure subscription exists and is named here — not the personal directory dev-ps and UAT borrow, and not dev-ps's tenant either (Microsoft supports one authority per tenant). No subscription hosting anything live is transferred.
* Its Key Vault's **Permission model is Vault Access Policy**, not RBAC (Verified ID does not support RBAC), and the signing key grants `Key: Sign` to the two Verified ID service principals. **The two access policies are codified in terraform** — the `az-secuura-DEV-docker/main.tf` pattern — so the next `plan` does not strip them. A hand-made policy that terraform would remove is not acceptance.
* Verified ID is onboarded with trusted domain `https://ps.secuura.net` and DID `did:web:ps.secuura.net`; the template states `Identity:WellKnownDocumentsPath: "/ssd-storage/.well-known/"`, both documents sit on the box's `ssd-storage` bind mount, and `https://ps.secuura.net/.well-known/did.json` **and** `/.well-known/did-configuration.json` **both resolve publicly over HTTPS** — fetched and quoted, since `/.well-known` is excluded from the 404→302 rewrite only since [PS-684](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-684/entra-verified-id-azure-tenant-setup-and-config-values-needed-before).
* The app registration in that tenant holds application permission `VerifiableCredential.Create.PresentRequest` with admin consent, **verified by reading back** `appRoleAssignments` rather than by the portal's green tick. Its client secret has a recorded expiry and a rotation schedule.
* `CredentialType` and `AcceptedIssuers` for production are **decided and written here** — which issuing tenant's `VerifiedEmployee` is trusted. The dev issuer must not be carried over by default.
* Repo: the blank block is replaced by the seven `__ENTRA_VID_*__` placeholders with matching optional fetches and substitute lines; the seven secrets exist under `/secuura/prod`, `entra-vid-callback-api-key` freshly minted at ≥ 32 characters. **Key names only — no value on this ticket, in the repo or in a session.**
* **The rollout order is followed and each step recorded:** all seven real → `Enabled: true` → real presentations verified → **only then** `EnforceSigningVerification: true`. Enabling enforcement early hard-blocks signing for every unverified user ([PS-676](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-676/enabling-entra-verified-id-instantly-hard-blocks-all-document-signing)), so the order is the acceptance, not a suggestion.
* A **real cross-tenant presentation completes on production** and the holder's wallet shows the `ps.secuura.net` verifier identity — the one check that proves the DID's signing key is doing its job.
* **No Playwright spec, deliberately** — it is the wrong tool twice over: the authority and tenant do not exist yet and are not reachable from the suite, and Microsoft refuses the Start POST on every local slot (a `localhost` callback → `BadRequest`, so the row goes `Rejected` at once and only a public-URL environment ever gets a QR). The verifiable criteria are the public `.well-known` fetches, the `appRoleAssignments` read-back, the terraform-codified access policies, and the real presentation above. The **offline** half stays an xUnit config-contract test: extend `DeployTemplateContractTests` so each `__ENTRA_VID_*__` placeholder in the prod template has a matching fetch **and** substitute line, and no template ships `EnforceSigningVerification: true` alongside an unset callback key.

title: Prod: Google OAuth client for ps.secuura.net, plus the Apple/GitHub optional delivery path (external-identity parity, production leg)
description:
[PS-744](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-744/uat-has-no-external-identity-parity-with-dev-ps-google-unconfigured) covers UAT only. Production's `ssd/dep-aws-secuura/Docker.appsettings.template.json` has the Google placeholders (`:105-106`, optional fetches in `setenv.sh:110-111`) but no client behind them, and Apple (`:113-121`) / GitHub (`:129-133`) are bare literals with no fetch — the only way to populate them is hand-editing the file on the box.

## Work

**Google** — new OAuth client (Web application) for production in the same GCP project as dev-ps/UAT, authorised redirect **exactly** `https://ps.secuura.net/signin-google` (`docs/sso-tenant-configuration.md` §6.1); secrets `google-client-id` / `google-client-secret` under `/secuura/prod` via terraform. Consent screen must be **In production** for real users.

**Apple / GitHub** — port dev-ps's optional path: `"Enabled": "__APPLE_ENABLED__"` + four Apple placeholders (`.p8` travels base64 as `apple-private-key-base64`; `substitute_escaped` in `setenv.sh`), `__GITHUB_CLIENT_ID__` / `__GITHUB_CLIENT_SECRET__`; all `fetch_secret_optional`, providers stay dark until a secret exists. Registration of a prod GitHub OAuth App (`https://ps.secuura.net/signin-github`, one app per environment) and Apple Services ID (`https://ps.secuura.net/signin-apple`) are separate decisions — record them here when taken.

Contract tests: `GoogleConfigContractTests`, `AppleConfigContractTests` (no template may ship `Enabled: true`), `GitHubConfigContractTests`, `DeployTemplateContractTests`.

## Verify

`curl -s https://ps.secuura.net/Identity/Account/Login | grep -c 'data-testid="login-google-form"'` → 1; a Workspace sign-in writes `ExternalTenant.Provider = 20` with `TenantKey` = the `hd` domain.

## Acceptance

* **Google.** A production OAuth client (Web application) exists in the same GCP project as dev-ps/UAT with authorised redirect **exactly** `https://ps.secuura.net/signin-google` — read back from the console, not assumed — and its consent screen is **In production**, not Testing. Secrets `google-client-id` / `google-client-secret` exist under `/secuura/prod` via terraform. **Names only: no value on this ticket, in the repo or in a session.**
* **Apple / GitHub delivery path ported from dev-ps**, so the only way to populate them stops being a hand-edit on the box: `"Enabled": "__APPLE_ENABLED__"` plus the four Apple placeholders (the `.p8` travels base64 as `apple-private-key-base64`, substituted with `substitute_escaped`), and `__GITHUB_CLIENT_ID__` / `__GITHUB_CLIENT_SECRET__`. All `fetch_secret_optional`, so each provider stays dark until its secret exists and a missing one never crash-loops the box.
* **No template ships** `Enabled: true` for Apple — the condition `AppleConfigContractTests` already enforces.
* `terraform.tfvars.example` and the `vars.tf` comments list every new key, so a tfvars built from the example produces the pairing.
* The two registration decisions are **recorded here when taken**, not left implicit: a production GitHub OAuth App (`https://ps.secuura.net/signin-github`, one app per environment) and an Apple Services ID (`https://ps.secuura.net/signin-apple`). "Not doing it yet" is an acceptable record; silence is not.
* On the box: `curl -s https://ps.secuura.net/Identity/Account/Login | grep -c 'data-testid="login-google-form"'` → **1**, and a Google Workspace sign-in writes `ExternalTenant.Provider = 20` with `TenantKey` = the `hd` domain.
* **xUnit config-contract tests instead of a Playwright spec** — **Playwright is the wrong tool here**: these clients are registered against `ps.secuura.net`, a host the suite cannot reach, and the provider buttons on a slot are driven by the local stack's own config. The named guards — `GoogleConfigContractTests`, `AppleConfigContractTests`, `GitHubConfigContractTests`, `DeployTemplateContractTests` — must each gain a case covering `dep-aws-secuura`: every `__APPLE_*__` / `__GITHUB_*__` / `__GOOGLE_*__` placeholder has a matching optional fetch **and** substitute line in that directory's `setenv.sh`, and no provider block is left as a bare literal. Red before the change, green after, inside the offline two-minute leg. (The *local* provider-button rendering is already covered by `systemTest/tests/functional/login_providers.spec.ts` — extend that only if the markup changes, which this ticket does not require.)

title: Prod: Identity issuer/data keys have no delivery path — no setenv fetch, blank template values (PS-598 production leg)
description:
[PS-598](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-598/identity-signing-encryption-keys-are-unset-two-live-readiness-blockers) asks for `Identity:IssuerSigningKeyBase64` and `Identity:DataEncryptionKey` in every environment's store. UAT already has the placeholders and optional fetches; production has neither: `ssd/dep-aws-secuura/Docker.appsettings.template.json:367-372` ships both as `""`, and `setenv.sh` fetches no `identity-*` secret at all (22 placeholders, none for identity).

Today `Identity:Enabled` is `false` on prod (`:368`), so `LiveConfigGuard`'s identity checks (`LiveConfigGuard.cs:81-125`, gated on `Identity:Enabled`) do not fire — the box boots. The moment the identity platform is switched on for production, both become live-boot refusals. Provision the path now so that switch is a one-line change.

## Work

* Template: `"IssuerSigningKeyBase64": "__IDENTITY_ISSUER_SIGNING_KEY__"`, `"DataEncryptionKey": "__IDENTITY_DATA_ENCRYPTION_KEY__"` (copy UAT's comment block, `dep-aws-uat` template `:560-574`).
* `setenv.sh`: two `fetch_secret_optional` + two `substitute` lines (UAT `:171-172`, `:250-251`).
* Secrets under `/secuura/prod`: `identity-issuer-signing-key` (32-byte base64 seed — generate with `/identity/genkey` as an Administrator on a `ShowDevTools: true` environment such as UAT; it is never persisted or logged) and `identity-data-encryption-key` (32-char AES, must differ from `doc-storage-key`, `LiveConfigGuard.cs:125`). Prod, UAT and dev must not share values.
* Decide separately whether production turns `Identity:Enabled` on; `ShareAssuranceTemplateContractTests` then requires `MinShareAssuranceLevel` stated.

## Verify

With Identity enabled on a prod-shaped config, `/Health/Data` preflight is empty; `IssuerDid` survives a `start-services.sh` restart.

## Acceptance

* `ssd/dep-aws-secuura/Docker.appsettings.template.json` states `"IssuerSigningKeyBase64": "__IDENTITY_ISSUER_SIGNING_KEY__"` and `"DataEncryptionKey": "__IDENTITY_DATA_ENCRYPTION_KEY__"` in place of the two `""` literals, carrying UAT's comment block across, and `setenv.sh` has the two `fetch_secret_optional` calls plus their two `substitute` lines — matching the UAT pattern exactly, so the prod file stops being the only one with no delivery path at all. **Key names and placeholder tokens only; no value on this ticket, in the repo or in a session.**
* Both secrets exist under `/secuura/prod` by the names `identity-issuer-signing-key` and `identity-data-encryption-key`, **minted by a person**: the issuer key a 32-byte base64 seed generated with `/identity/genkey` as an Administrator on a `ShowDevTools: true` environment such as UAT (it is never persisted or logged), the data key a 32-character AES key that **differs from** `doc-storage-key` — the condition `LiveConfigGuard` checks. Prod, UAT and dev must not share values; recorded here as "minted, distinct, shape confirmed".
* **Optional, not required, is deliberate and stays that way** while `Identity:Enabled` is `false` on prod: an optional fetch leaves the box bootable today, and the keys are in place for the moment the switch is flipped. Say so in the section comment so the next reader does not "fix" it to REQUIRED.
* Whether production turns `Identity:Enabled` on is **decided and recorded here as a separate line**, with its consequence noted: `ShareAssuranceTemplateContractTests` then requires `MinShareAssuranceLevel` to be stated in the same template.
* With a prod-shaped config and Identity **enabled**, `/Health/Data`'s Live-readiness preflight is **empty** — neither identity key appears — and `IssuerDid` survives a `start-services.sh` restart (the key is re-fetched, not regenerated).
* **xUnit config-contract test instead of a Playwright spec** — **Playwright is the wrong tool here**: the keys are consumed at boot on a box the suite cannot reach, and with `Identity:Enabled` false there is no surface to drive. Extend `DeployTemplateContractTests` so that for **every** deployment directory, each `__IDENTITY_*__` placeholder in the template has a matching fetch **and** substitute line in that directory's `setenv.sh`, and no template ships either identity key as a bare `""` while stating an `Identity` section — red for `dep-aws-secuura` before the change, green after, in the offline two-minute leg. `SeedPasswordContractTests` and `LiveConfigGuard` are the precedents.

title: Prod: AppSpecific:SigningKeyEncryptionKey is stated nowhere — LiveConfigGuard refuses a live boot, and PS-607's rotation cannot run until it exists
description:
`AppSpecific:SigningKeyEncryptionKey` appears in no deployment template and no `setenv.sh`. `ssd/Services/Security/LiveConfigGuard.cs:145-174` treats that as a live-mode violation (since `69d1586`, [PS-607](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-607/rotate-existing-personal-signing-certificates-onto-the-isolated-key)'s guard), so a `DeployMode: "live"` boot is refused. Unlike UAT this is a hard stop on production. And because the rendered template is mounted ONTO `/app/appsettings.json`, unstated means null → `SigningKeyProtector` falls back to `TemplateStorageKey`, which is the [PS-196](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-196/isolate-signing-key-encryption-from-the-document-key-kms-aes-gcm-kdf) inversion on real signing material.

## Work

* Template: add `"SigningKeyEncryptionKey": "__SIGNING_KEY_ENCRYPTION_KEY__"` beside `TokenSignKey` (token name already used by `tests/ssd.UnitTests/LiveConfigGuardTests.cs:222`).
* `setenv.sh`: `fetch_secret "signing-key-encryption-key"` (REQUIRED) + substitute.
* Secret `/secuura/prod/signing-key-encryption-key`: 16/24/32 printable chars, no `"`/`\`/newline, and it MUST differ from `doc-storage-key` and `template-storage-key` (`LiveConfigGuard.cs:166-174`). Minted by a person, never in a session.
* `terraform.tfvars.example` / `vars.tf` comment updated.

**Then** [PS-607](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-607/rotate-existing-personal-signing-certificates-onto-the-isolated-key)'s actual sweep over production's `PersonCertificate` rows — after a table backup, on a build ≥ `3bf4fc7` ([PS-605](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-605/signing-key-decryption-can-return-garbage-instead-of-failing-key-ring)), and only once this key is confirmed set (precondition 3 of [PS-607](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-607/rotate-existing-personal-signing-certificates-onto-the-isolated-key); otherwise the sweep re-encrypts irreplaceable material under the key it is moving away from).

## Verify

`/Health/Data` Live-readiness preflight shows no `SigningKeyEncryptionKey` line; after the sweep no `PersonCertificate` row opens with `TemplateStorageKey` alone.

## Acceptance

* `ssd/dep-aws-secuura/Docker.appsettings.template.json` states `"SigningKeyEncryptionKey": "__SIGNING_KEY_ENCRYPTION_KEY__"` beside `TokenSignKey`, and `setenv.sh` has a **REQUIRED** `fetch_secret "signing-key-encryption-key"` plus its `substitute` line. **The key name only — no value appears on this ticket, in the repo, in a script's output or in any session.**
* The secret `/secuura/prod/signing-key-encryption-key` exists, **minted by a person**, and satisfies the shape `LiveConfigGuard` requires: 16, 24 or 32 printable characters, no `"`, no backslash, no newline, and **different from** `doc-storage-key` and `template-storage-key`. Recorded here as "minted, shape confirmed" — never as the value.
* `terraform.tfvars.example` and the `vars.tf` comment list the key, so a tfvars built from the example produces the pairing.
* `/Health/Data`'s Live-readiness preflight on production shows **no** `SigningKeyEncryptionKey` line — i.e. a `DeployMode: "live"` boot is no longer refused for this reason.
* `SigningKeyProtector` no longer falls back to `TemplateStorageKey` on the write path, so [PS-196](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-196/isolate-signing-key-encryption-from-the-document-key-kms-aes-gcm-kdf)'s isolation (one config compromise cannot unlock documents *and* recover every signing key) actually holds in production rather than in no environment.
* [PS-607](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-607/rotate-existing-personal-signing-certificates-onto-the-isolated-key)**'s rotation sweep is explicitly blocked until the above is confirmed** — run before the key is provisioned and stated, it re-encrypts irreplaceable `PersonCertificate` material under the key it is meant to move away from. Preconditions, all three: this key confirmed set, a `PersonCertificate` table backup taken, and a build ≥ `3bf4fc7` ([PS-605](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-605/signing-key-decryption-can-return-garbage-instead-of-failing-key-ring)). After the sweep, no `PersonCertificate` row opens with `TemplateStorageKey` alone.
* **xUnit config-contract test rather than a Playwright spec** — **Playwright is the wrong tool here**: this is a boot-time guard on a box the suite cannot reach, and there is no page to drive. `tests/ssd.UnitTests/LiveConfigGuardTests.cs` already names the `__SIGNING_KEY_ENCRYPTION_KEY__` token; add a case asserting that **every deployment template running a non-**`dev` `DeployMode` **states the key** and that its placeholder has a REQUIRED fetch **and** a substitute line in that directory's `setenv.sh` — the `SeedPasswordContractTests` pattern, red before the change, green after, inside the offline two-minute leg.

title: Prod: AzureAdWorkforce has no delivery path — blank ClientId/ClientSecret, no setenv fetch, so a develop image throws on boot
description:
`ssd/dep-aws-secuura/Docker.appsettings.template.json:88-89` ships `"ClientId": ""`, `"ClientSecret": ""` as bare literals; `ssd/dep-aws-secuura/setenv.sh` fetches nothing for the workforce scheme. `ssd/Startup.cs:133-143` throws `InvalidOperationException` on a blank/`{`/`__` ClientId, and since [PS-588](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-588/e483-workforce-only-retire-the-ciam-scheme-entirely) the workforce scheme is the only sign-in. Same defect [PS-750](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-750/restore-uat-sign-in-on-develop-ciam-is-retired-in-code-and-uat-cannot) fixes for UAT.

## Work

**Repo (**`dep-aws-secuura`**)**

* Template: `__AZUREAD_WORKFORCE_CLIENT_ID__` / `__AZUREAD_WORKFORCE_CLIENT_SECRET__` in place of the literals; rewrite the section comment.
* `setenv.sh`: `fetch_secret` (REQUIRED, not optional — a required fetch fails before `docker compose up --force-recreate`, leaving the previous container running; an optional one replaces a working app with a crash loop) + two `substitute` lines. `DeployTemplateContractTests` enforces the pairing.
* Keep the `AzureAdCiam` section (`TenantId` read by `EntraPrefillService.cs:238`, `Instance` by `OutlookManifestBuilder.cs:253`).
* `aws-secuura-docker/terraform.tfvars.example` + `vars.tf` comment: add both keys.

**Azure** (registration shared with dev-ps and UAT, in the workforce tenant — confirm which in the portal)

* Authentication → Web → add `https://ps.secuura.net/signin-oidc-workforce` and `https://ps.secuura.net/signout-callback-oidc-workforce` (`docs/sso-tenant-configuration.md:290-302` already lists them).
* Certificates & secrets → new secret labelled "prod". Record the expiry.
* Confirm `signInAudience: AzureADandPersonalMicrosoftAccount` and `xms_edov` in `optionalClaims.idToken`.

**AWS**: `azuread-workforce-client-id` (public GUID, same as dev-ps/UAT) + `azuread-workforce-client-secret` under `/secuura/prod` via terraform.

## Verify

`az ad app show --id <clientId> --query '{aud:signInAudience,uris:web.redirectUris}'` lists both prod URIs; a develop image starts on the prod box; a workforce sign-in from an EXTERNAL tenant writes `ExternalTenant.Provider = 10`.

## Acceptance

* `ssd/dep-aws-secuura/Docker.appsettings.template.json` states `__AZUREAD_WORKFORCE_CLIENT_ID__` / `__AZUREAD_WORKFORCE_CLIENT_SECRET__` in place of the two bare `""` literals, and the section comment is rewritten to say where the values come from. **Keys and placeholder tokens only — no value is recorded on this ticket, in the repo, or in any session.**
* `ssd/dep-aws-secuura/setenv.sh` has a **REQUIRED** `fetch_secret` for each (not optional) plus the two `substitute` lines. Required is the point: a required fetch fails *before* `docker compose up --force-recreate`, leaving the previous container running, whereas an optional one replaces a working app with a crash loop.
* The `AzureAdCiam` section stays — `TenantId` is still read by `EntraPrefillService` and `Instance` by `OutlookManifestBuilder`.
* `aws-secuura-docker/terraform.tfvars.example` and the `vars.tf` comment list both keys, so a tfvars built from the example produces the pairing.
* The two secret names exist under `/secuura/prod` (`azuread-workforce-client-id`, `azuread-workforce-client-secret`) via terraform, minted by a person. The client id is a public GUID; the secret's **expiry date** is recorded here, since nothing else will remind anyone.
* Azure, read back rather than assumed: `az ad app show --id <clientId> --query '{aud:signInAudience,uris:web.redirectUris}'` lists **both** `https://ps.secuura.net/signin-oidc-workforce` and `https://ps.secuura.net/signout-callback-oidc-workforce`, `signInAudience` is `AzureADandPersonalMicrosoftAccount`, and `xms_edov` is present in `optionalClaims.idToken`.
* **The repo-side criterion is an xUnit config-contract test, not a Playwright spec** — **Playwright is the wrong tool here**: the production box and its secret store are not reachable from the suite, and the scheme throws at *startup*, before any page exists to drive. `DeployTemplateContractTests` already enforces placeholder↔fetch pairing; extend it so the prod template is covered explicitly: every `__AZUREAD_WORKFORCE_*__` token has a REQUIRED fetch **and** a substitute line, and **no deployment template ships a blank or** `{`**-prefixed** `AzureAdWorkforce:ClientId` — the exact condition `ssd/Startup.cs` throws on. Red before the change, green after, in the two-minute offline leg (`SeedPasswordContractTests` / `LiveConfigGuard` are the precedents).
* On the box: a `develop` image **starts** (no `InvalidOperationException` in the container log) and `/Health/Data` answers 200; a workforce sign-in from an **external** tenant writes `ExternalTenant.Provider = 10`.

title: Production cannot boot or sign in on develop: SSO, secrets and config work needed before a develop image goes to ps.secuura.net
description:
## Why this exists

The UAT stand-up plan ([PS-750](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-750/restore-uat-sign-in-on-develop-ciam-is-retired-in-code-and-uat-cannot) branch, 2026-09-10) deliberately excludes production, as [PS-744](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-744/uat-has-no-external-identity-parity-with-dev-ps-google-unconfigured) did. This is the production counterpart: one place holding every item that has to be true before a `develop` image can run at `ps.secuura.net`. Each sub-issue is a self-contained piece of work; this parent carries the sequence and the decisions.

Production today runs `secuura:secuura-latest` from `release/production-Apr-4-26` (`prod-d19e26d`), signs in through the retired CIAM tenant `psauthsecuuarademosg`, and is on the box Stuart said on 2026-09-02 is being replaced. **The replacement inherits whatever** `ssd/dep-aws-secuura/` **says in git — and what it says today does not boot.**

Re-verified against `develop` at `27849f9` on 2026-09-10:

| \# | Finding | Evidence |
| -- | -- | -- |
| 1 | **A develop image throws at startup.** `AzureAdWorkforce:ClientId` is `""` and there is no placeholder and no `setenv.sh` fetch | `ssd/dep-aws-secuura/Docker.appsettings.template.json:88-89`; `ssd/Startup.cs:133-143` throws `InvalidOperationException` on blank / `{` / `__` |
| 2 | **A live boot is refused for a second reason:** `AppSpecific:SigningKeyEncryptionKey` is stated nowhere and `LiveConfigGuard` treats that as a live-mode violation since `69d1586` | `ssd/Services/Security/LiveConfigGuard.cs:145-174`; no `__SIGNING_KEY_ENCRYPTION_KEY__` in any template |
| 3 | The tracked prod config still names the **cutover hostname** `aws-ps.secuura.net`; a fresh box would issue its Let's Encrypt cert and set `server_name` for the wrong host | `Docker.appsettings.template.json:277-280`, `deploy-from-ecr.sh:38`, `local-nginx.conf:47,56,59-60` |
| 4 | Identity keys have **no delivery path at all** on prod (UAT at least has the placeholders): `setenv.sh` fetches neither `identity-issuer-signing-key` nor `identity-data-encryption-key`; template ships `""` | `Docker.appsettings.template.json:367-372`; `setenv.sh` fetch list (22 placeholders, no identity pair) |
| 5 | Entra Verified ID is blank literals with `Enabled: false`; production needs **its own authority in a Secuura-owned tenant**, which does not exist | `Docker.appsettings.template.json:335-345`; `docs/entra-verified-id-runbook.html` Tenancy; [PS-708](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-708/give-the-dev-ps-entra-tenant-its-own-azure-subscription-and-its-own) comment 2026-09-08 ("production authority needs its own ticket (not created)") |
| 6 | Two dead secrets are still REQUIRED fetches (`ciam-client-secret`, `entra-s1-secret`); no C# reads either | `setenv.sh:106,:120`; grep of `ssd/**/*.cs` |
| 7 | Google is wired but unconfigured; Apple/GitHub have no delivery path | template `:105-106` placeholders present; `:113-121`, `:129-133` blank literals |
| 8 | platform-k on prod is off (`CardanoAnchor.Enabled: false`, no `UseConnectorKeyAuth`/`UsePerVerbEndpoints`/`OrgRegistrationEnabled` keys) and `vars.tf` does not list the three `platform-k-*` secrets `setenv.sh` fetches | template `:294-327`; `ssd/aws-docker/aws-secuura-docker/vars.tf:48-55` vs `setenv.sh:156-158` |
| 9 | Every existing production external login is CIAM (`LoginProvider = Entra`); the same migration question as [PS-750](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-750/restore-uat-sign-in-on-develop-ciam-is-retired-in-code-and-uat-cannot) Finding 4 applies, with real users | to be counted read-only on the prod DB before any cutover |

## Suggested order

1. Repo, once the UAT PR ([PS-750](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-750/restore-uat-sign-in-on-develop-ciam-is-retired-in-code-and-uat-cannot)) lands — port the `dep-aws-uat` delivery-path changes to `dep-aws-secuura`: [PS-820](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-820/prod-azureadworkforce-has-no-delivery-path-blank-clientidclientsecret) (workforce, boot blocker), [PS-821](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-821/prod-appspecificsigningkeyencryptionkey-is-stated-nowhere) (`SigningKeyEncryptionKey`, live-boot blocker), [PS-822](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-822/prod-identity-issuerdata-keys-have-no-delivery-path-no-setenv-fetch) (Identity pair), [PS-823](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-823/prod-google-oauth-client-for-pssecuuranet-plus-the-applegithub) (Apple/GitHub path), [PS-828](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-828/prod-tracked-config-still-names-the-cutover-host-aws-pssecuuranet-a) (`aws-ps` hostnames), and the dead-secret removal in [PS-826](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-826/prod-every-existing-external-login-is-ciam-psauthsecuuarademosg-count).
2. Azure / Google / AWS person-work: [PS-820](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-820/prod-azureadworkforce-has-no-delivery-path-blank-clientidclientsecret) (prod redirect URIs + prod-labelled secret), [PS-823](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-823/prod-google-oauth-client-for-pssecuuranet-plus-the-applegithub) (prod Google OAuth client), then one terraform apply of the new `/secuura/prod` keys (`aws-secuura-docker`, `recovery_window_in_days = 30`) covering [PS-820](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-820/prod-azureadworkforce-has-no-delivery-path-blank-clientidclientsecret)/821/822/823.
3. [PS-824](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-824/prod-entra-verified-id-needs-its-own-authority-didwebpssecuuranet-in-a) — Verified ID production authority in a Secuura-owned tenant. The long pole; proceeds in parallel with everything above.
4. [PS-825](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-825/prod-decide-the-platform-k-target-and-enable-the-connector-key-tier) — decide production's platform-k target with Kam and enable the connector tier.
5. [PS-826](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-826/prod-every-existing-external-login-is-ciam-psauthsecuuarademosg-count) — count the CIAM users and settle their route in BEFORE cutover; [PS-827](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-827/prod-prove-the-boot-unit-restores-the-stack-after-a-reboot-and-confirm) — reboot-survival test on the new box and the retired Key Vault name-level reconciliation ([PS-591](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-591/retired-azure-uatprod-infrastructure-still-exists-and-still-bills-ps)).

Sub-issues: [PS-820](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-820/prod-azureadworkforce-has-no-delivery-path-blank-clientidclientsecret), [PS-821](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-821/prod-appspecificsigningkeyencryptionkey-is-stated-nowhere), [PS-822](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-822/prod-identity-issuerdata-keys-have-no-delivery-path-no-setenv-fetch), [PS-823](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-823/prod-google-oauth-client-for-pssecuuranet-plus-the-applegithub), [PS-824](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-824/prod-entra-verified-id-needs-its-own-authority-didwebpssecuuranet-in-a), [PS-825](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-825/prod-decide-the-platform-k-target-and-enable-the-connector-key-tier), [PS-826](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-826/prod-every-existing-external-login-is-ciam-psauthsecuuarademosg-count), [PS-827](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-827/prod-prove-the-boot-unit-restores-the-stack-after-a-reboot-and-confirm), [PS-828](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-828/prod-tracked-config-still-names-the-cutover-host-aws-pssecuuranet-a).

## Done when

`/Health/Data` on production reports an **empty** Live-readiness preflight on a `develop` image, a workforce sign-in from an external tenant completes, and the cert and `server_name` are for `ps.secuura.net`.

## Deliberately out of scope here

The production box replacement itself, its data migration (`ssd/aws-docker/MIGRATION.md`) and the MySQL 8.0 → 8.4 pin — Stuart ruled on 2026-09-02 that those are not work items; the replacement inherits the branch's pins. This issue is about what the branch must say so that replacement can boot.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](<https://claude.com/claude-code>)

## Acceptance

This is the parent: it is accepted when the nine findings are each either closed by their sub-issue or recorded here as deliberately not done, with a reason. Specifically:

* **Each of the nine findings is re-verified against the then-current** `develop` **before cutover**, not against the 2026-09-10 `27849f9` reading — the branch has moved since, and a finding that fixed itself must be recorded as such rather than carried.
* **The two boot blockers are provably gone:** `/Health/Data` on production reports an **empty** Live-readiness preflight on a `develop` image ([PS-820](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-820/prod-azureadworkforce-has-no-delivery-path-blank-clientidclientsecret)'s `AzureAdWorkforce:ClientId`, [PS-821](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-821/prod-appspecificsigningkeyencryptionkey-is-stated-nowhere)'s `SigningKeyEncryptionKey`), and the container log shows no `InvalidOperationException` at startup.
* **A workforce sign-in from an external tenant completes** on `ps.secuura.net`, and the cert's CN and nginx's `server_name` are both `ps.secuura.net` ([PS-828](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-828/prod-tracked-config-still-names-the-cutover-host-aws-pssecuuranet-a)).
* **The suggested order is followed, and departures from it are recorded here** — repo ports first ([PS-820](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-820/prod-azureadworkforce-has-no-delivery-path-blank-clientidclientsecret)/821/822/823/828 + [PS-826](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-826/prod-every-existing-external-login-is-ciam-psauthsecuuarademosg-count)'s dead-secret removal), then the Azure/Google/AWS person-work and one terraform apply of the new `/secuura/prod` keys, then [PS-824](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-824/prod-entra-verified-id-needs-its-own-authority-didwebpssecuuranet-in-a) (the long pole, in parallel), [PS-825](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-825/prod-decide-the-platform-k-target-and-enable-the-connector-key-tier), and [PS-826](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-826/prod-every-existing-external-login-is-ciam-psauthsecuuarademosg-count)/827 **before** cutover. [PS-826](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-826/prod-every-existing-external-login-is-ciam-psauthsecuuarademosg-count) in particular gates the cutover: real users with no route in is the one failure here that cannot be rolled back.
* **No secret value ever appears** on this ticket, on any sub-issue, in the repo, in a script's output or in a session — key names and store paths only. This epic is almost entirely about secret *delivery*, which makes that the standing rule rather than a footnote.
* **No Playwright spec, deliberately** — it is the wrong tool for every finding here: these are deployment templates, secret delivery, an OAuth registration, a TLS hostname and a boot unit on a box the suite cannot reach, and two of them fail at *startup*, before a page exists. The offline half is carried by the sub-issues' xUnit config-contract tests (`DeployTemplateContractTests`, `LiveConfigGuardTests`, `SeedPasswordContractTests`, the provider config guards), which is what makes the repo side of this epic checkable in the two-minute offline leg rather than only on the box. The live half is the `/Health/Data` preflight, the cert read-back and the sign-in above.
* `ssd/aws-docker/MIGRATION.md`'s own sequence is reconciled with what was actually done, so the next box inherits a document that matches reality — the box replacement itself and the MySQL pin stay out of scope per Stuart's 2026-09-02 ruling.

title: run-shell-suites.sh restores git discovery but does not isolate suites: a suite that runs git from its cwd writes the repository it runs in (KS-1086 QA-6)
description:
## BLUF

* **The boundary.** KS-1086's fix (PR #953) clears the hook's repository-local git variables before the shell suites run. A suite's `git` calls then fall back to normal discovery. That restores discovery; it does not isolate.
* **The consequence.** A suite that runs `git` from its working directory, without first moving into a temp repo of its own, still writes to whichever repository it started in. Under a push, that is the pushing repository.
* **Today, no current suite does this.** All 18 ran under the fixed runner from a linked worktree, and the shared config, refs and HEADs came out identical. This is a boundary for a future suite, not a live defect.

## Recommendation

Low priority. Decide whether the runner should enforce isolation, or whether the fixture convention is enough.

The gate named two fix shapes:

* run each suite with its cwd in a fresh temp dir;
* or have the runner snapshot its own repo's config, refs and HEADs around the loop, and fail loudly on any change.

The second overlaps KS-948's proposed runner-level check that a suite run left nothing behind, so one change could close both. This is filing only; nothing is scheduled.

## Detail

**Source.** Tier-1 QA gate on PR #953 @ `de1ab62c0`, finding QA-6 (Observation), arm M3. MEASURED in scratch repositories.

* The suite was `git config qa.cwdplant 1` with no `cd`, run under the head runner from a linked worktree.
* It saw `GIT_DIR=unset`, with a cwd of `<worktree>/Blockchain/Dev`.
* The shared config gained `[qa] cwdplant = 1`.

**Current suites.** Gate arm F2 ran all 18 real suites under the head runner from a linked worktree. Shared config, refs, main HEAD and worktree HEADs were IDENTICAL.

**Scope, reasoned from the mechanism and NOT run:** the same would happen from a normal clone, and from a manual `npm run test:shell`.

**Where.** `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/run-shell-suites.sh`, in the suite loop (`bash "$REPO_ROOT/$rel"`). Each suite starts in the runner's own cwd.

**Board searched before filing.** The issue columns search title and description, archived included; the comment column searches comment bodies.

| term | issues | comments on |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `run-shell-suites` | KS-1086, KS-1046, KS-948, KS-926, KS-910, KS-903 | KS-1027, KS-1086, KS-909, KS-926, KS-936, KS-945, KS-948 |
| `run_shell_suites` | KS-1086, KS-971 | KS-1086, KS-731 |
| `git_local_env` | 0 | 0 |
| `local-env-vars` | 0 | 0 |
| `suite isolation` | 0 | 0 |
| `temp dir` | PS-529 | KS-1027, KS-682 |
| control: `leg 14` | KS-1086 | KS-1086, KS-485, KS-731, KS-772, KS-926 |

None of them covers a suite writing the repository it runs in through a cwd-relative `git` call. Two are adjacent but do not cover it:

* **KS-948:** a backtick in a case name executes as a command. Its fix shape includes a runner-level left-nothing-behind check.
* **KS-903:** a survey of repo-root derivations, including the env-dependent ones.

**Report.** `/Volumes/DevMASTER/!CODING/Testing Agent MAIN/projects/secuura/reports/2026-09-11-ks1086-953-de1ab62c0-tier1/report.md`

title: workflow-approve deletes the pending document and answers 200 "Document has been created" without reading originate's response — a refused forward (401, measured) loses the document
description:
## BLUF

* **Approving the last step of a workflow can silently lose the document.** `POST /api/workflow-instances/:id/approve` forwards the pending document to originate, deletes it from Redis without reading originate's response, and answers **200** `approved`**, "All workflow steps approved. Document has been created."**
* **Measured** by the QA agent's round-2 tier-1 gate on #951 (`02a22f4bb`, 2026-09-11):
  * the recorded forward (`x-user-id` only, no bearer) replayed into the real originate app gets **401**, with the gateway vouch secret unset and set alike;
  * with originate answering 401, the real gateway handler still returns **200** `approved` and **deletes the pending document**.
* **Pre-existing, not #951.** The same code is on develop `2d864ae92`.
* **NOT established: whether any environment has workflow-gated document types.** Reachability for real users is unknown. The gate assessed severity as Major; priority is left for the humans.

## Recommendation

1. Report approval and delete the pending document **only after originate returns 2xx**. On any other status, or a network error, keep the pending document and return an error to the caller.
2. Forward a credential originate accepts. Today the forward carries `x-user-id` alone, and originate answers 401.
3. Regression test: an originate stub returning 401 must not yield 200 `approved`, and the pending document must survive. Add the same cell for a network error.
4. If `GATEWAY_VOUCH_SECRET` is ever provisioned, this forward is also on KS-1083's vouch precondition list.

## Detail

**Code on develop** `2d864ae92`**,** `Blockchain/Dev/services/api-gateway/src/routes/verification.ts` (at `02a22f4bb`: route `:700`, `x-user-id` `:783`, `http.request` `:785`):

* `:781` `router.post('/api/workflow-instances/:id/approve', authenticateToken(true), …)`
* `:860-864` forward headers: `Content-Type`, `Content-Length`, and `x-user-id` from `pendingDoc.createdBy`. No `Authorization`, no `x-tenant-id`.
* `:866` `http.request` to originate `/api/documents`. The response callback only logs "Workflow approved — document forwarded to originate" on `end` (`:871`), whatever the status.
* `:880` `proxyReq.end()`, then `:881` `await redisService.deletePendingDocument(documentId)`, before any response has been read.
* `:889` the 200 body: `status: 'approved'`, `message: 'All workflow steps approved. Document has been created.'`

**Consequence by case:**

| originate outcome | pending document | caller is told | evidence |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| 401 | deleted | 200 approved, "created" | MEASURED (gate P2, F2b) |
| other 4xx / 5xx | deleted | 200 approved, "created" | READ |
| network error | deleted; "Failed to forward" logged | 200 approved, "created" | READ, not driven |

**Correction carried here:** KS-1084's body says this forward sends `x-user-id` / `x-tenant-id`. It sends `x-user-id` only (`:864`). A dated correction comment is on KS-1084.

**Board searched before filing** (team KS, archived included; titles, descriptions and comments):

* `/api/workflow-instances/:id/approve` → 0 issues, 0 comments
* `/api/workflows/:workflowId/approve` → 0, 0
* `workflow-approve` → KS-1083 and KS-1084, which name only this forward's vouch/tenant shape, not the lost document
* `workflow approve`, `workflowApprove`, `pending document`, `pendingDocument`, `approved and deletes` → 0 each
* `verification.ts:8` → KS-1083 and KS-501 (Done, an unrelated crash)
* controls: `verification.ts` → 33 issues; a nonsense term → 0

**NOT tested:** a live stack; any environment's workflow configuration; the sibling route `POST /api/workflows/:workflowId/approve` (`:943`), which was not examined.

**Source:** `Testing Agent MAIN/projects/secuura/reports/2026-09-11-ks1041-951-02a22f4bb-tier1-r2/report.md`, section "Open", O-1. Filed by Platform K seat s177 on Wednesday's brief; the QA agent cannot post.
