**BLUF:** Control added to my 06:11Z reach record (comment `f64a0a45`, not an edit): a count-only `SCAN MATCH *`, paged to the end, returns exactly the DBSIZE on both servers, so the scan enumerates on the real servers and the 0 keys under `secuura:gateway:*` (and the 0 doc-type and workflow keys) is a measured zero. It stays a zero at read time: keys under this prefix have a 3,600 s TTL, and the seed writes them only when `GET /api/admin/document-types` runs with demo seeding on.

- **kintsugi**, read 2026-11-05 06:16:55Z, `secuura-api-gateway` image `3466d93a4808` (REVISION head `5fc5569ed96ac61f64823cc9e1fa841899aa1f62`): DBSIZE 8, `SCAN MATCH *` distinct keys 8 (1 page, cursor finished), equal; keys under `secuura:gateway:*` were 0 at 06:10:31Z.
- **demo**, read 2026-11-05 06:16:59Z, `secuura-api-gateway` image `0bea5f7cb66e` (REVISION head `07a2d62be6a09c9cd504864d1cf1906543d55317`): DBSIZE 7, `SCAN MATCH *` distinct keys 7 (1 page, cursor finished), equal; keys under `secuura:gateway:*` were 0 at 06:10:34Z.

The no-password connection answered NOAUTH again on both. Only counts left the container: no key name, value or TTL was read. Reads only; nothing was written on either box. Everything under "Not measured" in `f64a0a45` still applies (stores other than the gateway's Redis, lapsed keys, whether the seed ever ran). Raw output: `5_Project_History/2026-11-05_seatU-14th/evidence/gwscanall_kintsugi_raw.txt` and `gwscanall_demo_raw.txt`.

**BLUF:** The read-only measurement Kam's card `secuura-ks1087-workflow-approve-credential-1102` (option b) asks for is made: **0 workflow-gated document types on kintsugi and 0 on demo, at 2026-11-05 06:07 to 06:10Z.** The gateway's Redis held no `secuura:gateway:doctype:*` and no `secuura:gateway:wf:*` key on either box. The server is not empty (DBSIZE 8 on kintsugi, 7 on demo) but holds 0 keys under `secuura:gateway:*` on both, so this zero is "no keys at read time", not "no workflow-gated types ever": the catalogue is written only when `GET /api/admin/document-types` runs with demo seeding on, and each key lives 3,600 seconds. Nothing is built or ruled here; item 2 stays unbuilt, as the card says.

**Reach in one line:** 0 gated types on kintsugi, 0 on demo, at 2026-11-05 06:07 to 06:10Z.

| | kintsugi | demo |
| -- | -- | -- |
| REVISION head (the ref) | `5fc5569ed96ac61f64823cc9e1fa841899aa1f62` | `07a2d62be6a09c9cd504864d1cf1906543d55317` |
| container, image id | `secuura-api-gateway`, `3466d93a4808` | `secuura-api-gateway`, `0bea5f7cb66e` |
| StartedAt | `2026-11-05T01:41:24Z` | `2026-11-04T23:48:07Z` |
| read at | 06:07:19Z, control 06:10:31Z | 06:07:33Z, control 06:10:34Z |
| DBSIZE | 8 | 7 |
| keys under `secuura:gateway:*` | 0 | 0 |
| `secuura:gateway:doctype:*` keys | 0 | 0 |
| `secuura:gateway:wf:*` keys | 0 | 0 |
| gated types (`requiresApproval` true and a workflow id) | 0 | 0 |
| approver roles named | none to read | none to read |
| TTL min and max of the doc-type and workflow keys | n/a (no keys) | n/a (no keys) |

**Where the store is (code read at develop `5fc5569ed96a`):**
- Document types and workflows are Redis keys `secuura:gateway:doctype:<id>` and `secuura:gateway:wf:<id>` (`api-gateway/src/services/redis.ts`: prefix constant `secuura:gateway:` at line 18, key builders at 515 and 230), each set with a 3,600 s TTL.
- A type counts as gated only when `requiresApproval === true` and `approvalWorkflowId` is truthy (`services/enforcement.ts:215-216`).
- The three seed types with `requiresApproval: true` (workflows `wf-1`, `wf-2`, `wf-4`, in `routes/admin.ts`) are written by `seedDocumentTypesIfEmpty` only when the catalogue is empty and demo seeding is enabled, and only when `GET /api/admin/document-types` is called.
- No SQL table holds document types in `api-gateway/src` or `Blockchain/Dev/migrations`: a case-sensitive grep for FROM, INTO or TABLE with `document_types` returned 0 lines; control: the Redis key builders above.

**Method and controls:**
- One `docker exec secuura-api-gateway node -e` per run, using the container's own `REDIS_URL` (never printed). Redis commands: SCAN, TTL, TYPE and GET on keys the scans returned (none were returned, so no value was read), plus DBSIZE and a count-only SCAN of `secuura:gateway:*`, as Wednesday approved. No key name, value or id is printed.
- The no-password connection answered NOAUTH on both boxes in both runs, so the authenticated connection is the one counted.
- The tool's logic was tested before the box runs against a fake Redis holding 7 doc-type keys (2 gated, 1 non-string, 1 unparsable): it counted them correctly, withheld a user-type approver's value, leaked none of the planted names, and issued only scan, ttl, type and get.
- Not demonstrated: a SCAN that returns keys on a real server. Both real prefix scans returned 0 in one page with the cursor finished; DBSIZE above 0 shows the server holds keys, none under this prefix.

**Not measured:**
- document types held anywhere other than the gateway's Redis (another service, or the gateway's in-memory fallback if Redis was unavailable to it; fallback mode is not inferred: the gateway log has 0 lines containing `allback` and 6 containing `Redis` on both boxes, counts only);
- types that existed before their 3,600 s TTL lapsed;
- whether the seed has ever run on either box;
- the approver roles of any type, since none exists to read.

**Instrument:** `make_gwdoctypes_u14.py` and `make_gwcontrol_u14.py` generate the box tools and check mechanically that they use only the approved Redis verbs; raw output is in `5_Project_History/2026-11-05_seatU-14th/evidence/` (`gwdoctypes_kintsugi_raw.txt`, `gwdoctypes_demo_raw.txt`, `gwcontrol_kintsugi_raw.txt`, `gwcontrol_demo_raw.txt`). Reads only; nothing was written on either box and no request was sent to any service.

**BLUF:** Item 2 stays unbuilt, per Kam's card `secuura-ks1087-workflow-approve-credential-1102`, option b (ruled 2026-11-02T12:44:48+11:00): "Wait: measure read-only whether workflow-gated document types exist; no build" ("No production change. Item 1 already stops silent loss."). This comment records the design measurements for when that read is done. Code read at develop `5fc5569ed96a`; no stack and no box. A separate gap that every option needs is filed as KS-2006.

**What unblocks item 2:** whether any environment has a workflow-gated document type. That is a read-only box read, and it has not been made.

## Measured (code read; paths under `Blockchain/Dev/services/`)

* **M1.** originate accepts only an RS256 Bearer, checked against auth's JWKS or static public key (`originate/src/middleware/auth.ts:61`, `:87-89`). If the token carries a `sessionId`, that session must be active (`:105-107`). Nothing else authenticates `POST /api/documents` (`originate/src/routes/documents.ts:188`).
* **M2.** The gateway cannot mint such a token. `api-gateway/src` has 0 non-test hits for `jwt.sign`, `PRIVATE_KEY`, `createSign` or `SignJWT`; control: `auth/src/services/jwt.ts` has 2 `jwt.sign`. auth has no service-token or client-credentials path: 0 hits for `client_credentials`, `serviceToken`, `service-token` or `SERVICE_TOKEN` in `auth/src` and `packages`.
* **M3.** originate takes the document's owner from the token, not from `x-user-id` (`documents.ts:239-251`, F-04). The `x-user-id` this forward sends today does not set the owner. The issuer org also comes from the token (`req.user.organizationId`, `:530`).
* **M4.** originate's create gate accepts the roles ISSUER_ADMIN, ORG_ADMIN, SYSTEM_ADMIN or SUPER_ADMIN (case-insensitive), or the scope `documents:write` (`documents.ts:400-403`, `originate/src/middleware/rbac.ts:47-64`). By default only role OWNER is granted that scope (`packages/shared/src/security/scopes.ts:287-292`).
* **M5.** A workflow step's approver defaults to role `admin` (`api-gateway/src/services/enforcement.ts:232`). The approve route also admits ADMIN_ROLES (`api-gateway/src/index.ts:915`: admin, ADMIN, SYSTEM_ADMIN, system_admin, super_admin, SUPER_ADMIN). `ADMIN` is not in originate's write roles and gets no scope. So with the approver's own token, an approver on the default step would still be refused, with 403 instead of 401.
* **M6.** The pending document stores the request body plus `createdBy`, and no tenant, org or role (`enforcement.ts:251-258`). The creator did hold a write role or scope when the document was held: KS-1871 refuses anyone else before gating (`api-gateway/src/routes/verification.ts:897-903`).
* **M7.** The approve forward also sends no `x-tenant-id` or `x-tenant-slug`; the direct-create forward does (`verification.ts:935-941`). Without them, originate answers 400 under production multi-tenancy, or uses `DEFAULT_TENANT_ID` (`packages/shared/src/db/tenant-context.ts:60-75`). Filed as KS-2006, to be built together with item 2.

## Options for item 2, and what each changes

* **A. Forward the approver's Bearer, plus the approver's tenant headers** (mirroring direct-create `verification.ts:933-941`). One file, about three lines.
  * The document's owner becomes the approver, not the creator (M3). The on-chain issuer org and the tenant become the approver's.
  * It works only when the approver holds a write role or OWNER (M4). The default `admin` step still fails (M5).
  * It fails safe: 502, with the pending document kept. But every success writes approver attribution, and an anchored document's issuer is on chain.
* **B. A service identity, with the creator attributed.** The gateway authenticates to originate as itself, and originate takes owner and tenant from vouched `x-user-id` / `x-tenant-id`.
  * No such credential exists (M1, M2). Building one needs either an auth-minted service token, or a new originate auth mode keyed on the gateway vouch (provenance is already checked at `originate/src/index.ts:221-224`).
  * The gateway must also store the creator's tenant and org when it holds the document (M6, M7), and someone must decide whose role counts at approve time.
  * Three services; a security design on a new trust path.
* **C. Store the creator's Bearer with the pending document and replay it.** Not recommended:
  * it puts a credential at rest in Redis;
  * tokens expire in about an hour (`originate/src/middleware/auth.ts:102`, comment);
  * an ended session is refused (M1).
* **D. No forward at approve.** Approve marks the document approved, and the creator's next call creates it with the creator's own token. A flow and product change.

Seat T 11th's recommendation to Wednesday was B as the target, with no build until the reach question is answered. That matches the card. Nothing deployed, nothing built: the ticket stays In Progress.

**BLUF:** Item 2 is still open and now measured live. The workflow-approve forward to originate carries no Authorization header, and originate refuses it with 401. Since PR 1008 the gateway reports that refusal as 502 `ORIGINATE_FORWARD_FAILED` and keeps the pending document. The forward code is unchanged on develop `d92b849ece73`. This ran on a disposable local stack at `ee1e1b832115`, not on kintsugi.

**What ran (stack `w25`, 2026-11-04 08:21Z, throwaway data):**
* A workflow instance and its pending document were seeded in the stack's own Redis. The approver sent `POST /api/workflow-instances/w25-ks1183-twin/approve` with its own Bearer token, and originate was running.
* Result: 502 in 32 ms, body `{"success":false,"error":{"code":"ORIGINATE_FORWARD_FAILED","message":"Approved, but the document could not be created in originate; the pending document was kept","status":401}}`.
* With originate paused, the same approve answered 502 with upstream `status: 0` in 15045 ms. That pair closed KS-1183. So the 401 above comes from originate itself, not from a timeout.

**Why originate answers 401 (code at `ee1e1b832115`, all under `Blockchain/Dev/services/`):**
* `api-gateway/src/routes/verification.ts:562-578` builds the approve forward to originate's `POST /api/documents`. It sends four headers: `Content-Type`, `Content-Length`, `x-user-id` (line 574, the pending document's `createdBy`) and the vouch header (`vouchHeaderFor('originate')`, line 578). It sends no `Authorization`. The source comment at lines 576-577 names this ticket.
* `originate/src/routes/documents.ts:188` is `documentsRouter.use(authenticate());`. `originate/src/middleware/auth.ts:87-89` answers 401 `UNAUTHORIZED` when the Authorization header is missing or does not start with `Bearer `.
* The direct-create forward in the same gateway file works differently. At lines 909-932 it copies the caller's `authorization` header (line 919). The approve forward copies nothing of the kind.

**Develop:** the three files above are byte-identical at `d92b849ece73` and `ee1e1b832115`, read in a kept seat clone.

**Not established here:** anything about kintsugi's configuration, data or env, and whether any deployed environment has a workflow-gated document type.

Verified by code read, not observed live: `Blockchain/Dev/services/api-gateway/src/routes/verification.ts:583` awaits originate's answer to the forward before anything is deleted, and `:612` answers 502 ORIGINATE_FORWARD_FAILED while the pending document is kept. Left open: item 2 (forwarding a credential that originate accepts) is a design call; the 2026-09-16 comment on this ticket says PR 1008 does not touch it.

## BLUF
PR #1008 (item 1) **merged** as squash `f7c2f4acb28875e3665a61c8eaaad5c54bd3aa55` on develop (single parent `73d3fcb902d2a78fe68a4349903ff6c6bd24d4d5`), on Wednesday's GO naming head `dd7086d5aa574285beffc515f9371a438621f25d` after a tier-1 QA gate (round 1) returned GO WITH FINDINGS. This ticket stays **In Progress** for item 2 (forwarding a credential originate accepts). Two follow-ups are filed: **KS-1183** (the forward has no timeout; the next PR) and **KS-1184** (the instance is persisted `approved` before the forward, which strands it).

## Recommendation
No action on this ticket from the merge. Item 2 remains a design call. KS-1184 sits beside it, because both decide what a refused forward should leave behind.

## Detail
**Merge, verified at origin:** develop tip = `f7c2f4acb`; one parent = `73d3fcb90`; tree `4124c19c5` = the predicted merge tree; files base..merge = the PR's two (`services/api-gateway/src/routes/verification.ts` blob `d0585dc34`, `services/api-gateway/src/__tests__/ks1087-workflow-approve-deletes-the-pending-document.test.ts` blob `7832724f3`), both equal to the gated head. The link to this ticket read `contributes` before the merge, with 0 closing phrases in the PR title, body, commit message and squash message.

**What the gate measured** (report `Testing Agent MAIN/projects/secuura/reports/2026-09-17-ks1087-1008-dd7086d5a-tier1-r1/report.md`, real `createVerificationRoutes` against a counting originate stub, at head and on the merged tree). A 2xx from originate (200/201/204/299) answers 200 and deletes the pending document once. A 3xx, 4xx or 5xx, a socket destroyed before headers, a closed port, or 401 headers with a body that never ends each answer 502 `ORIGINATE_FORWARD_FAILED` with `status` set to originate's code (0 for transport) and keep the pending document. 201 headers followed by a mid-body reset, or a body that never ends, answer 200 and delete, with no crash. The earlier code answered 200 and deleted in every one of those rows, including the closed port with 0 hits. Auth is unchanged, by parser (677/677 and 44/44 nodes equal outside the forward span, with controls that fire) and at runtime (401 with no token, 403 on the wrong role or user, 200 on the positive control). The 502 body is a fixed literal plus an integer in test, production and development, and never carries originate's body, path or port. Tampers reddened as predicted. api-gateway 45 files / 391 tests on develop → 46 / 394 on the merged tree, all green; ks1087 alone 3/3 at head, and 1/3 when copied onto the base (2 red, as it should be).

**Headers vs `'end'` (the gate's ruling): deleting on 2xx headers is right.** Originate persists at `services/originate/src/routes/documents.ts:667` (`saveDocument`) before its single `res.status(201).json(...)` at `:911`, so a 2xx status line means the document is committed. Moving the resolve into `'end'` would add a hang, because `proxyRes` has no `'error'`/`'aborted'`/`'close'` listener. That is covered in KS-1183. (Line numbers re-read on the merge commit, blob `c3a818ac8`.)

**Records (no action from the merge):**
- **R1:** the 502 echoes originate's status integer to the authenticated approver (401 = credential refused, 0 = transport). Mild topology disclosure, useful for diagnosis.
- **R2:** `POST /api/workflow-instances/:id/approve` and its new 502 are absent from `docs/openapi/secuura-api.yaml` (`workflow-instances` 0 hits). Pre-existing; a docs ticket candidate.
- **R3:** a final approve with NO pending document answers "All workflow steps approved. Document has been created." with 0 forwards, before and after #1008. A claim with nothing behind it; pre-existing; a ticket candidate.
- **R4:** `db.retry.test.ts` "reports available immediately when the probe succeeds at boot" ran at 5,347 ms under the gate's parallel load (vitest's default is 5 s). Serial runs are green. Pre-existing.

**Follow-ups filed** (board searches quoted in each ticket):
- **KS-1183** (Medium): the forward has no timeout. An originate that accepts and never answers leaves the approve unanswered, and a late 201 creates the document after the caller got nothing. It is its own tier-1 PR and the next one raised, carrying the gate's test-quality items F3–F6 for the ks1087 file.
- **KS-1184** (High, the gate's Major): `verification.ts:970-972` persists `approved` before the forward, so a refused forward strands the workflow (re-approve 400 with 0 forwards, reject 400, the kept document unusable until TTL). A design call; its reach depends on workflow-gated document types existing.

**Not tested by the gate:** a live originate (its 401 today is relayed), whether any environment has workflow-gated document types, an HTTPS originate, the Redis TTL value, nginx's bound on the hang, out-of-repo callers, and the four platform suites. Schemathesis was ruled not required, because the route is not in the published spec.

Nothing deployed.

## BLUF
PR #1008 raises **item 1** at head `dd7086d5aa574285beffc515f9371a438621f25d`, not yet merged. On approve, the gateway now reads originate's status:
- a non-2xx or transport error answers **502 `ORIGINATE_FORWARD_FAILED`** and **keeps** the pending document;
- only a 2xx deletes it and reports "created".
**This ticket stays open for item 2** (forwarding a credential originate accepts), a design call not touched here.

## Recommendation
No action needed on the PR. Item 2 still needs its design decision.

## Detail
- PR: https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/1008 (branch `feature/ks-1087-ornith-workflow-approve-keeps-pending`, base develop `93629700c`).
- Authored by the local model (Ornith) from a Wednesday-written brief; source-read by Wednesday; re-run by seat A at `dd7086d5aa574285beffc515f9371a438621f25d`.
- The READY's 401 cell named "the pending document survives" but never asserted it. Seat A added that assertion, plus "deleted exactly once on 201" on the control. Each is proved able to fail: deleting before the status check reddens the 401 cell by survival alone; never deleting reddens the control by deletion alone.
- Red before green: 2 of 3 red on the untouched product (both answered 200), 3/3 after.
- api-gateway 44 files / 388 tests pass (baseline 43 / 385). `tsc` rc 0.
- The route `/api/workflow-instances/:id/approve` is not in the published OpenAPI spec, so no contract documents the new 502.

## BLUF

**Priority set to High.** This is the coordinator's triage ruling, made under Kam's delegated scope; Kam may override it.

The reason is this ticket's own measured defect: workflow-approve deletes the pending document and answers 200 "Document has been created" without reading originate's response, so a refused forward (401, measured by the #951 round-2 gate) loses the document.

**Reachability through workflow-gated document types is NOT established.** No one has yet shown this path is reached by a document type that actually routes through workflow approval in a deployed configuration.

## Recommendation

No action needed on this comment. The priority is set, and the reachability question stays open on this ticket.

## Detail

- **Ruling:** coordinator brief to Platform K seat s178, 2026-09-11 01:50Z, item 0(c).
- **Measured, as filed:** the #951 round-2 gate measured the refused forward (401) and the 200 "Document has been created" that follows it.
- **Not measured:** whether any workflow-gated document type reaches this path on local, demo or any deployed configuration.
- **Change made by this comment's author:** priority, No priority → High. Status, assignee and relations are unchanged.

title: Launcher preflight: four findings — a concurrent seat clobbers the warnings file, KS-907 miscounts sessions, F-02 names a missing key, rule 7 still says extranet
description:
## BLUF

Four defects in `Launch_Claude.command`. **This ticket files them; it does not fix them.** None blocks a session today. Each one either loses a boot warning, misreports seat state, or tells a seat to do something wrong.

1. **The warnings file is one file per project, so a second seat's launch overwrites the first seat's warnings.** Measured by s172 on 2026-09-11: s173's launch at 07:11:31 overwrote s172's at 07:11:14, 17 s apart, and s172's own warnings were lost.
2. **The KS-907 seat registry counted a session running in** `Testing Agent MAIN` **as "a live session on this project".** Measured by s173 on 2026-09-11. The mechanism is not verified.
3. **The F-02 remedy tells the operator to** `ssh-add ~/.ssh/secuura_blockchain_deploy_rw` **— a file that does not exist on this machine.** git works regardless, through the repo-local `core.sshCommand` → `3_Access_Keys/github_deploy_rw`.
4. **Launch-prompt rule 7 still prescribes "an extranet to-do per person plus a Linear comment".** That contradicts Kam's 2026-09-05 ruling that everything goes through the tickets. The project `CLAUDE.md` step 3 was corrected on 2026-09-11; the launcher was not.

A fifth finding already has a home: the SessionStart hook still tells every seat to `POST /api/seen`. That is **KS-925**, and the evidence is added there.

## Recommendation

Fix all four in the **master launcher template** as well as this copy. Per the launcher notes, `Launch_Claude.command` is a per-project copy of a master template, so fixing one copy fixes no other project. One pass proves all four:

* launch two seats about 10 s apart and check both warnings survive;
* run with a non-Blockchain Claude session alive and check it is not counted;
* read the F-02 text against `ls`;
* grep the assembled boot prompt for `extranet to-do` and expect 0.

## Detail

**1 — clobbered warnings file.**

* `Launch_Claude.command:90` writes `PREFLIGHT_LOG="$PROJECT_DIR/4_Credentials/.launch_preflight_last.txt"`, one path per project. The boot prompt then tells the seat to relay that file verbatim (`:392`).
* s172 (PID 64454, launched 07:11:14 AEST) read a file stamped `# launch 2026-09-10T21:11:31Z`, which is s173's launch.
* In that file, the KS-907 line listed s172's own PID as an "other" seat.
* Control from s176 today: the stamp `2026-09-10T22:36:54Z` equals `ps -o lstart= -p $PPID`. The file is not always clobbered — only when two launches race.
* Workaround in use: compare the stamp with your own start before relaying the warnings.

**2 — KS-907 miscount.**

* s173 attributed one of the two "other live sessions" in its KS-907 line to the fleet QA agent, by its cwd (`Testing Agent MAIN`).
* The registry lives at `Launch_Claude.command:244-379`. It reads `ps -eo pid=,command=` at `:328`.
* Not re-measured here, and which predicate matched is not verified.

**3 — F-02 names a missing key.**

* `Launch_Claude.command:107`, `:133` and `:138` all say `ssh-add --apple-use-keychain ~/.ssh/secuura_blockchain_deploy_rw`.
* On this machine (s176, 2026-09-11 ~23:3xZ), `ls ~/.ssh/secuura_blockchain_deploy_rw` → `No such file or directory`.
* `3_Access_Keys/github_deploy_rw` is present, and `git fetch` returned rc 0 through `core.sshCommand` while the F-02 warning was showing.

**4 — rule 7.**

* `Launch_Claude.command:476` says: *"notify Stuart AND Peter — an extranet to-do per person plus a Linear comment @-mentioning them"*.
* Kam, 2026-09-05 13:55, verbatim: *"The team is not using the extranet much. I mentioned this yesterday. If anything needs to be escalated, please tell me and I'll send a WhatsApp message. Otherwise, everything has to be done through the tickets."*
* The project-root `CLAUDE.md` step 3 was rewritten to "on the tickets only" by s176 on 2026-09-11, as ruled by Wednesday. The pre-edit copy is in `5_Project_History/quarantine/2026-09-11-s176/`.

**Searched before filing:**

* `launch_preflight_last` — 14 KS hits. KS-907 and KS-911 name the file only as test hygiene ("every run overwrites it"); none covers the clobber.
* `secuura_blockchain_deploy_rw` — no launcher ticket.
* `extranet-session-check` and `api/seen` — found **KS-925**, which is finding 5, so it is not duplicated here.
* `Launch_Claude.command` — KS-907, KS-925, KS-655, KS-911, KS-912, KS-681, KS-78; none covers these four.
* Control: `KS-907` → 1 hit.

Filed by s176. Findings 1 and 2 are other seats' measurements, credited above. Findings 3 and 4 were re-measured at source by s176.

title: READ ONLY / unverified: the gateway's own Authorization-only calls to originate send no x-tenant-id — single-tenant originate may scope them to DEFAULT_TENANT_ID
description:
## BLUF

**READ ONLY, not driven by anyone.** api-gateway calls originate directly — outside `createProxyRoutes` — at several sites and sends only `Authorization`. With no `x-tenant-id`, originate's KS-458 block (`services/originate/src/index.ts:248-256`) sets `req.tenantId` to `DEFAULT_TENANT_ID` in single-tenant mode, so those calls **may** read or write in the default tenant rather than the caller's. Independent of PR #951 (unchanged by it). Raised by the #951 tier-1 gate (round 1, Open item b) and not measured.

## Recommendation

Measure before any fix: drive one site per shape (a read, a write) as a caller in a non-default tenant on a two-tenant local stack and compare which tenant's rows come back. **Unknown that could dissolve this:** whether originate's `authenticate()` sets the tenant from the forwarded JWT on these routes. If confirmed, route gateway→originate calls through one helper that forwards the verified tenant — the same helper #951's F5 residual needs for the vouch.

## Detail

Sites at `develop` `2d864ae92` (grep for the originate URL in `services/api-gateway/src`, headers read at each):

* `routes/proxy.ts:554-556` — `GET /api/signatories`, headers `{ Authorization }`
* `routes/proxy.ts:578-579` — `GET /api/third-party-verifiers`, headers `{ Authorization }`
* `routes/verification.ts:129-138` and `:167-176` — `GET /api/documents/:id`, headers `{ Authorization }` when present
* `routes/batch.ts:146`, `:194` — batch certify / verify via `ORIGINATE_SERVICE_URL`, `authorization` forwarded; `x-tenant-id` 0 mentions in the file
* `routes/platform.ts:249-251` — `POST /api/admin/refresh-tenants`, `Content-Type` + `Authorization`

Not in this ticket (different shape, tracked on PR #951's body as READ ONLY): `routes/verification.ts` `POST /api/documents` and the workflow-approve forward DO send `x-user-id` / `x-tenant-id`, but without the vouch, so #951 would strip them once its secret is provisioned.

**Board searched before filing:** exact `getReqTenantId` → 4 (KS-174, KS-22, KS-26, KS-48 — none about gateway direct calls), `tenantGucContext` → 6 (none), `KS-458` → 1 (itself); control `KS-468` → 1. Fuzzy `DEFAULT_TENANT_ID`, `x-tenant-id`, `signatories`, `third-party-verifiers`, `Authorization-only` → nearest KS-468 (Done — audited the 44 gateway proxy MOUNTS, not these direct calls) and KS-619 (Backlog — `middleware/auth.ts` conditional tenant overwrite).

Related: KS-1041 · KS-468 · KS-619 · PR [https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/951](<https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/951>) · gate report `Testing Agent MAIN/projects/secuura/reports/2026-09-11-ks1041-951-dd0a0c934-tier1/report.md` (Open b).

## Detail

- **The POST /api/documents forward** (`http.request` at develop `:1125`) sends `authorization`, `x-user-id`, `x-tenant-id` and `x-tenant-slug`.
- Found while filing KS-1087 from the #951 round-2 gate report. Appended here rather than edited into the body.

title: GATEWAY_VOUCH_SECRET: nothing provisions it and no deploy order or rotation is written — #951's control ships inert, and a gateway/originate mismatch drops gateway identity
description:
## BLUF

PR #951 (KS-1041 Step 2) adds a secret that lets originate tell a gateway-routed request from a direct one. **No tracked deploy, bootstrap or CI path supplies** `GATEWAY_VOUCH_SECRET`, so every environment boots with the control **DISABLED** (fail-open by design, with a WARN). And **when the gateway and originate disagree about the secret** — originate deployed first, a gateway rollback, a rotation, or a gateway container not recreated after `.env` changes — originate drops every gateway-set identity. This is one logical path: provisioning, deploy order, rotation. It is also where the **provisioning-safety question** lives — whether switching the control on breaks the gateway's own non-proxy writes to originate (Detail, first section).

## Recommendation

Needs decisions before code. Decide:

1. where each environment's value comes from — Key Vault → `deploy.sh` `--parameters gatewayVouchSecret=…`, and a `fill_if_blank "GATEWAY_VOUCH_SECRET" "openssl rand -hex 32"` line in `bootstrap-env.sh` for local;
2. the gateway-first deploy order and a rotation procedure (a dual-accept window or a transition flag), written into the runbook **before any box receives the secret**;
3. whether production should REQUIRE it (`enforceProductionConfig` in originate).
4. **Before provisioning on ANY box, answer the provisioning-safety question below.** The #951 round-2 tier-1 gate (commissioned 2026-09-10 22:52Z against `02a22f4bb`) is measuring it as a separate PROVISIONING SAFETY verdict.

## Detail

**Provisioning-safety question — READ ONLY, not driven (added by s174, 2026-09-11).** The gateway's own `POST /api/documents` handler (`services/api-gateway/src/routes/verification.ts:879`; the verification router is not mock-gated — `index.ts:876-891`) forwards to originate through its own `http.request` (`:1044`, headers built at `:1024-1042`) carrying `x-user-id`, `x-tenant-id` and `x-tenant-slug` and **no vouch** — the file has zero `vouch` mentions at `02a22f4bb`. With `GATEWAY_VOUCH_SECRET` set, originate's provenance middleware strips those headers. The handler's own KS-39 #4 comment (`:1036-1040`) states what a missing `x-tenant-id` does: the POST writes to the fallback tenant and the new document looks invisible / 404s on the next read. The workflow-approve forward (route `:700`, `http.request` at `:785`, `x-user-id` at `:783`) has the same shape. **Unknown:** whether originate's `authenticate()` recovers the tenant from the forwarded JWT — if it does, the consequence shrinks. If the question holds, the fix is the one #951's F5 residual already names: send every gateway→originate call through one helper that adds the vouch.

**F4 — nothing supplies it.** Re-measured at `dd0a0c934` from git objects: **0 mentions** of the secret in `deployment/azure/deploy.sh`, `services.parameters.json`, `env.demo.json`, `env.dev.json`, `sync-secrets.sh`, `setup-keyvault.sh`, `deploy-all.sh`, `scripts/bootstrap-env.sh`, and 0 files under `.github` (control: `services.bicep` → 10). `bootstrap-env.sh:198,200,208` generate `PII_ENCRYPTION_KEY`, `PII_LOOKUP_HMAC_KEY` and `DEMO_SERVICE_KEY`, not this. originate's `enforceProductionConfig` requires `DATABASE_URL`, `REDIS_URL`, `ANCHORING_SERVICE_URL` only. The #951 tier-1 gate counted 35 `--parameters` at `deploy.sh:721-757`, none of them this. Azure deploys therefore take the bicep default `''` and wire neither app.

**F3 — mismatch.** Measured in-process by the #951 tier-1 gate (round 1, cells S2.1 and S4.1): a merge-base gateway, or a head gateway with the secret unset, in front of an originate that has it → gateway-set `x-tenant-id` / `x-user-id` are stripped. Consequences read from source: the metering connector shim (`originate/src/routes/metering.ts:42`) stops matching and `authenticate()` answers 401; with `MULTI_TENANCY_ENABLED=true` in production `extractTenantContext` answers 400 "Missing tenant context" (`packages/shared/src/db/tenant-context.ts:67-74`); single-tenant falls to `DEFAULT_TENANT_ID` (`originate/src/index.ts:248-256`). **No forgeability window in any order** (gate cells S2.2–S2.4) — order affects availability and tenant scoping, not the hole.

**Board searched before filing** (exact to decide, fuzzy to discover): `gatewayVouchSecret` → 0; `vouch` → 12, none about provisioning (KS-1041, KS-1080 akto-autoheal, KS-1081 env-template drift, the rest Platform S identity/verify work); `GATEWAY_VOUCH_SECRET`, `deploy order`, `bootstrap-env.sh` → fuzzy noise, nothing about this secret; control `KS-1041` → 1.

Related: KS-1041 · KS-1081 (whichever env template wins must carry this variable) · PR [https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/951](<https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/951>) · round-1 gate report `Testing Agent MAIN/projects/secuura/reports/2026-09-11-ks1041-951-dd0a0c934-tier1/report.md` (F3, F4).

nodes.body:
**FYI, Kamil: KS-955 is going in, and it touches this ticket's area.** PR: https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/1756

**BLUF:** KS-955 does two things here:
- It fixes the unvouched gateway → originate forwards (your R2-1, "provisioning unsafe").
- It has `bootstrap-env.sh` generate `GATEWAY_VOUCH_SECRET` for fresh **local** clones. That changes the 2026-09-11 position, *"Do not set `GATEWAY_VOUCH_SECRET` on any environment yet"*, for local stacks. It went in only once the forward fix was in place and proven.

Nothing touches the VM demo, Container Apps or `deploy.sh`.

**What changes**

1. **P2a (api-gateway).**
   * `utils/originateForward.ts` reads the secret in one place and sends `x-gateway-vouch` to originate only.
   * The five hand-built forwards now use it: `POST /api/documents` and the workflow-approve forward (`verification.ts`); the upload, signatories and third-party-verifiers forwards (`proxy.ts`).
2. **P2c (`bootstrap-env.sh`).**
   * `fill_if_blank "GATEWAY_VOUCH_SECRET" "openssl rand -hex 32"`, written to `.env` only. An existing value is never overwritten.
   * A fresh local clone now boots originate `ACTIVE`, not `FAIL-CLOSED`.
3. **Not done:** O-4 (`SENSITIVE_KEYS`). It is recorded on this ticket (comment of 2026-10-26): shared-logger redaction runs only in production, and the gateway logs through its own winston logger.

**Evidence** (Peter's Mac, 2026-10-27; full Test Evidence on the PR and on KS-955)

* **Unit, red on develop and green on the branch:**
  * `ks955-hand-forwards-carry-the-vouch.test.ts`: 3 of 7 red on develop, 7 of 7 green.
  * `bootstrap_env_gateway_vouch.test.sh`: 4 of 7 red on develop, 7 of 7 green.
* **Live, R2-1 end to end:** new cell `systemTest/schemathesis/tests/test_tenant_isolation_gateway_create.py`. A super-admin creates a document through the gateway's `POST /api/documents` under a non-default tenant's override.
  * **Develop `a105a9df1` with a vouch secret set by hand:** create 201, then a **404** reading it in that tenant. It landed in the default tenant, as your gate measured.
  * **KS-955:** 200 in the tenant, 404 in the default tenant.
* **The cross-tenant pair (KS-1704):** both tests fail on develop because the secret is unset, and pass with it set.
* **Gates on the branch head all green,** including preflight 16/16. The remaining Schemathesis reds are the same as develop's, and all ticketed.

**Still with this ticket:** deployed provisioning (Key Vault → `deploy.sh`), deploy order, rotation, and whether production should require the secret.

No action is needed from you for KS-955. If you see a problem with local stacks booting `ACTIVE`, a note here would be very welcome. Thank you.

**P2b (your O-4 from 2026-09-11) was not done in KS-955. Recorded here so it is not lost.**

Adding `x-gateway-vouch` to the shared logger's `SENSITIVE_KEYS` (`packages/shared/src/logger/index.ts:19`, still 0 mentions) would not protect the gateway today, for two reasons:
- `redactValue` returns early unless `NODE_ENV === 'production'`.
- api-gateway logs through its own winston logger (`services/api-gateway/src/utils/logger.ts`), not the shared one.

Touching `packages/shared` also rebuilds every image. So the real fix belongs to whatever decides redaction for the gateway's logger; a key in a list it never consults would not do it.

**What KS-955 did do on your list:**
- **Item 1:** the five hand-built originate forwards now send the vouch through one helper (`services/api-gateway/src/utils/originateForward.ts`). It reads the secret in one place, sends it to originate only, and is red→green unit-tested.
- **P2c:** `bootstrap-env.sh` now generates the secret for a **local** fresh clone. Measured: a fresh worktree boots originate `ACTIVE`, and the KS-1704 tenant-isolation pair passes.

**Still open here:** deployed provisioning (Key Vault → `deploy.sh`), deploy order, rotation, and whether production must require it. Not yet run live: a document saved through the gateway's `POST /api/documents` with the secret set.

**BLUF:** reproduced again on 2026-10-16 (slot 2, develop `a92f46e14`). The Schemathesis `pre-merge` live integration suite had **2 failed of 436**, both tenant isolation, the same pair recorded on KS-1478 on 2026-10-14.

- `test_cross_tenant_isolation`: a document created as the super-admin was readable (200) with `X-Tenant-Override` set to a foreign tenant ("BUG-ISOLATION-001 regression").
- `test_api_key_cross_tenant_isolation`: a key created under Oxford was listed under the BUPA tenant override (KS-513 assertion).
- `GATEWAY_VOUCH_SECRET` is set (non-empty) in **0 of 2** containers checked (`api-gateway`, `originate`), and `scripts/bootstrap-env.sh` still has 0 mentions of it. Checked by key presence only; no value was read.

**Proposed acceptance criteria:**
- Local bootstrap and every deploy path provision the secret.
- The deploy order and rotation are written down.
- **A test demonstrates the fix:** both tests above pass on a freshly built slot with the secret provisioned, and fail with it unset.

## Since KS-1032 (2026-10-13) the unprovisioned secret is no longer inert: on every templated slot it silently drops the super-admin tenant override

**BLUF:** this ticket's title says the control "ships inert". After commit `d53d80cbb` (KS-1032, merged 2026-10-13) that is no longer true. With `GATEWAY_VOUCH_SECRET` unset, originate **drops** identity/tenant/role headers from every request, so a super-admin's `X-Tenant-Override` never reaches the RLS context. Nothing errors; the request reads the default tenant. That matches KS-1032's own commit message: *"a silent switch to the wrong tenant, not a refusal"*. That is the intended fail-closed behaviour on an unconfigured box. The gap is that **nothing provisions the secret**, so every box built from the templates is in that state.

**Measured, 2026-10-14, slot 1 of Peter's Mac, `develop` 3c0a52221:**
* originate at boot (container log): `[gateway-provenance] FAIL-CLOSED — GATEWAY_VOUCH_SECRET is unset, so identity/tenant/role headers are DROPPED from every request`.
* Templates: `Blockchain/Dev/env.example:478` and `.env.example:343` both read `GATEWAY_VOUCH_SECRET=` (blank). `bootstrap-env.sh` generates `POSTGRES_PASSWORD` / `REDIS_PASSWORD` per clone (KS-731) but not this key.
* Consequence: the systemTest tenant-isolation tests (`test_cross_tenant_isolation`, `test_api_key_cross_tenant_isolation`) passed in all 7 archived runs on 2026-10-09 and 2026-10-12, and **fail in 3 of 3 runs on 2026-10-14**, with a message that reads like a P0 leak. Detail and the misleading-verdict half are on **KS-955**.

**Not verified:** the green path with the secret set. Setting it means writing a secret value, which a person has to do. Nothing in any env file was read to establish the above; only the templates and the container log were.

**Proposed acceptance criteria (provisioning half):**
1. `bootstrap-env.sh` generates `GATEWAY_VOUCH_SECRET` per clone when blank (the KS-731 pattern) and writes the same value for gateway and originate.
2. The deploy order and rotation are written down, as this ticket's title asks.
3. **A test demonstrating the fix:** a bootstrap shell test proves a fresh `.env` gets a non-empty secret. On a stack built from it, originate does **not** log `FAIL-CLOSED … unset`, and the systemTest tenant-isolation tests pass.

Found during KS-1478 (Akto / Schemathesis tool bump), which did not cause it.

## BLUF

- **Do not set `GATEWAY_VOUCH_SECRET` on any environment yet.** The QA agent's round-2 tier-1 gate on #951 (`02a22f4bb`, 2026-09-11) returned GO WITH FINDINGS on the PR, and **PROVISIONING SAFETY: UNSAFE** as a separate verdict.
- **Why:** once originate has the secret, the gateway's own `POST /api/documents` forward carries no vouch. originate strips `x-tenant-id` and `x-user-id`, and the document is saved under **`DEFAULT_TENANT_ID`** instead of the caller's tenant. No error is returned. Measured at runtime, in-process, with real modules and a synthetic secret and key.
- **Merging #951 does not change this.** develop `2d864ae92` has the same forward (READ ONLY, not driven).

## Recommendation

A precondition for ANY provisioning, in this ticket's scope:

1. **One helper that adds the vouch to every gateway → originate call that bypasses the proxy middleware:**
   - `api-gateway/src/routes/verification.ts:1044` at `02a22f4bb` (develop `:1125`), POST /api/documents;
   - `verification.ts:785` (develop `:866`), the workflow-approve forward;
   - `api-gateway/src/routes/proxy.ts:522-526` at `02a22f4bb`, the multipart upload forward (latent: originate registers no `/upload` route).
2. **The gate's regression test:** record the real `verification.ts` forward, replay it into the real originate app with the secret set, and assert the tenant passed to `saveDocument` equals the JWT tenant. Include a vouched control and an unset control.
3. **O-4 (latent, READ):** add `x-gateway-vouch` to the shared logger's `SENSITIVE_KEYS` (`packages/shared/src/logger/index.ts:19`; 0 mentions today).

No action needed from anyone on this comment beyond keeping the secret unset.

## Detail

**The measurement (report R2-1):**

| cell | originate secret UNSET | originate secret SET (synthetic) |
|---|---|---|
| P1: recorded POST /api/documents forward, tenant the handler writes under | the forwarded JWT tenant | **`DEFAULT_TENANT_ID`**: `x-tenant-id` and `x-user-id` stripped, RLS = default, `saveDocument` = default |
| P1v control: the same forward plus a correct vouch | the forwarded JWT tenant | the forwarded JWT tenant |
| P2: recorded workflow-approve forward | 401, handler not reached | 401, handler not reached |

**Mechanism** (line numbers at `02a22f4bb`, from the report):

- `createGatewayProvenanceMiddleware` strips the unvouched trust headers.
- The KS-458 block (`originate/src/index.ts:248-256`) then sets `req.tenantId = DEFAULT_TENANT_ID`, and `tenantGucContext` seeds RLS from it. Both run at app level, before `documentsRouter.use(authenticate())` (`routes/documents.ts:145`), which sets `req.user` only.
- The gateway handler's own KS-39 #4 comment (`verification.ts:1036-1040`) describes the consequence: the new document looks invisible, or 404s, to its owner.

**Every gateway → originate call outside the proxy middleware:**

| call site (at `02a22f4bb`) | changed by provisioning? |
|---|---|
| `verification.ts:1044` POST /api/documents | **yes (R2-1)** |
| `proxy.ts:522-526` upload | yes, latent |
| `verification.ts:785` workflow-approve | no: 401 in both modes. Its own data-loss defect is filed as KS-1087. |
| `proxy.ts:606/630`, `platform.ts:248`, `verification.ts:129/167`, `batch.ts:91` (Authorization only) | no, see KS-1084 |

**NOT tested by the gate:**

- multi-tenant mode (`MULTI_TENANCY_ENABLED=true`);
- `NODE_ENV=production` variants (the KS-458 block is unconditional, READ);
- R2-1 on develop (READ ONLY, not driven);
- the upload forward under provisioning (not replayed);
- any live stack, and how many live JWTs carry a non-default tenant.

**Source:** `Testing Agent MAIN/projects/secuura/reports/2026-09-11-ks1041-951-02a22f4bb-tier1-r2/report.md`, sections R2-1, Open (O-4) and NOT TESTED. Posted by Platform K seat s177 on Wednesday's brief; the QA agent cannot post.

title: The Playwright env guard added in #896 reads config/ only — the variable breaking the CI run is read from fixtures/ and appears in no template
description:
## BLUF

PR #896 (KS-682) adds `systemTest/playwright/tests-unit/env-example.test.ts`. It pins `systemTest/playwright/.env.example` to every variable that `config/` **reads**. **The variable now failing the Playwright run in CI,** `BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_PASSWORD`**, is read outside that scope**, so the guard stays green over exactly the gap that breaks the run.

**This is measured on #896's head** `a7b588a05f1a40b29b429e7dafa4a84d9a6283d0`**, which is unmerged. The guard does not exist on** `develop`**.** s171 found it by reading during its Phase 1 review of #896 (2026-09-10), not by running a test, so it was not filed then. Filing, not fixing: `systemTest/` is Peter's authority.

## Measured

|  |  |
| -- | -- |
| Guard scope (#896 head) | `env-example.test.ts:23-24`: `PACKAGE_ROOT` = `systemTest/playwright`, `CONFIG_DIR = path.join(PACKAGE_ROOT, 'config')`. `:40` reads only `readdirSync(CONFIG_DIR)` |
| Where the variable is read (#896 head) | `systemTest/fixtures/provision-actors.ts:155`, `password: process.env.BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_PASSWORD ?? ''`. This is outside `systemTest/playwright/` entirely (`:110` on `develop` `2d864ae92`) |
| How the Playwright run reaches it | `systemTest/playwright/global-setup.ts:40` spawns `fixtures/pre-suite.ts`, which provisions the actors |
| In the `.env.example` the guard pins | `BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_PASSWORD` **0** · control `API_BASE_URL` **1** |
| Readers inside the guard's scope | `BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_PASSWORD` **0 files** under `playwright/config/` · control `TEST_ADMIN_PASSWORD` **1 file** |
| `Blockchain/Dev/docs/ENVIRONMENT-VARIABLES.md` on `develop` `2d864ae92` | `BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_PASSWORD` **0** · control `DATABASE_URL` **2** |
| `.github/workflows/` on `develop` `2d864ae92` | `BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_PASSWORD` **0 files** · control `API_BASE_URL` **4 files** |

## Why it matters

The guard's claim is true as written: it covers what `config/` reads. But a green guard reads as "the Playwright environment is documented", and the variable that decides whether the run can authenticate at all is read by the shared `fixtures/` the run spawns.

It also compounds with KS-969. Without `BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_PASSWORD` the pre-suite reports DEGRADED and exits 0, the actor manifest is not published, and `auth.setup` logs in with `''`. In CI that login returns HTTP 400, and 11 of the 12 tests never run. See KS-969 comment `e1358ef7`.

## Not decided here

Two questions for Peter:

* Should the guard also scan the `fixtures/` the suite spawns?
* Does `BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_PASSWORD` belong in any `.env.example` at all? It is a privileged bootstrap credential, and KS-969's open question comes first: what supplies it now that the published default is retired?

## Searched before filing

* Exact: `CONFIG_DIR` (10 hits, none about this guard), `env-example.test.ts`, `PACKAGE_ROOT`, `getTestAdminPassword` (KS-969 only).
* Fuzzy: "env-example guard", "readEnv config .env.example guard", "env drift guard fixtures directory".
* Opened, none carries this finding:
  * KS-967: a different pair of guards, the credential scanners.
  * KS-1081: two templates disagreeing with each other.
  * KS-973: pre-suite step items.
  * KS-682's 19 comments: `env-example` appears only in a bite table.
* Control: `KS-682` returns 1 hit.

Links: KS-969 · KS-966 · KS-682 · [https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/896](<https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/896>)

title: dev-ps nginx accumulated 939 container restarts (19 Aug – 8 Sep), then stopped — cause unexplained
description:
## The observation

The nginx container on dev-ps (`secuura-dk-nginx-1`) carries **939 restarts**. No other container on the box has any:

```
secuura-dk-nginx-1        restarts=939  created=2026-08-19T06:54:44Z
secuura-dk-secuura-ssd-1  restarts=0
secuura-dk-db-1           restarts=0
secuura-dk-phpmyadmin-1   restarts=0
```

**It is not happening now.** The last restart was `finished=2026-09-08T06:06:34Z` → `started=2026-09-08T06:07:34Z`, and the counter has been static at 939 across four readings today while uptime kept climbing (21 h → 26 h → 2 days), including two samples 20 s apart. So this is a **historical burst, not a live crash loop** — roughly 939 restarts over the 20 days from 19 Aug to 8 Sep, about 47/day, or one every \~30 minutes.

Raising it because \~47 restarts/day for three weeks on one container and zero on its three neighbours is not a normal steady state, and nothing currently explains it. If it resumes, the cause should already be written down.

## What has been ruled out

* **Not OOM** — `State.OOMKilled = false`, and the host is comfortable (disk 23 % used, \~2.5 GB of 3.9 GB available).
* **Not a failed start.** Exit code is **0**, i.e. a clean shutdown (nginx exits 0 on SIGTERM/SIGQUIT), not a config error — a bad config would exit non-zero and leave an error in the log. The container log shows only access lines and `access forbidden by rule` entries (the [PS-512](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-512/health-page-nginx-source-ip-gate-on-aws-uat) health allow-list doing its job), no startup failure.
* **Probably not the certbot hooks.** The box has:
  * `/etc/letsencrypt/renewal-hooks/pre/stop-nginx.sh` → `docker compose … stop nginx`
  * `/etc/letsencrypt/renewal-hooks/post/start-nginx.sh` → `docker compose … start nginx`

  That is the obvious suspect, but it does not fit for two reasons. First, `RestartCount` **counts restarts made by the restart policy** (`unless-stopped`), and a deliberate `docker compose stop` marks the container as user-stopped rather than incrementing it. Second, the rate is wrong: certbot runs at most 2–4×/day here, against an observed \~47/day. The certificate is also nowhere near due (`dev-ps.secuura.net`, expires 2026-11-12, 62 days out), so renewals were not firing repeatedly.

## Worth fixing regardless: certbot is scheduled twice

Independent of the restarts, certbot is registered through **both** mechanisms on this box:

* `/etc/cron.d/certbot` — `0 */12 * * * root test -x /usr/bin/certbot -a ! -d /run/systemd/system && … certbot -q renew`
* `certbot.timer` (systemd) — last run 2026-09-10 02:43 UTC

The cron entry guards itself with `! -d /run/systemd/system`, so on a systemd host it should no-op and only the timer should act. Worth confirming that guard actually holds here rather than assuming it, since a double-scheduled renewal that runs the stop/start hooks twice is a self-inflicted outage window on a box people are testing against.

## Next diagnostic step, if it recurs

`docker events` retains nothing useful this long after the fact (a 48 h query returned no nginx events), so the restart timestamps are gone. To catch it next time:

1. Check the Docker daemon's journal for the window — `journalctl -u docker --since …` records container death and restart-policy actions, and outlives `docker events`.
2. Correlate against `sysstat` (`sar`), which is already collecting on this box every 10 minutes, to see whether the restarts line up with load, memory or network events.
3. If it is reproducible, the useful question is *who signalled nginx* — a clean exit 0 every \~30 minutes suggests something issuing a stop, not nginx falling over.

## Impact

None observed. nginx has been stable for over two days, serves the site correctly, and dev-ps passed a full functional check immediately after the most recent deploy. Filed for the record and for the double-scheduled certbot, not because anything is currently broken.

Found while verifying a dev-ps deploy.

## Acceptance

* **The double-scheduled certbot is fixed, and that is the one actionable half.** `/etc/cron.d/certbot` and `certbot.timer` are both registered on `server-vm-dev`. The cron entry's `! -d /run/systemd/system` guard is **tested on this box** rather than assumed — run the guard expression and record its result — and whichever mechanism is redundant is removed. A double renewal runs the `stop-nginx.sh` / `start-nginx.sh` hooks twice, which is a self-inflicted outage window on a box people test against.
* **The renewal hooks are reviewed** while they are open: a `docker compose stop` / `start` pair around certbot means every renewal takes the site down briefly. Record whether that is intended or whether a reload would do.
* **The 939 restarts are recorded as unexplained, not guessed.** The three ruled-out causes stay on the ticket with their evidence — `OOMKilled = false` and a comfortable host, **exit code 0** (a clean SIGTERM/SIGQUIT, so not a config error), and the certbot hooks not fitting either the counter's semantics (a deliberate `docker compose stop` marks the container user-stopped rather than incrementing `RestartCount`) or the rate (2–4/day scheduled against \~47/day observed, with the cert 62 days from expiry). Closing this by asserting the hooks did it would be a guess; say "cause unexplained" instead.
* **The diagnostic recipe is left in place for a recurrence**, because `docker events` has already aged out: the Docker daemon's journal (`journalctl -u docker --since …`) records container death and restart-policy actions and outlives `docker events`; `sar` is already collecting every 10 minutes on this box for correlation against load, memory and network. The useful question is recorded as **who signalled nginx** — a clean exit 0 every \~30 minutes suggests something issuing a stop, not nginx falling over.
* **A recurrence would be noticed.** `RestartCount` on `secuura-dk-nginx-1` is sampled on a schedule (even a cron line that mails when it moves), so the next burst is observed while the evidence still exists rather than reconstructed 20 days later. This is the gap that made the ticket unresolvable, and it is the part worth fixing.
* **It is explicitly acceptable to close this with no root cause** — the impact is nil (nginx stable for over two days, site serving correctly, a full functional check passed after the most recent deploy), the counter has been static at 939 across four readings including two 20 s apart, and the burst ended 2026-09-08 06:06 UTC. What must **not** happen is closing it without the certbot fix and without the sampling.
* **No Playwright spec — it is the wrong tool here:** the subject is a container restart counter, a systemd timer and a cron entry on an Azure VM the suite cannot reach, with **no product behaviour involved and no user-visible symptom to assert**; the site was serving correctly throughout. The verifiable criteria are the guard-expression result, the removal of the redundant scheduler, the recorded `RestartCount` sampling, and the diagnostic recipe above.

title: No migration in this repo is retry-safe after a partial MySQL failure — non-transactional DDL leaves columns applied and the migration unrecorded, so every restart dies on "Duplicate column"
description:
Recorded as an open item on [Secuura/platform-s#809](https://linear.app/secuura/review/ps-749-recipients-act-on-shared-documents-identity-re-share-grant-25e5dd30a147) ("Separate ticket") and raised at review because nothing in Linear covered it ([PS-777](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-777/ef-migrations-remove-reverts-the-model-snapshot-too-far-the-next) is the adjacent snapshot-revert hazard, not this).

## What happened

`Ps749_ShareAncestry` carried `CHECK (ParentLinkId IS NULL OR ParentLinkId < Id)`. MySQL refuses any CHECK that names an AUTO_INCREMENT column, so the migration failed part-way — **after** its `AddColumn`s had applied. MySQL DDL is non-transactional, so the columns stayed, `__EFMigrationsHistory` never recorded the migration, and every subsequent boot re-ran it and died on `Duplicate column name 'Depth'` (24 restarts, exit 133). The in-memory xUnit provider cannot see any of this; it was found on the first boot against a real database.

## Why it is a class, not one migration

Every migration in `ssd/Migrations/` has the same shape: several DDL statements, no guard. Any one of them that fails after its first statement bricks the stack the same way, and the only recovery is a hand-run `DROP COLUMN` (or a `--reset`, which is not an option on UAT/prod). The [PS-749](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-749/document-share-and-other-functions) instance was caught because it was unreleased; a released one would be an outage.

## Suggested work

1. **Make the migrations idempotent** for the statements that can partially apply: `IF NOT EXISTS` guards on `AddColumn` / `CreateIndex` / `AddForeignKey` via raw SQL where EF's MySQL provider does not emit them, or a small `MigrationBuilder` extension that checks `information_schema` first.
2. **A startup diagnostic**: when `MigrateAsync` throws, log which migration and which statement, and whether `__EFMigrationsHistory` is behind the schema (the "columns present, row absent" signature), so the next person does not re-derive it from a crash loop.
3. **A contract test** that no migration's `Up()` contains a `CHECK` naming an auto-increment key (already on #809 as `No_check_constraint_anywhere_names_an_auto_increment_key`) — and, more generally, that every `Up()` is re-runnable against a schema where it half-applied. That second half needs a real MySQL, so it belongs in the live gate, not xUnit.

## Acceptance

* **The reproduction exists and is written down before any fix.** On a claimed slot: apply a migration, **hand-remove its** `__EFMigrationsHistory` **row** (the "columns present, row absent" signature MySQL's non-transactional DDL leaves behind), restart the stack — and record the crash: `Duplicate column name '…'`, the restart count, the exit code. Today that is a crash loop; a fix is only demonstrable against a captured failure.
* **The statements that can partially apply are made idempotent** — `IF NOT EXISTS` guards on `AddColumn` / `CreateIndex` / `AddForeignKey`, via raw SQL where EF's MySQL provider does not emit them, or a small `MigrationBuilder` extension that checks `information_schema` first. The criterion is re-runnability, not the mechanism.
* **After the fix, the same reproduction comes up** rather than crash-looping, and the history row is **re-recorded** — so the next restart is a no-op. Both the come-up and the re-record are asserted; coming up with the row still missing just defers the problem.
* **A startup diagnostic names the fault** when `MigrateAsync` throws: which migration, which statement, and whether `__EFMigrationsHistory` is behind the schema — so the next person does not re-derive it from a crash loop (shared with [PS-777](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-777/ef-migrations-remove-reverts-the-model-snapshot-too-far-the-next)'s diagnostic; implement once).
* **The** `CHECK`**-on-auto-increment contract test lands** — `No_check_constraint_anywhere_names_an_auto_increment_key`, already on #809 — in `tests/ssd.UnitTests`, red against the original `Ps749_ShareAncestry` shape and green against the corrected one. That is a **rule**, so it belongs in the xUnit estate: two minutes, nothing up.
* The claim "every migration in `ssd/Migrations/` has the same shape" is **checked rather than asserted**: the audit is run and its result recorded — how many migrations contain more than one DDL statement with no guard. If some are already safe, say which, because the scope of the idempotency work depends on it.
* **No Playwright spec — it is the wrong tool here:** a half-applied schema has no UI, the app never finishes starting, and there is nothing for a browser to assert. The split is explicit: the `CHECK` rule is **xUnit**; the re-runnability half needs a **real MySQL with prior state**, which the in-memory provider cannot model at all, so it is a **scripted migrate → interrupt → re-migrate reproduction on a claimed slot** (the steps above), run as part of the live gate and its output pasted onto the PR — not a spec file. `--reset` is not available as a recovery on UAT or prod, which is why this has to be provably safe rather than merely tested.

## Verify

On a claimed slot: apply a migration, hand-drop its history row (simulating the partial failure), restart — the stack must come up rather than crash-loop, and the row must be re-recorded.

title: CONFIG DRIFT: two tracked env templates disagree by ~39 vars — bootstrap-env.sh reads .env.example, CLAUDE.md documents env.example
description:
**BLUF —** `Blockchain/Dev/` **carries TWO tracked env templates that disagree by \~39 variables, and the two consumers read different ones:** `scripts/bootstrap-env.sh` **reads** `.env.example` **while the project** `CLAUDE.md` **documents** `env.example`**. A developer who follows the docs and a developer who runs the script get different environments.**

## Measured

| file | lines | vars (`^[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]*=`) | tracked |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| `Blockchain/Dev/env.example` | 444 | **103** | yes |
| `Blockchain/Dev/.env.example` | 302 | **64** | yes |

They are **separate files**, not a symlink or hardlink — different inodes (13295153 / 13295132).

**Consumers disagree:**

* `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/bootstrap-env.sh:26` — `ENV_EXAMPLE="$DEV_DIR/.env.example"`, and it errors with *".env.example not found"* / succeeds with *"Created .env from .env.example"*.
* The project `CLAUDE.md` documents `cp Blockchain/Dev/env.example Blockchain/Dev/.env`.

**Divergence is substantial, not cosmetic.** Variables present in one and absent from the other include `ADMIN_USER_EMAIL`, `ADMIN_USER_PASSWORD`, `ALLOW_DEFAULT_SEED_PASSWORDS`, `ENABLE_DEMO_SEED`, `ENCRYPTION_SALT`, `ENTRA_CLIENT_ID`/`ENTRA_CLIENT_SECRET`, `BACKUP_RETENTION_DAYS`, `API_BASE_URL` — against `API_GATEWAY_PORT`, `AUTH0_*`, `AZURE_AD_*`, `BILLING_SERVICE_URL`, `ENABLE_TEST_TOKENS` in the other direction. **Several are security-relevant gates** (`ALLOW_DEFAULT_SEED_PASSWORDS`, `ENABLE_DEMO_SEED`, `ENABLE_TEST_TOKENS`), so which template a developer copies determines which gates they even know exist.

## Class — this is the KS-1077 shape

**Two competing sources of truth for the same configuration, where each consumer picks one and nobody reconciles them.** That is exactly [KS-1077](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1077)'s two npm-audit allow-lists, where Kam ruled `one-list-triage-two` (2026-09-10 11:29) — make the local triage record the single source. **Worth resolving as ONE decision with KS-1077 rather than twice**, because the same ruling shape almost certainly applies: name one file the source, and reconcile the other into it.

## How it surfaced

Found 2026-09-10 (seat s170) doing the KS-1041 Step 2 config-drift pass required by the PR verification protocol Kam adopted the same day (§3b: *"a var read in code but absent from the template is a finding"*). Adding `GATEWAY_VOUCH_SECRET` meant choosing a template — and there were two.

## Explicitly NOT done

**No winner picked.** The var was added to **both** templates in [PR #951](<https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/951>) so neither consumer is left short, but reconciling the files is a decision about which is authoritative and what the \~39-var delta means — not a drive-by edit. **Scoped and evidenced only.**

Related: KS-1041, KS-1077.

title: SECURITY (local test stack): akto-autoheal runs as root with /var/run/docker.sock RW — env-scoping is only as strong as who holds the socket
description:
**BLUF —** `akto-autoheal` **runs as uid=0 root with** `/var/run/docker.sock` **mounted read-write, which grants host-equivalent read of EVERY container's environment through the daemon API and therefore defeats environment-variable scoping as a security control — but it is confined to the local Akto test harness: it sits on network** `akto_default` **rather than the platform's** `dev_secuura-network`**, and it is defined only in** `systemTest/akto/docker-compose.yml`**, so it does not exist on demo or kintsugi.**

The bound is in that sentence deliberately. A reader who stops after the first clause should not walk away believing this is live on a VM, and a reader who stops after the second should not walk away believing it is nothing.

## What was measured

| probe | result |
| -- | -- |
| containers with a bind mount of `/var/run/docker.sock` | **1 —** `akto-autoheal` (`willfarrell/autoheal:1.2.0`), mount **RW=true** |
| its user | `uid=0(root) gid=0(root)`, `Config.User` empty |
| tooling present inside it | `curl` **PRESENT**, `wget` **PRESENT** (no `docker` CLI, which is not a mitigation — the daemon API is HTTP over that socket) |
| its networks | `akto_default` — **not** `dev_secuura-network` |
| defining compose file | `systemTest/akto/docker-compose.yml` only |
| occurrences of `autoheal` in `Blockchain/Dev/docker-compose.yml` (the file the VMs run) | **0** |

**Controls, so the zeros discriminate:**

* The bind-mount scan enumerates and prints **all six** distinct bind sources across the 38 running containers (`docker/init`, `docker/init-platform`, `docker/seed`, one `secuura-api.yaml`, one `nginx-demo.conf`, `/var/run/docker.sock`) — so it can see bind mounts, and the absence of a repo-root or `.env` mount is a real null.
* The `0` for `autoheal` in the VM compose file is measured against a positive control in the same file: `originate` returns **1**. So the grep matches when the string is there.

## Why this matters beyond the container itself

**It is the general case of the specific control being shipped in KS-1041 Step 2.** That work scopes a gateway-vouch secret to exactly two of 34 containers by declaring it per-service, and verifies the scoping by probing container environments. **Any container with root + RW** `docker.sock` **can read those same environments through the daemon regardless of how narrowly they were declared** — so env-scoping is a control whose strength is bounded by who holds the socket, and nothing today records that dependency.

That is why this is filed separately rather than inside the KS-1041 PR: a finding about the estate's secret-handling as a class, buried in another ticket's PR description, is discoverable only by someone reading that PR, and it outlives the change that surfaced it.

## Explicitly NOT proposed

No fix, no privilege change, no compose edit. Changing a test stack's privileges was outside the commission this was found under and outside the current deploy grant. **Scoped and evidenced only — the remedy is a decision for whoever picks this up.**

## Provenance

Found 2026-09-10 (seat s170) while measuring the blast radius of the KS-1041 Step 2 vouch secret, at Wednesday's instruction to establish who can read it before building a control that depends on it. All readings taken read-only against the running local stack; nothing was changed.

Related: KS-1041 (the specific control this generalises).

nodes.body:
**Risk classification — this lands in Peter's §1b "systemTest gate / report / baseline logic" high-risk class.**

Added per Wednesday's routing note, because the class is not obvious from the title. `akto-autoheal` is part of the **Akto systemTest harness**, and a root container holding a read-write `docker.sock` alongside that harness sits squarely in the "gate / report / baseline logic" band — the band where a compromise does not merely leak, it can rewrite what a gate reports.

Under the PR verification protocol Kam adopted 2026-09-10, that classification means any change here needs the full reviewer pass rather than a spot-check. **Recording the class now so whoever picks it up does not have to re-derive it — and note the ticket still asks for scoping and a decision, not a fix.**

title: kintsugi lost demo-service to the KS-641 fail-closed gate — the flag is unset on BOTH boxes and enabling it is a one-line decision with no owner
description:
**BLUF — kintsugi served** `demo-service` **for 20 hours and now refuses to start it. That is KS-641's fail-closed gate working correctly, not a bug. The point of this ticket is that the box lost a running service and the decision to restore it has no owner.**

Found during the s169 whole-estate rebuild of kintsugi (KS-601, under Kam's 2026-09-10 15:24 AEST ruling).

## What changed

|  | before the rebuild | after |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `secuura-demo-service` on kintsugi | `Up 20 hours (healthy)` (measured 05:35Z) | `restarting`**, exit 1, 18 restarts** |
| image | `62fb55bf4fa1` (2026-08-19) | `c4823b0d2fc1` (2026-09-10) |

Log, every restart:

```
FATAL: DEMO_SERVICE_ENABLED must be exactly "true" to run demo-service.
This is a deliberate opt-in, not a default — refusing to start.
```

**The swap itself succeeded** — the container is on the new image. The service declines to start.

## Why — and why it is not a regression in the code

**KS-641** ("inbound auth + fail-closed non-prod gate on demo-service") introduced the gate. `DEMO_SERVICE_ENABLED` is **unset on both kintsugi and demo**. The old image kintsugi was running had no such check, which is why it served for 20 hours — *it ran because the gate did not exist yet, which is the defect KS-641 fixed, not a capability that was lost.*

On **demo** this is the status quo, already recorded in the s168 handover as *"a deliberate opt-in guard working as designed"*. **On kintsugi it is new**, because kintsugi was three weeks behind and had never received KS-641.

## The decision, and why it is deliberately not taken here

`DEMO_SERVICE_ENABLED` **stays OFF** — ruled 2026-09-10, on three grounds: it matches demo (and Kam ruled the same day that *"everything that we do this week is replicated and fixed on both servers"*, making parity an instruction); OFF is the gate's own intent as a fail-closed opt-in; and OFF is the branch that requires no signature, since enabling a fail-closed non-prod auth gate is a config change with a security shape.

**So this ticket is not a request to flip the flag.** It exists because a service that was serving is now not, on both boxes, and *"enabling it is a one-line change nobody has decided to make"* is precisely the kind of state that gets rediscovered by accident weeks later.

## What is needed

1. **A decision with a stated reason** on whether `demo-service` should run on either box at all — or a decision that it should not, recorded so the next rebuild does not re-raise this.
2. If it should run: set `DEMO_SERVICE_ENABLED=true` in that box's `.env` (gitignored, so this is a per-box config action, not a code change) and recreate the container.

## Note on classification, recorded because it cost a correction

This was initially reported as *"the known demo-service down"*. **That classification was borrowed from the s168 record of DEMO and applied to KINTSUGI, a different box, where nothing had established it.** The mechanism was evidenced; the *expectation* was not. Flagged here so the distinction survives: on demo this is status quo, on kintsugi it is a state change.

⚠ The rebuild did not hide it — the swap ran with an exception keyed to the **failure signature** (`DEMO_SERVICE_ENABLED must be exactly`), not the service name, so the same service failing for any other reason still halts the run. Every hit is recorded in `.rebuild/blocked.txt` on the box.

nodes.body:
**`secuura-demo-service` stopped on BOTH boxes, per Kam's 2026-09-05 ruling** (card
`secuura-demo-service-crash-loop` = "stop — docker stop it", 14:53; his panel the same day, 16:42:
*"docker stop only, docker start is the undo, nothing else"*). `docker stop` was the only command run —
no env change, no compose edit, no `rm`.

**What it was doing.** Crash-looping once every ~62 seconds, always the same line:

```
FATAL: DEMO_SERVICE_ENABLED must be exactly "true" to run demo-service.
This is a deliberate opt-in, not a default — refusing to start.
```

| | demo | kintsugi |
|---|---|---|
| `RestartCount` at stop | **20,022** | **19,232** |
| container created | 2026-09-10 | (same vintage) |
| `ExitCode` | 1 | 1 |
| after `docker stop` | `exited`, RestartCount **unchanged** | `exited`, RestartCount **unchanged** |
| log lines in the following 2 min | **0** | **0** |

Read back ~2.5 minutes after the stop on each box: still `exited`, count still frozen, no new lines —
so the loop is genuinely stopped, not merely between restarts. Undo is `docker start
secuura-demo-service` on either box.

**Why it came back, and the line the next deploy seat needs.** The container is `restart:
unless-stopped`, and a deploy **recreates** it, which discards the "manually stopped" flag. So every
