title: Person.IdToken1/2/3 are not an identity record — make the wallet (IdentityProfile / Did / VerifiableCredential) the source of truth, have the resolver and the Entra completion read and write it, and freeze the three columns
description:
Asked by Stuart on 2026-09-10, reviewing an Entra-verified person's row on dev-ps: *"the current person has a set of three ID tokens in the database row … is this enough?"* The answer is no — they are enough to say "this person once completed Entra Verified ID as this DID", and that is all they say. The status resolver's own comments already call them legacy.

## What the three columns hold today (`Person.IdToken1/2/3`, each `varchar(256)`, plus `IdVerifiedOn`)

| Column | Holds | Written by | Note |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| `IdToken1` | the Entra `oid` from an SSO sign-in | Entra external signup | an SSO subject, not a verification; `GooglePrefillService` / `GitHubPrefillService` deliberately refuse to write their subject ids into it because "Person.IdToken1 currently means Entra oid" |
| `IdToken2` | the Verified ID credential id (the presentation's `jti`) | `EntraVerifiedIdService.RecordVerificationAsync` | **NULL for both verified people on dev-ps** — Microsoft's presentation carries no `jti` (PS-802) |
| `IdToken3` | the subject DID (`did:jwk:…`) | same | the person's public key stored as an opaque string; \~230 chars for P-256, so it fits — an RSA `did:jwk` is 400+ and would not |
| `IdVerifiedOn` | the completion stamp | same | what `IdentityStatusResolver` keys the Entra level on (`EntraVerifiedIdLevel`) |

Readers: `IdentityStatusResolver` (level from `IdVerifiedOn`, issuer from the `KycVerification` row, DID from `IdToken3`), `EntraVerifiedIdService.GetPersonVerificationInfoAsync`, `EntraIdentityBackfillService` (imports 3 → `Did`, 2 → `VerifiableCredential`), the two erasure services (null all three).

## Why it is not enough

1. **Fixed arity.** One provider, one credential, one DID. A second verification, a re-issued credential, a second DID has nowhere to go but overwriting. Stripe IDV already had to grow its own columns (`IdvLevel`, `IdvVerifiedOn`) for the same reason.
2. **Nothing about the credential.** The issuer DID lives on `KycVerification`, not the person; there is no type, level, issued-at, expiry, revocation state, or the presentation that proved it. `VerifiableCredential` has all of those.
3. **Nothing about the key.** A `did:jwk` *is* key material; `Did` carries method, controller, activation and deactivation. `IdToken3` carries a string.
4. **The 256-character trap** above.
5. **Three unrelated concepts under one name and one erasure path** — which is how `IdToken1` came to mean something different from its neighbours, and why every new provider has to reason about which column is safe to touch.

## Wanted — the wallet is the source of truth

The designed model exists: `IdentityProfile` → `Did` → `VerifiableCredential` (PS-350 … PS-378), and PS-790 / PS-432 already mirror the columns into it on completion and on backfill; PS-802 closes the no-`jti` gap. Finish the move:

1. `IdentityStatusResolver` **reads the wallet and** `KycVerification`, not `IdVerifiedOn` / `IdToken2` / `IdToken3`: level from the approved verifications (as it already does for the native flow) and the imported profile; DID from `Did`; issuer from the verification row. Same answer on every surface (PS-789 made them agree; this removes the second source).
2. `EntraVerifiedIdService.RecordVerificationAsync` **writes the wallet directly** (profile, DID, credential — through the same `BackfillPersonAsync` path) and stops writing `IdToken2` / `IdToken3`; `GetPersonVerificationInfoAsync` reads the wallet.
3. `IdToken2` **/** `IdToken3` **frozen as compatibility stamps** — still nulled by erasure, no new writers, a migration later drops them once nothing reads them. `IdToken1` renamed for what it is (`ExternalSubjectId` or similar) or moved onto the `AspNetUserLogins` row that already keys on it; the prefill services' refusal note goes with it.
4. **A backfill pass on deploy** (the PS-432 button already does it) so existing Entra-verified people have wallet rows before the resolver switches.

## Out of scope

Organisation.`IdToken1/2` (tenant id / verified domain) — a separate legacy pair with its own reader (`OrgTrustEvidence.HasLegacy*`), tracked with the ExternalTenant registry work.

## Verify

* dev-ps, [stuart@obeden.com](<mailto:stuart@obeden.com>) and [peter@obeden.com](<mailto:peter@obeden.com>): dashboard card, `/identity/verify`, `/EntraVerify` and the wallet all agree, with `IdToken2` / `IdToken3` nulled by hand — the resolver no longer needs them.
* A fresh Entra completion writes profile + DID (+ credential) and nothing to `IdToken2` / `IdToken3`.
* Erasure still clears everything the person's identity touched.

## Acceptance

* `IdentityStatusResolver` answers from the **wallet** (`IdentityProfile` → `Did` → `VerifiableCredential`) plus `KycVerification`, and no longer reads `IdVerifiedOn` / `IdToken2` / `IdToken3`. One source, same answer on every surface.
* `EntraVerifiedIdService.RecordVerificationAsync` writes the wallet through the same `BackfillPersonAsync` path and **stops writing** `IdToken2` / `IdToken3`; `GetPersonVerificationInfoAsync` reads the wallet.
* `IdToken2` / `IdToken3` are frozen compatibility stamps — still nulled by both erasure services, **no new writers**, and a grep shows no reader outside the backfill importer. `IdToken1` is renamed for what it is (an external SSO subject id) or moved onto the `AspNetUserLogins` row, carrying the prefill services' refusal note with it.
* The backfill pass runs before the resolver switches, so an existing Entra-verified person does not lose their level at deploy.
* Erasure still clears everything the person's identity touched — profile, DID, credential **and** the frozen columns — asserted, not assumed.
* **xUnit companion** (the rule half, where most of this belongs — fast, no stack): resolver tests over a person with wallet rows and **NULL** `IdVerifiedOn` / `IdToken2` / `IdToken3` returning the correct level, issuer and DID; a person with only the legacy columns and no wallet rows returning the pre-backfill answer the migration expects; and a contract test that `Person.IdToken2` / `IdToken3` appear in no write path other than erasure. Multiple DIDs and multiple credentials per person must each have somewhere to go — the fixed-arity complaint above — so pin a second credential and a second DID resolving without overwriting the first.

**Playwright test that demonstrates the fix** (required — the claim is "the same answer on every surface", and only a browser can check the surfaces agree): **extend** `systemTest/tests/functional/identity_wallet.spec.ts` (it already owns the holder wallet card and the verifiable-credentials view and asserts the surface rather than specific data) and lean on `identity_status_journey.spec.ts` for the cross-surface agreement it already walks. Against a live stack, for a person whose wallet holds a DID and a credential but whose `IdToken2` / `IdToken3` have been **nulled**, assert:

1. **the previously failing case** — `identity-wallet-did` is non-empty and `identity-wallet-credential-<credentialId>` is present; today the resolver takes the DID from `IdToken3`, so with that column null the wallet surface has nothing to show and this assertion fails on `develop`;
2. `identity-wallet-assurance` and `current-assurance-status` report the **same** level for that person with the legacy columns null — the single-source claim, also failing today;
3. a completion driven through `/EntraVerify` (`entraverify-start-verification-btn` → the local `Rejected` outcome, per the Entra-on-localhost note) still lands the person on a wallet that renders — i.e. the new write path does not break the flow's own surface;
4. **control, passes today and must keep passing:** `identity-wallet-none` / `identity-wallet-empty` still render for a person with no credentials, the credentials view still loads with `credentials-tab-vc-link` active, and the dashboard assurance card still agrees with `/identity/verify` for an **unchanged** verified person — the agreement [PS-789](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-789/the-dashboard-id-card-and-the-hosted-verification-pages-disagree-with) established must not regress while the second source is removed.

It must fail on today's `develop` and pass after the change.

title: No Playwright e2e test has run on any PR since 2026-09-07 — the suite dies at a static lint gate before any browser opens, and the job name hides it
description:
**BLUF — no Playwright test has executed on any PR since 2026-09-07. The** `Playwright suite` **job goes red at a static lint gate that runs BEFORE any browser opens, so the red names the wrong subject and the coverage hole has been invisible for three days.**

This is a **test-coverage** ticket, not a CI-config ticket. It was found while measuring CI gate failures (KS-1075) but must not be closed as gate tuning: the gate is a symptom, the missing e2e coverage is the defect.

## What happens

`Playwright suite` (job in `.github/workflows/pr-platform-suites.yml`) fails at **step 6, "Quality gate — static (tsc/ESLint/Prettier/knip/audit)"**. That step runs `npm run format:check && npm run lint && …` ahead of the suite. It exits 1, so **the job stops before a single browser test runs.**

```
  27:1  error  Missing JSDoc @param "label" declaration  jsdoc/require-param
  27:1  error  Missing JSDoc @throws declaration         jsdoc/require-throws
  27:1  error  Missing JSDoc @example declaration        jsdoc/require-example
  48:1  error  Missing JSDoc comment                     jsdoc/require-jsdoc
✖ 4 problems (4 errors, 0 warnings)
```

All four in `systemTest/playwright/global-setup.ts`. Prettier passes cleanly — it is the ESLint jsdoc rules alone. ESLint's own output says **3 of the 4 are** `--fix`**-able**.

## Why it hid — the part worth keeping

**The job's name names the wrong subject.** "Playwright suite :: failure" reads as *browser tests ran and failed*. Nobody re-reads a suite they believe is already running. The same shape as a wrapper printing a banner it did not earn: the red was true, and what it implied was false.

## Proven pre-existing, with controls

* Measured identically on **two unrelated PRs** — #938 (one nginx `location` block, zero service code) and #939 (TypeScript type declarations in one service): same rules, same line numbers, same count.
* `global-setup.ts` is touched by **neither** — 0 hits in each diff, against controls of 4 and 3 files actually touched.
* Last changed `42e778203`, **2026-09-07**, *"KS-969 round 2: a role collapse is not a success…"* — three days before either PR.

## What needs doing

1. Fix the four jsdoc errors in `systemTest/playwright/global-setup.ts` (3 are `--fix`-able).
2. **Then confirm the suite actually runs and report what it finds** — three days of unrun e2e may be hiding real failures. A green job after the lint fix is not the same as a suite that was green all along, and it must not be reported as one.
3. Consider whether a static lint gate belongs *ahead* of the suite in the same job at all: as configured, any lint error in the harness silently converts "e2e coverage" into "no e2e coverage" while still reporting a normal-looking red.

## Related

Found during KS-1075 (CI gate measurement, commissioned by Kam as `measure-then-decide`). KS-1075 covers the two *other* gate causes — a `bash -e` swallowed diagnostic and an empty npm-audit allow-list — and should not absorb this one.

nodes.body:
**Verify-only record (2026-09-14, s215) — measured from the live Actions runs, not re-run; no edit, no state move. Assigned to the board account (was unassigned).**

**Item 1 — the four jsdoc errors in `systemTest/playwright/global-setup.ts`: already fixed on develop.** Commit `6a047445b` ("reunite globalSetup with its docblock — playwright lint is red on develop"), merged via PR #896 (`38a919d40`, 2026-09-11). Live confirmation: on develop's own push at `8861e6216`, `pr` run 34755906547 / job `Playwright suite` 103721950421, **step 6 `Quality gate — static (tsc/ESLint/Prettier/knip/audit)` = SUCCESS**. Same at the 2026-09-13 PR heads that ran since.

**Item 2 — "confirm the suite actually runs and report": it does not, and the reason has moved one step later.** In the same job, **step 7 `Quality gate — unit suite (test:unit)` FAILS** on the Playwright harness's own unit test — `✖ assertSlotNamedForLocalTarget › refuses every slot's gateway when no slot is named, naming both forms of the slot command` (`AssertionError: Missing expected exception: slot 1`; expected `/^Error: No stack slot named…SECUURA_STACK_SLOT=2 npx playwright test --project=api…/`). Steps 8 `Boot isolated platform stack`, 9 `Install Playwright browser engine`, 10 `Run Playwright API tests` are **SKIPPED**; step 11 uploads nothing (`No files were found with the provided path: systemTest/playwright/results/`). **So no browser test has executed at M18** — this ticket's own sentence ("a green job after the lint fix is not the same as a suite that was green all along") is the finding, one gate further on. **The newest record confirms it (2026-09-14):** the `pr` run 34785721735 at PR #942's head `53b9c3cc1` (= its branch + develop `8861e6216`), job `Playwright suite` 103802165697 — step 6 static SUCCESS, **step 7 FAILURE on the same one cell** (`ℹ tests 348 · pass 347 · fail 1`: `assertSlotNamedForLocalTarget › refuses every slot's gateway when no slot is named…`, `Missing expected exception: slot 1`), steps 8–10 SKIPPED, step 11 `No files were found … systemTest/playwright/results/`. Same at develop's own M18 push run. The unit test is the harness's own (`systemTest/playwright/**`), not a product test.

**Item 3 — whether a static gate belongs ahead of the suite:** a workflow-design call, Kam's; not taken here.

**Board search** for the failing symbol before recording: `assertSlotNamedForLocalTarget` 0 hits (nonsense-token control 0). The `systemTest/playwright/**` unit suite belongs to no current lane; whether a ticket is filed for the step-7 red is the coordinator's call. **Not closed as gate tuning** — nothing here changes what the job enforces.

title: A domain-verified organisation should own a did:web on its verified domain — today every organisation is minted a did:key, provisioning never asks for did:web, and the well-known endpoint serves only the platform's own DID
description:
Asked by Stuart on dev-ps, 2026-09-10, after provisioning the six unprovisioned organisations and reviewing the Identity management → Organisations tab: every organisation, DomainVerified or not, shows a `did:key:z6Mk…`.

## What exists

| Piece | Ticket | State |
| -- | -- | -- |
| DID service: mint / resolve / update / deactivate for `did:key` **and** `did:web` (`DidService.CreateAsync(method, …, webDomain)`) | [PS-360](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-360/t11-did-create-resolve-update-deactivate-didweb-didkey) | Done |
| Organisation identity provisioning + DomainVerified derived from the SSO tenant / verified domain | [PS-427](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-427/identity-provision-organisation-identity-derive-domainverified-from) | Done — but `IdentityProfileService.GetOrCreateForOrganisationAsync` always calls `_dids.CreateAsync(DidService.MethodKey, …)`: `did:key`, never `did:web`, whatever the trust level |
| The platform's own `did:web` and the two well-known documents it resolves to (`/.well-known/did.json`, `/.well-known/did-configuration.json`, file-backed, `WellKnownController`) | [PS-684](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-684/entra-verified-id-azure-tenant-setup-and-config-values-needed-before) | In progress — serves the **platform's** DID only |
| DIF domain-linkage verifier (given a domain and a DID, is the linkage published and validly signed?) | [PS-775](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-775/verify-a-domains-well-known-did-configuration-dif-domain-linkage-the) | Done |
| A verified linkage granting DomainVerified | [PS-776](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-776/let-a-verified-domain-linkage-count-as-organisation-evidence-and-show) | Backlog |

So: a `did:web` can be minted, a linkage can be verified, and the platform can publish its own — but nothing gives an **organisation** a `did:web` on **its** domain, and nothing links one it already has.

## Wanted

A DomainVerified organisation can hold `did:web:<its verified domain>` as its organisation DID, and the platform's records, credentials and admin screens use it.

Two routes, both probably needed:

1. **Bring your own.** The organisation already publishes `did:web:<domain>` (its own `did.json` and `did-configuration.json` on its domain — e.g. an Entra Verified ID issuer). It gives the platform the DID; the platform runs the [PS-775](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-775/verify-a-domains-well-known-did-configuration-dif-domain-linkage-the) verifier against the verified domain, and on a valid linkage records that DID against the organisation's identity profile. The keys stay the organisation's.
2. **Minted here, published there.** The platform mints `did:web:<domain>` for the organisation ([PS-360](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-360/t11-did-create-resolve-update-deactivate-didweb-didkey) already can) and hands the organisation the two documents to host on its domain; the DID becomes live once the [PS-775](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-775/verify-a-domains-well-known-did-configuration-dif-domain-linkage-the) verifier finds them published. Key custody stays with the platform's signing-key store, as for the platform's own `did:web`.

## Decisions this needs

* **What the existing** `did:key` **becomes.** Every organisation already has one and credentials may reference it. Options: keep it as the platform-internal controller and add the `did:web` as the public identifier (an `alsoKnownAs` / service entry on the DID document), or migrate. Migration touches every credential that names the org DID.
* **Where the record lives.** The `Did` row (method, value, controller organisation) already exists; the linkage result (domain, last checked, outcome) is the same thing [PS-776](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-776/let-a-verified-domain-linkage-count-as-organisation-evidence-and-show) needs to store — design once, use for both.
* **Only DomainVerified and above.** An Unverified organisation has no verified domain to bind to; the option must not appear for it, and TenantBlocked must still override ([PS-776](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-776/let-a-verified-domain-linkage-count-as-organisation-evidence-and-show)'s rule).
* **Where it surfaces.** Identity management → Organisations (DID column, today `did:key` for all nine on dev-ps), the organisation's own verification page (`/organisation/verify`), and [PS-803](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-803/an-organisation-created-with-no-name-a-consumer-identity-signup-ks-199)'s naming of unnamed organisations.

## Out of scope

Serving an organisation's DID documents **from the platform's domain** — a `did:web` is bound to the host it resolves on, so the platform can only ever serve `did:web:<platform domain>…`; the organisation's own domain has to publish its own.

## Verify

dev-ps: Obeden PTE Ltd (DomainVerified) holds `did:web:obeden.com` after publishing the documents (route 2) or after the platform verifies a DID it already publishes (route 1); the Organisations tab shows it; an Unverified organisation is not offered either route.

## Acceptance

* **The route is chosen and written down** — bring-your-own, minted-here-published-there, or both — together with what the existing `did:key` becomes (`alsoKnownAs` / service entry on the DID document, or a migration) and, if a migration, the list of credential kinds that name the org DID and have to move with it.
* `IdentityProfileService.GetOrCreateForOrganisationAsync` **stops hard-coding** `DidService.MethodKey`: the method follows the organisation's trust level and verified domain, and `DidService.CreateAsync(…, webDomain)` ([PS-360](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-360/t11-did-create-resolve-update-deactivate-didweb-didkey), already built) is the path taken for `did:web`.
* **The linkage record is designed once.** Domain, last-checked timestamp and outcome live in one place, shared with [PS-776](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-776/let-a-verified-domain-linkage-count-as-organisation-evidence-and-show) rather than duplicated — both tickets need the same row.
* **The offer is gated, in both directions:** only **DomainVerified** and above sees either route, **TenantBlocked** overrides regardless ([PS-776](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-776/let-a-verified-domain-linkage-count-as-organisation-evidence-and-show)'s rule), and an **Unverified** organisation is offered neither — asserted, not assumed, because an Unverified organisation has no verified domain to bind to.
* **The surfaces agree:** Identity management → Organisations shows `did:web:<domain>` in the DID column for an organisation that holds one (today it prints `did:key:z6Mk…` for all of them), and `/organisation/verify` shows the linkage state. Serving an organisation's DID documents from the platform's own domain stays out of scope, as above.
* **xUnit companion** (this is where the rules belong — two minutes, nothing up): the method-selection rule (trust level + verified domain → `did:key` or `did:web:<domain>`, and the TenantBlocked override), and the gating rule that an Unverified organisation is offered neither route. Both must be red before the change.

**Playwright test that demonstrates the fix** (required for the part that is a surface): **extend** `systemTest/tests/functional/organisation_verification.spec.ts` (it already owns `/organisation/verify`) and assert the admin column alongside it, rather than adding a spec. Against a live stack:

1. **the previously failing case** — as the AccountAdmin of a **DomainVerified** organisation, `/organisation/verify` offers the `did:web` route at all (confirm the testid when the control is added — none exists today, so there is nothing to name yet); on `develop` no such control is rendered and this assertion fails;
2. once a `did:web` is recorded, the organisation's row on `/IdentityAdmin/Organisations` (`identity-admin-org-row-…`) shows `did:web:` in its DID cell — also failing today, where every row shows `did:key:`;
3. as the AccountAdmin of an **Unverified** organisation, neither route is offered, and the control is absent rather than present-and-disabled;
4. **control, passes today and must keep passing:** every organisation still *has* a DID — an organisation with no verified domain keeps its `did:key` — and `identity-admin-org-trust` plus the `identity-admin-org-override-form` still behave as `identity_admin.spec.ts` asserts.

**Playwright is the wrong tool for the linkage itself** and must not be asked to prove it: a valid DIF domain linkage requires the organisation's own public domain to serve `did.json` and `did-configuration.json`, which no local slot can do. That half is verified on dev-ps by hand — Obeden PTE Ltd (DomainVerified) holding `did:web:obeden.com` with the [PS-775](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-775/verify-a-domains-well-known-did-configuration-dif-domain-linkage-the) verifier reporting a valid linkage — and recorded here with the verifier's output.

title: Per-tenant databases never receive the file migrations — CORE_MIGRATIONS FORCEs RLS with ZERO policies, so a per-tenant DB is dark on 5 core tables from boot 1 (permanent)
description:
## BLUF

**Per-tenant databases receive** `CORE_MIGRATIONS` **and NEVER the file migrations — not on any boot.** Measured, not read. The consequence is not "039 is missing": `CORE_MIGRATIONS` **enables and FORCEs** row-level security on five core tables while **every policy for them lives only in** `migrations/*.sql`, so a per-tenant DB lands with **FORCE RLS and ZERO policies**. A non-superuser runtime role then reads **zero rows** from `documents`, `certifications`, `audit_logs`, `custody_events` and `shares` — unconditionally, with no GUC able to fix it — and the boot log reports `{migrated: N, skipped: 0}`.

**Latent today, live the moment** `PROVISION_PER_TENANT_DB=true` — i.e. the moment KS-160 Path A (per-tenant-DB isolation) ships. This is a landmine directly under that roadmap item.

## The defect, in source

`services/api-gateway/src/startup-migrations.ts`

* **:932** `applyFileMigrations(pg, dbUrl, 'main', fileMigrations)`
* **:939** `applyFileMigrations(pg, platformDbUrl, 'platform', fileMigrations)`
* **:1108** `migrateDatabase(pg, tenantConnStr, tenantDbName, CORE_MIGRATIONS)` ← the tenant loop, **no** `applyFileMigrations` **call anywhere in it**

`applyFileMigrations`' own signature makes it structural, not an oversight in one call: `dbName: 'main' | 'platform'`. A tenant database is not a value that type admits, and the routing inside it (`if (dbName === 'main' && m.isPlatform) continue`) has no third branch.

**The trap is the split:** `CREATE POLICY` appears **0 times** in the whole of `startup-migrations.ts` (control: the same grep finds **19** in `migrations/*.sql`), while CORE_MIGRATIONS runs `ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY` + `FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY` at :439-440 (`custody_events`), :485-486 (`shares`), :551-552 (`documents`) and a `format()` loop at :633-634. **Enforcement ships in the array; permission ships in the files. Tenant DBs get only the array.**

The second path that can seed a tenant DB does not close the gap either: `services/tenant-provisioning/src/index.ts:62` `createTenantDatabase()` applies `INIT_SCRIPTS_DIR` (`docker/init`, bind-mounted at `docker-compose.yml:2038`) — **12 .sql files, 0** `CREATE POLICY`**, 0** `tenant_scope_bypass` (control: `migrations/` has 17 files with `CREATE POLICY`, 3 with `tenant_scope_bypass`).

## Measurement

Disposable `postgres:15-alpine`, SSL enabled with a locally-signed CA so the product's hard-coded `?sslmode=require` tenant connection could genuinely succeed. Product's own `runStartupMigrations()` driven from source; `startup-migrations.ts` blob verified **identical on** `origin/develop` **and HEAD** (`6a1b53bafa1ad707e663814f95ed92a668e96280`), `migrations/` identical too. Platform DB + main DB + one genuinely separate tenant DB (`tenant_alpha`). Four boots.

| read on `tenant_alpha` after 3 boots | value |
| -- | -- |
| public tables (**connection proof**) | **27** — `documents`, `users`, `anchor_store` all present |
| `_secuura_migrations` table exists | **0 — the file stage never ran, once** |
| `pg_policy` rows | **0** |
| tables with RLS **enabled** | **5** — all also `FORCE` |

**Same reader on the main DB (positive control):** `_secuura_migrations` **48 rows**, `039_rls_fail_closed.sql` **recorded**, `pg_policy` **28**, RLS tables **25**.

### The consequence, measured as an action (not asserted)

`secuuraadmin` is a superuser and bypasses RLS, so the owner read proves nothing. Re-measured as `s163_app` — `LOGIN NOBYPASSRLS`, non-superuser, the KS-109 runtime-role shape:

```
tenant_alpha  documents / certifications / audit_logs   ->  0 , 0 , 0
tenant_alpha  documents WITH both GUCs the product sets ->  0    (no policy exists to satisfy)
tenant_alpha  organizations (non-RLS table, 1 row)      ->  1    <- NON-ZERO CONTROL: login + grants work
superuser, row_security=off, tenant_alpha documents     ->  1    <- the row DOES exist
secuura       documents, NO GUC set                     ->  0
secuura       documents WITH app.tenant_scope_bypass    ->  1    <- DISCRIMINATION CONTROL
secuura       documents WITH app.current_tenant_id      ->  1
```

The zeros on `tenant_alpha` are real zeros, not an unreachable database: the same role, in the same database, reads 1 from a non-RLS table.

## Scope — honest in both directions

**REFUTED for the configuration running today.** `PROVISION_PER_TENANT_DB` defaults false (`services/tenant-provisioning/src/index.ts:245`), so every `tenant_config` row points at the shared app DB — which *does* get the file migrations via the `'main'` path. Confirmed in my own run: the 6 seeded tenants all carried `db_name = secuura`. **5 occurrences of the flag repo-wide, all code/comment, ZERO config sites** (control: `MULTI_TENANCY_ENABLED` appears in `docker-compose.yml`).

⚠ **NOT measured against demo or UAT** — both are held. The above is source + a local reproduction.

**CONFIRMED for per-tenant DBs.** Set the flag — or provision any tenant whose `db_name` differs from the app DB — and that tenant is dark on its five core tables from its first boot, permanently, with a success line in the log.

## Fix shape (not implemented here)

Give `applyFileMigrations` a tenant arm and call it from the loop before `migrateDatabase`, with the file corpus filtered the way `'main'` filters it. The `'main' | 'platform'` union is the thing to widen — an omission should stop compiling rather than be remembered. Any fix must also address the **ordering** KS-1054 documents (039 needs tables CORE creates), or a tenant DB simply reproduces the boot-1 window instead of the permanent one.

## Provenance

QA gate finding **F-928-3**, read-from-source and explicitly UNMEASURED, carried inside KS-1054. Measured here by s163 on 2026-09-09, local disposable containers only, removed at close. Demo, UAT and every shared database untouched.

---

## TLS: the tenant connection is VERIFY-FULL, and that is what makes F-928-4's counter load-bearing

**The product hard-codes** `?sslmode=require` **on the tenant connection string** (`startup-migrations.ts:1105`), and `pg-connection-string` **2.12.0 treats** `require` **as** `verify-full` — it says so itself at runtime: *"The SSL modes 'prefer', 'require', and 'verify-ca' are treated as aliases for 'verify-full'."* So the tenant loop does not merely want TLS; it requires a **CA-verifiable certificate chain and a matching hostname**.

**Proved both ways before any of the measurement above was trusted**, against the same container and the same connection-string shape:

```
no trusted CA   ->  "unable to verify the first certificate"
trusted CA      ->  connected, current_database() = tenant_alpha
```

That is why this ticket's zeros mean something: had I not stood the CA up, the tenant DB would have been unreachable and I would have measured my own container instead of the product.

**The consequence on a real deployment:** on any deployment whose tenant database does not present a CA-verifiable certificate, **the tenant loop connects to nothing at all** — and because of the counter defect below, the boot still logs `{migrated: N, skipped: 0}`.

### F-928-4 — the counter cannot report a failure under any condition (measured)

Registered a tenant pointing at `tenant_does_not_exist` — **proved absent** in `pg_database`, **proved present** in the loop's own `SELECT` — and booted:

```
[INFO] Tenant DB migrations complete {"migrated":8,"skipped":0,"total":8}
```

**Mechanism, to the line:** `migrateDatabase` (`startup-migrations.ts:800`) swallows every per-statement error in its own inner `try/catch` and returns `applied`, so it **never throws**, so the tenant loop's `catch` arm at `:1112` is **dead code**. And `new pg.Pool()` does not connect eagerly, so even total connection failure surfaces inside `pool.query` and is swallowed with the rest. `migrated++` therefore counts a tenant whose database does not exist.

### These three legs are ONE path, which is why they are on one ticket

**Tenant provisioning is broken and nothing reports it:**

1. a per-tenant DB arrives **deny-all** on five core tables (the body of this ticket),
2. it **cannot be connected to at all** without a CA-verifiable cert,
3. and the boot **reports success under every one of those failures**.

Filed together deliberately — as three separate tickets each one looks survivable on its own.

title: Fresh databases are FAIL-OPEN until the second boot — 039_rls_fail_closed does not apply on boot 1 (file stage runs before the CORE stage it depends on)
description:
## BLUF

**On a freshly provisioned database,** `users.tenant_isolation` **is FAIL-OPEN after the first boot — an unset tenant GUC sees ALL rows.** `039_rls_fail_closed.sql` does not apply on boot 1 because the file stage runs **before** the CORE stage that creates a table it depends on. Seven file migrations fail on boot 1; all seven succeed on boot 2.

⚠ **PRODUCTION IS NOT IMPLICATED by this mechanism.** A long-lived database already has the dependency tables, so `039` applies on the first boot after deploy. **The exposure is freshly provisioned databases: new environments, CI and local stacks, DR restores, and newly provisioned tenant DBs.**

## Provenance — this is the QA gate's measurement, not mine

Measured by the cross-project QA agent on 2026-09-09 against PR #928, on a real `postgres:15-alpine` driven by **the product's own** `runStartupMigrations()` via `tsx`, `MIGRATIONS_DIR` pointed at the repo `migrations/`, a fresh database per side. Report: `2026-09-09-s161-batch-six-prs/report.md` §2, with boot transcripts in its `evidence/` directory.

**I have NOT re-run it.** Filed because §2 of that report says it bears on the deploy hold and asks for it loudly. The numbers below are relayed; the mechanism is the gate's, and the pre-deploy check is the gate's own recommendation.

## The measurement

```
after boot 1:  USING ( current_setting('app.current_tenant_id',true) IS NULL
                       OR current_setting(...) = ''
                       OR tenant_id::text = current_setting(...) )      <-- unset GUC sees ALL rows

after boot 2:  USING ( current_setting(...) IS NOT NULL AND <> ''
                       AND tenant_id::text = current_setting(...) )
                     OR current_setting('app.tenant_scope_bypass',true) = 'platform_admin'
               + policy users_auth_lookup
```

`039` fails on boot 1 with `type "oauth_apps" does not exist` — the file stage runs before the CORE_MIGRATIONS stage that creates that table.

**Seven file migrations fail on boot 1 and all seven succeed on boot 2:** `006, 008, 026, 027, 028, 039, 047`. `048_ks754_widen_processed_by_to_text.sql` **applied cleanly on boot 1.**

## Why it matters beyond the fresh DB

**Both #928 and #929 assume** `039` **is in force.** #929's whole justification is that fail-closed RLS with an unresolved tenant GUC produces a 0-row UPDATE. On a database where `039` has not applied, that condition does not arise from that cause — **and cross-tenant rows are visible.**

The same assumption runs through **KS-1052** (the credential-lifecycle guards) and the KS-963 work.

## 🔴 Pre-deploy check — put this on any deploy that touches these services

On the **target** database, confirm **both**:

1. `048` is present in `_secuura_migrations`.
2. `pg_policy` for `users.tenant_isolation` shows the `IS NOT NULL AND <> ''` form — **not** the `IS NULL OR = ''` form.

⚠ `run-migrations.sh` **exits 0 when migrations fail**, so compose's own gate does not catch this. The check has to be made against the database, not inferred from a runner's exit code.

## Related, un-driven, and probably the more serious half

**QA F-928-3 (read from source, NOT measured):** the tenant loop calls `migrateDatabase(pg, tenantConnStr, tenantDbName, CORE_MIGRATIONS)` only — **it never calls** `applyFileMigrations`. If `039` exists only as a file, **tenant databases never receive the fail-closed flip at all**, on any boot. The gate never configured `PLATFORM_DATABASE_URL` and provisioned no tenant DB, so this is a code-path reading and not a measurement. **It should be measured before it is believed, and if true it is worse than the boot-1 window** — a permanent state rather than a transient one.

## Fix shapes (not a ruling)

1. **Order the stages by dependency** — run the CORE stage before the file stage, or make `039` tolerate the absent table and re-assert later.
2. **Make boot-1 failure visible where it counts:** related to **F-928-2** (migration failure is still log-only; `runStartupMigrations()` is `Promise<void>`, so no call site can branch on `failed`). That is a design decision with deploy consequences and is **Kam's**, tracked separately.
3. **Provisioning-time assertion** — a new environment is not "ready" until the `pg_policy` shape check above passes.

## Related

* **KS-1052** — the credential-lifecycle guards that assume `039` is in force.
* PR **#928** (KS-950) — surfaced this; its `INCOMPLETE — 7 FAILED` log line is the first thing in the system that says so out loud.
* PR **#929** (KS-943).

*Filed by s162, 2026-09-09, on Wednesday's brief item 4. Numbers relayed from the QA gate and labelled as such.*

nodes.body:
**BLUF:** Facts only; the ticket stays In Progress. The fresh-database sweep owed on this ticket is done, on a throw-away PostgreSQL. At develop `4ccdc3b3e7cf` this ticket's own defect does **not** reproduce: after boot 1 on a bare database `users.tenant_isolation` is in the fail-closed form, `038a` and `039` are recorded, `auth_find_oauth_app_by_client_id` exists, and as the NOBYPASSRLS app role `secuura_app` a witness row is invisible to an unset tenant and to another tenant (0 / 0) and visible to its own (1), for `users` and `certifications`. The same harness at the pre-fix merge-base `0d156d12` reproduces the old shape. The sweep also found a neighbouring window, filed as KS 2039: `rights_holders` has no RLS and no `tenant_id` until boot 2, on a bare database. The migrations image rebuild was not run.

**Method.** develop `4ccdc3b3e7cf` and the merge-base `0d156d12`, each fetched by sha. A throw-away PostgreSQL 15.19 (Homebrew) on a unix socket only: 0 inet sockets by `lsof`, with a positive control that sees 1. A bare database per tree and per runner (no `docker/init` scripts), two boots each, with both product runners: the gateway's `runStartupMigrations` via tsx (pg 8.23.0, tsx 4.23.15, the gateway lock's versions; `MULTI_TENANCY_ENABLED` unset) and `scripts/run-migrations.sh`, unmodified. After each boot, one read-only catalog read, then a witness read as `secuura_app` (`rolsuper` f, `rolbypassrls` f): witness rows inserted as the owner inside one transaction, counted as `secuura_app` with the tenant setting unset, set to another tenant, and set to the row's tenant, then rolled back (0 left behind, read back). The read is the database, not the exit code.

**Results** (counts are `unset / another tenant / own tenant`; the owner sees every witness):

| Scenario | Failed on that boot | `users` form | `039` | function | `tenant_isolation` policies | `users` | `certifications` | `rights_holders` |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| develop, gateway runner, boot 1 | 006, 008, 026, 027, 028 | fail-closed | recorded | present | 25 | 0 / 0 / 1 | 0 / 0 / 1 | 1 / 1 / 1 (RLS off, no `tenant_id`) |
| develop, gateway runner, boot 2 | none | fail-closed | recorded | present | 25 | 0 / 0 / 1 | 0 / 0 / 1 | 0 / 0 / 1 (own setting `app.tenant_id`: B=0, A=1; RLS on) |
| develop, `run-migrations.sh`, boot 1 | 006, 008, 026, 027, 028 (exit 3) | fail-closed | recorded | present | 25 | 0 / 0 / 1 | 0 / 0 / 1 | table absent |
| develop, `run-migrations.sh`, boot 2 | 026, 027, 028 (exit 3) | fail-closed | recorded | present | 25 | 0 / 0 / 1 | 0 / 0 / 1 | table absent |
| merge-base `0d156d12`, gateway runner, boot 1 | 006, 008, 026, 027, 028, 039, 047 | FAIL-OPEN | not recorded | ABSENT | 20 | 1 / 0 / 1 | 0 / 0 / 0 (forced RLS, 0 policies: deny-all) | 1 / 1 / 1 (RLS off, no `tenant_id`) |
| merge-base `0d156d12`, gateway runner, boot 2 | none | fail-closed | recorded | present | 24 | 0 / 0 / 1 | 0 / 0 / 1 | 0 / 0 / 1 (own setting `app.tenant_id`: B=0, A=1; RLS on) |
| merge-base `0d156d12`, `run-migrations.sh`, boot 1 | 006, 008, 026, 027, 028, 039, 047 (exit 3) | fail-closed | not recorded | ABSENT | 20 | 0 / 0 / 1 | table absent | table absent |
| merge-base `0d156d12`, `run-migrations.sh`, boot 2 | 006, 008, 026, 027, 028, 039, 047 (exit 3) | fail-closed | not recorded | ABSENT | 20 | 0 / 0 / 1 | table absent | table absent |

**Controls.**
- The non-RLS tracker table reads 41 to 59 as `secuura_app` in every scenario, so the instrument sees rows; the owner sees each witness; the rollback leaves 0 rows and the helper function gone.
- The merge-base tree on the same harness reproduces the old shape: gateway runner, boot 1, the seven original failures (`006`, `008`, `026`, `027`, `028`, `039`, `047`), `users.tenant_isolation` in the FAIL-OPEN form, the function absent, and the witness visible to an unset tenant (1). Boot 2 heals it. So the harness shows both states.
- The first witness run and the scripted rerun on the same boot-1 state are byte-identical; a rewritten witness script gave the same counts as its predecessor on an unchanged state.
- `rights_holders` after boot 2 is read with its own setting, `app.tenant_id` (its policy does not use `app.current_tenant_id`): another tenant 0, own tenant 1.

**What the two runners do differently** (measured):
- At the merge-base, a failed `039` under the gateway runner leaves `users` FAIL-OPEN after boot 1. Under `run-migrations.sh` the same failure leaves `users` already fail-closed, with the function absent and `039` unrecorded; `psql -f` without `--single-transaction` (READ in the script) would apply the statements before the failing one. The window this ticket describes is therefore the gateway-runner path.
- `run-migrations.sh` alone on a bare database has no CORE stage. At the merge-base that means `oauth_apps`, `svc_webhooks`, `certifications`, `charge_events` and `rights_holders` are never created (all absent after both boots, 7 failures on each); at the head `038a` creates the first four, and only `rights_holders` is still absent, so `026` to `028` fail on every boot (head: boot 1 `applied=55 failed=5`, boot 2 `applied=2 failed=3 skipped=55`). It exits 3 each time, at the merge-base and at the head; the description's "`run-migrations.sh` exits 0 when migrations fail" is out of date.

**Differences from the 2026-09-28 measurement.** That run used PostgreSQL 18.3; this one uses 15.19, the major version compose pins (`postgres:15-alpine`). It read 22 `tenant_isolation` policies at the merge-base; this harness reads 20 (not investigated). At the fix it read 25; this harness reads 25. A fresh database at the head carries 25, the same as Kintsugi; demo reads 26 (comment of 2026-11-05), so demo's extra policy does not come from a fresh build. A data point, not an investigation.

**What this does not show.**
- "Bare" means the `docker/init` scripts did not run. Compose mounts `./docker/init` into Postgres's init directory (READ, `docker-compose.yml:159`), so a compose-initialised database starts with tables this run had to wait for. Not run.
- The migrations image rebuild (needs Docker) was not run.
- Not run: `MULTI_TENANCY_ENABLED` and per-tenant databases (the KS 1055 path), traffic across a real boot gap, PostgreSQL 18, Node 24 (the harness ran on Node v26.8.1).
- Two harness adaptations, both in the harness and not in product code: a PATH shim points `run-migrations.sh`'s TCP-only `pg_isready` probe at the unix socket, and the compose grants from `docker/init/01-create-app-role.sh` were applied to `secuura_app` after each sh-runner boot (the gateway runner provisions its own). The script wrote its fixed `/tmp/migrate-err.log`; copies are in the record.
- Whether any deployed database ran without the init scripts is UNMEASURED, and no real row was written across a boot gap by this work (KS 2039 states the same).

**Against the Done rule** (unit tests on develop plus the fix in the running Kintsugi build): the 2026-11-02 and 2026-11-05 comments already show the six PRs merged, reachable from the Kintsugi deploy, and `038a` and `039` recorded on Kintsugi and demo. This run adds the item those comments left unrun, `039` and `038a` on a bare database across two boots and `certifications` read as the app role, on a disposable database. It does not cover the image rebuild, and it adds KS 2039, which this ticket's fix does not claim to cover. I changed no ticket state.

Evidence: `5_Project_History/2026-11-06_seatC-35th/evidence/` (`ks1054_matrix.md`, `*_boot1_*`, `*_boot2_*`, `cluster_proof.txt`), tools in `tools/`.

**BLUF:** Facts only, ticket stays open. PR 1624, which is attached to this ticket and was unresolved in the census, is merged, and it belongs to another ticket. The fresh-database live sweep is still unrun.

**Read-only reads, 2026-11-05 03:06Z** (SELECT in a read-only transaction, database `secuura`; both boxes' REVISION head is 07a2d62be6a0):
- The tracker holds `038a_ks1054_core_tables_before_039.sql` and `039_rls_fail_closed.sql` on kintsugi and on demo. The function `auth_find_oauth_app_by_client_id` exists on both. `tenant_isolation` policies: 25 on kintsugi, 26 on demo.
- GitHub: PR 1624 is merged to develop (merge_commit_sha 115797747cb60009e781d80e9059dbbed69e1ac3, an ancestor of 07a2d62be6a0). Its attachment title on this ticket reads "Refs KS-1662: prove the transfer-custody tenant predicates without RLS", so it carries nothing for this ticket's scope.
- PRs 1332, 1346, 1348, 1350, 1357 and 1359 are merged with merge_commit_sha 0de108577e61, 8ba2da02d980, a72149a1a803, 37205947ddd2, 93a10a06dfd2 and 91a8f6b721bc, all ancestors of 07a2d62be6a0.

**Not measured:** 039 and 038a on a bare database across two boots, and `certifications` read as the app role (a fresh database, not a read of these boxes). The difference between the two boxes' policy counts (25 and 26) was not investigated.

Delivered: PRs 1332, 1346, 1348, 1350, 1357 and 1359 merged as 0de108577, 8ba2da02d, a72149a1a, 37205947d, 93a10a06d and 91a8f6b72 on develop, all reachable from the kintsugi deploy b1fb543640e7 (2026-11-01). Verified by code read at b1fb543640e7, not observed live: migrations/038a_ks1054_core_tables_before_039.sql and deployment/azure/check-startup-migrations.sh are in the tree, and the 2026-11-01 deploy's rsync record lists the 038a file. Left open: the merge comment of 2026-09-28 says NOT Done, live sweep owed: 039 and 038a applied on a bare database across two boots, certifications read as secuura_app, and a migrations image rebuild. That needs a fresh database and two boots, not a read-only probe, and was not run here.

A second follow-up, on the callers' wording rather than the predicate. rc 1 from the startup check means either that migrations failed or that the check could not be verified, but both callers printed a line claiming they FAILED. deploy.sh:859 now reads "startup migrations FAILED or could not be verified — see above" and deploy-all.sh:314's smoke value reads "failed or could not be verified — see above"; deploy-all.sh still fails against "0 failed", so nothing about the pass/fail outcome moves.

Message text only — no exit code, counter or branch changed; a control cell in each new suite pins that rc 1 still counts an ERROR (deploy.sh) or a FAIL (deploy-all.sh) and rc 2 still counts a SKIP. Proved red-first on macOS and in python:3.12-slim: with the previous wording exactly one cell in each suite fails and the controls stay green; with the change each suite reads 4 passed, 0 failed.

Not covered: neither script was driven end to end, and neither was run against any real environment, so a live sweep is owed.

Follow-up to the exit-status note above. That note covers python3 being ABSENT. This change closes the remaining case: a python3 that is PRESENT BUT BROKEN — on PATH, but exiting non-zero — was read as "the /health body is not JSON" and the check exited 2 (PASS-WITH-SKIP), so a deploy whose migration status could not be read did not fail. It now exits 1 and names the parser, matching the absent case. A genuinely non-JSON body still exits 2, pinned by a control cell.

Proved red-first on macOS and in python:3.12-slim (bash 5.2.37, coreutils 9.7, Python 3.12.14): the change adds four cells to the existing suite, and with the predicate at its previous state two of them (P10, P10b) fail and nothing else does; with the change the suite reads 40 passed, 0 failed on both runners. Each cell's fixture guard is asserted green, so neither red is vacuous.

Not covered: the macOS python3 shim case is not reproducible on this Mac and is unmeasured on a Mac without developer tools; neither deploy script was run whole (their migration call sites were executed against the real predicate with a broken-python3 stub, and both now count a failure); the scripts were not run against any real environment, so a live sweep is owed.

Merged `a72149a1a803d802430568254e7fa9afa7029321` (PR #1348, round-2 head `94e31db501cd01aaec7437418d7efbb592b1b59a`): `deploy.sh` now exits non-zero when post-deploy verification counts issues. Comment `b82bebb3` named the round-1 head `1bb58b4ebb97`; a review found that head's test could not see a changed return value and failed on Linux, both were fixed at the round-2 head, and the counts that comment gives hold there.

Merged `37205947ddd2775a72a417beb5b7ac8e3240fbf3` (PR #1350, `deployment/azure/check-startup-migrations.sh`, `deploy.sh`, `deploy-all.sh`): the startup-migration check now reports a third result when it did not run. For `ran:false` or an absent field, both deploy scripts print SKIPPED instead of a pass, and the deploy still succeeds. For an empty or non-JSON body, `deploy.sh` still fails the deploy through its health check and `deploy-all.sh` prints SKIPPED; that difference is unchanged. One exit status changes: when `python3` is not on PATH, the check now fails the deploy in both scripts (before, `deploy.sh` passed it). Offline gates green; NOT Done per secuura-test-discipline §5f — live sweep owed (torn-down rebuilt stack, all containers verified up), unverified: both scripts against a real environment.

PR #1348 raised against `develop`, head `1bb58b4ebb97`, base `8ba2da02d980`.

This is the half PR #1346 did not carry. `verify_deployment()` in `deploy.sh` counted its errors and then returned 0, because its last command was a log line — so the deploy read as successful over failed startup migrations. It now returns 1 when the error count is non-zero, which is the strength `deploy-all.sh` already had. One `return` is the whole change: the script runs under `set -euo pipefail` and the function is called unchecked at both call sites, so a non-zero return aborts with that status at either, and no call site needed editing.

Evidence: the shell suite reads 14 passed / 0 failed on the branch, and 13 passed / 1 failed with `deploy.sh` alone reverted to `8ba2da02d980` — the single red being the new cell, with its two companion cells still green, so the red is neither a fixture failure nor an unconditional one. The cell extracts the real summary block from `deploy.sh` by its own marker and executes it with an injected error count, rather than grepping for the fix: a grep passes on a commented-out line, and a line-number pin drifts.

Still open on this ticket, not fixed here: a `ran:false` body still prints a pass line although the gateway's own module says that is not a clean run; an absent, empty or non-JSON body still counts as a passing check in the smoke summary; and `python3` missing from PATH reads a failed body as "not JSON — SKIPPED", failing open. Each of those is about the pass LINE rather than the exit status, and passing on an absent field is deliberate, because failing closed there would block a rollback to an older image.

`deploy.sh` was not run against any real environment. A live sweep is owed and this ticket stays In Progress.

Merged to `develop` as PR #1346, squash `8ba2da02d980e7e8065e8ce614b034adc2b7c2eb`, tree `fd0d6bc033a9`, parent `bd740147c3d8`. Verified at source: develop equals the squash by ls-remote, the commits API reports that tree, and a contents-API blob read on all four changed paths equals the head's blob. The helper's recorded mode is `100755` in the merged tree by `git ls-tree`, with a `100644` control from the same commit.

**The squash subject was composed rather than taken from the PR title, and the reason matters.** The PR title said the deploy scripts "fail on failures". QA measured that `deploy.sh` prints an ERROR and `found 1 issue(s)` but **returns exit code 0** over failed migrations, so the deploy does not read as failed from that script — only `deploy-all.sh` fails. The landed subject says exactly that: "deploy scripts read /health startupMigrations; deploy-all fails on them". A squash subject is permanent, so it had to be true.

**What is therefore still open on this ticket:** making `deploy.sh` exit non-zero on failed migrations, which is what the ruling's "the deploy reads as failed" requires of the `deploy.sh:823` check. That is a follow-up PR, not covered here.

Also recorded by QA, none blocking: a `ran:false` body still prints a pass line in the summary; an absent, empty or non-JSON body likewise counts as a passing check; and `python3` missing from PATH reads a failed body as "not JSON — SKIPPED", a new dependency that fails open.

This changes runtime code in the deploy path and the scripts were run against no real environment, so a live sweep is owed and this ticket stays In Progress. Nothing was deployed by the merge.

PR #1346 raised against `develop`, head `2075c3ec7078`, base `0aa9b52c691b`.

One predicate both deploy scripts call: `Blockchain/Dev/deployment/azure/check-startup-migrations.sh`, invoked from `deploy-all.sh` and `deploy.sh`. It reads `startupMigrations.failed` from `/health` and fails the deploy step on a non-zero count, keyed on `failed` and never on `error`. `/health` itself is unchanged — the diff carries no service code. An absent field passes and says so, so a rollback to an older image is not blocked; a non-JSON or empty body is skipped and named rather than counted as a pass; a non-integer value is refused rather than read as zero.

Evidence: the shell suite reads 11 passed / 0 failed on the branch and 0 passed / 11 failed with the test half alone (both deploy scripts reverted to `0aa9b52c691b` and the new helper removed), restored byte-identically afterwards. The helper's recorded mode is `100755`, asserted by `git ls-tree` rather than by the on-disk bit, because this repo sets `core.filemode=false` and both scripts invoke the helper directly. The branch was rebased twice and its diff is byte-identical to the diff stored before the first rebase (`cmp` rc 0, 12,296 B). Push preflight: 12/15 legs ran, 3 skipped (legs 3, 4, 8 — local stack not up), nothing failed. That is not a pass and is recorded as a ratio.

Not covered: the deploy scripts were not run against any real environment, and no migration was run against a real database. A live sweep is owed on this runtime change, so this ticket stays In Progress.

Merged 0de108577e6199de3c9402c0643a2944d86aee97 (PR #1332, migrations/038a_ks1054_core_tables_before_039.sql); offline gates green; NOT Done per secuura-test-discipline §5f — live sweep owed (torn-down rebuilt stack, all containers verified up), unverified: 039 and 038a on a bare Azure database across two boots, certifications as the app role (secuura_app; default-deny N-G39-1), and the migrations image rebuild

**Round 2 of 2 pushed to #1332 — head `f2423bf7aa6c64952cf425d4160a048a55ffaaee`** (fast-forward from `f5381338359d`, base `develop`).

Round 1 was NO GO on the gate's `N-1332-1` blocker. This commit fixes N-1332-1, N-1332-2 and N-1332-3 together.

**N-1332-1 — fix shape (b), chosen on a measurement.** A new file migration `038a_ks1054_core_tables_before_039.sql` creates `oauth_apps`, `svc_webhooks`, `certifications` and `charge_events` before 039 runs, so 039 finds them present on its only pass. The deciding fact: `scripts/run-migrations.sh` — the compose `migrations` service's runner, and the one a deploy uses — is a single pass with no CORE stage and the same record-then-skip shape, so the alternatives would have fixed the gateway and left the container path still recording a half-applied 039.

**Regression on a real PostgreSQL 18.3** (unix socket only, 0 inet sockets proven by `lsof`), under the real unmodified runner, on bare databases, three-sided:

| tree | 039 recorded | `auth_find_oauth_app_by_client_id(text)` | policy | `tenant_isolation` policies | four tables |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| merge-base `0d156d12` | 0 (039 fails) | ABSENT | 0 | 22 | 0 |
| round-1 head `f5381338` | 1 | **ABSENT** | 0 | 22 | 0 |
| this commit | 1 | **PRESENT** | 1 | 25 | 4 |

The DDL is derived from `CORE_MIGRATIONS` at develop `215cc6875e2b` and proved schema-identical to it by `pg_dump --schema-only`, because shape (b) creates a second creator of the same tables.

**N-1332-2** — both CORE-stage catches never touched `totalFailed`, so a stage that died was served as `failed: 0`. **N-1332-3** — `error?` was declared and never passed; `applyFileMigrations` now returns a `firstError` the way `migrateDatabase` already did.

api-gateway **88 files / 795 tests, 0 failed**. Tests-including tsc **29 → 29, delta 0**. Arms **3/3** red their own cell. Push preflight **12 of 15 legs, 3 skipped** — not a pass, stated as a ratio.

**Not in this commit:** `N-1332-5` (the deploy scripts still do not read the `startupMigrations` field) — named unraised, not dropped. `N-1332-4` is not commissioned. A deploy must rebuild **both** the migrations image and the api-gateway image; nothing has been deployed.

**F-928-3 — the section of this ticket marked UNMEASURED is now measured. Split out to KS-1055.**

**BLUF: confirmed, and it is a different defect from this one.** KS-1054 is a *window* — a fresh DB is fail-open until boot 2, then heals. What I measured on a genuinely separate tenant DB does not heal on any boot: the file-migration stage never runs against a tenant database at all, so `_secuura_migrations` **does not exist** there after three boots (control: 48 rows on the main DB, same reader).

**And the consequence is the opposite sign from this ticket's.** CORE_MIGRATIONS `ENABLE`s and `FORCE`s RLS on five tables (`startup-migrations.ts:439-440, 485-486, 551-552, 633-634`) while `CREATE POLICY` appears **0 times** in that whole file (control: 19 in `migrations/*.sql`). A tenant DB therefore lands with FORCE RLS and **zero policies** — not fail-open, **deny-all**. Measured as a `NOBYPASSRLS` non-superuser role: 0 rows from `documents`/`certifications`/`audit_logs`, and still 0 with both GUCs set, while the same role reads 1 from a non-RLS table in the same database (non-zero control) and the row is provably there under `row_security=off`.

**Scope, both directions:** latent today — `PROVISION_PER_TENANT_DB` defaults false, so every tenant points at the shared app DB, which does get the files. It goes live the moment per-tenant DBs are provisioned, i.e. exactly when KS-160 Path A ships.

**Ordering matters to whoever fixes either one:** on my fresh main DB, boot 1 failed 7 file migrations including **`039_rls_fail_closed.sql` → `type "oauth_apps" does not exist`**, and boot 2 applied them — this ticket's window, reproduced. A tenant arm added to `applyFileMigrations` without fixing that ordering just reproduces KS-1054 inside every tenant DB instead of fixing anything.

Measured by s163, 2026-09-09, on disposable local containers (removed at close). Demo, UAT and every shared database untouched.

title: FLAKE (3rd occurrence, first with a name): ks949 seed-site enumeration fails ~1 in 7 full auth runs and passes alone — timeout hypothesis refuted
description:
## BLUF

`ks949-platform-admin-seed-identity.test.ts` **fails intermittently in the FULL** `services/auth` **suite and passes on every re-run.** This is the **third** occurrence of a self-healing auth failure. It is the first one with a **name**, which is the only reason it is a ticket rather than a memory.

**Cell:** `the real person is gone from every EXECUTABLE seed site › the enumeration actually finds seed sites, including the one the gate planted in`

## The measurement, 2026-09-09

| run | scope | result |
| -- | -- | -- |
| 1 | full `services/auth` suite | **FAILED** — `Error: STACK_TRACE_ERROR` at `ks949-platform-admin-seed-identity.test.ts:314` |
| 2, 3 | full suite, identical tree | 642/642 green |
| 4, 5 | full suite, after an unrelated mock fix | 641/642 then 641/642 (a *different*, deterministic failure, since fixed) |
| 6, 7 | full suite | **642/642 green** |
| — | that file ALONE | **30/30 green, 2.73 s** |
| control | full suite on clean develop `d4cf7e3cf`, separate worktree | **635/635 green** |

## Hypothesis TESTED and NOT SUPPORTED — do not re-propose without new evidence

**Timeout under full-suite parallelism.** The failing cell walks the whole `Blockchain/Dev` tree reading every `.ts/.js/.mjs/.cjs/.sql/.sh` file, which is the slowest thing in the suite, and `STACK_TRACE_ERROR` is a shape vitest produces for a task-level abort. **Refuted by the same instrument:** it passes under *identical* parallelism on runs 2, 3, 6 and 7. A timeout that fires once in seven identical runs is not explained by the walk being slow.

**Mechanism therefore UNESTABLISHED.**

## 🔑 How this was caught — the part worth keeping

`HANDOVER-s161.md` **§3 records two earlier occurrences (**`api-gateway` **1/293,** `auth` **2/633) whose test names were NEVER captured.** Without a name there is nothing to pick up, which is precisely why s161 declined to file them and why that was the right call at the time.

That handover shipped an instrument for the next occurrence:

```bash
npx vitest run --reporter=json --outputFile=/tmp/vitest-run-$(date +%s).json
```

…with the standing instruction: **capture the name FIRST, before re-running, because a re-run destroys the evidence** — and both earlier events were lost to exactly that.

**It was used on the third occurrence and it produced the name. The instrument paid inside one day of being written.** That is the difference between *"we keep seeing flakes"* and *"we caught the third one because the second one left us a tool."* This ticket exists to make that fact survive the handover it came from.

## Why this is now closeable when the first two were not

It carries a **named subject**, a **reproduction attempt with its result** (7 full runs + 1 isolated + 1 clean-develop control), and a **refuted hypothesis** so the next person does not spend the hour re-proposing it. Mechanism-unestablished is a fine state for a ticket; *unidentified* was not.

## Where to start

1. Re-run the full suite in a loop capturing JSON per run until it reproduces (it took 1 in 7 here) — **do NOT pipe through** `tail`**/**`head`, which is how the first two names were lost.
2. When it reproduces, read `failureMessages` from the JSON rather than the terminal: `STACK_TRACE_ERROR` is what the JSON reporter emitted, and the human reporter may carry more.
3. `ks949…test.ts:314` is the tree-walk control cell — `expect(sites.length).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(3)`. Worth logging `sites` on failure, since an enumeration that transiently returns fewer sites is a different defect from a timeout, and both would present this way.

## Related

* **KS-1052** — found during that work; carries the same record.
* `5_Project_History/HANDOVER-s161.md` §3 — the two earlier occurrences and the instrument.

*Filed by s162, 2026-09-09, on Wednesday's ruling.*

nodes.body:
**BLUF:** Measured 2026-10-30 (UTC): the ks949 seed-site enumeration cells failed in 7 of 11 whole `services/auth` suite runs on one laptop, against the "about 1 in 7" this ticket records. Every failing cell ran 5.0 to 7.8 s, and on an untouched tree vitest's default reporter printed `Error: Test timed out in 5000ms.` for both failing cells. The file passes 31 of 31 when run alone (4 of 4 runs). Facts only: nothing was changed in the file and no ticket was filed.

**Runs** (vitest 4.1.12, `--maxWorkers=3`, Node v26.8.1, macOS 27.0.1 arm64, a laptop shared with other seats; develop `a786e06e6f6e` and `530f091120d5`):
* auth service untouched: 4 runs, 3 failed 2 cells each (one of them with the default reporter), 1 passed all 1326 cells.
* branch of KS 1804 (one test file changed): 3 runs, 2 failed 2 cells each, 1 passed all 1328.
* branch of KS 1792: 2 runs, both failed (3 cells, then 2).
* branches of KS 1797 and KS 1791: 1 run each, both passed every cell.
* Failing cells: `the enumeration actually finds seed sites, including the one the gate planted in` (in all 7 failing runs), `no executable seed site anywhere in the tree names the real address` (5 of 7), `the platform admin seed is NOT seeded when DEMO_SECUURA_PASSWORD is unset` (3 of 7).
* The suite without that file passed on each tree where I ran it (110 files / 1300 cells on the KS 1792 branch, 1301 on KS 1797, 1296 on KS 1791). The file alone passed 31 of 31 on four trees.

**What the file does.** `walk(devRoot)` (lines 300 to 314 of `ks949-platform-admin-seed-identity.test.ts`) reads every .ts, .js, .mjs, .cjs, .sql and .sh file under `Blockchain/Dev`, and `walk(repoRoot)` (lines 525 to 536) lists `.env.example` files across the checkout. Both skip `node_modules`, `dist`, `build`, `coverage` and `.git`; the first also skips `__tests__` and `__mocks__`. Each checkout here carries 40 `node_modules` trees; both walks skip them, so I make no claim that they matter.

**Not measured:** why the walks are slow here (disk, file count or load: the 1-minute load average was between about 4 and 13 during these runs, with other seats' pre-push hooks running), whether a checkout with a different file count passes, Node 24, any other host.

**BLUF: a tenth occurrence, reported by Seat V 3rd on 2026-10-27 — and a note that this ticket's DESCRIPTION and its comment thread now disagree about the shape.** Facts only. The refuted "timeout under full-suite parallelism" hypothesis is **not** re-proposed.

**Whose measurement this is.** The occurrence below is **Seat V 3rd's report**, recorded in `5_Project_History/history.md` (its 2026-10-27 section) during its KS-1523 work on this laptop with several seats live. It is **not** my measurement and **not** Wednesday's; I did not run the suite and am not re-running it.

**What V 3rd's record gives:**

* explicit `Test timed out in 5000ms` in **three cells** of `ks949-platform-admin-seed-identity.test.ts`;
* its own judgement that the finding is **a duplicate of this ticket**, after it had first written up a board-search result it had not run (its entry records that correction against itself, and the corrected counts: `ks949` 14 open hits, `platform-admin-seed-identity` 4, `Test timed out in 5000ms` 3);
* its reading that KS-1155 and KS-1328 have since established the 5 s fleet-load class.

**What V 3rd's record does NOT give** — stated as absent rather than filled in:

* the **cell names** — not recorded;
* the **exact run** (tree, command, json path) — not recorded;
* the **load figure** — not recorded;
* durations for the three cells — not recorded.

**The note worth more than the occurrence.** V 3rd framed its shape as differing from this ticket's — *"explicit `Test timed out in 5000ms` in three cells vs its `STACK_TRACE_ERROR` in one"*. That contrast is true of this ticket's **description** and false of its **comments**. Measured over the thread as it stands (7 comments before this one, sorted by `createdAt`): **5 of the 7 contain the literal string `Test timed out in 5000ms`**.

| comment | date | what it already records |
| -- | -- | -- |
| 1 | 2026-09-13 | occurrences 4 and 5 — measured **durations 5,683.5 ms** and **5,982 ms**, at load 18.42 and load 16–18 |
| 2 | 2026-09-14 | occurrences 6–8 — `Test timed out in 5000ms` on the first full run **3 of 3**, loads 12.8 / 7.6 / 4.6, and **0 of 3** on a rerun |
| 3 | 2026-10-12 | Seat F 17th — same signature on three of four trees, loads 8–14 |
| 4, 5, 6 | 2026-10-12 | Seat V 5th — three occurrences **with cell names and line numbers** (`:318`, the enumeration cell, and *"no executa…"*) |
| 7 | 2026-10-13 | **occurrence 9 — the first deliberate reproduction, with a mechanism control** |

So the 5 s-budget shape has been this thread's record since comment 1, and a reproduction recipe has existed since comment 7. The description's framing — `STACK_TRACE_ERROR`, *"Mechanism therefore UNESTABLISHED"*, and the refuted-hypothesis warning — is the September-9 state and predates all seven. **A reader who stops at the description will draw the contrast V 3rd drew.** Reconciling the description with the thread would prevent the next seat re-deriving it; that is a suggestion about this ticket's text, not a hypothesis about the defect.

**Not established here:** nothing about the mechanism. This comment adds one unquantified recurrence and a reading of the existing thread. It does not propose that the 5 s budget is the cause, and it does not re-open the hypothesis the description refutes.

*Seat G 22nd, 2026-10-27, board-hygiene lane. No suite run; no state change to this ticket.*

## Occurrence 9 — and the first DELIBERATE reproduction, with a mechanism control (pull request 1538 gate, Sonnet tier 2, 2026-10-13)

**Facts only. This does not re-propose the hypothesis this ticket refutes; it reports a reproduction recipe that did not exist before, and the measurement that goes with it.** Source: the gate on pull request 1538 (KS-1009), report sha256/16 `d1d48d9c8fd56dd6`, §1. The gate was looking at an unrelated PR and carried this file's flake as an attack point.

### It was produced ON DEMAND, not waited for

| run | box | result |
| -- | -- | -- |
| whole `services/auth`, head, under CPU contention (12 busy-loop node processes) run 1 | loaded | `Test timed out in 5000ms` — the ks949 cell |
| same, run 2 | loaded | **two** ks949 cells, same error |
| whole `services/auth`, **develop** (the PR's new file absent), loaded run 1 | loaded | the same ks949 cell |
| same, loaded run 2 | loaded | at least four tests (output truncated at four): ks949 again, plus ks1186 and ks728 |
| both branches, idle | idle | **0 failures** |

So the recipe is: run the whole suite with the box under deliberate CPU contention. That is the part this ticket did not have — occurrences 1 to 8 were all caught, not caused.

### Mechanism control — the cell is WALL-CLOCK bound

`--testTimeout=150` on `ks949` alone makes the **same three walk-dependent cells** fail with `timed out in 150ms`. The budget, not the work, is what they are racing.

The walk itself, measured: **0.2 s warm**, **2.0 s on a cold first read of the project volume**, **0.24 s under the same CPU load**. `seedSites()` walks the whole `Blockchain/Dev` tree (`devRoot = here/../../../..`), skipping `node_modules`/`dist`/`build`/`coverage`/`.git`/`__tests__`/`__mocks__`, reading every `.ts/.js/.mjs/.cjs/.sql/.sh`; the gate measured **2120 files seen**. Three cells in the file call it, and none sets an explicit timeout, so vitest's 5000 ms default applies to all three. Cells: `:318`, and the two at `:293-316`.

**Reading:** this is consistent with occurrences 4 to 8 (durations measured over the 5 s budget under load) and with the neighbouring class in [[KS-1155]]. It does not revive the refuted claim that the walk is slow under *identical* parallelism — the gate's idle runs are green, as runs 2, 3, 6 and 7 were in 2026-09-09.

### The fix shape already exists, merged, next door

[[KS-1155]] fix-shape 1 shipped for `packages/shared` as pull request #1254, squash `ac38dc21dba4449aec68bd18ee71e1a5083ddba9`: the budget is set from `vitest.config.ts` through one setup file, touching **zero** guard files, so no assertion is loosened and every other cell in the package keeps the 5 s default. The same shape applies here (`services/auth`), or `seedSites()` is hoisted into a `beforeAll`. KS-1155 also carries the raised-timeout list.

### A low-load data point from the same seat, today

On the pull request 1538 predicted-merge tree `efa0aa0747e0dc48d2d3734fa8f5582062071c1f`, on an unloaded box: whole `services/auth` **94 files / 1061 tests, 0 failed, 26.94 s**. Green, as expected at low load.

### Not established

Which exact load the earlier authors had. Whether the three cells are the only ones in `services/auth` on a tree walk (the gate did not enumerate the suite for the class).

*Filed as a comment, not a new ticket: the pull request 1538 gate named this Minor M1 and the merge brief asked for a ticket, but a dup-search (positive control `tree-walking guards`, found in 6 issues, so the pipeline can see) returned this ticket as the subject's existing home. A ninth duplicate would not help anyone. — Seat J 7th*

## Third occurrence from Seat V 5th, same session (facts only; the refuted hypothesis is NOT re-proposed)

On the KS-1517 round 2 closing-amendment tree (`6c73effc` plus the uncommitted amendment; develop `898a1ae1` as base):

| run | scope | result |
| -- | -- | -- |
| 1 (first full run) | full `services/auth` | **2 failed / 1051 passed (1053)**, both `Test timed out in 5000ms`, at `ks949-platform-admin-seed-identity.test.ts:318` and `:349`. Load average read right after: 9.08 / 8.03 / 7.74 |
| 2, 3, 4 | the file alone | **31/31** each (3.33 s, 0.89 s, 0.91 s) |
| 5 | full `services/auth` again | **1053/1053**, rc 0, load ~6.3 |

Ruled out on this tree before the re-run: the amendment adds a FIFO cell, so a leaked FIFO could hang a walk. The worktree held **zero** non-regular entries (node_modules and .git pruned), and `git status` showed only the three edited files. The FIFO cell builds in a temp dir.

The changed files are `scripts/typecheck-tests/check.cjs`, a ks1000 test and `CLAUDE.md`; ks949 reads none of them.

## Second occurrence from Seat V 5th, same session (facts only; the refuted hypothesis is NOT re-proposed)

On the KS-1517 round 2 tree (develop `b2085e99` merged in):

| run | scope | result |
| -- | -- | -- |
| 1 | full `services/auth` | **2 failed / 1047 passed (1049)** — both `Test timed out in 5000ms` in `ks949-platform-admin-seed-identity.test.ts`: *"the enumeration actually finds seed sites…"* and *"no executable seed site anywhere in the tree names the real address"* |
| 2, 3 | that file ALONE | **31/31 each**, rc 0 |
| 4 | full `services/auth`, identical tree | **1049/1049**, rc 0 |

At run 1: `uptime` load averages **6.50 / 5.68 / 5.81**, and **another seat's** pre-push hook (a `git push` of a KS-1518 branch, running `preflight.sh`) was live on the same machine. This time I recorded load as a number, which my first occurrence comment did not.

Not a regression of the change under test: the round-2 diff is three files (`scripts/typecheck-tests/check.cjs`, the ks1000 suite, `CLAUDE.md`), and `ks949-platform-admin-seed-identity.test.ts` contains **0** references to `check.cjs` or `typecheck-tests`.

New detail worth having: this occurrence took **two** cells in the same file, not one, and the second is the address-scan cell rather than the enumeration-control cell. Both are in the same describe and both walk the tree.

Tally contribution from this session: 2 of 3 first full runs red, 0 of 2 re-runs, 0 of 5 file-alone.

## Occurrence from Seat V 5th, 2026-10-12 (facts only; the refuted hypothesis is NOT re-proposed)

Same signature, on the KS-1517 branch over develop `92f68da94123`:

| run | scope | result |
| -- | -- | -- |
| 1 (first full run) | full `services/auth` | **1 failed / 1024 passed (1025)** — `Test timed out in 5000ms`, `ks949-platform-admin-seed-identity.test.ts:318`, cell *"the enumeration actually finds seed sites, including the one the gate planted in"* |
| 2 | full `services/auth`, identical tree | **1025/1025, rc 0**, 21 s |
| 3, 4, 5 | that file ALONE | **31/31 each**, rc 0 |

At run 1 there were **8** of my own `vitest`/`preflight` processes live, and a second seat was mid-push (its in-hook preflight runs the 83-suite shell set). I did not measure machine load as a number, so I am recording process count, not load.

**Not a regression of the change under test:** `ks949-platform-admin-seed-identity.test.ts` contains **0** occurrences of `check.cjs` or `typecheck-tests`, which are what my branch changes, so it cannot see them.

Noting only, per this ticket's own instruction: the failing cell at `:318` is the async recursive `readdir` walk of `devRoot` declared at `:300` and awaited at `:314`, and it carries no explicit timeout. I am **not** asserting that is the mechanism — the description records the timeout hypothesis as tested and unsupported, and nothing I measured bears on it either way.

Tally contribution: 1 of 2 first-runs red, 0 of 1 re-runs, 0 of 3 file-alone.

## Occurrences from Seat F 17th, 2026-10-12 (measured; no new hypothesis)

**BLUF:** `Test timed out in 5000ms` in `ks949-platform-admin-seed-identity.test.ts` on the FIRST full `services/auth` vitest run, on three of four trees today, each at machine load 8 to 14. Every file-alone run passed, and an unloaded rerun passed. The same cells fail on the UNPATCHED base, so it is not a regression of any change under test (PR #1477, KS-1186).

| tree (develop it sits on) | first full run | rerun |
|---|---|---|
| base `f9c7880f` (unpatched) | 3 cells timed out | n/a |
| predicted merge over `22668829` | the same 3 cells timed out (load 8 to 14) | file alone 30/30 three times (3.9 s, 1.1 s, 1.1 s); full suite 88 files / 920 tests green |
