title: develop is RED on the services/originate jest suite and NOTHING catches it — the suite is a blocking gate nowhere automated
description:
## BLUF

`develop` **is RED on the** `services/originate` **jest suite right now, and no instrument in this repository objects.** Measured tonight: 2 of 4 cells in `ks444-webhooks-create-description-guard.test.ts` fail on develop's own blob. **The suite is a blocking gate NOWHERE automated**, so the mainline can be red indefinitely and nothing says so.

Filed on Wednesday's ruling as a **new** ticket rather than folded into KS-961, because KS-961 is In Review and adding scope to an in-review ticket either reopens reviewed work or buries the new scope under a review that never covered it.

## The measurement

```
npx jest src/__tests__/ks444-webhooks-create-description-guard.test.ts   (in services/originate)
  2 passed   the two NEGATIVE cells (400s an object, 400s a null)
  2 FAILED   both POSITIVES - expected 201, received 500
  EXIT=1
```

Run on blobs verified byte-identical to develop: the test file is `229a3ccde` at both `origin/develop` and `b6884888d`; `routes/webhooks.ts` is `c88eb97db` at both. **PR #926 is the fix and it is open and unmerged**, blocked on an approval.

**Scope of the redness, which the QA gate did not measure:** the full service run is **48 suites / 509 tests, 1 suite / 2 tests failed** — the ks444 positives are the *only* failures in the whole service. ⚠ That run covers **48 of develop's 49** originate suites: it was executed on a tree missing `ks754-processed-by-widened.test.ts`, which is **unswept and named rather than rounded away**.

## Why nothing catches it — four instruments, each checked with a control

| instrument | originate/jest | control on the same file |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `scripts/preflight/preflight.sh` (13 legs, 428 lines) | **0 hits** | `step` -> 18 hits |
| `.githooks/pre-push` (244 lines) | **0 hits** | `preflight` -> 18 hits |
| 17 GitHub workflows | only `ci.yml` + `deploy-demo.yml` invoke workspace tests, **both** `workflow_dispatch`**-only** | 17 mention `test` |
| the 7 `pull_request`-triggered workflows | **none runs any service unit suite** | read their `run:` steps individually |

**This conclusion does not depend on the Actions billing state.** Even with Actions fully funded, no PR-triggered workflow invokes this suite. Actions being retired (Kam, 2026-08-27) is a second, independent reason.

## The actual gap

**The only instrument that would ever catch a red mainline is a human filling in a Test Evidence line — and it only fires if a PR happens to touch that service.** `docs/DEV-PROCESS.md` requires `**Unit suites (touched services):** run/result | not run + why`. A suite that is red on develop and untouched by the current PR is invisible to that, by construction.

## The precedent that makes this concrete

`DEV-PROCESS.md` **has already made this exact argument once, for a different subject, and acted on it.** Cross-cutting guards get their own Test Evidence line specifically because, under "run `npm test` in the touched service", they *"execute only when someone touches* `shared`*, which is the change least likely to add a fifteenth service error handler"* — and it concludes **"A guard on no path that runs is not a guard."**

**The same argument applies to a red mainline suite, and nothing currently makes it.**

## Fix shapes (not a ruling - the cheapest is probably the third)

1. A preflight leg that runs the touched service's unit suite, so a red mainline blocks the next push that goes near it.
2. A periodic mainline run whose only job is to answer "is develop green" - no PR coupling.
3. A **baseline-diff** rule in the Test Evidence block: the author records develop's own result for the suites they ran, so "2 failed" is visibly pre-existing rather than silently attributed to the change. This is the same shape KS-660 already applies to Schemathesis ("the failing SET ... + its diff vs the develop baseline set, never a bare count").

## Related

* **KS-961** - the aggregate workspace suite never runs on a PR. Adjacent, In Review, deliberately not extended.
* **KS-1046** - `PREFLIGHT PASSED` printed identically whether 13 legs ran or 10. Same family: a claim whose check did not run.
* **KS-927 / PR #926** - the fix for the red itself.

## Ask

**Kam or Wednesday to pick a fix shape** (or rule that the red simply waits for #926 and no instrument changes). Nothing here is urgent in the sense of a live outage - it is urgent in the sense that the next person to read a green board about `originate` will be reading a false one.

*Filed by s162 (Platform K), 2026-09-09, on Wednesday's ruling. Measurement is mine and reproducible from the commands above.*

nodes.body:
**Carried here from KS-826 — closed as Duplicate of this ticket and archived on 2026-09-14 (s222), under Kam's 2026-09-14 08:55 standing rule (true duplicates are closed and archived by us, no external review).** KS-826's surviving clause — its 2026-09-07 comment 920f558b gave the ks444 red to KS-927 and kept the ticket open ONLY for "no gate ever runs the four service suites" — is this ticket's ask.

What KS-826 held that this ticket did not:
- **The scope is every `services/*` unit suite, not originate alone.** Measured at `0e8d3e60a` / `055182bfe`: `referral` 5 suites / 26 tests · `staking` 3 / 61 · `vc-issuer` 8 / 86 · `originate` 44 / 476 — all otherwise green at the head, all unread by any gate. Whichever fix shape is picked above (a preflight leg / a periodic mainline run / a baseline-diff line), it covers the four, and KS-1146 (the `services/auth` instance) defers its decision here.
- **"Own it or gate it"** — KS-826's framing of the decision: (1) diagnose and fix the red so the suites are worth gating, or (2) add the suites to the gate and let the red block today; doing neither is the state to stop. A pre-existing low-value red is an argument for quarantining it with a written reason, never for leaving an unread red in a suite nobody runs — "a red with no reader teaches the fleet that reds are decorative".
- **KS-652** (no CI job runs any `services/*` unit suite) is the earlier ticket for this gap; KS-826's comment reads it as not actionable as written — it proposes a job on a PR gate that no longer runs.

Survivor: this ticket, by Wednesday's acceptance of the 2026-09-13 proposal's stated preference (it holds the measurement with four controlled instruments, the three fix shapes, the ask and the relations); KS-826 was the older id and its title still named the ks444 red it had given away.

title: CLAUDE.md's "rebuild local after any merge to develop" needs its written exception — a merge with zero buildable surface is a measured no-op
description:
## The ask

**Give** `CLAUDE.md`**'s "rebuild local after any merge to** `develop`**" rule its own written exception**, so the next seat does not have to re-derive it — or, worse, skip it without measuring.

Current wording (project `CLAUDE.md`, "Local + new-Azure sync workflow" §1):

> *"After any merge to* `develop`*, rebuild local so it stays current."*

## Why

On 2026-09-09 (s161) #904 was merged to `develop`. Measured before spending ~30 min of image builds:

```
2 files:  systemTest/__tests__/pre_suite.test.sh            +26/-1
          systemTest/__tests__/quarantine_call_sites.test.sh +27/-1
files with a buildable/deployable surface: 0
```

No service, frontend, package, migration, Dockerfile or compose file. **An image rebuild could not have changed anything** — so the local `develop` ref was synced and the images left alone, and the report said so plainly rather than claiming "local rebuilt".

That was the right call, but it is the **second** time in one session a written rule needed a measured departure. **A rule with a legitimate exception that every seat rediscovers is a rule someone will eventually skip without measuring** — and the departure is invisible unless the operator volunteers it.

## Suggested wording

> *"After any merge to* `develop` *that touches a **buildable surface** (*`services/`*,* `frontend/`*,* `packages/`*,* `migrations/`*, a Dockerfile or a compose file), rebuild local so it stays current. A merge touching only test scripts, docs or CI config is a **measured no-op** — say so, name the file count, and sync the ref instead of rebuilding."*

The load-bearing half is **"say so"**: the exception is only safe while the operator states which branch they took and on what measurement.

## Scope note

⚠ **There are TWO copies of this file** — the project-root `CLAUDE.md` and the repo copy at `2_Project_Files/CLAUDE.md`. Both need the edit or they drift, which is its own recurring trap here.

## What is NOT established

Whether the rule has ever actually been skipped *without* a measurement. **Not swept** — this is filed on the near-miss shape, not on an observed incident.

Filed by s161 on Wednesday's instruction, 2026-09-09.

title: Access-log visit id: bound the Download signature (exp + 24h) and adopt the visit on the PDF-password path
description:
Follow-up from Peter's reviews of [Secuura/platform-s#787](https://linear.app/secuura/review/ps-767-the-access-log-correlation-id-groups-a-visit-signed-into-the-f5638e4683a0) ([PS-767](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-767/senddocslinkaccesslogcorrelationid-correlates-nothing-a-fresh-guid-per)) and [Secuura/platform-s#794](https://linear.app/secuura/review/backlog-sweep-2026-09-08-ps-792-ps-797-ps-798-ps-796-ps-791-full-5a5cd42cd5d4) ([PS-792](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-792/the-pdf-password-forms-refusals-write-no-access-log-row-while-every)), 2026-09-09. All three notes were explicitly non-blocking and each is a **runtime change** in `SDViewDownload.cs`, so they were kept out of the approved branches and grouped here to go through their own gate.

## 1. `Download` puts no expiry bound on the visit signature (#787, note 1)

`Download(token, exp, sig, vid)` calls `TryAdoptVisit` regardless of `exp` — the comment justifies it with "a reader who took four minutes and then clicked Download", which is right, but nothing bounds it to four minutes. A signed download URL that is saved or forwarded can re-stamp rows under that visit id indefinitely, so a third party's download could appear inside the original recipient's visit. Not an authorisation weakness (the token remains the access control, unchanged); the row's own IP, user-agent and timestamp keep it recoverable.

**Fix:** a generous ceiling such as `exp + 24h` in `Download` before adopting — preserves the intent without the open end. Adoption still never refuses; past the ceiling the request simply keeps its own id. Pin it in `AccessLogCorrelationContractTests` (source shape) and `AccessLogVisitCorrelationTests` (behavioural: a signature whose `exp` is older than the ceiling is not adopted).

## 2. The [PS-792](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-792/the-pdf-password-forms-refusals-write-no-access-log-row-while-every) password-path rows land outside the visit (#787, note 3)

`EnterPdfPassword` (GET) and `EnterPdfPasswordPost` each mint their own correlation id and then redirect to `Landing`, which mints another. So the Expired / Unauthorized rows [PS-792](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-792/the-pdf-password-forms-refusals-write-no-access-log-row-while-every) added on that form group with nothing, and #787's own PR text ("[PS-792](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-792/the-pdf-password-forms-refusals-write-no-access-log-row-while-every) will add rows on the password path that this id groups") was written on an assumption that needs one more step to become true.

**Shape of the fix:** `Landing`'s redirect to `EnterPdfPassword` (`:216`, `:234`) has to carry the visit — a signed `{linkId}.{exp}.{vid}` like the stream URL — and both password actions adopt it via `TryAdoptVisit` before their first `TryLogAccessAsync`; the POST's redirect back to `Landing` then needs `Landing` to *adopt* rather than mint when a valid signed `vid` arrives. Note the ordering subtlety: today `Landing` refuses Expired / Unauthorized *before* the password redirect, so a password-path refusal only occurs when the link is revoked between the landing and the submission, or when the form URL is hit directly. Decide whether that is worth the extra plumbing before building it; if not, close this half with the reason written down.

## 3. [PS-792](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-792/the-pdf-password-forms-refusals-write-no-access-log-row-while-every)'s new rows are pinned by source text only (#794, note 4)

`PasswordFormRefusalsLogContractTests` asserts the four `TryLogAccessAsync` calls exist in the source. `TryLogAccessAsync` swallows and warns by design, so a row that never reached `SendDocsLinkAccessLog` would still pass everything on that branch. Low risk (`Landing` has made identical calls for a while), but it is the mirror image of the case [PS-791](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-791/share-revoke-notify-has-no-systemtest-handle-and-no-assertion-that-a) makes for itself.

**Fix:** a behavioural test in the `AccessLogVisitCorrelationTests` style — drive `EnterPdfPassword` / `EnterPdfPasswordPost` against an in-memory context with an expired and a revoked link and assert the row is written with `Viewed` + `Expired` / `Unauthorized`. Naturally combines with (2), since that is where the rows' correlation id gets asserted too.

## Acceptance

* **(1) The ceiling exists and is stated.** `Download` adopts a visit only while `now <= exp + 24h`; past the ceiling the request keeps its own correlation id and adoption still never *refuses*. The window is a named constant, not a literal buried in the action.
* **(1) Pinned in both estates' styles:** `AccessLogCorrelationContractTests` for the source shape, and `AccessLogVisitCorrelationTests` behaviourally — a signature whose `exp` is inside the ceiling **is** adopted, one older than the ceiling **is not**, and a boundary case either side of `exp + 24h`. These are rules: they belong in `tests/ssd.UnitTests`, run in about two minutes with nothing up, and must be red before the change.
* **(2) Decided in writing, either way.** Either `Landing`'s two redirects to `EnterPdfPassword` carry a signed `{linkId}.{exp}.{vid}`, both password actions adopt it before their first `TryLogAccessAsync`, and `Landing` adopts rather than mints when a valid signed `vid` arrives — or this half is closed with the reason recorded here (the ordering note above: a password-path refusal only happens on a link revoked between landing and submission, or on the form URL hit directly). A silent drop is not an outcome.
* **(3) The** [PS-792](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-792/the-pdf-password-forms-refusals-write-no-access-log-row-while-every) **rows are pinned by behaviour, not by source text.** A test in the `AccessLogVisitCorrelationTests` style drives `EnterPdfPassword` / `EnterPdfPasswordPost` against an in-memory context with an **expired** and a **revoked** link and asserts a row actually reaches `SendDocsLinkAccessLog` with `Viewed` + `Expired` / `Unauthorized` — `TryLogAccessAsync` swallows and warns, so `PasswordFormRefusalsLogContractTests` alone cannot see a row that never landed.
* A saved or forwarded signed download URL cannot re-stamp rows under the original recipient's visit id indefinitely — the stated purpose of (1).

**Playwright test that demonstrates the fix** (required for the half that is a surface — the admin access log has **no Playwright handle at all** today, which is part of why (3) was only pinnable by source text): a spec — suggest `systemTest/tests/functional/access_log_visit_correlation.spec.ts` (no existing spec selects `accesslog-table`; `pdf_password.spec.ts` drives the password form but never looks at the log) — that, against a live stack, asserts:

1. a recipient who opens a share link and then downloads within the window produces rows on `/SendDocsLinkAccessLogAdmin` whose `accesslog-correlation` values are **identical** — **control: this passes today** ([PS-767](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-767/senddocslinkaccesslogcorrelationid-correlates-nothing-a-fresh-guid-per)) and must keep passing;
2. **the previously failing case** — a **password-protected** link where the form is reached and refused writes its refusal row with the **same** `accesslog-correlation` as the landing row; today `EnterPdfPassword`, `EnterPdfPasswordPost` and `Landing` each mint their own, so the values differ and this assertion fails on `develop`;
3. the refusal row is present at all for both the expired and the revoked case (`accesslog-event-filter-select` on the Expired / Unauthorized kinds finds it), which is (3)'s behavioural claim seen from outside;
4. **second control:** the log still records and filters the `Viewed` kind for an ordinary successful view, and `accesslog-export-csv-link` still downloads — the admin surface is not disturbed by the plumbing.

The 24-hour ceiling in (1) is deliberately **not** asserted through the browser: it is a rule over a signature's `exp`, not reachable from a journey without fabricating a stale signature, so it stays in `AccessLogVisitCorrelationTests` where it runs in seconds.

## Verify

Runtime change → full gate per CLAUDE.md: xUnit red-proof for each new fact, then a full systemTest run on a claimed slot with numbers on the PR and here. `share_recipient_states` and the anonymous share-access utilities are the nearest live neighbours.

title: No independent liveness signal for our own VMs — kintsugi was dead for 53 h and Azure health read `Available` the whole time
description:
## BLUF

`secuura02-kintsugi-vm` **was down for 53 hours and nothing told us. The first signal was Stuart's tooling — a person, not a monitor. And Azure's own platform health read** `Available` **for the whole 53 hours, which is why the one alerting surface we do have would not have fired either.**

Both halves are one logical path — *we have no independent liveness signal for our own VMs* — so they are one ticket per Kam's 2026-09-06 aggregation rule, not two.

## What happened

* Azure live-migrated the VM at **2026-09-07T03:56:13Z** (`PlatformInitiated`, *"paused 0.993s, memory-preserving"*). The guest did not survive it.
* The workload died at ~**04:00Z**. On-disk logs **stop at 03:55:01Z** with **zero** entries for 53 h (control: **53** entries in the same hour).
* It came back only because a person went looking on **2026-09-09**, and was force-reset at **09:31:45Z**.

## Half 1 — no liveness signal

Nothing watches whether kintsugi is serving. There is no uptime check, no synthetic request, no alert on absence of logs. Detection was **incidental**.

⚠ This is the same shape as **KS-670** (demo's on-chain verification down **6 days**, found by a person). Two incidents, same missing control. That is the argument for fixing the class rather than the instance.

## Half 2 — the alerting surface we DO have was lying

Azure marked the box **Available at 03:59:30Z** and said *"no additional action is required"* — while the guest was dead and stayed dead for 53 hours. `memory-preserving` migration means **no reboot**, so Caddy survived in memory and kept answering at the edge while sshd, the guest agent and dockerd were all gone.

**So a health check that trusts either Azure resource health OR a naive port-200 on the front door would have reported green throughout.** Any monitor built here has to make a request that actually traverses the app, and has to alert on **silence** (no logs / no successful synthetic) rather than on an error, because a dead guest produces no errors at all — it produces nothing.

## Why this is due now

The incident record is closed (`5_Project_History/HANDOVER-kintsugi-outage-CLOSED.md`). **Recurrence is not** — Azure live-migrates this box as routine platform behaviour and the guest does not survive one. Boot diagnostics / serial console is now **ENABLED**, so a repeat leaves evidence; nothing currently tells us the repeat *happened*.

## Suggested shape (not a decision — the approach is open)

1. An external liveness check per VM (demo + kintsugi) that traverses the app, not just the edge — the front door answered while the box was dead.
2. Alert on **absence** — no successful synthetic in N minutes, or no new log lines — not on error responses.
3. Do **not** key anything off Azure resource health alone. This incident is the counter-example, in our own record.

## What is NOT established

* Whether the demo VM has the same exposure — **not measured**; it is the same subscription and region and probably does, but I did not check.
* The remount-read-only theory for the guest's death is **strongly supported, not proven**: no kernel message survived, because it could not be written to the disk it was about.

## Provenance

Azure activity log (read in slices — the API truncates silently at 50), the guest's own journal, `df` 37% and a clean `fsck` refuting ENOSPC and corruption from inside. Recorded by s160, filed by s161.

title: An organisation created with no name (a consumer-identity signup, KS-199) shows as "(unknown)" on Identity management → Organisations — nothing identifies it, and nobody is ever asked to name it
description: Seen by Stuart on dev-ps (`6282dbc`, 2026-09-09) on Identity management → Organisations: a third row, **"(unknown)"**, Unverified, with a `did:key` DID beside Obeden PTE Ltd and [secuura.ai](). ## What it is Organisation **9**: `Name`, `Code`, `FullLegalName` and `EntityType` all NULL, created 2026-08-21 13:08Z when [lhsgstuart@gmail.com]() signed up with **Google**. That is the designed outcome for a consumer identity with no organisation evidence — `OrgChoicePolicy.OrgChoiceOutcome.CreatesUnnamedOrganisation` (*"a new Organisation row is created with a NULL name (*[KS-199](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-199/organisation-required-for-upload))", `ssd/Services/OrgChoicePolicy.cs:66`). Its identity profile was provisioned at signup (profile 3, `AddedBy` = the person), trust Unverified — correct for a Gmail account. The admin tab then renders `org?.Name ?? "(unknown)"` (`IdentityManagementAdminController.Organisations`), so an administrator sees a row that names nothing: not the organisation id, not who is in it, not that it is a one-person consumer organisation. Two of them would be indistinguishable. Also on dev-ps: seed organisation **5** (`Code` `fsttwo`, holding [firsttwo@lhsg.com]()) has a NULL name from `DbSeeder` — a seed artefact, but it will render the same way once provisioned. ## Wanted 1. **Admin surfaces identify an unnamed organisation** by something stable and human: the organisation id and its first member's email, e.g. *Unnamed organisation* [Secuura/Distributed_Secuura#9](https://linear.app/secuura/review/ks-4-phase-5b-billingprismavq-tenant-isolation-ks-31-baseline-ks-24-f9b23f910c9a) *— [lhsgstuart@gmail.com]()*, with the same treatment wherever `Organisation.Name` is printed for administrators (Users tab, Organisation Verifications, dashboards). Never a bare "(unknown)". 2. **The person is asked to name it.** A consumer signup that creates an organisation lands its first member on a settings prompt (or the organisation page) to give it a name, and the prompt stays until one is given — the [KS-199](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-199/organisation-required-for-upload) NULL is a transitional state, not a permanent one. 3. **Seed data names every organisation** (`DbSeeder`: organisation 5). ## Verify * dev-ps as an Administrator: the Organisations tab shows *Unnamed organisation* [Secuura/Distributed_Secuura#9](https://linear.app/secuura/review/ks-4-phase-5b-billingprismavq-tenant-isolation-ks-31-baseline-ks-24-f9b23f910c9a) *— [lhsgstuart@gmail.com]()*; provisioning organisation 5 shows it as *Unnamed organisation* [Secuura/secuura-extranet#5](https://linear.app/secuura/review/ks-147-auto-surface-reply-on-question-to-dos-prominent-answer-button-9fcfa5ef4281) *— [firsttwo@lhsg.com]()* until the seeder names it. * A fresh Google/GitHub signup on a slot: the person is prompted to name their organisation; after naming, the admin tab shows the name. ## Acceptance * No administrator surface prints a bare **"(unknown)"**. `IdentityManagementAdminController.Organisations` and every other place that prints `Organisation.Name` for an administrator (Users tab, Organisation Verifications, dashboards) renders a stable, human label — *Unnamed organisation # — * — from one shared formatter, so two unnamed organisations are distinguishable. * The Organisation cell on `/IdentityAdmin/Organisations` gains a testid of its own: today it is a bare `@r.Name` inside `identity-admin-org-row-@r.SubjectId` with nothing to select (suggest `identity-admin-org-name`; confirm the name when adding it, per the `--` rule). * A consumer signup whose `OrgChoicePolicy` outcome is `CreatesUnnamedOrganisation` lands its first member on a name-your-organisation prompt, and the prompt **persists across navigations** until a name is saved — the [KS-199](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-199/organisation-required-for-upload) NULL is transitional, not permanent. * `DbSeeder` names every organisation it creates, including the seed organisation holding [firsttwo@lhsg.com]() (code `fsttwo`), so the seed stops manufacturing the same defect. * **xUnit companion** (the rule half, `tests/ssd.UnitTests`): the label formatter is a rule — pin that a NULL/blank/whitespace `Name` yields the id + first-member form, that a named organisation is returned unchanged, and that `"(unknown)"` appears in no output for any input. **Playwright test that demonstrates the fix** (required — the surface is the subject here): a spec — suggest `systemTest/tests/functional/unnamed_organisation.spec.ts` (no existing spec covers this; `identity_admin.spec.ts` asserts only that the governance screens load) — that, against a live stack as **Administrator**, loads `/IdentityAdmin/Organisations` and asserts: 1. **the previously failing case** — `identity-admin-orgs-table` contains **no cell whose text is** `(unknown)`; today the NULL-named seed organisation renders exactly that, so this assertion fails on `develop`; 2. that organisation's row (`identity-admin-org-row-…`) shows the **id and the first member's email** in its Organisation cell — also failing today, since the markup emits only `@r.Name`; 3. a fresh external signup through the existing join seam (the pattern in `google_join_seam.spec.ts` / `github_join_seam.spec.ts`) that creates an unnamed organisation is **prompted to name it**, the prompt is still present after navigating away and back, and once a name is saved the admin tab shows **that** name — none of which exists today; 4. **control, passes today and must keep passing:** a named organisation's row still shows its own name verbatim and carries no *Unnamed organisation* label, and `identity-admin-org-trust` on both rows still reads its trust level (the fix must not disturb the trust column or the override form). It must fail on today's `develop` and pass after the change.

title: The Verifiable Credentials page tells an Entra-verified person to "Verify my identity" and holds no credential for them — the wallet reads only the imported profile, and the import keys the credential on a `jti` Microsoft does not send
description:
Asked by Stuart on dev-ps (`6282dbc`, 2026-09-09): *"Should the DID be shown here?"* — the Verifiable Credentials page for [stuart@obeden.com](<mailto:stuart@obeden.com>), Entra-verified on 2026-09-04 (Person 8: `IdVerifiedOn` set, `IdToken3` = `did:jwk:…`, KycVerification 5 Approved with `IssuerDid`), shows **"No identity profile yet" / "Verify my identity"**.

## What the page does today (`Views/Shared/_IdentityWallet.cshtml`, `IdentityWalletService`)

The card is a viewer of the **wallet tables** only — `IdentityProfile` → `Did` → `VerifiableCredential`. It never consults `Person.IdVerifiedOn`, `IdToken3` or the approved `KycVerification`. So:

1. **No** `IdentityProfile` **→ "No identity profile yet" + a *Verify my identity* button**, even for a person the dashboard card, `/identity/verify` and `/EntraVerify` all call verified ([PS-789](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-789/the-dashboard-id-card-and-the-hosted-verification-pages-disagree-with) made those three agree; this fourth surface still disagrees). On dev-ps the two Entra-verified people (8, 15) have no profile because their verifications predate the [PS-790](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-790/after-an-entra-verification-the-page-offers-go-to-document-signing-and) import, and nobody has run the admin backfill (`POST /IdentityManagementAdmin/BackfillEntraIdentities`).
2. **After the import, the DID shows** (`identity-wallet-did`, the subject `did:jwk:…` from `IdToken3`) — that half is right. **But the credential does not**: `EntraIdentityBackfillService` writes the `VerifiableCredential` only when `IdToken2` (the credential id, taken from the presentation's `jti`) is set, and on dev-ps it is NULL for both people — Microsoft's presentation carried no `jti`. So the wallet then reads *Assurance · DID · "No credentials held yet" · Verify my identity* for someone whose verification is Approved with a recorded issuer DID.

## Wanted

* The wallet states the person's **effective** status the way the other surfaces do (`IIdentityStatusResolver`, [PS-789](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-789/the-dashboard-id-card-and-the-hosted-verification-pages-disagree-with)): a verified person never sees a *Verify my identity* call to action; an unverified one does.
* An Entra-verified person **holds a credential**: derive it from the approved `KycVerification` (issuer DID, level, completed-at, request id as a stable id such as `urn:entra:request:<ProviderSessionId>`) when the presentation carried no `jti`, rather than dropping it. The completion import ([PS-790](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-790/after-an-entra-verification-the-page-offers-go-to-document-signing-and)) and the admin backfill ([PS-432](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-432/identity-backfill-entra-verified-id-dids-and-credentials-into-the)) both go through `BackfillPersonAsync`, so one change covers both.
* The DID row stays; consider showing the **issuer** DID beside it for an Entra profile (it is on the KycVerification already).

## Verify

* dev-ps, [stuart@obeden.com](<mailto:stuart@obeden.com>) after the backfill: the page shows Assurance, the `did:jwk` DID, and one held credential issued by `did:web:verifiedid.entra.microsoft.com:2fefc32a…`; no *Verify my identity* button.
* A fresh Entra completion ([PS-790](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-790/after-an-entra-verification-the-page-offers-go-to-document-signing-and) path) lands the same way without the backfill.
* An unverified person still sees "No identity profile yet" and the button.

## Update 2026-09-10 — after the backfill on dev-ps (Stuart)

The backfill ran; [stuart@obeden.com](<mailto:stuart@obeden.com>)'s page now shows **Assurance · Standard · NIST IAL2**, the `did:jwk:…` DID, then **"Held credentials — No credentials held yet" and a *Verify my identity* button**. Stuart's review of that page, adopted as the wanted behaviour here:

1. **The statement is wrong** — the person holds an approved Entra Verified ID verification (issuer DID recorded on the KycVerification), so "No credentials held yet" is false; item 2 above (derive the held credential from the approved verification when the presentation carried no `jti`).
2. **The button reads "Add additional verification"** for a verified person (Stuart, 2026-09-10) — never *Verify my identity* once the effective status is verified; it still goes to `/identity/verify`, which shows the current status and the provider selection. An unverified person keeps *Verify my identity*.
3. **Formatting: the DID is unwieldy.** A `did:jwk` embeds the whole public key, so it is \~230 characters; `idk-mono` does carry `word-break: break-all`, so it wraps on a narrow viewport, but on a wide one it fills the row to the card edge as a single unreadable line. Wanted: a middle-truncated display (`did:jwk:eyJrdHki…Gh2byJ9`) with the full value as the title and a copy control — same treatment wherever a DID is printed in a card row. `did:key` values on the Identity management tables are short enough to stay whole.
4. *Assurance Standard / NIST IAL2* is correct for an Entra Verified ID completion (`IdentityStatusResolver.EntraVerifiedIdLevel`).

## Acceptance

* The wallet card states the person's **effective** status through `IIdentityStatusResolver`, the same source the dashboard card, `/identity/verify` and `/EntraVerify` use ([PS-789](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-789/the-dashboard-id-card-and-the-hosted-verification-pages-disagree-with)) — so this fourth surface stops disagreeing with the other three.
* A verified person never sees a *Verify my identity* call to action. The control reads **"Add additional verification"** (Stuart, 2026-09-10) and still goes to `/identity/verify`. An unverified person keeps *Verify my identity*.
* An Entra-verified person **holds a credential**: when the presentation carried no `jti` (`IdToken2` NULL), the credential is derived from the approved `KycVerification` — issuer DID, level, completed-at, and a stable id such as `urn:entra:request:<ProviderSessionId>`. One change in `BackfillPersonAsync` covers both the [PS-790](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-790/after-an-entra-verification-the-page-offers-go-to-document-signing-and) completion import and the [PS-432](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-432/identity-backfill-entra-verified-id-dids-and-credentials-into-the) admin backfill.
* The DID row stays, with the issuer DID shown beside it for an Entra profile.
* Every DID printed in a card row is **middle-truncated** (`did:jwk:eyJrdHki…Gh2byJ9`) with the full value as the title and a copy control — the same treatment wherever a DID appears in a card. Short `did:key` values on the Identity management tables stay whole.
* *Assurance Standard / NIST IAL2* for an Entra completion is unchanged (`IdentityStatusResolver.EntraVerifiedIdLevel`).

**Playwright test that demonstrates the fix** (required): extend `systemTest/tests/functional/identity_wallet.spec.ts` — it already owns this card, and the surface is the whole subject here. Against a live stack it must assert, for a person whose identity status resolves to verified:

1. `identity-wallet-credentials` holds at least one `identity-wallet-credential-*` row, and `identity-wallet-empty` is **absent** — **this is the assertion that fails on today's** `develop`, where the card renders "No credentials held yet" for a person with an approved verification and a recorded issuer DID;
2. `identity-wallet-verify-link` reads **"Add additional verification"**, not "Verify my identity" — the second failing assertion today;
3. `identity-wallet-did-row` is present and `identity-wallet-did`'s **visible text is shorter than its** `title` for a `did:jwk` (the \~230-character value is truncated, the full value recoverable), with no horizontal page scroll at desktop width;
4. the issuer DID is shown beside the subject DID for an Entra-sourced profile;
5. **control (passes today and must keep passing):** for a person with no identity profile, `identity-wallet-none` is shown and `identity-wallet-verify-link` still reads **"Verify my identity"** — the fix must not suppress the call to action for someone who genuinely needs it.

Use a persona of this spec's own rather than the shared AccountAdmin, since the assertions depend on that account's verification state. The xUnit companion stays the pin for the derive-from-`KycVerification` rule itself (no `jti` → a credential with the `urn:entra:request:` id; `jti` present → today's behaviour).

title: tests/e2e 2.4.6 'SQL injection in registration name is sanitized' asserts against an ECHO — a permanent red carrying no signal
description:
## BLUF

`auth-exhaustive.spec.ts:734` **fails on an echo, not an injection, and the assertion cannot tell them apart.** It is red in **5 of 5** measured runs and will stay red for any application that stores and returns a user-supplied display name.

## Measured

`POST /api/auth/register` with `name = "Robert'); DROP TABLE users; --"`:

* returns **201**
* body carries `"displayname":"robert'); drop table users; --"` back **verbatim**
* **the injection did not execute** — no SQL error, no `syntax error`, no 5xx. The sibling assertions on `'sql'` and `'syntax error'` both **pass**. Parameterised SQL held.

The only failing line is:

```js
expect(body.toLowerCase()).not.toContain('drop table');   // line 751
```

**Control that it is not simple unfiltered input:** sibling **2.4.7 (XSS in name) passes**, so the field is not merely echoed unfiltered everywhere.

## Suggested fix

Re-aim it at what it means to assert: no SQL error **and** `status < 500` (both already true), or assert the stored value equals the exact input. **The output-escaping question is separate** and needs frontend evidence — deliberately UNMEASURED here: I measured the echo, not the renderers.

## Provenance

* the 201 + verbatim echo + passing siblings | recorded on KS-734's 2026-09-02 comment, which asked for this ticket; re-confirmed red in 5 of 5 runs 2026-09-09
* **Attribution, measured not assumed:** not #745's — its three hunks all sit in `2.8 MFA / TOTP` (lines 1207–1352); this is line 734.

title: tests/e2e auth-exhaustive races its OWN lockout — same commit gives 1 or 11 failures, so the suite cannot gate anything
description:
## BLUF

`tests/e2e/tests/auth-exhaustive.spec.ts` **is non-deterministic against an unchanged product.** It brute-forces logins, `playwright.config.ts` sets `fullyParallel: true`, and every run leaves **4** `lockout:*` **keys** in redis — so its own ordinary login cells race its own lockout. Until this is fixed the suite cannot be used as a gate, because a failure count carries no information.

## Measured — 2026-09-09, `develop` `b6884888d`, `lockout:*` cleared before EACH run

| run | command | result |
| -- | -- | -- |
| A | three specs | **23 failed / 54 passed** |
| B | three specs | **11 failed / 71 passed** |
| C | `auth-exhaustive.spec.ts` alone | **1 failed / 52 passed** |
| D | `auth-exhaustive.spec.ts` alone | **11 failed / 42 passed** |

**Nothing about the product changed between any of them.** Lockout keys were counted after every run: 4 each time, so the suite reliably creates them and unreliably outruns them.

**The flapping cells move as ONE block** — both 23-failure runs carried exactly the same 23, which is what rules out twelve independent flakes and points at a single shared cause. They are all in `auth-exhaustive.spec.ts`: 2.1.1–2.1.5, 2.2.8, 2.2.9, 2.8.1, 2.9.1, 2.9.2, 2.9.4, 2.9.5.

**The deterministic remainder is 10 recruitment/wallet cells** (red in 5 of 5 runs) plus `auth-exhaustive.spec.ts:734`, whose assertion is wrong rather than the app — filed separately.

## Suggested fix (not prescribed)

Either serialise this file (`test.describe.configure({ mode: 'serial' })` or a dedicated non-parallel project), or give the brute-force cells a **dedicated account** so they cannot lock the fixture persona the rest of the file logs in with. The second is likely better: it keeps the parallelism and removes the coupling.

## Class

This is the **KS-724** family — a harness that stops testing while still producing results. There, a scan evicted its own bearer; here, a suite locks out its own persona.

## Provenance

* the four runs, lockout counts, and the identical 23-cell block | measured live on the local stack, recorded in `Blockchain/Dev/tests/e2e/BASELINE.md` | 2026-09-09
* Filed from KS-734's baseline work (s160), which made the suite installable and could then measure it.

title: The review-stream overlay covers 57 of 114 active tickets, and DEV-PROCESS still says 'nothing left over'
description:
## BLUF

**The review-stream overlay Kam adopted on 2026-09-03 now covers exactly half the board, and** `DEV-PROCESS.md` **still says it covers all of it.** A handover organised by stream today silently omits **22 of the 32** PR-bearing tickets.

## Measured, 2026-09-09

`DEV-PROCESS.md` §*The four review streams, built 2026-09-03* states:

> All **97** active Platform K tickets now sit under four parents — 40 + 19 + 18 + 20, nothing left over

Today, over `state.type in (started, unstarted)` on team KS:

|  | count |
| -- | -- |
| active Platform K tickets | **114** |
| directly under a review-stream parent | **57** (KS-485 19 · KS-772 15 · KS-770 12 · KS-771 11) |
| under some other parent | 5 |
| **no parent at all** | **52** |
| **NOT under a review stream** | **57 of 114** |

The doc's per-parent figures (40/19/18/20) do not match any parent's current child count either.

## Why it bites right now

Building the review blocks for Kam's handover, **22 of the 32 tickets that carry an open PR have no stream parent** — including every one of today's ready items: KS-926, KS-963, KS-968, KS-991, KS-992, KS-993, KS-1026, KS-936, KS-942, KS-945, KS-961, KS-909, KS-931, KS-791, KS-798/799/841, KS-764, KS-682, KS-971, KS-229, KS-1004.

The rule in the same doc is *"Every new K-side ticket that reaches Todo is parented into one of the four"*. That step is not happening — and nothing fails when it is skipped, which is why it went unnoticed for six days. **Same family as KS-926: a rule with no check behind it.**

⚠ There is also a **discoverability trap in the doc's own shape**: three parents are findable by title (`Review stream: …`) but the fourth, **KS-485**, is titled *"Security review — plan, methodology & handover (Platform K)"*. A title search for review-stream parents returns **3 of 4**. This session hit exactly that and only caught KS-485 by reading DEV-PROCESS.

## Checklist

- [ ] Parent the 22 PR-bearing tickets into their stream (placement already derived per-PR in the s159 review-block report — reuse it rather than re-deriving)
- [ ] Sweep the remaining unparented active tickets (52 total with no parent)
- [ ] Correct the counts in `DEV-PROCESS.md` §*The four review streams* — or, better, stop hardcoding a number that decays and point at a query
- [ ] Rename KS-485 so all four parents are findable by title, **or** name all four explicitly in the doc so a title search is not the discovery path
- [ ] Decide where the check lives so an unparented Todo cannot sit unnoticed — the board equivalent of KS-926's census

## Provenance

Linear GraphQL, team KS, `state.type in (started, unstarted)`, direct `parent` field. PR->ticket map from the 43 open PRs. Measured 2026-09-09 by the Platform K s159 seat.

title: The merge gate cannot see a WITHDRAWN approval — #813 reads approved+clean against the reviewer's written refusal
description:
## BLUF

**A reviewer can withdraw an approval and BOTH GitHub instruments keep reporting the PR as approved.** The repo's merge gate is *"approval is the signal, the author merges"* (CLAUDE.md, Kam 2026-08-25). On PR #813 that gate currently reads GREEN against the reviewer's explicit written refusal.

## The instance

Peter, on #813 (KS-791, verify-file):

* **14:52:21Z 2026-09-08** — submitted `APPROVED` at `54225cbbd`
* **14:56:21Z 2026-09-08** — submitted `COMMENTED` at the same commit: *"My earlier approval on this PR was premature and I'm withdrawing it — I'll ask a maintainer to dismiss it, since I can't retract it myself."*

Nobody dismissed it. Measured today:

| instrument | reads #813 as |
| -- | -- |
| `GET /pulls/813/reviews` | `PeterObeden: APPROVED`, `commit_id == head.sha` -> **at-head approval** |
| search index `is:pr is:open review:approved` | **matches #813** |
| `mergeable_state` | `clean` |
| Peter's own prose | **withdrawn, holding for complete systemTest evidence** |

`commit_id == head.sha` **does not catch this.** That discriminator exists for a *stale* approval — one the head moved past. A **withdrawn** approval sits at the head, because the head never moved. The check we rely on is blind to it by construction.

## It is not a one-off — swept, with the arithmetic closed

Across all **43** open PRs, exactly **two** carry an `APPROVED` later followed by a `COMMENTED` review from the same reviewer: **#813** and **#785**. Both comment bodies say *"holding"*. No others.

* **#785** (KS-229) — also holding; there the last `APPROVED` sits at a **superseded** commit, so the `commit_id` check *does* catch it — but the **search index still counts it approved**.
* So the index's headline **"10 approved"** is really **8**.

## Why it matters

A withdrawn approval is invisible to every automated read of this repo's merge gate. The only instrument that sees it is the reviewer's prose. Any session — human or agent — that clears the queue by "approved + clean" will merge #813 against a written refusal.

## Checklist

- [ ] Ask a maintainer to **dismiss** the stale `APPROVED` on #813 (Peter asked for this on 2026-09-08 and it has not happened)
- [ ] Same for #785's superseded approvals
- [ ] Add the withdrawn-approval case to the boot/pre-merge sweep: an `APPROVED` is only live if **no later review from the same user exists at or after it** — not merely `commit_id == head.sha`
- [ ] Write the rule into `docs/DEV-PROCESS.md` next to the existing at-head paragraph, which currently names only staleness as the failure mode
- [ ] Decide whether a `CHANGES_REQUESTED` should be the house convention for withdrawal, since GitHub gives a reviewer no retract action

## Provenance

`/pulls/{n}/reviews` for all 43 open PRs + `search/issues` index counts (10 approved / 2 changes_requested / 30 none = 42 open at sweep time, +#918 opened during the session = 43). Measured 2026-09-09 by the Platform K s159 seat.

nodes.body: **BLUF:** Delivered: PR 1136 merged as f372149518f8 on develop; no deploy surface (docs only: Blockchain/Dev/docs/DEV-PROCESS.md, the squash's only file). Verified by docs read: `Blockchain/Dev/docs/DEV-PROCESS.md:219` states that the merge-gate endpoint is blind to a withdrawn approval (KS-1035). Left open: that is the documentation item only. The description still lists five unchecked items when read today, among them asking a maintainer to dismiss the stale APPROVED on #813 and the superseded approvals on #785, and nothing on the ticket records them done.

## Record 8d from the tier-1 gate on PR #813 (KS-791), 2026-09-14 09:11:56Z — the instance this ticket describes, re-read at merge time (merge seat s228)

`GET /pulls/813/reviews` at 09:14Z: `5143298493` APPROVED and `5143348040` COMMENTED ("Holding my approval… withdrawing it"), both at `commit_id 54225cbbd` while the head is `7b6fb960d` (s226's 2026-09-14 07:14Z push: the unpushed 09-11 head `7be1eccbe` plus develop M38 merged in). The approval is withdrawn by the reviewer's own words and stale by `commit_id`; the merge protocol's review gate reads only CHANGES_REQUESTED (none on #813) and treats a stale APPROVED as neither a block nor a condition — under the 2026-09-11 TESTED grant the condition is the QA gate's verdict at the current head plus the Test Evidence block (tier-1 GO WITH FINDINGS 09:11:56Z at `7b6fb960d`). Nobody dismissed either review; the merge seat touched nothing on them. Report `2026-09-14-ks791-813-7b6fb960d-tier1-r1` §7 and §8 8d. Facts only.

title: KS-926 residue: the three guards that could NOT be wired, and what each needs first — a wrong diff base, a self-contradicting default, and a whole-machine read
description:
**From KS-926.** Fourteen of the seventeen unreached guards were wired. **These three were not, and each needs a fix before it can be** — recorded so the next reader inherits the reasoning rather than re-deriving it. All three reasons are measured, at `fe0fd640c`.

## 1. `check-no-demo-mutation.sh` — WRONG DIFF BASE for this branching model

Line 58 defaults to `BASE="origin/main"` and diffs `BASE...HEAD`. **Under Git Flow,** `develop` **is permanently ahead of** `main`, so every develop-based branch shows the whole develop↔main delta as its own change.

**Measured on a branch that touched nothing:** it reported 4 demo files as modified —
`deployment/azure/env.demo.json`, `migrate/Dockerfile`, `migrate/init.sql`, `migrate/run-platform.sh`.

**Fix:** base it on the merge-base with `origin/develop` (or on `GITHUB_BASE_REF` when set, which it already honours at line 51-52). Wired as-is it would demand `[demo-mutation-allowed]` from every author on every push — a `--no-verify` generator.

## 2. `check-no-trust-header-reads.sh` — its printed advice contradicts its own default

Line 48: `level="${TRUST_HEADER_LINT_MODE:-fail}"` — **the default is** `fail`**.**
Line 60, printed to the user: *"Set* `TRUST_HEADER_LINT_MODE=fail` *to switch this from warn to a hard CI gate once cleanup is complete."*

**It tells you to set a variable to the value it already has**, and describes itself as a warn-mode lint when it is a hard gate. Verified three ways: `warn` → exit 0, `fail` → exit 1, unset → **exit 1**.

**Fix:** one of — correct the message to match the default, or make the default `warn` and the message true. **Deciding which is the point**, not a formality: it is red with 9 real findings (its own ticket), so the default decides whether wiring it freezes the repo.

## 3. `check-container-isolation.sh` — not a property of the tree

It reads **whole-machine Docker state** (`docker ps -a`, `docker network ls`). Here it failed on:

* **another session's containers, days old** — `ks597-qa-pg`, `qa-ks800-wabot-negctl`, `qa-ks800-wabot-guarded`, `secuura-queue`, `secuura-guardian`
* having only **1** platform stack up, which it itself calls a *"vacuous"* comparison

**A pre-push gate that reds on a colleague's stale container is exactly the** `--no-verify` **generator KS-926 warns about.** Its home is stack start-up (`start-local.sh` / `start-environment.sh`, where `check-slot-credentials.sh` already lives), not the push.

## Where they are recorded now

`Blockchain/Dev/scripts/run-code-guards.sh`, `DEFERRED` bucket — each with its reason inline. The census counts them as accounted-for, so they do not fail the push, and they cannot be silently forgotten either: removing one from the bucket without wiring it fails the census.

Verified by code read at b1fb543640e7; not run. Left open: guard 1 landed; guards 2 and 3 and two guard-1 follow-ups remain, each re-read and still true at that sha.

- **Landed (guard 1):** `check-no-demo-mutation.sh` defaults its base to `origin/develop` (:62) and refuses an unresolvable base with exit 2 (:66-69).

Measured directly with `grep -n 'BASE='` at the live tip: lines 56 (`origin/${GITHUB_BASE_REF}`), 59 (`$1`), 62 (`origin/develop`).

**So the reason text at `run-code-guards.sh:116` is now stale** — it still says "it defaults to `BASE=origin/main` (line 58)". **STAYS IN PROGRESS — guard 1 only; guards 2 and 3 are untouched.**

**Guard 1 — done.** `check-no-demo-mutation.sh` defaults to `origin/develop` at `:62` (since #1185), and #1209 (`6cf8229ab`) added the exit-2 refusal of an unresolvable base.

That has been false since #1185 — the script defaults to `origin/develop` at `:62`. **The string is what is wrong, not the script.** It has already misled once: it was quoted into a PR body as though it described live behaviour.

*Round-20 closing pass, Seat B 24th, 2026-09-25.*

Gate record — batch gate `2026-09-22-batch1180-1197-r1` graded #1185 GO WITH FINDINGS; #1185 merged to develop as `2d49c4bddeeb9489231277450c0517839b2e2cbf`. Minor DEMOBASE-MISSINGBASE-FAILOPEN: record-class, ships-with; next-round cell proposed by the gate. The gate's NOT-PINNED row, verbatim:

title: Security: 9 trust-header reads outside auth middleware (pen-test F-04) — surfaced by wiring check-no-trust-header-reads.sh in KS-926
description:
**Found by RUNNING a guard that had never run.** KS-926 wired the `check-*.sh` guards; this one had no live entry point, so its findings had never been seen. Its default level is `fail`, so it is red the moment anything invokes it.

## The 9, verbatim from the guard

```
services/api-gateway/src/routes/verification.ts:1041  req.headers['x-tenant-id']
services/api-gateway/src/routes/verification.ts:1042  req.headers['x-tenant-slug']
services/security/src/index.ts:968                    req.headers['x-tenant-id']
services/prism/src/index.ts:111                       req.headers['x-tenant-id']
services/originate/src/index.ts:230                   req.headers['x-tenant-id']
services/originate/src/routes/metering.ts:42          req.headers['x-user-role'] === 'connector' && x-tenant-id
services/originate/src/routes/metering.ts:43          req.headers['x-user-id']  -> sets (req as any).user
services/originate/src/routes/metering.ts:45          req.headers['x-tenant-id'] -> sets (req as any).tenantId
packages/shared/src/db/tenant-guc.ts:119              req.headers['x-tenant-id']
```

`metering.ts:42-45` **is the one to look at first:** it builds `req.user` and `req.tenantId` **from headers**, gated only on `x-user-role === 'connector'`. That is the trust-header vulnerability in its literal form if the header is reachable from outside.

## The guard's own instruction

> Use `req.user.*` (set by `authenticate()` middleware) instead of `req.headers['x-user-*']`. Direct header reads re-introduce the trust-header vulnerability.

The guard already excludes legitimate middleware paths (`/middleware/auth.ts`, `authenticate.ts`, `scopes.ts`, `tenant*`, `db/tenant-context.ts`, `security/gdpr-compliance.ts`) and lines marked `F-04-allowed`, so **these 9 are outside the sanctioned set by the guard's own definition.**

## Triage needed per site

Some may be legitimate **forwarding** (api-gateway 1041-42 sets `forwardHeaders`, which is a different act from trusting) and should carry `F-04-allowed` with a reason. Others look like real trust. **Do not bulk-annotate** — that converts a finding into a silence.

## Blocks

`check-no-trust-header-reads.sh` cannot be wired into the pre-push gate until this is 0 or the legitimate sites are annotated. Related: KS-619 (gateway tenant resolution falling through to the caller's `x-tenant-id`), and KS-926.

nodes.body:
**KS-1600** carries an open question against this ticket's effect. The pull request 1547 round-2 gate (report `ccbe317fcbf769f3`) measured that a forged `x-tenant-id` sent **directly to originate's router** is honoured — `ORG_ADMIN(A1)` + `organizations:register` + `organizationId: A1` with `x-tenant-id: T2` returns 201 with the key stored in tenant T2. The gate's reading is that KS-1032, now on `develop` `92d1316ffe31cb13b3f7e843e7891225383b2f84`, shuts that path, because `gatewayProvenance` strips trust headers when `GATEWAY_VOUCH_SECRET` is unset and the KS-458 resolution reads `x-tenant-id` only on a vouched request. **That is a reading, not a measurement** — the gate's harness mounts the router without `index.ts`'s middleware, so it was never run end to end.

The instrument that would settle it, recorded on KS-1600: one end-to-end request through originate's real middleware stack on `develop` `92d1316f`, `GATEWAY_VOUCH_SECRET` unset, forged `x-tenant-id: T2`, expecting the key to land in the caller's own tenant rather than T2.

Facts only; no state change asked for here.

## BLUF

- **Recorded from KS-1041, so this residual stays on a live ticket when KS-1041 closes.** KS-1041 wrote down that services other than originate also read trust headers, and that nobody had read their sites.
- **This ticket is the live home for that class:** trust-header reads outside auth middleware, triaged per site.
- **Not commissioned and not ruled.** KS-1041's two steps did not widen to these services.
  - Step 1: #938 → `0f8fb33c3` closed nginx `/originate/`.
  - Step 2: #951 is originate's gateway-provenance middleware. It stays inert while `GATEWAY_VOUCH_SECRET` is unset (KS-1083).

## Recommendation

No action needed now. When this ticket's per-site triage runs, include the services KS-1041 named.

## Detail

- **KS-1041's wording, verbatim:**
  - `923cfb00` (2026-09-10): *"`api-gateway`, `auth`, `billing`, `prism`, `security` and `tokenisation` also read these headers. **I am not asserting they are safe — I have not read their sites.**"*
  - `116ed2d6`, and PR #951's *Not in scope*: *"the seven other services that read trust headers"*.
  - Six are named and "seven" is counted. Both are quoted as written; neither was re-measured here.
- **Overlap with this ticket's 9 sites:**
  - api-gateway, security and prism appear in both.
  - auth, billing and tokenisation do not appear here. This ticket's guard excludes middleware paths (`/middleware/auth.ts`, `authenticate.ts`, `tenant*`, and others), which may be why — not checked.
  - `originate/src/index.ts:230` and `routes/metering.ts:42-45` are the originate sites that #951's middleware covers once the secret is provisioned. Until then they behave as before.
- **Board searched before posting** (literal, live tickets only):
  - `trust headers` → KS-1041 only;
  - `x-user-role` → KS-1041 and KS-1032;
  - `x-tenant-id` → 8, of which KS-1032 is the only one about reads across services;
  - `header-reading` 0 · `seven other` 0.

title: KS-754 gate F-4: DEPLOY CONDITION — apply 048 BEFORE rolling the originate image, or every connector erasure shreds the DEK then aborts forever (and run-migrations.sh exits 0 when migrations fail)
description:
🔴 **THIS IS A DEPLOY CONDITION, not only a ticket. No deploy is authorised by the #914 gate.**

## The condition — for whoever rolls originate

**Apply migration 048 BEFORE rolling the originate image, and confirm** `processed_by` **is** `text` **in the target DB first.**

## What happens if you don't — driven, not theorised (gate scenario S2)

Head code against a DB where 048 has not landed: **every connector erasure anonymises the user, destroys the DEK, then aborts.** `USER_ERASED=0`, DSR left `processing`. The cause (`22P02`) is **not transient**, so the connector's unbounded retry **never** succeeds — each iteration re-runs steps 1–11. This turns the F-1 finding from transient into **deterministic**.

## Why the existing guard does not save you — and this is its own defect

`docker-compose.yml` **does** gate originate on `migrations: service_completed_successfully`. But `scripts/run-migrations.sh` **exits 0 when migrations fail, by design** (its own closing block; BACKLOG #6). **So compose's condition is satisfied by a run in which 048 failed.**

On **Azure** there is no such ordering at all: migrations run at **api-gateway** boot (`startup-migrations.ts`) while originate is a separate app.

## Fixes — two, and they are separable

1. The deploy-ordering condition above, recorded where a deployer reads it (PR body + `DEPLOYMENT-ARCHITECTURE.md` / the DR runbook), not only here.
2. `run-migrations.sh` **must not exit 0 on a failed migration** — that is a gate that cannot fail (KS-926 family), and it is what makes the compose guard decorative.

## Related

F-1 (same erasure path, made deterministic by this) and the KS-926 checks-that-cannot-fail campaign.

Report: `.../2026-09-09-qa-gate-ks754-pr914/report.md`

title: KS-754 gate F-3 (MINOR): migration 048 ships with ZERO automated coverage — test:migrations is hard-wired to 044, so a migrations/ change fires a gate about a different migration
description:
**Source:** tier-1 QA gate on PR #914, 2026-09-09.

## The gap

048's new suite **mocks** `$executeRaw` **outright and never touches a database** — its name claims the column widening it does not exercise.

The repo's only migration-behaviour gate, `npm run test:migrations`, is **hard-wired to one file**:

```
MIGRATION="$HERE/../044_vault_entries_repair.sql"
```

The CI job gated on *"did this change touch* `migrations/`*?"* therefore runs the **044** scenarios. So a `migrations/` change fires a gate about a **different migration** — and Actions is retired for this repo anyway.

The gate driver ran 048 by hand and it holds. **Nothing will drive it again.**

## Why it matters

KS-667's own argument applies verbatim: 048's claimed behaviours are behaviours of **Postgres executing it**, which a mock cannot assert.

## The fix

Make `test:migrations` take the migration(s) under test rather than a hard-wired path, and add 048's scenarios (FK drop forced; constraint name; idempotency — all three already driven by hand in the gate report §5).

## Family

This is a **check that cannot fail** in the KS-926 sense — the gate runs and asserts something other than the change that triggered it.

Report: `.../2026-09-09-qa-gate-ks754-pr914/report.md`

title: Reshape the advisory gate: it is NON-DETERMINISTIC on an unchanged tree — 8 advisories in 30 min, one appeared then vanished. Warn-then-fail, keyed on REACH and SEVERITY (window length is Kam's)
description:
## BLUF

**The advisory gate is NON-DETERMINISTIC ON AN UNCHANGED TREE.** Two runs of the same commit, minutes apart, give different verdicts — because it hard-fails on a dataset that a third party edits continuously and we do not control.

**That is a correctness problem, not a throughput one.** A gate that answers differently on identical input cannot distinguish *"this commit is unsafe"* from *"you ran it at the wrong minute"*.

**Kam ruled the reshape on 2026-09-09 (**`both`**): warn for a window, then hard-fail. The WINDOW LENGTH is explicitly reserved for him and is an open question at the foot of this ticket — it is not proposed here as a number.**

⚠ **And the design must be REACH- AND SEVERITY-AWARE, or it weakens the gate in the one case it exists for.** Detail in *The design constraint* below.

## The evidence — measured across three runs in about half an hour, 2026-09-09

```
run 1  ~21:4x   audit-locks  31 advisories match, 29 baselined   ->  2 missing
run 2  ~22:0x   audit-locks  32 advisories match, 31 baselined   ->  1 missing
run 3  ~22:15   audit-gate   37 reported,         34 baselined   ->  5 missing
```

**The arithmetic is closed, which is what makes this a measurement rather than an impression.** Between runs 1 and 2 exactly **two** baseline rows were added — 29 + 2 = 31, so the *baselined* count is fully explained. **The MATCH count still moved 31 → 32.** Nothing in the repo's dependencies changed: one JSON file was edited, touching zero `package.json` and zero lockfiles.

**Eight distinct advisories touched this repo in half an hour. Three were baselined. The gap widened while it was being closed.**

### 🔴 And one went the OTHER way — this is the part that makes it non-determinism

Between runs 2 and 3, `GHSA-2wm5-q62r-hmrv` (colord) **stopped being reported by the root gate entirely**. Its own output:

```
CLEANUP (advisory): 1 baseline entry is no longer reported — remove:
  - GHSA-2wm5-q62r-hmrv (colord, KS-1024)
```

**An advisory that blocked every push fifteen minutes earlier was no longer reported at all** — with no change on our side. **The dataset does not only grow. It churns.**

## Why the obvious fix is a trap

Baselining the current five turns the preflight green **now**. Run 3 proves that says nothing about run 4. **A green preflight after a triage round is evidence that the external set was quiet for one run, not that the tree is clean** — and the same three runs above show how long "quiet" lasts.

**Triage cannot outrun publication.** That is the loop this ticket exists to break.

## ⚠ The design constraint — a FLAT window would weaken the gate

Written flat, *"warn for a window, then hard-fail"* lets a **production-reaching** advisory sit unblocked for the whole window.

**That is not hypothetical, and the counter-example arrived the same morning the option was drafted:** `GHSA-8m3c-c648-2xjj` — nodemailer's `resolveContent()` bypassing `disableFileAccess`/`disableUrlAccess` on the legacy signature — is a **production dependency of** `services/auth` **and** `services/originate`, the two services that send mail. It survives `npm ci --omit=dev` and reaches a runtime image. **A flat window would have left that unblocked.**

**So the window must key on the same discriminator that has decided every one of these triages:**

| class | behaviour |
| -- | -- |
| measured NOT to reach a shipped tree, **and** moderate or below | **WARN** for the window, do not block |
| reaches a shipped tree | **HARD-FAIL immediately**, no window |
| **HIGH or CRITICAL**, wherever it lives | **HARD-FAIL immediately**, no window |

**This preserves the property Kam wants — nobody blocked for changing nothing — without buying it with the property the gate exists for.** It is deliberately the same test as the standing authority's own clauses: *what does this reach* is the only question that discriminated all morning.

**A necessary consequence, stated so it is designed rather than discovered:** the warn path needs the reach measurement to be **automatic**. Today it is done by hand, per advisory, by whoever is blocked. A gate that warns-or-fails on reach must derive reach itself, or the window just moves the manual step earlier.

## 🔴 OPEN QUESTION FOR KAM — the window length

**He ruled the shape, not the number, and it is not being chosen here.**

Recommendation offered as a recommendation only: long enough that a normal working day is not interrupted by a third party's publishing schedule, short enough that a warn cannot be ignored into permanence. **The data point this ticket can contribute is that eight advisories arrived in half an hour, so any window shorter than that is indistinguishable from no window at all.**

## What is NOT claimed

* **No root cause for the churn.** Whether the 31→32→37 movement is newly-published advisories, a registry re-index, or an `npm audit` dataset refresh is **NOT measured**. The *effect* is measured; the mechanism is not, and the reshape does not depend on which it is.
* **Whether we actually call the vulnerable nodemailer signature** — see the linked note; unmeasured at filing.
* **No claim that any current advisory is exploitable here.** Reachability has not been measured for any of them; that has been true of this baseline since KS-470.

## Provenance

Measured by s154, 2026-09-09, on `develop` `f9296f9e` while blocked from pushing KS-754 — the three runs are its own, and the arithmetic was closed before the conclusion was drawn. Ruled by Kam 2026-09-09 08:12 (`both`), confirmed *"Okay, go ahead with your recommendation."* The reach/severity split is Wednesday's design constraint. Related: KS-1024 (the triage that produced this), KS-470, KS-531.

title: Substrate: data_subject_requests is defined in THREE files that disagreed about processed_by's foreign key — and after KS-754 they agree for two different reasons
description:
## BLUF

**Three files define** `data_subject_requests`**, and before KS-754 they disagreed about whether** `processed_by` **carried a foreign key.** Two had `REFERENCES users(id)`; one never did.

**That disagreement is evidence a question was open, and it has NOT been reconciled.** Filed rather than fixed, deliberately.

🔴 **After KS-754 the three now AGREE — for two different reasons. That looks like convergence and it is not.** One file never had the constraint; the other two lost it because widening the column to `TEXT` forced the drop. **A future reader sees three files agreeing and stops asking.** This ticket is the record that they arrived there by different routes.

## The three definitions, as they stood

| file | before KS-754 |
| -- | -- |
| `Blockchain/Dev/migrations/001_initial-schema.sql:468` | `processed_by UUID REFERENCES users(id),` |
| `Blockchain/Dev/deployment/azure/migrate/init.sql:473` | `processed_by UUID REFERENCES users(id),` |
| `Blockchain/Dev/docker/init/01-schema.sql:495` | `processed_by UUID,` ← **no FK** |

## The real question, which is bigger than one column

**Why do three files define the same table at all, and which is authoritative?**

That is the substrate shape: a schema defined in more than one place drifts silently, and the drift is only ever noticed when someone changes one of them. **This one was noticed because a migration forced a read of all three.** Nothing else would have surfaced it.

**Not established, and this ticket does not guess:**

* **Which file is authoritative.** The migration chain is what an existing database actually ran, but both init files are used for provisioning paths of their own.
* **Whether the docker file's missing FK was deliberate or an omission.** No comment, ticket or commit message explains it. It could be either.
* **Whether other columns or tables disagree across the same three files.** **NOT SWEPT.** `processed_by` was read because a change forced it; nobody has compared the three definitions as wholes. **That sweep is the valuable part of this ticket and it is unstarted.**

## Recommendation

1. **Sweep the three files against each other** — the whole schema, not this column. That is the finding this ticket exists for.
2. **Then decide which is authoritative**, and make the others derive from it or be deleted.
3. **Do NOT close this by noting that the three now agree on** `processed_by`**.** They do, and it means nothing: see the BLUF.

## What KS-754 did and did not do

**Did:** dropped the FK on the two files that had it, because `users.id` is `uuid` and Postgres refuses a `TEXT` column under an FK to a uuid PK. Forced by the change, not a reconciliation.

**Did NOT:** add the FK to the docker file, align the files to each other, or touch `migrations/001` at all (it is applied history; the runner keys on filename with no checksum, so editing it would make a fresh replay differ from what every existing database ran).

## Provenance

Found by s154, 2026-09-09, during the KS-754 consumer enumeration on `develop` `f9296f9e` — the three definitions turned up in a frame-1 sweep for the column name. Wednesday ruled it a finding to file unreconciled. Related: KS-754, KS-949 (the multiple-SQL-source class).

title: CLASS: the id-format contract seam — 79 of 83 path params are untyped and ~15 siblings answer 404 for a malformed id; needs a structural guard, not per-route .uuid()
description:
## BLUF

**KS-1013 fixed one route. The seam it sat on is a class, and the class is a CONTRACT seam rather than a per-route omission.**

A read-only sweep of 17 sibling `GET` routes found **NO 500s** — so the 500 variant is not broadly exposed and **KS-1013 was genuinely narrow.** That is the good news and it is the reason this is not urgent.

**But ~15 siblings answer** `404` **for a malformed id** — which is the exact wrong answer KS-1013's own commit message argues against: telling a caller "not found" about an id that could never name anything in any tenant.

## The numbers

|  |  |
| -- | -- |
| path params named `id` in the published spec | **83** |
| carrying `format: uuid` at base | **3** |
| carrying it at head (after KS-1013) | **4** |
| sibling GETs swept | 17 |
| 500s found | **0** |
| answering 404 for a malformed id | **~15** |

**So "KS-1013 matches its three siblings" is literally true and is 4 of 83.** Worth stating plainly, because the PR body's phrasing invites a reader to think the spec is broadly typed. It is not.

## The fix shape — structural, NOT per-route

**Do not solve this by adding** `.uuid()` **to routes one at a time.** That is a convention nobody can enforce and the sweep above is the evidence: 79 of 83 params never got it.

**A structural guard at the router, keyed off the spec's declared format**, is the shape. The spec already knows which params are `format: uuid`; the runtime should refuse what the contract declares illegal, without a per-route edit.

## Folded in — two more findings on the same seam

**F-2 (MINOR, measured).** `format: uuid` and the enforced zod regex **describe different sets**: `urn:uuid:<uuid>` is spec-legal and gets **400**. 1 of 13 candidates tested; both controls behaved. So KS-1013's "runtime-is-truth" claim holds for 12 of 13 — true, and not universal. **A structural guard derived from the spec would close this by construction, which is why it belongs here rather than as its own ticket.**

**F-3 (MINOR, forward-looking, measured).** A zod **v3 → v4** bump silently NARROWS this guard on **5 of 10** candidates, while `format: uuid` keeps declaring them legal. The repo pins `^3.22.4`, so it needs a deliberate major bump to bite.

🔴 **F-3 is a landmine attached to a future upgrade, and that is why it is in this ticket rather than a separate one** — whoever does the zod major bump needs to meet it, and they will be reading the id-format ticket, not a MINOR filed six months earlier.

## Aggregation note

F-4, F-2 and F-3 are **one logical path** — the id-format contract seam — per Kam's aggregation rule. They are not three tickets that arrived together; they are three symptoms of the spec and the runtime disagreeing about what an id is.

## What is NOT established

* **The sweep was read-only and covered 17 GETs.** Not all 83 params, and no non-GET verbs. The `0 500s` result is bounded by that.
* **Whether a structural guard would break any existing caller** — unmeasured. Some of those 79 params may legitimately not be UUIDs.
* **The ~15 count is approximate**, as the gate reported it.

## Provenance

Found by the QA gate during the KS-1013 / PR #910 tier-1 pass, 2026-09-09, sweeping outward from the route under test. Relayed via Wednesday; all counts are the gate's measurements. Related: KS-1013 (the instance), KS-663 (contract drift).

One more instance for this class, measured at runtime by the tier-2 gate on PR #962 (KS-1029), 2026-09-13: **`rejectControlBytes()` (`packages/shared/src/middleware/index.ts:591`) inspects `req.body` only**, so a control byte in a path parameter is never refused by the shared boundary. At base, `PATCH /api/gdpr/dsr/<uuid>%00` reached the `::uuid` cast with a NUL in the bound string and answered 500 (row E5 of the gate's shapes table); #962's `UUID_PATTERN` guard closes it on that one route. Every other path-param route keeps its own guard or its service's catch.

## Recommendation
No action on this ticket now. Recorded here because a structural path-param guard (this ticket's ask) is what closes the class; a per-route pattern closes one route at a time. KS-431 family. The guard-side tickets are KS-573 (mount assertion) and KS-800 (body-parser ordering) — neither covers params.

## Detail
- **Source:** `Testing Agent MAIN/projects/secuura/reports/2026-09-12-ks1029-962-ac6f4fa91-tier2-r1-relaunch-20260913b/report.md`, Observations O-1 and §2 (rows E5 and the encoded control-byte family: trailing `%0A`, `%0D%0A`, `%00`, `%20`, `%09`; all 500 at base, 404 at head, 0 DB calls at head).
