title: Eight dashboards show a slot picker that filters nothing — latent today, wrong the day /metrics lands
description:
## What

All 12 dashboards under `observability/grafana/dashboards/` carry a `slot` template variable, so every one presents a slot picker. Only **four** actually use `$slot` in a query.

Measured 2026-09-07 by counting panel targets containing `$slot`:

| Dashboard | Panels filtering by slot |
| -- | -- |
| `k6_engineering` | 32 |
| `k6_executive` | 12 |
| `test_quality_trends` | 8 |
| `platform_engineering` | 4 |
| `platform_auth` | **0** |
| `platform_cardano` | **0** |
| `platform_document_lifecycle` | **0** |
| `platform_queue` | **0** |
| `platform_slo` | **0** |
| `platform_traffic_services` | **0** |
| `security_posture` | **0** |
| `test_openapi_coverage` | **0** |

On those eight, moving the picker changes nothing.

## Why it is not urgent, and why it is not nothing

It is **not currently misleading**, because those eight query application `/metrics` endpoints that no service implements ([KS-984](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-984/no-service-exposes-metrics-the-secuura-services-scrape-job-has-never)) — the panels are empty whatever the picker says. Nothing wrong is being displayed.

It becomes wrong the moment [KS-984](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-984/no-service-exposes-metrics-the-secuura-services-scrape-job-has-never) lands. Those panels will then merge all four slots into one number, with a picker sitting above them implying they are scoped. That is precisely the defect [KS-971](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-971/k6-performance-harness-slot-isolation-a-slot-1-memory-verdict-can-be) existed to remove — a plausible-looking dashboard that quietly answers about the wrong system — reintroduced through the panels nobody had to touch.

## Evidence that the other four are correct

Same sweep, evaluating every slot-aware panel for `slot1` vs `slot2` against live Prometheus during a four-slot run: **56 slot-aware panels, zero returned identical data**. Where the filter exists it discriminates properly. This ticket is only about the panels where it is absent.

## Scope

Add the `slot` filter to those panels' PromQL when their metrics start existing, or drop the picker from dashboards that will never be slot-scoped. Do it **with** [KS-984](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-984/no-service-exposes-metrics-the-secuura-services-scrape-job-has-never), since the correct filter cannot be written or tested against metrics that do not yet exist.

A validator check in the shape of `observability/scripts/checks/container-join-slot.mjs` — fail the build when a dashboard declares a `slot` variable that no panel consumes — would stop it recurring, and would have caught this.

## Depends on

[KS-984](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-984/no-service-exposes-metrics-the-secuura-services-scrape-job-has-never) (no service exposes `/metrics`).

Found while verifying [KS-971](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-971/k6-performance-harness-slot-isolation-a-slot-1-memory-verdict-can-be) on a live four-slot stack.

title: No service exposes /metrics — the secuura-services scrape job has never collected a single series on any slot
description:
## What

`observability/prometheus/prometheus.yml` defines a `secuura-services` scrape job over seven service targets. Every one of them is **down with HTTP 404**, and has been since the job was written — the endpoints do not exist.

Measured 2026-09-07 on a freshly rebuilt four-slot stack:

* `secuura-services` targets: **7 down, 404 Not Found** (every other job is `up`, except `kafka`, which is phase2-only and correct).
* `prom-client` is a dependency of **no** service.
* No `/metrics` route is registered anywhere under `services/*/src`, using `/health` as a positive control.

## Why it matters

This is not an observability-stack defect — the stack is healthy and correctly configured. It is that the thing it is pointed at does not exist. The consequence is that **every application-level panel across eight dashboards renders empty**:

`platform_auth`, `platform_cardano`, `platform_document_lifecycle`, `platform_queue`, `platform_slo`, `platform_traffic_services`, `security_posture`, `test_openapi_coverage`.

So the platform currently has **no application telemetry at all** — no request rates, error rates, latency, queue depth or SLO burn from the services themselves. What Grafana does show comes from cAdvisor, the DB/Redis/nginx exporters, and the test harnesses pushing their own results.

## Not to be confused with

[KS-971](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-971/k6-performance-harness-slot-isolation-a-slot-1-memory-verdict-can-be) corrected this job's **target ports** (they were 3000-3006 against services that listen on the 4000-range and 8080) and added `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/__tests__/prometheus_targets.test.sh` to stop them drifting again. That work made the job name the right addresses. It did not, and could not, make the endpoints exist.

## Scope

Instrumenting the services. Roughly: add `prom-client` to the service template, register a `/metrics` route alongside the existing `/health`, and export the handful of series the existing dashboards already query.

## Blocks

* Per-slot application metrics. The scrape job uses static container names, so only slot 1 is discovered. Making slots 2-4 discoverable needs either a Docker socket mounted into Prometheus (root-equivalent) or a generated targets file plus a per-slot `docker network connect` — not worth its cost while the job collects nothing on any slot. Revisit **after** this, not before.
* The slot picker on those eight dashboards, which currently filters nothing because their panels have no slot-aware data to filter.

Found while verifying [KS-971](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-971/k6-performance-harness-slot-isolation-a-slot-1-memory-verdict-can-be) on a live four-slot stack.

title: KS-969 round-1 gate residue: the pre-suite step and its own test suite — six items on one path
description:
## BLUF

Six findings from the **#892 / KS-969 item 1 round-1 tier-2 gate**, left open after round 2 closed
F1 (BLOCKER), F2 and F3. **One ticket, six items** (Kam's 2026-09-07 13:23 rule). **No round 3 —**
**Wednesday spent the cap deliberately**, so these are scheduled work, not a gate on #892.

Two of them (**items 3, 4, 5**) are defects in **the suite I wrote**, not in the product. Recorded
as plainly as the rest.

## SEARCHED BEFORE FILING

SYMBOL `runPreSuiteStep`, `provisionActors`, `writeRejectedManifest`, `ALLOW_REMOTE_PROVISION`,
`_run_pre_suite` · PATH `pre-suite`, `pre_suite.test.sh`, `actor_manifest` · STRING "pre-suite",
"PROVISIONED", "unredacted", "seeded actors". Only **KS-969** (parent) and **KS-966** match.

---

## ITEM 1 (MAJOR, was F4) — akto's provisioning creates actors akto cannot read

`playwright/config/actorManifest.ts`, `performance/runner/actor_manifest.ts` and
`schemathesis/tests/actor_manifest.py` all exist and are imported by live code. **akto has no**
**manifest consumer at all** — no `actorManifest`, no `generated/actors`. Its Secuura credentials come
from `config/secrets.yml` (`.env.example:40`).

So every akto run performs a real **account-creating** provisioning pass whose output akto never
reads, then prints `PROVISIONED — 5 generated actor(s)`. Under this PR's own vocabulary
(`pre-suite.ts:17`, *"the manifest is written; suites read generated actors"*) **that banner is false**
**for akto** — on the suite whose whole job is BOLA/BFLA role enforcement, a reader is told the wrong
identity was under test.

May be deliberate staging for KS-969 item 4. **Decide: either give akto a manifest consumer, or do**
**not hook it and say why.** A green banner asserting something untrue today is the worse of the two.

## ITEM 2 (MAJOR, was F5) — the schemathesis DEGRADED banner never reaches the run record

`_run_pre_suite` uses `subprocess.run` with inherited fds while `Logger` writes the archived log
itself. Measured with `--enable-logger-file`: **pre-suite lines in the archived log = 0.**
On the fatal path the log at least records `Pre-suite provisioning step failed`; on the **DEGRADED**
path `pre_rc == 0`, so nothing is logged and **the archived artefact contains no record that the scan**
**ran on seeded accounts** — the entire point of the banner. The silent fallback, relocated into the
artefact layer.
**Fix-shape:** capture the child's output and re-emit through `Logger`, or log the outcome
unconditionally rather than only on non-zero.

## ITEM 3 (MINOR, was F6) — `pre_suite.test.sh` mutates a shared stack and clobbers the real manifest

Run against any stack answering on `localhost:6882`, the suite **creates five real accounts** with
`FIXTURE_SEED="presuite-test-$$"` — **a fresh seed every run**, so they accumulate and are never
cleaned up — and **overwrites** `systemTest/fixtures/generated/actors.json`, leaving every consumer
pointed at throwaway identities until someone re-provisions.
**This is confirmed by consequence:** the author exhausted the local register limiter (100/hour)
during development, which is exactly this defect compounding. Round 2 partly mitigates it (a role
collapse no longer publishes the manifest), **but the account creation is unchanged.**
**Fix-shape:** a stable seed, and gate the live arm behind an explicit opt-in rather than "a stack
answered".

## ITEM 4 (MINOR, was F7) — the `ALLOW_REMOTE_PROVISION` control is inert and its comment is wrong

`pre_suite.test.sh` comments a cell *"the SAME remote target with the documented override must NOT*
*refuse"* — but it targets `http://127.0.0.1:1`, a **local** host, so it passes through the
`LOCAL_HOSTS` branch and the override is never exercised. Proved by tamper: making the override
branch permanently unreachable still left the suite fully green. **The documented escape hatch is**
**untested in both directions.** The cell still does the job of proving the step does not refuse
everything — so this is a weakened control plus a misleading comment, not an absent one.

## ITEM 5 (MINOR, was F8) — the DEGRADED stream routing is documented and pinned by nothing

`pre-suite.ts` routes DEGRADED to stderr with a comment explaining why. Collapsing both branches to
`console.log` left the suite green, because the harness merges the streams with `2>&1`. **A**
**documented invariant with no test is a comment.**

## ITEM 6 (MINOR, was F9) — unredacted server-error passthrough, PREMISE UNVERIFIED

`provision.ts:282` interpolates the server's `error.message` verbatim into the Error, and
`pre-suite.ts` interpolates that into the DEGRADED banner. Against a stub that echoes the request
body, **the generated password appeared in the banner in cleartext.**
**The gate proved the pipe is unredacted; it did NOT prove the real endpoint echoes payloads** — it
never reached a real stack. **Recorded with the premise unverified rather than smoothed over.** Value
at risk is low (generated `.invalid` local accounts); fix-shape is trivial — redact `password` keys
before interpolation.

## PROVENANCE

QA tier-2 gate on **#892 @** `f54b2dce1`, reported 2026-09-07. F1/F2/F3 closed in round 2 at
`42e778203`. Wednesday ruled **no round 3**, so these ship as their own work.

nodes.body:

Round 2 follows that precedent: both files restored from M38's blobs (`b95f4ee39` / `01024fadd`), the three hunks re-applied by hand in the files' own 4-space / single-quote style — the `redactSecrets` docblock + function; the four-line item-6 comment + the one redacted interpolation site; the four-line residue-(e) comment above `invokedDirectly` — as ONE new commit `e62fd23cd` on top of `9d0e2016a` (never a rewrite), after `develop` `311988614` was merged in `--no-ff`. New fixture blobs `cff58deaa` / `c3846e272`; the three cell files byte-unchanged (`1e384fb1d` / `2de77e9db` / `2cc4be3d6`). True numstat against develop: `4 0` · `30 1` · `106 0` · `154 0` · `203 0` (+497 −1), plain and `-w` identical.

Tamper T2 (the interpolation site put back to raw) → exactly 2 red in `provisionRedaction.test.ts`, restored by content (`hash-object` = `cff58deaa`), 5 / 5 again. Push fast-forward, push-protocol PROTOCOL-CLEAN; the hook ran the systemTest format gate (OK) and no 15-leg preflight for this `systemTest/`-only range.

**Not run:** live provisioning (a stack is on hold — item 6's premise, a real endpoint echoing payloads, is still unverified by design); the four platform suites; items 3/4 (#927's file); items 1/2; the gate's eight tampers beyond the one re-run here.

**Two records from the gate, carried here as facts (Wednesday's routing: this ticket, the PR's own; a board search for `buildPassword` returned 0 issues and `redactSecrets` only the Playwright-coverage ticket — no prior record):**
- **R-1 (the gate's G7):** for the five deterministic actors (owner, issuer, approver, verifier, orgAdmin) the DEGRADED banner still carries `spec.key` and `spec.email`, which are the two inputs of `buildPassword(key, seed)` (`systemTest/fixtures/actors.ts:91-97`: `Ks256-${key}-${seed}-Pw!`; the seed is parseable from the `ks256-<key>-<seed>` local part of the `.invalid` address) — so the redacted password of a `.invalid` test account on a local stack is reconstructible from the thrown message. A property of KS-256's deterministic actors, recorded here; not a defect of this PR, whose item-6 fix-shape (redact the password before interpolation) is delivered exactly.
- **R-2:** `redactSecrets` boundaries measured by the gate: order-dependent with overlapping secrets (unreachable — one secret per call); exact-substring only — a JSON-escaped or case-changed echo is not redacted (unreachable for the generated alphabet; reachable only for a hand-typed `BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_PASSWORD`, which is never interpolated).

**For the merge seat:** the delta for the gate is `git diff -w 0e78c7270 <head> -- systemTest/fixtures/` = the three hunks (plain = `-w`); equality targets are the two new fixture blobs `cff58deaa` / `c3846e272` + the three unchanged cells. The branch key `ks-973` will make the integration try to move this ticket at the squash — it must be restored to In Progress: items 3/4 are not started and wait on #927.

## PR #989 — READY FOR QA (tier 1, round 1) — items 5, 6 + the two round-5 residues built; items 3/4 wait for #927; items 1/2 recorded (s227, 2026-09-14). THE TICKET STAYS OPEN.

**BLUF.** https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/989 at **`9d0e2016ae60658ec908ee5e500583fd3a318c8a`** (`git ls-remote` 07:21:54Z; first push, push-protocol CLEAN), on develop M38 `0e78c7270`; 5 files, +332 −1, two commits. Tier 1 as ruled by Wednesday: the redaction reaches every suite's pre-suite error path — a secret-handling surface.

**Built here:** item 6 — `redactSecrets(text, secrets)` in `provision.ts`, applied at the ONE site that interpolates a server message (the throw at the end of `provisionActor`, with the actor's password; `login`/`createAsAdmin`/`bootstrapToken` return null and interpolate nothing). **The premise that a real endpoint echoes payloads stays UNVERIFIED** — no stack was reached; the pipe is redacted regardless. Item 5 — the DEGRADED-to-stderr routing pinned by a cell that spawns the real `pre-suite.ts` against `127.0.0.1:1` and reads the streams apart. Residue (comment `a55ab963` §1) — `provision-actors.ts`' drift-arm `quarantineManifest` call is driven end-to-end with a stubbed `fetch` and the REAL rename aimed at a temp target: a pre-created manifest is superseded, nothing published; the F1-spec negative control holds. Residue (§2) — the symlink shape of `invokedDirectly` pinned as KNOWN (exit 0, empty output) + a comment at the site; not fixed.

**Evidence:** red-first on develop's `provision.ts` 4 failed / 5 passed — two assertion reds show the generated password in the thrown message AND in the DEGRADED banner (the gate's measured shape); 9/9 after. Tampers: the CLI tail collapsed to `console.log` reds exactly the streams cell; the redaction call reverted reds exactly the two password cells. Whole `performance` unit suite **59 files / 1051 tests** (baseline 56 / 1042); lint 0/0, knip 0, `format:check` rc 0, KS-989 gate OK. `fixtures/generated/` absent before and after in the worktree — every cell uses its own temp dir.

**Not built, by partition:** item 1 lives in `systemTest/akto/tests/preSuiteSetup.ts` / `akto/src/**` (L12); item 2 in `systemTest/schemathesis/scripts/run.py:353-391` (L11). **Not started:** items 3/4 edit `systemTest/__tests__/pre_suite.test.sh`, which PR #927 (`1041d2d32`, open, unmerged at 07:21:40Z) holds — they begin only on a develop that contains #927's merge. **This ticket does not close on #989.**

## Two items from the #892 round-5 gate that belong here, NOT in round 5

Round 5 was bounded to F-1 and F-2 by Kam's word ("F-1 and F-2 only, F-2 first"), so neither of these was touched. Recording them so they are not mistaken for tested.

### 1. A SECOND unguarded `quarantineManifest` call — `provision-actors.ts:178`

Round 5's F-1 fix wrapped the call at `pre-suite.ts:157`. **There is another one at `provision-actors.ts:178`, and it was NOT driven by any cell.**

**It cannot break the same contract** — it sits inside `runPreSuite`'s own `try`, so a throw there is caught and classified. **But it is untested**, and "covered by an outer try" is a structural argument, not a measurement. If the F-3 work touches this path, drive it.

### 2. `invokedDirectly` can silently exit 0 through a symlinked path (F5-3, curio)

`pre-suite.ts` decides whether it was run directly by comparing a **realpath'd** `import.meta.url` against an **unresolved** `pathToFileURL(process.argv[1])`. Invoked through a symlink the two differ, `invokedDirectly` is false, the CLI body never runs — and the process **exits 0 having done nothing**.

**Correctly bounded and NOT a live defect:** all four production hooks resolve real paths before invoking it, so this is reachable only by manual invocation through a symlink. Recorded because a silent exit 0 is the shape that gets mistaken for success.

Both from the tier-2 gate on #892 round 5 (GO with findings; neither is gating). #892 is merged — `develop` `512480ef1`.

**UPDATE to item 3 — its severity note is now out of date, and in the direction that understates it.**

Item 3 currently credits a round-2 mitigation:

> *"Round 2 partly mitigates it (a role collapse no longer publishes the manifest), **but the account creation is unchanged**."*

**Round 3 and round 4 have replaced that mitigation with an ACTIVE MUTATION.** A role collapse no longer merely declines to publish — it now **moves an existing `generated/actors.json` aside** to `actors.superseded-<stamp>.json` (round 3), and as of round 4 a provisioning **throw** does the same from `runPreSuite`'s catch.

`pre_suite.test.sh` runs the real step against any stack answering on `:6882` with a fresh `presuite-test-$$` seed. So each run of that suite now:

1. creates five real accounts (unchanged — the original finding), **and**
2. **moves the real manifest aside**, leaving every consumer with no manifest until someone re-provisions.

**(2) is new.** The mitigation the severity note credits is gone, replaced by something with a larger footprint. That is not an argument against the quarantine — the quarantine is correct and was commissioned — it is an argument that **this item got more urgent, not less**, and the note should not be read as reassurance.

**Fix-shape is unchanged** (a stable seed, and gate the live arm behind an explicit opt-in rather than "a stack answered"), but the opt-in gate now matters for a second reason: an accidental run no longer just adds accounts, it also removes the manifest the other suites depend on.

**Not filed as a new ticket** — it is the same defect and the same fix, and this board's rule is one ticket per logical path with items inside.

*Source: #892 round-3 QA gate finding F1-C, 2026-09-07T10:49:17Z. Verified against `1e31c80b9`: the quarantine call is live in both `provision-actors.ts`' drift arm and `pre-suite.ts`' catch arm.*

# F1 fix-shape — specification, written while the ticket is HELD

**BLUF — the F1 fix must handle a manifest that ALREADY EXISTS on disk, not merely decline to write a new one. A live instance is present right now on `worktrees/seat-a`, and it is the exact shape the round-2 fix does not cover.**

No code and no branches were touched to write this: `#892` is carded to Kam for a possible narrow round 3, and KS-973's files are `#892`'s files. This is a specification so that round starts from a written defect rather than a memory.

## The claim in the code that is not true

`provision-actors.ts:154-156` states the mechanism in its own words:

> *"when we cannot keep the promise we do not make it: the manifest is NOT published, every consumer falls back to its seeded accounts **because the file simply is not there**, and the rejected copy goes to a sidecar for diagnosis."*

**"Because the file simply is not there" is an assumption about the filesystem, not a property the code establishes.** `writeRejectedManifest` writes `generated/actors.rejected.json`; nothing touches `generated/actors.json`. A **non-write is not a removal.** If a previous run already published a manifest, it survives the rejection and every consumer reads it — believing it current.

## The live instance, on `worktrees/seat-a` at `42e778203`

Metadata only; no credentials or actor bodies read out:

| file | seed | provisionedAt |
|---|---|---|
| `generated/actors.json` | `presuite-test-72460` | **2026-09-07T07:57:14Z** |
| `generated/actors.rejected.json` | `presuite-strict-47722` | **2026-09-07T08:50:37Z** |

The rejected run is **53 minutes newer** than the published manifest. So the most recent provisioning pass was refused, and the file the three consumers resolve is still the **07:57** one. The fallback the comment promises did not happen, because the file was there.

**`generated/` is gitignored** (`systemTest/fixtures/.gitignore:8`), which is why this persists silently across runs and never shows up in `git status`. A clean working tree is not evidence the manifest is clean.

## It compounds with item 3 of this ticket, and that is the worse half

The surviving manifest's seed is **`presuite-test-72460`** — the `presuite-test-$$` shape that **item 3** records `pre_suite.test.sh` writing into the real manifest path. So the two defects interlock:

1. **item 3** puts throwaway test identities into `generated/actors.json`;
2. **F1** then declines to overwrite it on a rejected run and leaves them standing.

The consumers on that worktree are currently pointed at accounts a test suite created for itself. Fixing either one alone leaves the pairing live.

## Fix-shape

**Quarantine the stale manifest on rejection — do not merely skip the write.** On the `drifted.length > 0` path, if `MANIFEST_PATH` exists, move it aside (e.g. `actors.superseded-<provisionedAt>.json`) *before* returning, then write the rejected sidecar as now. **Move, never delete** — the standing rule, and the superseded file is the diagnostic record of what the suites *would* have run on.

**Why quarantine rather than a reader-side freshness check.** `manifest.ts` argues that the guard living in the FILE rather than in a reader is load-bearing, because `schemathesis/tests/actor_manifest.py` parses the JSON directly and a TypeScript-side check would never cover it. That argument is correct and it applies here too: a `provisionedAt`/`seed`/`baseUrl` staleness check would have to be implemented in **both** languages across **three** consumers, and any consumer that forgot it would silently keep the old behaviour. Making the filesystem state true is one change in one place and cannot be forgotten by a consumer.

**The no-stale-manifest case must not change.** When no manifest exists, the current non-write is already correct, and the fix must not start creating or removing anything there.

## What a test must pin, and how it can fail

Two cells, and the second is the one that makes the first mean anything:

1. **Pre-create a manifest, then provision with a drifted role.** Assert `MANIFEST_PATH` no longer resolves to the pre-created content, and that a superseded copy exists. *Red-proof:* with only the round-2 fix in place this cell fails, because the stale file is still there and still readable.
2. **Negative / positive control — provision with NO pre-existing manifest and a drifted role.** Assert nothing is quarantined and no manifest is published. Without this, a fix that unconditionally deleted or wrote something would pass cell 1.

A cell asserting only *"`writeManifest` was not called"* is the check that cannot fail here — it is true today, on the very worktree that carries the live instance.

## Also correct the comment

`provision-actors.ts:154-156` must stop asserting *"the file simply is not there"* once the behaviour changes — and if round 3 is not authorised, it should stop asserting it anyway, because it is the load-bearing sentence a reader would rely on and it is false. Same class as the `documentRepo` comment corrected on KS-597 today: a comment that describes a property the code does not have.

title: start-secuura.sh banner prints admin@secuura.com / admin123, which has returned 401 since PR #888
description:
## BLUF

`Start_Up/start-secuura.sh` ends every successful start with a **Credentials** block that still prints `Admin: admin@secuura.com / admin123`. Since PR #888 ([KS-966](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-966/retire-the-published-system-admin-credential-kam-rotate-properly-a) items 1+2) retired the published SYSTEM_ADMIN default, that login **returns 401** — measured on a fresh slot-2 stack on 2026-09-07. The banner now hands every operator a credential that does not work, on the one screen they are guaranteed to read.

Found during the [KS-682](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-682/playwright-slot-isolation-port-the-proven-platform-s-mechanism-no-run) four-slot isolation sweep, not by reading the script.

## Measured

```
POST /api/auth/login  {"email":"admin@secuura.com","password":"admin123"}
  -> 401 {"code":"UNAUTHORIZED","message":"Invalid email or password"}
```

`demo@secuura.io / demo123` on the same banner line still authenticates (200), so the issuer half is correct and only the admin half is stale.

## Why it is its own ticket rather than a [KS-966](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-966/retire-the-published-system-admin-credential-kam-rotate-properly-a) sub-item

[KS-966](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-966/retire-the-published-system-admin-credential-kam-rotate-properly-a)'s ruled order item 3 — *"4 startup/scripts + 3 harnesses — env var, no fallback"* — covers scripts that **read** the fallback. This is the script **printing** it: a documentary line, not an executable read, so it is not caught by that sweep's definition of "site" and would survive item 3 landing. Related to [KS-966](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-966/retire-the-published-system-admin-credential-kam-rotate-properly-a) so it is sequenced beside it; raised separately so it is not lost inside a routing change.

## Suggested fix

Either drop the admin line from the banner, or print the mechanism instead of a value — e.g. *"Admin: provisioned per run, see* `systemTest/fixtures/provision-actors.ts`*"* — since [KS-966](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-966/retire-the-published-system-admin-credential-kam-rotate-properly-a)'s answer was that no shared admin credential should exist to print.

## Context

* The banner also prints `Project: <compose default>` for slot 1 while the container labels read the worktree-derived project name (`ks-682` in this sweep). Minor; noted while here, not the subject of this ticket.
* Raised from the [KS-682](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-682/playwright-slot-isolation-port-the-proven-platform-s-mechanism-no-run) sweep; platform-k base code, so filed to Kamil per the review-authority rule.

nodes.body: **BLUF:** Delivered: PR 1180 merged as 24895c50557f on develop (the start-secuura.sh banner no longer prints the retired admin default), in the tree deployed to kintsugi at b1fb543640e7 (carried deploy record of 2026-11-01, not re-measured today). Verified by code read, not observed live: `Start_Up/start-secuura.sh` has one `admin123` at b1fb543640e7, at `:614`, and no banner line prints the credential. Left open: `:614` is the script's own admin-login check, which still posts the retired admin@secuura.com / admin123 (this ticket records that default as returning 401), and the 2026-09-10 comment on this ticket records that ADMIN_USER_PASSWORD is never forwarded to the auth container, the cause behind the 401, which this PR does not touch.

## The cause behind the 401, measured on a fresh slot-1 stack (2026-09-10) — `ADMIN_USER_PASSWORD` is never forwarded to the auth container

Found while running the KS-682 Playwright suite on a freshly built slot 1 (`wt/ks-682` @ `07ddef716`, `./Start_Up/start-secuura.sh --rebuild`, `ENABLE_DEMO_SEED=true`, `ALLOW_DEFAULT_SEED_PASSWORDS=true`, `ADMIN_USER_PASSWORD` set in `Blockchain/Dev/.env`). Appending rather than opening a ticket: this is the mechanism behind what this ticket already reports.

**Observed, in order:**

1. `POST /api/auth/login` `admin@secuura.com` / the value from `.env` → **401** `Invalid email or password` — the symptom this ticket names.
2. `docker logs secuura-auth`: `Demo user seeding skipped — no password supplied, and no pre-existing row to remediate {"email":"admin@secuura.com","hint":"set ADMIN_USER_PASSWORD to seed this account instead"}` — while `issuer@`, `verifier@`, `holder@` and the demo tenants all logged **`Demo user seeded`**. So `admin@secuura.com` is **never seeded**, not seeded with a different password. That answers the "wrong password vs never seeded" question left open on KS-682 on 2026-09-08.
3. `docker exec secuura-auth env`: `ALLOW_DEFAULT_SEED_PASSWORDS` present, **`ADMIN_USER_PASSWORD` absent**.
4. `grep -rn ADMIN_USER_PASSWORD Blockchain/Dev/docker-compose*.yml docker-compose*.yml` → **0 hits**. `docker-compose.yml:761` forwards `ALLOW_DEFAULT_SEED_PASSWORDS` to `auth`; `:598` forwards `ENABLE_DEMO_SEED` to `originate`; nothing forwards `ADMIN_USER_PASSWORD` to anything. `auth`'s `env_file` (`:711`) is `.env.local`, which does not carry it either.

**So:** the variable is documented in `.env.example:133`, read by `services/auth/src/repositories/userRepo.ts` (its own log hint names it), and **not in the compose contract** — the value an operator sets is inert. The seeder then correctly skips the admin row, the banner prints a credential for an account that does not exist, and every consumer of `admin@secuura.com` on a fresh local stack gets 401. The same class as `LOCAL_LOGIN_LIMITER_DISABLED` going missing, in the other direction (template has it, compose does not).

**Consequence beyond the banner:** `fixtures/provision-actors.ts` bootstraps roles as `admin@secuura.com` (`BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_PASSWORD`), so on a fresh local stack provisioning **cannot** grant roles, every actor lands as `OWNER`, KS-969 round 2 refuses the manifest, and the Playwright suite's fallback (`getTestAdminEmail()` → `admin@secuura.com`) 401s too — the suite cannot authenticate at all from a clean build. That is the local-side half of KS-1076.

**Fix-shape, for whoever owns it (platform-k, so not mine):** forward `ADMIN_USER_PASSWORD=${ADMIN_USER_PASSWORD:-}` in the `auth` service block beside `:761`, and pin it with the same env-contract check the other seed flags have. Or, if the design is that the admin account is not seeded locally by intent, remove line 133 from `.env.example` and the hint from the seeder so nobody sets a value that does nothing.

Not changed on any branch. Worked around for the KS-682 slot runs by pointing the suite at `issuer@secuura.com`, which did seed.

title: systemTest actor/credential path: provisioning is never invoked, so the generated-actor path never resolves — and exactly one site (the SYSTEM_ADMIN persona) can never use it
description:
**KS-966 item 4 was stood down on measurement.** It was scoped as *"route the 12 systemTest sites through the existing generated-actor path"*. **That path never runs**, and for one site it could not work even if it did. This is the one logical path — the systemTest actor/credential story — with its items inside it, per Kam's 2026-09-07 13:23 rule.

## Searched before filing (958 issues, including archived)

| searched | hits |
| -- | -- |
| SYMBOL `getGeneratedActor` | KS-966 only (this ticket's parent) |
| SYMBOL `ADMIN_ACTOR_KEY` | KS-966 only |
| SYMBOL `provision-actors` | KS-966 only |
| PATH `systemTest/fixtures/generated` | **none** |
| SYMBOL `TEST_ADMIN_PASSWORD` | KS-967 only (as a guarded key name, different subject) |
| STRING `actor manifest` / `actors.json` | **none** |

**No existing ticket covers this.** Four sessions worked this repo today, so the check was worth making.

---

## ITEM 1 — Wire actor provisioning into a pre-suite step

`getGeneratedActor()` reads `systemTest/fixtures/generated/actors.json` (`playwright/config/actorManifest.ts:45`) and returns `undefined` when absent. Measured on `origin/develop`:

* **0** files tracked under `systemTest/fixtures/generated`; the manifest is **absent** on a fresh tree.
* Written **only** by `systemTest/fixtures/provision-actors.ts`.
* **Nothing automated invokes it**: no npm script · no `.github` workflow · no shell runner · **not** `playwright/global-setup.ts` (imports only `getApiBaseUrl`) · **not** `auth/auth.setup.ts` (imports `getTestAdminEmail`/`getTestAdminPassword` and logs in with them). Its only references are its own docstring showing manual invocation.
* **CONTROL:** the same `git grep` over the same paths finds `"test:unit"` in `playwright/package.json`. The instrument fires, so the zeros are real zeros.

**So the fallbacks are the live path, not redundancy.** This item is a pre-suite hook (a Playwright setup-project dependency, or the slot runner) **with its own test** — not a tail-end edit.

## ITEM 2 — The SYSTEM_ADMIN split. **M = 1**, and here it is

Of the 12 occurrences, **8 are documentary** (comments, docstrings, `@example` blocks) and belong to KS-965, not here. **Four are executable credential sources**, and three of them are satisfied by `orgAdmin`:

| site | drives | verdict |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `schemathesis/tests/conftest.py:83` | `resolve_credentials("orgAdmin", …)` | **already keyed to** `orgAdmin`, with env override + fallback |
| `schemathesis/scripts/setup_api_key.py:53` | `POST /api/admin/api-keys`, gated `requireRole('SYSTEM_ADMIN','ORG_ADMIN')` | **ORG_ADMIN is admitted** by the route |
| `schemathesis/tests/test_authentication.py:26` | `POST /auth/login` only (success / invalid / missing-field) | **login requires no role at all** |
| `schemathesis/config/fixtures.py:82` | `Persona(key="super_admin", role="SYSTEM_ADMIN", …)` — *"Cross-tenant reads via X-Tenant-Override"* | **🔴 genuinely requires SYSTEM_ADMIN** |

**So exactly ONE site cannot be served by the generated-actor path** — and it cannot be served by design, not by omission. The manifest module says so in its own words:

> *"*`orgAdmin` *stands in for* `admin`*: SYSTEM_ADMIN is deliberately not grantable through the API, so it can never be generated."*

**That single site is the whole decision.** Either its cross-tenant persona keeps a seeded SYSTEM_ADMIN credential supplied by environment, or the suite loses cross-tenant coverage. **Nothing else in the 12 needs a ruling.**

## ITEM 3 — `TEST_ADMIN_PASSWORD` is documented, but documented WRONG

The concern raised was that it might be undocumented. **It is named** — `playwright/README.md:27` and `:152`, `playwright/docs/setup_guide.md:89` and `:238`. **The defect is sharper than absence:**

* `playwright/.env.example:27` has it **commented out**, so `cp .env.example .env` supplies nothing.
* `playwright/docs/setup_guide.md:89` documents its **default as the retired literal** — a value that no longer works, because #888 removed the seeder's published default *and* the `getTestAdminPassword()` fallback.

**So a runner who follows the documentation sets a password that cannot authenticate**, and with GitHub Actions retired (20 of 20 runs `startup_failure`, measured 2026-09-07) nothing fails loudly to tell them. **This is an operational precondition #888 introduced without updating its documentation.** The security change was right; this is its unpaid half.

Both of those lines also carry the retired literal and are in KS-965's documentary census — **fix them here, since here is where their wrongness is load-bearing.**

## ITEM 4 — Only then, the 12 sites

Blocked on items 1–3. Doing it first inverts the F3 error corrected on KS-968 today: removing the harmless thing and leaving the one that detonates.

---

*Filed by s146 from the KS-966 item-4 measurement. Items 3 and 4 of KS-966 are closed by comment against this ticket. The 12/8/4/1 counts are mine and were re-derived after I found my first pass had omitted* `.py` *from its extension list — which had hidden six of the eight executable files.*

**Evidence added here, not a new ticket.** Wednesday commissioned a ticket for "the KS-969 / KS-966 composition seam". I searched the board before filing it, and **it is already recorded on this ticket** in comment `e1358ef7` (2026-09-08, *"The defect is step 5, and it is narrow"*). So this adds s171's CI measurement to it rather than opening a second ticket.

**Search, so the absence is checkable:**

## What CI adds to the 2026-09-08 local reading
From s171's review of the PR #896 run logs, 2026-09-10:
- The empty-password login inside `auth.setup` returns **HTTP 400, not 401**. Validation rejects it before authentication runs, so the error a reader sees is one step further from its cause than the 401 above.
- The Playwright step is red having run **0 of 11** tests: `1 failed / 11 did not run`.

## Where it sits on `develop` now (re-read at `2d864ae92`)
- `systemTest/fixtures/pre-suite.ts:114`: the DEGRADED banner still promises *"the suite keeps its correctly-roled SEEDED accounts"*.
- `systemTest/fixtures/pre-suite.ts:110`: `exitCode: required ? 1 : 0`. DEGRADED exits **0** unless `SYSTEMTEST_REQUIRE_PROVISIONED` is set, so the run carries on into the failure.
- `systemTest/fixtures/provision-actors.ts:110`: `password: process.env.BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_PASSWORD ?? ''`. On #896's head the same line is `:155`.

Setting a value to make the suite pass is still ruled out. This comment records evidence only and fixes nothing, because `systemTest/` is Peter's authority. The sibling finding, that the Playwright env guard in #896 cannot see this variable, is filed separately and linked here.

## Evidence for THIS ticket's open design question — from the KS-1013 gate (F-6)

The QA gate measured something on the local stack that bears directly on the `BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_PASSWORD` question this ticket holds:

**The local SYSTEM_ADMIN credential is a historical artefact, not a reproducible seed.**

* `ALLOW_DEFAULT_SEED_PASSWORDS` is **SET BUT EMPTY**
* `ADMIN_USER_PASSWORD` is **unset**
* so the seeder **short-circuits** — and **a COLD START would have no usable admin at all**

Login works today only because the row survives from an earlier run. **Nobody has provisioned that credential; it is left over.**

**Why it belongs here rather than as its own ticket:** this ticket's open question is *what SHOULD supply an admin credential in a local test stack now the published default is retired*. ⛔ It was ruled that the answer must be a DESIGN answer, not a value — setting `BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_PASSWORD` to unblock a suite is how a retired default comes back.

**F-6 is evidence that the question is not hypothetical.** The current answer is "an artefact of an earlier run", which survives exactly until someone runs a clean stack. Any future gate that depends on that persona is depending on a row nobody can recreate.

**Not established:** whether a cold start has actually been attempted — the gate inferred the short-circuit from the env vars and the seeder's code path, and did not restart anything.

*Measured by the QA gate during the KS-1013 / PR #910 tier-1 pass, 2026-09-09. Relayed via Wednesday; the env-var readings are the gate's.*

## ⚠ PREMISE CORRECTION — provisioning IS invoked; it runs and correctly REFUSES

**BLUF: the title is false as measured. `provisioning is never invoked` — it was invoked six times tonight, on the same stack, with the same result each time.** A reader who takes the title at face value will go looking for a provisioner that does not run and find one that does. **The failure is real and still reproduces; only the mechanism in the title is wrong.**

Measured s153, 2026-09-08, against images rebuilt at develop `5ffaaf396` — four schemathesis `pr` runs, one k6 smoke, one Playwright run. Six invocations, identical output.

## What actually happens — the suite prints its own diagnosis

    [provision-actors] seed "local" -> 5 actors against http://localhost:6882
    [provision-actors] 4 actor(s) hold a role other than the one requested
        (issuer, approver, verifier, orgAdmin). MANIFEST NOT PUBLISHED —
        suites keep their seeded accounts. Rejected copy: fixtures/generated/actors.rejected.json
    [pre-suite:playwright] DEGRADED — 4 actor(s) did not get the role they were provisioned for.
    [pre-suite:playwright] This is almost always BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_PASSWORD being unset:
        no self-service path can grant a role, so every actor lands as OWNER.

The chain, end to end:

1. **`BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_PASSWORD` is unset.** The KS-949 / KS-964 / KS-966 rotation retired the published SYSTEM_ADMIN default and nothing supplies a replacement in a local test stack.
2. No self-service path can grant a role, so **all five actors land as `OWNER`** (`via: existing`).
3. Four drift from the role requested, so the provisioner **refuses to publish**, writes `fixtures/generated/actors.rejected.json`, **and moves any previously published `actors.json` aside**.
4. Playwright reads `fixtures/generated/actors.json`. It is absent **by design**.
5. `getGeneratedActor(ADMIN_ACTOR_KEY)?.password ?? ''` → **empty string**.
6. `auth.setup` posts an empty password → 401 → the suite's dependency edge suppresses everything downstream.

## 🟢 Steps 1–3 are the guard WORKING — do not "fix" them

The refusal is correct, and the reason it lives in the filesystem rather than in a reader is written into its own comment: `schemathesis/tests/actor_manifest.py` parses the JSON directly, so a TypeScript-side staleness check would never have covered it, and any consumer that forgot one would silently keep the old behaviour. It also moves a superseded manifest aside rather than deleting it, because **a non-write is not a removal** — an earlier pass's `actors.json` would otherwise still be the file every consumer reads.

## The defect is step 5, and it is narrow

The refusal promises *"suites keep their correctly-roled SEEDED accounts"*. **Every other consumer honours that. Playwright's admin path does not** — it falls back to `''` rather than to a seeded account, so a **DEGRADED** run becomes a **FAILED** one.

⚠ **The `?? ''` is deliberate and its intent is right.** Its own comment names it *"KS-966 site 8"*: an empty string is substituted so that a run with no generated actor **fails as an empty credential rather than authenticating on a value published in this repository**. **The intent is correct; the consequence is that the one suite reading that path cannot fall back at all.** This should not read as anyone's mistake.

## The blast radius, in the order that does not mislead

> **Coverage 0 of 12 — of which 1 failed and 11 did not run.**

`auth-setup` is a dependency, so its failure suppresses the whole `api` project. **Reported as "1 failed" out of a twelve-test suite it reads as 92% green, and the true figure is nothing at all.** The count is 1; the coverage is zero. Worth stating in that order for any suite with a dependency edge.

## 🔴 OPEN QUESTION — and `BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_PASSWORD` must NOT just be set

The one-line unblock looks like supplying `BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_PASSWORD`. **It was deliberately not tried, and Wednesday has ruled explicitly that it must not be** (2026-09-08): setting a credential in order to make a suite pass is the anti-pattern, and this one sits on the very rotation surface whose purpose was retiring a published default. **A value that unblocks a test is exactly how a retired default comes back.**

> **The question this ticket needs answered: what is supposed to supply `BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_PASSWORD` in a local test stack now that the published default is retired?**

That is a design answer, not a value.

## Suggested retitle

*"systemTest actor provisioning is refused (all actors land as OWNER with BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_PASSWORD unset) — and Playwright's admin path falls back to an empty credential instead of a seeded account"*

## Also measured, unchanged from s152

`quality:static` **4 errors** (same file, same lines — 3 of 4 `--fix`-able) · `test:unit` **48/48** · `test:e2e` **1 failed / 11 did not run**. Byte-for-byte the same as the pre-rebuild run, so **this High has not quietly fixed itself.**

*No fix attempted. Nothing changed. Reported only.*

## LIVE REPRODUCTION — this ticket was filed from a static read; here it is executing

Ran the Playwright platform suite against a **fully-up local stack** (33/33 services, gateway healthy)
on 2026-09-08. **The defect this ticket describes is what breaks the suite.**

    test:e2e   →   1 FAILED, 11 DID NOT RUN
    auth-setup › authenticate once and persist session
    POST /api/auth/login  --data '{ "email": "admin@secuura.com", "password": "" }'

### The chain, traced end to end

1. `auth/auth.setup.ts:24` builds its payload from `getTestAdminEmail()` / `getTestAdminPassword()`.
2. `config/environment.ts:179` `getTestAdminPassword()` resolves **`TEST_ADMIN_PASSWORD`** first.
3. The suite's `.env` carries **six** keys and `TEST_ADMIN_PASSWORD` is **not one of them** — it has
   `TEST_USER_PASSWORD` (a different key). Measured by name and length only, never values:
   `API_TOKEN`, `TEST_USER_EMAIL`, `TEST_USER_PASSWORD`, `HEADLESS`, `TIMEOUT`, `SCREENSHOT_ON_FAILURE`.
4. So it falls through to the generated-actor path — **which this ticket establishes is never
   invoked** — and reaches the terminal fallback.
5. It returns **`''`**. The function's own docblock says so in terms:
   *`getTestAdminPassword(); // '' unless an actor was provisioned`*.
6. Login posts an empty password and fails.

### Why the blast radius is the part worth recording

**`1 failed / 11 did not run`.** The eleven are the `api` project, which declares `auth-setup` as a
dependency — so when setup fails, **none of them execute**. The suite's headline reads as one failure;
what actually happened is that **zero of twelve tests exercised the system**.

That matters beyond this ticket: the four platform suites are the merge gate, and this one can report
a single red while asserting nothing at all about the platform. It is the same shape as KS-1010 — a
suite going green (or nearly-green) by not running.

### Attribution

Not a platform defect: the stack was healthy, and preflight legs 3 and 4 passed **321/321** and
**341/341** probed against the same gateway in the same session. The failure is entirely the harness's
credential-resolution chain, which is this ticket.

*Added by s152 — reproduced, not inferred. Nothing changed; no `.env` was edited and no credential was
written.*

## #892 MERGED — round 5 closes it. `develop` `4f337be83` → **`512480ef107349a61b3da89eb3af4e8a31e65d84`**

Gate verdict: **GO with findings — no Blocker, no Major.** Both round-4 Majors closed and independently red-proofed by the gate.


Negative controls, all 0 in the predicted tree: #793's `audit-baseline.json`, #720's `BACKLOG.md`, #721's `CLAUDE.md`, **and any `Blockchain/Dev/` path**. 12 files changed, all under `systemTest/`.

### What round 5 closed

**F-2 — the suite quarantined the developer's live manifest.** Reproduced first: a sentinel `actors.json` was renamed away by a run reporting `29 passed, 0 failed`, rc 0. Fixed with the stash/restore + `trap … EXIT` from `quarantine_call_sites.test.sh`. **The gate's independent red-proof met the binding condition verbatim** — trap removed, manifest destroyed, trailer still `25 passed, 0 FAILED`. The suite's report is provably blind to it, which is why no added cell could have closed it.

**F-1 — `runPreSuite` could throw against its own `:90` docstring.** The in-catch `quarantineManifest()` call is wrapped, and the failure is **reported rather than swallowed** — swallowing is worse, because a surviving stale manifest outranks the seeded accounts in every consumer. **The gate went further than my red-proof:** it asserted the contract on the *function* rather than the CLI exit code — CONTRACT HELD at head, CONTRACT BROKEN at parent, same instrument. TOCTOU reproduced **11/12 at parent, 0/12 at head**, with all 24 processes accounted for and the race entered 10 times and handled 10 times — so the zero is not vacuous.

### The cell count: 29, 25 and 24 are all correct

The brief said 24, I measured **29**, the gate measured **25**. The gate explained the delta: it gates off the live PROVISIONED arm (4 cells) because that arm creates accounts on `:6882`. **25 + 4 = 29.** Only the configuration differs.

### State deliberately NOT changed

Wednesday reserved the `Tested Not Deployed` question for this work. **I have not moved this ticket** — the state choice *is* that question, and it is hers. Nothing has been deployed; the demo remains on `400517aaf` and this round does not change that.

- **KS-992** — both quarantine guards `rm -rf` a directory they may have failed to snapshot (class note, names both files, carries the gate's honest limit: mechanism proven, realistic trigger not).
- **KS-993** — nothing type-checks `systemTest/fixtures/`, so this round's own TypeScript was checked by no compiler.
- **[KS-973](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-973)** — a second unguarded `quarantineManifest` at `provision-actors.ts:178` (untested, though structurally safe), and the `invokedDirectly` symlink curio.
- **[KS-989](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-989)** — the gate's "THERE IS CI" finding, reconciled three ways after I re-derived it: configured **yes**, executing in Actions **no**, executing locally **no** (preflight leg 12 is `--check-unreached`, a reachability assertion, not an execution).

## ITEM 2 — partition RE-DERIVED at `develop` `6c60cc09b`. The ticket was right; a mail was wrong; and the real defect is that the PREDICATE was never written down.

## BLUF
**8 documentary · 4 executable · M = 1. This item's existing text is CORRECT and stands.** The
conflicting version — *"12 occurrences across 8 EXECUTABLE files"* — is **wrong**: it inverted the
label. It is 8 **documentary**, and they are occurrences, not files.
**But re-deriving it took four candidate predicates, because "the 12" was never anchored to one.**
That is the finding, and the predicate is now recorded below so nobody re-derives it again.

## THE PREDICATE — the thing that was missing
> Occurrences of the literal `admin123` in **`systemTest/schemathesis/`** plus
> **`systemTest/fixtures/actors.ts`** (the generator's own header, which names the schemathesis and
> playwright credentials).

`git grep -an "admin123" <sha> -- systemTest/schemathesis systemTest/fixtures/actors.ts` → **exactly 12**.

**Predicates that do NOT give 12**, recorded so the number is never re-fitted to a different scope:
`admin123` in all of `systemTest/` = **23** · `admin@secuura.com` in `systemTest/` = **41** ·
`SYSTEM_ADMIN` in `systemTest/` = **74** · `SYSTEM_ADMIN` in `systemTest/schemathesis/` = **34** ·
`admin123` in `systemTest/schemathesis/` alone = **10**.

## THE 12, CLASSIFIED BY READING EACH ONE
**EXECUTABLE — 4** (a live path reads the value):
`config/fixtures.py:82` `password="admin123"` · `scripts/setup_api_key.py:53`
`DEFAULT_ADMIN_PASSWORD = "admin123"` · `tests/conftest.py:83` (the `resolve_credentials` fallback) ·
`tests/test_authentication.py:26` `TEST_ADMIN_PASSWORD: str = "admin123"`.

**DOCUMENTARY — 8** (a human reads it): `fixtures/actors.ts:11` and `:12` (header comment) ·
`config/fixtures.py:11` (docstring table) · `docs/getting_started.md:130` (doc table) ·
`scripts/setup_api_key.py:106` (a `>>>` docstring example) · `tests/actor_manifest.py:76` (docstring) ·
`tests/test_seed_demo_gate.py:5` and `:38` (docstrings describing the **product's** demo-seed
behaviour — a different subject, and not a credential to rotate).

**Why this is a reproduction and not a fit:** the predicate was chosen by SCOPE (the schemathesis
credential surface plus the generator header), and the four executable sites then came out **exactly**
as this item already named them — a list written before the re-count. If the predicate had been wrong,
that list would not have matched.

## WHICH ARTEFACT WAS WRONG
- **This ticket (item 2): CORRECT** — no edit needed.
- **`HANDOVER-s146.md:51`: CORRECT** — *"8 documentary · 4 executable · 3 satisfied by `orgAdmin` ·
  M=1"*.
- **The 2026-09-07 06:43Z item-4 mail: WRONG** — *"12 occurrences across 8 EXECUTABLE files"*. It lives
  only in mail, which cannot be edited, so the correction is recorded here instead.

## ⚠ A NUMBER COLLISION ON THIS TICKET FAMILY, worth flagging
**KS-966's own measurement table uses "12" for something else entirely** — *"the executable 93 splits
again: 8 env-var-with-a-published-fallback, **12 comment lines inside executable files**, 73
hardcoded."* That is a **different 12** on the **parent ticket**, and it also sits beside an **8**.
Two unanchored numbers with the same values on the same ticket family is exactly how the wrong
partition got written in the first place. **Anyone quoting "the 12" or "the 8" on KS-966 or KS-969
should name the predicate with it.**

## ⚖️ RULING RECORDED — `schemathesis/config/fixtures.py:82` is PERMANENTLY OUT OF SCOPE
**The `super_admin` persona keeps a credential source outside the generated-actor path BY DESIGN, and
it must not be "cleaned up" by a later sweep.** It genuinely requires `SYSTEM_ADMIN` (cross-tenant
reads via `X-Tenant-Override`), and **SYSTEM_ADMIN is deliberately not grantable through the API** —
the manifest module says so in its own words:

> *"`orgAdmin` stands in for `admin`: SYSTEM_ADMIN is deliberately not grantable through the API, so it
> can never be generated."* — `performance/runner/actor_manifest.ts:116`, and the same sentence at
> `playwright/config/environment.ts:31` and `schemathesis/tests/conftest.py:78`.

**This is a design fact, not a preference.** Removing that fallback does not migrate the site — it
deletes the suite's cross-tenant coverage. The other three executable sites ARE satisfiable: `:53`'s
route admits `ORG_ADMIN` (`requireRole('SYSTEM_ADMIN','ORG_ADMIN')`, read not guessed), `:83` is
already keyed to `orgAdmin`, and `:26` only drives `POST /auth/login`, which requires no role at all.

**M = 1 confirmed.**

**On item 3.** ## BLUF — the cross-ticket split, stated so NEITHER ticket can close assuming the other did it
**KS-965 carries the two DOCUMENTARY sites. KS-969 item 3 carries FOUR EXECUTABLE ones that KS-965's
own scope excludes.** The handover framed this as two documentary sites going to KS-965. Re-measured
at `develop` `9e9a88709`, that is not the whole set — and the remainder is the half that actually
breaks a run.

## RECOMMENDATION
Fix the four executable sites under **KS-969 item 3** (they are code paths in the systemTest
credential story, which is this ticket's subject). Leave the two documentary ones to **KS-965**.
Neither ticket closes until both halves are named done.

## WHY THE SPLIT IS NOT WHERE IT LOOKED
**KS-965's own description scopes it deliberately:** *"87 documentary occurrences… wrong rather than
dangerous… Once the credential no longer works, a document naming it is misleading, not exploitable."*
That reasoning is right, and it is exactly why it **cannot** absorb an executable fallback: a code path
that resolves to the retired literal does not mislead a reader, it **fails a login at runtime**, far
from its cause, with no CI to say why.

## THE MEASUREMENT — every `admin123` site under `systemTest/`, classified by READING it
24 occurrences. Control: 100 more files outside `systemTest/`, so the path filter discriminates.

**EXECUTABLE — a live path that will actually attempt the retired credential (KS-969 item 3):**
| site | what it is |
| -- | -- |
| `schemathesis/scripts/setup_api_key.py:53` | `DEFAULT_ADMIN_PASSWORD = "admin123"` |
| `schemathesis/scripts/setup.py:139` | `os.getenv("TEST_ADMIN_PASSWORD", DEFAULT_ADMIN_PASSWORD)` — imported from the line above at `:73` |
| `schemathesis/tests/conftest.py:83` | `resolve_credentials("orgAdmin", "TEST_ADMIN_EMAIL", "TEST_ADMIN_PASSWORD", "admin@secuura.com", "admin123")` |
| `schemathesis/tests/test_authentication.py:26` | `TEST_ADMIN_PASSWORD: str = "admin123"` |

**DOCUMENTARY — KS-965:**
`playwright/docs/setup_guide.md:89` (publishes `admin123` as the **default**) and
`playwright/.env.example:27` (**commented out**, so already inert).

**NOT IN EITHER — flagged so a later sweep does not "tidy" them:**
`schemathesis/config/fixtures.py:82` is the `super_admin` persona and is **permanently out of scope**
for the generated-actor migration (KS-969 item 2 — SYSTEM_ADMIN is deliberately not grantable through
the API, so it must keep a credential source outside that path). `tests/test_seed_demo_gate.py:5,38`
mention `admin123` while describing the **product's** demo-seed behaviour — a different subject, not a
credential to rotate. `akto/config/secrets.example.yml:55,69` is an example file the documented setup
**copies** to `secrets.yml`, so it is arguably executable — I have left it with KS-965 but it is worth
a second opinion.

## WHY `admin123` NO LONGER WORKS, verified rather than assumed
KS-964/KS-949 made the seeder require `ADMIN_USER_PASSWORD` with **no published default** — the guard
cell `ks949-platform-admin-seed-identity.test.ts:478` lists `['ADMIN_USER_PASSWORD',
'TEST_ADMIN_PASSWORD']` as GUARDED and scans every `.env.example`. That guard is why
`playwright/.env.example:27` is commented out, and it is also why it **cannot** catch the four sites
above: they are `.py`, not `.env.example`.

**Consequence, which is the whole reason this item exists:** a runner following
`setup_guide.md:89` exactly sets `TEST_ADMIN_PASSWORD=admin123`, and one who sets nothing gets the
same value from `setup.py:139` — both fail authentication, and with GitHub Actions retired there is no
CI to say why.

title: MAJOR: when both platform-admin rows exist the id-row rewrite throws 23505, the seed loop swallows it, and the KS-966 F3 email arm never runs — with a green cell standing over the hole
description:
**MAJOR. When both rows exist, the platform-admin remediation throws 23505, the loop swallows it, and the email-keyed arm — the whole KS-966 F3 fix — NEVER RUNS. A green cell stands over the hole.**

**"Both rows present" is not an exotic state. It is the state Kam's own row is in**: `…0020` holding one address, and a distinct row holding `admin@secuura.com`.

Found by the #888 round-2 tier-1 gate. **Pre-existing — reproduced identically against round 1's** `userRepo.ts`**, so it is not introduced by round 2 and is equally open on** `develop` **today** (merged at `9e9a88709`).

### The mechanism — and my published one was WRONG

I argued in #888 and on KS-966 that the collision came from **rewriting the address onto the row found BY that address**. That is wrong, and it matters: **writing the same address back onto the row that already holds it cannot collide with itself.**

The collision is on the **other** side:

1. `if (byId)` (`userRepo.ts:1363`) rewrites the `…0020` row's `email_lookup_hash` to the hash of `admin@secuura.com`.
2. If a **distinct** row already holds that hash, that write violates `users_email_lookup_hash_uniq` → **23505**.
3. The seed loop's `catch` (`userRepo.ts:~1506`) turns it into `logger.error('Failed to seed demo user', …)` and `continue`s — **no rethrow**.
4. `if (emailRowIsDistinct)` sits at `:1388`, *after* the throwing statement. **It never executes.**

**So I located the hazard on the wrong row, then declined a rewrite that was harmless and left standing the rewrite that actually detonates.** The gate accepted my *conclusion* (the email row should get credential-neutralisation only) and rejected my *reasoning* — and the wrong reasoning is why the hole is still open.

**The arm itself is correct and merely unreachable:** the gate neutered only the id-row guard and the email arm fired perfectly — suspended, sentinel hash, verify FALSE.

**Verified independently on** `origin/develop` **before filing:** `byId` at `:1363` precedes `emailRowIsDistinct` at `:1388`; the id-row UPDATE writes `email_lookup_hash = $3`; the loop catch logs and continues without rethrowing. And `users_email_lookup_hash_uniq` **exists and is UNIQUE on the deployed demo database** (measured read-only 2026-09-07, with controls: `users` 33 columns, `uuid_generate_v4` present).

---

## ITEM 1 — the misleading green cell. Fix this first.

`services/auth/src/__tests__/ks952…`/`ks949-platform-admin-seed-identity.test.ts`:

```
it('remediates BOTH when both exist, and the id row still gets the full identity rewrite')
```

**It passes, and it is asserting that a live hole is closed, on a credential surface.** It passes because the vitest `db` double answers `{rows: []}` to every UPDATE and **cannot enforce a unique index** — so the 23505 never happens in the test and the swallow never happens either.

The tester's words: *"the one thing here I would fix before the deploy rather than after."* It could not go into #888 because what merges must be what was gated, so it is the first item here.

**A mocked** `query` **cannot express this defect at all.** The regression test must drive the same both-exist scenario against a **real Postgres carrying** `users_email_lookup_hash_uniq`. That is the important half of this ticket — more than the fix.

## ITEM 2 — the fix, three shapes offered by the gate

* **Order the two remediations email-row-first**, so the credential neutralisation lands before the statement that can throw; **or**
* make the id-row rewrite **conditional on** `!emailRowIsDistinct`; **or**
* **wrap both in one transaction**, so the credential neutralisation is not lost to the identity rewrite's failure.

Whichever is chosen, **the swallowing catch is part of the defect**: a remediation whose failure is indistinguishable from success at `logger.error` level is the same class as KS-962, where the seed failure logs at `debug` and is invisible.

## ITEM 3 — do NOT probe the demo

**Likelihood on the demo is UNKNOWN.** The gate had no authorisation to contact the box and did not. **That probe is Kam's to authorise and he has not.** Do not go and look.

---

**Related:** KS-966 (#888, where the F3 arm shipped — my incorrect mechanism is corrected in a comment there) · KS-949 (the identity half) · KS-962 (the sibling swallow, at `debug`) · KS-963 (the PII cutoff).

*Filed by s146 after the #888 merge, from the round-2 gate verdict. The mechanism above is the gate's; the develop-side verification and the deployed-index measurement are mine.*

nodes.body:
**BLUF:** The read-only state check of the users table is made on kintsugi and demo, as Wednesday approved (SQL sha256 `5826161acf89ecac22332aef2334d8cff7ee953ea62fc784a78a9c53f280541c`, run as the owner role `secuura`). On both boxes the seeded platform-admin id row `...0020` is present, `active`, role `system_admin`; **no row carries the neutralisation signature** (password hash `!disabled:no-seed-password-supplied`), so the KS-966/968 arms have suspended nothing; and no row lacks an email lookup hash. This is the state the first boot LEFT, not the pre-deploy state the 2026-10-12 deploy note wanted: PR 1485's squash `8f674b3c46e7` is already an ancestor of both boxes' REVISION heads. One probe, P1, is invalid (see below). This comment decides nothing and moves no state.

| probe | kintsugi | demo |
| -- | -- | -- |
| total rows in `users` | 25 | 34 |
| id row `...0020` present | 1 | 1 |
| id row by status/role | `active/system_admin` (1) | `active/system_admin` (1) |
| rows with the sentinel password hash | 0 | 0 |
| rows with no `email_lookup_hash` | 0 | 0 |
| unique index `users_email_lookup_hash_uniq` present | 1 | 1 |
| P1 `SYSTEM_ADMIN` rows | **invalid, not a measurement** | **invalid, not a measurement** |

**P1 is invalid.** It printed 0 on both boxes, but its filter was the upper-case `role = 'SYSTEM_ADMIN'` and the stored word is lower-case (P2 prints `system_admin`), so it counted nothing for a reason unrelated to the data. The SQL had no control on P1, which is how it passed unnoticed until the output was read. A corrected count (`lower(role) = 'system_admin'`) has not been run; it would need its own written OK. Nothing below depends on P1.

**Where and when:**
- kintsugi: `secuura02-kintsugi-vm`, REVISION head `5fc5569ed96ac61f64823cc9e1fa841899aa1f62`, read 2026-11-05 06:19:11Z.
- demo: `secuura02-demo-vm`, REVISION head `07a2d62be6a09c9cd504864d1cf1906543d55317`, read 06:19:14Z (reads only; the demo freeze is on redeploys).
- Database `secuura`, the only one of the two non-template databases with `public.users` on each box (`secuura_platform` has none, so `platform_admins` was not read).

**Instrument and controls:** `psql` through the `secuura-postgres` container as `secuura` (current_user `secuura`, rolsuper true, rolbypassrls true), inside one `BEGIN READ ONLY ... ROLLBACK`; `SHOW transaction_read_only` read `on`. The SQL's bytes were embedded in the tool and the sha256 was compared on each box before `psql` ran (EQUAL on both). It selects words and counts only: no email, hash, id, name or password is in the output. Controls that held: total rows above 0, the id row found, the index found. No control existed for P1.

**What this does and does not say about the both-rows state:**
- The row that holds the seeded admin address (user `admin`, domain `secuura.com`) is found by `email_lookup_hash`, an HMAC with a secret; it was not computed, so whether a distinct second row holds that address is **not established**.
- The deploy note's bad outcome, the account holding the address suspended, leaves the sentinel hash behind. It is absent on both boxes, and the id row is active.
- Why it is absent is **not measured**: no both-rows state ever existed, `ADMIN_USER_PASSWORD` was set (the note says that re-activates the email row as a system admin, which P1 would have shown), or the seeder did not run. The environment flags and the auth boot-log lines (`Demo user NOT seeded`, `remediation FAILED`) were not read.
- The per-environment first-boot outcome stays Kam's decision card; nothing here chooses it.

**Evidence:** `5_Project_History/2026-11-05_seatU-14th/evidence/ks968_kintsugi_raw.txt` and `ks968_demo_raw.txt`; the SQL is `drafts/ks968_state_read.sql`. Nothing was written on either box.

**BLUF:** Delivered: PRs 1485 and 905 merged as 8f674b3c46e7 and ede711ca9ad1 on develop, deployed to kintsugi at b1fb543640e7 (2026-11-01). Verified by code read, not observed live. Left open: two items are not recorded as done: the read-only check of which state each environment is in, which the 2026-10-12 deploy note requires, and the per-environment first-boot outcome without `ADMIN_USER_PASSWORD`, listed as a decision for Kam in the 2026-11-02 triage plan.

- **In the code at b1fb543640e7:** with both platform-admin rows present the email row is neutralised (`auth/src/repositories/userRepo.ts:1695`, `:1747`, `:1764`, KS-968); the regression test runs against a real Postgres (`auth/integration/ks968-platform-admin-seed-with-both-rows.integration.ts`). PR 905 warns at the column that comparing `users.email` to a literal is void.
- **Deploy note, from the 2026-10-12 09:17Z comment:** in the both-rows state without `ADMIN_USER_PASSWORD`, the first boot of this code suspends the account that holds `admin@secuura.com`, so the deploy seat checks read-only which state an environment is in before deploying.

## BLUF
**KS-968 is merged: #1485, squash `8f674b3c46e7`, on `develop`. The ticket stays open until auth is deployed with it, and the DEPLOY NOTE below must be read first.**

## Recommendation
Do not deploy this to an environment until the deploy seat has checked, read-only, which state it is in. In the both-rows state without `ADMIN_USER_PASSWORD`, the first boot of this code **suspends the account that holds `admin@secuura.com`**. **Do not answer that by setting `ADMIN_USER_PASSWORD` blindly**: the gate found that doing so RE-ACTIVATES the EMAIL row as `system_admin` (not the id row), even when that row was an `OWNER`. Which outcome each environment gets is Kam's choice.

## Detail
- **The defect, measured on a real Postgres:** with the id row and a distinct row holding the address both present and no seed password, the email row stays `['active', 'LIVE-B']` (the id-row rewrite threw 23505, the loop swallowed it, the email arm never ran). The new suite is 6/6 green on the fix and 2 of 6 red on develop's `userRepo.ts`.
- **Fix:** the id-row rewrite runs only when no distinct row holds the address; with both rows the id row is left alone and the email row is neutralised; a failed remediation logs a distinct error first. The misleading mocked cell is replaced.
- **Gate:** Opus, GO WITH NOTE at head `ebdb123d5963`, 0 Major; Wednesday's head-bound GO 2026-10-12T08:56:35Z. Gate: 9 of 11 mutants killed; 3 boots in a row and 2 concurrent boots stay correct; no state suspends the wrong row or locks out the operator's id row.
- **Not exactly "unchanged":** with a legacy plaintext email row (no lookup hash) develop suspended both rows; this leaves the id row ACTIVE.
- **Landed on a moved tip, so the strict set ran twice:** first on tree `88a9408dc01f`, then on the exact final tree `2c26402eb038` (develop moved 6 files, including a `scripts/` shell suite; none are this PR's files, overlap computed with a control): `services/auth` 90 files / 934 tests twice, tsc, `check:openapi`, `check:test-types`, the integration suite 6/6, `run-shell-suites` 82/82.
- **Verified at source:** one parent, tree equals the predicted tree, six files, each delta equal to the PR's own.
- **Carried to KS-1494:** the integration suite's loopback guard can be bypassed by `?host=`, the untested rethrow, two lookups outside the named try, the file's own tsc errors, a whitespace `ADMIN_USER_PASSWORD`.
- **Not run:** the four platform suites; any look at demo or kintsugi (this ticket forbids probing demo); the RLS-forced app role.

- Seat V 3rd (Sonnet 5.5), 2026-10-12. Evidence: `5_Project_History/2026-10-12_seatV-3rd/` (`merge_1485.log`, `full_auth_1485b_predicted.log`, `ks968_integration_on_base.log`).

## BLUF
**KS-968 is built and up as PR #1485 (head `ebdb123d5963`), waiting for an Opus gate. The regression test runs against a REAL Postgres, as this ticket asked.** With both the id row and a distinct row holding `admin@secuura.com` and no `ADMIN_USER_PASSWORD`, the remediation threw 23505, the loop swallowed it, and the email row stayed ACTIVE on its old credential. Reproduced on a real database: the email row stays `['active', 'LIVE-B']`. Fixed: the id-row rewrite runs only when no distinct row holds the address; with both rows present the id row is left alone and the email row is neutralised.

## Recommendation
Gate and merge #1485. **Before it deploys, decide the deploy order:** on any environment in the both-rows state with no `ADMIN_USER_PASSWORD`, the first boot of this code SUSPENDS the account that holds `admin@secuura.com`. That is KS-966 F3 finally working, but it locks out anyone logging in as that address. Likelihood on demo and kintsugi is unknown; this ticket forbids probing demo, and I did not look.

## Detail
- **Shape chosen:** the gate's second (conditional id-row rewrite). The first (email row first) still throws 23505 on the id-row write every boot; the third (one transaction) rolls the neutralisation back with the failed rewrite.
- **The swallowing catch:** a failed remediation now logs a distinct `Demo user remediation FAILED — the pre-existing row was NOT neutralised and its credential may still work` first; the loop still continues, so boot is unchanged.
- **Item 1, the misleading green cell:** replaced; its mocked db could not enforce the unique index, so it passed over the hole. The new suite is `services/auth/integration/ks968-...integration.ts` (6 cells: positive control that the index exists and a colliding write throws 23505; neither row; id only; email only; both rows; failure named), run by hand with `npm run test:auth-integration` against a throwaway database (49 of 49 migrations applied). **No gate runs it**; it is not part of `vitest run`, the preflight or CI.
- **Proof:** 6/6 green with the fix, twice. On develop's `userRepo.ts`, 2 of 6 are red (both-rows and failure-naming). Three mutants of the fix are each killed. Mocked `ks949` 31/31; `services/auth` 89 files / 927 tests, 0 failed, twice; tsc, `check:test-types` and eslint clean.
- **Not run:** any look at demo or kintsugi; the RLS-forced app role (the suite connects as its own cluster's superuser); the four platform suites.

- Seat V 3rd (Sonnet 5.5), 2026-10-12. PR: https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/1485

## BLUF
**The mechanism the ticket describes is still in the code on `develop` `a31b775`; leaves my lot.** #905 added the schema comment only ("this PR closes nothing on this ticket", its own words). In `repositories/userRepo.ts` the `if (byId)` rewrite (:1593) still precedes the email-row arm (`if (emailRowIsDistinct)`, :1618), and the per-account catch (:1737) still logs `Failed to seed demo user` and continues.

## Recommendation
This touches platform-admin seeding and KS-966's credential retirement, so it needs Wednesday's sequencing rather than a drive-by build. Shape from the ticket: run the email-keyed arm before the id-row rewrite, or make the rewrite tolerate the distinct-row case, with a cell that holds both rows and fails on the swallowed 23505.

## Detail
- Read at source only; not executed against a database, so the 23505 itself is the ticket's measurement, not mine.
- KS-1168 (filed from this ticket's comments) tracks the `ILIKE`-over-ciphertext sibling.
- Seat V 3rd (Sonnet 5.5), 2026-10-12 (lot L06). Evidence: `5_Project_History/2026-10-12_seatV-3rd/` (`planted_red_L06.log`, `kintsugi_probe_L06_2026-10-12.out`).

## PR #905 squash-merged onto develop as M50 `ede711ca9ad13a320a3f409efb459c61ac3998bd` (merge seat s228, 2026-09-14 11:06:09Z) — merged; this PR closes nothing on this ticket

**What landed:** the 16-line `--` comment block at `users.email` in `Blockchain/Dev/docker/init/01-schema.sql` (blob `403838f06`; 16 added, 0 removed, 0 DDL tokens in the delta — control 177 in the whole file). Verified: one parent == T `25b71f50b` (M49, Peter's #991 merge), tree == the prediction `e37b855b7`, the blob == the gated head's. Wednesday's through-code read is the delta leg (stated as hers); the merge seat re-read the delta and ran the repo-walking guards on the predicted tree (ks879 8/8).

**This ticket stays open** — the schema comment is one leg of the trap this ticket records; the 23505 rewrite and the rest of its residue are untouched by #905. The Linear integration walked it In Progress → In Review at the PUT (branch key `ks-968`); CAS-restored to In Progress (its pre-PUT state) within the minute.

**Filed from the measured-and-unfiled finding in comment `1079a310`: KS-1168** (Medium, related) — `userRepo.ts:1017` (`listUsersInner`) and `:1061` (`countUsersInner`) run `ILIKE` over `email` / `first_name` / `last_name` / `display_name`, four of the six columns written through `encryptPiiCol`, so the search can never match a ciphertext row — the runtime form of the trap the new comment warns about at the column. Board searched first: `ILIKE` and `userRepo.ts:1017` hit only this ticket's own comments; `userRepo.ts:1061` and `searchUsers` 0. Facts only; no state change by the merge seat beyond the restore.

**PR #905 (the `users.email` literal-comparison warning in `docker/init/01-schema.sql`) is READY FOR QA at `8d800be1915bfa87b5513c985d78be987ae07abc` (tier 2, round 2) — 2026-09-14, s232. This PR does NOT fix this ticket's MAJOR; the ticket stays open.**

**What round 2 did.** The 2026-09-08 review held approval on two lines inside the comment block: (1) `auth_find_user_by_email_hash` "doesn't exist"; (2) `mfa_secret` "is listed as encrypted, and isn't — swap for `phone_number`". The reply on the PR carries every line number.

**The head.** `develop` `b76e8e6e8` merged in `--no-ff` as `0a1e24bd6` (the one both-sides-changed file in today's bundle: develop's `processed_by TEXT` at `:495` and this block at `:19-32`, 460 lines apart — the merged file carries both), then one commit `8d800be19` with the two sentences. Comment lines only: every changed line begins with `--`; word-bounded DDL tokens in the changed lines 0. `git diff --numstat develop...HEAD` = `16 0`; blob `eca686d35` → `403838f06`.

**Measured:** the push's in-hook 15-leg preflight `PREFLIGHT INCOMPLETE — 12/15 legs ran, 3 SKIPPED. Nothing failed.` (legs 3/4/8 need a local stack; leg 14 shell suites 33/33; leg 15 all 21 tracked guards accounted for); the three greps with their controls. **Not run:** every suite (a `--` comment; no runtime surface — the review's own table agrees); no stack; no Postgres parse of the seed file.

## Review of PR #905 — holding off on approval for two lines, not for the idea

Posted in full on [PR #905](https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/905#issuecomment-5585902926); recorded here so it survives outside the PR.

Kam, the intent is good and I'd like to see it land. A `WHERE` clause that answers a different question and doesn't error is exactly the kind of thing that deserves a warning at the column, and putting it where someone writing the query actually looks is the right call. The core claim checks out cleanly against the code.

I'm not approving **yet**, and only because of two small factual slips *inside the warning itself*. Since the whole point of this comment is to stop people trusting statements that look like evidence, its own accuracy carries a slightly higher bar than a normal comment would. Both are one-line fixes and then it's a clean approve from me.

---

### What I verified, and how

Read-only inspection of the worktree at `claude/schema-sql-review-ks968-d5ea36` against `origin/kamilkreiser/ks-968-schema-trap-literal-comparison`. No stack started, no suite run — see the "why no suites" note below.

| Claim in the added comment | Checked against | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `users.email` is AES-GCM ciphertext | `encryptPiiCol(norm, 'email', id)`; `decryptEmail(row.email, row.id)` — `userRepo.ts:121` | ✅ correct |
| Lookups resolve via `email_lookup_hash` | `userRepo.ts:242-247` — `getUserByEmail` → `lookupHash(normalised)` → `SELECT * FROM users WHERE email_lookup_hash = $1 LIMIT 1` | ✅ correct |
| Path is `userRepo.ts -> lookupHash -> auth_find_user_by_email_hash` | repo-wide grep for `auth_find_user_by_email_hash`, all file types, `node_modules` excluded | ❌ **zero hits** |
