title: The default-password CI gate catches one shape and calls it clean — 16 published passwords are exempt by design, and 4 of 5 canaries walk past it
description:
## The finding

`Blockchain/Dev/scripts/check-no-default-passwords.sh` is a **live CI gate** (`pr-security-gates.yml:63`, `security-scan.yml:422`). It is far blinder than its name suggests, and the documented exemption is the *small* half.

## The exemption (known, by design)

Line 34 is `| grep -v 'seedPw(' \`. With **only that line deleted** (sha-asserted both ways and restored), the lint exits 1 with **16 flagged lines — sixteen other seeded accounts' published default passwords**, invisible to it by design.

## The blind spots (not by design)

Five canaries planted through the real script:

| plant | result |
| -- | -- |
| `services/`, `.ts`, ends `123` | **SEEN** — positive control, the instrument is live |
| `services/`, `.ts`, not ending `123` | MISSED — any other password shape |
| `frontend/`, `.ts`, ends `123` | MISSED — only `services/` and `packages/` are scanned |
| `services/`, `.sql`, ends `123` | MISSED — only `.ts/.tsx/.js`; **the seed SQL that** `fixtures.ts` **cites as source-of-truth is invisible** |
| `scripts/` subdir, `.ts`, ends `123` | MISSED — `--exclude-dir=scripts,tests,__tests__` |

So the gate catches exactly one shape — a `*123` literal, in a `.ts/.tsx/.js` file, under `services/` or `packages/`, not in an excluded directory, and not behind `seedPw(`.

## Why this is worth its own ticket

A guard with a documented exemption is a guard with a hole of a **known** size — and the hole never appears in the guard's own green result. This one passes today, passed before [KS-949](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-949), and would have passed with the real-person account and its published password still in place. It is a live gate that gives false assurance in CI.

- [ ] Widen the file-type and directory scope, or state the scope in the gate's own output so a green result says what it actually covered
- [ ] Decide whether the `seedPw(` exemption should survive at all now that one account (the platform admin) is held to a stricter rule than the lint enforces
- [ ] A password shape that is not `*123`

## Provenance

The exemption and the `docker-compose.yml:755` default were disclosed by the filer while doing KS-949 and **confirmed at source** by the tier-1 QA gate on PR #885 (2026-09-06T21:29:45Z); the 16-line count and the five canaries are the gate's measurement, not the filer's.

*Filed by s143 (seat A), 2026-09-07.*

title: A backtick in a shell-suite case name executes as a command and rewrote package.json mid-run — every cell still PASSED; 9 suites share the pattern
description:
## A backtick in a shell-suite case name is COMMAND SUBSTITUTION — it runs, and the pass/fail column says nothing

Found by walking into it on KS-945. **Nine tracked shell suites share the vulnerable call-site**
**pattern.** No suite carries a live instance right now, so this is a latent hazard, not an outage.

### What happened

Case names are passed as the first argument to a helper (`expect "name" <exit> '<body>' …`), so the
name sits in a **double-quoted shell word at the call site**. Seven KS-945 case names were written
with markdown-style backticks for readability:

```
expect "KS-945: `npm add` is an install" 1 '…'
expect "KS-945: `npm init <package-spec>` installs, unlike `npm init -y`" 1 '…'
```

The shell ran them. During a suite run this executed `npm add`, `npm it`, `pnpm add`, `yarn` and
`npm init` **for real, in the working tree**:

* `npm init` rewrote `Blockchain/Dev/package.json` — 14 insertions, 4 deletions, including rewriting
  the unicode escapes in two long `// overrides` comments and changing the `repository.url`.
* The package managers rewrote `Blockchain/Dev/package-lock.json` — 12 insertions, 31 deletions.

Both were restored from `HEAD` and verified byte-identical, `git status` clean on both paths. Nothing
was committed and nothing left the machine.

### Why it belongs to the KS-926 family

**It was invisible in the pass/fail column. Every affected cell still PASSED.** The suite reported
`50 passed, 0 failed` while rewriting two tracked files underneath itself.

It surfaced only because a *red-proof* run — a deliberate tamper, run for an unrelated reason —
printed package-manager output **inside its FAIL lines**:

```
FAIL: KS-945: bare yarn install v1.22.22
FAIL: KS-945: [ERR_PNPM_MISSING_PACKAGE_NAME] `pnpm add` requires the package name is an install
FAIL: KS-945:  installs, unlike Wrote to …/Blockchain/Dev/package.json:
```

A green run could not show it, because the substitution output was swallowed into a name that was
never printed on success. **The tamper is what made it visible** — which is the family's own thesis.

### Scope, with a control

* **0 of 14** tracked `*.test.sh` currently contain an unescaped backtick in a case name. **That zero**
  **discriminates:** the same query run against a deliberately bad file detects it (verified in the
  same batch), so it is a real zero and not a query that cannot match.
* **9 of 14** use the `expect()` helper and therefore share the call-site shape:
  `run_in_slot`, `slot_target`, `stop_secuura`, `stack_guard`, `check_shared_relink`,
  `check_container_isolation`, `preflight_deps`, `stack_env`, `check_script_portability`.

### Fix shape

`check_shared_relink.test.sh` now carries a per-suite check that refuses an unescaped backtick in any
case name (added in KS-945, red-proofed **without executing the tamper** — the check is a grep, so it
was run against a bad name directly). **That guard should move up into**
`run-shell-suites.sh` **so it covers all fourteen**, rather than being re-implemented per suite — which
is itself the KS-926 mechanism-1 shape: a check that exists in one place and is absent everywhere else.

Worth considering alongside: have the helper reject a name containing a backtick outright, so the
failure is a clear message rather than a silent execution.

### Provenance

* the executed commands and the two rewritten files | observed in a red-proof run of
  `check_shared_relink.test.sh`; `git diff --stat` on both paths before restore; restore verified with
  `git diff --quiet HEAD` | measured 2026-09-07
* 0 of 14 and 9 of 14, with the known-bad control | `git ls-files '*.test.sh'` piped through the same
  query, plus a purpose-built bad file that the query detects | measured 2026-09-07

nodes.body: **Record from the #879 review (2026-09-08, finding 3) — carried here, not fixed on #879.** The reviewer measured that the case-name backtick check in `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/__tests__/check_shared_relink.test.sh` (`grep -v` on an escaped backtick, the `unescaped=` line near the tally) filters the whole LINE, so a case name carrying BOTH an escaped and an unescaped backtick is dropped rather than caught — a fail-open shape on one input. Reproduced by him on a two-line fixture: `expect "KS-x: \`safe\` and `evil`" 1 'body'` NOT flagged; `expect "KS-y: `bare`" 1 'body'` flagged. Low likelihood; it carries into this ticket's re-home of the check into `run-shell-suites.sh`. Searched this ticket for `escaped and an unescaped` and `#879` before writing: 0 hits (s229, 2026-09-14).

**Board correction — this ticket was moved by MY commit, not by anyone deciding to work it.**

Linear's GitHub integration transitions any ticket whose id appears in a commit message or PR body. My commits carried `Refs …` trailers naming this ticket, so the automation moved it. The move is recorded against `(automation)` at the same timestamp as the PR attachment, which is how I found it.

Restoring the state a human set. Nothing about this ticket's substance changed, and no one was working it.

**The lesson, which is mine:** a `Refs` trailer is not a neutral citation — it is a state change on someone else's ticket. Cite by identifier in prose where the ticket should NOT move; use the trailer only where the transition is the intent.

## The damage was worse than filed: it also pruned the workspace install and broke the push gate

Adding this because the original description understated it, and the extra harm is the part that
argues for raising the priority.

Restoring `package.json` and `package-lock.json` from `HEAD` was **not sufficient**. The commands the
case names executed — `npm add`, `yarn`, `npm init`, `pnpm add` — also rewrote **`node_modules`**
against the mid-run lockfile state, and the restore did not put that back.

The first loud symptom came only at the next push, from preflight leg 1:

```
=== 1/13  OpenAPI spec drift (generated spec vs Zod source) ===
DEPS MISSING — this working tree's workspace install is absent or incomplete. This is NOT spec drift.
  - node_modules/.bin/tsx — the root install; runs scripts/generate-openapi.ts
```

`tsx` had been pruned out of the workspace. **The push was refused** (`GIT PUSH EXIT=1`, captured from
git rather than from a pipe). Fixed with `npm ci` as the gate itself instructs — not bypassed, no
`--no-verify` — and verified by re-checking the two paths leg 1 names.

### Why this matters for the ticket

The original description said the harm was two tracked files, restored and verified. **The real blast
radius of one backtick in a case name is: two tracked files rewritten, the workspace install pruned,
and the next push blocked** — from a suite run that reported `50 passed, 0 failed`.

It also means the damage is **not fully visible to `git status`**, which is how I first cleared it:
`node_modules` is gitignored, so the working tree read as clean while the install was broken. A
reviewer checking this class should not treat a clean `git status` as evidence that a suite run left
nothing behind.

That strengthens the fix shape already in the description — hoist the check into
`run-shell-suites.sh` so it covers all fourteen suites, and have the helper reject a backticked name
outright rather than executing it.

### Provenance
- the pruned install and the refused push | preflight leg 1 output in the push log, `GIT PUSH EXIT=1`
  captured from git; `[ -x node_modules/.bin/tsx ]` false before `npm ci`, true after | measured 2026-09-07
- that `git status` read clean throughout | `git status --porcelain` showing only the two intended
  source files while the install was broken | measured 2026-09-07

title: Launcher suite: four side-effect and guarded-surface gaps from the KS-911/912 gate (incl. a SILENT destructive path on settings.local.json)
description:
Four pre-existing launcher findings from the KS-911/KS-912 by-hash gate (`PASS WITH FINDINGS`, 2026-09-06T12:18:53Z). **None was introduced by KS-911/912** — the tester says so explicitly — and none blocked the relaunch. Grouped as one path: the suite's no-damage claim and its side-effect surface.

`L`-numbers are against the shipped launcher `sha256 932a2cc3aebe6cf838bf885ac92eec08e259f0572c0e08910088ac58e269f55c`.

- [ ] **F-2 (MINOR) — the guard fails OPEN for a live seat when suite eviction composes with the documented** `SECUURA_SEAT_SCAN=0` **escape hatch.** Measured with one live fixture seat throughout:

  ```
  boot, scan OFF, BEFORE the suite : count=1, says pull: NO
  run the suite                    : seat still ALIVE, entry EVICTED from the registry
  boot, scan OFF, AFTER the suite  : count=0, says pull: YES
  ```

  Needs both halves, so it is narrow — but the escape hatch exists for the day the scan over-matches, which is also a day someone may run the suite. **Fix:** back up and restore the real `SEAT_FILE` the way the suite already backs up the preflight log, or route every registry case through `LAUNCH_TMPDIR` so the suite never writes the real registry.
- [ ] **F-3 (MINOR) — the "must not damage the live project" claim guards 1 of the 2 repos the launcher writes.** The launcher writes `user.name`/`user.email` to `${PROJECT_DIR%/*}/Extranet` at `L202-208` (KS-148) exactly as it does to `2_Project_Files`, but only `2_Project_Files/.git/config` is hashed before and after. Evidence: with the sandbox Extranet's email set to `kamil.kreiser@datasec.com.au`, **one** suite execution rewrote it to `kamil.kreiser@secuura.ai` — md5 `61238ef0` -> `8a2f8bda`, **cells that noticed: 0**. The write is intended and idempotent in steady state, so this is a guarded-surface gap rather than a launcher defect — but it is the one place workspace hard rule #5 (never mix GitHub accounts) is enforced, so it belongs inside the assertion. **Fix:** hash the Extranet config alongside `REPO_CFG`, skipping cleanly when the clone is absent.
- [ ] **F-4 (MINOR) —** `.claude/settings.local.json` **is rewritten on every launcher run (8 per suite execution) and guarded by no cell, and its failure mode is silent destruction.** A hand-formatted one-line file was reformatted by a single dry run (md5 `01ab75cd` -> `561024c9`); unrelated keys survive. But the embedded python at `L221-242` does `except Exception: data = {}` — so an **unparseable** file is silently discarded. Measured: a file containing `not json at all` came back as a fresh two-key JSON document, prior content gone, **nothing on stdout or stderr**. Pre-existing, but it sits inside the suite's own no-damage claim and it is a silent destructive path.
- [ ] **F-5 (POLISH) — the fix quotes its own detector.** The KS-911 F1 comment at `L246-247` reproduces the removed sentinel verbatim, so `grep -rl 'do not edit the sentinels'` still lists `Launch_Claude.command` itself. Any future check written as "is the sentinel gone?" reads non-zero forever. **Fix:** describe the removed wording instead of reproducing it.

**Not a finding, recorded so the next person to touch the trap sees it:** the suite's EXIT trap kills its fixtures with job control live, so bash prints `Terminated: 15` to stderr *after* the totals. Cosmetic, predates this change, same family as the operator-pane noise F-2 of KS-911 removed.

⚠️ **Do not fix while two seats are live** — the launcher is live on disk under a by-hash gate. `.pre-` restore copies exist for both files.

Source: `[QA -> Wednesday] Secuura SEAT B KS-911 + KS-912 (launcher, by hash)` 2026-09-06T12:18:53Z, forwarded whole and read here. F-1 and the registry's `exec` premise are filed separately — different mechanism. Follows [[KS-911]] / [[KS-912]].

title: Launcher: the assembled boot prompt is asserted by no cell — KS-907's fix can vanish at 18/0, and the seat sentence misled a live seat tonight
description:
**Nothing asserts what the boot prompt actually SAYS.** The launcher computes `$GIT_SYNC_STEP`, the suite reads it from a standalone marker, and the prompt the session actually receives is checked by no cell. Two consumers have now been proven wrong through that gap in one night.

## Item 1 — `$GIT_SYNC_STEP` never reaches an assertion (QA FINDING 1, MAJOR)

The `DRY_RUN` markers at `L659` print the variable **directly**. The boot prompt consumes it **separately** at `L483`. Two independent consumers of one variable; the suite reads only the first.

QA evidence — a one-line tamper (`887c3c23`) replacing `${GIT_SYNC_STEP}` at `L483` with literal text, marker untouched:

```
suite result:  18 passed, 0 FAILED   — every cell green
boot prompt:   199 lines -> 191 lines, "pull latest on the current branch" GONE
```

Proven with an instrumented pair (shipped + tampered, each printing `$INITIAL_PROMPT` under dry-run): shipped YES, tampered NO.

**Impact:** a future edit near `L483` — a 200-line block that is edited often — silently reverts KS-907 while the guard stays 18/0. KS-907 exists because a second seat's boot fast-forwarded a live branch under the first seat, before that session had read the brief telling it it was a second seat.

## Item 2 — the seat sentence reads as an assignment, and it misled a live seat tonight

Seat A was told by its boot prompt that its working copy was `worktrees/seat-b` — **this seat's worktree.** Seat A measured the pane mapping, disbelieved the launcher, and proceeded correctly as seat A; nothing was written into the wrong tree. A seat that trusted the line would have written into another live session's worktree.

Seat A's measurement, verbatim:

> pane %130 -> pane_pid 1790 -> cockpit label "Secuura/Blockchain" (no -B) = SEAT A = me
> pane %129 -> pane_pid 89454 -> cockpit label "Secuura/Blockchain-B" = SEAT B = s140e,
>             live since 22:24:23, PID 89456, working in worktrees/seat-b

**⚠️ The mechanism is NOT what it was handed to me as, and the correction changes the fix.** It was relayed as "the seat registry decides which worktree a pane is told to use, and no cell asserts the assignment is right." Measured here: **there is no assignment mechanism at all, and the registry has nothing to do with it.**

```
L344-346:  SEAT_WORKTREES="$(ls -1 "$PROJECT_DIR/worktrees" | sed 's|^|worktrees/|' ...)"
L363:      Sync YOUR OWN working copy instead${SEAT_WORKTREES:+ (this project has: ${SEAT_WORKTREES})},
```

`SEAT_WORKTREES` is a plain directory listing, **byte-identical for every pane**. `grep -c SEAT_WORKTREES` = 3, all three above. The sentence states a true fact — but its subject is *"YOUR OWN working copy"*, so a one-entry list reads as an assignment. With exactly one worktree present, that misreading is at its maximum.

The launcher says so itself at `L261`: *"The cockpit passes NOTHING that distinguishes the seats — both panes invoke a byte-identical command line."*

So this is a **wording defect plus a missing capability**, not a wrong computed value — nothing computed the wrong seat. The existing mitigation is the very next clause (*"if you have not been told which one is yours, ask before writing anywhere"*), and it worked: this seat asked, seat A measured.

**Fix shape (two options, the first is trivially safe):**

1. Reword so the list cannot read as ownership — e.g. *"this project contains the following worktrees: …; if you have not been told which is yours, ask."*
2. Actually derive the pane's seat. The cockpit label **is** reachable — it is in the parent shell's command line, which is how both seats identified themselves tonight (`ps -o command` on the launcher's own parent shows `[cockpit] Secuura/Blockchain-B exited`). That is a feature, not a guard, and it should not be attempted while two seats are live.

## Item 3 — the premise the whole registry rests on is asserted by no cell (QA NOT-TESTED 2)

The QA agent rated this **above FINDING 1**. The launcher registers `$$` and its `lstart` believing `exec` **replaces** the process, keeping pid and start time. The dry run `exit 0`s instead of exec'ing, so the entry it writes is stale the instant it is written. `exec claude … "$INITIAL_PROMPT"` (`L663`) is the only line below the dry-run exit and **is exercised by nothing** — not the suite, not the QA pass.

If that line were ever changed to anything that forks (a wrapper, `claude &`, `bash -c`), every registry entry would be invalid on arrival, the guard would silently stop working, and all 18 cells would stay green.

## Why these are one ticket

All three are the same mechanism: **a value the launcher computes correctly, consumed somewhere no cell looks.** Items 1 and 2 are literally the same variable's journey into `$INITIAL_PROMPT`; item 3 is the assumption that the prompt is ever `exec`'d at all. One fix — emit the assembled prompt behind a `DRY_RUN_INITIAL_PROMPT` marker and assert its **text** — makes all three assertable.

## Regression tests

Two cells against the assembled prompt, not the marker: empty registry -> prompt contains PULLTEXT; one live seat -> contains ROTEXT and **not** PULLTEXT. Red-proof by deleting the `L483` interpolation and requiring exactly those cells to fail. Item 2 adds a third: the prompt's named-worktree text against the pane's own cockpit label.

⚠️ **Do not fix the launcher while two seats are live.** It is live on disk under a by-hash gate; a relaunch is gated. `.pre-` restore copies exist for both files.

Sources: QA verdict `[QA -> Wednesday] Secuura SEAT B KS-911 + KS-912 (launcher, by hash)` 2026-09-06T12:18:53Z, read whole; item 2 from Wednesday's addendum quoting seat A, with the mechanism re-measured in this seat and corrected. Follows [[KS-911]] / [[KS-912]].

nodes.body:
**Provenance note, at Wednesday's request.**

The claim in this ticket that items 1 and 2 are *"literally the same variable's journey into `$INITIAL_PROMPT`"* is **this seat's measurement, not Wednesday's endorsement.** She has not read `L483` or `L659` and says so explicitly; she ratified the *filing decision* (one ticket, one logical path, per Kam's creation rule) and not the code claim.

What it rests on, so the next reader can re-derive rather than inherit it:

```
L352/L369  GIT_SYNC_STEP="1. Git sync — ..."      (the value, built two ways)
L483       ${GIT_SYNC_STEP}                        (consumer 1: the boot prompt)
L659       printf 'DRY_RUN_GIT_SYNC_STEP_BEGIN\n%s\n...' "$GIT_SYNC_STEP"   (consumer 2: the marker the suite reads)
L344-346   SEAT_WORKTREES="$(ls -1 "$PROJECT_DIR/worktrees" | sed 's|^|worktrees/|' ...)"
L363       ...instead${SEAT_WORKTREES:+ (this project has: ${SEAT_WORKTREES})},   <- inside GIT_SYNC_STEP
```

`L363` sits **inside** the `GIT_SYNC_STEP` heredoc, so the seat sentence is carried by the same variable that item 1 shows is never asserted in the prompt. That is the whole of the "same journey" claim, and it is checkable in one `grep -n 'GIT_SYNC_STEP\|SEAT_WORKTREES' Launch_Claude.command`.

Wednesday verified the item-2 refutation itself at the source (`grep -c SEAT_WORKTREES` = 3, `L346`'s `ls -1`, `L261`'s "the cockpit passes NOTHING that distinguishes the seats") and recorded the corrected classification — a wording defect plus a missing capability — as the record.

title: KS-921 residue: the re-link guard's awk parser is still case-sensitive — a lowercase `copy --from=builder … node_modules` reports 1 of 1 CLEAN, which is the #851 outage shape exactly
description:
## The re-link guard's own coverage and correctness residue — two false cleans, two false blocks, and a blind spot in the cross-check

From the **#870 tier-1 re-gate** (PASS WITH FINDINGS, verdict 2026-09-06T12:31Z; merged at
`066cff67554a5bd5398fcc9fb4b9ade422fbbd5b`, parents `e57bd5ac2` + `2f6b30fde`). All six findings are
**in the guard itself** — none was introduced as a live break, and **blast radius today is zero,**
**measured**: all 25 real Dockerfiles use canonical uppercase keywords and the guard is green on all 25
in both modes. That is why #870 was a GO. Every one of these is prospective on **authoring**.

Filed as one ticket per Kam's creation rule — the logical path is *the guard's own residue*. P2 on the
strength of F-A.

### F-A is reproduced here, not restated

I re-measured F-A myself before filing, from the **merged** tree, with the guard scoped by its own
`DEV_DIR` argument (`check-shared-relink.sh:69`) so each fixture gets its own root:

| case | differs from its control by | expected rc | actual rc |  |
| -- | -- | -- | -- | -- |
| `ctl_pass` | — canonical, correct | 0 | **0** | guard can say clean |
| `ctl_user_fail` | `USER` before the re-link | 1 | **1** | guard can catch the ordering violation |
| `subj_a1` | **only** `USER` → `user` (2 diff lines) | 1 | **0** | **FALSE CLEAN** |
| `ctl_a2` | `COPY --from=builder /app/node_modules ./node_modules` after the re-link | 1 | **1** | guard can catch the clobber |
| `subj_a2` | **only** `COPY` → `copy` (2 diff lines) | 1 | **0** | **FALSE CLEAN** |

Both false cleans print `OK — 1 Dockerfile(s) … dev-tree (KS-490): 1 of 1 clean.` under
`SHARED_RELINK_STRICT=1`. Each subject is byte-identical to a control that **does** fail, so the
harness discriminates in all four directions — an rc 0 here is the guard's answer, not the harness's.

`subj_a2` is **the #851 outage shape exactly**: a whole-tree `node_modules` write clobbering
`@secuura/shared` after the re-link, reported clean.

### The checklist

- [ ] **F-A — MAJOR, false clean. The SECOND OCCURRENCE OF F-1'S OWN CLASS.** F-1's `-i` landed on the
      *shell* class selectors (`:103`, `:121`) but the **awk parser it feeds is still case-sensitive on**
      **all four keywords** — `check-shared-relink.sh:162` `/^FROM[ \t]/`, `:173` `/^COPY[ \t]/`, `:195`
      `/^RUN[ \t]/`, `:223` `/^USER[ \t]/`; `toupper` appears **nowhere** in the file (verified by grep
      on the merged tree). **The cross-check cannot help:** these files DO match the precise selector,
      so there is no divergence to report — *both layers bypassed*. Fix shape: match on
      `toupper(first token)`, the same way the selector was fixed. Cells: the two rc-0 cases above,
      each asserting rc 1 **and** the specific clause-A message.
- [ ] **F-B — MAJOR. Clause A's link TARGET has no red-proof.** The cell named for it
      (`__tests__/check_shared_relink.test.sh:211`, *"A: a link to a DIFFERENT target does not satisfy*
      *the rule"*) varies the **destination** (`node_modules/@secuura/other`), not the target. Widen the
      guard regex target from `\/shared` to `\/[^ \t]*` and **the suite stays 26 passed, 0 failed**
      while the tampered guard accepts a link to `/WRONG-TARGET`. Cell to add: a fixture varying the
      **target** (`ln -s /elsewhere node_modules/@secuura/shared`), expecting rc 1 and `final stage has NO`.
- [ ] **F-C — MAJOR, false block, and it is from F-4's own widening.** `check-shared-relink.sh:210`,
      group `(\/[^ \t]*\/)?` **requires a leading** `/`, so `./node_modules/@secuura/shared` and
      `app/node_modules/…` fall out and are rejected with a message that is factually wrong about the
      file — the same complaint that made F-4 a Major. F-4's own stated rule is *"any destination*
      *ENDING at node_modules/@secuura/shared"*, and `./node_…` ends there. Confirmed on the merged tree.
- [ ] **F-D — Minor.** F-5 lowercased the **declared** side only (`:202` vs `:190`, consumed at `:264`),
      so `AS builder` + `--from=Builder` still fails under STRICT — a false block the day STRICT becomes
      the default, which is the harm F-5 was filed for.
- [ ] **F-E — Minor.** `USER root:root` and `USER 0:0` false-block at `:241` — the "one literal
      spelling" shape reappearing inside F-2's own oracle.
- [ ] **F-F — Minor.** The cross-check reads only `find . -name Dockerfile` (`:85`), so a
      `Dockerfile.prod` or a `Containerfile` is invisible to **both** instruments — the F-1 failure mode
      in the one dimension the new protection does not cover. Confirmed on the merged tree.

### Why three of these are KS-926 campaign members

F-B, F-A and F-F are members **7, 8 and 9** of the KS-926 family, and they are the sharpest yet
because **they are all inside a guard written to close this exact class**:

* **7 — F-B:** a cell whose *name* claims the axis it does not vary; widen the guard and the suite
  stays 26/0. *"A cell that cannot tell the fix from its own fallback is not a regression test"* in its
  purest form.
* **8 — F-A:** a fix applied at one layer and not at the layer it feeds, so the guard is blind on the
  axis it was **just repaired for** — and blind on the precise shape of a real past outage.
* **9 — F-F:** a protection described as *"the thing that notices the NEXT miss"* that can only notice
  misses of one kind.

With the launcher's member 6, **four of the nine were found inside work produced to close the family.**
That is the finding — a guard is exactly where this class hides, because a guard is the thing nobody
tests adversarially.

### Provenance

* The six findings, their line numbers and fix shapes | the QA agent's #870 re-gate verdict, relayed
  verbatim in Wednesday's RULING mail 2026-09-06T12:34:33Z (DKIM-verified: `spf=pass`,
  `dkim=pass header.i=@agentmail.to`, `dmarc=pass`, four failing-value controls absent) | read 2026-09-06
* F-A, F-C and F-F **independently confirmed by me** against the merged tree `066cff675` — awk keyword
  matches and absent `toupper`, the `:210` leading-slash group, and `:85`'s exact-name `find` | read 2026-09-06
* The F-A reproduction table | five fixtures run against `check-shared-relink.sh` from `066cff675`,
  each scoped by its own `DEV_DIR`, under `SHARED_RELINK_STRICT=1` | measured 2026-09-06
* **NOT measured by me:** F-B's 26/0-under-tamper, F-D and F-E. Those are the tester's, named as such.

nodes.body: **BLUF:** Delivered: PR 1444 merged as 40ed3573b491 on develop (F-C: the re-link guard accepts relative destinations; F-E: it accepts a uid-0 user with a group), after PRs 876 (8aefd2b06bf2) and 874 (bc067e3e9182); all are scripts and tests in the tree deployed to kintsugi at b1fb543640e7 (carried deploy record of 2026-11-01, not re-measured today). Left open: the description lists six items, F-A to F-F, all unchecked when read today. PR 1444's subject covers F-C and F-E; F-A and F-B (both MAJOR: a false clean of the same class as F-1, and no red-proof for clause A's link target), F-D and F-F are not recorded as delivered on the ticket, and the 2026-09-13 held-open comment on it records the residue.

**Held open — a residue by this ticket's own words; not moved by the 2026-09-14 class-h pass** (card secuura-fourteen-merged-own-pr-tickets-never-moved, close-by-residue; re-verified at source by s218).
- Residue (the description's six checklist boxes F-A … F-F, all unticked), measured at develop `8861e62161466c40f08d2b10a30edeb203123993` on 2026-09-14: **F-A LANDED** — `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/check-shared-relink.sh:180-181` `if (toupper(kw) ~ /^(FROM|RUN|…)$/) L = toupper(kw) substr(L, length(kw) + 1)` ahead of the `/^FROM[ \t]/` `:183`, `/^COPY[ \t]/` `:293`, `/^RUN[ \t]/` `:327`, `/^USER[ \t]/` `:361` tests (commit ff7704135 in #876; blob `7426b1874bbb`), with four `F-A:` cells in `scripts/__tests__/check_shared_relink.test.sh` (blob `239ea9637886`). **F-B NOT landed** (no `/elsewhere` or `WRONG-TARGET` fixture: 0 hits, control `F-A:` = 4). **F-C NOT landed** (`:348` still requires a leading `/` in the link target). **F-D** unmeasured by grep alone. **F-E NOT landed** (0 hits for `root:root` / `0:0` in the suite). **F-F NOT landed** (`:90` still `find . -name Dockerfile`).
- PR #876 merged 2026-09-07T00:49:35Z as `8aefd2b06bf29bcac099ce3a1af49bf7f89608fc`; PR #874 is OPEN at `6f7885602` (attached). Lane family: L8 (owns check-shared-relink.sh and its suite). The F-A box is met on develop and the description is not edited by this pass; four of six boxes remain.
- Stays open; not moved by the 2026-09-14 class-h pass. No state write, nothing deployed, no environment touched.

title: KS-921 residues: five Dockerfile shapes the re-link guard cannot read, an nginx final stage it can NEVER pass, and one A_FAIL branch no test can red
description:
## KS-921 gate residues F-3, F-6, F-7 — five legitimate Dockerfile shapes the guard cannot read, one it can never pass, and one branch no test can red

From the #870 gate. Deliberately **not** fixed in that PR: F-1/F-2/F-4/F-5 were, because they are false cleans and false blocks that bite today; these three are shapes with **no live exposure** and one design question that deserves a decision rather than a patch.

**Live exposure today is zero, measured:** all seven frontend Dockerfiles use nginx/alpine final stages, **none** consumes `shared-builder`, and no frontend source imports `@secuura/shared` (0 files). So nothing in the tree hits these paths now — which is exactly why they should be recorded rather than left to be discovered by whoever first writes one.

### F-6 comes first, because it is the one with no answer

**For an nginx final stage the guard offers no route forward.** A static-serving final stage legitimately has no `node_modules` at all, so clause A's `final stage writes node_modules nowhere` fires and there is no way to make the file green except by adding a pointless `node_modules` write purely to satisfy the check.

**A guard with no green path for a legitimate shape is a design question, not a bug.** The options are roughly: exempt a final stage that writes no `node_modules` and consumes no builder tree; require an explicit opt-out marker; or narrow the class further so such files never enter it. **This is the first item on this ticket and it should be decided before anything below it is coded**, because the answer changes what the other shapes need.

### F-3 — five legitimate shapes the parser cannot read

1. **BuildKit heredoc** — `RUN <<EOF … EOF`. The parser joins on trailing `\` and treats each logical line independently, so a re-link inside a heredoc body is invisible.
2. **An nginx final stage with no** `node_modules` — see F-6.
3. **The non-final-stage write.** Clause A is stated over the FINAL stage. A Dockerfile whose runtime stage is not the last `FROM` in the file (a valid multi-target build) is judged against the wrong stage.
4. `npm i` **shorthand.** The install detector matches `npm ci|install`; `npm i` alone is not matched, so a stage installing that way reads as writing no `node_modules`.
5. **The JSON** `COPY` **form** — `COPY ["--from=builder", "/app/node_modules", "./node_modules"]`. Valid Dockerfile, unreadable to a whitespace-token parser.

Plus the two parser edges the gate noted.

### F-7 — and this one is the same family as three tickets already on this board

**The** `A_FAIL` **branch for "final stage writes node_modules nowhere" is pinned by NO test.**

Measured 2026-09-06, by neutering it (`note("A_FAIL", …)` → `note("A_OK", …)`) and re-running:

```
suite with the branch neutered ............ 26 passed, 0 failed
"final stage has NO" ...................... pinned by 4 cells
"runs BEFORE the last instruction" ........ pinned by 1 cell
"runs after a non-root" ................... pinned by 1 cell
"writes node_modules nowhere" ............. pinned by 0 cells
```

The tamper was restored and the file verified byte-identical by sha256.

**A branch no cell can red is a check that cannot fail** — and it is the fourth mechanism of that family on this board tonight, alongside [KS-926](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-926) (a check nothing runs), [KS-927](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-927) (a check running with the half that would notice already dead) and [KS-928](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-928) (a check whose wiring is unasserted). Here the guard runs, the suite runs, the wiring is asserted — **and one branch of it still cannot be shown to work.**

Note the ordering trap for whoever fixes it: this branch is also *unreachable in practice for the current class*, since every one of the 25 files writes `node_modules` in its final stage. Pinning it needs a fixture, and the fixture is the nginx shape from F-6 — **so F-6's decision and F-7's cell are the same piece of work.**

### Fix shape

Decide F-6 first. Then a cell per F-3 shape, each red-proofed by the shape it describes, and the F-7 cell falling out of F-6's chosen semantics. **No shape should be "supported" without a cell that reds without it** — the guard already shipped one branch without that and this ticket is the receipt.

*Filed by s141 (seat A), 2026-09-06, from the #870 gate at Wednesday's direction to ticket rather than widen that PR. The F-7 measurement above is mine; the shapes are the gate's.*

nodes.body: **BLUF:** Delivered: PR 876 (F-3 node_modules write spellings, 8aefd2b06bf2), PR 886 (F-QA-2 message, 61df129e9c58), PR 879 (852e1fff773b) and PR 874 (bc067e3e9182) are merged on develop, and PR 1121 (4a61519883fe) adds the KS-957 red-proof of the tooling tokens; all are in the tree deployed to kintsugi at b1fb543640e7 (carried deploy record of 2026-11-01, not re-measured today) and are developer tooling and tests. Left open: residue by this ticket's own words. The 2026-09-13 held-open comment records that F-3's heredoc and non-final-stage shapes were deliberately not fixed (the heredoc case is a stated rule at `check-shared-relink.sh:218-224`, not a fix) and that no suite cell names a runtime stage that is not the last FROM. The only commit since then on the deployed history that names KS-930 is PR 1121, which is KS-957's.

## CORRECTION to the 2026-09-14 08:00:51Z record above (comment `93033711`) — "identical on the base (not regressions)" is FALSE for two of the four spellings, by measurement at the named base (merge seat s228, on Wednesday's ADDENDUM 09:17:07Z)

The record carried Peter's finding-4 sentence from the #879 review ("not regressions; all of these behave identically on the base") for four spellings. The tier-2 round-2 gate on #879 measured each against the guard at the PR's own base `a0ad0a084` (blob `9141597bd`), at develop M38 (`7426b1874`) and at the head `0374bec00` (`d41c79538`), same fixture skeleton, both modes (report `2026-09-14-879-ks945-tier2-r2` §8 FINDING 3a; evidence `17_finding4_at_base.out`, `20_regression_fixture_full_output.txt`):

- `RUN /usr/local/bin/npm ci --omit=dev` — **rc 1 at `a0ad0a084` and at M38 (BLOCKED), rc 0 at the head (CLEAN)** → a regression of #879, not a pre-existing gap.
- `RUN corepack yarn install` — **rc 1 at `a0ad0a084` and at M38, rc 0 at the head** → a regression of #879.
- `RUN npx create-vite my-app` — clean at base and head alike (as recorded).
- `RUN sh -c "npm ci"` — clean at base and head alike (as recorded).

The sentence in the record is therefore wrong about two of its four members. Source of the error: the review body asserted "identical on the base" without a base/head table (unlike its finding 2, which had one); s229 transcribed it faithfully on Wednesday's brief, which instructed the seat to route the finding as Peter wrote it — the error is Wednesday's brief's, carried into the record, and is corrected here by the gate's instrument. The two regressed spellings are members of the FINDING 1 class in the comment above (the wrapper/prefix-before-the-manager mechanism), which this ticket's class-(a) build closes. Nothing else in the record changes: the disposition ("the natural limit of a line-oriented guard, better on a ticket") stands; #879 merged onto develop by Wednesday's ruling with this class disclosed. Facts only; no state change.

## FINDING 1 from the tier-2 round-2 gate on PR #879 (KS-945), 2026-09-14 09:12:12Z — the generalised class this ticket's class-(a) build must cover: a wrapper or prefix before the manager hides an install after the re-link (merge seat s228, on Wednesday's ADDENDUM 09:17:07Z)

**The finding, as the gate wrote it (report `Testing Agent MAIN/projects/secuura/reports/2026-09-14-879-ks945-tier2-r2/report.md` §8, Major):** `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/check-shared-relink.sh:169-216` (`pm_writes`), specifically `:192` `if (a[i] != "npm" && a[i] != "yarn" && a[i] != "pnpm") continue` after the `:191` skip loop that steps over only `""`, the bare word `sudo`, and `NAME=value` — reads only the LEADING word of each separator-split segment, so ANY word in front of the manager hides an install from the guard. **Twelve spellings are BLOCKED by the guard at the PR's own base `a0ad0a084` and at develop M38, and are certified `1 of 1 clean` at the head `0374bec00`** — a false-CLEAN regression, the #851 direction: `RUN /usr/local/bin/npm ci --omit=dev` · `RUN env NODE_ENV=production npm ci` · `RUN exec npm ci` · `RUN time npm ci` · `RUN nice npm ci` · `RUN nohup npm ci` · `RUN command npm ci` · `RUN echo x | xargs npm ci` · `RUN sudo -u node npm ci` · `RUN ./node_modules/.bin/npm ci` · `RUN corepack yarn install` · `RUN corepack pnpm i`. Oracle: Purpose (the guard's own header and the PR's comment — "a false clean is neither visible nor cheap… an unknown verb now blocks"), History (the base caught these), Product (the COPY clause of the same file states "widening what the parser SEES can only ADD node_modules writes, never remove one, so this direction fails safe" — the RUN clause narrowed what it sees). Repro: `git show 0374bec00:Blockchain/Dev/scripts/check-shared-relink.sh > g.sh`; write `d/services/thing/Dockerfile` = the suite's canonical skeleton with one of the lines above AFTER the `ln -s` line; `bash g.sh d` → `OK — 1 Dockerfile(s) … 1 of 1 clean`, rc 0 (both modes); the same fixture against `git show a0ad0a084:…` → `::error::… the re-link runs BEFORE the last instruction that writes node_modules`, rc 1. Evidence `20_regression_fixture_full_output.txt`, `08_falsification.out`, `10_extra_shapes.out`, `17_finding4_at_base.out`. Severity Major (a false CLEAN reproduces the #851 outage class); likelihood in operation low — the 25-file corpus writes none of these spellings in any stage, and it takes an author placing an install after the re-link AND spelling it with a prefix.

**Why #879 merged anyway (Wednesday's ruling, stated so it can be read):** against develop M38 the head CLOSES 14 false-clean spellings the corpus does write (`npm run` ×50: bare `yarn`, `npm run build`, `yarn --frozen-lockfile`, `npm init <spec>`, `npm init foo --yes`, `(npm ci)`, `npm install-test`, `npm exec`, bare `npm`, `npm -vv`, `npm --version=1`, `yarn add`, `npm audit fix`, `npm prune` — each rc 0 at M38 / rc 1 at head) and OPENS the 12 above, which the corpus never writes; likelihood-weighted the merge reduces the open false-clean surface, and the class already has this ticket as its home with the class-(a) build queued behind #879's merge.

**Five pre-existing shapes of the same family (the gate's observations; not named here before — searched this ticket for `heredoc` (the false-BLOCK direction only), `RUN [` 0, wrapper words 0):** `if … then npm ci … fi` · `for … do … done` · `{ npm ci; }` · `RUN ["npm","ci"]` (the JSON exec form, which the COPY clause already normalises and the RUN clause does not) · a heredoc body carrying the install after the re-link.

**Fix-shape (the gate's, prose):** stop trusting the leading word alone — after the leading-word pass, ALSO scan every token of the segment: a whole-word manager token (boundary class excluding `[A-Za-z0-9_.-]`, so `mynpm` still misses and `/usr/local/bin/npm`, `"npm"`, `corepack npm` all hit) whose FOLLOWING token is not on the read-only/probe allowlists is a write — the base's substring instrument re-admitted with a left boundary; it can only ADD writes (fails safe, the file's own stated principle). A wrapper-skip list (`env`+assignments, `exec`, `time`, `nice`, `nohup`, `command`, `xargs`, `sudo` with flags, `then`, `do`, `else`, `{`, `(`) is the deny-list alternative and fails open on the next wrapper. Separately normalise RUN's JSON exec form as the COPY clause does, and read heredoc bodies as RUN text (or deny a final stage that contains a heredoc after the last write — the fail-closed reading).

**Regression cells (the gate's, described):** one cell per spelling above, each expecting exit 1 and the A-clause message; negative controls `RUN echo npm ci` and `RUN mynpm i` expecting 0, so the widened match cannot resurrect the argument-position false block; a cell asserting `RUN ["npm", "ci"]` after the re-link is a write.

**FINDING 2 (Minor, recommendation only):** `npm cache clean --force` / `npm cache verify` as a standalone RUN after the re-link false-BLOCK at the head (rc 0 at base) — the read-only allowlist at `check-shared-relink.sh:203` has no `cache`; corpus 0; in practice joined to the install with `&&`. Consider `cache` for the allowlist, with a cell.

Facts only; no state change on this ticket by the merge seat.

**Record from the #879 review (2026-09-08, finding 4) — four residual false cleans, routed here by the reviewer; not fixed on #879.** Measured by him at `79f1fcb48` and identical on the base `a0ad0a084` (not regressions): `RUN /usr/local/bin/npm ci --omit=dev` — clean (an absolute path defeats the whole-token manager-name match) · `RUN npx create-vite my-app` — clean (`npx` is not in the manager set) · `RUN corepack yarn install` — clean (`corepack` is not stepped over the way `sudo` is) · `RUN sh -c "npm ci"` — clean (the manager sits inside a quoted argument). His read: the natural limit of a line-oriented guard, better on a ticket than as scope creep in that PR. Searched this ticket's description and comments for `corepack`, `npx create-`, `/usr/local/bin/npm` and `sh -c` before writing: 0 hits (control `heredoc` = 1) (s229, 2026-09-14). This ticket's own F-3/F-6/F-7 residue is unchanged by #879 (markers re-read at its head 2026-09-14).

**Held open — a residue by this ticket's own words; not moved by the 2026-09-14 class-h pass** (card secuura-fourteen-merged-own-pr-tickets-never-moved, close-by-residue; re-verified at source by s218).
- Residue (comment 240e6985, 2026-09-06): "F-3's heredoc and non-final-stage shapes — NOT fixed, deliberately. Both measured as false blocks … Friction, not danger, so they queue behind the false cleans. Next unless reordered." No later comment closes them. Landed since: F-6 (nginx) via ff7704135 and rounds 1–3 (suite cells `F-6:` at `:506-546`, `F-6 inv:` `:638-642`); F-7's shape in kind (the exemption pin at `:506`).
- Develop probe (read 2026-09-14 at `8861e62161466c40f08d2b10a30edeb203123993`): `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/check-shared-relink.sh:218-224` (blob `7426b1874bbb`) documents "heredoc bodies land here, which is why RUN <<EOT disqualifies a stage by itself" — the heredoc false block is now a stated rule, not a fix; no suite cell names a runtime stage that is not the last FROM. KS-957 (Backlog, unassigned) carries F4/F5/F6 claim-level residues and 0 hits for heredoc / non-final.
- PRs #876 merged 2026-09-07T00:49:35Z as `8aefd2b06bf29bcac099ce3a1af49bf7f89608fc` and #886 merged 2026-09-07T00:50:26Z as `61df129e9c580e3b4622d9b5de11f2abd765b8f6`; #874 (`6f7885602`) and #879 (`79f1fcb48`) OPEN, both attached. Lane family: L8.
- Stays open; not moved by the 2026-09-14 class-h pass. No state write, nothing deployed, no environment touched.

**Round 3 pushed — `a15a5146ec22b515c5f35911dc7c59953375558e`, PR #876.** Kam authorised exactly one narrow round, regression only.

**The regression, and it was larger than the one spelling the verdict named.** Round 2's boundary class `[^A-Za-z0-9_.-]` treats `-`, `.` and `_` as word characters, so a runtime name carrying a version or variant suffix was invisible. Ten shapes were **rc 1 at base `306d0db92` and rc 0 `A_EXEMPT` at round-2 head `3047bcb1d`** — regressions against base, not gaps:

`node-22` · `node22` · `node.22` · `node_22` · `nodejs-22` · `node-lts` · `npx` in the final CMD · `apk add nodejs-current` · the `nodejs.org` tarball install · `apt-get install nodejs-legacy`

The successor brief named six (the suffixed spellings). The gate's own F2 named four more, each also rc 1 at base — so all ten are inside "regression only" and all ten are closed. `npx` is the odd one: not a suffix problem at all, it named the tooling and sat in neither token list, so it joined the tooling clause rather than the word-arm.

**The fix mirrors what the file already did.** `base_is_js_runtime` has always allowed the suffix — `^(node|nodejs|bun|deno)([0-9._-]|$)` — fifteen lines from the clause that did not. The trailing class now matches it instead of inventing a second convention.

**The price, pinned rather than left to be found.** `node-red` is now denied and that is correct (it IS a JS runtime). `node-exporter` is now denied and that is a **false block**, accepted knowingly: this arm fails toward blocking, which a human sees, over exempting, which nobody sees, and no class file reaches the arm today. Both are cells. The false-block class as a whole is gate finding F3 — out of scope by the regression-only ruling.

**Evidence.** All ten measured at three SHAs over the same fixture before the fix was written. Plant-point control run first: the suite's own green shape reads `rc 0 A_OK` at all three guards and the same file minus one re-link line reads `rc 1` at all three. Suite 71 → **86 passed, 0 failed**. Red-proof A (revert the class only) reds **exactly 11** cells, both pair controls and all 71 pre-existing cells green; red-proof B (drop `npx` only) reds **exactly 1**. Both restored by inverse edit, sha256 byte-identical, suite re-run green. Leg 13 on the real tree unchanged: rc 0, 25 Dockerfiles, 4 copy / 21 re-install. Full 13-leg pre-push preflight passed.

Claim-level findings F4/F5/F6 aggregated on **KS-957**, not fixed here.

## F-3: two of the five shapes are FALSE CLEANS on the #851 outage, not friction — fixed in [#876](https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/876) @ `af954c691`

**This ticket's framing needs correcting on one point, and it is the one that matters.** F-3 is
written as five *legitimate shapes the parser cannot read*, with live exposure zero. Live exposure
**is** zero — I re-confirmed it — but two of the five are not readability problems. **They are false
cleans on the exact clobber the guard exists to catch.**

Measured on the merged guard at `066cff675`, each fixture being the canonical clobber file with
**only the spelling of the last `node_modules` write changed**, `SHARED_RELINK_STRICT=1`:

| the last write | rc | verdict |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `COPY --from=builder /app/node_modules ./node_modules` | **1** | blocked — *control* |
| `COPY ["--from=builder", "/app/node_modules", "./node_modules"]` | **0** | `1 of 1 clean` |
| `COPY --from=builder ["/app/node_modules", "./node_modules"]` | **0** | `1 of 1 clean` |
| `RUN npm i --omit=dev` | **0** | `1 of 1 clean` |

### Why this hid, and why it belongs to the KS-926 family

On a file with **no other parseable write**, these shapes *do* exit 1 — through the
`writes node_modules nowhere (unexpected shape)` **fallback**, whose message is factually wrong about
the file. Reading only the exit code, the guard looks like it handles them.

**The fallback is the only thing between the parser gap and the false clean, and it stops standing
there the moment the file carries a write the parser CAN read** — which all 25 real files do. That is
the campaign's "which clause judged it" question arriving inside this ticket, so the new cells assert
the **clause**, not the exit code: exit-code-only cells would have passed against the unfixed guard.

### Fixed

- `COPY` — normalise JSON/exec array punctuation before the destination test (the test took the last
  whitespace token, `"./node_modules"]`, bracket and quotes attached). **Widening what the parser sees
  can only add writes, never remove one — this direction fails safe.**
- `RUN` — `npm i` writes the same tree as `npm install`. `([ \t]|$)` stops it swallowing `npm init`,
  and a cell pins that.

**Red-proofed separately:** removing the `COPY` normalisation → **28 passed, 2 failed** (exactly the
two JSON cells); reverting `(ci|install|i)` → **29 passed, 1 failed** (exactly the `npm i` cell). Each
tamper restored by inverse edit, byte-identical by sha256. Suite **26 → 30**. Real tree unchanged at
**25 of 25 clean** in both modes.

### Where the rest of this ticket stands

- **F-6 (nginx) — sent to Wednesday as a DECISION, no code**, per her instruction. Made concrete
  first: `a_plain` (nginx final, no node_modules) rc 1; **`b_relink_anyway` — adding the re-link
  honestly — ALSO rc 1**, because the rule anchors on a `node_modules` write and there is none to
  anchor to; `c_pointless_write` (install a node tree into the nginx image purely to satisfy the
  check) rc 0. **The guard's one route to green makes the image worse.** My recommendation is option A
  (exempt a final stage that writes no `node_modules` and copies no builder tree), with the cost named:
  it changes the shape of F-7's cell.
- **F-7 — still blocked on F-6**, exactly as this ticket says. Under option A its cell would pin the
  *exemption* rather than the failure. Whoever takes it should be told that before starting.
- **F-3's heredoc and non-final-stage shapes — NOT fixed, deliberately.** Both measured as false
  *blocks* (rc 1, `final stage has NO re-link`, on a file that re-links inside a `RUN <<EOT` body, and
  on one whose runtime stage is not the last `FROM`). Friction, not danger, so they queue behind the
  false cleans. Next unless reordered.

### Live exposure re-confirmed, with a control

**7** frontend Dockerfiles, **6** with an nginx final stage, **0** consuming `shared-builder`; and
across all **35** Dockerfiles in the tree, **zero** JSON-form `COPY` and **zero** `npm i` — against a
positive control of **25** files that *do* consume `shared-builder`, so the zeros discriminate.

### One thing I did not assert

I reasoned that this ticket's own F-3 example — `COPY ["--from=builder", …]`, flag *inside* the array
— is invalid Docker, and was about to write that down. `docker build --check` reports
**"Check complete, no warnings found"** for both spellings, so I make no such claim; I did not build
either. The fix handles both, and the unambiguously valid spelling has the same hole, so nothing rests
on it.

title: Launcher boot step tells every agent session to POST /api/seen as EXTRANET_ME=kam, which clears Kam's own unread flags — and the extranet is input-only
description:
## What is wrong

`Launch_Claude.command:522` (boot step 7) instructs every session:

> "…GET the summary for this operator (EXTRANET_ME), and fold my open tasks + replies-to-me + new documents into the confirmation below; **mark seen afterwards**."

which routes to the `extranet` skill's step 3:

> `POST $EXTRANET_URL/api/seen {"person":"$EXTRANET_ME"}` so "new" resets next session.

And in this project's `4_Credentials/.env`:

```
EXTRANET_ME=kam
```

So the "operator" an agent marks caught-up as **is Kam himself**. An agent that follows the boot step clears **Kam's** unread flags on his own portal — the tasks, replies and documents he has not yet read. The next time he opens the extranet, the things an agent read on his behalf are no longer marked new to him.

It is the human's signal, and an automated session destroys it as a side effect of booting.

## Why it is a defect and not a preference

Two independent reasons, either of which is sufficient:

1. `EXTRANET_ME` **is doing two jobs.** It identifies *whose* summary to fetch — correct, an agent working for Kam should see Kam's queue — and it also identifies *who has now seen it* — wrong, because the agent saw it and Kam did not. One variable, two meanings, and the second one is only ever wrong when an agent uses it.
2. **The extranet is input-only for agents** (standing rule for this project). `POST /api/seen` is a write. The boot step asks for a write the operating rules forbid, so the instruction cannot be followed as stated regardless of who `EXTRANET_ME` names.

## Reproduced

Not by running it — running it *is* the defect, and it is not reversible from the API. Established from the artefacts instead:

* `4_Credentials/.env:4` → `EXTRANET_ME=kam` (agent key on line 3 not reproduced here)
* `Launch_Claude.command:522` → the "mark seen afterwards" instruction
* `Notes (MASTER)/skills/Current/extranet.md:27` → the `POST /api/seen {"person":"$EXTRANET_ME"}` step
* `…/extranet.md:111` → `POST /api/seen | {person}` in the endpoint table

The three artefacts compose into the behaviour without needing to execute it. **This session declined the step and said so rather than skipping it silently** — that is the current mitigation, and it relies on every future session making the same judgement, which is not a control.

## Fix shape

Any of these closes it; the first is the smallest:

1. **Drop "mark seen afterwards" from the launcher's step 7** and the corresponding step from the skill, for agent sessions. The summary is read-only; nothing needs the flag reset, and "new since last session" is more useful to an agent unreset anyway.
2. **Separate the two meanings** — `EXTRANET_ME` for whose queue to read, a distinct `EXTRANET_SEEN_AS` for whose flags to clear, unset by default so the write never happens unless someone deliberately sets it.
3. **Make** `/api/seen` **refuse an agent key** for a person other than the key's own identity, server-side, so no launcher wording can cause it. This one belongs to the extranet app rather than the launcher.

## Scope

The launcher is a per-project copy of a master template, so fixing this copy does not fix the others — the same boot step exists in every project's launcher, and any project whose `EXTRANET_ME` names a human has the same defect. Whoever picks this up should decide at the template level, not here.

Filed at Wednesday's direction (2026-09-06) after this session declined the boot step. Not applied mid-queue: the launcher is not this seat's to edit.

title: `/shared` ships the TypeScript compiler and a 267 MB dev tree into all 24 runtime images — KS-490 closed the service tree only
description:
## KS-490 closed the SERVICE tree and left the SHARED tree open — `/shared` ships the TypeScript compiler into all 24 runtime images

KS-490's two PRs (#849, #851) removed the build toolchain from the runtime *stages* and pruned each service's *own* `node_modules`. **Neither touches** `/shared`, and every runtime stage copies it wholesale.

### Measured on the live demo box, in RUNNING containers

| Reading | `secuura-security` | `secuura-governance` |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `/shared/node_modules/typescript` | **present, 22.9 MB** | **present, 22.9 MB** |
| `bin/tsc` | **present** | **present** |
| `/shared` total | **267.2 MB** | **267.2 MB** |
| top-level entries under `/shared/node_modules` | **243** | **243** |

*(The #851 gate's tester reported 342 packages; I counted **243 top-level entries** with* `ls | wc -l`*, which counts a scoped* `@org` *directory once regardless of what it contains. Both numbers are probably right about different things — stating my instrument rather than reconciling them by assertion.)*

### It is footprint and attack surface, NOT loadability — measured, with a control

```
require.resolve('typescript', {paths:['/app']})  ->  MODULE_NOT_FOUND
require.resolve('express',    {paths:['/app']})  ->  resolves
```

The control is what makes the first line meaningful: the resolver works, and `typescript` genuinely is not reachable from the app's module paths. So no runtime code can load it — but a compiler binary and 267 MB of dev tree are present in every running container, which is exactly what KS-490 exists to remove.

### Cause

`shared-builder` runs `npm ci` **without** `--omit=dev` and is never pruned, and all 24 runtime stages `COPY --from=shared-builder /shared /shared`.

### Fix shape — and the hazard it carries

Prune `shared-builder` after its build: one place, all 24 services.

⚠ **This is exactly the hazard #851 just fixed.** `@secuura/shared` is a hand-made undeclared symlink; pruning removed it, and three runtime stages that did not re-create it shipped images that crashed on start with `Cannot find module '@secuura/shared'`. **A** `/shared` **prune therefore needs a real start probe per service, not reasoning** — the same shape of evidence #851 ended up needing. See [KS-490](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-490) and #851's fix commit.

*Filed by s140 (seat A), 2026-09-06, from #851's gate findings (F1).*

## The 342-vs-243 count, settled — and 342 is not reproduced by any instrument I ran

Wednesday's instruction was to settle this with **one named instrument and say which**, not to reconcile it by assertion. Here is what each candidate instrument actually returns.

### 243 is settled, and two independent instruments agree exactly

| instrument | environment | result |
| -- | -- | -- |
| distinct top-level directory names in `packages/shared/package-lock.json` (a scoped `@x/y` contributes the directory `@x` once) | the repo alone, no container | **243** |
| `ls /shared/node_modules \| wc -l` | running container `secuura-security`, local stack | **243** |

The lockfile is the artefact that *decides* what lands in `/shared`, and it needs no container — anyone can reproduce it from the repo. It agrees with the container to the unit. **s140's 243 is correct and is a directory count.**

Control on that instrument: `ls -A` returns **245**; the two extra are `.bin` and `.package-lock.json`, which `ls` omits. So the pair can differ, and does.

### The other number — what each plausible instrument gives

| instrument | result |
| -- | -- |
| top-level **packages** in the lockfile (scoped counted individually) | 306 |
| every package entry in the lockfile (top-level + nested) | 347 |
| installed top-level package dirs, in the container | 301 |
| **all installed package dirs** (top-level + scoped + nested), in the container | **324** |
| `find /shared/node_modules -name package.json` | 722 |
| the same, capped at depth 3 | 483 |

**None of them is 342.** The nearest are 324 and 347.

Two things that fall out of this and are worth keeping:

- **`find -name package.json` is not a package-count instrument.** It returns 722 and 483 depending only on the depth cap, because packages ship their own sub-manifests (`dist/package.json`, `esm/package.json`). This was the instrument I had *predicted* I would use; it would have produced a confident wrong number. Measured before trusting.
- **The lockfile and the container legitimately differ**: 306 top-level in the lock against 301 installed, and 41 nested against 23. That is the expected shape for optional/platform-specific packages that do not install on this architecture — the lock describes every platform, the container holds one.

### So: 342 is UNREPRODUCED, not reconciled

I am not going to invent a derivation that lands on 342. The honest state is that the tester's figure does not match any instrument I ran, and the two candidates it could plausibly be (324 all-installed-dirs, 347 all-lock-entries) are 18 and 5 away. **If the tester names their instrument, it can be settled in one command; until then this is an open discrepancy, not a resolved one.**

What it does **not** change: 243 directories is right, and the finding this ticket exists for is unaffected by which package-count instrument is used.

### The footprint finding itself — re-measured, and it stands

Measured in the running container `secuura-security` on the **local** stack (stated explicitly; s140's identical figures came from the **demo** box, so the two environments agree):

```
/shared                                    267.2 MB
/shared/node_modules/typescript            present
/shared/node_modules/typescript/bin/tsc    present
```

Same total to the tenth of a megabyte as s140's demo reading, which is a useful corroboration across two environments.

**Nothing was changed.** Read-only `docker exec`, local stack. The demo box was not touched and stays pinned at `db1848abf`.

### Still to do on this ticket
The prune itself, which carries the hazard the ticket already names — the same one #851 paid for — so it needs **a start probe per service, not reasoning**. That is the next piece of work and it is not started. [KS-921](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-921)'s guard (PR #870) is the structural protection against exactly the failure a `/shared` prune would risk, so the two are worth landing in that order.

*Measured by s141 (seat A), 2026-09-06.*

| property | value |

| id | `a0000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000060` |

[KS-737](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-737) — *platform-admin login skips MFA entirely when* `mfaCode` *is omitted* — is **archived**. title: SigningKeyProtectorTests: "a legacy blob under an unknown key is refused, not guessed" failed once with "No exception was thrown" — on a fixed tree, 0/5 isolated afterwards
description:
## Observed — 2026-09-06, worktree `obeden-ssd-ps781` at `00f364a` + the [PS-781](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-781/stripe-identity-is-offered-on-identityverify-but-can-never-be-started) change

First full `dotnet test` of the tree (4,079 tests): **1 failure**, captured this time:

```
Failed ssd.UnitTests.SigningKeyProtectorTests.A_legacy_blob_under_an_unknown_key_is_refused_not_guessed [2 ms]
  Assert.ThrowsAny() Failure: No exception was thrown
  Expected: typeof(System.Exception)
```

Then: the same class in isolation **5/5 green**, and the full suite again **4,079 / 0**. The [PS-781](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-781/stripe-identity-is-offered-on-identityverify-but-can-never-be-started) change touches `KycVerificationController`, two test files and systemTest — nothing under `Services/Security` or anything the protector reads.

## Why this is filed rather than shrugged off

[PS-583](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-583/intermittent-failure-in-signingkeyprotectortests-and-the-shared-root) saw exactly this test flake once on 2026-08-12, kept only the test *name*, and was closed as "the tree was moving" after 10/10 + 40/40 green re-runs on a detached checkout. That explanation does not fit today: this was **my own worktree, nothing switched its branch, and the build and the run were sequential** — a fixed tree. [PS-583](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-583/intermittent-failure-in-signingkeyprotectortests-and-the-shared-root)'s one recorded gap was that the assertion message was lost; this time it is kept, and it says the *decrypt did not throw*.

## A hypothesis worth ruling in or out (not a finding)

"Refused, not guessed" for a wrong key is a **probabilistic** property if the legacy blob format is not authenticated. Under CBC + PKCS#7, decrypting with the wrong key yields a padding error *most* of the time — but about **1 in 256** wrong-key decryptions produce a final byte that happens to be valid padding, and then nothing throws; the caller receives garbage as if it were the plaintext. If the test generates a fresh random key per run, a \~0.4% flake rate is exactly what a 1-in-\~250 event looks like across the day's runs. An AES-GCM (authenticated) path cannot do this: a wrong key always fails the tag.

So the question is not "why is the test flaky" but **"does the legacy path authenticate before it decrypts?"** If it does not, the test is telling the truth about the code, and the fix is in the protector (verify a MAC/tag before touching the padding, or refuse legacy blobs whose key id is unknown *before* decrypting) — not in the test.

## Suggested

1. Read `SigningKeyProtector`'s legacy-blob branch: what is checked before `Decrypt`, and whether a padding exception is the *only* thing standing between a wrong key and a "success".
2. Make the test deterministic either way: if the legacy format is authenticated, seed the key so the run is reproducible; if it is not, the test should assert the guard that *should* exist and the code should get it.
3. Re-check [PS-583](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-583/intermittent-failure-in-signingkeyprotectortests-and-the-shared-root)'s conclusion in that light — its refutation was statistical, and a 1-in-256 event survives 50 runs about 82% of the time.

Related: [PS-583](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-583/intermittent-failure-in-signingkeyprotectortests-and-the-shared-root) (the earlier flake), [PS-196](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-196/isolate-signing-key-encryption-from-the-document-key-kms-aes-gcm-kdf) / [PS-607](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-607/rotate-existing-personal-signing-certificates-onto-the-isolated-key) (signing-key isolation — same component).

## Acceptance

* **The code question is answered first, from source.** `SigningKeyProtector`'s legacy-blob branch is read and the answer written here: what is checked **before** `Decrypt`, and whether a padding exception is the only thing standing between a wrong key and an apparent success. If the legacy format is **not** authenticated, the test was telling the truth about the code and the fix belongs in the protector — verify a MAC/tag before touching the padding, or refuse a legacy blob whose key id is unknown *before* decrypting — not in the test.
* **The test becomes deterministic either way.** If the format is authenticated, the key is seeded so the run is reproducible; if it is not, the test asserts the guard that *should* exist and the code grows it. "Re-ran it and it passed" is not an outcome.
* **The criterion is a repeat-count run on a fixed tree, with the count stated** — not a new product spec. On a **throwaway worktree detached at a named sha** (so nothing can move the tree underneath it, which is [PS-583](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-583/intermittent-failure-in-signingkeyprotectortests-and-the-shared-root)'s whole lesson), run `SigningKeyProtectorTests` under `--repeat-each`-equivalent repetition at a count chosen for the hypothesis, **state the count**, and state what it can and cannot rule out. A \~1-in-256 event survives 50 runs about 82% of the time, so a 40/40 or 50/50 green **refutes nothing** — the count has to be large enough to matter, or the claim has to be stated as "not refuted" rather than "refuted".
* **The assertion message is captured on any failure**, as it was this time and was not on [PS-583](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-583/intermittent-failure-in-signingkeyprotectortests-and-the-shared-root). A re-run destroys the only evidence; the message (`Assert.ThrowsAny() Failure: No exception was thrown`) is what distinguishes "the tree was moving" from "the decrypt did not throw".
* [PS-583](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-583/intermittent-failure-in-signingkeyprotectortests-and-the-shared-root)**'s conclusion is re-checked in this light** and the result recorded on **this** ticket ([PS-583](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-583/intermittent-failure-in-signingkeyprotectortests-and-the-shared-root) is closed; do not edit it): its refutation was statistical, over a sample too small for a 1-in-256 event, so "refuted" may have been too strong.
* **No Playwright spec, and no new product spec at all — both are the wrong tool here:** this is a one-off investigation into a probabilistic property of a crypto path with no surface, no route and no `data-testid`. If the investigation finds a real defect, *that* fix gets its own xUnit cases in `SigningKeyProtectorTests` (a wrong key is refused **deterministically**, a legacy blob with an unknown key id is refused before any decrypt attempt) — which is where it belongs: a rule, two minutes, nothing up. The deliverables of **this** ticket are the source reading, the stated repeat count with its result, and the captured assertion message.

title: vite is a production dependency of services/auth — esbuild and fsevents ship into the runtime image, imported by nothing
description:
## `vite` sits in auth's production `dependencies`, dragging esbuild and fsevents into the runtime image

Found by the #849 (KS-490) tier-2 gate as F-2, and measured before filing.

### The measurement

| Reading | Value |
| -- | -- |
| `services/auth/package.json` → `dependencies.vite` | `7.3.6` |
| `services/auth/package.json` → `devDependencies.vite` | **absent** |
| runtime sources under `services/auth/src` importing `vite` (excluding `__tests__`) | **0** |
| CONTROL: runtime sources importing `express` | **15** |

The control is what makes the zero mean something — the same grep shape finds 15 files for a package auth genuinely uses at runtime, so 0 for `vite` is a real absence and not a grep that cannot match.

### Why it matters

Because `vite` is a production dependency it survives `npm prune --omit=dev` and `npm ci --omit=dev`, and it pulls `esbuild 0.28.1` and `fsevents 2.3.3` with it. Both carry install scripts, which is why auth's production set shows three `hasInstallScript` entries where the estate has only one package that actually requires compilation.

**This is not a security finding on its own** — the runtime `npm ci --ignore-scripts` means none of those install scripts ever runs, and that is why #849 passed. It is image weight and attack surface: a build toolchain shipped into a running container that no runtime code imports.

### The fix

Move `vite` to `devDependencies` in `services/auth/package.json`, regenerate the lock, and re-measure the runtime `node_modules` file count (the tester counted **5,591 files** in auth's runtime tree). Expect esbuild, rollup and fsevents to leave with it.

**Verify before assuming:** confirm nothing in auth's build path (not just `src/`) needs `vite` at runtime — a config file or a script entry could. The import walk above covers `src/` only.

*Filed by s140 (seat A), 2026-09-06, from #849's gate findings.*

title: A clean stack has no supported way to obtain its first privileged account
description:
## The gap

On a freshly built stack there is no supported path to a first privileged account:

* `POST /api/admin/seed-demo-users` is now default-deny (B-3 hardening) and needs **both** `ALLOW_DEFAULT_SEED_PASSWORDS=true` and `ENABLE_DEMO_SEED=true`.
* Registration cannot mint a privileged role — KS-82 deliberately refuses a client-supplied role.

Both of those are **correct** and neither is questioned here. The gap is that nothing owns the bootstrap step, because historically the seed accounts were simply always present, so no one had to.

## Status of the original claim — corrected

An earlier KS-487 comment (2026-09-01 11:36Z) asserted a hard **deadlock**: that a clean stack could never call `seed-demo-users` at all. **That was retracted 21 minutes later by its own author** (11:57Z) — `services/auth/src/routes/auth.ts:47` fires `userRepo.seedDemoUsers()`, so there is no deadlock. This ticket carries the *remaining* gap only: not "impossible", but "undocumented and unowned".

## What would close it

One of: a documented first-run procedure naming the two env vars and their intended lifetime; or a one-shot bootstrap command that creates a single named admin without the demo-persona list; or an explicit decision that operators set the env vars, written where an operator will find it (`DEV-PROCESS.md` or the deployment runbook).

## Provenance

Recorded on [KS-487](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-487) as prose (2026-09-01, with its correction) rather than a ticket, because the Linear workspace was at its free issue cap. The cap was lifted 2026-09-06, so it is filed now. **This is the finding whose existence-only-in-prose was the reason the table was built.**

*Filed by s140 (seat A), 2026-09-06, from the KS-487 stream-B table.*

title: Audit the eleven cwd- and script-relative repo-root derivations under scripts/ and systemTest/ — one family, several blind in different ways
description: ## BLUF**The** `$(cd ../.. && pwd)` **/** `$(dirname "$0")/../..` **family appears eleven times across** `scripts/` **and** `systemTest/`**, in at least three variants with different failure modes.** KS-859 fixed one of them (`no-tracked-credentials.sh`); the rest are unaudited.## ScopeEnumerate every repo-root derivation under `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/` and `systemTest/`, classify each as script-relative, cwd-relative, or git-derived, and record for each whether it is:- **layout-dependent** (breaks where the repo root is not two levels up — the KS-859 defect), and/or- **cwd-dependent** (breaks when invoked from elsewhere — worse), and/or- **env-dependent** (breaks under an inherited git environment).Known starting points, measured at `34347a8fa`: `action-pins-labelled.sh:46` and `bare-path-scripts-executable.sh:57` are cwd-relative. `run-shell-suites.sh:45` **is NOT blind** — its KS-731 zero-suites guard fails loudly, and is the model for what a safe one looks like.## Why one ticket rather than elevenThis is a survey, not a defect: the deliverable is the classification plus a ticket per genuinely-blind site. Filing eleven speculative tickets before measuring would be the aggregation shape Kam withdrew.## Fix shapeThe audit first. Then, per blind site, the KS-859 idiom — ask git from a self-derived directory with the environment scrubbed — and a shared helper if the count justifies one.Charter named by the #858 gate as its round-2 work. Parent: KS-859, merged at `34347a8fafb5feca69d59dcee12b8aca9ce4a69d`.

title: no-tracked-credentials.sh cites two scripts as "structurally immune" exemplars — both use a WORSE cwd-relative root derivation
description: ## BLUF**The comment added by #858 points the next reader at two scripts as exemplars of the safe idiom. Both use a strictly worse one.**`no-tracked-credentials.sh:81-82` says:> `bare-path-scripts-executable.sh` and `action-pins-labelled.sh` already derive their root this way and are structurally immune; this is the same idiom.Measured at the merged tip `34347a8fa`:`action-pins-labelled.sh:46          REPO_ROOT="$(cd ../.. && pwd)"bare-path-scripts-executable.sh:57  REPO_ROOT="$(cd ../.. && pwd)"`That is **cwd-relative**, not script-relative. It depends on the caller's working directory, where the idiom the comment describes (`$(dirname "$0")/../..`) does not. They are not immune, and they are not the same idiom.## Why it mattersThe comment is load-bearing prose: it exists to tell the next person what shape to copy. Pointing at a worse form is how the family spreads.## Fix shapeCorrect the comment to describe the idiom without endorsing those two, and either fix their derivations or reference the audit ticket that covers them.Residue of the #858 tier-2 gate (F-QA-01, Minor). Parent: KS-859, merged at `34347a8fafb5feca69d59dcee12b8aca9ce4a69d`.
