**BLUF:** The premise of this ticket does not hold as written at develop `79145a312f01`: the two scripts it names do not derive their root from the caller's working directory. A held comment-only pass built from this ticket's description was therefore not raised.

Measured at develop `79145a312f01` with `git show`:
- `bare-path-scripts-executable.sh` line 56: `cd "$(dirname "$0")/../.."`, then line 57: `REPO_ROOT="$(cd ../.. && pwd)"`.
- `action-pins-labelled.sh` line 55: `cd "$(dirname "$0")/../.."`, then line 56: `REPO_ROOT="$(cd ../.. && pwd)"`.
- `no-tracked-credentials.sh` line 83: `DEV_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/../.." && pwd)"`, which already derives its root in one step from `$0`.

The line numbers in the description (46 and 57) are from an older tip. What is true is narrower: in each of the two scripts the `../..` is resolved after a `cd` to a directory derived from `$0`, so as written the root does not depend on the caller's directory; that `cd` is not checked, so if it failed the root would follow the caller's directory. Whether this ticket becomes "check the cd" or closes is not decided here. No state, assignee or priority was changed.

title: Every ADMITTED erasure authenticates twice — the door's chain and the catch-all both run authenticateToken, doubling a remote key validation on a partner path
description:
## BLUF

On the erasure path an **admitted** request authenticates **twice**; a refused one authenticates once. Measured fresh by the round-3 gate across 14 shapes × 2 modes: **refused = 1, admitted = 2**.

Carried out of KS-861 when #845 merged, per the ruling that F-11 is a follow-up and not a gate item. **Not a live defect — a cost defect on a partner-facing path.**

## Mechanism

`services/api-gateway/src/routes/proxy.ts`:

* `:677` — the erasure door's chain carries `authenticateToken(true)`
* `:696` — the catch-all `router.use('/api/gdpr', authenticateToken(true), proxy('originate', …))` carries it again

An admitted request passes through the door, `next()`s, and hits the catch-all's copy. A refused one is stopped by the responding handler, so the second never runs — the correct direction, and why this is a cost issue rather than a correctness one.

## Why it matters

In production `authenticateToken` validates an `sk_` key **over HTTP** to the security service — `services/api-gateway/src/middleware/auth.ts:257` → `validateApiKey:209` → `POST /api/keys/validate`. So every admitted erasure doubles a remote call on a partner-facing path. It surfaces as latency, not as an error, which is why nothing has flagged it.

## Fix shape (from the round-2 tester)

Either the door's chain omits `authenticateToken` and relies on the catch-all's, or `authenticateToken` short-circuits when `req.user` is already set. **The second touches shared auth middleware and therefore every route** — it wants its own measurement rather than being folded in as an obvious win.

## Note on the round-3 fix

The F-9 fix (an inner express `Router`) was checked against this and **does not** close it for free — that was the stated condition for folding it into round 3, and it was not met.

## Acceptance

An admitted erasure invokes `authenticateToken` **once**, driven by counting invocations of an injected factory (the harness in `ks843-erasure-path-bypass.test.ts` already injects one); a refused erasure still invokes it once; guardrail behaviour and the 403/200 outcomes across the 14 shapes are unchanged.

title: Dead-estate pointers in RUNTIME SOURCE outside deployment/azure — system-status.ts hard-codes secuura-staging-* hosts, westeurope and a dead URL suffix
description:
## BLUF

KS-490 (3) / PR #852 closed every dead-estate pointer under `deployment/azure` — **6 of 6, and that claim is correct for that directory.** The class does not stop there: it extends into `services/`, where the pointers sit in **runtime source**, not in a template nobody consumes.

Found by the KS-490 (3) tier-2 gate. **Pre-existing at the merge base — not a defect in #852.**

title: KS-386 residues from the round-2 gate: G-1 column ordinal drift, G-2 the second-image orphan, G-3 the in-memory docstring is wrong at the wire, G-4 two write spellings the guard cannot see
description:
## BLUF

Four Minors from the KS-386 round-2 tier-1 re-gate, none blocking. All four shipped as-is under the two-round cap — the gate PASSED and #839 merged as `b6ae609e6`. **This description is taken from the gate report's own findings section**, `projects/secuura/reports/2026-09-06-s138-ks386-839-regate-3b5a09403/report.md` §3, with its evidence file names; every fix-shape below is the report's, and the report marks all four *advisory only — no change was made by the tester*.

---

## G-1 · MINOR · A fresh-init schema and a migrated schema still differ: `user_id` and `created_at` are in **opposite ordinal positions**

**Oracle:** product, internal consistency. The claim under test was the builder's own — "the two shipped schemas now match the migrated one."
**Evidence class: MEASURED.** `pg_attribute` projection of both schemas, `evidence/cols-qa_i.txt` vs `evidence/cols-qa_mig.txt`, diff in `evidence/schema-diff-freshinit-vs-migrated.txt`:

```
  fresh-init (i)          migrated (mig)
  4|user_id|text|f||      4|created_at|timestamp with time zone|f|now()|
  5|created_at|…|now()|   5|user_id|text|f||
```

Sorted by name the two are **identical** — names, types, nullability, defaults, comment, both indexes. The difference is ordinal position only.
**Cause (read, not speculated):** `init.sql` and `docker/init/04` declare `user_id` *between* `mime_type` and `created_at`; migration 035 `ADD COLUMN`s it, so on a migrated database it lands last. No DDL reconciles the two short of a table rewrite.
**Blast radius:** nothing in the service is positional — the only INSERT names its columns and every read is by name. It bites anything comparing schemas structurally (a `pg_dump` diff, a drift detector, a snapshot test) or any future `INSERT … VALUES` with no column list, **which would write a** `user_id` **into** `created_at` **on one of the two shapes.**
**Falsifying tamper:** reorder `user_id` and `created_at` in `init.sql` to match 035's result and the ordered diff goes empty.
**Fix-shape:** accept and document the ordinal difference in the comment block that already explains the coupling, or move the `user_id` declaration in both shipped files to sit after `created_at`.

## G-2 · MINOR · A partial write leaves an orphan attestation, and the 500 says "No document was accepted" **when one was**

**Oracle:** explainability — "the most serious defect class is claiming something true that isn't."
**Evidence class: MEASURED**, driven on the tester's own copy of schema (i) with a trigger failing the **second** image only (`RAISE EXCEPTION` on `mime_type = 'image/jpeg'`, the back image).
**Repro:** schema (i) → install a constraint/trigger rejecting only the second INSERT → boot kyc at `3b5a09403` → initiate (bearer) 201 → `/document` with front PNG + back JPEG → `/selfie`.
**Observed:**

* `/document` → **500** `KYC_ATTESTATION_WRITE_FAILED` **— "No document was accepted."**
* `svc_kyc_images` holds **the front row anyway** (`data` NULL, `user_id` set) — *the message is false about the state it describes*. `dbSaveImage` is called once per image and each `query()` is its own autocommit statement; there is no transaction around the pair.
* `/selfie` then answers **200** `success:true` and writes **a second row**.
* `svc_kyc_verifications` for that subject: `documents` **IS NULL**, `liveness_completed` **true**. The record claims a completed liveness check for a subject whose document step failed, and two attestation rows exist that nothing references.

**Privacy or correctness?** **Correctness and honesty, not privacy.** The orphan rows carry `user_id`, so the KS-291 erasure path (`DELETE … WHERE user_id = $1`) still reaches them; nothing becomes undeletable and no payload is held. What is exposed is a compliance record asserting more than happened, and a client sentence that contradicts the database.
**Not introduced by #839** — the pair was untransacted before it too, and the builder named it without widening. What **is** new is the sentence "No document was accepted", now a specific claim the state can contradict.
**Fix-shape:** wrap the front/back pair in the existing `transaction()` helper — the orphan disappears and the sentence becomes true. **Regression test the owner should add:** drive `/document` against a DB that rejects the *second* insert, assert `count(*) = 0`, and assert `/selfie` does not then succeed.

## G-3 · MINOR · `dbSaveImage`'s "ONE HONEST LIMIT" docstring is wrong about the path this gate is about

**Oracle:** product — the code contradicts its own comment. **MEASURED** (two boots, driven) **and READ** (`index.ts:290-293`, `db.ts:125-147`).
The docstring, added by this diff, says *"when* `isDbAvailable()` *is false this returns early and writes nothing, and the route still answers 200."* Driven both ways into that state, the route answers **404** `NOT_FOUND` **"Verification not found"**, not 200 — `dbGetVerification` returns `undefined` before `dbSaveImage` is ever called, because nothing keeps verifications in memory.
**Why it matters even though reality is better than described:** this docstring is the written scope of F-1(b)'s exemption. A future reader will believe there is a live 200-with-no-row hole here and either chase it or, worse, treat a genuine one as already known.
**Also worth the owner's eye, pre-existing, not #839:** in that state `POST /api/kyc/initiate` still returns **201 with a** `verificationId` that is never persisted anywhere and 404s on the very next call.
**Falsifying tamper:** the finding *is* the tamper — boot with no `DATABASE_URL` and drive; a 200 from `/document` would refute it. **Fix-shape:** restate the limit as "the route 404s because the verification itself was never persisted", or delete the paragraph.
**Owned:** that sentence is mine, written in round 2 while trying to be explicit about a limit.

## G-4 · MINOR (carried from pass-1's H-b hunts, now louder) · The retitled cell claims "exactly ONE write path IN THIS FILE" while two spellings *in that file* are invisible

**Oracle:** explainability — a guard's title is a claim, and this one over-reaches.
**Evidence class: MEASURED.** Both planted in `index.ts` as **real payload writes**:

* `INSERT INTO "svc_kyc_images" (id, data, mime_type) VALUES ($1,$2,$3)` → **0 failed / 26**
* `INSERT INTO public.svc_kyc_images (id, data, mime_type) VALUES ($1,$2,$3)` → **0 failed / 26**

Both reader functions return `[]` on both. An `UPDATE` split across lines **is** caught (1 failed / 25), so the blindness is specifically about how the table **name** is spelled, not about whitespace.
F-2 as filed — the corpus overclaim — **is** closed. This is the residue: the docstring's "OTHER LIMIT" paragraph names the behavioural limit and the string-literal limit but says nothing about name spellings, and the retitle to "IN THIS FILE" makes the in-file claim stronger than the regex supports.
**Likelihood in operation: low** — nobody in this codebase quotes or schema-qualifies that identifier today, verified by `git grep -a`.
**Fix-shape:** match `(INSERT\s+INTO|UPDATE)\s+(?:"?public"?\.)?"?svc_kyc_images"?`, or name the spellings in the docstring's limits paragraph as the corpus limit is now named.

---

## Scope

One ticket, four items, product. G-3 is docs-only and can land with any of the others. G-1 and G-4 are decisions as much as fixes; G-2 is the only one with real design weight.

## Provenance

KS-386 round-2 tier-1 re-gate, verdict 2026-09-06T00:43:59Z, PASS, scored 1.0. #839 merged `b6ae609e6847b399ef695c9cd69fe1ef671693df`. Text from the report's §3 findings, read at `/Volumes/DevMASTER/!CODING/Testing Agent MAIN/projects/secuura/reports/2026-09-06-s138-ks386-839-regate-3b5a09403/report.md`.

Left open: the 2026-09-25 comment on this ticket keeps it In Progress because PR 1204 covered G-4, one of the four Minors. The first version was transcribed from the ruling mail because I had the report path without its `!CODING` segment and concluded it was unreachable. It is reachable, and the primary text is sharper in three places the transcription lost:

- **G-1 is a SWAP, not a shift.** Fresh-init has `user_id` at 4 and `created_at` at 5; migrated has them the other way round. And the consequence is named concretely: a column-less `INSERT … VALUES` would write a `user_id` **into `created_at`** on one of the two shapes.
- **G-2's sharpest point was missing.** It is not only that an orphan row survives — it is that the 500's sentence *"No document was accepted"* is **false about the state it describes**, because a document row was written. That is the finding, and my version buried it.
- **G-3 carries a pre-existing extra** I had not recorded: in that same state `POST /api/kyc/initiate` returns **201 with a `verificationId`** that is never persisted and 404s on the very next call.

G-4 also gains the exact regex the report proposes, and the fact that a multi-line `UPDATE` **is** caught — so the blindness is specifically about the table name's spelling, not whitespace.

Each finding is marked *advisory only* in the report: the tester made no change.

title: `@secuura/shared` `main` points at an untracked, never-built `dist/index.js` — anything outside vitest's alias resolves to nothing
description:
**Category 1. Low. AUTHORISED, UNFILED — Linear's free-tier cap is refusing creation.**

## BLUF

`packages/shared/package.json` `main` points at `dist/index.js`. `dist/` **is gitignored, untracked, and no install step builds it.** In a tree that has never run a build, `require.resolve('@secuura/shared')` **throws** `MODULE_NOT_FOUND`.

Measured 2026-09-06 during the KS-830 cell, in a fresh clone at `904ca6ef2` after a clean `npm ci` (1937 packages, exit 0):

|  | working checkout | fresh clone |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `require.resolve('@secuura/shared')` | `packages/shared/dist/index.js` | **THROWS** `MODULE_NOT_FOUND` |
| entry sha256 | `52ff4828de770b62669e828139c1d03b72834fb82c38f85ab1538fdddd38bce9` | n/a |
| `dist/` present after `npm ci` | YES (built earlier by hand) | **NO** |
| `npm ls @secuura/shared` | `@secuura/shared@0.3.0 -> ./packages/shared` | **identical** |

The workspace symlink is the same in both. The only variable is whether somebody has run a build in that tree.

## Why it is currently invisible

`packages/shared/vitest.config.ts` aliases `@secuura/shared` to `src/index.ts`, and that alias covers the whole of the shared test suite's import graph — so **the suites are green in both trees** and nothing surfaces the gap. The alias's own comment explains it was added for class identity (KS-727), not for resolvability; the resolvability fix is a side effect nobody declared.

## Why it is worth a ticket anyway

Anything in that package that runs **outside** vitest's alias — a script, a tool, a `node -e`, a consumer resolving the workspace package by name without a prior build — resolves to nothing on a fresh checkout. A new developer or a CI job that does not build first gets `MODULE_NOT_FOUND` from a package that `npm ls` reports as correctly linked, which is a confusing failure to diagnose.

**Priority Low, deliberately:** nothing is broken today, no suite depends on it, and the alias hides it everywhere it currently matters. This is a trap, not a defect.

## Fix shapes (not chosen — whoever picks this up should)

* Add a `prepare` script so the workspace builds on install; or
* point `main` at `src/index.ts` and let consumers transpile; or
* declare `exports` with a source condition.

Each has consequences for the Docker builds, which is why this is filed rather than fixed in passing.

## Provenance

Found while running the KS-830 `npm ci` cell on Wednesday's ruling of 2026-09-05T23:09:26Z; carried out of KS-830 as its own item on her 23:15:00Z ruling, both SPF + DKIM `header.i=@agentmail.to` + DMARC pass. KS-830 comment `565ea3cc-bc90-47c9-aa72-319bbc397605` holds the full measurement. **It is NOT the cause of KS-830's red** — that was measured and excluded.

---

*Filed by s138 (seat A) 2026-09-06. Text authored by s137 and preserved at* `5_Project_History/unfiled-tickets-s137/unfiled-dist-resolution-trap.md`*; creation was refused by Linear's cap on 2026-09-05T23:33:40Z and retried after Kam upgraded the plan (panel, 09:45).*

Priority raised **Low → Medium** on the measurement in the comment above (Wednesday, 2026-10-19 08:08Z, under her v1.3 board authority): the "no suite depends on it" basis for Low no longer holds. Kept as the single ticket for this root cause — no duplicate filed — with the `prepare`-script fix shape in the description as the preferred one. Not queued to a lane now: `packages/shared` is outside every live lane, so it goes to the Spark/backlog pool.

— Seat R 54th, Platform K

## 🔴 This ticket's central assessment is now false: a suite DOES depend on it, and it fails 76 of 117 files

Measured today, 2026-10-19, in a fresh clone at develop `722e07f19cee683ea037930e601e380a9491f7b5` after a clean `npm ci` (1937 packages) — I am a reboot successor seat and a fresh clone was mandatory, which is how I hit this.

This ticket says, as its stated reason for **priority Low**:

> **Priority Low, deliberately:** nothing is broken today, no suite depends on it, and the alias hides it everywhere it currently matters. This is a trap, not a defect.

**Three of those four clauses do not hold.** `services/api-gateway`'s whole vitest suite depends on it and is unrunnable until `packages/shared` is built:

| `packages/shared/dist` | api-gateway suite |
| -- | -- |
| absent (fresh clone, straight after `npm ci`) | **76 of 117 files FAILED**, 28 failed / 371 passed / 175 skipped — **574 tests of 1137 even reached** |
| built (`npm run build --workspace=packages/shared`, rc 0, 29 dist files) | **117 passed (117) · 1137 passed (1137)**, rc 0 |

Error signatures from the unbuilt run, as emitted:

- `Error: Failed to resolve entry for package "@secuura/shared". The package may have incorrect main/module/exports specified in its package.json` — 13 occurrences
- `Error: Cannot find package '@secuura/shared/documents/default-type'` — 7
- `Error: Cannot find package '@secuura/shared/security/scopes'`
- and one suite's own guard says it outright: `Error: api-gateway: the @secuura/shared build is stale or incomplete`

## Why "the alias hides it" is only true inside this package

The description is right that `packages/shared/vitest.config.ts` aliases `@secuura/shared` to `src/index.ts` — but that config governs **the shared package's own** suite. `services/api-gateway` has its own vitest config and no such alias, so it resolves the workspace package **by `main`**, which is the untracked `dist/index.js` this ticket is about. The alias therefore hides the gap exactly where it does not matter and not at all where it does.

## The second half of the mechanism, not yet in this ticket

`npm ci` **does not** build it, and the reason is specific: the root `package.json` carries

```
"postinstall": "node scripts/fix-libsodium-symlink.js && npm run build --workspaces --if-present"
```

which **would** build `packages/shared` — but installs here run with ignore-scripts, so `postinstall` never fires. So the trap is not "nobody thought to build it"; it is that the step which was meant to build it is suppressed.

## Why this is a reporting hazard, not just an inconvenience

The failure does not look like a missing build. It looks like **a catastrophic regression**: 76 red files. A seat that measures the suite before building — which is the natural order, since `npm ci` reports success — will either report a false catastrophic red, or, worse, take **574** as the suite denominator and then report "1137 passed" later as a 563-test improvement. Both readings are wrong and neither is obviously wrong from the output.

## Recommendation

Raise the priority off Low, and prefer the `prepare`-script fix shape already listed in the description — it is the one that survives ignore-scripts for consumers who run `npm ci` and then a suite. I am not changing the priority myself; flagging it for triage.

Related: **KS-1646** (a fresh clone has no pre-push gate) is the same fresh-clone class but a different mechanism — that one is `core.hooksPath`, this one is the unbuilt `dist`. A successor hitting both in one boot, as I did, needs both fixes.

**Searched before posting here rather than filing a duplicate:** `@secuura/shared` (11 hits), `postinstall` (5), `fresh clone` (9), `ignore-scripts` (13), `build --workspace` (1), `shared build` (2), `dist/index.js` (5) — title+description, case-insensitive, all states — with a positive control (`preflight`, 15 hits) and a negative control (`zzqqxnonsense`, 0 hits) to prove the filter discriminates in both directions. This ticket is the match.

— Seat R 54th, Platform K

title: KS-695 F5: build the dedicated `subjects:erase` scope gate on POST /api/gdpr/erasures — Kam ruled it 2026-09-03 and it has never been built

## Why it was not built when it was found

The session that found it (Peter's #790 F5) recommended a dedicated scope and **deliberately did not implement it**, on the grounds that widening or narrowing an authorisation check is not an agent's call. Kam's ruling is that call. It has been outstanding since 2026-09-03.

nodes.body:
**BLUF:** Kam ruled this question on 2026-11-05 16:10:04 AEDT (card `secuura-ks843-erasure-flip-trigger-1105`): option **a**, "Keep logged grace; flip after 30 days of zero un-scoped Platform S erasure calls".

Question as asked: "KS-843: what evidence flips SUBJECTS_ERASE_SCOPE_ENFORCED, given you ruled no re-mint?"

The build is queued to a lane seat. This ticket stays In Progress.
No re-mint (KS-889 ruled b): the flip waits for other evidence; logged grace continues.

## BLUF
@stuart.jamieson we want to tighten the erasure endpoint this week, and for that we need two answers from you: **a window this week when Platform S can switch to new keys, and roughly how long that switch takes on your side.** Nothing changes for Platform S until we have agreed the window with you.

## What we need from you
1. A window this week (day and time, with your timezone) when you can switch Platform S to the new keys.
2. Your best estimate of how long the switch takes, from the moment you receive a new key to the moment Platform S is using it everywhere. A rough figure is fine ("about 30 minutes", "about a day"). We will keep the old keys working for longer than your estimate, so Platform S is never cut off part-way.

## Why
Today the erasure endpoint (the request and the status read) accepts any Platform S key. We have built the stricter rule, that only a key carrying an explicit erasure permission is accepted, and it is running in a "log it, but allow it" mode. To turn the stricter rule on, Platform S's keys have to be replaced by new ones that carry that permission. We have decided to start now.

## What happens if we do nothing
Nothing breaks for Platform S. But the endpoint keeps accepting any Platform S key, the stricter rule stays off, and this ticket stays open past 31 October.

## How it would go, so you can plan
1. You tell us the window and the switch time.
2. We create the new keys and keep the old ones working for longer than your estimate. We agree with you how the new keys reach you. After that overlap the old keys stop working, so the switch has to happen inside it.
3. You switch Platform S over, inside the window.
4. We watch our logs until they show Platform S calling with the new keys, then turn the stricter rule on and tell you.

We will not replace any key or switch anything on before you have confirmed the window.

Posted by the Platform K agent on Kam's behalf.

## BLUF
**Built and merged; the enforcing half waits on a Kam step. Leaves the lot as a card for Kam.** I touched nothing about the Platform S keys or the flag.

## Recommendation
Kam's call, as already ruled on 2026-09-06 (option A, logged grace): pick the cutover window with Stuart, rotate Platform S's connector keys with `API_KEY_ROTATION_GRACE_SECONDS` set for that window (the 09-08 note on this ticket explains why, to avoid a 401 on every S call), then flip `SUBJECTS_ERASE_SCOPE_ENFORCED` once the log shows S on the new key. Until then the ticket's item 3 (refuse callers without the scope) holds only in grace mode.

## Detail
- **Built, on develop:** the scope and its mint (PR #841), the gate on both erasure routes with the F-7 and F-9 rounds (merge `ba28db317`), and the canonical-path fix (#1019, squash `581c9db0d`). The `ks843-erasure-scope-gate` and `ks843-erasure-path-bypass` cells run in the 876-test green suite.
- **Live on Kintsugi:** `SUBJECTS_ERASE_SCOPE_ENFORCED` is unset (grace) and the gateway log holds 0 `[KS-843]` lines since the 10-07 deploy, so Platform S has not used the door there. A human OWNER token is refused `403 INSUFFICIENT_SCOPE` at the door.
- **Why not Done:** deployed code that does not yet enforce is not the end state the ruling describes.

Verified 2026-10-12 by Seat K 4th (lane K, verify-and-close lot L02) in a clean clone of develop `65d7722f83a6`. Kintsugi (`secuura02-kintsugi-vm`) runs revision `69f2045af2a4f5f0b83b2f76c62514512abdc7b5`, deployed 2026-10-07; the gateway container was created 2026-10-07T04:48:05Z and has 0 restarts. Kintsugi runs `NODE_ENV=development`. Gateway suite on develop: 97 files / 876 tests, 0 failed. Evidence: project history folder `5_Project_History/2026-10-12_seatK-4th/` (`box/`, `redproof/`, `live/`, `tickets/`).

## Your cutover ruling still holds — but with #880 merged it needs one parameter it used to get for free

**BLUF: Kam's 2026-09-06 ruling (option A, logged grace) is PRESERVED, not changed.** Nothing here re-opens it. What changes is that one step of it — rotating Platform S's connector keys — stops being safe *by default* the moment [KS-577](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-577) / [#880](https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/880) merges, and needs an explicit setting instead.

Raised here because the dependency was findable from this ticket but not from #880, which is how it nearly reached a merge unexamined.

### What the ruling says, verbatim

> **Kam ruled 2026-09-06 13:59 (card `secuura-ks843-cutover-stuart`, option A): logged grace.** … **Platform S's connector keys are rotated, and the switch flips to scope-only once the log shows S on the new key.** Not before.

Option A was chosen for a stated reason: *"Never breaks S; no synchronised window with Stuart needed."*

### Why #880 removes that property, measured from the code

`revokePriorConnectorKeys` (`services/security/src/index.ts`) reads `API_KEY_ROTATION_GRACE_SECONDS`, **defaulting to `'0'`**:

* `grace = 0` → `UPDATE svc_api_keys SET is_active = false WHERE connector_id = $1 AND tenant_id = $2::uuid AND id <> $3 AND is_active = true` — **immediate**.
* `grace > 0` → `expires_at = LEAST(COALESCE(expires_at,'infinity'), NOW() + grace)` — a bounded overlap.

It runs only `if (data.rotate && data.connectorId)`, and the gateway passes `connectorId: platform-s:${externalRef}` — so it lands **exactly on S's prior keys for that externalRef**, in that tenant, and nothing else.

**Two consequences worth stating precisely:**

1. **It is a 401, not a 403.** Revocation kills the key at *authentication*, above `requireScopeOrRole` — so it breaks **every endpoint S calls**, not only the erasure path this cutover concerns.
2. **The ruling's trigger condition stops being observable.** Option A flips to scope-only *"once the log shows S on the new key"*. At `grace = 0` there is no interval in which S is transitioning — the old key works, then it 401s. The `[KS-843]` log evidence the flip depends on cannot accrue.

**This ticket already predicted it.** From its own Related section: *"KS-577 — … for this cutover it happens to provide the overlap window that makes a zero-downtime swap possible. Named so nobody mistakes the convenience for a reason to leave it open."* That paragraph was right. What was missing was anything connecting it to #880's merge decision.

### The remedy — no code change, and Kam's default stays as he ruled

Either of these preserves option A exactly:

* **Set `API_KEY_ROTATION_GRACE_SECONDS`** to the agreed cutover window on the security service for the rotation, then unset it. #880 already implements this path.
* **Or mint with `rotate: false`** for the cutover — purely additive, i.e. today's behaviour — and perform the real `rotate: true` retirement once the log shows S migrated.

**#880's default of `0` is not being challenged**: it is what Kam ruled on 2026-08-07 and the docblock says so. The cutover sets the parameter for its own window; the default stands.

### Not done here

Not raised with Stuart — the cutover conversation is Kam's to open. #880 untouched. This is a record of a precondition, not a proposal to change either ruling.

*Reciprocal note on KS-577 / #880 so the dependency is findable from both ends.*

## Measured on the demo box — a backfill is NOT possible; re-mint is the only path

**BLUF: NO.** Nothing on the `svc_api_keys` row determines the connector for the pre-existing keys. A backfill would recover **5 of 32 active keys (16%)**, leave 26 with no evidence at all, and one is ambiguous. That is not a backfill, it is a partial guess — so the only sound path is a **re-mint of Platform S's keys**.

### The window, measured (read-only, on the demo VM)

| Reading | Value |
|---|---|
| `svc_api_keys` rows | **39** before the probe (the brief said 43 — the measured number is 39) |
| rows with `connector_id` | **0** |
| still active with a null connector | **32** |

### Can anything imply the connector?

The only other connector reference on K is `action_provenance.connector_id` — 4680 rows, all populated, **6 distinct connectors**, carrying `organization_id`. That is the only candidate join. Against the null-connector keys:

| Connectors implied by the key's org | Keys | Active keys |
|---|---|---|
| **0 — no evidence at all** | 33 | **26** |
| 1 — unambiguous | 5 | 5 |
| 2 — ambiguous | 1 | 1 |

`action_provenance` covers **6 organisations**; the null-connector keys span **21 distinct organisations, and 18 of them carry no `organization_id` at all**. So for the large majority there is simply nothing on K to join to.

**Control:** the same join returns non-zero for organisations known to have provenance (e.g. `bb9d5300…` → 1, `aeb2e3b1…` → 2), so a 0 means "no evidence", not "the query cannot match". The first run of this query failed on a `uuid = text` mismatch and was re-run with an explicit cast — the numbers above are from the corrected query.

### What follows

The KS-843 cutover flip's prerequisite cannot be met by a migration. **The re-mint is Stuart's window and Kam's call** — this comment records the measurement; it is not a request to anyone, and no message has gone to Platform S from here.

*s140 (seat A), 2026-09-06, on the demo box after the leg-2 rebuild (`security` current, `connector_id` live).*

## ⚠ Correction — KS-869 merging is NOT sufficient for the cutover flip

My earlier comment here (`6b975c92…`) said the flip's prerequisite is **KS-869 merged**. **That is not enough, and I am correcting it before anyone acts on it.**

KS-869 merged today (`50913d2c3`). But its `COALESCE` backfill has an **empty window** for keys that already exist: `memApiKeys` warms only from the database at boot, so every pre-fix row re-warms with `connectorId` undefined, every later save passes NULL, and COALESCE correctly declines it. **Backfill happens only for keys minted after KS-869 deploys.**

**So the `[KS-843]` grace log will still record `connectorId: null` for every EXISTING Platform S key.** Kam's 13:59 ruling flips the switch *"once the log shows S on the new key"* — and the log still cannot say which connector it is looking at.

**The real prerequisite is KS-889**, which carries the measurement that decides it: does anything on the row (`key_prefix`, `organization_id`, `name`) determine the connector? If yes, a one-off backfill. If no, **Platform S's keys must be re-minted** — Stuart's window, therefore Kam's call, and it belongs with the KS-577 rotation conversation rather than as a separate ask.

**Also note:** `security` was not in today's demo rebuild set (its `src` did not change), so the box still runs Sept-3 security code. KS-869's behaviour is on `develop`, not yet on the demo.

The erasure door itself **is** live on the demo as of `14914258c`, in **grace** mode — the ruled shape. Nothing has changed for Platform S.

## The demo hold is LIFTED — Kam, 2026-09-06 15:12 AEST

His words, verbatim: *"the items tested not deployed. lets deploy and archive these"* (15:06), and asked directly whether that lifts the demo stop — *"yes. lift until we get through these tickets and the backlog."* (15:12)

**Scope in his own framing: a window, until the Tested-Not-Deployed set and the backlog are worked through.** The demo box only; production is untouched (there is none in scope).

**This ticket's deploy is therefore unblocked**, subject to the plan below.

## ⚠ The recorded hold ticket cannot carry this note

The hold has been referred to all day as **KS-641**. That ticket was **archived 2026-09-05T06:45:19Z** and Linear refuses comments on it (`commentCreate` → *"Entity not found: Issue"*, while the same id reads fine — the archived-issue signature). So the lift is recorded here and on the sibling ticket instead of there. The hold was always Kam's word carried in the briefs; KS-641 was only ever its label.

## ⚠ And the deploy path in the commission is the wrong one

The commission named `deployment/azure/deploy.sh` and `.github/workflows/deploy-demo.yml`. **Neither is the live demo.** Both target the Container Apps estate **deleted 2026-07-31** — `deploy-demo.yml`'s own guard input reads *"this path deploys the DELETED Container Apps estate, NOT the live VM demo."*

The live demo is a **single VM** (`secuura02-demo-vm`, `20.212.118.59`), stack at `/home/secuura/secuura/Dev`, redeployed by rsync + `docker compose build` + `up -d`. Verified reachable read-only just now: aarch64, 32 containers up, **disk 80% full (13 GiB free)**, **1.7 GiB RAM available**. Those two numbers are the real constraint on an on-box ARM64 rebuild, not the deploy command.

Nothing is built or shipped until that plan is confirmed.

**For this ticket specifically:** the erasure door deploys in **grace mode**, which is exactly the shape Kam's 13:59 logged-grace ruling calls for — nothing changes for Platform S. The **flip** to scope-only remains blocked on **KS-869** (PR #854), because until `connector_id` is persisted the grace log records `connectorId: null` after a restart and cannot say which connector was admitted.

## BLUF — the cutover flip now has a prerequisite: KS-869

**The `[KS-843]` grace log's `connectorId` is NULL for every Platform S key after a security-service restart.** `svc_api_keys.connector_id` exists as a column and is **never written and never read** (KS-869) — the association lives in the in-process map only.

**Until KS-869 ships, the log cannot say WHICH connector was admitted.** So Kam's 2026-09-06 13:59 ruling — *flip to scope-only once the log shows S on the new key* — has a prerequisite: **KS-869 merged, and the log observed after a restart.**

**Kam's ruling stands unchanged.** Logged grace is still the shape; what gains a prerequisite is the *mechanism that produces the evidence for the flip*, not the decision.

**Nothing changes for Platform S. Nothing deploys (KS-641).**

## The chain, traced end to end

```
security  /api/keys/validate :1182  →  connectorId: apiKey.connectorId || null
gateway   auth.ts:230               →  meta.connectorId = data.connectorId || ''
gateway   auth.ts:272               →  userId = `connector:${meta.connectorId || 'api-key'}`
gateway   auth.ts:281               →  req.user.connectorId = meta.connectorId
scopes.ts (the grace log)           →  connectorId: user.connectorId ?? null
```

After a restart every connector also collapses to `userId = connector:api-key`, so audit attribution loses the same distinction.

KS-869 is in build now, with a **driven** restart as its red-proof rather than the static read that found it.

## BLUF — MERGED. Three rounds, two holes, both closed.

**#845 merged as `ba28db317f982045567ecab13ae4956925bb3a2f`** (tree `8457a3a776e1f492600527b175d3e84c6cbd77c9`, first parent `af0782572` = the asserted tip, 7 files +821 −5). The **third tier-1 gate PASSED** (2026-09-06T04:43:36Z). **Nothing deployed — the demo hold stands (KS-641).**

## The door's behaviour, as the tester measured it

| principal / mode | result |
|---|---|
| unauthenticated | **401** |
| `connector` role, no scope, **enforcing** | **403**, upstream never called |
| `connector` role, no scope, **grace** (default) | **200**, 1 upstream hit, **1 `[KS-843]` warn** |
| holder of `subjects:erase`, either mode | **200**, 1 upstream hit |

Driven across **14 gated spellings × 5 principals — 530 rows** — plus a replica of originate's own mount.

## The three rounds

| round | verdict | report |
|---|---|---|
| pass 1 @ `87450b54c` | findings F-1…F-8 | `…-s138-ks843-845-half2-87450b54c/` |
| re-gate @ `59248bf38` | **NO GO** — F-9 regression, F-10 undisclosed coverage loss | `…-s138-ks843-845-half2-regate-59248bf38/` |
| round 3 @ `e1d9d9380` | **PASS** | `…-round3-e1d9d9380/` |

**F-9** — round 2 replaced express's matching with a case-sensitive regex, so six case spellings (`ERASURES`, `Erasures`, `Erasures/`, `//ERASURES`, `/API/GDPR/ERASURES`, `GET …/ERASURES/abc`) ran originate's erasure handler in enforcing mode for a principal with neither scope nor role. Round 3 gave the matching back to express (an inner `Router` mounted at `/erasures`, fed the separator-collapsed `req.url`): **all six now 403 / 0 hits**, and the erasure handler ran **0 times** at the replica where round 2 ran it on all six. **F-7 stayed closed** — six separator shapes and both exact paths. The 20-shape evasion table was re-derived and **nothing newly opened**.

**F-10** — the restored `S_CONNECTOR_SCOPES` mint-set cell **diffs EMPTY** against the parent's copy (26 lines).

## Residues — filed per defect, none of them blockers

- **KS-870** (P3) — F-11: every *admitted* erasure authenticates twice (refused 1 / admitted 2), doubling a remote key validation on a partner path.
- **KS-871** (P3) — F-12: the audit log reads `req.path` *after* the response, so a **refused** erasure is logged as `/`. Began at round 2, went one level further at round 3. **Whether it is latent or live is UNMEASURED** — the tester did not run the middleware and could not tell if `isDbAvailable()` is ever true on the demo.
- **KS-872** (P3) — O-3: `packages/shared` project `tsc` is red on develop (`crypto.JsonWebKey` gone in `@types/node` 26.1.0). **Not this commit** — the diff against `packages/shared` is empty.

## Residues recorded here rather than filed

- **O-1** — the six *separator* spellings' "logged exactly once" is asserted by no cell. The **case** grace cell asserts the log; the separator grace cell asserts 200 + 1 hit only. One line (a warn spy + count) closes it on the next touch of that file.
- **O-2** — the `req.url` restore has **source-pin coverage only**. The proxy collapses separators on the way out, so no upstream-facing assertion can see the difference. A declared limit, not an oversight.
- **O-4** — the comment strip in the F-7+F-9 source cell is **conservative**: it fails safe on a trailing comment. **Do not "fix" it into a fail-open strip.**

## ⚠ Read this alongside KS-869 before acting on the cutover

Kam's logged-grace ruling (comment `fc148e79…`) makes the flip conditional on *"the log shows S on the new key"*. **KS-869 — filed today — is that `connectorId` is never persisted**, so after a security-service restart the `[KS-843]` warn records `connectorId: null` and cannot say which connector was admitted. **The cutover evidence is weaker than this ticket previously described.** KS-869 should land before anyone reads that log as a basis for flipping `SUBJECTS_ERASE_SCOPE_ENFORCED`.

## BLUF — Kam ruled the cutover: LOGGED GRACE

**Kam ruled 2026-09-06 13:59 (card `secuura-ks843-cutover-stuart`, option A): logged grace.** The gate ships as **role-OR-scope with a refusal log and a scope-only switch** — which is already the shape built on this ticket. **Platform S's connector keys are rotated, and the switch flips to scope-only once the log shows S on the new key.** Not before.

**Nothing deploys under the demo hold (KS-641).** This ruling sets the *shape*, not a release.

## What that means in the code as it stands

`requireScopeOrRole(subjects:erase, ['connector'], SUBJECTS_ERASE_SCOPE_ENFORCED)`:

- **Switch unset (today's default):** a `connector`-role key without the scope is **admitted and logged** — one `[KS-843]` line per request carrying the connector id, org, tenant, method, the URL as the caller typed it, and the granted scopes. That log is the cutover evidence.
- **Switch `'true'`:** the same caller is **refused 403**. A holder of `subjects:erase` passes in both modes.
- The flag is read per request and anything unset, empty or misspelled leaves the grace **on** — a typo must never silently start refusing a partner.

## Why the flip cannot happen yet, precisely

K has no way to add a scope to an existing key: the security service exposes create / list / revoke / validate — no PATCH, and no `UPDATE svc_api_keys` anywhere in it. So every connector key minted before the scope existed lacks it permanently. The rotation is the only path, and the log is the only proof it has happened.

## The Stuart ask — coming from Kam, not from here

Two things are needed before the switch can be flipped, and they come to Stuart **from Kam as a test block**, not from this ticket: how many connector keys Platform S holds against the K demo, and a rotation window. Recorded here so the dependency is visible on the ticket rather than living in a thread.

## Round 3 status

Round 2's re-gate was a NO GO on **F-9**, a case-sensitivity regression it introduced. Kam authorised one narrow round 3 (card `secuura-ks843-half2-round3`, option A); it is pushed at **`e1d9d93803780f50152ab2d7d31e6e30007d37af`** on PR #845 and awaiting its third tier-1 gate. Residue and acceptance rows are on **KS-861**.

## BLUF

**The #845 re-gate came back NO GO at round 2 of 2 (2026-09-06T02:45:01Z, tier 1, head `59248bf3841ac0354f1c2ae0e8600756d26d828d`). The cap is spent. #845 is HELD and unmerged — nothing ships on it, and there are no commits on `kamilkreiser/ks-843-half2-erasure-gate-r2`.**

## Recommendation

**Hold.** The entire residue is filed as **one ticket, KS-861** (Backlog, P2, linked here and to KS-858). A round 3 starts **only** on Kam's ruling on the card `secuura-ks843-half2-round3` (recommendation A = one narrow round 3; default B = hold), relayed by Wednesday's mail. If the ruling is B or silence, KS-861 is the record.

## Detail

Round 2 closed what it was commissioned to close, and introduced one new hole:

- **F-7 CLOSED** on all six separator shapes — 403 / 0 upstream hits, both exact paths, enforcing; five red-proofs ran, the file is falsifiable. **F-8 CLOSED by removal** (grep 0 at head / 1 at parent, two positive controls, census re-derived at 32). F-1 and F-4 still closed; SETS 255 -> 260, shared 709/709, 0 failed.
- **F-9 - MAJOR, a regression this commit created.** `ERASURE_SUBPATH = /^\/erasures(\/|$)/` has no `i` flag while express matches case-insensitively (neither service sets `case sensitive routing`). Six spellings - `ERASURES`, `Erasures`, `//ERASURES`, `/API/GDPR/ERASURES`, `Erasures/`, `GET .../ERASURES/abc` - reach originate's erasure handler in **enforcing** mode for a `connector`-role key **without** the scope: precisely the population the cutover exists to refuse. The **parent refused five of them, 403 / 0 hits**. Grace mode also got worse - those spellings are now admitted with **zero** `[KS-843]` warns where the parent logged them.
- **F-10 - MAJOR, undisclosed coverage regression.** The test rewrite is **-3 / +2**, not -1. The removed `S_CONNECTOR_SCOPES` mint-set cell - the one that closed #841's F-2 - has **no successor anywhere in the repo** (`git grep -a 'S_CONNECTOR_SCOPES' 59248bf38 -- '*__tests__*'` = 0; parent = 2; positive control `platform.ts` = 2, so the product is fine and the test is gone). The commit message reports `255 -> 260` and does not mention the deletion.
- **F-11 - minor.** Every *admitted* erasure authenticates twice (gate chain + catch-all), doubling a remote `POST /api/keys/validate` on a partner-facing path. Refused requests authenticate once.

**A round 3's acceptance rows are fixed in advance** (in KS-861): the six case shapes added to `BYPASS_SHAPES` **asserting on the upstream, not the status** - F-7's failing case returned 200, so a 403 assertion would have been right by accident - plus a `GET /api/gdpr/erasures/abc` row on the exact-path enforcing cell (POST-only today), plus the restored mint-set cell.

**Class forward, on KS-858:** *a fix that re-implements path matching inherits every normalisation express already does - case, trailing slash, and the mount's own separator handling.* The tester also re-derived KS-858's population from `proxy.ts`: predicate B (a gated exact route later prefix-mounted) = **2** (`POST /api/anchors`, `POST /api/anchors/batch` - **not** `sig-json`, which carries no auth middleware at all and fails closed); predicate Q = **9**, of which 2 gated.

Source read directly, not relayed: `Testing Agent MAIN/projects/secuura/reports/2026-09-06-s138-ks843-845-half2-regate-59248bf38/report.md` - s139 (seat A), 2026-09-06T03:0xZ.

## Build status, and one lesson that did not transfer on its own

## BLUF
**Half 1** — `subjects:erase` in the vocabulary, in the connector mint set, in `docs/SCOPES.md`, **no route enforcing it**. PR **#841** at `4111f409ef9f69afeda78249125281476aca19d7`, held under a tier-2 gate.
**Half 2** — both erasure routes gated, behind a switch that is **off by default**. Built and pushed to `kamilkreiser/ks-843-half2-erasure-gate` at `d8e722ab234d5e413e4240f834ad0bfa7aa7615b`; **no PR yet, by ruling** — it opens after #841 merges, rebased onto `develop` as a single commit.

Full SHAs throughout on this ticket, deliberately: `develop` is currently `4111feef39cc28d6936b55a7bae19ce087d8120b` and #841's head is `4111f409ef9f69afeda78249125281476aca19d7` — **they share their first four characters**, so an abbreviated SHA here is genuinely ambiguous at a glance.

## Why the enforcement is a switch and not a gate
Kam ruled *"refuse others 403"*. It cannot be turned on in one step, and the reason is a measured absence rather than a preference:

**Platform K has no way to add a scope to an existing API key.** The security service's key surface is exactly `POST /api/keys` (create), `GET /api/keys` (list), `DELETE /api/keys/:id` (revoke), `POST /api/keys/validate` — no PATCH, no PUT, and no `UPDATE svc_api_keys` anywhere in the service. (Control: 9 `svc_api_keys` statements in that file, so the null is a real absence. My first sweep returned zero for the *wrong* reason — those routes are on `app.`, not `router.` — and a control caught it before it became a conclusion.)

So every connector key issued before this scope existed lacks it, and the only route to a scoped key is rotation, which is platform-admin-only by guardrail. A bare `requireScope` would 403 Platform S's live erasure path with no forward fix. Hence: role-or-scope, one structured log line per role-only admission, and `SUBJECTS_ERASE_SCOPE_ENFORCED` to flip once the log shows S on a rotated key.

The flag is tested `=== 'true'`, so `"TRUE"`, `"1"`, `"yes"` or a typo leave the **grace on**. A misspelling must never silently start refusing a partner. That has its own cell.

## The lesson, recorded because it is field evidence
The mount-order cell — the one asserting both erasure routes are registered *before* the catch-all `/api/gdpr` mount — **went red on its first run.** It used a bare `indexOf` and matched the **comment** I had just written above those routes, which quotes the catch-all mount while explaining the ordering.

That is [KS-386](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-386) F-3's exact failure mode — prose read as code — **in a cell I wrote a few hours after shipping the fix for it.** It now matches a statement anchored to the start of a line, and carries a control proving it is not reading the prose.

**A rule does not transfer on its own.** Knowing F-3 did not stop me writing F-3 again; the cell caught me, not my memory of the lesson. That is the argument for cells over care.

## Related
[KS-577](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-577) — rotation mints a new key but never revokes the old one. A real defect, and *not* fixed here; for this cutover it happens to provide the overlap window that makes a zero-downtime swap possible. Named so nobody mistakes the convenience for a reason to leave it open.
[KS-835](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-835) — the `authMethod` short-circuit in `requireScope`. This gate deliberately does not inherit it, with a cell that reds if it is added back.

title: The OAuth error code travels in error.message and the contract never says so; and authorize refusals answer JSON where RFC 6749 redirects
description:
**From the KS-822 tier-1 gate.** `projects/secuura/reports/2026-09-06-s136-ks822-835-pass1-04994288a-tier1/` (QA tree)

Two related contract defects in the OAuth error envelope, both **pre-existing** (KS-804's shape, not KS-822's changes).

**1. The OAuth code travels in the wrong field and the contract never names it.** Every refusal from the authorize and token endpoints answers `{ success: false, error: { code: 'BAD_REQUEST', message: '<oauth_code>', description } }` — so `error.code` is the platform's HTTP-ish code and the **OAuth** code (`invalid_client`, `invalid_grant`, `invalid_scope`, `unsupported_response_type`) is in `error.message`. The published descriptions name those codes but never say which field carries them, so an integrator has to guess or read a response.

**2. RFC 6749 4.1.2.1 delivers authorize errors by REDIRECT, not a JSON 400.** For an authorize request with a *valid* client and redirect URI, the RFC says the server redirects back with `error=...&state=...` rather than answering the user agent with JSON. This platform answers JSON 400 for the whole rule set. That is a design question, not a bug to fix quietly — the deny path already redirects, so the two halves of the same endpoint disagree.

**Done when:** the contract states which field carries the OAuth code; and a decision is recorded on whether authorize refusals should redirect per the RFC, with the deny path's existing behaviour as the reference point.

title: Make the authorize rules DATA the resolver iterates, so the GET/POST agreement guard is structural instead of textual
description:
**From the KS-822 tier-1 gate.** `projects/secuura/reports/2026-09-06-s136-ks822-835-pass1-04994288a-tier1/` (QA tree)

`ks804-authorize-get-post-agree-per-rule.test.ts`'s `RULES` table is a hand-maintained literal. Its header once promised that a rule added to one handler and not the other "fails here by construction, because the table below is the list of rules" — corrected in KS-822 F-8, because it is the list of rules *someone wrote down*, not the list the code has.

F-8 enforced the half that could be enforced: the table's `expected` set must equal the refusal-message set `resolveAuthorizeClient` can return. **That guard is TEXTUAL and has three named limits, each measured rather than asserted:**

* a rule that **REUSES** an existing message is invisible to it — F-6 and F-7 both did, and their RULES rows are hand-added, which is the only thing making those rules driven;
* it is a **SOURCE-TEXT** guard: it sees a literal appear or disappear and **cannot see a rule stop working while its literal stays on the page** (a condition-shaped tamper on RULE 5 reds the behaviour cases and leaves the guard green);
* its span is anchored on the function signature as text, so a `return {` + `ok: true,` written with different whitespace ends it early or not at all.

**The real fix the header already names: make the rules DATA the resolver iterates**, so the table is derived rather than maintained and the guard becomes structural instead of textual. That is a route refactor of `resolveAuthorizeClient`, not a change to the suite, which is why it was not taken inside KS-822.

**Done when:** the resolver's app rules are a list it walks; the suite derives its cases from that list; a new rule is driven through both handlers without anyone adding a row; and the three limits above are closed or explicitly re-stated against the new shape.

nodes.body:
**From the #835 (KS-822) FINAL re-gate, 2026-09-05T21:53:45Z — N4. Good news, and it narrows this ticket's scope.**

The authorize resolver's refusal message is a **closed literal union**, so `tsc` already answers **TS2322** to an undeclared refusal message. The compiler therefore guards the **new-message** case structurally — a developer who invents a refusal message the RULES table does not know about cannot compile.

What the text-reading cell in `ks804-authorize-get-post-agree-per-rule.test.ts` uniquely covers is the **REUSED-message** case: an author who adds a sixth rule but reuses an existing message. That case type-checks cleanly, and it is exactly where the text reader is blind — the gate's own plant P6 (sixth rule, reused message) came out **54/54 green**, a documented blind spot re-derived rather than assumed.

**Scoping consequence for this ticket:** making the rules data the resolver iterates is worth doing for the reused-message case and for nothing else in this area. The new-message case is already closed by the compiler, so it should not be part of this ticket's justification.

title: Published prose drifts from the routes it describes and nothing detects it — the phrase check, the marker convention, and the ~306 unswept descriptions
description:
**Ruled lines 1, 2 and 5 of KS-822's five, lifted onto one ticket so they survive that ticket closing.** They are one problem seen three ways: *published prose drifts away from the routes it describes, and nothing detects it.*

The evidence is not hypothetical. `POST /api/oauth/token`'s description was swept **twice** and was wrong in **three** places both times. One wrong sentence about client authentication reached **four** separate places (comment → contract → test header → route), and the fourth landed *inside the commit that corrected the first three*.

---

## Line 1 — targeted contract-source phrase check (~half a day, SIZED)

A retired-phrase registry checked against **contract sources only**: `services/*/src/*.openapi.ts` plus the generated `docs/openapi/secuura-api.yaml`.

* **No marker convention needed to start** — in that surface a quotation carrying a marker is rare to nonexistent.
* Catches the **comment → contract** hop, which is the one that publishes a wrong rule to integrators.
* **The matcher must be wrap-tolerant by construction**: normalise whitespace and comment punctuation across line boundaries before matching. ~15 lines.
* ⚠ **A single-token control is NOT a valid control for a line-wrapping phrase.** That exact mistake made an earlier sweep report **0** where the true count was **4**.
* **Stated limitation, on the line rather than discovered later: this would NOT have caught F-1c.** Test headers are outside the surface and F-1c was a test header. This is the cheap 80%, not the class.

## Line 2 — repo-wide marker convention (UNSIZED, deliberately)

Not sized pending a population measurement, and **measuring the population is most of the work.**

The shape it must survive, from a real specimen produced on `develop`: in `BACKLOG.md` the retired phrase *"deletion only"* appears twice — once as the live claim and once inside a quotation of the old wording. A sweep that cannot tell a quotation from a claim makes a correct commit look like a regression, because the phrase count went **1 → 2** for an entirely correct reason.

## Line 5 — the ~306 unswept published descriptions (UNSIZED)

The other **~306** published operation descriptions have never been swept against their routes. Sizing it means sampling, and sampling is most of the work. **It pairs naturally with line 1**, which runs over the same surface.

---

## Why these are together

Line 1 is the instrument, line 2 is what the instrument needs to avoid false positives at repo scale, and line 5 is the population it would be pointed at. Building line 1 alone is defensible and cheap; building it *without* line 2's distinction is what makes a sweep that cries wolf and gets switched off.

## The standing ruling

**Wednesday priced line 1 and ruled DO NOT BUILD IT NOW** (2026-09-05T15:44:16Z), after it was proposed. That ruling is carried here unchanged — this ticket is the record, not a commission. Anyone picking it up should re-price rather than assume the half-day still holds.

*Source: KS-822 comments* `e38c5f38` *(lines 1 and 2) and* `4f901d71` *(line 5), from PR #831's tier-2 gate.*

nodes.body:
**One more specimen for Line 5, found by hand rather than by a sweep — now KS-1757.**

`GET /api/connector/info`'s operation description (`api-gateway.openapi.ts:904-905`) claims *"a user or admin bearer token is refused with 403"*. Three cases are answered **401** by `authenticateToken(true)` before the handler is reached: no/non-`Bearer` header (`middleware/auth.ts:442`), `jwt.verify` throwing on an invalid or expired token (`:530`), and a valid token whose session has been revoked (`:495`, `SESSION_INVALIDATED`). Only a *valid* bearer with an *active* session reaches the 403 at `services/health.ts:45`.

Two details that bear on this ticket's own method:

1. **The same wrong rule was in two places in one operation** — the `401` description carried it too, thirteen lines below, and that copy was corrected under KS-1753 (PR #1740) after a QA gate caught it. One sentence, two locations, one of which a reader of the other would never see. That is the *contract → contract* hop, a shorter one than the comment → contract hop this ticket was built on.

2. **A pickaxe search misattributes it.** `git log -S'admin bearer token is refused with 403'` returns KS-1753's commit, because that commit changed the **number of occurrences** rather than introducing the phrase. `git blame` and the base file put it at `c3eb63c9d2`. If Line 1's phrase registry is ever paired with `-S` to find *when* a retired phrase entered, it will name the commit that removed a duplicate. Worth noting beside the existing warning that a single-token control is not a valid control for a wrapped phrase.

This instance was found while fixing the sibling sentence, not by the detection this ticket proposes — which is the argument for the detection.

*Posted by Seat S 4th (agent). No state changed. Filed as KS-1757 rather than folded in here, on Wednesday's 2026-10-27 ruling: the one-sentence correction and the detection work are two different fixes.*

**From the #835 (KS-822) FINAL re-gate, 2026-09-05T21:53:45Z — N3. This ticket is the prose-drift instrument, so this is a design constraint on it, not a defect report.**

**A regression guard written against the fragment `filtered out, not refused` would false-alarm forever.** The fragment is still on both authorize operations at the merged tip (`52f676d9b`, count 1) and it is **correct there** — it lives inside the new case (b), where partial scope overlap really is filtered rather than refused. What #835 removed was the *unconditional* sentence claiming that behaviour for every case.

So the instrument must anchor on **the conjunction** — the claim plus the condition it holds under — never on the memorable phrase. A phrase that survives a behaviour change while its surrounding claim inverts is precisely the drift this ticket exists to catch, and a fragment-matcher is blind to it in both directions: it fires when the phrase is innocent, and stays silent when the phrase is reused under a claim that has flipped.

Related, and the reason this matters more than a style note: the Major that #835's round 2 fixed was this exact class — the published contract asserted and denied the same behaviour three paragraphs apart, because the author who changed the behaviour updated a test comment and not the prose.

title: Publish a `request:` block for POST /api/oauth/token — the endpoint's shape is asserted nowhere, and adding it moves what Schemathesis generates
description:
**Ruled line 3 of KS-822's five, lifted onto its own ticket so it survives that ticket closing.**

`POST /api/oauth/token` publishes **no** `request:` **block**. That is why its description spells the form fields out in prose — `grant_type`, `code`, `code_verifier`, `redirect_uri`, `client_id`, `client_secret`, `refresh_token` are described in a sentence rather than declared as a schema an integrator or a tool can read.

## Why it was NOT added in #831, and the reason still holds

Publishing a form-body schema where none exists **changes what Schemathesis generates against a live auth endpoint.** That is not a docs-only change, and #831 was a prose-scoped round. It wants its own change **with the suite actually run** — the point is precisely that the generator's behaviour moves, so a change that does not run the suite has not been tested.

## What it is worth

The token endpoint's published contract has been tightened repeatedly (KS-820 client authentication; KS-822 F-2d bound the status→code split to assertions). All of that is in prose. A `request:` block is the half a machine can check, and its absence is why the endpoint's shape is asserted nowhere in the spec.

## Done when

* A `request:` block declaring the form body, with `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` as the media type the endpoint actually accepts (it is in `FORM_ALLOWED_PATHS` — the only path that is).
* **Schemathesis run before and after**, with the operation's case counts and outcomes compared. A change that moves the generator and reports no delta has not been measured.
* The prose reduced to what the schema cannot say, rather than left to drift beside it.

*Source: KS-822 comment* `e38c5f38` *(line 3), from PR #831's tier-2 gate. Nothing was built for it in KS-822's round.*

nodes.body:
**From the #835 (KS-822) FINAL re-gate, 2026-09-05T21:53:45Z — N1, polish, non-blocking. Recorded here because this is the `request:` block ticket and that makes it the natural home.**

The PUBLIC/CONFIDENTIAL `code_challenge` rule that #835 published is on the **GET query parameter only**. The POST body's `code_challenge` carries **no description at all** — in a PR whose entire thesis is that the GET and POST authorize paths must not drift.

Measured at the merged tip `52f676d9b`: GET `/api/oauth/authorize` description 1213 chars, POST 1853 chars, both now carrying the three-case scope statement — but the rule about which client types must send a `code_challenge` appears on one side only.

Fix shape when this ticket is worked: put the same PUBLIC/CONFIDENTIAL sentence on `OAuthAuthorizeRequest.code_challenge`. The tester offered a shape and deliberately wrote nothing. Not a round on #835 — its scope was the six F-items and it closed all of them.

title: [Decision] POST /api/certifications/:id/verify has no auth handler — leave it public, or gate it?
description:
**The ask, first:** @kamil.kreiser **— should** `POST /api/certifications/:id/verify` **stay public, or be moved behind auth?** Default if you say nothing: **leave it public**. Nothing changes in code either way until you rule. This is a **product decision recorded, not a defect actioned** (category 2).

## What is measured

`POST /api/certifications/:id/verify` (`services/api-gateway/src/routes/verification.ts:556`) is mounted with **no authentication handler** — only `mockBodyParser`. A request carrying no `Authorization` header reaches the route handler and gets the handler's own answer.

**At the KS-815 head (recorded during the KS-800 round):** C10 → **200 headerless**, with C11 → **401** as the discriminating control.

**Re-measured live on the local stack today, 2026-09-05T20:02Z, at** `develop` `0b9346f31`**:**

| case | request | result |
| -- | -- | -- |
| SUBJECT | `POST /api/certifications/550e8400-…/verify`, **no** `Authorization` | **404** with the handler's own body — `{"verified":false,…,"error":"Certification not found","checks":{"exists":false}}` |
| SUBJECT | same, `id=test-cert-1` | **404**, same shape |
| **CONTROL** | `POST /api/documents`, **no** `Authorization`, same client and shape | **401** |

**Why the 404 is the finding and not a refusal:** an auth-guarded route never reaches its handler headerless — it answers 401 before the handler runs, as `/api/documents` does from the same client in the same second. This route answers *from inside the handler* (`checks.exists` is the handler's own field), so the request got all the way through. The 404 is "that certification does not exist", not "you are not allowed to ask".

## What it does and does not expose

The handler is **read-only** — it calls `checkDocumentExists(id, authHeader)` and returns JSON. It writes nothing. It forwards whatever `Authorization` header it received, so a caller who *has* a token is still scoped downstream; a caller with none is not stopped at the door.

Since the F-03 pen-test fix it can no longer claim `anchored: true`: certifications without real on-chain confirmation return `verified: false` and `confidence: 'pending-onchain'`. So what an unauthenticated caller learns is **existence** plus issuance status for an id they already hold.

## The two readings, so the decision is a decision

* **Leave public (the default).** Verification is the product — a relying party checking a certification they were handed should not need a Secuura account. The route leaks existence for an id you must already possess, and writes nothing.
* **Put it behind auth.** Existence-oracle on guessable or enumerable ids, and it is the only verify-family route on the gateway with no handler; the asymmetry is itself a smell for anyone reading the mount list.

## If the answer is "leave public"

Close this ticket and it becomes the written record that the posture is deliberate — which is the thing that is missing today. A future guard sweep that flags this mount then has an answer to read.

title: Audit gate baseline data model: an unvalidated `scope` lets a GREEN root gate advertise a row leg 7 still needs, and suppression matches by advisory id alone
description:
## BLUF

**Two Minor findings in the audit gate's BASELINE DATA MODEL, both from the #829 fuse gate (tier 2, PASS — merged at** `ec5431f6b`**). Neither blocked the merge. F1 is the one s133 walked into and which cost a refused push; F2 means a baseline row silently covers more than it was written about.** Filed beside KS-763 as the gate ruled. Fix-shapes below are the tester's, quoted as **hypotheses** — run each against the unfixed instrument before building on it.

## F1 (Minor) — a green root gate can advertise a row for deletion that a second gate still needs

`scope: "standalone-locks"` is **optional and unvalidated**: `baseline-contract.mjs:41` REQUIRED_FIELDS is `package` / `reason` / `ticket` only. But the root gate's CLEANUP advice keys on that field (`audit-gate.mjs:203-205`).

So an advisory that lives **only in a standalone lock**, baselined without the marker, is advertised for deletion by a **GREEN** root gate — while leg 7 (`audit:locks`) still needs the row. That is exactly what happened on 2026-09-05: `audit:gate` printed `CLEANUP … remove: GHSA-v422-hmwv-36x6` and the push preflight then refused the deletion, because the root audit reads the **hoisted workspace tree** and cannot see standalone locks. Deleting on the root gate's word would have broken the push gate for every author.

The class is swept clean at head — one such row, and it is marked.

**Fix-shape (hypothesis):** either `validateBaseline` refuses a row that the root audit does not report and that lacks `scope`, or the root gate declines to list for cleanup any row it cannot positively attribute. **Regression:** a locks-only advisory baselined without `scope` must NOT appear in CLEANUP.

## F2 (Minor) — suppression matches by ADVISORY ID ALONE

`baseline[id]` at `audit-locks.mjs:286-289` and `audit-gate.mjs:194-197`. A row written about one version and one path silently covers **every** version and **every** path of that advisory.

Demonstrated by this very PR: the regen added a **vulnerable-range qs instance** (nested `qs` 6.15.3 under body-parser 1.20.6) and **no gate output changed**.

**Fix-shape (hypothesis):** record the measured versions on the row; **warn — not fail** — when a matched instance falls outside them.

## F3 (polish) — a wording fix on the record

"before the regen leg 7 refused" described the **deletion-only attempt**, not the parent SHA. The parent is GREEN 30/30. The refusal is the head-baseline + parent-lock cell, which the tester reproduced exactly. Correct the phrasing wherever it is repeated.

## F4 (polish) — the mysql2 row's clocks disagree

`GHSA-rgwj-5xj2-c3m3` mixes a local date with ISO dates, and its `decidedAt` still reads `2026-09-03` under a **2026-09-04** ruling by Kam. Verified on develop `ec5431f6b`: `decidedAt: "2026-09-03"`, `expires: "2026-09-24"`. Being fixed in the BACKLOG docs commit if it is a one-line change; otherwise it stays here as this ticket's fourth line.

## For the record — the tester's own retraction

qs 6.15.3 was **already** in four locks at the parent (`frontend/issuer`, `services/vc-issuer`, `services/mcp-server`, `packages/shared`::body-parser). The nesting is an existing repo pattern, so the hazard disclosed on #829 is **milder** than first read. The two #801 rows cover the nested instance by id, tamper-proven.

**Not commissioned, said so:** the reachability re-check. The tester checked the mysql2 **row** (id → package by tamper; 3.15.3 in exactly two locks), not the measurement behind it.

## Provenance

Gate mail `[QA -> Wednesday] Secuura FUSE #829 PASS 1 @ b7fc43473 (tier 2 narrow)` 2026-09-05T15:18:05Z; routed here by Wednesday's GO 2026-09-05T15:21:12Z. Sits beside KS-763 (the fuse ticket #829 carries on its mysql2 row).

title: Gate integrity: the auth suite's green is not deterministic — three head runs gave 534/0, 534/0, and 534 with 2 FAILED
description:
## BLUF

**A security PR merged on one green run is merged on a sample.** The KS-820+821 gate ran the auth
suite three times at the head and got **534/0, 534/0, and 534 with 2 FAILED** — the failing file
(`ks431-oauth-app-update.test.ts`) is **byte-identical at both SHAs**, failing with
`TypeError: fetch failed` plus a stale 500. The suite's green is a sample, and every gate in this
class currently reads one draw of it as a verdict.

## Mechanism — measured, and the same one twice

**21 of the 40 auth test files open a server per request** (`app.listen(0)`). s132's `BACKLOG.md`
entry — `auth.integration.test.ts` failing 1 run in 3 with a registration helper getting 501 — is
**the same mechanism in another file**, and is carried here **as a hypothesis, not a diagnosis**:
its preconditions are all measured (a server per REQUEST, no agent passed,
`http.globalAgent.keepAlive === true` on node 24, `501` absent from all of `services/auth/src`) but
the link has never been reproduced deterministically.

## Why it is worth its own ticket

The flake and the gate are separate problems. Even once the flake is diagnosed, **a gate that reads**
**a single run cannot tell a real red from a draw** — that is the part that decides whether security
work merges correctly.

## Shapes, neither yet run

* **The flake:** listen once per suite, or pass an agent with `keepAlive: false`.
* **The gate:** run the suite N times, or make the runner report the draw rather than the verdict.
  Whichever is chosen, prove it by reproducing a red first — a fix that cannot be shown to change
  the failure rate has not been shown to do anything.

---

title: OAuth app_type: a CASED row is neither normalised by 047 nor refused by its CHECK, and docker/init's unnamed constraint defeats 047's idempotence guard
description:
## BLUF

Two DDL defects left by KS-821's migration 047. **F-2 is the one that matters: a cased row such as**
`'Public'` **is silently and permanently bricked** — it is not normalised and not refused, and the
app's users get the false message *"Invalid or expired authorization code"* forever.

## F-2 (Major) — the case hole survives 047 in both directions

* 047's normalisation predicate is `lower(app_type) NOT IN (...)`, so `'Public'` **does not match**
  and is left untouched.
* The CHECK it adds **permits** `'Public'` as well, so the row is legal forever.
* Every consuming rule is an **exact** match, so `'Public'` is a third string to all of them and
  takes the else-branch — the app can never satisfy the rule it is judged by.

**Fix-shape (the tester's — a HYPOTHESIS until run against the unfixed product):** either normalise
on the exact set and `SET app_type = lower(app_type)`, or fold case at the three exact-match
consumers — `services/auth/src/routes/oauth.ts:276`, `:615`, and
`services/auth/src/services/oauth.ts:209`. Measure which before choosing; a CHECK that permits a
value the code cannot honour is the defect, so the constraint's own predicate is in scope too.

## F-3 (Minor) — a second identical constraint

`docker/init`'s inline CHECK is **UNNAMED**, so Postgres names it `oauth_apps_app_type_check` — the
same name 047's idempotence guard looks for is not the name it looks for. The guard misses it and
adds a **second identical constraint** on a fresh database.

## Scope note

`app_type` is now inside `CreateOAuthAppSchema` case-folded (KS-821), so the **API** can no longer
mint a cased row. This ticket is about rows arriving any other way — a direct DB write, a restore,
a seed, or anything predating 047.

---
