title: Gateway mount-auth check scores authenticateToken(false) as green — six /api mounts satisfy neither leg of its own assertion
description:
## BLUF

**The KS-570 mount-auth check scores** `authenticateToken(false)` **as green, so six** `/api` **subtree mounts pass an assertion they do not actually satisfy.** Raised by Peter reviewing PR #730; **pre-existing on** `develop`**, not #730's doing and not its job to fix.** The fix is small — tag `authed` only when `required === true` — but the value is in whatever the retag then surfaces.

## Mechanism

`collectMounts`'s mock adds the middleware to `authTagged` regardless of the `required` argument, so `authenticateToken(false)` reads as `authed: true`. But `(false)` calls `next()` for a caller carrying no `Authorization` header at all (`services/api-gateway/src/middleware/auth.ts:317-323`).

The guard's assertion is *"every /api mount either requires auth or is public by design with a stated reason"*. These mounts satisfy **neither** leg: they require nothing, and they are recorded in no by-design allowlist.

## The six, measured — not adopted

Measured at PR #730's head `3fe1b6f1a` (Peter's ref) and again on `develop 9b89f4fce`, comment lines excluded:

| mount | `proxy.ts` @ `3fe1b6f1a` | `proxy.ts` @ `develop 9b89f4fce` | state |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| `/api/certifications` | 521 | 521 | **defended** — `attachScopes` + `requireScope('certifications:read','certifications:write')` follow |
| `/api/credentials` | 703 | 703 | straight to `proxy(...)` |
| `/api/referrals` | 786 | 777 | straight to `proxy(...)` |
| `/api/governance` | 875 | 861 | straight to `proxy(...)` |
| `/api/nft` | 892 | 878 | handler, then `proxy(...)` |
| `/api/billing` | 941 | 927 | straight to `proxy(...)` |

⚠ **A naive grep returns SEVEN on both refs.** The extra hit is a comment — the KS-442 note reading *"*`/api/credentials` *is already authenticateToken(false), its 401 came from the service"*. Excluding comment lines gives six on both refs, matching Peter's list exactly. Anyone re-running this should exclude comments or they will chase a mount that does not exist.

`/api/status` is deliberately **not** in this list: on `develop` it carries no auth middleware at all, and PR #730 gives it `authenticateToken(true)`.

## What is NOT established

**The anonymous-caller half is unmeasured.** Peter could not probe it (no Docker available to him) and inferred from the signature-only `authenticate()` in `@secuura/shared` that an anonymous caller would most likely 401 downstream. **That inference has not been tested and must be measured before any severity is stated on this ticket.**

Two things keep this below KS-570's severity, and it is worth being exact rather than alarming:

* the revocation check runs **before** the `required` branch, so when a token IS present, `(false)` does still catch a revoked session — the KS-570 class is genuinely covered by these mounts;
* five of the six go straight to a service that may well enforce its own auth.

## Done means

1. `collectMounts` tags `authed` only when `required === true`.
2. Each of the six is then either given real auth, or recorded in the by-design allowlist **with a stated reason** (the `/api/certifications` one is already effectively defended by `requireScope` and may only need recording).
3. **The anonymous-caller behaviour of each is measured, with a control**, before any of them is called safe.

## Two smaller notes from the same review, accepted for later, not fixed now

* `authed` is `layers.some(...)`, so it asserts the middleware is **present**, not **ordered before** the proxy.
* The `> 40` floor sits against a corpus of roughly 62, so it catches total collapse but not the loss of a third.

*Filed from PR #730's review (Peter's item 2), 2026-09-01. He offered to file it himself; filed from our notes at his suggestion since the probe setup is here.*

nodes.body:
**BLUF: with leg 2 of the mount-auth check corrected ([PR #1701](https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/1701), KS-1713, not merged), two of this ticket's six `authenticateToken(false)` mounts, `/api/certifications` and `/api/nft`, no longer score as authenticated and carry explicit entries in the test. Neither carries `authenticateToken(true)`, so part (b) of this ticket is still open for both.** Everything below was read from source at develop `28e2d27de337`; none of it was probed live by me.

**Enumeration.** `routes/proxy.ts` registers 65 mount groups. 8 have a guard other than `authenticateToken` that answers an anonymous request with 401 or throws.
- 6 also carry `authenticateToken(true)`, so leg 1 covers them: `proxy.ts:442` `/api/webhooks`, `:461` `/api/users/lookup`, `:635` `/api/documents`, `:857` `/api/platform/organizations/erase-connector`, `:873` `POST /api/anchors`, `:879` `POST /api/anchors/batch`.
- 2 do not: `proxy.ts:642` `/api/certifications` (`authenticateToken(false)`, `attachScopes`, `requireScope`) and `proxy.ts:1159` `/api/nft` (`authenticateToken(false)`, then an inline NOT_DEPLOYED guard).
- No `proxy.ts` mount has a guard that verifies the credential itself, meaning one that still answers 401 when `req.user` is already populated. The only such guard is `requireAdmin` in `admin.ts`, on 39 gateway-local route groups.

**What the source says about the two.**
- `/api/certifications`: `requireScope` answers 401 when `req.user` is absent, so an anonymous caller is refused before the proxy. `authenticateToken(false)` sets `req.user` only from a credential it accepts, and its `SESSION_INVALIDATED` 401 is not gated on `required`, so a revoked-session token is refused here too. The anonymous refusal sits in an authorization guard, which is a weaker posture than `authenticateToken(true)`.
- `/api/nft`: the inline guard answers 404 `NOT_DEPLOYED` to every non-localhost caller while `NFT_SERVICE_URL` is still the default, and calls `next()` otherwise. It is not authentication. A request that reaches `nft-certificate` meets `authenticate()` on `/api` (`app.ts:45`), with two public-by-contract ops: `POST /nft/verify/asset` and `POST /nft/verify/transaction`.

**Relation to the 2026-09-09 comment on this ticket.** That comment measured both mounts live and recorded them as "refuse at the gateway, correctly authed, no entry needed". Its table does not record the status codes, so I cannot tell from it which layer answered for `/api/nft`, and I have not re-measured. The outcome (anonymous refused) is consistent with the source. What changed is the classification: the old leg 2 counted any guard that refused an anonymous request as authentication, which is why no entry was needed then. PR #1701 narrows that, so both now have entries worded as read from source, not probed live.

## PR [#923](https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/923) — part (a) BUILT, READY FOR QA. Not merged.

**BLUF: `d127dc7d4` is on origin, preflight PASSED, api-gateway 294/294.** The retag is done, the corpus is widened to gateway-local routes, and the seven mounts that then surfaced are each **measured** rather than assumed.

- **PR:** #923 · **head:** `d127dc7d4655a4e227d4f6e511f469c456eaabb7`, read from `git ls-remote origin` in the same action as the push
- **branch:** `kamilkreiser/ks-736-mount-auth-retag` · **base:** `develop` @ `b6884888d`

## Three defects, not one — and the third was forced by fixing the second

1. **The retag** (as filed): `if (required) authTagged.add(mw)`. Trivial, exactly as the BLUF said.
2. **The corpus** (Peter's item 4): widened to `createAdminRoutes`. **It surfaced two instances nobody had — `GET /api/verification/policy` and `GET /api/settings/notifications`** — beyond Peter's seventh.
3. ⚠ **The scoring, and this nearly shipped as a 48-route FALSE finding.** Widening brought in 48 `/api/admin/*` routes reading as unauthenticated. **They are not** — they carry `requireAdmin` (401 without a Bearer, RS256-verified, role-gated, fails closed), a *stricter* guard than `authenticateToken(true)`, which the injected mock cannot be. Recognising it by **name** would break this file's own "identity, not name" rule. So `authed` gained a second leg that asks what the middleware **does**: given no `Authorization` header, does it respond instead of calling `next()`. **That is also precisely the property this ticket is about** — `(false)` fails it by construction.

## The disproven inference, re-tested — and Peter's finding was the exception, not the rule

This ticket says severity cannot be stated until the anonymous half is measured, and Peter disproved the "services will 401 downstream" inference with `/api/privacy/settings` answering 200. **Measured all seven** (controls: `/api/documents` 401, `/api/oauth/scopes` 200):

| mount | anonymous | verdict |
|---|---|---|
| `/api/certifications`, `/api/nft` | refuse **at the gateway** | correctly authed — no entry needed |
| `/api/credentials` `/api/referrals` `/api/governance` `/api/billing` | gateway passes; **service** 401s | new `AUTH_ENFORCED_DOWNSTREAM` list |
| `/api/privacy/settings` · `/api/settings/notifications` · `/api/verification/policy` | **200**, by design | `PUBLIC_BY_DESIGN` |

**So of the original six, four are enforced downstream and two at the gateway — the inference holds for all six.** The three that answer 200 are all gateway-local routes, which is the surface the check could not see. **Peter's instance was the exception; the widening is what found the other two.**

**Recording the four downstream ones as PUBLIC_BY_DESIGN would have been false** — they are not public. They satisfy *neither* leg, exactly as this ticket says, so they get their own list, and the header states plainly that this is a **weaker posture** than `authenticateToken(true)`: KS-570's own warning is that the gateway's session-revocation check lives *inside* that middleware, so these mounts skip revocation even where the service verifies the signature. **An entry means "measured to refuse today", not "safe by design".**

## Evidence

api-gateway **294/294** (27 files, 0 failed — nothing to attribute) · tsc (compiles `__tests__`) exit 0 · eslint exit 0 · preflight PASSED.

**Red-proofed three ways**, each restored byte-identical (sha256 `9bc17879…`), all 5 cells running in every tamper — and **each tamper reddens a DIFFERENT assertion**, which is what shows the three changes are independently load-bearing rather than one change wearing three hats: revert the retag → stale-allowlist fires; drop the widening → stale-allowlist fires; neuter the behavioural leg → *unexplained* fires with the 48 admin routes.

## NOT covered
- **Part (b) is NOT done** — nothing is re-gated. Deciding which mounts should carry `authenticateToken(true)` is a security-posture change and stays separate, per this ticket's own suggested split.
- **Sub-paths not swept** — probes hit each mount's root. `/api/billing/webhooks` is explicitly no-auth (Stripe-signed) and mounted separately.
- Live probes ran against a local stack whose image predates `develop`; the source-level scoring is unaffected.

*Posted from the Platform K session (s160). No merge attempted — no approval exists, and one cannot be self-supplied.*

## Sizing: **M** — the retag is trivial; Peter's 2026-09-01 measurement is what carries the size

Sized, not started (s103).

**The fix named in the BLUF is genuinely S**: tag `authed` only when `required === true`, one condition in `collectMounts`'s mock. If that were all, this would be S.

**It is M because the 2026-09-01 comment moved two things:**

1. **The recorded inference is disproven.** The ticket said severity could not be stated until the anonymous-caller half was measured, and the standing inference was that services would 401 downstream. Measured: `GET /api/privacy/settings` answered an anonymous caller **200 with a body**. So "the service enforces its own auth" cannot be assumed for the other mounts — **each of the six needs its own anonymous probe**, and that probing is the bulk of the work, not the retag.
2. **The surface is wider than the six.** The seventh instance sits in `services/api-gateway/src/routes/admin.ts:1456`, a **gateway-local route**, not a `proxy.ts` subtree mount — and `collectMounts` only scans subtree mounts. Peter's suggested "done means" item 4 (cover locally-handled routes too) is the right call, and it means the retag lands against a corpus that must first be widened. A retag against the narrow corpus would ship a guard that still cannot see the instance that prompted the widening.

**Severity stays low and should be stated that way.** No user data is exposed on the seventh instance — the handler falls back to a `'default'` bucket, not caller-supplied identity, and the identical authed/unauthed bodies are that fallback rather than a leak. It is *by design* (KS-719, Kam 2026-08-29) and merely unrecorded in any allowlist, which is precisely the second leg these mounts fail. **Recording, not fixing.**

**Suggested split if it needs to move faster:** (a) widen the corpus + retag, with the six/seven recorded in the by-design allowlist where they belong — M; (b) whatever the retag then surfaces — unsized until (a) runs, and deliberately not estimated here.

## The anonymous-caller half is now MEASURED — and the recorded inference does not hold

This ticket says severity cannot be stated until one thing is measured:

> **The anonymous-caller half is unmeasured.** Peter could not probe it (no Docker available to him) and inferred from the signature-only `authenticate()` in `@secuura/shared` that an anonymous caller would most likely 401 downstream. **That inference has not been tested and must be measured before any severity is stated on this ticket.**

Docker was available today, so it has been probed.

**Result: an `authenticateToken(false)` route answered an anonymous caller with `200` and a body — not a downstream 401.** So the inference is disproven for at least one route, and "the service will enforce its own auth" cannot be assumed for the rest without measuring each.

**Environment:** Mac, slot 1, 33 containers / 33 healthy, branch `feature/ks-611-post-apitimestampsbatch-errors-on-every-sweep` @ **`35a35ca3d3539c9da391254855789c8fbc92d82c`** (KS-611/#734 — a timestamping contract change plus systemTest housekeeping; nothing touching the gateway).

## How it surfaced

An **Akto `pre-merge` scan** (344 endpoints, 80 s) flagged `GET /api/privacy/settings` as **NO_AUTH / REMOVE_TOKENS, HIGH**. Verified by hand rather than taken on Akto's word:

```
GET /api/privacy/settings            (no Authorization header)  -> HTTP 200
{"success":true,"settings":{"autoRejectUnknown":false,"preferRangeProofs":true, …}}

GET /api/privacy/settings            (valid ISSUER_ADMIN bearer) -> HTTP 200   (identical body)
```

## ⚠ It is a SEVENTH instance, outside this ticket's six

`services/api-gateway/src/routes/admin.ts:1456`:

```js
router.get('/api/privacy/settings', authenticateToken(false), async (req, res) => {
  const userId = req.user?.userId || 'default';
```

This is a **gateway-local route in `routes/admin.ts`**, not one of the six `proxy.ts` subtree mounts this ticket enumerates. `collectMounts` scans the proxy mounts, so **this class extends beyond the surface the check looks at** — worth widening the "done means" step 1 to cover locally-handled routes as well as subtree mounts, or the retag will still miss these.

## Severity — low, and I want to be exact rather than alarming

**No user data is exposed.** The handler falls back to a `'default'` bucket rather than any caller-supplied identity — the Pen-test F-04 fix removed the spoofable `x-user-id` fallback — so an anonymous reader gets documented defaults, not somebody's settings. The identical authenticated/unauthenticated bodies above are that fallback, not a leak.

**And it is deliberate.** `routes/admin.ts:1441-1446` records the KS-719 decision (Kam, 2026-08-29): the GET keeps optional auth *"so anonymous readers still get the documented defaults"*, while the PUT was tightened to `authenticateToken(true)` precisely because an unauthenticated write landed in a bucket every anonymous caller then read back.

So for this route the honest reading is: **by design, safe, and not recorded in any by-design allowlist** — which is exactly the second leg this ticket says these mounts fail. It needs recording, not fixing.

## Suggested addition to "done means"

4. Include gateway-local `router.<verb>('/api/…', authenticateToken(false), …)` routes, not only `proxy.ts` subtree mounts — `GET /api/privacy/settings` is one, and the KS-719 rationale is already written next to it, so recording it is cheap.

## Harness note (mine, not yours)

Akto will fail the `pre-merge` gate on this every run until it is triaged into the by-design allowlist. That is systemTest work and I own it. `GET /api/oauth/scopes` was already bucketed `known-fp`; this one was not.

Refs as KS-NNN text. Measured and filed by agent on Peter's behalf, 2026-09-01.

title: Verify results show the user nothing about what was registered — a renamed file confirms green with no explanation (PS-723)
description:
## BLUF

**A verify result shows the user nothing about what was registered, so a renamed file confirms green with no way to notice the rename.** Stuart hit this on PS-723 and ruled the direction: *"it should be explained to the user, otherwise confusion will result… b should also have the note to the user that the filename has changed."*

The API is not the problem — it already returns the registered `title`, `issuer` and `certifiedAt`. **The portal never displays them**, because it reads a nested shape the backend does not emit. And the portal already sends the presented filename, which the backend silently discards. So both halves of the comparison exist today and nothing joins them.

## RECOMMENDATION

Render the registered metadata beside the confirmation, plus a plain-language line that verification is **content-based** — a rename neither breaks nor fakes it. Where the presented filename differs from the registered title, say so explicitly rather than leaving the user to spot it.

One decision is **not mine and should be made before any code**: the flat-vs-nested contract question in §2. That is Peter's call.

## 1. What the verify response actually returns

Measured live, `POST /api/verification/verify` with `contentHash` — the path a renamed-file verify takes:

```
verified: true
title: "E2E Test Certificate"     <- the REGISTERED title
issuer: "demo"
documentType, status, contentHash, certifiedAt
certification: { certifiedAt, certifiedBy, certifierOrganizationId }
checks: { documentExists, hashValid, integrityVerified, ... }
```

So the metadata Stuart wants shown is already on the wire.

⚠ **The OpenAPI schema understates this. **`VerifyResponse` declares 20 properties and **none** is `title` / `originalFilename` / `registeredAt` / `registrant`; the live response carries `title` and `issuer` anyway. Same declared-vs-actual family as **KS-712** — worth fixing in the same pass so the contract stops lying about this endpoint.

## 2. Why nothing renders — the mechanism

`frontend/verifier/src/components/ResultPage.tsx:423` guards the entire "Document Details" card:

```tsx
{result.verified && result.document && ( ...Title... Issuer... )}
```

* The API returns `title` and `issuer` **at the top level** and emits **no** `document` **object** (measured top-level keys: `verified, documentId, title, documentType, status, contentHash, certifiedAt, issuer, blockchain, certification, checks, verifiedAt`).
* `result.document` is therefore undefined, the guard is falsy, and **the card never renders**.
* The portal references `result.document.*` **5** times and `result.title` **0** times. Control: `result.verified` matches **14** times, so the grep discriminates.
* The data is **not** lost in parsing — `VerifyResponseSchema` is `.passthrough()`, so the top-level `title` survives into the parsed object and is simply never read.
* The schema *does* declare `document: DocumentSummarySchema.nullable().optional()` carrying `title` + `issuer`. **The frontend was written against a nested shape the backend does not produce** — one side moved and the other did not.
* Confirmed on the path in use: all three verifier call sites hit **v1 **`/verification/verify`. v2 is a different shape entirely (`count, hash, matches, verifiedAt`) and the portal does not use it.

### The contract question — Peter's call, not to be decided in the fix

Either the **frontend reads the flat fields**, or the **backend nests them** under `document` to match the schema the client already expects. Both work; they differ in blast radius (the backend shape is consumed by the Outlook add-in and issuer too). Naming it rather than picking it.

## 3. `fileName` is already sent, and silently discarded

`frontend/verifier/src/components/VerifyPage.tsx:127` sends `{ contentHash, fileName: file.name }` and `:138` threads `fileName` into the result object. So the **client already holds both halves** of the comparison — presented name and registered title — and needs no new input to detect a mismatch.

Server-side, however:

* `VerifyRequest` declares only `documentId, hash, title, contentHash` — `fileName` **is not in the contract.**
* **No backend route handler reads it**: 0 files under `services/*/src/routes/` reference `fileName`, against a control of **8** referencing `contentHash`.

So the field is sent on every verify and thrown away. Either consume it (and declare it) or stop sending it — the current state is a silent no-op.

## 4. Scope — three surfaces, per Stuart, not just the verifier portal

His comment names them: *"This affects Outlook plug ins, and Verify functionality in 'Views' and directly from the menu."* Verify call sites in the tree:

| app | file |
| -- | -- |
| verifier portal | `frontend/verifier/src/components/VerifyPage.tsx`, `ResultPage.tsx` |
| **Outlook add-in** | `frontend/outlook-addin/src/utils/api.ts` |
| issuer portal | `frontend/issuer/src/services/api.ts`, `components/admin/ConnectorsPage.tsx` |

Whatever wording is agreed should land on all of them, or the same confusion simply moves to whichever surface is left out.

## 5. Design constraint — the KS-695 erasure interplay

**KS-695 item 2 brings** `documents.title` **INTO erasure coverage**, because S sends the real filename as `Title` on originate (`CardanoAnchorService.cs:407`). For S-originated documents that field **is** the original filename — exactly what this ticket wants displayed. Item 3 goes further: connector-scoped dissolution blanks all connector documents' titles.

So the two pull opposite ways: PS-723 wants the registered name shown; KS-695 makes that same field erasable PII that can legitimately be blank. Both are correct on their own terms.

**This must be specified, not discovered:** decide what a verify result shows for a document whose title has been erased — a blank, or an explicit *"registered name erased"* state. Rendering empty silently would recreate today's confusion in a new form.

## Not in scope here

No fix in this ticket — it is the specification and the evidence. No change to PS-723, which is Stuart's.

## Related

* **PS-723** — *Verify still confirms if filename has changed* (Stuart, 2026-09-01). The originating report and his ruling.
* **KS-712** — the declared-vs-actual spec gap this endpoint also exhibits.
* **KS-695** — `documents.title` erasure coverage; the design constraint in §5.

title: test:pr never re-imports the OpenAPI spec, so Akto scans a collection that has drifted from it — a declared operation is not a scanned one
description:
> **Origin.** Parked on [KS-712](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-712) comment `718362a9` (2026-08-28T22:30:04Z) under "Related, found today and unfiled for the same reason" — `issueCreate` was refusing workspace-wide. Filed 2026-08-29. **No new measurement was taken for this ticket**; the numbers are the ones recorded on 2026-08-28 against PR [#762](<https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/762>).

## BLUF

**Declaring an operation in the OpenAPI spec does not put it in Akto's scan collection. **`test:pr` does **not** re-import the spec — only `test:pre-merge` runs `feed-har` — so the collection Akto scans drifts away from the spec silently, and a PR that adds operations gets an Akto result that never touched them.

This is the [KS-712](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-712) premise reaching one step further than that ticket states it. KS-712 says: an operation absent from the spec is invisible to both tools. This says: an operation **present** in the spec can still be invisible to Akto.

## Measured

On PR #762, which declares four operations (`GET`/`PUT` on `/api/privacy/settings` and `/api/settings/notifications`):

| operation | occurrences in the Akto report |
| -- | -- |
| the two endpoints #762 declares | **0** |
| control endpoint A | 105 |
| control endpoint B | 7 |

The two controls are what make the zero readable: the report was produced, it was parsed, and it does contain occurrence counts — the declared endpoints simply are not in it. Without the controls, `0` and "the grep could not have matched" are the same reading.

## Why it is worth a ticket rather than a note

The failure is **silent and it points the wrong way**. An author who declares a new operation, runs `test:pr`, and sees no Akto finding on it will reasonably conclude the operation was scanned and is clean. Under the current wiring that conclusion is unsupported: the operation was never in the collection. Every "Akto clean" claim in a Test Evidence block on a spec-adding PR carries this caveat, whether or not the author knows it.

This sits directly against the merge flow adopted 2026-08-25, where the **Test Evidence block carries the testing claim**. A block that says "Akto FAIL 3, none on a touched route" is true and still misleading if the touched routes could not have been scanned.

## Not fixed, and why

Re-importing the spec into Akto **mutates harness state** — the collection is shared, and @PeterObeden has live work on it ([KS-717](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-717)). Doing it unilaterally mid-review would corrupt someone else's measurements to fix a reporting gap. It belongs with the harness owner, alongside [KS-716](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-716).

## Possible shapes (for whoever owns it — not a design commitment)

1. Have `test:pr` re-import when the spec's hash has changed since the last import — cheap, and the common case is no change.
2. Fail `test:pr` loudly when an operation touched by the diff is absent from the collection, rather than reporting a clean scan of it. This is the honesty-guard shape already used elsewhere in the harness.
3. Leave `test:pr` alone and have the Test Evidence template require the author to state Akto collection coverage explicitly, so the gap is visible rather than assumed away.

Option 2 is the one that fails closed, but it is the harness owner's call.

nodes.body:
@kamil.kreiser — could you take a look? This is your ticket and I have **not** touched it, but there is now a measured reason it matters more than when you filed it.

Re-verified today on `feature/ks-1286-…` (2026-09-28): the premise still holds exactly as you wrote it. `test:pr` is `vitest run tests/prScan.test.ts` and `test:pre-merge` / `test:security` are the same shape — **none of them import**. The import lives only in `bin/setup.ts`, run separately, so a re-import still depends on someone remembering.

**Why it now looks like the largest lever on scan coverage.** Full OWASP run on slot 2, 50,162 results:

| bucket | count | share |
|---|---|---|
| `byDesignFilter` (template did not match the endpoint) | 36,946 | **74%** |
| `rateLimited` (429, new under KS-709) | 8,730 | 17% |
| `clean` | 2,338 | 5% |
| `notApplicableStack` | 1,717 | 3% |
| `authzPrecondition` | 419 | 1% |

`byDesignFilter` is by far the biggest bucket, and Akto's `api_selection_filters` match on **parameters** — which is precisely what your measurement showed the import restores: `loadParamsOfEndpoint` saw `identityCommitment` only *after* a re-import, and collection `urlsCount` went **190 → 352**.

**I am being careful not to overclaim:** most of that 74% is legitimate (194 templates × 348 endpoints — most genuinely do not apply), and I have not measured how much a re-import would recover. It could be a few percent. But it is the only bucket big enough for the answer to matter, and nobody has measured it.

Your false-zero warning is carried forward and is the part I would most want preserved in any fix: `getCollectionEndpointCount` read **325 before and after** an import that actually took it to 361, so the result must be verified on a **fresh re-read**, never on the value the import call returns.

Not picking this up — it is assigned to you and I did not want to take it without asking. If you would rather I did the harness side, say so here.

## BLUF

**Measured today: after a spec re-import, Akto CAN see `identityCommitment` at parameter level.** This ticket's premise — that `test:pr` never re-imports, so a newly declared field is invisible to Akto — is confirmed by the fact that the re-import was what changed it.

## Evidence

Ran the OpenAPI import against the widened spec (Peter's requirement 3 on [#760](https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/760)), on a tree rebased onto `436f37bed` so it carried KS-721's field.

Two Akto instruments queried for `POST /api/anchors`:

```
/api/loadParamsOfEndpoint   identityCommitment 1x    control 'metadata' 4x
/api/fetchAllParams         identityCommitment 0x    control 'metadata' 0x
```

One instrument sees it, the other sees neither it nor the control — so the positive comes from the endpoint that actually holds request-parameter data, not from a lucky substring match.

**Collection state, before → after the import:** `OpenAPI Secuura API` urlsCount **190 → 352**, api_info **325 → 361**. 27 collections before and after, none created, none lost.

## ⚠ A false zero that will bite the next person

**The endpoint count read 325 before the import and 325 after.** `getCollectionEndpointCount` called immediately after ingest returns a stale `api_info` list; a fresh capture moments later shows 361. That is the KS-700 shape — an operation that plainly worked, reporting a number that says it did nothing. Anyone automating a re-import check against that call will conclude the import is a no-op.

Worth folding into this ticket's fix: whatever makes `test:pr` re-import should verify the result on a **re-read**, not on the value the import call returns.

## What this does not settle

The re-import here was manual and one-off. This ticket is about `test:pr` doing it as a matter of course, and that is unchanged — the next `test:pr` run still will not re-import. So the KS-712 sweep benefit remains dependent on someone remembering to import by hand.

*Measured 2026-08-31 (session 93) on the local Akto stack, from the #760 review thread. Local containers only, not a shared instance. No code written for this ticket.*

title: Declare the remaining ~157 routed-but-undocumented /api operations in the OpenAPI spec — the KS-712 remainder
description:
> **Origin.** Assembled from the measurement parked on [KS-712](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-712) comments `ae3aab1a` (the 173-op survey) and `4b388b0b` ("the remaining ~157 operations are being sized as their own ticket"), on 2026-08-28 when `issueCreate` refused workspace-wide. Filed 2026-08-29 once creation worked again. **No new measurement was taken for this ticket** — every number below is the one already recorded on KS-712 and is dated to that run.

## BLUF

KS-712 established that **173 routed** `/api` **operations are absent from the OpenAPI spec**, which makes them invisible to both Schemathesis and Akto. Two slices of that gap have since been declared:

| slice | ops | where |
| -- | -- | -- |
| MFA · wallet-auth · social sign-in | 16 | [#760](<https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/760>) |
| the two settings PUTs (+ their GETs) | 4 | [#762](<https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/762>) / [KS-719](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-719) |
| **this ticket — the remainder** | **~157** | not started |

This is the mechanical bulk of the gap. It was deliberately not attempted in the KS-712 pass: *"That is a large mechanical change and wants its own PR and its own review; flagging the scope rather than half-landing it."*

## Shape of the remainder (from the KS-712 run, 2026-08-28)

Of the 173 routed-and-undocumented operations:

* **By method:** GET 83 · POST 64 · DELETE 12 · PUT 11 · PATCH 3. **90 of 173 are write methods** — the half that matters most for an untested surface.
* **By area: **`/api/admin` 58 · `/api/auth` 14 · `/api/users` 11 · `/api/workflows` 8 · `/api/anchors` 8 · `/api/platform` 7.
* **Unauthenticated response:** 401 ×149 · 400 ×8 · 200 ×15 · 204 ×1.

Subtracting the 20 already declared, the remainder is dominated by `/api/admin` (58 operations, none declared) — a single area worth about a third of the whole job.

## Suggested order

The dependency order recorded on KS-712 was MFA → wallet-auth → social callback → the rest; the first three are done. For the remainder, largest-coherent-area-first keeps each PR reviewable:

1. `/api/admin` (58)
2. `/api/users` (11) + `/api/platform` (7)
3. `/api/workflows` (8) + `/api/anchors` (8)
4. the long tail

## Constraints that apply to every slice

* **KS-424 guard:** every new operation needs an explicit `security:` block, or `check:openapi` fails.
* **The gateway BIND-MOUNTS** `docs/openapi/secuura-api.yaml` — a spec change is published by *restarting* the gateway container, not by rebuilding an image. Verify the served spec, not the file on disk.
* Declaring an operation does **not** put it in Akto's scan collection — see the sibling ticket on `test:pr` never re-importing the spec. A slice of this work is only "covered" once both tools actually exercise it.
* Each slice will widen the Schemathesis failing set. Record the failing **set**, diff it against the previous run on the same instrument, and classify new entries rather than counting them.

## Two things this ticket is NOT

1. **Not a decision about behaviour.** Where declaring an operation would bless behaviour that has not been ruled on, split it out — that is exactly what happened with the two unauthenticated PUTs, which became KS-719 rather than being documented as-is.
2. **Not a total.** 173 is a floor, not a count: **60 of 105** `/api` **mount bindings did not resolve** to a defining file (dynamic mounts, re-exports, barrel files), so those services are counted only where they register absolute paths. The CI guard proposed on [KS-663](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-663) — assert every routed `/api` path appears in the spec — is the only thing that turns this from a survey into a number that stays true.

## Sizing

**Peter-sized, and deliberately routed to him** — this is mechanical spec authoring across ~157 operations in at least four PRs, on a surface he originally reported. Not a one-session job and not a job worth interleaving with security findings.

## Method (for the numbers above)

Recorded in full on KS-712 comment `ae3aab1a`: route registrations extracted from each service's **compiled** `/app/dist` **in the running container** (not parsed TypeScript — static parsing undercounts by 34% because a third of registrations are named exports), mount bindings resolved precisely rather than cross-producted, then **every candidate probed against the live gateway**, with the probe as the arbiter. `/api/docs/*` excluded as a Swagger catch-all that answers 200 on any nonsense path; the control that catches it is one nonsense path per prefix.

nodes.body: **BLUF:** Delivered: PR 1394 merged as 4eaf7741a6a4 on develop, which declares GET /api/anchors/tx/{txHash} in the published OpenAPI contract (`Blockchain/Dev/docs/openapi/secuura-api.yaml:14836` at b1fb543640e7), in the tree deployed to kintsugi at b1fb543640e7 (carried deploy record of 2026-11-01, not re-measured today). Left open: that is one operation. This ticket's scope is the remaining ~157 routed-but-undocumented /api operations, and the other two commits on the deployed history that mention KS-723 (KS-1175 and KS-717) are not declarations of them. The 2026-09-29 comment on the ticket asks that GET /api/anchors/{id} be taken early in slice 3.

Two of the undeclared `/api/anchors` operations are on Platform-S's hot path, so they belong early in slice 3: `GET /api/anchors/{id}` (`services/anchoring/src/index.ts:827`) and `GET /api/anchors/tx/{txHash}` (`:1089`). S's refresher polls them for every in-flight anchor (`ssd/Services/CardanoAnchor/CardanoAnchorService.cs:273-278`). The spec (2026-09-29) declares `/api/anchors`, `/thread-mint`, `/thread-state/{documentId}` and `/document/{documentId}` only. S's PS-614 gate reads the spec for verbs, so today a change to those two routes' response shape would be invisible offline.

title: The whole super-admin surface is silently unscanned — no system_admin block means the HAR replay fallback never fires (0 of 16 endpoints, incl. KS-694's GDPR routes)
description:
## BLUF

Every **super-admin-only** endpoint is invisible to Akto on a stock local checkout, and nothing says so. `config/secrets.yml` carries no `system_admin` block — `config/secrets.example.yml` documents one — so `resolveReplayTokens()` returns `adminToken: null`, the issuer→admin fallback never fires, and each endpoint `ISSUER_ADMIN` cannot get a 2xx from stays a spec-imported placeholder (`responseCode: -1`) that `api_selection_filters` excludes from **every** BOLA/BFLA/authz template.

The bias is the problem: the endpoints that are hardest to authenticate to are the privileged ones, so the harness systematically skips the surface where an authz defect matters most — and reports green.

## Measured — 2026-08-29, local slot-1 stack, Akto 2.22.2

```
collection 56068490 "OpenAPI Secuura API": 323 endpoints
  absolute (scannable)  : 307
  relative (unscannable):  16

endpoints scanned, BOLA run:
  relative : 0 / 16
  absolute : 46 / 80 sampled     <-- discriminating control
```

The 16 that never get scanned:

```
/api/admin/audit/export      /api/analytics/activity        /api/analytics/certifications
/api/analytics/governance    /api/analytics/overview        /api/analytics/revenue
/api/analytics/users         /api/analytics/verifications   /api/audit-log
/api/billing/customers/by-email  /api/gdpr/consent/check    /api/gdpr/deletion-log
/api/m365/callback           /api/oauth/authorize           /api/onedrive/files
/api/system-errors
```

The 7 `analytics` paths are excluded on purpose (`VOLATILE_PATH_RE`, KS-357). **The other 9 are not excluded by anything — they are simply unreachable by the replay persona.** They include `/api/gdpr/deletion-log`, `/api/gdpr/consent/check` and `/api/system-errors` — the exact routes **KS-694 (Urgent)** just put a role gate on, and `/api/oauth/authorize`.

Note the tell: an unscannable entry is stored as a bare path (`/api/audit-log` — the tenant-provisioning upstream path) while a scanned one is a full gateway URL (`http://localhost:6882/api/documents`). That difference is a cheap, reliable detector.

## Proof of causation

Adding the documented `system_admin` block to local `secrets.yml` (gitignored; seeded `admin@secuura.com`, per `secrets.example.yml`):

```
captured 2xx samples : 71 → 79
audit-log in api_info: /api/audit-log  →  http://localhost:6882/api/platform/audit-log
ADD_USER_ID on it    : 0 rows → 1 row
```

That change is what made **KS-708** reproducible at all. Before it, `ADD_USER_ID` reported *"188 tested, 0 vulnerable"* while never touching the endpoint under investigation.

## The documentation understates it

`secrets.example.yml:30-34` says `system_admin` is *"optional. Only needed to seed the locked-account test-role… Absent ⇒ that one role is skipped (best-effort), and* `AUTH_BYPASS_LOCKED_ACCOUNT_TOKEN_ROLE` *keeps skipping honestly."*

That is not the whole consequence. Absent, it also removes the entire super-admin surface from HAR replay, and therefore from every similarity-based authz template. Nobody reading that comment would expect it.

## Suggested shape

1. **Warn loudly when** `adminToken` **is null** — name the count of endpoints that will consequently have no 2xx sample. Silence is the actual defect; a skipped endpoint should never be indistinguishable from a clean one (the KS-700 / KS-709 principle, applied to coverage rather than results).
2. Correct the `secrets.example.yml` comment to state the coverage consequence.
3. Consider failing `test:setup` when the block is absent, or defaulting it to the seeded local admin.

## Done means

1. A run without a system-admin token says so, with the affected endpoint count.
2. `secrets.example.yml` states the real consequence.
3. The relative-vs-absolute URL split is asserted somewhere, so this cannot silently regress.

nodes.body:
## BLUF

One observation for this ticket, measured rather than reasoned: when the **issuer** token is dead, the system-admin fallback feeds the replay **completely on its own**. So the fallback does work where a `system_admin` block exists. The side effect is that every uploaded sample then carries the system-admin bearer instead of the issuer's.

## What was run

Slot 4, 2026-09-30, Akto 2.36.4, found while verifying KS-1363:

| Run | Issuer token | Replay result |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `test:pre-merge`, normal | real login | 61 samples in pass 1, **76** total, from 138 GET endpoints |
| `test:pre-merge`, `ISSUER_TOKEN=<deliberately invalid>` | invalid (every issuer GET 401s) | 61 in pass 1, **76** total, from 138 GET endpoints |

Identical counts: every endpoint the invalid issuer couldn't reach fell back to the system-admin session (`resolveReplayTokens` → `captureGetSamples` in `systemTest/akto/src/setup/harReplay.ts`), and it reached all of them.

## Why it may matter here

* The BOLA/BFLA templates then mutate a **super-admin** request, not an issuer one, and nothing in the run says which identity fed the samples. A dead issuer credential is invisible behind a full replay.
* KS-1363 now reports *whether* the replay fed, but deliberately not *as whom* (kept out of scope, per this ticket).

No code change made. Offered only as evidence for whoever picks up item 1 ("warn loudly when `adminToken` is null"), since the reverse case (a null *issuer* masked by the admin) is the same visibility gap.

title: Akto reports a PASS for a test that executed NOTHING — 'clean 0 / not-applicable 969 ✓' is a second false-zero axis that richCaptureFailed does not catch
description:
## BLUF

**KS-700 closes one false-zero axis and this is the other one.** On @PeterObeden's 2026-08-28 review run, `analytics: code injection` returned **clean 0 · not-applicable 969** and reported **✓**. The capture *succeeded* — so `richCaptureFailed` is correctly false — and the scan still measured nothing that actually executed. A green tick on zero executed requests.

⚠ **Provenance: Peter's measurement from his** `test:security` **run, not independently reproduced here.** Filed so the class is tracked rather than living in a PR thread.

## ✅ Done so far — PR [Secuura/Distributed_Secuura#1336](https://linear.app/secuura/review/ks-1286-akto-2356-honest-coverage-paced-tiers-stall-stop-and-slot-safe-cba284970402) ([KS-1286](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1286/akto-image-2222-2356-latest-paired-local-pair-verified-2026-09-28-and)), merged 2026-09-28

These sections are delivered; the ticket stays open for criteria 1 and 3 below.

* ✅ **A 429 result is no longer scored as a pass** — its own `rateLimited` bucket (it was 79% of a full scan's "passes"); COVERAGE DEGRADED when refusals outnumber what executed.
* ✅ **A zero-run report says NO COVERAGE** instead of "0 vulnerable" (the `-t` filter case in Kamil's comment).
* ✅ **Pacing** so the platform's limiter no longer decides coverage — 0 of 50,306 full-scan results refused (open decision on the platform side: [KS-1374](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1374/akto-scans-are-now-paced-to-fit-the-platforms-rate-limit-test-times)).

## Why KS-700's fix does not cover it

KS-700 distinguishes *"asked Mongo and got nothing"* (`richCaptureFailed`) from *"never asked"*. Both are about the **capture**. This is a third state the capture cannot see: **the capture worked, and what it faithfully reports is that nothing ran.** `clean 0` with `not-applicable 969` means every candidate was filtered out before a request was sent — so the ✓ attests to an empty set, not to a clean one.

Read the way a reader naturally reads it, *"analytics: code injection ✓"* means the endpoints were tested and were fine. It means neither.

`DEV-PROCESS.md` already says an Akto PASS should be read as *"nothing was reported"*, not *"nothing is there"* — this is the sharpest instance of why.

## Suggested shape

Treat **executed == 0 with a non-zero candidate count** as its own verdict, the way `richCaptureFailed` is — not PASS. Something like `NO COVERAGE — 969 candidates, 0 executed`, failing or warning per tier. The count is already computed: `executedResultCount(breakdown)` in `src/scan/runTiming.ts`, and `clean + vulnerable` is the executed figure.

Note the same shape appears in the aggregate: this session's `test:pr` runs report `not-applicable 3281` and `not-on-stack 360` against `clean ~803` — so roughly 80% of every run is filtered before a request is sent. That is not necessarily wrong, but nothing currently asserts a floor on it.

## Done means

1. A scan where a whole test category executes nothing does **not** report ✓.
2. ✅ **Done** — a control: a category that genuinely executes and is clean still passes (so the fix is not "fail everything"). Shown live on slot 2, 2026-09-28: `clean 140 · rate-limited 0` reported PASS three times in the same run.
3. Reproduced from a real run, not only a unit test — the [KS-700](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-700/akto-harness-prints-a-false-zero-when-its-mongo-capture-fails-no) review's own standard.

**BLUF:** PR 2065 makes the Akto PASS line print the rate-limited ratio beside the count. Head `9eb86dfdaa20`, READY FOR GATE, not merged. The verdict, the exit status and the COVERAGE DEGRADED threshold are unchanged, and this ticket stays open for its four scoped scans that execute nothing.

**What a run now reads.** `verdict: PASS — no vulnerabilities found · rate-limited 939 of 9543 applicable (9.8%)`. That example is the 2026-10-06 buckets published on KS-1374, fed through the shipped function; before this change that run printed a bare PASS. The figure is `rateLimitedRatio`, the one the scan metrics already record.

**Why it is your file and this was still done.** Platform K is ours and the rule is that we fix it and tell you here. Ruled by Wednesday, the fleet coordinator, 2026-11-06T07:29:54Z; not a Kam ruling. Your ruling stands: "a 429 on the auth probe is *inconclusive* — neither pass nor fail, but visible."

**Not answered.** Your question in comment 1adaebbe, whether a heavily throttled run should still be able to report PASS. The COVERAGE DEGRADED threshold stays until the controlled re-run on KS-1374 gives a figure. That re-run is owed and not yet run.

**One pin moved.** `consoleSummary.test.ts.snap` line 5 pinned the line with no ratio. It now carries it, changed by hand; that line is the whole snapshot diff.

**Measured.** Red on develop `cd773edc2bb8` by assertion: 7 of 7 cells, 0 TypeErrors. Whole Akto unit suite: before 131 files, 2194 cells passing; after 132 files, 2207 cells passing. 12 of 12 planted changes caught. Node v26.8.1, not LTS.

**Not run or not covered.** No stack and no scan, so the line has not been read from a real run. The `quality` gates of Schemathesis, Playwright and Performance were not run. The HTML report's PASS chip carries no ratio, so the console and the HTML differ on this one figure; that is not changed here.

**BLUF:** four scoped Akto scans in `test:security` currently execute nothing on `develop`. The KS-1447 gate now fails them correctly, but the HTML report headline still reads PASSED. Measured on 2026-10-27 under KS-1608, on two slots of the Mac with a `develop` control. I'm adding it here rather than raising a new ticket, because it is this ticket's symptom: clean 0, every result in skip or N/A.

**The four scans, on both builds:**

| Scan | Slot 3: KS-1608 branch `4ce20980e`, Akto 2.41.6 | Slot 4: `develop` `d54320361`, Akto 2.38.5 |
|---|---|---|
| Document BOLA | clean 0 · authz-precondition 471 · N/A 1,304 | clean 0 · authz-precondition 466 · N/A 1,299 |
| KYC object-level auth | clean 0 · authz-precondition 471 · N/A 1,304 | clean 0 · authz-precondition 466 · N/A 1,299 |
| Verifier rate limit | clean 0 · N/A 1,065 | clean 0 · N/A 1,059 |
| Cross-tenant BOLA (BUG-ISOLATION-001) | clean 0 · authz-precondition 471 · N/A 1,304 | clean 0 · authz-precondition 466 · N/A 1,299 |

Each fails with `"<scan> executed NOTHING: N result(s), 0 reached a verdict … (KS-1447)"` at `tests/fixtures.ts:140`.

**What Akto recorded** (slot 3; slot 4 has the same shape):
- **Document BOLA** (`ADD_USER_ID`, `FUZZ_USER_ID`, `REPLACE_AUTH_TOKEN`, `BFLA_INSERT_ADMIN_IN_URL_PATHS`, `BFLA_WITH_GET_METHOD`): mostly `"Request API failed authentication check, skipping execution"`. That is 140 for `BFLA_INSERT_ADMIN_IN_URL_PATHS`, 134 for `ADD_USER_ID` and 52 for `REPLACE_AUTH_TOKEN`. The rest are `api_selection_filters` mismatches.
- **Verifier rate limit** (`BYPASS_CAPTCHA_ADDING_HEADER`, `PAGINATION_MISCONFIGURATION`, `REMOVE_CAPTCHA`): every result is an `api_selection_filters` mismatch. These templates need query or captcha parameters the verifier endpoints don't have.

**A contrast, not yet explained:** on the same stack and collection, the same day, `test:pr`'s BOLA + BFLA + broken-auth scan reached 470 clean verdicts. The scoped scans in `test:security` reached none.

**The headline:** slot 4's HTML report reads **PASSED** with 0 vulnerable, while 4 of the 13 tests failed. The report's verdict reflects vulnerabilities only, not the KS-1447 gate. Slot 3's reads FAILED only because of 7 vulnerable results from other templates.

**Not established:** the root cause. I'm stating no cause and no classification beyond "present on `develop`, not introduced by KS-1608 or by Akto 2.41.6". Run directories are held locally on request.

**Ruling (Peter, 2026-10-15): Option A.** The KS-1447 zero-execution gate (`assertScanExecuted`) stays. The four scans it fails (Document BOLA, KYC Object-Level Auth, BUG-ISOLATION-001 Cross-Tenant BOLA, Verifier Rate Limit) are fixed here under KS-709, on their own branch, worktree and slot, not on KS-1447. PR #1558 merges with the security tier reported as red for those four, explained in its Test Evidence block. The gate is not loosened for them.

**BLUF:** KS-1447 now fails these runs. `assertScanExecuted` (`systemTest/akto/tests/fixtures.ts`, commit `c554b6344` on the KS-1447 branch) runs on every tier before `assertNoVulnerabilities`. It fails a scan when no result reached a verdict (clean + vulnerable + known-FP = 0). Its first live security-tier run found **4 of 13 scans that executed nothing**, and before KS-1447 all 4 were reported as PASS. The guard is in place; the four scans' preconditions are not fixed.

**Measured (slot 1, 2026-10-15, develop `0543ff1e6` with the KS-1447 harness, Akto 2.38.5, `npm run test:security`): 4 failed, 9 passed.**

| Scan | Results | Clean | Buckets |
|---|---|---|---|
| Document BOLA | 1,775 | **0** | authz-precondition 466 · not-applicable 1,309 |
| KYC Object-Level Auth | 1,775 | **0** | authz-precondition 466 · not-applicable 1,309 |
| BUG-ISOLATION-001 Cross-Tenant BOLA | 1,775 | **0** | authz-precondition 466 · not-applicable 1,309 |
| Verifier Rate Limit | 1,065 | **0** | not-applicable 1,065 |

The other 9 scans executed between 149 and 10,692 results each (the Full OWASP scan: 10,692 clean of 51,170).

**Inference (not verified):** the three BOLA/OLA scans never get the second-user ("attacker") auth role their templates need, which is the KS-314 authz-precondition class. Every applicable result therefore stops at the precondition. The rate-limit scan selects templates that don't apply to any endpoint in its scope. Both causes predate KS-1447; the new gate only stops them being reported as a pass.

**Open:** make these four scans execute something, or decide (by ruling) what each one should cover. The security tier stays red until that is done.

## Real-run reproduction for "Done means" 1 and 3 (2026-10-14): 4 of 13 security workflows execute nothing and vitest still reports ✓

**BLUF:** in today's `test:security` run (Akto 2.38.2, slot 1 of Peter's Mac, `develop` 3c0a52221), **4 of the 13 workflows executed 0 requests**: verdict `INCONCLUSIVE — no tests executed to a verdict`. The test file still reported **13 passed (13)**, exit 0. The harness labels them INCONCLUSIVE on the console and in the HTML (4 mentions, checked against results.json), so the KS-1286 work holds. But the **suite verdict is still green on an empty set**, which is criterion 1 of this ticket, now reproduced from a real run (criterion 3).

| Workflow | result docs | clean (executed) | authz-precondition | by-design N/A | templates |
| -- | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- |
| Document BOLA | 1,765 | **0** | 461 | 1,304 | 5 |
| KYC Object-Level Auth | 1,765 | **0** | 461 | 1,304 | 5 |
| Cross-Tenant BOLA (BUG-ISOLATION-001) | 1,765 | **0** | 461 | 1,304 | 5 |
| Verifier Rate Limit | 1,059 | **0** | 0 | 1,059 | 3 |

* **Deterministic:** identical counts in the full run and two targeted re-runs on 2.38.2, **and** in a control run on Akto **2.37.1** against the same platform build. So it is **not** caused by the Akto bump (KS-1478).
* The first three are the same 5-template BOLA/BFLA set (`ADD_USER_ID`, `FUZZ_USER_ID`, `REPLACE_AUTH_TOKEN`, `BFLA_INSERT_ADMIN_IN_URL_PATHS`, `BFLA_WITH_GET_METHOD`). The dominant skip reason, from Akto's own rows, is *"Request API failed authentication check, skipping execution"* on 321 endpoints.
* Akto's auth detection is populated (all 354 `api_info` rows have `allAuthTypesFound`: 319 `BEARER`, 29 `UNAUTHENTICATED`, 6 both), so it is not a "calc job hasn't run" timing issue.
* **Cause not established.** KS-1440 (2026-10-07) recorded only **1** INCONCLUSIVE workflow, and its run archive is no longer on disk to compare. One candidate, **not verified**: KS-1032 (merged 2026-10-13) makes originate drop identity/tenant/role headers when `GATEWAY_VOUCH_SECRET` is unset (KS-1083; see KS-955 for the measured effect on the tenant tests).

**Decisive check (for whoever picks this up):** on a slot with `GATEWAY_VOUCH_SECRET` set, run `npx vitest run tests/securityWorkflows.test.ts -t "document endpoints: BOLA/IDOR"`. If `clean` becomes > 0, KS-1032 / KS-1083 is the cause. If it stays 0, look at the BOLA templates' role/auth configuration.

**Acceptance criterion to add (a test demonstrating the fix):** a workflow whose candidate count is > 0 and whose executed count is 0 fails its test (or is reported `NO COVERAGE` and counted against the tier). A unit test proves a stubbed `clean 0 / authz 461 / N/A 1,304` run is **not** a pass, and its control (`clean > 0`) still passes.

## Data point: another INCONCLUSIVE that vitest passes (Akto 2.37.1, slot 1, 2026-10-07)

In the one `test:security` run, the workflow **Public Verifier security > verifier: rate limiting enforced** scanned 3 templates over 350 endpoints (1,050 results) and the console printed `verdict: INCONCLUSIVE — no tests executed to a verdict`. Vitest still listed it as passed (✓, 18.8 s).

So the console and the HTML report are honest about it, and the test assertion is the part that is not, which matches the narrowing already recorded on this ticket. No change was made for it in PR #1411.

## BLUF — reproduced today on the security tier, and the gap is narrower than the title implies: the *report* already refuses to show it green, the *vitest assertion* does not Re-verified from source 2026-10-05, prompted by a sweep on the rebuilt slot 4. This ticket is still live, and I can narrow where the hole actually is. ### Current measurement `npm run test:security` on slot 4 today (recorded on KS-1408): **4 workflows executed nothing — reported INCONCLUSIVE — yet the suite still showed ✓ and the run was treated as a pass.** That is this ticket's false-zero axis, observed on the tier that matters most. ### The narrowing: the reporting layer is already correct The anti-false-green guard **exists and works** in the report path. Measured at `origin/develop` @ `22b268143`: | site | behaviour | | -- | -- | | `src/report/consoleSummary.ts:250-255` | *"Verdict keys on vulnerabilities alone; INCONCLUSIVE (not green) when nothing executed"* → renders `INCONCLUSIVE — no tests executed to a verdict` | | `src/report/reportHtml.ts:248` | emits `INCONCLUSIVE` | | `docs/how-to-test-with-akto.md:494` | *"**INCONCLUSIVE** — No vulnerabilities **and** nothing executed to a verdict (`clean + vulnerable == 0`) — **never shown green** (preserves the anti-false-green guard)"* | So the run *tells the truth on screen*. **What does not act on it is the test assertion.** The verdict is computed, rendered, documented as never-green — and then the suite passes anyway. The gap is the step between `INCONCLUSIVE` and the exit status, not the detection of it. That is a materially smaller fix than "teach Akto to notice", and it means the detection logic is already there to assert against. ### Why this matters more than its Low priority suggests This is the **fourth instrument** in the family KS-1063 named as a design question rather than a run of bugs: | instrument | how a non-run reads as a pass | ticket | | -- | -- | -- | | `preflight.sh` leg count | `PREFLIGHT PASSED.` identical whether 13 legs ran or 10 | KS-1046 | | service unit suites | blocking gate automated nowhere, `develop` stays red | KS-1051 | | pre-push hook + `check-package-format.sh` | exit 0 over `0 packages checked, 4 skipped` | KS-1063 (fix shape 1 shipped #1353) | | **Akto security tier** | **4 workflows execute nothing, verdict says INCONCLUSIVE, suite still ✓** | **this one** | KS-1063's fix is the precedent and the shape: `check-package-format.sh` now prints `NOTHING CHECKED … This is NOT a formatting failure` and **exits 1**. The same rule applied here would be: a tier in which any workflow executed nothing does not pass. ### Suggested done-means - A scan run where ≥1 workflow is `INCONCLUSIVE` **fails** the suite, with a message naming which workflows executed nothing and why that is not a formatting/vulnerability failure. - Red→green proven both ways: a run with an inconclusive workflow fails before and after; a run where every workflow executed passes unchanged. - The distinction between *no vulnerabilities found* and *nothing ran* is visible in the exit status, not only in the HTML. ### Assignment note, not an action This is filed to @kamil.kreiser, but the whole fix lives in `systemTest/akto/`. By the standing split — platform-k work outside `systemTest/` to Kamil, the test estate to Peter — this looks like Peter's. Flagging rather than reassigning; it is your ticket. *Posted by Claude at Peter's request, 2026-10-05. Code read at `origin/develop` @ `22b268143`; run figures from the slot-4 security tier recorded on KS-1408 today. The akto unit suite itself is green — 1,901/1,901 measured the same day — so this is not a suite-health problem, it is a verdict-to-exit-status problem.*

## 2026-10-05: reproduced from a real run (criterion 3), with the cause in source

**BLUF.** A live `test:security` run on 2026-10-05 reproduced this ticket's class four times. Four workflows executed **nothing** and Akto's own verdict says **INCONCLUSIVE**, yet each shows ✓ in vitest. The console and HTML are already honest (they print INCONCLUSIVE, "not shown as a pass"). The gap is the **test assertion**, which only ever checks for vulnerabilities.

>>> Evidence

* **Run:** platform-k slot 4 rebuilt from KS-1408 head `941e930aa` (all of today's `develop`), Akto 2.36.10, `security-ks-1408-2026-10-05T12-14-19Z`. Across 13 workflows: 8 PASS, 3 FAIL (one LOW; that's KS-1421), **4 INCONCLUSIVE, "no tests executed to a verdict"**. Vitest: 12 passed, 1 failed.
* **Example:** *Document Lifecycle security › document endpoints: BOLA/IDOR*: `1740 results (0 executed)`, buckets `clean 0 · vulnerable 0 · authz-precondition 447 · not-applicable 1293`, and vitest still ✓ (20.6 s).
* **Cause (develop `d784b613c`):** `assertNoVulnerabilities` (`systemTest/akto/tests/fixtures.ts:92-104`) throws only when `CRITICAL + HIGH + MEDIUM + LOW + vulnerable > 0`. It never checks that anything executed. Every workflow in `tests/securityWorkflows.test.ts` uses it (`:132, :146, :174, :190, :204, :232, :249, :264, :291`, …). Meanwhile `src/report/consoleSummary.ts:250-255` and `src/report/reportHtml.ts:248` already compute INCONCLUSIVE for the same result, so the three surfaces disagree: console and HTML say INCONCLUSIVE, the vitest gate says pass.
* **Suggested shape, unchanged from above:** fail (or mark as a distinct non-pass) when `clean + vulnerable == 0` with a non-zero candidate count, using the executed figure the report already derives. The 2026-09-28 control (`clean 140` → PASS) still stands as criterion 2.

Linked: KS-1421 (the other `test:security` gap found in the same run) · KS-1408 (where it was measured).

>>>

@kamil.kreiser — for when you have a moment, since this is your ticket and I've changed something next to it rather than closing it. No rush, and nothing is blocked on it.

In short: the 429 case is fixed and verified live, but your three "Done means" criteria are untouched — a category with `clean 0 / not-applicable 969` and no throttling still shows ✓.

Two things I'd value your view on:

1. **Where the `rateLimited` bucket sits.** I kept it inside the applicable denominator, on the reasoning that the test could have applied and the platform simply refused it — so a throttled run reads as reduced coverage rather than a smaller surface. Treating it like `byDesignFilter` and excluding it is the alternative; it would keep the ratios kinder, but perhaps too kind. Happy to go either way.

2. **Whether a heavily throttled run should still be able to report PASS.** Today it can, if even a few results ran clean. On the pre-merge tier that was 8,120 of 9,180 "passes" being 429s (since reduced by pacing on the branch). It feels like the same family as criteria 1–3, so perhaps one fix covers both.

Thank you.

## Live results after the fix — all three tiers re-run on slot 2

Akto 2.35.6, slot 2, 2026-09-28, branch head `ba1d0d15a` (now inside the squashed KS-1286 commit). All figures measured.

| tier | results | clean (before) | clean (after) | rate-limited | passes that tested nothing | verdict | wall |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `test:pr` | 8,702 | 508 | 401 | 107 | **21%** | PASS | 27.6s |
| `test:pre-merge` | 20,911 | 9,180 | 1,060 | 8,120 | **88%** | PASS | 44.5s |
| `test:security` (full OWASP) | 50,162 | 11,068 | 2,338 | 8,730 | **79%** | FAIL (1 LOW) | 423.8s |

The pre-merge gate is the one that matters most: 8,120 of its 9,180 passes were the platform answering 429. (Since then, pacing on the branch has brought refused results on the full scan to 0.)

>>> Verdicts, the control, and what's still open

**Verdicts behave as this ticket asks.** The security tier produced 5 INCONCLUSIVE verdicts, two of them new and exactly this ticket's case:

* `clean 0 · not-applicable 4036 · rate-limited 140` → INCONCLUSIVE (was `clean 140` → PASS)
* `clean 0 · authz-precondition 84 · not-applicable 6018 · rate-limited 586` → INCONCLUSIVE (was `clean 586` → PASS)

**The control from "Done means" (2) holds:** a category that genuinely ran clean still passes — `clean 140 · rate-limited 0` appears three times and reports PASS each time.

`otherError` stayed **0%** on every run — the fix moved only the intended results.

**Still open:** criteria 1–3 (`clean 0 / not-applicable 969` with no throttling still shows ✓). `executedResultCount(breakdown)` in `src/scan/runTiming.ts` is the hook; set any floor from post-fix numbers.

**Commits:** `b2aac1ea9` (the bucket + `rateLimitedBucket.test.ts`, 10 cases, red before / green after) and `ba1d0d15a` (pipeline built once via `bucketStagesExpr()`, pinned by `bucketPipeline.test.ts`). Gates green; 1307/1307 unit at the time.

**One honesty note:** the first `bucketPipeline.test.ts` had a false green — `expect(indexOf(a)).toBeLessThan(indexOf(b))` passes when `a` is absent (`-1`). It was caught by breaking the source on purpose. Presence is now asserted separately, and two older assertions with the same shape were hardened.

>>>

## The 429 instance is fixed — this ticket's own "Done means" is still open

A short update to my note above. The rate-limited-counted-as-clean case is fixed on the KS-1286 branch (`b2aac1ea9`). That's a different instance of the same false-pass family, not this ticket's fix: criteria 1–3 (`executed == 0` against a non-zero candidate count) are still open.

>>> What changed, and the proof

**Cause:** `bucketSwitchExpr()` in `src/report/skipBuckets.ts` keyed on `testResults[].errors` and ended `default:"clean"`; a 429 carries no error, so it fell into `clean`.

**Measured** (slot 2, Akto 2.35.6, run `6aba139ce86558333055a8f9`): 8,735 of 50,018 results carried a 429, none with an error, all classified `clean` — 79% of that run's 11,038 "passes". Across all 30 stored runs: 29,642 of 274,351 results.

**The change:** a `rateLimited` bucket, evaluated last before the default, so it only catches results that previously reached `clean`. It stays in the applicable denominator (the test could have applied; the platform refused it), so a throttled run reads as reduced coverage. Carried through console, `<hexId>.report.json` and the HTML from the shared formatters. `bin/skip-baseline.ts` now builds the same pipeline, so the baseline classifies like production.

**Proof:** `tests/unit/report/rateLimitedBucket.test.ts` (10 cases, red on the old code, green after); `scan:skip-baseline` re-classifies that run as `rateLimited=8735 / clean=2303`, with `otherError` 0% on every run.

**For whoever picks up criteria 1–3:** `executedResultCount(breakdown)` in `src/scan/runTiming.ts` is still the hook, and any executed-vs-candidates floor is best set from post-fix figures — pre-fix `clean` was inflated by up to 79%.

>>>

## Another way into the same false-pass family: rate-limited results counted as clean

> **Update 2026-09-28: fixed on the KS-1286 branch** (`b2aac1ea9`, now inside the squashed branch commit) — 429 results have their own `rateLimited` bucket. The comments below record the fix and its live results.

Seen on slot 2, 2026-09-28, Akto 2.35.6, while bumping the image for KS-1286. It isn't this ticket's `clean 0 / not-applicable 969` axis, nor KS-700's capture failure — it's a `clean` count that included results the platform refused with 429.

>>> The measurement, the cause, and where the fault sits

Full OWASP run, summary `6aba139ce86558333055a8f9`, 347 endpoints, 194 templates, 50,018 results:

| | |
| -- | -- |
| results whose captured response was a 429 | **8,735** |
| …of those with an error recorded | **0** |
| …bucketed by our `bucketSwitchExpr()` as | **`clean` — all 8,735** |
| the run's total `clean` | **11,038** |
| share of `clean` that was a rate-limited non-test | **79%** |
| endpoints affected | **290 of 347** |

The verdict was PASS apart from one unrelated LOW. Re-derived with a second, independently written query: 8,735 both times.

**Why:** `src/report/skipBuckets.ts` keyed every non-clean branch on `testResults[].errors` and defaulted to `clean`. Akto records a 429 as a completed result with no error, so it fell through. The status code was in the captured `testResults[].message` all along; we just weren't reading it.

**The ruling it restores** — already carried verbatim in `systemTest/schemathesis/config/auth_probe_checks.py`:

> **Ruling (Peter, 2026-09-18):** a 429 on the auth probe is *inconclusive* — neither pass nor fail, but visible.

**Where the fault sits**

* **systemTest (ours)** — the fall-through to `clean`, now fixed.
* **Akto (contributing, not ours to change)** — records a 429 without an error, and `api/fetchTestRunStatusSummaries` samples only the first 3,000 non-vulnerable results, so it reported 51 where the true figure was 8,735 (`TestRunStatusHelper.SAMPLE_LIMIT`, v2.35.6).
* **Platform (working as designed)** — the gateway's global limiter (`RATE_LIMIT_MAX_REQUESTS=2000`, `RateLimit-Policy: 2000;w=60`). A 194-template scan over 347 endpoints simply exceeds it.

The exact status histogram added on the branch is what made this visible.

>>>

## A third door into the same failure, found while reproducing KS-708

Not the `clean 0 / not-applicable 969` axis this ticket describes, and not KS-700's capture failure — a **third** way to get a green tick over an empty set, and the cheapest one to hit by accident.

A `-t` filter that matches no test name runs nothing and still reports success:

```
npx vitest run tests/securityWorkflows.test.ts -t "Cross-Tenant BOLA"

 ↓ 13 tests, all skipped
 Test Files  1 skipped (1)
      Tests  13 skipped (13)
=== VITEST EXIT: 0 ===

[report] report written: ks708-repro-2026-08-28T14-19-10Z-report.html
         (0 runs, 0 vulnerable, 0 issue card(s))
```

`"Cross-Tenant BOLA"` is the `label:` passed to `runner.run()`, not the vitest test name (`[slow] Akto BOLA scan finds no cross-tenant object-level auth bypass`). An easy mistake, and the output for it is **exit 0 plus an HTML report asserting `0 vulnerable`** — indistinguishable at a glance from a scan that ran and found nothing.

Had I trusted it, I would have reported KS-708 as not reproducible. It reproduces.

## Why it belongs on this ticket

Same principle: **a report must not describe an empty set in the language of a clean one.** This ticket's suggested shape — treat `executed == 0` against a non-zero candidate count as its own verdict — covers this case too, if the check sits at report-generation rather than inside a single scan. `0 runs` should render as `NO COVERAGE`, never as `0 vulnerable`.

Cheap independent guard: fail when a `-t` filter selects zero tests. Vitest has no built-in for it, but the report generator already knows the run count.

## Related

The same reproduction also turned up **KS-715** (capture dies on ENOBUFS → no verdict) and **KS-716** (the super-admin surface is never scanned, so `ADD_USER_ID` reported "188 tested, 0 vulnerable" while never touching the endpoint under investigation). Three different ways to read a zero that was never measured, in one session.

title: Give the dev-ps Entra tenant its own Azure subscription and its own Verified ID authority — it is borrowing Obeden's
description:
> **Re-checked 2026-09-08** (see the comment of that date): a real presentation has now completed on dev-ps (09-04), but it stored nothing that references the verifier authority, so the migration is still config + documents only; dev-ps’s verifier DID is `did:web:dev-ps.secuura.net`, a domain-named DID whose *string* survives a move to a new tenant (only the keys and the two `.well-known` documents change); and Microsoft’s Admin API docs state *“currently only one authority is supported”* per tenant, which settles step 1 and makes this a prerequisite for a supported production authority rather than tidy-up. The text below is kept as written.

## The interim arrangement

Entra Verified ID is being onboarded in **Obeden** for testing, because that is where an Azure subscription and Key Vault (`secuura-ps-dev-kv`) already exist. The dev-ps auth tenant — **Secuura Platform S Dev**, `secpsdev.onmicrosoft.com`, `eb25c656-754b-49d2-9dc2-864317c843ac` — is Entra ID Free with no subscription attached, so it cannot host a Key Vault and cannot complete Verified ID onboarding.

That gets dev-ps a working verifier. It is not where this should end up.

## Why it should not stay there

* **A dev DID would live in a directory that matters.** The same reasoning `docs/sso-tenant-configuration.md` applies to app registrations — *"a dev-stage registration then lives in a directory that matters; a throwaway avoids that entirely"*.
* **Possible dead end for production.** It is unconfirmed whether one tenant can host more than one Verified ID authority. If it cannot, a future production authority in Obeden collides with the dev one, and this migration stops being tidy-up and becomes a prerequisite. **Establish this first** — it decides the priority of everything below.
* dev-ps's auth tenant is deliberately separate (the A/B/C model in `docs/sso-tenant-configuration.md`). Its Verified ID authority should follow the same boundary.

## What the work actually is

**Not** "move the tenant under the Secuura directory" — Entra directories do not nest. There is no parent/child. The work is: **attach a subscription to** `secpsdev`, then onboard Verified ID in it.

**Do NOT transfer the subscription that hosts dev-ps.** `ssd/dep-az-dev/setenv.sh:9-11` authenticates to Key Vault with the VM's **system-assigned managed identity**. Managed identities are tenant-bound: a Change-directory wipes them along with every RBAC assignment, and Key Vault's own `tenantId` stops matching. dev-ps would silently lose the ability to render its own config on the next deploy.

The route is a **new** subscription on `secpsdev`. Per `docs/sso-tenant-configuration.md`, after 15 Aug 2026 a **free Azure account** is the sanctioned way to get a directory with a subscription attached — the same pattern the doc already recommends for tenant C.

## Steps

1. Confirm whether a tenant can hold multiple Verified ID authorities. This sets the priority.
2. Attach a subscription to `secpsdev` (free Azure account, or a new pay-as-you-go).
3. Key Vault in that subscription — **Permission Model: Vault Access Policy**, not Azure RBAC. The portal now defaults to RBAC and Verified ID cannot manage its keys under it.
4. Onboard Verified ID; trusted domain `https://dev-ps.secuura.net`.
5. New app registration in `secpsdev` with the application permission `VerifiableCredential.Create.PresentRequest` on resource `3db474b9-6a0c-4840-96ac-1fceb342124f`, plus tenant admin consent.
6. Repoint dev-ps configuration and **republish the** `.well-known` **documents** — see the migration cost below.
7. Decommission the Obeden authority once dev-ps verifies against the new one.

## Migration cost — the DID changes

A new authority means a **new DID**, so this is not a config-only swap. All of these move:

| What | Why |
| -- | -- |
| `EntraVerifiedId:Authority` | new tenant GUID — tenant-specific, `/organizations` does not work for client credentials |
| `EntraVerifiedId:ClientId` / `ClientSecret` | new registration, new Key Vault secrets |
| `EntraVerifiedId:VerifierAuthority` | **the DID itself changes** |
| `.well-known/did.json` + `did-configuration.json` | regenerated by the new authority and republished via `WellKnownController` |
| `Person.IdToken3` on anyone verified against the old authority | subject DIDs issued under the retired authority no longer resolve to a trusted verifier |

That last row is the reason to do this **before** any real verification traffic, not after. Nobody has completed a presentation yet, so today the cost is zero.

## Acceptance

* **Step 1 is answered with a dated citation, before anything else is done.** Microsoft's Admin API documentation line that only one authority is supported per tenant is quoted with the date it was read — the 2026-09-08 re-check already relies on it, and it is what makes this a prerequisite for a supported production authority rather than tidy-up. If that line has changed, the ticket's priority changes with it.
* A subscription is attached to `secpsdev` via a **new** free or pay-as-you-go account. **The subscription hosting dev-ps is not transferred** — and the acceptance states positively that dev-ps's system-assigned managed identity still works: `ssd/dep-az-dev/setenv.sh` renders config successfully on the next deploy, and Key Vault's `tenantId` still matches. A Change-directory would have wiped the identity and every RBAC assignment silently.
* The new Key Vault's permission model is **Vault Access Policy, not Azure RBAC** — confirmed by `az keyvault show` reporting `enableRbacAuthorization: false`, because the portal now defaults to RBAC and Verified ID cannot manage its keys under it.
* The app registration in `secpsdev` carries the **application** permission `VerifiableCredential.Create.PresentRequest` on resource `3db474b9-6a0c-4840-96ac-1fceb342124f` with **tenant admin consent granted** — `AcquireTokenForClient(".default")` fails outright without pre-consented app permissions, so an un-consented registration looks configured and does not work.
* Each of the five moving config values is repointed per the migration table, by **key name only** — `EntraVerifiedId:Authority`, `ClientId`, `ClientSecret`, `VerifierAuthority`. No secret value is opened, read or quoted; the Key Vault secret names are named and the step handed over.
* Both `.well-known` documents are regenerated by the new authority and republished through `WellKnownController`, and **resolve on the domain in the DID**: `curl -s https://dev-ps.secuura.net/.well-known/did.json` returns a document whose `id` equals the new `EntraVerifiedId:VerifierAuthority`, and `did-configuration.json` resolves too — `validateLinkedDomain = true` means both must, or presentation fails.
* The Obeden authority is decommissioned **only after** dev-ps verifies against the new one, and the `Person.IdToken3` consequence is recorded as nil because nobody has a subject DID under the retired authority worth preserving. The 09-04 presentation stored nothing referencing the verifier authority — restate that as the reason the cost is zero, so a later reader does not assume it was overlooked.

**No Playwright test applies, and the local suite cannot stand in for one.** The change is Azure tenancy plus per-environment configuration; nothing in platform-s code changes except which values a deployment renders. Worse, a local slot *cannot* exercise this path at all — Entra Verified ID's Start POST is refused by Microsoft on every `localhost` callback, so a local row goes `Rejected` immediately and never produces a QR. A spec written against a slot would prove nothing about the new authority.

The verifiable criteria are the deployed-environment checks above: the two `curl` results on `dev-ps.secuura.net` with the DID `id` matching `VerifierAuthority`, the `az keyvault show` permission-model field, the consent state on the registration, and one real presentation completing on dev-ps against the new authority.

**Controls that must keep passing unchanged:** `systemTest/tests/functional/well_known_did.spec.ts` — it already asserts the `.well-known` routes serve what the controller is configured with, so a repoint that breaks the *route* rather than the value turns it red; and `systemTest/tests/functional/entra_verify_flow.spec.ts`, whose local expectation is the `Rejected` outcome described above and which must not be "fixed" into self-gating on whether Entra is configured — both directions of that gate fire locally.

## Notes

Raised 2026-08-27 while stepping through [PS-684](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-684/entra-verified-id-azure-tenant-setup-and-config-values-needed-before) for dev-ps.
