## BLUF — routed here, not filed as a new ticket, and it is time-sensitive
**PR #889 (KS-597) changes the blast radius of the cascade delete at
`services/originate/src/routes/adminConfig.ts:838` from ZERO rows to real rows.** The endpoint and
its authz gap are pre-existing and are this ticket's class; **what changes is the consequence.**
Raised by the round-1 QA gate on #889 as MAJOR and explicitly out of scope for that PR — its own
words were *"the one I would not want quietly filed."*

## RECOMMENDATION
**Whoever owns this should look before the KS-597 backfill runs.** Kam authorised that backfill at
10:34 today as its own round after the fix merges — so this lands directly in front of a round that
already has a yes. No action is being asked of #889; it is not gated on this.

## DETAIL — verified independently at #889's head, not taken on report
```
adminConfig.ts:37-38   adminConfigRouter.use(authenticate(), requireRole('SYSTEM_ADMIN', 'ORG_ADMIN'));
adminConfig.ts:827     adminConfigRouter.delete('/organizations/:id', ...)
adminConfig.ts:837     const result = await runWithPlatformScope(async () => {
adminConfig.ts:838       await db.$executeRaw`DELETE FROM documents WHERE issuer_organization_id = ${orgId}::uuid`;
```
A hard delete, under **platform scope with RLS bypassed**, with **no tenant predicate**, on a router
any **ORG_ADMIN in any tenant** reaches.

**Why it was inert until now:** the column was populated on no rows, so the DELETE removed nothing.
Measured read-only on the local dev database just now: **59 documents, 0 carrying an
`issuer_organization_id`** (control: 6 organizations, so the query discriminates). The gate measured
the same shape at larger scale — 0 of 95,127.

**Why it stops being inert:** #889 is the change that starts populating that column at registration.
Once it does, deleting an organisation destroys every document attributed to it — and by the same
gate's **Finding 1**, which documents those are is decided by an **unverified request-body field**
(the issuing organisation is taken from the body with no check that the caller belongs to it).
Finding 1 is carded to Kam as a product question and is NOT being decided here.

On a document-authenticity product, registered documents are the unrecoverable asset. Flagging the
combination — an unverified attribution field feeding an unscoped hard delete reachable by
ORG_ADMIN — rather than either half alone.

Siblings for context, not duplicates: KS-643, KS-692 (same authz class, different verbs); KS-239 and
KS-695 own the erasure semantics.

**State on 2026-09-02, after today's landings — still In Progress, correctly.**

**On `develop` (merge `a1fa3ae`, 08:52Z, via the review-queue drain PR #735):** PS-729 (deactivated users now reach `/AccountDeactivated`, not the failed-attempts Lockout copy) and PS-730 (`/OrgDocuments` at full functional parity with `/MyDocuments`, plus its follow-ups PS-739 — account admins may assign signing rights org-wide — and #737, Declare aligned to the CertifyController role rule). Both sub-issues are Done with their gate results attached.

**What keeps this open:** PS-701 (phase 6) stays In Review because its acceptance is the live S→K erasure round-trip, and KS-695 (Kamil) is still Todo, unstarted. The `@k-live` erasure specs are unwritten as well as unrun. The epic's own verify list still owes the production orphan pre-check (with a `mysqldump` before the FK migration's DDL) — UAT and dev-ps were checked clean on 31 Aug, production never.

**Deployment (checked read-only via SSM today):** UAT runs the `uat/bug-fixes` image `b5250cb` built 27 Aug and started 28 Aug — nothing merged to `develop` since then is on UAT, this epic included. Production runs the legacy `release/production-Apr-4-26` image, up five weeks. So no PS-690 behaviour is in front of a user yet; the "org admins immediately gain org-wide reach" customer note from the merge comment applies at whichever deploy carries `56f3ad4` or later.

## Defect found in manual testing: a deactivated user is told the wrong thing at sign-in

⚠️ **This should be its own ticket** — Stuart asked for one, but Linear refused creation: *"You've exceeded the free issue limit for this workspace."* That cap has bitten before (it blocks issue **creation** only). Filing here on the parent so the trail exists; please promote it to a real issue once the cap is cleared.

**Defect in delivered PS-698 work (PS-690 phase 3), found by Stuart after the merge to develop.**

### What happens
An org admin deactivates a member. The member's next sign-in shows `/Identity/Account/Lockout`:

> **Account temporarily locked** — This account has been temporarily locked because of repeated failed sign-in attempts. Please try again later…

Every clause is wrong for this state: it is not temporary, it was not caused by failed attempts, and "try again later" is false — nothing changes until an admin reactivates.

### Why
Deactivation kills sign-in with `SetLockoutEndDateAsync(user, DateTimeOffset.MaxValue)` (`PersonController.cs:646`). Identity reports `IsLockedOut`, **indistinguishable** from a real failed-attempt lockout, and every sign-in route sends that to the generic Lockout page.

`/AccountDeactivated` — written for exactly this state, its doc-comment noting Lockout's "copy is about failed sign-in attempts; this state is deliberate and admin-made" — is only reached from `TenantResolutionMiddleware`, i.e. an **already-signed-in** session. A user who signed out, or returns later, never sees it. The page is unreachable on the most common path.

### Scope — five sites, so SSO and 2FA users see it too
- `Areas/Identity/Pages/Account/Login.cshtml.cs:208` (password) and `:623` (its 2FA branch)
- `Areas/Identity/Pages/Account/ExternalLogin.cshtml.cs:243` (Entra/Google/GitHub/Apple)
- `Areas/Identity/Pages/Account/LoginWith2fa.cshtml.cs:137`
- `Areas/Identity/Pages/Account/LoginWithRecoveryCode.cshtml.cs:78`

### Fix (agreed with Stuart)
A **specific message per state**: `Person.DeactivatedAt != null` → `/AccountDeactivated`; otherwise the existing Lockout page, whose copy is correct for the case it actually describes. One shared helper rather than five copies — `Login.cshtml.cs` already injects `ApplicationDbContext`.

**Accepted trade-off:** this tells an unauthenticated caller "deactivated" rather than "locked" — a small enumeration signal. It does not meaningfully widen what exists: the Lockout page already confirms the account exists, versus "Invalid login attempt." for an unknown email, an asymmetry `account_security.spec.ts` already pins.

### Tests
- Source-scan contract test pinning that **every** `IsLockedOut` redirect routes through the shared helper, so a sixth site cannot quietly reintroduce the wrong page.
- Unit coverage for the deactivated-vs-locked decision.
- **Invert `person_deactivation.spec.ts`**, which asserts `/Lockout/i` today — it codified the defect as expected and passed while the user was told something untrue. That inversion is the red-provable change.

### How it escaped
The phase-3 spec verified the *mechanism* (sign-in refused) without checking that what the user is **told** is true. Worth carrying forward: a refusal test should assert the destination's meaning, not merely that a refusal happened.

**Merged to `develop`** — [PR #662](https://github.com/Secuura/platform-s/pull/662), merge commit `56f3ad4`. All seven phases are now on develop.

**Verified after the merge, on develop's own tip:**
- `dotnet build` clean, **xUnit 2,494 / 2,494** — this is the first run of PS-690 together with develop's newest 12 commits (PS-703, PS-705, PS-712–715), a combination that had never been tested before the merge.
- All five migrations present on develop: `Ps690DocumentStoreOrganisationFk`, `Ps690SendDocsLinksCreatedByRestrict`, `Ps690PersonDeactivation`, `Ps690PersonErasure`, `Ps690OrganisationDissolution`.
- Pre-merge evidence (branch head `42ebc4b`): full Playwright suite **638 passed / 4 failed / 8 skipped** on stack slot 2, all 15 PS-690 legs green; the 4 failures were pre-existing identity ones that develop's PS-703 has since addressed on its side.

**Deployment pre-check — the FK migration's guard, run read-only against both boxes:**

| | UAT | dev-ps |
|---|---|---|
| Orphan `DocumentStore` rows | **0** | **0** |
| Orphan `SendDocsLinks.CreatedBy` | **0** | **0** |
| Documents / Organisations | 44 / 15 | 2 / 9 |

Both clean, so `Ps690DocumentStoreOrganisationFk`'s `SIGNAL` guard will not fire and the constraint applies. **Production has NOT been checked** — it is the only box where a hand-deleted organisation is plausible, and per the standing rule it should also get a `mysqldump` before any DDL runs.

**What a deploy changes for existing users:** anyone holding `SsdOrganisation` or `SsdAccountAdmin` immediately gains reach over every document in their own organisation (new `/OrgDocuments` surface plus the verb set across nine controllers), scoped strictly same-org. That is PS-690's intent, but it is a visible product change worth flagging to affected customers rather than letting them discover it.

**Nothing changes on the blockchain.** No migration touches `DocumentTransaction`; `PayloadJson` stays byte-untouched; no anchor is rewritten and no new anchor traffic starts by itself. The two new sweeps idle on empty tables.

**Still open:** PS-701 stays In Review. `PlatformKErasureClient` is live in DI, but KS-695 has not shipped, so if anyone performs an erasure or dissolves a K-registered org before it does, K answers 404 and the sweep retries unbounded (~every 30s) until the route exists. Correct by design, but worth knowing.

**All seven phases complete on `project/ps-690-org-owned-docs`; the project→develop PR is open for review: [PR #662](https://github.com/Secuura/platform-s/pull/662).**

| Phase | Ticket | State | PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 Ownership contracts + data model | PS-696 | Done | #654 |
| 2 Org-wide visibility | PS-697 | Done | #655 |
| 3 Person deactivation | PS-698 | Done | #656 |
| 4 S-side GDPR erasure | PS-699 | Done | #657 |
| 5 Organisation dissolution | PS-700 | Done | #658 |
| 6 S→K erasure bridge | PS-701 | **In Review** (k-live blocked on KS-695) | #659 |
| 7 End-to-end verification | PS-702 | Done | #661 |

**Verification on the branch with develop merged in (`60ea07d`):**
- xUnit **2,410 / 2,410** (2,246 when the project started).
- Playwright **621 passed / 5 failed / 7 skipped** on stack slot 2 (`ssd-ps702`, 172.31/16, ports +100 — never the shared `:5122`; torn down scoped, 0 containers / 0 volumes). All five failures pre-existing and unrelated, verified in code: three provider tests expect a `hosted session`/`assessor` wording that exists nowhere in the app; one expects an account admin to reach `/PolicyAdmin`, Administrator-only since PS-444; `login_return_url` failed a different test on each of two runs.
- Offline systemTest gates: prettier, tsc, eslint 0/0, knip, `test:unit` **251 / 251**.
- All five new migrations applied on a **fresh** database during the slot-2 build.
- Every behaviour change red-proven against the branch's own prior code.

**Still owed:** the `@k-live` erasure round-trips, blocked on **KS-695** (Kamil). The S-side bridge is complete and its wire contract is the repo's statement of that ask; until K ships, a K-registered org's dissolution deliberately holds at `AwaitingKErasure` — the ordering is the safety property. PS-701 stays In Review for that reason.

**I have not merged #662** — the project→develop merge is yours to take, per the branch plan.

## Accepted implementation plan (2026-08-27)

Project branch: `project/ps-690-org-owned-docs` (created from develop @ 297b6c6, pushed). Each phase is a sub-issue + feature branch PR'd into the project branch; develop merged in periodically; one final project→develop merge after full testing. Stop for review after each phase.

### Binding product decisions

1. **Visibility**: SsdOrganisation + SsdAccountAdmin gain an org-wide documents view with lifecycle powers; SsdUser/SsdPowerUser keep seeing only their own uploads + rights-held docs.
2. **Multi-user delete**: deactivate — login destroyed, Person row kept with name intact for lineage ("Former member"); PII anonymisation only on explicit GDPR erasure (which also fires the S→K erasure).
3. **Sole-user delete**: the delete flow offers org dissolution in the same action — impact preview, then anchor `delete` events → K erasure → confirm → local deletion.

### Hard invariants

K-erasure-first ordering (the once-only `PlatformKOrganisation.EncryptedApiKey` must survive until K confirms — and under this plan the Organisation row is never deleted at all); PS-694's "a jurisdiction fact may widen obligations, never narrow them" (erasure is never gate-able; new erasure code lives in `Services/Erasure/`, leaving `IdentityErasureService.cs` untouched per its source-contract test); KS-389 (soft-delete anchors as `action=delete`, never `/revoke`); PS-693 count-creep contract; history never rewritten (`PayloadJson` byte-identical across erasure — display snapshots only); S holds no K user id, so the bridge is `external_ref`(PersonGuid)-addressed — K-side dependency isolated to Phase 6.

### Phases

| # | Phase | K-dependent | Migrations |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Ownership contracts + data-model hardening: verify-then-constrain FK+index on `DocumentStore.OrganisationId` (Restrict, no backfill — org-at-upload IS ownership-of-record); `SendDocsLinks.CreatedBy` Cascade→Restrict + `ShareLinksCreated` in the delete impact; `OwnersId` pinned as write-once uploader attribution; the global tenant filter pinned unchanged. | No | 2 |
| 2 | Org-wide visibility: new `OrgDocumentsController` + `OrgDocumentPolicy` (org-admin ∧ same-org disjunct added to each surface predicate: SignPolicy, Senddocs, Assign, Watermark/Certify/ViewPdf/Lineage). Full verb set for org admins, acting as themselves; attribution untouched. | No | 0 |
| 3 | Person deactivation: `DeactivatedAt`/`DeactivatedById`; explicit predicates NOT a global Person filter (sign-in chokepoints must see the row; five sites must-NOT-filter, pinned by source-scan tests both directions); `LockoutEnd=max` + security-stamp bump + immediate `TenantResolutionMiddleware` gate; Identity row kept locked (email reserved until erasure); delete modal offers Deactivate when blocked, hard delete stays for clean users; "Former member" rendering. | No | 1 |
| 4 | S-side GDPR erasure, resumable: `Services/Erasure/` — `PersonGdprErasureService` + `PersonErasure` state table (PersonGuid-keyed) + sweep; K client stubbed; K failure never blocks local erasure. Field-by-field anonymisation (PersonGuid retained; `PayloadJson` untouched — Art. 17(3); `ActorName` → "Former member (erased)"; SignedBy/ValidatedBy/WatermarkedBy join-driven; email freed via tombstone address). | Interface only | 1 |
| 5 | Organisation dissolution: **soft-org-delete** (`Organisation.DissolvedAt` + `OrganisationDissolution` state machine Requested→DocumentsDeleted→AwaitingKErasure→KErased→Dissolved, resumable sweep, merge-service transaction/fingerprint pattern). Docs deleted via the existing path (anchored delete verbs); K-registered orgs refuse at Preview until Phase 6; sole-user in-flow offer; PS-648 empty-org reclaim as the trivial subcase; billing history, audit, ledger all retained. | Entry-gated | 1 |
| 6 | S→K erasure bridge: real `PlatformKErasureClient` (external_ref-keyed person + connector-scoped org erasure, org operational key auth, idempotent + status read); gates lifted; Pending backlog drains. | **Yes** | 0 |
| 7 | End-to-end verification: systemTest journeys (org visibility matrix, deactivation, erasure, dissolution) + k-live round-trips; full suites on a slot stack; testing docs per PS-693. | Partially | 0 |

### K-side asks (KS ticket for Kam; blocks only Phase 6)

1. Erasure addressable by `external_ref` (S's PersonGuid) — K's route is keyed on `users.id`, which S no longer holds (PS-465 dropped PlatformKAccount). Idempotent + status read.
2. `documents.title` included in erasure anonymisation (real filenames currently survive `executeErasure`).
3. Connector-scoped org erasure for `platform-s:<OrganisationGuid>` (blank org display + connector docs' titles, revoke the operational key by `svc_api_keys` id, retain anchored hashes/graph).
4. Sequenced on top of PS-319/KS-480's connector-key model.

### Decisions taken (veto points)

1. Sole-user dissolution ends in an anonymised tombstone Person, not a hard row delete (row survives for ledger integrity; login deleted, PII erased).
2. Deactivated users keep their email reserved until explicit GDPR erasure frees it.
3. Org admins get the full verb set (incl. sign/certify/watermark) over same-org docs — narrowable to share/assign/delete with a one-line change per policy site.
4. The DocumentStore global query filter never changes in this project; stale `OrganisationId` on movers' old uploads is correct ownership-of-record, not repaired.

Full plan (with per-phase file/test/migration names, risks, and exit criteria) is in the session plan file; phase sub-issues carry their own detail.

title: Enforced PDF access control — check-before-open, revoke & "self-destruct" on distributed documents
description:
## The idea

Embed code in a distributed PDF so that, before it opens, it calls back to Platform S to check whether opening is still allowed — and can be revoked or "self-destruct" after the fact. Recorded here as a feature investigation, with the feasibility findings from a design discussion.

## Key finding: code baked *into the PDF* does not deliver this

PDFs can carry JavaScript, and a document-open script can in principle phone home (`SOAP.request` / `Net.HTTP`). In a demo it looks like it works, but as a security control it fails in the field:

* **Almost nothing runs it.** Chrome (PDFium), Firefox (PDF.js), macOS Preview, and mobile viewers either don't execute PDF JavaScript or run a subset with networking disabled. The network APIs realistically only work in full Adobe Acrobat/Reader. A viewer that ignores the script just opens the document — the control fails **open**.
* **The code is trivially removable.** A PDF is a static file; `qpdf`, `mutool`, Ghostscript, or a re-save via Preview strips the JavaScript in seconds. There is no tamper-proof or mandatory-execution guarantee in the format, so "code that cannot be destroyed" is not achievable.
* **You can't self-destruct a file you no longer hold.** Once the bytes are on the recipient's disk you cannot remotely delete or corrupt them.

**Principle:** in-PDF code is client-side DRM, and client-side DRM against a motivated recipient always loses — you're asking the recipient's own machine to enforce a rule against them. Real "check before open" and "revoke/self-destruct" only work when a **controlled viewer** or the **server** does the enforcing.

## Options compared

### A. Server-mediated view-only (≈ what Platform S already does)

Document stays encrypted at rest (`DocStorageKey` / `LocalDiskStorageProvider`); recipients reach it via authenticated, permissioned links (`SendDocsLinks`, `SendDocsPermission`, logged in `SendDocsLinkAccessLog`). The "allowed to open?" check runs server-side on every view, and "self-destruct" is real: expire/revoke the link or delete the server copy.

* ✅ Enforceable, low friction, in-browser, already built.
* ⚠️ Only holds while access is **view-only / streamed**. Granting `Download` hands over bytes we can't recall — download is the explicit "control ends here" action.

### B. FileOpen-style DRM (most realistic true-DRM path for us)

A handler inside Acrobat/Reader calls a license server before rendering; exposed as an API/web service that Platform S drives server-to-server to apply a policy per document at distribution time.

* ✅ Same enforcement model as Adobe RM but built as an API to drive from another app — much lighter to integrate than a full AEM stack. Enforces control on **downloaded/offline** copies with revocation.
* ⚠️ Recipients must use Adobe Acrobat/Reader + authenticate.

### C. Full Adobe Rights Management (AEM Forms — Document Security, formerly LiveCycle RM)

Policy-based AES encryption where the **decryption key lives on the RM server**, not in the file; the doc carries only a policy reference + server URL. Acrobat fetches the key on each open after auth, enforces permissions in memory, supports offline **lease**, revocation, permission changes after distribution, and full audit.

* ✅ Strongest control; genuine recall on distributed/offline copies.
* ⚠️ Heavyweight, licensed enterprise stack; mandates Acrobat + recipient auth; biggest build cost.

## Recommendation

If the requirement is "recipient must not retain an openable copy after we revoke it," lean into the model we already have — **view-only, server-rendered access with expiring, per-open-authorised links** — and treat `Download` as the explicit point where control ends. Do **not** ship phone-home / self-destruct JavaScript baked into the PDF as a security control: it demos well and fails quietly in production. If enforced **offline** access is genuinely required, that's a licensed controlled-viewer DRM integration (FileOpen the most realistic path), not a PDF-JS snippet.

## Suggested next step

Decide whether the real requirement is online-only revocation (covered by tightening the current view-only path) or enforced offline control (scopes a FileOpen/AEM evaluation). A follow-up could map exactly where the current `SendDocs` flow draws the `View` vs `Download` line.

## Acceptance

This is a **feature investigation**, and the findings above are the substance of it. Acceptance is therefore partly a recorded decision and partly the one checkable claim the recommendation rests on.

* **The requirement is decided and written down**, on this ticket and in `docs/`: online-only revocation (covered by tightening the existing view-only path) **or** enforced offline control (which scopes a FileOpen / AEM evaluation). Those are genuinely different projects with different costs, and until one is chosen nothing here can be built.
* **The "do not do this" is recorded as a decision, not just as prose.** The finding that in-PDF JavaScript fails open in Chrome (PDFium), Firefox (PDF.js), macOS Preview and mobile viewers, and is strippable with `qpdf` / `mutool` / Ghostscript / a Preview re-save, is written where the next person proposing a phone-home PDF will read it. A design note that only says "we chose option A" invites the same proposal again in six months.
* **If option A (tighten the existing path) is chosen**: the `View` versus `Download` line is mapped explicitly — every route and control that can put bytes on a recipient's disk is listed, and `Download` is documented as the point where control ends. That is the ticket's own suggested next step, and it is the deliverable.
* **If option B or C is chosen**: a costed evaluation with the licence model, the Acrobat/Reader requirement for recipients, and the recipient-authentication implication, since both options mandate a controlled viewer and that is a customer-facing constraint, not an implementation detail.
* **No claim is made that the platform cannot support.** Nothing in the UI, the docs or sales material may say a distributed copy can be recalled or self-destructed unless option B or C ships — the same class of inaccuracy as [PS-945](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-945/register-page-remove-inaccurate-end-to-end-encrypted-claim)'s end-to-end encryption pill, and worth checking for in the same pass.

**Playwright test that demonstrates the claim** (required for the option-A half, because the recommendation is "the enforcement we already have is real" and that is an assertion about live screens, not a theory): suggest `systemTest/tests/functional/share_permission_boundary.spec.ts`. The nearest existing files each cover one slice — `share_recipient_states.spec.ts` the state badges, `share_revoke_notify.spec.ts` the notification, `my_documents_drawer_revoke.spec.ts` the revoke control, `sdviewdownload_session_seal.spec.ts` the session seal — and none of them pins the View-versus-Download line as a boundary. Against a live stack it must:

1. share a document with `senddocs-share-permission-view-btn` selected, and as the recipient assert `sdview-inbox-view-link` is present and `sdview-inbox-download-link` is **absent**;
2. as that recipient, issue a direct GET of the download route for that link and assert it is **refused** — not merely unlinked in the UI. This is the assertion that distinguishes a real server-side control from a hidden button, and it is the whole basis of the recommendation;
3. **revoke** the link and assert the recipient's next view attempt is refused and that `link-expired-heading` or the equivalent revoked message renders — so "self-destruct is real while access is view-only" is demonstrated rather than asserted;
4. share the same document with `senddocs-share-permission-viewdownload-btn`, assert `sdview-inbox-download-link` is present and the download succeeds — then revoke and assert the **link** is dead while acknowledging in the spec's own comment that the downloaded bytes are not recoverable. That comment is the documentation of where control ends, in the place a future reader will look;
5. **control that must keep passing**: every assertion above should pass on today's `develop`. That is the point — this spec **pins** the existing enforcement rather than demonstrating a fix, so that a later change to the share path cannot quietly widen the boundary. If any of steps 1–4 is red today, that is a defect to raise on its own ticket, and it would materially change this investigation's recommendation.

**Which assertion fails on** `develop` **today**: none is expected to, and that is deliberate for this one ticket — the spec's job is to make the current guarantee regression-proof before anyone builds on the claim. If step 2 or step 3 fails, option A's premise is wrong and this ticket's recommendation must be rewritten before the decision is taken.

The rules behind it belong in xUnit as they already partly do: `SendDocsPermission` mapping to the allowed routes (`NoAccess` 0, `View` 10, `Download` 20, `ViewAndDownload` 30), expiry and revocation refusing before any blob is read, and the access-log row written for each attempt including the refused ones.

**Why no Playwright test applies to the other half**: options B and C are **licensed third-party DRM integrations** requiring Acrobat/Reader and a licence server. Neither the controlled viewer nor the licence handshake can be driven by Playwright, which is a browser automating our own pages. The criterion for that half is the costed evaluation named above, plus — if it ever proceeds — a recorded manual observation in Acrobat with the version, the date and whether revocation took effect on an offline copy.

title: Entra Verified ID: Azure tenant setup and config values needed before the feature can be enabled anywhere
description:
## What this is

The three code defects blocking Entra Verified ID are fixed ([PS-673](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-673/entra-verified-id-callback-can-never-authenticate-behind-nginx-api-key), [PS-674](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-674/entra-verified-id-accepts-a-credential-from-any-issuer-and-ships), [PS-675](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-675/entra-verified-id-never-binds-the-presented-credential-to-the-signed)). **Everything remaining is person-work in Azure and in the secret store** — none of it is code, and none of it was tracked anywhere.

There is also **no runbook**: `docs/sso-tenant-configuration.md` covers the SSO schemes (`AzureAdCiam` / `AzureAdWorkforce`) and has zero overlap with Verified ID, despite `systemTest/tests/functional/entra_verify_flow.spec.ts` pointing testers at it.

## Azure tenant setup

1. **Onboard Verified ID** in the tenant — create the authority and its DID.
2. **Key Vault** with the authority's signing key, and access granted to the Verified ID service principal. The app never touches this key; Entra holds and uses it server-side.
3. **Verify the domain and publish the DID documents.** The presentation request sets `validateLinkedDomain = true`, so for a `did:web` verifier both of these must resolve on the domain named in the DID:
   * `https://<domain>/.well-known/did.json`
   * `https://<domain>/.well-known/did-configuration.json`

   **Nothing in this repo serves either file** — no route, no static asset. This needs a hosting decision (an nginx `location`, or a controller), and is the item most likely to be missed because it looks like Azure's job and is not.
4. **App registration** with the **application** permission `VerifiableCredential.Create.PresentRequest` on resource `3db474b9-6a0c-4840-96ac-1fceb342124f`, and **tenant admin consent granted**. The code uses `AcquireTokenForClient(… ".default")`, which fails outright without pre-consented app permissions. Graph is not used by this path.
5. **A client secret** on that registration, with a rotation schedule.
6. **Decide the credential type and its issuers.** Whether Secuura issues these credentials itself — in which case an **issuance flow is needed and does not exist at all**, only presentation was ever built — or relies on a third-party issuer whose DIDs go in `AcceptedIssuers`.
7. Confirm Microsoft's outbound callers can reach `https://uat-ps.secuura.net/EntraVerify/Callback` and the production equivalent (no security-group or WAF block).

## Config values someone must supply, per environment

From the secret store, never committed. `EntraVerifiedId` is currently absent from **all four** `Docker.appsettings.template.json` files, so the keys are not even discoverable from a deployment — adding the block with blank values and `Enabled: false` is part of this work, following the convention `docs/sso-tenant-configuration.md` already mandates for `AzureAdWorkforce`.

| Key | Shape |
| -- | -- |
| `ClientId` | app registration GUID |
| `ClientSecret` | from the secret store |
| `Authority` | `https://login.microsoftonline.com/<tenant-guid>` — **tenant-specific**; `/common` and `/organizations` do not work for client credentials |
| `VerifierAuthority` | the real `did:web:` value from the Verified ID authority |
| `CredentialType` | the real type. Ships blank since [PS-674](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-674/entra-verified-id-accepts-a-credential-from-any-issuer-and-ships) — it used to default to Microsoft's public tutorial credential |
| `AcceptedIssuers` | at least one trusted issuer DID. Empty means *any issuer* and the feature refuses to run ([PS-674](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-674/entra-verified-id-accepts-a-credential-from-any-issuer-and-ships)) |
| `CallbackApiKey` | ≥32 characters, its own value ([PS-673](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-673/entra-verified-id-callback-can-never-authenticate-behind-nginx-api-key)) |

## Do not enable before these land

* [PS-676](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-676/enabling-entra-verified-id-instantly-hard-blocks-all-document-signing) — enabling the flag currently hard-blocks document signing for every user without a completed verification, with no warn mode. On an existing deployment that is everyone.
* [PS-676](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-676/enabling-entra-verified-id-instantly-hard-blocks-all-document-signing) also covers the in-process request cache, which loses every in-flight verification on restart or redeploy.

## Acceptance

* A runbook in `docs/` describing the Azure steps and the config keys, linked from wherever a person would look — `entra_verify_flow.spec.ts` currently misdirects them.
* `EntraVerifiedId` present in all four deployment templates with blank values and `Enabled: false`.
* The `.well-known` DID documents served from the verifier's domain.
* One environment (UAT) verified end to end with a real presentation.

### Added criteria

* **The** `EntraVerifiedId` **block is pinned by a contract test, not by diligence.** It is currently absent from **all four** `Docker.appsettings.template.json` files, so the keys are not even discoverable from a deployment. Adding the block with blank values and `Enabled: false` is only half the fix; an **xUnit contract test** in `tests/ssd.UnitTests` — name it `EntraVerifiedIdTemplateContractTests`, in the shape of the existing `SeedPasswordContractTests` — asserts every deployment template states all seven keys (`ClientId`, `ClientSecret`, `Authority`, `VerifierAuthority`, `CredentialType`, `AcceptedIssuers`, `CallbackApiKey`) and that none of them carries a real value. **That test is red on today's** `develop`, which is the point: it converts "invisible from the repo" into an offline failure.
* **The** `.well-known` **hosting decision is made and implemented.** `validateLinkedDomain = true` means both `did.json` and `did-configuration.json` must resolve on the domain in the DID, and **nothing in this repo serves either** — no route, no static asset. This is the item most likely to be missed because it looks like Azure's job and is not. Verified by both documents resolving on the verifier's domain, with `did.json`'s `id` equal to the configured `VerifierAuthority`.
* **The issuance question is answered, not deferred by omission:** does Secuura issue these credentials — in which case an issuance flow is needed and **does not exist at all**, only presentation was ever built — or do we rely on third-party issuers whose DIDs go in `AcceptedIssuers`? The estimate changes by an order of magnitude between those two answers.
* **Admin consent is confirmed as granted**, not merely requested: `AcquireTokenForClient(".default")` fails outright without pre-consented application permissions, so an un-consented registration looks configured and does not work. Graph is not used by this path, so a Graph consent proves nothing here.
* [PS-676](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-676/enabling-entra-verified-id-instantly-hard-blocks-all-document-signing) **lands before the flag is enabled anywhere.** Enabling it today hard-blocks document signing for every user without a completed verification, with no warn mode — on an existing deployment that is everyone — and the in-process request cache loses every in-flight verification on restart or redeploy.
* `CallbackApiKey` is ≥ 32 characters and **its own value**, per [PS-673](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-673/entra-verified-id-callback-can-never-authenticate-behind-nginx-api-key). Keys and lengths only: no value is opened, read or quoted anywhere in this work, and the secret-store entries are named and handed over.
* The runbook is linked from where a person would actually look — `entra_verify_flow.spec.ts` today points testers at `docs/sso-tenant-configuration.md`, which has **zero overlap** with Verified ID.

**No Playwright test applies to the substance of this ticket, and a local slot cannot stand in for one.** Everything remaining is person-work in Azure and in a secret store; the code defects are already fixed ([PS-673](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-673/entra-verified-id-callback-can-never-authenticate-behind-nginx-api-key)/674/675). Worse, platform-s **cannot** exercise this path locally at all: Entra Verified ID's Start POST is refused by Microsoft on every `localhost` callback, so a local row goes `Rejected` immediately and never produces a QR. A spec written against a slot would prove nothing about the tenant setup.

The verifiable alternatives are the xUnit contract test above (offline, catches the missing config block on every branch), the two `.well-known` URLs resolving with a matching `id`, the consent state on the app registration, and **one UAT presentation completed end to end** — which is already the fourth existing bullet and is the only criterion that proves the whole chain.

**Controls that must keep passing unchanged:** `systemTest/tests/functional/entra_verify_flow.spec.ts` keeps expecting the local `Rejected` outcome and **must not be "fixed" into self-gating on whether Entra is configured** — both directions of that gate fire locally, which is why it was written the way it was. `systemTest/tests/functional/well_known_did.spec.ts` goes green once the documents are served and must stay green afterwards. Neither needs a new file.

## Notes

Compiled 2026-08-26 from a full read of `ssd/Services/EntraVerifiedId/`, the controller, the settings, both deployed nginx configs and the deployment templates. Filed because it is otherwise invisible: the code is now correct, so nothing in the repo will tell anyone why the feature still does not work.

nodes.body:
**UAT leg decided and wired (PS-750 / PR #811, 2026-09-11).** Per the runbook's Tenancy section, **UAT shares the development authority** (`did:web:dev-ps.secuura.net`, tenant `efc17e5f-…`) but gets **its own app registration + client secret** in that tenant — application permission `VerifiableCredential.Create.PresentRequest`, admin consent verified by reading back `appRoleAssignments` (the "Provided access token contains no roles" trap from 09-04), plus its own `entra-vid-callback-api-key`.

`dep-aws-uat/Docker.appsettings.template.json` now carries dev-ps's block: `Enabled: true` with the seven `__ENTRA_VID_*__` placeholders, optional fetches in `setenv.sh`, `EnforceSigningVerification: false`. Four of the seven secrets (`authority`, `verifier-authority`, `credential-type`, `accepted-issuers`) take dev-ps's values verbatim; three are UAT's own. UAT serves **no** `.well-known` documents (dev-ps does), so its linked-domain check depends on dev-ps being up — noted in the template comment and in `docs/identity-provider-configuration.md`, whose "nothing in this repository serves these" line was stale and is corrected. The runbook's "absent from all four templates" sentences are corrected too.

Carry-over for the UAT run: the matcher is fail-closed on email, and the fresh UAT DB seeds only the `@lhsg.com` trio — a UAT Person matching the wallet holder's credential email (the `stuart@obeden.com` card that completed on dev-ps 09-04) must exist before a presentation is attempted. This ticket's acceptance ("one environment verified end to end") is already true of dev-ps; a UAT presentation would make it true of a second. Production's own authority is PS-824.

## ✅ A real presentation completed end to end — dev-ps, 2026-09-04 20:05

**First time in any environment.** `/EntraVerify` reports *"Identity Verified — Verified on 04 Sep 2026 at 20:05 via Microsoft Entra Verified ID"*, and the dashboard shows **Your ID Verified · since 04 Sep 2026**.

It was a genuine **cross-tenant** presentation, which is the case that actually matters: the credential was issued by the **Obeden PTE Ltd** tenant (`2fefc32a-…`) and verified by an authority in a different directory. Not a card we issued to ourselves.

### What it took, after the config was right

1. **`entra-vid-authority` was a bare tenant GUID**, not a URL. MSAL threw `UriFormatException` while being constructed — the request never reached Microsoft. The Providers page still said *Configured*, because readiness only checks the value is non-placeholder, never that it parses.
2. **The `VerifiedEmployee` card had to come from a tenant we accept.** The wallet's "Card missing" was our own `acceptedIssuers` filtering, not a missing credential — the card is issued by Obeden's authority, and the config named the dev-ps one.
3. **`entra-vid-accepted-issuers` repointed** to `did:web:verifiedid.entra.microsoft.com:2fefc32a-…:a7b6240f-…`, applied and the container restarted.

The linked-domain proof passed too — the wallet showed the verified badge against `https://dev-ps.secuura.net/`, so `validateLinkedDomain: true` resolved the `.well-known` documents this platform serves itself. Obeden's own domain proof (404 earlier) evidently satisfied Microsoft from its cached `linkedDomainsVerified`, so it did not block the run.

### Three defects the successful run exposed

None of these could have been found earlier, because nothing had ever reached the verified state:

- **PS-772** (High) — the completion left its own `KycVerification` row Pending at level None, so the history listed the successful verification as *Expired*. **Fixed**, six behavioural tests driving the real callback.
- **PS-773** — the dashboard "Your ID Verified" card lands on `/identity`, the DEV-badged platform page, and *Verify my identity* still defaults to mock with no statement of your current level.
- Readiness accepts an `Authority` that cannot be parsed (item 1 above), reporting *Configured* for a value that throws on first use. Not yet filed.

### Status of this ticket

Its acceptance says **"One environment (UAT) verified end to end with a real presentation."** That is now true of **dev-ps**, not UAT. Leaving this In Progress rather than closing it — whether dev-ps satisfies the criterion, or UAT is still wanted, is Stuart's call.

## dev-ps deployed — `e8c0411` (develop), 2026-09-04 07:43 UTC

The prerequisite listed two comments up is done: dev-ps is no longer serving the old `secpsdev` credentials.

**Deployed:** image `secuuradev.azurecr.io/ssd:e8c0411`, digest `sha256:4e6bcca348b28c…`. Verified by digest rather than by tag — the running container's `.Image` equals the digest pushed, so the box is provably running the binary that was built from `develop` at `e8c0411`, not a same-tag stand-in. `restarts=0`, all four containers up.

**A config change had to ship with it.** `deploy-from-acr.sh` updates the image only, and `Docker.appsettings.template.json` on the box still dated from 2 Sep while #762 changed that file. Since a deploy template *replaces* `appsettings.json` rather than layering over it, deploying the image alone would have run the new binary against the old template and silently dropped anything the old one did not state. Checksums were compared before deploying: that one file differed, everything else (compose, nginx, `setenv.sh`, `start-services.sh`, `deploy-from-acr.sh`, the unit file) was byte-identical. Shipped with a timestamped backup at `Docker.appsettings.template.json.bak-20260904-074258`, and the new checksum confirmed on the box afterwards.

**Post-deploy checks:**

| Check | Result |
| -- | -- |
| `/health/anchoring` | 200 `Healthy` |
| `/EntraVerify` | 302 to auth, as expected |
| `/.well-known/did.json` | **200** — `did:web:dev-ps.secuura.net`, 1 signing key |
| `/.well-known/did-configuration.json` | **200** — linkage `iss: did:web:dev-ps.secuura.net`, `origin: https://dev-ps.secuura.net/`, valid to 2051 |

The linked-domain proof resolving matters more than it looks: `validateLinkedDomain = true`, so a wallet fetches exactly those two documents and will refuse the presentation if they do not check out. That leg is now confirmed good from the public internet.

**Note on `entra-vid-verifier-authority`:** deliberately *not* changed today, and that is correct. The authority owning `did:web:dev-ps.secuura.net` was always in `efc17e5f`; `secpsdev` never completed onboarding, so it never had an authority to own it. Only the client credentials had been pointed at the wrong tenant. The DID served above confirms the value still matches.

**Still unverified, and it is the whole remaining question:** whether a presentation now completes. `/IdentityAdmin/Providers` is auth-gated so readiness could not be checked anonymously, and nothing here exercises the wallet. Signing in on dev-ps and running `/EntraVerify` through to a presented credential is what closes this ticket.

**PR [#762](https://github.com/Secuura/platform-s/pull/762) merged to `develop`** — merge commit `e8c04119f`, 2026-09-04T07:26:16Z. 10 commits, 16 files.

What landed:

- The `Identity` section stated in every deployment template that offers Entra, so `Identity:Enabled` is discoverable in the file an operator edits (a template **replaces** `appsettings.json` rather than layering over it, so an unstated key is invisible and unchangeable, not "inherits the default").
- One consent gate per verification instead of two — the hosted hand-off now precedes the gate, and the exemption is narrowed to the flow that actually *asks*. `/EntraVerify` asks and records (PS-714); `/idv` records on Start without asking (PS-383), so exempting "hosted" wholesale had removed the only affirmative consent a Stripe subject ever sees.
- `Back` returns to where the reader came from on both hosted flows, via a new `identityverify` return surface, instead of always ejecting them to the dashboard.
- Two Verified ID Key Vault access policies codified in `main.tf` — they were granted through the portal, so the first plan proposed **deleting** them, which would have installed the secrets while breaking the authority they exist to reach, presenting as a credential fault.
- The runbook rewritten against what the setup actually took (see the previous comment), including a new section on whether UAT and production share a verifier authority.

**Merged without the full systemTest run, deliberately.** Not documentation-only — 15 of 16 files are runtime code — so the rule applied and was waived by Stuart after being shown that. `dotnet test` was green on the merged tree: **3,939 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped, 6s**. The Playwright journeys were not run, so the consent hand-off, the return navigation and the sidebar grouping are unverified *as rendered pages*. Risk judged acceptable because `Identity:Enabled` ships `false` everywhere and `EntraVerifiedId.Enabled` is true only on dev-ps, making those surfaces unreachable wherever Identity is off. Full note on the PR.

This ticket stays **In Progress** — merging the config work does not satisfy its acceptance criterion, which is one environment verified end to end with a real presentation.

**Reopened and held open until a real presentation completes on a live environment** (Stuart, 2026-09-04).

Moved back to **In Progress**, not just unarchived. Left in *Done* it would very likely archive itself again — it was archived at `05:29` on 2026-09-02, thirty-three minutes after being marked Done at `04:56`, which is the signature of an automatic sweep rather than a deliberate filing. Unarchiving a completed issue only postpones that.

**What closes this:** one environment verified end to end with a real credential presentation — which is this ticket's own acceptance criterion and has still never happened anywhere. Everything up to the wallet hand-off is now proven (token, authority, `PresentRequest` permission); the completion leg has not been exercised, and a host run structurally cannot exercise it.

**Not blocking, but required before that run:**

- Restart the dev-ps container so it picks up the three Key Vault values changed today. Until it cycles it is still serving the old `secpsdev` credentials, so a test against it right now would reproduce the original 401 and mean nothing.
- Seed a dev-ps Person whose email matches the wallet holder's — the matcher is fail-closed on email.
- Confirm a `VerifiedEmployee` credential actually exists in the Default Directory.

## Entra Verified ID now authenticates end to end — 2026-09-04

Reopened briefly to record this, because it closes out the two setup steps this ticket listed under *Azure tenant setup* (item 4 — app registration permission and admin consent) and the `Authority` / `ClientId` / `ClientSecret` rows of the config table. Every authentication-side fault is now cleared. What remains is a hostname constraint, not configuration.

### What was actually wrong, in the order it surfaced

**1 · Wrong tenant.** The app registration was created in `secpsdev.onmicrosoft.com`, which has no Verified ID authority — its setup wizard was never completed. The authority owning `did:web:dev-ps.secuura.net` lives in **Default Directory `efc17e5f-7637-4118-b92c-c5236d591cad`** (`philipcuffyahooco.onmicrosoft.com`). Symptom was a bare `Unauthorized` from the Request Service.

**2 · No API permission at all.** With the tenant corrected the token was issued but authorised nothing:

```
invalid_aad_access_token — "Provided access token contains no roles."
```

`platform-s-verified-id` (`f445c68d-c73f-4519-a4d0-53e98058f982`) requested **no Verified ID permission whatsoever**. Granted least-privilege: **`VerifiableCredential.Create.PresentRequest`** (`410607a4-22de-48a8-b35d-ad33c0c2e1bf`), deliberately not `.All`, because the service only ever calls `createPresentationRequest` (`EntraVerifiedIdService.cs:246`) — we present, we never issue. If issuance is ever built, `IssueRequest` is added then.

Confirmed as an app role assignment on SP `55fed9c3-c090-402e-88cd-3c422ec3c29b`, granted **2026-09-04T06:49:37Z** — verified by reading the assignment back, not by trusting the command's silent exit.

**3 · Rights to grant it.** Stuart held 19 directory roles in that tenant, none able to consent — no Global, Application, Cloud Application or Privileged Role Administrator, and no PIM eligibility. Sole Global Administrator is **Philip Cuff**. Cloud Application Administrator has since been assigned. Worth noting this role suffices only because the resource is the Verified ID Request Service; it cannot consent application permissions on Microsoft Graph itself.

### Where it stands

```
Failed to create verification request: BadRequest —
  "badOrMissingField", target "callback.url" — "URL must be public"
```

Authentication, authority and permission are all proven correct; the request body is the only remaining objection. The callback is derived from the browsing host (`EntraVerify.cs:98`, `Url.Action(..., Request.Scheme)`), so a host run resolves it to `https://localhost:5131/...`, which Microsoft cannot reach — and **no setting overrides this**, it follows the request. Local tunnelling was considered and dropped; **the completion leg will be verified on dev-ps**, where the hostname is already public.

### Key Vault (dev-ps) — updated, not deployed

`terraform apply` on `az-secuura-DEV-docker`: **0 added, 3 changed, 0 destroyed** — `entra-vid-client-id`, `entra-vid-client-secret` and `entra-vid-authority` repointed to the philipcuff tenant. Confirmed against the vault: those three updated `2026-09-04T06:12:03Z`, the other four untouched at `03:20:58Z`.

The dev-ps box already carries the full wiring — 7 `__ENTRA_VID_*` placeholders in its template, 7 matching fetches in `setenv.sh`, `EntraVerifiedId.Enabled: true`, the `Identity` section present, `setenv.sh` still executable. **No config copy is needed, only a container restart** — which has deliberately not been run, so dev-ps is still serving the old secpsdev values until someone cycles it.

### Carry-over for the dev-ps run

- The credential matcher is **fail-closed on email**: the signed-in Person's email must equal the email claim in the presented credential, or the presentation succeeds and is then rejected as not identifying the holder. A dev-ps Person needs seeding to match the wallet holder's address.
- Confirm a `VerifiedEmployee` credential actually exists in the Default Directory (Manage → Credentials) before reading an empty presentation as a platform fault.
- The Verified ID **admin** API (listing authorities) needs Global Administrator or Authentication Policy Administrator — Cloud Application Administrator keeps returning `No acceptable wids`. That path is a confirmation convenience, not a requirement.

### Bearing on PS-708

Every permission change on this authority is gated behind one person outside the project, because the authority sits in a personal Default Directory. Today that stopped a test mid-flight for as long as it took to get a role assigned. It recurs on every config change until the authority moves to a tenant the team controls.

## `did:web:dev-ps.secuura.net` is live — Registered and domain Verified

Deployed `bc587fe` to dev-ps (build → ACR → `az vm run-command`), asserted on `=== DEV deploy complete ===` rather than the exit code, per the deploy note's warning that run-command reports success even when the inner script dies.

Independently confirmed from outside Azure:

```
GET https://dev-ps.secuura.net/.well-known/did.json                -> 200 application/json
GET https://dev-ps.secuura.net/.well-known/did-configuration.json  -> 200 application/json
```

The `linked_dids` JWT carries `kid: did:web:dev-ps.secuura.net`. Portal shows **Registered** and **Verified**.

### Acceptance items now closed

* ✅ **`.well-known` DID documents served from the verifier's domain** — by `WellKnownController` (#665), from `/ssd-storage/.well-known/` on the existing bind mount. No nginx change on any environment; nothing claimed `/.well-known/`.
* ✅ **`EntraVerifiedId` present in all four deployment templates** — dev-ps wired with placeholders and optional Key Vault fetches; UAT, prod and local blank with `Enabled: false`.
* 🔄 **Runbook in `docs/`** — https://github.com/Secuura/platform-s/pull/660, open and mergeable.
* ⬜ **One environment verified end to end with a real presentation** — the remaining item.

### A defect the deploy prep found

`Startup.UseStatusCodePages` rewrites **every** 404 into a 302 to `/PageNotFound`, so the controller's "no DID hosted here" answer reached callers as a redirect to an HTML page. The callers are machines — Microsoft's resolver, any verifier checking a linked domain — and to a human curling it, a redirect reads as an auth problem.

`/.well-known` is now excluded. Found by curling dev-ps before deploying, not by a test: the unit tests assert `NotFoundResult` and are correct — the rewrite happens in middleware above the controller.

### Authority details for the record

| | |
| -- | -- |
| Organization name | `Secuura (Dev)` |
| DID | `did:web:dev-ps.secuura.net` |
| Trusted domain | `https://dev-ps.secuura.net` |
| Key Vault | a dedicated vault (Vault Access Policy); the seven `entra-vid-*` **secrets** stay in `secuura-ps-dev-kv`, which is what `setenv.sh` reads |

The signing key needed **Key: Sign** under Cryptographic Operations — the default management template omits it, and its absence produced a silent `failedAdminServiceApiCall` with no detail.

### Remaining, and none of it needs a rebuild

1. App registration + `VerifiableCredential.Create.PresentRequest` + admin consent
2. Create the Verified Employee credential, and decide the issuer — verifier and issuer are different DIDs
3. The seven `entra-vid-*` secrets into `secuura-ps-dev-kv`
4. Re-run the deploy to re-render config — `setenv.sh` runs on every start, so the same image picks the secrets up
5. Present from a wallet, with a `Person.Email` on dev-ps matching the credential's `mail` claim (PS-675 fails closed on a mismatch)

**The three dead keys are now removed** — PR https://github.com/Secuura/platform-s/pull/653.

`TenantId`, `CredentialManifest` and `CallbackBaseUrl` are gone from `appsettings.json` **and** from `EntraVerifiedIdSettings`. Keeping the properties would have left the class still advertising them as configurable, which is the same trap one layer down.

This directly serves this ticket's acceptance item *"`EntraVerifiedId` present in all four deployment templates"*: the block that gets copied is now the block that is real. Copied as it stood, all four environments would have inherited keys that look like configuration and are not.

Both files carry a comment explaining the removal, positioned where someone would be standing when tempted to add them back.

### One thing this changes about step 7

> *Confirm Microsoft's outbound callers can reach `https://uat-ps.secuura.net/EntraVerify/Callback` and the production equivalent*

Still correct, but the URL Microsoft is **told** to call is not that string from configuration — it is built per request from `Url.Action(..., Request.Scheme)`, i.e. the host the browser reached. Behind nginx that depends on the forwarded headers, not on any setting. So step 7 needs someone to look at the **rendered** callback URL on UAT, not to assume it matches a configured value. Removing `CallbackBaseUrl` makes that unavoidable rather than merely true.

No behaviour change — unread configuration cannot misbehave. Full suite 2,282 passed, 0 failed.

## Config table re-checked — three of these keys are dead

Re-verified 27 Aug 2026 against `develop` at `7e71410`, by asking which `EntraVerifiedIdSettings` properties the code actually **reads**. Everything in this ticket's table is genuinely required, but the wider block ships three keys that are read **nowhere**:

| Key | Reads | Note |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `CallbackBaseUrl` | **0** | The misleading one — see below |
| `TenantId` | **0** | The tenant is carried by `Authority`, which is where the code takes it from |
| `CredentialManifest` | **0** | An issuance concept; this integration only presents |

### `CallbackBaseUrl` is worth a moment

The callback URL is **not** taken from configuration. `EntraVerify.cs:83` builds it per request:

```csharp
var callbackUrl = Url.Action(..., Request.Scheme);
```

— the host the user's browser actually reached. Setting `CallbackBaseUrl` pins nothing.

That has an operational consequence for **step 7** of this ticket. "Confirm Microsoft's outbound callers can reach the callback" is right, but the URL they are *told* to call depends on the **forwarded headers** being correct behind nginx, not on config. If `X-Forwarded-Proto` / `Host` were wrong, Microsoft would be handed a wrong callback URL and no amount of `CallbackBaseUrl` configuration would correct it. Worth checking the rendered URL on UAT rather than assuming it matches the key.

### Where this bites

Nowhere today — unread config cannot misbehave. It matters at exactly one moment: **the acceptance item "EntraVerifiedId present in all four deployment templates"**. Copy the block across as-is and every environment inherits three keys that look like configuration and are not. Either drop them while adding the block, or make `CallbackBaseUrl` an override the code honours.

## Status strip re-checked — all four claims still hold

| Claim | Verified |
| -- | -- |
| Code complete | 6 tickets, all merged (PS-673/674/675/676 + PS-692, PS-695) |
| Azure tenant not started | this ticket, still Backlog |
| Config absent from deployments | confirmed absent from all four `Docker.appsettings.template.json` |
| Never enabled anywhere | `Enabled: false` in the tracked config, and no template overrides it |

Readiness document updated with both: https://claude.ai/code/artifact/0ab9f452-e0e8-43a3-a43c-084adeaf7cbe

**Readiness document** (kept current through this session's changes): https://claude.ai/code/artifact/0ab9f452-e0e8-43a3-a43c-084adeaf7cbe

It covers the four fixed defects (PS-673/674/675/676), the per-environment config keys, the ordered Azure steps from this ticket, and the rollout order. Re-verified against `develop` at `6d96da8`.

**One dependency worth knowing before this is scheduled:** PS-695 — `ErasePersonAsync` does not clear `Person.IdVerifiedOn`, `IdToken2` or `IdToken3`, and `IdToken3` is the subject DID. Found while updating the document after PS-694.

It is cheaper to fix **before** this ticket than after. No real subject DID has ever been stored, because the callback that writes those columns has never run anywhere — so closing PS-695 first means there is no historical residue to sweep. Once Verified ID is live on any environment, there is.

Nothing here blocks the Azure work itself; it is an ordering preference, not a prerequisite.

title: Security: /api/status revoke/unrevoke has no tenant ownership check — an ISSUER_ADMIN in any tenant can revoke another tenant’s credential (KS-586’s deferred half, now untracked)
description:
## Summary

`POST /api/status/:id/revoke` and `/unrevoke` enforce an **admin-class role** but **no tenant ownership check**. An `ISSUER_ADMIN` in one tenant can revoke or un-revoke a credential in **another tenant's** status list. Reproduced live on `develop 576ebef85`.

This is the **second half of KS-586**, which fixed the role gap and explicitly deferred the tenant gap — but **KS-586 is now** `Done`**, so nothing tracks the remainder.** That is why this ticket exists.

## ⚠️ What is already FIXED — read this before working the ticket

**KS-586 is done and its fix is live. **`/api/status` is no longer "no authorization at all". Anyone picking this up from a summary of [KS-570](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-570) will be looking for a defect that is not there.

| probe (local, `develop 576ebef85`) | result |
| -- | -- |
| `holder@secuura.com` (**OWNER**, non-admin) → revoke | **403 **`Role OWNER is not authorized for this action` |

The role gate at `services/vc-issuer/src/routes/status.ts:42-53` (`STATUS_WRITE_ROLES`, applied as a router-level gate ahead of the route table) works. Commit `bda40c91c` on `develop`, present in the running container.

## The defect that IS live — reproduced, controls both ways

Two `ISSUER_ADMIN`s in **different tenants**:

* `demo@secuura.io` — tenant `default`
* `registrar@oxford-test.invalid` — tenant `oxford`

| # | actor | request | result |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| 1 | demo (owner) | `POST /api/status` create list | **201** |
| 2 | demo (owner) | `POST /api/status/:id/allocate` `cred-xtenant-probe` | **200**, index 0 |
| 3 | **oxford registrar (foreign tenant)** | `POST /api/status/:id/revoke` that credential | 🔴 **200** — `{"revoked":true,"reason":"cross-tenant probe"}` |
| 4 | demo (owner) | `GET /api/status/:id/revoked` | **200** — `{"revokedIndexes":[0],"totalRevoked":1}` — the write really landed |
| 5 | **control** — oxford registrar | revoke against a **non-existent** list id | **404 **`Status list not found` |
| 6 | **control** — holder (OWNER) | revoke the same list | **403** (role gate) |

**Controls 5 and 6 are what make row 3 mean something.** Row 5 proves the 200 was a genuine authorisation pass and not a blanket accept — the same foreign caller is refused when the target does not exist. Row 6 proves role is still evaluated, so the only thing missing is the tenant comparison.

## Root cause

`services/vc-issuer/src/routes/status.ts`. The router-level gate checks **role only**:

```ts
return requireRole(...STATUS_WRITE_ROLES)(req, res, next);
```

There is no comparison of the caller's tenant to the status list's owner — **because the status list has no owner to compare to.** Status lists live in a process-local `Map` with no tenant linkage. The code says so itself (`status.ts:35-38`):

> *"Tenant scoping is NOT enforced here yet: status lists live in a process-local Map with no tenant linkage, and the ownership model is the KS-539/KS-547/KS-586 joint authorization decision — tracked on KS-586."*

**"tracked on KS-586" is no longer true.** KS-586 is `Done` (2026-08-12) and KS-547 is `Done`; KS-539 is open but scoped to *governing rules for document operations by agents*, not status-list tenancy. The deferral outlived its tracker — which is the actual reason this went untracked for two weeks.

## Why this is not a duplicate

* **KS-586** — `Done`. The **role** half. Fixed.
* **KS-570** — the **authentication** half: the gateway mount at `proxy.ts:702` has no `authenticateToken`, so revoked-session JWTs still pass. Different layer, still open.
* **KS-588** — `Backlog`. **Test coverage** for `/api/status` authorization. Would catch this once it exists; is not the fix.
* **This ticket** — the **tenant/ownership** half. No ticket held it after KS-586 closed.

## Severity

**High.** Revocation state is an integrity operation on a document-authenticity platform — an attacker with any admin-class role in any tenant can un-revoke a credential their victim revoked, or revoke a live one. Same family as [KS-643](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-643) (cross-tenant API-key revoke) and [KS-642](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-642), and it sits on the same **KS-621 tenancy boundary** that is currently held for @kamil.kreiser's design ruling.

Not raised to Urgent: exploitation needs a valid admin-class credential in *some* tenant, so it is privilege-escalation-across-tenants, not anonymous.

## Suggested fix — NOT implemented, deliberately

The ownership model is a **KS-621 boundary decision** and is @kamil.kreiser's call, exactly as with KS-643. Filing only, per the same hold.

The prerequisite is structural: **a status list must carry an owning tenant before any check can be written.** The process-local `Map` has nowhere to put one, so this is not a middleware one-liner — it needs the list persisted with a tenant column, which is likely the same decision as KS-539's ownership model.

Note the interlock, learned from KS-578/KS-643: adding a tenant check **without** giving lists an owner would refuse every caller, since no list has a tenant to match.

## Reproduction

Local stack, `develop 576ebef85`, both accounts seeded. Full curl sequence is rows 1–6 above. Probe artefacts were written to the **local** stack only (`ks661-tenantprobe-*`); status lists are process-local and clear on a `vc-issuer` restart. **Nothing was written to demo.**

Handed over by @peter on KS-570 (2026-08-26 08:10Z): *"The one still open is the /api/status authorisation gap … I will let you file that one too, as you hold the evidence for it."* — filed with the measurement rather than the paraphrase, which is how the KS-586 half turned out to be already fixed.

nodes.body:
**BLUF:** PR 2090 (head `4c4f696f7699`, one commit on develop `9cdb9321aa8a`) is raised for gate 208 finding N1 on this ticket and waits for its gate. It changes two documentation sentences, one in each fragment, and nothing else. Nothing is merged or deployed.

- **The change:** the flow and cheat fragments said that `test_tenant_admin_cannot_write_status_lists` reads 404 for its revoke and unrevoke rows against a stack running this change. Gate 208 measured it at 400, "credentialId is required and must be a string": the test's own helper sends bodies with no credentialId, and the status routes refuse that before the ownership read; the test accepts only a 403, so it stays red either way. The product sentences about the 404 for a refused caller are unchanged.
- **Checked by Seat T 14th, by reading:** the 400 text exists at the three lines named in `routes/status.ts`; the helper's bodies carry no credentialId; the helper accepts only 403 (found by grep, with a control that finds nothing for an absent text). The docs check passes and a planted defect makes it fail. No test was run (none changed).

Recording this here because this ticket exists precisely to catch it, and it just caused a round trip.

`services/vc-issuer/src/routes/status.ts:36` reads:

Both halves of that were already out of date — the role gate landed with KS-586, and this ticket has tracked the remainder since 2026-08-26. This ticket's own description already warns *"anyone picking this up from a summary of KS-570 will be looking for a defect that is not there"* — which is exactly what happened.
