## The "catered for" half is done and merged. The rest is not mine to do.

Production is now fully built and fully dark:

- **Identity reserved** — [PS-636](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-636) / [PR #577](https://github.com/Secuura/platform-s/pull/577). `prod` keeps the original `b7e6c1a2-…` Id, with a contract test asserting it, because a store listing pins an Id permanently.
- **Manifest renders** — [PS-637](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-637) / [PR #578](https://github.com/Secuura/platform-s/pull/578). Same code path and same tests as dev and UAT.
- **Config in place** — `dep-aws-secuura/Docker.appsettings.template.json` carries the identity keys alongside the others, so nothing has to be invented at go-live.
- **Switched off** — `AppSpecific:Outlook:Enabled` stays `false`. Nothing deployed, nothing submitted, nothing distributed.

The gate turned out better than a process: because the endpoint 404s while the flag is off, **production serves no manifest at all**. It cannot be sideloaded early even by someone who wants to. `OutlookManifestBuilderTests` pins exactly that — prod config renders a valid manifest in-process, and the endpoint still returns nothing.

## What remains, and why I have not done it

Three things, none of which are code:

1. **The A-or-B decision** — AppSource listing vs Microsoft 365 Integrated Apps. That is a product call about how the add-in reaches customers, not an implementation detail.
2. **Partner Center checks.** Whether new Outlook submissions still accept the XML manifest (Microsoft has been migrating to the unified JSON manifest), and which compliance requirements apply at our tier. I have no Partner Center access, and my knowledge cutoff makes anything I assert here unreliable — this is precisely the class of thing that is cheap to check now and expensive to discover in a review rejection.
3. **`SupportUrl` and the privacy page.** `manifest.xml` points at `https://secuura.net/support`; someone should confirm that page exists and is useful, since store review checks it and a customer will click it.

One thing worth writing into the privacy copy whoever does it: the add-in hashes attachments client-side and sends **only the hash** — the file never leaves Outlook. That is a genuinely strong privacy story and should be stated plainly rather than buried.

The ticket stays open on those three. No code is blocking them.

title: Outlook add-in on dev-ps: AppDomains for the new sign-in providers, and first end-to-end install
description:
Depends on [PS-636](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-636>), [PS-637](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-637>), and [PS-643](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-643>) — dev-ps cannot receive this until its deploy trigger is repointed at `develop`.

**Base branch:** `develop`**.** `project-sso` is merged ([Secuura/platform-s#571](https://linear.app/secuura/review/merge-project-sso-into-develop-dev-ps-deployment-config-85d2ec2731ab)) and develop is 8 ahead / 0 behind it, so there is one lineage again and all of this tranche lands there.

## What already works — most of it

dev-ps needs almost nothing on the server side. Verified on `ssd/dep-az-dev/`:

| Piece | State |
| -- | -- |
| Add-in bundle in the image | ✅ `dev-deploy-azure.yml:96` passes `--build-context addin=../outlook-addin`; `ssdDockerfile:16-34` builds and bakes it |
| Rebuild on add-in changes | ✅ `dev-deploy-azure.yml:43` includes `outlook-addin/**` in the path filter |
| `AppSpecific:Outlook` | ✅ `Enabled: true`, `UploadEnabled: true`, `PromoBannerEnabled: true` (`Docker.appsettings.template.json:172-177`) |
| nginx framing for the taskpane | ✅ `dep-az-dev/local-nginx.conf:85` — the same `location ^~ /outlook-addin/` block as UAT |
| `AppUrl` | ✅ `https://dev-ps.secuura.net/` |

**The only thing missing for dev-ps is the manifest** — which is [PS-636](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-636>) + [PS-637](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-637>). Worth stating plainly so nobody plans server work that is already done.

## The one genuine gap: AppDomains for the non-Entra providers

`manifest.xml:37-43` lists the domains the auth dialog may travel through:

```xml
<AppDomain>https://login.microsoftonline.com</AppDomain>
<AppDomain>https://ssdobeden.ciamlogin.com</AppDomain>
<AppDomain>https://psauthsecuuarademosg.ciamlogin.com</AppDomain>
```

The comment above it records why: the [PS-394](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-394/outlook-add-in-authenticated-compose-frontend-dialog-auth-attach) compose flow opens an Office dialog on `/Outlook/Auth` that navigates out to the identity provider and back, so *"those domains must be listed here."*

**The SSO work — now on develop — added sign-in providers that are not in that list.** `dep-az-dev/Docker.appsettings.template.json` configures Google (`/signin-google`), Apple (`/signin-apple`) and GitHub alongside Entra. By the manifest's own stated reasoning, a user signing into the add-in dialog with Google is navigating to a domain the manifest does not declare.

The Entra domains are already covered — dev-ps CIAM is `ssdobeden.ciamlogin.com` (shared with UAT) and workforce is `login.microsoftonline.com`, both listed. This is specifically about the **new** providers, and it affects every environment that enables them, not just dev.

Scope: add the provider domains per environment, driven by the same table as everything else — each environment declares what it actually has enabled. Confirm by signing in through each enabled provider inside the dialog, not by reading the manifest and concluding it looks right. If a provider turns out not to need the entry, record that finding rather than leaving a speculative domain in the list.

## First end-to-end install

Nobody has installed this add-in against dev-ps. Do not assume the environment is up — see the billing note on [PS-643](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-643>). Establish that first; if it is down, that is a prerequisite finding, not a failure of this ticket.

Then, in one mailbox:

1. Sideload dev and UAT together. **Two entries in the ribbon** — this is the [PS-636](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-636>) acceptance test and the reason the whole tranche exists.
2. Confirm each opens its own host: check `/api/outlook/status` `appUrl` from the panel, not the ribbon label.
3. Verify an attachment on dev-ps and confirm the verdict came from dev-ps's platform-k, not UAT's.
4. Compose flow: sign in through the dialog with each provider dev-ps has enabled; attach a document; confirm the share link points at `dev-ps.secuura.net`.
5. Redeploy dev and confirm the panel picks up the change without a manual re-install — the version/caching behaviour from [PS-637](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-637>).

**Production is out of scope here.** Its identity and manifest are built by [PS-636](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-636>)/[PS-637](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-637>) and stay dark behind `Outlook:Enabled: false`; nothing is installed or distributed for prod until [PS-641](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-641>) is decided.

## Acceptance

* **dev-ps being up is established first, as a prerequisite finding.** If it is down (see [PS-643](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-643/dev-ps-deploys-from-a-dead-branch-repoint-dev-deploy-azureyml-at)'s billing note), that is recorded as the blocker it is — not reported as this ticket failing, and not worked around.
* **The AppDomains gap is closed per environment, from what each environment actually enables** — **already satisfied in code** by PR #580 (see the correction below): the list is derived at render time from the provider keys Startup itself gates on, so an environment is covered without editing a list. What is still open is the confirmation: a provider that turns out **not** to need an entry gets that recorded as a finding rather than left as a speculative domain.
* **Confirmed by signing in through each enabled provider inside the Office dialog**, not by reading the manifest and concluding it looks right. The manifest's own comment explains why the list exists; it cannot tell you whether it is complete.
* **The five install steps are each observed with their stated evidence**, in one mailbox: two ribbon entries with dev and UAT sideloaded together (the [PS-636](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-636/outlook-add-in-give-each-environment-its-own-add-in-identity) acceptance test, and the reason the tranche exists); `appUrl` read from `/api/outlook/status` **in the panel**, never inferred from the ribbon label; the attachment verdict traced to **dev-ps's** platform-k rather than UAT's; a share link pointing at `dev-ps.secuura.net`; and a redeploy picked up with no manual re-install.
* **Production stays dark** — `Outlook:Enabled: false`, nothing installed, nothing distributed, no manifest shared. [PS-641](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-641/outlook-add-in-cater-for-production-without-applying-it-distribution) decides that, not this ticket.
* No server-side work is done that is already done: the bundle, the path filter, the `AppSpecific:Outlook` flags, the nginx framing block and `AppUrl` are all verified present per the table above, and the ticket says so rather than re-doing them.

**No Playwright test applies to the install itself.** The surface is an Outlook ribbon and an Office auth dialog inside a real mailbox, against a deployed environment — Playwright drives neither, and the systemTest estate only ever runs against a local slot. The mailbox walk-through is irreducibly manual, which is why each of its five steps above names the artefact that evidences it.

**Correction, re-checked against** `develop` **2d9a6639 on 7 Oct 2026 — the AppDomains half is already done.** PR #580 ("derive the add-in's AppDomains from the providers actually configured") **merged on 21 Aug 2026**. `manifest.xml` no longer carries a static `AppDomain` list at all — it has a `{{ADDIN_APP_DOMAINS}}` placeholder, and `ssd/Services/Outlook/OutlookManifestBuilder.cs` builds the list at render time from the **same configuration keys Startup gates each provider on**: `AzureAdCiam:Instance`, `AzureAdWorkforce:Instance`, `Apple:Enabled`, a non-empty `Google:ClientId`, a non-empty `GitHub:ClientId`, plus the add-in's own origin.

An earlier revision of this section proposed an xUnit contract test and asserted it would be red on `develop`. **Both halves of that were wrong**, and the claim is withdrawn: the test exists and is green. `tests/ssd.UnitTests/OutlookManifestBuilderTests.cs` already covers precisely the cases that were proposed — `An_enabled_provider_is_declared_and_a_disabled_one_is_not`, `An_empty_client_id_does_not_declare_the_provider`, `A_configured_entra_tenant_is_declared`, `The_addins_own_origin_is_always_declared`, `A_malformed_configured_domain_is_skipped_rather_than_emitted` and `Domains_are_not_repeated`. The *rule* is therefore already pinned offline, and no new xUnit test is needed for it.

**What remains is only the half that cannot be automated:** confirming in a real mailbox that each enabled provider's dialog actually completes, and the first end-to-end install. Those are the Acceptance bullets above. Worth re-reading the whole ticket before picking it up — if the install has also been done since, this may be finished rather than In Progress.

**Controls that must keep passing unchanged, on a local slot:** `systemTest/tests/functional/outlook_backend.spec.ts` and `outlook_identity_lines.spec.ts` — they cover the add-in's server side and its identity lines, so a manifest or AppDomain change that disturbs the backend contract turns them red. Neither needs editing for this work, and needing to edit them would itself be the signal that the change went further than intended.

nodes.body:
## New Outlook confirmed too — full client coverage

A complete process restart of new Outlook for Windows (not just closing the window — it stays resident in the tray) re-synced its app catalogue, and both add-ins now appear there as well. That completes client verification:

| Client | Secuura (Dev) red | Secuura (UAT) blue |
| -- | -- | -- |
| Classic Outlook (Windows) | ✅ | ✅ |
| New Outlook (Windows) | ✅ | ✅ |

For the record, since three UI paths cost real time today: **new Outlook has no sign-out option** — the catalogue refresh lever is a full process quit (tray icon included) or toggling classic/new. And the panel surfaces on a message's `...` → Apps, only on messages with attachments (`ItemHasAttachment` is the sole activation rule now).

Install/remove loop that works, immediate, no portal:

```powershell
New-App -Mailbox <user> -Url "https://dev-ps.secuura.net/outlook-addin/manifest.xml"
Remove-App -Mailbox <user> -Identity <AppId>
```

Still open, now purely functional testing: sign in through each provider inside the dialog (dev: Entra/Google/Apple; UAT: Entra only, by configuration), the same-attachment dev-vs-UAT verify comparison, and confirming a redeploy is picked up without re-install (PS-637 versioning).

## Visual confirmation in a real client — red and blue side by side

Classic Outlook for Windows now shows **Secuura (Dev) in red and Secuura (UAT) in blue** as separate ribbon buttons in one mailbox — the colour differentiation working exactly as intended at real ribbon size, on top of the two-AppId coexistence already proven via `Get-App`.

Two client-cache findings from getting there, both worth knowing:

1. **Classic showed a third, plain "Secuura" button** (navy, no environment suffix) that does not exist server-side — `Get-App` lists exactly two Secuura rows, and no row carries the old shared Id `b7e6c1a2-…`. So production's reserved Id is **not** squatted in the mailbox; the third button is a stale classic-Outlook ribbon cache entry from the pre-PS-636 install, and a full client restart should clear it.
2. **New Outlook / OWA lag behind.** Both add-ins render in classic but neither appears yet in new Outlook — its add-in list syncs from a different path than the EWS route `New-App` writes, on a schedule measured in hours. Classic proving the mailbox state correct means the remainder is client propagation, with no server-side lever. In new Outlook they will surface on a message's `...` → Apps control, on messages **with attachments**.

Remaining verification unchanged: provider sign-ins inside the dialog, redeploy pickup without re-install, and the same-attachment dev-vs-UAT verify comparison.

## Trap for whoever verifies this next: the Outlook Apps catalogue lags reality

Worth an hour of someone's time if it isn't written down.

The **Apps → "Built for your org"** catalogue in new Outlook showed a single card named plain **"Secuura"**, navy icon, described as *"Verify email attachments against blockchain-anchored **certification** records"* — at a moment when `Get-App` reported two correctly-installed add-ins:

```
DisplayName : Secuura (UAT)   AppId : 8cdff773-…   Enabled : True
DisplayName : Secuura (Dev)   AppId : 98206f09-…   Enabled : True
```

That card is **stale cache**. Nothing in the repo or served by any environment carries that text:

| Source | Description |
| -- | -- |
| The cached card | "…blockchain-anchored **certification** records" |
| dev-ps serves | "**DEV ENVIRONMENT** — not for use against real documents…" |
| uat-ps serves | "**UAT ENVIRONMENT** — not for use against real documents…" |
| prod row | "…blockchain-anchored **declaration** records" |

Even the pre-PS-636 manifest said "declaration", so that entry predates this whole tranche. It also showed the plain "Secuura" name and original icon — i.e. an identity that no longer exists in that form anywhere.

**Someone checking their work in that view would conclude the identity, description and icon changes had not taken.** They had. `Get-App -Mailbox <user>` is the authoritative source; the catalogue is not, and a full sign-out is what clears it.

Related: `Get-App -OrganizationApp` (no `-Mailbox` — the switches are mutually exclusive) is the authoritative view for tenant-wide deployments, and it correctly showed **no** Secuura entry, which is how we established the Integrated apps deployment had never gone live.

## Verification status

Server side for dev and UAT is **complete**: both installed, both enabled, distinct AppIds, manifests served from their own hosts, badge sourced from `/api/outlook/status`.

Remaining is client-side and behavioural:

- Open the panel from a message **with an attachment** — activation is `ItemHasAttachment` only now, so a message without one renders no buttons and is indistinguishable from a failed install.
- Sign in through each provider inside the dialog.
- Confirm a redeploy is picked up without re-installing ([PS-637](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-637) versioning).
- UAT still needs a deploy of `c133267`+ for its blue icon and the two manifest fixes.

## ✅ ACCEPTANCE TEST PASSED — dev and UAT coexist in one mailbox

Verified 2026-08-24 in a real Outlook mailbox (`stuart@obeden.com`):

```
DisplayName     AppId                                  Enabled
Secuura (Dev)   98206f09-0f5f-445e-88b8-f03c63798016   True
Secuura (UAT)   8cdff773-01a3-4855-aba4-a466e4fb918d   True
```

**Two rows, two AppIds, both enabled.** This is what the whole tranche was built for. Before [PS-636](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-636) the second install would have silently replaced the first, leaving a tester verifying documents against a system other than the one they believed they were using.

Also confirmed along the way:

- **[PS-637](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-637)** — both were installed straight from `https://<host>/outlook-addin/manifest.xml`. The served manifest is what a real client consumes, not just something that parses.
- **[PS-640](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-640)** — the environment badge rendered `UAT` in the panel, sourced from `/api/outlook/status`, not from the manifest. That is the check that survives someone re-installing over an existing entry.
- **`DisplayName` is honoured** — Outlook lists `Secuura (Dev)` / `Secuura (UAT)`. An earlier screenshot showed only "Secuura" in the Apps flyout header; that is a shortened form in that surface, not a defect.

## CORRECTION: the sideloading blocker I logged above was wrong

My previous comment claimed `My Custom Apps` was missing from the role assignment policy and was the reason no upload option appeared. **It was present all along:**

```
My ReadWriteMailbox Apps
My Custom Apps
My Marketplace Apps
```

Do not chase that. The real situation was narrower: the *portal* path was unavailable (Microsoft has been removing "Add a custom add-in" from new Outlook/OWA in favour of centralised deployment), and the **Integrated apps deployment never went live** — `Get-App -OrganizationApp` listed no Secuura entry at all, which is why nothing ever appeared. It was not propagation latency.

**The working install route is Exchange Online PowerShell**, and it is immediate — no 24-hour wait:

```powershell
New-App -Mailbox <user> -Url "https://dev-ps.secuura.net/outlook-addin/manifest.xml"
Get-App -Mailbox <user> | Format-Table DisplayName, AppId, Enabled
Remove-App -Mailbox <user> -Identity <AppId>
```

That restores the tight verify loop this ticket's plan assumed. `Get-App -OrganizationApp` (no `-Mailbox`; the two switches are mutually exclusive) shows tenant-wide deployments.

## What is still outstanding

1. **Sign in through each provider inside the dialog.** Dev advertises Entra CIAM, workforce, Google and Apple; UAT advertises only its own origin and CIAM, correctly, because it has no other provider credentials. Untested.
2. **Redeploy-picks-up-the-change** — the [PS-637](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-637) version/caching behaviour, unverified against a client.
3. **UAT needs a deploy** of `c133267` or later for its blue icon, the `SupportUrl` fix and the entity-rule removal. It currently runs `1.0.2425.57`, which predates all three.
4. **Production** stays off — `ps.secuura.net/outlook-addin/manifest.xml` returns 302, which is [PS-641](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-641)'s gate working as intended.

## BLOCKER: the tenant does not permit sideloading, so per-user install is unavailable

The acceptance test this ticket is written around — sideload dev and UAT into one mailbox, confirm two ribbon entries — **cannot be performed as written**. There is no "Add a custom add-in" option anywhere in Outlook on the web or desktop for this tenant.

That is not a UI change or a missing menu. Sideloading is gated by an **Exchange mailbox role assignment**, and when the role is absent the entry point disappears entirely rather than appearing disabled:

| Role | Grants |
| -- | -- |
| **`My Custom Apps`** | "Add a custom add-in" — from file or URL. **This is the one missing.** |
| `My Marketplace Apps` | Installing from the Office Store |
| `My ReadWriteMailboxApps` | Add-ins requesting read/write mailbox access |

Check and grant, in Exchange Online PowerShell:

```powershell
Get-ManagementRoleAssignment -RoleAssignee "Default Role Assignment Policy" | Format-Table Role
New-ManagementRoleAssignment -Role "My Custom Apps" -Policy "Default Role Assignment Policy"
```

Or Exchange admin center → Roles → User roles → *Default Role Assignment Policy* → tick **My Custom Apps**. Up to an hour to take effect, then sign out and back in — the client caches its capability list.

**Note it applies to everyone holding that policy.** If tenant-wide sideloading is not wanted, create a second role assignment policy carrying those roles and assign it only to testers via `Set-Mailbox -RoleAssignmentPolicy`.

### What this costs, and why it matters beyond this ticket

Without it, **every** add-in change — dev, UAT and eventually production — has to go through M365 Admin Center → Integrated apps, whose propagation window is **up to 24 hours**. That is a workable release path and a hopeless test loop. This ticket's plan assumed a tight sideload-verify cycle; if the role stays off, the plan needs rewriting around centralized deployment, and any estimate for add-in work should carry a day of latency per iteration.

Two options: grant the role to a small test group, or stand up a separate tenant where sideloading is permitted. **This is a decision for Stuart, and it gates the remaining verification here.**

## Second requirement: three connectors installed side by side

Requested: dev, UAT and production installable simultaneously, production once it is deployed.

**The design already supports it and needs no further code.** Each environment is a distinct add-in identity (PS-636), so Outlook treats them as three separate add-ins rather than one being replaced by another:

| Env | Add-in Id | Ribbon | Icon | Manifest today |
| -- | -- | -- | -- | -- |
| dev-ps | `98206f09-…` | Secuura (Dev) | **red** | 200, live at `1.0.2427.156` |
| UAT | `8cdff773-…` | Secuura (UAT) | navy — blue pending a UAT deploy | 200, live at `1.0.2425.57` |
| Production | `b7e6c1a2-…` | Secuura | navy (unchanged, by design) | **302 — add-in disabled** |

Measured 2026-08-24. All three identities and display names are contract-tested as distinct, so the "three coexisting" property is enforced rather than hoped for.

**What is actually outstanding for three-up:**

1. **The sideloading role above**, or three separate Integrated apps deployments — one per environment, each assigned to whoever needs it.
2. **UAT needs a deploy** of `c133267` or later to pick up its blue icon. I could not do this: Actions is billing-blocked, `uat-ps:22` is closed (pull-based deploys by design), and no AWS profile on this machine belongs to the platform-s account that owns the ECR repo.
3. **Production is deliberately off** — `AppSpecific:Outlook:Enabled` is `false`, which is why `ps.secuura.net/outlook-addin/manifest.xml` 302s rather than 200s. That is the go-live gate from [PS-641](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-641): while the flag is off there is nothing to install, so production cannot be deployed early by accident. Flipping it is a deliberate act, not part of this ticket.

So three-up is one tenant-policy decision and one UAT deploy away for dev+UAT, and gated on the production go-live decision for the third.

**Deployed to UAT** — in image `884a2a2`, still live in the current `6899ab3`.

The `AppDomains` entries are rendered by `OutlookManifestBuilder`, so this ships as part of the manifest PS-637 serves. That endpoint is confirmed working on UAT:

```
GET https://uat-ps.secuura.net/outlook-addin/manifest.xml  ->  200, valid <OfficeApp>
```

**Partially verified.** The manifest is served and parses; I have **not** checked that the `AppDomains` block within it carries the right hosts for this environment, and I have not exercised whether Outlook accepts them — that needs a real host. `OutlookManifestBuilderTests` passes in the suite (37/37 across the guard set), which pins the generation logic but not the deployed output.

Anyone with the add-in against UAT could settle it cheaply by reading the served manifest's `AppDomains` — it is a plain GET, no session needed.

Note this ticket is still **In Progress** in Linear while the code is on UAT. Left as-is rather than moved, since I do not know whether you consider it finished.

## dev-ps is up, and running the whole tranche — deployed manually 2026-08-21

`secuuradev.azurecr.io/ssd:7dd4855` (develop @ `7dd4855`, digest `sha256:8004d8c8…`) is live on `server-vm-dev`. The running container's digest was read back off the box and matches what was pushed, so this is that image and not a coincidence.

**The open question on this ticket is answered: the environment exists and works.** My earlier note said dev-ps might never have deployed successfully — it has now.

### Measured against the live box

| Check | Result |
| -- | -- |
| `/health/anchoring` | 200 |
| `/api/outlook/status` | `version: 1.0.2424.735`, `environment: "dev"` |
| `/outlook-addin/manifest.xml` | **200**, `application/xml`, 9692 bytes (was 302 to the not-found handler) |
| Manifest `<Id>` | `98206f09-…` — dev's own, not the shared one |
| Manifest `DisplayName` | `Secuura (Dev)` |
| Taskpane URL | `https://dev-ps.secuura.net/outlook-addin/taskpane.html` |
| Unsubstituted placeholders | 0 |
| `taskpane.html` headers | `Cache-Control: no-cache` **and** the CSP `frame-ancestors` for the Office hosts |

That last row is the one I most wanted to see. It confirms the mid-implementation reversal was right: had the header gone into a nested nginx `location`, `add_header` would have reset the inherited headers and dropped `frame-ancestors`, and Outlook could not have framed the panel at all. Both headers are present together on the real box.

### PS-639's own behaviour, proven rather than asserted

The served `AppDomains` are:

```
https://dev-ps.secuura.net
https://ssdobeden.ciamlogin.com
https://login.microsoftonline.com
https://appleid.apple.com
https://accounts.google.com
```

**GitHub is absent — correctly.** The deploy logged `WARNING: optional secret 'github-client-id' not found in Key Vault 'secuura-ps-dev-kv'`, so `Startup` never registers the GitHub scheme, and the manifest does not declare a domain for a provider this box cannot use. That is the derivation working against a real deployment, not a test double. If GitHub sign-in is wanted on dev, add `github-client-id` / `github-client-secret` to the vault and redeploy; the manifest follows automatically.

### CI still cannot do this

Every push to develop today created a run that died as `startup_failure`, zero jobs, `path: BuildFailed` — the billing-block signature, including all of today's merges. [PS-643](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-643)'s trigger fix did work: runs are now being *created* on develop pushes where previously nothing fired. They just cannot execute. **Until billing is restored, every dev-ps deploy is manual:** build `--platform linux/amd64` with `--build-context addin=../outlook-addin`, `az acr login --name secuuradev`, push, then `az vm run-command invoke` on `server-vm-dev` running `deploy-from-acr.sh`.

### What is still not done

Everything requiring a mailbox. **Two entries in one ribbon** — the acceptance test this tranche exists for — plus signing in through each provider inside the dialog, and the redeploy-picks-up-changes check. Sideloading is now one paste of `https://dev-ps.secuura.net/outlook-addin/manifest.xml` into **Add a custom add-in → Add from URL**.

## Code half merged — [PR #580](https://github.com/Secuura/platform-s/pull/580). Verification half still open, deliberately.

**Done:** the served manifest derives its `AppDomains` from the same configuration keys `Startup` gates each provider on — `Apple:Enabled`, a non-empty `Google:ClientId`, a non-empty `GitHub:ClientId`, plus the configured `AzureAdCiam` / `AzureAdWorkforce` instances and the add-in's own origin.

That coupling is the fix, not the list. A static list is a second place to remember, and this one had already been forgotten once when Google/Apple/GitHub arrived. A manifest can now neither list a provider that is off nor omit one that is on, and an environment on its own Entra tenant is covered without editing anything. 1875 tests pass, 6 new — pinning both directions, because asserting only the positive would let the list quietly become "everything, always", which is roughly what it was before.

**Not done, and this is why the ticket stays open:** nothing has been sideloaded against dev-ps. I can assert what the manifest *contains*; I cannot assert that Outlook accepts it, that two entries appear in one mailbox, or that a Google sign-in completes inside the dialog. Those are the acceptance tests for this whole tranche and they need a person and a live environment.

## Before that can happen

[PS-643](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-643) fixed the deploy trigger. It did **not** fix the billing block — GitHub Actions has been failing in ~3s since 2026-07-17, so dev-ps may never have deployed successfully at all. Establish that the environment is up and running current `develop` before treating any of the remaining checks as meaningful; a stale box would make every one of them a false result.

## The remaining checklist

1. Sideload dev and UAT together → **two entries in the ribbon**. This is the [PS-636](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-636) acceptance test and the reason the tranche exists.
2. Confirm each panel's badge and `/api/outlook/status` `appUrl` name their own host — not the ribbon label, which only says what was installed.
3. Verify an attachment on dev-ps and confirm the verdict came from dev-ps's platform-k.
4. Sign in through **each** provider dev-ps has enabled, inside the dialog. If one turns out not to need its `AppDomain` entry, record that finding rather than leaving a speculative domain in the list.
5. Redeploy dev and confirm the panel updates without a re-install — the [PS-637](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-637) version/caching behaviour.

Fetching the manifest is now one paste: `https://dev-ps.secuura.net/outlook-addin/manifest.xml` in **Add a custom add-in → Add from URL**. If it 404s, the add-in is disabled or the identity is unset — both are config, not code.

title: Compose seeds published *123 credentials by default, and the 11 rotation vars never reach the auth container from .env — every compose deploy (local, demo VM, Kintsugi)
description:
## BLUF

**Any compose deploy of this platform comes up seeding the published** `*123` **credentials, and the documented way to rotate them silently does nothing unless you happen to put them in the one undocumented file.** Two halves of the same asymmetry in `Blockchain/Dev/docker-compose.yml`:

* the single variable that **enables** published default passwords is interpolated from `.env` and **defaults to** `true`;
* the eleven variables that **replace** those passwords are not interpolated at all, and reach the container only via `.env.local` — which no example file and no doc mentions.

So the natural path (`.env`, which is what `env.example` and the deploy docs use) gives you: seeding **on**, published credentials **live**, and your rotation **ignored** — while the seeder logs that it updated the accounts.

Blast radius is **every compose deploy**: local, the demo VM, and Kintsugi. `docker-compose.local.yml` `include:`s `Blockchain/Dev/docker-compose.yml`, so the canonical local stack inherits it, and the demo VM + Kintsugi run that file directly.

## Recommendation

Two small changes, both in `Blockchain/Dev/docker-compose.yml`:

1. Flip the default: `ALLOW_DEFAULT_SEED_PASSWORDS=${ALLOW_DEFAULT_SEED_PASSWORDS:-false}`, and set it explicitly to `true` in the local-dev path that actually wants it. Opting in should be an act, not an omission.
2. Interpolate the eleven rotation variables in the `auth` service's `environment:` block the same way every other secret is (`- DEMO_USER_PASSWORD=${DEMO_USER_PASSWORD:-}` …), so `.env` — the file everyone edits — is a working channel. Then document them in `env.example`.

Neither is a code change to the auth service; the seeder's logic (`userRepo.ts:965-995`) is correct as written.

## A — the gate defaults to ON, and its stated premise is dead

`Blockchain/Dev/docker-compose.yml:626`

```yaml
- ALLOW_DEFAULT_SEED_PASSWORDS=${ALLOW_DEFAULT_SEED_PASSWORDS:-true}
```

The pen-test **F-05** fix gated the demo seeder on this variable. The auth service states the premise the gate rests on, at `services/auth/src/repositories/userRepo.ts:987-991`:

> *"The hardcoded fallbacks remain only because the seeder itself is now gated on* `ALLOW_DEFAULT_SEED_PASSWORDS=true` *(above) — i.e. **a deploy that doesn't explicitly opt in never sees these strings**."*

That premise is false for every compose deploy, because the compose file opts in on your behalf.

The justification for the default is at `:623-625`:

> *"Defaults to true here ONLY because docker-compose.yml is the local-dev compose; production is on Container Apps where this env var is unset and the gate stays closed."*

**That reasoning died with the KS-414 VM pivot (2026-07-08).** The Container Apps estate was deleted on 2026-07-31. Since the pivot, `Blockchain/Dev/docker-compose.yml` is not "the local-dev compose" — it is *the* deployment artefact for the demo VM and now for Kintsugi as well. The comment describes an architecture the project no longer has.

Measured on the running local stack:

```
$ docker exec secuura-auth sh -c 'echo $ALLOW_DEFAULT_SEED_PASSWORDS'
true
```

## B — the eleven rotation variables never reach the container from `.env`

Derived from source rather than from any prior write-up — every `seedPw()` call site in `services/auth/src/repositories/userRepo.ts`:

`ADMIN_USER_PASSWORD` · `DEMO_APEX_PASSWORD` · `DEMO_BUPA_PASSWORD` · `DEMO_DELTA_PASSWORD` · `DEMO_GREENFIELD_PASSWORD` · `DEMO_HOLDER_PASSWORD` · `DEMO_ISSUER_PASSWORD` · `DEMO_OXFORD_PASSWORD` · `DEMO_SECUURA_PASSWORD` · `DEMO_USER_PASSWORD` · `DEMO_VERIFIER_PASSWORD`

| check | result | control |
| -- | -- | -- |
| occurrences of each of the 11 in `docker-compose.yml` | **0 / 11** | `ALLOW_DEFAULT_SEED_PASSWORDS` → **1** |
| present in the running `secuura-auth` container | **0 / 11** | gate present, value `true`; 95 env vars total |

Both zero-results carry a control that fires independently, so they are real absences and not a grep that could never match.

The code's own rotation instruction (`userRepo.ts:992-993`) is:

> *"For per-tenant rotation, set* `DEMO_<TENANT>_PASSWORD` *env vars in Azure Key Vault and **surface them to the auth container**."*

"Surface them to the auth container" is the whole problem — it names no channel, and only one of the two obvious ones works.

## The correction — this is NOT "rotation is impossible"

An earlier write-up of this (KS-601 comment `4ada1e3a`) concluded the documented rotation *cannot work*. **That over-claims, and the correction matters because it changes the fix.** The `auth` service does declare an env_file:

```yaml
env_file:
  - path: .env.local
    required: false
```

Tested rather than assumed: of the **66** variables declared in `.env.local`, **66** are present in the running container. `.env.local` is a fully working injection channel.

So the accurate finding is an **asymmetry of channel**, which is worse than a flat "it doesn't work" because it fails silently in exactly one direction:

| variable | channel | reaches container from `.env`? | effect |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| `ALLOW_DEFAULT_SEED_PASSWORDS` | `${…:-true}` interpolation | **yes**, and defaults **true** | published `*123` credentials get seeded |
| the 11 `*_PASSWORD` vars | `.env.local` env_file only | **no** | rotation silently ignored |

`.env` is the file `env.example` is copied to, the file the setup instructions name, and the file compose reads for `${…}` interpolation — but it is *not* an env_file for `auth`, so values placed there are invisible to the seeder. Neither `env.example` nor `.env.local.example` mentions any of the eleven, or the gate.

## Why it fails convincingly

Recorded on Kintsugi during the KS-601 Stage C build (2026-08-20) — **this half is that session's on-box measurement; I have not re-run it here**, because reproducing it locally means changing `demo@`'s password and breaking the preflight persona:

Setting the eleven in `.env` and recreating the auth container printed `Demo user updated to match seed config` account after account — on a code path that genuinely does execute an `UPDATE … password_hash`. **The old password still authenticated.** Only a negative control (attempting a login with the *old* credential and expecting it to fail) caught it. Fixed on that box with a compose override making all 11 visible, then verified both directions: old `demo123` → **401**, new credential → **200**.

That is the part worth carrying: the failure produces success-shaped log output, so anyone rotating credentials and checking the logs will believe they succeeded.

## Scope note

Not in scope here: whether the demo VM *should* keep its seeded public credentials. Those are deliberate, documented sample logins for public demos (project `CLAUDE.md`). This ticket is about a deploy coming up more permissive than its operator intended, and a rotation that reports success without doing anything.

## Evidence

* `Blockchain/Dev/docker-compose.yml:570-666` — `auth` service; `:626` the gate; `:623-625` the dead premise; `env_file` at `:576-578`.
* `Blockchain/Dev/services/auth/src/repositories/userRepo.ts:965-995` — the F-05 gate, the `seedPw()` helper and its rotation instruction.
* `docker-compose.local.yml:33-35` — `include:` of `Blockchain/Dev/docker-compose.yml`.
* `Blockchain/Dev/env.example`, `Blockchain/Dev/.env.local.example` — neither names the eleven or the gate.
* KS-601 comment `4ada1e3a` — the Kintsugi on-box record (superseded on the "cannot work" point by the correction above).

## Suggested owner

Unassigned deliberately. Compose/deploy topology rather than service logic — @peter or @stuart to route; happy to take it myself if neither has context loaded.

nodes.body:
**One more instance of the same mechanism, found during the KS-1016 verification run (2026-09-10).**

`ADMIN_USER_PASSWORD` is read by `services/auth/src/repositories/userRepo.ts:1123` (`requiredSeedPw('ADMIN_USER_PASSWORD')`) and listed in `Blockchain/Dev/.env.example:133`, but it does not appear anywhere in `Blockchain/Dev/docker-compose.yml` on develop — so a value in a local `.env` never reaches the auth container. Observed on a fresh slot-4 stack with the key set in `.env`:

```
[auth] Demo user seeding skipped — no password supplied, and no pre-existing row to remediate
       {"email":"admin@secuura.com","hint":"set ADMIN_USER_PASSWORD to seed this account instead"}
```

and `env` inside `secuura-s4-auth` has no `ADMIN_USER_PASSWORD` entry. The hint in the log therefore points at something the operator cannot make work locally. `DEMO_SECUURA_PASSWORD` shows the same skip line for `platform.admin@secuura-test.invalid`, so it is likely the same gap.

Effect on the harness: every `super_admin` persona login is 401, which on the Schemathesis pre-merge run reads as 18 pytest failures plus the sweep's persona auth and the coverage gate (runs `pre-merge-ks-1016-2026-09-10T07-56-30Z-slot3` and `…T08-33-27Z-slot4`, identical sets). Attributed here rather than to that branch — it is compose plumbing, not test code.

**Update, same day:** the forwarding already exists on PR #896 (KS-682) — `ADMIN_USER_PASSWORD` appears 3× in its `docker-compose.yml`, 0× on develop and 0× on #933. So this instance closes when #896 merges; nothing further is needed here for it beyond the record. KS-955 §5 describes the wider chain this sits in (401 → 429 → account lockout); the 429 half was confirmed removable with `LOCAL_LOGIN_LIMITER_DISABLED=true` on slot 4 (12 rapid logins, all 200), the 401 half is this.

Related: KS-966 (the change that made the key required), KS-972 (the banner still printing the old value), KS-955, KS-969. Branch under verification: `feature/ks-1016-test_anchor_read_honesty-hardcodes-docker-exec-secuura`. Host: local Docker Desktop, one slot at a time, macOS arm64.

title: KS-256 review follow-ups: 5 example-fixable 400s, the tsx transpile-only spec-gate trap (§10), and a new `userAgent: Demo Issuer` instance
description:
The three items left open from @kksecura's 2026-08-19 review of PR #568. Split out per his own §8 reasoning — the parameter-example work is the bigger half of the same problem, and bundling it would expand a PR he has already reviewed twice.

**Every figure below was re-verified against the branch head** `92feea4a9`**, not carried over from the review.**

---

## 1. §4 — the five example-fixable 400s are still published

His triage stands unchallenged: **5 strictly example-fixable**, or **8 counting parameter examples**. My original "at most 4" was low. All five are still live in `docs/openapi/secuura-api.yaml`:

| # | Defect | Count at head |
| -- | -- | -- |
| 1 | `example-documentId` violates `SAFE_ID_PATTERN` | **17** |
| 2 | `example-code` exceeds the documented max of 8 | **3** |
| 3 | `example-challengeId` is not a uuid | **1** |
| 4 | `example-country` is not exactly 2 chars | **2** |
| 5 | `transfer-custody` pins two mutually exclusive fields | 1 |

Number 5 is the sharpest, because the spec contradicts itself **four lines apart** (`secuura-api.yaml:6318-6322`):

```yaml
description: Exactly ONE of `newHolderId` / `newHolderEmail` is required — neither is 400, both is 400.
example:
  newHolderId: example-newHolderId
  newHolderEmail: demo.issuer@example.com     # ← publishing exactly what the line above calls a 400
```

A reader copying that example gets a guaranteed 400, and the description already tells them why.

**Fix direction:** these land in the Zod sources (`services/*/src/*.openapi.ts`), then `npm run generate-openapi`. Numbers 1–4 need the placeholder to satisfy the constraint the schema already documents; number 5 needs the example to pin one field only.

## 2. The bigger half — parameter examples

Verified at head: **132 path parameters, 2 carrying an example.** That is the §7 gap on [KS-256](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-256/add-openapi-inline-examples-to-all-329-operations-eliminate-coverage)'s own body, and it is why this is a follow-up rather than a patch. Together with `operationId`/`links` ([KS-188](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-188/stateful-testing-declare-openapi-links-operationid-so-postgetdelete) — 0 of 613 links covered) it is the next real coverage step, and it dwarfs the five above.

## 3. §10 — the trap that produced the build failure, recorded nowhere

`npm run generate-openapi` runs the `*.openapi.ts` files through `tsx`**, which is transpile-only**. A type error in the very file the generator reads therefore **cannot** fail the spec gate.

That is exactly how the `documentUuid` breakage shipped: `check:openapi` was **green** — drift clean, E1–E9 0 findings across 354 blocks — while `originate` would not compile, and the failure only surfaced in the Docker build (30/34 images, `originate` + `migrations` red, no containers started).

`check:openapi` **green is not evidence the images build.** Nothing in `scripts/`, `CLAUDE.md` or `package.json` says so today. Options, in increasing order of strength:

1. Document it where the gate is defined and in `CLAUDE.md`.
2. Add a `tsc --noEmit` pass over the `*.openapi.ts` sources to `check:openapi`, so the gate covers the files it consumes.

Option 2 would have caught the original defect at the gate rather than in a 50-minute image build. @kksecura offered the wording or is happy for us to take it — his call.

## 4. A new instance of the §3 class his sweep did not reach

`secuura-api.yaml:7265` publishes:

```yaml
userAgent: Demo Issuer
```

Same mechanism as the 16 `address` fields fixed in `704c8c0f2`: a legitimate `FIXTURE_PERSON_VALUES` member landing on a **non-person** field, so **E5 passes it** — the guard is working to spec and the spec is wrong for the field. Not a leak; a documentation defect, since no client sends `Demo Issuer` as a user agent.

**Verified the rest are correct** — the other 21 `Demo Issuer` hits are all on genuine name fields and should stay:

```
17  displayName     2  channelName     1  fullName     1  name
 1  userAgent   ← the defect
```

**Fix direction:** same as §3 — either give `userAgent` its own fixture, or stop masking-category-3 claiming it. Worth deciding once for the class rather than per field, since `address` and `userAgent` are now two instances of it.

---

## Why these are not on [KS-256](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-256/add-openapi-inline-examples-to-all-329-operations-eliminate-coverage)

[KS-256](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-256/add-openapi-inline-examples-to-all-329-operations-eliminate-coverage)'s own acceptance already carries the 26×400 triage as an open box, and its two remaining boxes are gated on [KS-660](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-660/ci-every-needs-build-suite-job-dies-in-3s-with-zero-steps-develop-is) (CI executes zero steps). Items 1 and 4 here are small, item 2 is large, and item 3 is a gate change — none of them belongs in a PR that has been reviewed twice and is waiting on sign-off.

*— raised by agent on Peter's behalf, 2026-08-19. Figures verified at* `92feea4a9`*.*

nodes.body: KS-1285 (Schemathesis 4.27.2 → 4.27.5, 2026-09-21, slot 1, same head and seed): the examples-phase 400 set is **unchanged by the upgrade** — 17 operations answered 400 to their examples-phase case at 4.27.2 and 18 at 4.27.5 (all 17 still present; `POST /api/governance/proposals` added because 4.27.4 now fills missing values from schema `default`s). 4.27.5's "drop/skip examples that violate their own schema" removed none of them: these examples are schema-valid and fail runtime validation, which is this ticket's point. Numbers on KS-1285's evidence comment.

## Results 2026-09-14 — what today's 4.27.1 sweeps say about the three open items

Slot 3, from-scratch stack, `develop` @ `64c386e04` (PR #993 bump); `full-2026-09-14T15-04-07Z-slot3` 342 ops, 0 errored.

* **§4 — example-fixable 400s.** 4.27.1 now falls back to a generated valid body when an operation's `example`/`examples`/`default` are all invalid (changelog 4.27.1), so a bad inline example no longer costs an operation its positive coverage — it costs the *example* its purpose. The `positive_data_acceptance` bucket moved accordingly under the bump (KS-1169's before/after: 10 ops left it, 17 entered). Re-verify the five ops named here against the new run before spending effort on them; the fix is still the right one, the urgency may have changed.
* **§10 — the tsx transpile-only spec-gate trap.** Not exercised by today's runs (spec unchanged on `develop` today); no new evidence either way.
* **`userAgent: Demo Issuer` instance.** Not re-checked today.

One adjacent item worth folding in: the `LoginRequest` inline example `demo.issuer@example.com` / `<your-password>` locks itself out (F-06) on every sweep — details on KS-256. Refs as KS-NNN text.

## Item 2 fixture set — DESIGN FOR AGREEMENT (no code, no branch)

**@PeterD — this is a proposal, not a change.** Implementation stays deferred to the post-#568 tranche, per the hold agreed on this ticket. What follows is the judgement half: the fixture entries the remaining 90 path-parameter examples need, what each one means, and the four findings that change the shape of the job.

## BLUF

- **The sizing reproduces exactly.** 132 path-parameter occurrences on `c114ceddd`, **42 with an example, 90 without**, 15 distinct name+format combos, 62 `id (string)`, across 29 route groups — every figure in the 2026-08-21T00:46Z comment, re-measured from the tree rather than trusted. Control: the same script on `develop` returns **2/132**, matching the pre-tranche number.
- 🔴 **The content gate is structurally blind in exactly the position these 90 examples occupy.** E5 and E8 — the two rules that exist to stop a published value naming a live account — **cannot fire on a path-parameter example**. Proved by injecting E8's own founding defect and watching the gate pass. So this tranche gets no safety net: every value has to be right by construction.
- 🔴 **The spec on this branch publishes 17 URLs on `secuura.io`, and `secuura.io` does not resolve — NXDOMAIN, no NS, no SOA.** That is the KS-669 class again on a different host, and no guard rule covers URLs. It also **blocks `presentations/{id}` outright** (§6), so it needs a decision before implementation, not after.
- 🔴 **My own first draft of the set failed the gate, and testing it is how I know.** Five proposed values tripped E7 at the 40-character boundary — and chasing that found that **`FX.anchor.id` (`anc_…`) is a prefix the anchoring service has never minted**. Fix proposed and tested: widen `BENIGN_SHAPES` by one line rather than bend the values.
- **The count is 21 new fixtures, not ~15** — the 15 was name+format combos; the semantic count is higher because one name (`id`) spans many resources. They cover **62 of the 90**; the other **28 stay route-local or unresolved**, and `address` ×2 should reuse the existing `FX.wallet.address` rather than gain a fixture.

---

## 1. Sizing, re-verified against `c114ceddd`

Parsed the generated `docs/openapi/secuura-api.yaml` at both refs and counted `in: path` parameters carrying `example` on the parameter or its schema.

| ref | operations | path params | with example | without |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `develop` `29287565e` | 319 | 132 | **2** | 130 |
| `c114ceddd` (#568 head) | 319 | 132 | **42** | **90** |

The 90 break down exactly as the ticket recorded: 62 `id (string)` · 5 `customerId` · 5 `sessionId` · 3 `id (uuid)` · 2 each `cid`/`dsrId`/`did`/`address` · 1 each `chartName`/`widgetType`/`errorId`/`code`/`codeId`/`tier` · 1 `index (integer)`. Group spread also matches: billing 11 · kyc 9 · governance 7 · status 7 · m365 6 · transfers 6 · webhooks 5 · oauth 4 · long tail 1–3.

One number I read differently: **29** route groups counting by top-level resource (which is what reproduces your spread), **63** counting by resource + sub-path. Same data, and the 29 is the right unit for fixture design.

## 2. 🔴 The gate cannot see these examples — measured, not inferred

`leafName()` (`check/finding.mjs`) reports the last non-numeric segment of the dotted path. For a scalar `example:` on a parameter, that segment is the literal string **`example`** — never the parameter's `name`. E5 (`isPersonField`) and E8 (`IDENTIFIER_FIELD_RE`) both key off that field name, so neither can match.

I ran the gate four times against the `c114ceddd` spec, injecting `a0000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000010` — `demo@secuura.io`'s user id, **E8's own founding defect**:

| # | where the leak was injected | example blocks | gate |
|---|---|---|---|
| baseline | untouched spec | 394 | **exit 0** — clean |
| B1 | as a **path-parameter** example on `/api/billing/customers/{customerId}/invoices` | 395 | **exit 0 — E8 silent** |
| B2 | as a scalar `properties.userId.example`, 32 sites | 426 | **exit 0 — E8 silent** |
| C | inside an **object-valued** example under key `userId` | 394 | **exit 1 — E8 fires** |

Run C is the control, and it fails independently: same value, same rule, same spec — it reports `components.schemas.OperationStatus.example.userId` correctly. So B1/B2 are a real structural blind spot, not a dud value or a broken harness. Note B1's block count rose to 395: the example **was** collected, it just was not inspected.

What *does* still reach a path-parameter example, tested the same way — all four fire and exit 1: **E1** (`someone@gmail.com`), **E3** (`issuer123`), **E4** (`doc-1777346021120-1e528170`), **E7** (a `sk_live_…` blob). Those run in the global sweep, which walks the whole document and needs no field name.

**Two consequences.** For this tranche, E5/E8 give no protection and review is the only control. And more usefully: the one-line fix is to sweep a parameter's example under the parameter's own `name` instead of `example`, which would put all 132 — and every scalar property example — back under E5/E8. Worth its own ticket; I have not written it, and it is not this ticket's scope.

## 3. 🔴 `secuura.io` — 17 published URLs, and the domain does not resolve

`c114ceddd` publishes `https://example.secuura.io/resource` **17 times**; `develop` publishes it **0 times**. They come from `scripts/openapi-examples/synthesize.ts:203`, which returns that literal for `format: uri`, and the codemod baked it into six `*.openapi.ts` files — including `successUrl`, `cancelUrl`, `redirectUri` and `webhookUrl`.

Measured, with a control set:

| domain | DNS status | NS |
|---|---|---|
| `secuura.io` | **NXDOMAIN** | none, and no SOA |
| `secuura.ai` | NOERROR | `dns1/dns2.registrar-servers.com` |
| `secuura.net` | NOERROR | `dns1/dns2.registrar-servers.com` |
| `secuura.com` | NOERROR | `ns3/ns4.afternic.com` (parked) |

`example.secuura.io` has no A record. I could not establish registration status — `whois secuura.io` falls through to IANA and returns the `.io` **TLD** record, so its `status: ACTIVE` line describes the TLD, not the domain. The DNS result is what I am relying on: the apex has no delegation.

This is not a new sin of yours — `fixtures.ts` already says it in its own words: *"`secuura.io` is not a domain we are known to control (we hold secuura.ai and secuura.net), so publishing it in customer-facing docs points integrators at third-party infrastructure."* That reasoning was applied to emails and E1 enforces it. **There is no equivalent rule for URLs** — E1 splits on `@` and only inspects addresses — which is why KS-669 had to find `exports.secuura.com` by hand, and why this passes a clean gate.

Worth stating plainly in both directions: **#568 removes all 3 `demo@secuura.io` addresses** `develop` publishes (0 remain) — a real improvement, and exactly what E1 is for. The URL class is the part that travels the other way.

Suggested resolution, for agreement: point the synthesiser at `https://example.com/resource` (RFC 2606, already `EXAMPLE_DOMAIN`), regenerate, and add a URL-host rule alongside E1. That is a one-line change in `synthesize.ts` plus a regen — but it is your file and your branch, so I have proposed rather than touched it.

E7 also runs *before* the fixture-list check and never consults it, so **adding them to `FIXTURE_ID_VALUES` does not help** — and E7 is one of the rules that still applies in the path-parameter position (§2), so this would have bitten in the real tranche.

The string `anc_` appears exactly **once** in the whole anchoring service — in `anchoring.openapi.ts`, i.e. the published example itself. So the fixture is format-**false**: an integrator copying it uses a prefix the platform does not produce. That is the fourth instance of this ticket's recurring class, after the 16 `address` fields, `userAgent`, and `channelName: Demo Issuer` — a value that is plausible, certified by a guard, and wrong.

**So: keep `prefix_<uuid>` and widen the rule, rather than bend the values to fit it.** Two changes, both tested:

1. `BENIGN_SHAPES` += `/^[a-z]+_[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{12}$/i` — a prefixed uuid, when a bare uuid is already benign.
2. `FIXTURE_ID_VALUES` += the **19** of the 21 that are identifier-shaped (`FX.statusList.id` `'1'` is not identifier-shaped, and `FX.did` carries colons so `IDENTIFIER_VALUE_RE` skips it — neither needs an entry).

## The advisory

**GHSA-ggr8-5vv4-36mx \[high\]** — *"DeepmergeTS has stack exhaustion when merging recursive object graphs."* Merging an object containing a cycle or very deep nesting recurses until the call stack blows and the process crashes. Affects `<8.0.0`; we pinned **7.1.5**.

Note the advisory carries **no CVSS vector** (score reports 0) — "high" is the publisher's own label, not a scored assessment.

## Why an override, not a dependency bump

It is transitive and **upstream has not fixed it**:

```
services/originate
  └─ prisma@^7.8.0            ← devDependencies
       └─ @prisma/config
            └─ deepmerge-ts   ← pinned EXACTLY 7.1.5 by @prisma/config
```

Checked against the registry on 2026-08-19: `@prisma/config@latest` **(7.9.1) still pins** `deepmerge-ts@7.1.5`, and `prisma` already resolves to the latest 7.9.x via `^7.8.0`. So bumping Prisma changes nothing; an `overrides` entry is the only route until Prisma moves.

## Reachability today: none that ships

* `prisma` is the **CLI**, in `devDependencies`. The runtime deps are `@prisma/client` + `@prisma/adapter-pg`, neither of which pulls `deepmerge-ts`.
* `services/originate/Dockerfile:79` runs `npm ci --ignore-scripts --omit=dev`, so it is **not in the runtime image**. No deployed service carries this code. (The lock entry is even marked `"devOptional": true`.)
* The vulnerable path is `@prisma/config` deep-merging **Prisma's own config file** at CLI invocation — developer-authored input, not untrusted API input — and the impact is a crashed CLI, not a compromised service.

Build-time only, developer-input only, crash not compromise. Accepted on reachability, not absence — same standard as [KS-599](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-599/bump-nanoid-ghsa-2v37-7h3g-55p8-high-dompurify-ghsa-55q2-fjhq-7xh7).

title: The OpenAPI spec is now a consumed contract, but nothing in CI stops it drifting — plus two known spec/code divergences
description:
Raised by Platform S, 2026-08-19, from a full S↔K audit against K develop `74a330fc0`. **Nothing is broken today** — the spec is in sync. This is about keeping it that way now that something depends on it.

## What changed on our side

[PS-614](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-614>) (merged, S develop `2403313`) makes Platform S read `docs/openapi/secuura-api.yaml` at gate time and fail its build when S's lifecycle-verb vocabulary disagrees with K's published enum, in either direction.

We built it because of [KS-556](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-556>): K added `protect`/`unprotect`/`restore` on 2026-08-03, S adopted them on 2026-08-18, and for 15 days those events anchored with **no** `documentType` **at all**. Nothing failed, because every guard S had compared one hand-maintained copy of K's list against another. Reading K's own spec is the fix.

**Your spec is a strong contract, and that is why we chose it.** Verified: it is *generated* (`scripts/generate-openapi.ts:28`) from the same `LIFECYCLE_VERBS` / `LIFECYCLE_EVENT_ACTIONS` constants the runtime validates against, and the enums match exactly — 22 and 13, diffed programmatically, empty symmetric difference. That is a better guarantee than a hand-written spec could give.

## The gap

`check:openapi` **is not wired into any CI workflow.** It exists as an npm script (`Blockchain/Dev/package.json:43`), but grepping all 17 files in `.github/workflows/` for `openapi` returns **zero** hits. (`quality:static` in `pr-platform-suites.yml:238` runs in `systemTest/playwright`, a different workspace.)

So the spec is correct today by diligence, not by enforcement — and it is now load-bearing for a consumer outside this repo. A PR that changes a verb without regenerating would leave S's gate green while S sends something K rejects, which is the [KS-388](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-388>) 400-the-whole-anchor case.

**Ask:** run `check:openapi` in the PR workflow.

## Two divergences worth closing while you are there

**1.** `/api/v2/verification/verify-file` **is in code but absent from the spec.** Handler at `services/originate/src/routes/verificationV2.ts:497`; `verify-file` does not appear in `secuura-api.yaml` at all. The v1 equivalent is missing too. It is the only verify variant where the **server** computes the hash — i.e. the one a client cannot lie to — so it is the one most worth publishing. Invisible to a spec-reading consumer today.

**2.** `documentUuid` **is stricter in code than in the spec.** Code requires UUID **v4** specifically (`services/originate/src/routes/documents.ts:350` `UUID_V4_RE`, 400s v1/v5/v7); the spec publishes `format: uuid` (`secuura-api.yaml:4556-4557`), which any RFC 4122 version satisfies. A client generating a v7 UUID passes spec validation and is rejected at runtime. We happen to send v4 ([PS-570](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-570>) enforces the version nibble before sending), so this has not bitten us — but it would bite a new integrator. Either publish the v4 constraint or relax the code.

## One observation, no action implied

`emitLifecycleAnchor` (`services/originate/src/routes/documents.ts:1120-1128`) posts only `{documentId, contentHash, network}` to `/api/anchors` — no `metadata.documentType`, no `metadata.timestamp`. So lifecycle events recorded through **K's own** endpoints anchor unlabelled, while the same verbs sent by S on the flat path carry the verb on-chain. Consistent with [KS-319](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-319>)'s scope, but it means the [KS-556](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-556/add-protectunprotectrestore-to-the-ks-134-lifecycle-verb-vocabulary) / [KS-534](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-534>) / [KS-415](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-415>) vocabulary only ever reaches the ledger via the flat path. Flagging in case that is not intended.

## Verification

* A PR that edits a verb constant without regenerating the spec **fails** CI.
* `verify-file` (v1 and v2) appears in the published spec.
* `documentUuid`'s published constraint matches what the code enforces.

*Everything above verified read-only against develop* `74a330fc0`*. Happy to review a draft against our gate before you merge — we are the consumer and can tell you quickly whether it reads correctly from our side.*

nodes.body:
State corrected: In Review to In Progress. Divergence 2 is delivered; divergence 1 is open and tracked on KS-791.

Done: PR 808 (d2fe7d6d2) publishes the documentUuid v4 constraint the runtime already enforces (divergence 2). It was approved on the PR and is an ancestor of the kintsugi deploy b1fb543640e7. The ticket's headline ask, check:openapi in the gate, was recorded on 2026-09-04 as already satisfied.

Left: divergence 1, the verify-file operations. It was kept out of PR 808 because the live endpoint answered 415 at the gateway, and it now sits on KS-791 (PR 813).

**Merged to `develop` — PR #808, squash `d2fe7d6d255a19b7bc2a809d2e1a2fe8b1139908`.**

- Approval: Peter at head `3d8b40a07f0b5052513be2cf8fb899d1520279a5` (2026-09-08T14:18:43Z), re-verified immediately before the merge: approval at head, no later Peter review or comment, Test Evidence present.
- Squash parent `7bcb6612897f012d2051b6ff848b3fbcbb7d2542` = the `develop` tip asserted before the merge; tree `689662d87a247648d93ae9cd59983222c8a036f8` = `git merge-tree --write-tree` of that tip and the head.

State unchanged (In Review): this PR closes divergence 2 only; Peter (2026-09-08) asked to keep KS-663 open because its third criterion, a regeneration check that fails server-side, is still unmet.

## PR #808 approved — divergence 2 verified live

Approved [#808](https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/808) (divergence 2, the `documentUuid` v4 constraint). Full review posted on the PR; summarising here with the evidence, and flagging what remains open on this ticket.

Credit where due to the authoring session: divergence 1 was deliberately pulled from that PR after a live probe found `verify-file` 415ing at the gateway, so publishing its spec would have created a divergence rather than closing one. That is now KS-791 / [#813](https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/813). Recorded as a finding rather than an omission, which is the right way round.

### What was verified

| Claim | How it held up |
|---|---|
| Runtime enforces v4 | `documents.ts:331` `UUID_V4_RE`, applied at `:438` |
| Published pattern matches it | `[0-9a-fA-F]` / `[89abAB]` is an exact expansion of the `/i` flag — no widening, no narrowing |
| Scoped correctly | `DocumentCreateRequest.documentUuid` only; response schemas deliberately untouched, since `ks584-p3-verify-list.test.ts:222` asserts a legacy non-v4 pkey is returned as `documentUuid` |
| `userUuid` / `organizationUuid` | Left as bare `format: uuid`, matching the KS-596 ruling that those accept any RFC 4122 version |
| Runtime blast radius | None — no spec-driven request validator anywhere in `services/` or `packages/` |

### Test evidence

Run against branch head `3d8b40a07` on a local Docker stack built from that commit (33 containers, 32 healthy), 2026-09-08.

| Suite | Result |
|---|---|
| `test_document_uuid_validation.py` | **9/9 passed** |
| `test_document_uuid_contract.py` | **7/7 passed** |
| Served spec carries the constraint | Confirmed at `/api/docs/openapi.yaml`, on `DocumentCreateRequest` only |

Offline property-based generation probe, 300 examples each, to rule out `format: uuid` and `pattern` starving generation:

| Spec | Populated `documentUuid` | Violating v4 | Health-check failures |
|---|---|---|---|
| PR head | 56 | **0** | none |
| `develop` | 93 | **93** | none |

The counterfactual is the useful half: on `develop` every generated value was unusable input the runtime was always going to 400. So this change does not only document the constraint — it stops the contract suite spending `POST /api/documents` draws on values the endpoint could never accept.

The four platform suites were not re-run, matching the PR author's own statement. For a spec-only change with no runtime consumer of the spec, the two modules above are the directly relevant coverage.

**One process note:** the first invocation returned `16 skipped`, not passes — no `API_TOKEN` for that stack. `scripts/setup.py` provisioned one and the re-run was green. Worth knowing, since a gate reading only the exit code would have read that first result as a pass.

### Suggest keeping this ticket open

Of the three verification criteria in the description, one is now met:

| Criterion | Status |
|---|---|
| `documentUuid`'s published constraint matches the code | **Met** — #808 |
| `verify-file` (v1 and v2) appears in the published spec | Moved to KS-791 / #813 |
| A PR that edits a verb constant without regenerating **fails CI** | **Still open** |

On the third — and this is the original ask, so worth being precise rather than assuming it was covered: `check:openapi` runs from `scripts/preflight/preflight.sh:111`, a local pre-push hook. Grepping `.github/workflows/` for `openapi` still returns zero hits, on this branch and on `develop`. A local hook is bypassable and does not run server-side, so the criterion as written is not yet satisfied. It does not appear to have a ticket of its own.

One related suggestion while that is being picked up: nothing currently couples the published pattern to `UUID_V4_RE` — they are independent literals in two files, so relaxing one leaves the other silently wrong, which is the same drift class this ticket was raised about. A small assertion reading `UUID_V4_RE.source` against the generated spec would close it and would sit naturally alongside the CI wiring.

Happy to be corrected if the CI leg exists somewhere I did not look.

**PR [#808](https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/808) is open** — branch `feature/ks-663-wire-check-openapi-into-the-gate`, head `3d8b40a07`, rebased onto `develop` `d928a27f8`.

This branch had been committed and **unpushed since s123**. The reason was never the code: the pre-push preflight's advisory leg hung on an unreachable npm endpoint with no timeout, so the push could not complete. **KS-788 merged this morning (#807) and bounded it — this branch then pushed in 76 seconds, 11/11 legs, rc 0.**

Scope is **divergence 2 only**. Divergence 1 (the verify-file spec) stays out: a live probe found the route 415s at the gateway, so publishing its spec would create a divergence rather than close one. That is KS-791.

## Divergence 1 — the probe changed the answer: publishing it now would CREATE a divergence, so it is blocked

I authored both verify-file operations (v1 + v2) in the generated source, regenerated (spec 307 → 309), and `check:openapi` went green — KS-424 security guard satisfied, all 405 examples resolved. Then I probed the live endpoint before finalising, and **reverted them.** Here is why.

### verify-file is unreachable through the gateway — 415 on every file content-type

The endpoint's entire purpose is *"raw file bytes as the body; the server computes the hash."* Live on the local stack (`:6882`), against `POST /api/v2/verification/verify-file` with a real body:

| request Content-Type | result |
|---|---|
| `application/octet-stream` | **415 `UNSUPPORTED_MEDIA_TYPE`** |
| `application/pdf` | **415** |
| `text/plain` | **415** |
| none | **415** |
| `multipart/form-data` | **415** |
| `application/json` | 400 (handler reads raw bytes; JSON body-parser already consumed them) |

Only an **empty** body reaches the handler's own 400 (nothing for the media-type filter to reject). So there is no content type on which verify-file can actually receive a file through the gateway.

### This is already known — BACKLOG.md:122

> verify-file (v1 AND v2) is unreachable through the gateway — 415 from the JSON-only content-type enforcement. Where: `api-gateway/src/middleware/contentType.ts` (`enforceJsonContentType`). Verified live 2026-08-12 … raw-byte server-side-hash verification only works in-cluster (direct to originate).

Re-verified live today. The enforcement is a deliberate gateway control (content-type confusion defence); it predates this and is not a regression.

### Why I did not ship the ops

The two ops I wrote documented an `application/octet-stream` request body. **The gateway 415s that.** Publishing them would replace "absent from the spec" with "the spec says POST octet-stream and the gateway refuses it" — a spec/code divergence, which is the exact thing this ticket exists to close, and the exact KS-388 "S sends something K rejects" shape the ticket cites. A spec op for the consumer (Platform S) that 415s on use is worse than its absence.

### So divergence 1 is BLOCKED, and the two must be fixed together

To publish verify-file honestly, the gateway must first let those two paths through — whitelist them in `enforceJsonContentType`, or route them past it, so an `application/octet-stream` (or a raw binary) body reaches the handler. **Then** the spec ops (which I have, ready) can be added against a contract that actually holds. That gateway change is security-adjacent (it relaxes a content-type control for two paths) and should be reasoned about deliberately, not folded in at the tail of a session — so I am sizing it rather than rushing it.

**Recommended follow-up:** one ticket that (a) whitelists the two verify-file paths in the gateway content-type enforcement, and (b) publishes the two spec ops I drafted. I can hand over the drafted ops. Filing it unless you would rather fold it into the BACKLOG item.

## Net state of KS-663

- **Headline ask** (run `check:openapi` in the gate): already satisfied by preflight leg 1. No duplicate added.
- **Divergence 2** (documentUuid v4): FIXED, `df169eaf5`.
- **Divergence 1** (verify-file in spec): BLOCKED on the gateway 415 (BACKLOG:122). Publishing it requires the gateway fix first; the spec ops are drafted and ready to add once it lands.
- **The `emitLifecycleAnchor` observation:** unchanged, no action (as the ticket said).

Two of three parts closed; the third is correctly blocked rather than shipped as a new divergence. Leaving KS-663 In Review pending the gateway follow-up decision.
