title: The extranet test board has never shown a green run — 0 passed in 22, and the latest red is E2E 210/0 with Schemathesis producing no results
description:
## BLUF

**The team's own status board has never once been green.** The extranet Testing tab has recorded **22 Platform K runs since 2026-05-25: 17** `failed`**, 5** `error`**, 0** `passed`**.** Not one.

And the most recent red is misleading: **E2E passed 210/0**, and the run is marked failed because Schemathesis produced no parseable results.

A board that is permanently red is a board everyone learns to ignore — at which point it can never signal anything, which is the whole reason it was built ([KS-138](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-138), now Done and archived).

## Measured

`GET /api/tests/platform-k/runs` (22 runs, oldest 2026-05-25):

```
failed : 17
error  :  5
passed :  0
```

Latest dashboard (`GET /api/tests/platform-k/latest`, run of 2026-08-10T00:01:44Z, target "Azure Demo"):

```
✗ Findings to fix
  Schemathesis (API contract)   FAIL   — "No Schemathesis results parsed this run."
  End-to-end (e2e-v2)           PASS   — 210 pass · 0 fail · 10 skip · 2 flaky
```

So the one suite that produced results **passed cleanly**, and the red comes from the other leg producing nothing.

`platform-s` has **0 runs**, which is consistent and expected — [KS-139](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-139) (upload the S suite) is still open.

## A verdict bug in the generator, read rather than guessed

`secuura-extranet/ci/build-dashboard.mjs`:

```js
// :39
const schemathesis = (args.schemathesis || 'unknown').toLowerCase(); // success|failure|skipped|unknown

// :181
const schemathesisClean = smt.state === 'ok' ? realFail === 0 : schemathesis === 'success';
const overallPassed = schemathesisClean && e2e.ok;

// :190  — the BADGE, which handles 'skipped' correctly
pill(schemathesis === 'success', schemathesis === 'success' ? 'PASS'
     : schemathesis === 'skipped' ? 'SKIPPED' : 'FAIL');
```

**The badge and the verdict disagree about what** `skipped` **means.** Line 190 renders a skipped Schemathesis leg as `SKIPPED`; line 181 scores anything that is not exactly `'success'` as not-clean. The workflow passes `--schemathesis "${{ steps.schemathesis.outcome }}"`, and a skipped GitHub step reports `outcome: 'skipped'` — so **an e2e-only run is structurally incapable of reporting** `passed`, while its own dashboard says the missing leg was merely skipped.

Whether that is what happened on any given run I have **not** established — per-run dashboards return 404, so `latest` is the only one readable, and its badge says `FAIL` rather than `SKIPPED`, meaning that particular run's Schemathesis leg ran and failed rather than being skipped. **The verdict bug is real in the code either way**; it is not necessarily the cause of all 22 reds.

## Next action

1. **Fix the verdict/badge disagreement** — `skipped` should not fail a run, since the badge already says it does not. Small change, `build-dashboard.mjs:181`. *(Not done in this session: the extranet auto-deploys on push to* `main`*, and this session is under the deploy hold.)*
2. **Find out why Schemathesis produces no NDJSON** on the demo target — the artifact path is `systemTest/schemathesis/output/schemathesis-reports/schemathesis-output.ndjson`. This is the substantive half.
3. **Then** get one green run on the board, so a future red means something.

## The pattern

Fourth instance today of the same defect — **signals firing into channels nobody reads** — and the only one aimed at humans rather than CI:

* [KS-637](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-637) — nightly Internal Audit, 40 consecutive failures.
* [KS-636](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-636) — base-image watchdog flagged a CRITICAL, unread 13 days.
* [KS-635](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-635) — a baseline exception expiring 2026-08-31 whose owner is archived.
* [KS-634](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-634) — no gate runs the service unit suites.

This one is different in kind and worse in effect: the others are unread, **this one is read and disbelieved.**

*Found during the 2026-08-14 backlog sweep, running the extranet skill's test-runner review that boot skipped.*

nodes.body:
**Measured 2026-09-07, in a catalogue pass over all 293 open tickets:** GitHub Actions is retired for this repo and I verified it directly rather than taking it on trust. **2,000 runs across 20 API pages are 100% `startup_failure`, back to 2026-08-20** — it never became non-uniform, so the outage is at least 18 days and widening the pages could not find its start. The three most recent runs return **zero jobs**. **16 workflow files are still in the repo doing nothing.**

**This is the cause of the symptom in this ticket.** The extranet Testing tab's runner dispatches a GitHub Actions workflow (`extranet-test-run.yml`). Actions has been dead for at least 18 days, and the board has been red for far longer — 17 `failed`, 5 `error`, 0 `passed` in 22 runs since 2026-05-25.

**So the board is not broken; it is disconnected.** No amount of fixing the parsing or the dashboard will make it green while its trigger cannot start a job. Any fix has to answer what executes the suites now that Actions does not — which is the same question **KS-652** and **KS-961** face.

Sibling **KS-139** (upload the Platform S suite so the runner executes it) is blocked by the identical cause. That one is Stuart's, so it is an escalation for Kam rather than something I have touched.

— catalogue pass 2026-09-07 (Blockchain-B, board-only seat). Measured, not inferred.

title: node:24-alpine carries a CRITICAL (CVE-2026-59873) — our own base-image watchdog flagged it on 2026-08-01 and the failure went unread
description:
## BLUF

**The base-image CVE watchdog fired on 2026-08-01 and nobody heard it.** Its scheduled run failed — which is, by the workflow's own design, the alarm — reporting `node:24-alpine`**: 1 CRITICAL / 4 HIGH — CVE-2026-59873**. That is the base image for **all ten backend services**.

Thirteen days unread at the time of filing. The watch is monthly, so without intervention the next signal is **2026-09-01**.

## Evidence

`.github/workflows/base-image-refresh.yml`, run `30685775724`, `event=schedule`, `created 2026-08-01T05:24:40Z`, `conclusion=failure`. Failing step: **"Evaluate watch conditions"**. Job log:

```
=== Trivy scan (CRITICAL/HIGH) of fresh local bases ===
  node:24-alpine                            : 1 CRITICAL / 4 HIGH — criticals: CVE-2026-59873
  nginx:1.30-alpine                         : 0 CRITICAL / 0 HIGH
  nginxinc/nginx-unprivileged:1.30-alpine   : 0 CRITICAL / 0 HIGH
  edoburu/pgbouncer:v1.25.2-p0              : 0 CRITICAL / 2 HIGH
  redis:8-alpine                            : 0 CRITICAL / 0 HIGH
  postgres:15-alpine                        : 1 CRITICAL / 14 HIGH — criticals: CVE-2025-68121
```

The postgres critical is the known [KS-365](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-365) residual (local-dev surface only, upstream's to fix) and is **not** why the run failed. The run failed on **Case 2** of its own contract:

> The run FAILS in exactly two cases, both worth a human: … 2. any OTHER base reports a CRITICAL → a pinned base has re-accumulated a critical CVE; treat like KS-363 (refresh/bump + redeploy).

`node:24-alpine` is that other base. The workflow did exactly what it was built to do.

**Every pinned base also reported** `MOVED` — all six tags were republished upstream since the last pull, so the images we build on are behind their own tags regardless of the CVE.

## Scope

`node:24-alpine` is the `FROM` for **10 service Dockerfiles** (`nginx:1.30-alpine` for the other 2). So this is not one service — it is the whole backend, local and demo alike.

## What I have NOT established

* **Whether CVE-2026-59873 is exploitable in our usage.** I did not look it up: the project rule forbids fetching external URLs/changelogs unless asked. Someone should read the advisory before sizing this.
* **Whether it is still present today.** The scan is from 2026-08-01 and the tag has moved since. It may already be fixed upstream — a re-run answers it in minutes.

**Neither gap is a reason to leave it.** A critical on the base image of every service, flagged by our own watchdog and unread for a fortnight, is worth a human either way.

## Next action

1. **Re-run the watch now** (`workflow_dispatch` on `base-image-refresh.yml`) to get a current reading rather than a fortnight-old one.
2. Read CVE-2026-59873 and decide: rebuild on the moved tag, bump the base, or accept with a written reason.
3. If a rebuild is needed it lands behind the Kintsugi hold like everything else — it is a rebuild of every service image.

## The process defect, which is the more important half

**A failed scheduled run is this watch's ONLY notification channel**, and it is one nobody checks. The workflow header says so plainly: *"Scheduled-run failures notify via GitHub, which is the reminder."* That reminder went nowhere for 13 days.

Same shape as [KS-635](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-635) (an audit-baseline expiry whose owning ticket was archived) and [KS-634](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-634) (no gate runs the service unit suites): **we have signals that fire correctly into channels nobody reads.** Worth deciding once, for all three, where an unattended failure should actually land.

*Found during the 2026-08-14 backlog sweep while verifying KS-365.*

nodes.body:
**BLUF:** Kam ruled the 31-decision card `secuura-backlog-31-decisions-1109` on 2026-11-09 at 13:44:07 (live board), in these words: "Decision secuura-backlog-31-decisions-1109: a — All recommendations (A and B)". Option a reads: "Every row ruled as recommended; a board seat files and moves the tickets; the KS-607 demo rows still wait for a separate yes." This ticket is row C2 of the decision pack. Section C rows are ruled by Wednesday, with Kam holding a veto, and Wednesday ruled this one as recommended: a local scheduled scan (Trivy) of the base images on a Secuura seat's schedule, reporting to the board. Each deploy also records which base image it built on. This adds a doctor check and a portability item.

Measured in the decision pack: the monthly alarm fired on 2026-08-01 and went unread, and GitHub Actions has been dead since 2026-08-20 (KS-638). The build goes to a build seat; nothing was changed in code by this comment.

Comment only: the state stays Backlog.

## Evidence only — what the Kintsugi rebuild actually baked (2026-08-15, session 35)

**No action taken on this ticket: not closed, not re-scoped, not re-prioritised, and the watch was NOT dispatched.** Adding evidence for whoever decides it.

**Why I did not re-run the watch, even though it is this ticket's own Next Action #1:** `base-image-refresh.yml` is shared CI, and dispatching it is actioning the ticket rather than informing it. Flagging that the ticket's first step is currently blocked by scope, not by difficulty — **it is a `workflow_dispatch` away for anyone who has that scope**, and it would answer the "is it still present?" gap in minutes.

## What I could measure: the demo VM after the full rebuild

The 2026-08-14 Kintsugi deploy rebuilt **all 30 service images natively on the VM**, so it re-pulled `node:24-alpine` at that moment. Read directly from the running containers today:

| | |
| -- | -- |
| Node | **v24.19.0** |
| Alpine | **3.24.1** |
| Arch | **aarch64** |
| Base rootfs (from image history) | `alpine-minirootfs-3.24.1-aarch64.tar.gz` |
| Service image created | **2026-08-14T03:31:59Z** (the rebuild) |

**Consistent across four services checked independently** — `auth`, `originate`, `api-gateway`, `anchoring` — all `node v24.19.0 / alpine 3.24.1`. Confirms the ticket's scope claim that this is one base under the whole backend, not a per-service question.

## The digest this ticket asked for is not recoverable from the VM

`docker image inspect node:24-alpine` on the demo VM returns **`No such image`** — the base tag is not retained after the build, so there is **no `RepoDigest` to read**. The build cache that would have held it was pruned during the same deploy (14 GB, to make room for the rebuild).

**So the specific artefact the next-action asks for — "the digest now baked" — cannot be produced after the fact.** The version triple above is the strongest available substitute, and it is arguably the more useful one anyway: **CVE applicability is decided by package versions, not by a manifest digest.**

**Worth carrying:** if a future rebuild wants its base digest recorded, that has to be captured *during* the build (`docker image inspect node:24-alpine --format '{{index .RepoDigests 0}}'` before pruning), because it is gone afterwards.

## What this does NOT establish

- **Whether `node:24-alpine` at 24.19.0 / alpine 3.24.1 still carries CVE-2026-59873.** I did not look up the advisory — the project rule forbids fetching external URLs unless asked, and the ticket already flags this same gap. **Nothing here should be read as "it is fixed" or "it is still present".**
- **Whether the demo's build pulled the same digest the 2026-08-01 scan saw.** The scan ran on x86-64 CI; the demo is **aarch64**, so they are different manifests under one tag regardless.

## Net
The demo is running a base that was **freshly pulled on 2026-08-14**, thirteen days after the flagged scan, on a tag the watch reported as `MOVED`. That is a genuinely newer base than the one scanned — **but "newer" is not "clean", and only the advisory or a re-run settles it.**

title: Retired Azure UAT/prod infrastructure still exists and still bills — PS-565 recorded it as gone
description:
[PS-565](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-565/remove-the-dead-azure-deployment-directories-and-az-deploy-scripts) removed the Azure deployment directories and recorded that *"that infrastructure and its Key Vaults no longer exist, so nothing there could run"*. **That is not correct.** Both resource groups are present in the subscription right now, Key Vaults included.

Found while removing the matching terraform stacks on [PS-589](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-589/move-dev-ps-to-azure-tracking-project-sso>) — the code is gone (`056a0f6`), the resources are not.

## What is actually there

Subscription `a0ee7d32-2e4a-47a0-9a49-9c001817a545`, region `southeastasia`.

`secuura-ps` (was prod)

| resource | detail |
| -- | -- |
| `server-vm` | `Standard_B2ls_v2` — **deallocated** |
| `server-osdisk` | StandardSSD_LRS |
| `server-ip` | Static / Standard — `4.194.63.230` |
| `kv-secuura-prod-sg` | Key Vault (contents not enumerated — no list permission, and not needed) |
| `backup-vault` | Recovery Services; `server-vm` still **Protected** |

`secuura-uat-ps` (was UAT)

| resource | detail |
| -- | -- |
| `server-vm` | `Standard_B2ls_v2` — **deallocated** |
| `server-osdisk` | StandardSSD_LRS |
| `server-ip` | Static / Standard — `20.205.232.149` |
| `kv-secuura-uat-sg` | Key Vault |
| `secuurauatacr` | Container registry, Basic SKU — **45 tags** of the `ssd` repo |

Plus `AzureBackupRG_southeastasia_1`, holding restore point collections for `server-vm` and `secuura02-demo-vm`.

## Why it matters

The VMs are deallocated, so **compute is not billing** — which is probably why this went unnoticed. Everything around them is: two OS disks, two *static* Standard public IPs (these bill whether attached or not), two Key Vaults, a registry holding 45 image tags, and an **active backup policy still protecting a VM that has not run in months**.

Live UAT and prod are on AWS (`uat-ps.secuura.net`, `ps.secuura.net`), so none of this serves traffic.

## The awkward part: terraform cannot clean it up

The stacks that built it had **no backend block** — local state, never committed. So the state is wherever it was applied from, probably nowhere recoverable. Without state, the terraform code could not destroy these resources; it could only ever have *created* more. Both stacks declared resource groups that already exist, so an apply by anyone assuming they were current would have collided with live infrastructure. That is why the code was removed rather than kept "just in case" — it was a hazard, not an escape hatch.

Cleanup is therefore a **manual delete** (or an import-then-destroy, which is not worth it for two dead boxes).

## Before deleting anything

1. **The two Key Vaults are the real question.** They hold the secrets the old Azure deployments ran on — plausibly the last copy of some values. Check contents and confirm each is either in the AWS Secrets Manager equivalents or genuinely dead, *before* deleting. Soft-delete/purge-protection settings matter here.
2. `secuurauatacr` **holds 45** `ssd` **tags** — the deployment history of the old Azure UAT. Confirm nothing references it.
3. **The backup vault** must be unprotected before the VM/RG can be removed, and deleting it discards the restore points.
4. Note `secuura02-demo-vm` also appears in the backup RG — check whether the demo environment is a separate live concern before touching it.

I have not deleted or modified any of it.

## Acceptance

* [PS-565](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-565/remove-the-dead-azure-deployment-directories-and-az-deploy-scripts)**'s record is corrected first.** Its claim that the Azure infrastructure and Key Vaults "no longer exist" is amended or annotated, because that sentence is what let this go unnoticed — and `ssd/dep-az-dev/README.md` is checked for the same assumption while nearby.
* **Both Key Vaults are adjudicated before anything is deleted.** `kv-secuura-prod-sg` and `kv-secuura-uat-sg` are enumerated **by secret name only** (`az keyvault secret list --query "[].name"`), and each name is matched to its AWS Secrets Manager equivalent or recorded as genuinely dead. **No secret value is retrieved, shown or copied** — if a value turns out to be the last copy of something, that is a hand-over, not a step to perform here. Soft-delete / purge-protection state is recorded for each vault before the delete, since it decides whether the delete is reversible.
* `secuurauatacr` and its 45 `ssd` tags: confirmed that nothing references the registry — no deploy script, no compose file, no pipeline — and the decision to discard the tag history stated rather than implied.
* The backup vault is **unprotected before** any resource-group delete (`server-vm` is still `Protected`), and the loss of its restore points is accepted in writing.
* `secuura02-demo-vm` is adjudicated **separately** — it appears in `AzureBackupRG_southeastasia_1` and is not covered by this ticket's "two dead boxes" framing. Establish whether the demo environment is live before touching anything of its.
* **After the delete:** `az group show` for `secuura-ps` and `secuura-uat-ps` both return NotFound, and the next billing period is quoted as a **measured figure** — the two static Standard public IPs (`4.194.63.230`, `20.205.232.149`), two StandardSSD OS disks, two Key Vaults and the Basic registry gone. A "should be cheaper" is not the criterion; the delta is.
* Terraform is **not** used — no import-then-destroy, no apply. The stacks had no backend block and their state is unrecoverable; an apply would have collided with live infrastructure, which is why the code was removed. Record that the cleanup was a manual delete, so nobody later reads the absent terraform as an oversight.

**No Playwright test applies, and nothing in platform-s changes.** This is cloud-resource cleanup in a subscription — there is no code, no view and no route involved, so there is nothing for a browser to drive and no assertion a spec could make. The verifiable criteria are the `az` command observations above: the by-name vault listings, the `az keyvault show` soft-delete state, the unprotect confirmation, the two `az group show` NotFound results, and the measured billing delta.

nodes.body:
**Correction: the terraform state is NOT lost. It exists, and that changes the cleanup path.**

I previously recorded — here and in commit `3766f94` — that the retired Azure stacks had local state that was "wherever it was applied from, probably nowhere recoverable", and concluded cleanup had to be a manual click-through delete.

**That was wrong.** The state files are on disk in the root checkout, untracked:

| file | size |
|---|---|
| `az-secuura-docker/terraform.tfstate` | 66,554 bytes |
| `az-secuura-docker/terraform.tfstate.backup` | 66,549 bytes |
| `az-secuura-docker/terraform.tfvars` | 1,724 bytes |
| `az-secuura-UAT-docker/terraform.tfstate` | 60,634 bytes |
| `az-secuura-UAT-docker/terraform.tfstate.backup` | 58,389 bytes |
| `az-secuura-UAT-docker/terraform.tfvars` | 1,722 bytes |

All six are now copied into the secrets store under `ssd/az-docker/…`, verified by checksum.

### What this means

Cleanup can be a proper `terraform destroy` rather than deleting resource groups by hand. That is materially better: it removes the backup vault's protected item, the Key Vaults, the ACR and the networking in dependency order, and it tells you what it is about to remove before it does.

The code was deleted from the repo by PR #472, but it is recoverable:

```
git show 1765a9c^:ssd/az-docker/az-secuura-docker/main.tf
```

or restore the whole directory from the commit before the merge. Pair it with the state and tfvars from the secrets store, `terraform init`, then `plan -destroy` to review before committing to anything.

### Urgency

These files were sitting **only** in a working directory. They are correctly gitignored (root `.gitignore` `*.tfstate` / `*.tfvars`, so they were never committed and there is nothing to purge from history) — but "gitignored and untracked" also means a `git clean -fdx` would have destroyed the only means of cleanly tearing down that infrastructure. They are now in the store, so that risk is closed.

The earlier statement that the code "could only ever have created, not destroyed" still holds as a reason not to keep the directories in the repo — an apply against existing resource groups would still collide. The difference is that destruction is now a supported path rather than an impossible one.

**Key Vault access review — I cannot enumerate either vault, and one access policy is worth a look.**

Both vaults are **access-policy mode, not RBAC** (`enableRbacAuthorization: false`), and the signed-in user (`Stuart@philipcuffyahooco.onmicrosoft.com`, oid `985f067a-…`) holds no policy on either, so the data plane is closed — no names, no values.

### Who *can* read them

| principal | `kv-secuura-prod-sg` | `kv-secuura-uat-sg` |
|---|---|---|
| `server-vm` (VM managed identity) | Get, List | Get, List |
| `terraform-secuura` (SP) | Get, List, Set, Delete, Purge, Recover | Get, List, Set, Delete, Purge, Recover |
| `philipcuff_yahoo.co.uk#EXT#@…` (**guest**) | get, list, **set** | get, list, **set** |

The first two are expected — the box read its own secrets, and the terraform SP provisioned them.

The third is a **guest (B2B) identity backed by a personal Yahoo address, with read *and write* on both the old production and UAT vaults.** The tenant is itself named `philipcuffyahooco.onmicrosoft.com`, so this is very likely the tenant owner rather than anything untoward — flagging it as a fact, not an alarm. Standing write access to retired production secrets is still worth a deliberate decision rather than inheritance.

The `server-vm` policies are now pointing at deallocated VMs and can go with them.

### Deletion safety (for the cleanup itself)

| | value |
|---|---|
| soft delete | **enabled**, 7-day retention |
| purge protection | **not enabled** |

So a deleted vault is recoverable for 7 days and *can* be purged deliberately — deletion is reversible short-term but not permanent-by-default. Worth knowing before anyone removes a resource group.

### To let me list the contents

Least privilege for this: grant **`list` only, not `get`**. `list` enumerates secret names; `get` returns values. Names are all that is needed to decide whether anything here is missing from AWS Secrets Manager.

```
az keyvault set-policy --name kv-secuura-prod-sg --object-id 985f067a-4a44-4f8e-9a26-95ba35e7ee75 --secret-permissions list
az keyvault set-policy --name kv-secuura-uat-sg  --object-id 985f067a-4a44-4f8e-9a26-95ba35e7ee75 --secret-permissions list
```

I have not run these — granting access to production secrets is a security change and is yours to make, not mine to self-authorise. Even with the grant I will report **names only**; values stay unread, per the standing rule that cost a full rotation on PS-309.

title: Wire the status-page XSS probe into preflight (or decide not to) — it runs today only by hand
description:
## BLUF

`scripts/security/status-page-xss-probe.mjs` exists, passes, and is **proven able to fail** — but nothing runs it automatically. Decide whether it joins `scripts/preflight/preflight.sh` as a 7th check.

## Recommendation

Wire it in, in a session scoped to preflight. Not as a rider on a security PR.

## Why it was left unwired

`frontend/status/index.html` is a static page with no `package.json` and no test runner, so the probe has no suite to live in. Preflight is the natural home — it is explicitly "the cheap cross-cutting sweeps the per-package gates miss", and this is exactly that shape.

But preflight is the **shared pre-push gate**. Adding a check to it changes the pre-push path for Peter and Stuart, and a new gate that turns out to be flaky blocks their pushes in a repo where neither knows a change happened. That is the reasoning Wednesday set on KS-628 and it applies unchanged here: being permitted and being right are different questions.

## What wiring it involves

* Add a 7th step to `scripts/preflight/preflight.sh` invoking `node scripts/security/status-page-xss-probe.mjs` from `Blockchain/Dev`.
* The probe needs no running stack and no network — it reads the file and drives the page's own `render()` in-process, so it is fast and deterministic.
* Its one fragility: it parses the page's `<script>` block by string split. If the page gains a second `<script>` or moves to a bundler, the probe exits 2 with an explicit "page structure changed" message rather than passing silently. Worth confirming that failure mode is acceptable in a gate before adding it.

Filed from session 30 alongside the KS-487 B-5 fix.

title: kyc `livenessVideo` is accepted by spec and runtime, then silently discarded — no code path reads it
description:
## BLUF

`livenessVideo` is accepted by both the OpenAPI spec and the runtime Zod schema on `POST /api/kyc/{id}/selfie`, and **no code path anywhere reads, stores or processes it.** A caller who uploads liveness evidence gets `success: true` and the bytes are discarded.

## Recommendation

Decide which half is right, then make the other match — do not align one to the other by reflex. Either implement storage + liveness processing, or remove the field from the schema and the spec. Documenting it as inert (done in KS-487 B-4) is a stopgap, not the fix.

## Detail

* Declared: `services/kyc/src/index.ts` `submitSelfieSchema` (`livenessVideo: z.string().optional()`) and `services/kyc/src/kyc.openapi.ts` `KycSelfieUploadRequestSchema`.
* Repo-wide grep for `livenessVideo` returns **only those two declarations plus a comment** — no reader, no writer, no persistence.
* Meanwhile the handler sets `livenessCompleted: true` and `livenessScore: 0.95` in mock mode regardless of what was sent (and regardless of whether `livenessVideo` was sent at all).

This is the KS-624/625/KS-488-C-2 family: a contract that advertises a capability the runtime does not have. Found while fixing KS-487 B-4 (magic-byte verification on the sibling image fields).

Filed from session 30. Not fixed in the B-4 PR — that PR's scope is image content verification, and silently deleting or implementing a published field is a contract change that deserves its own decision.

title: Implement real wallet signature verification (CIP-8/COSE + address binding) — needs the COSE key back in the request contract
description:
## BLUF

Implement real wallet signature verification for `POST /api/wallets/verify`.
The endpoint currently **fails closed with 501** (KS-488 C-2, PR #685) — it used
to return `verified: true` for any three non-empty strings. This ticket is the
work that makes it actually verify.

**It is not a patch.** It requires a breaking request-contract change, new crypto
dependencies, and test vectors from real wallets. That is why C-2 shipped the
refusal rather than an implementation.

## The blocker: the published contract cannot express a verifiable request

CIP-30 `signData` returns `{ signature, key }` — a COSE_Sign1 plus a **COSE_Key****
****carrying the public key**. This service already models that shape in its own
`CardanoDataSignature` (`services/wallet-connector/src/types/index.ts:149-152`).

The published request schema is `{ address, message, signature }` — **no key**.
A Cardano address is a blake2b hash of the public key, so the key cannot be
recovered from it. There is nothing to check the signature against.

The field was removed by **KS-475** as "unread", which was true — the runtime
never read it, because the runtime never verified anything
(`wallet-connector.openapi.ts:139-143`). KS-475 was a correct fix for a
spec/runtime mismatch; its side effect was to delete the one field a real
implementation needs.

**Class rule worth keeping:** when a spec and a runtime disagree, establish which
one is right *before* aligning them. Aligning documentation to a stub silently
converts "not built yet" into "not in the contract", and the next reader cannot
tell the difference.

## Work required

1. **Contract (breaking):** re-add `key` to `WalletConnectorVerifyRequest` — the
   CIP-30 COSE_Key hex. Reintroduce a response schema (C-2 deleted
   `WalletConnectorVerifyResponse` because the operation had no success shape).
   Restore `200`, and remove the C-2 `expected-statuses` exception from
   `systemTest/schemathesis/schemathesis.toml` in the same PR so the operation is
   held to normal positive-acceptance again.
2. **Cardano path (CIP-8/COSE):** parse COSE_Sign1, verify Ed25519 over the
   `Sig_structure`, then — **the load-bearing step** — derive the address from the
   embedded public key and check it equals the claimed `address`. Without that
   binding, an attacker supplies their own key with their own valid signature and
   "verifies" as any address they name. Verifying the signature alone is not
   verifying ownership.
3. **EVM path:** the spec's old description also promised `ecrecover`. Decide
   whether EVM is in scope at all or whether the operation is Cardano-only —
   promising both again without building both repeats the original defect.
4. **Dependencies:** COSE/CBOR + Ed25519 (`@emurgo/cardano-message-signing-nodejs`
   and `cardano-serialization-lib` are WASM; a pure-JS `cbor` + `@noble/ed25519` +
   blake2b path avoids WASM). Two known traps apply: ESM-only packages imported
   from CJS crash at runtime in a way tsc and vitest both mask, and the demo VM is
   **ARM64**, so WASM/native builds must be checked there, not just on the dev
   machine.
5. **Test vectors:** real `signData` output from at least two wallets (Eternl,
   Lace). Hand-rolled vectors would test our own encoder against itself.
6. **Negative tests that must pass:** valid signature from a *different* key
   claiming this address; replayed signature against a different message;
   malformed COSE; wrong network id.

## Reachability, for prioritisation

Authenticated and gateway-routed (`api-gateway/src/routes/proxy.ts:627`,
`authenticateToken(true)`), published in the OpenAPI spec. **No in-repo consumer**
(swept `*.ts/tsx/js/py/yaml/gs` — only the route, its spec entry and the generated
yaml), so nothing internal is blocked by the 501 today. Priority should follow
whether an external integration needs wallet-ownership proof; until then the
refusal is the correct state.

## Do not

Re-open this as a "quick fix" that returns `200 { verified: false }` or restores a
permissive default. The C-2 regression suite
(`__tests__/ks488-c2-wallet-verify-fail-closed.test.ts`, 13 tests) asserts no
response may claim `verified: true`, independently of status code, and was
mutation-tested to confirm it fails if the old behaviour returns.

## Cross-reference from KS-684 — the harness is about to build a guard whose removal is YOUR trigger

Recording the dependency in both directions so neither side is a surprise later.

## What KS-684 is adding

`POST /api/wallets/verify` currently returns a deliberate, documented **501 Not Implemented** — the fail-closed replacement for the stub that answered `verified: true` for any input (KS-488-C). Schemathesis' `not_a_server_error` check treats **any** 5xx as a failure, so every sweep reports that correct behaviour as a defect. Measured on a from-scratch stack, 2026-08-25: **29 × 501** in a single `pre-merge` sweep.

KS-684 scope item 7 fixes the reporting side with the `integration_5xx_guard` shape already used for the 13 by-design-503 operations — two halves, never one:

1. exclude the operation from the blanket `not_a_server_error` check, **and**
2. restore coverage with a narrow guard so anything **other than** the ruled 501 still fails.

The exception covers the ruled shape only. A bare exclusion would be masking.

## Why this ticket needs to know

**When KS-627 lands, that guard must come out — and something has to tell us.**

Once real CIP-8/COSE verification replaces the 501, the operation will start returning 200/400/401 like any other. At that moment:

* the **exclusion** becomes wrong — the operation should be back under the ordinary `not_a_server_error` check;
* the **narrow guard** becomes wrong — it asserts a 501 that should no longer exist;
* and if neither is removed, the harness will be quietly tolerating a 5xx on an endpoint that is supposed to have stopped emitting one. That is the exact masking pattern the guard was built to avoid, arrived at from the other direction.

So the guard should be written with a **tripwire**: if `/api/wallets/verify` stops returning 501, the harness must go red and say *"KS-627 has landed — remove the KS-684 exception"*, rather than silently continuing to accept whatever it now returns.

## What we are NOT asking for here

Nothing on this ticket changes, and no work is being requested. The guard is entirely inside `systemTest/`; this is a pointer so that whoever implements CIP-8/COSE verification knows a test-side exception is keyed to the current 501 posture and expires with it.

**One thing worth confirming when you get to it:** whether the replacement keeps 501 in the operation's documented status list. The spec currently declares `401, 403, 404, 415, 429, 500, 501, 502, 503` for this operation. If 501 stays declared after real verification lands, the harness needs to know whether it is still reachable or purely vestigial.

## Status of the guard itself

**Not yet built.** Item 7 is the one KS-684 scope item still open, because the 501 posture is platform behaviour and the ruling is Kamil's, not the harness's. It is recommended for its own ticket so a platform decision cannot hold up the Schemathesis 4.25.2 bump — KS-662 is sequenced behind that bump.

title: /presentations/verify reports a presentation verified without checking the holder signature — challenge/domain compared, proof never validated
description:
## BLUF

`POST /api/presentations/verify` reports a verifiable presentation as verified **without ever checking the holder's signature**. It compares `challenge` and `domain` strings and stops. A presentation carrying a garbage `proofValue` verifies `true` provided the challenge and domain match — so the holder-binding guarantee the endpoint exists to provide is not enforced.

**Tracking ticket in the KS-621 pattern: severity provisional, fix shape deliberately blank.** The by-design-or-remediate ruling is Kam's. Filed off [KS-489](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-489) Review D pass-2 (peter, 2026-07-21) — unhomed since.

## The finding, re-verified at `c13b5ba9a` (2026-08-13)

`services/vc-issuer/src/routes/presentations.ts` — citation unmoved:

* `:316-322` — the only proof checks performed: `if (challenge && proof.challenge !== challenge)` and `if (domain && proof.domain !== domain)`.
* `:323` — `// In production, verify the cryptographic signature` — the check that would bind the presentation to its holder is a comment.
* `:349-350` — the response reports `challengeValid` / `domainValid`, and the overall verdict is built from those.

Note the failure mode inside the failure mode: both checks are **conditional on the caller supplying the value** (`!challenge || …`). A verify request that simply omits `challenge` and `domain` skips them, leaving no check of any kind.

## Why this is the one that matters more than its label suggests

**It is reachable, and the prism finding is not.** `/api/presentations` is proxied to `vcIssuer` behind `authenticateToken(true)` (`api-gateway/src/routes/proxy.ts:712, 715-717`). By contrast the prism forged-signature path has no gateway mapping and no internal consumer (detail on that ticket). Of the two findings in this pair, **this is the live one**.

**And the platform has already ruled on this pattern — in this very service.** `services/vc-issuer/src/routes/credentials.ts:125-128` documents the Audit A-11 remediation: the issuance path used to stamp `Ed25519Signature2020` over an HMAC with a hardcoded fallback key, which the comment calls *"fraud-grade for a credential issuer"*, and the gate at `:129-145` now refuses to issue without a real `VC_SIGNING_KEY`. The **issuance** half was fixed to fail closed. The **verification** half, three files over, still returns `true` on an unverified signature. Same service, same class, one half fixed — the [KS-623](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-623) shape, where a fixed half makes the surviving half read as closed.

## The deciding question

**Is** `/presentations/verify` **a real verification endpoint, or demo scaffolding?**

* If **real** → the missing Ed25519 check is a Wave-2 integrity item, and the A-11 gate on the issuance path is the precedent for how this service is expected to fail (closed, with an explicit refusal, not a cheerful `true`).
* If **scaffolding** → then per the KS-520/522 honesty precedent it must not answer `verified: true`; an unverified presentation is not a verified one, and the response should say which checks actually ran.

Either way the current response is the problem: it reports a verdict it did not compute. **Fix shape blank pending the ruling.**

## Provisional severity

**Med-High** per Wednesday's SCORE ruling (session 25). Linear has no Med-High level, so this is recorded as **Medium** — the label is carried here rather than silently rounded. Stated plainly: **the reachability evidence argues this should outrank the prism High**, since this path is live behind auth and that one has no caller. Not re-ranking it myself — flagging it so the ordering is Kam's choice and made on the evidence rather than inherited.

## Open leg, named so it cannot quietly close

Not live-proven. The reachability above is derived from the gateway route table and the code, **not** from a request that actually returned `verified: true` on a forged `proofValue`. That proof is cheap to produce against the local stack (`secuura-vc-issuer` is Up + healthy) and should be run before anyone accepts or dismisses this — same discipline as KS-622's untested has-MFA enumeration leg.

title: prism issues VCs with random bytes as the Ed25519 proof and verifies them as passed — the A-11 fraud pattern fixed in vc-issuer, never fixed here
description:
## BLUF

`services/prism` issues verifiable credentials whose `Ed25519Signature2020` proof is **64 random bytes**, and its `/verify` returns `passed: true` without checking anything. This is the identical pattern that was ruled fraud-grade and **fixed in** `vc-issuer` **under Audit A-11** — `services/vc-issuer/src/routes/credentials.ts:125-128` says so in its own comment. It was never fixed in prism.

**Tracking ticket in the KS-621 pattern: severity is provisional and the fix shape is deliberately blank.** The by-design-or-remediate ruling is Kam's, and it turns on the deciding question below. Filed off [KS-489](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-489) Review D pass-2 (peter, 2026-07-21) — the finding has had no home since.

## The finding, re-verified at `c13b5ba9a` (2026-08-13)

Peter's citations are unmoved — verified line-by-line, not assumed:

| Site | Code |
| -- | -- |
| `services/prism/src/index.ts:658-663` | `type: 'Ed25519Signature2020'` … `proofValue: crypto.randomBytes(64).toString('base64')` |
| `services/prism/src/index.ts:787` | `checks.push({ check: 'proof', passed: true }); // Mock verification` |
| `services/prism/src/index.ts:35` | `const PRISM_MODE = process.env.PRISM_MODE \|\| 'mock';` |

## Two corrections to the original framing — both make it read differently

**1.** `PRISM_MODE` **is decorative. It is never branched on.** Peter's write-up says *"*`PRISM_MODE` *defaults to* `'mock'` *with no production gate on the issue path → a prod deploy that **forgets the flag** forges credentials."* Measured: `PRISM_MODE` occurs **5 times** in the file — the declaration (`:35`), the `/health` response (`:376`), the `/api` info response (`:390`), the boot log (`:893`) and the boot banner (`:899`). `grep -c "if.*PRISM_MODE\|PRISM_MODE ===\|switch.*PRISM_MODE"` returns **0**.

So the risk is not a forgotten flag. **The flag has no effect at all**, and it is *already set to a non-mock value in both deploy paths*: `docker-compose.yml:965` sets `PRISM_MODE=basic`, and `deployment/azure/services.bicep:980` sets `PRISM_MODE=basic`. The behaviour is byte-identical to mock.

**2. The service actively misreports its own mode.** Because `:376` and `:390` echo `PRISM_MODE` into `/health` and `/api`, prism currently answers `mode: "basic"` to any operator, monitor or auditor asking whether it is mocked — while forging every signature. That is worse than a missing gate: a missing gate is silent, this one answers the question wrongly. Anyone who checked "is this service mocked?" the obvious way would have been told no.

## Reachability — the reason severity is provisional, not asserted

Bounded to what I could prove, and it cuts **toward** lower live risk:

* **The gateway does not route to prism's credential path.** `/api/credentials` → `vcIssuer` (`proxy.ts:697-699`), `/api/presentations` → `vcIssuer` (`:712,:715-717`). The **only** prism mapping is `/api/did` (`proxy.ts:645-647`), authenticated.
* **Zero internal consumers.** Repo-wide, `PRISM_SERVICE_URL` / `prism:4001` has no caller outside the gateway's own service-config and system-status listing. No frontend calls `/api/prism`.
* **But the service is live**: `secuura-prism` is Up + healthy in the local stack, and it was in the Container Apps bicep. The forging path is **one route mapping away** from being reachable, with nothing in the code to stop it.

This is the same disposition class as [KS-488](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-488)'s C-2 wallet-verify stub — **latent, not live**: reachable in principle, no current consumer trusting the result.

## The deciding question (this is what the ruling turns on)

**Does** `services/prism` **have a future in which it runs for real — or is it a stub that should refuse to issue at all?**

The question as originally posed — *"does prism ever run non-mock?"* — assumes a mode switch that could be flipped. There isn't one. So the real question is narrower and sharper:

* If prism is **dead or demo-only scaffolding** → the honest fix is to make it *say so* (refuse to issue, or label the proof honestly per the KS-520/522 precedent, where a `mock_tx_` anchor is never presented as on-chain proof), and stop `/health` reporting `basic`.
* If prism is **intended to become a real DID/VC service** → this is a Wave-2 integrity item and the A-11 remediation already applied to vc-issuer is the template.

**Fix shape deliberately blank pending that ruling.** Specifying it now would pre-decide the product question, which is the KS-621 lesson.

## Provisional severity

**High**, per Wednesday's SCORE ruling (session 25) — carried as given. Recorded honestly: the reachability evidence above argues this is *latent*, while the reachable half of the same finding class sits in the vc-issuer holder-binding ticket. If Kam re-ranks the pair, the argument for putting the reachable one first is in both tickets.

## Adjacent, deliberately not filed as a third ticket

Peter's pass-2 also carries a **Low**: `services/vc-issuer/src/routes/credentials.ts:100` — `const issuer = req.body.issuer || defaultIssuer`, caller-controlled, then signed with the platform `VC_SIGNING_KEY` at `:146`. The A-11 gate (`:129-145`) removed the hardcoded-key fallback but **not** the caller-supplied issuer identity, so the finding survives its own fix. The session-26 brief scoped this to two tickets, so it is recorded here rather than filed unasked — flagging it for a ruling on whether it needs its own home.

It is waiting for review; nothing is merged or deployed.

- The verify route no longer passes a proof it never checked: `verified` is false, with the reason "Proof signature not verified: not implemented".
- `GET /api` lists the issue route as not implemented.
- `PRISM_MODE=basic` in `docker-compose.yml` and `services.bicep` is left in place and is now inert.
- No code in the repo calls prism's issue route or reads its mode; the gateway sends `/api/credentials` to vc-issuer. So nothing known reaches the forging path today; this makes it refuse regardless.
- Tests: 10 new cells, 7 red on develop for the predicted reasons and 10 green with the change; one mutant per changed site; the 39 existing prism cells unchanged. Real signing (option 2) is not built.

https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/2130

**BLUF:** Kam ruled the 31-decision card `secuura-backlog-31-decisions-1109` on 2026-11-09 at 13:44:07 (live board), in these words: "Decision secuura-backlog-31-decisions-1109: a — All recommendations (A and B)". Option a reads: "Every row ruled as recommended; a board seat files and moves the tickets; the KS-607 demo rows still wait for a separate yes." This ticket is row A6 of the decision pack, ruled as recommended: option 1. Make prism honest now: it refuses to issue (a 501, the same fix as the wallet-verify one in PR 685) and stops reporting its mode as "basic". Small; one revert undoes it.

A build seat does the work; nothing was changed in code by this comment.

Alongside this comment the ticket moves from Backlog to Todo.

## A third instance of this pattern exists — and it was remediated on 2026-08-13, before your ruling

Recording this here **so your ruling covers three instances knowingly rather than
two blindly.** This is an input to the decision, not a pre-emption of it.

**The third instance:** `wallet-connector`'s `POST /api/wallets/verify` returned
`{ verified: true }` for any request carrying three non-empty strings. No
cryptography ran. Found as KS-488 **C-2**; fixed to fail closed with 501 in
**PR #685**.

## Why it was not held for your ruling, when KS-624 and KS-625 are

The three are the same pattern — a service asserting cryptographic validity it
does not perform — but they are not equivalent on the axis that matters here:

| | reachable? | does it *claim* to verify? |
|---|---|---|
| **prism** (KS-624) | **Latent** — gateway routes only `/api/did` to prism; `/api/credentials` + `/api/presentations` go to vcIssuer | yes — answers `mode: "basic"` while stamping `crypto.randomBytes(64)` |
| **vc-issuer verify** (KS-625) | proxied behind auth, reachable | yes |
| **wallet-connector verify** (C-2) | **live, published, gateway-routed, authenticated** | yes — the OpenAPI description asserted *"Verifies CIP-30 (Cardano) signatures via the COSE key, or EVM signatures via ecrecover"* |

"These mocks are acceptable pre-funding" is a coherent position for a latent stub
behind an unrouted path. It is a materially different proposition for an endpoint
that is **actively returning a false cryptographic assurance to whoever calls it**,
while its own published documentation tells the caller verification happened.

That distinction is our judgement, not yours — which is exactly why it is written
here rather than left implicit in a merge.

## If you rule "by design, leave them"

**Reverting C-2 is one revert.** PR #685 is a single squashed commit touching one
handler, its spec entry, one schemathesis exception and a test file. Nothing
depends on the 501. Say the word and it goes back.

Note what reverting would restore, so the choice is explicit: an authenticated,
published endpoint answering `verified: true` to any caller, with a spec that says
it verified a CIP-30 signature. If the ruling is "acceptable pre-funding", the
honest form of that is a stub that *says* it is a stub — which is the shape C-2
shipped (501 `NOT_IMPLEMENTED`), not the one it replaced.

## What C-2 did NOT do

It did not implement verification, and it did not pretend to. Real CIP-8/COSE
verification is filed as **KS-627** — it needs a breaking contract change (the
CIP-30 COSE key was removed from the request schema by KS-475 as "unread", and a
Cardano public key cannot be derived from a blake2b address, so no correct
implementation can exist against the published contract), new crypto dependencies,
and test vectors from real wallets.

## The question still open for you, unchanged

KS-624 and KS-625 remain **by-design-or-remediate**, untouched, awaiting your call.
Nothing about prism or vc-issuer changed on 2026-08-13.

title: Document reads are scoped by tenant and owner, never by organization — cross-org protection is emergent, not enforced
description:
**TRACKING TICKET — deliberately NOT a fix spec.** Filed off the KS-486 finding-2 disposition (2026-08-13, `develop de4781ca2`). Its purpose is to give the gap a permanent home so it cannot be lost, **without committing to a security model that has not been decided.** The fix shape is blank on purpose — see *Why there is no acceptance criteria* below. Related: [KS-619](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-619) (the finding-3 defence-in-depth ticket, same pattern).

## BLUF

**Nothing is leaking.** Cross-org document reads are denied today, and that was proved with a control. But the denial does **not** come from an organization boundary — neither the repository layer nor the route layer contains an `organization` predicate anywhere on the document-read path. What actually denies the read is a **per-owner 404-cloak**, which covers cross-org access only as a side effect.

So the property "one organization cannot read another organization's documents" is currently **emergent, not enforced**. Whether that needs to change is a product question that is on Kam's desk, not a call this ticket makes.

## What each layer actually does (verified on `develop de4781ca2`, not inherited)

**Repository layer —** `services/originate/src/repositories/documentRepo.ts`**: tenant only.**
Every read/write predicate is `tenant_id` and nothing else (15 occurrences). The block comment at `:190-201` documents this as deliberate, citing KS-4 and the migration-011 RLS policy. `getDocument()` (`:203`) scopes both its `external_id` and its `uuid` lookup by `AND tenant_id = $::uuid`; the update path does the same (`:461-462`). **Zero** `organization_id` **predicates in the file.** `owner_user_id` appears only in INSERT column lists and one response mapping (`:146`, `:325`, `:350`, `:384`) — never in a WHERE.

**Route layer —** `services/originate/src/routes/documents.ts`**: owner identity, not organization.**
The denial that produces the 404 is at `:888`:

```js
if (userId && document.owner?.id && document.owner.id !== userId && !isAdmin && !isRecipient) {
  // Return 404 (not 403) to avoid leaking document existence to non-owners
  return res.status(404).json(...);
}
```

There is no organization term in that condition. Grepping `organization` across the whole file returns 12 hits and **none of them is a read predicate** — they are `onBehalfOf` resolution (`:84`, `:335`), KS-597 metadata passthrough (`:355-359`, `:398-411`), and an `issuerOrgId` on a different (write) route (`:683`).

## The correction this makes to finding 2's framing

KS-486 finding 2 was dispositioned as *"the route layer treats org as a boundary and denies cross-org, while the repo does not"*. The first half is **imprecise, and the imprecision matters**: the route enforces **ownership**, which is a different rule that happens to also deny the cross-org case that was tested.

Two consequences that an org-boundary framing would hide:

1. **It is stricter than org in one direction** — two users in the *same* organization also get 404 on each other's documents unless one is an admin or the named recipient. Anyone reasoning "org-mates can see org documents" would be wrong about current behaviour.
2. **It is weaker than org in another** — the protection is attached to `owner.id`, so any condition that makes a caller the owner, an admin, or the recipient removes it entirely, and any code path reaching `documentRepo` *without* this route check has no org protection at all. That second case is the actual risk, and it is exactly what a repo-layer predicate would cover and a route-layer one would not.

## Why it is not live-exploitable today

From the finding-2 investigation, kept because it is the evidence that this is remediation and not an incident: `demo@` (org `fb1dfc8c`) fetching a tenant-A document owned by org `a0000000-…-0010` returns **404**, while **super_admin fetching the same document returns 200** and SQL confirms the row exists, is anchored, and has an owner. The 200 is the control — without it the 404 could have been a dead probe rather than a denial.

## The open product question — this is what the ticket is waiting on

> **Is** `organization` **a security boundary in Platform K that MUST hold, or a UX/labelling grouping where** `tenant` **is the real boundary?**

Routed to Kam (not Stuart — out sick per the 2026-08-12 ruling 12). It is a statement about what Platform S's tenancy model *is*, not something derivable from Platform K's code, because:

* Tenant provisioning does `CREATE DATABASE` per tenant, so **tenant** is a hard boundary and organizations live *inside* it, many-to-one — 79 orgs across 7 tenants locally, only 4 of which sit alone in their tenant.
* The S↔K contract puts **independent end-customers in one tenant**: `register-connector` is one platform-admin-authorised handshake per Platform S Organisation, and a provisioning key is constrained to its own tenant.

## Why there is no acceptance criteria

Writing "add repository-layer organization scoping, red-proved, with an admin-bypass control" as acceptance would **pre-decide the question above** — it only makes sense if the answer is "org is a boundary". If the answer is "org is a label", that same change is wrong: it would be a real behaviour change against a 94k-document default tenant, and it could break flows that legitimately cross orgs within one tenant (lineage, transfers, shares). So the fix shape stays blank until the ruling lands, and the severity below is provisional for the same reason.

The options analysis already exists and should not be re-derived — it is on [KS-486](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-486) in the finding-2 disposition comment (A: declare tenant the boundary + contract line with S · B: enforce org in the repo layer · C: formalise and regression-test the existing route control). The standing recommendation there is **C now, B as target, gated on the ruling** — C being the only option that is strictly positive under *either* answer, because it pins the control that is actually protecting us today with a test.

## Provisional severity

**Medium, provisionally.** Not live-exploitable, so not Urgent/High on today's evidence. If the ruling is "org IS a security boundary", this becomes a **Must** and should be re-rated upward when its fix ticket is written; if the ruling is "org is a label", it settles as documentation plus the route-level regression test and may drop.

## Open questions carried (not tidied away)

1. **The route-level control is not fully mapped.** The finding-2 work established that the denial exists, distinguishes admin from non-admin, and produces a real 404 — it did **not** trace every path that reaches `documentRepo` to confirm all of them carry the check. The risk is precisely a path that reaches the repo without it, so this is the gap most worth closing next, and it is worth doing regardless of how the product question is answered.
2. `super_admin` **+ a forged** `x-tenant-id` **returned 404 where the code reading predicted 200** — a defence that was not located. Also carried on KS-619. A hypothesis worth testing first, raised while re-reading the route on `de4781ca2`: `routes/documents.ts:846-848` computes `adminUsingOverride = userJwtTenant && userJwtTenant !== tenantId` and **skips the cross-tenant registry fallback** when it is true (the BUG-ISOLATION-001 fix, 2026-05-02). That would produce exactly this 404. **Untested — stated as a hypothesis, not a finding.**

## Verification method + stated limits

Every citation above was read on `develop de4781ca2` in this session rather than copied forward, and the negative claims are grep-backed (`organization_id` predicate count in `documentRepo.ts`: **0**). **Limit:** the same-org corollary in point 1 of *the correction* is derived from the code, **not live-proven** — a two-user same-org test was not run, because only one user in that organization owns documents locally and user emails are encrypted at rest, so selecting a second seeded login was not cheap. It should be proved live by whoever writes the eventual fix.

**BLUF:** Kam ruled the 31-decision card `secuura-backlog-31-decisions-1109` on 2026-11-09 at 13:44:07 (live board), in these words: "Decision secuura-backlog-31-decisions-1109: a — All recommendations (A and B)". Option a reads: "Every row ruled as recommended; a board seat files and moves the tickets; the KS-607 demo rows still wait for a separate yes." This ticket is row A5 of the decision pack, ruled as recommended: option 2 now. Keep the owner-based rule and close the no-owner gap; that work is KS-1695, already In Progress with five costed fixes. Whether an organisation should be a hard wall at all is a long-term question, carried to the monthly meeting agenda beside the ownership-model work in PS-690.

No new build comes from this ruling: KS-1695 carries on as it is, and this comment does not touch it.

Comment only: the state stays Backlog.

## The "nothing is leaking" premise does not hold for OWNER-LESS rows — measured

This ticket's BLUF says *"**Nothing is leaking.** Cross-org document reads are denied today, and that was proved with a control... What actually denies the read is a **per-owner 404-cloak**, which covers cross-org access only as a side effect."*

**That cloak does not run when the owner is empty.** `documentRepo.ts:176` derives `''` from `owner_user_id` NULL + `issuer_user_id` NULL, and `documents.ts:1124`'s condition is a conjunction — `userId && document.owner?.id && ...` — which is **false** on `''`. So for owner-less rows the per-owner cloak is skipped entirely, and the emergent cross-org protection described here is **absent rather than merely unenforced**.

Measured by gate BX1 on real Postgres 15 as `secuura_app` (NOSUPERUSER, NOBYPASSRLS), 2026-10-20: a **bare-connector `POST /api/documents`** row (owner NULL, issuer NULL) is **200 on `GET /api/documents/:id` to a same-tenant `ISSUER_ADMIN` of ANOTHER organisation**, on `develop` as well as on the landing. Another tenant is still 404. The positive control in the same run: a row with a non-empty owner is 404 to that same reader, so the cloak works where there is an owner to compare — which is exactly this ticket's thesis, holding everywhere except the empty case.

**No change proposed here, and this ticket's scope is untouched** — it remains the tracking ticket for the organisation-boundary question, which is still Kam's. This comment exists only so the "nothing is leaking" sentence is not read as current for every row class.

Full measurement table, the second gap found alongside it (`GET /api/certifications/:id` has no ownership check at all), and the five costed remedy shapes are on **KS-1695**. Context: KS-1659 merged as `3cc46ae41fed0ba8f9b3423f7737344a4916c948`, which adds holder-less connector certifications as a new row type in the same owner-less class — the gate's control proved the class pre-existed it.

For context: these results were measured on the KS-1455 branch (`feature/ks-1455-bump-systemtest-schemathesis-pin-4294-4300-or-later-release`, PR https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/1438), which is going to be merged today.

**Still live on Schemathesis 4.30.0 (KS-1455, 2026-10-09).** `test_connector_key_lifecycle.py::test_another_organisations_key_cannot_read_an_ownerless_connector_document` is still an expected failure (xfail) on both full runs (seeds 1455 and 20261009, slot 4, measured at `bf9568582`). The 404 cloak still skips ownerless (connector-created) documents.

Suggested acceptance criteria:
* Document reads are scoped by organisation, so another organisation's key gets a 404 for an ownerless connector document.
* The xfail marker is removed, so the test runs as a normal test: red on today's code, green on the fix.

Evidence: https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/1438

## Test Evidence — PR https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/1403 (harness, head `d1d9f54d7`)

*Split from #1399 (closed) into four PRs: A harness #1403 (this ticket's test), B package refresh #1401, C observability #1400 (merged), D docs #1402.*

**BLUF.** The harness PR pins your ticket in a test, so it can't be forgotten. No platform code changes. Thank you, Kamil.

**For this ticket:** `tests/test_connector_key_lifecycle.py` carries `test_another_organisations_key_cannot_read_an_ownerless_connector_document` as a **strict xfail citing KS-621**. Measured live on slot 4 (2026-10-06): Organisation B's connector key read Organisation A's connector-created document with **200**, where KS-568 row 4 expected 404. It reports as a known failure on every run, and turns red the moment the cloak covers ownerless documents, which is your cue to remove the marker.

>>> Evidence (slot 4, 2026-10-06): integration 427 passed / 0 failed in the `pre-merge` run; this xfail is one of the skips the gate counts as unverified.

>>>

Refs as KS-NNN text. Posted by agent on Peter's behalf; edited 2026-10-06 to point to the split PR.

## Addendum 2026-10-06: a live cross-organisation read, through the case the BLUF's proof did not cover (ownerless documents)

**BLUF.** Kamil, this ticket's BLUF says *"Nothing is leaking"*. That was proven on a document that HAS an owner. Today a live test read **another Organisation's connector-created document: 200, where the 404 cloak was expected**. The document had no owner, so the route's owner check never ran. This is the "weaker than org" direction your description predicted ("any condition that makes … protection removed"), now reached by an ordinary connector flow rather than an admin. I've appended it here rather than raising a new ticket, because it is this ticket's class. The fix shape stays your and Kam's call (the org-boundary question is still open). Thank you.

>>> Evidence (re-verified at source, `develop` `f556373b9`; live on slot 4, 2026-10-06)

**Mechanism (code).** `services/originate/src/routes/documents.ts:1047`:
```ts
if (userId && document.owner?.id && document.owner.id !== userId && !isAdmin && !isRecipient) { … 404 … }
```
The cloak requires `document.owner?.id` to be truthy. A document created by a connector key WITHOUT `onBehalfOf` gets no owner: the connector principal `connector:platform-s:<externalRef>` is not a UUID, so it is folded to NULL on write (`utils/principalId.ts`; `documentRepo.ts` ~:373-374). The owner then resolves to `owner_user_id || issuer_user_id || ''` → `''` (`documentRepo.ts` ~:176). With an empty owner the whole condition is false, the creating-connector exception (`:1053`) is never consulted, and the read proceeds for any authenticated caller in the tenant.

**Live (test).** `systemTest/schemathesis/tests/test_connector_key_lifecycle.py::test_read_back_survives_key_rotation`, KS-568 row 4, on Peter's branch:
1. Organisation A's connector key (minted via `register-connector`, default tenant) creates a document with no `onBehalfOf`.
2. After a rotation, A's new key reads it: 200, as expected.
3. **Organisation B's connector key (same tenant, different Organisation) reads `GET /api/documents/doc-1791287114130-0f34cadf` → 200** with the full body. The test expected 404.

Both connector Organisations sit in the default tenant because `register-connector` was called without `tenantSlug`. That is also how every Platform S Organisation is provisioned (one handshake per S Organisation, many per tenant: the S↔K contract your description cites).

**Scope of what is and isn't shown:**
* Shown: one ownerless connector document readable by a second Organisation's connector, live, once.
* Not shown: the same against human JWT callers in another Organisation (the code path says yes, since the condition is the same; not probed); list endpoints; how many ownerless documents exist on demo (not queried; demo not touched).
* Duplicate check (Platform K + Platform S, 2026-10-06): no other ticket names the ownerless-document case. Related: PS-690 (Stuart, In Progress: org-owned documents ownership model) and KS-480 §6.

**How the systemTest records it.** It is not hidden. The row-4 cross-Organisation assertion will land as `xfail(strict=True)` citing this ticket, so it reads as a known failure on every run and flips red-to-green when the cloak covers ownerless documents.

>>>

Refs as KS-NNN text. Posted by agent on Peter's behalf.

**No change to this ticket's content or severity.** Recording the consolidation so the survivor carries the record rather than it living only on the closed side.

KS-620 was filed 14 minutes before this one (00:39:02 vs 00:53:52, 2026-08-13) off the same finding, under an instruction that superseded itself four minutes later. title: Gateway tenant resolution falls through to the caller's x-tenant-id when a token has no tenantId claim — make it unconditional and fail closed
description:
**Remediation, not a defect.** Filed off the KS-486 finding-3 investigation (2026-08-13), which **disproved** an exploitable cross-tenant path — see that ticket's disproof comment for the full evidence. Nothing is currently leaking. This is the defence-in-depth gap the disproof exposed.

## The gap

The gateway overwrites the caller's `x-tenant-id` from the verified JWT — but **conditionally**:

```js
// services/api-gateway/src/middleware/auth.ts:387
} else {
  if (decoded.tenantId) req.headers['x-tenant-id'] = decoded.tenantId;
  ...
}
runWithTenantId((req.headers['x-tenant-id'] as string | undefined) || decoded.tenantId, next);
```

**If a token carries no** `tenantId` **claim, the caller's own header survives** and then seeds the RLS tenant context. Downstream, `services/originate/src/index.ts:220-227` adopts the same header, and `tenantGucContext()` turns it into the RLS GUC — so since KS-458 flipped RLS fail-closed, the header is not filtered *by* the isolation control, it is the *input to* it.

The equivalent api-key path is already written the right way and is worth copying:

```js
// auth.ts:311 — KS-458: the gateway is the trust boundary
runWithTenantId(meta.tenantId, next);   // verified credential, NEVER the inbound header
```

## Why it is safe today, and why that is not enough

The conditional never fires open **because of a constraint two services away**: `svc_api_keys.tenant_id` is `NOT NULL` (migration 018, KS-33), so every API key carries a tenant → every `/api/keys/validate` returns one → every connector token carries the claim. User tokens set it from the row. Verified live: 786 keys with 0 nulls, and forged-header requests returned 404 against a 200 control.

Three things make that a thin guarantee:

1. **Migration 018 documents its own down-path** — `ALTER TABLE svc_api_keys ALTER COLUMN tenant_id DROP NOT NULL;` is written into the file. If it is ever run, the header-trust path reopens silently, with no code change and nothing to notice it by.
2. `ConnectorTokenClaims.tenantId` **is already declared optional** (`services/auth/src/services/jwt.ts:239`) and spread conditionally (`:263`). The type system permits exactly the token this conditional cannot handle safely; only the database prevents one existing.
3. `users.tenant_id` **is nullable** (`is_nullable: YES`) — currently 0 of 82 rows are null, but that is data, not a constraint. And `admin@secuura.com` (super_admin) demonstrably issues a token today with **no** `tenantId` **claim at all**, proving the no-claim token shape is not hypothetical. For that role cross-tenant selection is by design, so it is not a defect — but it shows the branch is reachable in production traffic.

## Proposed change

Make the tenant resolution unconditional and fail closed:

* If a verified token has no `tenantId` **and** the caller is not a role legitimately entitled to select one (the existing `SUPER_ADMIN_ROLES` + `x-tenant-override` branch), **reject** rather than falling through to the caller's header.
* Never let an inbound `x-tenant-id` reach `runWithTenantId` or a downstream service — mirror the api-key path, which already seeds strictly from the verified credential.
* Consider stripping inbound `x-tenant-id` at the edge outright, so downstream services cannot be reached with a caller-set value even in-cluster.

## Acceptance

* A token with no `tenantId` claim, from a non-super-admin caller, **cannot** cause any tenant scope to be adopted from a request header — proved with a red test (forged header, verify the denial, with a passing control so the denial is not a dead probe).
* The super-admin `x-tenant-override` path keeps working — regression-covered, since that is a real capability.
* One open question worth answering during the work: during the KS-486 disproof, `super_admin + x-tenant-id: <other tenant>` returned **404** where the code reading predicted 200. Something beyond the JWT overwrite also blocks it and I did not locate it. Whoever picks this up should find that mechanism — it may already be most of the fix, or it may be incidental and not load-bearing.

nodes.body:
**BLUF:** Built as ruled (card secuura-backlog-31-decisions-1109 = a, row A4) in PR 2128, head aff0f43e4079, not merged: a verified token with no tenantId is now refused 401, except for the platform roles (isPlatformRole: SUPER_ADMIN, SYSTEM_ADMIN). Those keep the default tenant and their x-tenant-override switch, and both are pinned by test.

- **Correction to this ticket's title (facts only):** the caller's x-tenant-id did not fall through, at develop 4d6b7bb17fd3 or when this ticket was filed. At develop ea39d7728 (2026-08-13), auth.ts:369 already ran `if (!decoded.tenantId) decoded.tenantId = DEFAULT_TENANT_ID;` before :387 copied the tenant onto x-tenant-id. The line came in with commit 29033ce47 (2026-03-22). The edge also strips inbound x-tenant-* except x-tenant-override (index.ts:309 then, utils/trustHeaders.ts:43-44 now).
- **The open question in the description, answered:** that default is why the super_admin forged-header probe answered 404 where 200 was predicted. The token carried no tenant, so the request ran in the default tenant.
- **What changed:** the default is now reachable only for a platform role. Any other role without a tenant gets the existing invalid-token 401 body, on required and optional routes alike.
- **Proof:** a no-tenant ordinary-role token with a forged x-tenant-id was 200 in the default tenant on develop; it is 401 with the change, with 0 upstream hits. SUPER_ADMIN with no tenant lands in the default tenant. Lower-case super_admin with an override lands in the override. An ordinary role's override is still ignored. Removing the platform exemption reddens the two platform cells and a repaired fixture. Removing the refusal reddens the forged-header cell. Existing count, not re-measured: 0 null tenants among 82 users and 786 keys on 2026-08-13.
- **Not run:** the four platform suites, a live stack, Node 24, demo.

The same PR carries the claim guard ruled on KS 1208. It goes to a tier-1 gate next: https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/2128

**BLUF:** Kam ruled the 31-decision card `secuura-backlog-31-decisions-1109` on 2026-11-09 at 13:44:07 (live board), in these words: "Decision secuura-backlog-31-decisions-1109: a — All recommendations (A and B)". title: GET /api/anchors/{id} and verify report different statuses for the same anchor — 91 UAT anchors read "failed" while verify says confirmed
description:
Raised from the S side 2026-08-12 (S ticket: [PS-577](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-577>)). @kamil.kreiser — one authenticated call settles this; details below.

## The observation

Platform S polls `GET /api/anchors/{id}` to learn when an anchor confirms. On UAT, **91 transactions are stuck reporting** `failed` — while `POST /api/verification/verify`, asked about the same document's content hash, reports the **same anchor id** as confirmed on chain.

Concretely, anchor `anchor_0f9a2acf-756d-46ee-b257-762a245d6ca2`:

```
POST /api/verification/verify  {"providedHash":"6ffa6a0d4378007a480af701b6113cc0252544bcfde93cf11c2654c8bbe2367e"}

  verified   : true              status  : anchored
  anchorId   : anchor_0f9a2acf-756d-46ee-b257-762a245d6ca2
  bc.status  : confirmed         txHash  : e64759a924ea314e…
  anchoredAt : 2026-08-09T06:18:39.090Z
  checks     : documentExists ✓ hashValid ✓ isCertified ✓ isAnchored ✓ integrityVerified ✓
```

S recorded its failure for that same anchor at **06:32:20** — **fourteen minutes after** `anchoredAt`. So this is not a race between a poll and a late confirmation.

A second sample behaves identically: document ref `doc-1785566174843-631e2310` (an originate/upload), `verified: true`, `confirmed`, txHash `38adf13132f6856a…`, while S has it marked failed.

## What has been ruled out on the S side

Both plausible S-side causes were eliminated before raising this:

* **Not a failed/unauthenticated read.** All six affected organisations are registered with connector keys, and each has rows that *did* confirm — org 6: 77 confirmed vs 58 failed, org 9: 39 vs 20, org 13: 8 vs 6. Reads plainly work for these tenants.
* **Not an S mapping bug.** For an `anchor_…` reference S takes the `status` field from `/api/anchors/{id}` **verbatim** — no interpretation layer is involved. S is reporting the exact word it is given.

Spread is across every verb (share 39, upload 16, share-attach-consent 13, certify 5, sign 5, watermark 4, and the share-edit verbs), so it is not verb-specific.

## The question

Does `GET /api/anchors/{id}` return a stale or different status than the anchor's true state?

Candidates worth checking:

1. The anchors read serves a row that `reconcileDocumentAnchorState` ([KS-535](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-535/a-failed-on-chain-anchor-still-reports-statusanchored-async-failure)) later healed, without the anchors view reflecting the heal.
2. There are two anchor records and the endpoints resolve different ones — the [KS-563](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-563/verify-api-iscertified-is-true-for-merely-anchored-documents-so)/584 "answer from the row that evidences its claims" family, except here it is the *anchors* endpoint that looks wrong.
3. `/api/anchors/{id}` is correct and verify is optimistic — in which case S's reading is right and the bug is elsewhere.

**The one call that settles it:**

```
GET /api/anchors/anchor_0f9a2acf-756d-46ee-b257-762a245d6ca2
```

on demo-pk, authenticated. If it returns `status: failed` while verify reports that anchor confirmed with tx `e64759a924ea314e…`, the inconsistency is confirmed and the question becomes which is authoritative. I could not make this call myself — the endpoint requires auth — so the diagnosis above is inferred from S's behaviour plus the eliminations, not directly observed.

## Why it matters to S

1. Users see **"anchor failed" on documents that are anchored and confirmed on chain** — a false negative on a trust surface.
2. **S never collects the real transaction hash.** Those rows keep their `anchor_…` placeholder permanently, so the chain evidence K is holding is silently lost to S.
3. It makes S's anchoring-failure count unusable as an alert signal.

## What S has done meanwhile

S no longer takes a bare `failed` as final ([Secuura/platform-s#440](https://linear.app/secuura/review/ps-577-dont-take-anchor-failed-as-final-when-ks-own-verify-disagrees-4a8640ddf0ac), merged). When the anchors endpoint reports failed, S asks verify and prefers the evidenced answer **only** when verify names the same `anchorId`, reports it anchored, not simulated, and carries a real 64-hex transaction hash.

That is a mitigation, not a fix — it recovers the lost hashes and stops the false failures, but the two endpoints still disagree, and S is now quietly compensating for it. Worth resolving at source.

Related: [PS-577](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-577>), [KS-535](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-535/a-failed-on-chain-anchor-still-reports-statusanchored-async-failure), [KS-563](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-563/verify-api-iscertified-is-true-for-merely-anchored-documents-so).
