@peter — **answering your gating question, so KS-608 can be written.**

## BLUF

**Same lifecycle fact, different resolution scope — NOT two facts by design.** Your outcome 4 is ruled out and **KS-608 survives**. But its invariant needs re-scoping before you write it, or it will fire false positives on 12 content hashes on demo today.

And there is a real defect underneath: **3 anchors on demo read `status: failed` while carrying a real 64-hex tx hash, a real block number, and a set `confirmed_at`.**

## Recommendation

Write KS-608, but scope the invariant to **the same anchor id**, not the same document. And add a second, stronger invariant that needs no cross-endpoint comparison at all (below) — it is self-contained, and it would have caught this class without depending on which endpoint wins.

---

## 1. Why it is not "two facts by design"

Both fields read the same column, `anchor_store.status`. Neither is a submission-vs-confirmation distinction like the one KS-563 established.

- **`GET /api/anchors/{id}`** (`services/anchoring/src/index.ts:765`) looks up **one anchor row by anchor id** and returns `status: anchor.status` verbatim. It answers *"what happened to this submission attempt?"*
- **verify's blockchain block** (`services/api-gateway/src/routes/verification.ts:216–262`) resolves over **every anchor for the document**, sorts by `blockNumber` descending, takes the top one, and maps `latest.status === 'confirmed' ? 'on-chain' : 'pending-onchain'`. It answers *"does this document have on-chain evidence?"*

Same fact, resolved over different row sets — one row versus best-of-N.

## 2. What that means for KS-608's invariant

*"The two endpoints must not contradict each other about the same anchor"* is correct **only if scoped to the same anchor id**. Verify is not answering about an anchor; it is answering about a document/content hash. Where a document has both a failed and a confirmed anchor, **both endpoints are correct and they still disagree**.

That is not hypothetical. On demo right now:

| content hashes with… | count |
| --- | --- |
| exactly 1 anchor | 104 |
| more than 1 anchor | 31 |
| …of those, carrying **both** a confirmed and a failed anchor | **12** |

A document-scoped invariant fails on all 12 while nothing is wrong. An anchor-scoped one holds.

## 3. The real defect — and a better invariant

demo has 92 failed anchors. They are not one population:

| class | count | evidence | verdict |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| KS-587 simulated placeholders | **83** | placeholder tx, **0** with a block number | correctly `failed` |
| `ConwayMempoolFailure "All inputs are spent"` — never landed | **6** | tx `null`, no block, `confirmed_at` null | correctly `failed` |
| `ConwayMempoolFailure "All inputs are spent"` — **landed anyway** | **3** | **real 64-hex tx, real block number, `confirmed_at` SET** | **`failed` is wrong** |

Your ticket's own sample is in the third class:

```
anchor_0f9a2acf-756d-46ee-b257-762a245d6ca2
  status       : failed
  transaction  : 28ecec5c29ce886346…   (real 64-hex)
  block_number : 4554493
  confirmed_at : 2026-08-09 06:29:49+00
  retry_count  : 3
  error        : ConwayMempoolFailure "All inputs are spent.
                  Transaction has probably already been included"
```

The error text says the transaction probably landed; the block number says it did. This is the [KS-535](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-535) wallet race — two deployments selecting the same UTxOs, the loser recording a terminal failure for a transaction the winner already got on chain.

**So the second invariant, which I would rate above the cross-endpoint one:**

> An anchor carrying a real 64-hex `transaction_hash` **and** a non-null `block_number` must not read `status: failed`.

Single endpoint, no correlation, no ambiguity about which side is authoritative, and it catches exactly the rows S is stuck on.

## 4. One honest limit on this analysis

Your numbers are from **UAT**; I measured **demo**. The specific tx verify reported to you (`e64759a924ea314e…`) **does not exist in demo's anchor_store** at all, and the ticket's anchor carries a different tx on demo (`28ecec5c…`). So I have not reproduced S's exact verify response — what I have is the mechanism, plus three live instances of the contradiction on demo.

Also worth flagging for your 91-vs-92 arithmetic: on demo the large majority (83) are KS-587 placeholders that are **correctly** failed. If UAT splits the same way, most of S's stuck rows are not this bug — they are documents that genuinely never anchored, and S is right to show them failed. The bug is the tail.

All reads were read-only SELECTs against demo. Nothing written, Kintsugi hold intact.

## One question ahead of the investigation — it gates the systemTest leg

@kamil.kreiser — before you dig into this, there is a single semantics question whose answer decides whether the systemTest regression for this class can be written at all. It does **not** need the investigation done, the authenticated call made, or the 91 rows resolved.

> **Are `GET /api/anchors/{id}.status` and verify's `blockchain.status` the same lifecycle fact, or two different facts by design?**

## Why it matters more than it looks

The systemTest leg is filed as **KS-608** (child of KS-492, currently **Blocked** on this ticket). Its invariant is *"the two endpoints must not contradict each other about the same anchor"* — deliberately stated so it holds whichever endpoint turns out authoritative, and asserts nothing about repair.

That works under three of your four candidate outcomes, but not the fourth:

| Outcome | Effect on KS-608 |
| --- | --- |
| The anchors read is stale (a row `reconcileDocumentAnchorState` healed) | Invariant stands |
| Two anchor records, the endpoints resolve different ones | Invariant stands |
| Verify is optimistic, the anchors read is right | Invariant stands |
| **The two fields are different lifecycle facts by design** | **Invariant is wrong** — they are permitted to differ, and KS-608 gets deleted rather than adjusted |

**The fourth is not hypothetical, which is why I am asking rather than assuming.** KS-563 already established that `status` flips to `anchored` on **submission**, not confirmation — *"a chain blob is authoritative, and the status fallback applies only when there is no blob at all"*. This platform has drawn exactly that submission-vs-confirmation distinction once already. If it applies to the anchors read too, then `failed` from `/api/anchors/{id}` alongside `confirmed` from verify may be two honest answers to two different questions — and S's mitigation is compensating for a contract it misread rather than a defect.

I am not asserting that is the case. Stuart's elimination work is solid and the fourteen-minute gap makes a poll race implausible. But it is the one branch where writing the test first wastes the work.

## What I am NOT waiting on

Your investigation, the disposition of the 91 UAT rows, KS-587's re-anchor-or-mark-failed decision, and the KS-584/KS-563 row-selection family. None of those change what KS-608 asserts.

A one-line answer unblocks it. If the honest answer is *"don't know until I make the call"*, that is fine too — say so and KS-608 stays blocked on the full investigation rather than on a question you cannot yet answer.

*— posted by agent on Peter's behalf, 2026-08-12.*

title: BM-2: Verification is a configurable workflow via smart contracts — record the workflow path, not casual views
description:
## BLUF

**Verification is a CONFIGURABLE WORKFLOW, not a fixed function.** Clients configure verification workflows via smart contracts; Secuura does NOT prescribe compliance. The workflow PATH is verified against the smart contract and recorded; simple interactions like document VIEWING are NOT recorded on-chain (noise). A third-party verifier (e.g. recruiter verifying a university document) sees the inspectable steps (identity checks, domain matching). End-user sees a binary "verified"; audit/legal sees full rigor.

## Carried ruling (PS-556, Kam 2026-08-11)

A verification is a **public, repeatable READ** — it sits OUTSIDE canonical lineage (lineage = versions from certifications/modifications). If a verification act is recorded at all, **S records it for S's own reporting/lineage annotation — K does NOT become a source of record for verification acts.**

Source: 2026-08-11 technical weekly (Stuart, Phil, Kam).

**Certification is an UMBRELLA term** = attestation + signing + (optional) watermarking. Attestation = a user attesting a document is correct — on-chain, distinct from the file itself. Watermarking is a distinct, optional element. **ANY modification (including watermarking) creates a NEW document version, tracked via document lineage, and requires mandatory RE-CERTIFICATION.**

Likely an epic: data model + lineage enforcement + re-certification triggers + API/spec surface. This is the parent ticket — split into sub-tickets when the build starts.

title: Rescue the sign-up intent: re-challenge with prompt=create when a sign-in turns into an Entra self-service sign-up
description:
## Depends on a decision, not just on code

**Do not start this before the registration-lock question is settled.** Registration was closed on UAT on 2026-07-30 because signing up granted `SsdAccountAdmin` to anyone. This ticket makes the sign-up route reachable again by a different door, so it inherits that risk in full. The `SsdAccountAdmin` auto-grant has to be fixed — or the new route has to be proven not to hit it — before this ships.

## Context

[PS-551](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-551/external-sign-in-failures-crash-the-app-aadsts50021-on-the-entra-self) stops the crash: a user who takes Entra's own *"No account? Create one"* branch during a plain sign-in request now lands back on the login page with a readable message instead of an HTTP 400. But they still cannot sign up. On UAT `WhiteLabelNoRegister: true` hides the **Create an account** link, so the working path — `/Account/Register` → `EntraIDSignUp` handler → `prompt=create` — is unreachable, while Entra's hosted page keeps offering the branch that dead-ends.

## The idea

When the OIDC callback comes back classified as the self-service-sign-up rejection (`AADSTS50021`), re-issue the challenge with `prompt=create` so Entra runs a *declared* sign-up, which is the flow that already works locally. The user completes sign-up in one continuous journey instead of being told to go away.

Alternatives worth weighing in the plan, since this may not be the best answer:

1. **Re-challenge with** `prompt=create` — best UX, but silently re-opens registration on tenants that closed it. Needs the gate check first.
2. **Suppress the sign-up affordance at the Entra end** for this app, so "No account? Create one" never appears on a sign-in request. Removes the dead end rather than paving it; no app change.
3. **Leave** [PS-551](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-551/external-sign-in-failures-crash-the-app-aadsts50021-on-the-entra-self)'s message as the answer and route new users through an admin invitation.

## Groundwork already done in [PS-551](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-551/external-sign-in-failures-crash-the-app-aadsts50021-on-the-entra-self)

* `ssd/Services/Security/ExternalAuthFailureMapper.cs` classifies provider failures into opaque codes. Adding a third code (e.g. `CodeSignupUnavailable`) for the AADSTS50021 case is a two-line change, and [PS-551](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-551/external-sign-in-failures-crash-the-app-aadsts50021-on-the-entra-self) deliberately left it out — pointing a user at a create-account flow that doesn't work would be worse than the generic message.
* The distinct AADSTS50021 text is already captured in the `LogWarning` from `ssd.Startup`, so the trigger is observable in `/AdminLogs` before any code is written.

## Tripwire to respect

`Microsoft.Identity.Web` installs its own `OnRemoteFailure` (the B2C password-reset handler) in a post-configure that runs **after** the OIDC options lambda — but only when `MicrosoftIdentityOptions.IsB2C` is true, i.e. only if `AzureAdCiam:SignUpSignInPolicyId` is set. That key is commented out in every config today. If this work introduces it, [PS-551](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-551/external-sign-in-failures-crash-the-app-aadsts50021-on-the-entra-self)'s handler is silently replaced and the crash comes back. There is a comment in `ssd/Startup.cs` at the handler saying so. Re-verify [PS-551](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-551/external-sign-in-failures-crash-the-app-aadsts50021-on-the-entra-self)'s behaviour if the key is ever set.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The registration-lock decision is recorded (including what happens to the `SsdAccountAdmin` auto-grant) before any code lands.
- [ ] A brand-new user can complete sign-up from the sign-in entry point, or is cleanly told they cannot — no dead end either way.
- [ ] If `AzureAdCiam:SignUpSignInPolicyId` is introduced, [PS-551](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-551/external-sign-in-failures-crash-the-app-aadsts50021-on-the-entra-self)'s `OnRemoteFailure` is re-verified as still installed.

**Playwright test that demonstrates the fix** (required, and it is reachable without touching the Entra tenant): extend `systemTest/tests/functional/login_external_error.spec.ts`. That spec already drives `/Identity/Account/Login?authError=<code>` **directly** and asserts the copy renders in `login-error-banner`, deliberately outside the dev-only local-login block — which is exactly the seam this ticket needs. Add cases asserting:

1. the new code for the AADSTS50021 case (e.g. `signupUnavailable`) renders its **own** banner text in `login-error-banner`, distinct from today's `cancelled` and the catch-all `failed`. **Fails on today's** `develop` — `ExternalAuthFailureMapper` has only the two codes and the self-service-sign-up rejection falls into the generic message, which is [PS-551](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-551/external-sign-in-failures-crash-the-app-aadsts50021-on-the-entra-self)'s deliberate stopping point;
2. whichever option is chosen, the page offers **no dead end**: if option 1 (re-challenge with `prompt=create`) is taken, the banner carries an actionable control that starts the declared sign-up; if option 3 (admin invitation) is taken, the banner says so and names the next step. Assert the branch that was actually chosen — and nothing that leaves the user with a message and no route;
3. on a `WhiteLabelNoRegister` configuration the banner does **not** offer self-service sign-up, and `login-register-link` stays absent — this is the registration-lock guard expressed as a test, and it is the assertion that stops this ticket re-opening the hole UAT closed on 2026-07-30.

**Control assertions that pass today and must keep passing:** the whole of `login_external_error.spec.ts` as it stands — `cancelled` and `failed` still render their current copy in `login-error-banner`, still outside the local-login block, and no external failure returns HTTP 400 or the generic error page ([PS-551](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-551/external-sign-in-failures-crash-the-app-aadsts50021-on-the-entra-self)'s fix). `login-microsoft-btn` / `login-entra-form` still start the normal sign-in.

**The decisive criteria here are not Playwright's, and they come first.** This ticket's own first line says so:

* **The registration-lock ruling is a written decision**, recorded on this ticket, covering what happens to the `SsdAccountAdmin` auto-grant. No test substitutes for it, and no code should land before it — verify by reading the recorded decision.
* **The auto-grant itself is a rule, so it belongs in xUnit** (`tests/ssd.UnitTests`): a test asserting that an account created through the new route does **not** receive `SsdAccountAdmin`, and that the mapper classifies the AADSTS50021 text into the new code. Two minutes, no stack, and it is the assertion that proves the inherited risk was actually removed rather than routed around.
* **The** `IsB2C` **tripwire is a configuration check, not a journey.** If `AzureAdCiam:SignUpSignInPolicyId` is introduced, `Microsoft.Identity.Web`'s post-configure replaces [PS-551](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-551/external-sign-in-failures-crash-the-app-aadsts50021-on-the-entra-self)'s `OnRemoteFailure`. Pin that in a startup/options contract test in `tests/ssd.UnitTests` — "the configured `OnRemoteFailure` is still ours after post-configure runs" — because the browser symptom of getting this wrong is the HTTP 400 returning silently on a deployed CIAM tenant that no local slot exercises.
* **The real-IdP leg cannot be automated.** Entra's hosted "No account? Create one" branch needs a workforce-tenant user per `docs/sso-tenant-configuration.md` §2; record one manual pass on dev-ps (which anchors against a real tenant) with the `/AdminLogs` warning line as the evidence that the trigger fired, and say so on the PR rather than implying the suite covered it.

**If option 2 is chosen** — suppressing the sign-up affordance at the Entra end — there is **no app change and therefore no Playwright test**; the deliverable is the tenant configuration plus a line in `docs/sso-tenant-configuration.md` recording it, and a manual pass showing the branch no longer appears on a sign-in request. Say that explicitly on the ticket rather than closing it with an unrelated green suite.

title: Architecture P1: defuse the MULTI_TENANCY registry upsert — it silently collapses registrations per (hash, tenant) if the flag is ever enabled
description:
**Ask:** In the same phase that touches registration (plan-sheet requirement — not later, not beside), defuse `platform_document_registry`'s armed landmine: UNIQUE `uq_pdr_hash_tenant (content_hash, tenant_id)` + `ON CONFLICT (content_hash, tenant_id) DO UPDATE` in `registerInPlatformRegistry`. Either re-key the registry on the document UUID, or explicitly remove/disable the upsert.

**Why it matters:** the code path is dormant ONLY because `MULTI_TENANCY_ENABLED !== 'true'` on local and demo (0 registry rows in both DBs). If that flag is ever switched on with today's code, the upsert wakes and silently collapses registration pointers — newest write wins per (hash, tenant) — which directly violates ruling (b): duplicate bytes = two registrations, distinguished by UUID. A landmine that has been found and left armed is worse than one nobody found.

**Spec:** `1_Project_Definition/architecture/2026-08-07_K-side-plan-sheet.md` ("The MULTI_TENANCY landmine — inside P1, not beside it").

nodes.body:
## Confirmed live on `develop` `541acae81` — the landmine is still armed, both halves

**The upsert**, `services/originate/src/routes/verification.ts:396` (read from `origin/develop`, not the working tree):

```sql
ON CONFLICT (content_hash, tenant_id) DO UPDATE SET
  document_id = EXCLUDED.document_id, title = EXCLUDED.title, status = EXCLUDED.status, updated_at = NOW()
```

**The constraint**, from the live database:

```
uq_pdr_hash_tenant   (plus platform_document_registry_pkey, idx_pdr_hash, idx_pdr_doc)
```

So both halves are present and they compose exactly as the description says: two documents with the same `content_hash` in one tenant do not collide loudly — the second **overwrites the first's `document_id`** in the registry, and the first registration stops being findable by hash. Silent, and it looks like a successful registration to the caller.

One method note, because it nearly gave me a wrong answer: my first search matched `services/originate/dist/routes/verification.d.ts` — **build output**, which is not the authority and which does not exist at `origin/develop` at all (`git show` refused it). Reading a `dist/` file would have been reading yesterday's compile. The line above is from the `src/` file at the SHA. Also: the search only ran at all once `--include=*.ts` was quoted — unquoted, zsh's `nomatch` kills grep before it starts and the result reads as a clean zero.

Sequencing point from the description stands: this belongs in the same phase as [KS-597](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-597), not after it — registration is the write path that arms it.

No code written. Left in Todo.

title: Three undeclared-verb catalogue skips cite CLOSED tickets (KS-406 / KS-421) — are the defects still live?
description:
## Summary

`tests/test_undeclared_method_safety.py::test_known_undeclared_verb_defect_is_tracked` skips three parametrised cases, each naming a ticket that is **Done and archived**:

| Case | Cited ticket | Ticket state | Skip reason |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| `/tiers/calculate-discount-GET` | [KS-406](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-406/design-call-undeclared-http-methods-return-401-auth-first-instead-of) | ⚠ Done 2026-07-08 | authed GET executes (200) on an undeclared verb |
| `/tiers/calculate-vote-power-GET` | [KS-406](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-406/design-call-undeclared-http-methods-return-401-auth-first-instead-of) | ⚠ Done 2026-07-08 | authed GET executes (200) |
| `/billing/customers/by-email-PUT` | [KS-421](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-421/blocking-prs-billing-get-apibillingcustomerscustomeridpayment-methods) | ⚠ Done 2026-07-10 | authed PUT crashes (500) |

The catalogue is doing its job — it records a known defect so the sweep does not re-report it — but it points at tickets closed a month ago. Either the defects are still live and need a current owner, or they were fixed and the entries should be removed so the tests execute.

**This is the same class the** [KS-589](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-589/systemtest-schemathesis-integration-mode-anchor-honesty-consistency-a) **report fix addresses**, one layer over: a stale ticket reference reads as "tracked" when nothing tracks it.

## Why you

The question is a platform one, not a harness one: **did** [KS-406](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-406/design-call-undeclared-http-methods-return-401-auth-first-instead-of)**'s auth-first-401 posture decision and** [KS-421](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-421/blocking-prs-billing-get-apibillingcustomerscustomeridpayment-methods)**'s billing classifier actually resolve these three, or not?** Once that is known, the systemTest side is mechanical (remove the entries, or repoint them at a live ticket) and I'll do it.

[KS-406](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-406/design-call-undeclared-http-methods-return-401-auth-first-instead-of) was a *design decision* (adopt auth-first 401 for undeclared verbs) rather than a fix, so its two entries may be permanently correct behaviour that should be recorded as accepted rather than as a tracked defect. [KS-421](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-421/blocking-prs-billing-get-apibillingcustomerscustomeridpayment-methods) was a real fix for `GET .../payment-methods`; whether it covered the `PUT .../by-email` sibling is worth checking.

## Reproduce

```bash
TOKEN=$(curl -s -X POST http://localhost:6882/api/auth/login -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"email":"admin@secuura.com","password":"admin123"}' | jq -r '.data.accessToken')

# undeclared GET — expect a safe rejection (401/403/404/405), not 200
curl -i -X GET  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" http://localhost:6882/api/tiers/calculate-discount
curl -i -X GET  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" http://localhost:6882/api/tiers/calculate-vote-power

# undeclared PUT — expect a safe rejection, not 500
curl -i -X PUT  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{}' \
  http://localhost:6882/api/billing/customers/by-email
```

The suite's own guard: `cd systemTest/schemathesis && venv/bin/python3 -m pytest tests/test_undeclared_method_safety.py -v -rsxX`

## Environment

**Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS** (kernel `7.0.0-28-generic`, **aarch64**) on Parallels, 8 vCPU / 31 GB, `10.211.55.4`. Node 24.19.0, PostgreSQL 15.18, Redis 8.10.0, Python 3.14.6, Schemathesis 4.24.3. Run `full-2026-08-07T14-12-05Z`, seed `2794626967`.

## Outcome wanted

For each of the three: **live defect** (→ new ticket, repoint the entry) or **accepted/fixed** (→ remove the entry so the test executes and asserts the safe rejection). A skip is not a pass — while these sit in the catalogue the vectors are unverified.

Refs as KS-NNN text. Found by the [KS-589](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-589/systemtest-schemathesis-integration-mode-anchor-honesty-consistency-a) sweeps, 2026-08-07.

nodes.body: For context: these results were measured on the KS-1455 branch (`feature/ks-1455-bump-systemtest-schemathesis-pin-4294-4300-or-later-release`, PR https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/1438), which is going to be merged today.

**Answering the question in the title: yes, all three defects are still live on Schemathesis 4.30.0 (KS-1455, 2026-10-09).** On both full runs (seeds 1455 and 20261009, slot 4, measured at `bf9568582`), all three `test_known_undeclared_verb_defect_is_tracked` cases are still expected failures (xfail):
* `GET /tiers/calculate-discount` (authenticated, runs an undeclared verb)
* `GET /tiers/calculate-vote-power` (authenticated, runs an undeclared verb)
* `PUT /billing/customers/by-email` (authenticated, crashes with a 500)

The markers already cite this ticket (re-pointed under KS-589, written "was KS-406, closed"), so nothing needs changing there. *Corrected 2026-10-09: an earlier version of this comment wrongly said the markers still cite the closed tickets.*

Suggested acceptance criteria:
* Each undeclared verb answers 404/405 rather than executing or crashing.
* The three xfail markers are removed, so the cases run as normal tests: red on today's code, green on the fix.

Evidence: https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/1438

## BLUF

**Half of this ticket is already done, and it was done by someone else.** The three skips no longer cite closed tickets — [KS-589](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-589) re-pointed them at KS-595 itself on 2026-08-10. The surviving question is the one in the title, and it is unanswered: **are the three defects still live?**

## Verified on `develop` `454a64ebb`

`systemTest/schemathesis/tests/test_undeclared_method_safety.py:54-68` now reads:

```
# KS-589 (2026-08-10): re-pointed at KS-595. Prior behaviour: these cited KS-406 and KS-421,
# both Done and archived, so three skips every run named tickets nobody was working — the same
```

with each case carrying `"KS-595 undeclared-verb catalogue (was KS-406, closed)"` / `"KS-595 billing 500 class (was KS-421, closed)"`.

So the "skips cite closed tickets" defect is closed. **Not closing this ticket**, because the substantive half has not been touched.

## What it is now waiting for

A measurement of the three cited behaviours against current `develop`:

| Case | Claimed behaviour |
| -- | -- |
| `/tiers/calculate-discount` GET | authed GET executes (200) on an undeclared verb |
| `/tiers/calculate-vote-power` GET | authed GET executes (200) |
| `/billing/customers/by-email` PUT | authed PUT crashes (500) |

The third overlaps the raw-500 class tracked on [KS-593](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-593). **Retitling would be fair** — the ticket now means "confirm or clear three undeclared-verb defects", not "fix three stale citations".

*Backlog sweep 2026-08-14.*

## Data point for the factual half: all three still behave the same on a rebuilt stack, 2026-08-12

This ticket asks *"did KS-406's auth-first-401 posture decision and KS-421's billing classifier actually resolve these three, or not?"* — a platform/design question that is still yours. But the **factual** half can be answered without you, and today's runs answer it for free, so you do not have to re-run to find out.

**Conditions — deliberately the strongest available.** Ubuntu VM, containers **and volumes deleted**, all ~31 services **rebuilt from source** on current `develop` (`bd9abdfe4`, i.e. including your KS-531 #673), database wiped and reseeded, 32 containers healthy. So this is not a stale image or a drifted local stack.

**Result: all three still register as Known Failures**, in both the `full` (14:16) and `pre-merge` (15:35) tiers:

```
test_known_undeclared_verb_defect_is_tracked[/tiers/calculate-discount-GET]
test_known_undeclared_verb_defect_is_tracked[/tiers/calculate-vote-power-GET]
test_known_undeclared_verb_defect_is_tracked[/billing/customers/by-email-PUT]
```

Each is `xfail(strict=True)`, so **had any of them started behaving safely, it would have flipped to an Unexpected Pass and failed the suite loudly.** None did. The entries are therefore not stale descriptions of something already fixed — the observed behaviour is unchanged on today's `develop`.

**What this does not settle**, and why the ticket stays yours: whether the two `/tiers/…` GET cases are a *defect* at all. Your own framing is that KS-406 was a **design decision** (adopt auth-first 401 for undeclared verbs) rather than a fix, so those two may be permanently-correct behaviour that should be recorded as **accepted** rather than tracked as an open defect. That distinction cannot be read off a test result — it needs your call. The `/billing/customers/by-email` PUT is the different one: KS-421 fixed `GET …/payment-methods`, and whether it was ever meant to cover the PUT sibling is worth checking.

Once you decide, the systemTest side is mechanical either way — remove the entries so the tests execute and assert the safe rejection, or repoint them at a live owner. As this ticket already says: *"a skip is not a pass — while these sit in the catalogue the vectors are unverified."*

**One related change that landed today (KS-519), so it does not surprise you here.** The guard that surfaced this class — `tests/unit/test_known_defect_refs_are_live.py` — now also covers **prose and config surfaces** (`systemTest/CLAUDE.md`, `known_issues_and_baseline.md`, `schemathesis.toml`), matched by an explicit tracking-**verb** regex rather than a bare `KS-NNN`, so legitimate provenance ("this setting exists because of KS-544") survives while a stale *tracking* claim is caught. It found two more true positives on its first run, both since repointed.

Refs: KS-406 / KS-421 (the cited closed tickets) · KS-519 (the register work that produced these runs) · KS-589 (the guard's origin).

— posted by agent on Peter's behalf.

**The three skips now cite this ticket (KS-589 / PR #656).**

`tests/test_undeclared_method_safety.py` had three entries in `KNOWN_UNDECLARED_VERB_DEFECTS` naming **KS-406** and **KS-421**, both Done and archived — so every run printed three skips pointing at shipped work:

```
SKIP  KS-406 undeclared-verb catalogue — authed GET executes (200)   (×2)
SKIP  KS-421 billing 500 class — authed PUT crashes (500)
```

All three now cite **KS-595**, with the original refs kept in the text for provenance ("was KS-406, closed"). The three operations are unchanged: `GET /tiers/calculate-discount`, `GET /tiers/calculate-vote-power`, `PUT /billing/customers/by-email`.

A guard was added so this cannot recur: `tests/unit/test_known_defect_refs_are_live.py` fails the offline gate if any skip reason, xfail reason or catalogue entry names **only** closed tickets. It deliberately allows a closed ref alongside a live one, so the history can stay — an over-broad rule would just push the next author to delete the explanation instead of fixing the reference.

Your question on this ticket — *are the defects still live?* — is unanswered by this change and still needs a platform check. The skips are xfail-marked, so if a defect has silently been fixed the marker flips to an Unexpected Pass and forces its own removal. Nothing here blocks you.

title: not_a_server_error recurs — 17 raw 5xx across 8 ops (KS-431 / KS-449 / KS-497 recurrence, full-2026-08-07 sweep)
description:
## Why a new ticket

The whole predecessor chain is **Done and archived**:

* [KS-421](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-421/blocking-prs-billing-get-apibillingcustomerscustomeridpayment-methods) — Done 2026-07-10 · [KS-431](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-431/16-write-operations-return-raw-500-internal-error-unmasked-by-the-ks) — Done 2026-07-13 · [KS-449](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-449/write-path-residuals-from-ks-430-ks-431-remaining-raw-500s-request) — Done · [KS-497](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-497/write-path-raw-500-internal-error-recurs-on-4-platformtenants-ops-ks) — Done 2026-07-29, archived

Each closed having fixed the raw-500 class down to its listed operations, and each time it has come back on different ones. Filed fresh per that precedent.

## Finding

**17** `not_a_server_error` **failures across 8 operations** — an unhandled value reaches a handler or the DB and throws, instead of being rejected with a mapped 4xx.

`GET /api/users/admin/list` · `POST /api/documents/{id}/lifecycle-events` · `POST /api/documents/{id}/revoke` · `POST /api/documents/{id}/share` · `POST /api/m365/outlook/exchange-token` · `POST /api/security/rate-limit/check` · `POST /api/users/admin/create` · `POST /api/webhooks/{id}/rotate-secret`

**Three of these are the** [KS-564](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-564/share-lifecycle-events-and-certificationsissue-all-fail-on-recipient) **endpoints** — `/share`, `/lifecycle-events`, and the `documents/{id}` family. Kamil shipped the connector-actor fix on 2026-08-07 (`develop` `307483672`, PR #652) and verified all three return 201 on demo for a connector. These 5xx are on *fuzzed* input rather than the connector path, so they are likely a different trigger on the same handlers — but worth confirming they are not a regression from that change.

`GET /api/users/admin/list` and `POST /api/users/admin/create` are already documented on [KS-565](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-565/sweeps-2026-08-05-untracked-failures-across-10-ops-response-schema) **§2** with root causes traced (`parseInt(offset) || 0` lets `-1` through to Postgres; `data.email.toLowerCase()` with no type guard). [KS-565](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-565/sweeps-2026-08-05-untracked-failures-across-10-ops-response-schema) also notes **the negative-offset pattern is six sites across four services**, not the two the sweep reaches.

## Important — this count was inflated until today

`not_a_server_error` read **79 failures** on the previous sweep. It dropped to **17** once the governance active-proposal cap was cleared: the cap throws a bare `Error` that the route maps to `500 INTERNAL_ERROR`, and every fuzzed proposal-create was counting as a server error. That mis-mapping is filed separately. **62 of the previous 79 were that one defect** — worth knowing before sizing this.

## Where this was run

**Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS** (kernel `7.0.0-28-generic`, **aarch64**) on Parallels, 8 vCPU / 31 GB, at `10.211.55.4`.

| Component | Version |  | Component | Version |
| -- | -- | -- | -- | -- |
| OS | Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS (aarch64) |  | Docker | 29.7.2 |
| Python (venv + host) | 3.14.6 |  | Node (services) | 24.19.0 (`node:24-alpine`) |
| Schemathesis | 4.24.3 |  | PostgreSQL | 15.18 (`postgres:15-alpine`) |
| pytest / Hypothesis | 9.1.1 / 6.165.2 |  | Redis | 8.10.0 (`redis:8-alpine`) |

Run of record: `full-2026-08-07T14-12-05Z`, seed `2794626967`, 24.1 min.

## Reproduce

```bash
TOKEN=$(curl -s -X POST http://localhost:6882/api/auth/login -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"email":"admin@secuura.com","password":"admin123"}' | jq -r '.data.accessToken')

# KS-565 §2 — negative offset reaches Postgres
curl -i -X GET -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  'http://localhost:6882/api/users/admin/list?offset=-1'

# KS-565 §2 — non-string email hits .toLowerCase()
curl -i -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"email":{},"password":"Str0ng-Passw0rd!","role":"OWNER"}' \
  http://localhost:6882/api/users/admin/create
```

Full sweep: `cd systemTest/schemathesis && python3 scripts/run.py full` — 94 replayable crash files with `code_sample` curls under `output/reports/full-2026-08-07T14-12-05Z/schemathesis-crashes/`.

## Fix direction

Per [KS-421](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-421/blocking-prs-billing-get-apibillingcustomerscustomeridpayment-methods) / [KS-431](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-431/16-write-operations-return-raw-500-internal-error-unmasked-by-the-ks) / [KS-497](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-497/write-path-raw-500-internal-error-recurs-on-4-platformtenants-ops-ks): classify the error at the route boundary — map known provider/validation failures to 4xx/503, keep genuine unknowns as 500 with structured logging, and guard path params and body fields before they reach the DB. Add unit tests pinning each classifier. **Fix all six negative-offset sites, not the two the sweep found** ([KS-565](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-565/sweeps-2026-08-05-untracked-failures-across-10-ops-response-schema) §2 lists them).

## Note

The report had been attributing this class to [KS-431](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-431/16-write-operations-return-raw-500-internal-error-unmasked-by-the-ks) **with a bare ticket reference**, which reads as ownership. PR #656 now renders `KS-431 (closed — recurrence untracked)`; this ticket is the live owner.

Refs as KS-NNN text. Found by the [KS-589](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-589/systemtest-schemathesis-integration-mode-anchor-honesty-consistency-a) sweeps, 2026-08-07.

The two adminConfig routes need SYSTEM_ADMIN or ORG_ADMIN and the null share recipient needs a document-write role plus a document; the one kintsugi login is an OWNER, so those three are proven by the unit cells (red at base, green after, in the PR) and the deployed bytes.

## Recommendation

I could not run it: the Schemathesis venv is machine-bound (BACKLOG), and the admin-gated operations need credentials this agent login does not have.

## Detail
- **Linked PRs:** #756 (`80880bb71`) and #757 (`0874b0ebe`) are in kintsugi's running revision `69f2045af2a4`. **#1428** (`1e7f90e26`, originate: refuses a negative offset, a null share...) merged 2026-10-08 and is **not** in it; it is in the deploy Seat D 17th is running.

## Appended 2026-10-07 — raw 500 recurs on `POST /api/auth/wallet/verify`

**BLUF:** `not_a_server_error` fires on `POST /api/auth/wallet/verify`, a raw `500 INTERNAL_ERROR` on fuzzed input. The pair is **not** in `schemathesis-baseline.json` at `develop` b280b74ff. Its sibling `POST /api/auth/wallet/authenticate` is already baselined here (the "wallet-authenticate uuid-cast 500"); `wallet/verify` is a different operation in the same class.

**Evidence.** Run `pre-merge-ks-1445-2026-10-07T14-30-16Z-slot2`: Schemathesis 4.29.4, slot 2 on Peter's Mac, stack built from the KS-1445 branch (no service changes in that branch). Test case `xPmeIe`.
- Body: `{"nonce": " 4\u008dÝ…", "signature": "_", "walletAddress": "Þ򴫱\u008cÜ"}`, with no `challengeId`.
- Response: `500 {"success":false,"error":{"code":"INTERNAL_ERROR","message":"An unexpected error occurred"}}`.
- Path (`services/auth/src/routes/wallet.ts`): the body **passes** `verifySignatureSchema.parse` (about `:287`), then reaches `findChallenge(data.challengeId, data.nonce)` (about `:290`), a DB lookup, and later CIP-8 verification.

**Not established.** I did not identify the exact throw site. Slot 2's auth log around the run shows several error types on this route: `SyntaxError … is not valid JSON` from a `JSON.parse`, `CIP-8 parse/verify error`, `Challenge not found`. I could not tie one of them to `xPmeIe`. Replay with `st replay xPmeIe` against a stack to pin it.

**Counts are a floor.** It fired in that run and not in the run before it on the same commit.

**Fix direction:** as above. Classify at the route boundary, so a fuzzed nonce or address is a mapped 4xx, never a raw 500.

## ⚠ The class is twice as wide as recorded — `limit` has the identical flaw

Every one of those sites also parses a `limit` the same way, and **a negative `LIMIT` is equally fatal**. Measured on the local stack:

```
SELECT 1 LIMIT -1;   ->  ERROR:  LIMIT must not be negative
SELECT 1 LIMIT  1;   ->  1                    (control)
```

**And `Math.min` is what makes this look guarded when it is not.** `Math.min(parseInt(x) || 50, 200)` clamps the *upper* bound only — `Math.min(-1, 200)` is `-1`. So the sites that appear defended are defended against the wrong direction. That covers the six above plus limit-only sites in `analytics` (`dashboard.ts:29`/`:39`, `analytics.ts:364`), `billing` (`billing.ts:464`/`:488`) and `originate` (`documents.ts:247`).

**Sizing consequence:** the recorded scope is 6 sites × 1 param. The measured scope is ~11 sites × up to 2 params, plus one derived-offset path.

## Recommended fix shape — one helper, not eleven patches

**Do not patch the sites individually.** This class has recurred through KS-421 → KS-431 → KS-449 → KS-497 → KS-593, each closing "down to its listed operations" and each returning on different ones. Per-site patching is what produces that chain: the fix travels with the operations the sweep happened to sample, and property-based generation samples rather than enumerates.

Shape: a shared `parsePaginationParam(raw, { default, min, max })` (or extend the existing `@secuura/shared` pagination package, which already exists) that returns a clamped value **or** a typed 400, adopted at every site. Then:

- **A guard test over the corpus, not the instances** — every request-derived `parseInt` of a pagination param must go through the helper, asserted as an exact set of call sites the way KS-751's caller guard does it. That is what makes the sixth recurrence not happen, and it is the part this ticket has never had.
- Sub-class B is separate work: validate the nonce/uuid **before** it reaches the cast, and assert the body carries no driver text.

## Test shape

- Red-before-green per sub-class, and per parameter: `offset=-1`, `limit=-1`, `page=-1` each independently, since they fail at different layers.
- Pin the **exact message** `OFFSET must not be negative` — Peter's 2026-08-28 "empty body" reading was a reporting artefact (he read an uncaptured NDJSON body as an empty one, and corrected it on 08-28T15:37); the body is populated, and a test asserting emptiness would pass for the wrong reason.
- **Do NOT extend the KS-703 NUL guard to numeric params** — measured and settled on 2026-08-28: `parseInt('\x00')` is `NaN`, `NaN || 0` is `0`, so a NUL never reaches the driver through a numeric param. That branch could never fire.
- Net out KS-686's 501 in any before/after count, or the result is unreadable.

## Size: L, and it splits cleanly into two

- **A (pagination range):** the helper + ~11 call sites + the corpus guard — **M**, and the guard is the half that matters.
- **B (uuid-cast disclosure, 2 wallet ops):** **S**, but it is the one with a disclosure component and should carry KS-703's acceptance shape.

They share no code and can land in either order. **Recommend B first** — it is smaller, it is the one leaking driver text, and it does not need the helper design settled.

## Answering as #757's author — the shape deliberately does not extend to numeric params, and there is nothing there for it to catch

## BLUF

**Deliberate, and measurement backs it.** #757 guards `search` and `role` — *string* params whose raw value reaches the query. A NUL in a **numeric** param never gets that far, because `parseInt(x) || 0` turns it into `0` before anything else runs. So extending the guard to `offset`/`limit` would add a branch that can never fire.

The negative-offset defect is a different failure entirely: not an unstorable byte, but a **validly-parsed number with an out-of-range value**. It needs a range check, not a byte guard. That stays this ticket's — and KS-565 §2's six sites across four services remains the important half, as you say.

## Measured — 2026-08-29, live local gateway

```
GET /api/users/admin/list?offset=%00   -> 200   ← NUL in a numeric param: harmless
GET /api/users/admin/list?limit=%00    -> 200   ← same
GET /api/users/admin/list?offset=-1    -> 500   {"code":"INTERNAL_ERROR","message":"OFFSET must not be negative"}
GET /api/users/admin/list?offset=0&limit=5  -> 200   (control)
```

`parseInt('\x00')` is `NaN`, `NaN || 0` is `0` — the NUL is gone before Postgres sees anything. `parseInt('-1')` is `-1`, which is truthy, so it survives the `|| 0` and reaches the query as a negative OFFSET. **The `|| 0` fallback is exactly what makes numeric params immune to the byte class and exactly what fails to protect them from the range class.**

Could be a driver/PG version difference between our stacks; flagging rather than resolving, since it may matter to whoever writes the guard's test.

## What #757 actually covers, precisely

* **Params:** `search` and `role` only.
* **Routes:** `GET /api/users` and `GET /api/users/admin/list`.
* **Bytes:** **U+0000 only.** Other C0 control bytes (U+0001 and friends) are stored happily by Postgres and return 200 today, here and everywhere else.
* **Placement:** before the `parseInt` lines, so it cannot interact with numeric coercion either way.

The reason it is that narrow is in the code comment: the platform's existing control-byte guard (KS-471/472, `findControlBytePath`) walks the request **body** only — nothing walks the query string — and widening it across the whole query string platform-wide is a **new rejection on every published GET contract**. That is the KS-703 ruling still open with Kam, not something #757 decided.

## So the two classes are orthogonal

| | byte class (KS-703 / #757) | range class (KS-593 / KS-565 §2) |
| -- | -- | -- |
| Trigger | U+0000 in a **string** param | valid negative in a **numeric** param |
| Reaches Postgres? | yes, as an unstorable byte | yes, as a legal-but-wrong value |
| Neutralised by `\|\| 0`? | n/a — no coercion on strings | **no** — `-1` is truthy |
| Fix shape | reject the byte, 400 | clamp or reject the range, 400 |
| Scope | 2 params, 2 routes | **6 sites, 4 services** |

Nothing in #757 helps `offset=-1`, and nothing a range check does would help `search=%00`. Fixing one in the other's PR would blur two classes that this ticket's own history shows are easy to conflate — the same trap as my `organizationId=abc` control above, where a `%00` → 500 looked like the byte class and was not.

Different host and seed, sampled not enumerated — **not evidence of a fix**, and nothing in KS-589 touches this check. Your description's six-site negative-offset inventory and the *"fix all six sites, not the two the sweep found"* instruction remain the right sizing.

No action needed here — attribution only.

title: positive_data_acceptance recurs at scale — 734 failures across 64 ops (KS-255 / KS-515 recurrence, full-2026-08-07 sweep)
description:
## Summary

This register tracks the biggest single class in the sweeps: the API politely refusing (4xx) request bodies the published spec says are valid. The steady fix is to bring each operation's spec and validator into line, in whichever direction is right for it. A small new member was added on 2026-09-28: `POST /api/gdpr/consent`, where the database declines a value the spec allows. Details are below for whenever it's picked up. Thank you, Kamil.

+++ The register (2026-08-07) and the 2026-09-28 addendum

### Why a new ticket

The predecessors are Done and archived: [KS-255](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-255/fix-tighten-openapi-request-schemas-add-400-responses-for-12-endpoints) (Done 2026-06-15) and [KS-515](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-515/write-path-requestresponse-schema-drift-27-ops-ks-430-recurrence-new) (Done 2026-07-29, itself the [KS-430](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-430/write-path-request-schema-contract-drift-across-60-operations-unmasked) recurrence). This is the same class recurring at a larger scale, filed fresh per the [KS-430](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-430/write-path-request-schema-contract-drift-across-60-operations-unmasked)→[KS-515](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-515/write-path-requestresponse-schema-drift-27-ops-ks-430-recurrence-new) / [KS-431](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-431/16-write-operations-return-raw-500-internal-error-unmasked-by-the-ks)→[KS-497](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-497/write-path-raw-500-internal-error-recurs-on-4-platformtenants-ops-ks) precedent.

### Finding

**734** `positive_data_acceptance` **failures across 64 operations**, about 75% of all check failures in `full-2026-08-07T14-12-05Z` (seed `2794626967`, 22,744 cases, 317 operations; Ubuntu 24.04.4 aarch64 VM, Schemathesis 4.24.3, Postgres 15.18). Each failure card embeds a curl; the run also wrote 94 replayable crash files. Counts are a floor, not a total: generation samples rather than enumerates.

### Fix direction

Per [KS-423](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-423/blocking-pr-pre-merge-schemathesis-coverage-6-contract-drift-failures) / [KS-430](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-430/write-path-request-schema-contract-drift-across-60-operations-unmasked): compare each route's validator with the spec, then tighten the spec to the runtime truth **or** loosen the runtime where the spec is right. Never narrow the generator. Cluster by service registration file.

### Addendum 2026-09-28 ([KS-1353](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1353/bump-systemtest-schemathesis-pin-4275-4280-first-minor-since-427x-9)): `POST /api/gdpr/consent`

* **What:** a spec-valid body answered **400** `VALIDATION_ERROR` *"One or more field values cannot be stored (too long or not an allowed value)"*. It's a draw: 2 of the 6 [KS-1353](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1353/bump-systemtest-schemathesis-pin-4275-4280-first-minor-since-427x-9) sweeps (sweeps 2 and 5, ×1 each).
* **The case:** `userId` (uuid), `purpose: "marketing"`, `source` = a 5-character string with a supplementary-plane character, `expiresInDays: 552`, plus 3 undeclared keys (allowed, since the schema doesn't set `additionalProperties: false`).
* **Where the 400 comes from:** `services/originate/src/routes/gdpr.ts:153` (`mapGdprWriteDbError`) maps Postgres **22001 / 23514 / 22007 / 22008 / 22021** to this 400. Its own comment says *"Value the spec permits but the schema can't store"*. So the refusal is deliberate; the gap is that the published contract doesn't declare the constraint.
* **Which constraint fired isn't recoverable:** the originate logs predate a slot rebuild. Candidates: `source`'s unusual character (22021 or a length limit), `expiresInDays` with no declared `maximum` (22008), or the extra keys if they reach a stored column. (An earlier note that said "extra keys → 400" was too specific.)
* **Direction:** a targeted probe per candidate names the Postgres code, then declare it in the spec (`maxLength`, `maximum`, a `pattern`, or `additionalProperties: false`).
* Listed in [KS-1361](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1361/schemathesis-baselinejson-lags-the-linear-registers-37-of-90-failing) for baselining against this ticket.

+++

**One more member of this class, `GET /api/platform/document-lookup` (measured 2026-10-30).**

- **Run:** `pre-merge-2026-10-30T10-03-47Z-slot1` (platform-k slot 1, Peter's Mac, Schemathesis 4.32.1, seed 881726611). The platform is `develop` `4c14143b3` unchanged; the branch it ran on, KS-1609, changes only `systemTest/` and docs.
- **Check:** ST202 `positive_data_acceptance`, case `iHOnxs`.
- **What happened:** `GET /api/platform/document-lookup?hash=` → **400** `{"success":false,"error":{"code":"BAD_REQUEST","message":"hash or documentId query parameter is required"}}`.
- **Why it is spec-valid:** the published operation (added under KS-1773) declares both `hash` and `documentId` as optional `string` query parameters, with no `minLength` and nothing saying one of them must be sent. So `?hash=` alone is valid against the contract.
- **Same shape as** this register's 2026-09-01 note: a cross-field rule the spec doesn't express ("Either challengeId or nonce is required").
- Not in `schemathesis-baseline.json`, and not added to it.
- **Direction, as for the rest of the register:** express the rule in the contract (for example `minLength: 1` on both, plus an `anyOf` requiring one of the two), or have the handler treat an empty `hash` as absent and fall through to `documentId` as the description already says.
- The KS-1773 deploy note records that no `hash` / `documentId` request was sent, so this path was not exercised there.

**BLUF:** a `positive_data_acceptance` failure on `POST /api/did` in today's pre-merge sweep is a **systemTest harness bug, not a platform defect**. Nothing to do on the platform side; it is being fixed in KS-1680.

- **Where:** run `pre-merge-2026-10-23T13-01-26Z-slot1` (platform-k slot 1, seed `2796048272`, Schemathesis 4.32.1), check ST202 "Schema-valid request rejected", response **400** `VALIDATION_ERROR` "Must not contain control byte U+0012".
- **Cause (verified from the request as sent):** the positive-phase body sanitizer (`systemTest/schemathesis/config/positive_sanitizer.py`, KS-472) leaves a raw control-byte key unchanged when the same object already has a `_` key: here `services[4]` carried both `"\x12"` and `"_"`. The platform's 400 is the correct KS-472 behaviour.
- It appears only when a draw generates that key pair, so it can come and go between runs.

The fix and its red→green test land on the KS-1680 branch. Thank you, Kamil.

## Addendum 2026-10-06 (KS-571): `/share` and `/transfer-custody` join the register — the exception that hid them is gone

**BLUF.** Two operations that had been hidden from this check now show it, Kamil. `systemTest/schemathesis/schemathesis.toml` used to let `POST /api/documents/{id}/share` and `/transfer-custody` answer 400 under `positive_data_acceptance`. That was meant for the connector-only `onBehalfOf` 400, but it hid every 400 on those operations. KS-571 replaced it with a narrower mechanism (the sweep no longer sends `onBehalfOf` from JWT personas). The real spec-vs-handler gaps underneath are now reported: **26 + 12 failing cases**. Thank you.

>>> Evidence (re-verified at source, `develop` `f556373b9`; sweep `full-ks-571-2026-10-06T10-09-50Z-slot4`, seed 571, slot 4, Schemathesis 4.29.3)

Spec-valid bodies the handler refuses with 400 (positive phase, no `onBehalfOf` in the body):

| Operation | Handler refusal (`services/originate/src/routes/documents.ts`) | Cases | What the spec says |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| `POST /api/documents/{id}/transfer-custody` | `:1629` "One of newHolderId or newHolderEmail is required" | 26 | request schema has no `required` and no `oneOf`/`anyOf` |
| same | `:1635` "Supply either newHolderId or newHolderEmail, not both" | 3 | mutual exclusion not expressed |
| same | `:1653` "newHolderId must be a valid UUID" | 6 | `newHolderId` is `type: string`, no `format: uuid` |
| `POST /api/documents/{id}/share` | `:2215` "Each recipient must have either an email or a userId" | 16 | `recipients[]` items have no `required` and no `anyOf` |

(Case counts are from the run's HAR, by reason. They overlap the 26 / 12 `positive_data_acceptance` failures reported for the two operations; the 3 `/share` 500s in the same run are KS-593's class, not this one.)

**Also worth knowing.** Before KS-571, `/version` (25) and `certifications/issue` (11) failures under this check were almost all the connector-only `onBehalfOf` 400, not this class (before→after 25→1, 11→1). Their entries in `config/schemathesis-baseline.json` cite this ticket. That baseline correction is Peter's (KS-1361), not yours.

**Suggested direction (same as the register):** express the rules in the published contract. For transfer-custody, `oneOf` [newHolderId] / [newHolderEmail] plus `format: uuid`; for share, recipient items with `anyOf` [email] / [userId]. Or relax the handler where the spec is right.

>>>

Refs as KS-NNN text. Posted by agent on Peter's behalf.

## Addendum 2026-10-05 (KS-1408 sweeps): `POST /api/kyc/{id}/review`

**BLUF.** One new member, Kamil, reproduced in both 4.29.3 sweeps: `POST /api/kyc/{id}/review` answers **400** to a generated body that is **valid against the published request schema** (checked with `jsonschema_rs` against the spec, not assumed). It wasn't on this register or in the baseline. Thank you.

>>> Evidence and what was ruled out

| | 4.28.0 | 4.29.3 | 4.29.3 re-run |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| failing cases | 0 | 1 | 1 |

* Generated value (no pool-drawn ids), `fuzzing` phase, positive mode. Body validates against the spec, response 400.
* **Ruled out:** the 4.29.x false positive (a pool draw overwriting the case). That mechanism affects `negative_data_rejection`, not this check, and this case had no pool draw.
* Two other new `positive_data_acceptance` pairs from the same sweeps (`POST /api/identity-credentials/issue`, `PUT /api/nft/admin/platform-fee`) were sent **no body**. Neither spec marks the body `required`, so they belong to KS-1364's class (In Progress) and are recorded there instead.

Run directories: `systemTest/schemathesis/output/reports/full-ks-1408-2026-10-05T09-32-24Z-slot4`, `…T10-23-55Z-slot4`.

>>>

Class register addendum, 2026-09-15 — two `positive_data_acceptance` ops not yet in the baseline or on any ticket by name, same class ("read the counts as a floor"): **`POST /api/security/keys`** ×1 and **`POST /api/billing/checkout/custom`** ×1, on `pre-merge-2026-09-15T12-41-42Z-slot3` (seed 1721585185, slot 3 rebuilt from scratch, macOS arm64, Schemathesis 4.27.1, head `f2c2f84e0` of PR #997 — https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/997). `billing/checkout/custom` is a by-design-503 op (KS-268 set): the "rejection" it reports is the declared 503 to a schema-compliant request, i.e. the unconfigured-provider posture, not a validator defect — worth a `positive_data_acceptance` `expected-statuses` entry of the KS-686 shape rather than a fix, Peter's call on the systemTest side. `security/keys` is the ordinary class. PR #997 changes no service or spec code. Floor, not total.

## Results 2026-09-14 — `positive_data_acceptance` on 4.27.1: 69 operations in `full`, and the auth/MFA cluster is the untriaged core

**Where:** the Mac, slot 3, from-scratch stack, `develop` @ `64c386e04` (4.27.1) + `claude/schemathesis-systemtest-tickets-be524a` @ `ab3ad5c21`. `full-2026-09-14T15-04-07Z-slot3` — 342 ops, 0 errored, ~8,400 cases, 22.3 min. Counts are a floor, not a total.

**69 operations failed `positive_data_acceptance`** (the register's 2026-08-07 figure was 64 — same order, different sample). 20 of them are not in the baseline; the rest are baselined under this ticket or KS-1015:

**Untriaged (from the baseline gate, evaluated by hand — KS-752):** `GET /api/auth/social/{provider}/callback` ×21, `POST /api/billing/admin/credits` ×22, `POST /api/auth/social/link` ×12, `POST /api/documents/{id}/revoke` ×10, `GET /api/auth/social/{provider}` ×7, `POST /api/auth/mfa/disable` ×7, `POST /api/users/me/mfa/disable` ×7, `POST /api/users/me/mfa/verify` ×7, `POST /api/auth/wallet/authenticate` ×6, `DELETE /api/auth/wallet/unlink` ×4, `POST /api/identity-credentials/issue` ×3, `POST /api/nft/ipfs/upload` ×3, `PATCH /api/did/{did}` ×2, `POST /api/delegations` ×2, `POST /api/timestamps/verify` ×2, and ×1 each on `POST /api/analytics/reports`, `POST /api/auth/mfa/backup-codes/regenerate`, `POST /api/credentials`, `POST /api/gdpr/consent`, `POST /api/security/events`. `pre-merge` (`…T14-48-37Z-slot3`) adds `POST /api/security/audit`, `POST /api/security/keys`, `PUT /api/nft/admin/platform-fee`, `POST /api/billing/checkout/custom` ×1 each.

**Two things to know before triaging against this class:**
1. 4.27.1 changed generation (dependency inference, response-value reuse, a valid-body fallback when examples are invalid), so the population moved: KS-1169's own before/after shows 10 ops LEAVING this bucket and 17 entering. `PATCH /api/did/{did}`, `POST /api/delegations`, `POST /api/identity-credentials/issue`, `POST /api/nft/ipfs/upload`, `POST /api/analytics/reports`, `POST /api/security/events` are new under the bump.
2. `POST /api/users/me/change-password` is in the failing set but KS-575 established it 404s "User not found" for a validly-authenticated user (platform-side; Kamil) — the rejection is a handler 404, not a validation 400.

The `/api/auth/` + `/mfa/` cluster (10 ops above) is the KS-1015 finding-1 set and still has zero baseline coverage. Refs as KS-NNN text.

KS-1169 (Schemathesis 4.25.2 → 4.27.1, `full` sweep, slot 2, 2026-09-14): `positive_data_acceptance` failing ops **45 → 52** (+17 new, −10 gone). The 10 that left did so because 4.27.1's coverage-phase fix now produces a body the validator accepts (they moved to by-design 503s — see KS-593). The 17 new: `PATCH /api/did/{did}`, `POST /api/analytics/reports`, `/auth/mfa/backup-codes/regenerate`, `/auth/mfa/disable`, `/billing/checkout/bundle`, `/delegations`, `/delegations/validate`, `/m365/connections/init`, `/nft/estimate`, `/nft/ipfs/upload`, `/nft/mint`, `/oauth/apps`, `/onedrive/files/{id}/sync`, `/platform/tenants`, `/security/rate-limit/reset`, `/timestamps/verify`, `/users/me/mfa/verify`. Also relevant: 4.27.0 fixed `positive_data_acceptance`/`negative_data_rejection` false positives on 429 responses. `validation_mismatch` warning 64 → 49 ops.

Five operations outside the 64 (the floor, as the ticket says), 2026-09-10, Mac, slot 1, `pre-merge-ks-682-2026-09-10T10-52-00Z-slot1` (`billing/admin/credits` also in `…T10-36-34Z-slot1`): `positive_data_acceptance` on `POST /api/billing/admin/credits` ×6, `POST /api/security/audit` ×1, `POST /api/security/events` ×1, `POST /api/timestamps/verify` ×1, `PUT /api/nft/admin/platform-fee` ×1 — each a 400 `Required` on a field the spec leaves optional (`action`/`eventType`/`hash`/`percentage`). Same shape as the class; not baselined, no new ticket. PR under review https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/896 (no service code).

## Still recurring — pre-merge, 2026-09-03, on the Mac Recording a fresh observation, not a re-scoping. **38 operations** in this class failed on `pre-merge-2026-09-03T12-18-51Z`. **This is a much thinner sample than the run of record, so please do not read 38 as an improvement on 64.** The ticket's figures come from a `full` sweep (22,744 cases, 317 operations); this was `pre-merge` with `--max-examples 6`, ~2,016 cases across 340 operations. Property-based generation samples rather than enumerates, so the two numbers are not comparable in either direction — this only confirms the class is live, on a different host and a newer Schemathesis. **Environment (differs from the ticket's run of record, which was the Ubuntu VM):** | | | | -- | -- | | Host | macOS, Docker Desktop 8 CPU / 31.3 GiB, aarch64 — slot 1, gateway `:6882` | | Schemathesis | 4.25.2 (ticket's run: 4.24.3) | | Python / pytest | 3.14.6 / 9.1.1 | | Run validity | **OK — 0 of 340 operations errored** | | Duration | 14.9 min, 12 workers | Caveat on the host: three other platform-k stacks were up on the same 8 CPUs, so no timing here is quotable. Verdicts should be unaffected — contention manufactures timeouts, not check failures — and run validity came back clean.
The 38 operations (all positive_data_acceptance) ``` GET /api/platform/tenants/{id} PATCH /api/platform/tenants/{id} PATCH /api/platform/tenants/{id}/status PATCH /api/users/admin/{id} POST /api/anchors POST /api/anchors/thread-mint POST /api/billing/customers POST /api/billing/customers/{customerId}/default-payment-method POST /api/certifications/issue POST /api/delegations/validate POST /api/documents/{id}/anchor POST /api/documents/{id}/sign-cert POST /api/documents/{id}/sign-wallet POST /api/documents/{id}/version POST /api/issuer-certs POST /api/issuer-certs/sign POST /api/issuer-certs/{id}/revoke POST /api/issuer-certs/{id}/rotate POST /api/m365/connections/complete POST /api/m365/documents/sync POST /api/m365/sites POST /api/nft/estimate POST /api/nft/mint POST /api/nft/record POST /api/oauth/apps/{id}/rotate-secret POST /api/onedrive/files/{id}/sync POST /api/platform/organizations/register-connector POST /api/platform/tenants POST /api/referrals/apply POST /api/referrals/generate POST /api/stake POST /api/stake/complete-unstake POST /api/stake/unstake POST /api/transfers/{id}/approve POST /api/transfers/{id}/cancel POST /api/transfers/{id}/execute POST /api/transfers/{id}/reject POST /api/v2/verification/verify ```
Two representative failures, both "valid data should have been accepted": ``` PATCH /api/platform/tenants/{id} [400] {"code":"BAD_REQUEST","message":"No fields to update"} curl -X PATCH -H 'Authorization: ' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{}' \ http://localhost:6882/api/platform/tenants/00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001 POST /api/anchors [400] {"validation":"regex","message":"Invalid documentId format","path":["documentId"]} ``` The `PATCH …/{id}` shape is worth a look when this is picked up: the spec permits an empty object, the handler requires at least one field. That is a spec-tightening fix rather than a handler change, and the same shape appears on `PATCH /api/users/admin/{id}` (*"No valid fields to update"*). Artefacts: `systemTest/schemathesis/output/reports/pre-merge-2026-09-03T12-18-51Z/` (HTML report, NDJSON, JUnit XML, VCR cassette, HAR, per-call metrics). Mapped by hand against `config/schemathesis-baseline.json`, because the automated baseline gate did not run — it is skipped whenever the sweep fails, which is [KS-752](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-752) and exactly the case here. *Observed while validating KS-717 on a branch that changes only `systemTest/akto` and three docs — the OpenAPI spec and all platform code are byte-identical to `develop`, so nothing here is attributable to that branch.*

## Sizing: **M**, down from L — the 2026-09-01 run changed the shape, not just the number

Sized, not started (s103).

| run | failures | operations | shape |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| `full-2026-08-07` (record) | 734 | 64 | deep — many failures per op |
| `pre-merge` 2026-08-20 | — | 42 | — |
| `full-2026-09-01` | **60** | **60** | **broad and shallow — one each** |

**That difference is the whole sizing argument.** 734 failures over 64 ops is a set of operations each rejecting many valid bodies — dozens of individual schema decisions. 60 failures over 60 ops is one rejected case per operation, which is far more consistent with a small number of *shared* causes (a common validator, an envelope-level constraint, a generator interaction) reaching many operations, than with 60 unrelated bugs.

**So the first unit of work is a triage pass, not fixes:** group the 60 by *reason for rejection* and see how few distinct causes there are. If it collapses to a handful, this is M and possibly S. If it really is 60 independent spec-vs-handler disagreements, it re-sizes to L and should be split.

⚠ **Do not start by fixing operations.** Sizing this from the 08-07 numbers would have bought a 64-operation programme for what the current data suggests is a much smaller one. Re-measure first, on current `develop`, and record the run of record — the two 08-05 runs already demonstrated on this board that runs disagree about *which* operations fail even when they agree about the class.

## Still live 2026-09-01 — 60 failures across 60 operations, but the scale is very different from the 08-07 run

**Run:** `full-2026-09-01T11-57-02Z` · Schemathesis **4.25.2** · 338 operations · ~8,400 cases · 23.2 min.
**Branch:** `feature/ks-611-post-apitimestampsbatch-errors-on-every-sweep` @ **`35a35ca3d3539c9da391254855789c8fbc92d82c`** (PR #734 — a `.strict()` change on `POST /api/timestamps/batch` plus systemTest housekeeping; nothing touching the operations below).

## BLUF

`positive_data_acceptance` remains the largest failing class: **60 failures across 60 distinct operations** — one per operation, no clustering.

**Compared with the 08-07 run this ticket was raised on (734 failures / 64 ops):** the *operation* count is essentially unchanged (60 vs 64), but the *failure* count is down an order of magnitude. **Do not read that as improvement** — this run used `--max-examples 25` against a different budget on 08-07, so fewer draws per operation means fewer recorded failures for the same underlying defect. **The breadth is the signal here, not the count.**

## What it looks like

**Every one of the 60 is an HTTP 400** — the API rejecting a body the spec says is valid. Sampled shapes:

`POST /api/analytics/reports` — spec marks `type` and `period` optional, runtime requires both:
```json
{"code":"BAD_REQUEST","message":"Invalid report request","details":[
  {"expected":"'summary' | 'detailed'","received":"undefined","code":"invalid_type","path":["type"],"message":"Required"},
  {"expected":"'hour' | 'day' | 'week' | 'month' | 'quarter' | 'year' | 'all'","received":"undefined","code":"invalid_type","path":["period"],"message":"Required"}]}
```

`POST /api/auth/wallet/authenticate` — a cross-field rule the spec does not express:
```json
{"code":"VALIDATION_ERROR","message":": Either challengeId or nonce is required"}
```

So the dominant shape is **spec/runtime divergence on requiredness** — either a field the Zod schema requires but the spec marks optional, or a conditional rule (`oneOf`-style) the spec cannot express as written. That is consistent with this ticket's existing framing.

## One thing worth separating

Several of the 60 are **M365 operations** (`/api/m365/documents/sync`, `/outlook/exchange-token`, `/sites`, `/connections/init`). I checked whether these were KS-693's *"503 when `ENTRA_*` is unconfigured"* — **they are not**: all four return **400**, not 503. So they belong here, not on KS-693. Recording the check so nobody re-derives it.

## Environment

Mac, slot 1, 33 containers / 33 healthy, seeded users, Schemathesis 4.25.2, Python 3.14.6, anchoring in mock mode. Artefacts under `systemTest/schemathesis/output/reports/full-2026-09-01T11-57-02Z/`.

Refs as KS-NNN text. Measured and filed by agent on Peter's behalf, 2026-09-01.

## Still live — re-measured 2026-08-20, `positive_data_acceptance` on **42 operations**

Fresh datapoint from a `pre-merge` sweep run while verifying KS-666 (stack-slot isolation). **Not new work and not a new ticket** — recording it here because this ticket owns the class and the measurement is current.

**Run:** `pre-merge-ks-666-2026-08-20T13-29-08Z-slot3`, Schemathesis 4.24.3, local stack on slot 3 (`:7082`), 13,724 cases generated, 65 unique failures total.

`positive_data_acceptance` — reported as **"API rejected schema-compliant request"** — is the dominant class at **42 of 52 failing operations**:

```
DELETE /api/platform/tenants/{id}     PATCH  /api/platform/tenants/{id}
PATCH  /api/users/admin/{id}          POST   /api/anchors
POST   /api/anchors/thread-mint       POST   /api/billing/checkout/custom
POST   /api/certifications/issue      POST   /api/documents/{id}/anchor
… 34 more
```

## How this relates to the 734/64 figure in the description

The earlier measurement was a **full** sweep (`full-2026-08-07`); this is **pre-merge**, which runs fewer examples per operation. So 42 ops vs 64 ops is a difference in sweep depth, **not** evidence of partial remediation — please don't read it as progress. Same class, smaller sample.

## Attribution

The branch this ran on (KS-666) changes only `systemTest/` harness plumbing, `Blockchain/Dev/scripts` gates, compose files and docs — **zero** files under `services/`, `packages/`, `frontend/`, `contracts/`, `migrations/` or `docs/openapi/`. It cannot have caused an API-vs-spec disagreement, and no remediation for this class is being attempted there.

## Caveat on the mapping

Ten of these are expected: `docs/known_issues_and_baseline.md` §11 records ~10 precondition refusals as **working-as-intended** under KS-478 / KS-466 §11, and they surface under this same check name. KS-665 covers a further 5 as example-fixable 400s. I have **not** individually attributed the remaining ~27, so the count above is the raw check total, not a defect count.

Artifacts: `systemTest/schemathesis/output/reports/pre-merge-ks-666-2026-08-20T13-29-08Z-slot3/` (allure + NDJSON + VCR).

**Now surfaced in the report against this ticket (KS-589 / PR #656).**
