**BLUF:** this adds one more genuine 500 on schema-compliant input to §2, in the same class. `POST /api/documents` answers **500** when `title` is longer than 500 characters, because nothing checks the length before Postgres rejects it. A KS-1042 live test found it on 2026-10-21. KS-1042 did not cause it: no product code changed, and slot 1 was built from develop `280fdbcd1`.

**New §2 row**

| Operation | Site | Mechanism |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `POST /api/documents` | `services/originate/src/originate.openapi.ts` (`title: z.string()`, no `.max()`) → `migrations/001_initial-schema.sql:97` (`title VARCHAR(500) NOT NULL`) | A 10,000-character title passes validation, reaches the insert, and Postgres raises `22001`. Nothing handles that, so it comes back as a 500. The published `DocumentCreateRequest.title` declares no `maxLength` either. |

**Measured** (slot 1, 2026-10-21, ISSUER_ADMIN, body `{"title": "x" * 10000}`):
```
POST http://localhost:6882/api/documents  →  500 Internal Server Error
originate: Raw query failed. Code: `22001`. Message: `value too long for type character varying(500)`
originate: Failed to create document
```

**Not measured:** the other create paths that write `documents.title`: certifications issue, `/:id/version`, sign-cert and sign-wallet. They write the same column, so they probably return the same 500, but only `POST /api/documents` was driven.

**Repro** (any account that can write documents; the token is not shown):
```bash
curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' -X POST http://localhost:6882/api/documents \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d "{\"title\":\"$(printf 'x%.0s' $(seq 1 10000))\"}"
```

**Fix direction (your call, Kamil):** add `.max(500)` on `title` in every schema that writes `documents.title`, placed after `.trim()` per KS-202. That also publishes `maxLength: 500` in the spec once it is regenerated. An over-long title should get a 4xx, not be truncated.

**Acceptance criteria for this row**
1. **Automated test:** the 10,000-character case of `systemTest/schemathesis/tests/test_fuzz_comprehensive.py::test_string_parameter_fuzzing` (added under KS-1042) goes from **500 (red)** to a 4xx with an error body (green). Add an originate route test pinning 400 at 501 characters and 201 at 500.
2. **Docs updated:** the published spec, where `DocumentCreateRequest.title` gains `maxLength: 500` via `npm run generate-openapi`. No other doc names the limit.
3. **systemTests updated:** nothing beyond the KS-1042 test above, which already drives this. Once `maxLength` is published, the Schemathesis sweep will also generate at the boundary.

For context: these results were measured on the KS-1455 branch (`feature/ks-1455-bump-systemtest-schemathesis-pin-4294-4300-or-later-release`, PR https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/1438), which is going to be merged today.

### §3 answered — `POST /api/timestamps` is a 503, not a raw 500, but a SECOND 503 shape

`integration_5xx_guard` fired once. The body is a well-formed 503 envelope, just not the one the guard accepts:

```
[503] {"success":false,"error":{"code":"QUALIFIED_TSA_UNAVAILABLE","message":"requireEidas: no eIDAS-qualified TSA is reachable — refusing to fall back to a mock token"}}
curl -X POST -H 'Authorization: Bearer …' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"hash":"abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789","requireEidas":true}' http://localhost:7082/api/timestamps
```

That is the KS-523 fail-closed posture (`requireEidas` refusing the mock fallback), not the "unconfigured integration" `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` envelope the guard was written for. So it is a correct, deliberate 503 that the harness does not yet recognise — a ruling question, not a platform bug: either the guard learns the `QUALIFIED_TSA_UNAVAILABLE` code for this op (systemTest, Peter) or the fail-closed path should answer the same envelope code as the unconfigured path (platform, Kamil). Related: KS-753 (mock TSA fallback on the batch path). `POST /api/credentials` did NOT fire this run.

### §2 sibling — `GET /api/platform/audit-log` ACCEPTS the invalid offset/limit with 200 (rather than 500)

§2 names `api-gateway/src/routes/platform.ts:374` as a negative-offset site with no guard. This sweep shows the audit-log read on that surface answering **200** to schema-violating `limit`/`offset` — 34 accepted negative cases, e.g.:

```
GET /api/platform/audit-log?offset=-1      → 200   (offset declared integer, minimum: 0)
GET /api/platform/audit-log?offset=AAA     → 200
GET /api/platform/audit-log?offset=0.5     → 200
GET /api/platform/audit-log?limit=<object> → 200   (limit: type / maximum violated)
```

Caught by `by_design_input_tolerance_guard` (KS-662): the ruling for this op tolerates an **unknown query key** only, so a declared parameter violated and still accepted is outside it — exactly the case KS-662's table lists under "Still FAILS". Not a new class; it is §2's pattern surfacing as an accept instead of a 500. Fix per §2 (`.int().min(0)` at handler entry, and the type check).

### Also in this run, filed elsewhere

`POST /api/status/{id}/revoke` and `/unrevoke` accepted a wrong-typed `index` (`"AAA"`, `{}`, `null`, `false`, a float) with 200 — 13 negative cases. Same KS-662 "still FAILS" class; noted here because it is the same fix shape, but the KS-662 ruling on those ops is Kamil's to widen or not. Note the guard also has a harness defect (fires on positive cases) that inflates its counts — that half is on KS-1170, not here.

title: [Parked] Register watermarked/signed versions with K — requires splitting UsePerVerbEndpoints
description:
## Problem

Only the **original upload** becomes a document in platform-k. Watermark, sign and certify go to flat `POST /api/anchors` and exist there as anchors only:

```csharp
// CardanoAnchorService.AnchorOrOriginateAsync
if (isUpload && s.UseOriginateForUpload) { … OriginateDocumentAsync … }
return await AnchorAsync(tx, doc, actingPersonId, ct);   // everything else
```

So any derived version's hash misses K's `documents` table and can only be answered from K's chain index. That is the root cause behind [PS-530](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-530/share-view-verify-reports-not-registered-for-documents-secuura), and behind the testers' original report in [PS-522](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-522/verify-should-state-which-lifecycle-actions-have-and-have-not-been).

**Both verify surfaces are affected identically**, which is worth stating because it means one fix covers both:

* the share view posts `DocDisplaySha256Hash` — the displayed (derived) version;
* the Outlook add-in attaches `_docState.GetCurrentAsync(doc.Id)`, the ledger tip, and the recipient hashes exactly those bytes.

Same question, same miss. They already render from one resolver and one `verdictOf` after [PS-522](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-522/verify-should-state-which-lifecycle-actions-have-and-have-not-been)/[PS-530](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-530/share-view-verify-reports-not-registered-for-documents-secuura), so they cannot diverge — they go green together or not at all.

## platform-k already built this endpoint, for us

```
POST /api/documents/:id/version   — KS-86
```

> "Records a new versioned document (with `parent_document_id` pointing at the source) for any byte-changing action the caller has already performed externally — typically a watermark or an X.509 sign-and-sidecar. Platform K is a hash-only registry; the bytes themselves live with the issuer **(e.g. SSD)**."

Body: `{action, newContentHash, metadata?, title?}` with `action` locked to `'watermark' | 'sign-cert'`.

S has never called it — S calls only `/api/documents`, `/api/anchors` and `/api/verification/verify`. This also explains the `lineage` / `newerVersions` / `hasNewerCertifiedVersion` fields K returns and S discards ([PS-522](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-522/verify-should-state-which-lifecycle-actions-have-and-have-not-been)): they walk `parent_document_id`, which is precisely what this endpoint populates.

So this is not a new contract to agree with @kamil.kreiser — it is the shape K designed and S never adopted.

## Scope

1. On the **watermark** and **sign** produce-events, call `POST /api/documents/{parentK}/version` with the new content hash, mapping S's verb to K's enum (`sign` → `sign-cert`).
2. Anchor the returned id — K deliberately does **not** anchor from `/version`, leaving the Cardano cost decision to the issuer.
3. Store the new K document id per version so subsequent events target the right parent.
4. Stop discarding K's `lineage` / `newerVersions` / `hasNewerCertifiedVersion` on verify ([PS-522](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-522/verify-should-state-which-lifecycle-actions-have-and-have-not-been) noted these are already returned).

## Known limits — worth setting expectations before the work starts

* The derived document is created as `status: 'draft'`, and K's `isCertified` requires `certified | anchored | signed`. So `/version` alone buys **recognition**, not a green tick: the document is found, title/type/lineage populate, and "not registered" goes away. Green needs step 2 to succeed.
* Step 2 needs `CardanoAnchor:Enabled = true`. On a deployment with anchoring off this still will not verify — it will simply stop claiming the file is unknown.
* Only versions created **after** this ships are affected. Existing watermarked/signed documents stay as "recognised, not confirmed" unless backfilled; a backfill is deliberately out of scope here.

## Must not regress

A failure of `/version` must fall back to the existing flat anchor rather than dropping the event. K's [KS-388](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-388/k-freeze-documenttype-as-a-strict-enum-originate-flat-anchor-metadata) principle is "never silently anchored", and S's counterpart is that a lifecycle event always leaves a chain record — losing one to a new API call would be a worse defect than the one being fixed.

## Acceptance

* On a **watermark** and on a **sign** produce-event, S calls `POST /api/documents/{parentK}/version` with the new content hash and the mapped action (`watermark`, and S's `sign` → K's `sign-cert`) — observable in the app log against a K that is up, with the request path and the mapped verb quoted.
* The id K returns is **anchored** by S (step 2), and is **stored per version**, so a second derived event targets the new row as its parent rather than the original upload.
* S stops discarding K's `lineage`, `newerVersions` and `hasNewerCertifiedVersion` on verify — the `VerifyResponse` DTO declares them and they survive deserialisation.
* **Must not regress**: a failed or refused `/version` call falls back to the existing flat `POST /api/anchors` rather than dropping the event. A lifecycle event always leaves a chain record. An xUnit test forces `/version` to fail and asserts the flat anchor was taken.
* The known limits are stated in the PR rather than discovered by a reviewer: `/version` alone gives recognition and not a green tick (K creates the row as `draft`, and `isCertified` needs `certified | anchored | signed`); green needs the anchor in step 2 and therefore `CardanoAnchor:Enabled = true`; and only versions created after the change are affected, with a backfill out of scope.

**Playwright test that demonstrates the fix** (required, and this is one of the cases that genuinely needs a live S↔K pair): suggest `systemTest/tests/k_live/version_registration.spec.ts`, tagged `@k-live` so it pairs S slot N with platform-k slot N. `chain_match.spec.ts` is the nearest existing file but it is about a hash matching an existing registration, not about creating a derived one, so this belongs in its own spec. Against a live stack with K slot N **up**, it must:

1. register a PDF, **watermark** it, then verify the watermarked bytes at `/Verify` (`verify-file-input` → `verify-submit-btn`), and assert `verify-result-check-documentexists` is **ticked** and `verify-result-recognised-unconfirmed` is **not** the verdict shown;
2. repeat for a **signed** version, asserting the same two things, so both produce-events are covered rather than just the one that was implemented first;
3. assert `verify-result-registered` renders for the derived version, which is the user-visible half of "not registered goes away";
4. assert the lineage line names the **parent** document, proving `parent_document_id` was populated and that S is no longer discarding K's `lineage`;
5. **control that must keep passing**: verifying the **original upload** still reports exactly what it reports today — registered and anchored — so the change added a derived registration rather than moving the original's.

**Which assertion fails on** `develop` **today**: steps 1, 2 and 3. Today `CardanoAnchorService.AnchorOrOriginateAsync` sends everything except the upload to the flat `POST /api/anchors`, so a watermarked or signed hash is absent from K's `documents` table and `/Verify` reports it as recognised-but-unconfirmed or not registered at all — which is the defect behind [PS-530](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-530/share-view-verify-reports-not-registered-for-documents-secuura). Step 5 passes today and must keep passing.

**Read the skip kinds line before believing a green run.** If K slot N is not up, all `@k-live` specs — including this one — stand down as environmental skips and the run reports green while the S↔K path was never exercised. A 14-environmental-skip run does not prove this ticket; say so and prove it from the app log against a K that is up, with the counts.

The rules stay in xUnit: the S-verb → K-enum mapping, the per-version parent id bookkeeping, the fallback-to-flat-anchor on failure, and the DTO now carrying `lineage` / `newerVersions` / `hasNewerCertifiedVersion`.

nodes.body: Stale, checked at develop `477eb57` (2026-09-29): S **does** call `POST /api/documents/{parent}/version` — `watermark` and `sign` (as `sign-cert`) route through `VersionThenAnchorAsync` and then `POST /{new}/anchor`, advancing `PlatformKTipDocId` (`ssd/Services/CardanoAnchor/CardanoAnchorService.PerVerb.cs:59-67, 139-247`). Scope items 1–3 of this ticket are done. What remains is item 4 only: S still discards K's `lineage` / `newerVersions` / `hasNewerCertifiedVersion` on verify. Suggest retitling to that, or closing in favour of a verify read-back ticket. PS-549 (parse K's certification object) is therefore no longer blocked by this one.

## Correction: this is already built

Before writing anything I went looking for the S-side integration points and found the whole scope of this ticket already implemented, as **PS-124's per-verb path** in `ssd/Services/CardanoAnchor/CardanoAnchorService.PerVerb.cs`:

```csharp
case "watermark":
    return await VersionThenAnchorAsync(tx, doc, parentKId, "watermark", …);
case "sign":
    // routed as sign-cert — the signed bytes are a new K version forked from the watermark
    return await VersionThenAnchorAsync(tx, doc, parentKId, "sign-cert", …);
```

`VersionThenAnchorAsync` does exactly what this ticket asked for, and already handles what I listed as "must not regress":

- POSTs `/api/documents/{parent}/version` with `{action, newContentHash, title}`
- anchors the new id (`POST /api/documents/{newId}/anchor`) — KS-282 and KS-281 already resolved
- advances `DocumentStore.PlatformKTipDocId` so the next verb forks from the right parent
- **falls back to flat `/api/anchors` on every failure path**, so no event is ever lost

`PlatformKRootDocId` / `PlatformKTipDocId` are populated by `AnchorResultApplier` on the upload genesis. Nothing needs writing.

## So the real question is the flag

```csharp
// CardanoAnchorSettings
public bool UsePerVerbEndpoints { get; set; } = false;
```

Default false, and not set in any `appsettings*.json` or `dep-*` config. The feature has never been switched on.

## Why it can't simply be switched on

**The flag is all-or-nothing.** It routes far more than the two mutating verbs — `certify`, `share`, `rights-assign` / `rights-reassign` and a batch of lifecycle verbs all move to their own K endpoints. And unlike `/version`, some of those bodies carry personal data:

```csharp
// CertifyAsync
var holderEmail = EmailFromActorName(tx.ActorName);
```

K's certification endpoint requires a holder, so enabling the flag to fix document verification would, as a side effect, start sending **user email addresses to platform-K**. The `/version` body itself carries none — only action, hash and filename.

That is a data-sharing decision, not a config tweak, and it is not one to take as a by-product of fixing a verify surface.

## Recommendation

**Split the gate** so the two mutating verbs (`watermark`, `sign` → `/version`) can be enabled independently of the address-carrying verbs. Small, reversible, and it delivers this ticket's goal — derived versions become real K documents and both verify surfaces can go green — with no new PII leaving S.

Then enabling it is one setting, and the PII-carrying verbs stay off until they are decided on their own merits.

Scope of this ticket is therefore **not** "implement version forking" but "let it be turned on safely". Awaiting a decision before proceeding.

title: anchoring threadTokenMint test fails only under root-visible npm install layout — nested @lucid-evolution/plutus duplicate-instance (pre-existing, layout-dependent; KS-559 A/B-cleared)
description:
**Found during KS-559 validation (2026-08-04, Agent Teams pilot) — pre-existing, NOT caused by the dep sweep (controlled A/B in two independent environments: identical failure with pre-KS-559 and post-KS-559 locks).**

`services/anchoring` test `threadTokenMint.test.ts › parameterises mint + spend with a deterministic per-seed policyId` fails with `Could not serialize the data: Error: Unsupported type` in `applyParamsToScript` — the classic **duplicate-instance** signature: the test's `Constr` comes from the top-level `@lucid-evolution/plutus@0.1.31` while `@lucid-evolution/utils@0.1.70` serializes against its own nested `plutus@0.1.33` copy, and the cross-copy instanceof check fails.

**It is INSTALL-LAYOUT-DEPENDENT, which is why it looks flaky across setups:**

* `npm ci` in a **parentless standalone** copy of services/anchoring (= what the Dockerfile does) → **110/110 pass**. Verified on macOS host for both develop and KS-559 locks.
* `npm ci --workspaces=false` with the **monorepo root visible** as a parent dir (worktree, full-repo container mount) → **109/110, this test fails**. Verified on macOS host AND in node:24-alpine, again for both locks.

Same lock file both ways (`packages` dict byte-identical to develop) — npm physically lays the tree out differently when it can see a parent workspace root, and one layout resolves the utils→plutus import to the nested copy.

**Why it matters:** (1) any dev running anchoring tests inside the monorepo checkout with a standalone install hits a phantom red; (2) the nested plutus duplication itself (0.1.31 vs 0.1.33) is fragile — a future hoist change could flip the shipped image's behaviour. Fix options: dedupe/pin `@lucid-evolution/plutus` so one copy exists; or make the test/lib resolution layout-proof; or document the supported install layout for the suite.

Evidence + repro commands in the KS-559 PR thread and session history 2026-08-04. Credit: caught by the KS-559 deps teammate's controlled A/B refusing to accept an unqualified 110/110.

nodes.body:
**BLUF:** QA gate 248 (PR 2081, KS-1171 8k, 2026-11-07) re-measured the cause this ticket describes and says the product mint has the same shape, which is the question the gate 70 comment on this ticket leaves open ("whether the anchoring image's install layout reproduces the split in a built container"). It is still unmeasured. Kam's card `secuura-anchoring-second-fee-on-empty-reply-1107` = a, "Merge PR 2081, and fix the empty reply before anchoring next deploys (recommended)", ruled 2026-11-08 at 20:31:42 +11:00, names "Medium to measure the mint on an image". This ticket (Backlog, Medium) already carries that work, and Wednesday's ruling of 2026-11-01 put the gate 70 finding here instead of on a new ticket, so no second ticket was filed. Evidence class: MEASURED AT RUNTIME for the identity check; READ ONLY for the product mint and the image's lock file. No state, assignee or priority of this ticket was changed.

**What gate 248 measured:** at develop and at the PR 2081 head the same cell fails with the same message, "Could not serialize the data: Error: Unsupported type", 2 of 2 alone in each tree. The cell imports only the lucid-evolution packages, and none of the PR's three product files is in its import graph. `Constr` comes from one copy of `lucid-evolution/plutus` (0.1.31) and `applyParamsToScript` serialises with another (0.1.33 in that tree): `l.Constr === p.Constr` is false, and the same call with the other copy's `Constr` succeeds.

**New here (read only):** `Blockchain/Dev/services/anchoring/src/cardano/threadTokenMint.ts` line 92, lines 267 to 269, and the `applyParamsToScript` call below them use the same pairing, so the real thread-token mint may throw the same error. The failing step is before signing, so by read no fee is at risk. The image installs from `Blockchain/Dev/services/anchoring/package-lock.json`, which also splits plutus (0.1.31 and 0.1.36), by gate 248's read.

**Also new:** the cell goes green if the blueprint is absent (it warns and returns): gate 248's own first run read 856 of 856 for exactly that reason, and the same holds for a failed lucid import. Fix shape (gate 248): a missing blueprint fails the cell.

**Still unmeasured:** the mint on any image or box, with any key. Anchoring's deploy stays held for Kam's word.

**Source:** gate 248 verdict, finding F2 and ask 2, `/Volumes/DevMASTER/WEDNESDAY/0_Brain/reference/2026-11-07_gate248-tier1-pr2081-ks1171/verdict.md`. This seat re-read the verdict and the lines named above and ran nothing else. The High half, the empty reply, is KS-2103.

**BLUF:** QA gate 70 (KS 1384 R2b, 2026-11-01) measured this failure again and found it deterministic, NOT host-dependent. The `threadTokenMint.test.ts` emulator round-trip fails because two copies of the scoped npm package `lucid-evolution/plutus` are installed: the test's `Constr` and the serializer inside `applyParamsToScript` come from different copies, so `Constr` identity is false. The product mint imports the same pair.

What the gate measured:
* `lucid.Constr === utils-plutus Constr: false`, its log `evidence/q7_constr_identity.log`. The cell fails with "Could not serialize the data: Unsupported type".
* The product `services/anchoring/src/threadTokenMint.ts` (lines 267-269 at the R2b head `ecfe4f07fdce`) imports `lucid-evolution/lucid` from the workspace root and `lucid-evolution/utils` from anchoring's own `node_modules`: the same pair of copies.
* Not tested: whether the anchoring image's install layout reproduces the split in a built container.

It is outside the KS 1384 train: that delta touches no package or lockfile.

Source: QA gate 70 verdict, finding G70-F6 and Q7, `/Volumes/DevMASTER/WEDNESDAY/0_Brain/reference/2026-11-01_gate70-ks1384-r2b-1884/verdict.md`. Recorded here on Wednesday's ruling of 2026-11-01 00:55:12Z, instead of a new ticket.

**Seen again 2026-10-18 (Seat R 48th), with one layout detail this ticket does not yet record.** While raising KS-1626, anchoring's full suite read **370/371 at the untouched develop tip `5d1be7b06279`** — this exact test, `threadTokenMint.test.ts › parameterises mint + spend with a deterministic per-seed policyId`, `Could not serialize the data: Error: Unsupported type` at `applyParamsToScript` — and identically after the change (375/376).

**The new detail:** the install was a plain **root-workspace `npm ci`** at `Blockchain/Dev` (not `npm ci --workspaces=false`), in a fresh git worktree. That layout splits the copies the same way: `@lucid-evolution/plutus` **0.1.31** at the root and **0.1.33** nested under `services/anchoring/node_modules`; `utils` 0.1.68 / 0.1.70. From inside anchoring, Node resolves `@lucid-evolution/lucid` to the **root** copy and `plutus` / `utils` to the **nested** ones. So the phantom red also hits anyone who installs the monorepo the ordinary workspace way, not only the `--workspaces=false` variant measured here.

Not acted on — recorded so the next seat that sees 1 failure in anchoring does not mistake it for its own change.

## It reproduces again at develop `6ab9d5021e96` — the 2026-08-14 sweep note's own prediction has come true

That note closed with: *"A `npm install` that re-resolves `utils` to 0.1.70 in the root tree brings it straight back, and nothing prevents that."* Nothing did. Re-measured today from a fresh worktree at develop `6ab9d5021e96ea1481cb6c6ff2d6d33b414aecb7`, `npm ci --offline` from `Blockchain/Dev` (the hoisted workspace layout — the same layout the sweep note found GREEN).

**Deterministic, 2 of 2 runs, same cell, same throw. Not flaky.**

```
FAIL src/__tests__/threadTokenMint.test.ts > threadTokenMint emulator round-trip
     > parameterises mint + spend with a deterministic per-seed policyId
Error: Could not serialize the data: Error: Unsupported type
  at serialize            node_modules/@lucid-evolution/plutus/dist/index.js:272:13
  at Object.to            node_modules/@lucid-evolution/plutus/dist/index.js:276:61
  at applyParamsToScript  node_modules/@lucid-evolution/utils/dist/index.js:306:37
  at                      src/__tests__/threadTokenMint.test.ts:71:31
```

Whole-suite effect: `services/anchoring` reads **334 passed / 1 failed over 24 files** at develop, bare, before any edit — so no seat can currently report the anchoring suite as green.

## The duplicate is back in the INSTALLED tree, in a different shape from the one this ticket describes

The sweep note verified one hoisted copy each (`plutus 0.1.31`, `utils 0.1.68`). Today there are two of each — measured on disk, not read off a lock:

| package | `Blockchain/Dev/node_modules` | `Blockchain/Dev/services/anchoring/node_modules` |
|---|---|---|
| `@lucid-evolution/plutus` | 0.1.31 | **0.1.33** |
| `@lucid-evolution/utils` | 0.1.68 | **0.1.70** |
| `@lucid-evolution/core-types` | 0.1.24 | **0.2.1** |
| `@lucid-evolution/uplc` | 0.2.21 | **0.2.22** |

**The shape differs from the ticket's description in one way worth recording.** The ticket (and the sweep note) describe top-level `utils@0.1.70` carrying a *nested* `plutus@0.1.33`. What is installed today is the duplicate one level out: the root tree holds the 0.1.31/0.1.68 pair, and `services/anchoring/node_modules` holds the 0.1.33/0.1.70 pair beside it. Vitest runs with `services/anchoring` as its root, so that directory is the first one Node resolves from.

**This is the ROOT lock's own shape, not a bad install.** `Blockchain/Dev/package-lock.json` pins both sets explicitly — `node_modules/@lucid-evolution/{utils 0.1.68, plutus 0.1.31}` *and* `services/anchoring/node_modules/@lucid-evolution/{utils 0.1.70, plutus 0.1.33}` — and the installed versions match it exactly. So the condition is no longer only in anchoring's standalone lock, as the sweep note recorded; the hoisted workspace install now reproduces it too.

## What I did NOT establish

**I am not claiming which copy threw.** Both `plutus` copies carry `throw new Error("Could not serialize the data: …")` at line **272**, and both `utils` copies have the `parameters.reduce` at line **306**, so the stack trace's line numbers do not discriminate between them. The cross-copy `instanceof` mechanism this ticket already names remains the obvious candidate and is consistent with everything above — but it is a hypothesis here, not a measurement. Resolving it needs the module-identity check, not the trace.

## Nothing touched

Every `package.json` and lockfile is out of scope for this round's seats, so I changed none of them, and this ticket's own fix options (dedupe/pin `plutus`, align `utils` across both trees, or make the resolution layout-proof) are unchanged. Recording the evidence only.

The sweep note's instruction still stands and is now doubly earned: **do not close on a green run in one layout.**

*Measured by Seat L2 (security + anchoring lane), 2026-09-25, while building KS-1129. Found because the anchoring baseline for that ticket was red before any edit of mine.*

## Sweep note — **does not reproduce today, and I am not closing it on that alone**

Re-run on `develop` `454a64ebb`, this Mac, hoisted workspace layout — i.e. the layout the ticket says FAILS:

```
services/anchoring $ npx vitest run src/__tests__/threadTokenMint.test.ts
  Test Files  1 passed (1)
  Tests       1 passed (1)
```

## Why it passes — the duplicate is gone from the INSTALLED tree

The ticket's mechanism is two `@lucid-evolution/plutus` instances, so a `Constr` built by one fails the `instanceof` check in the other. Checked the actual installed layout rather than the lock:

```
@lucid-evolution/plutus : 0.1.31   (one copy, hoisted)
@lucid-evolution/utils  : 0.1.68   (one copy, hoisted)
```

**One `plutus`, so no cross-copy `instanceof` to fail.** The ticket's failing tree had top-level `plutus@0.1.31` against `utils@0.1.70` carrying its own nested `plutus@0.1.33`.

## Why it is NOT closed — the condition is still pinned where it ships

`services/anchoring/package-lock.json` — the lock the Dockerfile actually installs from — **still pins exactly the failing combination**:

```
node_modules/@lucid-evolution/utils               -> 0.1.70
node_modules/@lucid-evolution/utils/node_modules/@lucid-evolution/plutus -> 0.1.33
node_modules/@lucid-evolution/plutus              -> 0.1.31
```

So the duplicate has not been resolved; it has been **hoisted away locally**. A `npm install` that re-resolves `utils` to 0.1.70 in the root tree brings it straight back, and nothing prevents that.

## The more interesting finding

The hoisted tree runs **`utils@0.1.68`** while anchoring's own standalone lock ships **`0.1.70`**. Local dev and the built image are on different minors of a Cardano serialisation library. That is the [KS-531](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-531) class — the standalone locks diverging from the hoisted tree — showing up on a dependency that does on-chain script parameterisation, where a serialisation difference is not cosmetic.

## What it is waiting for

Pin one `@lucid-evolution/plutus` (an `overrides` entry, or align `utils` across both trees) so the duplicate cannot re-form, then re-run in both layouts. **Do not close on a green run in one layout** — that is what makes this ticket layout-dependent in the first place.

*Backlog sweep 2026-08-14.*

title: Move operational connector keys out of the application database (PS-473 §2)
description:
Split out of [PS-473](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-473/s-dr-harden-the-k-identity-tier-protect-the-organisationperson-guid), whose §1 (the identity ledger) shipped in [Secuura/platform-s#375](https://linear.app/secuura/review/ps-473-refuse-to-hand-platform-k-a-second-identity-for-the-same-tenant-c765108456d4). This half has a genuine design decision in it and should not ride along on a ticket that is otherwise done.

## The gap §1 does not close

The identity ledger protects the `Organisation.Id → OrganisationGuid` mapping — the *unrecoverable* thing. It does nothing for the connector keys themselves, which still live in `PlatformKOrganisation.EncryptedApiKey` in the application database.

The realistic incident is not total loss but a **point-in-time restore to before some Organisations were registered**. Those rows come back without keys, and K will not re-issue: re-registration returns the existing organisation and **no key** (verified against local K 2026-07-30), and rotation is platform-admin-only. Recovery is a per-Organisation admin action.

[PS-503](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-503/connector-key-decryption-can-silently-return-garbage-instead-of-trying) raised the stakes independently: `Rotate()` is `Encrypt(Decrypt(...))`, so anything that corrupts a decrypt writes the corruption back over the only copy. That specific hole is fixed, but it is a reminder that these keys have no second copy anywhere.

## Proposal (Stuart, 2026-07-30): AWS Secrets Manager

**What it fixes.** Decouples key durability from the database lifecycle, and adds versioning, a deletion recovery window, and cross-region replication. Fits the existing Terraform / S3-remote-state / prod-CMK setup ([PS-302](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-302/review-g1-aws-infrastructure-security-new-stacks-terraform-backup)).

**What it does not fix.** K's refusal to re-issue is unchanged. This lowers the probability of needing a rotation, not the blast radius when one is needed. [KS-480](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-480/sk-k-side-support-consistent-userorg-ownership-credential) §4/§5 still has to be settled.

## What it costs — the reason this is its own ticket

* **A distributed write we do not have today.** K returns the key exactly once, so the secret write must succeed **before** the row is marked `Provisioned`. Get that order wrong and a `Provisioned` row points at a secret that was never written — unrecoverable in precisely the same way, reached by a different route. Today this is one atomic DB write.
* **A provider seam is required.** Local and dev have no AWS. Needs `IPlatformKKeyStore` with database and Secrets Manager implementations, the same shape as `IDocumentStorageProvider`.
* **It lands on the anchor write path.** Needs the existing per-org cache plus a fallback, or an AWS blip stops anchoring — which today it cannot.
* **Granularity is a real choice, not a detail:**
  * *One secret per Organisation* — clean per-org IAM and rotation, bills per secret.
  * *One JSON secret keyed by org GUID* — cheaper, atomically updatable, but loses per-org access control and rewrites wholesale on every change.

## Verify

* Kill the secret store mid-registration: no row is left `Provisioned` without a retrievable key.
* With the key store unreachable, anchoring degrades to the fallback identity rather than failing.
* Restore the database to a point before an Organisation was registered: its key is still retrievable from the secret store and the org keeps working.
* Local and dev, with no AWS configured, keep using the database implementation with no config change.

## Acceptance

* **The granularity choice is made and reasoned**, not left open: one secret per Organisation (per-org IAM and rotation, bills per secret) or one JSON secret keyed by org GUID (cheaper, atomic, loses per-org access control). Whichever it is, the trade-off it accepts is written down.
* `IPlatformKKeyStore` exists with **two** implementations — database and Secrets Manager — selected by configuration, in the same shape as `IDocumentStorageProvider`. **Local and dev, with no AWS configured, keep using the database implementation with no config change**; that is the seam's whole point.
* **The write is ordered before the mark.** A row reaches `Provisioned` only after the secret write has succeeded. The failure mode this closes is explicit: a `Provisioned` row pointing at a secret that was never written is unrecoverable by exactly the same route the ticket exists to prevent.
* The anchor write path **degrades rather than stops**: with the key store unreachable, anchoring falls back (per-org cache, then the fallback identity) and does not fail. An AWS blip must not stop anchoring, which today it cannot.
* A point-in-time database restore to **before** an Organisation was registered leaves that organisation's key retrievable from the secret store, and the organisation keeps working — rehearsed on a slot, with the row counts before and after.
* Stated plainly in whatever closes this: K's refusal to re-issue is **unchanged**. This lowers the probability of needing a rotation, not the blast radius when one is needed; [KS-480](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-480/sk-k-side-support-consistent-userorg-ownership-credential) §4/§5 still has to be settled.
* No secret value is read, logged or printed at any point — the key is named (`CardanoAnchorSettings.PlatformKCredentialKey`, the new store's secret id scheme) and the rest is handed over.

**No new Playwright spec applies here.** The subject is server-side **write ordering** and a **storage-provider seam**: nothing changes in any view, route or control, so there is no journey a browser could drive that is not already driven. Reaching for Playwright would test the admin page plus five unrelated things and still not pin the ordering, which is the actual risk. The criteria belong in the xUnit suite, where they run in about two minutes with nothing up:

1. a **write-ordering test** — a key-store stub that throws on write, asserting no `PlatformKOrganisation` row is left at `Provisioned`, and that the failure is surfaced rather than swallowed;
2. a **provider-selection test** pinning the database implementation when no AWS configuration is present, so a local stack cannot silently acquire an AWS dependency;
3. a **degradation test** — an unreachable store resolves through the cache, then the fallback identity, and the anchor still completes.

**The control is Playwright, and it needs no new file:** `systemTest/tests/functional/admin_connector_keys.spec.ts` already drives the Administrator connector-key surface and must stay green **unchanged** through this work — if the seam alters what that page shows or does, the change has leaked past its own boundary. `systemTest/tests/k_live/verb_matrix.spec.ts` against K slot N is the second control: anchoring still works end to end, with K actually up (a 14-skip `@k-live` stand-down does not count).

## Prerequisite

Not blocked, but worth doing after the current develop backlog reaches UAT — this touches the anchor write path, and validating it against a UAT that is 30 commits stale would prove little.

title: M365-6: remaining hosts — Excel, PowerPoint (and what "Microsoft family" excludes)
description:
Once one document host is proven (M365-4), the rest should be mostly configuration rather than new engineering — **if** the M365-3 split held.

## Scope

* **Excel** and **PowerPoint** taskpanes on the shared core, reusing the M365-4 panel if M365-1 concluded that one "document" panel serves them all.
* Per-host manifest entries (or host list in the unified manifest, per M365-2).
* Sideload verification per host, on web and desktop.

## Treat this as the test of the refactor

If adding Excel takes more than configuration and a small adapter, **M365-3 didn't go far enough** — raise that rather than working around it here. That's the signal worth watching.

## What "Microsoft family" does NOT mean here

Worth being explicit, because the phrase is broader than the work:

* **Teams** — a different extensibility model (bots, tabs, message extensions), not an Office add-in. Real, but a separate project.
* **SharePoint / OneDrive** — file-level integration would be Graph API work, not a taskpane. Arguably a better fit for automatic registration of documents at rest, and worth its own ticket if wanted.
* **Office on iOS / Android** — add-in support is narrower than desktop/web; check per host before promising it.
* **Outlook desktop (classic Win32)** — already in scope for the existing add-in, but its Word-based HTML rendering is the reason the email banner needed table markup. Any new HTML output faces the same constraint.

None of the above is planned by this project. Listed so the scope isn't assumed wider than it is.

title: M365-5: rename the API surface off /api/outlook once a second host uses it
description:
**Deliberately deferred, not forgotten.**

The moment Word calls `POST /api/outlook/verify`, the route name is a lie. Same for `OutlookApiController`, `OutlookSettings`, `AppSpecific:Outlook:*` and the `Outlook-Share` label.

## Why not do it in M365-4

Renaming a live API while simultaneously standing up a new host mixes two failure modes — a Word bug and a broken Outlook panel would be indistinguishable. Ship the second host on the existing paths, confirm it works, then rename as its own reversible change.

## Scope when it happens

* `/api/outlook/*` → something host-neutral (`/api/addin/*` or `/api/office/*`), with the **old paths kept as aliases** for at least one release so a stale sideloaded manifest doesn't break.
* `OutlookApiController` → matching name; `OutlookSettings` / `AppSpecific:Outlook` → same, with config keys **read from both** during the transition or a deploy will silently disable the feature.
* `SendDocsLinks.Label = "Outlook-Share"` — this one is **data, not code.** Existing rows carry that literal, and the admin/Dashboard/My-documents chips render it verbatim. Changing it needs either a migration or per-host labels with the old value still recognised. Probably the fiddliest part.

## Worth weighing

Doing nothing is defensible too. The names are internal, the cost of churn is real, and "outlook" as a legacy path prefix is a common and harmless outcome. Decide explicitly rather than by drift.

title: M365-4: first document host — verify and upload the open file (Word)
description:
Build **one** host properly rather than three shallowly. Word assumed as the first — M365-1 may choose Excel instead, in which case this ticket applies unchanged to that host.

## Scope (assuming M365-1 lands on verify + upload)

* **Verify the open document.** Read the file via `Office.context.document.getFileAsync(Office.FileType.Compressed)`, hash it client-side with the existing `utils/hashing.ts`, and call `POST /api/outlook/verify` — unchanged, and still hash-only, so **the document never leaves the client**.
* **Upload the open document.** Same file read, then `POST /api/outlook/documents/upload`. Honours the existing `Outlook:UploadEnabled` flag and the `documentUpload` capability with no server change.
* Sign-in via the existing Dialog bridge and the shared session store from M365-3.

## Known traps

* `getFileAsync` **returns the file in slices.** It has to be reassembled before hashing, and there is a size ceiling. This is the main new mechanic and the likeliest source of bugs.
* **The saved file is not what's on screen.** Unsaved edits are not in the bytes Office hands over, so a verify can legitimately fail on a document the user believes is fine. The panel has to say so plainly rather than report "not verified".
* **Not every host has a document to read** — a brand-new unsaved file needs a sensible empty state.
* The verification-state colouring from the Outlook panel (green registered / red otherwise) should carry over, but "registered" means the same thing and reuses the same `Registration` field.

## Naming

`/api/outlook/*` becomes a misnomer the moment a second host calls it — see M365-5. Do not rename as part of this ticket; just be aware the paths are shared.

## Verification

Sideload in Word on **web and desktop** (they differ). At minimum: verify a registered document, verify an unregistered one, upload a new one, and confirm the "unsaved edits" case reads honestly.

title: M365-3: split the add-in into a host-agnostic core and an Outlook host adapter
description:
Refactor with **no behaviour change**, so a second host can be added without forking the codebase. Can start before the M365-1 decision — the split is right regardless of which features are chosen.

## The coupling is already almost isolated

Measured on `develop`:

| File | Outlook-specific references |
| -- | -- |
| `src/utils/office.ts` | **26** |
| `src/utils/api.ts` | 0 |
| `src/utils/share.ts` | 0 |
| `src/utils/session.ts` | 0 |

That is the whole problem in one file. `api.ts`, `share.ts` and `session.ts` are already portable — the auth/session store, the API client, the HTML builders and the escaping all work in any host.

## What to do

* Move the portable modules into a `core/` (or shared package) with no `Office.*` mailbox usage.
* Define a **host adapter interface** for what genuinely differs — read a target audience, write output somewhere, attach a file, identify the current document — and make the existing `office.ts` the Outlook implementation of it.
* Leave `AttachPanel` where it is; it is the Outlook *panel*, not the shared core.
* Keep `Office.context.ui.displayDialogAsync` in the core: it is common to every host, so the sign-in bridge is shared, not adapted.

## Constraints

* **Zero behaviour change.** The Outlook panel must work identically afterwards; the 48 frontend tests are the safety net and must stay green without being rewritten to fit the refactor.
* Watch `getSenderEmail()` — it reads `Office.context.mailbox.userProfile`, which does not exist outside Outlook. It belongs behind the adapter, and its *callers* need to cope with a host that has no "sender".

## Why now

Doing this before the first Word build is what stops a second panel copy-pasting `office.ts` and quietly diverging — which is how two-host add-ins usually rot.

title: M365-2: manifest strategy — unified JSON manifest vs a second XML manifest
description:
**This is the actual blocker to running anywhere but Outlook.**

## Why the current manifest can't be extended

`outlook-addin/manifest.xml` is:

```xml
<OfficeApp ... xsi:type="MailApp">
  <Hosts>
    <Host Name="Mailbox" />
```

In the classic XML manifest `xsi:type` is **exclusive**. A `MailApp` cannot also declare Word or Excel — those are `TaskPaneApp` with `Document` / `Workbook` hosts. There is no attribute to add; the schema does not allow one manifest to be both.

## The two routes

**A — a second XML manifest** for the document hosts, shipped alongside the Outlook one.

* Lower risk, nothing about Outlook changes
* Two manifests to build, version, distribute and (if published) certify — `build-manifest.sh` and the per-environment `manifest.dist.xml` flow both fork
* Users install "Secuura for Outlook" and "Secuura for Word" as separate add-ins

**B — the unified JSON manifest for Microsoft 365**, one package targeting Outlook + Word + Excel + PowerPoint.

* One install, one listing, one identity — much better product story
* Replaces the Outlook manifest, so it is a change to a shipping surface, not an addition
* Needs verification of current support for each host and each platform we care about (web / Windows / Mac), and of how it interacts with sideloading and with AppSource

## What to produce

1. Confirm — **against current Microsoft docs, not memory** — which hosts and platforms the unified manifest supports today, and whether Outlook add-in features we rely on (the Dialog API bridge, taskpane, commands) are fully covered.
2. A recommendation with the migration cost of B stated honestly, including what happens to existing sideloaded installs.
3. Whether AppSource publication (see [PS-436](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-436/outlook-add-in-offer-an-install-the-add-in-link-on-shares-and)) pushes the decision either way.

## Related

`build-manifest.sh` currently emits a per-environment `manifest.dist.xml` (gitignored). Whichever route is chosen, that tooling needs to handle more than one target.

title: M365-1: decide the feature set per host — "share" does not exist in Word
description:
**Do this before any code.** Everything else in the project depends on the answer.

## The problem

The Outlook panel does two things: mint **per-recipient tracked links**, and **attach a file** to the message. Neither has an equivalent in Word, Excel or PowerPoint — there is no recipient and no message body.

So "port the add-in to Word" is not a meaningful instruction. The question is which Secuura capability belongs in a document editor.

## Candidates, with a view on each

| Feature | Fit | Reuses |
| -- | -- | -- |
| **Verify the open document** | **Strong.** The natural document-editor question is "is this file authentic?" | `POST /api/outlook/verify`, unchanged |
| **Upload the open document to Secuura** | **Good.** One click from "I've finished this" to "it's registered." | `POST /api/outlook/documents/upload`, unchanged |
| **Insert a share link at the cursor** | **Plausible, more work.** Needs a recipient picked in-panel, since there is no To/Cc to read | `POST /api/outlook/share` + new recipient UI |
| **Show provenance / lineage for the open file** | Interesting, needs a public per-document view that does not exist yet | — |

Verify + upload are the pair I'd argue for first: both reuse endpoints as they stand, and neither needs a recipient concept.

## Also to decide

* **Which hosts, in what order.** Word and Excel are not equally valuable — pick one to build properly first.
* **Does the panel need to differ per host at all,** or is one "document" panel enough for Word/Excel/PowerPoint?
* **Is this AppSource-bound?** It changes the manifest decision in M365-2 and interacts with [PS-436](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-436/outlook-add-in-offer-an-install-the-add-in-link-on-shares-and) (the install link, still blocked on there being no published add-in).

## Output

A short written decision on this ticket: features, host order, and whether one panel serves all document hosts. M365-2 and M365-4 are blocked until it exists.

title: Outlook add-in: single shared link mode (recipients can currently see each other's tokens)
description:
**Follow-up to** [PS-424](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-424/outlook-add-in-multi-select-share-upload-and-send-mode-outlook-share), from a trade-off flagged and deliberately accepted during that work.

## The problem

An email has **one body**, but the compose panel's tracked-link mode mints **one link per recipient**. All of those links land in that single shared body, so:

* Bob can open Alice's link.
* `FirstOpenedAt` on Alice's link may actually be Bob.
* Revoking Bob's link doesn't stop him — he still has Alice's.
* The recipient list is disclosed to everyone, even for a message composed with Bcc.

Fine for a single trust group. **An information-disclosure defect otherwise** — e.g. a payslip to an employee, Cc'd to HR.

## What ships today ([PS-424](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-424/outlook-add-in-multi-select-share-upload-and-send-mode-outlook-share))

Per-recipient links are kept, because they produce the correct **audit records** — one `SendDocsLinks` row per recipient, each independently revocable. The panel groups them by recipient in the body and states the trade-off explicitly:

> Each recipient gets their own tracked link, valid for 7 days with view and download access. Because an email has a single body, all recipients can see each other's links.

Disclosure is the interim mitigation. It is not a fix.

## Proposed

Offer a **single shared link per document** for the whole message as an alternative mode:

* one `SendDocsLinks` row per document, not per (document, recipient) pair
* no per-recipient attribution in the access log — that is the explicit cost, and the UI must say so
* revocation becomes all-or-nothing per document, which is the behaviour a user probably expects from "one link in one email"

Open question for product: which should be the **default**? Per-recipient gives better audit; shared gives correct confidentiality when recipients shouldn't see each other. Arguably the choice should follow whether the message has more than one recipient.

## Where it lands

`ShareLinkService.CreateAsync` already takes `Recipients` and fans out N×M — the natural seam is a mode flag on `ShareLinkRequest`. `buildShareHtml` (`outlook-addin/src/utils/share.ts`) already groups by recipient and would collapse to a flat list. Both are covered by existing tests.

## Acceptance

* **The default is decided and recorded** before code lands — per-recipient (better audit) or shared (correct confidentiality), or chosen by recipient count. The open question above is the blocker, not the implementation.
* `ShareLinkRequest` carries a **mode flag**; in shared mode `ShareLinkService.CreateAsync` creates **one** `SendDocsLinks` row per document for the whole message, not N×M, and the token in the body is the same for every recipient.
* **Revocation matches the mode**: revoking in shared mode cuts access for everyone on that document; in per-recipient mode it still cuts exactly one recipient and leaves the others working.
* **The cost is stated in the UI, in both directions** — shared mode says the access log cannot attribute an open to a person; per-recipient mode keeps today's [PS-424](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-424/outlook-add-in-multi-select-share-upload-and-send-mode-outlook-share) disclosure sentence about recipients seeing each other's links.
* `buildShareHtml` collapses to a **flat list** in shared mode (no per-recipient grouping), so a Bcc'd message does not disclose the recipient list.
* The access log and lineage are **coherent** with whichever mode was used — no per-recipient rows in shared mode, and `FirstOpenedAt` means what the mode says it means.

**Playwright test that demonstrates the fix** (required, for the S-side half — which is where the disclosure actually bites): extend `systemTest/tests/functional/outlook_backend.spec.ts`, which already exercises the add-in's S endpoints without needing Outlook, and assert:

1. a share request in **shared** mode for one document and **three** recipients creates **one** `SendDocsLinks` row — the Manage shares grid (`sharelinks-table`) lists a single row for that document, and the response carries one token. **Fails on today's** `develop`, which fans out to three rows and three tokens by design ([PS-424](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-424/outlook-add-in-multi-select-share-upload-and-send-mode-outlook-share));
2. **revocation is all-or-nothing** in shared mode: revoking that one row makes the token return the Permission Denied path for a session-less fetch, and there is no second token still live — which is the defect's sharpest consequence today, where revoking Bob leaves him Alice's link working. Assert that specific case **in per-recipient mode too**, as the control: Bob's revoked token must fail while Alice's still resolves;
3. a request in **per-recipient** mode is unchanged — three rows, three independently revocable tokens — so the new mode is additive and the audit path [PS-424](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-424/outlook-add-in-multi-select-share-upload-and-send-mode-outlook-share) chose deliberately is intact;
4. the **mode actually used** is visible to the user: Manage shares distinguishes a shared-link row from per-recipient rows (today every Outlook row reads "Outlook-Share"), so someone auditing later can tell which guarantee applied.

**Control assertions that pass today and must keep passing:** per-recipient mode's audit behaviour in full — one row per recipient, each revocable alone, `FirstOpenedAt` recorded per row; a live token still returns 200 for a session-less recipient; and the [PS-424](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-424/outlook-add-in-multi-select-share-upload-and-send-mode-outlook-share) disclosure sentence still appears whenever per-recipient mode is used. A green run must not be reachable by replacing per-recipient mode rather than adding a second one.

**Two parts are not Playwright's**, and both matter here:

* **The body-building half is the add-in's own test estate.** `buildShareHtml` runs in Outlook, which the platform-s suite cannot drive (see [PS-925](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-925/outlook-on-outlook-on-the-web-every-share-now-attach-after-the-first) for why). Extend `outlook-addin/src/utils/share.test.ts` — it already covers the grouped output — with shared-mode cases asserting a **flat** list, **one** link, and **no recipient addresses in the body at all** (the Bcc case, which is the information-disclosure point and is red today).
* **The fan-out rule belongs in xUnit.** "How many rows does a request for M documents × N recipients create, and what does revoking one do" is a rule, not a surface: pin `ShareLinkService.CreateAsync` in `tests/ssd.UnitTests` across both modes and the 1×1 / 1×N / M×N matrix. It runs in two minutes with nothing up, and it is what the Playwright spec should be able to assume rather than re-derive.

nodes.body:
## Reviewed 2026-09-09 while clearing the Outlook backlog — deliberately NOT implemented in that pass

The rest of the backlog (PS-805, PS-575, PS-576) went onto `project/outlook-backlog`. This one stayed off it, for two reasons that turned into one.

**The data model does not have a place for a shared link.** `SendDocsLinks.Email` is `[Required]` (`ssd/Models/SendDocsLinks.cs:13`), and it is not decorative: it drives the *Shared with me* inbox (matched by recipient email), the `IX_SendDocsLinks_Email_Expiry` index, and the access-log attribution. A one-link-per-document share has no single recipient to put there. Every option is a design decision, not a mode flag:

- **nullable `Email`** — a migration, plus every reader of `Email` learning what null means (the inbox stops seeing these shares entirely)
- **a sentinel address** — lies to the inbox and the access log, and any self-share / issuer-org check that reads it
- **a recipient list per link** — a new table, and the revocation model changes with it

**And the product default was already flagged open on this ticket.** Per-recipient gives the audit trail; shared gives correct confidentiality when recipients must not see each other. Picking one silently — in a batch of unrelated fixes — is exactly the kind of choice that should have a name on it.

So: the seam is still where the ticket says (`ShareLinkRequest`, `buildShareHtml`), the interim mitigation (grouped links + the explicit disclosure line) is unchanged, and this needs a decision on both points before it is code. Two questions, one answer each, and it becomes a small ticket.

title: KMS: move platform wallet mnemonic to Key Vault (KS-326 follow-up)
description:
**Follow-up carved out of** [KS-326](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-326/phase-0-crypto-agility-foundation-kms)**.** [KS-326](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-326/phase-0-crypto-agility-foundation-kms) (Phase 0 — crypto-agility + KMS) was closed as Done, but only the **JWT signing key** half of its KMS item actually shipped (PR #361/#362 — JWT private key now loads from Azure Key Vault with an env fallback). The **platform wallet mnemonic** was left behind and is still loaded from an env var.

**Current state (verified in code):**

* `PLATFORM_WALLET_MNEMONIC` is read from `process.env` in `services/anchoring` (e.g. `services/anchoring/src/index.ts:850`), then passed to `initWallet(mnemonic, network)` in `services/anchoring/src/cardano/wallet.ts` to derive the BIP-39 → BIP-32 → Ed25519 signing key.
* The JWT-key KMS plumbing already exists to reuse: `packages/shared/src/vault/key-vault.ts` (Key Vault `getSecret` with env fallback).

**Ask:**

- [ ] Load `PLATFORM_WALLET_MNEMONIC` from Azure Key Vault via the existing `key-vault.ts` helper, with an always-on env fallback (mirror the JWT-key pattern, so local/dev with no Key Vault still works).
- [ ] Support rotation (versioned secret) — note a mnemonic rotation also rotates the derived wallet address, so document the operational impact.
- [ ] Keep behaviour-preserving defaults: no Key Vault configured → falls back to `PLATFORM_WALLET_MNEMONIC` env, identical to today.

**Why it matters:** the mnemonic is the platform wallet's root secret; leaving it in env is a wider blast radius than the JWT key that already moved. Not urgent (env is the current accepted posture), but it closes the gap [KS-326](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-326/phase-0-crypto-agility-foundation-kms) implied was done.

**Refs:** [KS-326](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-326/phase-0-crypto-agility-foundation-kms) (parent, closed), PR #361/#362 (JWT-key KMS pattern to follow), `docs/security/POST-QUANTUM-CRYPTO-MIGRATION-PLAN.md` §5 Phase 0 / §7.

---

## Summary

`systemTest/playwright/` covers **8 of 310** published API operations (2.6 %) and issues **no writes at all** — so no complete business flow exists anywhere in the suite. This ticket takes Playwright to full coverage of the published contract, driven by the documented product flows, reusing the personas the platform already seeds.

## Current state (measured 2026-07-24 — see R1–R3 for today)

|  |  |
| -- | -- |
| Published contract | `Blockchain/Dev/docs/openapi/secuura-api.yaml` — 278 paths / **310 operations** / 42 tags |
| Playwright today | 3 clients, 3 spec files, 11 tests, **8 operations** |
| Writes today | **zero** — read-only plus two unauthenticated 401/403 checks |
| Zero-coverage domains | Billing 21, M365 22, Governance 18, NFT 18, KYC 16, GDPR 15, Analytics 12, Staking 12, VC/VP/StatusList/DID 24, Webhooks 7, Tenants 6, Timestamps 6, API Keys 4, Sessions 2 |

Covered today: `POST /auth/login`, `POST /auth/refresh`, `GET /users/me`, `GET /documents`, `GET /documents/{id}`, `POST /verification/verify`, plus unauth-only checks on `POST /documents/{id}/verify` and `POST /notifications`.

> **Design verified against the Playwright docs for the pinned** `@playwright/test` **1.61.1** (2026-07-24). *Pin is now 1.64.1 — re-check per R6.* Every design decision cites its source in **Playwright references** at the end.

## Implementation principle — use Playwright's own primitives

**Never implement something ourselves if Playwright already provides it.** Anything the framework ships — polling, stepping, retries, parallelism, artifact attachment, context isolation — is used as-is. Our code exists only to express *Secuura's* domain (personas, flows, coverage classes) or to fill a capability the framework genuinely does not have. A hand-rolled equivalent of a framework feature is a review rejection.

| Need | Mechanism | Ours or Playwright's? |
| -- | -- | -- |
| Wait for an async outcome | `expect.poll` (`{ timeout, intervals, message }`) | **Playwright's.** `helpers/settle.ts` is a thin wrapper supplying the project deadlines **\[ref 8\]** |
| Ordered, named stages in a flow | `test.step()` | **Playwright's** |
| Per-persona session isolation | `playwright.request.newContext()` | **Playwright's** **\[ref 2\]** |
| Persist an artifact + surface it in the report | `testInfo.outputPath()` + `testInfo.attach({ path })` | **Playwright's** **\[ref 6\]** |
| Parallelism, retries, sharding, reporters, tagging | runner config | **Playwright's** |
| Setup/teardown lifecycle | fixtures with `use()` | **Playwright's** **\[ref 7\]** |
| **Capturing API exchanges as a durable artefact** | `helpers/exchangeRecorder.ts` | **Ours — the framework has no equivalent** (upstream request closed unimplemented, **\[ref 5\]**). Built *on* `testInfo.attach`/`outputPath` |
| CSRF double-submit echo | `helpers/csrf.ts` | **Ours** — application-protocol concern |
| Coverage classification vs the OpenAPI spec | `coverage/*` | **Ours** — Secuura-domain concern |
| Persona catalogue, flow definitions | `config/`, `helpers/flow.ts`, specs | **Ours** — Secuura-domain concern |

## Stack isolation — Playwright runs on its own Docker instance

* ~~**CI**~~ *(moot — GitHub Actions retired 2026-08-27, see R4/R5)* — the `playwright` job in `.github/workflows/pr-platform-suites.yml` boots via `boot-platform-stack` with `stack_prefix: pr-playwright`, gateway **6982**, postgres 6532, redis 6479, pgbouncer 6533; pointed at by `API_BASE_URL: http://localhost:6982/api`. Distinct `COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME` / `STACK_PREFIX` → separate containers, volumes, networks. Siblings sit on 6882 / 7082 / 7182.
* **Local** — the suite does not start or stop a server (`playwright.config.ts`); it attaches to whatever `API_BASE_URL` points at. Use its own instance for destructive flows (F14 erasure, F5 revoke).

Any environment posture we choose applies to Playwright alone. The only shared thing is the composite action's *source file*.

## Scope boundary

Playwright asserts **business outcomes of documented flows**. It does not re-test what the sibling suites own — see `Projects Documents/API_Security_Functional_Testing_Architecture_Flow_Diagrams.html` §2–3 and the Coverage & Scenario Matrix in `QA_Tool_Cheat_Sheet_Secuura_API_Testing.html`.

| Excluded from Playwright | Owner |
| -- | -- |
| Boundary values, negative **data**, fuzzing | Schemathesis |
| Status/header compliance, undeclared verbs, redirects, rate-limit headers, 429 | Schemathesis |
| RBAC matrices, cross-tenant, IDOR/BOLA | Schemathesis (+ Akto) |
| Unauthenticated 401/403 sweeps | Schemathesis + the [KS-380](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-380/harden-the-pre-release-gate-required-checks-on-develop-preflight) preflight |
| OWASP API Top 10, injection, SSRF, BFLA | Akto |
| Throughput, latency, saturation | Performance (k6) |
| Real Cardano chain integrity / anchor-vs-chain | anchoring Integration suite ([KS-489](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-489/review-d-blockchain-anchoring-smart-contract-integrity)-D) — see Risk 3 |

**A distinction that matters, because it looks like the excluded category but is not:** a *documented business outcome that is not success* — a verification returning **Expired**, a tampered document returning **Failed**, a certifier **Rejecting** a request — is in scope. Those are product states the stakeholder guides describe, reached with valid inputs. What is excluded is malformed **data** (missing fields, oversize values, type confusion). F6 and F7 exist precisely to cover the former.

Consistent with Playwright's Best Practices — *"Only test what you control."* — which is why provider-gated paths (Stripe, M365) record a by-design 503 rather than reaching for the third party. **\[ref 1\]**

**Two existing specs are duplicates and are retired in Phase 0**: `notifications.spec.ts` (both tests assert unauth → 401/403, already swept for every bearer op by the [KS-380](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-380/harden-the-pre-release-gate-required-checks-on-develop-preflight) preflight) and the invalid-credentials / missing-email cases in `login.spec.ts` (negative data, owned by Schemathesis `test_authentication.py`).

## Persona policy

**Use the existing** `default`**-tenant personas first.** The seeder (`services/auth/src/repositories/userRepo.ts` → `demoAccounts`) provides 17 accounts across 7 tenants. ## ⚠ Two platform capabilities we do not have — needed by F6 and F13

Two flows assert a documented product state that **cannot currently be reached on demand**. Neither blocks Phase 0, but both block their own flow's plan from being finalised. Raised with @kamil.kreiser and @stuart.jamieson in the comments — **and probed ourselves first** (see Risk mitigation), because the capability may already exist.

| Need | Flow | Why it is needed | What "available" looks like |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| **Induce an expired certification** | **F6** | The Verifier guide documents **Expired** as one of five verification result states. Verifying it requires a certification that is *already* past its expiry. If expiry is purely wall-clock with no way to set a past date, F6's expired leg is unreachable and the state stays permanently untested | Either an issuance parameter accepting a past `expiresAt` (non-prod only), or a supported way to age an existing certification. A test must be able to produce one deterministically, in-run, without clock manipulation on the host |
| **Raise a system error on demand** | **F13** | F13's only real journey is *error → resolve*. Asserting it requires a system error to exist first. Provoking one by genuinely breaking a service is not acceptable in a shared or CI stack | A non-prod-only way to emit a synthetic entry into the system-errors surface with a known signature, so the test can find it, resolve it, and assert it reflects as resolved |

**If either already exists**, this is a documentation gap rather than a build ask. **If neither is feasible**, the affected leg is recorded as a documented coverage gap rather than quietly dropped: F6 keeps its tampered + not-found legs, F13 falls back to `positive-path` for the whole read surface.

### Acceptance criterion per flow

Each flow is accepted on **one stated business outcome**, not a set of status codes. These are what the child plans must satisfy.

* **F1** — a token issued at login authenticates `GET /users/me` as the expected persona for all five accounts; a refreshed token works, and the pre-logout token stops working.
* **F2** — a document type created by admin is returned by the subsequent list, and each of the three new personas can log in at its intended role.
* **F3** — a document created by `issuer@secuura.com` is retrievable by id and its certification appears in the certification list. **The anchor leg is blocked on D1.**
* **F4** — verifying the spine document's content hash returns `verified: true` and identifies the issuing party.
* **F5** — after revoke, the same verify call that previously returned verified now reports **revoked**, and the status list reflects it.
* **F6** — a **tampered** payload verifies as failed, and an unknown hash returns `verified: false` without an error. The **expired** leg — an expired certification verifying as expired, not as valid or missing — requires the capability gap above to be closed; until then it is a documented gap, not a silent omission.
* **F7** — a rejected certification request ends in a rejected state, the requester can see the rejection, and the document is **not** certified.
* **F8** — a document certified with `x-api-key` (no bearer, no cookies) is retrievable and verifies identically to one certified by a browser persona. Proves the partner path end-to-end.
* **F9** — custody transfers from `demo@secuura.io` to `holder@secuura.com`: the recipient is notified (`expect.poll` **— delivery is async**), and the prior owner can no longer mutate the document.
* **F10** — a registered webhook's test delivery appears in its delivery list (`expect.poll` **— delivery is async**); rotating the secret changes the signing secret without dropping the registration.
* **F11** — a credential issued for a document verifies as a presentation and its DID resolves — **or** the by-design 503 on `POST /api/credentials` is the recorded outcome.
* **F12** — an async export reaches a downloadable state within `EXPORT_SETTLE_TIMEOUT` and the downloaded artefact contains the requesting tenant's data.
* **F13** — the audit trail contains the lifecycle events of a document **this flow created itself**. The *error → resolve* journey requires the capability gap above; until then the whole read surface is asserted as `positive-path` and **declared as such**.
* **F14** — the subject's export contains their record; after erasure the same export no longer returns personal data and the deletion log records the event.
* **F15** — a KYC session initiated at verification level `NONE` reaches a terminal reviewed state and the subject's verification level changes.
* **F16** — a wallet challenge is issued and the account reflects the linked wallet address. **Stops short of asserting signature validity** — `POST /api/wallets/verify` returns `verified:true` for any signature and is an open Known Failure ([KS-488](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-488/review-c-sk-channel-paymentswebhooks-and-integrations-m365-kyc-wallet)-C).
* **F17** — an authorised app receives a token that can call an in-scope operation, and revoking the grant stops it working.
* **F18** — a connector reaches a connected state and a sync lists at least one document — **or** the by-design 503 is the recorded outcome.
* **F19** — a customer's purchase appears in their purchase list and their credit balance reflects it — **or** the by-design 503 is the recorded outcome.
* **F20** — a proposal created by `demo@secuura.io` receives a vote from `holder@secuura.com` and reaches a terminal state — **or** the documented precondition refusal ([KS-478](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-478/ks-466-11-state-machineprecondition-400s-resolve-via-ks-188-stateful)) is recorded.
* **F21** — a stake is recorded and the resulting reward balance reflects it — **or** the documented precondition refusal is recorded.
* **F22** — a referral code applied by a second user is attributed to the referrer and moves a milestone — **or** the documented precondition refusal is recorded.
* **F23** — a minted NFT certificate is retrievable and its asset verifies — **or** the chain/IPFS-dependent outcome is recorded as such.
