title: Harvest OpenAPI example values from the platform-s test suite (KS-256 tier-1)
description:
## Why this is a separate ticket

[KS-256](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-256/add-openapi-inline-examples-to-all-329-operations-eliminate-coverage) adds realistic examples to the Secuura OpenAPI spec by harvesting real request/response values from test traffic. It defines **two harvest tiers**:

* **tier-2** `platform-k` — the Distributed_Secuura suites. **In scope for** [KS-256](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-256/add-openapi-inline-examples-to-all-329-operations-eliminate-coverage).
* **tier-1** `platform-s` — traffic reaching the platform-k API *through* platform-s. **Deferred here.**

Peter's call, 2026-07-20: [KS-256](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-256/add-openapi-inline-examples-to-all-329-operations-eliminate-coverage) is interested in platform-k alone. `config.tiers` now defaults to `['platform-k']`, which also resolves a discrepancy @kamil.kreiser raised — his 2026-07-16 sign-off said *"platform-s tier default off — correct"*, but the code had it on.

**This ticket is the deferred half.** It is not blocking [KS-256](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-256/add-openapi-inline-examples-to-all-329-operations-eliminate-coverage).

## The machinery already exists — nothing needs building

The harness in `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/openapi-examples/` (Distributed_Secuura) already supports this tier end to end. It was **run successfully against platform-s on 2026-07-17** and captured 11 endpoint templates. Retained deliberately rather than deleted.

To run it:

```bash
cd Blockchain/Dev
HARVEST_EXAMPLES=1 PLATFORM_S_SYSTEMTEST=/path/to/platform-s/systemTest \
  npx tsx scripts/openapi-examples/orchestrate.ts --dry-run --only-platform-s
```

Drop `--dry-run` to execute. The harness README documents it in full.

## What was learned on the 07-17 run — read before starting

**1. The yield is small, and it is structural rather than an effort problem.** platform-s reaches the platform-k API through only \~3 clients (\~8 endpoints). Both tiers combined reached **\~13 of 310 operations (\~4%)**. Three "levers" were applied to widen it and it did not move materially. Set expectations accordingly: this is a quality improvement on a handful of endpoints, not a coverage strategy.

**2. Three levers were needed to capture anything useful:**

* **Lever 1** — bring the capture proxy up *before* platform-s starts, so its login flows through the monitor.
* **Lever 2** — `"UsePerVerbEndpoints": true` in `ssd/dep-ssd-local/Docker.appsettings.Development.json`. **Must be reverted afterwards.** Use `/bin/cp -f`; bare `cp` is interactive on this setup and silently no-ops. Verify the revert with `diff`, not a container `cat`/`grep` — that image has neither binary, so the check returns a false negative.
* **Lever 3** — platform-s's own `dock_run --reset` for a clean state. This resets **platform-s's own** `mysql-data`/`dpkeys` only.

**3. Read the config that is actually MOUNTED, not the one that looks right.** A whole analysis pass was wasted concluding the capture would find nothing, based on `ssd/Docker.appsettings.Development.json`. The running container mounts `ssd/dep-ssd-local/Docker.appsettings.Development.json`. Check with `docker inspect`.

## Hard constraints (from [KS-256](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-256/add-openapi-inline-examples-to-all-329-operations-eliminate-coverage), non-negotiable)

* **15 minutes between harvest passes** — the API rate limiter is in-memory; restart `api-gateway` before each pass to zero it.
* **Pin** `-p distributed_secuura` on every compose call, or compose creates duplicate containers.
* **Restore** `:6882` after teardown, from the repo-root `docker-compose.local.yml` — otherwise the gateway stays up with no published port and the API goes dark.
* **Never run** `wipe_platform_k_users.sh` — it deletes Distributed_Secuura's Postgres rows. Explicitly ruled out.
* **PII**: redaction happens in memory before anything is written (R15b) — no raw capture ever reaches disk. Any harvested value still needs **human triage** before it can be published. Real values live in a JSON store **outside** the repository; `check-no-pii-store.sh` fails the build if one is ever tracked.

## Definition of done

- [ ] platform-s harvest pass run, captures flushed
- [ ] Triage the fields it surfaces — MASK or ALLOW into `traffic-fields.ts`
- [ ] Confirm the platform-s config lever is reverted (`diff`-verified)
- [ ] Report the coverage delta: how many additional operations/schemas got a real value
- [ ] Decide whether the yield justifies keeping this tier at all, or whether the machinery should be retired

## Acceptance

* The coverage delta is reported as a **figure, not an adjective**: how many of the \~310 operations and how many schemas gained a real harvested value, against the \~13 (\~4%) both tiers reached on 2026-07-17. The 07-17 run is the baseline and is quoted as such.
* Every field the pass surfaces is triaged **MASK or ALLOW** in `traffic-fields.ts` — no field left undecided. `check-no-pii-store.sh` is green and no PII store is tracked; the real values stay in the JSON store outside the repository, and nothing harvested is published without the human triage step.
* The `UsePerVerbEndpoints` lever is **reverted and proven reverted** by a `diff` on the **host** against `ssd/dep-ssd-local/Docker.appsettings.Development.json` — not by a container `cat`/`grep`, which returns a false negative because that image has neither binary. Use `/bin/cp -f`; a bare `cp` is interactive on this machine and silently no-ops.
* The config read is the **mounted** one, confirmed with `docker inspect` — `ssd/dep-ssd-local/Docker.appsettings.Development.json`, not `ssd/Docker.appsettings.Development.json`. A whole analysis pass was lost to that once.
* Teardown leaves the environment as found: `:6882` restored from the repo-root `docker-compose.local.yml`, the gateway reachable, every compose call pinned `-p distributed_secuura`, 15 minutes between passes with `api-gateway` restarted before each, and `wipe_platform_k_users.sh` never run.
* **The keep-or-retire decision for the platform-s tier is recorded with the yield figure as its stated reason.** This is the real deliverable: the 07-17 evidence says the ceiling is structural (\~3 clients, \~8 endpoints), not an effort problem, so "retire the tier" is an acceptable and possibly the correct outcome — and it should be chosen on the number rather than drifting.

**No Playwright test applies.** Nothing in platform-s changes — no view, no route, no behaviour. The deliverable is example values in the Secuura OpenAPI spec, produced by a harness that lives in `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/openapi-examples/` in the Distributed_Secuura repository; platform-s is only the traffic source, and the one platform-s edit in the whole exercise is a config lever that must be reverted. There is no surface for a spec to drive and no assertion it could make. The checkable criterion is the **measured coverage delta** above plus the `diff`-verified revert.

**Scope flag:** almost all the work, and the entire deliverable, sits in the Distributed_Secuura repo under the `openapi-examples` harness. Worth confirming this belongs in team PS at all rather than as a KS ticket — it is filed here because the *traffic* is platform-s's, which is a weaker reason than it first looks.

## Reference

* [KS-256](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-256/add-openapi-inline-examples-to-all-329-operations-eliminate-coverage) — the parent ticket, its plan attachment (§7.0-B covers the platform-s tier in detail, §7.1 the coverage reality), and PR #568.
* Harness README: `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/openapi-examples/README.md`

**Stuart, 5 Nov 2026: in favour of retiring the platform-s harvest tier. @peter@obeden.com, it's your call with him, since you made the 20 Jul split. Do you agree?**

The reason is the only figure we have: the 17 Jul baseline, about 13 of 310 operations (about 4%) across both tiers, with the ceiling structural (about 3 clients and 8 endpoints). No new pass has been run, so this ticket's "coverage delta" acceptance would not be met by a fresh number. If you'd rather have one first, say so.

If you agree, the ticket closes as retired, and the harness in Distributed_Secuura is platform-k's to remove or keep. The ticket's own scope flag still applies: nearly all of this lives on the KS side.

title: S↔K: consistent Organisation/user ownership + DR credential reconciliation — retire shared 'common access' identity
description:
## Directive

Organisation/user **ownership must be handled consistently across S and K**. The current shared "common access" service identity — where any user's actions anchor under one shared K service account when per-user provisioning isn't `Provisioned` — **was a development stopgap and is not an acceptable end state**. It must be retired in favour of a proper, per-owner identity model that is consistent on both platforms and survives disaster recovery. This ticket covers both the drift bug that exposed the problem and the ownership-model fix.

## The problem that surfaced it (DR credential drift)

S mints a **random** K password per user, stores it AES-encrypted **only in S's own DB**, and has **no reconciliation path**. So when a fresh/rebuilt S meets a K that already holds the prior instance's users:

* fresh S generates a *new* random password → `POST /api/auth/register` → **409 CONFLICT** (K rejects, no upsert) → S retries `login` with the *wrong* password → **401** → row marked `Failed: "email collision (password mismatch)"`, needs manual admin action.
* **⚠️ Lockout landmine:** the background provisioner retries every 30s; K locks an account after **5 failed logins / 15 min** (email + /24 IP). A drifted S will **mass-lock the affected K accounts** before it caps at `ProvisionMaxAttempts` (5).
* K exposes **no admin/force-set-password** endpoint — only user-driven `forgot→reset` (emailed token) or `change-password` (needs the old password). So S cannot programmatically re-sync.

### Evidence

S: random password `PlatformKProvisioningService.cs:88-92,129-157`; stored encrypted `PlatformKAccount.cs:25`, key `CardanoAnchorSettings.PlatformKCredentialKey`; 409→login→`Failed` `PlatformKProvisioner.cs:169-190`; "rotate NOT exposed" `CardanoAnchorAdminController.cs:455-461`; shared-identity fallback `CardanoAnchorAuthClient.cs:228-231,247-256`.
K (`ef687539c`): register 409 on ACTIVE `auth.ts:146-150`; login 401 `auth.ts:419-423`; lockout `accountLockout.ts:30-51`; no admin set-password (`users.ts:538` — password not a settable field); passwordless API-key connector auth `api-gateway/middleware/auth.ts:210-252`; no `client_credentials` grant `oauth.ts:294-296`.

## Target (consistent ownership, no shared identity)

1. **Retire the shared "common access" service identity as the ownership mechanism.** It stays only as an explicit break-glass (`PerUserAccountsEnabled=false`) during an incident — **not** the steady state. Per-user/per-org attribution in K must be the norm.
2. **A single, consistent ownership model across S and K** for Organisation + users: how an SSD Organisation maps to a K tenant, and how each S user maps to a K identity, defined once and honoured by both. (Ties to \[\[secuura-domain-split\]\] / the tenant-slug item PS-317.)
3. **DR-safe identity** — reconstructable or restorable without drift.

## Direction (options, to decide with K — see KS companion)

* **(A) Passwordless per-owner identity — preferred.** Move S's service/per-org identity to K's `x-api-key: sk_...` connector model (already exists, no password to drift). Represent ownership via tenant + connector key + per-user records rather than S-minted passwords. Removes the entire password-sync class.
* **(B) Deterministic per-user credentials.** If email+password stays, derive the K password via KDF/HMAC over `PlatformKCredentialKey` + stable `PersonGuid` so a rebuilt S regenerates the *same* value → register-409→login succeeds → self-heals. Trade-off: the key becomes load-bearing; rotation = re-provision.
* **(C) DR runbook (do regardless).** Treat the K credential tier as protected, co-restored DR state: the `PlatformKAccount` table **+** `PlatformKCredentialKey` **+** service `AuthEmail`/`AuthPassword`, restored to a **point consistent with K's own** `users` **snapshot** (K has `DR-RESTORE-RUNBOOK.md`). Same tier as DataProtection keys (`/var/dpkeys`) and `DocStorageKey`.
* **Explicit non-goal:** "service-identity-only" as the *answer*. That IS the shared common access being retired.

## Cross-team

The reconciliation + ownership model has a hard K-side dependency (no admin set-password today; API-key connector path). Companion KS ticket raised and assigned to Kam — see the linked issue. Kam added as subscriber here.

## Verify

Once landed: rebuild a "fresh" S against a K that already holds its users → provisioning reconciles (or the passwordless identity needs no reconciliation) with **no 409/401 loop and no account lockouts**; per-user/per-org attribution appears in K with no shared-identity fallback in steady state.

Refs: PS-317 (tenant-slug), PS-284 (async anchoring + negative-cache that bounds the login storm).

---

**Companion K-side ticket (Kam):** [KS-480](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-480/sk-k-side-support-consistent-userorg-ownership-credential)

## Acceptance

* **The shared "common access" identity is no longer the ownership mechanism.** It survives only as an explicit break-glass (`PerUserAccountsEnabled=false`) during an incident, and the steady state shows per-user / per-org attribution in K with **no shared-identity fallback**. `CardanoAnchorAuthClient.cs:228-231,247-256` is the code that has to stop being the normal path.
* **One of the three directions is chosen and reasoned**, not left as a menu: (A) passwordless per-owner identity on K's existing `x-api-key: sk_...` connector model — preferred, and it removes the whole password-sync class; (B) deterministic per-user credentials derived by KDF/HMAC over the credential key plus a stable `PersonGuid`, which self-heals a rebuilt S but makes that key load-bearing and turns rotation into a re-provision; or (C) the DR runbook alone. Whichever is chosen, the trade-off it accepts is written down, and (C) is done **regardless**.
* **The DR tier is defined as co-restored state**: the `PlatformKAccount` table, the key named by `CardanoAnchorSettings.PlatformKCredentialKey`, and the service identity's configured `AuthEmail` / `AuthPassword` keys — restored to a point consistent with K's own `users` snapshot, per K's `DR-RESTORE-RUNBOOK.md`. Same protection tier as the DataProtection keys (`/var/dpkeys`) and `DocStorageKey`. **Keys and table names only; no credential value is opened, read, logged or quoted** — and nothing in the fix may add a second copy of a password anywhere.
* **The measured figure that closes this is a lockout count of zero.** Rehearse the drift case — a fresh or rebuilt S meeting a K that already holds the prior instance's users — and report: register 409s, login 401s, provisioning retries, and K `account_locked` events. All four must be zero in the steady state, and the lockout count is the one that matters, because today it is non-zero **by construction**: the provisioner retries every 30 s, K locks after 5 failed logins / 15 min on email + /24 IP, and `ProvisionMaxAttempts` is 5 — so a drifted S mass-locks the affected K accounts before it ever caps out. A rehearsal that reports "provisioning reconciled" without that count has not measured the landmine.
* No `PlatformKOrganisation` or `PlatformKAccount` row is left in a `Failed: "email collision (password mismatch)"` state needing manual admin action.
* The K-side dependency is tracked, not assumed away: K exposes no admin or force-set-password endpoint (`users.ts:538`) and no `client_credentials` grant (`oauth.ts:294-296`), so option A or B has to be agreed with Kam on [KS-480](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-480/sk-k-side-support-consistent-userorg-ownership-credential) §4/§5 before S builds against it.

**A Playwright journey is the wrong tool for the decisive criterion.** The subject is credential provisioning between two platforms and its behaviour under a disaster-recovery restore — there is no view, route or control involved, and the failure mode (a retry loop locking accounts on the far side) is invisible to a browser. The verifiable criterion is the **measured DR rehearsal above, reported as four counts**, plus xUnit coverage of the parts that are *rules*: that the chosen identity scheme produces no 409→login→Failed path for an already-registered user, and — if option B is chosen — that the derivation is stable across process restarts for a given `PersonGuid` and is asserted with the secret-safe helpers (`SameSecret` / `systemTest/tests-unit/helpers/secret_assert.ts`), never with a bare `Assert.Equal`, whose failure message would print both values.

**Controls, needing no new spec:** `systemTest/tests/functional/provisioning.spec.ts` and `admin_connector_keys.spec.ts` stay green **unchanged** — the Administrator provisioning and connector-key surfaces still show row states and still refuse to expose a key, so a change to the identity model has not leaked into the UI or weakened it. `systemTest/tests/k_live/verb_matrix.spec.ts` with K slot N up is the end-to-end control: anchoring still works under the new identity, with attribution present. A 14-skip `@k-live` stand-down does not satisfy that — the whole claim is about the S↔K pair.

**Proposed title:** *S↔K key recovery: a KeyInvalid state, a supported inlet for a rotated connector key, and grant-driven self-recovery (covers greenfield-against-populated-K)* — Integrate S with K, Medium, Related: PS-319 · PS-505 · KS-576 · KS-582.

---

## BLUF

S has **no way to recover from a dead per-Organisation connector key, and no way to initialise against a K that already holds its Organisations.** Found while investigating key expiry after the local provisioning key lapsed on 2026-08-31 (PS-319). Three dead ends, verified in code:

1. K's re-registration is idempotent on `externalRef` and **returns no key** (KS-480 §4).
2. K's `rotate: true` exists but **Guardrail 1 403s any provisioning-key caller** — rotation is platform-admin-bearer-only (`platform.ts:503`, deliberate, KS-480 §5).
3. Even the sanctioned human path dead-ends on S: `PlatformKOrganisation.EncryptedApiKey` is written **only** by the registrar's mint path (`PlatformKOrgRegistrar.cs:482`). If an admin rotates a key on K today, S has nowhere to put it — no admin surface, no CLI. The entity's own comment says it: *"there is no way to re-read it"*.

And the greenfield case is terminal by design: a fresh S database against a populated K gets `AlreadyRegistered` + no key → `Failed`, pinned by the PS-319 step-3 DR facts.

What does **not** expire: per-org operational keys are minted without `expiresAt` (`platform.ts` sends none), so routine comms never drop from expiry — the ways an org key dies are **revocation**, **loss of S's DB / credential key**, or a hand-minted key with a date. The provisioning key is the one that can expire, and its expiry kills **new-org registration and greenfield init**, silently.

Mid-incident, break-glass already exists (`UseConnectorKeyAuth=false` → shared service identity, alarmed three ways) — so "comms down now" has a stopgap; this ticket is the *recovery* that lets break-glass be disengaged.

## Scope (S side)

**1. `KeyInvalid` lifecycle state on `PlatformKOrganisation`.** Set when K answers a **definitive** credential rejection for the stored key (`Key revoked` / `Key expired` via the validate response → gateway 401), never on transport errors. Surfaced on `/Health` (per-org count, `Warn`) and in the anchoring health, so a dead key is visible as *that*, not as an anchor backlog.

**2. A supported inlet for a rotated key** — the small DR escape hatch that works with K exactly as it is today: an **Administrator-gated** action (real admin surface per PS-420 — DevTools never ships) that accepts `organisationId` + the plaintext key (+ `keyId`) from an admin-run K rotation, encrypts it through `PlatformKCredentialProtector`, and moves the row `KeyInvalid`/`Failed` → `Provisioned`. Plaintext is handled once, in-request, never logged.

**3. Grant-driven self-recovery (the end-state; needs the K half — see KS-576 / KS-582).** When a one-shot **re-key grant** is configured (secret-store value, consumed on use), the registration sweep drains `KeyInvalid` rows **and** `AlreadyRegistered`-no-key rows by calling `register-connector` with `rotate: true` + the grant, storing the returned key exactly as first registration does. One mechanism covers mid-operation key death **and** greenfield-against-populated-K; plaintext never passes through a human. The `AlreadyRegistered` → `Failed` DR fact from PS-319 step 3 becomes conditional: terminal **unless** a grant is present.

**4. Expiry visibility (consumer half).** If K exposes the calling key's metadata (a `whoami`-style read — asked for on KS-576), `/Health` gains a `Provisioning key expires: <date>` line at `Warn` inside 30 days and a preflight pin, and the registrar can tell *expired* from *revoked* from *transport*. This would have flagged the 2026-08-31 lapse weeks ahead.

## Sequencing

1 and 2 need nothing from K and can land now. 3 waits on KS-576/577/582 (revoke-on-rotate + the grant as the approval artifact). 4's S half is trivial once K has the endpoint.

## Verification

- xUnit: `KeyInvalid` set only on definitive rejection (transport → stays `Provisioned`); inlet encrypts and flips state; grant-drain registers `KeyInvalid` and `AlreadyRegistered` rows and consumes the grant; no grant → existing terminal behaviour unchanged (the PS-319 step-3 facts still pass).
- Live (slot stack + local K): revoke one org's key on K → S shows `KeyInvalid`, anchors park; admin-rotate on K + inlet → row `Provisioned`, anchors drain. Then the greenfield rehearsal: fresh S DB against the populated local K + a grant → every org recovers without a human touching a key.
- Testing docs: a new area (key recovery), so both HTML docs gain a row — no count edits.

**S and K currently disagree about who owns a document.** K is org-owned end to end: the connector is `platform-s:<OrganisationGuid>`, reads of everything anchored are keyed by the org's once-only `EncryptedApiKey`, and the person is `onBehalfOf` attribution only. S is person-owned end to end: `DocumentStore.OwnersId` (required RESTRICT FK → Person, write-once — the transfer in `AssignController.cs:227` is commented out) is the access predicate on every surface, and `DocumentStore.OrganisationId` is a bare int with no FK — a tenant tag, not ownership. The intended model (org owns documents; single-user org is the degenerate case) is the one K already implements; S has not caught up.

Three concrete points for this ticket's scope:

1. **The orphaning constraint is the ordering constraint.** Force-deleting an `Organisation` cascades `PlatformKOrganisation` (`ApplicationDbContext.cs:949-953`) and destroys the unrecoverable key — the org's whole anchored estate on K becomes permanently *unreachable*, not deleted (`OrganisationMergeService.cs:34-50` already documents this as the merge blocker). Any future org dissolution (PS-648 defers here) must run K-erasure first, hold the connector key until it confirms, then delete locally. Nothing in S does or can do this today.

2. **No S→K erasure bridge exists, and S cannot address K's.** There is no `HttpMethod.Delete`, revoke, deregister or GDPR call anywhere in `Services/CardanoAnchor/`. K's Art.-17 crypto-shred erasure (pseudonymise `action_provenance`, keep `external_ref`) is exactly the non-destructive user-deletion semantic we want — but it is keyed on K's `users.id`, which S no longer holds (per-user credential tier removed in PS-465 phase 4; S has only `PersonGuid`). Either K accepts `external_ref` on the erasure route (KS-480 candidate), or S must capture the resolved id at provisioning time.

3. **K's erasure misses `documents.title`** — S sends the real filename as `Title` on originate (`CardanoAnchorService.cs:407`), and K's `executeErasure` anonymises metadata/certification_metadata/owner_did but not `title`. Filenames survive erasure; worth raising K-side regardless of the ownership decision.

title: Migrate document/template/credential at-rest encryption to authenticated AES-GCM + KDF (M-B3)
description:
**Severity: Medium.** Carved out of [PS-202](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-202>) (Crypto & input-validation backlog) — the one **M-B3** item that is a data migration, not a code-only fix, so it lives here in the PQC program where the hybrid algorithm choice is decided. [PS-202](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-202/crypto-and-input-validation-backlog-aes-gcmkdf-request-size-magic-byte) shipped all its other items and is closed.

## Problem

`AESHelper` encrypts **documents, templates, and stored credentials** at rest with **unauthenticated AES-CBC**, using a raw config key **with no KDF** (`AESHelper.cs:20-22,102-105,161-166`) and **no MAC**. That is malleable (no integrity guarantee) and not quantum-forward.

## Scope

Migrate document / template / credential at-rest encryption to **authenticated AES-GCM with KDF-derived keys** (hybrid / PQC-aware per this project's guiding principle). This is a **data migration**, not a drop-in code change: existing stored blobs must be re-encrypted and the key rotated.

## Already done — do not repeat

The **signing-key** portion of this work was completed under [PS-196](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-196>) (HKDF-derived, isolated key + rotation ring). This issue covers only the remaining **documents / templates / credentials** blobs.

## Acceptance

* At-rest encryption for documents/templates/credentials uses authenticated AES-GCM with KDF-derived keys, aligned with this project's hybrid classical+PQC approach.
* A migration path re-encrypts existing stored data and rotates the key with **no data loss**.
* A tampered (bit-flipped) at-rest blob is **detected** (integrity failure), not silently decrypted.

**Why no Playwright test applies, and what replaces it**: this is at-rest cryptography plus a data migration, and by requirement it is **invisible** — a document, template or stored credential that works today must work identically afterwards, with the same plaintext hash and the same provenance chain. There is no new route, control or copy string, so a browser journey could only re-prove that viewing and signing still work. Per the platform convention, a rule belongs in the xUnit suite; every claim above is a rule.

The verifiable criteria, all in `tests/ssd.UnitTests`:

1. **Round trip under the new envelope** — encrypt then decrypt returns the original bytes for each of the three blob kinds this ticket covers (document, template, stored credential), and the plaintext SHA-256 is unchanged from what `DocumentStore.Sha256` recorded.
2. **KDF-derived keys, not raw config keys** — assert the key used is derived (per `AppSpecific:TemplateStorageKey` as *input*, never as the key itself), and that two purposes derive different keys. This is the half of M-B3 that the "no KDF" finding names, and it is otherwise untested.
3. **Tamper test that must throw** — flip one bit of the ciphertext and assert the read raises an integrity failure. This is the third acceptance bullet above, and it is the one that fails on `develop` today: `AESHelper` uses unauthenticated AES-CBC with no MAC (`AESHelper.cs:20-22,102-105,161-166`), so a bit-flipped blob decrypts to malleable garbage rather than being detected.
4. **Migration with no data loss** — verify-before-swap on the plaintext hash, resumability, and a forced verify failure leaving the original blob intact; plus a measured "zero remaining, zero mismatches" figure per environment with the date, which is the only real proof the re-encryption ran.
5. **Do not repeat** [PS-196](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-196/isolate-signing-key-encryption-from-the-document-key-kms-aes-gcm-kdf) — a test or review note confirming the signing-key path is untouched, since that portion is already HKDF-derived with its own rotation ring and re-doing it here would be the easy mistake.
6. **Control that must keep passing** — the existing `AESHelper` tests, the `PdfSignatureVerificationService` tests and, on the gate slot, `my_documents.spec.ts`, `sdviewdownload_session_seal.spec.ts`, `watermark_select.spec.ts` and `sign_form.spec.ts`, which are green today and must be green against **migrated** data; that is how a silently corrupted blob surfaces.

No key, derived key, passphrase or credential value appears in a log line, an exception message or a test failure — config keys are named, values never are.

Source finding: [PS-202](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-202/crypto-and-input-validation-backlog-aes-gcmkdf-request-size-magic-byte) (M-B3). Coordinated with [PS-196](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-196/isolate-signing-key-encryption-from-the-document-key-kms-aes-gcm-kdf).

title: Akto CI scan throughput: ~21 s local vs ~10 min in the isolated pr-akto stack (~28×) — investigate worker starvation / run-pickup latency (KS-435 durable fix)
description:
[akto-2187-findings.md](https://uploads.linear.app/ee72b345-5a75-4c1a-9bbb-09a6955f4499/12359f7f-c7d7-4777-aa45-e997d8acaf8d/dc8d8d55-c175-422c-b4ed-85b2faed7c2f)

## Problem (split out of [KS-435](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-435/akto-suite-pr-full-scan-times-out-at-the-poll-ceiling-in-the-isolated) — the durable-fix track)

KS-435's immediate unblock raised the poll ceilings (`PR_TIMEOUT_MS` 660s→1200s, `PRE_MERGE_TIMEOUT_MS` 720s→1260s). But the underlying anomaly is untouched: **the same all-endpoint** `test:pr` **scan completes in \~21 s on a local host and takes \~10 min in the isolated** `pr-akto` **CI stack** — a ~28× gap that is too large to be plain CPU starvation of a co-scheduled stack.

## Evidence

* Local ([KS-433](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-433/akto-bolabflabroken-auth-finding-on-a-write-path-unmasked-by-the-ks) triage, 2026-07-11): `npm run test:pr` → COMPLETED ~21 s, 316 endpoints, 7902 results, 0 vulnerable.
* CI: three runs died at the ~594 s poll ceiling (PR #480 ×2 attempts, PR #488, develop post-merge run on `9a1ade224`); green runs (#481, #489) finished just under it — so real CI wall-clock is ~9–10 min.

## Suspects ([KS-435](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-435/akto-suite-pr-full-scan-times-out-at-the-poll-ceiling-in-the-isolated) options 2/3)

1. `akto-testing` worker CPU/IO starvation — the runner co-schedules the 31-service platform stack + Akto's dashboard/mongo/testing/puppeteer.
2. Scheduled-run pickup latency — the testing worker polls for queued runs; check `LAST_TEST_RUN_EXECUTION_DELTA` / pickup-interval behaviour under load.
3. Runner resources — larger GitHub runner class, or trim what boots in the akto job.

## Direction — right-size the runner, keep coverage intact (consolidated from [KS-446](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-446/akto-suite-pr-durable-ci-throughput-fix-stop-the-full-scan-sitting-at), closed as duplicate)

Having weighed the two levers, the clear preference is to **increase the runner's resources (CPU/RAM)** — the isolated stack's runner is simply under-provisioned for co-hosting the full platform + full Akto stack. That is the root cause and the honest fix. In order of preference:

1. **Right-size the runner** — move the `pr-akto` job to a larger runner (more vCPU/RAM), or split the platform stack and the Akto stack onto separate runners so the akto-testing worker isn't starved. Expected to be the whole fix.
2. **Confirm it's genuinely resource starvation** vs. a stall on scheduled-run pickup (~21s local vs >594s CI) — verify (1) is the right lever before spending on it.
3. **Coverage/scope trim — avoid.** The full all-endpoint BOLA/BFLA/Broken-Auth scan is the value of the gate; narrowing it to win on runtime would quietly reduce security coverage rather than fix the real constraint. Last resort only, flagged explicitly, never silent.

## Done means

CI `Akto suite (PR)` wall-clock understood + brought down to low single-digit minutes — achieved by **more runner capacity**, not a further ceiling raise and not by reducing coverage. (Or an explicit, documented decision that ~10 min is accepted and the raised ceiling is the permanent posture — then tighten the ceilings to the measured runtime.)

Consolidates [KS-446](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-446/akto-suite-pr-durable-ci-throughput-fix-stop-the-full-scan-sitting-at) (durable CI-throughput fix), closed as a duplicate of this ticket. Related: [KS-435](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-435/akto-suite-pr-full-scan-times-out-at-the-poll-ceiling-in-the-isolated) (parent, Done, #490), [KS-413](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-413/akto-pr-gate-scan-is-endpoint-bound-times-out-at-the-poll-ceiling) (prior poll-ceiling class).

## Second correction — I named the wrong limiter

My earlier comment said the 429s come from nginx's `limit_req` zone at `rate=50r/s`. **That is wrong**, and I have now measured it rather than inferred it.

A captured 429 pulled straight from the run's Mongo results on slot 2 (2026-09-28):

```
"statusCode": 429,
"body": "{\"success\":false,\"error\":{\"code\":\"RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED\",
          \"message\":\"Too many requests, please try again later.\"}}",
"headers": "{... \"Server\":\"nginx\", \"RateLimit-Policy\":\"2000;w=60\" ...}"
```

That is the **api-gateway application limiter** — `services/api-gateway/src/index.ts:475`, `RATE_LIMIT_MAX_REQUESTS=2000` (`Blockchain/Dev/.env.example:205`), 2000 requests per 60s window. nginx's own 429 would carry neither the `RateLimit-Policy` header nor that JSON body; the `Server: nginx` header is just the proxy passing the app's response through.

**Nothing else in my earlier comment changes.** The counts (107 / 8,120 / 8,730 across the three tiers) stand, and so does the reading that the CI elimination on this ticket is true *of CI* — CI is ~28× slower and never approached the budget, whichever layer enforces it.

### One practical consequence, since it came up

**`LOCAL_LOGIN_LIMITER_DISABLED=true` (KS-191) would not help.** It gates `shouldSkipLoginLimiter` (`rateLimitSkip.ts:69`) — the per-IP limiter on `/api/auth/login` alone — while these 429s land on ordinary API paths (one of the captured ones is `POST /api` with a NoSQL-injection body). It also only takes effect if the **platform** stack was started with it exported, so setting it in a systemTest `.env` does nothing.

The knob that would actually move these is `RATE_LIMIT_MAX_REQUESTS`, which changes the system under test — a decision, not a default.

Code corrected in `src/report/skipBuckets.ts`, `src/scan/types.ts` and `src/scan/scanMetrics.ts` (commit `f3fb25e3e`); the notes now cite the app limiter with this evidence and record that the KS-191 flag does not apply.

Kamil's KS-618 point is unaffected and still explains *why one scanner exhausts the budget* — every client resolves to the same key. It simply is not the nginx zone doing the refusing.

**Correction to my comment above — the attribution was wrong.**

I addressed that comment to @kamil.kreiser and called the elimination table "your elimination table". It is not his. The ten-hypothesis BLUF containing the row `Rate limiting | zero 429s | ❌` is **Peter's** comment on this ticket (2026-08-14). Kamil's comments here are the post-merge review of PR #698's residues and the 2026-09-10 budget reassignment — neither contains that table.

The measurement and the reasoning in my comment are unaffected: the 429 figures (107 / 8,120 / 8,730 across the three tiers on slot 2, 2026-09-28) stand, and so does the reading that the CI elimination is true *of CI* and should not be carried to local runs. Only the name attached to it was wrong.

The same misattribution had reached the code in two places — `src/report/skipBuckets.ts` and `src/scan/scanMetrics.ts` both said "Kamil's KS-441 elimination table". Both now read "the KS-441 elimination table (Peter, 2026-08-14)". Fixed in `a3c6813b8`.

The question in that comment is still open and is for whoever owns the limiter: exempt the scanner's source on test stacks, or pace Akto below 50 r/s?

@kamil.kreiser — could you take a look at one of your eliminations here, in light of new local data?

Your elimination table lists **"Rate limiting — zero 429s — ❌"**. On the Mac that does not hold. Measured on slot 2, Akto 2.35.6, 2026-09-28:

| tier | results | HTTP 429 with no error recorded |
|---|---|---|
| `test:pr` | 8,702 | 107 |
| `test:pre-merge` | 20,911 | **8,120** |
| `test:security` (full OWASP) | 50,162 | **8,730** |

**I do not think this contradicts your measurement — I think it confirms your explanation of it.** CI is ~28× slower, so the engine never approached the gateway's threshold and genuinely saw zero 429s. Locally the scan is fast enough to trip it. If that reading is right, "rate limiting is eliminated" is true *of CI only* and should not be carried forward to local runs, which is now where all our scanning happens.

The threshold is `nginx-demo.conf:171` — `rate=50r/s, burst=100` — and the comment above it says the rate was chosen to cut "a sustained scan down", benchmarked against a scanner at ~80 r/s. Akto is that scanner. Because it reaches the gateway as a direct client with no `X-Forwarded-For`, the whole 80-thread scan shares one `$secuura_limit_key` bucket — which is exactly the failure mode you predicted on **KS-618**: *"a single scanner would consume the budget and 429 every real user, while gaining no per-attacker bound at all."*

Until KS-709 these 429s were invisible: Akto records a 429 as a completed result with no error, so our classifier scored them as **passes**. That is now fixed (`rateLimited` bucket), which is how they became visible at all.

**The question for you:** is the right response to exempt the scanner's source from the limiter on test stacks, or to pace Akto below 50 r/s? The first touches a live security control in your area and I have not gone near it. Happy to do the second in the harness if you prefer it.

**Reassigned to @stuart.jamieson as a budget item — Kam's call, 2026-09-10.** This is no longer an engineering question; it is a spend decision, and the engineering is already done.

## What has been established

The `Akto suite (PR)` gate runs the same all-endpoint scan in **~21 s locally and ~10 min in CI — a ~28x gap.** The cause is not the scan. `ubuntu-latest` is **2 vCPU / 7 GB**, and the job boots **two full stacks on it** — the ~31-service platform stack (the scan target) plus Akto's own (dashboard, mongo, akto-testing, puppeteer). That is roughly **35 containers contending for 2 cores.**

## Why the cheap fix was rejected, and should stay rejected

Narrowing the scan to fewer endpoints would win back the runtime — by **silently reducing security coverage.** The full BOLA / BFLA / broken-auth sweep *is* the value of this gate. @peter ruled that out explicitly, and this ticket carries it as "last resort only, flagged, never silent."

## The decision, and it is one of two

1. **Buy runner capacity** — a larger GitHub-hosted runner class for this job. Restores low single-digit minutes and keeps coverage whole. **This costs money, which is why it is yours.**
2. **Accept ~10 min as the permanent posture** — then the poll ceilings (raised to 1200 s / 1260 s as a stopgap under KS-435) should be *tightened* back down to just above the measured runtime, so a real hang still fails fast instead of hiding inside a generous ceiling.

**Either is a legitimate answer. What is not sustainable is the current state:** a stopgap ceiling wide enough to mask a genuine failure, on a ticket parked as Blocked.

## What is blocked on this

Nothing of Peter's should wait on it — that is why it has moved. It has been open since 2026-07-11 and Blocked for six days.

_Filed by Wednesday on Kam's instruction. No spend has been committed and nothing has been changed on the runner._

## Verification of your post-merge list, plus three extensions — **not actioned, still yours**

@peter I re-verified your list against `origin/develop` @ `5f3cc8fef` rather than taking it on report. **Items 1 and 2 both confirmed live**, and your fixes are the right ones. **I have not touched any of it** — you marked the list "All are mine" and I am leaving it that way; this comment exists so that when you pick it up you start from a complete class rather than finding the rest afterwards.

**Honouring your binding instruction: I will not dispatch `pre-merge-platform-suites.yml` until the job cap is raised.**

### Confirmed live on `develop`
| Item | Site | Confirmed |
| -- | -- | -- |
| 1 | `pr-platform-suites.yml:521` `AKTO_MONGO_VERSION: "8.2.12"` vs `docker-compose.yml:63` default `6.0.28` | ✅ |
| 2 | `constants.ts:108` `PRE_MERGE_TIMEOUT_MS = 3_600_000` vs `pre-merge-platform-suites.yml:190` `timeout-minutes: 30` | ✅ |
| 3 | `constants.ts:94` "21 min ceiling", `:100` "stays inside its 30-minute cap" | ✅ both now false |
| 4 | `engineDiagnostics.ts:2,20` "`AKTO_DIAG=1`" / "OFF by default" vs `config/index.ts:110` `env('AKTO_DIAG','true')` | ✅ defaults ON |
| 5 | `pr-platform-suites.yml:510` "force IPv4" with no `-Djava.net.preferIPv4Stack` in the value | ✅ |
| 6 | `runTiming.ts:203` "fixed ~10-12 s … NOT configurable" vs measured 41–43 s CI / 11 s VM | ✅ |
| 7 | `test_login_rate_limit.py:78` skips unless `LOGIN_LIMITER_PROBE=1`; pytest exits 0 on skip | ✅ |

### Three things the list does not carry

**1. There are eight numbered items, not seven.** Your headline says seven; the body runs 1, 2, 3–5, 6, 7, **8**. Item 8 (the `kill -3` race at `engineDiagnostics.ts:86-89`) is the one that falls out of the count. It fails safe and nothing turns on it — flagging only because a register that drops an item silently is the shape this ticket keeps finding.

**2. Item 3's class is six sites wider than the two you cited — and the extra ones are the load-bearing ones.** Beyond `constants.ts:94,100`:

- **`systemTest/CLAUDE.md:1761`** — still states `PRE_MERGE_TIMEOUT_MS = 1260s` **and** "*while staying inside each Akto job's 30-min `timeout-minutes`*". False twice in one sentence.
- **`systemTest/akto/docs/how_to_test_with_akto.md:211, 218`** — `1260 s (21 min)`; **`:222`** — "*keeping each Akto CI job inside its 30-minute `timeout-minutes` cap*".
- **`constants.ts:77, 86`** — two more "30-minute cap" assertions.

This matters more than the two comments in `constants.ts`: **`CLAUDE.md` and `how_to_test_with_akto.md` are what someone reads *before deciding a dispatch is safe*.** They currently tell that person the ceiling is 21 minutes and fits inside the cap — which is item 2's hazard restated as documentation, one layer up from where you filed it.

**3. Item 4's class has a third site:** **`types.ts:186`** also says "*Off by default*", alongside `engineDiagnostics.ts:2,20`.

### On sequencing
No disagreement with yours (1+2 on one branch, 3–6 folded in, 7 to KS-492, 8 as a follow-up). One suggestion: **fold the six doc sites from point 2 into that same branch** — they are the same defect as the two comments you already grouped there, and splitting a class across two sittings is how the second half gets forgotten.

**Nothing here is in flight from my side.** If you would rather hand any of it over, say so on this ticket and I will take it; otherwise it stays yours and I will not touch these files.

## Post-merge code review of PR #698 — changes required

> **STATUS: RECORDED, NOT ACTIONED (Peter's call, 2026-08-14).** Nothing below is in flight and no branch is open. This list is a register, not work in progress — so if you are reading it expecting a fix to be on its way, it is not. Items 1 and 2 are **live on `develop` right now**; see the two notes marked *"while this is deferred"*.

Adding this as a new comment rather than folding it into the BLUF above, because it is a **work list**, not a revision of the findings.

PR #698 merged to `develop` at 13:24 with all five checks green. Reviewing the merged diff afterwards turned up **seven** items. Two of them I would not leave sitting on `develop`; the rest are documentation drift and one missing gate. All are mine.

### 🔴 1. CI still runs Mongo 8.2.12 — the experiment override was never rolled back

`.github/workflows/pr-platform-suites.yml:521`

```yaml
AKTO_MONGO_VERSION: "8.2.12"   # labelled "EXPERIMENT 3"
```

The compose default is correctly `6.0.28`, but the workflow overrides it, so **every PR now runs the merge-blocking Akto security gate against Mongo 8.2.12**. That matters because `systemTest/akto/docker-compose.yml` records, a few lines above its own default, that Akto bundles `mongodb-driver-sync` 4.2.1 — which predates Mongo 6/7/8 — so **6.0 is the supported pairing** (upstream akto#5473). The experiment was also *refuted* (966 s, indistinguishable from baseline), so it buys nothing and carries driver-compatibility risk on a blocking gate.

**Fix:** delete the `AKTO_MONGO_VERSION` override. Keep `AKTO_MONGO_SLOWMS: "20"` — that one is a read-only logging overlay, cheap, and it is what *cleared* Mongo as a suspect.

**While this is deferred:** it is not silently dangerous — 2.18.7 on 8.2.12 has passed a full clean rebuild + setup + scan on the VM *and* a green PR run in CI. The exposure is that an unsupported driver pairing is now the **default experience of a merge-blocking gate**, so any future weirdness in the Akto scan has an extra uncontrolled variable underneath it. If a strange Akto failure appears before this is reverted, **check this first**.

I reported to Peter earlier that "Mongo 8 is not the default anywhere". That was true of the compose file and false in effect. Peter caught it.

### 🔴 2. The pre-merge ceiling can never fire — the job cap was not raised with it

`src/core/constants.ts:108` vs `.github/workflows/pre-merge-platform-suites.yml:190`

`PRE_MERGE_TIMEOUT_MS` went 1260 s → **3600 s**, but `Akto pre-merge (full)` still carries `timeout-minutes: 30`. Only the *PR* job's cap was raised (30 → 45). So:

* poll budget = 90% of 3600 s = **54 min**, against a **30 min** job cap → the runner kills the job before the harness can report, losing the report and the artifact;
* the constant's own comment extrapolates the pre-merge tier at **~2260 s = 37.7 min**, which is **already over the 30-min cap**.

The comment says the old 1260 s value "would have FAILED on its first run — a live landmine, masked only because pre-merge-platform-suites.yml is workflow_dispatch-disabled". That landmine was **relocated, not defused**, and it is masked by exactly the same thing.

**Fix:** raise the pre-merge akto job to `timeout-minutes: 65` (poll budget 54 min + stack boot + teardown), with the arithmetic recorded beside it per MUST #13 rule 4.

**While this is deferred:** the pre-merge workflow is `workflow_dispatch`-disabled, so this cannot fire on its own. The risk is entirely on **whoever dispatches it first** — they will get a killed job at 30 minutes with no report and no artifact, which looks like a failure of the thing being tested rather than a cap that was never raised. **Do not dispatch `pre-merge-platform-suites.yml` until this is fixed**, or raise the cap in the same sitting.

### 🟠 3–5. Three comments that now state the opposite of the code

The "documented capability that does not match reality" class — the same shape as MUST #13 rule 6's corollary.

| Location | Says | Actually |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `constants.ts:94,100` | "21 min ceiling"; "stays inside its 30-minute `timeout-minutes` cap" | 60 min; it does not (see item 2) |
| `engineDiagnostics.ts:2,20` | "`AKTO_DIAG=1`"; "Strictly best-effort and **OFF by default**" | defaults **ON** (`config/index.ts:106`) |
| `pr-platform-suites.yml:510` | "KS-441 test B: **force IPv4**" | no `-Djava.net.preferIPv4Stack` in the value — only `-Duser.timezone=UTC -Xlog:gc:…` |

**Fix:** correct all three to describe what the code does. For the third, either drop the IPv4 preamble or keep only the sentence that explains why the GC flag was retained.

### 🟠 6. A comment that contradicts our own measurement

`src/scan/runTiming.ts:203`

> "Pickup is a fixed ~10-12 s `Thread.sleep` in Akto's engine and is **NOT configurable**"

We measured pickup at **41–43 s in CI** against 11 s on the VM, and the report lists that 4× variance as an **unexplained anomaly** — a fixed sleep should not vary by environment. The comment presents as settled the one thing we could not explain.

**Fix:** state the measured range and flag the variance as open, rather than asserting a constant.

### 🟠 7. The KS-492 skip is not actually recorded anywhere

`systemTest/schemathesis/tests/test_login_rate_limit.py:78`

The test skips unless `LOGIN_LIMITER_PROBE=1`, and its docstring states *"a skip here is a RECORDED coverage hole, never a pass"*. But **pytest exits 0 on a skip** and the integration leg gates on the exit code — so in every CI run it will skip, nothing goes red, and nothing reports the hole. The claim is true only if a human reads the console.

This is precisely the shape already recorded under MUST #13 rule 6a, from the anchoring suite: *"`run.py` scored it as `_run_pytest_anchoring(...) == 0` — pytest's exit code, which is 0 for a skip"*. Fixed there by `suite_gates.log_anchoring_results`; the same treatment is needed here.

**Fix:** surface the skip through the suite gate (and the HTML report) so an unexercised brute-force control is visible as a coverage hole. The test itself is fine — the gate around it is missing. Tracked on [KS-492](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-492/review-g-systemtest-all-tools-security-regression-coverage), where the anti-automation row is already ⬜ and says so.

### 🟡 8. Probable race in the thread dump

`src/scan/engineDiagnostics.ts:86-89` — the comment says *"give the JVM a moment by reading afterwards rather than racing it"*, but there is **no delay** between `kill -3` and reading `docker logs`; only process-spawn latency separates them. It fails safe (warns, and says UNKNOWN rather than clean), but expect intermittent missing dumps. Also asymmetric: a missing thread dump logs "UNKNOWN, not clean" while a missing `docker stats` snapshot logs nothing at all.

### Not changing

The instrumentation itself — `runTiming.ts`, `memoryBudget.test.ts`, the throughput/decomposition reporting and the headroom warning. That is the durable output of this ticket and it is clean; items 3–6 are comments *around* it, not defects in it.

### Suggested sequencing, when this is picked up

1 and 2 on one small branch (both are one-line changes plus recorded reasons), 3–6 folded in with them since they touch the same files. 7 belongs to KS-492. 8 is a follow-up whenever the file is next opened.

## BLUF — updated 2026-08-14 (final), supersedes my earlier comment on this ticket

**Ten hypotheses eliminated by measurement, and the tenth — the one genuine lead — died on the final CI run. There is no lead left.** The environment is exonerated: the cost is inside Akto's engine. Offered with the caveat that my *eliminations* are solid (each is a measurement) but my *suggestions* have a poor record — ten wrong in a row.

Full report attached to this ticket. PR #698 — all five checks green, the Akto suite included (965 s).

## The measurement

| Environment | PR-tier scan | Per executed request |
| -- | -- | -- |
| Ubuntu VM (8 CPU) | 22 s | \~11 ms |
| Mac (6 CPU) | 22 s | \~11 ms |
| **Ubuntu @ CI-spec (2 CPU / 7.7 GiB)** | **31–37 s** | **15–18 ms** |
| **GitHub CI (2 CPU / 7.8 GiB)** | **965–1013 s** | **455–480 ms** |

Nine CI runs, mean \~978 s, range 963–1013 s — a **5% spread**, so any real improvement would be unmistakable. None of six interventions moved it.

**The runner spec, previously unrecorded anywhere:** 2 vCPU, 7.8 GiB, 72 GB disk, `ubuntu-24.04`, kernel 6.17.0-1020-azure, x86-64.

## Eliminated

| Hypothesis | Measurement |  |
| -- | -- | -- |
| CPU / RAM | VM at identical spec → 31–37 s | ❌ |
| Network transport (serial) | container→target **1.2 ms** | ❌ |
| Disk / datastore | Mongo insert **1.04 ms**, fsync 0.48 ms | ❌ |
| Rate limiting | **zero 429s** | ❌ |
| GC / JIT | **0 Full GC**, 2–15 ms pauses | ❌ |
| JVM IPv4 | 971 s, flag verified live | ❌ |
| Mongo cache | 1013 s; **zero ops >20 ms** vs 45 on the *fast* VM | ❌ |
| Mongo version 8.2.12 | 966 s | ❌ |
| CPU steal / throttling | **steal 0 ticks, nr_throttled 0** | ❌ |
| **Target saturation at 80-way** | **80 concurrent served in 370 ms** — \~1% of the window | ❌ |

**Mongo is fully cleared** — it serves everything promptly because it is barely being asked.

## Engine phase decomposition — first ever captured for CI

| Phase | CI | VM @ same spec |
| -- | -- | -- |
| Pickup | **41–43 s** | 11 s |
| **Execution** | **918–960 s** | **16–18 s** |
| Drain | 1 s | 0–1 s |

The cost is entirely in **execution**. Also unexplained: pickup is a *hardcoded* `Thread.sleep` in Akto's compiled engine, yet takes 4× longer in CI.

## THE LAST HYPOTHESIS — 80 concurrent requests in flight (tested, ELIMINATED)

From the CI thread dump:

```
80  okhttp3.internal.http.RealInterceptorChain.proceed   ← blocked mid-HTTP-request
46  com.akto.testing.workflow_node_executor.ConditionalGraphExecutor.executeGraph
43  ForkJoinPool.unmanagedBlock / LockSupport.park
```

This overturned the "idle engine" reading — low CPU is consistent with 80 *blocked* threads, not an idle one — and exposed a flaw running through the whole investigation: every latency probe had measured a **single** request to `/health` on an **idle** stack (1.2 ms). Nobody had measured the platform under **80 concurrent requests**.

### Concurrency probe — both sides now measured (CI run 31800366014)

Fired at the same endpoint from inside `akto-testing`, where Akto actually sits. The VM control was taken **first**, deliberately, so the CI figure could be interpreted rather than rationalised:

| Concurrency | VM @ CI-spec (2 CPU / 7.7 GiB) | GitHub CI | Ratio |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| 1-way | **4 ms** wall | **8 ms** wall | 2× |
| **80-way** | **106 ms** for ALL 80 (\~1.3 ms each) | **370 ms** for ALL 80 (\~4.6 ms each) | **3.5×** |

**CI is genuinely slower under load — and it does not matter.** At 370 ms per 80-way batch, the same run's 2,095 executed requests cost `2095 ÷ 80 × 370 ms ≈ 10 s` of target time. The measured execution window was **920 s**. The target accounts for **\~1%** of it. The 80-way ratio (3.5×) is also only mildly worse than the 1-way ratio (2×) — a slight super-linearity, not the collapse the hypothesis needed.

I said in the previous revision of this comment that if CI came back fast, this hypothesis dies like the other nine and there is no lead left. **That is what happened** — reported as plainly as I would have reported a win.

**Where that leaves it.** The cost is inside Akto's engine — between receiving one response and issuing the next — not the network, the datastore, the host, or the target's ability to serve load. Two engine-side questions remain, in cost order:

* **(a) x86-64 vs aarch64** — the one variable never controlled (CI is x86-64; both fast hosts are aarch64). Testable with an aarch64 runner. This is now the leading suspect **by elimination, not by evidence**, and should be weighted accordingly.
* **(b) Akto's own request scheduling** — needs upstream help or bytecode-level work on a vendor image.

Neither is cheap, which is itself an argument for the first recommendation below.

## Two things for @stuart.jamieson and @kamil.kreiser

**1. Running Akto locally is \~28× faster.** 31–37 s locally versus 965–1013 s in CI, for identical work on identical CPU/RAM. For day-to-day security work the local run is not merely quicker — it is a far better feedback loop. CI is currently the slowest possible way to obtain this signal.

**2. A larger runner — suggested humbly, and now with a caveat I did not have before.** This ticket's original direction was "right-size the runner". The concurrency result weakens that:

* The target's response time was never the constraint, and neither was CPU, RAM, IO, GC or the datastore. **If the residual is architectural, more x86-64 cores buy nothing.**
* Dropping 8 → 2 CPUs locally cost only \~12 s, which already pointed the same way.
* Larger GitHub runners bill at a multiple on every PR. If that is not affordable, **living with current throughput is a legitimate decision**, not a failure — the raised ceilings in PR #698 make it survivable.

If a cheap experiment is wanted before any spend, an **aarch64 runner** is the one to try: same class, different architecture, and the only variable never controlled. A different machine entirely (self-hosted, or post-AWS-migration per [KS-418](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-418/systemtest-all-tools-enable-nightly-platform-test-suites-after-full)) remains more promising than a bigger one of the same class.

## What PR #698 leaves in place

Instrumentation, so the next person starts with data rather than four 45-minute cycles: throughput per executed request, the engine decomposition above, a warning above 70% of poll budget, and `AKTO_DIAG` (default on, 2.2 s / 147 KB) which produced the thread dump. It caught two of my own errors on first use — the [KS-610](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-610/akto-pr-tier-scan-takes-21-min-in-ci-against-a-20-min-poll-budget-and) headroom figure and a GC counter that could never be non-zero.

Timeouts were raised to measured behaviour with reasons recorded. **All of it is accommodation, not repair, and says so in the code.**

## Root cause is the runner size (maps to Suspect #3 — larger runner class)

The `Akto suite (PR)` job runs on **`ubuntu-latest`** — a standard GitHub-hosted runner: **2 vCPU / 7 GB RAM / ~14 GB disk** (the job even runs a "Free runner disk" step to fit). On that one small box the job boots **two full stacks**:
- the isolated **platform** stack (the scan target, ~31 services), and
- **Akto's own** stack (dashboard + mongo + akto-testing + puppeteer).

≈35 containers contending for 2 vCPU. The `akto-testing` Java worker — which executes every endpoint×template probe and polls Mongo to pick up the queued run — is CPU/IO-starved, so the same scan that takes **~30–50 s on a well-resourced local machine** takes **~10 min** here. That is the ~28× gap; it's a **resource-contention** problem, not a scan-cost or Akto-version problem (confirmed again on the 2.12.4 bump, PR #492).

## Expected fix: upgrade the runner

Moving the akto job to a **larger runner class** (e.g. a 4- or 8-vCPU GitHub larger runner) should collapse most of the gap — more cores for the testing worker + the co-scheduled stacks, and faster run-pickup. Once that lands and the real CI wall-clock is measured, the poll ceilings (`PR_TIMEOUT_MS` 1.2M / `PRE_MERGE_TIMEOUT_MS` 1.26M, raised by KS-435) can be **tightened back down** to the measured runtime rather than left wide.

Net: the raised ceiling (KS-435) keeps PRs unblocked today; the durable fix here is **bigger hardware** (plus optionally trimming what co-boots in the akto job).

Fresh **local** throughput data from the Akto 2.11.5 → 2.12.4 bump verification (PR [#492](https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/492)), 2026-07-11, for the CI-vs-local gap this ticket tracks:

| Scan | Local wall-clock (2.12.4) | Results |
|---|---|---|
| `test:pr` | ~51.5 s | 318 endpoints, 7,952 |
| `test:pre-merge` | ~82.5 s | 19,111 |
| full-OWASP (`test:security`) | ~280 s | 45,524 |

Local runtime scales cleanly with result count and stays in seconds/low-minutes — consistent with this ticket's premise that the ~10 min CI wall-clock is an **isolated-stack throughput** problem, not scan cost. (My `test:pr` was ~51.5 s vs the ~21 s baseline because I had concurrent scans in flight — an upper bound.) The 2.12.4 image pair changes nothing here; the ~28× CI gap and worker-starvation / run-pickup investigation remain open.

**Left in Backlog — not moved to Done:** the durable fix (CI wall-clock understood + brought to single-digit minutes) is unaddressed by the version bump. This comment is data only.

title: systemTest (all tools): enable nightly platform test suites after full AWS migration
description:
## Reminder: re-enable the nightly system-test suites once we have fully migrated to AWS

The nightly platform test suites (Schemathesis, Playwright, Performance, Akto) are currently **disabled** — the workflow only runs on manual `workflow_dispatch`. They were prepared to run on a daily schedule but the `schedule:` cron is commented out pending the AWS migration.

### What to do when AWS migration is complete

1. In `.github/workflows/nightly-platform-suites.yml`, **uncomment the** `schedule:` **block** to re-enable the daily trigger:

   ```yaml
   schedule:
     - cron: '0 14 * * *'   # 14:00 UTC — ~midnight Sydney, 22:00 Singapore
   ```
2. Re-point any `--env`/base-URL config from the local isolated stacks to the AWS targets if the nightly is meant to hit AWS rather than a fresh ghcr build.
3. Flip the STATUS header comment in the workflow back to **LIVE**.
4. Confirm the four suite check-runs appear and the shared `build` → fan-out topology still holds.

### Context

* Start time chosen: **14:00 UTC** (≈ midnight Sydney AEST/AEDT year-round, 22:00 Singapore SGT).
* All four suites already start **simultaneously** off the single schedule (each `needs: [prep, build]`), so enabling the one cron enables all four together.
* The Performance job runs a single isolated stack with all scenarios **serial**: smoke → auth-spike → (15m 429 cooldown) → smoke → spike → (15m) → smoke → stress → (15m) → smoke → scalability → (15m) → smoke → nightly soak (~4h4m). ⚠ ~5.9–6.1h total — near GitHub's 6h/job cap; re-check headroom on the AWS runners.
* Everything stays **report-only** (`continue-on-error`); no merge gating.
* Prepared on branch `feature/nightly-schedule-perf-sequence`.

nodes.body:
**BLUF:** The 2026-10-05 comment said the blocker had lifted. That's no longer true: since 2026-10-12, every workflow run on this repo fails within seconds and no step ever executes. The full measurement is on KS-412.

- **Last run with real duration:** 2026-10-12 07:49Z. The 600 runs since then all take ≤ 8 s (one Dependabot job excepted), and the sampled run's jobs have 0 steps.
- **`nightly-platform-suites.yml` on `develop` `d0c5d2e0e`:** `schedule:` is still commented out (lines 54–55), and the STATUS header still reads "NOT RUNNING … Actions is RETIRED".
- The title and the description's step 2 still describe an AWS migration. Per the 2026-09-08 review, that migration doesn't exist for platform-k. Reframing the ticket is still open.

Nothing changed in the repo.

## Done / not done (2026-10-16)

| Item | State | Evidence |
| -- | -- | -- |
| Serial performance sequence prepared | ✅ Done | PR #468 |
| "Pending AWS migration" wording corrected in docs | ✅ Done | PR #891 |
| GitHub Actions executing (precondition) | ⬜ No | every run since 2026-10-12 has 0-step jobs |
| Step 1: uncomment `schedule:` | ⬜ Not done | lines 54–55 still commented |
| Step 2: re-point config to AWS | ➖ N/A | no platform-k AWS target exists |
| Step 3: STATUS header back to LIVE | ⬜ Not done | header reads "NOT RUNNING" |
