| Re-check the ~6 h Performance chain against the job cap | ⬜ Not done | old estimate only |
| Reframe the title/description away from AWS | ⬜ Not done | still says "after full AWS migration" |

## BLUF — the stated blocker has lifted: GitHub Actions is executing again

**This ticket is `Blocked` on "Actions is retired". Measured today, that is no longer true**, so the precondition this ticket has been waiting on is met and it is ready to be picked up.

### What was measured (2026-10-05 ~14:40Z, `gh run list` on Secuura/Distributed_Secuura)

Runs are completing with real steps and real durations, not the zero-step `startup_failure` signature we recorded through September:

| run | conclusion | duration |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `pr` | failure | **848 s** |
| `pr` | failure | **843 s** |
| `PR Security Gates (KS-168)` | failure | **307 s** |
| `Security Scanning` | failure | **117 s** |
| `pr-premerge-ack` | **success** | 11 s |
| `PR — Lockfiles (path-skip twin)` | **success** | 9 s |

Minutes of runner compute, and two green checks. Compare the 2026-09-07 measurement quoted in the workflow header — *"the 20 most recent runs on this repo are 100% `startup_failure`"*.

### Why that is decisive for this ticket

`.github/workflows/nightly-platform-suites.yml` at `origin/develop` states its own exit condition in the STATUS header:

> *"GitHub Actions is RETIRED for this repo … **If Actions ever returns, the target schedule is `0 14 * * *`** (14:00 UTC ≈ midnight Sydney / 22:00 Singapore)."*

Actions has returned. The four steps in the description above are unchanged and still correct — uncomment `schedule:`, flip the STATUS header back to LIVE, confirm the `build` → fan-out topology, and re-check the ~5.9–6.1 h Performance chain against GitHub's 6 h/job cap on whatever runners are now serving.

### Not verified here

- **Whether the billing fix is permanent or incidental.** I measured one day of runs; I did not confirm with anyone that it is intended to stay. Worth asking Kam before committing to a nightly schedule, since his 2026-08-27 ruling was that billing *would not* be fixed.
- **The ~6 h headroom.** Not re-measured; the figure in the description is the old estimate.
- **`workflow_dispatch`.** The header says it did not work either. I did not dispatch anything to test it (KS-441 / the never-dispatch rule).

**Status left as `Blocked`** — unblocking is Peter's call, not an automatic consequence of this measurement.

*Posted by Claude at Peter's request, 2026-10-05. Facts from `gh run list`, `gh api repos/.../rulesets`, and `origin/develop` @ `22b268143`.*

## Review of PR #891 — the nightly-schedule wording, and this ticket's premise

Kam raised [PR #891](https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/891) to correct the published claim that the nightly `schedule:` was *"DISABLED pending full AWS migration (KS-418)"*. Posting the review evidence here since it bears directly on this ticket.

**KS-418 itself is untouched by that PR** — deliberately so. Kam kept the ticket id out of the branch name (`docs/nightly-schedule-true-reason`) precisely so the Linear integration would not auto-transition it. That was a thoughtful call and it worked.

### What the PR corrects

Four sites said the schedule was waiting on an AWS migration, and that `workflow_dispatch` was the working fallback. Both halves turn out not to hold:

- **There is no Platform K AWS migration to wait on.** No AWS deployment target exists in the repo (`deployment/` holds `azure/`, `caddy/`, `cardano/`), and the demo runs on the Azure VM. Platform S did migrate to AWS — the citation appears to have travelled between the two platforms.
- **`workflow_dispatch` is not a fallback.** GitHub Actions is retired for this repo per Kam's 2026-08-27 ruling that the billing will not be fixed.

### Test evidence

Verified on the merged tree at `721e5b773`, then re-verified after `57a695de6`.

| Claim | Method | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Workflow still parses | `yaml.safe_load` | PASS — keys `name`, `on`, `permissions`, `concurrency`, `jobs` |
| Behaviour unchanged | trigger set inspected | PASS — exactly `{workflow_dispatch}`; `schedule:` still commented out |
| Jobs intact | parsed job list | PASS — `prep`, `build`, `schemathesis-soak`, `playwright-nightly`, `performance-nightly`, `akto-security`, `integration` |
| Actions genuinely retired | `gh run list --limit 20`, run 2026-09-09 | PASS — 20/20 `startup_failure`, latest 2026-09-09 07:58Z |
| No AWS deployment target | `deployment/` listing | PASS — `azure/`, `caddy/`, `cardano/` only |
| DEV-PROCESS anchor is real | file + heading read | PASS — `Blockchain/Dev/docs/DEV-PROCESS.md:77`; v3 (27 Aug) records that Actions will not be restored |
| Stale claim eliminated | `git grep` tree-wide | PASS — zero hits; only the deliberate verbatim quote at `nightly-platform-suites.yml:34` remains |
| HTML well-formed after edit | `html.parser` tag-balance | PASS — zero unbalanced tags, both files |
| Mermaid node not broken | regex on the `FULL` node | PASS — matches `TIER --> FULL["..."]`, no stray quotes or brackets |
| Merge handled doc renames | diff vs `origin/develop` | PASS — followed the kebab-case renames, nothing dropped, no conflict markers |
| Branch currency | `git rev-list --count` | PASS — 0 commits behind `develop` |

**Not run, and why:** no unit suite, no platform suite, no build, no Docker stack, no `.env` work. Documentation and comments only — there is no runtime behaviour to sweep, so the live-stack requirement does not apply. **Migrations / config:** none.

### Addition pushed

I added one commit (`57a695de6`) carrying the same correction into the two platform-k HTML reference docs, which held the claim in three further places — the performance card, the k6 `<pre>` block and the pipeline-tier row in the cheat sheet, plus the Mermaid `FULL` node in the flow diagram. They had escaped the original `grep` because it searched for *"pending **full** AWS migration"* and these omit the word "full".

### What this means for KS-418 — for discussion, nothing changed yet

This ticket's title and description still carry the premise the PR corrects: *"enable nightly platform test suites after full AWS migration"*, with step 2 asking to re-point config at the AWS targets. On the evidence above there is no such migration pending, and the real blocker is that Actions is retired.

I have **not** rewritten anything here. Two sensible options when there is a moment:

1. **Re-frame** the ticket around *"re-enable the nightly suites if GitHub Actions is ever restored"*, keeping the cron and topology steps and dropping the AWS re-pointing step.
2. **Park it** as blocked-on-Actions, given the manual local-run process has replaced it.

Happy either way — flagging it so the ticket does not quietly keep asserting something the docs no longer do.

### Also left open

The cheat sheet still shows `✅ Live` badges against the PR gate in places. If Actions is retired repo-wide those read a little oddly for the same reason, but that is a broader question about how the PR tier is described rather than this PR's defect, so it was left alone.

## PR #891 is on origin at a new head — `3c07157a2` -> `721e5b773`

**BLUF: #891 was `dirty`; it is now `clean`. Landed by merging `develop` IN, not by rebasing — zero force pushes.**

- **Old head** `3c07157a2` -> **new head** `721e5b773`, a true fast-forward (`..`, not `+`)
- `mergeable_state` **dirty -> clean**
- **PREFLIGHT PASSED 13/13**
- The branch's own diff is unchanged: 4 files, 35 insertions, 16 deletions

### Why it read `dirty` — it was never a real conflict
`develop` **renamed** two of the files this PR touches (`how_to_test_secuura.md` -> `how-to-test-secuura.md`, `quick_start.md` -> `quick-start.md`). Git followed the renames and the merge applied with **no conflict at all**; the content is preserved byte-for-byte.

### One consequence, recorded because it is a fact about the PR, not a request
Peter's approval of 2026-09-08 sits at commit `3c07157a2`. The new head is `721e5b773`, so:

- the approval is **still recorded** and was **not dismissed**
- the approved commit `3c07157a2` **remains a reachable ancestor** — a force push would have orphaned it, which is one reason the merge route was chosen over rebasing
- but `commit_id != head.sha`, so by this repo's own standard it is **no longer at-head**

**Whether to seek a re-confirm is Kam's call.** Recording the state here so the ticket carries it; **nothing is being asked of anyone on this ticket.** Tracked with the wider at-head / withdrawn-approval problem on **KS-1035**.

## PR #891 reviewed and **approved** — the premise of this ticket has changed, and the docs now say so

[PR #891](https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/891) (Kam) corrects four published passages that told a reader the nightly `schedule:` was *"DISABLED pending full AWS migration (KS-418)"* and that the workflow *"runs only on manual `workflow_dispatch`"*. Both halves were wrong, and the second was the costly one — it invited someone to press a button that cannot work.

I re-measured the claims independently rather than taking the PR body at its word. They hold.

### Test evidence — re-measured in a clean worktree, 2026-09-08

| Claim | Result | How it was checked |
| --- | --- | --- |
| No AWS deployment target in this repo | ✅ confirmed | `git ls-tree origin/develop Blockchain/Dev/deployment/` → `azure/`, `caddy/`, `cardano/`. No AWS path. |
| Kam ruled 2026-08-27 that Actions is retired | ✅ confirmed | `Blockchain/Dev/docs/DEV-PROCESS.md` v3 footer, 27 August 2026 — records the ruling and replaces the earlier "suspended, not retired" framing. |
| 20 most recent runs are 100% `startup_failure` | ✅ confirmed | `gh run list --limit 20` re-run today: 20 of 20, still. |
| `DEV-PROCESS.md` §Manual CI-gate equivalents is a real destination | ✅ confirmed | Present at line 77, with the per-job local command map. |
| Behaviour unchanged | ✅ confirmed | On the merged tree the `schedule:` block is still commented out and the trigger set is still exactly `{workflow_dispatch}`. |
| Retirement corroborated beyond that PR | ✅ confirmed | KS-789, KS-910, KS-926, KS-1012 all rest on the same finding. |

**Merge check.** GitHub shows `CONFLICTING`, but that looks like a rename-detection artefact rather than a real clash — merging `origin/develop` into the branch locally returns exit 0, auto-merging all four files, with the edits landing correctly on the two docs `develop` renamed to kebab-case in the meantime. A plain `git merge develop` and push should clear it.

**Not run, and correctly so** — documentation and comments only, so no unit suite, no platform suite, no build and no Docker stack applies.

### What this means for this ticket

**The condition this ticket waits on does not exist.** There is no Platform K AWS migration to complete — Platform S migrated to AWS, this repo did not, and the demo runs on the Azure VM. The nightly is off because **GitHub Actions is retired for this repository**, which is a different situation with a different exit: the suites run locally now, per `DEV-PROCESS.md` §Manual CI-gate equivalents.

So the trigger for re-enabling the cron is no longer *"AWS migration complete"* — it is *"Actions restored"*, if that ever happens. The title and description here still carry the old framing and are mine to bring into line with the corrected docs.

### One small note for the record

The PR deliberately kept `ks-418` out of the branch name to avoid auto-transitioning this ticket, which was thoughtful. The `(KS-418)` in the PR **title** did it anyway — the integration moved this ticket `Todo → In Progress` at 04:18:00 on 7 September, three seconds after the PR opened. Worth knowing for next time: the branch-name precaution alone is not sufficient. I will set the state back myself.

Nothing here reflects on the change, which is accurate, carefully evidenced and carries no runtime risk.

title: CI: require all systemTest (all tools) PR suites + pre-merge to block merges on failure (branch protection + sign-off)
description:
## Goal

Make **every** systemTest PR suite **and** the pre-merge tests actually **block a merge on failure**. The workflow YAML already runs each suite to completion and then hard-fails its check (complete-then-block); what's missing is the **settings half** — a red check only prevents merge when branch protection marks it **Required**, and a check is matched by its **check-run display name**, not its job id. The pre-merge gate specifically must be a **manual human approval** (not an auto-pass).

## Background (already in place, code side)

`.github/workflows/pr-platform-suites.yml` (build-once → isolated per-suite stacks) runs each suite `continue-on-error` then an Enforce step fails the required check on any failure:

* **Schemathesis** — blocking spec-auth ([KS-380](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-380/harden-the-pre-release-gate-required-checks-on-develop-preflight)) + pytest ([KS-126](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-126/schemathesis-pytest-suite-runs-only-ad-hoc-locally-wire-it-into-ci-dev)) + offline quality/unit gate; [KS-270](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-270/featschemathesis-add-low-frequency-auth-profile-to-reduce-429s-on) auth sweep stays informational by design.
* **Playwright** — blocking `quality:check` + `npm run ci`.
* **Performance** — quality/unit gate + k6 smoke, complete-then-block.
* **Akto** — quality/unit gate + PR-gate scan, complete-then-block via step-outcome (emits Allure, not JUnit).

## Tasks (settings — cannot be code)

1. **Branch protection ruleset — mark these check-run display names Required** (match by display name, not job id):
   * `build`
   * `Schemathesis suite`
   * `Playwright suite`
   * `Performance suite (k6 smoke)`
   * `Akto suite (PR-gate subset)`
     Require `build` too — in the build-once topology a `build` failure **skips** the suite jobs, so confirm a required-but-skipped check does not wedge the PR (skipped ≠ stuck).
2. **Pre-merge must be a MANUAL human-approval gate — no auto-pass.** The comprehensive `run.py pre-merge` sweep (`pre-merge-platform-suites.yml`) must require a designated human to **manually click Approve** before the PR can merge; it must never pass on its own.
   * Implement via the GitHub `pre-merge-signoff` **Environment** with **required reviewers** (an Environment reviewer *is* a manual Approve/Reject gate): pin the `Pre-merge sign-off (human)` job to that Environment so the run **pauses and waits** for a human decision, and no merge proceeds until a reviewer manually approves. GitHub → Settings → Environments → `pre-merge-signoff` → add required reviewers (start with @peter).
   * Mark the `Pre-merge sign-off (human)` check **Required** in the branch-protection ruleset so the manual approval is enforced, not advisory.
   * Per CLAUDE.md, "PR checks green" is **not** the pre-merge sign-off — a human must have run/confirmed the comprehensive pre-merge sweep and then manually approved.

## Notes / carve-outs

* Two deliberate non-blocking exceptions stay as-is: the rate-limited [KS-270](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-270/featschemathesis-add-low-frequency-auth-profile-to-reduce-429s-on) Schemathesis auth sweep (429 back-off would flap the gate) and **all nightly** runs (report-only soak).
* This ticket is GitHub **settings** work; no systemTest code change is required (the YAML is already complete-then-block, and the sign-off job already targets the `pre-merge-signoff` Environment — it just needs reviewers + to be Required). Verify on a draft PR: all five suite checks Required and red-on-failure blocks merge, and the merge stays blocked until a human manually approves the `Pre-merge sign-off (human)` gate.

---

## Precondition: the pre-merge ack checkboxes have no not-applicable path (added 2026-09-09)

**Close this before** `ENFORCE_PREMERGE_ACK` **is set to** `true`**, or turning enforcement on will require a false attestation on any PR that legitimately needs neither suite.**

`.github/pull_request_template.md` seeds two boxes under the heading **"Pre-merge acknowledgment (author)"**, instructing: *"Tick each box **only after** you have run that suite's pre-merge tier and it passed"*. `.github/workflows/pr-premerge-ack.yml` ([KS-413](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-413/akto-pr-gate-scan-is-endpoint-bound-times-out-at-the-poll-ceiling)) matches **only**:

```
^- \[[xX]\][[:space:]]*<!--ack:schemathesis-->
^- \[[xX]\][[:space:]]*<!--ack:akto-->
```

A tick, or nothing. No N/A marker, no label escape, no "suite not applicable" branch. So for an offline shell gate, a docs change or a workflow tweak, the only ways to satisfy the check are to tick a box asserting a sweep that did not happen, or to leave a box that reads as an omission.

**The exemption pattern already exists in that workflow** — drafts pass green unconditionally (`if [ "${DRAFT}" = "true" ]`). And the template models the right affordance one section down, in the PII block: *"Not applicable? Say so explicitly rather than leaving the boxes blank — a blank box reads as 'not checked', which is the state this section exists to make visible."* The ack section has no equivalent.

**How it surfaced.** PR [Secuura/Distributed_Secuura#921](https://linear.app/secuura/review/ks-778-the-pin-label-gate-could-not-see-two-legal-shapes-and-its-guard-0ba71ba302a2) ([KS-778](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-778/preflight-leg-10s-pin-label-parser-is-blind-to-a-quoted-uses-and-an)) changes exactly one file — `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/preflight/action-pins-labelled.sh`, an offline shell gate that reads `.github/` with `git grep` and prints to stdout. Measured: **0 of 1** changed files fall under `services/`, `frontend/`, `packages/`, `migrations/`, `contracts/`, `systemTest/`, any compose file or any `.env`, so neither pre-merge suite exercises anything in it. Both boxes were left unticked with the reason stated inline, following the PII section's pattern — a workaround, not a fix; the workflow still counts it as un-acknowledged.

**Not urgent today:** enforcement is soft by default (the repository Variable `ENFORCE_PREMERGE_ACK` is unset ⇒ warn + pass), and the workflow has not executed since 2026-08-17. It becomes live the moment task 2 above is actioned.

### Fix — one of these, not all

1. **An N/A marker** the workflow recognises, e.g. `<!--ack:schemathesis:na-->`, requiring a stated reason on the same line. Smallest, keeps the human in the loop, and mirrors the PII section so the template gains one convention rather than two. The assertion becomes "I considered this suite and it does not apply" — a true statement, still auditable.
2. **A label escape**, e.g. a `no-premerge-suites` PR label that passes both ack checks, reviewable in itself.
3. **A path-based skip** — passes when the diff touches nothing the suites cover. Most automatic, but duplicates suite-scope knowledge into the workflow and will drift.

### Done means

* A PR that legitimately needs neither suite passes both ack checks **without** anyone ticking a box that asserts an unrun sweep.
* The escape requires a stated reason — an acknowledgment, not a bypass. A blank body still fails.
* Red→green with `ENFORCE_PREMERGE_ACK=true`: a PR using the new form passes; the same PR with the reason removed fails. Proven both ways.
* Template instruction text updated to describe the not-applicable path, in the shape the PII block already uses.
* Ticking a box still means what it says today — this must not weaken the positive assertion.

@stuart.jamieson @peter — **this is a relay of Peter's own finding, placed here rather than left on [KS-441](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-441), because this is the ticket whose execution actually triggers that workflow.** Task 2 of this ticket ends with *"Verify on a draft PR … the merge stays blocked until a human manually approves the `Pre-merge sign-off (human)` gate."* **Whoever does that is the first person to dispatch pre-merge — and they will hit this.**

**Flagging it as a stopgap, deliberately. This comment is not the fix and should not be mistaken for one later.**

### The trap
`PRE_MERGE_TIMEOUT_MS` was raised 1260 s → **3600 s** (`systemTest/akto/src/core/constants.ts:108`), but `Akto pre-merge (full)` still carries **`timeout-minutes: 30`** (`.github/workflows/pre-merge-platform-suites.yml:190`). Only the *PR* job's cap was raised (30 → 45).

**The arithmetic:**
- poll budget = 90% of 3600 s = **54 min**
- job cap = **30 min**
- → **the runner kills the job 24 minutes before the harness can report.**

And the constant's own comment extrapolates the pre-merge tier at **~2260 s ≈ 37.7 min**, which is **already over the 30-min cap** on its own. The pre-merge tier has **never run in CI**, so nothing has surfaced this.

### What it looks like when it bites
**A killed job at 30 minutes with no report and no artifact — which reads as a failure of the thing being tested, not as a cap that was never raised.** That is the expensive part: the first person to see it will reasonably start debugging the platform.

### What to do
**Either** raise the pre-merge Akto job to `timeout-minutes: 65` (54 min poll budget + stack boot + teardown) **in the same sitting** as your first dispatch, **or** don't dispatch until someone has. Peter's recorded fix is the 65 with the arithmetic written beside it.

| `systemTest/akto/src/core/constants.ts:77, 86, 94, 100` | *"21 min ceiling"*, *"stays inside its 30-minute cap"* |

## Update — KS-413 supersedes parts of this ticket (2026-07-08)

Two things changed in [KS-413](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-413) that make the tasks below partly stale. PR: https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/458

Rationale: the checkbox is honor-system (verifies the box is ticked, not that the suite truly ran, and a description checkbox isn't author-attributed) — accepted as convenience for now; may tighten to a comment-based/author-attributed gate later.

### Still to do (settings only — the "enable" half)
Built but **non-blocking today** (Option A). To enforce, on the **develop AND main** rulesets:
1. Mark Required: `Pre-merge acknowledged — Schemathesis`, `Pre-merge acknowledged — Akto`, `Linear ticket present`, and `Akto pre-merge (full)`.
2. Turn on **required approving reviews = 1**.
(`Akto suite (PR)` on develop is already Required.)

**Scope addition — add an Akto _pre-merge_ blocking gate.**

The Akto PR scan is now **informational / non-blocking** (KS-413) because it's endpoint-bound and times out. That leaves Security Misconfiguration + the full OWASP set covered **only nightly (report-only)** — no blocking tier.

So the pre-merge gate this ticket enforces should also include **Akto**: a new blocking `akto` job in `pre-merge-platform-suites.yml` (alongside the existing Schemathesis pre-merge sweep) that boots the platform + Akto stack and runs the full OWASP scan (`npm run test:security`) or an SM-focused subset. - **This ticket (KS-412)** covers the enforcement half: once that job exists, its check-run must be **required** in branch protection for pre-merge (the same way this ticket already requires the four PR suites + the `Pre-merge sign-off (human)` gate).

title: Evaluation + roadmap: make the DocumentTransaction ledger the source of truth
description:
Feasibility review of replacing table-state with the `DocumentTransaction` ledger as source of truth, from a full read of `Services/Transactions/*`, `Services/Lineage/*`, `Services/CardanoAnchor/*`, the write sites, and `.planning/VOCABULARY.md` / `ps-109-baseline-matrix.md`.

## Verdict

**Feasible after prerequisites — for a limited definition of "source of truth"; not feasible today, and not worth it for access control in the foreseeable term.**

The ledger is **already authoritative for "which stored blob is current"** on every serve/derive path — `IDocumentStateResolver.GetCurrentAsync` is the single authority, with a table fallback for legacy rows ([PS-109](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-109/epic109-document-iteration-model-make-the-transaction-ledger-the), shipped). Lineage and the certify-hash panel are ledger-driven. But lifecycle **gates** (watermark/sign/certify queues), **access control** (shares, rights, ownership), and **revocation state** are answered entirely by `DocumentStore`/`SendDocsLinks`/`DocumentCertification` columns today.

## Single biggest blocker

The ledger is **provably incomplete**, both ways:

* **Forward (write holes):** four live paths mutate access state with **no ledger event** — `MyDocuments.MDblockfile` (the primary owner revoke UI), `Senddocs.ShareEditPost`, and the two Assign cascades (`AssignController.cs:217-221`, `:479-480`). A naive ledger fold would show shares as active that the owner explicitly revoked, i.e. **grant access that was revoked**. `LineageService.cs:94-97` already codifies the table as truth here.
* **Backward (history gaps):** `DocumentStore` predates `DocumentTransaction` by a month; pre-ledger docs have no genesis row (integrity check hard-fails on zero rows), and [PS-109](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-109/epic109-document-iteration-model-make-the-transaction-ledger-the) leaves `ResultFileGuid` NULL on legacy rows. Any "fold the ledger" read disagrees with reality for some documents until every path emits events **and** the historical corpus is backfilled or fenced by an epoch.

## Secondary blocker (legal, parallel)

`DocumentTransaction` stores PII (`ActorName` = "First Last (email)", `RecipientEmail`, repeated in `PayloadJson`) with **no erasure/redaction path**. Declaring an append-only, hash-chained, publicly-anchored table "immutable truth" collides with GDPR Art. 17 for regulated customers. Mitigating fact: **PII is not sent on-chain** (anchor payload is documentId/ContentHash/IssuerOrgId/CertId/action/timestamp only), so local-row redaction is technically possible — but a crypto-shred/tombstone design must exist first.

## Recommended approach

**Approach 2 — ledger-as-authority for lifecycle state with derived read models**, extending the shipped `DocumentStateResolver` direction; the tables are **demoted to transactionally-maintained projections** (same-transaction append+update, so they can't drift except by bug), verified by an extended integrity/reconciliation checker. Not full event-sourcing (Approach 1: the ledger can't rebuild `SendDocsLinks`/`OwnersId` from events never written; expiry is a future-dated fact) and not dual-write-as-endstate (Approach 3: institutionalises two truths — but its shadow-read/per-path-cutover *mechanics* are the right migration tool). Reframe entitlements (shares/rights/ownership/expiry) as: ledger = complete **audit** of entitlement changes; `SendDocsLinks`/`RightsHolderId` stay the operative store — folding per-link streams to answer live access buys nothing users see and risks granting revoked access.

## Phased roadmap (each step independently shippable)

* **Phase 0 — stop the bleeding (no schema change):** close the 4 write holes + fix the anchor leak. **Do these regardless of the strategic decision** — see the 4 sub-issues. Every day they stay open produces revocations that can never be truthfully backfilled.
* **Phase 1 — chain identity & integrity:** add `SendDocsLinkId` FK + stamping migration; concurrency control (`IsConcurrencyToken` on `DocumentStore.CurrentChainId` + retry, unique fork-guard index on `(DocumentStoreId, MutationPrevChainId)`, composite `(DocumentStoreId, Added DESC, Id DESC)` / `(DocumentStoreId, Action, Added DESC)` indexes); resolver follows the tip pointer instead of the timestamp scan.
* **Phase 2 — backfill:** synthetic chains for pre-ledger docs + share history (`IsBackfill` flag, excluded from anchoring/hash checks); fallback-hit logging as the cutover green-light.
* **Phase 3 — derived read models, per-path cutover (shadow-read → switch):** `IShareStateResolver`, then lifecycle-gate / rights / dashboard reads, each behind divergence telemetry with instant revert.
* **Phase 4 — enforcement:** continuous reconciliation as a scheduled hosted service with alerting (today `ChainIntegrityChecker` runs only from admin screens and nothing happens on failure); close verb gaps (`transfer-ownership`, `blob-purge`, certify attestation payload).

**Key risks to design around before any cutover:** delete semantics (blob physically erased after `delete` row → dangling `Result*` pointers); no concurrency control on tip advancement (races fork the chain, last-writer-wins); integrity failure has no runtime consequence; fold/replay performance under MySQL (add the composite index regardless); **no** `dotnet test` **in CI**; and the rollback trap — table columns must stay dual-written until org-wide reconciliation reports zero divergence.

See the 4 Phase-0 sub-issues (genuine correctness bugs, worth doing on their own merits). Full map/design/risk analysis available on request.

## Acceptance

This ticket's deliverable is an **evaluation and a roadmap**, so it closes on documents and decisions, not on behaviour:

* The verdict above is written into a tracked design document (`docs/` — not only this ticket), stating in one sentence what "source of truth" is being claimed and what it explicitly is **not**: the ledger is already authoritative for "which stored blob is current" via `IDocumentStateResolver.GetCurrentAsync`; entitlements (shares, rights, ownership, expiry) stay in `SendDocsLinks` / `RightsHolderId`, with the ledger as their audit.
* The four Phase-0 write holes are **named with file and line** and raised as sub-issues in their own right — `MyDocuments.MDblockfile`, `Senddocs.ShareEditPost`, `AssignController.cs:217-221` and `:479-480`. They are correctness bugs regardless of the strategic answer, and the roadmap must not be the thing they wait on.
* Approach 2 is recorded as the chosen direction with Approaches 1 and 3 and the reasons they were rejected, so a later reader cannot re-open the question from scratch — and so "dual write" is not mistaken for the endstate when its shadow-read mechanics are adopted as the migration tool.
* The PII / erasure blocker has an owner and a position: `DocumentTransaction` holds `ActorName`, `RecipientEmail` and repeats both in `PayloadJson`, with no redaction path. The document states that a crypto-shred or tombstone design must exist **before** the table is described as immutable truth, and records the mitigating fact that the anchor payload carries no PII so local redaction stays technically possible.
* Each of Phases 1–4 lists its own done-condition and the telemetry that would green-light the next — specifically the fallback-hit logging that gates Phase 3, and the "zero divergence org-wide" condition that gates dropping dual writes.
* The named pre-cutover risks each have a decision or an explicit "open": delete semantics leaving dangling `Result*` pointers, no concurrency control on tip advancement, integrity failure having no runtime consequence, fold/replay cost under MySQL, and the rollback trap. Of these, the composite index (`(DocumentStoreId, Added DESC, Id DESC)`) is worth doing on its own merits and should say so.

**Why no Playwright test here.** Nothing in this ticket changes what the application does — it is a feasibility verdict and a sequencing plan, and its only code-shaped outputs are the four sub-issues, which carry their own acceptance. A browser journey cannot assert that a roadmap is sound. The checkable criteria are therefore the tracked document above plus the four filed sub-issues.

**Where the testable work does land**, so the next reader is not left guessing: the Phase-0 holes are four access-state mutations that emit no ledger event, which is a *rule* — xUnit in `tests/ssd.UnitTests`, asserting each path appends its event in the same transaction as the column update. Phase 1's fork-guard and concurrency token are likewise xUnit. The first thing that genuinely needs a live stack is **Phase 3's shadow-read cutover**, where a derived read model must agree with the operative table on a real database — and the strongest candidate assertion there is the revocation case this ticket warns about: an owner revokes a share through `MyDocuments.MDblockfile`, and the derived `IShareStateResolver` must report it revoked. That is a Playwright/journey assertion, and it belongs on the Phase 3 ticket, not here.

title: Base-image refresh routine + track postgres CVE-2025-68121 (redis leg already done in triage)
description:
## Context — KS-363 follow-up (residual criticals after the base-image refresh)

After KS-363 (all built images → `node:22-alpine` / `nginx:1.29-alpine`, **0 critical across the 31 built images**), residual criticals appeared only against the two pinned third-party infra images. Investigated before assuming "major bump needed" — **major bumps buy nothing for either**, and the redis finding turned out to be a stale local scan cache, not a platform exposure.

## 1. redis — RESOLVED during triage (was a stale local image, demo never affected)

* The 6 crit / 59 high initially flagged were in a **stale local Docker cache** of `redis:7-alpine` (pre-pull digest).
* The current upstream digest `sha256:6ab0b6e7…` scans **0 CRITICAL / 0 HIGH** — and it is exactly what the ACR mirror holds and what `secuura02-demo-redis` runs. Verified via `az acr import --force` (digest unchanged → ACR already current).
* `redis:8-alpine` is identical (0/0) — no major bump warranted.
* Done: local image re-pulled + container recreated; demo redis app restarted (idempotent) and Running; portals/API re-verified 200.

## 2. postgres — CVE-2025-68121, unfixable by us today (local-only surface) — the one real residual

* `postgres:15-alpine`: 1 critical = **CVE-2025-68121** (Go stdlib `crypto/tls` incorrect certificate validation, in the image's Go helper binary; fixed in Go 1.24.13 / 1.25.7).
* Present **identically in** `postgres:16-alpine` **and** `postgres:17-alpine` — a major bump does not clear it. It clears when Docker Hub rebuilds the image against a patched Go toolchain.
* Demo uses managed `secuura02-demo-pg` (PG 15 flexible server), so this container image is **local dev only**.
* **Action:** periodically re-pull `postgres:15-alpine` and re-scan; close when the upstream rebuild lands.

## 3. Systemic: pinned-tag digests go stale silently

The ACR `node:22-alpine` mirror WAS genuinely stale during KS-363 (needed `--force` re-import before the demo build), and the redis false alarm came from the same mechanism on a local cache. Alpine-based images republish the same tag with fixes; mirrors/local caches keep old digests and quietly re-accumulate CVEs — and stale caches also produce misleading scan results.

**Proposal:** a lightweight refresh routine — periodically (e.g. monthly or per deploy): `az acr import --force` for the mirrored bases (`node:22-alpine`, `nginx:1.29-alpine`, `edoburu/pgbouncer:1.22.1-p0`, `redis:7-alpine`) + `docker compose pull` locally, then re-scan. Could live in `deploy.sh` or a small script + reminder.

## Scanner note

Trivy v0.58.1; the KS-363 Docker Scout baseline rated redis 0 critical — consistent with the stale-local-cache explanation (Scout scanned a fresh rebuild).

This ticket stays Blocked on that rebuild. Nothing is built or deployed by this comment. The watch for the rebuild is tracked on KS-2064; when this comment was written, KS-2064 said that nothing schedules a weekly watch.

Corrected facts. They come from Seat D 57th's read of the running containers on 2026-11-06 (Kintsugi 06:50:51Z, demo 06:51:02Z; read only, nothing exploited). I ran no scan and read no box.
* Where it runs: Kintsugi and the demo both run `postgres:15-alpine` as a container named `secuura-postgres`, not a managed server. Kintsugi: image `fe0737ba566a`, built 2026-08-13, PostgreSQL 15.19. Demo: image `57e5b9f69e67`, built 2026-07-07, PostgreSQL 15.18. These are two different builds of one floating tag. The description of this ticket says the demo uses a managed server and that the surface is local development only; comment 11767bef (2026-08-12) already records that the managed server was deleted on 2026-07-10.
* No managed server in reach: every database-shaped variable name in every container was classed without printing a value. Kintsugi 49 of 49 local, 0 managed; demo 53 of 53 local, 0 managed. A control (lines naming CARDANO in the env file) read 4, so the search could see lines.
* The version: `gosu` 1.19, built with Go 1.24.6 on both boxes, below the fix in Go 1.24.13. The scanner is right to flag it. The flaw is in certificate validation by `crypto/tls`.
* Reachability, by a read and not a test: the image's entrypoint script runs `exec gosu postgres` once at container start, so `gosu` is replaced by postgres and takes no network input. 0 `gosu` processes were alive on either box, against 11 postgres processes as a control. In the `gosu` binary's strings, `crypto/tls` appears once, and each of `crypto/tls.Client`, `crypto/tls.(*Conn).Handshake`, `net/http.(*Client)` and `net.Dial` reads 0; a made-up control string reads 0. A symbol search is a strong sign, not proof.

Not read: any other Go binary in the image, and the HIGH findings (this ticket records 13 on 2026-07-02, 14 on 2026-08-14 and 23 on 2026-09-02, with different scanner versions). Whether the boxes still run these image builds after today is unmeasured.

The earlier card on this ticket (secuura-ks-365-postgres-image-gosu-vulnerability-1106, ruled the same day at 14:59 AEDT) relied on a weekly image watch. None runs: KS-2064, read at develop 038e8ab5ae2d, records that the monthly workflow `.github/workflows/base-image-refresh.yml` has no schedule and that `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/base-image-watch.sh` is run by hand (comment 8fe9efd6 says on the 1st of each month). The exit event for this ticket stays the upstream rebuild of `postgres:15-alpine`.

Demo is frozen (Kam's card secuura-ks1401-058-merge-demo-billing-1104) and nothing here touches it.

**Moved `In Review` → `Blocked`. Nobody is reviewing this; it is waiting on Docker Hub.**

This ticket's own last comment records it as waiting on **two** conditions:

1. ✅ **#793 merged** — `base-image-watch.sh` carries its false-clear fix, so the watch can be trusted
   for the close decision.
2. ⏳ **Upstream** — a Docker Hub rebuild of the `postgres` image carrying the CVE-2025-68121 fix.

Condition 2 is **an event outside this repo and outside anyone here**. `In Review` asserts a reviewer
is holding something, and none is — every attached PR (#386, #387, #388, #390, #391, #786, #793) is
merged, #786 with Peter's approval at head.

Per the column convention on KS-854 — *before moving a ticket into a column, name the event that takes
it OUT* — the exit event here is **an upstream image rebuild**, which is exactly what `Blocked` is for.
Left in `In Review` it reads as work sitting on a colleague's desk, and it would keep surfacing in
every review sweep as if someone were sitting on it.

**Not closed**, because the CVE track is the point of the ticket and it is not resolved.

*(Disposition pass, s152.)*

## ✅ SECOND CONDITION MET — #793 is merged. Stating it rather than leaving it to be inferred.

`develop` `27b0ee294` → **`9806be0ac9a6ebd6e86f2ba896f1f0332ba21787`** ([#793](https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/793)). Tree predicted `2675f8e19` before the merge and re-derived identical from the object after; parents from the object; #905 still absent (negative control).

**This ticket was waiting on two things. One of them is now done.**

1. ✅ **#793 merged** — so `base-image-watch.sh` carries its false-clear fix, and the watch can be trusted for the close decision. **The reason I refused to run it at 14:32 no longer applies.**
2. ⏳ **Upstream** — a Docker Hub rebuild of `postgres:15-alpine` against Go ≥ 1.24.13. **Nothing we do moves this**, and today's re-scan showed the digest unchanged at `fe0737ba…` with CVE-2025-68121 still present in `gosu`'s vendored stdlib.

**So this stays a HOLD, but for one reason now instead of two.** The next re-scan can use the watch rather than a hand-rolled trivy invocation.

## Both of Kam's audit-baseline rulings are now on the trunk — verified on `develop`, not on the branch

| ruling | rows on develop |
| -- | -- |
| `earlier` (09:57) | GHSA-4mjr-xmp4-gh2g, GHSA-rgwj-5xj2-c3m3, GHSA-x5fp-wj9c-mxmx all read **`expires 2026-09-10`** — the date he chose, not the `2026-09-24` he declined |
| `add-dead` (10:35) | exactly **4** rows at **`expires 2026-09-06`** (`fast-uri`, ticket KS-763) — deliberately already expired, as ruled |

35 rows total, up from 31, **delta exactly +4 with zero develop rows lost** — the file was written once and the other 31 were not rebuilt. **No expiry date was refreshed.**

The re-triage ticket Kam asked for is **[KS-997](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-997)**.

## BLUF — periodic re-scan run 2026-09-08. **The residual has NOT cleared. Do not close.**

`postgres:15-alpine` still carries **CVE-2025-68121**, and the image has not moved at all since this ticket last recorded it.

## Measured, directly — the gate was deliberately NOT used

    digest:  sha256:fe0737ba566a2c5b2a28f34433c0a423261900ec17b9bf7ad115e1aae7e57f1b
    (identical to the digest this ticket's own comment records — the upstream
     rebuild has not happened, so there was never going to be a change to find)

    trivy 0.58.1, --severity CRITICAL --scanners vuln

    postgres:15-alpine (alpine 3.24.1)      Total: 0  (CRITICAL: 0)
    usr/local/bin/gosu (gobinary)           Total: 1  (CRITICAL: 1)

| Library | Vulnerability | Installed | Fixed in |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| stdlib | **CVE-2025-68121** | `v1.24.6` | 1.24.13, 1.25.7, 1.26.0-rc.3 |

*crypto/tls: incorrect certificate validation during TLS session resumption.*

**Both halves of this ticket's §2 hold exactly as written:** the alpine layer is clean (0 CRITICAL), and the one critical is the Go stdlib vendored into the image's `gosu` helper — **not something we can patch**. It clears when Docker Hub rebuilds against a patched toolchain, and the unchanged digest says that has not happened.

**Surface is unchanged too:** local dev only. The demo runs the compose stack on the VM, and this is the container image, not a managed server.

## ⚠ Why I did NOT run `base-image-watch.sh`

The watch is the right tool and it exists (merged via #786). But **the fix for its false-clear bug is on [#793](https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/793), which is open and unmerged** — and this ticket's own 2026-09-02 comment records what that bug is:

> *the gate could reach **"THE RESIDUAL CLEARED"** with no currency control running at all — an empty reference image made both control arms vanish, and that verdict is the one that sends an operator at the live registry with `az acr import --force`.*

**Running the unfixed gate to answer "has the residual cleared?" is running a check that can answer yes for the wrong reason, on exactly the question it would be wrong about.** So this re-scan is a direct trivy invocation instead: one command, one image, the CVE named in the output rather than a verdict computed from it.

## What this ticket is actually waiting on

1. **Upstream** — a Docker Hub rebuild of `postgres:15-alpine` against Go ≥1.24.13. Nothing we do moves this.
2. **[#793](https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/793)** — until it merges, the automated watch cannot be trusted for the close decision, so every check stays manual like this one.

**`In Review` remains correct** for this ticket, and for the reason its own 2026-09-02 comment gives: #793 is open and awaiting review. Not moved.

*Re-scan by s150, 2026-09-08. Nothing pulled to ACR, nothing deployed, no gate run.*

## Board reconcile — In Review is RIGHT here, and I am leaving it

The GitHub integration walked this ticket twice on the opening of [#793](https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/793): `Tested Not Deployed → In Progress` (14:32Z) then `In Progress → In Review` (14:33Z). No human moved it.

**I walked it to Tested Not Deployed myself an hour ago when [#786](https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/786) merged, and that walk was the wrong one — not this one.**

Tested Not Deployed claims the work is finished and waiting on a deploy. It is not. The through-code QA pass on #786 found the gate could reach **"THE RESIDUAL CLEARED" with no currency control running at all** — an empty reference image made both control arms vanish, and that verdict is the one that sends an operator at the live registry with `az acr import --force`. #793 is the fix and it is open, awaiting @peter.

A gate that can still falsely clear is not "tested". **In Review, until #793 lands.**

One consequence worth naming so nobody re-derives it: this ticket is no longer in the Tested-Not-Deployed census. It was not one of the five Kam asked to keep visible — it entered that state tonight, from my own walk, and is leaving it the same night.

## Two decisions recorded from Peter's #786 review, so neither is dropped

Both came out of the review of [PR #786](https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/786) and neither is fixed in it. Recording them here rather than leaving them in a PR thread.

### 1. The watch duplicates the scan leg — accepted, deferred, with the reason

Peter's review item 4: `base-image-watch.sh` carries a near-identical `docker run` + `python3` trivy parse to `refresh-base-images.sh`'s `scan` mode — same flags, same severity filter, same `0.58.1` pin, now hardcoded in both. The commit message's own principle ("two copies of the pull logic is how they drift apart") applies to the scan leg too, and the drift check covers the base **list** only, not the scan invocation or the trivy pin.

**Why it is not fixed in #786:** the watch needs machine-readable rows that `refresh-base-images.sh` does not emit — and as of the F-5 fix it needs **two more** fields (result-group count and total findings, the liveness proof that stops an empty scan reading as "cleared"). The right fix is a row-emitting flag in `refresh-base-images.sh`, which is the script the **ACR import leg** depends on. That is its own change with its own blast radius and its own reviewer.

**Open question for whoever picks it up:** the trivy pin is now in two places. That is the part most likely to drift silently, and it is cheap to cover with one more self-test case comparing the two pins — cheaper than the full de-duplication, and it removes the sharpest edge.

### 2. `alpine:3.22` is scanned by nothing — a gap, not a decision

QA F-3 on the same PR. `frontend/demo-overlay/Dockerfile:40` builds `FROM ${REGISTRY_PREFIX}alpine:3.22`, so it ships inside an image, and it is in **neither** `LOCAL_BASES` (so the ACR leg never `import --force`s it) **nor** the watch's `BASES` (so it is never scanned). Nobody chose that.

#786 adds a self-test that derives every base from the Dockerfiles and compose files and requires each to be gated or explicitly excluded — it discovers **11** where `BASES` holds **6**. The five extra now sit in `EXCLUDED_BASES` with reasons, and `alpine:3.22` is labelled a **genuine gap** rather than a decision, precisely so this comment has something to point at.

Four of the five are defensible exclusions — `busybox:1.37`, `bloxbean/yaci-cli:0.10.6` and `ollama/ollama:0.31.1` are local-development runtime images that are never a `FROM` for anything shipped, and `nginx:alpine` is an **unpinned floating tag** that cannot meaningfully be watched for digest drift (the drift is the tag's purpose). That last one is worth a separate look: an unpinned tag sits in the same compose file as the pinned nginx that **is** gated.

**The ask:** a ruling on whether `alpine:3.22` joins `BASES` + `LOCAL_BASES`. It is a two-file change that also puts the image in the ACR import leg, which is why #786 does not make it unilaterally.

## The replacement mechanism is built — PR #786

The dead cron now has a hand-runnable successor: **`Blockchain/Dev/scripts/base-image-watch.sh`**, on [PR #786](https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/786) (`57b4af8b6`), review requested from Peter.

**What it restores.** `refresh-base-images.sh` never gated — it reports and exits 0. The two failure conditions that made its report actionable were written in the *workflow*, so when Actions stopped, the scanner survived and the gate disappeared. This script is those conditions, as distinct exit codes: **10** = the residual cleared, run the ACR leg and close this ticket · **11** = an unexpected critical on a pinned base · **12** = the gate's own self-test failed · **0** = status quo. It delegates pulling to `refresh-base-images.sh local` instead of re-implementing it.

**It cannot pass vacuously.** `--self-test` needs no docker and asserts exit codes on five synthetic reports, three of them known-bad inputs that must fail — including *a scan that produced no row for postgres at all*, which would otherwise read as a clean pass. It also asserts the script's base list still matches `LOCAL_BASES` in `refresh-base-images.sh`, so a base added there cannot silently go unscanned. A full run executes the self-test first and refuses to report green if it fails.

**On the one deviation, stated plainly:** it does *not* exit non-zero on the postgres residual. That CVE is not ours to fix and does not clear with a version bump, so gating on it means red every month forever — and a permanent red is read as noise and then ignored, which is how a *real* critical ends up in a channel nobody checks. The pair `(postgres:15-alpine, CVE-2025-68121)` is baselined by exact match, its **disappearance** is what fires (exit 10), and a *different* critical on that same image still fails. The baseline is one line, printed on every run.

### The first run found what §3 predicted

**Five of the six pinned bases came back `MOVED`** — `node:24-alpine`, `nginx:1.30-alpine`, `nginxinc/nginx-unprivileged:1.30-alpine`, `edoburu/pgbouncer:v1.25.2-p0`, `redis:8-alpine`. Only postgres was unchanged, and only because I had pulled it minutes earlier for the re-measurement above.

That is *"pinned-tag digests go stale silently"* demonstrating itself, and it is the same `MOVED on all six` the 2026-08-01 run reported and nothing ever consumed.

```
node:24-alpine                          : 0 CRITICAL / 6 HIGH   (openssl 3.5.7-r0)
nginx:1.30-alpine                       : 0 CRITICAL / 4 HIGH   (openssl 3.5.7-r0)
nginxinc/nginx-unprivileged:1.30-alpine : 0 CRITICAL / 2 HIGH
edoburu/pgbouncer:v1.25.2-p0            : 0 CRITICAL / 40 HIGH  (openssl 3.5.6-r0)
redis:8-alpine                          : 0 CRITICAL / 2 HIGH   (openssl 3.5.7-r0)
postgres:15-alpine                      : 1 CRITICAL / 23 HIGH — CVE-2025-68121
                                          (gosu stdlib v1.24.6; openssl 3.5.7-r0)
VERDICT: status quo. exit 0.
```

**Noted, not gated:** `edoburu/pgbouncer` carries **40 HIGH** and sits a release behind on openssl (`3.5.6-r0` against `3.5.7-r0` everywhere else). Zero criticals, so the gate is silent on it by design — flagging it here so the number is on the record rather than only in a run nobody kept.

**The reminder half is not mine.** The script is not wired to any hook or schedule — Actions is retired and re-arming it there would be building on the thing that failed. Wednesday runs it on the 1st of each month from a Secuura session.

**This ticket still does not close.** The residual is still present; the close condition is unchanged. What has changed is that we will now be *told* when it clears, instead of finding out by accident.

**Correction to the comment above — one version number.**

I wrote the `libcrypto3` / `libssl3` installed version as **`3.5.5-r0`**. It is **`3.5.7-r0`**, fixed at `3.5.8-r0`. Verified against the scan output: `3.5.7-r0` and `3.5.8-r0` are the only two `3.5.x-r0` strings it contains.

It matters enough to correct rather than leave: `3.5.5` implies three patch releases of drift on the openssl leg, `3.5.7` is **one**. Anyone sizing the alpine refresh off the wrong figure would over-estimate how far behind that layer is.

Everything else in that comment stands as measured — CVE-2025-68121 still present in `gosu`'s vendored Go stdlib (`v1.24.6`), alpine layer 0 CRITICAL, the digest move `fceb6f86…` → `fe0737ba…`, and the missing 2026-09-01 watch run.

## Re-measurement 2026-09-02 — Case 1 still NOT met, and **the watch this ticket relies on is dead**

Ran the periodic action this ticket prescribes (*"periodically re-pull `postgres:15-alpine` and re-scan; close when the upstream rebuild lands"*). Two results, and the second one changes the ticket's standing.

### 1. The residual is still there — correctly parked

**Pulled first, because a stale local image is this ticket's own documented trap.** The local copy was from **2026-02-26**; the tag had republished:

```
digest BEFORE pull:  sha256:fceb6f86328c36f2438fae3b851b0cc57c4a7e69a58c866d9ce24281f2cf0c9c
digest AFTER pull:   sha256:fe0737ba566a2c5b2a28f34433c0a423261900ec17b9bf7ad115e1aae7e57f1b
```

Six months stale — exactly the §3 mechanism ("pinned-tag digests go stale silently"), caught by doing the pull rather than trusting the cache.

Trivy **0.71.0** (the ticket's earlier figures were 0.58.1), `--severity CRITICAL,HIGH`, on the fresh digest:

| target | type | CRITICAL | HIGH |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| `postgres:15-alpine` (alpine 3.24.1) | alpine | **0** | 2 |
| `usr/local/bin/gosu` | gobinary | **1** | 21 |

- **CVE-2025-68121 is still present** — `stdlib` **v1.24.6**, fixed in 1.24.13 / 1.25.7 / 1.26.0-rc.3. So the Case 1 condition (*postgres scans 0 CRITICAL → run the ACR leg and close*) has **not** been met. **This ticket stays open, still correctly.**
- **Worth sharpening for whoever closes it:** the critical is not in postgres or in alpine. It is in the vendored Go stdlib of the **`gosu` binary** inside the image. The alpine package layer is now **0 CRITICAL**. Clearing this needs Docker Hub to rebuild postgres with a `gosu` compiled against Go ≥ 1.24.13 — nothing in our control, as the ticket already says, but now located precisely rather than attributed to "the image".
- **New since the last measurement:** 2 HIGH on `libcrypto3` / `libssl3` — **CVE-2026-14456** (OpenSSL QUIC DoS, unbounded memory growth), installed `3.5.5-r0`… fixed at **`3.5.8-r0`**. This one *is* fixable by an upstream alpine refresh, unlike the gosu critical.

### 2. 🔴 The monthly watch has stopped, and nothing said so

The last comment here rests on *"the mechanism is doing its job"*. **It is not doing its job any more.**

`.github/workflows/base-image-refresh.yml` is scheduled `cron: "0 2 1 * *"` — the 1st of every month. Its run history:

```
2026-08-01T05:24:40Z  completed/failure   <- the run the last comment analysed
2026-07-02T06:56:49Z  completed/success
2026-07-02T06:46:07Z  completed/failure
```

**There is no 2026-09-01 run.** It was due yesterday and never fired, because GitHub Actions stopped starting jobs on 17 August (org billing) and Kam decided on **2026-08-27 not to restore it** — a decided state, not an outage, so nothing re-arms by itself.

The consequence for this ticket specifically: its "correctly parked" status was justified by an alarm that would tell us when the upstream rebuild landed. **That alarm is gone.** Parked now means *nobody will be told* — the ticket would sit until someone happened to re-run the scan by hand, which is what just happened, by accident of working the queue.

### 3. What this makes actionable

§3 of the description already proposed the remedy and even named the fallback: *"a lightweight refresh routine … Could live in `deploy.sh` or a small script + reminder."* With Actions retired, **the local-script form is no longer one of two options — it is the only one that can work.** That is in our hands and needs no external input.

Not building it in this comment; recording that the option set has collapsed to one, so whoever picks this up does not re-litigate scheduling it on Actions.

**Also still unconsumed:** the 08-01 run reported `MOVED` on **all six** pinned bases. Today's postgres pull confirms that drift is real and ongoing (six months on one tag). The watch reported drift; nothing ever acted on it; and now the watch does not report at all.

## Sweep note — **the watch you built fired, and it worked. Nobody read it.**

Verified on `develop` `454a64ebb`, 2026-08-14.

The monthly watch (`.github/workflows/base-image-refresh.yml`) ran on **2026-08-01** and **failed** — which is its designed alarm. It failed on **Case 2**, not on this ticket's postgres residual:

```
node:24-alpine    : 1 CRITICAL / 4 HIGH — criticals: CVE-2026-59873
postgres:15-alpine: 1 CRITICAL / 14 HIGH — criticals: CVE-2025-68121   <- this ticket's residual, expected
```

**Filed separately** rather than folded in here, because a critical on the base image of all ten services is not "the postgres residual" — see the new ticket.

## On this ticket's own residual

`postgres:15-alpine` still reports CVE-2025-68121, so the Case 1 condition (*postgres scans 0 CRITICAL → upstream rebuild landed → run the ACR leg and close*) has **not** been met. **This ticket stays open, correctly.** The mechanism is doing its job.

## What it is waiting for

`postgres:15-alpine` to scan 0 CRITICAL upstream. Nothing to do until then — which is worth saying explicitly, because an untouched High-priority ticket reads like neglect when it is actually a correctly-parked watch.

**One thing that would improve it:** every one of the six pinned bases also reported `MOVED` on that run — all six tags republished since the last pull. The watch reports drift but nothing consumes the report, so the images we build on are silently behind their own tags. Consider whether "MOVED on N bases" deserves its own periodic rebuild rather than only being noted.

*Backlog sweep 2026-08-14.*

**BLUF — retitled, and recording why so the correction is public rather than silent.**

**Old title (verbatim):**
> Residual infra-image criticals after KS-363: refresh stale redis:7-alpine digest (demo+local), track postgres CVE-2025-68121, add base-image refresh routine

**New title:**
